title: The tune success message claims a live re-read the sensing coordinator does not have — two probes were bought AFTER it reported applied
description:
COST A REAL, MEASURED DRAIN TONIGHT (staging, 2026-08-07).

'spacetraders tune --operation sensing expansion_enabled 2' printed:
  '✓ expansion_enabled: 1 -> 2 flag — the coordinator re-reads its config live and applies it on the
   next tick; no restart.'
That sentence is FALSE for this coordinator, and the tool's own help says so two screens earlier:
  'The SENSING coordinator has no live reader yet: a sensing tune persists immediately but is applied
   at the coordinator's next REBUILD (daemon restart or relaunch) — until then the RUNNING loop keeps
   its launch values, so do not rely on a sensing tune ... taking effect without a bounce.'

EVIDENCE THE WRITE DID NOT BITE:
  tune issued              ~03:09:50 local
  probe bought             03:10:13     <- after
  probe bought             03:10:19     <- after
  cycle line 03:11:03      'bought 2 reused 0 queued 3'
  treasury 385,572 -> 277,640 while the operator believed spending was off
After a daemon restart the very next cycle line read 'bought 0 reused 0 queued 0' and buying stopped.
So the tune was correct and the CONFIRMATION was wrong — the worst arrangement, because the operator
stops watching.

WHY P0 RATHER THAN A COSMETIC STRING BUG: this is the confirmation on a SPENDING switch. An operator
turning off spending in an emergency reads that sentence and reasonably stops escalating. Silence
would have been safer than a false success. The generic message is presumably emitted for every
operation and is true for the ones with live readers (bootstrap, contract, scoutpost) — which is
exactly why it must be per-operation, not a constant.

FIX, in order of value:
  1. Make the message reflect the TARGET coordinator's actual capability. The registry already knows
     which knobs bind at rebuild — several descriptions say 'applies at coordinator rebuild
     (restart/relaunch), not next tick' per KNOB. Emit that same distinction in the confirmation, per
     (operation, key).
  2. For a rebuild-only tune, say plainly what is still required: 'PERSISTED, NOT YET IN EFFECT —
     restart or relaunch the coordinator to apply.'
  3. Consider refusing to report success at all for a spending switch that cannot take effect, or
     offering to bounce the coordinator.

RELATED, AND THE REASON THIS KEEPS COSTING: sp-2p73w records the same class (coordinators capture
config at launch; a tune on a running coordinator is invisible until relaunch). That bead was filed
from the growth side. This is the sensing side, with money attached and a false confirmation on top.
There is no 'relaunch' verb in the CLI at all — 'container' exposes only get/list/logs/stop — so the
only lever an operator has is a full daemon restart.
notes:
Found while stopping a live treasury drain, not in review. The tune itself was right and persisted correctly (verified before restarting: expansion_enabled=2 source=live-config, capital_multiplier_k_milli reverted to 2000). Only the claim about when it applies was wrong.

Do not fix by making the sensing coordinator re-read live without thinking it through — several sensing knobs (inflight_cap, value_clamp_r) bind when the scan rotation is BUILT and their descriptions say so honestly. The defect is the confirmation message overstating, not the absence of a live reader.

title: [P0] Market-scan budget divides its fixed rate across 14,305 markets of which only 54 are SCANNABLE — parked probes admitted 0.15% of the time (19 spends vs 12,459 serve_from_store) and the allowance is left half-unspent
description:
The fleet cannot keep even 54 markets fresh. Measured on staging (TORWINDSTG, player 1,
2026-08-06). Two compounding causes, both live-observable.

CAUSE 1 — THE DENOMINATOR COUNTS MARKETS THAT CANNOT BE SCANNED.

  spacetraders_daemon_scan_budget_coverage{budget="market",player_id="1"} 14305
  (metric help: 'the denominator the fixed allowance is divided across, so a waypoint's
   scan interval is rate/coverage')

14,305 / 0.35 req/s = ~40,900 s = ~11.4 HOURS per market nominal. Measured staleness on the
markets we actually hold a probe on: avg 418 min, max 599 min — same order, so the
denominator is doing exactly what the metric says.

But a market with NO HULL STANDING ON IT cannot be scanned at all. The parked rotation
already knows this — the rotation field comment in probe_sensing_heartbeat.go says it
'drops anything unscannable', and the rotation is 54. So ~14,250 markets that can never
consume a scan are each drawing a share of the rate away from the 54 that can.

internal/domain/marketscan/budget.go documents the linear-decay property as INTENDED
('knowing twice as many markets means looking at each half as often … the price of a fixed
budget'). That reasoning is about MAP GROWTH. It does not follow for markets that are
physically unreadable: they are not being looked at half as often, they are not being
looked at at all, and their share is dead weight.

  Interval(b, weight, totalWeight)  budget.go:236
  MaxStaleness(b, marketsKnown)     budget.go:267 -> Interval(..., marketsKnown*clamp)
  marketsKnown <- b.aggregateLocked()  internal/application/ship/market_scan_budget.go:199,264,329

CAUSE 2 — DISCRETIONARY READS ARE STARVED TO 0.15%.

  scan_budget_decisions_total{budget="market",...}
    class=discretionary  decision=serve_from_store  12459
    class=discretionary  decision=spend                19     <-- 0.15% admitted
    class=earning        decision=spend             11389
    class=paired         decision=spend                25
    class=paired         decision=serve_from_store      19

The parked-probe rotation is the discretionary class. It is refused 99.85% of the time.
Every admitted read goes to 'earning' — a hull already standing somewhere scanning what is
under it. That is why the ONLY fresh markets are the 3 systems the trade fleet already
works, and why coverage can never expand on its own: the mechanism that would open new
ground is precisely the one being starved.

AND THE ALLOWANCE IS LEFT HALF-UNSPENT. Because unscannable markets hold shares they never
spend, actual draw is far below the 0.35 ceiling: ~11,400 spends over ~20h is ~0.16 req/s.
The sensing pacer confirms slack independently — 0.62 req/s issued against 1.53 residual,
brake 1.00 (fully released, limiter not under pressure). So this is not a case of the guard
correctly protecting a saturated API. There is real headroom being reserved for markets that
can never use it.

CONSEQUENCE — this is the top of the chain behind sp-a2dc5 and the trade collapse:
  ~14.3k-market denominator + 0.15% discretionary admission
    -> only trade-visited markets stay fresh -> 3 tradeable systems -> 49 sinks
    -> the fleet-wide 2-tranche absorption cap binds
    -> 194 of 213 tours (91%) die 'could not reserve tour depth'
sp-a2dc5's 'rotation bound 23m14s vs a real ~7h interval' is very likely a SYMPTOM of this
same denominator disagreement, not an independent defect. Reconcile the two before fixing
either.

ASK:
 1. Divide the rate across the SCANNABLE set, not every market ever heard of. A market with
    no hull present cannot consume a scan and should not hold a share. Keep the fixed 0.35
    ceiling — this is not a request to raise it (sp-k4z5b settled that a budget bounds COST,
    not staleness).
 2. Give the discretionary class a floor so the parked rotation cannot be starved to 0.15%
    by earning reads. Scheduling fairness within the existing ceiling, not a weaker guard.

NOT TRACED, do not assume: I did not follow how aggregateLocked() populates marketsKnown.
14,305 does not match market_data rows for player 1 (531) nor sensing_slots WANTED (9,419),
so it is counting something broader again — possibly per-good rows, all charted
marketplace-trait waypoints, or unscoped across players (market_data is MULTI-PLAYER,
PLAYBOOK 11). Pin that down first: if it is counting other players' rows the denominator is
simply wrong and the fix is smaller than the above.

ENV NOTE: market_data_max_age_minutes was tuned 75 -> 720 on the live staging tour container
on 2026-08-06 as a stopgap; revert with 'tune --operation tour market_data_max_age_minutes 0'
if you need original conditions. It does not affect any measurement in this bead — all
figures here are from the metrics endpoint and the budget code.

Filed by economy-analyst, read-only, from live staging measurement.
notes:
DENOMINATOR TRACED (step zero). 14,305 was NOT market_data and NOT per-good, so the
multi-player hypothesis is ruled out: MarketRepositoryGORM.ChartedMarketSystemCounts counts
`waypoints` rows in the open era that are not FUEL_STATION and carry the MARKETPLACE trait.
Re-run on staging: 14,851 over 1,607 systems (gauge 14,794 on its 5-min TTL; it grows with
charting). `waypoints` has NO player_id column - it is the shared universe map. Reconciles
against the other candidates: market_data holds 531 rows over only 86 distinct waypoints
(it IS per-good, but it is not the denominator); sensing_slots WANTED is 10,351; the parked
rotation is 54. So the denominator was arithmetically exactly what it claimed. The defect
was semantic, and the fix is the one the ASK describes, not a scoping change.

FIXED (commit c3402da5 + a9dacc1a + 2b188a07, branch sp-b3ny4, base 9c8b19ba).
CAUSE 1: the denominator is now the ACTIVE DEMAND SET - markets asked about within a
one-hour window (parkedsensing's own intervalCap). Asking is the only way a scan happens,
so the markets being asked about are exactly the markets able to spend; the set is pruned,
not monotone. ChartedMarketCounter/charted/chartedAt/refreshChartedCount deleted.
CAUSE 2: a discretionary floor of one admitted read in ValueClampR, derived (s = 1/clampR is
exactly the share that lets the class fund MaxStaleness on its own). Placed at rule 5 only -
it cannot reach the token cap or the dueness rule. The 0.35 ceiling is untouched.

THIS EXPLAINS sp-a2dc5 - SAME DEFECT, NOT AN INDEPENDENT ONE. MaxStaleness inverts exactly:
23m14s -> 61 markets, 10m17s -> 27, 23m37s -> 62. Those are the ONLY three values in the
entire staging log, all tiny, none near the ~95h the 15k denominator implies - because the
refusal line only prints WHEN the bound is small (selection bias). The tour was reading
len(seen) while the coverage gauge read charted. Mechanism: refreshChartedCount accepted a
legitimately-empty count as a new denominator, and on this database an unresolvable era makes
eraScopePredicate(nil) emit `era_id IS NULL`, which matches 0 of 78,066 waypoint rows and
returns (empty, nil) - collapsing charted to 0. The function's own comment promised the
invariant its code did not enforce (it guarded err != nil only). Deleting the second count
makes the disagreement structurally impossible. sp-a2dc5 needs NO change to
market_freshness.go or trade_fleet.go for the bound itself.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE THE OPERATOR MUST KNOW. In the healthy (uncollapsed) state the bound
was 15,023*8/0.35 = ~95 HOURS, so max(75min, bound) meant the firm-sink FRESH money guard was
effectively INERT - accepting rows up to four days old. After this change the bound is ~23 min
at a ~60-market rotation, so the FLOOR becomes the operative number again and the guard bites.
Keep market_data_max_age_minutes at 720 across the deploy; revert only after parked-market
staleness is confirmed low.

VERIFICATION: RED first on both causes (expected Spend, got ServeFromStore). 89 packages
green, -race clean on marketscan/ship/trading/captain/cmd, build+vet+gofmt clean. 9 mutation
probes, all KILLED with named tests; two probes SURVIVED first and drove two extra tests
(weight sum and fleet median must be taken over the rotation, since learned spreads
deliberately outlive it).

ADDENDUM - sp-rsk2m FOLDED IN (commit 9bd3e774), and it closes the other direction of the same
defect. FreshnessCap is now max(floor, min(bound, derivedCapCeiling)), ceiling 12h: the derived
term could previously widen without limit, and at the census it reached 88h16m22s - a fail-closed
money guard admitting prices nearly four days old, silently. The ceiling bounds the DERIVED term
only (an operator floor above it still wins) and is deliberately NOT applied to MaxStaleness, whose
job is the scanner's spending escape rather than a consumer's trust decision. Headroom checked
against measurement per sp-rsk2m's warning: 12h is only reached past ~1,890 markets, vs a measured
4 scanned in the last hour / 18 in six / 86 with cached data at all. sp-rsk2m's suggested denominator
(sensing_slots slot_kind=MARKET) measures 10,978 and would still derive ~70h, so the demand set is
the tighter and correct fix.

COLLISION WARNING FOR THE sp-a2dc5 LANE. aggregateLocked no longer contains max(tally, census) -
BOTH terms are deleted (b.seen and b.charted: 0 references). sp-a2dc5's (a) prerequisite is already
satisfied here, and its intended end-state is preserved: an unasked budget reports an empty rotation
so consumers fall back to their operator floor (test:
TestRotationInputs_AnUnaskedBudgetReportsAnEmptyRotationRatherThanAWidenedCap). If that lane lands
its own edit to aggregateLocked first, it conflicts in the same function.
close_reason:
Merged as 37771abb, with sp-rsk2m folded in. Root cause of the staging trade collapse.

THREE FIXES. (1) DENOMINATOR: the fixed rate was divided across every market ever charted or asked about, but only a market a hull stands on can consume a read — the rest held shares they could never spend. Now len(b.demand): the set asked about within the rotation's own intervalCap, PRUNED. b.seen and b.charted have zero references left; census and uptime tally are both gone. It tracks rather than snapshots — probes D1/D2 prove the prune and the refresh are each load-bearing.
(2) DISCRETIONARY FLOOR: the parked rotation was admitted 0.0% live (1,454 serve_from_store, 0 spend — worse than the bead's 0.15%), starved by earning reads from hulls already on station, so only trade-visited markets stayed fresh and coverage could never expand. Now a PRIORITY derived from ValueClampR (s = 1/ValueClampR, exactly the share that lets the class fund MaxStaleness unaided) — deliberately NOT a reservation, which would have been a second bucket and therefore extra rate.
(3) CEILING: the derived cap had no upper bound, so it widened without limit as the map grew.

THE LIVE FINDING, verified independently before gating: at census 15,797 the bound computes 100.3h, so max(12h floor, 100.3h) = 100.3h — the firm-sink money guard was admitting 4.2-DAY-OLD PRICES on main, and sp-a2dc5's restored floor was completely INERT underneath it. Neither P0 closed this alone; that is exactly why the sequencing argument mattered.

THE CEILING WAS WRONG AT 12h AND sp-a2dc5's TESTS CAUGHT IT — the best moment of the pair. Three tests went red on rebase and were RIGHT, not stale: staleMarkets stages a row at marketDataAgeFloor + 1h, and sp-a2dc5 had just moved that floor to 720, making the row 13h against an era-5 incident rotation of 13h56m. That row IS explained by its rotation; a 12h ceiling refused it — precisely the too-tight cap sp-rsk2m forbade and what sp-k4z5b was raised for. THE FIXTURES WERE NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: 'that would have been rewriting a P0 incident's acceptance criterion to fit a constant I chose.' Now 24h, sized above the largest rotation bound on record rather than picked. Verified: 0 changes to the rotation/placement test helpers.

ARITHMETIC CONFIRMED — THE FLOOR BINDS BY ~20x, and it is intended, not an accident: at demand N=4/54/86 the bound is 0.03/0.34/0.55h, so max(12h, ·) = 12h in every case. The ceiling engages only above 3,780 markets at 0.35.

HUNK 2 WAS A GENUINE BEHAVIOURAL CONFLICT and was resolved in this lane's favour, on my ruling. sp-a2dc5 claimed 'a freshness bound wants the LARGEST count'; this lane superseded it, because erring large is what produced the inert guard. Both biases were compensating for an INACCURATE denominator — with an accurate one you want bounds, not a bias, and max(floor, min(bound, ceiling)) supplies both. The other two sp-a2dc5 claims (never publish an uptime tally; uncounted -> UNKNOWN -> caller's floor) are PRESERVED and tested.

RULINGS #4: reads increase, bounded and stated — the escape now fires at ~23m instead of ~100h, at rate/ValueClampR = 0.044 req/s INDEPENDENT of N. Spends are strictly TIGHTER: max(floor, min(MaxStaleness(N_demand), 24h)) <= max(floor, MaxStaleness(N_census)) for all inputs; no buy admitted that was previously blocked. Rate, burst and rule 4 untouched.

8 probes re-run post-rebase, all killed, each naming its tests. BUILD/VET/TEST/RACE all RC=0, 89 packages.

NOT YET DEPLOYED. Watch after deploy: coverage 15,797 -> tens; parked_sensing_staleness_seconds median 9.3h -> under 1h (the primary falsifier); discretionary spend >= 1-in-8. NOTE the expansion_enabled=2 freeze FLATTERS these — a small demand set is the best case, and coverage EXPANSION is unobservable until probes resume.

title: [P0] REGRESSION of sp-k4z5b: rotation bound computes 23m against a real ~7h interval, so the 75-min floor binds again — 3 of 54 parked markets visible, 91% of tours dying
description:
MEASURED (staging TORWINDSTG, 2026-08-06).

Staleness of the markets the fleet has a probe PARKED on (sensing_slots state=PARKED,
slot_kind=MARKET, joined to market_data, deduped per waypoint):

  parked slots 54 | avg age 418 min (7.0h) | min 45 min | max 599 min (10h)
  WITHIN the 75-minute tour cap: 3

So 51 of 54 probes standing watch produce data the tour planner will not look at. The 3
markets that ARE fresh are fresh because TRADE hulls physically visit them, not because the
sensing rotation scanned them.

Scan attribution today (870 total 'MarketScanner] Successfully scanned' lines):
  tour 302 | construction 162 | scout_tour 109 | contract 107 |
  probe_sensing_coordinator 89 | contract_fleet 87 | idle 14
54 parked probes produced 89 scans in ~20h — about 1.6 scans per probe per day.

ROOT CAUSE (not the sensing pacer). The sensing coordinator's own heartbeat looks healthy
and is NOT the gate: pacer 0.45-0.73 req/s, sensing residual ~1.65, brake 1.00 (fully
released, so the API limiter is not under pressure). The reads are declined DOWNSTREAM at
the MarketScanner choke point by the fleet's ONE market-scan budget:

  [MarketScanner] Serving X1-BR4-CE5F from store - market-scan budget
  {"action":"scan_served_from_store"}

internal/application/ship/market_scan_budget.go: const defaultBudgetReqPerSec = 0.35,
explicitly 'sized from the era-5 measurement this budget was written for' (era-5 total
market reads 0.644 req/s of a 2.00 req/s ceiling).

THE ARITHMETIC THAT NOW BITES. sensing_slots holds 9,419 WANTED + 54 PARKED MARKET slots
across 1,482 sensing_systems. Spreading 0.35 req/s over ~9.4k known market slots is
~26,900 s = ~7.5 h per market — which matches the measured 7.0h average almost exactly.
The budget's design note says this is intentional: 'because the interval widens with the
map — it is the number that stops mattering how large the map gets.' That property is
CORRECT and worth keeping (it is what makes parking more probes API-safe).

THE OPEN QUESTION, and the thing to check first: the tour's cap is documented as
'Effective cap = max(market_data_max_age_minutes, rotation bound)', with
market_data_max_age_minutes sitting at its 75-minute default. If the rotation bound were
tracking the real ~7.5h interval, those 51 parked markets would be VISIBLE and this would
be a non-issue. They are not visible. So either the rotation bound is not being computed
from the true budget-derived interval, or it is not reaching the freshness clause. Confirm
WHICH before changing any number — that determines whether this is a cap-adaptation defect
or a budget-sizing decision.

DO NOT 'fix' this by raising inflight_cap (parked-scan concurrency, currently 3). That is
upstream of the gate: more concurrent attempts would still be served from store. And do NOT
weaken the 0.35 budget without pricing it against the 2.00 req/s server ceiling — it is a
rate guard, RULINGS #4.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the top of the causal chain behind sp-9cwf4 and the fleet's trade
collapse. 3 visible systems -> 49 sinks -> the fleet-wide 2-tranche absorption cap binds ->
194 of 213 tours (91%) die 'could not reserve tour depth'. Coverage famine is the cause;
sink contention is the symptom.

Filed by economy-analyst from live staging measurement.
notes:
CODE MERGED as f731c12a, deliberately AHEAD of sp-b3ny4. Bead stays OPEN because it is blocked by sp-b3ny4 and that is correct: this lane makes the bound track the right SIGNAL, but the bound is only right once sp-b3ny4 fixes the POPULATION it is derived from.

SEQUENCING WAS INVERTED ON THIS LANE'S EVIDENCE, against my framing. I called (b) a belt to (a)'s braces and said it was worth landing regardless. Wrong: (b) is a PREREQUISITE for sp-b3ny4. MaxStaleness = Interval(b, baselineWeight, marketsKnown x clamp), so the bound is PROPORTIONAL to the denominator — at ~15,000 markets it computes ~94h, at sp-b3ny4's ~54 scannable it computes ~20m. cap = max(floor, bound), so narrowing the denominator makes the FLOOR binding the instant sp-b3ny4 lands, and at 75 that is precisely the sp-k4z5b incident. sp-ry4r8 had deleted the 720 floor arguing 'the bound is ~13h56m so the floor is inert' — narrowing the population turns that argument inside out.

SECOND PREREQUISITE: once the census is ~54, len(seen) routinely EXCEEDS it, so max(tally, census) would let an uptime counter override the narrowed denominator and silently re-inflate the bound. (a) removes that term from the freshness face only; pacing keeps its own max(seen, charted).

(a) PROOF THE BOUND TRACKED UPTIME, NOT THE MAP: it moved 23m14s -> 23m37s (61 -> 62 markets) in FOUR SECONDS, while the census sits on a 5-minute TTL.

DENOMINATOR TRACED; sp-b3ny4's 'maybe it is a scoping one-liner' escape hatch is CLOSED BY DISPROOF. marketsKnown <- max(len(seen), charted); charted <- ChartedMarketSystemCounts (market_repository.go:240), era-scoped waypoints with the MARKETPLACE trait, fuel stations excluded. Of the three hypotheses: per-good rows NO; all charted marketplace-trait waypoints YES; unscoped across players IMPOSSIBLE — the waypoints table has NO player_id column at all (verified in information_schema; it is the shared universe map) and market_data has exactly 1 distinct player_id on staging. marketsKnown never reads market_data. 14,305 / 14,900 / 15,023 are ONE counter over time, climbing ~1,400/hr with charting. 531 vs 86 was a GRAIN difference (~6.2 goods per market), not a disagreement.

MY BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS ALSO CORRECTED: the refusal lines came from a process that booted 08:09:45 and restarted 09:34:14 — a short-lived process's last gasps, exactly when the tally term is smallest. The symptom is LATENT, not relieved; it returns on every restart-into-a-cold-census and every new era. The 75->720 staging tune landed ~20:25, eleven hours later, and does not touch the evidence.

THREE STALE-MARKET TESTS went green-for-the-wrong-reason when the floor rose, and are now pinned RELATIVE to the floor rather than a literal age: TestStocker_Pick_StaleForeignMarketExcludes, TestStocker_Standing_StaleForeignMarketParksFailClosed, TestTour_PlacementArmed_StalenessGateExcludesStaleListings. Neighbouring rotation-arm tests swept and NOT vacuous; two comments the helper change falsified were corrected.

STILL OPEN AND IMPORTANT: sp-rsk2m — THE DERIVED BOUND HAS NO CEILING. At today's census it computes ~94h, so a guard documented as fail-closed is silently admitting market data almost FOUR DAYS old. Live right now. Overlaps sp-b3ny4; fold or close as duplicate but KEEP THE CEILING.

go test -race ./... RC=0, 89 packages, zero failures. 3 mutation probes killed, each naming its tests.
close_reason: Merged as f731c12a; unblocked and closed now that sp-b3ny4 (37771abb) has landed. Together they close the freshness collapse: this lane made the bound track the right SIGNAL (removing the uptime tally, restoring the proven floor), sp-b3ny4 fixed the POPULATION it derives from and bounded it. Neither was sufficient alone — this lane's floor raise was INERT under sp-b3ny4's uncapped 100.3h bound, and sp-b3ny4's narrowing would have re-fired the sp-k4z5b incident without this lane's floor. THIS LANE'S TESTS CAUGHT sp-b3ny4's 12h ceiling as too tight, which is the single best outcome of the pairing. One claim of this lane's was superseded on my ruling: 'a freshness bound wants the largest count' — see sp-b3ny4's close reason.

title: [P0] Gate feed HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCK: an unaffordable IRON step aborts the whole leg, so QUARTZ_SAND behind it is never bought — starves the FAB_MATS factory and stalls the gate on its last material
description:
The gate factory dispatches haulers to buy an input the spend guards RELIABLY refuse, 297 times,
and each rejection is discovered only AFTER the hull has flown the leg. Affordability is fully
knowable before dispatch. Every acquisition failure in the log is this one good.

OBSERVED (staging, TORWINDSTG, X1-KP46, 2026-08-05):

  WARNING: Gate factory: acquired nothing of IRON at X1-KP46-H51 — the spend guards stopped
           the fill, so TORWINDSTG-C feeds no factory this leg
           {"action":"buy_acquired_nothing","good":"IRON","ship":"TORWINDSTG-C"}

  count of "acquired nothing of IRON" : 297
  count of "acquired nothing of" ANY  : 297
  -> 100% of acquisition failures are IRON. NO other input has failed even once, across
     8 goods and 223 successful input deliveries (COPPER 1343u/50, SILICON_CRYSTALS 1240u/47,
     COPPER_ORE 1138u/29, IRON 586u/24, ELECTRONICS 525u/23, QUARTZ_SAND 500u/20,
     MICROPROCESSORS 475u/23, IRON_ORE 230u/7). This is not general flakiness — it is one
     (good, market) pair that is structurally unaffordable and is retried forever.
  Hit across MULTIPLE hulls: TORWINDSTG-B, -C and -D all fly the leg and all return empty.

WHY IT ALWAYS FAILS: X1-KP46-H51 sells IRON as EXPORT at SCARCE supply, priced 2956-3480/unit
and climbing as we bid against ourselves (three consecutive fills went 2956 -> 3207 -> 3480 in
seven minutes). A full 60-unit trade-volume fill is ~209,000 credits, which breaches the
working-capital reserve. The guard is CORRECT and must not be touched (RULINGS #4). The defect
is that the leg is dispatched at all.

THE INFORMATION IS AVAILABLE BEFORE DISPATCH: we know the market (H51), the good (IRON), the
cached purchase price, the intended unit count, and the current deployable capital. The product
of the first four compared against the fifth predicts the rejection exactly. Nothing about this
requires flying there to discover.

IT IS ALSO THE LEAST VALUABLE LEG. F45 (the FAB_MATS factory, the ONLY source of the only
material the gate still needs) currently reads:
    IRON              IMPORT  supply=MODERATE  vol=111  buy=292   <-- already adequate
    QUARTZ_SAND       IMPORT  supply=SCARCE    vol=60   buy=52
    SILICON_CRYSTALS  IMPORT  supply=SCARCE    vol=60   buy=98
    COPPER            IMPORT  supply=SCARCE    vol=60   buy=670
So the input we repeatedly fail to buy — at 3480/unit from a scarce EXPORT — is the one the
factory is LEAST short of, while three genuinely scarce co-inputs are available cheaply
(QUARTZ_SAND is 23/unit at X1-KP46-B7 and X1-KP46-H53, EXCHANGE, LIMITED, volume 180).

COST: 297 wasted hauler legs. This lands at the worst possible time — FAB_MATS is now the ONLY
incomplete gate material (1141/1600, 459 remaining) and hauling capacity is the scarce resource.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. PREDICT BEFORE DISPATCH: before routing a hull to acquire input G at market M, compare
   (cached unit price x intended units) against currently deployable capital. If the spend guard
   would reject it, do not dispatch the leg — choose another input, another market, or no leg.
   Test: stub a market whose fill exceeds headroom; assert ZERO navigate commands are issued
   (assert on the command count, not on the eventual outcome).
2. BACK OFF A LOSING PAIR: after N consecutive rejections for the same (good, market),
   deprioritise that pair for a cooldown rather than retrying every discovery pass. 297 identical
   retries is not resilience. Test asserts attempt count stops growing.

title: [P0] PROD dead 21.5h: one hull the API cannot return (TORWIND-5, error 3000) crash-loops the contract worker forever — no quarantine, 34,279 restarts, 372k idle
description:
PROD (TORWIND) HAS EARNED NOTHING FOR 21.5 HOURS. One hull that the upstream API cannot return
(TORWIND-5, persistent error 3000) crash-loops the contract worker forever. There is no quarantine
for an unreadable ship, so a single poisoned hull takes down the entire pipeline indefinitely and
leaves 372,173 credits idle.

OBSERVED (prod, TORWIND, X1-BG40, 2026-08-05 22:15 UTC):
  last transaction    2026-08-05 00:43:43  -> 21.5 HOURS of zero economic activity
  treasury            372,173 (frozen)
  containers          RUNNING 10 (all heartbeating CURRENT, 22:15:xx), FAILED 34,279 cumulative
  daemon              ALIVE and healthy — this is NOT a dead daemon or a crashed process

THE UPSTREAM FACT (not our bug, but the trigger):
  GET /my/ships/TORWIND-5 -> {"code":3000,"message":"The server did not return a valid response."}
  Reproduced repeatedly over 21.5h. It is NOT transient.
  ISOLATED TO THAT ONE HULL — verified ship by ship:
    TORWIND-1 OK DOCKED @ X1-BG40-A2      TORWIND-2 OK IN_TRANSIT @ X1-BG40-K87
    TORWIND-3 OK IN_ORBIT @ X1-BG40-G47   TORWIND-4 OK IN_ORBIT @ X1-BG40-A3
    TORWIND-5 ERR 3000
  WORSE: GET /my/ships (the LIST endpoint) ALSO fails, so the poisoned hull breaks FLEET-WIDE
  reads, not merely its own single-ship read. Any code path that enumerates the fleet is affected.

THE LOOP WE OWN (verified in gobot/daemon.log):
  INFO  Resuming existing active contract   {contract cmsfd1yqu3uavsl73370nq0ph, ship TORWIND-5}
  INFO  Contract profitability confirmed
  INFO  Contract deliveries processing started
  INFO  Contract delivery status  {units_fulfilled:0, units_remaining:47, units_required:47}
  INFO  Contract delivery processing initiated
  INFO  Ship state reload initiated  {ship_symbol: TORWIND-5}
  ERROR Ship state reload failed          x9
  ERROR command execution failed          x10
  ERROR Worker for ship TORWIND...        x2
  ERROR Container contract...             x2
  -> worker dies -> container respawns -> resumes the SAME contract on the SAME hull -> repeat.
  34,279 cumulative FAILED containers is this loop, running since the era began.

COLLATERAL DAMAGE — SILENT DOUBLE DELIVERY:
  contract cmsfd1yqu3uavsl73370nq0ph  ALUMINUM x47 -> X1-BG40-D40
  API reports unitsFulfilled = 94 against unitsRequired = 47, and fulfilled = STILL false.
  The daemon's own view reads units_fulfilled:0. It delivered 47, crashed before recording the
  delivery, resumed from a stale view, and delivered 47 AGAIN. ~47 ALUMINUM wasted (~17,625 at
  the 375/unit ask the log itself planned against). The over-delivery stopped only because the
  loop now crashes BEFORE it can deliver at all — the waste was bounded by a deeper failure,
  not by any guard.

WHY P0: an entire agent has produced zero income for 21.5 hours and cannot self-recover. Every
existing recovery path is defeated — the daemon is alive, the coordinators heartbeat, the
containers restart successfully. Nothing is "down", so nothing intervenes. It will loop forever.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. QUARANTINE: after N consecutive ship-state-reload failures on the SAME ship, mark that hull
   unavailable, exclude it from selection, and let the pipeline continue with other hulls. One
   unreadable ship must never be able to block a coordinator indefinitely. Test drives an API
   stub that fails only for ship X and asserts other hulls still get dispatched.
2. FLEET-READ RESILIENCE: a fleet enumeration must survive one member failing to deserialise —
   return the readable ships and report the unreadable ones, rather than failing the whole call.
   Test: list endpoint where one entry errors; assert the other N-1 are returned.
3. NO SILENT RE-DELIVERY: before delivering, reconcile against the SERVER's unitsFulfilled, not
   only local state. A contract already at or above unitsRequired must never be delivered into
   again. Test asserts zero delivery calls when server-side fulfilled >= required.
4. AUTO-FULFIL THE OVER-DELIVERED CASE: when server unitsFulfilled >= unitsRequired but
   fulfilled=false, fulfil the contract rather than looping. This alone unblocks prod today.
5. CRASH-LOOP CIRCUIT BREAKER: a container that fails and respawns more than N times on the same
   root error must stop and raise, not restart silently forever. 34,279 restarts is not recovery.
6. OBSERVABILITY: emit a counter/alert for "container restarted >N times on identical error" and
   for "agent has had zero transactions for >M minutes while coordinators are healthy". Both
   conditions were invisible for 21.5 hours.

NOTE ON SCOPE: criteria 1, 2, 5 and 6 are general resilience and are what actually matter — the
specific upstream 3000 will presumably clear on its own or at the next weekly reset. The lesson
is that ONE bad hull silently cost a full day of an agent's income.

RELATED: sp-rnm3q (staging, refuel escalation) is a DIFFERENT bug but the same theme — a
transient/one-off upstream condition escalating into a long, self-inflicted outage with no
re-evaluation once the condition clears.

Three purchases landed inside 68 MILLISECONDS, all recording the SAME balance_after — none observed the others' spend. This drained the staging treasury from ~380k to ~46k in twelve minutes and deadlocked every income path in the fleet.

  13:41:49.306986  PURCHASE_CARGO  construction_supply  -99,660  balance_after 115542
  13:41:49.374545  PURCHASE_CARGO  construction_supply  -98,714  balance_after 115542
  13:41:49.374580  PURCHASE_CARGO  construction_supply  -98,714  balance_after 115542
                                                        --------
                                                        -297,088 in 68 ms

  Note: identical amounts (-98,714) 35 MICROSECONDS apart, and all three record an
  IDENTICAL balance_after — the ledger shows they each read the same pre-buy treasury.

WHY EACH ONE PASSES: at the time treasury was ~412k and the working-capital reserve 189,701.
A single 99k buy leaves ~313k, comfortably above the reserve, so the guard correctly allows it.
Three of them leave ~115k — BELOW the reserve by ~75k. The guard is evaluated PER-BUY; the
breach is only visible in AGGREGATE.

BLAST RADIUS (the reason this is P0, not P1): the drained float then blocked EVERY spending
path at once, and the guards — behaving correctly — turned it into a hard deadlock:
  contract:     "source-buy would breach the reserve floor - treasury 46412, cost 52992,
                 reserve 50000; parking" (four successive workers spawned, hit the wall, parked)
  construction: "Factory input buy would breach - treasury 46412, cost 130800, reserve 150000"
  tour:         "Capital budget: tour max-spend cut from 11603 to 0 - trade's 60% share of 0
                 deployable (treasury 46412, reserve 150000)"
  Net effect: nothing could buy, therefore nothing could earn, therefore nothing could recover.
  Only refuels (unguarded) kept spending, ~200 credits/min. Contracts do NOT rotate, so there
  was no cheaper contract to fall through to. Recovery required scrapping a hull for 139,511.

THIS IS THE sp-w3he CROSS-CONTAINER SPEND CAP'S JOB. Either it is not wired into the new
construction_supply path at all, or these three buys share a container/goroutine set and bypass
it. RULINGS #4: money guards fail closed and are never weakened — this is a guard that is not
being CONSULTED on a new path, which is the same failure with a different shape.

THREE OPERATIONS SHARE ONE TREASURY with no visible arbitration: construction_supply, tour, and
contract all bought within the same 90-minute window (PURCHASE_CARGO -761,919 total against
SELL_CARGO +326,938). Even without the 68ms race, three independent spenders against one float
and per-buy-only guards is structurally unsafe.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Concurrent buys cannot collectively breach the working-capital reserve. A test must launch N
   simultaneous purchase attempts whose SUM exceeds the reserve headroom and assert that the
   total spend leaves treasury >= reserve. Per-buy-only checking must FAIL this test.
2. The reservation must be taken BEFORE the API call and released on failure — checking a
   balance that a sibling is about to change is the bug; an atomic reserve/commit is the fix.
3. construction_supply specifically is covered (it is the path that raced here), and the test
   names it.
4. Cross-operation: a construction_supply buy and a contract buy racing must also be serialised
   against the same float, not just two construction buys.
5. Observability: emit a counter when a buy is denied for AGGREGATE (not per-buy) headroom, so
   this is visible without forensic ledger archaeology.
6. Regression: a single buy with ample headroom is unchanged (no new serialisation latency on
   the common path).

/tmp/st-staging-daemon-gatefleet.log). The gate-fleet operation (commits 76440cc1 / 5f3986be)
is the code that introduced the concurrent construction_supply buyers. NOT on prod.

halt the drain. Restarting the gate operation before this is fixed RE-ARMS the same drain.

incident window.

RESIDUAL FOUND BY sp-v2a2h (2026-08-05), squarely in this bead's family and deliberately left here rather than fixed there.

Two CONCURRENT delivery legs in the same tick both derive their commitment figure before either one buys, and only a lot's OWN material carries a reservation. So the cross-material arm of a mixed delivery trip can still be double-bought WITHIN a single tick. sp-v2a2h closed the across-tick and across-restart cases (commitment now derived from hull cargo, which cannot lapse while cargo is aboard) but the same-tick concurrent case remains.

This is pre-existing, not a regression from sp-v2a2h.

title: Refuel 500 costs 41min: retry budget too short (3 attempts/~5min) + hulls carry OVER-CAPACITY fuel (729/600) and refuel anyway
description:
A transient upstream 500 on the refuel endpoint costs ~41 MINUTES and blocks the entire serial contract pipeline. Two defects compose: the retry budget gives up far too early, and hulls are carrying OVER-CAPACITY fuel that makes the refuel attempt pointless in the first place.

OBSERVED (staging, TORWINDSTG, X1-KP46, 2026-08-05). Full verified causal chain:

  09:28-09:34  refuel at X1-KP46-I56 fails 3x
               error: "failed to refuel: ... max retries exceeded: server error (500)"
  09:34:19     "Refuel retries exhausted at waypoint, attempting alternate fuel stop"
  09:34:19     "Rerouting to alternate fuel stop after exhausting retries" -> X1-KP46-K84
  12:34:20Z    departs I56 (-206,104) -> K84 (-64,82), ~144 units, flightMode=DRIFT
  13:15:00Z    arrival — a 41-MINUTE leg
  meanwhile    contract_fleet_coordinator logs "Contract already has an active hull -
               waiting" every tick; the serial pipeline is blocked behind this one hull.
               Zero transactions for 33+ min; treasury flat ~25k/hr; the gate's factory
               input purchases then fail the working-capital reserve and park.

  THE HULL DID NOT NEED FUEL. Live API at the time: fuel 729/600 — OVER CAPACITY.
  A second hull, TORWINDSTG-9, also reads over capacity (726/600). All nine other hulls
  read exactly at-or-under capacity and behave normally. TORWINDSTG-7 read 613/600 earlier
  after its own refuel-retry storm (see sp-ehf4x) — three sightings, all post-refuel.

DRIFT IS NOT THE BUG — it is correct behaviour. routing_engine.py only reaches DRIFT when
neither BURN nor CRUISE is viable (viable_modes empty), and it carries a +100000s penalty so
it is a genuine last resort. Given fuel believed low, DRIFT was the right call. Do not "fix"
the flight-mode selector.

=== FIX 1 (Admiral-directed): RETRY BUDGET IS FAR TOO SHORT ===
gobot/internal/application/ship/refuel_retry.go, refuelShipWithRetryCore:
  maxAttempts = 3, backoff = backoffBase * 2^(attempt-1).
  Measured from the incident: attempt 2 at 09:31:16, attempt 3 at 09:34:19 (183s apart),
  total window roughly 5-6 minutes before giving up.
REQUIRED: keep retrying a RETRYABLE (5xx) refuel failure for AT LEAST 10 MINUTES of
wall-clock before escalating to the alternate-stop reroute. A 500 is transient by nature and
the escalation is enormously more expensive than waiting — 41 minutes of a blocked pipeline
versus a few more minutes of backoff.
  - Bound the budget by TOTAL ELAPSED TIME, not attempt count, so backoff growth cannot
    silently shorten it.
  - Cap the backoff interval so the tail does not become one long sleep (e.g. cap at 60-90s
    and keep retrying until the 10-minute budget is spent).
  - Keep isRetryableRefuelError's non-transient fast-fail path unchanged — a 4xx must still
    fail fast, NOT burn 10 minutes.

=== FIX 2 (Admiral-directed): OVER-CAPACITY FUEL ===
Hulls reach fuel_current > fuel_capacity (729/600, 726/600, 613/600). This is reported by the
LIVE API, not merely a local artifact, and the local ships row shows 600/600 — so local and
remote disagree AND the remote value is impossible.
  Suspects to investigate, in order:
  a) the units we send. adapters/api/client_fleet.go RefuelShip(..., units *int) sends
     body["units"] when non-nil, else {}. If any caller computes units without clamping to
     (capacity - current), we can request an overfill. FIND THE CALLER THAT COMPUTES UNITS.
  b) adoptRefuelledFuel (adapters/api/ship_repository_actions.go:173) adopts
     UpdateFuelFromAPI(result.FuelCurrent, result.FuelCapacity) VERBATIM — it does not reject
     or clamp a current > capacity response, so a bad API value is persisted unchallenged.
  REQUIRED: (i) never request more units than the tank can take; (ii) treat a
  current > capacity response as anomalous — clamp, log loudly, and do not let it silently
  drive later fuel math.

=== FIX 3 (falls out of the above): DO NOT REFUEL A FULL TANK ===
refuelShipWithRetryCore enters its retry loop with NO fullness precondition — only
refuelShip's HasFuel station check. A hull at or above capacity should skip the refuel
entirely rather than call the endpoint, fail, retry 3x, and reroute 144u across the system
for fuel it does not need. This alone would have prevented the whole incident.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A 5xx refuel failure is retried for >= 10 minutes wall-clock before any alternate-stop
   reroute. Test with a fake clock + an API stub returning 500, asserting elapsed budget.
2. A 4xx refuel failure still fails fast (regression on isRetryableRefuelError).
3. A hull whose fuel >= capacity SKIPS the refuel call entirely (no API call made — assert on
   the stub's call count, not just on the outcome).
4. A refuel request never asks for more units than (capacity - current).
5. An API response with current > capacity is clamped and logged; the persisted row never
   holds an over-capacity value.
6. Regression: normal refuel-to-full on a partially empty tank is unchanged.

RELATED: sp-ehf4x (contract worker silent ~4 min after refuel-retry exhaustion) is the SAME
code path — that bead's dead window and this bead's 41-minute detour are two symptoms of the
same escalation. Consider fixing together.

CONTEXT: found on the staging stack (deploy/staging, db spacetraders_staging, socket
/tmp/spacetraders-staging.sock, log /tmp/st-staging-daemon-gatefleet.log). Reproduce there,
NOT on prod. Prod is separately down on an upstream Get Ship 500 for TORWIND-5 — same upstream
flakiness class, different endpoint, which is why the retry budget matters generally.
notes:
ORCHESTRATOR INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of the FIX 2(b) falsification, read from the PRE-FIX source (main, gobot/internal/domain/shared/fuel.go) rather than taken from the report:
  NewFuel lines 18-20: if current > capacity -> returns an error, "current fuel cannot exceed capacity". REJECTS over-capacity outright.
  ReconstructFuel line 44: Current: min(current, capacity). CLAMPS.
Both predate this fix. So an over-capacity tank is genuinely UNREPRESENTABLE in local state, and the bead cited "local 600/600 while the live API said 729/600" as evidence of a MISSING clamp when it is in fact the clamp WORKING. TWO INDEPENDENT VERIFICATIONS NOW AGREE (the implementer via RED-state assertions plus mutation M12, and this direct read of the pre-fix value object).
CONSEQUENCE, restated so nobody re-derives it wrongly: over-capacity fuel did NOT cause the 41-minute detour. The chain was FIX 3 (refuelling an already-full tank) -> FIX 1 (giving up after ~6s of backoff) -> the 144-unit DRIFT reroute. FIX 2 is hygiene plus the loud logging the bead also asked for, not the root cause.
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main 6e31d50d (lane commit 4c391f2c), pushed to origin. Reviewed: SHIP, no blocking findings.

ALL SIX ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MET. maxAttempts DELETED and replaced by a 10-minute budget bounded by TOTAL ELAPSED TIME off an injected clock, backoff capped at 60s including the first interval; asserted against a test-local LITERAL 10*time.Minute so lowering the constant cannot make it pass. isRetryableRefuelError untouched — a 4xx burns exactly zero wall clock. A full tank now skips the refuel entirely, asserted on command count so call-and-discard and skip-but-still-dock are both rejected; against unmodified code that test records 6 commands, reproducing the incident in a unit test. Requests clamped at the single funnel, asserted on what the API client received.

THE BEAD WAS WRONG ON FIX 2(b), CONFIRMED FOUR WAYS AND BY THREE INDEPENDENT READERS. ReconstructFuel has applied min(current, capacity) since 964111cd on 2026-07-09 — FOUR WEEKS BEFORE THE INCIDENT, so the clamp was live during it — and NewFuel rejects over-capacity outright, making an over-capacity tank UNREPRESENTABLE locally (the escape hatch of a direct struct literal was checked too: every Fuel{ construction is inside fuel.go). The local-versus-remote disagreement this bead cited as proof of a MISSING clamp was the clamp WORKING. What was actually missing was the LOUDNESS, the other half of its own clamp-and-log-loudly requirement.

THE CAUSAL STORY IN THE DESCRIPTION IS THEREFORE ALSO WRONG: the 41 minutes came from FIX 3 (refuelling an already-full tank) then FIX 1 (giving up after ~6s of backoff) then the 144-unit DRIFT reroute. FIX 2 is hygiene, not root cause. Also, FIND THE CALLER THAT COMPUTES UNITS has no answer — the fleet only automated refuel sends Units: nil, which the API cannot overfill.

BEYOND THE BRIEF: a cancelled context now abandons the retry budget, because extending a blocking sleep from 6s to 10 minutes turns cancellation-deafness into a shutdown hazard.

TWO EXISTING TESTS WERE VACUOUS AND ARE NOW STRONGER: both exhaustion tests seeded exactly 3 errors, so under an elapsed-time budget the loop OUTLASTS a finite queue and succeeds at the origin — they would have passed without ever reaching the reroute they exist to pin.

FOLLOW-UPS: sp-az5a5 (no metric for either anomaly — log lines only). sp-ehf4x is NOT closed by this: the fix makes the reroute far rarer but any reroute still reaches that wedge, and its NOTES invert its description (the stall is TRANSIENT, not permanent).

title: Yards take ABSOLUTE precedence over markets: every yard slot outranks every non-yard slot regardless of coverage, and ALL of a system's yards are manned, not one
description:
ADMIRAL DIRECTIVE, 2026-07-31, verbatim: 'yards should take absolute precedence over other markets! They should be the first ones to be manned. ALL yards of a system!'

THIS OVERRIDES THE CONSTRAINT sp-7qhum WAS BUILT UNDER. I instructed that lane to 'keep coverage-first as the primary sort key' and it correctly complied. The Admiral has now overruled that. Coverage-first is no longer primary for yards.

WHAT SHIPPED (sp-7qhum, d3d15c89) AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. yardFirstOffsets promotes a dark yard only WITHIN its own system's run of coverage values. Its own doc comment states the limit as a feature: 'a system's slots occupy a fixed run of coverage values — parked+0, parked+1, … — This changes only WHICH of the system's placements gets WHICH value in that run. The multiset is untouched.' So a yard in a system already holding 3 probes competes at coverage 3 and is beaten by every coverage-0 market slot in every other system. There are ~8,900 such rows. The measured result after 90 minutes of live running with buying restored: 56 probes bought, only +5 landed on yards (9% conversion), and heavy yards priced stayed flat at 4 of 86.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR.
1. ABSOLUTE PRECEDENCE — every yard slot sorts ahead of every non-yard slot, whatever the coverage of either. Coverage-first still applies WITHIN each tier (order yards among yards by coverage, and non-yards among non-yards exactly as today). This is a two-tier partition, not a new tiebreak.
2. ALL YARDS OF A SYSTEM — no per-system cap and no 'first yard only'. A system with nine shipyards gets all nine manned. 677 systems hold 2+ yards; the largest holds 9.
3. Keep the existing demand weighting WITHIN the yard tier — yardscan.RankPresence already puts heavy-selling yards first; reuse it, do not reinvent it.
4. Feasibility STILL comes before priority. reachableFills (buyqueue.go:1330) must continue to run BEFORE this partition, exactly as sp-7qhum ordered it. A yard in a system no hull can walk to must not be promoted to the head — that is the sp-1r08q failure and the sp-2rfl failure both, and an absolute-precedence rule makes it far more damaging, not less.

SIZE OF THE CHANGE, MEASURED LIVE (player 5, 2026-07-31): 1,573 of 9,201 WANTED slots (17%) sit on a SHIPYARD-trait waypoint. So this promotes 1,573 rows above 7,628. The fleet holds 763 sensing probes.

CONSEQUENCE TO STATE PLAINLY IN THE HANDBACK, NOT TO SOFTEN. With 1,573 yard slots and 763 probes, absolute precedence means placement capacity goes to yards until yards are exhausted, and market coverage grows only after that. That is what was asked for and it is coherent — yards are what make every future hull purchase cheap, and market coverage is already oversupplied (measured ~103 fresh sinks per trade hull; the binding constraint on trading is sink DEPTH, not market count). But it does invert the anti-concentration property coverage-first was introduced for (67% of parked probes had pooled into three systems). Yards are spread across ~1,131 systems so concentration is unlikely to bite — VERIFY that rather than assuming it, and report the projected distribution.

ACCEPTANCE.
- The falsifier is that a yard slot at HIGH coverage beats a non-yard slot at coverage 0. Build the fixture that way explicitly; it is the exact case today's code gets wrong.
- The fixture must SATURATE the queue with coverage-0 non-yard slots, more than the head size, or the partition is never load-bearing and the test passes with the change deleted.
- Assert ALL of a multi-yard system's yards are promoted, not just the first — use a system with at least 3 yards. A test with one yard per system cannot distinguish the new rule from the shipped one.
- Assert reachability still partitions FIRST: an unreachable yard must not appear at the head.
- Every mutation names its killing test. At minimum: collapse the two tiers back to a tiebreak; cap yard promotion at one per system; move the partition ahead of reachableFills.

Related: sp-7qhum (d3d15c89) built the within-system version; sp-fox5u (84b083bc) owns the no-spend relocation half; sp-qkskz is making the yard counters observable and is in flight — coordinate names, do not duplicate counters.
close_reason: Closed

title: [P0] Shipyard reads run 3.2x over budget: parked-sensing discovery is hardcoded Earning-class, so it skips the trait filter, the rescan TTL, and the budget entirely
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 (6h mean, Prometheus, ceiling 2.00 req/s):
  Get Shipyard  0.388 req/s = 19.4% of the account  <-- largest single consumer
  Get Market    0.319 req/s = 16.0%  (budget 0.35 -- INSIDE its allowance)
  Buy+Sell Cargo 0.069 req/s = 3.5%

The shipyard budget is defaultShipyardScanBudgetReqPerSec = 0.12
(internal/infrastructure/config/shipyard_scan.go:61), sized by its own comment to
take yard reads "to roughly 6% of the ceiling instead of 44.7%". Actual: 19.4%.
That is 3.2x the configured allowance. The market budget, by contrast, is holding.

ROOT CAUSE -- a false premise stated in the code's own doc comment.

internal/application/shipyard/queries/get_shipyard_listings.go:41 asserts:

    "EVERY CONSUMER OF THIS QUERY IS A PRE-COMMIT PRICE READ."

and on that basis hardcodes the read class at line 86:

    h.yards.ReadShipyard(ctx, ..., marketscan.Earning)

THE PREMISE IS FALSE. Verified non-test consumers of GetShipyardListingsQuery:

  PRE-COMMIT (legitimately Earning):
    internal/adapters/grpc/fleet_autosizer_ports.go:337
    internal/adapters/grpc/bootstrap_ports.go:557
    internal/application/shipyard/commands/purchase_ship.go:326
    internal/application/shipyard/commands/batch_purchase_ships.go:187

  *** NOT PRE-COMMIT (discretionary discovery, mis-classed) ***
    internal/adapters/parkedsensing/ship_ports.go:287   <-- the parked-sensing
        scanning path: pure discovery, the exact traffic the budget exists to pace
    internal/adapters/expansion/adapters.go:672         <-- expansion discovery
    internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_queries.go:389 <-- gRPC/CLI surface
        (reached by `spacetraders shipyard listings`, adapters/cli/shipyard.go:79)

Because Earning is "metered but never denied" (domain/marketscan/budget.go:354),
and because ReadShipyard sets `deniable := class != marketscan.Earning`
(application/ship/shipyard_scanner.go:168), a sensing read:
  - SKIPS the cached SHIPYARD trait filter (shipyard_scanner.go:171)
  - SKIPS the rescanTTL floor (shipyard_scanner.go:181)
  - CANNOT be declined by the budget (shipyard_scanner.go:186)

There is no way for a caller to ask for a deniable read: GetShipyardListingsQuery
(line 16-20) carries only SystemSymbol, WaypointSymbol, PlayerID. No Class field.

POSITIVE FEEDBACK LOOP (makes it compounding, not merely additive):
get_shipyard_listings.go:85 calls h.yards.NoteTarget(query.WaypointSymbol) BEFORE
the read, documented as "The fleet is buying at this counter, not merely
shopping -- the strongest demand signal the budget has." So every discretionary
sensing read falsely raises that yard's demand weight, which shortens its
interval, which keeps it hot in the rotation. Sensing is inflating the very
signal the budget uses to allocate attention.

FIX SHAPE (implementer to confirm; do not treat as binding):
  Add a Class field to GetShipyardListingsQuery, defaulting to Discretionary
  (the ZERO VALUE is already Discretionary by deliberate design --
  domain/marketscan/budget.go:56-62 -- so an unstamped query becomes deniable,
  which is the fail-safe direction). Stamp Earning explicitly at the four
  pre-commit call sites. Leave parkedsensing / expansion / gRPC-CLI at the
  Discretionary zero value. Gate NoteTarget on Earning so only a real buy
  intent raises demand weight.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - RULINGS #4 is NOT weakened: every pre-commit money-guard read stays Earning
    and stays undeniable. This bead makes the budget stricter, never looser.
  - ARM IT. No feature flag, no default-off seam (standing Admiral order).
  - Do NOT weaken the guards to make the number go down -- the shipyard config
    comment says exactly this ("never by weakening the guards").

VERIFICATION: this is unverifiable today because neither budget emits any metric
(see the scan-budget observability bead). Land that first, then show the
Earning-class share of shipyard reads falls and rate(...{endpoint="Get Shipyard"})
converges toward 0.12 req/s.

MUTATION PROBE REQUIRED: revert the class default to Earning and confirm a NAMED
test fails. A failure list that does not name the test written for this guard
means the fixture is wrong, not that the guard is covered.
notes:
ADDITIVE MEASUREMENTS from a second, independent diagnosis (2026-07-31, 42m32s daemon window). Same root cause, converging numbers — recorded here rather than as a duplicate bead (sp-fbk1q, now closed).

DECISION-COUNTER EVIDENCE, which the original bead predates (these counters only became scrapeable with sp-qkskz/sp-e4dkw):
  shipyard earning/spend                1,080
  shipyard discretionary/spend             30
  shipyard discretionary/serve_from_store  50
  shipyard overdrafts/earning             830
So 97% of shipyard SPENDS are Earning, and 830 of them overdrafted the bucket. The budget is not being ignored — it is being legitimately overridden by a class that Decide() admits unconditionally as its first rung. That confirms the bead's root cause from the decision side rather than the rate side.

For contrast, the market budget on the same window: earning/spend 588, overdrafts/earning 40. The market side is holding, exactly as the bead says.

WHOLE-FLEET CONTEXT the original bead does not have: the account is at 1.79 req/s against the hard 2.00 ceiling (4,581 requests / 2,552 s), i.e. 90% of the limit, with 175 observed 429s. Get Shipyard is 962 of those 4,581 (21%). This is not merely over-budget in the abstract — it is displacing work: the sensing brake is pinned at its 0.1 floor, SensingRate is 0.010 against a MinBudgetRate of 0.1, and expansion has been skipped for budget on every tick, so no probe-less system is ever seeded.

EXCHANGE RATE, worth stating in the handback: those 962 Get Shipyard calls produced FIVE newly-priced yards in the same window.

DO NOT ATTACK THE RATE KNOB. Raising or lowering budget_req_per_sec cannot bind while 97% of reads are Earning, and denying Earning reads would convert a live money guard into a stale one (RULINGS #4). The lever is exactly what this bead already identifies: the hardcoded class at get_shipyard_listings.go:86 and the false premise at :41.

The deniable seam appears to have landed already in 02a65c05 (shipyard_scanner.go:168 'deniable := class != marketscan.Earning'), so the remaining work looks like switching the discovery caller off Earning rather than building new machinery — verify that before starting.
close_reason:
FIXED — all THREE claims checked in code on main (0346650b), not just the headline.

(1) HARDCODED EARNING — gone. get_shipyard_listings.go no longer hardcodes the class: it carries a Class marketscan.Class field (:36) and passes query.Class through to ReadShipyard (:125). The bead's cited line 86 no longer exists.

(2)+(3) TRAIT FILTER / RESCAN TTL — both now reached on the discovery paths. The deniable mechanism itself is UNCHANGED and correctly so (shipyard_scanner.go:168 deniable := class != Earning, gating the trait filter at :170 and the rescanTTL at :179) — that is the intended contract for a genuine pre-commit read. What changed is the CLASS each caller passes, which is what decides whether those two gates apply:
  - container_ops_queries.go:397 (gRPC/CLI) — left at the Discretionary zero value, with a comment saying it is 'paced like any other discovery read and — being deniable — no longer marks the yard as one the fleet is buying at'.
  - expansion/adapters.go probePriceAt — now takes class per caller; its doc names this bead's exact three consequences: 'Collapsing both onto Earning is what let a fleet-wide sweep bypass the trait filter, the rescan floor and the allowance together.' relayAndRecheck=Earning (pre-commit), resolveInPlaceBuy=Discretionary (the sweep).
  - parkedsensing/ship_ports.go:288 — still Earning, DELIBERATELY, and the bead was wrong to call it 'pure discovery'. It is the buy queue's pre-commit quote: buyqueue.go fillSlot calls Quote(), checks it against the working-capital floor, and buys on the next lines. I verified that call chain independently while building sp-e46yc.
Pre-commit sites correctly remain Earning: bootstrap_ports.go:571, fleet_autosizer_ports.go:360, purchase_ship.go:332, batch_purchase_ships.go:194.

LIVE CORROBORATION: shipyard budget shows 12 spend / 219 serve_from_store = 94.8% declined. title: [P0] Scan budgets are unobservable: marketscan + yardscan emit ZERO metrics, so a 3.2x shipyard overdraft ran invisibly
description:
The market and shipyard scan budgets (sp-ntgfj / sp-mb0er) are ARMED and REACHED
in production, but they emit ZERO metrics. Verified 2026-07-30:

  grep -rn "prometheus|metrics\.|Inc\(\)|Observe\(" internal/domain/marketscan/ internal/domain/yardscan/ \
    | grep -v _test.go   ->   NO MATCHES

There is no admit counter, no deny counter, no overdraft counter, no
serve-from-store counter. `spacetraders_daemon_parked_sensing_rate_req_per_sec`
reports the sensing subsystem's aggregate rate (1.083 req/s observed) but says
nothing about which budget admitted or denied, or by which class.

WHY THIS IS P0: internal/infrastructure/config/shipyard_scan.go instructs the
operator to "Raise it when Forced overdrafts are persistently high" -- and
nothing in the codebase counts overdrafts. The knob's own documented operating
procedure is unexecutable. As a direct consequence, shipyard reads have been
running at 3.2x their configured budget (0.388 req/s measured vs 0.12 configured)
with no signal (see the shipyard-overdraft bead).

A budget that cannot be observed cannot be tuned, and cannot be shown to hold.

SCOPE: emit, from BOTH internal/domain/marketscan and internal/domain/yardscan:
  - admit decisions as a counter, labelled by decision (Spend | ServeFromStore)
    and by Class (Discretionary | Earning), player_id as today's convention.
  - an overdraft counter: reads admitted whose token draw exceeded the
    allowance (i.e. Earning reads admitted while the bucket was empty). This is
    the exact quantity the config comment tells the operator to watch.
  - the budget's own effective rate + the coverage denominator (MarketsKnown /
    yardsKnown), so the coverage-decay invariant is observable rather than
    merely asserted in a comment.

Naming follows the existing spacetraders_daemon_ namespace.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - Counters only where the quantity is monotone. DO NOT observe signed values
    into a Summary/Histogram _sum -- see the sp-fpgl2 postmortem: a signed _sum
    makes rate() ramp instead of average and produces a climbing phantom
    "average". If a quantity can go both ways, use two one-way counters.
  - ARM IT. No feature flag, no default-off seam (standing Admiral order).
  - RULING #2: re-derive from durable state each tick; hold nothing cross-tick.

ACCEPTANCE: after deploy, a PromQL query can answer "what fraction of shipyard
reads in the last hour were Earning-class, and how many were overdrafts?" -- and
`sum(rate(<admit counter>[30m]))` for the market budget reconciles with the
measured `rate(spacetraders_daemon_api_requests_total{endpoint="Get Market"}[30m])`
(0.319 req/s at time of filing) to within the sampling error.

  coverage: market 14807, shipyard 1837

  overdrafts_total: market {discretionary 33, earning 60}

THE OVERDRAFT CASE SPECIFICALLY — the incident this bead was written about — IS observable. No budget=shipyard series exists in overdrafts_total, but that is ZERO OVERDRAFTS since the 20:37 restart, not missing code: a prometheus CounterVec child is only created on first Inc, and the shipyard call sites above exist on main.
