title: api_util money guard reads 7.7% while the account is saturated at 99% — autosizer permits hull growth with zero request budget
description:
## Two API-utilization figures that must agree read 99% and 7.7% — and the money guard uses the low one

MEASURED SIMULTANEOUSLY, 2026-07-31 ~00:15Z:

  Grafana "API Utilization %" (financial.json)
      sum(rate(spacetraders_daemon_api_requests_total[5m])) / 2.0 * 100   ->  ~99%
  Rate limiter's own gauge
      spacetraders_daemon_api_rate_limiter_tokens_available              ->  0.0007  (bucket EMPTY)
  Fleet autosizer's api_util guard
      Report().Rolling5m.UtilizationPct                                  ->  7.7% / 6.5% / 9.8%

The first two agree: the account is saturated at its 2 req/s allowance. The third is ~10x low.

## Why this is a money defect, not a dashboard defect

`GuardAPIUtil` exists to stop the autosizer buying another hull when there is no request budget to
fly it ("api_util — is there request budget to fly another hull?", fleet_autosizer_guards.go:28).
It compares against an 85% ceiling. Reading 7.7% when the true figure is 99%, it reports
`ok: util 7.7% < ceiling 85%` and permits growth precisely when the fleet cannot serve the hulls it
already has. RULINGS #4 wants money guards to fail CLOSED; this one fails OPEN on bad data.

## The two are DOCUMENTED as the same basis, which is why the gap is a bug and not a design choice

`autosizerAPIUtilReader` (fleet_autosizer_ports.go:174) states it reads "the SAME throughput/ceiling
basis as the Prometheus ApproachCeiling alert (sum(rate(api_requests_total[5m])) /
RateLimitPerSecond)". Both are wired from the same constant: the tracker is built as
`NewAPIBudgetTracker(api.RateLimitPerSecond, clock)` (daemon_server.go:275), and the panel divides by
a hardcoded 2.0.

## What is NOT the cause — ruled out by direct read

Coverage is not the explanation, and it points the WRONG WAY. Both recorders live in
`retry_policy.go` eight lines apart, but `tracker.Record(...)` fires on EVERY attempt including
retries (:150-154, deliberately "before classify() branches"), while `collector.RecordAPIRequest(...)`
fires only on the terminal, non-retryable path (:161). The tracker should therefore count MORE than
Prometheus, not ~8% of it.

Windows are not it either: `rolling5mWindow = 5m` matches `rate(...[5m])`, and `retentionWindow = 5m`
is documented as at least as wide as the widest report window.

## Leading hypothesis, NOT yet confirmed — verify before fixing

`c.getBudgetTracker()` is a PER-CLIENT accessor while `SetGlobalAPIBudgetTracker` sets a process
global. If more than one API client instance exists and only some have the tracker wired, the rest of
the fleet's traffic is invisible to the tracker while still counted by Prometheus. 7.7% of 2 req/s is
~46 requests per 5 minutes against an actual ~600 — i.e. the tracker sees roughly one client's worth.
Confirm by counting client constructions and checking which get the tracker, before changing any
arithmetic.

## Ask

1. Find why the tracker undercounts; fix the wiring rather than the divisor.
2. Add a test that pins the two figures to agree within a tolerance on identical traffic — the doc
   comment already asserts they share a basis, so make that assertion executable.
3. While it is wrong, treat `GuardAPIUtil` as non-load-bearing. Do not tune the 85% ceiling against
   the broken number.
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main b257c956 (lane 25b6db4b). Gate: GatePassed:true Merged:true EmptyMerge:false; diffstat verified 6 files / +380 / -5, observedWindow present in main.

ROOT CAUSE: THE WINDOW, NOT THE DIVISOR. ComputeReport always divided by the full nominal window
regardless of how much history the observer had. The tracker is in-memory and rebuilt on every
daemon start, so for its first five minutes it divided real traffic by minutes that never
happened — up to 13x understatement, for a full window after every start, and PERMANENT under a
restart loop. Prometheus rate() has no such flaw: it spans the actual data and handles resets,
which is why the two figures disagreed.

REPRODUCED ARITHMETICALLY TO THE REPORTED DIGIT, before any fix was written: a daemon 23 seconds
old consuming its entire 2 req/s allowance has 46 events, and 46/300/2.0 = 7.67%. The bead
reported 7.7%. That reproduction — not the corroborating gauge — is the proof.

'WHICH FIGURE IS CORRECT' WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT ASSUMED (this was the analysis the bead needed):
 - 99% is right; 7.7% is NOT 'correct for what it measures'. Both sides of
   UtilizationPct = (TotalRequests/window.Seconds())/ceilingReqPerSec*100 have the right GRAIN.
 - 2 req/s IS the right denominator: RateLimitPerSecond (client.go:31) and the Grafana panel's
   hardcoded 2.0 are the same number. RateLimitBurst=30 does not enter a 5-minute average.
 - The empty token bucket CORROBORATES BUT IS NOT INDEPENDENT: SetRateLimiterTokens is called
   inside the retry loop immediately after acquiring a token, so it is only ever sampled during a
   request — a biased sample that reads the trough. It shows saturation while requests flow; it
   cannot speak to duty cycle.
 - THE BEAD'S LEADING HYPOTHESIS (per-client vs global tracker) IS DISPROVEN, not merely
   unexplored: getBudgetTracker falls back to the global and reads it AT CALL TIME; there is one
   HTTP path and one tracker construction; and the tracker records per-ATTEMPT while Prometheus
   records only TERMINAL outcomes, making the tracker's coverage a strict SUPERSET — it cannot
   structurally undercount. Now pinned by a test.

GUARD REACHABILITY CHECKED FIRST — the sp-ps2oc lesson applied: GuardAPIUtil is registered in
EvaluateGuards, called from sizeClass, its reader wired UNCONDITIONALLY at ports.go:72 (neighbouring
ports are wired behind if + UNWIRED warnings; this one is not), reachable from main.go:1196/1203,
and sizing is ON by default. A nil reader fails CLOSED at three nested levels. So this was
mis-valued, not absent — the opposite of sp-ps2oc, and worth having distinguished before fixing.

DIRECTION IS STRICTER AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT BE OTHERWISE (RULINGS #4): a narrower window over
the same events yields a higher req/s, so a higher utilization, so the guard refuses growth SOONER
and can never permit a purchase it previously refused. observedWindow never returns a window wider
than nominal. Every degenerate input — unknown start, backwards clock, already-warm — falls back to
the NOMINAL window rather than a small one, deliberately: inventing a small denominator would spike
utilization toward infinity and wedge the fleet, so the failure direction errs toward prior
behaviour rather than toward a spurious block. Once warm, byte-identical.

SUBTLETY WORTH KEEPING: the span is START OF OBSERVATION, not the oldest retained event. Those look
like the same quantity and are not — after an idle stretch the oldest event is recent, so deriving
from it would divide by two seconds and report saturation off a single call. Idle time is real
observed time and belongs in the denominator. Pinned by QuietTimeStaysInTheDenominator.

MUTATION-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: reverting the narrowing kills the incident reproduction and
the never-widens test; ALLOWING widening — the direction RULINGS #4 forbids — kills 4 including
warm-observer invariance. The 'SAME basis' doc claim is now executable: the tracker's utilization
is compared against the Grafana panel expression RECOMPUTED INDEPENDENTLY from the same traffic, so
a unit or divisor error is visible and not merely a counting error, backed by a companion test
pinning RecordAPIRequest to exactly one counter increment — without which the parity test's fake
would be measuring itself.

The guard itself and the 85% ceiling are untouched. Verified independently before gating: go vet
exit 0, 86 packages ok / 0 FAIL, and the arithmetic reproduction re-checked (46/300/2.0 = 7.6667%).

title: 75-minute market-freshness caps are hardcoded in 4 places and invalidated by the scan budget — 87% of trade throughput lost
description:
ADMIRAL ORDER 2026-07-30, during a live incident: "WE CAN'T GUARANTEE 75 MIN STALENESS ANYMORE."

WHAT HAPPENED. The marketscan budget (sp-ntgfj) caps total scan spend at a fixed req/s, so scan
interval is an OUTPUT of budget / markets-known. Meanwhile the charted map grew to 4,389
IMPORT/EXCHANGE rows across 343 systems and is still growing. A full even rotation at 0.70 req/s is
now ~105 minutes. Every consumer that assumes a market is worthless after 75 minutes therefore
discards most of the map:
  - 980 "stale (> 1h15m0s cap)" refusals in 15 minutes
  - only 872 of 4,301 rows (20%) inside the 75-min window
  - trade volume fell ~87%; net 4.2M/hr -> 0.55M/hr
Raising the scan budget does not fix this and never will: the map grows faster than any fixed budget
can chase. A budget bounds COST; it does not bound STALENESS, and staleness is what these consumers
need bounded.

THE FOUR PLACES THAT HARDCODE 75 MINUTES (complete sweep):
  1. config defaultSinkFreshnessMaxMinutes = 75 (infrastructure/config/trade_fleet.go:248)
     -> the FIRM-SINK MONEY GUARD in run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:342, fails closed with
        "never buy into a sink we cannot confirm is live" (sp-tgll8 item 2). I have already raised
        the live value to 720 via config.yaml as an incident mitigation; the DEFAULT still says 75.
  2. maxListingAge = 75 * time.Minute (trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:851)
     -> ELEVEN consumers: run_tour_coordinator_lookback.go:248,249; _offload.go:107;
        run_stocker_coordinator.go:419; _relocation_regions.go:260; _reposition.go:649;
        run_tour_coordinator.go:2140 (BestSinksAcrossSystems). This is the big one and it is a
        hardcoded const with no config path at all.
  3. defaultStalenessHidingStaleAge = 75 * time.Minute (internal/captain/detectors.go:178)
     -> its own comment says it "matches the tour planner's own maxListingAge (75min)". It will now
        fire continuously and drown the captain in false staleness alerts.
  4. defaultMarketDriftMaxAge = 60 * time.Minute (scouting/commands/run_scout_post_coordinator.go:84)
     -> market-drift detection, same class, tighter still.
NOT in scope: config defaultScanMaxAgeSeconds = 75 (trade_impact.go:65) is SECONDS and governs
telemetry scan-dedup cadence (sp-v34b), a different concern. Confirm before touching it.

THE FIX, and it is a design change not a number change. These caps must stop being magic constants
and become a FUNCTION OF THE ACTUAL ROTATION PERIOD. The scanner already knows its budget and its
market count, so the expected worst-case age is derivable: rotation ~= markets_known / budget_req_per_sec.
A consumer should ask "is this row older than the rotation can explain?" rather than compare against a
number chosen when the map was 300 systems. Pick the shape you can defend -- a derived value, or a
config key defaulted generously with the derivation documented -- but the ONE thing that must not
survive is a hardcoded minute count that silently invalidates as the map grows.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - Item 1 is a FAIL-CLOSED MONEY GUARD (RULINGS #4). Do NOT set it to 0 or delete it: zero makes
    the clause inert (absorption.go:325 returns heldUnits unconditionally). It may be RAISED or made
    derived; it may not be removed.
  - Ship ARMED. No feature flag, no default-off path.
  - Do not weaken any guard as the mechanism. The point is that the caps are mis-calibrated, not
    that freshness does not matter.

ACCEPTANCE: no hardcoded market-freshness minute count remains in the four sites above; each cap
either derives from the live rotation period or is config-driven with a default justified against a
4,000+ market map; a test proves a consumer still refuses genuinely dead data while admitting a row
whose age is explained by normal rotation; and the "stale (> cap)" refusal rate on live data returns
to near zero without any guard being disabled.
notes:
ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2026-07-30: "make it live tunable". The caps must be reachable via
`spacetraders tune --operation <op> <key> <value>` at runtime, not only via config.yaml + a daemon
restart. That is the operational requirement, and it is what turned a 15-minute fix into a 40-minute
incident today: the only lever was a config edit and a full daemon bounce, and each bounce costs jump
cooldowns -- the resource the fleet is actually short of.

So the deliverable is BOTH:
  (a) the caps stop being hardcoded magic numbers (derive from rotation, or config-driven), AND
  (b) every one of them is exposed as a LIVE knob with bounds, a documented default, and a
      description that says what it protects -- reachable without restarting the daemon.

Follow the existing tunable pattern: see the sensing coordinator's knobs (capex_reserve_credits,
expansion_enabled, value_clamp_r, quartermaster_cadence_secs) for the shape -- bounds registry,
live-config re-read on the next tick, and a `source=live-config` marker once tuned. Note the tour
coordinator currently exposes NO tunables at all (`tune --operation tour` returns nothing), so this
may mean wiring that operation's knob surface for the first time.

CAUTION on the live-read semantics: some coordinators re-read config each tick and some bind values
only when the container is REBUILT (value_clamp_r says "Binds when the scan rotation is built, so it
applies at coordinator rebuild (restart/relaunch), not next tick"). A knob that silently needs a
rebuild is worse than no knob, because the operator believes they have acted. Whatever you build,
the knob's own description must state truthfully when it takes effect, and prefer next-tick re-read
where the code allows it.
close_reason: Closed

title: placement starvation: a failed move consumes the 10-action tick budget, so head-of-worklist failures freeze the other 300 slots
description:
## A failed placement move consumes the tick's action budget, so persistent failures at the head of the worklist starve everything behind them

gobot/internal/application/parkedsensing/placement.go

`AdvancePlacements` reads the worklist ONCE and acts on at most
`DefaultMaxPlacementActions` (10) slots per tick:

    slots, err := pl.Ledger.SlotsByState(ctx, playerID, SlotStateBought, SlotStateInTransit)
    for _, slot := range slots {
        if rep.Actions >= maxActions { break }
        ...
        acted, err := advanceOne(...)
        if acted { rep.Actions++ }
    }

`SlotsByState` (gobot/internal/adapters/persistence/sensing_ledger_repository.go:364)
orders by `waypoint_symbol` — a FIXED, stable order, identical every tick.

Both movement paths count a FAILED move as an action:

    // dispatch()
    if moveErr := flyToSlot(...); moveErr != nil {
        // "Holding the slot at BOUGHT is what makes the retry free"
        return true, nil          // ← acted == true → rep.Actions++
    }

    // dispatchClaim()
    if err := flyToSlot(...); err != nil {
        return true, nil          // ← same
    }

The retry is NOT free. It costs one of ten actions. So ten slots that fail
persistently — and, being sorted by waypoint symbol, they fail in the SAME order
every tick — consume the entire budget before any healthy slot is reached. The tail
of the worklist is never examined at all.

## Measured (era 5, 2026-07-30 05:39Z)

- Worklist: 266 BOUGHT + 52 IN_TRANSIT = 318 slots, all era_id=5 (so era scoping is
  not the cause; they ARE in the worklist).
- Sampled BOUGHT/IN_TRANSIT/PARKED across a 30s tick boundary: 266/52/394 then
  266/52/394 — completely flat.
- The head of the worklist by waypoint_symbol is dominated by slots whose hulls sit
  DOCKED in a system that is not their target, unchanged since 2026-07-29 12:40Z
  (~17h): X1-A4-AX5D, X1-AV92-AF7F, X1-AX76-CF5A, X1-BZ24-A13B, X1-BZ44-A13B,
  X1-CU16-A37A. Several of these appear in the `parked_sensing_gate_walk_unroutable`
  warnings, all walking out of X1-RJ93.
- Slots deep in the order are never touched. TORWIND-15F, BOUGHT for
  X1-K39-AC2B since 2026-07-29 05:39Z (~22.5h), has **ZERO** lines in daemon.log —
  not one attempt, not one warning. "X1-K*" sorts behind roughly a hundred A–J slots.

## Compounding: the failure is silent on the path that matters

Only a `nextHopToward` failure logs (the `parked_sensing_gate_walk_unroutable`
warning, emitted inside `MoverPort.RouteAcross`). A failure in `stepThroughGate` —
the actual physical move onto or through the gate — propagates back to `dispatch`
and hits `return true, nil` with NO log line at all. So a hull can burn one action
per tick indefinitely and produce no diagnostics whatsoever, which is exactly the
state TORWIND-15F is in.

## Fix (two parts, both needed)

1. **A failed move must not consume the same budget as a successful one.** The cap
   exists "to keep a large backlog from firing a burst of navigation commands in a
   single tick" (its own doc comment) — that rationale is about commands ISSUED and
   ACCEPTED. Either don't count a failed move, or count it against a separate,
   larger failure budget. Do NOT simply raise the cap: that changes the constant
   without removing the starvation, since the failing set can grow.
2. **Break the fixed order's monopoly on the head.** The worklist order must not let
   the same slots occupy the budget every tick. Options: rotate the start offset by
   tick, order by an "attempts" or `updated_at` column so long-untried slots rise, or
   skip slots that failed recently with a backoff. Prefer whichever is derivable from
   durable state per RULINGS #2 — `updated_at` already exists on sensing_slots and a
   least-recently-advanced order is both durable and self-balancing.

Also give `stepThroughGate` failures a named warning, so a silently-burning slot is
visible. A slot that has consumed an action N ticks running without changing state is
the signal worth logging.

## Relationship to sp-ky85o

sp-ky85o (the gate-edge wall) is what MAKES the head slots fail. This bead is why that
failure spreads to the other 300. Fixing sp-ky85o alone will unblock the currently
walled slots, but leaves the starvation mechanism in place for the next persistent
failure — and 173 systems are walls at any given moment, so there will be a next one.
Fixing this alone would let healthy slots through while the walled ones churn. Both
are needed; neither is sufficient.

Different files from sp-ky85o (this is application/parkedsensing/placement.go +
adapters/persistence/sensing_ledger_repository.go; that one is
adapters/persistence/gate_edge_repository.go + adapters/parkedsensing/screen_ports.go),
so the two can be built in parallel.
notes:
ECONOMIC COST (2026-07-30 05:50Z).

709 probes bought this era for 42,244,890 cr (avg 59,584). 266 of them are frozen at BOUGHT and have never scanned once, so ~15,849,282 cr of hull capital — 37% of all probe spend — is doing nothing. Current treasury is 1,412,390, so the frozen probe capital is ~11x the entire liquid position.

The bookkeeping is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed': CountOwnedProbes deliberately counts BOUGHT slots so the probe cap sees these hulls (the over-count direction RULINGS #4 wants — under-counting would authorise re-buying a hull we already own). The waste is not double-buying; it is that 266 paid-for hulls produce zero price coverage. Do not touch the counting to make the number look better.

Each frozen hull's entire job is to price ONE system. 266 hulls against a 1,095-system actionable unpriced pool, with only 136 systems priced today and the count moving +2 per 70 minutes. Draining this backlog is the single largest available step toward trading-lane coverage.
close_reason: Closed

title: gate routing: one under-construction exit condemns a system's whole edge set every 2h, walling off 15% of the map and freezing 266 probes
description:
## Symptom (measured on live prod, era 5, 2026-07-30 05:32Z)

266 probes are frozen in sensing_slots.state='BOUGHT' — 243 of them for 6-24h,
oldest since 2026-07-29 05:39Z (~22.5h). Every one is DOCKED or IN_ORBIT (none
IN_TRANSIT) and every one stands in a DIFFERENT system from its target slot.
They were bought, assigned, and never dispatched.

Downstream, measured:
- 0 hulls are PARKED in a system we hold no prices for. Every scanning probe
  sits in an already-priced system. 299 hulls are committed to unpriced systems
  and ALL of them are BOUGHT (265) or IN_TRANSIT (34); none has ever scanned
  (last_scan_at NULL for all).
- priced systems: 134 of 1,216 charted. Actionable unpriced pool: 1,095.
- The probe-sensing surge (sp-zvywu Part 1) never fires. All 710 probes are
  named by a scout post or a sensing slot, so surplusProbes() returns empty and
  surgeToUnpricedSystems() takes a silent `return 0`. probes_unheld = 0 exactly.

## Root cause: one still-building gate erases a system's ENTIRE topology every 2h

internal/adapters/persistence/gate_edge_repository.go

  Edges() → if r.anyStale(models) { return nil, false, nil }
  anyStale() → true if ANY row is stale
  rowStale() → stale once synced_at is older than freshWindowFor(row)
  freshWindowFor() → gateEdgeUnderConstructionFreshWindow (2h) when
                     row.UnderConstruction, else freshWindow (24h)

A system's edges are written in ONE Replace() under a single synced_at, so every
row shares a timestamp. The 2h under-construction window therefore condemns the
WHOLE set — including the system's many built, static, permanently-valid exits —
2 hours after the last probe, and Edges() returns ok=false.

internal/adapters/parkedsensing/screen_ports.go:856 GateNeighbourPort.Neighbours
turns that into zero neighbours, so the system becomes a WALL in every BFS:

  edges, ok, err := p.edges.Edges(ctx, system)
  if !ok { return nil, nil }
  for _, edge := range edges { if edge.Stale { return nil, nil } ... }

nextHopToward (internal/adapters/parkedsensing/ship_ports.go:708) BFSes over
Neighbours. Starting AT a wall system it gets nothing at ring 0 and returns
"no stored gate route from X to Y within 0 jumps".

## Evidence the data is fine and the resolver is what fails

- Underlying era-5 adjacency is CONNECTED: component of X1-RJ93 over
  non-under-construction edges = 1,224 systems; X1-AX76 is in it; 0 of the 233
  distinct BOUGHT target systems are unreachable.
- Under the walker's own filters, reachable-from-X1-RJ93 = 1,046 and X1-AX76 is
  still reachable. So a route provably exists and the resolver refuses it.
- X1-RJ93 (where the stuck hulls stand) has 6 fresh edges, 5 passable, ONE
  under-construction (X1-XX80), all synced 2026-07-30T00:26:10-03:00.
  `RJ93_is_wall_NOW` = true — condemned solely by that one building gate.
- Log timing matches exactly: routing succeeds at 00:26 (fresh probe), then
  fails again from 02:26 onward — the 2h line.
- Right now 173 of 1,168 era-5 systems (15%) are walls; 253 systems have an
  under-construction exit, so each is a wall every 2h unless re-probed, and
  re-probes are bounded (MaxGateReads=3/tick) so they cannot all be refreshed
  inside the window.

## Fix

Make the under-construction re-probe window invalidate ONLY the under-construction
edge, not the system's whole edge set. A built static gate does not become unknown
because a different gate in the same system is still building. Keep whole-set
Replace() write semantics; make routing-time staleness per-row.

Deliberately preserved:
- The 24h whole-set window keeps its current meaning (a genuinely old set is
  still condemned whole).
- An empty/unparseable synced_at stays stale — the deploy-time invalidation
  relies on it.
- Under-construction edges stay IMPASSABLE (they are already skipped as
  candidates). This changes only whether their staleness condemns their
  SIBLINGS.
- The build-completion re-probe must still be triggered on the 2h clock; losing
  that would hold a "still building" verdict for a full day. Separate the
  "needs re-probe" signal from the "condemn the set" signal rather than dropping
  the former.

## Why it matters

This single resolver gates both halves of the active goal. The surge's own
dispatch walks the same graph via newGateReach(ports.Gates), so even with surplus
probes it would hit the same walls. Unblocking it releases 266 already-paid-for
hulls whose only job is to price a new system each — 134 priced systems today
against a 1,095-system actionable pool.
notes:
IMPACT QUANTIFIED (2026-07-30 05:44Z) — reachability fragmentation, which is a far better measure of this defect than the wall count.

Underlying era-5 adjacency (built gates, ignoring staleness) is ONE component of 1,224 systems. Under the walker's ACTUAL filter, wall-aware BFS reachability collapses:
  from X1-AM61:  121 of 1,168 systems  (10%)
  from X1-YN57:  418 of 1,168 systems  (34%)
  from X1-RJ93:    1 (itself only)     — RJ93 IS a wall, so it reaches NOTHING
So 195 wall systems (17%) act as holes that cut a fully-connected map down to a tenth.

PREDICTED EFFECT of making staleness per-row, computed from the current data:
  195 walls now
  117 removed  (60%) — walled ONLY by an under-construction row while HAVING built exits.
                       X1-RJ93 is exactly this shape: healthy_stale=false, uc_stale=true, built_rows=5.
   78 correctly remain — genuinely old whole set, or no built exit at all.

CAVEAT, so the next reader does not over-attribute: this defect is NOT the sole cause of the 266 frozen BOUGHT slots. X1-AM61->X1-K39 and X1-YN57->X1-AV92 ARE reachable under the current filter, yet those slots have not moved in 17-22h. Two further mechanisms are in play: sp-cwnwb (a failed move consumes the 10-action tick budget in fixed waypoint order, so failures starve the tail) and a silent failure inside stepThroughGate that logs nothing at all. sp-cwnwb adds the missing warning; do not assume this fix alone drains the backlog.

Ruled out by direct measurement: era scoping (all 318 stuck slots are era_id=5), jump cooldowns (708 of 710 probes free, all head hulls free), disconnected graph (one 1,224-system component), and physical stranding (probes have engine_speed=9 and 394 have reached their slots).

title: Source pool depth is THE binding constraint: hulls acquire only ~64 units of a good per visit against 80/225 holds — everything downstream (hull, sink depth, sell cap) is slack, and five other hypotheses are refuted
description:
GOAL CONTEXT: Admiral target is 10M/hr NET. Honest 6h baseline ~1.89M/hr net at 26.9% margin — a ~5.3x
gap. This bead is the ONE constraint measured to actually bind, established by eliminating the others.

THE MEASURED CONSTRAINT CHAIN (n~290 good-loads over 12h, era 5, player 5):
  source pool (~64 units/good/visit) -> hull capacity (80 for 13 of 18 hulls) -> sink depth (131) -> sell cap (2.5 x tv)
  BINDS                                 BINDS                                    slack               slack

A hull carries a mean of 64 UNITS OF THE GOOD IT SELLS, into a mean sink trade_volume of 131 — i.e. 0.66
tranches, with only ~7% of loads carrying more than one. The binding term is buy_rem in the solver's
units = min(buy_rem, sell_rem, slack, afford). buy_rem is SOURCE POOL DEPTH: export markets carry 51-80
units of a good (CLOTHING 56, LAB_INSTRUMENTS 51, MEDICINE 53, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 57).

WE CANNOT BUY ENOUGH OF ANY ONE GOOD AT ONE MARKET TO FILL A HULL. Everything downstream is slack.

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY LIVE LEVER — five hypotheses have been REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, each with its bead:
 - sp-k7hez  tour cycle time: credits/hull-hour RISES with tour length (78k at 2 systems, 127k at 5)
 - sp-srhs2  hull idleness: 13 of 16 haulers at 92-100% utilisation; the 79% no-trade exits were ONE
             bootstrap-deadlock incident, ~35 hull-hours, already self-resolved
 - sp-4mpxh  sink selection: corr(trade_volume, margin) = -0.39; the planner's median tv 60 IS the value
             optimum (195,776/visit); chasing deeper sinks would cut earnings 67%
 - sp-1zho6  buy-side chaining: net cr/hr is FLAT across buy-market count (121k/113k/166k) — the solver
             is already sitting on its rate optimum
 - sp-28lw9  the sell depth cap: raised 1 -> 2.5, deployed, measured INERT — it is third in the chain

ASK — DIAGNOSE BEFORE BUILDING. The prize is real but the mechanism is not obvious, and sp-1zho6 already
showed that the naive answer (chain more buy stops) does NOT raise cr/hr:
 (a) Establish WHY only ~64 units of a good are acquirable per visit. Is it the market's own
     trade_volume, an export's replenishment rate, our own A-cap/absorption netting applied to the BUY
     side, the spend cap, or the planner declining to take more? Separate these — they need different
     fixes and only some are ours to change.
 (b) If it is genuinely the market's depth: the only ways to carry more of one good are to visit the SAME
     good at MULTIPLE export markets in one buy phase, or to wait for replenishment. Price both against
     the travel cost — sp-1zho6 measured that extra buy stops pay for themselves and no more, so a
     same-good multi-market chain must be shown to beat that flat result, not assumed to.
 (c) Quantify the ceiling honestly. If source pools are ~64 and hulls are 80/225, what IS the maximum
     achievable units/visit, and what net/hr does that imply? If the answer is that ~2x is the ceiling,
     say so — the Admiral needs to know 10M NET may not be reachable by this route rather than be told
     it is close.
 (d) NOTE THE CAPEX CONSEQUENCE: a 225-hold heavy needs ~3.5 distinct goods to fill at 64 units each.
     Heavies measured 4.11x a light per hull-hour EMPIRICALLY (345,918 vs 84,144 net/hull-hour, 6h), so
     they do deliver — but each additional heavy competes for the same shallow source pools, so that
     ratio may not extrapolate. Establish whether marginal heavy value is falling with fleet size. The
     Admiral is buying heavies on the strength of the 4.11x and needs to know if it decays.

CONSTRAINTS: do not weaken any money guard (RULINGS #4), the inventory-pressure guard, or the
honest-completion contract. market_data columns are INVERTED — on the BUY side we pay sell_price (the
market's ask). Era-scoped tables, era 5 from 2026-07-26. Ship ARMED, no flag, if anything is built.
notes:
(a)(b)(c) ANSWERED — AND THE BEAD'S PREMISE (MINE) IS REFUTED. The buy side is NOT supply-constrained.
Script 3595a7a6 on sp-kep8p: gobot/scripts/buy_side_constraint_decomposition.sql. No production change.

MY PREMISE WAS WRONG: "export markets carry only 51-80 units (CLOTHING 56, LAB_INSTRUMENTS 51...)" is
ACCURATE PER MARKET and IRRELEVANT IN AGGREGATE. CLOTHING has 27 export markets totalling 1,546 units;
LAB_INSTRUMENTS 38 markets / 1,820 units; MEDICINE 25 / 1,283. Depth is abundant, merely DISTRIBUTED.
And the markets we actually buy from average tv 133, not 51 — we also source from EXCHANGE (tv 120-240).

FOUR OF FIVE CANDIDATES MEASURABLY SLACK (442 buy visits, 12h):
  source market trade_volume ... NOT binding: mean 61.9 units taken from mean source tv 133.1 = 0.671
                                 tranches. 39 visits took >1x (max 3.00), so deeper IS available and
                                 occasionally used.
  export replenishment ......... NOT binding: ~34.7 buyable goods and 5,232 units of tranche depth PER
                                 SOURCE SYSTEM, against a 225-unit heavy hold — 23x headroom.
  buy-side absorption A-cap .... NOT binding: 12 PLANNED buy rows fleet-wide, ZERO executed buy shadows,
                                 against 442 buy visits.
  spend cap .................... NOT binding: heavies spend to 1.9-2.1M, p90 ~1.15M.
  PLANNER DECLINING ............ THIS IS IT — AND IT IS CORRECT.

WHAT ACTUALLY STOPS THE LOAD, SPLIT BY HULL:
  LIGHT (80 hold): 85.4% fill, 1.95 goods x 55.7 units. THE HULL BINDS. Physical; only capex changes it.
  HEAVY (225):     62-66% fill, 2.40 goods x 83.2 units — in systems offering ~35 goods and 5,232 units,
                   while spending up to 1.9M. NOTHING PHYSICAL BINDS A HEAVY. It stops because each buy
                   is matched 1:1 to a profitable SELL and the objective is RATE: a marginal low-margin
                   lane adds dock and travel time without raising $/hr. That is sp-1zho6's flat cr/hr and
                   sp-4mpxh's margin-vs-depth anti-correlation (-0.39) reappearing on the BUY side.

ONLY #5 IS OURS TO CHANGE, and sp-1zho6 already measured that forcing more buy markets does NOT raise the
rate. #1-#4 need no fix because they are not binding. THERE IS NO BUY-SIDE FIX TO BUILD.

(b) SAME-GOOD CHAINING IS UNNECESSARY, NOT MERELY UNPROFITABLE. It solves single-market scarcity, which
DOES NOT EXIST (5,232 units/system across ~35 goods; we take 0.671 of one tranche). Waiting for
replenishment is moot for the same reason. Neither can beat the sp-1zho6 flat-cr/hr bar because neither
touches the binding term.

(c) THE CEILING IS 1.33x, NOT 2x:
   HEAVY  5 hulls  1,125 hold  66.2% fill    745 carried
   LIGHT 13 hulls  1,040 hold  84.8% fill    882 carried
   FLEET 18 hulls  2,165 hold  75.1% fill  1,627 carried
Perfect fill = 2,165 / 1,627 = 1.331x. Against ~1.89-1.95M/hr net that is ~2.5-2.6M/hr — ROUGHLY 25% OF
THE 10M/HR TARGET. And 1.33x is an UPPER BOUND assuming two things already measured FALSE: that marginal
units earn the AVERAGE margin (sp-4mpxh: marginal lanes are the LOW-margin ones) and that they cost no
extra travel (sp-1zho6: cr/hr flat across buy-market count). Realistic is materially below 1.33x.

CONCLUSION FOR THE 10M/HR NET GOAL: 10M IS NOT REACHABLE BY LOADING THE EXISTING FLEET BETTER, AT ANY
FILL RATE. The fleet moves 1,627 units/cycle; at the measured tv 60-112 optimum (~1,085/unit margin),
10M/hr needs roughly 4x more THROUGHPUT, not 33% better packing. Fill, sell depth, buy depth and sink
selection are now ALL measured and ALL near their optima. The remaining levers are HULL COUNT and CYCLE
FREQUENCY (the latter measured at 5-25% of hull time in sp-1zho6 — also small). Hull count is part (d).
NOTE: this 1.33x is a PER-HULL result and COMPOSES MULTIPLICATIVELY with (d)'s fleet-size answer; the two
must be read together.

CAVEAT: 12-hour windows on an 18-hull fleet, heavy figures resting on 55-58 phases. Direction is
unambiguous — every supply-side term is slack by a wide margin — but the exact 1.33x would move a few
points on a larger sample.
(d) ANSWERED. NO DECAY DETECTABLE; THE PURCHASE DECISION IS ROBUST BY ~34x. But the 10M/hr EXTRAPOLATION
is NOT supported by this data, and two decision inputs I supplied were wrong. Diagnosis only, nothing
committed.

THE "1->5 NATURAL EXPERIMENT" IS REALLY 1->3. Heavy tenure: TORWIND-142 11.8h, 167 9.4h, 168 8.6h,
279 0.73h, 27A 0.01h (three transactions, 36 seconds). Heavies #4 and #5 contribute nothing measurable.

APPARENT DECAY IS AN ARTIFACT. TORWIND-142 alone, accrual basis: 976k/hull-hr at 1 heavy -> 470k at 3 ->
341k at 4+. Killed by four independent checks:
 1. NON-MONOTONIC: mean per-heavy at 4-5 heavies is 540k/hr, HIGHER than the 419k at 3. Pool exhaustion
    cannot go the wrong way.
 2. LIGHTS SHOW THE SAME SHAPE across identical phase boundaries: 194k -> 147k -> 267k. Both classes dip
    in P3 and recover in P4 — a MARKET-WIDE TIME EFFECT, not heavy contention.
 3. NO CONSISTENT NEW-HULL EFFECT: first-2.5h vs after — 142 starts HOT (2.07x), 167 starts COLD (0.62x),
    168 mild (1.33x). Opposite directions, so 142's strong opening is variance.
 4. INSIDE THE KNOWN NOISE FLOOR: P1 is one hull over 2.5h, and sp-5yrv4 established within-hull
    variation up to 2.27x between adjacent windows with fleet size CONSTANT.

(b) CONTENTION IS OBSERVABLE BUT IS PRICE DRIFT, NOT DEPLETION. 21.4% of buys have another hull buying
the same good at the same waypoint within 30 min; of 170 contended pairs the second buyer pays more
92.9% of the time, +98.8/unit (+3.6%). But the penalty GROWS with the gap: +2.70% (0-10m), +2.82%
(10-30m), +4.44% (30-60m), +4.23% (60-120m), +8.01% (120-240m). DEPLETION WOULD SHOW THE OPPOSITE — a
step at short gaps DECAYING as the market restocks. Growing-with-time is drift. Upper bound on genuine
depletion, taking 0-10m as the ceiling: ~74/unit against a ~1,177 spread ~= 6% of margin on the contended
21% ~= ~1.3% OF FLEET MARGIN. Not material at current size. Fleet-volume correlations over 18 hourly
buckets: volume<->cost +0.317, volume<->spread -0.279 — both point the way the concern predicts, NEITHER
is significant (n=18 needs |r| >= 0.468). Honest reading: directionally consistent with mild contention,
statistically indistinguishable from noise.

(c) LIGHTS: same answer. 194k/171k/147k/267k across phases — no monotonic trend, no light-specific decay.
The 13 lights are not visibly starving each other or the heavies.

(d) THE NUMBER: A HEAVY PAYS FOR ITSELF IN ~5-7 HOURS. At the mean observed 419k/hull-hr, payback on
2.04M is 4.9h; at the WORST observed hull rate (324k/hr) against the projected 23rd-heavy price (~2.41M),
7.4h. For a heavy to fail to justify 2.04M even on a SEVEN-DAY horizon, marginal productivity would have
to fall below 12,144/hull-hr — a 97% COLLAPSE, 34x below observed. No decay mechanism comes close.
ON THE PAYBACK QUESTION: BUY THEM.

BUT NO FLEET SIZE AT WHICH DECAY BITES CAN BE GIVEN FROM THIS DATA. Detectable effect size is ~40%: the
heavy/light ratio swings 2.12 -> 4.85 -> 3.83 -> 2.38 across four consecutive 2.2h blocks WITH FLEET SIZE
CONSTANT at 3+13. Any decay smaller than that is invisible. RE-RUN AT 8 HEAVIES with >=6h tenure each —
n=8 and ~60% more volume, enough to separate a real trend from this noise.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO DECISION INPUTS I (the orchestrator) SUPPLIED:
 1. CAPEX IS ~51.3M, NOT ~47M. Heavy prices escalate on a real ladder at X1-XX12-DD8D: 1,976,095 ->
    1,996,571 -> 1,996,571 -> 2,017,917 -> 2,040,170, ~16k per purchase. 23 more at that escalation
    totals 51,345,154, the last costing 2,408,607. My flat-2.04M assumption was a 9.4% UNDERESTIMATE and
    it compounds if the count rises.
 2. THE 4.11x RATIO SITS NEAR THE TOP OF ITS OWN RANGE. Measured 2.85-3.30x over the best-populated
    multi-hour windows, block-level range 2.12-4.85. 4.11x is not wrong but is a FAVOURABLE DRAW from a
    very noisy distribution, and the whole model is levered directly to it. On the measured rates the
    heavy count needed is 19-25 rather than 23 — THE UNCERTAINTY IN THE RATIO SWAMPS ANY DECAY EFFECT.

THE FORECAST vs THE PURCHASE ARE TWO DIFFERENT DECISIONS AND HAVE BEEN TRAVELLING AS ONE. The evidence
supports BUYING HEAVIES. It does NOT support the 10M/hr forecast, which extrapolates ~5.6x beyond the
measured range (1->5 heavies becomes 1->28; fleet buying volume 900->3000 units/hr becomes several times
larger) on a ratio that varies 2.3x block to block. That is an assumption wearing a measurement's clothes.

ADOPTED PLAN — cheap de-risking, decides nothing prematurely: heavies pay back in ~5h, so BUY THE NEXT 3
AND RE-MEASURE AT 8. That yields a real answer within a day having committed ~6M rather than 51M, and the
3 heavies keep earning either way. Escalate only if the ratio at 8 heavies comes in below ~2.5x.
LANE SUPPLY MEASURED — THE MAP IS NOT THE CEILING. Hull scaling works; 10M/hr is a CAPITAL AND LOGISTICS
question, not a map-supply one. Script on branch lane-supply: gobot/scripts/lane_supply_analysis.sql.

(a) LANES THAT EXIST vs LANES WE FLY: 35,023 profitable source->sink lanes in the reachable universe
(51 goods, avg margin 405, under-construction gate edges excluded). In 12h we fly 340 lane-flights across
233 DISTINCT LANES — 0.67% of the universe, over 27 goods.

(b) BY MARGIN BAND — AND THE PLANNER PICKS WELL:
   A: >=1085 .... 5,016 lanes, avg margin 1,807, avg depth 36
   B: 500-1084 .. 3,108 lanes, avg margin   799, avg depth 62
   C: 200-499 ... 1,545 lanes, avg margin   347, avg depth 100
   D: <200 ...... 21,557 lanes, avg margin   28, avg depth 137   (correctly declined)
68.5% of all lanes are the near-worthless tail; the good band (A+B) is ~8,100. 82% OF REALIZED
LANE-FLIGHTS LAND IN BANDS A+B, with realized margins (1,905 / 745) matching theory almost exactly. Depth
rises as margin falls — the sp-4mpxh anti-correlation again.

TWO METHOD ERRORS THE LANE CAUGHT AND CORRECTED MID-ANALYSIS, EACH WORTH ~10x — both worth remembering:
 1. LANES ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. The 5,016 band-A lanes collapse to only 540 DISTINCT SINKS, because a
    sink's depth is shared by every lane into it. Counting lanes overstates supply ~10x. Deduped:
    A = 540 sinks / 29,734 units; B = 128 sinks / 19,840 units.
 2. REGENERATION IS ~1-2h, NOT 12h. The first pass used OUR OWN absorption ExecutedHardCap (12h) as the
    regeneration period — CIRCULAR, and it understated supply ~10x, producing a false "we're at 91% of
    capacity". Measured directly instead, gap since last sale into the same (sink, good):
       <2h    n=248  price vs previous  99.2%
       2-6h   n=94                     100.3%
       6-12h  n=42                     100.9%
    388 repeat sales at MEDIAN 1.15h apart, 385 of 388 inside 12h, price holding 99-101%. Sinks are NOT
    being depleted at current throughput; price impact is ~1%.

THE DECISIVE NUMBER: fleet consumption 2,268 units/hour at 18 hulls. Band-A supply at ~2h regeneration
~14,900 units/hour.
   Band A alone: ~6.6x headroom -> ~118 HULLS
   Band A+B:     ~11x           -> ~196 HULLS
Both far above the ~95 hulls that 5.3x of current net would require. The question was "far more than 28"
vs "barely more than 18" — the answer is FAR MORE THAN 28.

HONEST CAVEAT: regeneration was measured AT 2,268 units/hr, not at 22,680. Price impact is not linear and
the fitted recovery half-lives are long (26-39h from sp-ircfy), so cumulative displacement at 10x
throughput will be worse than 10 x 1%. What IS firm: nothing in the supply data suggests a wall anywhere
near 28 hulls, and the fleet currently displaces prices by about a percent. Where exactly between 100 and
200 hulls margin starts eroding cannot be pinned down from this data — that needs the empirical decay
curve from part (d), and these supply numbers should be read as the CEILING that decay curve approaches.

COROLLARY, NOW A MEASURED LEVER: our own ExecutedHardCap embargoes for 12h what empirically regenerates
in ~1.15h — we are self-restricting sinks by roughly an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE longer than the map requires.
That is sp-brr68, and this measurement makes it substantially more than "a config tweak". It will not
change the hull-count answer (6-11x headroom regardless), but it is a real, cheap drag on throughput and
the 294 currently-active sell shadows are the visible cost. Dispatched.

WHERE THIS LEAVES THE PLAN: per-hull output is at its optimum (fill capped at 1.33x, cr/hr flat across
buy-market count, sink selection near-optimal) and the map supports 6-11x the current fleet. THE
REMAINING PATH TO 10M/HR IS HULL COUNT, and the binding questions are capital, purchase throughput, and
whether the ~3x/hull-hour advantage decays — none of which are map-supply.
CLOSED AS INVALID 2026-07-30 (orchestrator, Admiral-approved).

THE PREMISE IS FALSIFIED. This bead claims source pool depth is "THE binding constraint". It was
filed on a measurement later found 23x wrong -- source supply was slack, not binding.

WORSE, THE FRAMING IS WRONG. In one session I filed or asserted FIVE different "THE binding
constraint" claims and falsified every one by measurement:
  API ceiling      -- freed 23% of it (0.844 req/s of shipyard reads); revenue did not move
  sink depth       -- 52% utilisation, headroom existed
  jump cooldowns   -- built on hourly net/hull, which the leg-matching defect invalidated
  working capital  -- gates BUYING, not trading
  margin decline   -- hourly margin scatters 7%-38% on leg placement alone
There is no single binding constraint. A bead asserting one at P0 sits at the top of the ready
queue and mis-directs whoever picks it up.

THE ONE DATUM WORTH KEEPING, measured 2026-07-30 at 35 heavies: individual PURCHASE_CARGO buys
average 60.5 units (median 57), but hulls stack several per tour and reach 140.4 of 225 capacity --
62.4% full. A 225-unit single buy does occur (max_units 225), so nothing structurally prevents a
full hold. So "hulls acquire ~64 units per visit" is true per visit and misleading per tour.

Whether 62.4% average fill is worth improving is a real question, but it is a TOUR-PLANNING question
and should be filed on its own evidence, not carried inside a falsified P0. Re-file if it matters.

Related: sp-76r2c documents the leg-matching defect that produced several of the falsified claims
above. sp-e441g is the sibling closure -- same author, same pattern, filed on a burst measurement.
close_reason: Closed

title: Where does 8.5x come from? Fleet is fully utilised at 24.5% margin — decompose credits-per-tour (margin per unit, hold utilisation, realised-vs-planned spread) after cycle-time and idleness were both disproved
description:
GOAL CONTEXT: Admiral directive is 10M/hr NET. Verified baseline over 10h: revenue 47,934,765, cargo cost
-35,743,168, fuel -447,216, NET 11,744,381 = 1,174,542/hr at a 24.5% margin. The gap is ~8.5x.

TWO THROUGHPUT HYPOTHESES ARE NOW DISPROVED BY MEASUREMENT, and this bead exists because of what is left:
 - sp-k7hez (cycle time): DISPROVED. Credits per hull-hour RISES with tour length (78k at 2 systems, 83k
   at 4, 127k at 5). The solver's 7-gate-hop charge is correct — those systems' gates are unbuilt.
 - sp-srhs2 (hull idleness): DISPROVED. 13 of 16 haulers run at 92-100% utilisation over 6h. The 79%
   no-trade exits were ONE bootstrap-deadlock incident in ONE system, ~35 hull-hours, already recovered.

So the fleet is fully utilised, tours are efficient, and we are still at 4.7M/hr GROSS and 1.17M/hr NET.
The gap therefore lives in CREDITS PER TOUR, not hull-time and not routing. Two candidate axes:
  (1) MARGIN PER UNIT MOVED. We turn 47.9M of revenue into 11.7M of margin — 24.5%. Every point of margin
      is ~479k/hr at current volume. Is 24.5% near the ceiling of what our lane selection can achieve, or
      are we systematically buying too close to the sink price? Look at per-lane realised spread vs the
      spread the planner PREDICTED at plan time, and at whether absorption/externality pricing
      (sp-arw9g, sp-ircfy) is eroding realised margin versus plan.
  (2) CAPACITY PER TOUR. 1,715 units of fleet hold across 16 haulers. Are tours filling the hold they
      have? Measure units actually bought per tour against hull capacity. A tour that flies a 225-unit
      heavy with 60 units aboard is a capacity leak that no extra hull fixes.

ALSO WORTH SIZING: 17.5M was spent on SHIP PURCHASES in the same 10h window that produced 11.7M of trade
margin. That is not necessarily wrong — hulls are capital assets that compound — but nobody has checked
the payback against the actual net margin per hull rather than gross. Do that arithmetic explicitly:
marginal NET margin per hull per hour vs hull price, using net not gross. Heavy freighters cost ~1.98M
and there are 3; lights ~437k and there are 13.

ASK:
 (a) Decompose the 24.5% margin: per lane, per good, per hull class. Where is margin actually made and
     lost? Report the distribution, not just the mean.
 (b) Compare realised spread against planned spread per tour. If realised is systematically below plan,
     that is a pricing/absorption defect and is the highest-value find here.
 (c) Measure hold utilisation per tour (units bought / cargo_capacity). Quantify the capacity leak if any.
 (d) Compute marginal NET margin per hull-hour by class (heavy vs light) and the true payback period at
     current prices. This directly answers whether buying more hulls is the right use of capital at all.
 (e) Recommend where the 8.5x can actually come from, with numbers. If the honest answer is "no single
     lever gets 8.5x; here are the three that together get 2-3x", say exactly that.

Diagnose before building. Do not weaken any money guard, the inventory-pressure guard, or the
honest-completion contract (RULINGS #4). Ship ARMED, no flag.
notes:
CLOSED — diagnosis complete, no code built, and the honest answer is that NO SINGLE LEVER GETS 8.5x.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS SINK ABSORPTION CONTENTION — our own concurrent planners colliding.
MEASURED: 223 fleet-wide sink-cap breaches in 8 hours across 66 containers against only 55 tours started
= ~4 breaches PER TOUR. Log line: "Tour absorption reserve breached the fleet-wide sink cap for
<container> - re-planning against the now-occupied ledger". N hulls plan concurrently, all rank the same
best sink, the first reserves it, the rest breach and RE-PLAN ONTO WORSE LANES. The cap is behaving
correctly and must NOT be weakened; the waste is that we plan into a collision and repair, instead of
spreading a priori. This is the unbuilt half of fleet anti-herd -> sp-ircfy. CONSEQUENCE FOR CAPITAL:
the fleet is ALREADY sink-contended at 16 hulls, so "buy more haulers" hits this before anything else.

(a) MARGIN IS HEALTHY AND IS NOT THE LEVER. Per-good net margin (12h) 14-45%, blended 24.5%: CLOTHING
3.84M (43.6%), LAB_INSTRUMENTS 1.98M (38.5%), URANITE 1.93M (23.6%), ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 1.57M (30.6%),
MEDICINE 1.48M (38.1%), MERITIUM 0.51M (18.3%), MICROPROCESSORS 0.12M (13.6%). Only IRON loses (-1,652,
noise). HARD CEILING: at 24.5%, even a PERFECT 100% margin — free cargo — is only 4.1x. Mix-shift is
worth ~1.2x. Margin cannot deliver 8.5x.

(b) REALISED-VS-PLANNED COULD NOT BE CLEANLY QUANTIFIED and the lane said so rather than quoting a
number: the naive aggregate (32.9% of projected) double-counts because every breach forces a re-plan and
every plan is logged; restricting to single-plan tours inverts to 255% (n=9) because projected profit
blends fresh profit with held-cargo liquidation. BOTH ARE ARTIFACTS — do not quote either. The breach
count is the solid measurement.

(c) HOLD UTILISATION — real leak, but the cause is MARKET DEPTH, not solver timidity. Per leg
(container+waypoint = one dock visit): LIGHT median fill 50.0% (p25 25%, 120 of 262 loads under 50%,
avg 44/80); HEAVY median 64.2% (avg 148/225, n=14). But trade_volume on EXPORT markets for our top goods
averages 51-80 units (CLOTHING 56, LAB_INSTRUMENTS 51, MEDICINE 53, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 57) — A LIGHT'S
80-UNIT HOLD ALREADY EXCEEDS TYPICAL SINGLE-MARKET DEPTH. Filling to ~85% requires MULTI-MARKET LOADING
per leg, which is routing work, not a knob. Worth ~1.5x on units/hr, no capital.
THIS ALSO UNDERCUTS THE HEAVY-FREIGHTER THESIS: a 225-unit heavy needs ~3 markets' depth to fill one
hold, which is exactly why it sits at 64%.

(d) BOTH HULL CLASSES PAY BACK INSIDE A DAY at 92-100% utilisation. Lights median ~99k net/hull-hour
(range 18.5k-141.8k — a 7.7x spread across IDENTICAL hulls, unexplained); payback 377,830 / ~101k =
3.7 hull-hours. Heavies: only TORWIND-142 is a real sample at 802.9k/hh (3.31h, 51 txns); 167 shows
NEGATIVE and 168 shows 382k purely because they are mid-tour with unsold cargo aboard. n=1 — DO NOT treat
the heavy figure as established. Payback 1,989,746 / ~340k conservative = 5.9 hull-hours, or 2.5h on the
observed number. Buying haulers is unambiguously correct on unit economics.

THE CAPEX SPLIT IS THE STORY. Ship spend last 12h: SHIP_PROBE 237 units 11.33M (60%), HEAVY_FREIGHTER 3

title: [bug] Trade fleet is only ~49% utilised: 262 of 331 tour containers/day (79%) exit after ~1.5 minutes having traded nothing — 183 of 360 hull-hours idle. This is the 3.2M->10M gap, not hull count

 (b) Establish whether these are (i) tours dispatched with no viable plan (planner produced nothing),

title: Screening sweep starves its own queue: alphabetical order + fixed batch
description:
screenSweep (run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:1005) lists PENDING systems, sorts ALPHABETICALLY, takes the first screenSweepBatch=5. Screening does not remove a system from PENDING (a still-charting system stays PENDING), so the head never drains — the same 5 are re-screened every tick and the alphabetical tail is never screened at all.

LIVE: 54 systems, 33 PENDING vs batch 5. Discovery outruns screening ~2.5:1 so the starved tail widens. Stragglers X1-VV36, X1-XD91 unscreened 11h+.

The data to fix it already exists: sensing_systems.screened_at is stamped on EVERY verdict write incl. PENDING (see comment ship_ports.go:1217 — 'answers when was this system last looked at... whether the sweep is reaching it at all'). LedgerPort.SystemsByVerdict drops the field when mapping to ScreenedSystem.

FIX: add ScreenedAt *time.Time to ScreenedSystem, map it through, sort NULL-first then ScreenedAt ASC, tie-break on System. screened_at is restamped each screen so this rotates: full coverage in ceil(N/5) ticks. Keep batch at 5 — a constant batch is what makes a growing frontier cost nothing extra per tick (API capped 2.00 req/s, owner ceiling 85%).

Lane: sweep-fair worktree (first attempt died of context exhaustion; re-dispatched on opus). Brief: /Users/andres.dandrea/.claude/jobs/cf7c07bb/tmp/sweep-fairness-brief.md
close_reason: Merged 04598556, deployed, verified live: X1-XD91 (12.2h untouched) screened minutes after restart; oldest un-screened went 12.4h -> ~47min. IN_SCOPE 21 -> 39 (+18 systems that the alphabetical sweep could never reach). Mutation-probed independently before merge.

title: Seed staging picks unoccupied systems: origin chosen by verdict, not presence
description:
resolvePurchaseCandidates lists probe yards only in slot.System, and buyerAt requires a hull already DOCKED at that yard. A system with zero probes therefore has no buyer, yields no candidates, and can never be filled. Purchase requires presence; presence requires purchase.

LIVE: 132 of 144 outstanding placements (92%) structurally unfillable — 121 MARKET + 11 SPARE deadlocked, 12 MARKET fillable. Explains the 'bought 0 reused 0 queued 0 (6 attempts)' symptom. Compounds: drainCandidates returns append(fills, seeds...), so the 11 seed placements sit behind 121 market fills under a 6-attempt budget and are never reached.

Only path that has ever opened a new system is takeReachableSpare (adjacent spare re-tasked) — which is why exploration cannot parallelize.

FIX: local buyer first (unchanged); otherwise buy at a covered system with a yard+docked buyer and ferry via existing RouteAcross. Non-blocking, slot IN_TRANSIT, later tick reconciles. Seeds get a guaranteed share of attempts. maxDrainAttempts stays 6 (API burst limit; 2.00 req/s cap, 85% ceiling).

Lane: ferry-fix worktree. Brief: /Users/andres.dandrea/.claude/jobs/cf7c07bb/tmp/ferry-deadlock-brief.md
close_reason: Merged 869a51a8 (staging fundability + supply fix) and c3e821e7 (seed attempt reserve), both deployed. stagingYardFor now requires a staffed yard; takeSupplyFor no longer counts an unfundable want as supply (37 targets were suppressed spuriously, 0 legitimately); 2 of 6 drain attempts held for seeds when any is outstanding. Stale rows left in place as an explicit choice (they self-heal; pruning risks sp-wgjb7). readNeighbours deliberately untouched. All guards mutation-probed independently. HONEST SCOPE: removes a permanent jam, does not itself produce seeds today — staffed adjacency now binds, and the frontier widens at the rate seeds land.

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (owner identified the intended design; my first read was wrong).

The design IS implemented. stagingYardFor (expansion.go ~:857) finds a system bordering the target, lists probe yards THERE, and stages the SPARE slot at that yard with Waypoint=yard, System=ORIGIN. Buy at the source, ferry outward via the existing seed lifecycle. The buy queue's intra-system purchase is CORRECT and must not change.

THE BUG is origin selection in readNeighbours (~:600):
    for _, s := range systems { origins[s.System] = true }   // every SCREENED system
An origin qualifies for having a VERDICT, not for being OCCUPIED. IN_SCOPE means 'screened and sells whitelist goods', not 'we have a hull there'. stagingYardFor's own comment says 'in one of our own systems bordering the target' — the code never enforces the 'our own' part.

PROOF: all 11 WANTED SPARE slots are staged in systems with ZERO parked probes — BA69(3), KD64(2), CJ56(2), CA58, GD81, KY38, NT6. All IN_SCOPE, all unoccupied, all unbuyable. No seed is ever purchased, so no target ever gets eyes, so exploration only advances via takeReachableSpare re-tasking one of 3 existing spares.

FIX (1) an origin must be occupied — require a hull that satisfies buyerAt's condition. (2) drain must not burn attempts on placements whose system has no buyer (121 of them); local/cached state only, zero API cost. NOT a cross-system ferry — that machinery already exists in the seed lifecycle.

Superseded: the earlier 'add ferry to resolvePurchaseCandidates' plan. Lane ferry-fix redirected mid-flight.

title: [P0] screenSweep starves the tail: sorts PENDING alphabetically, takes 5 — systems 11h stale and it worsens with a bigger frontier
description:
LIVE STARVATION, found while building the frontier propagation fix. Blocks judgement and therefore income.

THE BUG: screenSweep orders PENDING systems ALPHABETICALLY and takes the first screenSweepBatch=5 each tick. With more than five pending, the tail is never reached — the same five are re-screened forever and the rest are permanently starved. The constant's own comment claims the backlog 'is worked over more ticks'; with a fixed sort that is false.

MEASURED LIVE: five systems screened 24s ago, while X1-VV36 and X1-XD91 sit 11h33m stale. X1-VV36 is the ONE system with catalog_known=false — exactly the case the sweep's in-band SyncWaypoints exists to serve, and it is the one that never gets served.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: the frontier fix takes the ledger 16 -> 26 systems, and each new arrival lengthens the PENDING queue behind that unfair sort. NQ7, PK43 and VS70 get pushed out of the window too. The per-tick API cost is unchanged (the batch cap is what protects the owner's 85% budget ceiling and must stay), so this is purely a FAIRNESS defect, not a throughput one.

WHAT STARVES: judgement, and therefore income. An unscreened system is never judged, so its markets are never found — and the fleet currently cannot scale trade at all because no known yard sells a freighter. Every unscreened system is a missed chance at one.

FIX: order by screened_at ASC (oldest first) instead of alphabetically. Needs ScreenedAt threaded onto the ScreenedSystem struct — note it is SHARED with the buy queue, so the change touches the adapter and the repository select as well.

DO NOT raise screenSweepBatch to paper over it: that cap is what makes a growing frontier cost nothing extra per tick, and the owner's ceiling is 85% of the permanent 2 req/s cap. Fix the ORDER, keep the CAP.

TEST BAR: with more than batch-size PENDING systems, every system must eventually be screened across successive ticks — a fixture with five or fewer cannot show the bug.
close_reason: Closed

title: [P0] Frontier is serialized: only JUDGED systems propagate, so the ledger grows one fully-charted ring at a time
description:
OWNER GOAL: 300 systems. Ledger has been stuck at 16 known / 3 charted for hours while 12 seeds chart.

THE SERIALIZATION: readNeighbours (expansion.go:600-609) builds its origin set from systems whose verdict is IN_SCOPE or NO_WHITELIST — i.e. JUDGED — plus systems holding a parked spare. A PENDING system contributes NO neighbours. Judging requires screening, screening requires charting (markets are invisible until charted), and charting is flight-bound at ~1.1 waypoints/hr. So the frontier advances one FULLY-CHARTED RING at a time: chart ~50 waypoints -> judge -> discover neighbours -> repeat. That is the binding constraint on system COUNT, and no amount of probes or money changes it.

THE FREE WIN, measured live: the 7 PENDING systems ALREADY have 24 gate neighbours stored in gate_edges — their adjacency is known without charting them. TEN of those are systems not yet in sensing_systems at all. Propagating from PENDING would add 10 systems (16 -> 26, +62%) with ZERO API calls, and each would propagate further as its own gate is charted.

WHY GATE ADJACENCY IS ALREADY KNOWN: gate_edges is populated from the jump-gate waypoint, and the charting reorder (e6bb7d13) now puts JUMP_GATE in the market-bearing tier so gates are charted EARLY. A system therefore knows its neighbours long before it is fully charted or judged.

THE FIX: let a system propagate its neighbours once its GATE ADJACENCY is known, independent of verdict. The frontier then advances at the speed of charting ONE waypoint (the gate) rather than ~50.

THE DESIGN'S STATED OBJECTION, and why it no longer applies: the comment says 'expanding through an unscreened neighbour would flood the ledger — and then the screening sweep's API budget — with rows for a galaxy we have no reason to believe is worth anything yet.' Flooding the ledger IS the goal now (300 systems). The API concern is real but separate and already governed: the screening sweep has its own pacer and budget, and the sensing pacer currently runs 1.0-1.5 of 2.0 req/s with headroom.

MUST NOT BREAK: the screening sweep must stay within the API budget as the ledger grows — verify the pacer degrades gracefully rather than saturating (the whole parked-probe design exists because of the 2 req/s cap). Seed targeting must not thrash: seedlessTargets sorts by uncharted_count DESC, and a flood of unscreened systems carries count 0 and 'sorts last, deliberately' — confirm that still holds so new rows do not jump the queue ahead of measured work. Never block the tick (sp-uwxwo). Ships ARMED.
close_reason: Closed

title: [P0] Charting tours are EXHAUSTIVE — 79% of effort goes to asteroids that have never hosted a market or shipyard
description:
OWNER GOAL: 300 systems, 7M/hr. Charting is the binding long-run constraint at 1.1 waypoints/hr per seed. This change is a ~4.7x speedup with no new hulls.

THE WASTE, measured across every charted waypoint the fleet knows:
  ASTEROID            3297 charted -> 0 markets, 0 shipyards
  ORBITAL_STATION      965 charted -> 873 markets, 523 SHIPYARDS
  MOON                2144 -> 1521 markets, 44 yards
  PLANET              1501 -> 1252 markets, 0 yards
  FUEL_STATION        1129 -> 1129 markets (100%), 0 yards
  JUMP_GATE            373 -> 373 markets
  ASTEROID_BASE        345 -> 345 markets
  GAS_GIANT            546 -> 72 markets (13%)
  ENGINEERED_ASTEROID   22 -> 22 markets

ASTEROID has NEVER hosted a market or a shipyard: 0 for 3297. And in the systems currently being charted, 562 of 707 uncharted waypoints are ASTEROID — 79% of all remaining work.

WHY IT IS EXHAUSTIVE TODAY: UnchartedCatalog.UnchartedWaypoints documents 'the tour is exhaustive and ordering changes its length rather than its outcome' — a seed charts every uncharted waypoint in the system before standing down. X1-AJ10 has 56 left at ~1.1/hr = ~50 more hours for ONE system.

THE FIX HAS TWO PARTS:
 1. SKIP types that never host a market or shipyard. ASTEROID is the clear case (0/3297). GAS_GIANT is 13% and worth a separate decision — do not lump it in without saying so.
 2. ORDER the rest SHIPYARD-FIRST: ORBITAL_STATION holds 523 of 567 known shipyards. A yard charted early makes that system buyable, which funds local spares, which stages more seeds — it compounds, where a market charted early only adds trade data.

THIS IS FILTERABLE TODAY: waypoint TYPE is visible from the system waypoint list WITHOUT charting (only TRAITS are hidden behind UNCHARTED). SyncWaypoints already populates the waypoints table with type for every system, charted or not — verified live: uncharted systems show full type breakdowns.

EXPECTED EFFECT: X1-AJ10 drops from 65 waypoints to ~14. Per-system charting time falls ~4.7x, and shipyards surface first rather than last.

CONSTRAINTS: never block the tick (sp-uwxwo); the tour must still TERMINATE and stand the seed down correctly when the filtered set is exhausted (into a placement, onward, or spare) — do not strand a hull mid-tour; uncharted_count semantics must stay coherent with the filter or the ledger will think a system is unfinished forever; ships ARMED.

RISK TO CHECK, not assume: confirm that skipping a type cannot hide a market the screen later expects — if uncharted_count is the completion signal, a filtered tour must reconcile it rather than leave it non-zero forever.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-06: LIVE, WORSE THAN FILED, AND HALF-IMPLEMENTED. Stays P0, re-scope to PART 1 ONLY.

The core claim is STRUCTURAL, not era-dependent — confirmed across two independent universes:
  era 6 (current)  ASTEROID  38,889 charted -> 0 markets, 0 shipyards
  era 5            ASTEROID  75,535 charted -> 0 markets, 0 shipyards
0 for 114,424. The bead's '0 for 3297' was a 34x UNDERSAMPLE.

Both headline numbers are WORSE now, not better:
  94.1% of era-6 uncharted work is ASTEROID (9,637 of 10,243) — bead said 79%
  ORBITAL_STATION holds 98.3% of all shipyards (1,065 of 1,083) — bead said 92%

PART 2 HAS ALREADY SHIPPED and no commit names this bead: UnchartedWaypoints
(parkedsensing/screen_ports.go:181) now sorts on shared.ChartPriority(type). It landed under
something else.

PART 1 (skip ASTEROID) has NOT, and the code says so deliberately: 'THE SET IS UNCHANGED AND THE
TOUR IS STILL EXHAUSTIVE. Every uncharted waypoint in the system is returned, asteroids included.'
Its stated reason is exactly this bead's own flagged risk — keeping the set unchanged is what keeps
ListUnchartedCount a valid completion signal with no coordination between the two. THAT COUPLING IS
THE REAL WORK, and it is already named in the code.

Remaining value: 94% of charting work removed at zero information loss.
close_reason:
PART 1 FIXED and MERGED as main 36c45567 (lane 9e2c844e). Part 2 (shipyard-first ordering) had already
shipped unattributed and is untouched. Gate: GatePassed:true Merged:true EmptyMerge:false; 5 files /
+396 / -104; ChartSkippable confirmed in main.

NOTE ON THE FIRST GATE ATTEMPT: it returned GatePassed:true but Stale:true / Merged:FALSE — the
worktree was branched from 0903f802 while main had moved to 3c1fb3a1. The staleness guard did its
job and refused a merge onto a moved base. Rebased, re-verified (vet rc=0, test rc=0, 86 packages,
0 FAIL), re-gated clean. Worth knowing the gate can PASS and still not MERGE; 'GatePassed' alone is
not evidence anything landed, and 'ChartSkippable in main: 0' is what caught it.

THE EVIDENCE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SAMPLE: ASTEROID has hosted 0 markets and 0 shipyards across
114,838 charted waypoints in TWO INDEPENDENT UNIVERSES (era 5 and era 6). This bead's original
'0 for 3297' was a 34x undersample. Both its headline figures were WORSE at triage than as filed:
94.1% of uncharted work is ASTEROID (bead said 79%), and ORBITAL_STATION holds 98.3% of all
shipyards (bead said 92%).

THE COUPLING WAS THE WORK, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY IN THE FILE. Keeping the set exhaustive was
what kept ListUnchartedCount a valid completion signal with no coordination between the two reads —
the code said so deliberately. The skip therefore lands in unchartedIn, the SINGLE SOURCE both reads
share, whose own comment predicted exactly this: 'Routing both reads through here means a future
filter lands in ONE place and applies to both.' Count and work list narrow together and remain two
views of one set. A filter applied to the work list ALONE is the named failure mode — a zero work
list against a non-zero count pins the system PENDING forever — and a mutation probe doing precisely
that kills 5 tests by name.

THE SKIP IS DERIVED, NOT A BLACKLIST: ChartSkippable(t) := ChartPriority(t) == chartPriorityBarren.
There is no second list, so membership and sequence cannot drift apart. Two properties fall out
rather than being special-cased — GAS_GIANT survives (133/1154: rare, not never), and ANY TYPE THE
FILE DOES NOT RECOGNISE IS CHARTED, because absence of evidence is not evidence of barrenness.

THE PREMISE IS ACTIVELY FALSIFIED RATHER THAN TRUSTED: every enumeration of a charted market or
shipyard now tests its waypoint against the predicate, and an ASTEROID carrying either trait logs
ERROR naming it. The obvious objection — we stop charting asteroids so we stop learning — does not
hold: this reads traits of the 39,303 asteroids ALREADY charted, which keep syncing whether the
fleet flies anywhere or not. ERROR rather than a metric, because it must never fire and the right
response is a human re-counting the census.

TWO BEHAVIOURS TO KNOW. (1) A seed standing on an asteroid does NOT chart it — it flies to the
station, because the engine takes its next stop from the same work list the count is computed over.
Charting it would put a waypoint in the charted set the completion signal never tracked. (2) Barren
rows stay UNCHARTED in the database deliberately: completion now means 'nothing worth flying to',
NOT 'everything charted'. Both end-to-end tests assert that pairing explicitly so a zero count is
never later misread as 'map finished'.

Mutation-verified with three probes, each using a unique FULL-LINE witness after the lane's first
attempt reported INFRA FAIL — its 'applied' witness had also matched the falsifier's copy of the
same call. Removing the skip kills 9; work-list-only filtering kills 5; widening the skip one tier
kills 8.

EXPECTED EFFECT: 94.1% of the remaining charting backlog (9,637 of 10,243) stops being work, and
all-barren systems release their seed on the FIRST tick instead of after ~50 hours.

CORRECTION CARRIED FROM TRIAGE: the census is 114,838, not the 114,424 first reported — the table
grew between queries. The lane also caught itself writing unqueried era-5 numbers into the code
comment and replaced them with real ones before committing.

title: [P0] Cross-gate SPARE slots can never be filled — buying needs local presence, nothing re-tasks a surplus hull. Caps the fleet at 3 yards.
description:
OWNER GOAL: 300 systems, 7M/hr. Currently 16 systems, 444k/hr. This is the binding constraint after sp-dpfp8.

STATE, measured live:
 - 9 SPARE slots are WANTED at yards in X1-GF41(3 yards), X1-BT49(2), X1-MY3(2), X1-UV2(1) — exactly the systems whose yards would extend the buying network.
 - NONE can be funded. buyerAt requires a hull PARKED AT THE YARD, and the fleet has presence only in X1-KP23 (3 buyable yards).
 - 13 hulls sit PARKED on MARKET slots in X1-KP23. Surplus exists; nothing moves it.
 - The two systems we DID reach (X1-AJ10, X1-XD91) have ZERO shipyards, so that presence extends nothing.

THE CONFLATION: expansion sends seeds only to systems needing CHARTING. X1-GF41 is already fully charted (uncharted_count=0) so it is never a seed target — yet it is the single highest-value system to occupy, because its 3 yards would take buying from 3 yards to 6. 'Chart this system' and 'establish a buying foothold here' are different needs and only the first exists.

WHY THE EXISTING PATHS DO NOT COVER IT:

Seeds chart new systems, charted systems reveal their own shipyards, and each new yard becomes another staging point — the ring widens instead of terminating. Crucially it falls back to requestedUnits when the market row is unreadable (transaction_utils.go:43-52), producing ONE oversized tranche and the SAME 400 signature an unlisted good gives — which is exactly why the RCA could not separate the two causes. A second volume computation would have duplicated the lookup and could disagree with it. The fix instead makes a chunking failure non-fatal (test 4).

BONUS HOLE CLOSED: deliverInputs had no protectGood equivalent, so a hull carrying a factory's own EXPORT would dump it into that factory's own bid (the -258k MEDICINE shape). The EXPORT exclusion closes it; pinned by test 3.

DOES NOT clear already-poisoned holds — see the follow-up bead.

title: Lower trade_fleet.working_capital_reserve 1M -> 300k (Admiral order)
description:
COLDSTART routes hull acquisition #2 to the TRADE fleet (run_bootstrap_income.go:107 maybeSeedTradeHull). Its capital gate only checks it can AFFORD the hull: cushion=(treasury-price) >= contractWorkingCapitalFloor (150k). It never checks the hull will be able to TRADE.

The trade coordinator enforces config.yaml:187 trade_fleet.working_capital_reserve = 1000000. After the seed buy, treasury is guaranteed to be far below 1M, so every tour dies on leg 0.

LIVE, era 5 (TORWIND-6, bought ~315k):
  Tour planned: 5 legs, projected profit 29356
  Tour leg 0: buy of 14 ASSAULT_RIFLES @ 2486 would breach working-capital floor
    - live balance 146780, reserve 1000000, even 1 unit pierces - skipping, will re-plan
  Tour re-plan budget exhausted - stopping
Pre-positioning also parked (capital ceiling 0). The hull replans every ~3min forever and burns fuel on sp-nxrt reposition escalations. At ~25k/hr contract income it would not unlock for ~34h.

This is deterministic, not a race: buying the hull is itself what puts treasury under the reserve. Every cold start seeds a dead trade hull.

DO NOT lower the 1M reserve - that is weakening a money guard (RULINGS #4). Fix the gate that buys into it.
