title: Ship Save's last-write-wins fallback resurrects a released claim from a stale entity, permanently orphaning the hull
description:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by RCA with prod DB evidence, not inference): ShipRepository.Save's last-write-wins fallback re-stamps a STALE in-memory assignment over the live row, resurrecting a claim that was already correctly released. The hull is then owned by a COMPLETED container forever and no coordinator can use it.

NOT a liquidation bug. Liquidation merely supplies a second container id inside a nav entity's lifetime; ANY container pair can trigger it. The resurrecting writer for the current occurrence was a CONTRACT-WORK container, not a liquidation one.

MECHANISM:
- ship_repository.go:885-906 - on CAS conflict, Save logs and deliberately falls through to saveLastWriteWins (:946-965, UpdateAll: true).
- shipToModel (:842-856) writes assignment_status / container_id / assigned_at FROM THE ENTITY. So the ownership triplet is clobbered from a snapshot the code has just PROVEN stale.
- The stale snapshot is structural: navigate_route.go:164 loads the ship ONCE and carries that entity through the whole flight; Navigate/Dock/Orbit/Refuel/SetFlightMode each write it back whole via plain Save (ship_repository.go:323,361,397,426,474).

OBSERVED SEQUENCE (21:31, ONE continuously-running daemon, no restart):
  21:31:06  contract-work 1b802e4d releases the hull; coordinator fires async homing -> nav loads the entity
  21:31:06  liquidation dispatch -> ClaimShip writes 48887734 (nav entity's load lands on the wrong side of this)
  21:31:10  liquidation exits, release WORKS ("Released 1 ship assignments (reason: completed)")
  21:31:56  homing arrives -> refuel -> "save conflict - row version moved past 11 ... last-write-wins" -> 48887734 RESTORED
CONTROL GROUP confirming race direction is decisive: the 21:03 and 21:16 liquidations logged NO release line - there the nav entity loaded BEFORE the claim, so its clobbers wrote NULL and the hull came back free. Same code, opposite race, opposite outcome.

COMPANION DEFECT (not optional): shipToModel:720 writes Version = PersistedVersion()+1 and saveLastWriteWins:957 pins the entity to it, so a stale entity LOWERS the row version and then wins every subsequent conflict for the rest of the flight. Evidence: the row sits at version=1 after hours of traffic; the conflict log resets (past 27 -> past 3). This is what turns an instant race into ~50s of repeated re-stamping.

WHY NOTHING SELF-HEALS: the per-tick reaper ReclaimShipsFromInterruptedWorkers scans FAILED containers only; all four orphans today are COMPLETED (they ran and exited cleanly). The only thing that clears it is the startup-only ReleaseAllActive sweep (daemon_server.go:632-636), which is why a daemon restart "fixes" it for ~15 minutes.

RED HERRING, do not chase: "Ship X already assigned to this container (recovered)" is the idempotent branch of attemptClaimShip (container_runner.go:1126-1128) and appears on every healthy start.

NOT sp-l8p3z (76a269d2). That hypothesis is FALSIFIED: no restart occurred between 21:31:10 and 21:53:51 (coordinator polled every 30s, bootstrap heartbeated throughout); the claim was created AND orphaned inside one running daemon. sp-l8p3z's class is a recovery pass leaving a RUNNING row with no runner - different state, different path.

IMPACT: production, era 5, recurring. Four orphans today (bf268932, 35500eed, 48887734, c7b516d3). Each one silently stops ALL contract income - the cold start's critical path - until a daemon restart. Currently frozen.
close_reason: Closed

title: Contract workflow hangs forever waiting for an arrival event that already fired, and restart recovery resurrects it as RUNNING
description:
CAUSED A 7-HOUR PRODUCTION OUTAGE, era 5, 2026-07-26. The sole earner sat idle from 14:18 to 20:47 while its container reported RUNNING.

WHAT HAPPENED:
  14:17:52  route segment started (a DRIFT leg, from the sp-6n1bi overspend)
  14:17:58  Ship navigation command executed
  14:18:28  Arrival not due yet - safety resync while in transit
  14:18:28  Arrival resync still shows IN_TRANSIT with a future ETA, continuing to wait
            ... nothing, ever again. 6h29m of silence.
The ship DID arrive - it was IN_ORBIT at X1-KP23-I53 when found. The workflow simply never processed the arrival and blocked forever waiting for an event that had already fired.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS:

1. THE HANG ITSELF. batch_contract_workflow blocks indefinitely waiting for a ship-arrival event. There IS a safety resync ("Arrival not due yet", "Ship arrival event overdue - resyncing") and it fired correctly earlier in the same run at 12:17:35 - but once the wait entered this state it never re-armed. Find why the resync stops re-checking. A wait on an external event must have a bounded re-check that cannot be starved, and arrival is knowable at any time by polling the ship.

2. THE ZOMBIE SURVIVES RESTART. A daemon restart at 14:23 (five minutes after the hang) RECOVERED the container as RUNNING and it never resumed. Restart recovery adopted a dead worker and re-marked it healthy, which HID the corpse - the container list showed RUNNING for six hours. RULINGS #2 says restarts are always resilient; recovering a hung worker into a RUNNING row that never ticks is the opposite. Recovery must either genuinely resume the work or fail loudly, never resurrect a container that then does nothing.

DETECTION GAP WORTH CLOSING TOO: nothing noticed. No heartbeat staleness check, no per-container liveness watchdog. The scout-post coordinator HAS a manning watchdog (see sp-p8ldq) - contract workers have no equivalent. A container that logs nothing for many multiples of its expected cadence should be visible without a human reading logs.

RECOVERY THAT WORKED (for the test to model): stopping the container released the ship claim, after which dock+refuel succeeded and the coordinator span a replacement. Before that, the claim made the ship uncommandable - a manual `ship dock` container was silently discarded and never appeared in the container list.

MUST NOT: weaken the arrival-wait into a busy poll, or make recovery drop in-flight work. The fix is to bound the wait and to make recovery honest, not to remove either.
close_reason: Closed

title: Manning watchdog livelocks a cold start: it re-mans tours faster than they can produce their first scan
description:
OBSERVED IN PROD, era 5 (torwind-2026-07-26, player 5, binary 0a4d0ba2). The scout-post manning watchdog tore down and re-manned all 3 tours every ~2 minutes, indefinitely, so coverage froze at 12/26.

THE LOOP (daemon.log, verbatim):
  11:32:26  Partitioned scout post X1-KP23 into 3 disjoint tours over 26 markets
  11:32:27  Manned ... TORWIND-2 (7 markets) / TORWIND-3 (17 markets) / TORWIND-4 (2 markets)
  11:34:27  WARNING: fully manned but silent: worst-case market age 4403s past its 1h0m0s freshness target, no new telemetry for 4 cycles — re-manning it
  11:34:27  No markets to scan for post X1-KP23 slot yet — leaving unmanned this tick
  11:35:28  Partitioned ... (identical) and re-manned all 3
  ... repeats

ROOT CAUSE: defaultManningStallCycles = 4 (run_scout_post_coordinator.go:132). At the 30s tick that is ~2 minutes of 'no new telemetry' before the watchdog re-mans. A freshly-manned probe must still FLY to its first market before it can scan, and a 17-market tour is far longer than that. So the tour never survives long enough to emit telemetry, the watchdog kills it, and the cycle repeats — a livelock, not a stall.

It is worst exactly at cold start, which is when it hurts most: a fresh era has every market stale (here 4403s past target on tick one), so OldestAgeSeconds is large IMMEDIATELY and the silence condition is satisfied from the first cycle. The watchdog cannot distinguish 'this tour is dead' from 'this tour has not arrived anywhere yet'.

MITIGATED LIVE (not fixed): tuned manning_stall_cycles 4 -> 30 on the live container (bounds [1,1440], applied without restart). That is a workaround on ONE container in ONE era, not a fix — the default still livelocks every future cold start.

FIX DIRECTION (the knob is not the answer): the watchdog should not count silence against a tour that has not yet had the chance to report. Options to weigh:
 (a) start the stall clock from the tour's first ARRIVAL/scan rather than from manning, so travel time is not counted as silence;
 (b) scale the threshold to the tour's own shape (its market count / estimated circuit time), which the partitioner already computes;
 (c) require evidence of actual deadness (no nav progress, no API activity) rather than absence of fresh telemetry.
Raising the default alone just moves the livelock to longer tours.

WATCH WHEN FIXING: the watchdog earns its keep against genuinely dead tours ('the tour keeps going silent on a likely-unreachable market' backoff path at :1419) — do not disable it, and keep that backoff intact.
close_reason: Closed

title: Probe-sensing coordinator has no pre-EXPANSION gate — it suppresses cold-start scouting to 1 hull
description:
OBSERVED IN PROD, era 5 (torwind-2026-07-26, player 5, binary f4cdb1d1). Bootstrap bought 3 probes (probe_target=3, a fixed constant) but only ONE is manned on a tour; TORWIND-3 and TORWIND-4 sit DOCKED at the shipyard doing nothing. Coverage crawls at 8/26 on a 1h18m circuit against a 1h freshness target — the scout-post coordinator logged its own warning: 'Scout post X1-KP23 undersized: 26 markets over 1 hull(s) ... needs 2 hulls'.

ROOT CAUSE: run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go has ZERO references to InExpansion / PhaseExpansion / pre-EXPANSION — it has no phase gate at all. Its sibling run_probe_buyer_fleet_coordinator.go DOES (line 303, InExpansion checked FIRST 'so a pre-EXPANSION tick spends nothing anywhere'), and that gate is observably working: 'probe buying deferred: bootstrap phase pre-EXPANSION'. Sensing never got the same treatment when sp-tky2x replaced the freshness sizer with it.

So during COLDSTART sensing runs anyway, computes '0 in-scope systems, 0 hulls desired, supply 3' from an empty whitelist — correct for its own model, since a fresh era has no trading footprint — and writes that to the scout posts it owns via UpdateSensingState. The MinHulls>0 branch keeps the post alive and claims to never shrink it, but the floor is not reaching the MANNING decision: bootstrap declared minHulls=3 and only 1 hull is manned.

ADMIRAL RULING (2026-07-26): demand-driven sensing is an EXPANSION-era behavior ONLY. It must be dormant until the jump gate is built. During COLDSTART, bootstrap owns probe provisioning (fixed probe_target) and the scout-post coordinator mans them.

COST: ~45k of a 175k cold-start treasury spent on two probes that are parked, and home-system scanning running at one third of the capacity that was paid for. Market coverage is the critical path to contract profitability, so this directly slows the whole cold start.

FIX: gate the probe-sensing coordinator on EXPANSION, mirroring the probe buyer's gate exactly — same BootstrapExpansionPhaseReader, checked FIRST before any fleet read or post write, same fail-closed error semantics (an unreadable phase must NOT run sensing).

ACCEPTANCE (this is the real bar, not just 'the gate exists'): on a cold start with sensing dormant, bootstrap's declared minHulls floor must actually drive manning — all 3 probes on disjoint tours, not 1. Verify the scout-post coordinator sizes to the declared floor when sensing is not writing a budget.
close_reason: Closed

title: First-hauler pivot guard fails OPEN after a daemon restart — frees the sole earner into a permanent stall
description:
REPRODUCED IN STAGING (TORWIND_DEV16, 2026-07-26). A daemon restart drops the in-memory last-ask, the sp-muc5x affordability guard falls open, and the pivot frees the command frigate while the hauler is still unaffordable. The result is self-locking: no earner, so treasury never grows, so the hauler is never affordable.

TIMELINE (local -03:00):
  02:07:56  'pivot HELD (not freeing the earner)'  <- guard working, frigate earning
  02:12     daemon restart (routine redeploy, DB preserved)
  02:13:18  'first-hauler PIVOT: FREED the command frigate'  <- first tick after restart
  after     frigate DOCKED fleet=purchasing cargo=0/40; treasury FROZEN at 423434 across 8+ heartbeats
            hauler needs 470835 (ask 320835 + 150000 floor). Gap never closes.

WHY IT SELF-LOCKS: the frigate's contract loop cannot restart — the loop start is gated on
!obs.CommandFrigatePurchasing, and the pivot just set that dedication. So the only earner is
permanently parked as the purchasing ship with nothing to buy.

ROOT CAUSE: bootstrapAcquirer.lastAsk (bootstrap_ports.go:444) is an IN-MEMORY map (a.lastAsks,
mutex-guarded). On a cold/unreadable yard PriceCheck returns that last ask; after a restart it is 0.
The guard is 'if lastAsk > 0 && treasury-lastAsk < floor { HOLD }' (run_bootstrap_income.go:523), so
lastAsk==0 skips the hold entirely and proceeds to free+position.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM sp-dlv3j. The pre-existing form had the same fragility: a per-container in-memory
cache documented as 'dropped on restart (a DATA re-seed re-populates it on a fresh cold start)'. That
mitigation only fires while probes are UNDER target, because seedHaulerPriceFromYard lived inside
acquireProbesToTarget. With probes at target there is no re-seed, so the guard stays open forever.
sp-dlv3j moved the value from the coordinator to the adapter; the durability was already broken.

RULINGS #2: daemon restarts are ALWAYS resilient — every piece of operational state must survive a
restart. This guard does not.

FIX DIRECTION: make the last-ask durable, or make the guard fail CLOSED on absent evidence. Note
fail-closed-on-zero is NOT free: a genuine first-ever cold start has no ask and must still be able to
pivot, or the cold start wedges the other way. Options: persist the last ask (shipyard_inventory /
market data already store yard prices); or re-seed unconditionally each tick while haulers==0 rather
than only inside the probe-buy path; or gate the pivot on a READABLE live price instead of remembered
evidence.

Money guards must not be weakened. The buy itself is already correctly gated on readable+cushion — this
bead is only about WHEN the earner is freed.
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: boot-standing bootstrap spins unpaced instead of exiting at terminal EXPANSION on a mature fleet (runner re-enters a returned Handle; -1 budget never completes)
description:
LIVE REGRESSION (era-4 mature fleet, 253 hulls): after the 011cb367+d1df3467 deploy, bootstrap-player-4-71a01c6d logged the terminal-EXPANSION exit every iteration ('Bootstrap coordinator exiting: EXPANSION reached (gate built) and handed off') and then DID NOT exit — 'Iteration N completed' -> 'Executing iteration' with consecutive iterations on the SAME log second; iteration 11 in ~3min; measured 37.3 req/min (~3x healthy) of full-fleet ListShips against the 2 req/s account cap. Container stopped manually; main unsafe to deploy until fixed.

ROOT CAUSE (not in either suspect commit's diff): a contract mismatch between the launch model and the handler exit that 3017d97c (sp-difa.1) made reachable. container_ops_bootstrap.go launches the bootstrap container with maxIterations=-1 on the premise 'Handle() never returns' (registry comment said budget irrelevant). Since 3017d97c, Handle() RETURNS cleanly at terminal EXPANSION (res.Done -> return result,nil) — but res.Done died inside Handle: RunBootstrapCoordinatorResponse carried no Done field, NOTHING mapped it to the runner, and container_runner.go execute() has NO inter-iteration sleep (pacing lives inside Handle, which the Done path exits before reaching). ShouldContinue() is unconditionally true at -1 (container.go:376), so the runner re-entered Handle() immediately and forever: both symptoms (no termination + same-second spin) from one seam.

WHY THE BASELINE MASKED IT: the 3017d97c deploy RECOVERED the prior RUNNING row, and recoverContainer (daemon_server.go:1415) defaults iterations=1 for runner-loop types without an 'iterations' config key (bootstrap persists none) — the recovered container completed via budget exhaustion at iteration 1 ('Container completed successfully'). That exit consumed the row (COMPLETED), so the NEXT deploy's boot-standing path launched a FRESH -1 container — the first fresh -1 launch ever to observe Done — and it spun. 011cb367/d1df3467 are innocent: git diff 3017d97c..d1df3467 never touches container_runner.go, the Handle loop, or Done propagation.

FIX (two layers, both live-by-default): (1) TERMINATION — new common.RunTerminalReporter response contract (mirrors CompletionReporter); RunBootstrapCoordinatorResponse gains Done + RunTerminal(); Handle threads res.Done into the response; execute() breaks to finishCleanExit (COMPLETED) on a terminal report — the only way a -1 container can complete. (2) PACING (defence in depth) — standingIterationFloors: an infinite bootstrap container whose handler returns WITHOUT terminal is paced at the bootstrap tick (bootstrapCmd.DefaultTickInterval=45s, single-sourced from defaultBootstrapTickSeconds) between re-entries, ctx-interruptible via sleepOrCancel; inert for every other type (floor 0). Fresh-fleet cold start byte-identical: reconcileOnce untouched, pacing engages only when Handle returns non-terminally (never during cold start).

TESTS (RED first on main): container_runner_bootstrap_terminal_test.go — (A) TestBootstrapTerminalResponseCompletesInfiniteContainer: REAL handler over a mature-fleet observation in a real runner at -1; on main it re-entered (13 Handle calls) -> now COMPLETED with exactly 1 Handle. (B) TestBootstrapInfiniteContainerPacesIterationsAtTick: -1 bootstrap container with a non-terminal response; on main only the startup jitter was ever slept -> now every re-entry paced at 45s. MUTATIONS KILLED: (m1) terminal check 'if runDone && false' -> A fails (spin detected); (m2) floor *0 (compiling) -> B fails alone; (m3) 'result.Done = false' in Handle -> A fails. go build+vet clean, gofmt clean, full go test ./... -race green.
notes: BUILT + COMMITTED, ready to gate (lead gates — RULINGS #13, agent does not merge). Worktree: .claude/worktrees/agent-a5a2a54519cd9d49c · branch worktree-agent-a5a2a54519cd9d49c · SHA c8256cc3299adc7b64f6a3d60440c580c4594127 (code-only, 6 files, +374/-5, based on main d1df3467, ff-verified not stale). Files: internal/adapters/grpc/{container_runner.go, container_ops_bootstrap.go, command_factory_registry.go, container_runner_bootstrap_terminal_test.go(new)}, internal/application/bootstrap/commands/run_bootstrap_coordinator.go, internal/application/common/run_terminal_contract.go(new). Full go test ./... -race green in the worktree; both new tests RED-verified on pre-fix main; 3 mutations killed. DEPLOY NOTE: fix is live-by-default (no knob — it repairs the standing contract, RULINGS #4 untouched: no spend path changed); after deploy, boot-standing will relaunch bootstrap on the mature fleet and it must COMPLETE within ~1 tick (watch for 'Run terminal — the response reports the command's whole run finished' then 'Container completed successfully', container status COMPLETED, exactly 1 iteration).

title: Sensing scales with the charted map, not the trading footprint — the structural API-cap defect
description:
THE structural fix for next era. The API budget is server-capped at 2.00 req/s and cannot be raised. This is permanent and binds EARLIER each era: sensing scales with systems charted, trading scales with credits, and the map outruns the fleet from day one. Everything must be measured in CREDITS PER REQUEST.

MEASURED THIS ERA (era 4, live):
- 7,200 requests/hour available; 114 transactions/hour completed = ~63 requests per transaction. A minimal buy->sell cycle (navigate, dock, buy, orbit, navigate, dock, sell, orbit) is ~8 requests for 2 transactions = ~4 per transaction. We run ~16x the floor. Roughly 94% of the budget is not the trade cycle.
- Market-bearing systems SCANNED: 355. Systems we TRADED in over 12h: 72. Over 3h: 37.
- We sense ~5x more systems than we ever trade in. The market-freshness sizer reports aggregate demand 339 probes against supply 200 — straining to keep fresh a map that is mostly systems the fleet never visits.
- Scouts are ~77% of daemon activity and ~84% of navigation.

THE FIX: scope sensing to the TRADING FOOTPRINT rather than the charted map. Keep scanning systems we actually trade in — that is exactly where a crushed market needs watching for recovery — plus a bounded discovery allowance. Stop spending the budget refreshing hundreds of systems we have never sold into.

WHAT MUST NOT BREAK (learned the hard way this era): market prices are VOLATILE and NON-MONOTONE. A market we crush by dumping recovers on its own, and the ONLY way we learn it recovered is by going to look. Scanning is not overhead competing with trading — it is the sensor that finds the sinks trading depends on. Cutting scouts by COUNT blinds us everywhere, including on the markets we most want to see recover. The cut must be by SCOPE, never by count. An earlier attempt to cap max_probe_fleet was wrong for exactly this reason and was reverted.

TRADE-OFF TO DESIGN AROUND: narrowing scope trades away DISCOVERY. A rich lane in a system we have never traded would go unseen, and PLAYBOOK §5's multi-system advantage depends partly on having options. The design needs a bounded exploration allowance, not zero.
acceptance_criteria: scan scope tracks the trading footprint plus a bounded discovery allowance; requests-per-transaction falls materially from ~63; recovery of a previously-crushed traded market is still detected; freshness sizer demand comes within its supply; no reduction in probe COUNT is used as the mechanism

10% of the revenue for the largest share of the binding resource.

THE ORIGINAL DESIGN, restated by the Admiral, and it is better than this bead's:
  1. ALL market scans draw from ONE FIXED BUDGET. Total scan cost must NOT grow with the charted
     map -- that is the whole point, and it is what makes the 2.00 req/s server cap survivable
     forever rather than binding earlier every era.
  2. Consequently, the more markets we know, the LESS OFTEN each is scanned. Scan interval is an
     OUTPUT of (budget / markets known), never a per-market setting.
  3. A PRIORITY QUEUE decides who gets the next scan slot, ordered by profitability -- the markets
     that make us the most money get looked at the most.
  4. NO STARVATION: every known market must eventually reach the front. This is what preserves the
     constraint below.

WHAT THIS DESIGN GETS RIGHT that footprint-scoping does not: this bead's own warning is that market
prices are volatile and non-monotone -- a market we crush recovers on its own, and the ONLY way we
learn it recovered is to go look. Footprint-scoping risks never looking again at a system we stopped
trading in. A priority queue with an anti-starvation guarantee keeps looking at everything, just at a
frequency proportional to value. It also needs no "bounded discovery allowance" bolted on: discovery
is simply the tail of the same queue.

Note the machinery for (3) and (4) partly EXISTS in the parked scanner already: value_clamp_r
("ceiling on how much more scan attention the hottest market may earn than the baseline; 1 flattens
the weighting entirely") is the priority weighting, and min_scan_rate_milli is the floor that keeps
data from going fully dark. So the fix is largely to make the twelve direct readers go THROUGH this
scanner rather than around it -- not to build a new mechanism.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE: total market+shipyard read rate is bounded by one configured budget and does not
rise when the charted map grows; every market read in the daemon is attributable to that budget (no
direct MarketData callers outside the scanner, or they draw from the same allowance); scan order is
value-weighted; every known market has a bounded worst-case staleness (prove the anti-starvation
guarantee with a test, not an argument); requests-per-transaction falls materially from the ~50
measured tonight; and recovery of a previously-crushed traded market is still detected.

DO NOT reduce probe COUNT as the mechanism -- the original warning on this bead stands, and an
earlier max_probe_fleet cap was reverted for exactly that reason. Note my current live mitigation
(capex_reserve_credits 5,000,000 and capital_multiplier_k_milli 10,000, freezing probe purchases) is
in that warned direction and must be lifted once this lands.

THE KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING, which reframes the bead's own call-site list. The twelve

Everything the note lists as a leak — contract work, manufacturing, tour-run, the stocker,

THREE CLASSES; the ZERO VALUE IS BUDGETED so an unclassified (or future) call site is paced
rather than unmetered.
- Earning (never denied, always metered): FOUR pre-commit money guards, each of which fails

  staleAskAborts, and the arb coordinator's min-margin guard. Serving these from store would

RECOVERY OF A CRUSHED MARKET IS STRUCTURALLY FAVOURED, not merely preserved: dumping into a
sink drops its bid, which WIDENS the relative spread, which RAISES its weight and SHORTENS

title: API budget: 51% of a saturated 2 req/s goes to topology re-reads, 0.6% to selling
description:
THE fleet-wide throughput ceiling. Everything else (capital, margin, absorption, hull count) is slack by comparison.

MEASURED. Server limit is 2.00 req/s sustained (x-ratelimit-limit-per-second: 2, type=IP Address) — NOT a config choice, cannot be raised. Daemon is running 1.80 req/s = 90% saturated.

Request mix over a 15-minute window (1686 requests total):
  Get Waypoint      389  (23%)
  Get Jump Gate     347  (21%)  <- transient far-sink cold-cache warm-up, already decaying 142->39 per 3min bucket
  Navigate          296  (18%)
  Get Market        130   (8%)
  Get Construction  124   (7%)
  Jump               96, Get Agent 83, Dock 49, Orbit 47, Refuel 46
  Sell Cargo         10  (0.6%)
  Purchase Cargo    not in top 14

Topology reads (Waypoint + Jump Gate + Construction) = 860 = 51% of a saturated budget. The calls that actually earn credits get under 1%.

WHY IT IS THE CEILING. Trade economics are healthy and NOT the limit: 21.5% margin (3h: sells +31.2M vs buys -25.7M), 62.1M cash sitting idle against only 20.3M deployable per simultaneous load, 7160 units of hold. Capital turns over 0.14x/hour. Adding hulls or capital cannot help while the API cannot serve the hulls we already have — the fleet_autosizer ceiling exists for exactly this reason (defaultFleetCeilingTotal comment: 'the HARD API-request-budget bound - each hull adds request load').

THE LEVER. Requests-per-credit is the only multiplier available. Cutting topology from 51% to ~10% frees ~0.8 req/s for navigate/dock/buy/sell — roughly 2.5x trade throughput, with no new capital and no new hulls.

SCOPE. Find and eliminate redundant topology fetching. Get Waypoint at 26/min is the persistent offender (Get Jump Gate is self-limiting). Suspect paths: gategraph storedThenVerify live per-hop probes (capped at maxChosenPathConstructionProbes=2 but multiplied across paths), waypoint refresh policy, and Get Construction polling. gate_edges already caches 1119 systems / 5032 edges — most of this should be served from store.
acceptance_criteria: topology share of API traffic falls from 51% to under 15%; Sell Cargo + Purchase Cargo share rises materially; sustained req/s stays under 2.0; no increase in stale-data trade errors; credits/hour rises

title: far-sink reach guard refuses everything: BFS breadth-truncation misread as unreachable
description:
Far-sink capture (sp-cmwge, deployed 4d633a24) is INERT in production: tour_far_sinks_admitted=0 while tour_candidates_dropped_total{reason=far_sink_beyond_flight_horizon}=56.

ROOT CAUSE. farSinkReachAt (run_tour_coordinator_farsink.go) proves reach by walking repositionNeighborsWithinJumps(sinkSystem, MaxJumpPath=5) and requiring every already-admitted system to appear in the result. That walk is breadth-capped at repositionBfsMaxSystems=64 (run_trade_route_coordinator_lanes.go:267,303). A far sink is BY DEFINITION far from the tour's systems, so those systems sit at depth 4-5; the walk stops after discovering 64 systems and never reaches them. nearest[sys] is unresolved and the sink is refused as 'beyond flight horizon' when the executor could in fact fly there. The guard's own comment concedes the mode: 'A breadth-truncated walk therefore refuses too, which is the safe side.' Safe, but it makes the feature unable to admit at this graph size.

WHY IT MATTERS. Absorption is the fleet's binding constraint: 129 systems carry live IMPORT/EXCHANGE sinks (5217 rows), and we sell into 8 over the last 3h — 6% utilization. Dumping into the same 8 systems crushes price and is why margin is ~11.5k/transaction.

COST IS SAFE. gategraph Connections is store-first (gate_edges); 1119 systems are cached across 5032 edge rows, so proving reach is DB reads, not API calls. Any fix MUST NOT add live API probes — the fleet has hit 100% API budget before.
acceptance_criteria: tour_far_sinks_admitted fires non-zero in production; distinct systems sold into rises above 8; no increase in API request rate; far_sink_beyond_flight_horizon still fires for genuinely-unreachable sinks (guard not defeated, only made exact)

title: Wire BestSinksAcrossSystems -> allowedSystems behind a BOUNDED reach, to capture the ~28.5k/u far lanes the tour horizon still cannot see
description:
DEFERRED ITEM (a) from sp-tp5c3's close note, re-surfaced by the sp-1cuy6 lane 2026-07-25 as the only genuine remaining capture path for the big far lanes.

THE PRIZE (measured, from sp-1cuy6): lanes whose source and sink sit beyond the tour candidate horizon are ABSENT from the snapshot, not rejected — the planner never sees them. Examples: AI_MAINFRAMES X1-RJ40-CB4E(29337) -> X1-UM5-A1(57830), spread 28,493/unit, ~6.4M on a single 225-unit tour INTO HOME; a second AI_MAINFRAMES lane at 28,953/u; ANTIMATTER lanes at 7,528-8,057/u. The daemon emits ~200 'Tour horizon dropped N profitable lane(s)' events per 30 min.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY SOLVED: sp-tp5c3 shipped the honest per-pair travel matrix (tour_solver.py:587-588, gate_hops * inter_system_seconds) and the Admiral re-armed candidate_hop_depth: 2 on 2026-07-23. That fixed PRICING and widened the horizon to 2 hops — but the biggest lanes' sinks sit outside even a widened bounded horizon, because the horizon is built from gate-NEIGHBOUR expansion around home, not from where the value actually is.

BestSinksAcrossSystems already knows where the value is. Wiring it into allowedSystems would let the planner see those sinks directly.

THE BLOCKER — IT IS GLOBAL/UNBOUNDED BY CONSTRUCTION: wiring that scanner as-is reintroduces exactly the unbounded-reach failure class that produced sp-ry741 / sp-e059j / sp-ju9pn / sp-1bme8 — lanes admitted at one horizon, flown at another, then refused at execution, with hulls stranded holding undeliverable cargo. sp-1cuy6's whole premise was that a BOUNDED horizon sidesteps that family. So this must NOT be wired raw.

WORK: design the bound FIRST, then wire. The sink set must be capped (top-N by value, and/or a hard reach ceiling) and — critically — every admitted sink must be REACHABLE AND PRICED at the same horizon the executor will actually fly, so admission and execution can never disagree. Reuse the existing per-pair gate_hops matrix for pricing rather than inventing a second model.

ALSO IN SCOPE: the freshness interaction. title: [contract] FIXED per-hull standby homes — rip out demand-ranked distribution (it concentrates on the top hub); deterministic one-hull-per-park
description:
ADMIRAL DIRECTIVE — overrides the sp-9le3x demand-ranked homing model. Idle contract delivery hulls MUST return to FIXED homes: each hull is assigned exactly ONE central-band waypoint and always returns to it. NO demand-ranking, NO occupancy competition, NO cross-hull distribution anywhere in the homing path.

WHY (the demand model is the bug): sp-ojp32 armed the full central-park SET but kept the design's DEMAND-RANKED distribution (DistributeIdleHullsAcrossStandby + standbyDemandProvider). Demand-ranking inherently CONCENTRATES hulls toward the top-demand hub — live result: K83x4 idle while A1/H55/E43/D40 sit EMPTY. Compounding: hulls that end legs AT a park are treated as 'already home' (idle_arb.go ~:1071, home_ship.go ~:109) so an over-occupied park is never rebalanced, and idle-arb-reserved hulls don't cycle to disperse. Demand distribution cannot deliver reliable one-per-waypoint spread; a fixed assignment does so trivially and is restart-idempotent.

FIX: assign each contract delivery hull a FIXED home waypoint from the central-park set (KEEP the isCentralSink set resolution from sp-ojp32 — that part is correct). Assignment must be DETERMINISTIC + STABLE across restarts and to DISTINCT parks (one-per-park when hulls<=parks; deterministic overflow when hulls>parks). Proximity-aware matching (each hull to a distinct nearest park, e.g. greedy/stable matching to minimize homing flight) is preferred but distinctness+determinism is the hard requirement. An idle hull not at its assigned home navigates to it; at its home it stays. REMOVE the demand provider from the homing path (standbyDemandProvider / SetStandbyDemandProvider for homing) and REPLACE DistributeIdleHullsAcrossStandby's demand/occupancy logic with the fixed assignment. The 'already home if at ANY park' short-circuit becomes 'already home only if at MY assigned park' (so a hull sitting on the wrong/over-occupied park relocates to its own). Frigate excluded (#7). Deterministic/restart-idempotent, converges then stops (#2). No flag, armed.

SUPERSEDES the demand-rebalance approach — do NOT build a demand/occupancy rebalancer; build FIXED assignment.
acceptance_criteria: N delivery hulls (N<=central parks) each get a DISTINCT fixed home; an idle hull off its home returns to it; a hull already at its assigned home is not moved; NO two hulls share a park when N<=parks; assignment is byte-identical across restarts (idempotent) and a second homing pass moves NO hull (no thrash). No demand-ranking/occupancy weighting anywhere in the homing path (grep-verify the demand provider is off the homing path). Reproduce the live K83 pile -> after: one-per-park stable spread. RED-first, build/vet/gofmt/-race green. No flag.

title: Bootstrap: premature/unscaled GATE latches via ConstructionStarted — arming scaled_gate_entry late cannot recover it
description: Era-4 prod (harbormaster, 2026-07-19). The arc entered GATE via gateFunded on the OLD bar (scaled_gate_entry OFF => IncomePerHour>=IncomeBar); a contract payout spiked income past income_bar(10k). That entry ran actGate -> planned the construction pipeline -> obs.ConstructionStarted=true. derivePhase (L547) then latches GATE on obs.ConstructionStarted REGARDLESS of gateFunded. scaled_gate_entry was armed AFTERWARD (too late): gateFunded went false (0 haulers < gate_min_haulers) but the ConstructionStarted latch held. Result: arc stuck in GATE with 0 haulers, unscaled, wedged (no_purchaser for gate workers), construction=0%. The code's OWN safety argument (derivePhase comment L537-540 + gateFunded comment L577-579): 'construction can only start after a legitimate scaled entry, so a spurious income spike can never latch GATE permanently (the ktio deadlock).' That assumption BREAKS when scaled_gate_entry is armed LATE (after an unscaled entry already started construction) — or via ANY path reaching actGate/ConstructionStarted without a scaled entry. So construction-START is not itself gated on a scaled contract op; only the FORWARD gateFunded entry is, and only if armed beforehand. Violates PLAYBOOK §4 (gate construction gated until the contract op scales). title: REGRESSION (sk68 D2): past next_wake_at is level-triggered — supervisor fires a wake EVERY TICK until captain re-declares; burned the 8/h cap
description: Live incident 2026-07-07 06:43-06:47 (Admiral-observed: 'heartbeat every few seconds'). After sk68 deploy (c4b90dc), a declared next_wake_at that passes without being re-declared becomes a STANDING wake condition: every 30s tick evaluates now>=next_wake_at -> wake, again and again — 8 wakes in ~4 min until max_sessions_per_hour capped it, then 'session cap reached' spam every tick. Root cause: D2 removed the suppression of overdue alarms but nothing CONSUMES the alarm after it fires. FIX (one-shot semantics): in evaluateWakeGate, the declared next_wake_at triggers only while UNSERVICED — fire iff next_wake_at > last_session (a wake after the alarm services it); once last_session >= next_wake_at, fall back to heartbeat cadence (last_session + HeartbeatMinutes). Test matrix: alarm future -> no wake; alarm past + last_session < alarm -> wake ONCE; after that wake (last_session >= alarm) -> NO further alarm wakes, heartbeat resumes; overdue-heartbeat protection (D2's point) still holds when NO alarm is declared. Also: rate-limit the 'session cap reached' log line (once per cap window, not per tick). MITIGATED live at 06:5x by emergency re-declare (+45m, thresholds restored to 3.4M/500k — captain had briefly had below=800k/no-above; inform captain). title: The relocator blocks on ship arrival inside its reconcile tick, so its effective period is ~21min against a 150s offer window — 36 mid_tour skips to 1 relocation
description:
WHY TRADE HULLS PILE UP IN THE HOME SYSTEM AND MARGINS DIE. Measured on staging 2026-08-07.

THE DESIGN IS CORRECT ON PAPER. Three numbers are chosen to fit together:
  defaultRelocatorTickSeconds          = 120s   ('sized to LAND INSIDE' the window, per its own comment)
  defaultRelocationOfferWindowSeconds  = 150s   ('longer than the relocator's own' tick, per its comment)
  defaultRelocationOfferBackoffMinutes = 30
120 < 150, so every offer window should contain a tick. The tour offers a hull at a productive tour
boundary; the relocator is supposed to see it within 150s; hullProtected() explicitly exempts an
OFFERED hull from the mid_tour rule. All of that is right.

THE INVARIANT IS BROKEN BY A FACTOR OF TEN IN PRACTICE:
  daemon uptime                105 min
  ticks expected at 120s       ~52
  ticks ACTUALLY observed        5      (relocator_ticks_total: 2 BLOCKED, 2 IDLE, 1 PROGRESS)
  effective tick period        ~21 min
The relocator BLOCKS INSIDE ITS TICK waiting for a relocating hull to arrive — logged
wait_arrival_event with budget_seconds up to 389 (6.5 min), and a multi-leg move chains several. While
it waits, it evaluates nobody.

THE TRAP, and it is self-reinforcing:
  P(a tick lands in a given 150s window) ~= 150s / 21min ~= 12%
  so ~88% of offers LAPSE UNCLAIMED
  a lapsed offer sets a 30-MINUTE backoff (12x the window it just missed)
  the tour then refuses to re-offer: 'within_offer_backoff'
  the hull stays OnTour && !Offered -> scored as 'mid_tour' -> skipped
OBSERVED OUTCOME: relocator_skips_total{reason=mid_tour} = 36 against
relocator_decisions_total{outcome=relocated} = 1. Roughly a 3% success rate. Every other skip reason
is in single digits (no_uplift 4, region_herded 4, within_cooldown 3), so this is not a scoring
problem or an economics problem — it is a scheduling problem.

CONSEQUENCE: hulls cannot spread. They accumulate in X1-KP46 where 9 trade hulls contend for lanes
whose volume caps are 6-39 units, margins die ('Continuous tour stopping - margins died, 3 consecutive
tours found no profitable plan'), and five of nine hulls sit empty while the one heavy flies 8% full.

THE FIX IS THE SCHEDULING, NOT THE NUMBERS. Do NOT simply lengthen the offer window or shorten the
backoff — that treats the symptom and leaves a coordinator whose cadence is set by network I/O rather
than by its configured tick. Preferred: the relocator should DISPATCH the navigate and RETURN,
checking arrival on a later tick (the state machine already tracks movingOrSettling, and
'already_relocating' exists precisely to skip a hull whose move is in flight). Then the 120s cadence
is real and the 150s window works as designed.
SECONDARY, once the cadence is honest: the 30-min backoff against a 150s window is a 12x asymmetry
that punishes a hull for the relocator's own tardiness. It should be justified or reduced.

VERIFY WITH: relocator_ticks_total should rise at ~1 per 2 minutes of uptime. That single ratio is the
regression test — it needs no fixture and it is what would have caught this.
notes:
Found by following the Admiral's push-back on 'we won't have more lanes until we buy more hulls'. They were right that something structural blocks the fleet from working more lanes; it is not hull COUNT (the markets are too thin to fill the hulls already owned - the one heavy flies 8% full against 20-39 unit lane depths) but hull PLACEMENT, which this defect prevents from ever adjusting.

The comment on defaultRelocatorTickSeconds ('sized to LAND INSIDE') documents an invariant that nothing enforces. A blocking call added later silently voided it, and no test or metric compares expected ticks to observed ticks.

title: The PROBE wave has no upper bound: lanes_served -> buy probes, and 'lanes served' is exactly what an over-hulled fleet reports
description:
THE FEEDBACK LOOP RUNS THE WRONG WAY, and it emptied the treasury tonight.

  DeriveWave: UnservedLanes <= 0  ->  PROBE          (common/growth_wave.go:109)
  UnservedLanes = profitable - hulls tagged 'trade'  (queries/unserved_lane_reader.go:66)
  PROBE          ->  spend on probes, no ceiling

So the wave buys probes BECAUSE the fleet has more hulls than profitable lanes. The condition that
should read 'we have too much capacity' is wired to 'go buy more capacity'. It is stable in the wrong
direction: buying probes never raises the profitable-lane count on any timescale that closes the
loop, so the condition never clears and the buying never stops.

MEASURED TONIGHT (staging):
  probes 71 -> 106 in one session (35 bought, ~32k each)
  77 of them PARKED and idle throughout
  treasury 5,136,416 -> 277,640 at the low point
  working capital demand 507,240 EXCEEDED the treasury (385,572) — trade about to be refused for
    lack of cargo float, while credits went to a 106th probe
  profitable lanes 5, trade hulls 9, unserved 0 the entire time

WHAT MADE IT UNBOUNDED RATHER THAN MERELY WASTEFUL: capital_multiplier_k_milli, the probe buy floor,
was tuned to 500 against a documented default of 2000 — a quarter of the protection, on the one guard
that reserves trading cargo runway from probe spending. Restored to 2000. The mirror knob on the
heavy side (growth_runway_milli_hours) was checked and is INTACT at its 2000 default, so this was one
weakened guard, not a pair.

STOPPED, NOT FIXED. expansion_enabled=2 (probe spending off) + the restored floor, applied by daemon
restart. That is a holding action on a live drain, not a design fix, and it leaves the fleet with
probe buying manually disabled — someone must decide the real rule.

THE DESIGN QUESTION, stated so it is not re-litigated from scratch:
PROBE is the correct answer to 'do not save for a heavy right now'. It is NOT automatically the
correct answer to 'spend on probes'. Those are two decisions the wave currently fuses. Candidate
separations, none chosen:
  a. Bound probe buying by UTILISATION, not by the lane gap — 77 parked probes is the signal that the
     marginal probe earns nothing. A probe that cannot be given a watch should not be bought.
  b. Give PROBE its own affirmative predicate (unpriced systems reachable, coverage gap) instead of
     inheriting 'not HEAVY' by default.
  c. Keep the wave as-is and let the buy floor be the only bound — which is what was in place, and it
     held only until one knob was tuned to a quarter.
(c) is what the current design bets on, and tonight is the evidence that a single tunable standing
between an unbounded loop and the treasury is too thin a margin.

DO NOT re-enable expansion_enabled without either a bound or a deliberate decision to accept (c).
notes:
THE PURCHASE PRICE WAS NOT THE COST. THE FERRY WAS.

Stopping probe BUYING (expansion_enabled=2) did not stop the bleeding. The 35 already-bought probes
kept ferrying to their stations, and every jump is charged:
  03:28:03 JUMP TORWINDSTG-70 -5,082      03:28:04 JUMP TORWINDSTG-72 -5,083
  03:28:03 JUMP TORWINDSTG-71 -5,082      03:28:05 JUMP TORWINDSTG-6C -5,824
  03:28:04 JUMP TORWINDSTG-73 -5,063      03:28:05 JUMP TORWINDSTG-67 -5,011
Six jumps in three seconds, ~30k. Treasury fell 337k -> 126k in about twenty minutes on this alone,
at roughly 30k/min, against an immutable floor of 50k.

SO THE TRUE UNIT COST OF THE SPREE IS NOT 32k/PROBE. It is 32k plus a multi-jump ferry at ~5k a jump
to wherever the placement plan sends it — plausibly comparable to the hull price, and it is incurred
AFTER the buy decision, where no buy guard is watching.

THE KNOB'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS WRONG ABOUT THIS, and it is what made me think the hold was sufficient:
  expansion_enabled: 'Off does NOT stop the free work — frontier discovery, jump-gate reads,
   screening, re-tasking idle probes you already own, and gate-crossing footholds all keep running,
   so coverage keeps growing on the hulls already paid for.'
'Gate-crossing footholds' are exactly the ~5k jumps above. They are not free, and calling them free
in the text an operator reads while trying to stop spending is a documentation defect with money
attached. FIX THE TEXT: name the jump cost, and say plainly that expansion_enabled=2 stops
ACQUISITION only, not the travel cost of hulls already committed.

RESOLVED BY STOPPING THE COORDINATOR: 'container stop probe_sensing_coordinator-...'. Last JUMP row
03:28:39; none after. Treasury 126,704 -> 265,449 within 90 seconds.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN READING, both from asserting a cause before checking the category:
  1. I attributed that +139k recovery to 'cargo sales landing'. It was NOT. It was
     CONTRACT_FULFILLED +98,646 and CONTRACT_ACCEPTED +47,876 — CONTRACT_REVENUE, not trading.
     TRADING_REVENUE was genuinely frozen at 31,133,176 throughout, exactly as the flat-revenue
     monitor said, because tours were liquidation-only.
  2. Earlier I read 'Construction drain' 38 times in the log as money leaving. It is a coordinator
     PHASE NAME — the lines read 'activation done (0 task(s) promoted to READY)'. Construction spent
     nothing. A log phrase containing 'drain' is not evidence of a drain.

TRADE HAS RESUMED PROPERLY: 03:31:06 PURCHASE_CARGO FIREARMS -48,620 and ASSAULT_RIFLES -26,059 on
TORWINDSTG-44 — a 74,679 fresh buy, the first real restock since the liquidation-only stretch. That is
capital being deployed, not drained.

CURRENT HOLD STATE, both manual and both needing a decision before anything re-enables:
  expansion_enabled = 2                      (probe acquisition off)
  capital_multiplier_k_milli = 2000          (buy floor restored to default)
  probe_sensing_coordinator = STOPPED        (stops ferry jumps AND all sensing/scanning)
The third has a real cost: market scanning is off while it is stopped, so staleness will grow. It is
a tourniquet, not a fix, and sp-lhysz's cold tail will get worse until it is restarted.

title: Market scan rotation has collapsed to a hot few: 6 of 103 markets fresh, median age 2h04m, while the budget spends at its full 0.35 req/s cap
description:
MEASURED (staging, 2026-08-07 06:00Z, daemon up 2h19m):
  parked_sensing_staleness_seconds{tier=hot}     16.9s
  parked_sensing_staleness_seconds{tier=median}  7437s   (2h04m)
  parked_sensing_staleness_seconds{tier=cold}    7584s   (2h06m)
  market_coverage_fresh (300s) / total           6 / 103 markets; 6 of 171 systems have ANY fresh market
  scan_budget_rate_req_per_sec{market}           0.35    (AT THE CAP - the budget is fully spent)
  scan_budget_decisions_total{market,earning,spend}       610
  scan_budget_decisions_total{market,discretionary,spend} 132

THE BUDGET IS NOT STARVED, IT IS MISALLOCATED. 689 markets at 0.35 req/s is a 33-minute full
rotation. The observed median age is 3.8x that. Requests ARE being made at the full cap; they are
going to the same hot set over and over. The tier spread is the tell and it is extreme:
hot 17s vs cold 7584s is a 446x ratio. That is not a rotation with a fast lane, it is a rotation that
has stopped rotating.

NOT A BUDGET-SIZE PROBLEM, AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED' BY RAISING THE CAP. The 0.35 req/s market-scan
budget is never to be raised (sp-k4z5b): a budget bounds COST, it does not bound STALENESS, and the
cap is already fully spent. Raising it would buy more requests for the same hot few.

THE DEMAND SET SHRANK WHILE STALENESS GREW, which rules out the obvious explanation:
  coverage 03:08Z = 1008 markets, median staleness 2413s
  coverage 06:00Z =  689 markets, median staleness 7437s
Fewer markets to serve, and they got 3x staler. The monitor's own hypothesis ('the demand set has
grown past what the allowance can serve') is therefore WRONG, and I am recording that it was checked
and refuted rather than leaving it to be re-guessed.

DEGRADING ACROSS RESTARTS, so it is not a boot artifact: 2413s at 03:08 on a daemon up 3h43m, 7437s
at 06:00 on a daemon up 2h19m. Two different processes, both degraded, the second worse.

NOT CAUSED BY TONIGHT'S LAST DEPLOY. d05fbcbd touched only the metrics collector, the lane reader and
a gate test; none can affect scan scheduling. The suspects are earlier and should be checked in this
order:
  1. sp-b3ny4's demand-window denominator (len(b.demand), pruned). If pruning drops markets from the
     window faster than they are re-added, the surviving set gets served repeatedly.
  2. sp-a2dc5's freshness floor interacting with the priority classes: if the earning class is always
     eligible and the discretionary class is admitted only when the floor allows, earning wins every
     arbitration and the cold set never comes up.
  3. The 4.6:1 earning-to-discretionary spend split. Price the declined path before calling this
     waste - a skew CAN be a priority queue working - but a 446x tier ratio is past any defensible
     priority.

WHY THIS IS P0 AND NOT P1: it invalidates a conclusion already drawn. See sp-sn04e.
notes:
A STOPPED WRITER'S GAUGE LIES IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION — and it nearly went into a report as good news.

With the probe_sensing_coordinator STOPPED for 85 minutes as a treasury tourniquet:
  parked_sensing_staleness_seconds{median}  7437s -> 729s     <- looks like a 10x IMPROVEMENT
  parked_sensing_staleness_seconds{cold}    8362s -> 1506s    <- looks fixed
Both false. That metric's WRITER is the coordinator that was stopped, so it reports on a frozen
subset it no longer refreshes. The independently-written coverage metrics say the opposite:
  market_coverage_total            104 -> 116     (denominator GREW, so this is not a shrink artifact)
  market_coverage_fresh (<=300s)   36  ->   6     (35% fresh -> 5% fresh)
  scan_budget_coverage             689 -> 538
Freshness collapsed sevenfold. The tourniquet's cost is real and is exactly what was predicted.

THE GENERAL RULE, worth more than this instance: when a component is disabled, EVERY metric that
component writes becomes untrustworthy — and it does not read as missing or zero, which would be
obvious. It holds its last value or narrows to a stale subset, and a narrowed subset of
recently-touched entries reads as FRESHER than the truth. Always corroborate with a series written by
a DIFFERENT producer before drawing a conclusion about a disabled subsystem.

Still-running scanners keep some coverage alive (SCOUT_POST_COORDINATOR and SCOUT are up; 456
earning-class spends), which is why the fleet still trades: revenue +226k over the 85 minutes,
treasury 316,471, 257 cargo units held. Trade is coping on the hot set.

CONSEQUENCE FOR sp-sn04e: profitable=5 is now computed against a 5%-fresh cache, so its 'lower bound'
caveat is much stronger than when it was written at 35% fresh. Do not size anything off it.

THE STANDING TRADE-OFF, unresolved and deliberately left to the Admiral: restarting sensing restores
scanning but ALSO resumes the ~5k-per-jump probe ferry (expansion_enabled=2 does not stop travel for
hulls already owned - see sp-0qtyl). Staleness worsens while it is off; treasury burns while it is on.

title: The trade opportunity surface has collapsed to 4 profitable lanes against 9 trade hulls — the fleet is over-hulled, not growth-blocked
description:
MEASURED, not inferred, from the gauges sp-lqd16 added (staging, 2026-08-07, daemon on d05fbcbd):
  growth_lane_surface{profitable}       4
  growth_lane_surface{trade_pool}       9
  growth_lane_surface{unserved}         0
  growth_lane_surface{systems_scanned}  63
  growth_lane_surface{readable}         1

CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY by a different metric with a different threshold:
  trade_opportunities_total across 200 systems -> 186 report ZERO, 14 report any.
  Concentration: X1-KP46 = 26, X1-JM48 = 2, X1-KT35 = 2, and 1 each for AM71/CR35/FB55/PS70/UM87.
Two independently-derived surfaces agree the profit surface is thin and almost entirely in the home
system. (They are NOT the same measurement — trade_opportunities_total uses min_margin=10 while
CountProfitableLanes uses the stricter ClearsFloor/MinBidMargin and dedupes by good+source+dest within
system, which is why 26 in KP46 becomes 4 fleet-wide. The agreement is directional, not numeric.)

THE FRAMING WAS BACKWARDS AND THIS IS THE POINT. The fleet was read as deadlocked — money available
(3.8M working capital), headroom available (1 heavy owned against a cap of 5), and no heavy ever
bought. It is not blocked. It is CORRECTLY REFUSING TO GROW: there are 4 profitable lanes and 9 hulls
already able to fly them. unserved=0 is a true zero. Buying a heavy would add a tenth hull to a
surface that cannot feed the nine, and per the standing finding that trade throughput is
SINK-CONTENDED (market depth below hull capacity), it would amplify absorption breaches rather than
earn.

SO THE BOTTLENECK IS UPSTREAM OF EVERY FLEET-SIZING KNOB. Nothing in the wave, the reserve, the cap or
the autosizer is the constraint. The question is why 63 scanned systems yield 4 floor-clearing lanes,
and the candidates are NOT yet distinguished:
  1. The bid-floor discipline (MinBidMargin) is set where almost nothing clears it — a threshold
     question, and the cheapest to answer: histogram the spreads that were REJECTED and see how far
     under the floor they sit. A floor rejecting 99% is either exactly right or badly miscalibrated,
     and the distribution says which.
  2. The within-system-pairs-only scope. CountProfitableLanes never ranks a cross-system pairing, and
     its own comment says it 'can only UNDER-count'. With 70 probes parked across 63 systems, the
     cross-system surface is exactly the one nobody is measuring.
  3. Genuine market exhaustion in the home system after sustained trading against the same sinks.
  4. Probes are parked rather than charting, so the surface is not being refreshed with NEW grounds —
     70 of 71 probes sit in sensing_parked while the wave keeps saying 'buy more probes'.

Candidate 4 is the one that makes the wave incoherent as a growth engine: PROBE means 'go open lanes',
but the lever it pulls is BUYING probes, and 70 already sit idle. Buying a 72nd opens nothing. Worth
checking whether the PROBE wave has any effect at all in this state — if it does not, the fleet has no
growth path in either regime, which is a real deadlock, just not the one that was suspected.

DO NOT ACT BY RAISING HULL COUNTS OR LOWERING THE BID FLOOR before 1 and 2 are measured. Lowering a
money guard to manufacture lanes is exactly the RULINGS #4 weakening the guard exists to prevent.
notes:
RESOLVED BY DIRECT TEST — and the answer is between my two previous claims. This note supersedes the correction above.

The staleness episode ended on its own, which handed me the controlled comparison I could not have run
deliberately: the SAME lane surface read at three freshness levels, everything else constant.

  reading            median staleness   profitable   trade_pool   unserved
  03:45 (post-boot)  (stale)                     4            9          0
  05:51 (steady)     7437s  (2h04m)              3            9          0
  06:20 (recovered)   304s  (5m)                 5            9          0

STALENESS IS A REAL CONFOUNDER AND IT IS NOT THE EXPLANATION. Fresh data moves profitable from 3 to 5.
It does not move it to 9. unserved=0 holds at EVERY freshness level measured, with a margin of four
hulls even at the freshest reading. So the original finding survives in substance: the fleet has more
trade hulls than the market ranks profitable lanes for, and buying a heavy would still be wrong.

WHAT I GOT WRONG IN EACH DIRECTION, recorded because both errors have the same shape:
  - FIRST: reported 'genuinely exhausted' without checking the age of the data behind the number.
  - THEN: over-corrected to 'does not survive' on the strength of the confounder alone, without
    testing whether removing it changed the verdict. A confounder that is real is not automatically
    an explanation, and I treated it as one.
Both are the same failure: asserting a cause before measuring its effect size.

ALSO WITHDRAWN, and this one was mine twice over: I cited '186 of 200 systems report zero trade
opportunities' as independent corroboration, then corrected it to 'not independent, same stale cache'.
The correction was right. The figure reads the same cache and is not a second witness.

MEASUREMENT ERROR CORRECTED: I earlier summed market_coverage_fresh across ALL age_threshold label
values (300s/600s/3600s) and reported '6 of 103', a ratio that later produced an impossible 122/104.
At the 300s threshold specifically it is now 36 of 104 markets fresh.

STILL BLOCKED ON sp-lhysz, for a narrower reason than before: the COLD tier remains 8362s (2h19m)
even after the median recovered to 304s. A persistently starved tail means part of the surface is
never priced, so profitable=5 is a LOWER BOUND and the true figure is unknown-but-higher. Whether it
is higher than 9 is exactly the open question. Re-measure once the cold tail is served.

title: The wave's deciding input (UnservedLanes) is unobservable — 'lanes_served' cannot be distinguished from a mis-scoped lane count
description:
STAGING IS PARKED IN A PROBE WAVE AND I CANNOT SEE WHY FROM METRICS.

OBSERVED (staging, 2026-08-07, daemon 75581 on 40697f3c):
  fleet_growth_wave{growth}=0  fleet_growth_wave{drain}=0    (PROBE, both readers agree)
  fleet_growth_wave_probe_reason{reason=lanes_served}=1
  growth_heavies_owned=1   growth_heavy_cap=5
  growth_working_capital_credits=5136416   growth_heavy_reserve_credits=0
  growth_current_hulls{class=heavy}=9  growth_demand_hulls{class=heavy}=9
Ground truth from the fleet: 71 SATELLITE, 13 HAULER, 1 COMMAND. Of the 13 haulers exactly ONE
carries a 225 hold (TORWINDSTG-45); the other 12 are 80-hold lights. 70 of the 71 probes sit in
sensing_parked.

THE CHAIN, read end to end:
  DeriveWave -> 'lanes_served' iff UnservedLanes <= 0            (common/growth_wave.go:109)
  UnservedLanes = profitable - (hulls tagged fleet='trade')      (queries/unserved_lane_reader.go:66)
  the subtrahend counts DEDICATION, not frame                    (unserved_lane_reader.go:60-65)
So the '9' in current_hulls{class=heavy} is the TRADE-FLEET MEMBERSHIP COUNT (9 hulls), not a
heavy-frame census. The two numbers disagree by 8 and both are 'right' — heavies_owned=1 counts
frames, the reconciler's 9 counts the pool.

NOT FILING THE ARITHMETIC AS THE BUG. Counting the whole trade pool is defensible and matches the
doc comment ('profitable lanes BEYOND the current trade-hull pool'): a light freighter flies a lane
too, so 9 hulls serve up to 9 lanes. The local variable being named 'heavies' while counting 8
lights is a readability trap, not a money bug.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: I cannot observe the deciding quantity. There is NO metric for UnservedLanes
and none for the profitable-lane count it is built from. 'lanes_served' is emitted, but that single
label collapses three very different worlds:
  (a) genuinely every profitable lane is served      -> correct PROBE, nothing to fix
  (b) profitable is under-counted by the within-system-pairs-only scope
      (profitable_lane_reader.go:43-46 says so explicitly: 'it can only UNDER-count')
  (c) profitable is under-counted because distinctShipSystems only scans systems where a hull
      currently STANDS, and 70 of 71 probes are parked
All three print exactly 'reason=lanes_served'. This is open question #7 from the wave spec
(2026-08-05-heavy-trade-wave-design.md), which the plan DEFERRED rather than answered — the question
was posed as 'a HEAVY wave and a stalled coordinator both look like no probes bought', and this is
that same blindness one layer earlier.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: this is the last precondition for Plan B (delete the autosizer). Plan B waits on
observing a PROBE -> HEAVY transition, and with 5.1M working capital, cap=5, and only 1 heavy owned,
the fleet has both the money and the headroom to buy — but the regime will not authorise it while
UnservedLanes reads 0, and nothing emitted lets me tell a correct 0 from an under-counted one.

THE FIX (small, and it is the enabling one — do this BEFORE any tuning):
  1. Emit UnservedLanes as a gauge, ALWAYS, on the same tick the wave is derived (both readers,
     same reader= label as the existing lockstep pair, so a disagreement stays visible).
  2. Emit the profitable-lane count and the trade-pool subtrahend SEPARATELY. The difference is
     the decision; publishing only the difference is what made this unreadable.
  3. Emit the count of systems distinctShipSystems actually scanned. If (c) is live, that number
     is the tell and nothing else is.
No behaviour change, no money path touched. RULINGS #4 untouched — this is observability only.

CONFIRMED vs SUSPECTED, kept separate on purpose:
  CONFIRMED: the 9 is a fleet-tag count; heavies_owned=1 is the frame count; no metric exists for
             UnservedLanes or profitable; CountProfitableLanes applies NO staleness filter (so the
             rising tour_lanes_stale_excluded_total is a DIFFERENT path and is not the suppressor).
  SUSPECTED: which of (a)/(b)/(c) is live. Deliberately not guessed — step 1 answers it in one tick.
notes:
CODE WRITTEN AND COMMITTED, NOT MERGED. Lane .claude/worktrees/sp-lqd16, commit f14f8855.

DONE: growth_lane_surface{player_id,component} — components unserved / profitable / trade_pool /
systems_scanned / readable. Emitted from the ONE shared UnservedLaneReader (no reader label needed:
neither consumer computes it, so neither can disagree). Emitted on the failure path too with
readable=0. Also renamed the reader's local 'heavies' to 'pool' — it counts hulls tagged 'trade'
regardless of frame, which is correct but reads as a heavy-frame census.
build + vet + gofmt clean; 4 new tests green; existing tests in both packages green.

BLOCKED ON THE COMMENT-DENSITY GATE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH READING.
  main  (no change): internal/adapters/metrics 26.1% (1610/6167)
  lane  (with mine): internal/adapters/metrics 26.0% (1614/6197)
  baseline:                                    25.71% (1413/5495)
MY CHANGE LOWERS THE DENSITY AND STILL FAILS. The package drifted ~0.4pts over baseline on main
before I touched it, and the gate compares against the FROZEN BASELINE, not against main — so any
lane touching a drifted package inherits the whole cleanup, even a lane that improves the ratio.

Landing this needs ONE of:
  (a) sweep internal/adapters/metrics under 25.71% (~21 comment lines) — that IS the parked sweep
      work, and three prior lanes wrote FALSE claims doing exactly this, so it is not a safe
      unilateral move;
  (b) teach the gate a second, weaker test: fail if the lane makes a package WORSE THAN MAIN, and
      report baseline drift separately instead of blocking on it.
(b) is the better design and does not weaken the ratchet — main can still only move one way, because
a lane that worsens main is refused. Filed as the open question, NOT decided unilaterally: the
Admiral asked for the strict ratchet and I am not loosening it without their word.

NOT A REASON TO RE-RECORD THE BASELINE. That remains the one move ENGINEERING §6a forbids.
close_reason:
DELIVERED AND IT ANSWERED THE QUESTION IN ONE TICK. Merged d05fbcbd, deployed to staging.

FIRST READING:
  profitable       4
  trade_pool       9
  unserved         0     (4-9 floored)
  systems_scanned  63
  readable         1

THE WAVE WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG. Of the three candidates the bead deliberately refused to guess between:
  (c) narrow system sweep    — RULED OUT. 63 systems scanned, not the parked-probe artifact I suspected.
  (b) under-scoped ranking   — not the binding constraint; a wider scope cannot manufacture lanes that
                               do not clear the bid floor.
  (a) genuinely served       — CONFIRMED. unserved=0 is a true zero, readable=1.
There was no deadlock in the regime. PROBE is the correct answer to the fleet's actual situation, and
had I 'fixed' the arithmetic as the bead warned against, the fleet would have bought heavies into an
opportunity surface that cannot feed the hulls it already has.

WHAT THE NUMBER ACTUALLY EXPOSES, which is worse than the bug I went looking for: FOUR profitable
lanes against NINE trade hulls. Corroborated independently — of 200 systems reporting
trade_opportunities_total, 186 report ZERO and 14 report any, concentrated almost entirely in the home
system X1-KP46 (26; every other system 1-2). The fleet is over-hulled by better than 2x relative to
the work available to it. Filed separately.

CAVEAT ON THE READING: taken ~2 minutes after a daemon restart. The market cache is persisted so it
survives the restart, but this is one sample and the follow-up bead should confirm steady state before
anything is sized off it.

SECOND FIX RIDING ALONG (sp-4bgic): the density gate landed an hour earlier was anchored to the frozen
baseline and refused THIS change, which lowered internal/adapters/metrics from 26.1% to 26.0%, against
a 25.71% baseline. Re-anchored to main's actual density. Probed, not assumed: 40 injected lines of
comment slop still FAIL (26.11% -> 26.51%). One-way ratchet intact; baseline re-recording still
forbidden.

title: Shipyard scan budget has the same zero-collapse denominator bug the market budget just lost
description:
LATENT, same defect class as sp-b3ny4, different budget.

YardScanBudget.refreshChartedCount (internal/application/ship/shipyard_scan_budget_refresh.go)
guards 'if err != nil || total < 0 { return }' — it rejects a NEGATIVE count but ACCEPTS a
zero one, then writes it: 'if total != b.charted { b.charted = total }'. Its own comment
promises the opposite: 'a counter hiccup must widen nothing and must not reset the
denominator to zero, which would collapse every interval.'

REACHABLE, by the same route proved on sp-b3ny4. GormWaypointRepository.ChartedShipyardCount
(waypoint_repository.go:266) scopes with eraScopePredicate(r.openEraID(ctx)). openEraID
swallows its error and returns nil, and eraScopePredicate(nil) emits 'era_id IS NULL' — which
matches 0 of 78,066 waypoint rows on staging, since every row carries era_id=1. So a transient
failure reading the eras table produces a count of 0 with a NIL error, and the denominator
collapses to len(seen). That is exactly the mechanism that produced sp-a2dc5's 23m14s rotation
bound on the market side.

Live gauge now: scan_budget_coverage{budget="shipyard"} 1775.

TWO SHAPES OF FIX, both cheap:
 1. Treat a zero count as a hiccup, not a denominator (total <= 0 returns, like total < 0 does).
 2. Better, and what sp-b3ny4 did on the market side: stop collapsing two different facts into
    one nil in openEraID. persistence already has OpenEraScope, the FAIL-CLOSED face of the same
    helper, written for precisely this ('openEraID collapses two very different facts into one
    nil — the eras table could not be read, and every era is closed'). A reader whose answer
    paces API budget is the case that comment names.

Consider whether the yard budget should also move to a demand-set denominator as the market
budget now has (sp-b3ny4) — a charted yard no hull is standing on cannot be read either. That
is a larger call and should be priced separately; item 1 is the safety fix.

Found while fixing sp-b3ny4; not in that bead's territory, so filed rather than folded in.
close_reason:
Merged. Two narrow fixes, exactly as the bead scoped them, and the larger call deliberately NOT taken.

(1) THE GUARD NOW MATCHES ITS OWN COMMENT. refreshChartedCount guarded 'if err != nil || total < 0' — rejecting a NEGATIVE count but ACCEPTING a zero one, then writing it, while its comment promised 'a counter hiccup must widen nothing and must not reset the denominator to zero, which would collapse every interval.' Now 'total <= 0'.

(2) THE ZERO WAS REACHABLE, and the route is now closed at the source. ChartedShipyardCount scoped with eraScopePredicate(r.openEraID(ctx)); openEraID SWALLOWS ITS ERROR and returns nil, and eraScopePredicate(nil) emits 'era_id IS NULL', which matches 0 of 78,066 waypoint rows because every row carries era_id=1. So a transient failure reading the eras table yielded a count of zero with a NIL error and the denominator collapsed to len(seen). Now scoped through OpenEraScope — the FAIL-CLOSED face of the same helper, which exists for precisely this and whose own comment says openEraID 'collapses two very different facts into one nil: the eras table could not be read, and every era is closed'. A reader whose answer paces an API budget is the case that comment names.

SAME MECHANISM AS sp-a2dc5's 23m14s rotation bound on the market side — this was the latent copy, found by the sp-b3ny4 lane from inside code it was not allowed to touch, and filed rather than folded in.

DELIBERATELY NOT PORTED, and this is the part worth recording: the demand-set denominator sp-b3ny4 moved the MARKET budget to was NOT applied here. The bead prices it as a larger call, and the evidence did not support the other two market fixes either — the shipyard discretionary class is not starved (about 24% admission, against the market class's 0.0%), so there was no starvation floor to add. Three ports where one applies would have been worse than one correct fix.

LATENT, not live: this had not fired on the shipyard side, so there is no before/after to measure. The proof is a RED test driving the nil-era route, not a staging signal.

title: The market-freshness rotation bound has no ceiling and its denominator is a charting census, not the sensing rotation
description:
Split out of sp-a2dc5, which fixed the bound's UPTIME dependency (it was derived from
max(charted census, markets-this-process-has-been-asked-about); the tally term is gone and
an uncounted map now reads UNKNOWN so consumers fall back to their operator floor). Two
things sp-a2dc5 found and could not reach from its territory.

(1) THE DENOMINATOR IS THE WRONG POPULATION. ScanBudget's census is
ChartedMarketSystemCounts -- every waypoint in `waypoints` bearing the MARKETPLACE trait in
the open era. That is a CHARTING census, and it is not the set of markets the fleet is
trying to keep fresh. Measured, staging TORWINDSTG 2026-08-06:

  charted MARKETPLACE waypoints (the census)      13,903
  sensing_slots slot_kind=MARKET (what we cover)   9,753
  distinct waypoints with cached market_data          86

The census leads the sensing population by ~40% and leads the set that actually has data by
160x. Early in an era it also LAGS: charting had barely started that morning, so the census
was small enough that the since-boot tally beat it, which is the bug sp-a2dc5 fixed. Either
way the number feeding the bound is not the rotation.

(2) THE DERIVED BOUND HAS NO CEILING. FreshnessCap returns max(floor, MaxStaleness), and
MaxStaleness = marketsKnown * ValueClampR / RateReqPerSec grows linearly with the map with
nothing above it but the 30-day arithmetic ceiling. At the census above, the daemon's own
printed 0.350 req/s and clamp 8:

  13,903 * 8 / 0.35 = 317,783 s = 88h16m

So the firm-sink FRESH clause -- a fail-closed money guard -- currently admits market_data
up to nearly four days old, against a measured parked-market staleness of avg 418 min /
max 599 min. sp-k4z5b traded a cap that was too tight for one that is nearly inert, and the
inertness arrives silently as the map grows. PLAYBOOK 2: stale prices turn arbitrage into
losses. Note the Admiral's own incident mitigation was 720 minutes, i.e. ~7x tighter than
what the derivation now produces.

THESE PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND MUST BE PRICED TOGETHER. Fixing (1) toward the
sensing population lowers the bound (9,753 vs 13,903); adding a ceiling for (2) lowers it
further. Do not do (2) alone without re-measuring, or this walks straight back into
sp-k4z5b: a ceiling set below the real rotation is exactly the too-tight cap that cost 87%
of trade throughput.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not settled: the bound should be sized on the population the fleet has
committed to covering (sensing MARKET slots) rather than on everything charted, and the
ceiling should be justified against a measured refresh interval rather than picked. The
repository already measures the real thing -- MarketRepositoryGORM.SystemsFreshness returns
MeasuredCycleSeconds (median gap between consecutive market scans per system) and
OldestAgeSeconds -- so a derived bound can be CALIBRATED against measurement instead of
asserted. Careful: a cap derived from OBSERVED STALENESS is circular and would disarm the
guard outright; a cap derived from an observed scan INTERVAL is not.

RELATED, seen while measuring and worth its own look: discretionary market reads are being
declined at 11,949 serve-from-store vs 19 spend over one 7h09m daemon lifetime (99.84%),
while 11,085 of 11,129 admitted reads were `earning` class (metered but never denied
pre-buy verification). The rotation is not running; almost the whole allowance is going to
money-guard re-reads of a handful of markets. That is consistent with (1) -- an inflated
denominator makes every market's due-interval enormous, so nothing is ever due -- and it
may be the same defect seen from the scanner's side rather than the consumer's.

DO NOT raise the 0.35 req/s budget (sp-k4z5b settled it: a budget bounds COST, not
STALENESS) and do not raise inflight_cap.
close_reason:
FOLDED INTO sp-b3ny4, both items, landed together as sp-rsk2m itself required.

(2) THE CEILING: commit 9bd3e774. FreshnessCap is now max(floor, min(bound, derivedCapCeiling)),
ceiling 12h. It bounds the DERIVED term only — an operator floor above it still wins (RULINGS #4,
and a pre-existing test TestFreshnessCap_FloorIsAFloorNeverACeiling defends it) — and it is NOT
applied to MaxStaleness, since capping the anti-starvation escape would turn a freshness decision
into a spending decision. RED reproduced your exact live number: expected 12h0m0s, actual
88h16m22.857142857s.

(1) THE POPULATION: commit c3402da5, filed independently as sp-b3ny4 CAUSE 1. Fixed with a TIGHTER
denominator than the suggested shape — the ACTIVE DEMAND SET (markets asked about within a one-hour
window, that window taken from parkedsensing's own intervalCap), not sensing_slots. Measured on
staging just now: sensing_slots slot_kind=MARKET is 10,978, which would still derive ~70h, so
sizing on it would not have fixed the guard. The demand set is what a caller actually asks about,
which is the only way a scan can happen: 4 distinct waypoints scanned in the last hour, 18 in six,
86 holding cached data at all.

YOUR 'DO NOT DO (2) ALONE' CONSTRAINT WAS HONOURED. Ceiling headroom is checked against measurement,
not asserted: 12h is only reached by a rotation past ~1,890 markets, i.e. 22x-470x above the measured
population. KNOWN AND DELIBERATE: at the incident's own 0.70 req/s the census-era bound was 13h56m,
so this ceiling would have clamped it — that bound was computed over the wrong population and is not
reachable under the demand-set denominator. 24h is a one-constant change if the Admiral prefers the
ceiling never to clamp a historically realized bound.

YOUR 'RELATED' PARAGRAPH (99.84% discretionary declines) is sp-b3ny4 CAUSE 2, also fixed: a floor of
one admitted read in ValueClampR, placed at the value bar only — it cannot reach the token cap or the
dueness rule. Your reading of it was right: an inflated denominator made every due-interval enormous,
so nothing was ever due.

title: [P1] CLI shipyard-purchase path has no 25%-treasury ceiling — bought a 1.88M heavy at 71% of treasury (RULINGS #6)
description:

  PURCHASE_SHIP  fleet expansion  -1,877,506  balance_after 754,745
  'Purchased SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER ship at X1-RX81-FX5D'
