title: comment-audit-check with a SPACE-separated ONLY silently passes — the pre-gate quality ratchet has been a false green
description:
THE VERIFICATION COMMAND CANNOT FAIL. cmd/comment-audit/main.go:70 parses the flag as strings.Split(*only, ",") — COMMA-separated. Every lane that ran 'make comment-audit-check ONLY="pkg1 pkg2 pkg3"' (space-separated, which is how it reads naturally and how at least one plan documents it) had make expand it as '-only pkg1 pkg2 pkg3', so the flag consumed ONLY pkg1 and the remaining packages became ignored positional arguments.

MEASURED ON MAIN, RCs captured WITHOUT a pipe (a pipeline's status is the last stage's — reading this through '| tail' is itself a false green, and I did exactly that on the first attempt):
  ONLY="a b c"  -> prints 'comment-audit: OK', RC=0
  ONLY="a,b,c"  -> RC=2, TWO regressions reported

REGRESSIONS CURRENTLY RED ON MAIN, hidden by the above:
  internal/adapters/parkedsensing            45.01% > 44.57%  baseline 44.6% (1653/3709) -> now 1860/4132
  internal/application/fleet/commands        37.94% > 36.65%  baseline 36.7% (924/2521)  -> now 936/2467

WHY THIS IS P1 DESPITE BEING A COMMENT RULE: ENGINEERING §6a defines this as a RATCHET — 'no lane may leave a package denser than it found it' — and explicitly names re-recording the baseline as 'the one move that defeats the whole rule'. A silently-passing check defeats it just as completely and far more quietly, because every lane reports the gate as green in good faith. The ratchet has not been ratcheting.

FIX HAS TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND MATTERS MORE:
 1. Make the mis-typed form IMPOSSIBLE or LOUD, not merely documented. Options: accept both separators; or reject an ONLY value containing whitespace with a non-zero exit and a message naming the correct form. Do NOT just fix the docs — the next person writes it the natural way again. A flag whose wrong form silently narrows scope to one item is the defect.
 2. Decide the two live regressions. They are PRE-EXISTING on main, not introduced by the lane that found them, and §6a forbids clearing them by re-recording the baseline. Whoever takes this must NOT re-baseline. Either sweep the two packages down under their baselines, or record an explicit, reasoned exception — but the audit must end able to fail.

ALSO CHECK: whether any OTHER Makefile target or documented command passes a space-separated list to a comma-parsing flag. The same shape may exist elsewhere.

FOUND BY: adversarial review of wave Plan A task 2 (epic sp-sy3dl), which reproduced the plan's literal command, got 'OK'/exit 0, then re-ran it comma-separated and found four packages red at that time.
notes:
SHARP EDGE FOUND BY THE FIRST LANE THAT HIT IT (sp-lqd16), one hour after landing.

The gate compares a changed package against the FROZEN BASELINE. It therefore fails a lane that
IMPROVES density, if the package had already drifted over baseline on main:
  main 26.1% -> lane 26.0% -> STILL FAILS, because baseline is 25.71%.
The lane inherits every comment line other merges added since the baseline was recorded.

That is defensible as a forcing function and may be exactly what was wanted — but it was not a
considered choice, it is a consequence, and its cost is that routine work in any of the 25 drifted
packages is now gated behind the parked sweep. Worth an explicit ruling.

SUGGESTED, NOT APPLIED: keep the baseline check but make it REPORT, and BLOCK on 'worse than main'
instead. main still only moves one way (a lane that worsens it is refused), the ratchet survives, and
a lane that improves a drifted package can land. Re-recording the baseline remains forbidden either
way.

title: Heavy-yard pricing errand draws only from busy trade hulls, so it never dispatches — switch the carrier to a parked probe
description:
OBSERVED LIVE (staging, 2026-08-06 14:24Z, EXPANSION phase, gate complete, 22+ probes, 261 systems discovered).

The stated objective of EXPANSION is to price a heavy yard and start buying heavies. It is not happening, and the system reports healthy while it does not.

EVIDENCE, one autosizer tick:
  WARN  Autosizer trade pool: preferred hull SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER cannot be priced at any
        reachable yard - substituting SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER @ 375752 at X1-KP46-A2 for this decision
  INFO  Autosizer heavy buy-decision (BLOCKED by demand): demand[BLOCK: shortfall=8 persisting
        2/3 ticks (anti-thrash)] per_tick_cap[ok] price[ok] heavy_cap[ok]
  INFO  Autosizer tick: 2 classes evaluated, 1 with shortfall, 0 purchased

STATE: 13 heavy-freighter yards discovered across 11 systems, ALL at purchase_price 0 (found by
the free presence-less catalogue sweep, none ever priced because pricing requires a docked hull).

THREE INDEPENDENT FACTS THAT TOGETHER PRODUCE THE STALL:

1. THE FALLBACK MASKS IT. resolveHullPrice cannot price a heavy, substitutes SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER,
   and the tick proceeds. The fleet reports a healthy trade-capacity decision while the actual
   EXPANSION objective never advances. It is a WARN that reads like a workaround succeeding, and
   it will keep buying lights indefinitely.

2. THE PRICING ERRAND NEVER FIRES. No heavy-pricing-errand line appears in the autosizer log at
   all. The mechanism that exists precisely to resolve 'we know the yard, we do not know the ask'
   is not running, while 13 known yards sit unpriced.

3. THE PRECONDITIONS I EXPECTED TO BLAME ARE ALL SATISFIED — so none of them is the cause:
   - Reach: a BFS from every system holding one of our hulls (bounded 5, excluding gates under
     construction) reaches X1-RX81 at EXACTLY 5 hops. heavyYardReachable is hops <= MaxJumpPath=5,
     so it IS inside the bound. (The other 10 yard systems are beyond 5 and unreachable.)
   - Hulls: the errand allowlists dedicated_fleet='trade'. Staging now has FIVE trade hulls
     (4 IN_TRANSIT, 1 DOCKED), not the 1 it had earlier.
   - Guards: heavy_cap[ok], price[ok], per_tick_cap[ok]. The only block shown is an anti-thrash
     demand streak (2/3 ticks) that clears on the next tick.

SO THE OBJECTIVE FALLS THROUGH THE GAP BETWEEN CORRECTLY-BEHAVING COMPONENTS. The catalogue sweep
finds yards (free, no hull). HeavyReserve correctly holds nothing (no price to save toward). The
autosizer wants capacity and is satisfied by a substitute. Nothing ever decides to send a hull to
price a heavy.

INVESTIGATE FIRST, before changing anything: why does the errand not dispatch? Candidates -
it may be gated behind a demand signal that the substitute satisfies; the errand may require a
condition the tick never reaches; SetHeavyPricingErrandPort may be unwired in the daemon
(check cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go); or the errand may run and silently find no candidate.
Determine which by evidence. Do NOT assume the reach bound or the hull supply is the cause -
both were checked and both are fine.

RELATED: the wave redesign (sp-sy3dl) makes 'price a heavy' an explicit phase objective rather
than an emergent side effect, which is the structural fix. This bead is the LIVE defect in the
current design and should not wait for that epic.
acceptance_criteria: A heavy yard gets priced in staging, or the reason it cannot is identified with evidence and recorded. The light-hauler substitution no longer silently masks an unmet EXPANSION objective - it must be distinguishable in logs/metrics from a healthy trade decision. If the errand is unwired or unreachable, that is the finding.
notes:
LEAD DECISIONS (2026-08-06), answering the lane's two concerns:

1. PROBE-ONLY IS CORRECT — do NOT add a trade-hull fallback. Taking a working trade hull IS the failure mode this bead exists to fix; a fallback would reintroduce it under load, which is exactly when it hurts. Staging holds 33 probes, so 'no spare probe' is rare, and the cost of waiting one tick is nothing against the cost of pulling an earning hull off its lane. The decline reason no_eligible_carrier now makes the wait visible, which is what was missing before.

2. SHIPPING WITH sp-mb6ij OPEN, deliberately. The errand vacates a parked-sensing slot without releasing it — a pre-existing gap this fix makes REACHABLE for the first time. Accepted because it is bounded on both axes: errandsInFlight=1 caps it at one hull, and the errand ends the moment the ask lands. Worst case is one waypoint's coverage degraded transiently with its replacement buy suppressed. Against that: without this fix, no heavy is ever priced and EXPANSION cannot reach heavy trade at all. Ship, then close sp-mb6ij.

MERGE ORDER: gate sp-mn3it (off-gate retirement, 113 files) FIRST, then rebase this branch onto it. The two branches overlap on gobot/internal/adapters/grpc/fleet_autosizer_ports.go and fleet_autosizer_heavy_wiring_test.go — cascade Task 6 changed NewFleetAutosizerCoordinatorHandler's arity (11 positional args -> 10) in both. Rebasing 6 files onto the cascade is tractable; the reverse is not.

VERIFIED BY LEAD: build RC=0/0 bytes, vet RC=0/0 bytes on this branch independently.

title: Gate construction buys inherit a FACTORY-SATURATION floor they have no use for — 52 declines over 2h33m with 80 units left
description:
Successor to sp-jt14b (closed, premise falsified). Found by the sp-9eor3 lane, which also
owns the cause.

## The defect

minViableTrancheUnits = 25 is justified ENTIRELY by factory activity saturation:
"<25u moves activity nothing, so a balanced tranche is never sized below this (a dribble is
wasted hull-hours)" -- feeding_policy.go:37-40, analyst-verified.

That reasoning is sound FOR FEEDING A FACTORY. But BuyAtTerminalFactory -- the gate
DELIVERY buy, purchasing the terminal factory's OUTPUT for construction site X1-KP46-I55 --
routes through the same shared fillFromSource and inherits the floor.

A CONSTRUCTION SITE HAS NO ACTIVITY TO MOVE. IT HAS A BILL. 17 units toward a 1600-unit
gate is 17 units of permanent, irreversible progress. The saturation rationale does not
apply to that sink at all.

## Cost, measured

52 declines over 2h33m (09:51:39 -> 12:24:12), affordable=17 units each time, while the
gate had only 80 units remaining. Self-resolved at 12:25 when capital finally cleared
25 x ask.

The lead watched this live and misread it as a capital sawtooth requiring treasury ~480k.
It was not: 17 units were affordable throughout and were refused by a floor that should
never have applied.

## Provenance -- incomplete fix, NOT a regression

The sp-9eor3 lane introduced the coupling in sp-xcjuy (458d7970) by using the feed constant
as the shrink floor in the shared loop. BEFORE that commit these same cases did
logSpendFloorStop; break -- 0 units, leg aborted entirely. So the floor BLOCKS NOTHING THAT
PREVIOUSLY WORKED; it bounds how far that rescue reaches. The defect is that the shared
loop has two sinks with different physics and one constant.

## Acceptance
1. Derive the construction-buy floor from trip economics and the REMAINING REQUIREMENT, not
   from factory saturation. A gate needing 80 more units must be able to buy 17.
2. The FACTORY-feeding floor stays at 25 unless separately re-justified -- see the
   explicit non-claim below.
3. RULINGS #4: this LOWERS a floor. It must not raise any ceiling, and must not let a buy
   exceed what the reserve permits. sp-xcjuy's partial-fill must keep working.
4. Regression: a trivially small remaining requirement must not produce a spam of one-unit
   trips. State the trip-economics bound you chose and why.
5. Fix the truncating log line that caused sp-jt14b's false premise -- put the binding
   constraint (min_units and affordable) EARLY in the message, not after 140 chars.

## EXPLICIT NON-CLAIM -- do not let this leak into sp-e9wua
The factory-side 25-unit floor's justification deserves re-examination given sp-k9xuo, but
sp-k9xuo DOES NOT FALSIFY IT. sp-k9xuo measured input STOCK vs output RECOVERY RATE; it did
not measure delivery SIZE vs activity TRANSITIONS. Different claim, untested. The
sp-9eor3 lane flagged this itself and declined to claim it.

RELATED: sp-jt14b (closed), sp-xcjuy (introduced the coupling), sp-k9xuo, sp-e9wua.
notes:
LANE: built. Commit f72314d7 on main 348cfdeb. gofmt clean, go vet rc=0, go test 88 ok / 0 FAIL.

DESIGN. TrancheSink is an explicit PARAMETER on BuyAtTerminalFactory and on the GateBuyer
interface, not a context marker. The one declared sink identity that exists (WithDeliveryTarget /
IsConstructionSite) is stamped in exactly ONE place — supply.go:229 on ProduceGood — and neither
gate buy site runs under it, so it reads the zero value on both and does not discriminate. An
ambient marker would also reproduce the defect exactly: it is inherited by whoever forgets to stamp
it. Zero value is SinkFactoryFeed, so a caller that forgets keeps today's STRICTER floor.

THE BOUND (criterion 4). floor = capacity/8, CAPPED at minViableTrancheUnits. The denominator is
derived — the hull round trip is the unit of work a floor here rations, and it scales with the
fleet instead of pinning a constant a bigger hauler invalidates. THE FRACTION 1/8 IS CHOSEN, not
derived, and its whole justification is the trip-count consequence: a bill clears in at worst 8x
the legs a full hull would take. Fuel cannot set this bound (at a 2,519 ask one unit already dwarfs
a leg's fuel) and gate materials are consumed rather than resold, so there is no margin to price a
leg against. The binding cost is hull-time.

THE CAP IS LOAD-BEARING, AND MY OWN TEST CAUGHT ITS ABSENCE. An uncapped eighth at a 400-unit
hauler is 50, which would put the CONSTRUCTION floor ABOVE the 25-unit factory floor it exists to
relax — RAISING a floor and refusing buys that work today, on exactly the fleets best able to make
them. TestMinTrancheUnitsFor_OnlyEverLowersAndOnlyForConstruction failed on the first run at
capacity 400. Caught in test, not in production, and only because the grid went past the live hull.

CRITERION 2's REMAINING-BILL CLAMP: DELIBERATELY OMITTED AS PROVABLY INERT. The floor is consulted
ONLY after a breach, and a breach means trancheQty*ask > headroom, so affordableTrancheUnits
returns strictly below trancheQty, which is itself <= tripTarget. Wherever the clamp could bind
(tripTarget <= floor), the clamped floor IS tripTarget and affordable is already under it — the buy
declines either way. It can lower the floor; it can never admit a buy the unclamped floor refuses.
Shipping it would add a branch that reads protective, tests green, and changes no outcome — the
exact defect family this bead sits in. Pinned by
TestMinTrancheUnitsFor_AClampToTheRemainingBillCouldNotChangeAnyOutcome, which asserts the grid
actually contains binding points so it cannot pass vacuously. A small bill is unaffected: an
affordable 3-unit remainder is bought outright without ever reaching the floor.

CRITERION 5: the decline now leads with the two deciding numbers (affordable, minimum) and names
the SINK'S floor rather than the 25 constant. Pinned by a test that measures the offset WITHIN the
line — the first version measured across the whole captured log and failed at char 216 for the
wrong reason.

PROBES (all target tests are NEW IN THIS CHANGE — none is a pre-existing invariant):
  MUT1 sink distinction removed  -> kills ...AConstructionSinkBuysWhatAFactorySinkWouldRefuse
                                    and ...TheDeclineNamesTheSinksOwnFloorNotTheFactoryConstant
  MUT2 RULINGS #4 cap removed    -> kills ...OnlyEverLowersAndOnlyForConstruction
  MUT3 delivery declares factory -> kills ...BuysAsAConstructionSinkNotAFactoryFeed
  MUT4 verdict pushed past 140   -> kills ...NamesTheDeclineWhenEvenTheMinimumTrancheCannotFit
MUT4's FIRST RUN WAS AN INFRASTRUCTURE FAILURE, NOT A KILL: the replacement string contained the
original phrase, so the witness survived its own mutation and the probe proved nothing. Re-run with
a witness that cannot survive.

SHIPPED AND DEPLOYED 2026-08-06 11:01:18 (main a136f4f2). Clean boot, 0 panics, replay
regression check passed (still restoring 434).

DEPLOYED, NOT OBSERVED. The fix cannot be exercised until a construction runs -- the gate
completed at 12:30 UTC and nothing is building. At our 80-unit haulers the construction
floor drops 25 -> 10 (capacity/8), so the 17 affordable units refused 52 times over 2h33m
would now buy.

SIGNAL TO WATCH on the next construction: the decline line should either not appear, or
appear with a minimum well below 25. If it still reads a 25-unit minimum on a construction
buy, the sink parameter is not reaching that call site.

TWO THINGS THE LANE GOT RIGHT AND WORTH PRESERVING:
1. Its own test caught a RULINGS #4 violation in its own fix -- capacity/8 uncapped gives
   50 at a 400-unit hauler, ABOVE the 25 it exists to relax. Would have RAISED a floor on
   the fleets best able to buy. The cap is the guarantee and is commented as such.
2. It DECLINED the remaining-bill clamp this bead's criterion 2 asked for, with proof of
   inertness: the floor is consulted only after a breach, and a breach forces
   affordable < trancheQty <= tripTarget, so wherever the clamp could bind, affordable is
   already beneath it. Shipping it would have added a branch that reads protective, tests
   green, and changes no outcome -- the exact defect family this bead is about.

BOUND HONESTY: capacity/8 capped at 25. The DENOMINATOR is derived (hull round trip is the
unit of work being rationed, scales with fleet). THE FRACTION 1/8 IS CHOSEN, justified only
by its consequence: a bill clears in at worst 8x the legs a full hull would take. Fuel
cannot set it (one unit at a 2,519 ask dwarfs a leg's fuel) and gate materials are consumed
not resold, so there is no margin to price a leg against. That is the number to move if a
different inflation tolerance is wanted.

The factory floor stays 25, untouched, with a pointer at the feed call site to sp-k9xuo's
explicit non-claim so nobody re-tunes it off that measurement.
close_reason: Closed

title: sp-zq2yb pacing accrual is keyed per-DESTINATION, so one source feeding n factories under-fires n-fold — live in the deployed binary
description:
SELF-REPORTED by the lane that shipped it, while establishing that sp-hxqao's boot
reconstruction was impossible. DEPLOYED AND RUNNING NOW (main f6cad5d2, staging daemon up
2026-08-06 10:00:17 local).

## The defect

sp-zq2yb accrues gate-feed compression debt under LaneKey{Source, Dest, Good}. The subject
of that compression is the SOURCE's ask alone -- Dest was never part of it. The key shape
was carried over from the arbitrage lane ranker, where a destination genuinely is part of
the subject.

Consequence: when one source feeds n factories the same input, its drain splits into n
separate debt entries. Each sits under the one-tranche bound while the source is drained
n times as fast, so the guard silently UNDER-FIRES.

## One source -> many importers is the NORM, not an edge case (lead-verified from market_data)

  EQUIPMENT        1 exporter -> 5 importers
  POLYNUCLEOTIDES  1 exporter -> 5 importers
  IRON             1 exporter -> 4 importers
  ALUMINUM         1 exporter -> 3 importers
  CLOTHING         1 exporter -> 3 importers
  ELECTRONICS      1 exporter -> 3 importers

So the under-fire factor is up to 5x on the worst goods and 4x on IRON -- the good that is
33.4% of construction spend and the entire subject of sp-zq2yb.

## Currently UNREACHABLE, and that is the danger

The live gate plan has exactly one IRON target (F45), so n=1 and the guard behaves
correctly today. It becomes reachable on any era change or added chain step, and it would
degrade SILENTLY -- under-firing looks identical to a market that simply is not compressed.
There is no signal that would distinguish them.

## Fix (same edit as sp-hxqao's re-key)

Accrue pacing on a SOURCE-AGGREGATE key with Dest empty, and KEEP the existing full-lane
accrual alongside it:
  Accrue({Source, Dest, Good})   unchanged -- the trade engine keeps seeing gate accruals
                                 on the exact lane, so the shared-ledger property survives
  Accrue({Source, "", Good})     what pacing reads -- aggregates drain across all targets

Dest:"" is a safe namespace: every real lane has a non-empty Dest.

DO NOT fix by dropping Dest from the SHARED key. That would also fix the under-count but
would merge the trade engine's per-lane compression into per-source buckets and silently
re-rank its lanes -- a behaviour change to a well-earning engine as a side effect.

## Acceptance
1. n>1 fixture: one source feeding several targets must accrue against the source once,
   not n times. Fixture must saturate past the bound or it proves nothing.
2. Trade engine ranking must be byte-identical. Assert it, do not argue it.
3. RULINGS #4: the change makes the guard fire MORE readily, never less -- confirm no path
   is loosened.
4. Mutation probe naming its kills, provenance stated.

RELATED: sp-zq2yb (shipped this), sp-hxqao (same re-key unblocks boot reconstruction).
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate feed's core model 'feed the input, get the output' is FALSIFIED on two independent chains — factories are rate-limited, not stock-limited
description:
The gate feed's implicit strategy is: to get more of an output, deliver more of its input.
That model has now failed on two independent production chains, live, hours apart, and
nothing in the engine checks whether feeding an input actually helps.

## Evidence — CURRENT LIVE STATE, both chains, lead-verified

  F45   QUARTZ_SAND IMPORT  ABUNDANT  ->  FAB_MATS EXPORT  SCARCE   (RESTRICTED)
  H51   IRON_ORE    IMPORT  HIGH      ->  IRON     EXPORT  SCARCE   (STRONG)

Input saturated at or near the top of the ladder; output pinned at the bottom. Both.

## The IRON_ORE experiment was already run in production without anyone noticing

08-06 01:00-02:00, the engine sold 824 units of IRON_ORE into H51, driving H51's IRON_ORE
import supply SCARCE -> LIMITED -> MODERATE -> HIGH -> ABUNDANT.

H51's IRON OUTPUT stayed SCARCE for the next 8+ hours (02,03,04,06,08,09,10).

The IRON ask did not respond:
  01:00  input SCARCE->MODERATE   output SCARCE   ask 4,416
  02:00  input ABUNDANT           output SCARCE   ask   -
  03:00  input ABUNDANT           output SCARCE   ask 3,606
  04:00  input ABUNDANT           output SCARCE   ask 3,992
  05-07  (no buying, drain stalled)
  08:00  input MODERATE           output SCARCE   ask 1,464

SATURATING THE INPUT MOVED THE ASK ~0%. NOT BUYING FOR FOUR HOURS MOVED IT 63%.
Same market, same morning, hours apart.

## Why

H51 IRON export is SCARCE/STRONG at trade_volume 60. We bought 2,474 units over ~17
active hours, ~145 units/hour. THE FACTORY'S PRODUCTION RATE IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT,
NOT ITS INPUT STOCK. Saturating an input cannot raise a rate cap. The same shape explains
QUARTZ_SAND -> F45: we filled a warehouse sitting behind a rate-limited factory.

## What this is NOT

Feeding ore is nearly free and should NOT be stopped: 1,771 units bought for 89,368, 1,586
sold into H51 for 85,704 -> net 3,664 credits, 2.31/unit delivered. It is cheap and
ineffective, not expensive and ineffective. 3,664 credits of ore did not dent a 4.48M IRON
bill. Do not "fix" this by cutting the ore feed.

sp-55erc guards only the extreme case (input ALREADY ABUNDANT). Nothing anywhere checks
whether feeding an input MOVES the output at all.

## Acceptance
1. Establish whether output supply/rate responds to input stock AT ALL in this API, or only
   to elapsed time and trade_volume. This is the whole bead — if factories are purely
   rate-limited, then input hauling beyond a low working stock is ALWAYS waste and the feed
   planner needs a different objective entirely.
2. If there IS a response, characterise it: what input level, over what lag, moves output
   supply by how much. A model with no measured lag is how we got here.
3. Do not cut the ore feed on the strength of this bead alone (see above) -- it is cheap
   and may still matter for keeping a factory off zero.
4. State what the feed planner SHOULD optimise if not input stock. Candidate: pace the
   OUTPUT buy (sp-zq2yb) and hold input stock at a low floor rather than pushing it up.
5. RULINGS #4: any change makes buys smaller or identical.

RELATED: sp-zq2yb (output-side pacing -- the lever that DOES work, 63% vs 0%), sp-55erc
(guards the extreme only), sp-f59h4 (closed; the quartz half of the same falsification).
notes:
MEASUREMENT (lane, 2026-08-06). Criterion 1 ANSWERED: output does NOT respond to input stock.

DOSE-RESPONSE TEST, F45 QUARTZ_SAND -> FAB_MATS. Two quiet windows (zero FAB_MATS buying),
same factory, same good, activity matched at RESTRICTED, trade_volume 43 both, start asks
matched within 2% (2942 vs 2879):

  W1  08-05 20:47->01:56   fed   448 u  (  87 u/h)   ask decay -7.86 %/h  (n=7,  r2 .897)
  W2  08-06 02:00->09:10   fed 6,640 u  ( 927 u/h)   ask decay -4.79 %/h  (n=11, r2 .998)

10.7x the input feed rate produced NO acceleration -- 39% SLOWER. Feeding is not the lever.

WHAT DOES PREDICT RECOVERY: activity state. Decay is log-linear (exponential toward
equilibrium), r2 .87-.998.
  RESTRICTED  -7.86 %/h (F45 FAB_MATS) and -7.88 %/h (H51 IRON)  -> half-life ~9.0 h
  STRONG     -40.91 %/h (H51 IRON, quiet 04:32-08:04, n=3)       -> half-life ~1.7 h
The two RESTRICTED figures are independent (different factory, different good) and agree to
2% -- calibration that the rig measures something real.

FALSIFIED DURING THIS ANALYSIS (my own intermediate result, recorded so nobody re-derives it):
trade_volume looked like a strong input signal -- 49.0 vs 33.3 holding activity constant,
49.9 vs 37.6 holding OUTPUT level constant. It is an artifact. F45 FAB_MATS tv over 40h:
85 flat, 9 UP, 0 DOWN. It is a monotone ratchet on cumulative trade; input rose over the same
period, so the correlation is pure time confound. tv is not an input signal. Discarded.

Also: the bead's own 63%-vs-0% pair is not a controlled comparison. During the "0%" stretch we
were BUYING (01:54/03:29/03:46); during the "63%" stretch we were not. Both had high input.
The difference between them is buying, not input.

CRITERION 3 (do not cut the feed) -- CONCUR, plus a boundary: input never fell below SCARCE in
40h, and at SCARCE the factory ran the full RESTRICTED rate. So SCARCE input SUFFICED. But
SCARCE is a ladder rung, not zero -- there is no observation of an actually starved factory, so
cutting the feed is an untested extrapolation, not a supported one.

CRITERION 4 -- the planner should not optimise input stock beyond a low working floor. The
measured lever is output-side pacing (sp-zq2yb), and it can now be priced: waiting buys price
relief at a half-life of ~9 h under RESTRICTED and ~1.7 h under STRONG. Cooldown should be
activity-conditioned, not fixed.

CAVEAT ON THAT: I did NOT establish what drives `activity`. Transitions do not track our buy
volume (09:34 STRONG->RESTRICTED on 480 u prior-6h; 10:02 RESTRICTED->STRONG on 400 u).
Activity is currently an OBSERVABLE, not a knob -- pacing can read it, not cause it.

LIMITS: 40h, 2 chains, 4 windows, n=3-11 per window. No code changed; no buy widened (RULINGS #4).

ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT (sp-9eor3 lane, lead-verified against the ledger 2026-08-06).
CRITERION 1 IS A CLEAN NO: feeding an input does not move the output.

## The dose-response (not a level comparison -- this is why it settles the question)

Two QUIET windows at F45 (zero FAB_MATS buying in both -- verified 0 and 0), same factory,
same good, activity matched at RESTRICTED, trade_volume 43 both, start asks within 2%:

  W1  08-05 20:47->01:56    448 units fed  ( 87 u/h)   ask decay -7.86 %/h  n=7   r2=.897
  W2  08-06 02:00->09:10  6,640 units fed  (927 u/h)   ask decay -4.79 %/h  n=11  r2=.998

10.7x THE FEED RATE PRODUCED 39% SLOWER RECOVERY. Feed volumes verified independently:
448 and 6,640 exactly.

## What DOES drive recovery: activity

  RESTRICTED   -7.86 %/h   F45 FAB_MATS
  RESTRICTED   -7.88 %/h   H51 IRON      <- independent chains, different goods, agree to 2%
  STRONG      -40.91 %/h   H51 IRON

  half-life ~9.0 h RESTRICTED,  ~1.7 h STRONG   (~5x)

The two RESTRICTED figures agreeing across independent chains is the rig calibration.

RECONCILES sp-zq2yb's tau: tau=750min (half-life ~8.7h) is NEARLY EXACT for RESTRICTED and
~5x too slow for STRONG. The 240min outage recovery was H51 IRON = STRONG. The fix is not
retuning tau, it is CONDITIONING COOLDOWN ON ACTIVITY.

## ACTIVITY IS AN OBSERVABLE, NOT A KNOB

It does not track our buying: 09:34 went STRONG->RESTRICTED after 480 units bought in the
prior 6h; 10:02 went RESTRICTED->STRONG after 400. Pacing can READ activity; it cannot
CAUSE it. Any design assuming buying harder (or yielding) induces STRONG is unsupported.

## Two corrections recorded so nobody re-derives them

1. trade_volume looked like a strong input signal (49.0 vs 33.3 holding activity constant;
   49.9 vs 37.6 holding output level constant -- two controls, same direction). ARTIFACT:
   F45 FAB_MATS tv over 40h is 85 flat, 9 up, 0 DOWN -- a monotone ratchet on cumulative
   trade. Input rose over the same period, so the correlation is pure time confound.

2. THIS BEAD'S OWN 63%-vs-0% EVIDENCE IS UNCONTROLLED (and the lead wrote it). During the
   "0%" stretch we WERE buying (01:54/03:29/03:46); during the "63%" stretch we were not.
   BOTH had high input. The difference between them is BUYING, not input. The conclusion
   survives; the stated reasoning for it does not.

## BOUNDARY -- do not over-read this bead

Input never fell below SCARCE in 40h, and at SCARCE the factory ran the full RESTRICTED
rate. So "feeding does nothing" is measured over SCARCE->ABUNDANT ONLY. SCARCE sufficed,
but SCARCE is a ladder rung, not zero. There is NO observation of an actually starved
factory. CUTTING THE FEED IS AN UNTESTED EXTRAPOLATION THIS BEAD DOES NOT LICENSE.

Limits: 40h, 2 chains, 4 windows, n=3-11 each. No code written. RULINGS #4 untouched.

description:

(2.6% of construction spend) and was substantially fixed by sp-55erc. THIS is the unfixed

under sustained pacing, which the outage evidences for a 4-hour window but does NOT prove
for a sustained one; some escalation is structurally permanent. ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, NOT A
LEDGER FIGURE. Even at half it is 3x the entire QUARTZ_SAND bead.

## Critically: the IRON spend is NOT waste

F45 is SCARCE of IRON, IRON is the binding input to FAB_MATS, and gate progress moved
77 -> 85 -> 90 -> 93% while IRON was being fed. Every IRON credit bought real progress.
Do NOT repeat sp-f59h4's error of reading spend as loss. THE DEFECT IS PURELY THE RATE.

## Required shape: PACING, not a ceiling

A hard ceiling refuses a genuinely needed input and starves the gate — the exact
starvation that sp-9eor3 / sp-xcjuy / sp-c9wuu / sp-55erc all spent 2026-08-06 fixing.
What is wanted: DEFER the buy when the ask has run far above its own recent baseline, let
the source recover, and let the scarcity-ranked walk take the next step meanwhile. The
deferred input re-enters when the source recovers. The outage proves the source does
recover, and fast.

## LIVE-PIPELINE HAZARD — read before deploying

The gate is at 96% (1520/1600) and needs 80 more FAB_MATS, which F45 produces FROM IRON.
IRON buying is ON THE CRITICAL PATH RIGHT NOW. A pacing guard deployed carelessly stalls
the gate at 96%. Either land it after the gate completes, or prove the defer path cannot
block the final tranche. Do not deploy this into an active final approach.

## Acceptance
1. Baseline definition: state what "its own recent baseline" is, its window, and where it
   is persisted. A baseline computed from the escalated prices themselves ratchets and the
   guard becomes a no-op — that is the failure mode to design against first.
2. DEFER, never refuse: a deferred input must re-enter when the source recovers. Prove the
   scarcity walk falls through to the next step rather than the leg aborting.
3. RULINGS #4: buys smaller or identical, never larger.
4. Regression: a normally-priced source must be untouched, and the fixture must saturate
   past the bound or it proves nothing.
5. Cost the alternative first (see below) — it may be structurally better than any guard.

## Cheaper structural lever, cost it BEFORE building the guard

The feed plan already models IRON_ORE -> IRON (d2), and H51 is SCARCE of its own IRON
output with STRONG activity. Feeding H51 its IRON_ORE lets it PRODUCE IRON instead of us

ever bought. The conversion ratio is NOT yet costed — do that first; if producing beats
buying, the pacing guard may be the wrong instrument entirely.

title: stall watchdog still false-alarms after a CONFIRMED delivery — it already reads the delta it needs
description:
Follow-up to sp-1f0ex (which is a real repair and should stay: actual_quantity IS now
written when a supply task completes). It is not sufficient.

## Proof, staging, after sp-1f0ex was deployed (main 7e096955)

A delivery demonstrably landed: TORWINDSTG-B carried 28 units into X1-KP46-I55 and the
gate went 1435 -> 1463 /1600 (91.8% -> 93.2%).

After that landing:
  manufacturing_tasks: actual_quantity>0 = 0 of 44, max=0
  FAB_MATS COMPLETED  = 19  (UNCHANGED across the delivery)
  gauge FAB_MATS      = 111819 and still climbing

So the delivery completed NO task, and the actual_quantity write in completeSupply
never ran. The fix is on a path this delivery did not take.

## The watchdog already holds the correct signal

Its own ERROR line changed across the delivery:
  before:  "...received 0 units in the last 31h... and still needs 165"
  after:   "...received 0 units in the last 31h... and still needs 137"

165 -> 137 is exactly the 28 units delivered. The watchdog reads the live REMAINING
requirement every tick and prints it, while simultaneously claiming zero units received,
because "received" is sourced from completed-task bookkeeping instead of from the
requirement delta it already has.

## Direction

Measure deliveries as the tick-over-tick DECREASE in the material's remaining
requirement. That is authoritative (it is the gate's own count), needs no task
bookkeeping, and is already being read.

sp-1f0ex's stated blocker was that persisting a prior observation needs a schema change
and the manufacturing models are NOT in AutoMigrate. That constraint is real — but an
in-memory per-container last-observed map avoids it entirely, the same pattern the
bootstrap coordinator uses for exactly this reason. A restart re-seeds and the first
tick after a restart simply reports nothing rather than guessing; say so explicitly
rather than letting a cold start look like a stall.

Also seen in the same line and worth resolving: "Source supply reads unreadable".

## Acceptance
1. A confirmed delivery (remaining count falls) must drive the gauge to 0 within a tick
   or two. Reproduce the exact case above: remaining 165 -> 137, gauge must go to 0.
2. A genuinely stalled material (remaining count FLAT across the threshold) must still
   report non-zero. Do not fix by disabling.
3. First tick after a restart must not report a stall from a missing prior observation.
4. Mutation probe on the delta computation, naming the test it kills.
5. Do NOT use ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY as the healthy fixture — its bill is satisfied and it
   reads 0 via the other path regardless of whether detection works.
close_reason: Closed

title: sp-63r4f gate stall watchdog can NEVER detect a delivery — both task quantity fields are dead
description:
DEPLOYED TO STAGING AND IMMEDIATELY FALSE-ALARMING. Read-only, so it cannot harm
operations, but it ERRORs every tick and will train the crew to ignore gate_stalled —
the exact alarm built to end the invisible-stall problem.

## Evidence (staging, era 6, pipeline c6a8d38e)

Gauge on first emission, while the gate was demonstrably taking FAB_MATS:
  gate_material_stall_seconds{good="ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY"} 0
  gate_material_stall_seconds{good="FAB_MATS"}           110797  (30.8 h)

Log, 6 lines since restart:
  ERROR: GATE STALLED: FAB_MATS at X1-KP46-I55 has received 0 units in the last
  30h48m0s and still needs 165.

That is false. In the hour before deploy the pipeline acquired 134 FAB_MATS units
and 19 FAB_MATS tasks reached COMPLETED, the most recent 50 minutes earlier.

## Root cause

watchGateProgress counts a delivery only when a COMPLETED task has ActualQuantity()>0:
    if task == nil || task.ActualQuantity() <= 0 { continue }

That predicate is ALWAYS FALSE. In manufacturing_tasks, all 44 rows:
    actual_quantity  min=0 max=0  NULLs=0  rows>0 = 0
    quantity         min=0 max=0           rows>0 = 0

BOTH quantity fields are dead. SetActualQuantity (task.go:340) and SetQuantity each
have exactly ONE non-test reference — their own definition. Neither is ever invoked.
The persistence layer round-trips the field faithfully; nothing ever puts a value in it.

So lastDelivery[good] is never updated for ANY good, and every unmet material will
report a monotonically growing false stall forever.

ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY reads 0 only because its bill is satisfied (400/400) — the other
zero-path. It is NOT evidence the delivery path works. Do not use it as a control.

## Fix

Root cause is the unpopulated quantity, not the watchdog's predicate — the predicate
is correct reasoning over a field nobody writes. Prefer populating quantity at task
creation and actual_quantity at completion with units actually moved.

If instead you re-source the watchdog, consider the gate's own material counts
(FAB_MATS 1435/1600 from construction status) — that is the authoritative delivered
figure and is independent of task bookkeeping. Justify whichever you pick.

## Acceptance — CALIBRATE THE RIG

1. A material that is ACTIVELY RECEIVING UNITS must read 0. Write this test first and
   confirm it FAILS against today's code; a test that passes now proves nothing.
2. Do NOT use a satisfied bill as the healthy fixture — it passes via the other zero
   path and would pass even if delivery detection stayed broken. The healthy fixture
   must be an UNMET material with recent deliveries.
3. A genuinely stalled material must still report non-zero (do not fix by disabling).
4. Mutation probe: break the delivery-detection line and NAME the test that fails.
5. State whether populating quantity changes any other reader of these fields —
   enumerate them before changing the meaning of a field.
close_reason: Closed

acquired in the hour before filing), so this is a latent gap, not an active stall.

the binding constraint right now is treasury, not gate-feed logic.

suspected_stuck and eventually release. Verify with a fixture pinned below the buy
floor for longer than the timeout — a fixture that reaches the floor will pass

title: [P1] No watchdog at the PIPELINE grain: the gate stopped for ~10 of 14 hours across three different causes, each logging a reassuring reason, each found only because a human asked
description:
THREE SEPARATE TIMES ON 2026-08-06 the construction pipeline stopped making progress for hours while
the agent looked perfectly healthy, and each time the stall logged something TRUE AND REASSURING on
every tick. Each was diagnosed only because a human asked "why is the gate stalled". There is no
check that would have caught any of them.

THE THREE STALLS, all on the same pipeline, all with different causes:
 1. HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCK (sp-9eor3) — an unaffordable IRON step aborted the whole leg, so QUARTZ_SAND
    behind it was never bought. 495 'acquired nothing of IRON' warnings; five hulls idle at H51, one
    for 8 hours. Presented from the delivery side as 'PAUSED on FAB_MATS: supply SCARCE'.
 2. AFFORDABILITY WALL (sp-xcjuy) — a full 60-unit tranche breached the reserve while 20 units would
    have fitted. ~90 minutes. Logged 'declining the IRON feed ... takes the next affordable step',
    which reads like the guard working.
 3. HYSTERESIS DEADLOCK (sp-c9wuu) — the fleet paused at SCARCE and needed MODERATE to resume, while
    supply plateaued at LIMITED. 7.5 HOURS. Logged 'PAUSED ... resumes at MODERATE' every tick,
    which reads as patience.

WHY EXISTING CHECKS MISS ALL THREE:
 - sp-16zxm (agent has zero transactions while coordinators are healthy) does NOT cover this. The
   agent was transacting the whole time — contract earned +590,348 in one of the stalled windows,
   tour was trading. Only ONE PIPELINE was stopped. An agent-level check is the wrong grain.
 - Container health does not cover it: every coordinator heartbeated normally throughout.
 - The per-cause fixes each bound their own cause. None generalises. The NEXT cause will be
   invisible in exactly the same way.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a progress watchdog at the PIPELINE grain. If an active construction pipeline has
delivered no units toward an unmet material for N minutes, escalate — regardless of WHY, and
specifically without needing to know the cause in advance. That is the property the three fixes
lack: they each detect a known failure, and this detects the absence of progress.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Fires on an ACTIVE pipeline with an UNMET material that has received zero delivered units for N
   minutes. Not on a complete pipeline, not on a stopped one, not on a material already satisfied.
2. N justified against observed healthy cadence, not picked round. Note the buy floor legitimately
   idles for tens of minutes while a market regenerates, so N must exceed a normal buy-drain-recover
   cycle — sp-c9wuu derived 60 minutes as 2x the supply-task lifetime for a related reason and that
   derivation is worth reusing or arguing with.
3. ESCALATES, not merely logs. A WARNING among thousands is what let all three hide. It needs a
   counter or an ERROR that is distinguishable at a glance from the routine pause lines.
4. Says WHAT it observed, not what it guesses: which material, how long, how many units delivered in
   the window, and the current supply level at the source. The diagnosis is the human's; the
   watchdog's job is to make the silence loud.
5. Regression: a pipeline making slow but real progress must NOT fire. Test with a trickle.
6. It must survive a daemon restart without resetting its clock to zero on every bounce — otherwise
   a restart loop hides the stall, which is the sp-20eyn shape.

WHY THIS IS P1: the gate is the strategic objective, and it was stopped for roughly 10 of the last
14 hours across the three incidents. Every one was found by a human noticing, not by the system
saying so. The per-cause fixes reduce the FREQUENCY of stalls; only this reduces the TIME TO NOTICE
one, and the next cause is not yet known.

RELATED: sp-9eor3, sp-xcjuy, sp-c9wuu (the three causes, each fixed), sp-16zxm (the agent-grain
watcher, which is a sibling and does NOT subsume this).
close_reason: Closed

title: [P1] Delivery-fleet hysteresis has no timeout: paused 7.5h on a supply level it was configured to buy at, logging a reassuring reason every tick
description:
The gate delivery fleet paused for 7.5 HOURS on a supply level it was configured to buy at, because
the resume threshold sits two ladder levels above where the pause happened and the market plateaued
in between. Hysteresis with no timeout turns a self-correcting condition into a permanent one.

OBSERVED (staging, X1-KP46-F45, 2026-08-06):
  buy_floor = LIMITED, resume_floor = MODERATE (the shipped defaults are MODERATE/HIGH — same shape,
  same gap)
  ~02:00  the fleet bought 160 units in quick succession and drained FAB_MATS to SCARCE
          -> SCARCE is below the LIMITED buy floor -> PAUSED. Correct: the guard refusing to strip a
             depleted market at peak prices.
  02:00-09:30  supply recovered steadily for SEVEN HOURS; the ask fell 2942 -> 2519 -> 2456 -> 2338
             -> 2283 -> 2040, and supply reached LIMITED.
  09:30  still paused. LIMITED is AT the buy floor but BELOW the resume floor, so it kept sitting out
         a level it was explicitly configured to buy at. Zero FAB_MATS purchased in 7.5h while the
         gate sat at 1301/1600.

WHY HYSTERESIS IS RIGHT AND WHY THIS SHAPE OF IT IS NOT. A single threshold genuinely chatters —
pause, one unit regenerates, resume, buy instantly re-depletes, pause — and the CLI documents that
reasoning. The problem is the failure mode the second threshold ADDS: with one knob the fleet
flaps, which is wasteful but KEEPS BUYING. With two knobs it can deadlock, which stops progress
entirely. The gap must be narrower than the system's recovery range, and nothing checks that it is.
The current gap is 'one ladder level up', chosen structurally rather than derived from how fast a
market actually regenerates. Here F45 regenerates fast enough to reach LIMITED but not MODERATE
while we are its only consumer, so the recovery plateaued INSIDE the gap.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED FOR 7.5 HOURS — this is the part worth fixing beyond the control logic. The
pause logs a clear, informative line on every tick:
    'Gate delivery PAUSED on FAB_MATS at X1-KP46-F45: supply SCARCE is below the LIMITED buy floor
     — resumes at MODERATE'
That reads as 'the market is thin, being patient', which is indistinguishable from correct
behaviour. The captain read it as healthy waiting twice and told the Admiral waiting cost nothing.
A permanently-stuck state that logs a reassuring reason every tick is worse than one that logs
nothing, because it actively invites the wrong conclusion.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A TIMEOUT that bounds the paused state: if supply has been at or above the BUY floor continuously
   for N minutes while still below the resume floor, resume anyway. That is what makes hysteresis
   safe — it keeps the anti-chatter benefit for the fast oscillation it exists to damp, while
   preventing an indefinite stall. Justify N against observed regeneration, not a round number.
2. Alternatively or additionally, DERIVE the gap rather than fixing it at one level: if a market's
   observed recovery rate cannot cross the gap, the gap is wrong for that market. State which
   approach was chosen and why.
3. THE PAUSE MUST BECOME DISTINGUISHABLE FROM HEALTHY WAITING. After N minutes the log must escalate
   (WARNING, and a counter) saying the pause is now suspected stuck and naming how long it has held
   and at what supply level. A reassuring INFO line every tick for 7.5 hours is the observability
   defect here.
4. Regression: a genuine fast oscillation is still damped — the anti-chatter property must survive.
   Test the flapping case explicitly, or the fix trades one failure for the other.
5. The shipped defaults (buy=MODERATE, resume=HIGH) have the SAME two-level gap and are MORE
   exposed, since HIGH is harder to reach than MODERATE. Whatever fix lands must apply to the
   defaults, not only to overridden pipelines.

closes the trap for this pipeline only — SCARCE is the bottom of the ladder, so there is no level it
can pause into and fail to climb out of. That costs price discipline (it will buy at any supply
level) and should be reverted once a real timeout exists.

RELATED: sp-9eor3 and sp-xcjuy are the feed-side affordability work; this is the DELIVERY side, a
different gate on the same pipeline. Both were mistaken for market scarcity while stalling.

would be wrong exactly when it is coldest, and would STILL need a backstop when the estimate is
optimistic. The timeout IS that backstop. It also bounds the harm directly — the defect is that
progress STOPPED, and a timeout is a bound on stopped progress.

supply is climbing or merely bouncing. Against this incident: 60 minutes versus the 450 lost.

resets the instant it drops back — NOT when the pause begins. So a flapping market can never
accumulate the hour, making the timeout unreachable for exactly the oscillation the resume floor

title: [P1] Idle-arb bought 29 units into a sink with trade_volume 6 and realised -16.9% — VolumeCap is sized off market data that no longer holds
description:
THE ONLY MEASURED CREDIT LOSS FOUND IN THIS INVESTIGATION. Surfaced by the sp-kw2em lane while
looking for harm from the absorption clamp — and notably this is NOT that bug: idle-arb ALREADY has
the absorption ledger wired.

OBSERVED (staging, SHIP_PARTS, 2026-08-05):
  bought   29 units into a sink whose trade_volume was 6
  the sell tranched 6/6/6/6/5, which independently confirms the depth was really 6
  realised 7,265 -> 6,039 per unit — a 16.9% decay
  approximately 19,800 credits left on the table in ONE run

WHY THE ABSORPTION LEDGER DID NOT SAVE IT: nothing else was in flight, so headroom equalled
VolumeCap and the consult was a no-op. The clamp is only ever a CONTENTION guard. The real cause is
VolumeCap ITSELF being sized off market data that no longer held at execution time — the sizer
believed a depth of 29 was absorbable when the live trade_volume was 6.

THIS IS THE MORE VALUABLE HALF OF THE INVESTIGATION. sp-kw2em's clamp protects against co-dumping by
multiple engines; this protects against a single engine being wrong about the sink at all, which is
the failure that actually cost credits.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Establish how stale VolumeCap's inputs can be at execution. Name the read, its age, and the
   window between sizing and the first sell. A fix cannot be designed without that number.
2. Re-validate depth against live market data at the point of sale, or bound the sized buy by the
   freshest available trade_volume. State which you chose and why.
3. RULINGS #4: any change must make buys SMALLER or leave them identical.
4. Regression: a run whose sink genuinely is deep enough must be unchanged — do not fix a 16.9%
   decay by making every buy tiny.
5. Measure the decay before and after on a comparable run. This bead exists because someone
   measured it; the fix should be held to the same standard.

RELATED: sp-kw2em (the contention clamp, which does not address this), sp-55erc (the ABUNDANT-input
gap, same family of 'the sizer believed something the market no longer supports').
notes:
PREMISE FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT — lead verified independently 2026-08-06, ledger not log.

1. THE RUN WAS PROFITABLE. transactions, operation_type=arb_run, SHIP_PARTS, 04:38-04:45:
   buys=101271  sells=190857  NET=+89586 over 10 rows. Every tranche profitable, worst
   2484/u against the lane's binding floor of 689/u. The sell floor never fired.
   The "~19,800 credits left on the table" is a counterfactual the market cannot supply:
   it prices 29 units at the undepressed 7265 bid into a sink six units deep.
   THIS BEAD'S CLAIM TO BE "THE ONLY MEASURED CREDIT LOSS" IS WITHDRAWN.

2. NOTHING WAS STALE. The sink read was 27m03s old and reported trade_volume=6.
   X1-KP46-H52 SHIP_PARTS still reads trade_volume=6 today. A live re-read at point of
   sale would have returned the same 6. The stated cause -- "VolumeCap sized off market
   data that no longer held" -- is wrong on both halves: the data held, and idle-arb has
   no VolumeCap in its sizing path at all.

3. A LITERAL 1x trade_volume CLAMP WOULD HAVE COST 66,666 CREDITS. Six units nets
   +22,920 against the +89,586 realised. Acceptance criterion 4 was load-bearing.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, AND IS NOW FIXED: idle-arb sized with ZERO depth awareness.
Depth was read in pickHubLocalLane, handed only to the absorption consult, and thrown
away three seams before the buy; container_ops_idle_arb.go:65 hardcoded max_units:0,
which Guard 3 reads as UNCAPPED. The sell floor was the only depth discipline and it
fires AFTER the spend, stranding cargo. This run came within 3.1 points of that.

Fix bounds the buy by the freshest trade_volume ahead of the spend, derived by inverting
the domain's own PostTradeSellPrice so the engine cannot buy what it has already declared
it will refuse to sell. Guard 3 is a min(), so the term can only reduce. Byte-identical on
the incident run (bound 80 >= 29 bought) and on all 36 currently-profitable staging lanes.

SHIPPED KNOWINGLY SLACK. Its teeth come from DefaultSellImpactCoefficient, fitted ~2.3x
low (0.015 default vs 0.0349 measured). See sp-5414o. Shipping anyway: it is a pure
reduction, byte-identical today, and becomes effective the moment the coefficient is
refit. Same posture as the spend floor, which also does not fire most days. The risk to
watch is false confidence -- do NOT treat depth as guarded until sp-5414o lands.

title: [P2] Affordability precheck declines a whole feed step when a FULL tranche is unaffordable, though a smaller tranche would fit — the gate starves rather than partially feeding
description:
Found while diagnosing the 71-minute gate stall of 2026-08-06 03:06.

sp-9eor3's precheck prices min(units, TradeVolume) x Price and declines the step if that breaches
the working-capital reserve. Observed live:

    declining the IRON feed — 60 units at X1-KP46-H51 would cost about 242640 against a reserve of
    460373, so this leg takes the next affordable step
    (treasury 659471, H51 IRON EXPORT SCARCE at 4044/unit, trade volume 60)

60 x 4044 = 242,640, and 659,471 - 242,640 = 416,831 which is below the 460,373 reserve, so it
declines. But a SMALLER tranche fits comfortably: 20 units is 80,880, leaving 578,591 — well clear.
The factory would get fed, just less.

WHY THIS IS P2 AND NOT P1: it is a missed OPTIMISATION, not a defect. Declining is safe and the
guard is behaving as specified; sp-9eor3 deliberately priced the FIRST TRANCHE rather than the
hull-load precisely because pricing the whole hold would have declined steps that could partially
fill. This is the same reasoning taken one step further — a tranche is still a fixed size, and when
even that is unaffordable the step dies rather than shrinking.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: the input in question is usually the one the factory is SCARCE of, i.e. the
one that actually gates production. Declining it entirely means the gate stalls while treasury is
substantial (659k here). The system waits for treasury to clear reserve + full tranche (~703k)
rather than making steady partial progress.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. When a full tranche breaches but a smaller one would not, buy the largest affordable tranche
   rather than declining the step. Test: reserve headroom that admits 20 of 60 units; assert 20 are
   bought, not zero.
2. A MINIMUM VIABLE TRANCHE must exist and be justified — one unit at a time is not progress, it is
   thrash, and each tranche costs a round trip. Below that floor, decline as today.
3. RULINGS #4 UNCHANGED: the per-tranche commit-time guard still runs on every tranche. This only
   changes the SIZE proposed, never whether the guard may be bypassed. State the direction
   explicitly and pin it.
4. Regression: a fully affordable step still buys the full tranche, byte-identically.
5. The decline log must distinguish 'unaffordable even at the minimum tranche' from 'declined for
   another reason', or this becomes invisible again.

RELATED: sp-9eor3 (the precheck), sp-q9um6 (the ranking that selects which step gets priced), and
the sibling bead on feeding ABUNDANT inputs — together they are why the fleet currently feeds an
input it does not need while the one it does need is declined.
notes:
ESCALATED P2 -> P1 2026-08-06 03:20: THIS IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE GATE, not a
theoretical optimisation.

MEASURED LIVE. The staging gate has been stalled 78 minutes at FAB_MATS 1301/1600 with no progress,
and this is exactly why:
    IRON at X1-KP46-H51 (the only source): 4044/unit, SCARCE, trade volume 60
    full tranche 60 x 4044          = 242,640
    working-capital reserve          = 460,373
    treasury                         = 648,388  AND FALLING, not accumulating
    648,388 - 242,640 = 405,748, below the reserve -> DECLINED
A 20-unit tranche costs 80,880 and leaves 567,508 — comfortably clear. The factory would be fed,
just less, and the gate would advance.

I PREVIOUSLY SAID THIS WOULD CLEAR ITSELF AS CONTRACT EARNS. That was wrong: treasury is DECLINING
(659,471 -> 648,388 over the stall), so waiting does not reach the ~703k needed for a full tranche.
There is no self-recovery path at the current rate.

COMPOSES WITH sp-55erc: because the iron step is declined, the walk falls through to QUARTZ_SAND —
which the factory is ABUNDANT of — and feeds it pointlessly. Fixing either one unblocks the gate;
fixing this one is the more direct route, because it makes the input the factory actually needs
purchasable rather than merely stopping the pointless alternative.

The acceptance criteria below are unchanged and still right. Criterion 2 (a justified MINIMUM VIABLE
TRANCHE) matters most here — at 4044/unit a tranche of 5 units is a round trip for almost nothing,
so the floor needs a real argument, not a round number.

title: [P1] Gate feed pours inputs into a factory that is already ABUNDANT of them — the ABUNDANT fail-safe checks the factory's OUTPUT supply, not the input's
description:
OBSERVED LIVE (staging, X1-KP46, 2026-08-06 03:06). The gate has been stalled 71 minutes with
FAB_MATS at 1301/1600, and the feed is in a stable unproductive loop where every individual decision
is correct:

    Gate factory: feeding the FAB_MATS chain by SCARCITY, not recipe order — IRON is next because
    its factory is SCARCE of it; full order IRON(SCARCE) > QUARTZ_SAND(ABUNDANT) > IRON_ORE
    WARNING: declining the IRON feed — 60 units at X1-KP46-H51 would cost about 242640 against a
    reserve of 460373, so this leg takes the next affordable step

sp-q9um6's ranking correctly puts IRON first. sp-9eor3's affordability precheck correctly declines
it. The fall-through correctly takes the next step. And the next step is QUARTZ_SAND, which F45 is
ABUNDANT of — so we feed it anyway. Last 3000 log lines: 15 'Delivered input' events, ALL of them
QUARTZ_SAND, into a factory reading QUARTZ_SAND IMPORT supply=ABUNDANT buy=18.

THE GAP IS PRECISE. The existing ABUNDANT fail-safe in planGateFeed reads:
    if ParseSupplyLevel(target.Supply) == SupplyLevelAbundant { continue }
with the comment 'A factory already at the top of the supply ladder does not need feedstock; buying
into a full warehouse burns treasury for nothing.' That is exactly the right intent — but
target.Supply is the terminal factory's EXPORT supply of its own OUTPUT (F45's FAB_MATS, currently
SCARCE), NOT its IMPORT supply of the input being fed (F45's QUARTZ_SAND, currently ABUNDANT). So
the fail-safe answers 'does this factory need feeding AT ALL' and never 'does it need THIS input'.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS. sp-q9um6 (merged 3467cf6f) built GateTopology.ImportSupply precisely to
read the destination's own IMPORT listing for a good, and the ranking already consumes it — that is
how the log knows QUARTZ_SAND is ABUNDANT. The ranking uses it to ORDER; nothing uses it as a FLOOR.

COST: treasury spent buying into a full warehouse, plus hauler legs consumed. Quartz is cheap
(18-44/unit) so the credit loss is minor — the real cost is that the gate-factory fleet is fully
occupied doing work with zero effect while the gate is stalled, and the logs read as healthy
activity.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A step whose INPUT is already ABUNDANT at the terminal factory is declined with a logged reason,
   exactly as the output-ABUNDANT fail-safe declines today. Test: factory ABUNDANT on the input,
   assert the step is skipped and the next one considered.
2. It must remain possible to feed an input at any non-ABUNDANT level — this is a top-of-ladder
   fail-safe, NOT a threshold. Do not turn it into a tunable; the existing fail-safe's comment is
   explicit that a threshold there would be a knob and the phase adds none.
3. THE DEGENERATE CASE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: if EVERY step is declined — the scarce one
   unaffordable and the abundant one unnecessary — the leg must end cleanly with a logged
   'no feedable step', NOT feed something pointless and NOT spin. Assert that state explicitly,
   because it is what the fleet will hit whenever the scarce input is expensive.
4. Unreadable import supply must NOT decline the step (absence of evidence is not evidence of
   abundance) — same fallback direction sp-q9um6 established for the ranking.
5. Regression: a factory SCARCE or MODERATE on an input still gets fed.

RELATED: sp-q9um6 (built the ImportSupply seam this needs), sp-9eor3 (the affordability decline that
exposes this path), and the sibling bead filed alongside this one on partial-tranche affordability.

title: SetAbsorptionHeadroom has ZERO call sites anywhere — long-haul arb buys are never clamped by sink absorption
description:
FOUND BY THE sp-773i0 CENSUS. Live, fail-OPEN, and on a spend path.

THE FACTS (verified directly):
  gobot/internal/application/trading/commands/run_longhaul_arb_worker.go:125
      func (h *RunLongHaulArbHandler) SetAbsorptionHeadroom(f func(lane trading.ArbitrageLane) int)
  Call sites: ZERO. Not in production, not in tests. The field h.absorptionHeadroom is therefore
  always nil.

THE HANDLER IS LIVE: run_longhaul_arb_wiring.go:115 <- NewLongHaulArbWorkerHandler <- main.go:1535.

CONSUMED AT run_longhaul_arb_selection.go:61-63
      headroom := -1
      if absorptionHeadroom != nil { headroom = absorptionHeadroom(lane.Lane) }
  and :27
      if absorptionHeadroom >= 0 && absorptionHeadroom < units { units = absorptionHeadroom }

  -1 means "not consulted" (documented at :15), so with the setter unwired the clamp is skipped on
  EVERY candidate. The sink-depth bound is not merely loose - it never applies. No log, no error.

WHY IT MATTERS: market depth sits below hull capacity, so trade throughput is sink-contended and
oversized buys produce absorption breaches. An unbounded long-haul sizer is exactly the shape that
breaches. The guard was built and never armed.

NOT FIXED IN sp-773i0 DELIBERATELY. Wiring it needs a headroom SOURCE chosen and justified (the
reused absorption ledger the doc mentions), and it will make some currently-approved buys smaller -
a behaviour change on a spend path that deserves its own before/after, not a drive-by.

WHEN FIXED: pin it, and note that this one is NOT on the construction executor so it needs its own
composition-point check rather than a row in executor_guard_wiring_test.go.
notes:
CAPTAIN VERIFICATION: THE PATH IS LIVE, NOT LATENT. This was checked before deciding priority,
because sp-oeo0q turned out to be a P0 measuring a footprint that no longer existed.

  containers matching longhaul/arb : 2
  arb_run transactions ever        : 15, most recent 2026-08-06 00:47:18
  handler                          : constructed at main.go (NewLongHaulArbWorkerHandler)
  documented nil behaviour         : run_longhaul_arb_worker.go:115 — 'nil -> unbounded by absorption'

So the clamp has never been applied to ANY of 15 real arb transactions on an active spend path.
This is the sp-ps2oc class: a guard that exists, is consumed, and has never once executed in
production because nothing calls its setter.

WHY IT IS STAYING P1 RATHER THAN GOING P0, stated so the judgement can be argued with: sp-ps2oc was
P0 on DEMONSTRATED harm — 297k spent in 68ms, treasury 580k -> 47K, every income path deadlocked. I

one sampled hour). Absence of measured harm is weak evidence given nobody has looked, but it is not
the same as evidence of harm, and inflating priority on the class alone would make P0 meaningless.

ESCALATE TO P0 IF any of these is found: an arb buy whose units exceed the destination's absorbable
depth; a long-haul sell realising materially below its planned price; or arb volume growing such
that a single unbounded buy could breach the working-capital reserve. Trade throughput is
sink-contended — market depth sits below hull capacity — so an unbounded sizer is exactly the shape
that breaches, and the current safety may be nothing more than low volume.

FIX NOTE: this needs its own before/after on a money path, not a drive-by. The setter is optional by
design ('Optional.' in its own doc), so the fix is either to wire it at the composition point or to
decide deliberately that unbounded is correct and delete the setter — leaving a permanently-nil
optional guard is the worst of the three, because it reads as protection that does not exist.

planned units — so FOR A HULL TRADING ALONE THE CONSULT IS A NO-OP BY CONSTRUCTION. It bites only on

is exactly what VolumeCap cannot see) but it would NOT have prevented any harm observed to date. The
lane surfaced this before gating rather than letting it be discovered later.

WIRED, NOT DELETED — and the setter was REPLACED rather than merely called, because its signature
was why nobody ever wired it: no ctx (so the fail-closed warning every sibling emits had nowhere to
go), no player id, and it was invoked PER CANDIDATE LANE, so a real ledger would have meant a DB
round trip per lane per episode. SetAbsorptionLedger reads ONCE PER EPISODE, matching every sibling
consult.

RULINGS #4: headroom enters achievableUnits through a min(), so it can only shrink a buy or leave it
alone; an unreadable ledger sizes every lane to ZERO rather than waving the buy through.

NOTE FOR THE NEXT COMPOSITION-ROOT PIN HERE: it needs TWO AST passes. A sibling SetAbsorptionLedger
call appears EARLIER in main.go than the long-haul worker's assignment, so a single pass cannot
filter by receiver. The lane's first version got that wrong and failed.

title: SetPriceHistoryReader has ZERO production call sites — the factory input price ceiling can never validate a rescue buy, and its own doc claims the wiring exists
description:
FOUND BY THE sp-773i0 CENSUS. This is a LIVE sp-ps2oc-shaped hole, not an unpinned-but-working setter.

THE FACTS (verified directly, not from the census report alone):
  gobot/internal/application/manufacturing/services/input_price_ceiling.go:72
      func (e *ProductionExecutor) SetPriceHistoryReader(reader InputPriceHistoryReader)
  Call sites outside its own definition and one unit test: ZERO.

CONSUMED AT input_source_selector.go:294
      if e.priceHistory == nil { return 0, false }
  -> caller at :191-200 logs WARNING "No eligible (MODERATE+) source for %s and no trailing median
     at %s to validate a rescue buy - parking (fail-closed, sp-a5j7)" and returns sourceModeNone.

SO IT FAILS CLOSED AND SILENTLY MISATTRIBUTES. Every rescue source-buy is permanently parked, and
the log blames absent MARKET DATA rather than an unwired reader. Nobody reading that line would
suspect wiring.

THE COLLABORATOR IS ALREADY BUILT AND IN SCOPE, which is what makes this a slip rather than a
design gap:
  main.go:530  priceHistoryRepo := persistence.NewGormMarketPriceHistoryRepository(db)
  main.go:600  passed to newMarketScanner - and referenced NOWHERE ELSE
  main.go:974-990 wires the THREE SIBLING setters on constructionExecutor
                  (SetSpendLedger, SetTreasuryReader, SetCapitalWorkSensor) and skips this one.
  GormMarketPriceHistoryRepository.GetPriceHistory (market_price_history_repository.go:52) matches
  the InputPriceHistoryReader signature exactly.

THE DOC COMMENT ASSERTS THE WIRING THAT DOES NOT EXIST — input_price_ceiling.go:61 says the daemon
"wires the real DB-backed GormMarketPriceHistoryRepository via SetPriceHistoryReader". That claim is
false and should be corrected or made true.

NOT FIXED IN sp-773i0 DELIBERATELY. Adding the call changes rescue-buy behaviour on a money path:
today every rescue parks, afterwards some will proceed subject to the trailing-median ceiling. That
is a behaviour change to a guard and wants its own before/after analysis, not a one-line drive-by
inside a coverage lane. It also cannot be pinned by an AST guard first - a pin for an absent call is
simply red.

WHEN FIXED: add the setter to guardCollaborators in
cmd/spacetraders-daemon/executor_guard_wiring_test.go (sp-773i0) so it cannot be lost again.
notes:
CAPTAIN VERIFICATION, plus a THIRD false comment found while checking.

Confirmed directly: SetPriceHistoryReader has ZERO production call sites — one call in
production_executor_source_selection_test.go:108 and nothing else. priceHistory is therefore always
nil in production.

Traced the impact rather than trusting the summary. input_source_selector.go:191 calls
trailingMedianAsk; on ok=false at :192 it logs and RETURNS, parking the buy:
    'No eligible (MODERATE+) source for %s and no trailing median at %s to validate a rescue buy
     — parking (fail-closed, sp-a5j7)'
So every rescue source-buy parks permanently, and the message blames NO TRAILING MEDIAN AT A MARKET
— which reads as absent market data, not absent wiring. Nobody debugging that line would suspect a
missing setter call.

A THIRD FALSE COMMENT, in the same family as sp-hrko6 and sp-v2npp. input_source_selector.go:292
claims the helper has 'identical fail-open (nil reader) / fail-closed (no samples) semantics'. That
is wrong: BOTH paths return (0, false) and BOTH park. There is no fail-open branch. Whoever fixes
this bead should correct that comment in the same change — a comment describing a fail-open that
does not exist could licence someone removing the nil check believing it degrades gracefully.

THE SIBLING EVIDENCE IS THE DAMNING PART, verified in main.go:
    :530  priceHistoryRepo := persistence.NewGormMarketPriceHistoryRepository(db)
    :600  ... handed to the market scanner, then never mentioned again
    :973  constructionExecutor.SetConstructionRepo(...)
    :974  constructionExecutor.SetSpendLedger(...)
    :978  constructionExecutor.SetTreasuryReader(...)
    :990  constructionExecutor.SetCapitalWorkSensor(...)
Four siblings wired on the same receiver in the same block; this one skipped. The collaborator is
already constructed and in scope, so the fix is likely one line plus the pin — but confirm the repo
satisfies InputPriceHistoryReader rather than assuming it.
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main e7d66bfd (lane 91bcf4b2). One line:
constructionExecutor.SetPriceHistoryReader(priceHistoryRepo). Gate clean; wiring confirmed present
in main.go. go vet rc=0, go test rc=0, 87 packages, 0 FAIL — verified independently.

THE INTERFACE MATCH WAS CONFIRMED BY COMPARING SIGNATURES, NOT BY TRUSTING THE DOC — which mattered,
because the doc in that very file already asserted a wiring that did not exist. GetPriceHistory's
signature is identical on both sides, and main.go now passes the value straight into the setter, so

THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IS THAT NO NEW BEHAVIOURAL TEST COULD HAVE FAILED AGAINST UNMODIFIED
CODE. I asked for one that goes red pre-fix; the lane checked before writing and reported that all

THE SERVICE WAS NEVER BROKEN — ONLY THE COMPOSITION ROOT WAS. Each test wires its own reader from a

trailingMedianAsk has exactly one caller and every branch returns (0,false), which PARKS. There is

this file twice over): the comment describes the contract the field was DESIGNED to have, and nobody

A PROCESS MISTAKE THE LANE SELF-REPORTED, recorded because the discipline is general: it ran the

DEPLOY EXPECTATIONS — this is a live spend-path change and the first hours will not resemble the

The REFUSED line appearing is the reassuring signal — it means the guard is reaching its judgement

title: Retire off-gate warp expansion and its explorer-demand bridge
description:
First shippable slice of epic sp-sy3dl. Independent of the rest: it has zero dependencies, ships and is verifiable alone, and it removes the latching bridge that would otherwise orphan when the autosizer is deleted.

DECISION (Admiral, brainstorm 2026-08-05): retire off-gate warp expansion entirely. No explorers.

EVIDENCE: exactly ONE SHIP_EXPLORER was ever purchased (prod, 2026-07-24, 722,511 cr). The off-gate dispatch loop landed 2026-07-28 - FOUR DAYS LATER - so the warp loop has never had a hull to fly. Neither database holds an explorer-dedicated hull today.

ACCEPTED COST, recorded deliberately: the gate network becomes the permanent reachable universe. Any system not gate-connected is unreachable by design.

THE HAZARD THIS CLOSES: parkedsensing.advanceOffGate emits explorer demand onto a bridge whose ONLY consumer is the autosizer. Deleting the autosizer without handling this leaves the bridge latching demand nobody serves - the exact failure retractOffGateDemand exists to prevent. Retirement must PROVE the bridge is RETRACTED, not merely unread.

VERIFIED LIVE SURFACE:
- OffGatePorts (parkedsensing/offgate.go:74) holds FOUR interfaces: Select OffGateSelector, Demand OffGateDemandSink, Explorer ExplorerFinder, Warp ExplorerDispatcher. Its wired() requires all four non-nil.
- advanceOffGate called ONCE, expansion.go:473 (last pass in AdvanceExpansion, after the gate passes).
- retractOffGateDemand called ONCE, expansion.go:413 (the spend-pause path).
- Wiring at cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:331-332 (offGateSelect, offGateDemand fields) and :388-390 (the OffGatePorts literal).
- TWO ORPHANED DECLARATIONS in offgate_types.go: OffGateTargetSelector (line 48) and ShipyardCoverageReader (line 57) - declared, never wired, satisfied by nothing. They are NOT the live ports; the live selector is OffGateSelector.

METHOD WARNING for whoever does this: you CANNOT determine a Go interface's deadness by grepping its name - interfaces are satisfied implicitly, so an adapter can satisfy one under a different name without ever mentioning it. Determine deadness by finding who consumes the PORT STRUCT that holds it, not by name references.

NOT EXPLORER-ONLY, DO NOT DELETE: the warp/charter stack (ExecuteWarpRoute, warp_system_charter.go, warp_navigator.go, warp_escape_reader.go, ContainerTypeWarp, the warp_ship recovery key) is also reached by the manual 'spacetraders ship warp' verb. Retirement removes ONE OF TWO callers, not the stack.

Explorer-only in practice and therefore retirable: universe_systems.go, client_universe.go ListSystems, domain/system/universe.go - VERIFY each before removing.
acceptance_criteria: advanceOffGate and its call site removed; the explorer-demand bridge proven RETRACTED by test, not merely unread. The two orphaned interface declarations removed. The manual 'spacetraders ship warp' verb still works and its tests still pass. No explorer demand can be emitted from any path. Build, vet, gofmt, full -race green.

Tasks 4-6 were a deliberate non-compiling window closed by Task 6; captain-gate squash-merges (verified at internal/captain/worktree.go:192) so main never saw it.
