title: heavy_cap is keyed on the autosizer's container row; re-home it before that container disappears
description:
BLOCKS the autosizer deletion (sp-sy3dl). AutosizerCapPort resolves heavy_cap by querying container_type = ContainerTypeFleetAutosizer (internal/adapters/parkedsensing/heavy_reserve_port.go:~316, RUNNING preferred over PENDING with an explicit precedence ladder). resolveHeavyCap's !containerExists rung then returns (0,false).

IMPORTANT - THE SILENCE IS NOT A BUG TODAY. That rung is deliberately silent with a documented rationale: 'No autosizer, or one that cannot spend (terminal) => no heavy buyer => nothing to save for. Both are expected configurations rather than faults... every probe-only deployment would otherwise warn every tick.' Making it loud now would spam exactly the deployments it was written for. DO NOT simply add a warning.

THE ACTUAL PROBLEM: the rung's premise - no autosizer implies no heavy buyer - becomes FALSE the moment the fleet-growth coordinator is the heavy buyer. Deleting the autosizer container would then zero the heavy reservation silently and correctly-by-its-own-logic, while a real heavy buyer is running. A dormant-knob failure with no error surface.

FIX SHAPE: decouple the cap from the autosizer's container IDENTITY so it survives the coordinator swap. Whoever owns heavy buying owns the cap. The two-key precedence ladder (RUNNING over PENDING, id breaking ties) exists so the same container wins every tick during a replacement - whatever replaces this must reproduce that property or a mid-swap tick can read a different cap than the tick before.

SEQUENCING: this depends on where the cap lands, which the wave design decides. Do NOT start until the spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-heavy-trade-wave-design.md) is reviewed - unlike the purchaser extraction, this one cannot be done independently.
acceptance_criteria: heavy_cap resolves from whoever owns heavy buying, not from a hardcoded container type. The RUNNING-over-PENDING precedence is preserved with a test. A deployment with no heavy buyer still resolves quietly to no reservation; a deployment WITH one never silently resolves to zero.
close_reason:
Merged. heavy_cap now resolves by CAPABILITY in two independent places, neither naming a coordinator: (1) hullbuy.HeavyBuyerContainers() declares which container types buy heavies — homed in hullbuy because its package doc already establishes it as owned by no coordinator, and DefaultHeavyCap lives there for the same 'two readers must never disagree' reason; (2) the prefixed launch key is matched on its shared '_heavy_cap' SUFFIX so the prefix travels with its owner. prefixedHeavyCapKey deleted. A future growth coordinator with a <prefix>_heavy_cap key resolves with ZERO adapter changes; nothing unbuilt is stubbed, imported or named.

BOTH SIDES SATISFIED INDEPENDENTLY (not traded off): no heavy buyer -> silent rung untouched, log asserted EMPTY (NoHeavyBuyerAnywhereIsSilent). With a buyer -> a declared owner resolves normally; an UNDECLARED owner carrying the knob resolves off it and is announced LOUD (UndeclaredHeavyBuyerReservesAndWarns asserts non-zero reserve AND a warning). The loud rung reads the FULL ladder so an operator's explicit 0 HOLD still propagates — otherwise the fix would have recreated the permanent-expansion-starvation bug the prefixed-key ladder exists to prevent. Probes 2 and 3 prove the two rungs are independently bound.

PRECEDENCE PRESERVED and now applied on BOTH paths (SQL unchanged: RUNNING before PENDING, id ASC). A DECLARED owner outranks any knob-carrying stranger unconditionally, so a stray tune cannot capture the cap while a real owner is live.

7 mutation probes, all killed, each naming its dead; git status clean after every batch; probes re-run post-rebase.

STAGING IMPACT: NONE. buy_heavy_reserve stays 0 against target 1,916,613 (treasury below the entry threshold — documented anti-deadlock behaviour, not a fault). While a declared owner is live the stranger path cannot affect the result. Verified independently: zero require() assertions removed in the test-file rename (22 added), no file deletions, and 'already_at_heavy_cap' — the one other string ending in _heavy_cap — is a pricingErrandDecline log reason in another package, never a container config key, so the suffix match cannot collide with it.

RULINGS #4: the predicate authorises no spend, only withholds; the new rung holds MORE back, never less, and only where today it would hold nothing.

RESIDUAL, STATED NOT HIDDEN: an undeclared buyer with NO cap knob set anywhere is indistinguishable from no buyer using durable facts alone, and 'knob unset' is the common configuration. A ledger witness was considered and declined (third data source in a port whose premise is cheapness; cannot fire before the first purchase). The honest closure is the declaration itself, defended by probe 7. Net is not airtight.

ARM-TIME ITEM for the growth-coordinator lane (migration step 1): with BOTH coordinators declared and RUNNING the winner is status-then-id — deterministic but arbitrary between them. Only matters if their caps differ, and step 1 already switches the autosizer's heavy class off.

title: Extract the hull-purchase primitive out of the autosizer package so the contract scaler stops depending on it
description:
BLOCKS the autosizer deletion (sp-sy3dl). The contract scaler builds its OWN autosizerPurchaser and drives two hull classes through it - verified at internal/adapters/grpc/contract_scaler_ports.go:73 (construction), :169 (HullClassContractDelivery, dedicates to the exclusive contract fleet) and :191 (HullClassLight, deliberately UNTAGGED so the depot grower re-dedicates afterwards). PriceFor is also called with HullClassContractDelivery at :130.

So deleting the autosizer package wholesale breaks contract hull buying. Neither the brainstorm nor the original bead caught this; the spec lane found it.

FIX SHAPE: extract the buy primitive (and the price read it depends on) into a neutrally-owned package that belongs to NEITHER coordinator - both the contract scaler and the future fleet-growth coordinator consume it. The HullClass constants it keys on must survive the autosizer's deletion even where their demand providers do not: HullClassLight has no live provider (its demand is structurally 0) but the CONSTANT is load-bearing because it encodes 'buy untagged so the grower re-dedicates'.

DO THIS BEFORE the autosizer is deleted, and it is safe to do INDEPENDENTLY of the wave redesign - extracting a shared primitive out of a package that should not own it is correct whatever replaces the autosizer. That independence is the reason to do it first.

CARE: BuyAndDedicate is described as the money-integrity batch path with dedicate-at-purchase semantics. The dedicate-at-purchase tag differs per class (contract fleet vs empty). Preserve both behaviours exactly; a hull that lands untagged when it should be tagged, or vice versa, is a fleet-assignment bug that will surface far from this change.
acceptance_criteria: The buy primitive lives outside the autosizer package. Contract scaler compiles and behaves identically - contract hulls still dedicate to the contract fleet, light hulls still land untagged. Tests pin both dedicate-at-purchase behaviours. No behaviour change; this is a move, not a redesign.
close_reason:
Merged. Extracted the shared hull-purchase vocabulary into internal/domain/hullbuy (HullClass + constants, DedicatedFleet policy, BuyOrder, BuyResult, YardPriceReader, DefaultHeavyCap). Zero non-stdlib deps, so it sits BENEATH both coordinators rather than beside either; fleet/commands keeps type aliases so the autosizer is untouched and its deletion removes only the aliases.

CORRECTED THE LEAD'S CONSUMER TABLE IN TWO PLACES: cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go is NOT a survivor (its only fleetCmd reference is the handler-registration command type, never the vocabulary); and TWO survivors were missed - adapters/expansion/idle_explorer_port.go and adapters/grpc/fleet_autosizer_yard_ports.go, the latter being what BOTH contract-scaler price readers wrap. PurchaseRequest turned out not to be coupled at all and was not moved. All four real survivors now import hullbuy and no longer import fleet/commands.

Dedicate-at-purchase asymmetry pinned TWICE (domain policy table + the real buy seam, where a light makes ZERO AssignFleet calls). defaultHeavyCap now one compile-time source shared by the autosizer fallback and sensing, mirroring ImmutableReserveFloor. 5 mutation probes each naming its kills. 87 packages ok, -race clean, zero new comment-audit violations.

title: [P1] UpsertMarketData's DELETE is player-scoped but its PRIMARY KEY is not — one dead-era row permanently prevents a market from ever being cached again
description:
A FAIL-CLOSED WRITE bug, which is why nobody was looking there. It cannot cause a spend against a
stale price; it silently removes a market from the bot's world instead.

THE DEFECT — internal/adapters/persistence/market_repository.go:37-70:

    tx.Where("player_id = ? AND waypoint_symbol = ?", playerID, waypointSymbol).Delete(&MarketData{})
    ...
    tx.Create(&marketDataRecords)   // PK is (waypoint_symbol, good_symbol) — NO player_id

The DELETE is PLAYER-SCOPED. The PRIMARY KEY is NOT. So if a dead-era row occupies the same
(waypoint_symbol, good_symbol), the delete misses it and the insert hits a duplicate-key violation.
The whole transaction rolls back, and THAT MARKET CAN NEVER BE CACHED FOR THE NEW ERA — permanently,
for as long as the stale row exists.

EXACT PATH: MarketScanner.ScanAndSaveMarketWithOutcome (application/ship/market_scanner.go:167-172)
-> UpsertMarketData (market_repository.go:30) -> tx.Create (:67) -> PK violation -> rollback ->
logger.Log(ERROR) -> return false, err.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE DOWNSTREAM: reads return zero rows, GetMarketData returns (nil, nil), and every
consumer fails closed EXACTLY AS IF THE MARKET WERE UNSCOUTED. Loud in the logs, indistinguishable
from 'not scanned yet' in behaviour. A scout would re-scan it forever and never make progress —
the failure looks like absence of data, which is the one thing the system is designed to tolerate.

REACHABILITY IS NOT SPECULATIVE; THE CODEBASE NAMES THIS EXACT CASE ELSEWHERE:
 - models_navigation.go:71-73 explains SystemCoordModel is keyed (era_id, symbol) precisely to stop
   'a dead era's coordinates from colliding with A RECURRING SYMBOL'.
 - ShipyardInventoryModel, in the SAME FILE as MarketData (models_market.go:153), carries era_id.
 - gate_edges, system_coords, scout_posts and the sensing tables all carry era_id.
 market_data is THE OUTLIER. Probability rises with every un-pruned era.

SCALE, measured in-repo rather than asserted: migrations/047_fix_market_price_transposition.up.sql:16-18
records market_data at 30,657 rows spanning 'every era back to player 1', of which only 3,343
belonged to the live player — roughly 27k dead-era rows. (NOTE: a separate claim of '6,353 of 6,383
waypoints / 39,352 stale rows' circulated during triage and could NOT be verified — prod is out of
scope and staging is a fresh era-1 with no stale rows. Same direction and magnitude, different
figures. Do not cite the unverified numbers.)

READS ARE SAFE — established, not assumed, and worth recording so nobody re-investigates it:
every market_data read carries player_id = ?, and in every ranking/aggregate the player partition is
applied BEFORE the ORDER BY / MIN / MAX / DISTINCT ON. All six ranked queries in
persistence/market_selection_repository.go verified line by line (:29, :83, :117, :157, :232 which
also has a freshness cutoff, :341). A sweep for market_data queries lacking player_id returns exactly
two sites, neither a quote path: metrics/market_metrics.go:272 (deliberately enumerates player_id,
returns no prices) and era_repository.go:224 (the truncate). Coverage/freshness metrics
(briefing_source.go:317, :356) are player-scoped too. So a stale row can be selected by NAME or by
RANKING: neither.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. The write can no longer collide across eras. Preferred: add era_id to MarketData and to its
   primary key, matching ShipyardInventoryModel in the same file and SystemCoordModel's stated
   rationale. Alternative: make the DELETE match the PK's scope. Whichever is chosen, the DELETE's
   scope and the PK's scope MUST agree — that disagreement IS the bug.
2. Test the collision directly: seed a dead-era row at (waypoint, good), scan that market as the live
   player, assert the upsert SUCCEEDS and the live row is readable. Against unmodified code this test
   fails with a duplicate-key violation.
3. Regression: a normal upsert with no stale row present is unchanged.
4. Reads stay player-correct — the existing player_id scoping must not be weakened while adding era
   scoping. A test should assert a dead-era row is still never returned.
5. Consider a migration to prune existing dead-era rows, but do NOT let pruning substitute for the
   key fix — pruning cures today's instances, the key disagreement causes tomorrow's.

RELATED: sp-nkzq1 (the false comments asserting truncation makes this safe). Found by the sp-20eyn
lane, which verified the premise it was handed rather than inheriting it.
notes:
CROSS-REFERENCE CORRECTION: the description's 'RELATED: sp-nkzq1' is a bead ID I wrote before the
companion existed and it does not resolve. The false-truncation-comment bead is **sp-hrko6**.
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main 99c50774 (lane 7839c72c). PK is now (player_id, waypoint_symbol, good_symbol).
Gate: GatePassed:true Stale:false Merged:true EmptyMerge:false; verified in main — 3 primaryKey fields on
MarketData and repairMarketDataPrimaryKey present.

=== THIS BEAD'S OWN CRITERION 1 WAS WRONG, AND THE LANE WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE IT ===
I (captain) wrote 'add era_id to the primary key, matching ShipyardInventoryModel in the same file'.
I had NOT read ShipyardInventoryModel. Its key is:
    PlayerID       int    primaryKey
    WaypointSymbol string primaryKey
    ShipType       string primaryKey
    EraID          *int   index:idx_shipyard_inventory_era     <-- NULLABLE, NOT IN THE KEY
The precedent I cited argues for exactly the change the lane made — player_id + natural key — and
against the one I asked for. Verified directly before gating.
Three further reasons the lane gave, each sufficient:
 1. A NULLABLE column cannot participate in a Postgres primary key. era_id-in-the-key would first
    need a NOT NULL backfill of ~27k historical rows through the player->era mapping, including rows
    whose player has no era — precisely the risky populated-table migration the lane was told to stop
    on and report rather than push through. It stopped and reported. Correct call.
 2. era_id would not satisfy this bead's OWN core requirement. What must agree is the DELETE's scope
    and the key's scope. The DELETE is scoped player_id; era_id fixes the collision only INDIRECTLY
    via era being 1:1 with player, leaving key and DELETE expressed in different terms.
 3. player_id is already on the table, already NOT NULL, already indexed, and already the scope of
    the DELETE and of all 26 reads.
LESSON, worth more than the fix: do not cite a precedent into an acceptance criterion without
reading it. A wrong criterion in a bead is worse than none — it directs a competent lane at the
wrong design and costs them the work of refusing it.

=== THE ARMING TRAP WAS THE REAL WORK (sp-w3he / closed-is-not-armed class) ===
GORM's AutoMigrate adds columns and indexes but WILL NOT ALTER AN EXISTING TABLE'S PRIMARY KEY. The
struct-tag change alone would have left production on the old key while the code claimed otherwise —
dormant exactly where the data is, and passing every test, because tests create the table fresh.
repairMarketDataPrimaryKey therefore runs inside AutoMigrate, reads the live catalog, and widens only
if still narrow. Migration 052 is the operator-run equivalent; each no-ops once the other has run.

WIDENING IS SAFE IN A WAY NARROWING IS NOT: old key (waypoint, good) is a strict SUBSET of the new,
so old-key uniqueness already implies new-key uniqueness — it can never fail on duplicates. DROP and
ADD are ONE statement so the table is never momentarily unconstrained, and nothing references
market_data. The DOWN migration is the opposite case and refuses: it counts colliding pairs and
RAISEs rather than silently destroying one row per pair, and notes that boot AutoMigrate re-applies
the widening so a rollback is only meaningful as part of a coordinated daemon revert. Verified by
reading it.

ACCEPTED SCOPE EXPANSION, flagged by the lane for my call and taken: boot AutoMigrate is documented
'additive... never destructive' and this widens it to include one constraint replacement. No rows are
touched, the operation is atomic, and the alternative is a fix inert in production — which is worse.

MUTATION-VERIFIED. Reverting player_id out of the key kills the collision test, the cross-era
invisibility test and the key-shape assertion, with the exact predicted failure
'UNIQUE constraint failed: market_data.waypoint_symbol, market_data.good_symbol'. Two tests correctly
SURVIVE and the lane said so rather than counting them: the unchanged-behaviour regression and a
sqlite no-op check. That regression is also the calibration — a 'fix' so wide that a re-scan APPENDED
instead of replacing would pass the collision test and quietly break the cache.

READS WERE ALREADY SAFE AND STAY SO: all six ranked queries apply player_id before the ORDER BY /
MIN / MAX / DISTINCT ON, so a stale row is selectable neither by name nor by ranking. A test asserts
the dead-era row is still never returned AND still EXISTS — this widens a key, it does not delete
another era's history.

KNOWN GAP, stated rather than papered over: the Postgres DDL path has no automated test, because
tests run on sqlite which cannot ALTER a primary key — which is why the repair is Postgres-only.
Tested instead: the repair is a clean no-op on a correct schema, and the key parses as intended.

NO DEAD-ERA PRUNING, deliberately: pruning cures today's instances, the key change stops tomorrow's,
and TransitionEra documents an intent to RETAIN prior-era market rows ('truncating would destroy the
prior era's charts'). Discarding them is a separate decision with a separate owner.

title: EPIC: replace the fleet autosizer with a wave-based fleet-growth coordinator (probe/heavy alternation)
description:
Design epic. Replaces the fleet autosizer with a fleet-growth coordinator that alternates probe buying (frontier charting/scanning) and heavy-hull buying (trade capacity) in waves, driven by one live signal.

CORE INSIGHT: unserved_lanes = profitable_lanes - trade_hulls (floored at 0) oscillates on its own. Buying heavies drives it to 0 (switch to probes); buying probes charts more markets, raising profitable_lanes (switch back to heavies). No target counts, no era-scaled constants.

WHY WAVES AND NOT INTERLEAVING: a heavy is a lump (~1.5M on era-5 evidence), probes are a trickle. Continuous probe buying means treasury never accumulates enough for a heavy. Pausing probe buying is what makes the lump reachable.

DECISIONS TAKEN IN BRAINSTORM (2026-08-05, with the Admiral):
1. Delete the autosizer entirely. Verified proportionate: of its four classes, light is dead (only gate-factory remains, owned by the construction coordinator), contract_delivery is pinned at 4/4 hulls, explorer has NEVER had a single hull in either database. Its only live job is the trade pool.
2. Switch signal is utilization (lane-limited vs capacity-limited), NOT fixed targets or marginal-return modelling. The signal already exists and is wired: HeavyDemandProvider + autosizerHeavySources.UnservedLaneCount, read-only off the market cache via trading.RankSpreads.
3. Working capital floor = max(runway_hours x observed_cargo_spend_per_hour, trade_hulls x observed_typical_hold_fill_cost). Both terms derived from observed transactions - no hardcoded prices, which have swung 55% across eras 3-5.
4. Home: a NEW long-running fleet-growth coordinator dropping into the autosizer's container slot. NOT probe-sensing (already the biggest package) and NOT a fifth bootstrap phase (bootstrap's exit is load-bearing - it avoids a per-tick fully-paginated fleet re-read against an account-wide ceiling).
5. RETIRE off-gate warp expansion entirely. No explorers. This makes the gate network the permanent reachable universe.

FULL DESIGN: see the spec doc this epic produces.

NOT YET DECIDED / for the plan: hysteresis details, exact runway_hours value and how typical_hold_fill_cost is derived, migration ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec written to docs/superpowers/specs/ and committed. Spec covers: wave predicate (derived not stored), working-capital formula, coordinator architecture with the one-definition-two-consumers lockstep idiom, off-gate retirement including the latching explorer-demand bridge, testing strategy, and migration path. No implementation.
notes:
PLAN A COMPLETE 2026-08-06/07 — all six tasks merged.
  48910312  T1 the wave predicate
  f23e4f51  T2 the ledger observation surface (cargo outflow, high-water treasury, working capital)
  935432f4  T3 shared unserved-lane read + working-capital guard term + kept-surface renames
  7578f332  T4 the fleet-growth coordinator becomes the fleet's heavy buyer
  4e0408fd  T5 move the heavy-yard pricing errand onto the growth coordinator
  de70cd91  T6 wire the wave into the probe drain

EVERY task came back CHANGES_REQUIRED on first adversarial review; every one was fixed and re-approved. The reviews found four things the plan itself got wrong, none discoverable from the plan text:
 (1) T4 shipped NO LAUNCH SURFACE — the atomic commit switched the autosizer's heavy class off and repointed HeavyBuyerContainers at a container type with zero callers (no RPC, no CLI verb, no auto-launch). Deployed as written it would have stopped heavy buying fleet-wide with no recourse, and the atomicity argument INVERTS: the window that must never open would never close. Fixed by adding proto RPC + workflow verb + bootstrap LaunchStandingCoordinators — and the fixer correctly DECLINED my instruction to retarget LaunchAutosizer, because that would stop the autosizer launching (which Plan A's end state requires for its light class) and invert obs.AutosizerRunning; my literal instruction WAS the 'needs something Plan B owns' case.
 (2) Fixing that exposed a race with NINE call sites across five files: firstContainerIDOfType read the two live container statuses as SEPARATE queries, so a container promoted PENDING->RUNNING between them was in neither result — and a launch is exactly that transition. Long-haul, scout posts, auto-outfit, shipyard backfill and both bootstrap hand-offs all inherited it. Residual (check-then-act with no unique index) filed as sp-a7sdr.
 (3) T6's first cut RE-CREATED sp-zg71k's deadlock one layer up: buyerConfig returns buyerExists=true for a knob-carrying STRANGER, growthSwitchOn read only the bare growth_enabled key off that stranger's config, and ABSENT KEY = ON — so the wave derived HEAVY and binary-paused every probe purchase for a buyer that does not exist. Worse than the original, which only withheld credits.
 (4) T3 Step 4 instructed deleting distinctShipSystems as 'now-unused'. FALSE — three live non-test callers. Correctly not deleted.

CARRIED RULINGS, all implemented: Reachable(target, liveTreasury) COMPILES so the port must be asserted to read MAX(balance_after) OVER THE WINDOW (no test in package common can catch that wiring error); the SHIPPED reason constants win over the plan's prose and are now mechanically pinned; WaveProbeReasonNone stays '' as a Go constant but the metric emits reason='none', because a PromQL reason='' selector also matches series LACKING the label.

OUTSTANDING — the expansion_enabled=2 override I set by hand on staging is STILL IN PLACE. Task 6 deliberately did not remove it; that is an operational post-deploy step. Probe buying stays frozen until it is lifted, and it must not be lifted before Task 6 is deployed or probe buying resumes with nothing waving it.

title: [P1] containers table has NO retention policy and findContainerModelByID linear-scans it — 34,279 rows loaded into Go memory on every worker start
description:
Two aggravating factors found by the sp-20eyn lane while diagnosing the 24h prod outage. Neither
caused it; both made it worse and both outlive it.

1. NO RETENTION POLICY. The containers table accumulates forever. Prod holds 34,279 FAILED rows from
   the sp-20eyn crash loop alone, plus 30,016 STOPPED and 18,876 COMPLETED. Nothing prunes them.

2. findContainerModelByID calls ListAll(ctx, nil) with NO status filter and then linear-scans in Go.
   At 34k rows that loads the ENTIRE table on every worker start. The two compose: the crash loop
   inflated the table, and the inflated table made every subsequent worker start more expensive —
   a slow feedback loop on the exact path that was already failing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A retention policy prunes terminal containers (FAILED/STOPPED/COMPLETED) beyond a bounded age or
   count. Justify the bound; keep enough history for forensics — the 34,279 count was itself the
   evidence that identified the crash loop, so do not prune so aggressively that a future incident
   becomes invisible.
2. findContainerModelByID filters in SQL rather than loading and scanning in Go. Assert the query
   shape, not just the result.
3. Regression: existing container lookups behave identically.
4. Measure before/after on a table of realistic size — a fix that is invisible at 100 rows is not
   verified for 34,000.

RELATED: sp-20eyn (created the 34k rows and was slowed by them).
close_reason:
BOTH HALVES FIXED AND MERGED: query fix as main b4797bcb, retention as main fe498f80.

QUERY FIX, measured at the size prod actually reached (34,000 rows, like-for-like):
    before — ListAll + Go scan   78.9ms   34,000 rows read
    after  — indexed lookup      74.9us        1 row read
The row count is what matters: it no longer depends on table size at all. No new index and no schema
change — the PK is (id, player_id) and id LEADS it, so it is a prefix match the existing index
already serves. findContainerModelByID was the ONLY caller of ListAll on containers, so this removed
the last unbounded full-table read from the per-worker-start path.
The test asserts SHAPE, not result, and says why: a result-only assertion passes just as happily
against the full scan, because the scan does find the right container. It captures executed SQL and
asserts one row read — AND asserts the OLD shape still reads all 34,000, so green means 'measured',
not 'fixture too small to tell'.

RETENTION: 14-day age bound, terminal statuses only, no count cap, swept once at start then every
24h.

THE DESIGN TENSION AND WHAT DISSOLVED IT — this is the part worth carrying forward. I set two goals
that appeared opposed: bound the table, and do not destroy the evidence a future incident needs
(the 34,279 count was itself what identified the crash loop). A 7-day age bound does not bound a
pathological loop; a count cap that does bound it evicts oldest-first and destroys the BEGINNING of
an incident, the most valuable part. THEY ONLY CONFLICT IF THE ROWS ARE THE EVIDENCE. They are not:
container_total{status} is a registered counter, so the incident signal lives in Prometheus on its
own retention while the rows carry per-container detail useful only recently. The lane found that
reframing; it is better than either answer I would have chosen.

Start-sweep matters as much as the interval: a daemon restarting more often than 24h would otherwise
never prune, and a crash-looping daemon is precisely the condition that fills this table.

CONTRACT ASSERTED FIRST: age alone insufficient, status alone insufficient, only both. The test
seeds an OLD RUNNING, INTERRUPTED, PENDING and STOPPING row beside a RECENT FAILED, STOPPED and
COMPLETED one and requires all seven to survive — including INTERRUPTED, the restart-recovery queue,
which I had not named.

OBSERVABILITY as required: per-status breakdown logged and container_retention_deleted_total{status}
emitted, INCLUDING empty sweeps, so FAILED=0 ('ran, found nothing') never reads as silence ('may not
have run'). A sweep failing midway still reports what it deleted.

A PROBE CAUGHT DEAD CODE IN THE FIX ITSELF. The 'IS NOT NULL' guard for undatable rows SURVIVED its
mutation. Rather than assume a weak test the lane checked with a SQL harness: NULL < cutoff is NULL,
not TRUE, so the age predicate already excluded those rows — the clause was inert while reading as a
safety guarantee. Kept (it becomes load-bearing if anyone gives that COALESCE a non-NULL final
argument, which would silently turn every undatable row into an old one) with its comment corrected
to say where the protection actually comes from. Third instance this session of 'declared is not the
same as working'.

CAPTAIN DECISION — UNSCOPED BY PLAYER: retention now removes prior-era container rows that
TransitionEra leaves in place, a small behaviour change beyond this bead's wording. Judged correct:
'universe scrub' already deletes a closed era's containers wholesale, so the codebase has taken the
position that these rows are disposable; a 14-day-old dead-era row has no more diagnostic value than
a live-era one; and the counter preserves the signal regardless. TransitionEra's retention intent
concerns MARKET data ('truncating would destroy the prior era's charts') — analytical history, a
different class from operational debris.

CONSIDERED AND DECLINED with the number: an index on status. 880us across 34k rows twice per boot,
retention bounds the table further, and an index charges every container write.

title: [P1] No watcher for 'agent has zero transactions while every coordinator is healthy' — the exact signature of the 24h prod outage, and nothing can see it
description:
sp-20eyn criterion 6b, deliberately not done inside that lane because nothing in the contract pipeline can observe it.

THE GAP: prod TORWIND produced ZERO transactions for 24+ hours while the daemon was alive, all 10
coordinators heartbeat CURRENT, and containers restarted successfully. Every existing recovery path
is keyed on something being DOWN. Nothing was down. The outage was invisible to instrumentation and
was found only because a human asked.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a watcher OUTSIDE the pipeline — watchkeeper or a Prometheus alert rule — that fires
on the conjunction: transactions == 0 over M minutes AND coordinators heartbeating. Neither half
alone is a signal: a healthy idle fleet has quiet stretches, and a dead daemon is already covered.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Fires on the conjunction, not either half alone.
2. Chosen M is justified against the observed quiet-but-healthy distribution, not picked round. Note
   staging legitimately went ~3.6h without a FAB_MATS purchase while healthy, so a naive threshold
   on a single good would have false-fired; the signal must be ALL transactions for the agent.
3. Does not fire during a legitimate cold start before the first trade.
4. Sited where it can actually observe both facts — the contract pipeline cannot.

RELATED: sp-20eyn (the outage this would have caught).
notes:
SCOPE CLARIFICATION 2026-08-06: this bead does NOT cover the pipeline-grain stalls seen today, and
should not be closed as though it did. This watches for an agent with ZERO transactions while
coordinators are healthy. In all three of today's gate stalls the agent was transacting normally —
contract earned +590,348 during one of them — while a SINGLE PIPELINE was stopped for hours. Both
checks are needed; they are siblings at different grains. The pipeline-grain watchdog is filed
separately.
LANE DESIGN 2026-08-06. NO CODE WRITTEN — the natural home is a PROTECTED PATH; stopped for
authorisation. Everything below is measured, not inherited.

THE CONJUNCTION, VERIFIED FROM DATA (not taken from the bead). Prod player 6, the outage window
2026-08-05 00:43:43 -> 2026-08-06 01:37:09 (1,493.4 min = 24.9h) is that player's ONLY inter-
transaction gap over 60 minutes in its whole history. Across the SAME window container_logs holds
18,025 lines from 102 distinct containers, continuous from the first second to the last. Both halves
of the conjunction confirmed independently: coordinators demonstrably working, agent transacting
zero.

CRITERION 2 — M, JUSTIFIED AGAINST THREE INDEPENDENT HEALTHY BASELINES (max inter-transaction gap,
ALL transaction types, per the bead's own warning against a single good):
  prod player 6, outage excluded   58.4 min   (n=175)
  prod player 5, 55,449 txns/3d    55.7 min
  staging player 1, 4,485 txns/42h 107.8 min
  HEALTHY MAX OBSERVED             108 min  |  THE OUTAGE  1,493 min  (13.8x)
RECOMMEND M = 4h. That is 2.2x the observed healthy max, and still fires ~21h before this outage
was found by a human asking. The separation is so wide that anything in 3h-8h works; 4h is chosen
for margin because the total sample is only ~1 week and 108 min is a MAX, not a percentile — the
true tail is unmeasured. Even 6h would be a 4x improvement on 24h. NOT a round number picked for
tidiness, but also not a tight one: the cost asymmetry (a false fire burns a captain session; a
miss costs a day of trading) argues for margin.

CRITERION 3 — COLD START. Anchor the precondition on "this player has EVER transacted", not on
process uptime. A fresh era has zero transactions AND healthy coordinators by definition, which is
byte-identical to the outage signature. Uptime is the wrong anchor because it resets on every
restart and would re-arm a false window after each deploy.

CRITERION 4 — SITING. Prometheus is BLOCKED TWICE OVER, so the bead's "or a Prometheus alert rule"
is not currently an option:
  (a) No coordinator-heartbeat metric exists. The transactions half does (transactionsTotal, fed
      via RecordTransactionHandler at record_transaction.go:184 — verified, not assumed). The
      health half has no metric at all.
  (b) There is NO alert-evaluation pipeline. deploy/staging/monitoring/prometheus.staging.yml has
      no rule_files and no alerting/alertmanagers block; it scrapes and stores only. Nothing
      evaluates a rule and nothing routes one. Building that is far larger than this bead.
The WATCHKEEPER is the correct home: it reads both facts straight from the DB (transactions +
containers.heartbeat_at), it already has the detector framework, the HasSince cooldown idiom and
event emission, and it runs as a SEPARATE PROCESS under launchd with KeepAlive=true — supervised
from outside itself.

FATE-SHARING. The watchkeeper is right precisely BECAUSE it does not share fate with the daemon.
A watcher of "zero transactions" placed inside the daemon would be the mistake: the daemon is the
thing whose trading stopped. Residual, stated rather than hidden: launchd restarts a DEAD
watchkeeper but cannot detect a WEDGED one, so a hung watchkeeper is still a silent single point.
That is a smaller hole than the one this bead closes, not a reason to site it elsewhere.

THE BLOCKER. cmd/watchkeeper/main.go is a 118-line shell; the detector logic AND the sequential
dispatch list are in internal/captain/detectors.go (lines 220-223, calling detectStaleHeartbeats
and detectIdleShips). Adding a detector means editing internal/captain/** — PROTECTED. Stopped and
escalated rather than edited.

GRAIN — WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT COVER, VERIFIED. During today's 2h33m sp-lpy9i gate block
(09:51:39-12:24:12) the agent made 223 transactions across FOUR operation types
(construction_supply, contract, manual, tour) with a max gap of 43.9 min. An agent-grain watcher at
any defensible M is CORRECTLY SILENT there. Only the pipeline-grain watchdog (sp-63r4f/sp-zx0tu)
catches that class. The two are siblings at different grains, and neither substitutes for the
other: this one would also miss a stalled pipeline, and that one would miss this outage if every
pipeline were satisfied or absent.
=== LANE sp-16zxm DELIVERED as a Prometheus rule — commit 158acaf3, NO protected path touched ===

CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR LANE'S SITING CONCLUSION. Both "BLOCKED TWICE OVER" blockers are false
at base 7e2a201a, verified by direct read:
 (a) A coordinator-health metric DOES exist: spacetraders_daemon_container_running_total
     {player_id,container_type} (container_metrics.go:84, Reset()+Set(1) each scrape). The
     already-shipped EarnerDark rule uses it as exactly this conjunction's health half.
 (b) An alert-evaluation pipeline DOES exist: prometheus.yml:12 carries rule_files, and sp-y0f6
     shipped AND deployed the routing (Prometheus evaluates -> watchkeeper polls /api/v1/alerts
     -> prometheus.alert_firing -> captain wake).
 The file the notes cite, deploy/staging/monitoring/prometheus.staging.yml, does not exist;
 the real config is gobot/configs/prometheus/. Because the poller picks up ANY rule in
 fleet-health.yml, the watchkeeper detector edit is unnecessary — internal/captain/** untouched.

CORRECTION TO M. The prior derivation put HEALTHY MAX OBSERVED at 108 min and recommended
M=4h. That came from scoping prod player 5 to 3 days. Over player 5's FULL history the max
inter-transaction gap is 479.07 min (8.0h), so M=4h would have FALSE-FIRED on era 5's bootstrap.

Gap distribution, live Postgres, ALL transaction types, per player_id:
  player   n_gaps    p50    p90     p99   p99.9      max
  prod 5   76,142   0.04   0.27    1.17    3.44   479.07 min
  prod 4   26,993   0.10   0.75    2.72   25.69   226.78 min
  prod 3   52,858   0.05   0.41    1.54    3.70   104.83 min
  stg  1    5,149   0.05   1.11    3.44   51.73   107.82 min
  prod 6      177   0.97   2.63  259.63 1388.45  1493.43 min (contains the outage)

The tail is STRUCTURAL: every gap over ~2.5h sits at an ERA BOUNDARY. Prod 5's 479 min is 2.5h
into a 7-day era that went on to do 76k transactions (bootstrap). Prod 4's 226.8 min is its
era's final 4.5h (wind-down); its mid-era max is 150.5 min. Steady-state healthy max: 150.5 min.

CRITERION 3 CANNOT BE MET BY TIGHTENING THE HEALTH CLAUSE — measured, not assumed. During prod
5's 8.0h bootstrap gap the container complement was 10, identical to the 9-11 running throughout
the outage. Both halves of the conjunction are byte-identical between bootstrap and outage, so
the WINDOW must clear the longest healthy bootstrap. M = 12h = 1.5x the observed 8.0h max
(corpus ~5 eras / 5 weeks; 8.0h is a max not a percentile, so margin is deliberate).

ERA SCOPING (the bead did not raise this; it is load-bearing). A retired era keeps 2-5 containers
running indefinitely and never trades again. Without a bound, prod 5 paged for 20.7h after
retirement. A 24h liveness clause scopes to the live era WITHOUT pinning a player_id — pinning
one would silently stop watching at the next rollover. Post-retirement paging: 11.8h.

VALIDATION (exact expression parsed from the shipped file, query_range vs live Prometheus, 15d
retention, 600s step, for:30m applied):
  FIRES  the 24.9h outage — first sustained fire 2026-08-05 13:00Z, 12.3h after the last
         transaction and 12.6h BEFORE a human found it.
  FIRES  a SECOND, previously unreported prod dark period: 2026-08-06 01:38Z -> 16:35Z (15.0h),
         first sustained fire 10:20Z. Prod player 6 has now had two multi-hour dark periods.
  SILENT prod 5 bootstrap (8.0h, full complement) / prod 5 steady state 4d / prod 4 tail.
  promtool check rules -> SUCCESS: 6 rules found (RC=0), throwaway container; live Prometheus
  never reloaded or restarted.

RESIDUALS, stated not hidden:
 1. A daemon restart truncates the counter's visible history, so after a restart the effective
    window is "time since restart" and the rule can fire earlier than M. Harmless here (it only
    increases sensitivity) but it could re-admit a bootstrap false fire if a restart lands inside
    a bootstrap quiet period.
 2. Paging window is M..liveness (12h..24h of darkness). If nobody acts within 24h the alert
    self-silences.
 3. Not deployed: Prometheus must reload to pick up the rule. Left to the lead per dispatch.
=== STAGING WIRING — commit 29fb93d1 (branch now: 0452d250 rule + 29fb93d1 wiring, on main ebde3d5e) ===

THE RULE COULD NEVER FIRE AS FIRST DELIVERED. Staging is the system that actually runs, and the

title: [P1] fleet_autosizer_ports captures the API budget tracker at WIRING time, not per tick — a main.go reorder would silently capture nil and wedge all hull growth
description:
Found by the sp-fr19d lane while fixing the api_util window, and correctly NOT fixed there.

gobot/internal/adapters/.../fleet_autosizer_ports.go:72 captures the API budget tracker POINTER at
wiring time rather than re-reading the global per tick.

SAFE TODAY, PURELY BY ORDERING: main.go:778 (tracker construction) precedes main.go:1196 (autosizer
wiring). Nothing enforces or documents that dependency.

THE FAILURE MODE IF IT EVER REVERSES: the port captures nil. GuardAPIUtil's nil reader fails CLOSED
at three nested levels — which is correct as a guard, and is exactly why this would be so hard to
see: the fleet would simply stop growing, everywhere, permanently, with no error. A silent
total-stop that looks like 'the autosizer decided not to grow'.

THIS IS THE sp-ps2oc CLASS. There, NewSpendReservationLedger was never constructed outside its own
test and SetSpendLedger had no production call site, so a money cap fail-opened on every gate buy
ever made — invisible until forensic ledger archaeology. Same shape: a wiring assumption that
nothing pins, whose failure is silent. sp-ps2oc was closed with an AST guard
(spend_ledger_wiring_test.go) precisely so it could not silently disappear again; this deserves the
same treatment.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. The port re-reads the tracker at USE time rather than capturing it at wiring time, OR the
   ordering dependency is pinned by a test that fails if main.go is reordered.
2. Prefer the AST-guard pattern already established by spend_ledger_wiring_test.go if a structural
   pin is chosen — it is the precedent and it works.
3. Test: construct the port BEFORE the tracker exists and assert the guard still resolves a live
   tracker at call time (or that the build/test fails loudly, if the ordering pin is the chosen fix).
4. Regression: the normal ordering is unchanged and the guard behaves byte-identically once warm.
5. Do NOT weaken the nil-reader fail-closed behaviour — it is correct (RULINGS #4). The bug is that
   nil is reachable by accident, not that nil fails closed.

RELATED: sp-fr19d (the window fix, same file family), sp-ps2oc (the same class, already fixed with
an AST pin worth copying), sp-773i0 (composition-root setters are unpinned — likely the general
form of this).
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main 1c626d95 (lane 582dc116). Gate: GatePassed:true Stale:false Merged:true
EmptyMerge:false; resolver confirmed in main. go vet rc=0, go test rc=0, 87 packages, 0 FAIL (61s
cold) — verified independently by exit code and wall time.

BOTH FIXES WERE TAKEN, and the lane was right that they are not alternatives — I offered them as
either/or and that framing was wrong:
  RESOLVER  the reader now holds 'resolve func() apiBudgetReporter' instead of a tracker, wired
            with the accessor passed UNCALLED. The field CANNOT HOLD a wiring-time pointer, so the
            bug is unexpressible in the type rather than merely absent from this instance. It also
            degrades better in the reversed world: a nil read is transient and self-heals next
            tick, where a captured nil was permanent for process life.
  AST PIN   delete the SetAPIUtilizationReader call and you get the IDENTICAL silent total-stop.
            That is exactly how sp-ps2oc lost its money cap — to a refactor of an unrelated
            operation. No resolver design prevents a deleted call; only a check at the composition
            point sees it. Follows spend_ledger_wiring_test.go, the precedent that closed sp-ps2oc.

THE MOST VALUABLE PART WAS A HOLE THE LANE FOUND WHILE PROBING ITS OWN FIX. Its first mutation
attempt was an INFRA FAILURE and it reported it as one rather than counting the zero: reverting the
production type stopped the package compiling, so '0 killed' meant nothing. Redoing it honestly
exposed a real gap — a resolver that CLOSES OVER a wiring-time read:
    captured := globalAPIBudgetReporter()
    ...{resolve: func() apiBudgetReporter { return captured }}
sets only 'resolve', COMPILES, and is the original defect wearing the fix's clothes. A field-name
check passes it, and the behavioural tests cannot see it because they construct their own reader.
The analyser now also pins that 'resolve' is the NAMED FUNCTION PASSED UNCALLED — a closure or call
expression evaluates at wiring time by construction. Without that the pin looks complete and is not.
This is the second time this session a probe's INFRA failure, honestly reported instead of scored,
turned into the finding that mattered.

Also handled explicitly: the typed-nil trap. GetGlobalAPIBudgetTracker returns a concrete
*APIBudgetTracker, and assigning a nil one into an interface yields a NON-nil interface. Documented
rather than tripped over.

RULINGS #4 intact — the acceptance test's FIRST assertion is that a genuinely absent tracker still
reads readable=false. The bug was that nil is reachable by accident, never that nil fails closed.

Every defect shape is a named subtest: setter deleted (sp-ps2oc shape), bare nil reader, typed-nil
reader, the original captured pointer, a factory-built resolver, a resolver with a cached tracker
alongside it, and the closure capture.

CARRIED FORWARD: main gained 5f1d71f9, a DOCS-ONLY spec proposing to replace the autosizer with
probe/heavy alternation. Nothing is implemented so this fix stands — but if that design lands, the
api_util guard may move and THIS PIN MUST MOVE WITH IT rather than being quietly deleted. Noted on
sp-773i0 along with the generalised pattern: prefer the resolver where the shape allows, add the
AST pin regardless, carry the closure-capture trap into the general form, and note that this whole
class is invisible PRECISELY BECAUSE the downstream guard fails closed correctly — so any setter
feeding a fail-closed guard belongs in that bead's scope.

title: Gate feed picks inputs by plan ORDER, not by how short the terminal factory actually is — needs an import-supply seam
description:
FOLLOW-UP TO sp-9eor3 (criterion 6 / description criterion 3), deliberately NOT done in that P0 hotfix.

sp-9eor3 fixed the HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCK: an unaffordable step is now a fourth `continue` in
planGateFeed, so the walk skips it and feeds the next affordable step instead of ending the leg.
What it did NOT do is change the ORDER the walk considers steps in. planGateFeed still takes the
FIRST step that passes every guard, and gate.PlanFeed's order is recipe order, not need order.

So ordering still encodes priority by accident. In the incident, F45 read:
    IRON              IMPORT  supply=MODERATE   <-- already adequate, planned FIRST
    QUARTZ_SAND       IMPORT  supply=SCARCE
    SILICON_CRYSTALS  IMPORT  supply=SCARCE
    COPPER            IMPORT  supply=SCARCE
When IRON is affordable, it is still chosen ahead of three co-inputs the factory is genuinely
starved of. sp-9eor3 only removes the case where IRON is UNAFFORDABLE. An affordable-but-unneeded
input still wins.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN THE HOTFIX — IT NEEDS A NEW SEAM, AND THE OBVIOUS SHORTCUTS ARE WRONG.
The quantity to rank on is "the terminal factory's IMPORT supply level of the INPUT good".
GateFactoryTopology (run_construction_coordinator_gate_delivery.go) exposes only:
    TerminalFactory(good, system, playerID) / IsRaw(good) / Inputs(good)
and NEITHER value already in hand is that quantity:
  - source.Supply is the EXPORT supply of the input at the SOURCE market (H51's IRON = SCARCE)
  - target.Supply is the target factory's own EXPORT supply of its OUTPUT (F45's FAB_MATS)
Ranking on either is a plausible-looking wrong fix that would read as working. Ranking on
source.Supply would be actively perverse here: it would PREFER IRON precisely because the market we
buy it from is scarce, which is the opposite of the intent.

WHAT IT NEEDS
1. A seam that reads a specific waypoint's IMPORT listing for a specific good — supply level at
   minimum. Likely a method on GateFactoryTopology or a narrow sibling interface, plus the
   compile-time conformance assertion the file already keeps for its other four seams.
2. Rank candidate steps by that supply level (SCARCE first), replacing "first passing step wins".
   Note this means PRICING/RESOLVING MORE STEPS PER LEG than today's short-circuit walk does —
   the ABUNDANT fail-safe's comment ("It precedes the SOURCE lookup, so a declined step never
   prices an input it will not buy") shows the file deliberately avoids that, so the cost needs
   accounting for rather than assuming.
3. ONE BUY PER LEG MUST SURVIVE. It is the only bound on factory-fleet spend (an INPUT has no
   bill). Pinned by TestFeedGateLeg_BuysExactlyOnceEvenThoughThePlanHasSeveralSteps.

TEST (from sp-9eor3's brief, deferred with it): terminal factory reads MODERATE on the step-1
input and SCARCE on the step-2 input, BOTH affordable; assert step 2 is chosen. That test fails
against the code sp-9eor3 shipped, which is exactly why this is a separate bead and not a claim
sp-9eor3 can make.

FILES: gobot/internal/application/manufacturing/commands/run_construction_coordinator_gate_feed.go
       (planGateFeed), and the GateFactoryTopology interface in
       run_construction_coordinator_gate_delivery.go
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main 3467cf6f (lane 66d2018a). Gate: GatePassed:true Merged:true EmptyMerge:false; diffstat verified as 6 files / +575 / -3 with ImportSupply present in main.

THE SEAM, AND WHY NEITHER EXISTING VALUE WOULD DO — this was the bead's whole difficulty and the
lane confirmed it by mutation rather than by argument:
  TerminalFactory(input).Supply  = the SOURCE's EXPORT supply. Ranking on it prefers an input
                                   BECAUSE it is hard to buy — actively perverse, and exactly the
                                   trap flagged when this was deferred out of sp-9eor3.
  TerminalFactory(target).Supply = the target's EXPORT supply of its own OUTPUT. That is the
                                   ABUNDANT fail-safe's subject ('does this factory need feeding
                                   at all'), never 'which input is it shortest of'.
Only the destination's own IMPORT listing answers it, and no searching locator can reach it:
FindImportMarket returns the system's BEST importer, a different waypoint whenever the resolved
factory is not it — so the answer would silently describe some other market.
MarketLocator.TradeGoodAt reads ONE resolved waypoint's listing, as a thin export of the existing
scannedTradeGood — one market read in that file, not two that can drift, and no new API cost.
GateTopology.ImportSupply turns it into a level, IMPORT listings only. Declared on
GateFactoryTopology, so it is a compile-time obligation rather than a wiring step.

WHY THIS IS NOT RISKIER THAN THE ORDERING IT REPLACES — the property, not a promise:
PLAN ORDER IS THE FALLBACK, EXACTLY. The sort is STABLE and every unreadable step TIES, so with
no market data the resulting order is byte-identical to plan order. The evidence is that ALL 26
PRE-EXISTING feed-leg tests passed unchanged the moment the ranking went in, before a single new
test was written. Ties also preserve shallowest-first, which plan order already encodes and which
TestFeedGateLeg_FeedsTheTerminalFactoryBeforeAnythingDeeper pins — that test was the lane's
stop-and-report trigger and never went red.
UNKNOWN RANKS AS THE LADDER'S MIDDLE, deliberately: sorting unknown FIRST lets one unscanned
market capture every leg; sorting it LAST starves any factory with a stale listing.
COST: two passes. The cheap declines (no destination, ABUNDANT) filter every step first; only
survivors are ranked; source resolution and treasury pricing then run in ranked order and stop at
the first pass. An ABUNDANT target is never ranked into the queue, so the fail-safe's guarantee
that a declined step never prices an input it will not buy still holds.

MUTATION-VERIFIED. Making the sort inert (= plan order) kills 5:
  FeedsTheInputTheFactoryIsShortestOfNotTheFirstInTheRecipe   (the bead)
  RanksOnTheFactorysImportSupplyNotTheSourcesExportSupply
  AnUnreadableListingDoesNotOutrankAReadableOne  (carries its own inverse fixture)
  FallsPastTheScarcestInputWhenItIsUnaffordable  (composes with sp-9eor3)
  LogsWhenScarcityReordersTheQueue  (and asserts silence when nothing moved)
KeepsPlanOrderWhenNoImportSupplyIsReadable correctly SURVIVES that mutation — it pins the
fallback, so it must pass both before and after. Counted as a pin, not a kill.
The two probes that matter most: ranking on target.Supply, and ranking against the source
waypoint — BOTH plausible wrong fixes, both killed by the same 5 tests.
RanksOnTheFactorysImportSupply... is rigged so the SOURCE signal points the OPPOSITE way (IRON's
source SCARCE / quartz's ABUNDANT while the factory is MODERATE on IRON / SCARCE on quartz), so
it can only pass on the right quantity.
Plus 4 services-level tests on ImportSupply itself (9 subtests): EXPORT refused, EXCHANGE
refused, unknown reported honestly for unscanned / read-failure / null-supply / empty args.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BEFORE GATING: go vet exit 0; all 33 feed-leg tests plus the gate-topology
suite pass; 86 packages ok / 0 FAIL; TradeGoodAt read directly and confirmed to be a one-line
delegation adding no second market-read path.

REAL-WORLD MOTIVATION: observed live on staging — F45 at IRON MODERATE (vol 111) while
QUARTZ_SAND sat SCARCE, and recipe order fed IRON. sp-9eor3 stopped the walk DEADLOCKING there;
this stops it feeding the wrong input when both are affordable.

title: HeavyReserve holds the FULL hull ask with no affordability check, freezing probe buying the moment a heavy yard is priced
description:
A LATENT LANDMINE THAT ARMS ITSELF ON SUCCESS. It stays invisible while no heavy yard is priced, then fires the first time one is.

MECHANISM. common.HeavyReserve returns in.TargetYardPrice verbatim once capability is open, the cap is positive, we are under cap, and a price is known. That value reaches parkedsensing buyqueue.go (~line 303) as part of CapexReserve+heavyReserve, and domain/parkedsensing/floor.go ProbeBuyFloor ADDS it:
  floor := max(0, immutable); floor += max(0, capexReserve); floor += kMilli*cargoSpendPerHour/1000
So the probe-buy floor becomes roughly 50,000 immutable + the entire asking price of a heavy freighter. Era-5 evidence puts a heavy around 1,510,645. Prod treasury at time of writing was about 372,000. Probe buying therefore stands down COMPLETELY and expansion freezes — having just succeeded at the thing it was trying to do.

CURRENTLY DORMANT BUT LIVE. Prod era 6 knows 46 heavy-selling yards and has priced ZERO of them, so the reserve is 0 today. But yardqueue already gives dark yards ABSOLUTE precedence in the buy queue, so the next probe the drain buys may well land on one of those 46, price it, and arm this immediately. No new work is required to trigger it.

SEQUENCING — READ THIS BEFORE PRIORITISING. Fixing the probe-supply deadlock makes this MORE likely to fire, not less: more probes means more yards parked means a heavy gets priced. This must land BEFORE the seeding fix is deployed/armed, or the seeding fix will be what triggers the freeze.

THE DEFECT IS THE MISSING RELATIVE TEST, not the reserving itself. Saving toward a heavy is correct. Holding back a sum that exceeds what could plausibly be accumulated turns a savings plan into a deadlock. RULINGS #4 says never WEAKEN a money guard - this is not a weakening, it is making an unbounded hold bounded so it stops starving the fleet that funds it. Directions to evaluate: reserve only when the target is achievable within some horizon given income; scale the hold rather than taking the full ask at once; or stand the reserve down when it would push the floor above treasury. Whatever is chosen must keep the immutable 50k floor intact and must not authorise buying a heavy the fleet cannot afford.
acceptance_criteria: A priced heavy yard whose ask exceeds plausible reach does NOT zero out probe buying. Test: treasury well below the heavy ask, a heavy yard priced, assert probe buying continues and the immutable floor still binds. Test: treasury comfortably above the ask, assert the reserve still accumulates as before. Immutable 50k floor unchanged in both.
close_reason: Merged. HeavyReserve split into a TARGET (arithmetic unchanged) and HoldAt(treasury) - save toward a heavy only once half its ask is in hand, then hold every credit above that half up to the full ask; an unreachable ask withholds nothing. BROADER THAN FILED: the same number reached guardAffordability as treasury-floor-heavyReserve, so every non-heavy autosizer class was judging a negative budget too, not just probe buying. ProbeBuyFloor deliberately left treasury-blind with a test pinning that boundary - clamping it would weaken every caller's capex reserve when poorest. Anti-thrash proven by implementing the naive stand-down rule alongside and showing it violates monotonicity; notably the bead's own acceptance criteria PASS under the naive rule and would not have caught it. sp-fwk8z intent preserved. 9 tests, 6 mutation probes.

title: Probes gate probes: requestSeeds needs a probe-staffed yard, so seed requests never fire from a cold fleet
description:
THE BOTTLENECK OF THE WHOLE EXPANSION PHASE. Measured in prod era 6: 3 probes owned, 2 slots PARKED, 5,549 slots WANTED, 0 seeds requested.

MECHANISM. parkedsensing requestSeeds (internal/application/parkedsensing/supply.go ~line 246) can only raise a seed request if stagingYardFor returns a yard. That requires a system within GATE REACH holding a probe-selling yard that is BOTH (a) already STAFFED by one of our hulls and (b) free of an existing SPARE placement. When it returns empty the target is silently skipped with a continue.

So: to acquire a probe you must already have a probe parked at a probe-selling yard. A cold or nearly-cold fleet can never satisfy that, so seeds are never requested, the probe count never grows, and every downstream stage starves — charting, yard discovery, heavy-yard pricing, market coverage.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE IN A FIRST-MOVER ERA. Charting is GLOBAL: agents see each others charted waypoints (confirmed in prod era 6 — 1,014 systems carry charted waypoints against our 3 probes, so nearly all of it was charted by others). But if we are among the first to build the gate, nobody has charted anything, we are confined to the home system pre-gate, and uncharted waypoints expose type but NOT traits — so shipyards cannot even be guessed at. In that world CHARTING IS THE BOTTLENECK, charting needs probes, and probe supply is deadlocked here. Everything else in the expansion phase is downstream of this one guard.

DO NOT weaken a money guard to fix this (RULINGS #4). The fix is about REACHABILITY of a purchase, not about spending past a floor. Candidate directions to evaluate, not a mandate: allow staging from a yard reachable by an unstaffed-but-purchasable route; let bootstrap seed the first yard presence; or treat the home yard as an always-available staging point. Whatever is chosen must not create a second unguarded spending path — the existing design deliberately routes all probe acquisition through the buy queue under one floor and one probe cap.

RELATED: sp-z7u71 (pre-EXPANSION catalogue sweep — free discovery, merged, awaiting gate) is upstream-adjacent but does NOT help here: reading catalogues does not produce probes.
acceptance_criteria: A cold fleet (few or zero parked probes) can raise seed requests and grow probe count. Test: fixture with 0 parked probes and a reachable probe-selling yard asserts a seed request IS raised. No money guard weakened - the immutable floor and probe cap still bind, verified by test. No second spending path introduced: probe acquisition still routes through the buy queue.
notes:
MECHANISM CORRECTION (traced before dispatch). The description's suggested direction 'allow staging from a yard reachable by an unstaffed-but-purchasable route' is WRONG and must not be implemented.

staging.go:105-108 states the real constraint: a hull of ours must be STANDING at the counter, because the buy queue 'only ever buys where one of our hulls is already docked'. That is not an over-strict guard - it reflects the SpaceTraders mechanic that a ship purchase requires a ship present at that shipyard. Relaxing the staffed check would write placement rows that are refused every tick forever.

TWO-LEVEL DEADLOCK. yardpresence.go (the paid half of shipyard discovery) does move hulls to yards, but it draws from the drain's surplusPool. With 3 probes and 2 parked there is no surplus, so that pass is equally stuck cold. Both routes to getting a hull onto a probe-selling yard assume spare PROBES already exist.

THE ESCAPE IS A NON-PROBE HULL. The fleet holds a command frigate and haulers even when it holds no spare probes. Any hull docked at a probe-selling yard unlocks the purchase - the mechanic requires presence, not a probe specifically. So the cold-start fix is to dispatch an AVAILABLE NON-PROBE HULL to a probe-selling yard within reach when no staffed yard exists and no probe surplus is available, then let the existing buy queue fund the probe there under the unchanged floor and cap.

This keeps every money guard intact (RULINGS #4): it changes REACHABILITY of a purchase, not permission to spend. It also introduces no second spending path - acquisition still routes through the buy queue.

CAUTION: do not strand or starve the borrowed hull's own mission. The command frigate and haulers have jobs; taking one must be bounded and must not break contract/gate hauling. Check how the trade coordinator and captain reservation treat a hull before borrowing it.
close_reason: Merged. CORRECTED THE DIAGNOSIS: the foothold broker is only ever offered a SPARE/WANTED row and requestSeeds is its only writer, so with stagingYardFor returning empty no such row exists and foothold is handed nothing - its cold-empty surplusPool is a second lock on a door never reached. Fixing foothold's carrier selection alone (the lead's mid-task refinement) would still have yielded 0 seeds. Also structural: a non-probe hull cannot go through footholdFromSurplus because that path CLAIMS the target for the carrier, which would dedicate a frigate into sensing_parked (invisible to FindIdleLightHaulers forever), count it against CountOwnedProbes, and fill the very placement the probe was meant to fill. THE BORROWED HULL MUST BE A BUYER, NOT A CARRIER. staffCounters widens the seam buyerAt's DockedProbeAt fallback already opened: lends ONE hull per tick, in-system only, writing no placement row, no fleet tag, no claim, so the hull stays takeable by any coordinator. Money guards asserted intact by test. 39 tests, 6 mutation probes. Ships armed. Confirm live: seeds_unstaged nonzero + counters_staffed nonzero = working.

title: Reconcile duplicate comment doctrine + apply the existing commentclean tool at scale (sp-n2uve was closed unapplied)
description:
TWO PROBLEMS, ONE ROOT.

1. DUPLICATE DOCTRINE (my error, already merged). sp-pqmsh added PLAYBOOK §13 'comment discipline'. ENGINEERING.md §6 'Comment discipline (binding — never regress this)' ALREADY said the same thing, and said it better — it explicitly bans bead-ids in source 'neither as war-stories nor as bare (sp-xxxx) provenance tags' and gives the test 'does this help someone understand the code, or am I explaining my edit?'. PLAYBOOK §13 is now a second, divergable source of truth for one rule. FIX: delete PLAYBOOK §13's substance, leave at most a one-line pointer to ENGINEERING.md §6. Doctrine lives in ONE place.

2. sp-n2uve CLOSED BUT NOT APPLIED. That epic (Admiral-ordered, closed 2026-08-03) built gobot/tools/commentclean — an AST-equality-verified stripper for exactly these bead-id provenance tokens — and wrote the ENGINEERING.md §6 doctrine. Yet main RIGHT NOW carries 2,859 comment lines citing bead-ids, and the codebase is 29% comments (parkedsensing was 53% before sp-pqmsh's pilot sweep). The tool shipped, the epic closed, the rule is binding, and the codebase violates it at scale. Classic closed-is-not-armed.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR METHOD: sp-pqmsh swept parkedsensing by hand (agent rewriting prose), which is slow, risks deleting real invariants, and removed only ~20 of the 2,859 tokens. commentclean already does the provenance-token half deterministically with AST-identity proof. The remaining prose-collapse half is the only part needing judgment. DO NOT hand-sweep what the tool can strip.

PLAN:
a. Collapse PLAYBOOK §13 to a pointer at ENGINEERING.md §6.
b. Run commentclean --dry-run across gobot (respecting its existing exclusions: internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**, pkg/proto/**), review the diff, then --write. It self-verifies AST-identity.
c. Re-baseline gobot/.comment-baseline.json from the post-strip state.
d. Wire cmd/comment-audit as the regression gate (blocked: captain-gate and internal/captain are protected paths — needs the lead, not a build agent).
e. Only then consider further judgment-driven prose collapse, package by package.

REFERENCE: sp-pqmsh merged as aa737933 (rule + comment-audit tool + parkedsensing pilot sweep, verified comment-only, full -race green).
acceptance_criteria: PLAYBOOK §13 no longer duplicates ENGINEERING.md §6. commentclean applied across eligible gobot packages with AST-identity proven and tests green. Bead-id comment-line count on main falls substantially from 2,859. .comment-baseline.json re-baselined. comment-audit wiring path identified (protected-path handoff documented).
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTION (measured before dispatch, 2026-08-05). Step (b) as originally written is WRONG and must not be executed as stated.

MEASURED: 'go run ./tools/commentclean --dry-run' over the whole module reports ~4 strippable occurrences against ~2,800 skipped. Breakdown of skips: S-TOKEN-LITERAL 1828, S-SUBLABEL 205, S-CROSSLINE 151, S-HEADPUNCT 142, S-BANNER 126, S-GOVERNED 113, rest smaller.

  // Single-writer guard (sp-wrh84): take a Postgres SESSION advisory lock for
  // sp-01wc: wire the CAS-retry knob (live by default). Setter injection keeps
  // sp-muq66: the daemon's ONE treasury reader.  measured 0.167 req/s
Removing these requires REWRITING THE SENTENCE, which is not an AST-preserving deterministic transform. The tool correctly refuses; that refusal is its safety guarantee, not a gap.
