title: [P1] Gate purchasing ignores IN-FLIGHT units: bought 436 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY against a 400 requirement (144,464 credits wasted, 36 surplus stuck in a hauler)
description:
Gate material purchasing computes remaining need as (required - SERVER_fulfilled) and NEVER
subtracts units already bought and IN FLIGHT. Any hull that is slow to deliver causes the whole
shortfall to be bought a SECOND time. Observed live: 436 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY bought against a
400-unit requirement, 144,464 credits wasted, and 36 surplus units now stuck in a gate hauler's
hold that the construction site can never accept.

OBSERVED (staging, TORWINDSTG, gate X1-KP46-I55, 2026-08-05). The ledger is unambiguous —
every ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY purchase, with a running total:

  20:47:26  +28u  running=392  cost=109368
  20:47:27  + 8u  running=400  cost= 32224   <-- CORRECT. Stopped exactly on the 400 requirement.
  23:17:15  +28u  running=428  cost=111496
  23:17:15  + 8u  running=436  cost= 32968   <-- bought the SAME 36 units AGAIN.

  TOTAL 436 units / 1,997,124 credits against a requirement of 400.
  WASTE: 36 units, 144,464 credits.

  THE IDENTICAL 28+8 SPLIT IN BOTH BUYS IS THE PROOF. That is not a coincidence of market
  tranche sizes — it is the same shortfall computation producing the same plan twice.

MECHANISM (verified against the timeline):
  1. 20:47  gate reads ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 364/400. Coordinator computes 400-364 = 36 remaining,
            buys exactly 36, loads them onto TORWINDSTG-B. Correct so far.
  2.        TORWINDSTG-B is then stranded mid-route for HOURS by sp-rnm3q (a non-essential
            refuel failure aborted its delivery and sent it to an alternate fuel stop), so the
            36 units never arrive and the gate STILL reads 364/400.
  3. 23:17  Coordinator re-evaluates. Server still says 364/400. It computes 400-364 = 36 again,
            blind to the 36 units already paid for and physically in transit. Buys 36 MORE.
  4.        TORWINDSTG-B finally delivers its 36 -> ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY hits 400/400 COMPLETE.
  5.        TORWINDSTG-A is left holding ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY x36 for a material that is finished.
            Confirmed live: 'TORWINDSTG-A holding ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY x36, IN_TRANSIT @ X1-KP46-I56'.

THIS IS NOT RESTART-SPECIFIC, though a daemon restart sat between the two buys. The computation
is stateless with respect to in-flight inventory, so ANY delivery latency longer than the
coordinator's re-evaluation interval reproduces it. The restart is incidental; the long in-flight
window is the trigger, and sp-rnm3q manufactures long in-flight windows.

WHY IT LOOKED FINE FOR THE WHOLE BUILD UNTIL NOW: the running total climbed 20u at a time and
landed exactly on 400, because until this point every tranche was DELIVERED before the next
evaluation. The cap was never actually tested by a slow delivery. A guard that is only correct
when nothing is in flight is not a guard.

SAME FAILURE FAMILY AS PROD sp-20eyn: there, contract cmsfd1yqu3uavsl73370nq0ph was DELIVERED
into twice (94 units against 47 required) because local state was stale. Here we BUY twice
because in-flight state is not counted. Both are 'the fulfilment number I am reasoning about does
not include work already committed'. Worth fixing with one shared notion of committed-but-not-yet-
landed units.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Remaining need MUST be (required - fulfilled - in_flight - in_hold), where in_flight/in_hold
   counts units of that good already purchased for the gate and sitting in any hull's cargo or
   en route. Test: server says 364/400, one hull holds 36 of that good; assert the coordinator
   buys ZERO, not 36.
2. Never purchase a good whose requirement is already met. Test: material at 400/400; assert no
   purchase call is made at all (assert on the API client's call count, not just on spend).
3. Idempotency across re-evaluation: running the sizing pass twice with no delivery in between
   must produce a purchase plan the SECOND time of zero. This is the exact regression above.
4. Idempotency across a daemon restart: same as (3) but with the coordinator restarted between
   passes, so in-flight accounting cannot depend on in-memory-only state.
5. SURPLUS DISPOSAL: when a hull holds gate material that is no longer needed, it must be sold
   or re-tasked rather than carried indefinitely. TORWINDSTG-A is currently a gate hauler whose
   hold is occupied by dead cargo, reducing effective gate-hauling capacity. Test asserts the
   hull is released/unloaded rather than parked holding it.
6. OBSERVABILITY: emit a counter when a purchase is skipped due to in-flight coverage, and a
   WARNING when purchased-units for a good exceed its requirement. The 436-vs-400 overshoot was
   only visible by summing the ledger by hand.

MONEY IMPACT: 144,464 credits on this one good. The same bug applies to FAB_MATS (1141 bought,
459 still needed at ~1,700/unit) where the remaining spend is ~780k — a duplicate tranche there
costs proportionally more, and FAB_MATS is now the ONLY material left, so every remaining buy
runs through this code path.

RELATED: sp-rnm3q (creates the long in-flight windows that trigger this), sp-20eyn (same
committed-work-not-counted family, delivery side), sp-ps2oc (concurrent construction_supply buys
each passing the money guard individually — note 13:41:49 above shows TWO 22u buys in the same
second, that race is visible in this very ledger).
notes:
CONFIRMED THE EXACT GUARD AND ITS BLIND SPOT — the fix site is pinned.

The coordinator DOES have a bill-satisfied check and it works correctly. Live log, now that
ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY reads 400/400:

  INFO: Gate delivery trip: 0/80 units of hold loaded — nothing;
        skipped FAB_MATS: paused, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY: bill_satisfied

So the guard is not missing — it is evaluated against SERVER-FULFILLED ONLY. That makes it
correct in exactly one state (units already landed) and blind in the other (units bought and
in flight). This is the whole bug in one line: 'bill_satisfied' must mean
fulfilled + in_flight + in_hold >= required, not fulfilled >= required.

CONSEQUENCE IS SELF-LIMITING, NOT A LOOP (severity stays P1, do not raise):
  The surplus delivery was rejected with API 400 code 4801 'Construction material requirements
  for ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY have been met.' — exactly TWICE, both at 20:26:44 local, then the
  coordinator moved on. It does NOT retry-storm. But TORWINDSTG-A still carries the dead
  ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY x36 (plus COPPER_ORE x20), so 36 of its 80-unit hold is permanently
  occupied while FAB_MATS is the only remaining material. That is criterion 5.

SECOND-ORDER EFFECT WORTH NOTING FOR THE FIX: because A's hold is partly dead cargo, its
gate trips now load against a REDUCED capacity — observed 'Gate delivery trip: 36/60 units of
hold loaded' where 60 is what remained after the COPPER_ORE. Surplus does not just waste the
purchase price, it shrinks effective hauling capacity for the good that IS still needed.

NOT RELATED TO sp-rnm3q. My monitor's alert text attributed this abort to sp-rnm3q; that was
wrong. There is no refuel failure here — DNS is clean (zero 'no such host' in the current log,
resolves fine) and refuels are succeeding normally across the fleet. The abort is purely the
4801 surplus rejection.
SURPLUS LIQUIDATED 2026-08-06 on Admiral instruction. THE REALIZED LOSS IS NOW MEASURED, not estimated.

  paid       144,464 for 36 units  (4,013/unit)
  recovered   70,332               (1,954/unit avg, two tranches: 28u -> 55,020 then 8u -> 15,312)
  NET LOSS     74,132  — 51.3% of the purchase price

WHY THE RECOVERY WAS SO POOR, and it is inherent rather than bad luck: X1-KP46-D39 is the ONLY market
in the system that trades ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY, and it is the EXPORT we bought FROM, sitting at
supply=HIGH. Selling back into a saturated export is the worst possible venue, and there is no other.
Trade volume 28 forced two tranches. So the effective cost of this bug is roughly HALF the
over-bought value, permanently, with no better disposal available.

WHAT IT TOOK — this is the argument for criterion 5 (automatic surplus disposal), which was NOT
implemented in the fix: the hull had to be force-preempted from its coordinator
('ship reserve --force', the sanctioned sp-w3yd path whose own example is 'reclaim stranded cargo'),
docked, refuelled from 162 to 600 (D39 was 312 units away and unreachable on the fuel it had),
routed multi-hop via E43, docked again, sold in two tranches, then released. Seven manual daemon
operations for one bug's leftovers.

THE ENGINE DETECTS THIS AND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ACT. run_construction_coordinator_commitment.go:222
logs 'OVER-BOUGHT by N unit(s) ... occupies gate-hauling capacity until it is SOLD OR TRANSFERRED' —
disposal is explicitly left to an operator. Until that is automated, every recurrence needs a human
and costs ~50% of the surplus. Worth reconsidering whether the coordinator should self-liquidate,
now that the price of not doing so is a measured number rather than a hypothetical.

Note the hull also carried IRON_ORE x44 (genuine factory feedstock) throughout; only the
ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY was sold, and A returned to the gate-factory fleet with the iron intact.
close_reason: Fixed and merged. Root cause was THREE mechanisms, not the one the bead described: (1) supplyWorkers.reserved is in-process only and a restart wiped it (daemon booted 23:05:47Z, duplicate buy 23:17:15Z); (2) reservations expire on a trip-length timeout (90m here) regardless of delivery, lapsing ~60m before the second buy; (3) DECISIVE - deliverGateLeg never consulted the reservation at all, sizing PlanFill off the raw bill, and a delivery trip is MIXED so a lot minted for one material re-bought another at full outstanding bill. Fixing only 1 and 2 would not have stopped this buy. Fix derives committed units per tick from hull cargo (cannot lapse while cargo is aboard) combined with the live reservation per hull by MAX, consulted at BOTH sizing sites. Also closed a second instance: flushOnHandGateMaterials recorded only the lot's own good so other materials read a stale bill. Criterion 5 (surplus disposal) scoped out deliberately - see follow-up. 21 new tests, 7 mutation kills, full -race green.

title: Run the free shipyard-catalogue sweep in every bootstrap phase, not just EXPANSION
description:
run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:440 documents the yard-catalogue sweep as 'run on EVERY tick and gated on nothing'. That is false: expansionReached() at line 360 returns before line 440 is ever reached, so the sweep never runs until the home jump gate completes.

The sweep is free — no hull, no credits. ReadYardCatalogues needs exactly two ports and neither depends on post-EXPANSION state: OutstandingYards is a set difference over two LOCAL reads (charted SHIPYARD-trait waypoints in the open era minus waypoints already holding a shipyard_inventory row, never calls the API), and ReadCatalog is a presence-free GET. No sensing ledger, no whitelist, no treasury, no probe. portsFor is a memoized constructor with no phase assumptions.

COST OF THE BUG, PER ERA: the entire DATA/INCOME/GATE period is spent blind, and EXPANSION begins knowing zero shipyard catalogues. Since a heavy-hull yard can only be identified from a catalogue, the heavy-trade ramp starts cold every single era. This is a recurring per-era tax, not a one-off.

FIX: call the sweep in the pre-EXPANSION early-return branch. Do NOT hoist the existing call — post-EXPANSION ordering is load-bearing in both directions (must run AFTER the screen so systems charted this tick have enumerable waypoint rows, and BEFORE the drain which reads the rows the sweep writes). Adding to the early-return branch leaves the post-EXPANSION tick byte-identical.

DECIDED: keep MaxYardCatalogReads at 8 (API budget is not constrained during bootstrap). Keep health.TickIdle() so no stall streak survives the phase change, but log the catalogue report so the yard map building is observable pre-EXPANSION.

DO NOT TOUCH the era-scoping in OutstandingYards — it is correct and load-bearing; an unscoped work list 404s whole dead systems and previously burned ~290 failures/hour flat.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-EXPANSION tick reads shipyard catalogues and logs the report. Post-EXPANSION tick byte-identical (ordering vs screen and drain unchanged). Era-scoping untouched. Tests cover both phases. Build, vet, gofmt, -race green.
close_reason: Merged. The pre-EXPANSION branch of ReconcileOnce now runs the free shipyard-catalogue sweep; the post-EXPANSION call is unchanged and still sits between the screen sweep and the drain. Guards on the two ports individually, never ports.wired(). 12 tests, 4 mutation probes. NOTE ON VALUE: charting is global, so this pays off only when other agents have already charted - as a genuine first mover in a fresh universe there is nothing charted to read and the sweep correctly returns zero. Free and correct either way, but not the per-era win originally claimed.

title: Non-essential refuel failure aborts a COMPLETED delivery: hull arrives at the gate with cargo, opportunistic top-up fails, hull flown away without delivering
description:
A NON-ESSENTIAL refuel failure aborts an ALREADY-COMPLETED delivery. A hull that has physically ARRIVED at the construction site, carrying the exact cargo the gate needs, is flown AWAY without delivering — because a discretionary fuel top-up failed. Delivery costs zero fuel. This took both gate-delivery hulls out of service for ~55 minutes each and stalled the gate build at 72.3%.

OBSERVED (staging, TORWINDSTG, X1-KP46, 2026-08-05). Two hulls, two variants of the same defect:

=== VARIANT 1 — OPPORTUNISTIC refuel, AFTER arrival at the destination ===
TORWINDSTG-A, route F45 -> I56 -> I55 (I55 IS the gate = the delivery destination):
  execute_segment 0  F45 -> I56          OK  (planned_refuel @ I56 succeeded)
  execute_segment 1  I56 -> I55          OK  <-- ARRIVED AT THE GATE, 60 FAB_MATS aboard
  "Ship performing opportunistic refuel" {"refuel_strategy":"conservative","waypoint":"X1-KP46-I55"}
  -> refuel fails, 2 attempts over 14m45s
  -> "Rerouting to alternate fuel stop after exhausting retries" alternate=X1-KP46-J57
  -> "Alternate fuel stop reroute also failed ... context canceled"
  -> "Route segment execution failed" -> route FAILED
  -> "Gate delivery: delivering FAB_MATS to X1-KP46-I55 failed"
  NET: the hull was DOCKED AT THE DELIVERY WAYPOINT with the cargo. The route was complete.
  An OPPORTUNISTIC top-up — a pure optimization for the NEXT trip — failed, and that failure
  marked the whole route FAILED and propagated an error that abandoned the delivery. The hull
  then departed for J57 in DRIFT, 29 minutes AWAY from the gate it was standing on.

=== VARIANT 2 — PLANNED refuel whose FOLLOWING SEGMENT DECLARES requires_refuel:false ===
TORWINDSTG-B, route D39 -> E42 -> I56 -> I55, carrying 36 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY:
  route_segment 2: {"from":"X1-KP46-I56","to":"X1-KP46-I55","requires_refuel":false}
  execute_segment 1  E42 -> I56          OK
  "Ship performing planned refuel" @ I56 -> fails, 2 attempts over 13m45s
  -> reroute to X1-KP46-K84 -> context canceled -> route FAILED -> delivery abandoned
  NET: the executor's OWN route plan says the final hop to the gate needs NO refuel
  (requires_refuel:false). The hull had the fuel to finish. A top-up it did not need
  killed the delivery and sent it 27 minutes to K84 in DRIFT.

B's 36 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY is EXACTLY the amount that closes that material (364/400 -> 400/400).

TRIGGER WAS ENVIRONMENTAL, THE DEFECT IS NOT. The underlying refuel errors were
"dial tcp: lookup api.spacetraders.io: no such host" — a LOCAL DNS outage on the host, 35
occurrences, since fully recovered (other hulls refuelled normally minutes later). DNS is not
the bug and needs no fix. The bug is that a transient failure on a refuel THAT WAS NOT NEEDED
is fatal to a delivery. Any upstream 5xx flake reproduces this identically.

NOT sp-l7zha. That bead is CLOSED and its fix is deployed and CORRECT here: the 10-minute
elapsed-time budget is visible in the logs (14m45s / 13m45s including capped backoff), and the
full-tank skip correctly did not fire because both tanks were genuinely low (A 161/600,
B 237/600). The retry layer behaved exactly as specified. The defect is one layer up, in how
route_executor.go classifies the failure.

CODE POINTERS
  gobot/internal/application/ship/route_executor.go
    - the segment loop calls reactToSegmentFailure on ANY error
    - reactToSegmentFailure already has PRECEDENT for this exact treatment: it special-cases
      *ErrArrivalWaitExhausted as a "RECOVERABLE PARK, not a route failure" and returns without
      marking the route FAILED. A non-essential refuel failure belongs in that same class.
  gobot/internal/application/manufacturing/services/production_executor_sink.go:192
    - "failed to navigate to construction site %s for %s" — the caller that gives up on the
      delivery when navigate returns an error, even though the ship is physically on site.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. An OPPORTUNISTIC refuel failure NEVER fails the route. It is an optimization: log it and
   continue. Assert route status is COMPLETED, not FAILED.
2. A refuel failure at a waypoint where the ROUTE IS ALREADY COMPLETE (final segment executed)
   never fails the route and never triggers an alternate-stop reroute. The ship has arrived;
   there is nothing left to navigate.
3. The gate-delivery caller performs the supply when the ship is physically AT the site,
   regardless of refuel outcome. Test drives a delivery whose last segment succeeds and whose
   post-arrival refuel fails, and asserts the construction supply call WAS made (assert on the
   supply command count, not just the returned error).
4. A PLANNED refuel is non-fatal when the remaining segments do not require it — i.e. when
   current fuel covers them, or the next segment declares requires_refuel:false. Test builds
   B's exact shape: refuel at I56 fails, segment I56->I55 has requires_refuel:false, assert the
   route still completes and the delivery lands.
5. REGRESSION (do not weaken the real case): a PLANNED refuel that IS required for the next
   segment must still be fatal when unrecoverable. Test asserts route FAILED in that case.
6. OBSERVABILITY: emit a counter when a non-essential refuel failure is swallowed, so the
   distinction between "top-up failed, carried on" and "genuinely stranded" is visible without
   reading log cadence by hand.

BLAST RADIUS: both gate-delivery hulls simultaneously, ~55 min round trip each in DRIFT,
carrying the gate's materials away from the gate. Gate frozen at 1446/2001 (72.3%). Self-heals
once the hulls reach their alternate stops and the coordinator re-queues ("the task is
re-queued for the next activation"), so this is P1 not P0 — but it recurs on every transient
refuel flake and it targets precisely the hulls that are ABOUT TO SUCCEED.

REPRO: deploy/staging (db spacetraders_staging, socket /tmp/spacetraders-staging.sock,
log /tmp/st-staging-daemon-p0fixes.log). Prod is separately down on an upstream Get Ship 500.
notes:
BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THE GATE — the same DNS window hit a THIRD hull and stalled the CONTRACT pipeline too.

TORWINDSTG-5, carrying contract cargo SILVER x48 for cmsgk8xtm5bmjsl73qqz4b86c (SILVER x48 -> X1-KP46-H54, 0/48, pay 22878):
  arrival at X1-KP46-B6 -> 'Ship performing planned refuel' @ B6
  -> transient refuel failure -> 'Refuel retry budget exhausted' after 14m45s
  -> 'Rerouting to alternate fuel stop' alternate=X1-KP46-F44
  -> 'Waiting for ship arrival event' expected_seconds=2126 (~35 MINUTES)
  Container contract-work-TORWINDSTG-5-7e7623cb has now run 84 MINUTES against a 5.7-minute
  median contract cycle. Because sp-zve2q serialises contracts to ONE active hull, this single
  detour stalled the ENTIRE contract pipeline: 3 of 4 contract haulers sat idle
  ('idle_in_fleet: 3') and contract income went to ZERO for 1h15m (last contract txn 20:49:48).

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: -5's variant is NOT the same defect as A and B. Its refuel at B6 was a
PLANNED refuel and the hull was genuinely low (175/600), so escalating to an alternate stop is
DEFENSIBLE there. A (opportunistic top-up after arriving at the destination) and B (next segment
declares requires_refuel:false) are the ones that were never needed. Do not 'fix' -5's case by
weakening the planned-refuel escalation — acceptance criterion 5 already protects it.

WHAT ALL THREE SHARE, AND WHAT WOULD HAVE SAVED ALL THREE: none of them RE-EVALUATED after the
transient condition cleared. DNS recovered within minutes (other hulls refuelled normally), but
all three stayed committed to detours of 27-35 minutes each. The escalation is a ONE-WAY DOOR:
once the reroute is chosen it is never reconsidered, even when the original waypoint becomes
serviceable again and is nearer than the alternate.

SUGGESTED ADDITIONAL CRITERION (7): before committing to an alternate-stop reroute, and again on
arrival at the alternate, re-test the ORIGINAL refuel waypoint if it is still nearer/cheaper than
completing the detour. A transient failure must not permanently rewrite the route.

Also worth noting: the sp-ehf4x silent-worker bug did NOT fire here and its regression criterion
held. TORWINDSTG-5's worker heartbeated current (22:13:37) and logged 'Arrival not due yet -
safety resync while in transit ... due_in_seconds 296' — correctly distinguishing
waiting-for-arrival from wedged-while-docked. That is the behaviour criterion 4 asked for.
=== DELIVERED: 2b5996e8 (fix) + 7267aece (mutation-driven tests). Base 18d51968. NOT gated/pushed. ===

THE BOUNDARY. Post-arrival refuels run with the hull already standing at the segment's destination,
so the movement is DONE. What decides fatality is whether the REMAINING route needs the fuel:
 - opportunistic top-up -> never required (not in the plan) -> always absorbed
 - planned refuel -> absorbed ONLY if the hull can fly every remaining leg and still land holding
   DefaultFuelSafetyMargin
 - planned refuel the remaining legs DEPEND on -> still fatal, escalation included (criterion 5,
   and the -5 contract-hauler variant the bead told us not to weaken)
Predicate FAILS CLOSED: nil fuel reads unaffordable -> stays essential. RULINGS #4 respected — this
narrows when a FAILURE is fatal and grants no spending latitude.
Non-essential refuels now retry IN PLACE and never reroute (criterion 2); escalation is the
expensive half and it carries the cargo away from where it was due.

NOT the flight-mode reserve. FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment BREAKS at the first fuel-selling
waypoint (route.go:277-279), so it reads ZERO at every waypoint a refuel is attempted at — reusing
it would have excused exactly the failures that genuinely strand a hull. New fuelForSegmentsAfter
sums all remaining legs.

CRITERIA: 1 opportunistic-absorbed / 2 no-reroute + route COMPLETED / 3 supply-call-count asserted
at the sink / 4 planned-but-affordable absorbed / 5 essential still fatal + typed error / 6
non_essential_refuel_failures_total{player_id,kind} asserted via a counting collector. Criterion 7
(re-test the ORIGINAL waypoint before/after committing to a detour) NOT done — see deferred.

RED first: reproduced the incident's own signature ("refuel unrecoverable ... after 15 attempt(s)
over 10m2s, alternate-stop reroute also failed"). The FIRST fixture was MIS-AIMED — it tripped the
PRE-departure refuel, reaching the same retry code by another path and passing for the wrong
reason. Every test now asserts a refuel was actually ATTEMPTED, because a skipped refuel is the
same green for the opposite reason.

MUTATION SWEEP (8 probes, each atomic; tree verified 0 bytes after every one):
 KILLED P1 always-affordable / P3 margin-dropped / P4 escalation-restored / P5 opportunistic-fatal
 / P6 counter-mislabelled / P7 sink-abandons / P2b final-compare-inverted — each naming its killer.
 EQUIVALENT P2 (early-return `<=0` widened): the general comparison below returns the same answer
 for every reachable input, confirmed because P2b on that comparison IS killed by 3 tests.
 SURVIVING P8: swapping the CALL SITE back to the reserve is not caught. fuelForSegmentsAfter is
 tested directly, but no end-to-end test has a multi-segment route where the two figures differ —
 the package's mediator fake never moves the ship, so post-arrival state cannot be staged. REAL
 residual, filed below.

TWO PROCESS FAILURES WORTH KEEPING:
 1. `git commit -- <pathspec>` silently EXCLUDES untracked files. The new test file was left out of
    the first commit — the fix would have merged without its tests. Caught by asserting the file
    appears in `git show --name-only`.
 2. The probe harness's `git checkout -- gobot/` restore DESTROYED three uncommitted tests, and the
    next sweep then reported their targets as "SURVIVED". COMMIT FIRST is not advice; an uncommitted
    test is indistinguishable from an absent one, and the sweep reports the gap as real.

DEFERRED:
 - Criterion 7 (re-test the original waypoint before committing to a detour, and again on arrival).
   Untouched; it is a separate behaviour from classification and wants its own lane.
 - P8: an end-to-end multi-segment test pinning the call site. Needs a fake that moves the ship.
 - A non-essential refuel still spends the full retry budget before being absorbed, so a gate hull
   can stand on the site for that long before delivering. Much better than the observed detour, but
   not free; worth revisiting.
 - The sink's on-site fallback supplies from wherever the hull is on site. In the observed variant
   it was DOCKED (the post-arrival refuel docks and stays docked), but the fallback does not itself
   guarantee docked state.
close_reason:
Merged. A refuel the REMAINING route does not need can no longer abandon a completed delivery. Boundary: post-arrival refuels run with the hull already at the destination, so fatality turns on whether the remaining legs need the fuel — opportunistic (never in the plan) always absorbed; planned absorbed only if the hull can fly every remaining leg AND still land holding the standard safety margin; planned that the remaining legs DEPEND on stays fatal, escalation included. Predicate FAILS CLOSED (nil fuel read -> essential). Non-essential refuels now retry in place and NEVER reroute — escalation was the expensive half and is what carried the cargo away from the gate.

THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE WEAKENED THE GUARD, caught and verified independently: the obvious primitive FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment breaks at the first fuel-selling waypoint (navigation/route.go: 'if segments[i].ToWaypoint.HasFuel { break }'), so it reads ZERO at every waypoint a refuel is ever attempted at — a refuel only happens AT a fuel-capable waypoint. Reusing it would have classified criterion 5's genuinely-required refuel as non-essential. New fuelForSegmentsAfter sums all remaining legs instead.

Bead had SIX criteria plus a suggested seventh (my dispatch said four — I had read the bead through a truncated window). 1-6 covered, each with a named test. Criterion 3 asserts len(supplyCalls)==1 — the supply command COUNT, not the returned error, because a test checking only the error passes while the delivery never happens.

MUTATION SWEEP: 8 probes. 7 killed with named killers; P2 confirmed EQUIVALENT (not assumed — P2b on the same comparison IS killed by 3 tests). P8 SURVIVES and is a real stated residual: swapping the call site back to the reserve is not caught end-to-end, because the package's mediator fake never moves the ship, so no test has a multi-segment route where the two figures differ. fuelForSegmentsAfter is tested directly.

The first sweep found THREE survivors, and P4 proved the original 'no navigate was issued' assertions were VACUOUS — the reroute needs a waypointRepo to find an alternate and the fixtures wire none, so those assertions held whether or not escalation happened. Replaced with an error-type discriminator.

RULINGS #4: this narrows when a FAILURE is fatal; it grants no spending latitude the affordability guard did not already allow, and never lets a hull skip fuel it needs.

RESIDUAL: (a) P8 above — wants a fake that moves the ship; (b) a non-essential refuel still spends the full retry budget before being absorbed, so a gate hull can stand on site that long before delivering — far better than the observed detour, not free; (c) the sink's on-site fallback supplies from wherever the hull is on site and does not itself guarantee docked state (in the observed variant it was docked, since the post-arrival refuel docks and stays docked).

TRIGGER WAS ENVIRONMENTAL (local DNS outage, recovered) — not fixed and not the bug; any upstream 5xx reproduces identically. Criterion 7 (re-test the original waypoint before committing to a detour) deferred — different behaviour from classification, wants its own lane.

title: Strip archaeology comments from gobot source; enforce at the gate
description:
29% of non-test gobot is comments (57,633 lines). parkedsensing is 53% — more comment than code. 2,879 comment lines cite a bead ID; ~650 more carry narrative markers (measured live / the defect / used to / this fixed). The worst blocks carry no marker at all (yardqueue.go: ~60 lines retelling an incident).

CAUSE: build agents write justification inline to defend a change at the gate; captain-gate merges on tests green and never looks at comment density; CLAUDE.md's 'history lives in docs/retrospectives/' has no enforcement; and nothing ever deletes a comment, so later lanes edit code around stale narrative until it lies.

COST: not bytes. A comment describing a defect fixed three lanes ago misinforms the next reader, and every agent read pays for it in context.

SCOPE: (1) define the keep/cut rule — godoc on exported symbols and non-obvious invariants stay; incident retelling, measured counts, bead IDs, and defect history go to docs/retrospectives/ or are dropped; (2) sweep the worst packages first (parkedsensing 53%, bootstrap 38%, fleet 36%, adapters/expansion 31%); (3) add a gate check so the ratio cannot regress.
acceptance_criteria: Keep/cut rule written into CLAUDE.md or PLAYBOOK. parkedsensing comment ratio under an agreed threshold. captain-gate rejects a lane that raises comment ratio in a touched package. No behaviour change — tests byte-identical.

title: Standby homing re-dispatches a hull every sweep while its navigate is stalled — nothing tracks an in-flight homing, and sp-l7zha just widened the window to 10 minutes
description:
SPLIT OUT of sp-lkuh9 as an INDEPENDENT defect. sp-lkuh9 was the slot RESHUFFLE; this is a re-dispatch storm against a STABLE slot, and the two have different causes.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE THAT IT IS NOT A RESHUFFLE: the target slot was IDENTICAL (X1-KP46-H51) on EVERY dispatch. A reshuffle shows a CHANGING target. The assignment was perfectly stable throughout.

THE REAL CHAIN, from staging rows (read-only pull, nothing started or stopped):
  14:54:42Z  first HomeShipCommand for TORWINDSTG-7 -> H51
  14:57:04Z  the navigate stalls in "Transient refuel failure, retrying with backoff"
             the hull therefore stays IDLE at X1-KP46-I56
  every ~90s a fresh sweep fires ANOTHER HomeShipCommand for the same hull to the same slot
  15:02:16Z  one dispatch finally wins and the hull departs
  thereafter the remaining attempts fail with API 4214 "Ship is currently in-transit"
  At least SIX dispatches, not five as sp-lkuh9 originally recorded (that count came from
  local timestamps; the box is UTC-3).

CAUSE — NOTHING TRACKS AN IN-FLIGHT HOMING. Three independent gaps, all needed for the storm:
  1. idle_arb.go:482 — the `homed` map is PER-PASS and discarded at the end of the sweep, so
     the next sweep has no memory of what it just dispatched.
  2. HomeShip (wiring.go:124-146) is FIRE-AND-FORGET: it returns nil BEFORE the flight
     actually launches, so a successful return says nothing about whether the hull is moving.
  3. The only re-entry guard (home_ship.go:69) reads LOCAL ship state, which still reports
     IDLE during a refuel backoff — so the guard cannot see that a homing is already underway.

!! INTERACTION WITH sp-l7zha, WHICH IS ALREADY MERGED AND DEPLOYED — THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS !!
The stall here is a REFUEL RETRY. sp-l7zha (merged main 6e31d50d, deployed to staging 16:26Z)
deliberately EXTENDED the refuel retry budget from about 6 seconds of backoff to a
TIME-BOUNDED 10 MINUTES, because giving up early cost a 41-minute reroute.
That fix is correct and should stay. But it means the window during which a hull sits idle
mid-refuel is now up to TEN MINUTES rather than seconds — so this storm gets LONGER and FIRES
MORE DISPATCHES than the trace above, which was captured under the OLD short budget.
ANY COOLDOWN OR IN-FLIGHT MARKER MUST THEREFORE BE SIZED TO THE REFUEL RETRY BUDGET
(>10 minutes), NOT TO THE 90-SECOND SWEEP INTERVAL. Sizing it to the sweep leaves the storm
fully intact.

FIX DIRECTION: track an in-flight homing across sweeps — a per-process ship->homedAt marker
that outlives the pass, or a re-entry guard that consults actual navigation intent rather than
local idle state. Whatever is chosen must survive the case where the hull legitimately reports
idle because its navigate has not launched yet.

COST: wasted API calls, log noise that hides real problems, and 4214 errors that look like a
bug in homing when they are the symptom of duplicate dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A hull whose navigate is stalled in refuel backoff receives EXACTLY ONE HomeShipCommand for the duration of the stall, with the cooldown sized to the refuel retry budget rather than the sweep interval. Test drives a stalled navigate across multiple sweeps and asserts a single dispatch; a positive control (remove the marker) shows the storm returning.
notes: Found and measured by the sp-lkuh9 lane, which correctly declined to fix it in scope and proved it independent by showing the target slot never changed. Related: sp-lkuh9 (the reshuffle, fixed), sp-l7zha (the 10-minute refuel budget that widens this window).

title: Unpriced contract source-buy bypasses BOTH the working-capital floor and the aggregate spend cap — a map miss makes cost 0, which clears every guard
description:
PRE-EXISTING, NOT introduced by sp-ps2oc — found by that lane review while verifying the new cap. This is a money guard that FAIL-OPENS on missing data, which is the opposite of RULINGS #4.

THE CHAIN: MarketPrices[trade] is a map lookup. On a MISS it yields the zero value, 0. affordableSourceBuyLot then computes fullCost = 0. A cost of 0:
  - CLEARS ANY FLOOR — treasury minus 0 is always above the reserve, so the working-capital floor passes trivially and returns the FULL UNSHRUNK LOT rather than a shrunk one; and
  - takes the aggregate cap fail-open, because reserveConcurrentSpendOrPark returns early when projectedCost <= 0, so NO RESERVATION IS TAKEN AT ALL.
THE BUY THEN EXECUTES AT REAL PRICES, COMPLETELY UNGUARDED. Both guards are armed and both are blind, because each is reasoning about a cost of zero while the market charges the real amount.

WHY IT IS NOT THEORETICAL: WithSourceBuyFloor() is armed UNCONDITIONALLY, so the floor really is on. Reachability of the unpriced case is acknowledged TWICE in the code itself. A price map miss happens whenever the market data for that trade good has not been read or has aged out — exactly the cold or quiet regime.

RELATION TO sp-ps2oc: that P0 was the same failure in a different shape — a guard not being CONSULTED. This one is a guard being consulted with an input that makes it a no-op. sp-ps2oc did not create or widen it and deliberately did not touch it.

FIX DIRECTION: an unpriced good must FAIL CLOSED — refuse the buy, or resolve a price before sizing the lot. A cost of 0 from a map miss must never be treated as a real cost by either guard. Consider making the zero explicitly invalid at the point of lookup rather than relying on every downstream consumer to notice.
acceptance_criteria: A source-buy whose good is absent from MarketPrices does NOT execute, or executes only after a real price is resolved. Test asserts the guard REFUSES rather than passing with cost 0, and asserts the aggregate cap TAKES a reservation for the real projected cost. A deliberate positive control shows the old behaviour failing the new test.
notes:

title: Composition-root setters are unpinned: a live money guard was deleted by an unrelated refactor and nothing caught it (sp-ps2oc class)
description:
CLASS BEHIND sp-ps2oc, and it has now bitten TWICE IN ONE DAY.

WHAT HAPPENED: SetSpendLedger — the cross-container concurrent-spend cap from sp-w3he — was wired at the composition root onto factoryCoordinatorHandler. Commit 712b6f66 (sp-hoj8u, "retire all factory ops") deleted that handler and took the ONLY production call site with it. The guard then fail-opened on every gate buy ever made, and it took a 297k treasury drain and a hard fleet deadlock to notice.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: every test wires its OWN fake ledger, so the unit suite is green whether or not production wires one. The setter is optional by design (nil = fail-open for fixtures), which is exactly what makes an unwired production path indistinguishable from a correctly-wired one at test time.

THE SECOND INSTANCE, same day: SetGateFactory had NO production call site through SIX otherwise-complete tasks of the gate-fleet plan, leaving the feed leg, the role reallocation AND the factory routing all inert. Found only because three readers independently checked reachability.

THE MECHANISM TO EXTEND ALREADY EXISTS. Phase 3 task 7 built an AST composition-root guard (gobot/cmd/spacetraders-daemon, gate_factory_wiring_test.go) that parses main.go and fails the build if SetGateFactory is missing, is passed a nil argument, or is called on a different handler than the one registered. It was written RED-FIRST and failed against the real main.go with "factoryCalls: expected 1, actual 0". That is precisely the check this class needs, and it currently pins exactly one setter.

REQUIRED: extend that AST guard to cover every optional collaborator whose absence silently disables a guard or a capability. Same shape, same file, same technique: SetTreasuryReader, SetCapitalWorkSensor, SetPriceHistoryReader, WithSourceBuyFloor, SetSpendLedger. Enumerate the full set rather than trusting this list — the enumeration is part of the work.

NOTE the guard existing does not make it correct: the sp-ps2oc review found that its stated claim about a second handler was NOT implemented (it counted setters, not handlers). Whatever is added here must be probed with a REAL main.go mutation that compiles and ships, not merely asserted.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberate positive control per covered setter: delete its production call from main.go, see the build fail, restore it. The guard distinguishes missing / nil-argument / wrong-handler, and each distinction is proven by a mutation that compiles.
notes:
ANOTHER INSTANCE OF THIS CLASS, found by the sp-gef01 review — the THIRD in one day:
WithSourceBuyFloor() arms the contract source-buy working-capital floor UNCONDITIONALLY, and the aggregate spend cap projectedCost <= 0 fail-open is unreachable ONLY BECAUSE that floor is armed. So a money guard depends on a composition-root wiring that NOTHING PINS: WithSourceBuyFloor appears in exactly THREE TEST FILES, ALL UNDER internal/application/contract/services/, and NOTHING IN commands/ OR AT THE COMPOSITION ROOT asserts the production wiring exists.
The coupling between "the floor is armed" and "the cap fail-open is unreachable" is currently A COMMENT, NOT A COMPILE-TIME CONSTRAINT. If the floor were ever unwired the way SetSpendLedger was, the hole reopens silently and every test stays green — the exact shape of this bead.
ADD WithSourceBuyFloor TO THE SET THIS BEAD PINS. One test in commands/ (or an AST assertion at the composition root, matching the gate_factory_wiring_test.go / spend_ledger_wiring_test.go pattern) converts the comment into a constraint.
RUNNING TALLY FOR THIS CLASS: SetGateFactory (gate fleet inert through six tasks), SetSpendLedger (money cap fail-open for weeks, 297k drain), WithSourceBuyFloor (latent). All three are optional collaborators whose absence is invisible because every test supplies its own.
close_reason:

the deliverable — it found that this class is not merely unpinned but contains LIVE BUGS.

behaviour on money paths and deserve their own before/after, not a drive-by in a coverage lane):
  sp-f5lki (P1) SetPriceHistoryReader — every rescue source-buy parks permanently; the WARNING
                blames absent market data rather than absent wiring; four sibling setters are wired
                on the same receiver in the same block while this one is skipped; and its own doc

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
PATTERN FROM sp-a75fz (fleet_autosizer_ports.go api_util reader), offered as a candidate general form.

sp-a75fz was one composition-root setter with TWO independent silent failure modes. Both matter for
this bead because only one of them is fixable by design:

  1. THE SETTER IS NEVER CALLED. No design prevents this — sp-ps2oc lost SetSpendLedger to a refactor
     of an unrelated operation and nothing noticed. Only a check AT the composition point can see it.
     => needs an AST pin. sp-ps2oc's spend_ledger_wiring_test.go is the precedent.

  2. THE SETTER IS CALLED WITH A VALUE CAPTURED TOO EARLY. Fixable by design: make the field hold a
     RESOLVER rather than the resolved thing, so a wiring-time capture is unexpressible in the type.
     => a type change, not a test.

Prefer 2 where the shape allows it, and add 1 regardless. A resolver cannot save you from a setter
nobody calls.

ONE TRAP WORTH CARRYING INTO THE GENERAL FORM, found by mutation-probing the fix rather than by
review: pinning "the literal sets only the resolver field" is NOT sufficient. A resolver that closes
over a wiring-time read —

    captured := globalAPIBudgetReporter()
    ...{resolve: func() apiBudgetReporter { return captured }}

— sets only that field, compiles, and is the original defect wearing the fix's clothes. The AST check
must additionally pin that the resolver is a NAMED FUNCTION passed uncalled: a closure or a call
expression evaluates at wiring time by construction. Verified: that shape compiles, and the
field-name check demonstrably passes it.

Also worth generalising: these failures are invisible precisely BECAUSE the downstream guard fails
closed correctly (RULINGS #4). The symptom of an unwired api_util reader is a fleet that silently
never grows — it reads as a decision, not a fault. Any setter feeding a fail-closed guard belongs in
this bead's scope for the same reason.

title: DEPLOY PRECONDITIONS for the gate two-fleet operation (phases 1-3): migration 051 BEFORE the daemon, then verify role tags exist
description:
The gate construction revamp (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-gate-construction-two-fleet-design.md; plans phase1 merged ac8471a1, phase2 merged 5f3986be, phase3 in progress) ships ARMED — there is no feature flag to turn on. But it has two ordering preconditions that fail SILENTLY if missed.

1. MIGRATION 051 MUST BE APPLIED BEFORE THE DAEMON THAT WRITES THOSE COLUMNS IS DEPLOYED. 051 adds delivery_buy_floor / delivery_resume_floor to the pipeline row. Boot AutoMigrate would add them, but AUTOMIGRATE FAILURE IS NON-FATAL in this daemon, so a boot where it could not run leaves the floor writes hitting SQLSTATE 42703 while the daemon reports healthy.

2. THE FLEET ONLY ENGAGES FOR HULLS CARRYING A GATE ROLE TAG. The two workers are selected by dedicated_fleet in ('gate-delivery','gate-factory'), assigned at GATE-phase purchase in D/F/F/D order. Legacy 'manufacturing'-tagged gate hulls carry no role and are adopted by phase 3's reallocation planner. Post-deploy verification query:
   SELECT dedicated_fleet, count(*) FROM ships WHERE dedicated_fleet IN ('gate-delivery','gate-factory','manufacturing') GROUP BY 1;
   Expect a D/F/F/D mix (2 delivery, 2 factory) once 4 GATE hulls exist. ALL-DELIVERY OR ZERO-FACTORY IS THE FLEET-KILLER SIGNATURE — see the spec's CORRECTION 4.

3. CLAIM IDENTITY: ClaimShip authorizes a dedicated hull only when tag == operation (exact equality). A role-tagged hull claimed under any other identity is rejected at the DB and then silently never works. If hulls carry the tags but nothing moves, check claim identity before anything else.
acceptance_criteria: Migration 051 confirmed applied to the production DB before the daemon carrying phases 1-3 is deployed; post-deploy tag-count query run and recorded; a delivery leg and a factory feed leg each observed moving units (not merely reporting RUNNING).
notes:
!! CORRECTION TO THE dwell records DEPLOY CHECK ON THIS BEAD — MY EARLIER WORDING PRODUCES A FALSE ALARM ON THE MOST COMMON CASE !!

I wrote: "dwell records 0/N after the first tick IS AN ALARM". THAT IS TOO STRONG AND IS WRONG AFTER A RESTART.
roleSince is a PER-PROCESS IN-MEMORY map, so a daemon restart EMPTIES IT. If the fleet is already at its baseline mix when the daemon comes up — which it usually is, because the tags are persisted in the ships table — then NO MOVES ARE WANTED, so NO STAMPS ARE RECORDED, and the line correctly reads 0/N indefinitely. That is the honest state of an empty ledger with nothing to record, NOT an inert guard.

OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-05: after the 16:26Z restart the very first tick read "have 2D/2F + 0 unroled + 0 foreign, want 2D/2F, dwell records 0/4 — no role changes", and it still read 0/4 fifty minutes later with ZERO role moves issued in between. Fleet correct, guard fine, counter honest.

THE CORRECT RULE: dwell records 0/N is an alarm ONLY IF ROLE MOVES HAVE BEEN ISSUED AND IT STILL READS 0. Check the two together — grep for a move line ("X is now a factory/delivery hull") and only then treat a stuck 0/N as the inert-ledger signal. A non-zero numerator should appear on the FIRST TICK AFTER A MOVE, not on the first tick after boot.
The genuine inert-ledger symptom remains as described: a fleet that looks BUSY rather than stalled, churning role changes every tick while the counter stays at 0.

title: universe transition mints with an empty faction — era rollover cannot self-serve
description:
`spacetraders universe transition --agent TORWIND --confirm` (the no --token path, which mints from ST_ACCOUNT_TOKEN) fails 422 at the register call. The API requires a non-empty faction enum; the caller hardcodes an empty string.

FAILURE SIGNATURE:
  API error (status 422) code 3001, zodIssues: path [faction],
  code invalid_enum_value, received "",
  options [COSMIC VOID GALACTIC QUANTUM DOMINION ASTRO CORSAIRS OBSIDIAN AEGIS
  UNITED SOLITARY COBALT OMEGA ECHO LORDS CULT ANCIENTS SHADOW ETHEREAL]

ROOT CAUSE (exact):
  gobot/internal/adapters/cli/universe_transition.go:117
    minted, err := deps.api.Register(ctx, opts.accountToken, opts.agent, "")
  The api layer (adapters/api/register.go) is CORRECT — it posts whatever faction it is
  given. Only the caller is wrong. `player register --new` already exposes --faction;
  transition does not.

WHY THIS MATTERS: era rollover is a weekly critical path and this breaks its one-command
form. Worked around for torwind-2026-08-02 by minting via curl (faction COSMIC) and
feeding --token. The guard behaved correctly — validated-before-write, 'no changes made',
zero partial state.

NOTE the latent second half: newEraRecords() reads agentData.StartingFaction to populate
eras.faction. Era 3 (torwind-2026-07-12) has a NULL faction, so that read has silently
returned empty before — worth confirming the assignment path end-to-end, not just the flag.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `universe transition` accepts --faction (default COSMIC, the value every prior era used) and passes it to Register.
2. Minting without --token succeeds end-to-end against a real reset.
3. An invalid/empty faction is rejected LOCALLY before any API call or DB write, preserving the existing validated-before-write guarantee.
4. eras.faction is populated non-NULL on the new era row after a mint-path transition (covers the era-3 NULL regression).
notes:
BUILD LANE COMPLETE (2026-08-03) — worktree .claude/worktrees/sp-dqbzm, branch sp-dqbzm, HEAD af100ffa (3 commits, rebased onto local main 58df3bda). NOT gated — lead handles captain-gate.

THREE fixes, not one:
(1) FIRST HALF — universe transition takes --faction (default COSMIC) and sends it. Shared faction.go holds the /register enum (transcribed from the API's own 422 options list); both mint paths resolve+validate through it BEFORE any API call or DB write, and validation also runs on the preview so --dry-run can't promise what --confirm would refuse.
(2) COMPANION, not in the bead — player register --new was the ONLY other Register call site and equally broken: --faction shipped '(optional)' with an empty default, passed straight through, same 422. Same gate applied. So --new has been un-mintable too.
(3) SECOND HALF (era 3) — CONFIRMED END TO END. eras.faction and players.metadata both derive from ONE source, GetAgent().StartingFaction, and an empty read was skipped SILENTLY. Archaeology: era 3 was created by universe transition on the very day it landed (dda876b7, 2026-07-12); the /my/agent parse DID include startingFaction then, and the faction assignment was in the original commit — so the API genuinely returned empty and both sinks lost it (eras.faction NULL, players.metadata {}). Meanwhile the mint path already held TWO better values for the agent it had just created — RegisterResult.Faction (the register response's own echo) and the validated --faction — and discarded BOTH ('minted' was read for .Token only). Now: live read > register echo > validated request, so a mint records non-NULL UNCONDITIONALLY. The --token path still refuses to invent a faction (the agent was minted elsewhere) but now WARNS instead of skipping silently — the silence is what hid era 3 for three weeks.

FOURTH FIX, caused by fixing the mint: the in-sync idempotency check ran AFTER Register, so a re-run on an already-synced universe minted an agent (irreversible account slot) and discarded it. Unreachable while every mint 422'd; making the mint work exposes it. All read-only, token-independent checks now precede the mint.

AC STATUS: #1 done. #2 NOT verifiable from a build lane — minting is irreversible and the universe is currently in sync; verified as far as is safe (live preview against the real API+DB: bad faction refused locally with the enum listed, 'void' normalised to VOID and stated in the plan, zero mutation). Needs a real reset to close. #3 done. #4 done and asserted against a REAL eras.faction column, not just the fake.

TESTS: 10 new test funcs / 27 cases, all through CLI driving ports, asserted at the API + era-store boundaries. 11 mutation probes, 11 kills, each naming specific tests (incl. one isolating the ordering and one separating the register-echo source from its request fallback). Full suite green (84 pkgs w/ tests), -race green, gofmt/build/vet clean.

DECLARED TEST CHANGE: universe_transition_test.go asserted registerFaction == "" and its comment called that the intended default — it was pinning the defect. Assertion + comment updated per AC#1, not deleted.

FILED, NOT FIXED: sp-2zv0u (P3) — previewPendingMint doesn't consult eraInSyncWith, so a preview on an already-synced universe claims a pending rollover. Pre-existing, kept out to keep this diff reviewable.
CAPTAIN VALIDATION 2026-08-04 (post-deploy, CLI dea1d31f):

PARTIAL ACCEPT.

    --faction string  faction to mint the new era's agent under (mint path only;

    Default is COSMIC, which is the value every prior era used (eras 1,2,4,5; era 3 NULL).

PROCESS NOTE: the bead was closed before captain acceptance. Not reopening — the code is
correct as far as it can be checked — but AC#2/#4 are genuinely open and must be re-checked

title: BLOCKER FOR PHASE 3: the recipe map is CYCLIC, not a DAG — the depth-cap deletion rationale in the two-fleet spec is false
description:
Found by the whole-branch review of gate-topology phase 1. ZERO impact today (the methods involved are unwired); HIGH impact on phase 3, which is planned on the false premise.

THE CLAIM (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-gate-construction-two-fleet-design.md, 'What Gets Deleted' + 'Three things I'd flag'): 'Recursion is bounded by the recipe DAG terminating at raw goods', therefore the fabricate depth cap can be deleted and only cycle detection (visited) need remain.

IT IS FALSE ON BOTH HALVES.

1. goods.ExportToImportMap IS CYCLIC:
     IRON_ORE -> EXPLOSIVES -> LIQUID_HYDROGEN -> MACHINERY -> IRON -> IRON_ORE
   (supply_chain.go:26, :45, :16, :63, :48). BOTH gate materials feed into this cycle:
   FAB_MATS={IRON,QUARTZ_SAND} (:59); ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY -> ELECTRONICS/MICROPROCESSORS -> {SILICON_CRYSTALS,COPPER} (:87,:62,:65).

2. 'has no recipe' IS NOT 'is raw'. IsRaw(g) := !hasRecipe(g) returns FALSE for every actual raw material — IRON_ORE, SILICON_CRYSTALS, QUARTZ_SAND, every ore has a recipe entry. Including IRON_ORE, the literal good from sp-b27a2.

THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNOWS THIS, in the same domain package:
  - goods.IsMineableRawMaterial + mineableRawMaterials (supply_chain.go:212-247) curates the correct list.
  - supply_chain_resolver.go:326-335 needed a FACTORY-EXISTENCE check on top of hasRecipe for exactly this reason, with the comment 'SILICON_CRYSTALS has a recipe (needs EXPLOSIVES)'.

CONSEQUENCE IF PHASE 3 PROCEEDS AS SPEC'D: deleting the depth cap leaves ONLY  to terminate the walk, and every ore chain recurses five levels into EXPLOSIVES before it does. The depth cap is not the redundant backstop the spec calls it — it is doing real work.

REQUIRED BEFORE PHASE 3:
  (a) Correct the spec's depth-cap rationale (done in the same change as this bead).
  (b) Fix the comment at gate_topology.go:38-44 which asserts the DAG/raw-goods premise. Comment-only, cheap NOW while IsRaw is unwired.
  (c) Decide the real termination rule: use goods.IsMineableRawMaterial rather than !hasRecipe, and/or KEEP the depth cap. Do not delete the cap on the DAG argument.

ALSO: GateTopology.Inputs duplicates goods.GetRequiredInputs (supply_chain.go:251) with a DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT contract — nil vs []string{} for raw goods. Mixing them yields a silent nil-vs-empty divergence.

FIX: GateTopology.IsRaw is now goods.IsMineableRawMaterial(good) || genuinely-no-recipe. Both halves kept — a good absent from the map entirely is still raw. The curated list already existed (supply_chain.go:212) and supply_chain_resolver.go had already needed a factory-existence check on top of hasRecipe for exactly this reason, which is the corroboration this bead cited.

DOC CORRECTED IN THREE PLACES — the false DAG premise had been restated in IsRaw's own comment, in GateTopology's type comment, and in gate_topology_test.go's header. All now say: the map is CYCLIC, termination comes from the curated predicate plus cycle detection, and THE FABRICATE DEPTH CAP MUST NOT BE DELETED ON THE DAG ARGUMENT. Cap verified untouched (fabricate_depth.go present, defaultFabricateMaxDepth=3 intact); its own comment is now in agreement with IsRaw rather than in tension with it.

TERMINATION PROVEN ON THE REAL MAP, NOT A FIXTURE — and the walk test deliberately carries NO VISITED SET. The reviewer called this the strongest part of the change: WITH a visited set the walk terminates on any finite graph regardless of IsRaw, so the test would have passed under the OLD BUGGY RULE and proved nothing. A 1000-step budget converts non-termination into a named failure rather than a hang. title: Standby homing: adding a hull now RELOCATES already-parked hulls — contradicts AssignedSlot's own 'second pass moves no hull' contract
description:
Found by adversarial review of sp-9suun (which is otherwise sound and gated).

standby_assignment.go:24 truncates the slot set by PRIORITY and then RE-SORTS:
    orderedSlots := distinctSorted(truncateToFleet(slots, len(orderedFleet)))

Because the RETAINED SET now depends on fleet size, growing the roster re-sorts a DIFFERENT set and reshuffles existing assignments. On real era-5 slots [H49, J56, B7, E42, A1, AX5Z]:
  3 hulls -> sorted [B7, H49, J56]        -> C-1=B7, C-2=H49, C-3=J56
  4 hulls -> sorted [B7, E42, H49, J56]   -> C-2 moves H49->E42, C-3 moves J56->H49

Pre-sp-9suun the FULL set was always sorted, so appending a higher-symbol hull moved nobody. Ship symbols increment, so BUYING A HULL — the common case, which the scaler does twice on every cold-start ramp — was non-disruptive before and is disruptive now. Each relocation is fuel + travel time for zero placement gain.

This directly contradicts the function's own documented contract at standby_assignment.go:9-10 ('a second homing pass moves no hull').

COVERAGE GAP: sp-9suun's tests check the 2-hull and 3-hull cases independently but never assert stability ACROSS the transition. A test that adds a hull and asserts no existing assignment changed would have caught it.

FIX SHAPE (needs a decision, not a patch): zip the sorted fleet onto the PRIORITY-ORDERED retained slots without re-sorting — stable under append. But that also changes the fleet>=slots zip, so the two cases must be reconciled deliberately.

NOT a spend change; no money guard involved (RULINGS #4 untouched).
notes:
FIXED on branch sp-lkuh9 (base 3efb3883): 8557a053 (fix + tests) and f751fc4a (doc correction from probe P2, comment-only — 11 pure // insertions, 0 deletions).

THE FIX IS ONE LINE: stop re-sorting the truncated slots and keep the caller PRIORITY order. The retained set then becomes a PREFIX, so growing the roster only APPENDS a slot and every incumbent keeps its index. sp-9suun truncation is UNTOUCHED, per this bead own NOTES.

DESIGN RULING — STABILITY IMPLEMENTED, NOT NEAREST, AND THE ARGUMENT IS STRONGER THAN THE PURITY ONE I RAISED: AssignedSlot is called PER-HULL from THREE sites, so "nearest vacant to me" evaluated independently by two hulls can return THE SAME SLOT TO BOTH — the pile-up that fixed placement exists to prevent. Correct nearest-assignment is a GLOBAL MATCHING over a consistent position snapshot; this signature cannot express it, and attempting it re-introduces the concurrent race BY CONSTRUCTION. So the suggested-acceptance wording in this bead is not achievable at this seam.

!! DO NOT OVERSTATE THE RESULT — the lane policed this itself !!: the 13.1x is FULLY closed ON THE MEASURED INCIDENT, because on that live geometry the slot that opens for the 4th hull IS the 62u-adjacent E42. The test asserts total travel == 62.0u, exactly the adjacent minimum this bead demanded (old rule: 1360u on the fixture, 811u live). THAT IS GEOMETRY AGREEING WITH PRIORITY ORDER, NOT A GENERAL GUARANTEE. A future geometry where the next priority slot is far from the newcomer would still travel further.

TESTS: 4 new / 3 updated in the domain package plus 2 fixtures re-ordered in home_ship_test.go. BOTH new behaviour tests proven FAILING against unfixed code first, with the expected values (1360.0u, 12 relocations) HAND-COMPUTED IN ADVANCE. 113 pkgs green, -race green, build+vet unpiped rc=0, gofmt clean.
PROBES: P1 (revert the fix) killed 5; P3 (drop the roster sort) killed 10; P4 killed 2, labelled a PANIC-kill; P2 SURVIVED BY DESIGN — with the sort gone, truncateToFleet is PROVABLY A NO-OP for the result (positional zip, index always < fleet size). It was KEPT per the instruction not to revert sp-9suun, and f751fc4a rewrites the doc to say so rather than claiming a role a probe can falsify, warning that the redundancy is CONDITIONAL on the sort absence.

DEFECT #2 SPLIT OUT AS sp-ia0ny (P1) — proven INDEPENDENT, not a symptom of this one: THE TARGET SLOT WAS IDENTICAL (H51) ON EVERY DISPATCH, whereas a reshuffle shows a CHANGING slot. Real chain is a navigate stalled in refuel backoff while each ~90s sweep fires a FRESH HomeShipCommand, because nothing tracks an in-flight homing. Count corrected to AT LEAST SIX dispatches, not five — this bead figures were LOCAL timestamps and the box is UTC-3.

TWO DEPLOY CONCERNS FROM THE LANE: (1) the fix RE-PERMUTES THE CURRENT LIVE ASSIGNMENT ONCE on deploy — up to 6 hulls move, unavoidable because todays mapping IS the buggy one; worth timing away from an active contract. (2) Slot ORDER is now load-bearing in all regimes. TopDeliverySlots is verified deterministic (fixed anchor tuple + SliceStable with symbol tiebreak), but the demand-ranked central fill PAST the 4 anchors can re-rank as demand moves, which would now permute where the re-sort masked it. Exposure is small (a fleet of <=4 hulls never reaches the fill); flagged rather than pre-emptively frozen.

No contradiction found between bead and code — description, NOTES and live logs all held up. Not a spend change; no money guard touched. Ships ARMED, no flag.

title: Contract standby placement: add the two era-invariant FAR anchors (J-band sink + B7-class source base) — central-only set is structurally short
description:
ADMIRAL HYPOTHESIS (2026-08-02): idle contract hulls belong at the system EDGES (J56-in-era-5-style), plus one on the perpendicular axis. Analyst geometry on the full era-5 corpus CONFIRMS, and it is ERA-INVARIANT (eras 2, 4, 5 all show the same two far anchors). Keep the sp-yv230 fixed one-hull-per-park homing MECHANISM — only the candidate SET changes.

Warehouse-served contracts were SLOWER than direct (median cycle 6.5 vs 3.9 min; mean 13.2 vs 9.3) — the cycle-time benefit it was built for never materialized in production (sp-q1ptw's ~3-6x projection unvalidated).
3. Cost: 1+ warehouse hull parked full-time (zero duty, pure storage) + 1 stocker hull (~380k each at era-5 light prices) + prepaid inventory float + an open maintenance tail: sp-g0mdl (P1 dead warehouse capacity), sp-537w, sp-evdn, sp-2uft, sp-sjxi, sp-dm5e, sp-k6u4, sp-2rt8n — an entire bug queue for a 6% mechanic.

SUPERSEDES/CLOSES ON LANDING: sp-q1ptw (pre-stock mesh design — premise refuted), plus the depot tail above (lead/captain closes). Coordinate with sp-g4h4b (knob consolidation, in_progress) — overlapping contract-subsystem surface.

notes:
Companion placement bead filed the same session; the two change the same subsystem — lane-serialize if same-file overlap.
Companion placement bead: sp-9suun.

SIZING + THREE FINDINGS (sp-k0ye9 lane, 2026-08-06, measured before declining the lane).

SIZE: 29 non-test + 37 test files NAMED for the mechanic; 107 further non-test files
REFERENCE it. ~170 total. Heaviest referencing files:
   408  pkg/proto/daemon/daemon.pb.go        <- generated; RPC removal implies regeneration
   181  pkg/proto/daemon/daemon_grpc.pb.go
   168  application/contractscaler/commands/run_contract_scaler.go
    47  application/trading/services/tour_deposit_candidates.go          <- ADJACENT, NOT this mechanic
    43  cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go
    37  domain/contractscaler/plan.go
    33  application/manufacturing/commands/run_construction_coordinator_inventory.go  <- ADJACENT
THE RISK IS NOT THE COUNT. It is that deciding per-site whether a 'warehouse' reference
belongs to the CONTRACT DEPOT or to the TOUR/CONSTRUCTION storage path is judgment that must
hold across ~170 files. A half-finished removal leaves a writer gone while a caller silently
no-ops, or breaks an adjacent subsystem via a plausible-looking sweep.

FINDING 1 -- THE REMOVAL IS SAFER THAN THE BEAD IMPLIES: THERE IS NO LIVE STATE. Zero
warehouse/stocker/depot containers have EVER run on staging, and dedicated_fleet holds only
sensing_parked / trade / contract / purchasing / (empty) -- no depot tags. No running
container to orphan, no live claim to unwind, no migration to perform. Corroborated
independently by the lead: 0 warehouse/stocker hulls, 0 such purchases.

WarehouseWithdrawalModel are all in persistence.AllModels(), which AutoMigrate consumes.
TestAllModelsRegistersEveryModelStruct WILL NOT CATCH their deletion: that guard fails only
when a declared model is MISSING from the list, so deleting the struct AND its entry together
compiles and passes. Existing rows survive either way, but A FRESH DB WOULD NEVER CREATE THE
TABLES. Make this an explicit decision -- keep the three models registered, or accept the
history tables become legacy-only -- rather than letting it fall out of the sweep silently.

FINDING 3 -- RULINGS #4 RESOLVES, WITH A DISCRIMINATOR. MaxDeliveryHulls=6 is untouched; what
disappears is the warehouse/stocker BUNDLE -- spend legs, not a bound. That is a SINK removal,

warning: ceiling headroom past the knee must buy NOTHING. If removing the bundle leaves budget
some other leg now absorbs, that is a CAP change wearing a sink's clothes and #4 stops holding.

callers -- dead on arrival once depot goes), sp-g0mdl (P3), sp-dt5re (P3). NOTE ON sp-dt5re:

be worth keeping INDEPENDENTLY of depot rather than closing with it.

title: COGS inventory is valued at a LIFETIME average cost, not the cost of units actually held — TORWIND-2F5 reads 1212% on a ~34% window
description:
FOLLOW-UP TO sp-4gcts (merged 76757177), which fixed window-clipping and EXPOSED this second, distinct mechanism. Reproduced exactly against live data 2026-08-02 ~02:55 UTC. The Admiral found it on the dashboard; my acceptance test missed it.

MECHANISM. The hull_inv CTE values inventory at each boundary as net_units * avg_unit_cost, where avg_unit_cost = (all purchase spend before asof) / (all purchase UNITS before asof). That is a LIFETIME weighted average over every purchase the hull ever made of that good. But net_units are the units STILL HELD, which came from specific recent lots at different prices. The two are different populations, so the valuation is wrong whenever a hull has bought the same good at materially different prices over its life.

MEASURED for TORWIND-2F5, closing boundary:
  good       held   actually paid/unit   valued at/unit
  EQUIPMENT    60         1,983             2,633.9
  MACHINERY    60         2,125             2,322.4
  URANITE     105         3,394             3,277.5
  closing inventory valued 641,517 against 602,850 actually paid (+38,667 over-valued; errors do NOT cancel)

ARITHMETIC OF THE FAILURE, now-1h window:
  opening inventory  43,056   (PLATINUM 180 @ lifetime avg 239.2; actually paid 43,740)
  purchases         602,850
  closing           641,517
  COGS = 43,056 + 602,850 - 641,517 = 4,389
  margin = (57,600 - 4,389)/4,389 = 1212.4%   <- panel reads 1212.7%
The true figure is PLATINUM's round trip: bought 180 @ 243 = 43,740 at 01:57, sold 180 @ 320 = 57,600 at 02:41 = +13,860, about +31.7%. Whole-window COGS should be ~43,700, not 4,389 - a 10x error landing entirely in the denominator.

WHY IT SURVIVED sp-4gcts's ACCEPTANCE: that bead's tests were the named broken case and one healthy control. Both pass. NOBODY SWEPT THE POPULATION. Under the fix, the fleet max is 1212.7% (2F5); under the old formula it was 5,868.8% (TORWIND-349). Better, still wrong. ACCEPTANCE FOR THIS BEAD MUST INCLUDE A FLEET-WIDE SWEEP: no hull may exceed a plausible bound, and the max must be reported, not just the named case.

FIX SHAPE: maintain a RUNNING (moving) weighted-average cost chronologically - each purchase updates the average, each sale consumes units at the then-current average - so inventory at any boundary reflects what was actually paid for the units still held. The current version averages over all purchases ever and ignores that earlier sales already consumed some of them. FIFO is the alternative and is more faithful still, but moving-average is consistent with the existing design's intent and is cheaper in SQL. Whichever is chosen, opening and closing must use the SAME rule or the difference reappears as phantom COGS.

WHAT MUST NOT BREAK:
- sp-d767k: inventory is per-(hull,good) NET units, never derived from a last-sell timestamp. Hulls interleave lots.
- sp-4gcts's own property: a hull flat at BOTH boundaries must still reduce to the window's own spend, so a wholly-contained round-trip is scored exactly as before. Prove it again; do not assume the earlier proof survives a change to the valuation rule.
- The money columns (Realised Net, In Cargo, Net @ Cost) and the ten payback panels are out of scope.
- NOTE the 'In Cargo' column still uses the OLD window-clipped open_cargo CTE, so it can disagree with the closing inventory COGS uses. That divergence is real today (In Cargo showed 602,850 while COGS used 641,517) and is confusing on its face. Decide deliberately whether to unify them and say which.

CAUTION: the daemon is LIVE and trading. Pin fixed absolute windows in testing, never now-relative.
close_reason:
FIXED and merged to main as 227c7ed5. Three panels, one file, 3 lines.

THE FIX: inventory is now walked CHRONOLOGICALLY per (hull, good) — a purchase adds its spend and re-averages the holding, a sale releases units at the then-current average — so a boundary valuation reflects what was actually paid for the units still held. The previous version averaged over ALL purchases ever made of that good and multiplied that by units currently held: two different populations, wrong whenever a hull bought the same good at materially different prices.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE COMMITTED ARTIFACT, macros expanded to fixed absolute timestamps, run on the live DB:
  TORWIND-2F5, 02:00-03:00   1212.7%  ->  31.7%, with COGS = 43,740 = EXACTLY the PLATINUM lot's purchase cost
  In Cargo                    602,850 = exactly what was paid (previously the column showed 602,850 while COGS used 641,517)
  fleet max, same window      1212.7%  ->  63.5%   (no absurd rows remain)
  healthy control TORWIND-5F, 00:28-01:20:  51.9% OLD and 51.9% NEW — identical
The healthy case was RE-PROVED against the new valuation rule rather than inherited from sp-4gcts's proof, which is what I insisted on: flat at both boundaries means opening = closing = 0, COGS collapses to the window's own spend, and the expression reduces to the pre-fix formula exactly.

THE ACCEPTANCE RULE THAT CAME OUT OF THIS IS BETTER THAN THE ONE I ASKED FOR. I asked for a numeric ceiling on fleet-wide margin. The lane swept six consecutive 1h windows (37-46 hulls each) and found one row at 116.8% — above any bound I would have called plausible — and instead of capping it or accepting it, decomposed it lot by lot. It is REAL: TORWIND-27A bought 20 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY at 3,222/u at 19:42 and sold at 6,984/u at 20:35, a genuine 2.17x, with COGS = 64,440 = that lot's exact cost and opening 70,875 / closing 7,755 decomposing precisely to the other three goods held. A hard cap would have condemned working code. THE RULE IS: high margins must DECOMPOSE TO REAL TRADES, not sit under an arbitrary ceiling.

IN CARGO UNIFIED with the closing inventory COGS uses. Two readings of one quantity differing by 38,667 on the same row is indefensible — there is no version of 'cargo currently held, at cost' that legitimately has two values. This changes In Cargo and Net @ Cost from what sp-4gcts froze, deliberately, and fixes a second latent bug in them: the old window-clipped average missed cargo bought before the window entirely.

sp-d767k HONOURED AND STRENGTHENED: walking every event in order cannot be fooled by interleaved lots because it never consults an aggregate at all. Reference and reasoning kept in the comment.

COST CHECKED BEFORE COMMITTING TO THE APPROACH: the recursive walk runs 0.3-0.5s over 25,433 cargo rows / 1,591 (hull,good) pairs. Moving-average was chosen over FIFO on my steer; FIFO is more faithful on a hull interleaving lots at very different prices and is the documented upgrade path if a row ever looks wrong again. Payback panels byte-compared untouched.

PROVENANCE AND THE PROCESS LESSON: the Admiral found this on the dashboard, as they found sp-4gcts before it. Both times my acceptance test was 'the case named in the ticket plus one healthy control', and both times the surviving failure was in the population I never swept. sp-4gcts's fix was real and reduced the fleet max from 5,868.8% to 1,212.7% — better, still wrong, and a sweep would have shown that immediately.
