title: Per-hull Margin % divides window-clipped revenue by window-clipped cost — TORWIND-5F reads 10,310% on a real 22.4% run
description:
REPRODUCED EXACTLY against live data 2026-08-02 01:20 UTC.

Dashboard gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json, panel 'Per-Hull P&L - realised, deployed, and honest net', column 'Margin %':
    ROUND(100.0 * tx.net / tx.spent, 1)
  where tx.net   = SUM(t.amount)                                    (buys negative, sells positive)
        tx.spent = SUM(-t.amount) FILTER (transaction_type='PURCHASE_CARGO')
  both scoped by $__timeFilter(t.created_at).

TORWIND-5F over a now-1h window (00:20-01:20):
    sells inside window   111,720 + 331,440 + 6,560 = 449,720
    buys  inside window                                   4,320
    net = 449,720 - 4,320 = 445,400 ; 100*445,400/4,320 = 10,310%   <- matches the panel to the digit
The window caught the LAB_INSTRUMENTS SALE at 00:27 but not the PURCHASE at 00:03 that funded it, so a 443k sale is divided by an unrelated 4,320 SILVER_ORE buy.

THE TRUE FIGURE for that hull's run (23:56-01:19, five completed round-trips, from tour_leg_telemetry):
  MEDICINE        buy 375,640 -> sell 404,240   +28,600  (7.6%)
  FERTILIZERS     buy  12,480 -> sell  17,840   + 5,360 (42.9%)
  ELECTRONICS     buy 192,560 -> sell 228,440   +35,880 (18.6%)
  LAB_INSTRUMENTS buy 314,000 -> sell 443,160   +129,160 (41.1%)
  SILVER_ORE      buy   4,320 -> sell   6,560   + 2,240 (51.9%)
  TOTAL           buy 899,000 -> sell 1,100,240 +201,240 (22.4%)

THE MECHANISM IS ASYMMETRIC INVENTORY ACCOUNTING, not merely 'a short window'. The panel ALREADY carries a term for cargo BOUGHT inside the window and not yet sold — the open_cargo CTE, which values held units at that hull's average purchase cost and exists precisely because of sp-d767k (interleaved lots). There is NO mirror term for cargo SOLD inside the window that was BOUGHT before it. Cost is carried forward; revenue is not given its cost back. So the error is one-directional and always inflates: any hull whose buy and sell straddle the window edge reads high, and slid an hour the other way the same hull reads as a loss.

THIS IS NOT RARE. A round trip runs ~30 min against a default 1h window, so roughly half of all round-trips straddle an edge at any moment. The shorter the window the worse it gets, and now-1h is the dashboard's own default.

SAME DEFECT, SAME FILE, CHECK EACH: panel 'Gross Margin' (100.0*SUM(amount)/SUM(purchases), same time filter) and panel 'Profitability by Good' ('Margin %' computed the same way, grouped by good rather than hull) are both exposed to it. Fix or explicitly exempt each, and say which.

FIX SHAPE — cost of goods sold, and the machinery mostly exists. Give each SELL its matched cost regardless of when the buy happened: per (hull, good) average unit cost computed over a lookback that PRECEDES the window (not clipped to it), then COGS = units_sold * avg_unit_cost and Margin % = 100*(revenue - COGS)/COGS. open_cargo already computes exactly this avg_unit_cost expression; it is only restricted to the window. An equivalent framing is opening-inventory + purchases - closing-inventory.

WHAT MUST NOT BREAK:
- sp-d767k's rule stands: held cargo is per-(hull,good) NET units, bought minus sold, NEVER derived from a last-sell timestamp. Hulls interleave lots, and a hull that sold an OLDER lot after buying a NEWER one had its entire held inventory erased. Keep the comment and the behaviour.
- The SECOND target on that panel (the capex/payback query) deliberately has NO $__timeFilter and is all-time. It is NOT affected. Do not add a time filter to it.
- 'Realised Net', 'In Cargo' and 'Net @ Cost' are credit amounts, not ratios, and are correct as they stand. This bead is about the RATIO columns only. Do not restate the money columns.

ACCEPTANCE: replay TORWIND-5F over the 00:20-01:20 window and the column reads a value consistent with 22.4%, not 10,310%; a hull whose entire round-trip sits inside the window is UNCHANGED from today (prove it, so the fix is not a rewrite of the healthy case); and a hull that only BOUGHT in the window still shows its cost without inventing revenue. State plainly what the column now means, because 'margin over a window' is genuinely ambiguous when trades straddle it.

CAUTION: the daemon is LIVE and trading (192 legs in the last 30 min), so live numbers move under you. Pin a fixed absolute window in testing rather than now-relative, or you will chase a moving target.
close_reason:
FIXED and merged to main as 76757177. One file, 3 lines, panels 105 (Gross Margin), 113 (Per-Hull P&L) and 121 (Profitability by Good).

THE COLUMN NOW MEANS: Margin % = 100 x (revenue in window - COGS) / COGS, where COGS = opening inventory + purchases in window - closing inventory. Margin on the goods actually SOLD during the window, charged their real acquisition cost regardless of when they were bought. Inventory is valued at each boundary by the same per-(hull,good) NET-units rule open_cargo already uses, but with no lower time bound, so pre-window cargo is still valued. That is the mirror term the panel lacked.

I VERIFIED AGAINST THE COMMITTED ARTIFACT, not a prototype and not the lane's word — extracted panel 113's rawSql from the branch, expanded $__timeFilter/$__timeFrom/$__timeTo to fixed absolute timestamps (confirmed zero macros remained), and ran it against the live DB:
  broken case, 00:20-01:20 UTC : TORWIND-5F reads 44.2%  (was 10,310%)
  healthy case, 00:28-01:20 UTC: OLD SQL 51.9% / NEW SQL 51.9% - IDENTICAL, Spent and Earned unchanged
The healthy case is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION, not coincidence: flat inventory at both boundaries makes opening and closing zero, COGS collapses to the window's own spend, and the expression reduces to the old formula exactly.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN BRIEF, both the lane's and both right:
1. My 22.4% acceptance target was THE WRONG QUANTITY. 22.4% is the margin over TORWIND-5F's whole run; the 00:20-01:20 window contains only the LAB_INSTRUMENTS and SILVER_ORE sales, which this bead itself prices at 41.1% and 51.9% — blended, 44.2%. A window-scoped column cannot equal a whole-run figure unless the window covers the run. Over 23:56-01:20 the panel reads 30.2%, not 22.4%, because that window straddles at its START too (FERTILIZERS sold 00:00:55 was bought earlier). A column that reads 22.4% is a different column — lifetime margin — and would be its own bead.
2. Panel 113 has ONE target, not two. The capex/payback queries are separate panels (20-29), verified untouched by byte comparison. My 'do not add a timeFilter to the second target' instruction had nothing to apply to.

SIBLING PANELS both fixed, neither exempt. Profitability by Good was the worst hit: over 1h MEDICINE read 115.5% and ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 84.9%; they now read 35.0% and 17.6%. Fleet Gross Margin barely moved (32.1% -> 31.2%) because straddles largely cancel in aggregate — that panel was never badly wrong, and it was changed for consistency rather than because it lied. Do not read a trend into that delta.

THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS NOT ANY SINGLE NUMBER: the corrected figures are STABLE ACROSS WINDOW WIDTHS while the old ones swung with the slice. CLOTHING read 45.5% at 1h vs 21.0% at 13h before; now 31.3-35.3%. A real margin should not depend on how you cut time, and now it roughly does not.

PRESERVED: sp-d767k's rule (held cargo is per-(hull,good) NET units, never derived from a last-sell timestamp) and its comment, both asserted present post-edit; the money columns Realised Net / In Cargo / Net @ Cost, which are credit amounts and were always correct; and all ten payback panels.

KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: open_cargo's avg_unit_cost is still window-clipped, so the 'In Cargo' column can under-value a hull holding cargo bought before the window. Different column, out of scope here, worth its own bead.

PROVENANCE: the Admiral caught this, not me. I reported TORWIND-5F's run at 22.4% and they pushed back with the dashboard showing 10,310%. Both numbers were real; the panel's arithmetic was correct and its answer was not.

title: [bug] main is RED: two routing-service tour-handler tests fail on a pristine checkout, and no gate runs pytest
description:

routing-service suite is RED:

  FAILED tests/test_tour_handler.py::test_handler_forwards_inter_system_hops

This is PRE-EXISTING and not attributable to any pending lane: it was found as the CONTROL
arm while verifying the gatefee merge, and the identical two failures appear on merged and
pristine trees alike.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: captain-gate's RunGate runs ONLY `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`.
It never runs pytest, so no Go-side gate can catch a red routing-service suite. Every lane
touching the Python solver has been gated without its tests being run.

COMPOUNDING FRAGILITY: services/routing-service/generated/*.py is GITIGNORED
(gobot/.gitignore:80), so whether these tests pass at all depends on when the developer last
ran generate_protos.sh. A stale stub set and a current one are not the same test subject.
This makes "pytest green" claims in commit messages unreproducible by construction.

NOTE the most recent commit touching this area (sp-ircfy, 0dbd793e, 23:58) claims "252 pytest
green". Either that claim did not hold, or something regressed after it. NOT DIAGNOSED — the
11880 vs 23880 gap is roughly 2x and the sibling failure is about inter_system_hops
forwarding, so sp-tp5c3's travel-cost change (gate_hops x per-crossing, was flat 1 hop) is a
plausible but UNCONFIRMED origin. Do not treat that as the cause without checking.
notes:
TESTS FIXED AND GATED 2026-08-01 at main a0bdd7d2 (squash). Routing-service suite in the service venv: 271 passed, 2 skipped, no failures, nothing excluded.

ROOT CAUSE: the per-hop jump-gate fee is netted out of projected_profit. When that landed
the SOLVER-level tests were updated and the two HANDLER-level ones were not. Code was
correct; the tests encoded the pre-fee world. Confirmed by arithmetic, not by matching
observed output: the golden board grosses 23,880 and makes two crossings at the fitted
default 6,000/hop, so 11,880 is exactly right. The expectation is now written as
23_880 - 2 * 6_000 so it states the law and still fails if the fee stops being charged.

The hops test asserted 'declaring hops changes time, not tour shape'. That premise is now
false BY DESIGN: 2 declared hops put 4 x 6,000 = 24,000 of fee against a 23,880 gross
crossing, making it a net loss, so the intra-system tour correctly wins. It now proves what
its name claims — the field survives the wire — since an unbridged field would leave the
armed response identical to baseline.

THE TWO SKIPS ARE BOTH CORRECT, checked rather than assumed:
 - test_tour_solve_latency: pre-existing opt-in benchmark (RUN_LATENCY_BENCH=1).
 - test_replay_objective: added importorskip. It is a MODEL-PIPELINE test and its deps are
   deliberately absent from the pinned service venv. Verified it RUNS in the model venv
   .venv-p0: 40 passed. Coverage is not lost. Installing requirements-model.txt into the
   service venv was rejected — a dry-run showed it would bump the pinned grpcio 1.81.1 to
   1.82.1 under a live gRPC service, and that pin is what keeps launchd restarts
   reproducible.

STILL OPEN — THE BLINDNESS, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. captain-gate's RunGate runs only
go build and go test. NOTHING runs pytest automatically, in either venv. Wiring it needs
ProvisionWorktree to supply the service venv and generate protobuf stubs into the worktree,
neither of which it does today (it copies only pkg/proto/daemon and pkg/proto/routing).
Getting that wrong breaks every future gate, so it was not attempted at the end of a long
session. That is the remaining work on this bead.
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (mechanical, open-bead-vs-main sweep) — 1 commit(s) on main name this bead in the SUBJECT line:

  a0bdd7d2 2026-08-01 test(routing): repair two tour-handler tests that encoded pre-fee economics (sp-m28ei)

NOT a verdict that the bead is satisfied — the sweep matched commit subjects, it did not check
this bead's acceptance criteria. Several beads in this sweep are epics, are explicitly partial
(their own commit says 'residual' / 'deferred from' / 'part B+C'), or have acceptance criteria
that are a MEASUREMENT rather than a shipped artifact, and those correctly stay open.

Before closing on this evidence, read the acceptance criteria and confirm the commits above
actually satisfy them. A changed file is not a fixed bead.

The Python routing service — which plans EVERY tour — has no gating tests at all. Any change to tour_solver.py or the handlers can merge with its suite red, and did.

CONFIRMED FAILING ON MAIN (run with the service's own venv, ./venv/bin/python3 -m pytest, since bare python3 lacks grpc):
  tests/test_tour_handler.py::test_golden_tour                       assert 11880 == 23880
  tests/test_tour_handler.py::test_handler_forwards_inter_system_hops
Both fail identically on main with no lane's changes applied — I verified this directly rather than accepting the reporting lane's word, because the claim was load-bearing for accepting its build's test status.

CAUSE: sp-wtc47 subtracted gate fees from projected profit and never updated the golden expectations. Its own commit message notes captain-gate does not run this suite, so the breakage was known-at-write and caught by nothing. The 11880 vs 23880 gap is roughly the fee subtraction, so the test is very likely just stale rather than the code being wrong — but that must be CONFIRMED, not assumed, before the expectation is rewritten. Rewriting a golden to match current output is how a real regression gets blessed.

THIRD FAILURE, separate cause: tests/test_replay_objective.py cannot COLLECT at all — sqlalchemy is absent from the routing-service venv. Also true on main. A test that cannot be collected is invisible in a pass count, which is worse than a red one.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE TWO: the routing service decides which tours the fleet flies, and travel is 24.4% of net trading margin (sp-9idvn). It is the single least-gated component with the largest measured effect on profit.

SCOPE — two separable pieces, and the ordering matters:
1. Make the suite green FIRST, with each failure diagnosed rather than re-baselined. Prove the golden's new expected value is arithmetically the old one minus the fee term; if it is not, there is a real defect underneath. Install sqlalchemy (or make the import optional) so test_replay_objective collects.
2. THEN add pytest to captain-gate. Adding it while red would block every merge in the repo, which is why this order is not negotiable.

CAUTION on (2): captain-gate is a PROTECTED PATH (cmd/captain-gate/**). Do not modify it without an explicit Admiral decision — file the proposal, do not ship it. The pytest invocation must use the service venv (bare python3 lacks grpc) and must fail the gate on collection errors, not only on assertion failures, or the sqlalchemy class of problem stays invisible.

NOT URGENT TONIGHT: the daemon is stopped/idle and no Python change is queued to merge. This is a standing quality hole, not a live incident.

title: Probe expansion sizing ignores ferry cost — landed cost is 1.63x sticker price (10.15M bought, 6.44M to deliver)
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31, and it silently overran an explicit Admiral budget.

The Admiral authorized ~10M for a probe expansion. We bought 258 probes for 10,152,775 — on budget. Ferrying them to post cost a further 6,444,427 in jump fees. LANDED COST 16.6M, 63% over the authorization.

Nothing in the sizing path prices the ferry. A probe's true cost is purchase + (jumps from yard to post x per-gate fee), and only the first term is modelled. At the measured median gate fee of 5,160 and the observed ferry distances, that is a 0.63x multiplier the money guards never see.

EVIDENCE
- 263 PURCHASE_SHIP rows / 21,904,334 in 12h; net of 5 heavy freighters (~11.75M) = 258 probes / ~10.15M.
- Jump fees with no OperationContext (= sensing; sensingCtx sets only an API-budget source, so all sensing jumps land as operation_type 'manual') = 6,785,368 over 12h, 87% of it inside the 6h surge window.
- Probe jumps stepped 3-6/hr (06:00-13:00 UTC) to 111 -> 307 -> 273 -> 273 -> 195 from 15:00 UTC — a ~60x step, 98% of it hulls bought today ferrying to post.
- Fee share of net trading margin went 9.8-26.5%/hr pre-surge to 50.5-55.5%/hr across 16:00-19:00 UTC.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE OVERRUN: this distorts the probe ROI calculation that justifies expansion at all. A probe evaluated at 83k sticker that actually costs ~135k landed needs 63% more coverage value to break even. Every past sizing decision was made on the wrong number.

SCOPE — sizing only, do NOT touch these:
- Do NOT reduce probe COUNT as the mechanism. Standing warning on sp-ntgfj; an earlier max_probe_fleet cap was reverted for exactly this reason. The point is to price the ferry honestly, not to buy fewer.
- Do NOT weaken capex_reserve_credits / capital_multiplier_k_milli / probe_cap. Money guards fail closed (RULINGS #4). Adding ferry cost makes them STRICTER, which is the correct direction.
- Do NOT re-open sensing scope. Footprint-scoping is Admiral-rejected on sp-ntgfj.

CURRENT STATE: probe buying is OFF (sensing expansion_enabled=2), so this is not bleeding right now. It must be priced BEFORE it is re-armed — including by any automated re-arm on sink thinning, which does not know about the 1.63x.

ACCEPTANCE: the probe sizer's cost term includes expected ferry cost from the purchase yard to the intended post; a sizing decision logs purchase, ferry, and landed cost separately so the multiplier is visible; the guards bind on landed cost, not sticker. Prove with a test that a probe whose post is many gates away is sized differently from one bought at its destination.

RELATED: sp-9idvn establishes the per-ORIGIN-GATE fee model (286 scalars, learnable from the ledger). That table is the natural input to this estimate, and probe ferry routing is its second consumer after tour routing.
close_reason:
Built, gated and merged to main as 665af566 (5 files, +471/-9). The buy floor now binds on landed cost: FerryHops floored at 1 for a ferried counter with an unresolved hop count (fail-closed), FerryCost clamps each factor independently so two negatives cannot multiply into a phantom credit, LandedProbeCost floored at the quote so no malformed input can weaken the guard. DefaultGateFeeCredits=5900, the fleet MEAN of 4235 measured jumps (mean 5930, median 5504, p90 7475) - mean not median because the scalar multiplies a hop count to price a SUM of crossings and E[sum]=n*mean; the right-skew means the median would understate every multi-hop ferry, and understating is the one direction a money guard may not fail. sp-9idvn's per-origin-gate table is the natural refinement and this constant is its fleet mean.

Verified no guard became more permissive, mechanically: a local counter yields FerryHops=0 -> FerryCost=0 -> LandedProbeCost=quote, term-for-term identical to the previous check; a ferried counter always adds >=5900 so it is strictly harder to pass. Pre-existing floor tests unchanged and passing.

Mutation C (stop setting ferryHops) is the fixture-blindness proof: the fixture was tuned so 3 hops is distinguishable from BOTH 0 and a 1-hop fallback (floor 50000, quote 24356, treasury 85000 - local buys, one hop still buys, three hops refused), so without that middle row the acceptance test would have passed on the one-gate minimum alone with the wiring dead. Acceptance test asserts Attempts>0 BEFORE the refusal so a placement that never reached a counter cannot pass vacuously.

Also corrected the maxFerryHops doc, which asserted 'WHAT NINE COSTS IS TICKS, NOT CREDITS' - true of fuel, false of money, and that sentence is the belief that let this happen.

title: A declined market scan is stamped as a successful one — sensing freshness telemetry is 78.5% false
description:
CONFIRMED IN CODE AND MEASURED LIVE.

MECHANISM (two files, one boundary):
- application/ship/market_scanner.go: when the market-scan budget answers ServeFromStore, ScanAndSaveMarket returns nil. That is deliberate and CORRECT — its comment says 'Declining is a SUCCESS' because the caller's next act is the store read it would have done anyway.
- application/parkedsensing/scanner.go runScan: only an ERROR from Scan.Run skips MarkScanned. A decline returns nil, so it falls straight through to MarkScanned(ctx, player, waypoint, kind, at=clock.Now(), spread) and stamps sensing_slots.last_scan_at = now for a scan that never happened.

runScan's own comment states the invariant it breaks: 'a freshness stamp is a claim that data was written'. That holds for a FAILED scan, which is skipped. A DECLINED scan is neither failure nor success at this boundary, and nil collapses the two.

MEASURED (live, player 5):
- 909 slots stamped scanned within 75 min; 714 of them (78.5%) have market_data older than 75 min.
- Median gap between stamp and actual data write: 144 minutes. 
- 3,551 declines vs 310 real scans in one log window = 92% of attempts declined, so the stamp is wrong far more often than right.
- Fleet-wide: 909 slots CLAIM fresh, 216 markets ARE fresh.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is an observability defect, not (on current evidence) a credit leak — see the DO-NOT-CHASE note below. A sensing coordinator that declines every single scan is indistinguishable from one scanning perfectly. That is why this went unnoticed, and it blocks any future evaluation of sensing changes.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A TRAP. Do NOT simply skip MarkScanned on a decline. runScan refreshes the stamp on FAILURE on purpose: 'Leaving it stale would leave the slot due immediately and turn a failing waypoint into a hot retry loop against the API that is already failing.' At a 92% decline rate, making declines not advance the rotation clock would spin the whole rotation at full speed producing nothing.

THERE ARE TWO CLOCKS AND THEY MUST SEPARATE:
1. The rotation's LOCAL pacing clock — Scanner.requeue sets view.LastScan = at and scheduleFor orders the heap by it. This MUST still advance on a decline, or the hot-retry loop above.
2. The LEDGER's freshness claim — MarkScanned -> sensing_slots.last_scan_at. This must NOT advance, because no data was written.

So the fix is at the port boundary: Scan.Run must report DECLINED distinctly from SCANNED (it currently returns nil for both). Then runScan requeues as today (pacing preserved) but skips MarkScanned, exactly parallel to the existing failed-scan handling.

ACCEPTANCE: with the fix live, count of slots whose last_scan_at is fresh while their market_data is stale falls to ~0; rotation request rate does NOT rise (prove no hot-retry regression — this is the primary risk); a unit test drives the three outcomes (scanned / declined / failed) through runScan and asserts the stamp is written for exactly one of them.

DO NOT CHASE, already refuted with live data 2026-07-31:
- Do NOT bolt on footprint/scope-bounding of sensing. The Admiral explicitly rejected that on sp-ntgfj: a crushed market recovers on its own and the only way we learn is to go look; footprint-scoping risks never looking at a system we stopped trading in. The accepted design is one fixed budget + interval as an output + a value-ordered priority queue + anti-starvation, and it is already built and armed.
- Do NOT justify this bead as a profit fix. Plan-vs-realized price error was measured against market-row age: median error 0.00 pct at every age out to 12h, mean absolute error 1.51 pct (<75m) -> 2.09 pct (4-12h). Staleness adds unbiased VARIANCE, not bias, and the 12h credit delta across all engines is net POSITIVE. This is an instrument fix.
notes:
ROTATION ECONOMICS — measured 2026-07-31, and it says the DECLINE RATE IS NOT A BUG. Context for whoever fixes the stamp: do not try to make the rotation decline less.

Live Prometheus (15m rates):
  earning / spend                 0.2205/s   (never declined, Decide rule 1)
  discretionary / serve_from_store 0.1628/s
  discretionary / spend            0.0464/s
  daemon API TOTAL                 1.2199/s  against a 2.00 server ceiling
(Over a 1h window the same lane measured 0.2176 / 1.0085 / 0.0699 = 93.5% declines; the discretionary decline rate fell sharply after the probe surge ended and the 19:32 UTC restart. Both windows agree on the shape.)

THE ROTATION IS CHEAP BECAUSE IT DECLINES. A decline returns before apiClient.GetMarket, so it costs zero requests. The rotation's entire API cost is the discretionary/spend line — 3.8-5.4% of daemon traffic, ~2-3.5% of the server ceiling. The dominant market consumer is the EARNING class at 0.2205/s, 4.8x the rotation and never declined; that is where market API spend actually goes. Earning reads are the four pre-commit money guards and are RULINGS #4 protected — do not touch them from this bead.

DISCOVERY IS STRUCTURALLY UN-DECLINABLE, so no decline can ever cost us a new market: NeverScanned = time.Duration(math.MaxInt64) (budget.go:148) exceeds every MaxStaleness the package can compute, so Decide rule 2 admits an unscanned market unconditionally — above the interval check, the token check AND the weight bar. Every decline is therefore a REFRESH decline, and refresh is the component measured at ~1% of margin (see below).

REFRESH IS WORTH ~1% OF UNITS, CORROBORATED ON TWO INDEPENDENT CHANNELS.
  price error by row age:  median 0.00 pct at every age to 12h; mean abs 1.51 -> 2.09 pct
  under-fill by row age:   7.1% -> 7.7% -> 9.3% of solver legs short-filled (<75m / 1.25-4h / 4-12h),
                           units short 1.55% -> 2.56% -> 2.15%; ~1% of units, ~300k per 6h vs 29.8M
The under-fill channel matters because DEPTH is the binding term per sp-o2dzb, so it is the channel most likely to have hidden a loss that price error could not see. It agrees: real, positive, small. Caveat: current row age was used as a proxy for age at plan time (market_price_history is a change log and cannot date a scan), which biases toward finding LESS signal.

DO NOT RAISE market_scan.budget_req_per_sec AS A CASUAL KNOB TURN, despite the 39% API headroom. Interval and MaxStaleness are BOTH inversely proportional to the rate, so raising it shortens MaxStaleness, which tightens FreshnessCap (= max(floor, MaxStaleness)) IMMEDIATELY — while the data only gets fresher over the following rotation period. In that gap consumers refuse rows they accepted before. That is precisely the failure FreshnessCap's own doc comment says once cost 87% of trade throughput. The steady state is self-consistent; the TRANSIENT is the hazard. Any change here needs the transient analysed, and the payoff is only the ~1% above.
REFINEMENT to the 'do not raise budget_req_per_sec' warning above — it is bounded, and should NOT be read as 'never raise it'.

The mechanism stands (Interval and MaxStaleness both shrink the instant the rate rises, while row ages only improve over the following rotation), but the damage has a HARD BOTTOM already in the function. FreshnessCap applies floor as a FLOOR and never a ceiling:

  func FreshnessCap(floor, b, marketsKnown) {
      if marketsKnown <= 0 || b.RateReqPerSec <= 0 { return floor }
      if bound := MaxStaleness(b, marketsKnown); bound > floor { return bound }
      return floor
  }

so cap = max(floor, MaxStaleness). Raising the rate can tighten a consumer's cap DOWN TO ITS CONFIGURED FLOOR AND NO FURTHER. Its own doc says a consumer armed at a floor can never be disarmed through this function — the property the firm-sink money guard depends on (RULINGS #4).

THE MITIGATION IS THEREFORE AVAILABLE IN ADVANCE: set the floor first, then raise the rate. The transient is real but bounded and pre-emptable.

Exposure audited — the one call site passing floor=0 is NOT a gate. MarketFreshness.RotationBound (market_freshness.go:186) passes 0 deliberately: 'the age the current rotation cannot explain, with no floor applied — the number worth naming in a refusal log so an operator can see at once whether their floor is the binding term or the map is'. Verified it has exactly ONE non-test caller, run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:353, inside a log line. Diagnostic only. The two real gating sites (market_freshness.go:174 and captain/detectors_scout.go:226) both pass a floor.

NET: raising the rate is a legitimate operation with a known transient and a known mitigation. It is still only worth ~1% of units (see the two-channel measurement above), so it is a small prize — but it is not forbidden, and the earlier note should not be read that way.
MERGED + DEPLOYED 2026-07-31 ~20:47 UTC.

Merged to main as ec671eca (16 files, +788/-65). Gate: GatePassed/Merged true, Stale/Dirty/EmptyMerge false. Verified beyond the gate flag: git cherry showed both commits absent from main before merge, --diff-filter=DR empty, and git diff main scanstamp empty after (trees identical, nothing silently dropped).

MY PRESCRIBED FIX IN THIS BEAD WAS WRONG AND THE LANE OVERRULED IT CORRECTLY. The bead said 'runScan requeues exactly as it does today while skipping only the ledger write'. That does NOT preserve pacing: Scanner.SyncMembership (scanner.go:261) does s.members = members, builds a fresh NewNextDueHeap, and re-pushes every rotation member from the LEDGER-derived view every ~30s tick. I verified this directly; its own doc says the due time is 'recomputed from its own last scan' - from the view, not from requeue's in-memory write. So requeue's view.LastScan is authoritative for one tick and no longer, and skipping MarkScanned on a decline would re-pace every declined slot from its last REAL scan (median 144 min ago) => permanently due => the whole ~900-slot rotation spinning at full speed. The exact catastrophe this bead warned against, reached by this bead's own prescription. The stamp is not merely a report; it IS the durable pacing clock, so the two clocks had to separate IN THE LEDGER, not in memory.

WHAT SHIPPED: new column sensing_slots.last_scan_attempt_at (migration 050) as the durable PACING clock, advancing on every turn (scanned, declined or failed); last_scan_at keeps its meaning as the FRESHNESS claim and advances only on a real write. ScanAndSaveMarketWithOutcome returns (scanned, err) with ScanAndSaveMarket delegating and discarding, so all 20+ callers are byte-identical. readYard STILL RUNS on a declined turn - it is the only path that prices a yard we occupy and gating it would have silently dropped 92% of those readings. NULL coalesces to last_scan_at so the first tick after deploy paces identically to the last (without it, every existing row reads NULL and the entire rotation declares due at once - one full-speed sweep, the precise regression this exists to avoid). Identical collapse in ScanAndSaveMarketFresh fixed and proved inert (all 3 callers discard the bool).

6 mutations, all killed, each naming target tests; re-run and re-killed after the rebase onto 665af566. M2 IS MY PRESCRIPTION and it fails TestScannerRunScan_DeclineSurvivesTheReconcileRebuildWithoutBecomingDue, which carries a negative control feeding the stamp it would have had without the durable write - proving the rotation was capable of being due.

MIGRATION 050 APPLIED MANUALLY, and it is MANDATORY before any restart on this code. Confirmed: cmd/captain-migrate is NOT a database tool (it drives captain state/reports and emits bd commands, never touches Postgres); nothing in Go reads migrations/ (zero hits, no embed); the convention in gobot/CLAUDE.md:477 is manual psql -f, which is how 049 landed. GORM AutoMigrate DOES add the column but its failure at cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:143 is NON-FATAL - it warns and boots anyway. The lane probed the missing-column failure mode rather than assuming: ParkedSlotViews SUCCEEDS (SELECT * , field reads nil, coalesce falls back), but BOTH MarkScanAttempted AND MarkScanned FAIL with 42703 because both name the attempt column - and both are logged and swallowed. So a missed migration freezes last_scan_at fleet-wide, every 30s reconcile re-reads a frozen stamp, every slot reads permanently due, and the rotation churns at full speed. The hot loop arriving by deploy instead of by code.

Applied: docker exec -i spacetraders-postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U spacetraders -d spacetraders < gobot/migrations/050_add_sensing_slot_last_scan_attempt_at.up.sql
Baseline before: last_scan_attempt_at ABSENT. After: last_scan_attempt_at | timestamp with time zone | YES | (no default). ALTER TABLE + 2 COMMENTs.
Then make restart-daemon (launchd), new PID 91035. PROBE_SENSING_COORDINATOR RUNNING, zero AutoMigrate/42703/mark-scan-failure lines in the log.

STILL TO VERIFY before closing: last_scan_attempt_at filling (should reach the parked-slot count within a rotation), and the acceptance metric - count of slots whose last_scan_at is fresh while their max(market_data.last_updated) is stale - falling to ~0 from the measured 714 of 909.

VERIFIED WORKING IN PRODUCTION. Merged ec671eca, migration 050 applied, deployed 20:37 UTC 2026-07-31.

THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, run directly rather than waiting for the legacy decay: of every last_scan_at written SINCE the deploy, the count whose market data is older than the stamp by >2 min is ZERO. Median stamp-to-data gap is 0 SECONDS. Before the fix that population was 78.5% false with a 144-minute median gap. The defect is closed at the mechanism, not merely at the metric.

THE TWO CLOCKS ARE DEMONSTRABLY SEPARATED. First 5 minutes after restart: 873 parked market slots paced (last_scan_attempt_at) against 89 that actually wrote data (last_scan_at) — a 89.8% decline rate, matching the 92% measured before the fix. Under the old code all 873 would have claimed freshness.

PACING DID NOT REGRESS — the primary risk. Per-minute distribution since deploy: 20:37 -> 873, 20:38 -> 28, then steady state ~2/min. The 873 is the RESTART CATCH-UP BURST, not a hot loop, and it is pre-existing behaviour rather than anything this change introduced: at deploy every last_scan_attempt_at was NULL and coalesced to last_scan_at, which is exactly the clock the old code paced on. The rotation then settled and has continued turning; 908 of 965 parked slots paced within 11 minutes. Zero AutoMigrate/42703/mark-scan-failure lines in the log.

TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS I FELL INTO AND CORRECTED, recorded because they will recur:
1. I guessed the deploy moment as 20:47 UTC and tested 'stamped since deploy' against it, getting 1 row. The real deploy was 20:37 (derived self-calibratingly from min(last_scan_attempt_at), since the column was NULL before deploy). A wrong window made a working fix look like a dead one.
2. My first acceptance query counted data_at IS NULL as a false stamp and reported 26 of 45 stamps false. Decomposing it: 0 genuinely stale, 26 waypoints that have NEVER produced any market_data row. Those are not false stamps — the scan succeeded and wrote what there was.

METRIC FLOOR, for whoever reads the acceptance query later: 26 of 968 parked market slots have never had any market_data, so the falsely-fresh count as naively written FLOORS AT 26 AND CANNOT REACH 0. Exclude the NULL class or expect that floor.

That is arithmetic, not risk — last_scan_at no longer refreshes without a real write, so an unscanned slot cannot renew its claim. A bounded background check is armed to confirm the endpoint rather than assume it.

title: 11 of 52 trade hulls are parked in systems with ZERO profitable intra-system pairs — placement, not planning, is what makes hulls marginal
description:
GOAL-DIRECTED: more profitable trades. This is the largest profit lever identified today, and it is NOT in the solver.

MEASURED LIVE (player 5, verified independently of the lane that surfaced it): 11 of 52 trade hulls sit in systems with ZERO profitable intra-system good pairs — no (buy at waypoint A, sell at waypoint B) combination in that system where sell_price > purchase_price. Worst offenders:
  X1-TG88  4 hulls, 0 profitable pairs
  X1-TU10  3 hulls, 0 pairs
  X1-KP42  2 hulls, 0 pairs
  X1-BS29  1 hull,  0 pairs
  X1-RV70  1 hull,  0 pairs
  X1-GC55  3 hulls, 1 pair
A hull in a zero-pair system cannot trade locally at all. It must jump out to earn anything, and a jump now costs a MEASURED ~5,900 credits (2,274 jumps = 13.6M recorded since the fee accounting landed today). So these hulls pay the fleet largest per-unit cost to reach a market, on every single tour.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT PLACE TO LOOK, and the evidence that the alternatives are dead ends. sp-o2dzb replayed the live allocator with an argmin instrument and found the binding term is MARKET DEPTH (sell tranche ~46%, buy tranche ~27%) and HULL SPACE (~30%) — never the purse (afford bound 0% of allocations across four replays). Its termination census says 62-64% of allocation loops stop because there is NO POSITIVE SPREAD LEFT at live quotes, and under 1% stop on a cap. Its sweep, with positive controls firing in both directions, showed max_spend inert at x10 and x100, and REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES inert at 2.5. So the solver is not leaving money on the table; it is being handed hulls parked where there is no money.

ALSO CORRECTED, so nobody re-derives the wrong target: hulls are NOT 28% loaded. That figure came from comparing a tour_leg_telemetry row — which is ONE (leg, good, price) tranche capped at trade_volume — against the 225 hull. Hull-level occupancy is 174.4/225 = 77.5%, with 29 of 47 hulls at exactly 100%. Fill is not the problem and chasing it is a bad trade: doubling hull capacity in replay adds units worth 163 cr each against a 1,952 cr average, i.e. the marginal unit is worth 8% of the average one.

WHAT TO DETERMINE FIRST. Do not jump to relocating hulls. Establish, with evidence: (a) how a trade hull ends up in a system — is it placed, does it drift there on a tour that ended, or is it stranded? (b) does anything ever re-evaluate a trade hull position against local opportunity, or is placement one-shot? (c) for the 11, how did each arrive, and how long has it been there? (d) what does a hull in a zero-pair system actually DO each tour — measure its jumps per tour and net against a hull in a rich system such as X1-KY38.

Only then propose. The obvious fix (relocate to a system with pairs) has real hazards: relocation costs jumps and time, market pairs move as prices move so a system that is dead now may be rich in an hour, and concentrating hulls in the same rich system contends the same sinks — the fleet-wide absorption problem measured earlier at ~4 breaches per tour. A naive "move everyone to KY38" makes it worse.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not "hulls moved". It is that hulls in zero-pair systems either (a) earn measurably more after the change, or (b) are shown to be correctly placed for a reason the pair count does not capture — for example they are positioned for cross-system lanes the intra-system pair test cannot see. (b) is a legitimate and valuable outcome: the intra-system pair count is MY metric, and the solver plans cross-system tours, so it may simply be the wrong lens. Check that before acting on it.

Report per-hull net for the 11 against the fleet median (currently ~225k over 3h) so the size of the prize is known before anything moves.
notes:
PREMISE WITHDRAWN — the zero-pair systems are UNSCANNED, not poor. My LEFT JOIN read absence of data as absence of opportunity (unknown-is-not-impossible). Verified against waypoints.traits: X1-TU10 has 23 MARKETPLACE waypoints with 2 scanned; X1-TG88 has 6 with 0 scanned and 4 hulls parked there; KP42/RV70/BS29 all have marketplaces and zero scans. Fleet-wide 9 of 52 trade hulls are anchored in systems holding NO market data at all, and there are ZERO systems with a MEASURED zero profitable pairs.

DO NOT RELOCATE ON THIS BEAD. Moving hulls out of a 23-marketplace system on a measurement never taken could be moving them off the best opportunity in the fleet.

The symptom stands: those hulls are marginal and a blind home system means every tour opens with a jump out at ~5,900 credits. The CAUSE inverts from placement to sensing coverage, and so does the fix — scan first, decide placement after.

Re-scoped: step (0) is "for each system holding a trade hull, have we ever scanned it, and how many of its MARKETPLACE waypoints do we hold prices for?" title: Solver plans 63 units into a 225 hull against ~120 available depth — the binding term is NOT the tranche cap, and nobody knows what it is
description:
GOAL-DIRECTED: the Admiral wants more profitable trades. 39 of 52 hulls are marginal or losing. This is the largest unexplained gap between what the fleet could move and what it moves.

MEASURED (engine=solver legs only, which is now possible thanks to sp-fzt09s engine column — every previous analysis of this was contaminated by look-back and liquidation legs):
- solver plans 64 units, realizes 63. Execution is NOT the problem; the solver decides 63.
- hull capacity is 225. So 28% fill.
- available trade_volume at the waypoints the solver CHOOSES averages ~120 (buys 136, sells 106).
- the absorption ledger permits 137 per tranche and we use 76 = 55.7%.

THE OBVIOUS SUSPECT IS NOT THE ANSWER. REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES_PER_VISIT = 2.5 allows 2.5 x trade_volume = roughly 300 units per sink visit. We plan 63. The cap is nowhere near binding, so RAISING IT WOULD BE INERT. Same for MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES_PER_MARKET_GOOD_SIDE = 2 (both Go and Python sides verified in lockstep). Do not start there. A pinned value identifies the VALUE, never which term in the min() pinned it — enumerate EVERY term that can bound planned units before proposing anything.

AND THE DECAY MODEL IS NOT WRONG EITHER, which is the second thing that would waste a lane. Sell legs bucketed by size over 12h show realized-minus-planned unit price of +34, -18, -2, -10 across the <40 / 40-69 / 70-109 / 110+ bands. The model predicts large legs as accurately as small ones. Unit price does fall with size (4,497 -> 1,805) but that is GOOD MIX, not price impact: expensive goods move in small lots. Note gross revenue per leg RISES steeply with size: 81k -> 196k -> 253k -> 267k, so bigger legs are worth having if they are feasible.

Since we plan 63 against a ~120 trade_volume, the plan sits INSIDE tranche 1, where price is the live quote and no decay has been applied at all. So decay cannot be what stops it.

WHAT TO DO: enumerate every bound on planned units in tour_solver.py and the Go executor, then measure which one actually binds on live plans. Candidates to check and rule in or out with evidence, not reasoning: the greedy 1:1 buy/sell matching (min of buy depth, sell depth, hold space); MaxUnits / MaxSpend; working_capital_reserve (300k against a 43M treasury, so almost certainly not binding, but verify rather than assume); net_absorption netting other containers outstanding reservations out of the pool; hold space already occupied on arrival; and whatever bounds the BUY side, since sells are matched to buys.

Report WHICH term binds and how often, as a distribution over live plans. That is the deliverable. A fix is only worth proposing once the binding term is named.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not "fill went up". It is that you can state, for a sample of real plans, which single term produced the number — and demonstrate it by changing that term in a fixture and watching planned units move, while every other candidate term is held constant. If the honest answer is that 63 is economically correct and the fleet simply should not load more, say so with the arithmetic; that is a valid and valuable outcome.

CONTEXT: jump-gate fees (~5,928 each, 1,128 jumps in 3h) were just priced into the solver by sp-wtc47 and deployed. If fill is limited by something that interacts with route cost, that change may move the answer — measure after, not before.

title: Tour solver: price jump-gate FEES (credits) into projected profit — 2,288 jumps/24h at median 5,622 cr are unmodeled, flattering crossing tours ~5-10%
description: Economy-analyst, 2026-07-31. title: Read treasury from the ledger instead of Get Agent — removes 8.3% of the API ceiling; the completeness blocker is now empirically cleared
description:
UNBLOCKED. This was scoped under sp-ovroh and correctly held until the ledger was complete. sp-shq63 landed the jump and module fee accounting, and the completeness question is now settled by measurement, not argument: over 3,086 consecutive transaction intervals in 3 hours the unrecorded-spend gap is EXACTLY ZERO, and the ledger balance matches the live API to the credit (46,151,915 both). The same measurement before the fix read -7,036,882 over 4h. So jump and module WERE the complete set of credit-decreasing paths; the enumeration caveat the jump lane raised is answered.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING. Get Agent is measured at 0.167 req/s = 8.3% of the 2.00 ceiling, and it does NOT fall with the singleflight that landed as 523b2bea. That was predicted by the lane that built it: the reads are INVALIDATION-DRIVEN, not concurrent duplicates — every Buy Cargo, Sell Cargo, Refuel and Jump invalidates the agent cache, so nearly every read is forced cold. No window and no TTL collapses them. Reading the ledger removes them.

TARGET THE HOT CALL SITES, NOT THE DEAD ONE. run_tour_coordinator.go:2433 and :2551 (x46+ workers) and run_trade_route_coordinator_guards.go:47. Do NOT touch longHaulTreasuryAdapter.LiveTreasury — that IMPLEMENTATION is dead code (no long-haul containers in any status). Note the LiveTreasury INTERFACE does have live implementers (idle_arb.go:590, mediatorTreasuryReader at run_fleet_coordinator.go:1231), so do not conclude the interface is dead.

DESIGN, already worked out across two lanes:
  latest balance + age -> within bound ? use it : fall back to the coalesced live read -> both fail ? ERROR, never 0

THE FRESHNESS BOUND: 30s, from measured inter-transaction gaps (p50 3.51s, p95 18.98s, p99 40.84s, max 141.32s over 1,202 gaps). At 30s roughly 2% of reads fall back to live; at 60s under 1%. CARRY THE CAVEAT: those are BUSY-fleet gaps at 52 hulls. On a quiet or cold fleet gaps are unbounded and nearly every read correctly falls back — do not tune the bound on busy data alone, and make sure the fallback path is cheap because it will be the common path when the fleet is idle.

USE First + ErrRecordNotFound, NEVER Find. This is the trap and BOTH existing precedents have it: detectors_credits.go:83-94 (creditsFromLatestBalance) and era_repository.go:213-217 both use Find with Limit(1), which does NOT return ErrRecordNotFound on an empty result — it returns a nil error and a zero-valued struct, so the caller reads (0, nil): zero credits reported as a SUCCESSFUL read. Harmless where they live (wake gate, era accounting); catastrophic in a treasury path. They will look like house style. Do not copy them. See sp-2ms9x, and note the precise rule: the bug is Find into a SINGLE STRUCT — Find into a slice is fine because len()==0 is observable.

EMPTY MUST BE DISTINGUISHABLE FROM ZERO. A fresh era legitimately has an empty ledger and 0 credits is also a legitimate value. Also relevant: creditsFromLatestBalance has exactly one caller (detectors_credits.go:53, the no-era-anchor fallback) and is precisely the function this work will be tempted to reuse.

ROUTING, already decided: fleet_autosizer_ports.go:159 yes, same reader (it already fails soft, negligible volume, consistency win). bootstrap_ports.go:253 NO — keep it live-first: it runs at cold start when the ledger is legitimately empty, and with the Find bug it would read 0 and deadlock bootstrap. internal/captain/agentcredits.go stays independent — separate process with its own client, feeds the wake gate not a money guard, and its retain-last-live-across-transient-error semantics are deliberately the opposite of fail-closed.

ACCEPTANCE. The falsifier is not "fewer Get Agent calls". It is all of:
  1. the common path makes NO API call and returns the ledger value;
  2. a ledger newer than the bound is used, one older triggers the live fallback — test BOTH sides and probe the boundary;
  3. total failure (ledger unreadable AND fallback failing) propagates an ERROR to the caller, never a retained or zero value. Name this test and mutate it; it is the one that silently re-opens the money guard;
  4. report measured before/after Get Agent req/s.

RULINGS #4: the liveness of LiveTreasury is deliberate — a read failure makes readEnvelope fail-closed so the worker trades nothing that episode rather than sizing a buy on an unread treasury. Preserve that exactly. Coalescing/ledger must never convert a failure into a stale success.
notes:
BUILT on branch ledger-treasury, HEAD e86022fe, rebased onto main 49cd22c3. Not gated — handed to the lead.

MEASURED (live daemon + Prometheus :9091 + prod Postgres, 2026-07-31, 51 TRADING containers):
- BEFORE Get Agent: 0.191 req/s (30m) / 0.179 (1h) / 0.165 (6h) — premise confirmed, and total API is 1.62-1.82 req/s of the 2.00 ceiling, so Get Agent is 9-10% of consumption.
- PREDICTED ledger-hit rate: 99.24% of wall-clock time the newest ledger row is <=30s old (5,936 gaps over 6h: p50 1.91s, p95 12.79s, p99 23.26s, max 71.37s). Only 0.76% falls back to live — BETTER than the 2% the bead estimated, because this fleet is busier than the one measured. At 60s it is 99.95%.
- AFTER is not measurable from a build lane (no deploy). Post-deploy query:
    sum(rate(spacetraders_daemon_api_requests_total{endpoint="Get Agent"}[30m]))
    sum(rate(spacetraders_daemon_treasury_reads_total[30m])) by (source)

COMPLETENESS, re-derived independently — the bead's "gap exactly ZERO" needs restating, not retracting. A naive chain-seam check over 6h shows 314 seams out of 5,940 rows where balance_before != previous balance_after. Every single row is internally self-consistent (balance_after = balance_before + amount, 5,940/5,940). The seams split 133 up / 182 down, +12,348,449 vs -12,355,199, NET -6,750 credits on 24.7M gross = 0.027%. That symmetry is the signature of CONCURRENT INTERLEAVING among 51 hulls (a row's balance_before comes from its own API response, observed before another worker's in-flight spend landed), not of unrecorded spend — an unrecorded-spend leak is systematically negative, which is exactly what the pre-jump-fix -7,036,882 looked like. So: no drift, premise holds, and the ledger is continuously re-anchored to API truth.

RESIDUAL, quantified: the per-seam correction is p50 27,776 / p95 313,754 / max 2,321,885 credits. That is how wrong the latest balance can be at an instant. It is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here — a live Get Agent is equally blind to another worker's in-flight spend. The 30s bound adds no exposure beyond it, because any COMPLETED transaction writes a row and resets the age; only genuinely in-flight ones are missing.

SHIPPED ARMED, no flags. Also ships spacetraders_daemon_treasury_reads_total{source=ledger|live|error}.
close_reason: Closed

title: Live knob to disable the fleet autosizer — it spent 21% of the API ceiling on buy-decisions it was blocked from acting on
description:
ADMIRAL REQUEST. The fleet is bought MANUALLY; the autosizer is not used. Today the only way to stop it is a container stop, which does not survive a daemon restart.

WHAT IT COST, MEASURED. fleet_autosizer generated 14,053 shipyard scans — 96.7% of ALL Get Shipyard traffic and roughly 21% of the entire 2.00 req/s account ceiling. In that time it made 25 buy-decisions and bought NOTHING: 14 BLOCKED by demand, 11 BLOCKED by heavy_cap. Every one of those reads is classed marketscan.Earning (fleet_autosizer_ports.go:340), which Decide() admits unconditionally, so it also drove 7,326 budget overdrafts and starved discretionary market scanning.

Stopping the container was measured live: Get Shipyard went 8,838 -> 8,838 over 90 seconds (ZERO calls), total fleet rate fell 1.79 -> 1.42 req/s, and the sensing brake released from its pinned 0.1 floor to 1.0.

TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS THAT WILL SINK THIS IF MISSED.

1. THE KNOB MUST STOP THE READS, NOT JUST THE BUYING. This is the trap. expansion_enabled gates SPENDING while the free work — frontier discovery, gate reads, screening — keeps running, and that is correct for expansion. It would be WRONG here: the autosizer costs almost nothing in credits and everything in API requests. A knob that only gates the purchase decision leaves all 14,053 shipyard reads in place and delivers zero of the benefit. Gate the tick, or gate the read path, and prove it by measuring Get Shipyard call volume before/after with the knob off.

2. THE ENCODING MUST BE 1=ON, 2=OFF, NOT 0/1. `spacetraders tune <key> 0` means REVERT-TO-DEFAULT fleet-wide, so a 0/1 knob makes "off" literally unexpressible. expansion_enabled already learned this and documents it in its own help text — follow that precedent exactly, including saying so in the knob description.

DEFAULT ON. Do not ship this default-off. The knob is the control; the decision to disable is a tune, and live-config tunes persist across daemon restarts (verified tonight: expansion_enabled, capital_multiplier_k_milli and target_util_pct all survived two restarts). Shipping default-off would be a silent behaviour change for anyone else running this code, and it contradicts standing doctrine that features ship armed.

Name it consistently with the operation it belongs to, following the existing `spacetraders tune --operation <op> <key> <value>` shape.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not "the knob reads 2". It is that with the knob off, Get Shipyard call volume attributable to the autosizer is ZERO over a sustained window, AND the coordinator does not spin hot in place (check it is not tick-looping with the work skipped). Also assert the knob is re-read LIVE without a restart, like its siblings, and that flipping it back on restores the behaviour. Emit whatever the existing coordinators emit so an operator can see which state it is in.

CONTEXT WORTH KNOWING: heavy_cap is currently 12 and the fleet holds more heavies than that, which is why 11 of the 25 decisions were blocked by it. So even re-enabled, the autosizer would buy nothing at current settings — the knob is about reclaiming API, not about changing buying policy.
close_reason: Closed

title: Grafana cannot see jump costs: trade margin is overstated by ~1.75M/hr because TRAVEL_COSTS is absent from every cost aggregation, and no panel costs travel at all
description:
MEASURED AND NOW LIVE. sp-shq63 landed the JUMP and MODULE_INSTALL/REMOVE ledger types with a new TRAVEL_COSTS category. First live rows confirm the estimate: 11 jumps, -67,780 credits, mean -6,162 per jump. Historical measurement over a 4h window: 7,036,882 credits across 1,250 jumps (~5,629 each) = ~1.75M credits/hour that were invisible.

For scale, decomposed per hour over that window: trading +3,543,788, contracts +603,002, jump fees -1,753,326, true operating +2,393,465. JUMP FEES ARE 42% OF GROSS OPERATING PROFIT. Every dashboard currently draws the picture without them.

THREE CASES, AUDITED. Do not treat them alike.

1. ALREADY CORRECT, DO NOT TOUCH. financial.json computes operating profit as category != SHIP_INVESTMENTS, so TRAVEL_COSTS is included automatically and correctly (a jump fee is opex, not capex). frontier.json uses the same shape. Verify this holds rather than assuming, then leave it.

2. SILENTLY UNDER-REPORTING — THE SERIOUS ONE. trading.json computes Costs as category IN (TRADING_COSTS, FUEL_COSTS). Jump fees are excluded, so every trade margin and profitability number on that dashboard is OVERSTATED. This is the panel that has been lying, and by 42% of gross. navigation.json has the same shape at category = FUEL_COSTS for its fuel cost and fuel/hr panels, which now under-report total travel cost. Fix the aggregations so travel cost is counted where cost is counted. Where a panel means specifically FUEL, keep it fuel-only and add travel alongside rather than merging the two — they have different unit economics, which is exactly why TRAVEL_COSTS was made its own category instead of being folded into FUEL_COSTS.

3. MISSING ENTIRELY. No panel anywhere costs travel. navigation.json is the natural home: it already has Travel and Scout Health and travel failure panels, but nothing showing what travel COSTS. Add credits/hr on TRAVEL_COSTS, jumps/hr, and the per-jump fee distribution (p25/p50/p75) — that distribution has never been visible and is the number that tells us whether routing changes would pay for themselves.

ALSO WORTH A PANEL, and this is the insight the whole exercise produced: jump cost as a SHARE of gross operating profit. A single stat showing 42% is what makes the cost legible as a decision rather than a line item.

SANITY-CHECK YOUR PANELS AGAINST THESE NUMBERS. A travel-cost panel over a 4h window should read roughly 1.7-1.8M/hr at the current fleet size and ~270-310 jumps/hr. If it reads near zero, the category filter is wrong. If it reads far higher, it is probably double-counting against FUEL_COSTS.

CAVEAT ON HISTORY, state it in any panel description that spans it: there is NO BACKFILL, deliberately. The historical fees were discarded before anything could observe them and reconstructing them would be guesswork. So TRAVEL_COSTS is zero for all time before the deploy and real afterwards. A panel over a long window will show a step change that is an artefact of instrumentation, not of behaviour, and must say so or it will be misread as a cost spike.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not that a panel mentions TRAVEL_COSTS. It is that (a) trading.json Costs increases by the measured travel spend over the same window, (b) a travel-cost panel reads within the expected band above rather than zero, and (c) financial.json operating profit is UNCHANGED, since it already counted it. Check (c) explicitly — a change there means something was double-counted.

Also stale and out of scope for gobot but worth noting on the bead: visualizer/web/src/types/spacetraders.ts:344 (category union) and TransactionList.tsx:49 (filter dropdown) do not know TRAVEL_COSTS.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two latest-balance readers use GORM Find into a single struct: an empty ledger returns (0, nil) — unreadable balance silently becomes a value
description:
FOUND while auditing sp-shq63 against a trap warning from the lane that hit it.

THE DEFECT. GORM's Find does NOT return ErrRecordNotFound. When its destination is a SINGLE STRUCT, an empty result leaves the struct zero-valued and returns a nil error, so the caller reads (0, nil): a balance that could not be read, silently converted into the value zero. Empty and 'legitimately zero credits' become indistinguishable — and a fresh era legitimately has an empty ledger.

THE TWO SITES (both confirmed by direct read):
  internal/captain/detectors_credits.go:83-94  creditsFromLatestBalance -> Find(&tx), returns tx.BalanceAfter
  internal/adapters/persistence/era_repository.go:213-217 -> Find(&latest), returns latest.BalanceAfter

FIX: First (or Take) with an explicit errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) branch that reports 'unreadable', never 0.

SCOPE PRECISION — DO NOT OVER-APPLY. The bug is Find into a SINGLE STRUCT. Find into a SLICE is correct and safe, because len(result)==0 is directly observable by the caller. transaction_repository.go:78 FindByPlayer uses the slice form and is NOT affected; a blanket 'never use Find' rule would wrongly condemn it and every other correct slice read in the repo.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW, NOT LATER. Both sites are harmless where they live today (captain wake gate, era accounting — a 0 just fails to fire something), which is why nobody caught them. creditsFromLatestBalance has exactly ONE caller (detectors_credits.go:53, the fallback branch when no era anchor exists) and it is precisely the function the ledger-backed treasury reader will reach for. Promoted next to a money guard, an unreadable balance reported as 0 fails OPEN in the reporting sense and defeats the fail-closed contract (RULING #4).

RELATED: sp-shq63 (just landed, b8b6c983) closed the over-reporting hole from unrecorded jump/module fees. This is the same class — a treasury value that is wrong in a direction a guard cannot survive — reached by a different route. Both should be closed before the treasury reader is built.
close_reason: Closed

title: [P1] Dashboard erases held cargo for any hull that sells an older lot after a newer buy — 11 of 47 trade hulls mislabelled, 6.06M capital invisible, 8 panels affected
description:
The trading-hulls dashboard computes a hull's held cargo as "purchases since that hull's last sell".
That assumes strict buy-then-sell cycles. Hulls interleave lots, so any hull that sells an OLDER lot
after buying a NEWER one has its entire held inventory erased from the calculation.

THE HEURISTIC (configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json, open_cargo CTE):

    AND t.created_at > COALESCE(tx.last_sell, '-infinity'::timestamptz)

where tx.last_sell = MAX(created_at) FILTER (WHERE transaction_type='SELL_CARGO') for that hull.

WORKED EXAMPLE — TORWIND-2FD, which the dashboard currently labels STALLED:
  02:54  BUY  36 ANTIMATTER   -183k
  04:06  BUY  39 CLOTHING     -170k
  04:06  BUY 150 MEDICINE     -591k
  04:16  SELL 36 ANTIMATTER   +192k   <- the older lot, sold AFTER the 04:06 buys
The 04:16 sell becomes last_sell, so every purchase before it is excluded and In Cargo reports 0.
The hull is physically carrying 189/225 units worth ~761k at cost.

2FD is not stalled. Every CLOSED position it holds is profitable:
  FABRICS +134k, ANTIMATTER +9k, POLYNUCLEOTIDES +3k, CLOTHING +19k on the lot it sold.
Its whole apparent loss is unsold MEDICINE the panel cannot see.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS (live, player 5, 2026-07-31):
  trade hulls whose held cargo is erased ....... 11 of 47 (23%), 1,115 units invisible
  capital in cargo, correct (per-good net) ..... 23.71M cr
  capital in cargo, as the panel computes it ... 17.65M cr
  understated by .............................. 6.06M cr (26%)

EIGHT PANELS CONSUME THIS CTE, not just the STALLED label:
  stat      Capital in Cargo (at cost)          <- understated 26%
  table     Per-Hull P&L - realised, deployed, and honest net
  stat      Trade Fleet Paid Back
  stat      Median Payback Time                 <- inflated (net looks worse, payback looks slower)
  stat      p90 Payback Time                    <- inflated
  stat      Median Age, Unpaid Hulls
  table     Per-Hull Payback                    <- the STALLED / EARNING status column
  barchart  Payback % by Hull                   <- depressed
Every one is biased in the same direction: hulls look less profitable and slower to pay back than
they are. The bias falls hardest on ACTIVE hulls, because a hull that trades often is likelier to
interleave lots — so the dashboard systematically flatters idle hulls over working ones.

FIX: compute held cargo per (hull, good) as units bought minus units sold, valued at the hull's
average purchase cost for that good — not by a last-sell timestamp. A hull holds a good iff its net
units for that good are positive, regardless of when anything was sold.

string (e.g. 'PURCHASE 60 units of MEDICINE at X1-...'), which is fragile. Check whether
transactions.metadata carries units/good directly and prefer that. If it does not, say so — a
description-parsed dashboard is a fragility worth recording rather than hiding.

VALIDATE AGAINST THE SHIPS TABLE. ships.cargo_units is ground truth for whether a hull is carrying
anything. After the fix, no hull with cargo_units > 0 may report In Cargo = 0. That check is cheap
and is the falsifier: run it before and after.

title: Jump gate fees are charged but never recorded: no JUMP ledger type, JumpResult.TotalPrice is parsed and discarded — the ledger is incomplete for credit-decreasing paths
description:
FOUND BY THE sp-ovroh LANE while pressure-testing whether the ledger can serve as a treasury source. It cannot, yet, and this is why.

THE GAP. internal/domain/ledger/transaction_type.go declares exactly SIX transaction types — TypeRefuel, TypePurchaseCargo, TypeSellCargo, TypePurchaseShip, TypeContractAccepted, TypeContractFulfilled — and the DB confirms the same six over a 2h window. THERE IS NO JUMP TYPE. A jump charges a gate fee: the API returns it, adapters/api/client.go:529 parses it into JumpResult.TotalPrice, and NOTHING consumes it. Zero code consumers outside the struct assignment, zero log lines. Module install/remove is the same shape (shipyard fee, no ledger type).

The client itself knows the fee is real — its own comment says 'jump charges a gate fee (transaction.totalPrice) -> drop the stale-high cache' — so it invalidates the agent cache precisely BECAUSE credits moved. It just never records why.

VOLUME: 419 Jump calls in a 54-minute window.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING. It makes the ledger structurally unable to back a money guard. I argued to the lane that the ledger's only failure mode is STALENESS, and that the dangerous direction — over-reporting credits — 'requires credits leaving the account with no recorded transaction'. A jump is exactly that. Within any freshness window the ledger can report MORE credits than exist, which is the direction that authorises an unaffordable buy. A freshness bound bounds the window; it does not make the direction safe. My argument was wrong and this is the fact that breaks it.

What limits the damage today: balance_after re-anchors to API ground truth on every REFUEL/CARGO/SHIP row (record_transaction.go's AuthoritativeBalance branch), so unrecorded jump spend does NOT accumulate — exposure is bounded to whatever was spent since the last anchor. That is also why a spot check shows zero divergence: it proves the last anchor was fresh, NOT that the chain is complete.

THE FEE'S MAGNITUDE IS UNKNOWN AND CANNOT CURRENTLY BE MEASURED, because the value is discarded before anything could observe it. Absence of a recorded fee is not evidence of a zero fee. That is a second, independent reason to fix this: 419 jumps an hour against an unmeasured unit cost is an unquantified line in the fleet's economics.

FIX: record the gate fee as a ledger transaction. The value is already in hand at JumpResult.TotalPrice — this is plumbing, not discovery. Add the type, record on the jump path, and pass the API's authoritative post-transaction balance the same way cargo_transaction.go:705 and refuel_ship.go:220 already do, so the new row re-anchors the chain rather than merely appending to it. Do the same for module install/remove if the shape is identical; say so if it is not.

DO NOT paper over this with a 'conservative allowance' subtracted from ledger reads. That substitutes a guessed number for a measured one in a money-guard path, and nobody can currently even calibrate the guess.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not 'a JUMP row appears'. It is that after a jump, the ledger's latest balance_after equals the live API credits — assert the reconciliation, not the insertion. Include a jump in the fixture and check the chain closes across it. Report the observed per-jump fee distribution once it is finally visible; that number has never been seen.

BLOCKS: the ledger-backed treasury reader (sp-ovroh's re-scope). That work should not start until this lands.

title: Get Agent is called ~1x/5.8s (9.5% of the API ceiling) because every long-haul worker reads treasury live — needs COALESCING, not caching
description:
MEASURED LIVE (player 5, 42m32s uptime): 437 Get Agent calls, one every 5.8 seconds, 9.5% of all API requests. The fleet runs at 1.79 req/s against a 2.00 ceiling, so this is displacing sensing and expansion, both of which are currently starved.

CAUSE: longHaulTreasuryAdapter.LiveTreasury (adapters/grpc/container_ops_longhaul.go:188) calls api.GetAgent on EVERY read, per worker. With 47 trade hulls this multiplies.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY CACHING THE VALUE. The liveness is deliberate and the code says so at container_ops_longhaul.go:176: 'A read failure surfaces as an error so the worker's readEnvelope fail-closes (trades nothing that episode) rather than sizing a buy on a treasury it could not read (RULINGS #4).' LiveTreasury is a MONEY GUARD INPUT. Handing it a stale treasury is precisely the weakening RULINGS #4 forbids, and it would let a worker size a buy against credits that are already spent.

THE FIX IS COALESCING, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT THING. Many concurrent workers asking within the same short window should share ONE live round-trip rather than each making their own. The value every caller receives is still a fresh observation from that instant; what is removed is the duplication, not the liveness. singleflight-style de-duplication over a very short window is the shape.

A PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS REPO — read it before designing: internal/captain/agentcredits.go implements a shared refresh that retains the last live value across a transient error and deliberately avoids an unbounded GetAgent blocking interrupt delivery. Reuse its reasoning; do not invent a second, divergent treasury reader. Note the other direct callers too (fleet_autosizer_ports.go:159, bootstrap_ports.go:253) and say whether they should route through the same reader.

MUST PRESERVE: a read that genuinely fails must still surface as an error so readEnvelope fail-closes. Coalescing must not convert a failure into a stale success — if the shared call fails, every waiter gets the error.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not 'fewer calls'. It is that N concurrent workers within the window produce ONE API call AND each still receives a value observed within that window, AND a failing shared call propagates the error to every waiter rather than a retained value. Test all three; the third is the one that silently weakens the guard if it regresses. Report the measured before/after call rate.
notes:
CLOSED AS PARTIALLY-INVALID. Three premises in this bead were wrong and the lane proved each: (1) the named cause, longHaulTreasuryAdapter.LiveTreasury, is dead code — no long-haul containers in any status; (2) the requested singleflight already existed one layer down in GetAgent, with a passing 50-reader test and a 15s TTL from sp-oszc; (3) the call count is at its correctness floor, since the reads are invalidation-driven cold reads rather than concurrent duplicates, so no window or TTL lowers it without weakening RULINGS #4.

What DID ship, on its own merits and merged as the commit above: true singleflight replacing lock-across-the-fetch, justified by contention rather than volume — 30.1% of wall-clock with the agent-cache mutex HELD, head-of-line blocking every GetAgent caller including cache hits across 46 workers' money guards. The over-spend invariant moved from the lock to agentCacheEpoch (sample before request, re-check before store, drop the store if it moved) and is unchanged: after any spend the cache is EMPTY.

The ledger-backed treasury idea that this bead mutated into is NOT dead — it is blocked on sp-shq63 (jump gate fees are charged but never recorded, so the ledger can over-report and staleness is not its only failure mode). When that lands, the work belongs at run_tour_coordinator.go:2433/:2551 and run_trade_route_coordinator_guards.go:47, NOT here.

Carried forward so it is not lost: the 30s freshness bound measured from busy-fleet inter-transaction gaps (p50 3.51s, p95 18.98s, p99 40.84s, max 141.32s) with the caveat that quiet/cold-fleet gaps are unbounded and must not be tuned on busy data; and any new ledger reader must use First + ErrRecordNotFound rather than Find, because Find returns (0, nil) on an empty ledger and both existing precedents (detectors_credits.go:83-94, era_repository.go:213-217) have that bug.

title: Shipyard reads run ~3.6x their budget because 97% are classed Earning — 830 overdrafts; the lever is read VOLUME, not the rate knob
description:

The fleet as a whole runs at 1.79 req/s against a hard 2.00 ceiling (90%), with 175 observed 429s, so this is displacing real work — sensing sits at its floor and expansion is skipped every tick for budget.

  shipyard earning/spend              1,080
  shipyard discretionary/spend           30
  shipyard discretionary/serve_from_store 50
  shipyard overdrafts/earning           830
97% of shipyard spends are class Earning, which marketscan.Decide admits unconditionally as its FIRST rung. That is correct and must not be changed: an Earning read feeds a money guard before a buy or sell commits, and serving it from store would silently convert a live guard into a stale one (RULINGS #4). Earning is still metered — it draws from the same bucket — which is exactly why the overdraft counter reads 830.

SO RAISING OR LOWERING budget_req_per_sec DOES NOTHING, and neither does denying Earning reads. The only lever is HOW MANY reads are classed Earning.

WHERE TO LOOK. get_shipyard_listings.go is the money-guard price read and is classed Earning wholesale. The question this bead must answer is whether every caller genuinely needs a commit-time live price, or whether some are surveying/ranking reads that could be Discretionary and paced. The correct output may well be 'most of these are genuinely Earning and the fleet simply cannot afford this much yard reading at 47 hulls', in which case say so and propose reducing the number of yards consulted per decision instead. That is a legitimate finding, not a failure.

Emit a counter distinguishing commit-time reads from survey reads so the split is visible afterwards.

 4. "Read class mix" — spends by class, per budget. This is how we see sp-lr27k working: traffic
    should shift out of `earning` into `discretionary` over time.

 5. "Denials" — decision="serve_from_store" by budget. If this is flat zero the budget is declining
    NOTHING and is not actually binding — that is a real finding, so the panel must distinguish
    "zero denials" from "no data".

 6. "Coverage-decay invariant" — coverage and spend-rate on one time axis. The package's stated
    invariant is that total cost does NOT grow with the charted map. So coverage should climb while
    spend rate stays flat. Add a derived panel: per-waypoint scan interval = coverage / rate,
    in seconds — that is the number an operator actually reasons about ("each market gets looked at
    every N minutes").

 7. "Instrument self-check" — spend rate vs the matching endpoint counter:
      sum(rate(scan_budget_decisions_total{budget="market",decision="spend"}[...]))
      vs sum(rate(api_requests_total{endpoint="Get Market"}[...]))
    The metric's own HELP says these reconcile. If they diverge, the instrument is lying and every
    other panel is void. We shipped a money guard tonight (sp-fr19d) whose tracker disagrees 10x
    with Prometheus and nobody noticed for weeks — this panel is the check that would have caught it.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - Datasource: {"type":"prometheus","uid":"prometheus"} — matches navigation.json's existing
    prometheus panels. Do NOT use the postgresql datasource for these.
  - player_id is a LABEL. Use a Grafana template variable ($player) with a label_values() query, NOT
    a hardcoded 5. sp-ahepk is an open bead about exactly this hardcoding across other dashboards —
    do not add a new instance of it.
  - Use $__rate_interval, not a hardcoded [5m]. rate() needs a window >= 4x scrape interval or the
    series goes ragged.
  - NEVER rate() a gauge. rate_req_per_sec and coverage are gauges — use max/last, not rate.
  - File goes in gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/. Provisioning auto-loads that folder
    (updateIntervalSeconds 10, allowUiUpdates true), so no separate registration step. Match the
    schemaVersion and structural conventions of the existing files.
  - Give the dashboard a stable uid and title so it does not duplicate on reload.

VERIFY BEFORE HANDBACK: every panel query must return data against the LIVE Prometheus at
http://localhost:9091 (query API: /api/v1/query?query=...). A panel that returns an empty series is
not "no traffic yet" — check it against the raw /metrics output at http://localhost:9090/metrics
before calling it correct. An empty result read as success is how the original defect hid.
close_reason: Closed

title: [P1] Dark-market backlog enumerator is DORMANT: zero production construction sites, so frontier scan is a permanent no-op AND the dashboard reports 0 backlog
description:
The dark-market backlog enumerator (sp-jide) is complete, unit-tested, and WIRED
TO NOTHING. Verified 2026-07-30 on main (d3d15c89):

  grep -rn "NewDarkMarketScanner|SetDarkMarketScanner|darkScanner" --include='*.go' internal/ cmd/ \
    | grep -v _test.go

The ONLY non-test reference to the constructor is its own definition
(adapters/expansion/dark_market_scanner.go:63). The setter
(application/expansion/commands/scan_only.go:41) is never called outside tests.
There is no production construction site. `h.darkScanner` is therefore nil in
every deployed cycle, and:

  scan_only.go:57-58     if h.darkScanner == nil { return nil }
      -> the charted-but-unscanned MARKET backlog is enumerated ZERO times per
         cycle. The scan side of frontier expansion is a permanent no-op.

  frontier_status.go:103 if h.darkScanner == nil { return 0, 0 }
      -> and the frontier status surface REPORTS ZERO dark markets. "We have no
         backlog" and "we have never looked" are indistinguishable on the
         dashboard. This is the more dangerous half: the dormancy is invisible
         precisely where an operator would go to check for it.

WHY THIS MATTERS NOW: the Admiral's standing objective is spreading the trade
fleet throughout the known galaxy. This component's entire job is enumerating
charted systems whose markets we have never scanned -- the frontier work list.
It has been returning nothing since it landed.

Measured context (24h): 565 of 931 known market waypoints were scanned; 366 were
not. 277 scanned waypoints have never been traded at (a real ~22% exploration
budget, so exploration is not zero) -- but none of that came from this enumerator,
which never ran.

IT IS ALSO A BANNED PATTERN. scan_only.go:39-42 and
run_frontier_expansion_coordinator.go:326 document the nil case as leaving the
coordinator "byte-identical to pre-sp-jide" -- an explicit default-off arming

or do not ship. See the sp-nc0m arming-ledger history: this exact pattern has

  2. frontier_status must distinguish "backlog is empty" from "enumerator absent".
