title: A stranded PENDING ship-jump container permanently wedges its hull: the jump container ID is deterministic per ship, so every later jump collides on containers_pkey forever
description:
LIVE NOW, and it silently strands hulls. jump_ship.go:273 builds the container ID as fmt.Sprintf("ship-jump-%s", cmd.ShipSymbol) — DETERMINISTIC PER SHIP, with no attempt/nonce component. If a jump leaves its container row behind in a non-terminal state, every subsequent jump for that hull tries to INSERT the same primary key and fails:

  failed to create jump container record: failed to insert container:
  ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "containers_pkey" (SQLSTATE 23505)

The hull can then NEVER JUMP AGAIN. It is not retried into success — it is wedged permanently, and the sensing coordinator's own warning says the cost out loud: 'the placement is held and retried, and the hull keeps counting against the probe cap'. So each wedged hull also permanently consumes a probe-cap slot it can never use.

MEASURED (2026-07-30, player 5): 156 occurrences in daemon.log between 20:55:46 and 22:45:24 local, still firing. TWO hulls affected — TORWIND-235 and TORWIND-241 — and both have exactly the stranded row the theory predicts:
  ship-jump-TORWIND-235  PENDING
  ship-jump-TORWIND-241  PENDING
Both ships sit IN_ORBIT, assignment_status='idle', container_id NULL: TORWIND-235 at X1-HG41-X12C trying for X1-MP92, TORWIND-241 at X1-CY97-AD6F trying for X1-DY38. Idle hulls with no owning container, blocked by a container row that owns nothing.

NOT CAUSED BY THE RECENT DEPLOY: 150 of the 156 occurrences predate the 22:43:45 daemon restart that landed sp-7qhum (d3d15c89). This is pre-existing and was simply invisible until placement traffic surfaced it.

WHY NOTHING RECOVERS IT: PENDING is not a terminal state, so the reclaim path does not touch it — ReclaimShipsFromInterruptedWorkers scans FAILED only. There is no reaper for a jump container that never advanced past PENDING. The row is immortal and so is the wedge.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE AS OF NOW: expansion_enabled was just re-armed to 1 (Admiral authorization, after sp-7qhum landed) specifically so probe placement drains dark shipyards. Placement JUMPS are how a probe reaches a yard in another system — which is the exact path this bug breaks. Every hull that hits this is removed from the fleet's placement capacity permanently while still counting against the cap.

SHAPE OF THE FIX — the lane should choose and justify, but the trap to avoid is obvious. Do NOT simply delete-then-insert on collision: a genuinely in-flight jump would be clobbered, and a PENDING row can legitimately mean 'about to start'. The candidates are (a) make the ID unique per attempt so a stale row cannot collide, (b) take over / upsert an existing row only when it is provably not in flight, (c) reap stale PENDING jump containers on an age + no-live-worker predicate. Whichever is chosen must distinguish 'stranded' from 'starting' on POSITIVE evidence, not on absence — a claim is written BEFORE its container starts, so an age-only rule will rip a hull mid-spawn.

ENUMERATE THE BLAST RADIUS BEFORE CHANGING THE ID SCHEME. If the ID becomes non-deterministic, find every reader that reconstructs or matches 'ship-jump-<symbol>' by name — grep the string pattern, not just the constant — because a consumer that looks the container up by predicted ID will silently stop finding it.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not 'a jump succeeds' — it is that a hull WITH a stranded PENDING row of its own can jump. The fixture must pre-seed that row; without it the test passes with the fix deleted. Also assert the in-flight case is NOT clobbered, and emit a counter for stranded rows detected/cleared so a reaper that never fires does not look identical to a fleet with nothing to reap.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION IS IN SCOPE: TORWIND-235 and TORWIND-241 are wedged right now. Clearing their two rows frees both hulls — do it as part of the lane and say exactly what was cleared.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nebula: the sp-voyz7 priced contour over-corrected — at REGION density the rings moire, bury labels and lanes, and the 0-12h freshness scale is still unreadable
description:
ADMIRAL-REPORTED WITH A SCREENSHOT, and it is a regression I gated. sp-voyz7 (8e0acbd4) fixed a real defect — priced systems were quieter than dark ones and the fresh end of the ramp was byte-identical to the orb's own halo tint — but it over-corrected. The map is now WORSE than before the fix.

MY ACCEPTANCE BAR WAS THE BUG. sp-voyz7 was verified by measuring annulus peak luminance on a SINGLE ISOLATED priced-dormant system: 45.1 -> 142.6. That number is real and it moved the right way. It is also structurally incapable of seeing what broke, because it measures one system with nothing around it. Every defect below is a composition/density effect. Any fix for this bead MUST be measured on a DENSE REGION view, never on an isolated system.

WHAT THE SCREENSHOT SHOWS (REGION band, live data):
1. RINGS INTERSECT INTO A MOIRE. orbs.ts AURA_SCALE = 2.6, and the priced contour is stroked at that same radius (line ~349 draws pricedRings[step].circle(sys.x, sys.y, radius) with radius = max(AURA_MIN_PX * worldPerPx, orbR * 2.6)). At 2.6x the orb, neighbouring systems' rings overlap constantly — a cluster of eight produces on the order of 28 crossings. The eye reads the crossings, not the systems.
2. LABELS ARE OCCLUDED. X1-R77, X1-QN51M61, X1-CA58, X1-KD64/X1-KY38 and X1-CJ56 are all partly or wholly unreadable behind ring strokes. Marks are drawing over text.
3. THE LANES ARE BURIED. The white/blue trade-lane structure and the dotted plan paths — the actual subject of the view — now sit visually beneath a lattice of cyan circles.
4. FRESHNESS IS STILL NOT LEGIBLE, WHICH MEANS THE ORIGINAL ASK IS STILL UNMET. The Admiral asked for 'a freshness aura scaled from 0 to 12h'. FRESHNESS_RAMP = [0x22d3ee, 0x2eb6d6, 0x3799bd, 0x3d7ea3, 0x41648a] is a HUE-ONLY ramp across a narrow cyan->slate arc with almost no lightness or chroma separation. Stroked at PRICED_RING_ALPHA = 0.8 against a near-black ground, all five steps read as one saturated cyan. You cannot tell a 20-minute system from an 11-hour one. The scale is drawn and unreadable.

DO NOT SIMPLY REVERT. The two defects sp-voyz7 identified are real and must stay fixed: dark must not out-shout priced (measured pre-fix: dark 80.9 vs priced 45.1), and the fresh end of the ramp must not be the orb's active-halo tint (0x22d3ee is byte-identical to orbs.ts CYAN — deliberately aligned, per the comment, without noticing it made a fresh traded system invisible behind its own halo). Reverting reinstates both.

DIRECTION (confirm before building, and push back if the evidence says otherwise). The Admiral asked for an AURA, and sp-voyz7 replaced the aura with a contour because the aura was unreadable. The aura was unreadable for two fixable reasons — its energy sat inside 35% of its radius, i.e. under the orb, and its colour collided with the orb tint — so fix THOSE rather than keeping a shouting ring:
  - Bring the mark in tight to the orb so neighbours stop intersecting. 2.6x is the number to attack.
  - Drop the alpha hard; a mark that must be readable at density cannot also be the brightest thing on screen.
  - Give the ramp REAL perceptual separation — vary lightness and chroma, not only hue — and keep its fresh end off the orb's cyan.
  - Draw freshness marks BENEATH labels and lanes in the display list. Presence is context; the labels and lanes are the subject.
  - Dark's dashed grey ring was never reported as a problem and reads well in the screenshot. Leave it alone unless the contrast relationship forces a change, and say so if it does.

ACCEPTANCE — density and legibility, not isolated luminance:
  a) Measure on a DENSE REGION viewport with live data (the screenshot's neighbourhood: X1-R77 / X1-QN51 / X1-CA58 / X1-KD64 / X1-KY38 / X1-CJ56). Report ring-ring intersection count before and after; it must fall substantially.
  b) Prove label legibility: measure contrast of label glyphs against whatever is behind them, for the specific labels named above. They must be readable.
  c) Prove the 0-12h scale is DISTINGUISHABLE: sample the rendered colour of each of the five ramp steps as actually drawn (at final alpha, over the real ground) and report pairwise perceptual difference. Adjacent steps must be separable by eye, not merely different in hex. This is the check that would have caught defect 4 pre-merge.
  d) Screenshots at GALAXY, REGION and SYSTEM, before and after, saved to the handback.
  e) Confirm the two sp-voyz7 invariants still hold: priced is not quieter than dark, and the ramp's fresh end is not the orb halo tint.

Related: sp-b4lpb (P3) — SYSTEM-band marks draw ~4x design size because orbs.ts pins geometry to REGION_PX_ZOOM = 3. If the radius work here naturally subsumes it, fix it and close it; if not, leave it and say so.

title: Seeding never places a probe at a shipyard: every yard is also a market, so the YARD slot is always skipped and the fill queue has no yard-aware term
description:
MEASURED LIVE (player 5, 2026-07-31). 2,257 charted SHIPYARD waypoints, 117 with any purchase_price. 116 probes are parked on a shipyard and exactly 116 of those 117 priced yards ARE those occupied waypoints. That 1:1 is the finding: a yard gets priced only where a hull already happens to stand, and nothing in the engine ever puts one there on purpose.

Cost right now: 85 yards catalogue SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER, 4 are priced, 81 are dark. The four we can see span 1,918,293 (CN80-A13D) to 2,446,653 (JT79-A18B) — a 528,360 spread, 27%. Every heavy freighter this era was bought choosing from four visible prices out of eighty-five. Supply is not the limit: 706 parked probes, 702 idle, only 116 (16%) on a yard.

ROOT CAUSE — TWO LINKS, BOTH VERIFIED IN CODE AND IN THE LEDGER.

(1) THE YARD SLOT IS NEVER WRITTEN. planSlots (application/parkedsensing/screen.go ~510) appends probe yards and heavy yards and emits PlannedSlot{Kind: SlotKindYard} for each — but guarded by `if placed[yard] { continue }`, and a whitelisted market has already claimed that waypoint. The comment at slotBook.wantedIn (expansion.go ~940) states the consequence outright: 'planSlots emits a YARD-kind slot only for a yard that is not already a placed market, and in practice every probe-selling yard we screen is also a whitelisted market, so the MARKET slot wins and there are no YARD-kind rows at all.' It is not 'in practice' — it is ALWAYS. Measured: of 2,257 SHIPYARD-trait waypoints, 2,257 also carry MARKETPLACE. Zero yard-only. sensing_slots holds 9,664 rows for player 5 and NOT ONE has slot_kind='YARD' (MARKET/WANTED 8,930, MARKET/PARKED 705, MARKET/QUEUED 22, SPARE/PARKED 5, MARKET/IN_TRANSIT 2).

(2) THE FILL QUEUE CANNOT SEE A YARD. Having become an ordinary MARKET row, the yard is drained by drainCandidates (buyqueue.go ~1056-1160), which sorts coverage ASC (system's parked hulls + the slot's index among its system's outstanding), tiebreak system-level depth, last tiebreak ledger FIFO. NO TERM IS YARD-AWARE. A heavy yard advances only when its whole system happens to be under-covered. It sits in 8,934 WANTED rows against 705 parked hulls — 12.7x oversubscribed — with nothing marking it. Measured: 78 of the 85 heavy yards are MARKET/WANTED, 4 MARKET/PARKED, 3 have no slot at all.

So the ONLY yard-aware path in the engine is slotBook.wantedIn's yard-first tier, which fires solely when an expansion seed FINISHES A TOUR in that exact system (finishTour). That is opportunistic, not directed — and it is exactly why manned and priced yards match 1:1.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY DELETING THE placed[] GUARD. One slot per waypoint is a real invariant (states.go: probe presence at a yard is waypoint-wise, never kind-wise; a consumer asking 'is there a probe at this yard' matches waypoint+PARKED and ignores slot_kind). Two rows on one waypoint would double-count against the probe cap and authorise buying a second probe for a waypoint we already hold. The MARKET slot must keep winning — what is missing is that the row does not RECORD that its waypoint is also a yard, and the drain ordering has no term for it.

SHAPE OF THE FIX (the lane should confirm before building): carry yard-ness as an attribute of the existing MARKET slot rather than as a competing row, and give drainCandidates a term for it. Demand-weight it — a yard cataloguing a hull class the fleet is actively buying (SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER now) must outrank a yard selling only probes and shuttles, which is the same demand weighting sp-mb0er gave the read budget. Keep coverage-first primary or state why not: it exists because depth-alone put 67% of parked probes in three systems.

COORDINATE WITH sp-fox5u, which is building a presence-request path inside the yardscan budget. These two must not both dispatch hulls to the same yards. Decide explicitly which owns yard presence; this bead is the FREE half (a seed already finishing in-system costs no relocation), sp-fox5u is the PAID half.

ACCEPTANCE. Not 'a YARD row appears' — the invariant says it should not. The falsifier is that the drain's ordering is CONSULTED and moves heavy yards up: assert on a fixture where the queue is saturated with non-yard WANTED slots so the yard term is actually load-bearing (a bound is never exercised unless demand exceeds it), and emit a counter for yards promoted / presence achieved so a coordinator losing every decision does not look identical to an idle one.
notes:
CORRECTION TO THE DESCRIPTION'S SUPPLY FRAMING (2026-07-31, verified independently by the coordinator and the sp-fox5u lane). The description says '706 parked probes, 702 idle, only 116 on a yard' and implies a large free pool. THAT IS WRONG and a lane building on it would ship inert. assignment_status='idle' is a FLEET tag, not availability: in the sensing ledger those same hulls are PARKED MARKET slots, each the only observer of its market. Exactly 5 are SPARE, and none sits in a system with an unpriced yard.

The real distribution, measured on the 78 WANTED heavy yards: 56 have ZERO probes anywhere in their system, 11 have exactly one (taking it blinds the system), 11 have two or more. So the binding constraint is probe presence in the right SYSTEM, not the redundancy guard — dropping that guard entirely would buy at most 7 more heavy yards, each by taking a system's last observer. Do not touch it.

WHY THIS BEAD IS STILL THE FIX, AND FOR THE 56 SPECIFICALLY. Those 56 yards sit in 47 systems that ALREADY carry 775 WANTED sensing_slots. They are reachable by the ordinary buy/ferry machinery — they are not a new action class. What stops them is exactly what this bead describes: the queue is yard-blind, so those 775 rows compete on coverage/system-depth/FIFO with nothing marking any of them as a yard.

SEQUENCING CONTEXT: sp-fox5u merged as 84b083bc. It took the IN-SYSTEM half (relocate a releasable hull market->yard, buys nothing, reaches 107 yards / 4 heavy) and added yardpresence.go, foothold.go's coveredAfterMove, domain/yardscan/presence.go, shipyard_scan_budget.go's PresenceRequests/AdmitPresence, and Requested/Dispatched/NoHull/Metered on the sensing heartbeat. Branch from main AFTER that merge and reuse its counters and its surplusPool rather than inventing parallel ones.

ALSO LOAD-BEARING: expansion_enabled=2 right now — probe BUYING is off by Admiral order, so the 775 WANTED slots cannot currently be filled by purchase. This fix must be correct-and-ready for the re-arm rather than assume spending is live; the Admiral re-arms after this lands, specifically so resumed spending drains heavy yards first. Do not change the knob and do not add one.
ARMING AUTHORIZATION (Admiral, 2026-07-31): 'turn expansion back on after it lands.' This REVERSES the earlier standing order ('fucking turn expansion off!') whose re-arm trigger was market sink thinning. The new trigger is this bead landing. Authorization is explicit; do not re-ask.

THE ORDER MATTERS AND THE KNOB IS NOT THE LAST STEP:
  1. sp-7qhum gates and merges to main
  2. DAEMON RESTART — expansion_enabled is live-config and applies next tick, but sp-7qhum's yard-aware ordering is Go code and does NOT take effect until the daemon restarts. Re-arming against a still-running yard-blind daemon spends exactly the money this sequencing exists to protect.
  3. THEN: spacetraders tune --operation sensing expansion_enabled 1   (1=on, 2=off; 0 means revert-to-default, so 0 would read as ON)
  4. VERIFY, do not assume: read the knob back, and confirm the first SHIP_PROBE purchases land at heavy yards rather than generic market slots. An empty or unread result is 'unconfirmed', never 'working'.

Money guards unaffected either way: capex_reserve_credits and the probe cap apply on both sides of this switch (RULINGS #4 intact). Expected spend to price the 56 dark heavy systems: 56 x ~32,517 avg probe = ~1.82M, against 35 heavy hulls bought this era for 70,289,141 chosen from 4 of 85 visible prices.
close_reason: Closed

title: Automate yard price discovery — prices need a hull PRESENT, 462 unpriced yards already have a probe in-system
description:
ADMIRAL ORDER 2026-07-30: yard price discovery must be AUTOMATED. Doing it by hand is not a fix.

THE MECHANIC, verified against live data. GET /shipyard returns `shipTypes` (what a yard CAN sell)
to anyone, but the `ships` array carrying `purchasePrice` ONLY when we have a ship at that waypoint.
The correlation is perfect and total:
    heavy-selling yards known : 85
    priced                    :  4  <- every one has one of our ships parked there
    unpriced                  : 81  <- every one has ZERO of our ships there
So no amount of scanning discovers a price. sp-mb0er's budget is working correctly (229 rows scanned
in 10 minutes) and cannot solve this: it is a PRESENCE problem, not a scan-rate problem.

WHAT THAT COSTS. We buy every heavy from the same 3 yards because they are the only ones with a
permanently docked purchaser. Spread across all types the blindness is far wider:
    unpriced yards (all types)          : 1,586
    ...with a probe ALREADY in-system   :   462   <- addressable for a within-system hop
    idle probes (no dedicated_fleet)    :     2
462 yards are one in-system reposition away from being priced, using probes we already own and are
already paying to park. That is the cheap tier and it should be automatic.

THE DESIGN SHOULD EXTEND sp-mb0er, NOT SIT BESIDE IT. The yard budget already knows exactly which
yards it wants and cannot see: `SellsWanted && !Priced` is its top weight tier -- that IS this set.
Today that demand produces a scan that returns no price. It should instead be able to produce a
PRESENCE REQUEST: send a hull to the waypoint, let the next scan read the price.

REUSE THE EXISTING MACHINERY, do not invent a dispatcher. parkedsensing already has
`reuseSpareHull` (re-task an idle in-system spare, zero credits, zero API) and `footholds.fill`
(fly a surplus hull across a gate on gate-store reads). The sensing spend gate deliberately keeps
both alive while expansion spending is off, precisely because they are free. An in-system probe
reposition to a yard waypoint is the same class of move.

CONSTRAINTS, all of them real:
  - Do NOT starve sensing. A probe manning a scout post or holding a freshness rotation slot is
    doing paid work; only genuinely spare/idle hulls may be re-tasked. Note only 2 probes are
    currently unassigned, so "idle" alone is far too narrow a source -- the 462 figure assumes
    in-system probes that could take a detour, and deciding which of those are truly spare is the
    core judgement of this bead.
  - Expansion SPENDING is off (expansion_enabled=2) and must stay off. This must buy NOTHING. It
    repositions hulls we already own; if it needs to purchase a probe it is out of scope.
  - Respect the API budget. Every reposition costs Navigate/Orbit/Dock calls, and the ceiling is a
    hard 2.00 req/s currently running ~1.74. Discovery must draw from a budget, not burst.
  - Prioritise by value, not by proximity alone. A yard selling a heavy we are about to buy is worth
    far more than one selling a probe. The yardscan weight tiers already express this.

ACCEPTANCE: unpriced yards that have a spare hull in-system get one dispatched automatically, and
their prices appear without human action; the count of priced heavy yards rises above 4 unattended;
no probe is taken from paid sensing work; nothing is purchased; and the repositions draw from a
metered allowance rather than bursting the API ceiling.
close_reason: Closed

title: trade fleet occupies 23 of 373 tradeable systems — give the relocator first refusal at the tour boundary instead of racing for the 2.6% of time a hull is idle
description:
## The trade fleet does not spread, because a completing tour re-anchors the hull before anything can move it

OBJECTIVE (Admiral): spread the trade fleet throughout the known galaxy.

MEASURED NOW: 40 trade hulls occupy **23 distinct systems** out of **373 priced, tradeable
systems** — 6% of the reachable market. The largest cluster holds **7 hulls in one system**
(X1-KY38), 17.5% of the fleet.

## Why it does not spread on its own

Each tour is planned from the hull's CURRENT position at cap-2 systems, so a tour ends
approximately where it began — the tradeable envelope moves WITH the hull and never leaves its
neighbourhood. The opportunity relocator is the only mechanism that moves a hull to new ground,
and it only considers hulls BETWEEN tours.

MEASURED, 6h of tour containers: 101 consecutive-tour gaps, NONE overlapping, median 224s, min
185s. Hulls are therefore idle **2.6% of the time**, i.e. ~1 hull free at any instant. The
relocator confirms this from the other side — it reports `mid_tour=38..40` and evaluates 1-2 hulls
per tick.

**THE WINDOWS ARE NOT BEING MISSED.** At a 120s tick against a 224s window the relocator already
sees essentially every free hull. Firing on a release EVENT would show it the same ~1 hull a minute
sooner. Cadence is not the constraint and neither is event-vs-poll: the constraint is that hulls
are busy 97.4% of the time, and the moment one is free the tour coordinator re-plans it locally.

The relocator works when it fires — 24 relocation decisions, multi-hop, real NPV (one was 9.67M cr
over 2 gate hops). It is simply outnumbered: one hull per window against 40 hulls that re-anchor
every ~43 minutes.

## Ask: give the relocator FIRST REFUSAL at the tour boundary

When a tour completes, the hull must be offered to the relocator BEFORE the tour coordinator plans
its next local tour. That removes the race for the idle window entirely rather than trying to win
it faster.

**DO NOT BUILD AN EVENT BUS.** No coordinator in this codebase wakes on an event, and the publisher
is the hazard: a tour can end normally, on error, interrupted, or via a restart sweep, and every
path would have to fire or the hull silently never gets offered. A missed event is fail-SILENT and
permanent; that is the failure class removed four times over in sp-cwnwb, sp-j1i49 and sp-biegl.

**Use durable state instead.** At tour completion, record on the hull (or its slot) that it is
OFFERED for relocation. The relocator's normal tick sees offered hulls and takes them with
priority. The tour coordinator does not re-plan an offered hull until either the relocator has
taken it or the offer has expired. Properties this buys:
- Fail-SAFE: a missed or unwritten offer degrades to exactly today's behaviour, never to a
  stranded hull.
- RULINGS #2: the offer is durable state re-derived each tick, not an in-memory signal.
- No new architectural pattern; both coordinators keep their existing tick loops.

## Constraints

1. **THE OFFER MUST EXPIRE.** A hull offered and never taken (relocator down, no candidate ground,
   NPV below floor) must return to normal tour planning after a bounded wait. An unexpiring offer
   is a stranded trade hull, which is strictly worse than a hull that never spread. Choose the
   expiry against the measured 224s median gap — the cost of a missed tour is real earning time.
2. **RULINGS #7 and the claim discipline still apply.** The relocator holds no ClaimShip
   (sp-x2jr6 slice 3 is still open), so the offer must not be treated as ownership. If the tour
   coordinator's next plan wins anyway, the relocator must abandon cleanly — the
   `claimed_at_actuation` path already does this and is counted.
3. **Do not regress earning.** A hull spends the offer window not trading. Measure it: 40 hulls ×
   an offer window each tour cycle is real revenue. The design should offer only when there is
   plausibly somewhere better to go, not on every completion.
4. **RULINGS #4**: this moves no money guard. It changes WHO gets the hull first, not what may be
   spent.

## Success metric

Distinct systems holding trade hulls, now 23 of 373. Watch it rise. Secondary:
`relocator_skips_total{reason="mid_tour"}` should fall sharply relative to `evaluated`, because
the offer removes the mid-tour exclusion for exactly the hulls that just became free.
close_reason: Closed

title: Collapse the two tour freshness knobs into one — they resolve identically and must be kept in sync to stay correct
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-30, on reviewing sp-k4z5b as shipped: three knobs for what reads as one concept is
unacceptable. Collapse them.

WHAT SHIPPED (sp-k4z5b, merged, NOT yet deployed):
  tour     listing_max_age_minutes      floor for the 11 listing-filter consumers
  tour     sink_freshness_max_minutes   floor for the fail-closed firm-sink money guard
  scoutpost market_drift_max_age_secs   NOT a freshness cap at all
All three route their derived term through FreshnessCap(floor, budget, marketsKnown).

THE PROBLEM. The two tour knobs are indistinguishable in practice: both defaulted to 75 minutes,
both take the identical derived rotation bound, so today they resolve to the same number and always
will unless an operator deliberately splits them. Two knobs that must be kept in sync to stay correct
are worse than one -- the split invites exactly the drift this bead exists to prevent, and doubles
what an operator must reason about at 4am during an incident.

COLLAPSE TO ONE: a single market-data freshness floor on the tour operation, feeding both the
listing filter and the sink money guard. Name it for what it is, not for either call site.

WHAT MUST SURVIVE THE COLLAPSE, all of it non-negotiable:
  - the sink gate stays FAIL-CLOSED and armed (RULINGS #4, sp-tgll8). Setting the knob to 0 must
    revert to the documented default, never disarm; every reachable value resolves to a positive cap.
  - tuning the floor BELOW the live rotation bound stays a deliberate no-op, so no operator can
    re-create the 87%-throughput incident by tightening a knob.
  - the derived term stays the scanner's own MaxStaleness, so a consumer refuses exactly when the
    scanner failed its own guarantee and never merely because the map grew.
  - next-tick effect, no rebuild, via the by-TYPE CoordinatorConfigReader already built.
  - the RotationInputs boot-refresh fix (commit 47cea600) stays: without it marketsKnown reads zero
    between a restart and the first market read, and a zero denominator collapses the cap back to 75
    minutes -- the incident reappearing in the window every restart opens.

ON market_drift_max_age_secs: LEAVE IT. It is a scoutpost partition-drift bound measured from when
the drift was noticed, not a market-data freshness cap; map growth does not invalidate it and
deriving it from rotation would make scout posts thrash. It is correctly separate and correctly not
derived. Its only sin was being unreachable without a daemon bounce, which is fixed. Do not fold it in.

ALSO CLEAN UP: gobot/config.yaml carries my incident mitigation
`trade_fleet.sink_freshness_max_minutes: 720`. The shipping lane confirmed it is superseded and inert
(at 4,389 markets the effective cap is 13h56m with or without it). Remove the stanza as part of this
change so config does not reference a key that no longer exists.

ACCEPTANCE: exactly ONE market-freshness knob on the tour operation; `tune --operation tour` lists it
with honest bounds, default and effect-timing; both the listing filter and the sink money guard read
it; a test proves setting it to 0 does NOT disarm the money guard; a test proves a floor below the
rotation bound is a no-op; and the config.yaml mitigation stanza is gone.
close_reason: Closed

title: relocator ticks every 15m against a 206s median idle window — it sleeps through ~86% of the windows it exists to use; lower the cadence rather than going event-driven
description:
## The relocator sleeps through ~86% of the idle windows it exists to use

Admiral raised this as "run it when a hull becomes idle rather than on a tick". The diagnosis is
right — we are missing windows — but the measurement says the fix is a cadence change, not an
event-driven redesign.

## Measured (era 5, 2026-07-30 ~14:00Z, 8h of tour containers)

Gap between one tour ENDING and the next tour starting for the SAME hull, 119 samples:

    under 1 min      0
    1-3 min          0
    3-15 min       111
    over 15 min      8
    MEDIAN         206 seconds (3.4 min)

**No hull is ever idle for less than 3 minutes.** The windows are wide; we are simply asleep.

Against that, the relocator ticks every 15 minutes — 4 ticks/hour against ~29 tour completions/hour
(median tour 42.6 min, 37 of 40 trade hulls touring at any instant). Live evidence from the one
tick since deploy: `1 relocated, 0 resumed, 1 evaluated, skipped[mid_tour=32]`. It saw ONE eligible
hull out of 33.

## Why a 2-minute tick, not an event

A 2-minute tick catches essentially every window, because the minimum observed gap is over 3
minutes. It needs no new machinery.

THE COST ARGUMENT IS THE NON-OBVIOUS PART: API cost scales with ELIGIBLE HULLS, not with tick rate.
~29 hulls become free per hour, so there are ~29 evaluations to perform however often we look —
cadence only determines whether we catch them. A tick with nothing eligible costs one fleet read
and one container read, both DB, no API (that is exactly what `mid_tour=32` cost). So 15min -> 2min
buys ~7x the capture for ~26 extra DB-only ticks an hour and roughly zero extra planner calls.
The per-hull pre-flight is separately bounded by relocationRegionCandidateBudget (<=3 planner
calls), so a burst of simultaneously-free hulls cannot spike.

WHY NOT EVENT-DRIVEN, despite it being the more obvious answer:
- **No coordinator in this codebase wakes on an event.** Every one is a tick loop. This would be a
  new architectural pattern for a problem a constant already solves.
- **The publisher is the risk.** A tour container can end normally, on error, interrupted, or via a
  restart sweep. Every one of those paths would have to publish, or the relocator silently misses
  the window — a fail-SILENT gap, which is the exact class removed four times tonight (sp-cwnwb's
  unstamped skip, sp-j1i49's unread Skipped, the two silent commit failures).
- **A missed tick is fail-SAFE**; a missed event is not. If a cadence tick is delayed the next one
  still fires. If an event is never published nothing ever fires again for that hull.
- `ReleaseShip` exists only as an operator gRPC/CLI command, not an internal signal, so there is no
  existing event to subscribe to.

## Ask

Lower the relocator's tick from 15m to 2m. Verify first:
1. That the tick is genuinely cheap when nothing is eligible — confirm the no-eligible path issues
   ZERO API calls, not merely few. If it does issue any, the cost model above is wrong and the
   cadence must be sized against the pacer instead (currently 0.100 req/s, brake 0.89 — already
   throttling).
2. That `max 2 concurrent relocations` and the per-hull cooldown still bound behaviour at 7x the
   tick rate. The cooldown is keyed off DecidedAt, so it should, but a faster tick is exactly the
   condition that would expose a cooldown expressed in ticks rather than time.
3. That a 2-minute tick cannot re-enter a relocation still executing. One iteration currently spans
   the whole relocation flight; confirm the loop cannot start a second tick under it, or bound it.

IF the no-eligible tick turns out to cost API, fall back to 5 minutes — still catches the 3-15min
bucket's mass, still 3x the current capture.

## Not the constraint, for the record

The claim race is NOT what is limiting relocation. `relocator_skips_total{reason="claimed_at_actuation"}`
is 0. sp-x2jr6 slice 3 (a real ClaimShip) should stay parked until this lands and the counters
accumulate a real sample — with one evaluated hull per 15 minutes, there is not yet evidence
either way about whether slices 1+2 worked.
close_reason: Closed

title: placement action budget (10/tick) is now the binding constraint on arrivals — 293 in-flight slots share it, so 13 hulls already AT their target take ~30min to park
description:
## DefaultMaxPlacementActions=10 is now the binding constraint on placement throughput

sp-cwnwb fixed the FAIRNESS of the placement budget — a refused move no longer eats the budget a
successful one needs, and the worklist rotates least-recently-attempted so nothing starves. That
worked: 266 probes frozen for 28 hours drained to 16 within an hour.

But fairness redistributed a budget it did not enlarge, and the budget is now what limits arrival.

## Measured (era 5, 2026-07-30 ~13:45Z)

- 293 slots in flight (IN_TRANSIT), 16 still BOUGHT.
- Of the in-flight: 270 STILL_CROSSING, 10 IN_TARGET_SYSTEM, 13 AT_TARGET_WAYPOINT.
- Heartbeat, three consecutive ticks: `dispatched 10 docking 0 parked 0`. The accepted-action
  budget is saturated every tick, entirely by gate hops.
- PARKED has moved 399 -> 403 in ~75 minutes. PRICED is flat.

The arithmetic: DefaultMaxPlacementActions = 10 accepted commands per 30s tick, shared across all
in-flight slots. Rotation is fair, so each slot's share is 10/293 ≈ 3.4% of a turn per tick. The 13
hulls sitting ON their target waypoint therefore collect ~0.44 dock actions per tick between them,
and each needs TWO (dock, then park) — so ~30 minutes to land 13 arrivals that are already
physically at their destination. The 270 still crossing each need one action per gate hop, and a
hop only advances one ring per turn.

Zero docks across three ticks is CONSISTENT with that rate, not evidence of a defect — which is
exactly why this needs a bead rather than an investigation: the mechanism is working as designed
and the design is now too small.

## Why it matters

Every parked hull prices one system, and 245 of the in-flight hulls are bound for systems we hold
no price for. Trading-lane coverage is gated on arrival rate, and arrival rate is gated on this
constant.

## Ask

Re-size DefaultMaxPlacementActions now that fairness is guaranteed. It is a plain const
(RULINGS #5, deliberately not a knob), and its own doc says it exists "to keep a large backlog from
firing a burst of navigation commands in a single tick, not to express any economic preference".
That rationale bounds a BURST; it was never sized against a 300-slot steady state.

Constraints on the re-size, which is why this is not a one-line change:
1. **The real ceiling is the API pacer, not this constant.** The sensing cycle reports ~0.100 req/s
   with a residual and a brake. Raising the action budget above what the pacer will actually pass
   buys nothing and risks starving other sensing work (screening, yard reads) that draws on the
   same budget. Measure the pacer headroom first and size to it.
2. Placement competes with the buy queue, adoption, the orphan dispatch and expansion inside one
   tick. A larger placement budget is a redistribution unless the pacer has headroom.
3. Consider whether dock/park should be preferred over a gate hop when both are eligible. An
   arrival CONVERTS a hull into coverage; a hop only moves it closer. Completing arrivals first
   shortens the queue, which speeds everything behind it. That is a scheduling change rather than
   a sizing one and may be worth more than the constant.

Option 3 is probably the higher-value half: it costs no extra API budget at all, it just spends the
same actions in a better order.
close_reason: Closed

title: relocator has no metrics, no stall observer, and an unread Skipped field — a relocator losing every decision looks identical to an idle one, so sp-x2jr6 is unmeasurable
description:
## The relocator emits nothing, so a relocator losing every decision is indistinguishable from one with nothing to do

Self-reported by the lane that built it, and verified independently in shipped main (21f9d80a):

- **No metrics whatsoever.** `grep -c 'metrics\.' internal/application/trading/commands/run_opportunity_relocator.go` = **0**. The tour reposition paths immediately next door DO emit
  `metrics.RecordTourReposition(playerID, "success"|"failed"|"no_candidate")`
  (`internal/adapters/metrics/prometheus_collector.go:412`). The relocator simply never used it.
- **No stall observer.** Only two coordinators wire one: the fleet autosizer
  (`internal/adapters/grpc/fleet_autosizer_ports.go:143`) and probe sensing
  (`cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:1310`), both via `health.NewStallEscalator`. The relocator
  wires nothing (`grep -c 'StallObserver\|stall'` on its file = 0), so a permanently-racing
  relocator raises no `coordinator.stalled` event and trips no escalation counter.
- **`RelocatorTickResult.Skipped` is written and never read.** Its own comment says "keyed by
  reason, for the heartbeat" — and no heartbeat reads it. Verified: every non-test `.Skipped`
  reader in the tree belongs to a DIFFERENT type (parkedsensing reaper, buyqueue's
  SkippedNoYard, probe_sensing_heartbeat). Every exclusion reason the relocator computes is
  discarded when the tick ends.
- `RunOpportunityRelocatorResponse` is referenced nowhere outside its own file, so the tally
  never leaves the handler either.

## Why this is P1 and not cosmetic

It makes the feature unfalsifiable. sp-x2jr6 measured "3 of the first 4 relocation decisions
lost to the claim race" — and that number had to be hand-derived by joining daemon.log against
the containers table. sp-x2jr6 slices 1+2 then shipped a mitigation for exactly that race, and
**there is no way to tell whether it worked** without repeating the same manual dig. A
mitigation you cannot measure is a mitigation you cannot trust, and slice 3 (the real ClaimShip)
will have the identical problem.

Same failure CLASS as sp-biegl, inverted. sp-biegl: the placement machine filed refusal-only
ticks as PROGRESS, so a 28-hour freeze looked healthy. Here: nothing is filed at all, so a
total failure looks like an idle system. Both are "a broken state is indistinguishable from a
fine one", which is the property that let 266 probes sit frozen for 28 hours before a human
noticed by reading raw slot counts.

NOT affected, and worth recording so nobody re-checks it: the relocator has no `Actions` counter
and no `anyEffect()`, so it cannot produce sp-biegl's FALSE PROGRESS. `claimed_at_actuation` and
`actuation_recheck_unreadable` are safe in that specific respect. The gap is absence of signal,
not wrong signal.

## Scope

1. Emit the per-reason skip counts and a per-tick relocation outcome. Decide whether to share
   the tour's label space via the existing `RecordTourReposition` or to add a relocator-specific
   metric — sharing risks conflating two different actuators in one series; a separate one costs
   a new collector. Either is defensible; state the choice and why.
2. Wire `health.NewStallEscalator` the way the autosizer and probe sensing do, so a relocator
   that refuses every decision for N consecutive ticks escalates instead of looking idle. Reuse
   `StallEscalationTicks`; keep the escalator's exported surface as-is (`Observe` returns
   nothing, so no decision path can read the counter).
3. Either give `RelocatorTickResult.Skipped` the consumer its comment promises, or delete the
   field. A field whose doc asserts a consumer that does not exist is worse than no field.

Both files are already owned by the relocator lane, so this does not collide with the
parkedsensing or drift lanes.

## Sequencing

DO THIS BEFORE sp-x2jr6 slice 3. Slice 3 is the only change that actually closes the claim race,
and its before/after is unmeasurable until this lands. Measurement before mitigation.

Note the same limitation applies to sp-cwnwb's new `parked_sensing_gate_step_failed` warning:
useful per-event, but it is a log line rather than a countable signal, so the aggregate question
("is the placement machine failing every move?") still has no counter behind it.
close_reason: All three items merged (9489dbcd) and VERIFIED LIVE in production Prometheus, not just in code: spacetraders_daemon_relocator_ticks_total{verdict=PROGRESS}=1, relocator_decisions_total{outcome=relocated}=1, relocator_skips_total{reason=mid_tour}=32. The relocator now reports a per-tick verdict, per-hull decisions, and the per-reason skip counts it previously computed and discarded, plus a stall escalator with the licensed-and-lost BLOCKED/IDLE discriminator. sp-x2jr6's before/after is now measurable via rate(relocator_skips_total{reason='claimed_at_actuation'}[1h]), which was the whole point of doing this before slice 3. Discriminator ported onto sp-biegl so both coordinators share one rule.

title: stall detector filed refusal-only placement ticks as PROGRESS — a 22.5h freeze never escalated; decide IDLE vs BLOCKED for a refusal-saturated tick
description:
## A tick that refused every move was filed as PROGRESS, so a 22.5-hour freeze never tripped the stall detector

Found by the sp-cwnwb lane while fixing the starvation itself. Distinct bead because it is a
verdict-mapping question, not a budget question, and because the observability failure is worth
tracking on its own: the fleet froze 266 probes for ~28 hours and the health machinery reported
healthy ticks throughout.

## Mechanism

placement.go's PlacementReport.Actions documents itself as "counts everything above" —
Dispatched, Docking, Parked. But before sp-cwnwb, a REFUSED move also incremented it: both
dispatch() and dispatchClaim() ended a failed flyToSlot with `return true, nil`, and the caller
did `if acted { rep.Actions++ }`.

anyEffect() reads `Actions > 0` as "a placement advanced". So a tick that refused ten moves and
advanced nothing satisfied anyEffect and was filed PROGRESS. Every tick of the 22.5-hour freeze
looked like forward motion to the stall escalator, which is precisely why nothing escalated
while 266 hulls sat idle and one slot went 22.5h without a single attempt.

## What sp-cwnwb already changed, and what it deliberately did not

FIXED: Actions now excludes refusals, matching its own doc. Refusals draw on a separate bounded
budget. So a refusal-only tick no longer reports PROGRESS.

NOT FIXED, and left deliberately for this bead: such a tick now reports **IDLE**, not BLOCKED.
IDLE is defensible — nothing advanced — but it understates the situation. A tick that refused 30
moves is not idle; it is actively failing 30 times and getting nowhere. The distinction matters
because the escalator's whole job is to tell "nothing to do" apart from "cannot do the thing".

## Ask

Decide the verdict mapping for a refusal-saturated tick, then implement it:
  - refusals == 0 and no advances  -> IDLE (genuinely nothing queued) — unchanged.
  - refusals > 0 and no advances   -> BLOCKED, at least once the refusal budget is saturated
                                      (30/tick under the current default) for N consecutive
                                      ticks. A single refused move on an otherwise quiet tick
                                      should probably not escalate.
StallEscalationTicks already exists (health/stall.go, currently 3) — reuse it rather than adding
a second threshold, and keep the escalator's exported surface as-is (Observe returning nothing,
so no decision path can read the counter).

## Why this is worth doing rather than filing and forgetting

The starvation fix removes the false PROGRESS, so the freeze would now at least stop looking
healthy. But IDLE-forever is still a state a human has to notice by hand. BLOCKED is the signal
that reaches the heartbeat and the operator. Without it, the next equivalent jam is again found
by someone reading raw slot counts rather than by the machinery built to find it.

Related: sp-cwnwb also added the parked_sensing_gate_step_failed warning, so the underlying
refusals are no longer silent. This bead is about the aggregate verdict, not the per-slot log.
notes:
DISCRIMINATOR SETTLED — adopt the relocator's, not the budget-threshold framing in the description above.

sp-j1i49 shipped this exact mechanism for the opportunity relocator and drew a sharper line than
this bead originally proposed. Use it, so both coordinators share ONE rule rather than two similar
ones.

THE RULE: 'was the work LICENSED and then lost, or was there no work?'

  BLOCKED — a move was selected/licensed and could not be carried out, OR a signal the decision
            needed was unreadable. The unreadable case is in because it MASQUERADES as 'nothing
            worth doing', which is the identical hazard the autosizer names in
            stallReasonDemandUnreadable.
  IDLE    — genuinely nothing to do, and SILENT FOREVER. On a settled fleet this is the common and
            correct state; escalating it would page every tick, get muted, and then be ignored
            when it mattered.
  PROGRESS wins over a same-tick loss. A tick that advanced one placement and refused another did
            work. The alternative means the streak never clears on any fleet where one item is
            ever contended.

FOR THE PLACEMENT MACHINE this reads as: a move was selected and the actuator refused it ->
BLOCKED; nothing cleared the score / nothing was queued -> IDLE. NOTE THIS REPLACES the
'refusals > 0 AND the refusal budget saturated for N ticks' framing in the description: that
threshold is unnecessary, and worse, 'refusals > 0' alone cannot tell a refused-because-
legitimately-unaffordable from a refused-because-broken. The licensing question can.

TWO SUBTLETIES CARRIED OVER, both learned the hard way in sp-j1i49:

1. KEEP LIVE COUNTS OUT OF THE StallReason. The reason keys the streak, so a reason string that
   moves with a count restarts the streak every tick and can NEVER escalate — the subtlest way to
   leave this mechanism useless while it looks fully wired. Counts belong in a Detail field. Pin
   this STRUCTURALLY in a test rather than via a multi-tick fixture: a fixture only catches it when
   the counts happen to differ.
2. DO NOT RE-DERIVE THE VERDICT IN THE REPORTING PATH. sp-j1i49 had a probe survive every healthy
   fixture because Observe re-computed the verdict from the tick result instead of sharing the one
   already computed. It diverges only on inputs invisible in that result (the error, the
   kill-switch) — i.e. it looks right on every good tick and is wrong exactly when something has
   gone wrong, which is when the signal is the only thing anyone has. Compute once, hand the same
   verdict to every consumer, and test that both consumers agree on an ERRORED tick.

Reuse health.StallEscalationTicks; keep the escalator write-only (Observe returns nothing) so no
decision path can read the streak. Scope: the placement machine makes one fleet-wide pass per
tick, so a per-slot scope would let a slot that stops failing abandon its streak instead of
clearing it — mirror sp-j1i49 and leave scope empty unless there is a reason not to.
close_reason: Closed

title: Drift observability split, round 2 + tour telemetry 'planned' is a 2-second tautology — trace the two plan bases; sp-1ek0 plan-error gate is invalidated as estimator-honesty evidence
description: Economy-analyst, 2026-07-30 12:3xZ. THE PANEL (Prometheus tour_leg_price_drift_percent) climbed steadily 0->~125% buy drift over 06:30-12:20Z while the telemetry TABLE shows 0.5% mean / 0.4% value-weighted over the same legs. Counts nominally match (256.4 metric vs 256 table rows / 2h) BUT a 12:18Z deploy (7b67936f) reset counters mid-window so increase() is unreliable — the count-match cannot rule out a telemetry-nil observation population this time. NEW DISCRIMINATOR, the important one: tour_leg_telemetry.planned_at sits MEDIAN 2 SECONDS before realized_at (p90 7s) — in BOTH eras (yesterday evening AND this morning) — so the table's planned_unit_price is stamped at execution: plan-vs-realized over a 2s window = TAUTOLOGY. Consequences: (a) every 'plan error 0.1-0.5%' claim from this table (incl. the sp-1ek0 graduation gate's median plan-vs-realized) is NOT evidence of estimator honesty; (b) the Prometheus metric evidently carries a DIFFERENT (older, solve-time?) basis despite the unified call site at run_tour_coordinator.go:2675 — trace WHO calls recordLeg with WHAT trade/plannedAt, and whether a telemetry-nil family (farsink/stocker/arb?) observes without recording. ASK: (1) root-cause the two bases; (2) make BOTH sinks carry solve-time basis (drift vs original plan is the honest signal) value-weighted or labeled; (3) re-point the sp-1ek0 gate at tour_plan_rate{projected|realized} or a solve-time-basis drift. MONEY IS FINE meanwhile: net 2.58M/hr, margins ~26% accrual-corrected — if the metric's ~97% unweighted is honest it is concentrated in cheap goods (credit-weighted damage bounded by healthy P&L). Panel should not be trusted either way until traced. Kin of last night's pre-repair divergence (same panel, different mechanism).
notes:
SHIPWRIGHT (drift-lane, sp-fpgl2): ASK (3) DROPPED — premise dissolved, do not re-open. The bead asked to re-point the sp-1ek0 gate at tour_plan_rate{projected|realized} on the theory that its plan-vs-realized median was a 2-second tautology. It is not: computeTourGateMetrics grades PRICE only and never reads planned_at/realized_at, and PlannedUnitPrice is genuinely solve-time (ExpectedUnitPrice, written once at grpc_routing_client.go:479 from the planner response, never re-priced). Consequence (a) in the description is therefore WRONG as written. Team-lead ratified dropping ask (3).

Also settled: the bead's 'two plan bases' premise is FALSE (recordLeg feeds both sinks identical numbers; ONE non-test producer; telemetry never nil in production). The ~97-125% vs 0.5% split was NEITHER aggregation NOR population — it was rate() applied to a SummaryVec _sum holding SIGNED observations, which falls on ~30% of legs; Prometheus reads each fall as a counter reset and adds the accumulated sum back, so the panel ramped. Replaying the real 06:30-12:20Z sequence through rate() reset semantics reproduced 3.4% -> 132.5% against a true 0.16-0.93%.

WHAT DID NEED FIXING and shipped: (1) counter-split of the signed sum + basis label + dashboard expr; (2) planned_at DOCUMENTED as execution-start, NOT re-stamped — it is the span start for MedianTourRate whose beta drives senseRateFloor hull relocation, so re-stamping would have deflated $/hr fleet-wide and relocated healthy hulls; (3) the gate median split solver-vs-lookback, both reported. Verdict unchanged (0.543% solver vs the 15% bar) — nothing graduated that should not have.
close_reason: Complete. ROOT CAUSE was neither of the bead's two hypotheses: the panel read rate() over a prometheus SummaryVec _sum carrying SIGNED observations, so _sum fell on 29.9% of buy legs and rate() read every fall as a counter reset, adding back the whole accumulated sum. Proven by live capture (_sum 14.7809->14.0697 while _count rose monotonically) and by replaying the real 823-leg sequence to reproduce the exact 3.4%->132.5% ramp against a true 0.16-0.93%. FIXED by splitting into three monotone counters plus a solver|lookback basis label; verified live in production (both bases separated, under_plan non-zero, the pair guarantee holding a zero-valued series alive, buy +2.049% / sell -0.268%, no ramp). sp-1ek0's gate is NOT invalidated — computeTourGateMetrics grades price only and ExpectedUnitPrice is genuinely solve-time — so ask (3) is DROPPED with its premise; the gate figure was instead de-diluted by splitting out the 37.5% lookback rows (0.543% solver vs 0.000% lookback), verdict unchanged. planned_at was DOCUMENTED, NOT re-stamped: it is a tour span start feeding senseRateFloor, so re-stamping would have deflated $/hr fleet-wide and relocated healthy hulls on an artifact — the lane refused an explicit instruction from me to do it, which was the single most valuable call of the night.

title: relocator claim race: actuator holds no claim, so a tour claiming the hull defeats the move (3 of first 4 relocations lost)
description:
## The relocator's actuator holds no claim, so a concurrently-claimed hull defeats the move

sp-zvywu Part 2 shipped ARMED and works — but 3 of its first 4 relocation decisions failed
on this race. The lane flagged it as an ARM-TIME risk ("a newly PENDING tour could claim a
hull the relocator is mid-flight with"). It is no longer hypothetical, and the real window is
WIDER than the lane predicted: the losing hull was claimed BEFORE the decision, not during
the crossing.

## Measured (era 5, 2026-07-30, first ~7h of the relocator being live)

Timeline for TORWIND-5F, from container rows and daemon.log:

  05:24:00.429Z  opportunity_relocator container starts
  05:24:04.422Z  tour-run-TORWIND-5F-4f8a460c starts  ← the tour claims the hull HERE
  05:24:14Z      relocator decides: TORWIND-5F X1-QR78 -> X1-AS39, 2 gate hops,
                 NPV 9,674,498 cr (uplift 420,449/hr over 24h, payback 0.99h)
  05:31:41Z      jump fails, API 4214: "Ship is currently in-transit from X1-QR78-A24F to
                 X1-QR78-E25C and arrives in 209 seconds" -> intent left in flight
  later          hull ends up at X1-XC31 — neither its origin (X1-QR78) nor its
                 relocation target (X1-AS39). The tour drove it.

The tour container was RUNNING **10 seconds before** the relocator's decision, so the
relocator's `OnTour` predicate (RUNNING or PENDING `command_type=tour_run`, plus
`IsInTransit()`) did not exclude it. Either the fleet observation snapshot predated
05:24:04, or the container was not yet in a state `OnTour` matches at read time. Both are
the same bug: **observation and actuation are not atomic, and nothing in between reserves
the hull.**

Rate over the whole live window: 4 decisions, 3 `failed, intent left in flight` warnings.
Decisions were on 4 DIFFERENT hulls (TORWIND-5F, TORWIND-27B, TORWIND-2C6), so the
reconciler is not livelocked and correctly abandons a lost hull and moves on.

## What is NOT wrong — do not "fix" these

- **Not a livelock, and not expensive.** 7 `Ship navigation command executed` lines in 7
  hours. The failure is cheap; it is the OPPORTUNITY that is lost, not budget burned.
- **The retry semantics are correct.** "Intent left in flight for the next tick" is the
  documented restart-safety path: a not-yet-Completed record is FINISHED, never re-decided,
  because re-scoring from an intermediate position is the double-relocation bug.
- **RULINGS #7 is not violated.** The relocator only ever observes `DedicatedFleet()=="trade"`
  hulls and excludes `IsReservedByCaptain()`. The captain's frigate was never at risk.

## Fix options (needs a call, not obvious)

1. **Take a real claim before moving.** `RepositionToWaypointWithinJumps` documents that it
   "already holds shipSymbol claimed — travel()'s jumps set SkipClaim, trusting that claim",
   so the actuator is built to be called by a holder. The relocator holds nothing. Giving it
   a `ClaimShip` before the first hop closes the window properly. Risk: a claim the relocator
   fails to release strands a trade hull, which is worse than a lost relocation — so the
   release path has to be airtight across restarts.
2. **Re-verify at actuation.** Cheap: re-read the hull's claim/tour state immediately before
   the first hop and abandon if it changed. Narrows the window without introducing a claim
   the relocator must own. Does not close it.
3. **Accept it.** The cost is a missed relocation, retried next tick on a fresh ranking. At
   4 decisions per 7 hours the throughput loss is real but small, and each failure is ~2 API
   calls.

Recommend 1 with a restart-safe release, or 2 as the cheap interim. Option 3 is defensible
only while relocation volume stays this low.

## Related, filed separately by the lane, still open
- No `tune` wiring: the relocator is absent from `tuneOperationCoordinatorTypes` /
  `tunableKnobsByContainerType`, so there is no `tune --operation relocator` verb. Knobs are
  readable from the config column and survive restart.
notes:
CORRECTION (lead, verified by direct read of shipped main — supersedes the two-hypothesis wording above).

MY HYPOTHESIS B WAS WRONG, AND THE CHEAP FIX IT INVITES IS INERT. The bead said the cause was either (a) the fleet snapshot predated the claim or (b) the container was not yet in a state OnTour matches. It is (a), and more sharply: THE TOUR CONTAINER ROW DID NOT EXIST AT OBSERVATION TIME.

Verified, not inferred:
  - container_repository.go: ContainerModel is built with StartedAt: &now immediately before
    r.db.Create(model), so started_at IS row-creation time, not the RUNNING flip.
  - run_opportunity_relocator.go: Reconcile() is called at the TOP of the for loop; the
    select on time.After(tick) comes AFTER it. So the first Reconcile — and its first read,
    ObserveTradeHulls — runs before any wait.
Therefore the snapshot fired at ~05:24:00.43 and the tour row was INSERTed at 05:24:04.42,
four seconds LATER. TORWIND-5F was genuinely idle and genuinely unclaimed; OnTour and Pinned
were both CORRECTLY false. There was no row to match and no claim to see.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: do NOT 'fix' this by widening the container status set
or repairing the command_type match. That change is INERT for this incident and all 3 of the
4 lost decisions would still have raced. Only a commit-time re-check or a real claim closes it.

The ~14s observe-to-decide gap is NOT latency to optimise away: it is the bounded pre-flight
(up to relocationRegionCandidateBudget planner calls per hull). A correct observation takes
that long, which is exactly why the window has to be closed at the other end.

SEPARATE REAL DEFECT, shipped, found by the lane that built it (verified by the lead):
THE PENDING BRANCH OF OnTour IS INERT. tourContainerIDs does collect PENDING tour rows into
the id map, but the predicate is

    onTour := ship.IsInTransit() || (ship.IsAssigned() && tourContainers[ship.ContainerID()])

which keys on the HULL'S OWN CLAIM. During the PENDING window — between Add's INSERT and the
runner's ClaimShip — the hull is unassigned, so IsAssigned() short-circuits the whole
right-hand side to false and ship.ContainerID() is empty regardless. The PENDING entries can
never match. Worse, with IsAssigned() false the hull also reads Pinned:false, so it is FULLY
ELIGIBLE. The existing test passes only because its fixture assigns the hull to the PENDING
container, which is the narrow case rather than the real one — fixture blindness.

Fix is cheap, claim-free and cannot strand a hull: on non-terminal tour rows, ALSO match the
container's DECLARED hull from config["ship_symbol"] (container_ops_tour.go writes it) rather
than only the hull's own ContainerID. Note this would NOT have prevented the TORWIND-5F
incident either (no row existed at all) — it closes a narrower, separate window.

RECOMMENDED SLICING, revised:
  Slice 1 (cheap, no claim, cannot leak): re-read the chosen hull's assignment/reservation
    immediately before RelocateHull and abort if it is now claimed or captain-reserved. Shrinks
    the window from ~14s to milliseconds. Does NOT make observe-and-act atomic, so it does not
    retire this bead, but on the live numbers it should turn the dominant failure mode into a
    rare one at near-zero risk — and stays useful even after a real claim lands.
  Slice 2: the PENDING/declared-hull match above.
  Slice 3 (actually closes it): a real ClaimShip in the actuator with a restart-safe release.
    RepositionToWaypointWithinJumps documents that it expects to be called by a holder
    ('travel()'s jumps set SkipClaim, trusting that claim'), so this is the shape the actuator
    was designed for. Gate it on an airtight release: a leaked claim strands a trade hull,
    which is strictly worse than a lost relocation.
close_reason:
CLOSED WITHOUT BUILDING SLICE 3 — a real ClaimShip would be a REGRESSION, not a safety fix, and the race it targets has been dissolved.

THE DECIDING FINDING (verified in shipped code, not inferred): the tour container already holds the hull's claim for its ENTIRE life — container_ops_tour.go:243, 'The runner claims the hull (ship_symbol metadata), flips the row to RUNNING, and owns release-on-death'. The inter-tour gap AND the whole sp-e8d92 offer window sit INSIDE that claim. ClaimShip rejects an already-assigned hull (ship_repository.go:1591, ShipAlreadyAssignedError when AssignmentStatus='active' and a different ContainerID), so a relocator claim on an OFFERED hull would fail every time. Since sp-e8d92 deployed, offered hulls are the population that matters — so naive slice 3 would make sp-e8d92 INERT. That is the 'enumerate the rejected class before shipping an ownership guard' trap: the affected path's own hulls are in the rejected class.

MY ASYMMETRIC-RISK WORRY DID NOT MATERIALISE, and both release paths are clean:
  - RESTART: ReleaseAllActive (daemon_server.go:698, reason daemon_restart) releases every active assignment except captain reservations, so a relocator claim CANNOT survive a crash and cannot strand a hull. The intent stays uncompleted, the next tick resumes it, slice 1's re-check sees an idle hull, the move finishes.
  - PREEMPTION: PreemptForCaptain (ship_repository.go:1786) revokes a live coordinator claim inside SELECT FOR UPDATE and records the container it took it from. The relocator yields, and cannot re-take it because the hull then reads IsReservedByCaptain -> Pinned -> protected by the shared predicate.
The boot sweep is the backstop that makes any claim self-limiting. Good answer — just to a question that turned out not to need asking.

THE RACE IS NOT MATERIAL. Measured live: relocator_skips_total{reason='claimed_at_actuation'} = 1 against mid_tour = 156. About one hull in 157 decisions. sp-x2jr6 was filed on '3 of the first 4 relocations lost', which was 4 thin samples from before a restart at a 15-minute cadence; the counter shipped in sp-j1i49 answers it properly and says the constraint is tour occupancy, not contention.

WHAT ACTUALLY DISSOLVED IT: sp-e8d92. For an offered hull the tour holds the claim, so NO third party can take it — strictly stronger exclusivity than the relocator could grant itself — and the tour is parked by durable agreement. The offer plus the tour's own claim IS the mutual exclusion. The only residual exposure is expiry mid-move, already covered by slice 1's re-check and the tour re-planning from its current position.

RESIDUAL, RECORDED FOR ANYONE WHO REOPENS THIS: a genuinely UNASSIGNED hull (between tour CONTAINERS, not between tours) can still be claimed mid-relocation — the original TORWIND-5F shape. A claim would work there, but the population is small (continuous containers hold their hulls essentially always) and claiming it creates a NEW failure: the tour launcher's ClaimShip then fails, the runner retries with bounded backoff (container_runner.go:1104), and the container terminalizes FAILED — trading a rare lost relocation for container churn. Also considered and rejected: having the tour TRANSFER its claim for the window (TransferToContainer). It would work and would not strand, but it reinstates the cross-container handshake sp-e8d92 deliberately removed, and it changes WHO holds the claim rather than WHETHER the hull is held — exclusivity already holds.

IF IT EVER BECOMES MATERIAL, the narrow fix is: claim only when the hull is genuinely unassigned, and accept the container-churn cost. Justify it with the counter, not with the original incident.

title: Time-bucketed sums of transactions.amount mix unmatched trade legs — the measurement defect behind 7 false conclusions; needs position-matched accounting
description:
THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT BEHIND SEVEN WRONG CONCLUSIONS IN ONE SESSION (2026-07-30). Filed so the next
reader does not repeat them.

MECHANISM. transactions stores each trade leg as its own signed row: PURCHASE_CARGO negative,
SELL_CARGO positive. A hull buys in one clock hour and sells in another. Therefore ANY time-bucketed
SUM(amount) mixes unmatched legs and measures where the hour boundary fell, not economics. This is
not a rounding issue -- it inverts signs.

DEMONSTRATION, same goods, adjacent hours, from live data:
                     hour 06:00        hour 08:00
    CLOTHING        -2,132,071        +1,931,781
    URANITE           -647,190        +2,843,115
    MEDICINE        +1,427,360        -1,835,254
And at the hour level: 144 buys/141 sells produced 492,342 net while 164 buys/157 sells produced
7,375,778 -- a 15x swing on a 14% difference in trade count. Nothing about trade quality changed.

WRONG CONCLUSIONS THIS PRODUCED (all mine, all from this one substrate):
  1. "net per hour collapsed"                  -- was an open-position hour
  2. "margin is falling as the fleet grows"    -- margin oscillates +/-3 pts on leg placement
  3. "sink depth contention is the constraint" -- refuted separately at 52% utilisation
  4. "API ceiling is binding"                  -- falsified: freed 23%, revenue unchanged
  5. "cooldowns are binding, hulls parallelise"-- built on hourly net/hull
  6. "hull count shows no benefit"             -- constant net/hull IS linear scaling
  7. "trade quality varies 13x per hour"       -- the demonstration above
Each looked like a clean signal. Each was leg placement.

WHAT IS SAFE TO USE TODAY:
  - Windows of 3h or more, where most positions open AND close inside the window. The session's
    3-hour blocks (1.41M -> 3.09M -> 3.08M -> 3.27M -> ~3.2M/hr sustained) are the defensible series.
  - Counts (trades, sells, distinct hulls) rather than signed sums.
  - market_absorption_ledger, which records EXECUTED vs PLANNED per sink and does not have this
    defect.
WHAT IS NOT SAFE: any hourly or sub-hourly net, margin, net-per-hull, or net-per-good figure. The
Grafana payback panels (129-139) are LIFETIME by construction and therefore immune -- that was the
right call for a different reason than I gave at the time.

THE FIX: position-matched accounting. Match each PURCHASE_CARGO to the SELL_CARGO that closes it
(hull + good, FIFO within hull), and attribute the realised margin to the CLOSING timestamp. Then an
hourly figure means "positions closed this hour", which is answerable. Open positions become a
separate, explicitly-labelled inventory-at-cost figure rather than silently contaminating net.
  - the data needed is present: metadata->>'ship_symbol', metadata->>'good_symbol',
    metadata->>'units', amount, created_at.
  - sp-mjmqf just landed per-hull purchase attribution using the same metadata shape, so there is a
    precedent for the join.
  - a materialised view or a ledger table is preferable to repeating the CTE in every panel.

ACCEPTANCE: an hourly realised-margin figure that does not change sign when the same trade's legs
straddle an hour boundary; open inventory reported separately at cost; and a regression test that
feeds a buy in hour N with its sell in hour N+1 and asserts both hours report correctly (today hour N
reads as a loss and hour N+1 as pure profit).
close_reason: Closed

title: probe surge is armed but structurally dormant: surplus probes cannot exist while open placements outnumber hulls 10:1
description:
## The surge is armed, correct, and structurally unable to fire

sp-zvywu Part 1 shipped and is live on the reconcile path (verified:
surgeToUnpricedSystems is called from ReconcileOnce at
run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:1073, and the cap resolves through
`surge_inflight_cap` → defaultSurgeInFlightCap=8). It has produced ZERO dispatches
since deploy, and not because of a bug — because its precondition cannot occur in
this fleet regime.

## Measured (era 5, 2026-07-30 05:3xZ)

- probes_unheld = **0**, exactly. Every one of the 710 probes is named by either a
  scout post (275 with assigned_hull) or a sensing_slots row.
- Open placements far outnumber hulls: 6,959 slots in WANTED, of which 6,383 are in
  systems we hold no prices for. Against 710 probes.
- Actionable unpriced pool: 1,095 systems. Priced: 136 of 1,215 charted.

## Why it cannot fire

surgeToUnpricedSystems gates on surplusProbes(), which is idleOrphans() minus hulls
on a charting errand. idleOrphans requires `!holds.hulls[ship]` — a hull named by NO
slot. The orphan dispatch runs earlier in the same tick, claims any idle orphan into
an open WANTED row, and appends it to holds.hulls. With 6,383 breadth-oriented WANTED
rows permanently outstanding, every probe that becomes free is claimed by the primary
queue before the surge is reached. "Surplus" never exists.

So the surge takes its silent `return 0` at `len(surplus) == 0` on every tick, forever,
regardless of how large the unpriced pool is.

## This is a design gap, not a defect in the code as written

The primary placement queue is ALREADY breadth-oriented (6,383 of 6,959 WANTED are in
unpriced systems), so the surge's mission — breadth into unpriced systems — is not
being neglected; it is being done by the queue the surge was meant to supplement. The
surge was specified to spend SURPLUS capacity, and a fleet whose open-placement backlog
is 10x its hull count has no surplus by construction.

Two honest options for the Admiral to choose between:

1. **Leave it dormant and delete nothing.** It becomes live automatically if the probe
   fleet ever outgrows the placement backlog. Cost: a live code path that never runs,
   which is the kind of thing that rots and is exactly what "closed is not armed"
   warns about — a feature nobody can tell is working.
2. **Re-found it on a different precondition.** The valuable version is not "spend
   surplus hulls" but "prefer a system with NO price at all over a 6th market in an
   already-priced system". That is a RANKING change to the primary queue, not a
   separate actuator: 576 WANTED rows sit in already-priced systems and 413 hulls are
   committed to already-priced systems while only 299 are committed to unpriced ones.
   Re-pointing that 413 is worth more than any surge could be.

Option 2 subsumes option 1 and needs no surplus. Recommend 2, but it is a scope call.

## Blocked on

sp-ky85o first. Right now 0 hulls are PARKED in any unpriced system — every one of the
299 committed there is stuck at BOUGHT/IN_TRANSIT because the gate resolver walls off
15% of the map. Until that is fixed, neither the queue nor a surge can price anything,
so measuring any ranking change would be meaningless.
notes:
OPTION B2 IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — DO NOT BUILD IT. Verified by direct read, 2026-07-30.

buyqueue.go drainCandidates() ALREADY orders fills by COVERAGE ASCENDING with depth only as
the tiebreak, and it already solved this exact concentration problem once: its own comment
records 'measured on the live fleet as 67% of parked probes sitting in three systems while
covered systems held one each'. The ranking is per-SLOT, not per-system — the i-th outstanding
placement of a system ranks at parked+i, so a 0-probe system's FIRST slot competes at 0 and
outranks a priced system's second slot. That is precisely the breadth-first behaviour B2
proposed to add.

And the slots are NOT being scope-dropped. drainCandidates only admits a fill when
inScope[slot.System], dropping anything else — so that gate was the obvious suspect. Measured:
ALL 6,326 WANTED slots in unpriced systems carry verdict IN_SCOPE (760 unpriced systems
IN_SCOPE, 315 still PENDING, 13 NO_WHITELIST — but zero WANTED slots sit behind a non-IN_SCOPE
verdict). Every one of those 6,326 is a valid fill at coverage 0, i.e. already at the HEAD of
the queue.

CONCLUSION: nothing is mis-ranked. The queue already prefers a never-priced system over the
Nth market in a priced one, and the unpriced systems are already first in line. The reason 399
of 399 parked hulls sit in priced systems while 0 sit in unpriced ones is NOT ordering — it is
that the pipeline is blocked DOWNSTREAM of the buy: sp-ky85o (gate walls, fixed and deployed
09:15, unroutable warnings 682/1.2h -> 21) and sp-cwnwb (a failed placement move consumes the
10-action tick budget in fixed order, still open). The money is already spent — 266 hulls
bought and frozen at BOUGHT — and the queue that spent it chose the right targets.

This retires option B entirely. The remaining question is only whether to keep or delete the
dormant surge (option A vs D), and the case for D is STRONGER than when this bead was filed:
the surge is not merely unable to fire, it is redundant against an existing mechanism that
does the same job better (per-slot coverage indexing rather than one-per-system breadth).

Lesson for this bead's next reader: 'we do X, Y would be better' needs the X path read first.
B2 would have shipped an ordering that already existed and measured as inert.
DECISION (Admiral, 2026-07-30): 'do your recommendation' = option B2 + D.

B2 IS RETIRED — see the note above. It was already implemented in buyqueue.go drainCandidates
(coverage-ascending, per-slot indexed) and all 6,326 unpriced-system WANTED slots are already
IN_SCOPE at coverage 0. Building it would have shipped an inert duplicate. Nothing to do.

D IS APPROVED AND PENDING, blocked on sequencing not on the decision: delete the dormant surge.
Justification is stronger than when this bead was filed — the surge is not merely unable to
fire (probes_unheld = 0, structurally, while 6,959 open placements face 710 probes), it is
REDUNDANT against a live mechanism that does the same job better.

WHY IT IS NOT DISPATCHED YET: sp-cwnwb's lane currently has probe_sensing_fakes_test.go open in
internal/application/scouting/commands — the SAME package as probe_sensing_surge.go and
run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go. Deleting the surge now would collide with an in-flight P0.
Cut a FRESH worktree for D the moment sp-cwnwb gates (one worktree per lane; do not stack D
onto the starve branch).

SCOPE FOR THE D LANE when it is dispatched:
  - Delete probe_sensing_surge.go and run_probe_sensing_surge_test.go.
  - Remove the surgeToUnpricedSystems call from ReconcileOnce (run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go
    ~line 1073) and the 'surged' accounting it feeds, including any heartbeat/metric field.
  - Remove SurgeInFlightCap from the command struct, the sensingConfig resolve, the
    surge_inflight_cap tunable key, and defaultSurgeInFlightCap.
  - Remove UnpricedPoolPort / UnpricedSystems and its SurgeEnginePorts wiring in
    adapters/parkedsensing/surge_ports.go IF nothing else reads it — CHECK FIRST, the pool read
    is a genuinely useful era-scoped set difference and another consumer may have appeared.
  - Keep gateReach/newGateReach if the orphan dispatch or any other pass uses it. Verify by
    grep before deleting; do not remove a shared helper on the assumption it was surge-only.
  - Leave the sensing_slots schema untouched. No migration.
The commit must state that this deletes a feature that never executed in production and why
(precondition structurally unreachable + redundant against drainCandidates), so the deletion
is not later mistaken for a regression.
close_reason: Option D (delete the dormant surge) merged to main. Option B2 was RETIRED as already-implemented — buyqueue.go drainCandidates already orders coverage-ascending with per-slot indexing, and all 6,326 unpriced-system WANTED slots were already IN_SCOPE at coverage 0, so building it would have shipped an inert duplicate. The stale 'blocks sp-ky85o' edge was for measuring option B, which no longer exists.

title: Shipyard reads need the same one-budget treatment as market reads
description:
Follow-up to sp-ntgfj, which put market reads under ONE fixed budget
(internal/domain/marketscan + application/ship/market_scan_budget.go). Shipyard reads were
separately measured at 0.844 req/s — 44.7% of the entire 2.00 req/s server ceiling — and are
currently masked only by the Admiral's live mitigation quartermaster_cadence_secs 3600 -> 86400.
That mitigation must not be permanent: it is a blunt cadence floor, not a budget, so it will
bind wrongly again as the map grows.

WHY IT WAS STAGED OUT OF sp-ntgfj. Market reads have exactly ONE API choke point
(MarketScanner.ScanAndSaveMarket -> apiClient.GetMarket), so one gate covered every caller.
Shipyard reads do NOT: FOUR call sites reach APIClient.GetShipyard while bypassing
ShipyardScanner entirely —

  internal/application/manufacturing/services/market_locator.go:116
  internal/application/ship/commands/outfitting/outfitting.go:255
  internal/application/shipyard/commands/purchase_ship.go:552
  internal/application/shipyard/queries/get_shipyard_listings.go:55

plus ShipyardScanner.ScanAndSaveShipyard (shipyard_scanner.go:110) which is reached from
scout_tour, route_executor and warp_system_charter. So this needs the four bypasses routed
through the scanner FIRST, then the same gate applied — a real refactor, not a one-line hook.

Note purchase_ship.go is also touched by the unmerged sensing-spend-gate branch; coordinate.

THE DESIGN IS ALREADY BUILT AND SHOULD BE REUSED, NOT REDESIGNED. internal/domain/marketscan
is generic over "a thing with a cached row, a value weight and a fixed allowance":
  - fixed budget, interval = budget / yards known (total cost does not grow with the map),
  - value-weighted priority with a ValueClampR reserve,
  - a proven anti-starvation bound (ValueClampR * known / budget),
  - Earning class for reads a fail-closed money guard consumes (purchase_ship's price check
    is one — it must never be served from store),
  - Debit for reads that must be metered but cannot be denied.

Shipyard differs from market in one way worth designing around: hull PRICES need a hull at the
counter, while the catalogue survives a presence-less GET (see yard_ports.go). So the value
weight probably wants to be "does this yard sell a heavy type we might buy" rather than a
bid-ask spread, and the existing quartermaster_cadence_secs should become a FLOOR the budget
may not exceed rather than the thing that sets the rate.

- purchase_ship's pre-buy price verification is never served from store (RULINGS #4);
