title: expansion_enabled does not stop the sensing coordinator's OWN probe buying — 907k spent while the switch read off, and both spenders log as 'fleet expansion'
description:
ADMIRAL-REPORTED 2026-07-30, and they were right: probes kept being bought for hours after
expansion was "turned off". Verified live before filing.

WHAT expansion_enabled ACTUALLY GATES: only the requests the sensing coordinator makes to OTHER
engines -- charting-seed requests, and off-gate explorer demand. Those were correctly off; the
coordinator log reads "spending paused: no seed purchase, no explorer demand".

WHAT IT DOES NOT GATE: the sensing coordinator's OWN probe purchases, made for sensing coverage.
Same log line, same cycle, expansion_enabled=2:
    01:07:05  bought 6 reused 0 queued 5
    01:08:29  bought 6 reused 0 queued 5
    01:09:50  bought 6 reused 0 queued 6
    01:11:20  bought 6 reused 0 queued 6
Measured cost while the switch read OFF: 25 probes, 907,545 credits between 03:00Z and 04:11Z.
The Admiral had turned expansion off at ~21:46Z; buying resumed at 03:00Z and nobody noticed
because the switch said 2.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE: BOTH kinds of purchase are written with operation_type='fleet expansion'.
So the ledger shows "fleet expansion" spending money while the expansion switch reads off. Any
operator checking the switch against the ledger concludes the switch is broken. It is not broken --
it is MISNAMED for its actual scope, and the ledger label makes two different spenders
indistinguishable.

THE KNOB'S OWN DESCRIPTION IS ACCURATE and says exactly this ("stops everything that asks another
engine to buy"). That is not a defence: a switch called expansion_enabled that leaves the largest
probe-spending path running is a trap, and the description is not what an operator reads at 4am
during a money leak. The name and the ledger label are the defect, not the doc.

CURRENT MITIGATION IS A WORKAROUND, NOT A FIX. I stopped it by pushing the sensing money floors to
their maximums -- capex_reserve_credits 500,000 -> 5,000,000 and capital_multiplier_k_milli
400 -> 10,000 (0.4h -> 10h of cargo runway held back). That starves ALL probe buying including
legitimate coverage work, and it silently un-fixes itself the moment treasury grows past the floor.
I chose the floors over probe_cap deliberately: dropping the cap below our 676 owned probes risked
reaping them.

FIX, pick one and make it honest:
  (a) expansion_enabled=2 stops ALL probe spending, coverage included -- matches the name and what
      an operator expects from "off"; or
  (b) split the switch: one control for cross-engine expansion requests, one for the coordinator's
      own coverage buying, each named for what it stops; and
  (c) EITHER WAY: stop tagging both spenders operation_type='fleet expansion'. Give coverage buys
      their own operation_type so the ledger can tell an operator which engine spent the money.

ACCEPTANCE: with the switch off and the money floors back at their defaults (capex_reserve_credits
100000, capital_multiplier_k_milli 2000), a full sensing cycle buys ZERO probes and says so; and a
ledger query can separate coverage spend from expansion-request spend. Verify by watching real
cycles, not by reading the guard -- the failure mode here was a guard that was consulted and simply
did not cover the path that spends.
notes:
BUILD LANE (sensing-spend-gate) — DECISION AND EVIDENCE, 2026-07-30

CHOSE (a), NOT (b). Off means off: expansion_enabled=2 now stops ALL probe purchasing,
coverage included. The argument is not just the switch name — (b)'s engineering case
dissolves once you look at what the drain actually does.

The drain is not only a buyer. Per pop it tries, in order: reuseSpareHull (re-task an idle
spare already parked in-system — zero credits, zero API), then footholds.fill (fly a surplus
hull across a gate to occupy a system — gate-STORE reads and two ledger rows, zero credits,
zero API), and only then quote/claim/buy. So (a) implemented at the right granularity —
gate the PURCHASE, not the drain — keeps every free path that grows coverage on hulls
already paid for. That is exactly the concern that would motivate (b) (market freshness),
and it is preserved under (a). A second knob would therefore buy no freshness at all, only
a second control an operator must find at 4am. Two pinned tests hold that line:
TestDrain_SpendPauseStillReusesAParkedSpare and TestDrain_SpendPauseStillFillsAFoothold.

Two further reasons for (a):
 - The design's own stated invariant already draws the line at purchase INTENT
   ("EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE EITHER COMMANDS A HULL OR RAISES A PURCHASE INTENT",
   expansion.go). Drawing that line and then leaving the engine that EXECUTES intent
   ungated was internally inconsistent, not a deliberate scope.
 - The knob's own registry text already called itself the "expansion SPENDING switch".
   (a) makes that sentence true; (b) would have required renaming it anyway.

The gate sits AHEAD of every money read, so a paused tick makes no LiveCredits API call and
reports neither CapHeld nor FloorHeld — one unambiguous reason. That matters: see the live
line below, which today reads "held at the buy floor" because of the mitigation, sending an
operator to the treasury for a decision they made themselves.

(c) NEW OPERATION_TYPE: 'sensing coverage'. PurchaseShipCommand.OperationType is new and
defaults to 'fleet expansion', so bootstrap, the autosizer, the frontier expansion engine
and manual buys are byte-identical and their history stays comparable. Ledger query:
  SELECT operation_type, count(*), -sum(amount) FROM transactions
   WHERE transaction_type='PURCHASE_SHIP' AND metadata->>'ship_type'='SHIP_PROBE'
   GROUP BY 1;
Live today that returns ONE row: fleet expansion | 1088 | 57,354,914 — every probe ever
bought, both engines, one label. After deploy it splits.

COLLATERAL FOUND AND FIXED: frontier.json had SIX panels (Probes Bought, Probe Capex, Capex
per System/Market Priced, Probe Purchases, Cumulative Probe Capex) filtering
operation_type='fleet expansion'. Left alone they would have silently lost the LARGER
spender the moment (c) landed. They now scope on category='SHIP_INVESTMENTS' AND
metadata->>'ship_type'='SHIP_PROBE', which is exactly "a probe was bought" (category is a
pure function of transaction_type) and cannot go stale when another engine starts buying.
Panel descriptions say so, and say not to re-add an operation_type filter.

OBSERVED CYCLE LINES, at the DOCUMENTED default floors (capex_reserve_credits 100000,
capital_multiplier_k_milli 2000 — NOT the mitigation maxima), from a full ReconcileOnce in a
world wired to be able to buy (yard + docked hull + treasury above the floor):

  switch ON  : bought 1 reused 0 queued 1 (1 attempts)
  switch OFF : bought 0 reused 0 queued 0 (0 attempts, held at the expansion switch:
               expansion_enabled is off, so no probe is bought) ... expansion ...
               (spending paused: no seed purchase, no explorer demand)

Both halves of the tick now agree. Under mutation (k.SpendEnabled forced true) the OFF arm
reproduces the live defect verbatim: "bought 1 ... (spending paused: no seed purchase, no
explorer demand)".

MITIGATION MUST BE UNDONE AFTER DEPLOY, NOT BEFORE. Live container
probe_sensing_coordinator-player-5-bb435635 still carries capex_reserve_credits=5000000 and
capital_multiplier_k_milli=10000. Reverting them before the fix is deployed resumes the leak.
After deploy:
  spacetraders container tune <container-id> capex_reserve_credits 0
  spacetraders container tune <container-id> capital_multiplier_k_milli 0
(0 is the revert-to-default verb.) Expect the cycle line to change from
"held at the buy floor" to "held at the expansion switch".

NOT DONE, deliberately out of scope: stale SPARE (seed) wants written before the switch went
off are still filled for FREE by reuse/foothold while paused. They cost nothing, so no money
leaks, but a follow-up could reap them when the switch goes off.

title: Replay harness has bid/ask TRANSPOSED vs live — free-money self-spread invalidates any past lane-selection verdict (incl. sp-0hodc)
description:
Found by the sp-smbgd lane; VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by me before filing.

THE TRANSPOSITION. gobot/services/routing-service/replay_objective.py:115 builds its snapshot as
    bid=int(r.purchase_price), ask=int(r.sell_price)
The live convention, settled by sp-en5h7, is the OPPOSITE — see
gobot/internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_lanes.go:166-167
    Bid: g.SellPrice(),     // sell_price = what we RECEIVE selling TO it
    Ask: g.PurchasePrice(), // purchase_price = what we PAY buying FROM it
The same transposition is in the untracked probe replay_hopwiden_TEMP.py.

WHY IT SURVIVED sp-en5h7's 100-site alignment: the harness carries a comment ASSERTING the wrong
orientation -- "Bid = market BUY column (purchase_price), Ask = market SELL column (sell_price) --
same as collectSystemListings". A confidently-wrong comment reads as already-audited, so a reviewer
sweeping reader sites skips it. The comment is the defect's camouflage; fix it in the same commit.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is not a rounding error. At a real market purchase_price > sell_price (you pay
more than you receive). Transposed, every waypoint reports bid > ask AT THE SAME WAYPOINT -- a
free-money self-spread. The lane measured the effect: in-system tours inflate to 16-26M cr/hr, and
under that no cross-system haul is ever worth planning. The lane initially measured a FALSE
NEGATIVE on its own feature because of this, and the named MERITIUM lane was unreproducible until
the orientation was corrected -- then it reproduced immediately.

*** ANY PAST REPLAY VERDICT THAT TURNED ON LANE SELECTION IS SUSPECT. *** The bias is directional,
not random: it systematically favours in-system over cross-system. Verdicts to re-run, at least:
  - sp-0hodc (max_tour_systems 4->2, "cap-4 projects -26.1% vs cap-2") -- a pure lane-selection
    verdict, and the change is LIVE in production on its strength. NOTE: its live 3h validation
    came out neutral-to-positive on independent grounds (per-hull net +11.8%, margin flat at 26.4%
    once the accrual artifact is removed), so the REVERT still looks safe -- but the -26.1%
    magnitude that justified it rests on a transposed harness and should not be quoted again
    until re-run.
  - the +29% spend-sensitivity replay cited on sp-mf8ps (plan-level, per-tour budget 725k->1.45M).
  - any depth/horizon verdict from sp-kab1c / sp-tp5c3 lineage.

ALSO MISSING, independent of the transposition: neither tracked harness feeds inter_system_hops, so
an A/B on hop-depth pricing reads as INERT at depth > 1 -- it cannot see the thing it is testing.
The lane's corrected harness (adds the right orientation AND feeds inter_system_hops) is at
/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-andres-dandrea-IdeaProjects-cities-spacetraders-city/c77c9709-e861-4701-be33-49418a01712b/scratchpad/replay_affine.py
-- uncommitted, scratchpad, will be lost. Land it or port it deliberately.

FIX: correct the orientation in replay_objective.py, DELETE the misleading comment rather than
edit around it, feed inter_system_hops, and add a test that fails on a transposed snapshot -- the
natural falsifier is "no waypoint may report bid >= ask at the same waypoint", which is impossible
in a real market and catches this class permanently.
notes:
CORRECTION FROM ECONOMY-ANALYST (2026-07-30 03:45Z), ACCEPTED — this bead OVERSTATED the
orientation bug's reach. Read this before acting on the sp-0hodc claim above.

REPLAY A IS EXONERATED ON ORIENTATION. It fetched market history ONCE at process start 23:07Z --
BEFORE the sp-en5h7 column migration at 23:46Z -- so it read TRANSPOSED rows through the TRANSPOSED
mapping and got CORRECTLY-ORIENTED books. Wrong column of wrong data = right number; the in-memory
rows never saw the migration. The analyst had already documented this on sp-0hodc at ~01:0xZ, where
they voided and re-ran their own Replay B specifically for the post-migration form of this bug,
using a swap wrapper plus a crossed-quote filter. So the -26.1% is NOT tainted by orientation.

WHAT ACTUALLY TAINTS IT IS THE SECOND DEFECT IN THIS BEAD: inter_system_hops never fed, so every
crossing priced at a flat 1x1200s regardless of depth. That bias runs IN FAVOUR of cap-4 -- and
cap-4 lost anyway. Therefore:
    DIRECTION  -> STRENGTHENED (cap-4 lost despite a bias helping it)
    MAGNITUDE  -> unreliable, and unreliable in the CONSERVATIVE direction
The -26.1% stays quarantined pending a re-run on the corrected harness; the revert itself is if
anything better supported than before. Same qualifier applies to the +29% spend-sensitivity figure
(both arms equally biased, so directional only).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ORIENTATION FIX: it is still a real defect and still must be fixed -- any
replay run that read POST-migration rows through the transposed mapping is genuinely corrupt. What
changes is only the blast radius: pre-23:46Z runs are safe by accident, not by design, and that
accident is not repeatable. Fix it anyway; do not treat the exoneration as a reason to soften.

METHOD NOTE, worth keeping: two independent errors can cancel and produce a correct result, so
"the harness was wrong" does not imply "the verdict was wrong" -- and the reverse. Establish the
data's vintage relative to the schema change before ruling a past result in or out. I ruled Replay A
out without checking when it fetched.

title: Opportunity relocator (meta-planner) + sensing surge: auto-relocate hulls to measurably better regions; parallel probe dispatch when the reachable graph grows
description:
Admiral-directed build (2026-07-30, economy-analyst spec; captain retired — everything automated). Ship ARMED per Admiral no-flags doctrine; knobs are operational thresholds/caps only.

CONTEXT/ECONOMICS: the galaxy unsealed — 265 gate-reachable systems, 88 scanned, fleet trades ~45. The tradable envelope moves WITH the hull (cap-2 tours plan from the hull's position), so relocation unlocks distant regions. Armed reposition machinery (reposition_reach, reposition_rate_floor) only rescues UNDER-earners; nothing chases distant upside. Virgin-region prior ~2x lane quality (uncrushed depth, no contention); heavies baseline ~300k/hr; measured hop costs 850-1360s/hop (affine model bead sp-smbgd — use it for travel pricing). Probe supply ample: 676 probes, ~384 in sensor rotation, ~280+ surplus.

PART 1 — SENSING SURGE (extend probe_sensing coordinator): on reachable-graph growth (gate completions), enqueue new systems value-ranked and dispatch surplus parked probes IN PARALLEL (new knob: max in-flight expansion dispatches, e.g. default 8; existing API pacer + brake still govern; buying untouched behind the treasury floor). Replaces today's ~2 systems/hr sequential trickle.

PART 2 — OPPORTUNITY RELOCATOR (standing reconciler, ~15min tick, same actuator family as reposition_rate_floor with inverted trigger):
- OBSERVE: per-hull realized rate (EWMA over completed tours, TRANSACTION-based — not load-zero segments, see shared-cycle-rate-metric-hazard); fresh regional snapshots (system + 2-hop neighbors); hop distances.
- DERIVE per (hull, region): expected rate = planner-projected rate on the region's snapshot; RELOCATION NPV = uplift x min(remaining_era_hours - travel_h, horizon) - current_rate x travel_h - risk_margin; travel_h from the affine hop model.
- ACT: relocate top-NPV hull when NPV > threshold knob; caps: max_concurrent_relocations (2), anti-herd per region (reuse reposition_reach_max_hulls_per_system), per-hull cooldown, only at honest tour release, never mid-tour.
- FAIL CLOSED: stale/unreadable region excluded (per-activity age caps, reuse RankerAgeCaps); no relocation when remaining era < 2x travel + payback (endgame guard, ties to T-10h freeze).
- NO SPEND: moves hulls via existing ClaimShip occupancy/reposition primitives; RULINGS #7 pins respected; no money guard touched (RULINGS #4).
- Restart-safe per RULINGS #2 (persisted relocation intents; re-derive from live state on boot).

VALIDATION: replay-price candidate regions before first live relocation (widen-mode harness on the region snapshots); acceptance = first relocated hull's realized rate >= 1.2x its pre-move EWMA within 2 windows, transaction-based read. Calibration starting points: uplift bar 1.5x, risk_margin ~1 tour of earnings.

Both parts compose: surge produces the price data the relocator scores. Part 2 depends on Part 1 only for DEEP regions; near-band data exists already. Era clock: ~2 days left — if the lane cannot land safely this era, it is a next-era day-1 feature (NOT deferred-to-next-era as a backlog state: build now, value continues across resets since the coordinator re-derives from live data).
notes:
SPEC v2 (accepting shipwright retarget, st-wisp-gs8r2): Part 1 TRIGGER CHANGED to 'charted-but-unpriced systems, value-ranked' (1,067 of 1,183 charted systems have no market_data — under 10% priced); reachable-graph growth becomes one INPUT to the ranking, not the gating condition. In-flight cap + API pacer unchanged. Numbers refreshed: 1,215 in scope / 1,183 charted / 116 priced; 686 probes (~300 surplus); 26 trade hulls (14 heavy). CALIBRATION PROVENANCE (answering the sp-en5h7 transposition warning): ALL bead calibration inputs are transaction/timestamp-based, NOT price-history-based — heavies ~300k/hr from realized tour transactions; affine hop model (sp-smbgd) from leg realized_at wall-times (no prices); virgin ~2x is a PLAYBOOK realized-era prior (soft, marked as such); Replay A used pre-047 rows through the compensating mapping (verified correct orientation earlier tonight). Nothing on this bead was computed from transposed price history. HOP-MODEL CAP CAVEAT (their §5): measured on a 24h window that is ~85% cap-4-era crossings; per-hop cost is jump-cooldown + leg physics, cap-independent in mechanism — re-verify on accumulated cap-2 crossings before Part 2's first live relocation and refit if medians shift >15%. GO: build Part 1 with the retargeted trigger; Part 2 unchanged (their finding strengthens its premise — 90% of charted space unpriced means the envelope-moves-with-the-hull argument is stronger than v1 stated).
PART 1 GATED 2026-08-01 at main 6e06b6a2 (squash), on operator instruction that the 2026-07-31 halt is no longer in force.

Ships ARMED, verified rather than assumed. The only knob is surge_inflight_cap, an
operational cap whose zero value reverts to the documented default, so it cannot switch
the pass off. Dispatch sits behind 'if !cutoverPending', which is a PHASE condition and
not an arming seam — before the cutover a scout-tagged hull is not surplus and flying one
would take it out from under a live coordinator. The pool is CONSUMED, not merely
constructed: run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:1144 -> surgeToUnpricedSystems ->
probe_sensing_surge.go:120 ports.UnpricedPool.UnpricedSystems. This bead has shipped inert

MERGING MAIN EXPOSED AN IMPORT CYCLE that neither side had alone. main added
probe_sensing_yard_observability_test.go, which imports adapters/parkedsensing, while this

declarations to internal/domain/scouting (new surge_pool.go), where the adapter can reach

PART 2 (opportunity relocator) IS NOT DONE. This bead stays OPEN for it.
CORRECTION 2026-08-02 — MY OWN PRIOR NOTE ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. The line 'PART 2 (opportunity relocator) IS NOT DONE' that I appended on 2026-08-01 was written from this bead's own text without grepping main. PART 2 IS BUILT, WIRED AND ARMED.

It shipped 2026-07-30/31 under sp-e8d92 (P1, CLOSED) — a DIFFERENT bead — which is why this
one still reads as open work.

  internal/application/trading/commands/run_opportunity_relocator.go   1,093 lines
  internal/application/trading/commands/run_opportunity_relocator_stall.go
  internal/adapters/grpc/opportunity_relocator_ports.go

including SetStallObserver and SetMetricsSink. The skip map is keyed by reason and reported
to the heartbeat, not discarded.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS ON THIS BEAD IS MEASUREMENT, NOT CODE:
 1. The stated acceptance — first relocated hull's realized rate >= 1.2x its pre-move EWMA

 2. The HOP-MODEL CAP CAVEAT in the notes above — the affine hop model was fitted on a

title: Working-capital starvation by heavy capex: tour cycle rate collapsed ~5x (68->7-14/hr) starting 20:00Z — 4h BEFORE the cap change; treasury scraping 500-600k pins per-tour spend caps at ~125-150k vs the 400-800k a heavy fill needs
description: Found during sp-0hodc validation (economy-analyst, 2026-07-30 01:40Z). EVIDENCE: tour cycles/hr 68 (20:00Z) -> 34 -> 14 -> 7 (23:00Z), partial recovery to 13-14 post-restart; hourly MIN balance 912k (19Z) -> 1.4M (22Z) -> 500k (23Z) -> 546-594k (00-01Z); heavy spend 2.06M+4.15M+5.47M+1.72M+3.51M+1.79M per hour 19Z-01Z (~18.7M); probe buys correctly halted at the sensing buy floor since 21:00Z. MECHANISM: per-tour max_spend = 25% of LIVE treasury, so each heavy buy (executed at a burst peak, legally passing the 25%/floor guards) crashes the working capital every OTHER tour launches against — the buy guards protect the purchase, nothing protects operations' runway (the 50k anti-stall floor is ~1% of the fleet's ~6.75M/hr cargo spend rate). Spend-sensitivity replay already priced this: per-tour projected cph +29% at 2x budget (725k->1.45M). The sensing coordinator already solves this class for probes (capital_multiplier_k_milli = runway-aware floor); the autosizer has no equivalent, and sp-ftqgp's per-operation capital budget (construction vs trade) is the structural frame to extend to CAPEX vs trade. ASK: captain decision — throttle heavy buys until treasury sustains above ~1-2h of cargo runway, or accept degraded tour throughput while the fleet grows (era-clock calculus: heavies pay back ~7h; but cycle rate is down ~5x, so the externality currently dominates). Also POLLUTES the sp-0hodc validation: post-change tours run under half the pre-change working capital — expect the cap-2 realized numbers to underread until treasury recovers.
notes:
CAPTAIN DECISION (2026-07-30, orchestrator). Acted: heavy buying is now gated on the OBSERVED
WORKING-CAPITAL TROUGH -- no purchase unless MIN(balance_after) over the trailing 60 min is
>= 1.5M. It fires right now (trough 593,551), so buying is throttled until the trough recovers.
Self-correcting by construction: as the fleet grows, simultaneous open cargo positions grow, the
trough falls, and buying throttles itself with no constant to re-guess.

THE REAL DEFECT WAS MINE, AND NARROWER THAN THIS BEAD CLAIMS. My buy loop's 1.5M floor was a
PURCHASE-TIME check (cap = treasury - 1.5M); trading then spends straight through it, so 1.5M was
never actually standing. Verified hourly MIN(balance_after): 500,266 (23Z), 545,859 (00Z),
593,551 (01Z), 239,518 (17Z). The Admiral's order was "keep at least 1.5M working capital" and
the implementation did not deliver it. Fixed as above.

CONFIRMED HARM, and it is exactly 2 events -- not a 5x collapse:
  tour-run-TORWIND-2C1 20:40:52 -03  reserve_exceeds_budget (spend_cap=0: max_spend 0 - reserve 0)
  tour-run-TORWIND-27A 21:44:58 -03  same
Both "Re-plan produced no feasible tour - stopping". Plus 2 "Cumulative tour spend cap reached -
skipping buy". That is 4 capital-related events in 60,000 log lines.

MECHANISM REFUTED. This bead attributes the harm to per-tour max_spend = 25% of LIVE treasury
pinning tours at 125-150k. If that term were binding, cargo buy size would track treasury. It
does not -- average PURCHASE_CARGO is FLAT while treasury ranges 14x:

title: 12.5% of API attempts are retries on action endpoints, blocking fleet growth via the api_util ceiling
description:
Retries are 0.222 req/s against 1.556 req/s of useful requests -- 12.5% of all API attempts,
measured live 2026-07-30 over 45s from spacetraders_daemon_api_{requests,retries}_total.

This is not a metrics artifact. A retry is a real request to the server and does consume the
per-IP rate limit, so api_util is RIGHT to count attempts. The consequence is that retry noise
raises measured utilisation from 77.8% (requests) to 88.9% (attempts), which pushes it past the
autosizer's 85% ceiling and BLOCKS FLEET GROWTH. Reclaiming this budget is worth ~11 points of a
saturated ceiling -- the single largest headroom item now that topology fell to 2.2% (sp-zj19z).

Retries are concentrated on ACTION endpoints, not reads:
  Navigate 150+1, Refuel 46+40, Orbit 35, Dock 34, Sell Cargo 33, Jump 14

They are NOT 429s. The recent log shows logic-level conflicts:
  951  "in transit"
  300  "already at jump gate"
   47  "already at destination"
   15  "in transit from previous command"
    3  "Transient refuel failure"
plus explicit "Retrying after error in 5s (attempt 1)" / "in 30s (attempt 2)" backoff lines.

VERIFY THIS FIRST, IT IS THE CRUX: a log line saying "already at destination" does NOT prove an
API call was made -- it may be a local short-circuit that costs nothing. Before changing any
behaviour, establish for each conflict class whether it corresponds to a real outbound request.
The honest test is the retries counter, not the log text: instrument or correlate retry
increments per endpoint against these conflict messages. If they are local skips, this bead is
invalid and should be closed as such.

If they ARE real calls, the fix is to consult ship state before issuing an action that the
ship's current nav/dock state already satisfies -- and to not retry a command whose failure is a
terminal state conflict ("already at destination" will never succeed on retry) as opposed to a
transient error. Distinguish those two classes; retrying a terminal conflict is pure waste.

Do NOT weaken the api_util guard to work around this (RULINGS #4) -- the guard is reading the
truth. Fix the traffic, not the meter.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-07-30 (orchestrator, Admiral-approved). Filed on a burst, not a rate.

WHAT I FILED IT ON: a 45-second sample reading retries at 0.222 req/s against 1.556 req/s of
requests -- 12.5% of all attempts -- with the argument that api_util counts attempts (correctly,
since a retry does consume the per-IP limit) so retry noise pushes measured utilisation from 77.8%
to 88.9% and blocks fleet growth at the autosizer's 85% ceiling.

WHAT A LATER MEASUREMENT SHOWED: retries at 0.080 req/s -- about 4% of the 2.00 ceiling, and LOWER
than the 0.11 req/s baseline I had measured before that. Spread thin with no dominant offender:
Get Agent 33%, Sell Cargo 33%, Dock 17%, Refuel 17%, none of them a single fixable cause.

So the 12.5% was a burst caught in a short window, not a sustained rate. Same error I made four
other times in that session -- drawing a structural conclusion from a sub-two-minute sample of a
bursty metric. Anything claimed about API structure needs a window measured in tens of minutes.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE and is worth knowing if this is ever re-opened: retries ARE real API spend and
api_util is right to count them, so a genuine sustained retry rate would be worth attacking. The
observed causes were logic-level conflicts rather than 429s -- 951 "in transit", 300 "already at
jump gate", 47 "already at destination" in the log. But I never established whether those log lines
correspond to real outbound calls or to free local short-circuits, which was the crux the bead
itself named as needing verification first. That verification was never done, so there is no
evidence a fix would recover anything.

Re-file with a sustained measurement if retries are ever seen above ~10% of the ceiling over a
half-hour window.

title: [bug] detectStaleHeartbeats exempts a frozen IN_TRANSIT hull with no upper bound — a row stuck past its ETA is the exact death signal the check exists to catch, and nothing fired for 6.5h (PROTECTED PATH: captain/**)
description:
Found by the zombie-workflow lane (sp-l8p3z) and NOT fixed there. A watchdog exempts the exact condition
it exists to catch.

THE DEFECT: detectStaleHeartbeats (gobot/internal/captain/detectors.go, the sp-no9i exemption) exempts a
hull in nav_status IN_TRANSIT from the stale-heartbeat check, with NO staleness bound on the exemption.
The reasoning behind sp-no9i is sound in itself — a hull legitimately in transit is not reporting and
should not be flagged. But a row stuck IN_TRANSIT with an arrival_time HOURS IN THE PAST is precisely the
frozen-position death signal the detector exists to catch, and it exempts itself from detection.

OBSERVED: nothing fired for 6.5 HOURS against a frozen hull. The detector was silent for exactly as long
as the condition persisted, because the longer a hull is wrongly stuck IN_TRANSIT the more thoroughly it
is exempted. The failure mode is self-reinforcing.

FIX SHAPE (one predicate): exempt only while arrival_time has NOT yet passed, plus a grace margin for
clock skew and arrival-event lag. Past-ETA plus grace should fall through to the normal stale-heartbeat
path. Do NOT remove the sp-no9i exemption itself — an in-transit hull that is genuinely still travelling
must stay exempt; the bug is the missing upper bound, not the exemption.

** PROTECTED PATH — gobot/internal/captain/** IS OFF LIMITS TO BUILD AGENTS. ** This cannot be dispatched
to a standard build lane. It needs the Admiral or a lane explicitly authorised for the captain tree.
Flagging that here so nobody burns a dispatch discovering it.

RELATED CONTEXT: sp-b79f1 records two OTHER sources of misleading liveness data (ctx-cancel exits leaving
non-terminal rows; the heartbeat goroutine outliving an unrecoverable error, so FAILED rows carry
heartbeat_at up to 25 minutes AFTER stopped_at). A detector reading heartbeat freshness is downstream of
both. Fixing this predicate without fixing those leaves the detector reading data that still lies —
sequence accordingly.

Ship ARMED, no flag. Do not weaken the detector in the other direction: a false "hull is dead" is
cheaper than silence, but only just — this watchdog gates recovery actions.

title: [bug] ConstructionHasWork measures container LIVENESS, not work — an idle post-gate construction coordinator permanently fences off 40% of deployable capital from trade (~67% less buying power per tour)
description:
GOAL CONTEXT: Admiral directive is 10M/hr; we run ~3.2M/hr. This is a ZERO-SPEND lever that raises
trade's per-tour buying power by ~67% without buying a single hull.

THE DEFECT. common/capital_budget.go:189

    func (s *ContainerCapitalWorkSensor) ConstructionHasWork(ctx, playerID) (bool, error) {
        return s.hasActive(ctx, playerID, constructionCapitalContainerTypes)
    }

ConstructionHasWork does not measure WORK. It measures whether a construction container is RUNNING.
The caller (run_tour_coordinator.go:2522-2533) feeds it straight into
common.CapitalSplit(TradeCapitalSharePct, deployable, true, constructionHasWork) to decide how much
capital trade may deploy this cycle. So "a construction container is alive" is treated as
"construction needs money".

LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-07-29, era 5, player 5). The jump gate was COMPLETED earlier this session
(1600/1600). The construction coordinator nonetheless stays RUNNING and, every 30 seconds, logs:

    [construction_coordinator-player-5-66501d72] Construction drain: activating construction tasks
    [construction_coordinator-player-5-66501d72] Construction drain: activation done (0 task(s) promoted to READY)

Zero tasks promoted, tick after tick, for hours. Meanwhile every tour logs:

    Capital budget: trade's share is 679631 of 1132719 deployable (construction live=true, share 60%)
      - above the 358179 max-spend, so the dynamic cap binds

So trade is capped at 60% of deployable capital and the reserved 40% funds nothing. With construction
genuinely idle, trade's share should be 100%: max-spend ~358k -> ~597k per tour, a ~67% increase in
per-tour buying power. That converts directly into throughput, because the fleet is cycle-bound and
each tour is buying less than it could (see sp-k7hez).

WHY THIS IS SUBTLE AND MUST NOT BE FIXED NAIVELY. The current shape is deliberately fail-conservative:
hasActive returns TRUE when no reader is wired, and the caller defaults constructionHasWork=true when
sensing errors, precisely so a blind read never hands one engine 100% of the treasury. That property
is CORRECT and must survive. The bug is narrower: a container that is alive but has demonstrably
nothing queued should not count as demand.

DO NOT simply return false when the last tick promoted 0 tasks. A construction coordinator between
ticks, or one whose tasks are queued but not yet READY, legitimately needs capital reserved. Promotion
count is a symptom, not the demand signal. The sensor needs a real pending-demand read (outstanding
construction tasks / unmet material requirements), with the fail-conservative default intact on any
error or unwired reader.

ASK:
 (a) Establish what the honest demand signal is for the construction side — outstanding tasks, unmet
     material requirements, an active supply drain with a target — and read THAT, not container
     liveness. Same question for TradeHasWork, which has the identical shape and the identical latent
     bug in the mirror direction.
 (b) Keep every fail-conservative property: unwired reader -> true; sensing error -> caller keeps its
     proportional share; never hand one engine 100% on a blind or failed read (RULINGS #4).
 (c) Rename or re-document so the name stops lying. If it measures liveness it must not be called
     HasWork; if it measures work it must actually read demand.
 (d) Prove it both ways: with construction genuinely idle, trade gets 100%; with construction holding
     real pending demand, trade is held to its share EVEN IF no task was promoted on the last tick.
     That second test is the one that stops the naive fix.

MERGED to main as ed01e652 (gate green: full suite, Merged=true, EmptyMerge=false). DEPLOYED and VERIFIED
LIVE 2026-07-29 03:49 local: "Capital budget: trade's share is 3843666 of 3843666 deployable
(construction live=false)" — trade now takes 100% instead of 60%, and per-tour max-spend rose from
358,179 to 1,035,916. A 2.9x increase in buying power for zero credits.

pipelines is what excludes exactly that wreckage — not incidental.

material target is not yet delivered, read from the pipeline row (restart-safe, immune to activation
timing). Promotion counts are NEVER consulted — the new reader has no access to the task repository at
all, which is the structural guarantee against the naive fix I warned about.

with the CONTAINER reader unwired (blind) but the demand reader wired and reporting nothing outstanding,
the sensor released the reservation — a blind liveness read was being overridden by a successful bill
read. Fixed so a blind liveness read SHORT-CIRCUITS and never consults the bill ("an unwired reader is a

consulted; unwired bill reader -> true (the pre-fix answer); either read error -> surfaced, caller keeps

line item -> demand; STOPPED drain -> false. ONLY a positive "live AND nothing outstanding" releases.
RULINGS #4 intact.

this bead is about; it is no longer container-backed on both sides). ConstructionHasWork now genuinely
means has work.

PROVED BOTH WAYS through the real CapitalSplit so assertions are in CREDITS, not booleans, at the live
deployable=1132719: live drain + FILLED bill -> trade 1132719 / construction 0; live drain + OUTSTANDING
bill with ZERO promotions -> trade 679631 / construction 453088 (the anti-naive-fix test); STOPPED drain

they are TRAVELLING TO SELL. Throughput is therefore bound by buy->sell cycle time. A 16th hull cannot
raise throughput while the existing 15 are mid-cycle; it can only deepen inventory pressure.

Evidence 3 — a concrete, fixable driver of that cycle time. The tour solver logs, continuously:
  "Tour hop matrix could not prove N of M system crossing(s) over stored gate topology;
   each unproven crossing is charged 7 gate hops rather than its true distance"
Frequency over one log window (occurrences x ratio):
    86x  6 of 21 unproven  (29%)
    74x 11 of 66           (17%)
    52x  9 of 45           (20%)
    45x 15 of 36           (42%)
    17x  7 of 28           (25%)
     3x 17 of 45           (38%)
Up to 42% of crossings in a tour are unprovable, and each is priced at 7 gate hops instead of its true
distance. That is a systematic OVER-estimate of distance, so the solver routes around sinks that are
actually near, and picks longer circuits than the map would justify. Shorter proven routes = faster
cycles = more $/hr from the SAME hulls and the SAME capital.

Current topology: 6,278 gate edges across 1,400 systems, 504 under construction.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE ITEM FOR 10M/HR: it needs no credits. Every other lever (more heavies,
more lights) is gated by capital AND blocked by the inventory-pressure guard until cycle time improves.
Cutting the unproven-crossing rate converts directly into throughput on hulls we already own.

ASK (investigation first, do not jump to a fix):
 (a) Quantify the penalty: measure realised tour cycle time against unproven-crossing ratio. Establish
     how much of the 7-hop charge is real cost versus estimation error.
 (b) Establish WHY crossings are unprovable. 504 edges are under_construction; are the unproven ones
     genuinely unknown, merely stale, or known-but-unreadable? The three need different fixes.
 (c) Check whether the freshly-deployed parked-sensing gate reads (a718172a, 0562eb35 - deployed
     2026-07-29 01:51) are already closing this. If coverage is climbing on its own, the fix may be to
     PRIORITISE gate reads for systems that appear in tour hop matrices, not to add new machinery.
 (d) Only then consider the 7-hop constant itself. It is a fail-safe over-estimate; changing it is a
     routing-economics change and must not silently authorise long unprofitable hauls.

Do NOT weaken the inventory-pressure guard - it is the symptom reporter, not the disease.
Ship ARMED, no flag (Admiral standing order).
notes:
CLOSED — MY DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. The 7-hop charge is NOT an estimation error and must NOT be changed.
Investigation lane built nothing; branch clean at 84cea2df. Recommendation: NO CHANGE to the constant.

WHAT THE CHARGE ACTUALLY IS: the solver correctly refusing to price a route to a system whose jump gate
DOES NOT EXIST YET. Lowering it would authorise hauls the executor cannot fly — cross-system travel for
tours is gate-only, there is no warp path. If anything 7 is too lenient; true cost is unbounded until
construction completes.

MY PREMISE WAS WRONG THREE WAYS:
1. "6,278 edges / 1,400 systems / 504 under_construction" is the ALL-ERA table. Adjacency is era-scoped
   and era 5 opened at the 2026-07-26 universe reset. Live era-5 topology is 1,239 edges / 275 systems /
   96 under construction. Eras 2-4 (~5,200 edges) are dead universes, correctly invisible.
2. "Up to 42% of crossings unprovable" is really "ONE unreachable system among nine". An isolated system
   makes ALL of its pairs unprovable at once. 720 of 789 production log rows (91%) fit k(n-k)+C(k,2)
   exactly for k=1..3 isolated systems; in ~80% of plans exactly ONE system is isolated. Replaying REAL
   allowedSystems from the pre-positioning log over the era-5 store reproduced production EXACTLY
   (n=7->6 unproven, n=8->7, n=9->15, n=10->9, n=12->11).
3. The unproven crossings are none of my three buckets (unknown / stale / unreadable). A fourth: KNOWN,
   FRESH, and CORRECTLY REFUSED. Culprits X1-KK40, X1-PQ84, X1-PT70, X1-RR42 each have EVERY inbound
   edge flagged under_construction — unanimous across 5, 4, 3 and 2 independent neighbour reads — zero
   outbound edges (you cannot read a gate you cannot reach), all re-read AFTER the 01:51 deploy.

CYCLE TIME IS NOT THE CAP EITHER. Cycle time does scale with distinct systems (p50: 2 sys 43 min, 3->98,
4->167, 5->185; ~55 min per added system, matching the solver's own 1800s/crossing). But credits per
hull-hour is FLAT-TO-RISING in tour length: 78k (2 sys), 72k (3), 83k (4), 127k (5). Longer tours are
mildly MORE efficient, not less. The charge also never SELECTS: of 26 systems reachable only behind an
unbuilt gate, NONE was visited by any tour in 18h; all 25 visited systems are in the built graph. The
matrix is live, not dormant (tour_solver.py:613,642) — 7 hops x 1800s = 3.5h is simply decisive.

SELF-HEALING ANSWERED: coverage IS climbing (era-5 grew 1,154->1,239 edges and 257->275 systems in ~1
hour) but the unproven RATIO is flat post-deploy (23.8, 28.4, 19.5, 19.3, 21.1, 23.4% by hour). More
reading cannot close the gap because the gates are UNBUILT. Prioritising gate reads for systems in tour
hop matrices would spend budget for no gain — explicitly do not do this.

THE REAL BOTTLENECK IS UTILISATION -> filed as its own bead. Over 24h with 15 hulls, 360 hull-hours were
available and only ~177 were inside a trading tour. 262 of 331 tour containers (79%) EXITED AFTER ~1.5
MINUTES HAVING TRADED NOTHING.

Lane's honest limit, recorded: per-set reproduction is exact, but the WEIGHTED aggregate came to 12.8%
vs production ~21%, because sampled allowed-sets come only from plans that emit the pre-positioning log.
The aggregate is a lower bound; the mechanism is not in doubt.

ALSO SURFACED, NOT ACTED ON (own bead): parked_sensing_gate_walk_unroutable fired 207 times in 12h —
"no gate route could be named within 0 JUMPS of stored adjacency", a ZERO bound. Hulls TORWIND-E6/EE/FD
held and retried 54/52/50 times each.

oneHopTourSystems (run_tour_coordinator.go:2407) builds from neighborSystems -> GetJumpGateConnectionsQuery
-> apiClient.GetJumpGate, which returns raw live connections carrying NO construction state, while
gategraph/service.go storedDistances correctly skips e.UnderConstruction. So the tour graph ADMITS systems
the executor cannot reach. Fixing it is correct but NOT free — it means switching off the live
neighborSystems to a construction-aware source, changing failure modes (fail-open-to-nil vs live list) on
the DEFAULT path. It is cleanliness and risk-removal, NOT a throughput fix; it will not move 3.2M/hr.

title: [bug] Cargo-count desync fails the whole tour and strands the hull: 4219 states the true count (11 vs 71) and we neither clamp nor resync
description:
A tour sell aborts entirely - and kills the tour, stranding a fully loaded hull - when the daemon's local
cargo count for a good is ahead of the server's, even though the API response states the true count.

MEASURED (containers table, player 5):
  tour-run-TORWIND-D7-8f9d3fa8 FAILED exit 1:
    sell of 71 MACHINERY at X1-BT49-EX4F failed: partial failure: failed to sell cargo after
    0 successful transactions (0 units processed, 0 credits): API error (status 400)
    code 4219 "Ship TORWIND-D7 cargo does not contain 71 unit(s) of MACHINERY. Ship has 11 unit(s)."
    data = {"shipSymbol":"TORWIND-D7","tradeSymbol":"MACHINERY","cargoUnits":11,"unitsToRemove":71}

Two separate defects stacked:

1. DESYNC: we believed 71 units, server had 11 - a 60-unit gap. Root cause unknown; establish whether
   this is a lost-response double-count (see the sp-y2u4j family: lost BuyCargo/SellCargo responses),
   a partial sell whose local decrement never applied, or transfer/jettison not reflected locally.

2. NO RECONCILE ON REJECTION (the cheap, high-value half): the payload carries data.cargoUnits = 11,
   i.e. the server tells us exactly what is aboard. We neither clamp the sell to 11 and retry, nor
   resync cargo from the response. We abort at 0 transactions and fail the whole tour.

Consequence: the hull is released loaded (80 units, ~241,973 est. value on D7) and that hold then gets
dumped below the profit floor. This is a direct, measurable contributor to the below-floor liquidations,
and it is the SAME root pattern as sp-1xxw2 - authoritative correction arrives in the error body and is
discarded.

FIX SHAPE (build agent to confirm against the code):
 (a) On 4219, resync that good's units from data.cargoUnits, clamp the sell to min(planned, actual),
     and retry ONCE. A 71->11 clamp still books 11 units of revenue instead of zero.
 (b) Only if the clamped retry also fails should the leg fail.
 (c) Investigate and fix the underlying 60-unit drift separately; (a) and (b) are the containment and
     are worth shipping on their own.
 (d) Guard: never clamp UPWARD from the server value; the server count is authoritative and this must
     not become a path to selling units we do not hold.

Money-touching: keep the existing guards intact, fail closed on ambiguity (RULINGS #4).
Ship ARMED, no flag (Admiral standing order).
notes:
MERGED to main as 03d5ece3 (gate green: full suite, Merged=true, EmptyMerge=false, Dirty=false).
Rebased onto main first — the first gate returned GatePassed=true but Stale=true/Merged=false.

Landed in CargoTransactionHandler.executeTransactions, the single choke point every sell funnels
through — so arb, circuit, liquidation and manufacturing sells get the containment too, not just tours.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE 60-UNIT DRIFT FOUND AND FIXED (no follow-up bead needed): a multi-tranche sell whose
later tranche failed returned at the error line BEFORE the SaveWithRetry cargo persist, which sat after
the loop. Units earlier tranches really sold were written to the ledger but never removed from the hold,
so the cached count stayed permanently ahead of the server by exactly that amount. That is how a hull
comes to believe it holds 71 units it sold long ago. NOT a lost-response double-count, NOT transfer or
jettison. Fixed by extracting persistCargoDelta and calling it on the failure path too.

Second half: on a 4219 the cache is resynced ABSOLUTELY to server truth, not decremented by what sold —
applying -11 to a phantom 71 would leave 60 phantom units and re-arm the identical rejection next leg.
Downward only; the server count can shrink a phantom hold, never inflate one (RULINGS #4).

Fails closed on every ambiguity: payload naming a different good, absent cargoUnits (pointer, so absent
!= 0), non-4219 code, or a count at/above the planned size (self-contradictory -> distrusted entirely,
no retry). Purchases untouched. Ledger pinned to book only units actually sold.

9 mutation probes, all killed, zero survivors, each by the predicted tests. M6 initially SURVIVED —
the fail-closed tests asserted "no retry sent" but not "cache untouched", and an absent-reads-as-zero
parse silently wipes the hold without a stray call; fixed by adding held-count assertions. M9 replaced
the parser with construction's strings.Contains(err,"4219") and was killed by
TestIsCargoShortfall_DoesNotMatchIncidentalDigits — concrete evidence the shared classifier is stronger
than the incumbent, which would match a ship symbol SHIP-4219 or waypoint X1-BT49-4219.

MY BRIEFING TO THE LANE WAS WRONG on two of three prior-art pointers and the lane caught it by READING
them: cargo_manager.go:37 is a bare SyncShipFromAPI wrapper, not a 4219 reconcile (4219 appears only in
its doc comment as motivation); deliver_contract_terms_met.go DOES NOT EXIST — those 4219s are test-only
fixtures using it as a sample generic error. I inferred handlers from grep hits without opening them.
Lesson is the standing one: behaviour lives in what a file dispatches, not in what greps near it.

Classifier now shared at internal/domain/ports/cargo_shortfall.go beside APIError. Construction and
contract deliberately NOT rewired onto it — a behaviour change to other money paths, wrong to fold into
a P1 sell fix unasked. IsCargoShortfall exists unconsumed as the landing spot for that lane.

title: [bug] Router replans the SAME impossible jump: 4255 rejections carry authoritative data.connections and we discard them (5 tour kills/6h)
description:
Five tour-run containers died in 6 hours (TORWIND-41 x4, TORWIND-61 x1) because the router plans a jump
against a stale/incorrect jump-gate connection graph, and then DISCARDS the ground truth the API hands
back in the rejection.

MEASURED (containers table, player 5, 6h window):
  tour-run-TORWIND-41-e13a3217  jump to X1-AJ10-F24Z  -> 4255
  tour-run-TORWIND-41-ce06792c  jump to X1-AJ10-F24Z  -> 4255   (identical)
  tour-run-TORWIND-41-f748df7b  jump to X1-AJ10-F24Z  -> 4255   (identical)
  tour-run-TORWIND-41-48a6c68a  jump to X1-KP23-I53   -> 4255
  tour-run-TORWIND-61-22653242  no gate connection X1-BS29-A21D -> X1-UB61 after 3 live reads

The API error payload is explicit and actionable:
  code 4255 "Failed to execute jump. Waypoint X1-AJ10-F24Z is not connected to the current location."
  data.connections = ["X1-VV36-I60","X1-RX9-XZ2B","X1-GF41-I56"]

So the server TELLS US the true adjacency set in data.connections. We throw it away, leave the stale graph
in place, and the next tour replans the SAME impossible jump. Three of TORWIND-41's four deaths are the
identical origin+destination pair. This is a self-sustaining retry loop that kills a whole tour each time.

Cost: TORWIND-41 shows -81,830 realized over 3h, entirely attributable to repeated reposition failure
after cargo was already bought. Each death also strands a loaded hull, which then eats a below-floor
distress dump.

FIX SHAPE (build agent to confirm against the code):
 (a) On 4255, parse data.connections and RECONCILE the stored gate graph for that origin gate - the
     response is authoritative adjacency, better than any cached read.
 (b) Having reconciled, replan against the corrected graph rather than retrying the rejected jump.
 (c) Never re-emit an origin->destination jump already rejected as unconnected within the same
     reconcile generation. The identical-retry loop is the amplifier.
 (d) TORWIND-61's variant ("no jump gate connection ... after 3 live reads") shows the read path can
     already conclude no-connection - make that conclusion WRITE BACK to the graph too.

"fix(nav): re-anchor the hull on the server's truth when a jump is refused as not-connected
(sp-fwk8z follow-up)", committed 2026-07-28 23:39:07.

MY FILED HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, and the real cause is worth recording. I diagnosed a stale

it holds GF41->AJ10 = X1-AJ10-F24Z and GF41->KP23 = X1-KP23-I53, precisely the two waypoints the
API refused. Candidate ranking, BFS and gate-waypoint resolution were all faithfully correct from

The shipped fix: SyncShipFromAPI on a 4255, written through to the durable row the next tick

title: expansion_enabled=off idles 300+ owned probes — stops free placement, not just spending
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-29, on discovering that turning expansion off idled 300+ paid-for probes: "Expansion off = dont buy any probe, keep sensing with the existing ones. So turning expansion off without buying any probe should not change market coverage."

That is the intent. It is not the behaviour.

== THE DEFECT ==
The sensing coordinator's expansion_enabled knob (1=on, 2=off) is too coarse. Its own help text:
  "Off stops frontier propagation, charting seeds and seed requests; already-placed probes keep scanning."

So OFF stops opening NEW PLACEMENTS entirely. Probes already parked keep scanning their current market, but IDLE probes we already own are never dispatched anywhere new. Coverage growth stalls even though the capacity to grow it is already bought and sitting idle.

Credit cost of dispatching an idle owned probe to an unpriced market is ZERO. Commit d94262b8 ("dispatch idle orphan probes we already own to open placements (zero credits)") exists precisely to do this. The master switch disables it anyway.

== MEASURED ==
Fleet census at time of filing: 314 SATELLITE hulls, of which 308 idle in sensing_parked.
New systems priced per hour, against the expansion window:
  01:00 ->  1   (expansion turned OFF at 01:18)
  02:00 ->  1   OFF
  03:00 ->  5   OFF
  04:00 -> 20   (turned back ON at 04:20)
7 systems across three hours off, versus 20 in the first hour back on - roughly 8x suppression, while 300+ idle probes sat unused the entire time. Market coverage at the low point was 293 of 1238 known markets (24%), with 945 dark.

== WHY THE CONFLATION IS WRONG ==
Two separable concerns are welded together:
  1. SPENDING - buying new probe hulls. Already gated independently by capex_reserve_credits (plus the immutable 50k and the capital_multiplier runway term). That is the money guard and it works.
  2. PLACEMENT - dispatching hulls we ALREADY OWN to unpriced markets. Costs nothing.
An operator turning expansion off is nearly always trying to stop (1). There is no reason it should stop (2), and stopping (2) wastes an asset already paid for.

== FIX DIRECTION (verify before building) ==
Preferred: with expansion off, CONTINUE dispatching idle owned probes into KNOWN-BUT-UNPRICED markets, and stop only the credit-spending path plus true frontier growth (charting into undiscovered territory, seed requests that imply buying).

That distinction may or may not be clean in the code - "frontier propagation" might be what discovers the unpriced markets in the first place, in which case harvesting known-unpriced needs its own path. DETERMINE WHICH before changing anything and tell me. If the two genuinely cannot be separated, say so and propose the alternative (e.g. a third state, or documenting that the buy floor alone is the correct way to stop spending).

Whatever shape it takes, the operator-visible outcome must be: "stop spending" and "stop growing coverage with hulls I already own" become independently controllable.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Ship ARMED, no feature flag (standing Admiral order).
- RULINGS #4: do not weaken any money guard. This must not create a path that spends credits while expansion is off. Placement of owned hulls only.
- The knob's help text must be updated to match the new semantics - the current text is how the behaviour was discovered, and a stale description is its own defect.
- Protected paths untouched: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**.

== VERIFY ==
A regression test that fails on today's code: with expansion off and idle owned probes available, an unpriced known market still receives a placement. Mutation-probe it. Confirm no credit-spending path is reachable while off.
notes: MERGED to main as 2e045e21 (gate green: full suite, EmptyMerge=false, Dirty=false). Lane SHA was 13fc805b, 17 files +561/-54. Shipped ARMED per Admiral standing order. Key correction from the lane, worth keeping: the bead's proposed fix was a NO-OP — dispatchIdleOrphans never read cfg.Expansion; the real stall was one function upstream, AdvanceExpansion returning before markFrontier. The pause now sits INSIDE AdvanceExpansion: markFrontier + readUnmappedGates always run (both free); advanceSeeds/claimSpares/requestSeeds/advanceOffGate sit below it. title: tour_leg_telemetry drops ~25% of SELL legs — galaxy view under-draws lanes
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-28: "the galaxy view doesnt seem to be showing every lane". Investigated; they are right, and this is a SECOND defect distinct from sp-2uvec (which fixed the live-flows feed, a different endpoint and a different data path).

== THE DEFECT ==
tour_leg_telemetry records BUY legs reliably and SELL legs unreliably. Roughly a quarter of realized sell legs never get a row.

Measured against the ledger (transactions, operation_type=tour) as ground truth, same instant, four windows:

  window | telemetry buys | ledger buys | telemetry sells | ledger sells | missing sells
  -------+----------------+-------------+-----------------+--------------+--------------
    3h   |       75       |     75  OK  |       53        |      70      |  17  (24%)
    6h   |      143       |    143  OK  |       89        |     126      |  37  (29%)
   12h   |      229       |    229  OK  |      137        |     192      |  55  (29%)
   24h   |      256       |    256  OK  |      163        |     218      |  55  (25%)

BUY counts match the ledger EXACTLY in every window. SELL counts are short by 24-29% in every window. That asymmetry is the whole signal: whatever writes telemetry runs dependably on the buy path and not on the sell path.

== WHY IT MATTERS ==
The visualizer galaxy view renders LANES from this table. visualizer/server/routes/flows.ts, the /flows/lanes handler:
    SELECT tour_id, ship_symbol, leg_index, waypoint, is_buy, ...
      FROM tour_leg_telemetry
     WHERE realized_at IS NOT NULL AND realized_at >= $1
(plus a second source, arbitrage_execution_logs, for arb runs.)

Live lane counts at the time of filing: window=1h -> 9 lanes, 6h -> 29, 24h -> 54. Every one of those is computed from an input missing a quarter of its sell legs, so the galaxy view silently under-draws trade activity. A sell leg with no telemetry row is a lane that never appears.

It also corrupts anything else reading this table for realized-vs-planned analysis (price drift, plan accuracy), since the sample is biased toward buys.

== WHAT THIS IS NOT ==
NOT sp-2uvec (merged 58ddc03a). That fixed the daemon /api/flows live feed, which is fed by an in-process registry and serves CURRENT tours. This is the historical leg-telemetry table feeding /flows/lanes. Different endpoint, different table, different write path. Do not assume the sp-2uvec fix touches this.

== INVESTIGATION DIRECTION ==
- Find every writer of tour_leg_telemetry and compare the buy-leg path to the sell-leg path. The buy path is the reference implementation: it is provably complete.
- Prime suspicion: the sell-side write is conditional, or sits after an early return / error path / partial-fill branch that the buy side does not have. Look for sells that are split across multiple transactions (trade_volume tranching) and whether telemetry writes once per leg while the ledger writes once per tranche - that could account for a systematic ratio rather than random loss. NOTE: if that is the cause, the ledger/telemetry counts are measuring different units and the fix may be to reconcile the comparison rather than to add rows. Determine which before changing anything, and say so.
- Reconcile a specific missing sell end-to-end: pick a SELL_CARGO transaction with no matching telemetry row and trace why the write did not happen.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Ship ARMED, no feature flag (standing Admiral order).
- RULINGS #4: telemetry is pure observation - it must never gate or alter a trade decision. A recording miss must stay a recording miss.
- Protected paths untouched: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**.
- Another session is merging sensing/exploration work; stay out of internal/application/scouting/** unless genuinely required.

title: Daemon /api/flows publishes only 5 of 13 running tours — visualizer shows 38% of the trade fleet
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-28: noticed the visualizer showing only a handful of active tours while the fleet was running 13.

== THE DEFECT IS IN THE DAEMON, NOT THE VISUALIZER ==
Traced the whole chain; the visualizer renders faithfully what it is handed.

  UI  TradeFlowsView -> useFlowsPolling -> GET /api/flows/live
  visualizer/server/routes/flows.ts:264  fetchDaemonFlows()
  visualizer/server/routes/flows.ts:232  DAEMON_FLOWS_URL = http://localhost:9090/api/flows

  daemon GET :9090/api/flows                                              ->  5 flows
  spacetraders container list | grep TRADING RUNNING                       -> 13
  SELECT count(*) FROM containers WHERE container_type=TRADING AND status=RUNNING -> 13
  SELECT count(*) FROM ships WHERE assignment_status=active AND container_id LIKE tour-run-% -> 13

So three independent sources agree on 13 and the flow feed says 5. All five reported are program=tour, closed=false.

== WHO IS MISSING ==
  REPORTED (5): TORWIND-5F, TORWIND-6, TORWIND-A, TORWIND-B, TORWIND-C
  MISSING  (8): TORWIND-9, TORWIND-40, TORWIND-41, TORWIND-60, TORWIND-61, TORWIND-D6, TORWIND-D7, TORWIND-D8

Every missing hull except TORWIND-9 was acquired LATE in the era: 40/41 bought by the captain at X1-KP23-A2, D6/D7/D8 bought by the captain at X1-PH94-A2 (all five via , atomic buy+dedicate), 60/61 acquired by the fleet machinery. The five that ARE reported are the original trade hulls.

HYPOTHESIS (inference from membership only — NOT verified, do not trust it): the flow feed is populated at some registration/adoption point that hulls joining the trade fleet later never pass through, rather than being derived from live container state each request. TORWIND-9 is an ORIGINAL hull and is missing, which does NOT fit that theory cleanly — so the pattern is suggestive, not conclusive. Start from the publishing code, not from this paragraph.

== WHY IT MATTERS ==
The flows feed is the visualizer's entire model of trade activity. At 5/13 it under-reports the fleet by 62%, so the Trade Flows tab, the tour roster, and anything downstream silently misrepresent what the bot is doing. An operator watching it would conclude trade had collapsed while it was in fact running 13 tours and netting ~+900k/30min. Two of the five reported flows have currentLeg=null, so the feed is not gating on having an in-flight leg either.

== INVESTIGATION DIRECTION ==
- Find the daemon handler behind GET /api/flows (port 9090) and determine how it enumerates flows. Is it reading live container state, or an in-memory registry populated on some event?
- If it is an in-memory registry: what writes to it, and which code path do late-joining hulls miss? Note the daemon restarts during this era (04:54, 21:33) — an in-memory registry that is not rebuilt on restart is a strong candidate, and would ALSO explain TORWIND-9 (present before a restart, never re-registered after). That single mechanism fits all 8 misses; verify it before adopting it.

- Correct behaviour: the feed must reflect every RUNNING tour container at request time. A hull acquired mid-era, or a daemon restart, must not drop a live tour from the feed.

sp-8zhit (merged, aa0c2577) had the same shape:  was an in-memory map on a daemon-lifetime singleton, so a restart between buy and exit emptied it and hulls were released still loaded. If this is another daemon-lifetime in-memory structure that restarts do not rebuild, it is the same class of bug and the fix should consider whether other such registries exist.

title: Per-hull tour rate has no outlier protection: a near-zero span yields 836M/hr
description:
FOUND by the beta-rate lane 2026-07-28 while measuring, NOT touched (formula territory).

A live tour reports 836,660,303/hr computed off a near-zero wall-clock span. MedianTourRate (beta) survives it because the median is robust to a single outlier. The PER-HULL rate at run_tour_coordinator_rate_floor.go:278 has NO such protection when a hull has only one tour in the window — the outlier IS the hull's rate.

Consumers: the under-earner RELOCATION trigger. A hull whose single in-window tour has a degenerate span reads as astronomically productive and can never be flagged for relocation; the mirror case (a near-zero span on a loss) would flag it permanently.

Needs a minimum-span floor or an outlier guard in the rate computation. That is FORMULA territory — it changes what the number means, not just its input — so it needs its own lane and its own measurement, not a threshold bump.

Related and already shipped: 657c00f1 (matched nets for ComputeFleetTourRate) and 8a6a3e3c (same for beta). Both corrected the INPUT; neither touched the span/formula.

ALSO RECORDED, process hazard from the same lane: a mutation probe was contaminated by a timed-out earlier run that left a mutation applied. A COMPOUND MUTATION READS EXACTLY LIKE A PASSING ONE. Always verify the working tree is clean before probing, and diff after restoring.

title: [bug] Double ownership: a hull is assigned_hull on TWO scout posts while parked at a third waypoint
description:
Spotted while building the foothold surplus guard (40ad9cb7). Not caused by sensing — it looks like a defect in the scout-post engine.

OBSERVED LIVE: TORWIND-2 is named as assigned_hull on TWO scout_posts simultaneously, while its sensing_slots row has it PARKED at a THIRD waypoint. One physical hull, three claims.

WHY IT MATTERS: the foothold surplus predicate correctly refuses any hull named by a scout post (ScoutPost.MannedHulls, including extra slots), so it is SAFE against this today — it simply protects the hull. But the underlying double-ownership means:
 - scout-post coverage accounting is overstated: two posts believe they are manned by a hull that is physically at neither.
 - any engine that trusts assigned_hull to mean 'this hull is here' can act on a stale location.
 - a post whose hull silently left is not re-manned, because it still reads as manned.

WHY IT IS NOT THE SENSING ENGINE'S BUG: sensing owns sensing_slots and its rows are consistent (one hull, one slot, and the widened key now enforces one row per waypoint PER KIND). The duplication is between scout_posts rows.

SUGGESTED: enumerate the class before fixing — SELECT assigned_hull, COUNT(*) FROM scout_posts WHERE assigned_hull IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 — and check whether release-on-repurpose is missing, or whether two posts can be declared for the same coverage target. The scout stack is LIVE cold-start infrastructure (boot-standing, sp-9ujl; bootstrap-declared, sp-pt7d), so this is not dead code and a wrong hull count there degrades cold start on the next era.

title: [bug] reuseSpareHull shares the on-errand blind spot — can re-task a charting seed to a market placement
description:
Sibling of the seed duplicate-claim fix (84a7eee1). WORSE than the one just fixed.

buyqueue.go:789 reuseSpareHull selects a PARKED SPARE with an assigned ship and re-tasks it to fill a market placement. Like newSlotBook before its fix, it never reads seed_ship — so it can grab a hull that is mid-charting-errand and redirect it to a market slot, abandoning the charting mission silently.

WHY WORSE: the fixed bug produced phantom DISPATCHED rows (throughput loss, money-safe over-count). This one physically re-tasks a working seed, so a system being charted simply stops being charted and the ledger still believes a seed is out there.

WHY NOT FIXED IN 84a7eee1: BuyLedger does not read Systems(), so teaching it about seed state is an interface change with real conflict surface across the buy path. Deliberately deferred rather than bolted on next to a money guard.

RELATED, and probably the better fix for both: the probe ADOPTION pass (scouting/commands/probe_sensing_adoption.go:275) is what CREATES the resurrected SPARE rows in the first place — it indexes hulls by sensing_slots rows only and never reads seed_ship, so a claimed-but-not-yet-departed hull is re-adopted as a spare every tick. 84a7eee1 filtered the consumer (newSlotBook); closing it at the source would fix every consumer at once, including this one.

RECOMMEND: fix adoption at source, then re-evaluate whether the consumer-side guards are still needed or can be simplified.

title: Cross-gate placement is refused, not flown — 66 of 74 sensing placements are a gate away and unreachable
description:
Follow-up from sp-uwxwo (tick-starvation fix, 28381c82).

STATE: RouteAcross in the sensing MoverPort now REFUSES with a WARNING instead of blocking the tick. That was the right call for liveness — it is verified unreachable from all four IN_TRANSIT writers today, since each picks a hull in the slot's own system by construction, and refusing keeps the hull so the probe cap over-counts (money-safe, RULINGS #4).

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: of the 74 open sensing placements on era 5, only 8 are in the home system X1-KP23. The other 66 are one or more gates away and currently cannot be served at all — not by the orphan-dispatch path (deliberately same-system, using the predicate flyToSlot uses to choose NavigateWithin over RouteAcross), and not by RouteAcross now that it refuses.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a ledger-driven gate walk — dispatch a hull one hop per tick, persisting progress in the slot row the way SeedCommander already does for charting seeds, so no tick ever waits on a multi-jump route or a jump cooldown. RouteShipCommand blocks worse than NavigateRouteCommand did (multi-jump plus cooldown waits), so simply un-refusing it would reintroduce sp-uwxwo in a more severe form.

DESIGN NOTE: SeedCommander is the working precedent — 'A seed charts its target's waypoints one per tick and, when the system is charted through, is stood down.' The same shape applies to crossing gates: one hop per tick, state in the ledger, nothing held between ticks.

BLOCKS: full market coverage beyond the home system, which is the substrate for the owner's goal of scaling trading income.

title: Tours release hulls still holding unsold cargo — one was parked ON its own sink with 82,820 aboard
description:

== OBSERVED, two hulls simultaneously ==
  TORWIND-A  IN_ORBIT @X1-KP23-D41  20 MICROPROCESSORS  assignment=idle  container=NULL
  TORWIND-9  IN_ORBIT @X1-KP23-I53   9 CLOTHING          assignment=idle  container=NULL

title: sp-zve2q single-hull stickiness overrides source proximity unconditionally, even for a partial load
description:
ADMIRAL, observed twice 2026-07-27: 'we had assault rifles at 56 and the active worker had to leave J56 all the way down to the source and come back to J56' while idle contract workers sat next to the source.

== CORRECTION TO THE FIRST FILING ==
My original claim — 'worker selection ignores distance to the SOURCE' — is WRONG and is retracted. The coordinator DOES have closest-empty-hull logic and DID evaluate it. Its own log:

  02:33:05 Idle hull TORWIND-7 already holds ASSAULT_RIFLES for contract cms41jtz0 - selecting it
           to complete its load instead of sourcing a duplicate onto the closest empty hull
           (sp-zve2q deterministic single-hull)

The two nearer hulls were genuinely available (idle, 600/600 fuel, empty, released 'completed'). They were passed over ON PURPOSE.

== THE ACTUAL DEFECT ==
sp-zve2q's single-hull rule is UNCONDITIONAL: any hull already holding ANY quantity of the contract good wins the assignment regardless of where it is. Note the wording 'to complete its load' — the held load was PARTIAL.

Why that is systematically bad: the incumbent hull always finishes a cycle AT THE DELIVERY DESTINATION, which is the point maximally far from the source. So the stickiness rule reliably selects the worst-placed hull for the next source run.

MEASURED (era 5, X1-KP23; contract cms41jtz0, 19 ASSAULT_RIFLES -> J56, source E42):
  dist to E42 source:  A1 (TORWIND-5, idle) 39.0 | F46 (TORWIND-8, idle) 41.9 | J56 (incumbent) 673.3
  incumbent round trip J56->E42->J56          ~= 1,346 units
  near-source hull     A1->E42->J56           ~=   712 units
  => ~47% of travel/fuel wasted on the top-up, repeating every cycle.

== FIX DIRECTION ==
Keep sp-zve2q's intent (do not split a load / do not buy duplicates) but make it a WEIGHED preference rather than an absolute:
  - If the incumbent's held quantity is nearly complete, keep it (topping up is cheap relative to re-sourcing).
  - If the held quantity is a small fraction of the requirement AND a near-source idle hull is dramatically closer, prefer the near hull for the source leg.
  - dist(source,destination) is constant across candidates, so the comparison is just dist(hull,source) — cheap, no routing solve.
  - Use a margin, not a strict '<', so near-ties do not thrash the assignment.
  - Whatever the incumbent already holds must still reach the delivery — do not strand a partial load. Transfer-at-destination or let the incumbent deliver its share; the lane should choose and say which.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Ship ARMED, no feature flag / default-off (standing Admiral order).
- Respect contract fleet dedication; do not reach into other fleets.
- Do not re-assign a hull mid-delivery; selection applies at assignment time.
- Read sp-zve2q's original rationale before changing it — it exists to stop duplicate sourcing, and that must not regress.
- Protected paths untouched: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**.

title: Per-operation capital budget: construction and trade starve each other on a shared pool
description:
ADMIRAL DIRECTIVE 2026-07-27: 'Gate construction starves trading. We need to be able to trade and construct the gate at the same time.'

== ROOT CAUSE (measured live, era 5) ==
Capital is a SHARED POOL guarded by floors, never allocated. Floors say 'do not spend below X'; they do not reserve anything. So the engine with the LOWEST floor structurally outranks every engine above it, and the asymmetry below decides who eats:

  Trade (tour):        caps itself at 25% of live treasury (RULINGS #6 dynamic cap) + 300k floor
  Construction (input): NO proportional cap at all + 150k floor (effectiveReserveFloor, production_executor.go:88)

Construction therefore consumes 100% of capital above 150k — including the entire 150k-300k band trade needs to function. Trade is polite, construction is greedy, construction wins.

OBSERVED: the gate pipeline drove treasury 1.18M -> 193k. Trade then ran but crippled — tours planned +50,890 across 5 legs and the guard shrank leg 0 from 25 CLOTHING to 12, and a FOOD tranche to ONE unit ('shrinking buy ... to respect working-capital floor, live balance 343093, reserve 300000'). A manual leg bypassing the guard bought 60 FOOD for 89,520 and returned 153,840 — +64,320 on ONE round trip, more capital deployed on one good than the whole tour engine was permitted.

== WHY NOT JUST RAISE CONSTRUCTION'S FLOOR ==
That is what sp-q8bon did for the SAME bug one tier down (gate-fill dragged 638k->142k, contract engine parked against its 50k floor, full-economy deadlock; fix = raise non-contract floor to 150k, making 50k-150k contract-exclusive). Raising construction to >=300k+ only RELOCATES the starvation: construction then stalls on every treasury dip and the gate starves instead. It swaps the victim.

== FIX: per-operation capital budget, modeled on expansion's frontierCapacitySplit ==
Reference implementation (READ-ONLY — do NOT modify expansion, it is being rewritten elsewhere):
internal/application/expansion/commands/discovery_share.go:60 frontierCapacitySplit(share, capacity, discoveryHasWork, scanHasWork)

Its three properties are exactly what capital needs:
  1. PROPORTIONAL — each side gets a configured share; neither can crowd the other out.
  2. CLAMPED — share bounded to [min,max], so it cannot be misconfigured into total starvation.
  3. GRACEFUL DEGRADATION — if one side has no work, the other gets 100%. THIS IS THE KEY PROPERTY: no capital idles because construction is paused or trade has no lanes.

Design:
  deployable = live_treasury - shared base floor
  tradeBudget, constructionBudget = capitalSplit(share, deployable, tradeHasWork, constructionHasWork)
Each engine's spend guard draws against ITS OWN budget instead of the shared pool. Floors REMAIN underneath as the fail-closed backstop — this ADDS a constraint, never weakens one (RULINGS #4 intact).

RATIO: 60 trade / 40 construction (Admiral-approved). Trade is the compounding earner that funds the gate, so it takes the larger share; 40% of ~290k deployable still puts ~116k/cycle into FAB_MATS. One clamped integer, retunable.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Ship ARMED. NO feature flag, NO default-off, NO arm-seam (Admiral standing order).
- RULINGS #5: ONE base, derived tiers — follow the reserve_floor.go pattern (internal/application/common/reserve_floor.go), do not introduce a drifting parallel constant.
- RULINGS #4: money guards fail closed and are never weakened.
- Natural home for the split is a PURE function in internal/application/common/ alongside reserve_floor.go, mirroring frontierCapacitySplit's shape and testability.
- OPEN DESIGN POINT for the lane: how each side determines the OTHER's hasWork. Suggested: constructionHasWork = an EXECUTING CONSTRUCTION row in manufacturing_pipelines; tradeHasWork = a trade-fleet hull exists / trade coordinator live. Resolve it and say what you chose.
- Live validation available NOW: construction is currently STOPPED, so the split must hand trade 100% — a directly observable acceptance case.

title: Reconcile a hull's hold when it is dispatched to a DIFFERENT material's task — residue from the prior lot rides along
description:
Upstream cause of sp-w2qg5 (deployed 42b093af). That fix stops residue POISONING a delivery; it does not stop residue accumulating.

MECHANISM: the construction drain dispatches a hull to a lot for material X while it still holds leftovers from material Y's chain. Nothing reconciles the hold between lots. freeCargoSpace only runs when the hold is FULL (production_executor.go:1105), so a hull at 50/80 or 32/80 carries its residue indefinitely.

OBSERVED 2026-07-27 17:46Z — all four gate haulers simultaneously:
  TORWIND-9 @B7  EXPLOSIVES x25
  TORWIND-A @B7  EXPLOSIVES x25

title: HEAVY_TRADE: heavy-hauler acquisition as a concurrent capability gate
description: New capability: when the first shipyard selling heavy haulers is discovered, begin buying heavies and assigning them to trade, capped by a live-tunable knob (default 5). Runs CONCURRENTLY with EXPANSION (a capability gate, not a rung on the phase ladder — the phase ladder and the sensing cutover are untouched). Treasury is partitioned by a DERIVED reservation: heavyReserve = capabilityOpen AND owned<cap ? cheapestKnownHeavyPrice : 0, computed by one shared function that both the autosizer and the sensing buy-floor consume, so probe buying pauses and treasury accumulates until a heavy lands, then resumes. Owned by the fleet autosizer (it already buys trading hulls and tags them). Cheaper-yard re-targeting falls out of recomputing the target each tick. Auto-scaling of the heavy fleet is DEFERRED. Design approved by the Admiral 2026-07-27 in two sections; spec + plan on the lane branch.
