title: Redirect construction hulls to trade at EXPANSION entry
description:
At EXPANSION entry the gate is complete and the hulls bought for gate construction (gate workers / construction haulers) stop earning — they idle or keep polling a finished site while being among the largest-cargo hulls the fleet owns. Redirect them to trade at the phase edge so the capital works.

SCOPE: on the transition into EXPANSION, release every hull dedicated to construction and hand it to the trading fleet — re-tag and let the capacity reconciler / fleet autosizer place it, OR assign explicitly; the implementer decides after verifying which path actually adopts a freshly-released hull (a released-but-unadopted hull is worse than the status quo).

SAFETY REQUIREMENTS: (a) never yank a hull mid-delivery — a hull carrying construction materials or in transit to a construction site must finish or be released cleanly, never stranded with undeliverable cargo; (b) fire once on the transition edge and be harmless if re-run — this fleet has a history of phase-edge defects (the sticky GATE latch, cutover re-fire loops), so idempotence is load-bearing; (c) no spend — this is a redirect, so RULINGS #4 is not implicated, but no existing guard may be weakened; (d) if construction is NOT actually complete at EXPANSION (non-gate construction sites still consuming materials), STOP and report rather than stranding the manufacturing pipeline.

OPEN QUESTIONS for recon: which dedicated_fleet tag construction hulls carry; whether clearing the tag suffices for the autosizer/capacity reconciler to adopt, or an explicit trade-fleet assignment is required; where the EXPANSION edge is observable (bootstrap phase derivation vs construction coordinator); whether a construction container still claims the hull and must be stopped/released first.

Requested by the Admiral 2026-07-27. Runs as its own lane in parallel with the sp-k6v8z sensing extension.
close_reason: Merged to main via captain-gate. Redirects construction hulls to trade at EXPANSION (unconditional per-tick, idempotence derived from the observer's else-if ordering rather than a stored latch — so an in-transit hull is recovered when it goes idle), explicitly assigns the 'trade' tag (recon corrected the brief: nothing auto-adopts an untagged hull; the capacity reconciler is deleted and the sole adopter of an undedicated hull routes it to CONTRACT), and ensures the trade-fleet coordinator at EXPANSION so the destination is managed before hulls arrive. 22 tests, 11 mutation probes, review + fix round both clean.

title: [P1] construction --good-override strategy=prefer-buy is a SILENT NO-OP for gate materials — and the command's own documented example is exactly that case
description:
MEASURED, era 5, 2026-07-27 12:25Z. Gate-material purchases in the LAST 7 HOURS, complete list:
  07:23  PURCHASE 20 FAB_MATS at X1-KP23-F46
  07:39  PURCHASE 20 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY at X1-KP23-D41
  10:52  PURCHASE 20 FAB_MATS at X1-KP23-F46
Three purchases. 60 units in 7h = ~8.6 units/hr.

REMAINING: 1460 FAB_MATS + 320 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY = 1780 units => ~207 HOURS (8.6 days) at the observed rate. Construction has been frozen at 11% since 07:51Z. The era will not last that long.

THIS IS NOT THE sp-ijbe2 REGRESSION. That caused a 2h40m outage and was reverted (07a418a4, deployed 10:45Z, revert verified byte-identical to 70dd1369). The 8.6/hr rate spans the whole 7h window including healthy pre-regression time.

CONSTRAINTS MEASURED
- trade_volume = 20 at EVERY source (FAB_MATS @ F46 supply=HIGH ask=1170; ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY @ D41 supply=MODERATE ask=4304, @ A4 MODERATE ask=12476). 20 units per transaction is a MARKET cap, so 1780 units is ~89 buy-trips minimum regardless of any fix.
- The coordinator runs the DEEP fabrication chain (trigger production -> poll -> buy output) even where supply is HIGH. Log: 'Production complete: FAB_MATS now available at F46 (polled 1 times)' then 'Purchased fabricated output: 20 units'. PLAYBOOK §4a calls running deep against an abundant source the #1 gate stall.
- Money is NOT the constraint: treasury 705438, a record, with income/hr healthy. Contracts are unaffected.

THE PRESCRIBED FIX NO LONGER EXISTS. §4a says to switch to harvest via '--depth 3' and reinforce with 'construction override --strategy prefer-buy'. BOTH flags were retired by sp-sxyx6: 'construction start' takes no --depth, and 'construction override' takes only --min-supply, --price-ceiling-mult, --clear. 'smart' is the sole acquisition strategy and depth is pinned to the constant 3. There is NO live knob to force harvest-over-fabricate. See sp-poje3.
--min-supply is not the binding constraint either: FAB_MATS is HIGH, already above the MODERATE default floor.

SO THE OPERATOR HAS NO LEVER. This needs either (a) the acquisition strategy to prefer buying when the source is abundant rather than producing, (b) parallelism high enough that ~89 buy-trips complete in a viable window, or (c) an Admiral decision that this gate is not worth building this era.

Do NOT dispatch a code fix off this bead without a decision on which of those it is — the previous attempt to fix throughput (sp-ijbe2) caused an outage.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-07-31 — CONFIRMED OPEN, and the 'operator has no lever' claim is WORSE than filed. I verified this by direct read, not from the audit report alone.

THE LEVER EXISTS AND IS INERT.
  cli/construction.go:118 ships `construction override --good-override FAB_MATS:strategy=prefer-buy`
  (e0bba552, 2026-07-13). It feeds shouldBuyGood.

  manufacturing/services/supply_chain_resolver.go:154:
      // The target good is always fabricated, so skip this check for root
      if !isTargetGood {
          shouldBuy, marketData := r.shouldBuyGood(ctx, goodSymbol, systemSymbol, playerID)

  The ROOT good never reaches shouldBuyGood. :127 states it outright ('isTargetGood forces
  fabrication for the root good, even if available in markets'); :208 hardcodes AcquisitionFabricate.

  That path is reached unconditionally for every construction task:
  run_construction_coordinator.go:1138 -> :1169 resolveFabricationTree -> BuildDependencyTree(task.Good()),
  which makes the GATE MATERIAL the root. So pinning the gate material to prefer-buy is a NO-OP.

THIS IS THE DANGEROUS PART. It is not a missing lever — it is a lever that reports success and
changes nothing. An operator pulls it, sees no error, and reasonably believes the fleet is now
buying FAB_MATS when it is still fabricating them at supply=HIGH. A silent no-op knob is worse than
an absent one, because it stops anyone looking further.

STILL A DECISION BEAD, NOT A LANE. Per the bead's own body: do NOT dispatch a code fix without a
decision between (a) prefer-buy-when-abundant, (b) parallelism, (c) don't build this gate. The prior
throughput attempt (sp-ijbe2) caused a 2h40m outage and was reverted (07a418a4 over 8810c522) — that
revert is what is deployed today.

MINIMUM HONEST FIX regardless of which option is chosen: make the override either work on the root
good or REFUSE with an explicit error. It must not keep accepting the flag silently.

No commit on main since 2026-07-27 touches gate-material acquisition or parallelism (ea2afecb edited
only the playbook).
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-06. The THROUGHPUT half is obsolete; the SILENT-NO-OP KNOB half is still live and is now the whole bead. Dropped P0 -> P1.

=== A HYPOTHESIS I RAISED AND THAT WAS FALSIFIED — RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-RUNS IT ===
I (captain) proposed that this bead and sp-9eor3 were the SAME defect measured from opposite
ends: that a feed walk head-of-line blocking on an unaffordable step would produce exactly this
signature — long stretches with no gate-material purchases, punctuated by occasional legs. It is
WRONG, on two independently dispositive grounds:

  1. THE CODE DID NOT EXIST. planGateFeed/feedGateLeg and the whole two-fleet gate design arrived
     in 76440cc1 on 2026-08-05 03:35. This bead was measured 2026-07-27 — NINE DAYS EARLIER.
     'git log -S planGateFeed' returns exactly two commits: 76440cc1 and the sp-9eor3 fix
     694038e1. The mechanism was not in the era-5 binary and cannot explain era-5 data.
  2. MONEY WAS NOT THE CONSTRAINT. The head-of-line block only fires when the money guard refuses
     a buy. This bead's own text says 'Money is NOT the constraint: treasury 705438, a record'.
     The precondition was absent.
Corroborating, from era-5 data still in the local Postgres (this bead's own source system,
X1-KP23-F46/D41, purchase list matches the bead exactly): during the 07:51->12:25 freeze SEVEN+
distinct input goods were bought, INCLUDING QUARTZ_SAND — the very good sp-9eor3 unblocked was
never blocked here — plus ~205k spent on unrelated trading. The head-of-line signature is the
opposite: one good retried forever with everything behind it unreachable. Inputs flowed freely
while the gate MATERIAL was the bottleneck, which is this bead's own fabricate-instead-of-buy
diagnosis, not mine.

=== THROUGHPUT HALF: OBSOLETE, measured in the CURRENT era (staging, TORWINDSTG, X1-KP46) ===
FAB_MATS units purchased per hour, last 14h, BUCKETED (a mean would hide the punctuation this
bead is about — and the 12h mean of 61.8/hr does span a 3.6h stall, so it is not the number to
quote either):
  10:00 20u | 11:00 160u | 14:00 115u | 16:00 200u | 17:00 80u | 18:00 43u | 20:00 303u
  = 921 units over 7 ACTIVE hours of 14 (the missing hours are true zeros).
  65.8 units/hr overall, 131.6 units/hr while flowing — versus the 8.6 units/hr that triggered
  this bead. Roughly 8x. Remaining bill 459 units => ~7 HOURS, not the projected 207.
MECHANISM OF THE IMPROVEMENT: 76440cc1 appears to have delivered this bead's option (a)
architecturally without anyone recording it — the DELIVERY fleet calls BuyAtTerminalFactory on
the gate material, i.e. it BUYS terminal output instead of fabricating it. Caveat worth keeping:
that path is taken for gate-fleet-TAGGED hulls; supplyTask still routes untagged hulls to the
legacy resolveFabricationTree, which forces fabrication. Current-era operation_type split for
gate-chain goods over 12h is construction_supply 41 buys / contract 6, with no legacy-path
signature visible — but that split does not positively prove the legacy path is unused.

=== WHAT REMAINS, AND IS THE BEAD NOW ===
The named mechanism is INTACT in current main: supply_chain_resolver.go:168 is the ONLY caller of
shouldBuyGood and it sits inside 'if !isTargetGood', under the comment 'The target good is always
fabricated, so the strategy only decides for non-root nodes.' The ROOT good — the gate material —
still never reaches it.
Therefore --good-override ... strategy=prefer-buy is ACCEPTED (cli/construction.go:110),
VALIDATED (construction_override.go:46), and SILENTLY DOES NOTHING for a gate material. Worse,
construction.go:90's own documented example is 'FAB_MATS:...,strategy=prefer-buy' — a gate
material, i.e. the single case where it provably has no effect. A user following the built-in
example gets silence and reasonably concludes it worked.
That is this bead's own 'MINIMUM HONEST FIX' and it is untouched. P1 rather than P2 because a
knob that silently no-ops, advertised by its own example, misleads rather than merely underdelivers.

CREDIT: falsification and the six-ground analysis by the sp-9eor3 lane, which was asked to TEST
the hypothesis rather than confirm it and correctly refused it.
CONDITION ON THE 'THROUGHPUT HALF IS OBSOLETE' FINDING — named so it is falsifiable later.

That finding rests on gate hulls being TAGGED. supplyTask still routes UNTAGGED hulls to the
legacy resolveFabricationTree path, which still forces fabrication of the ROOT good — the exact
mechanism this bead named. The 65.8 units/hr measurement was taken while the gate fleet was
running tagged, so it does not speak to the untagged path at all.

If hulls ever run untagged — a role-assignment regression, a fleet rebuild, a cold start before
tagging converges — the throughput complaint returns in full, and it will look like a fresh
regression rather than this bead. Anyone re-measuring should check the tag distribution FIRST,
not the rate.

Credit: condition identified by the sp-9eor3/sp-q9um6 lane while reporting sp-q9um6.

title: Construction drain tick blocks on group.Wait(), so the retry sweep and re-dispatch run at the cadence of the SLOWEST in-flight haul (bounded only by the 1h30m task deadline)
description:
run_construction_coordinator.go:~370 — the dispatch loop ends in group.Wait(), which joins every worker before drainOnce returns. The next tick, and therefore the next ActivateConstructionTasks pass, cannot start until the slowest dispatched supply completes. The code comment at :360-361 states the intent ('a per-task deadline so a single wedged task can never hold group.Wait() — and thus this whole tick / the coordinator goroutine — forever') but the bound it relies on is the 1h30m task timeout, not a tick-length one.

CONSEQUENCE — everything downstream of activation stops while hauls are in flight:
  - sweepRetryableConstructionFailures (task_activator.go:246) is the FIRST thing in ActivateConstructionTasks, so a FAILED DELIVER_TO_CONSTRUCTION task cannot be swept back to PENDING. Its 2-minute constructionRetryBackoff (task_activator.go:595) is meaningless — the real cadence is haul-length.
  - Newly purchased hulls are not picked up until the current tick ends.
  - A hull released mid-tick holding gate material sits idle until the current tick ends.

MEASURED LIVE, era 5, 06:02Z:
  last 'Construction drain: activating construction tasks'  = 05:51:02  (13 min earlier)
  route segments still completing at 06:02:47 -> container alive, tick blocked
  ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY task: FAILED 05:50:09, retry_count=1, max_retries=3, can_retry=TRUE,
    pipeline EXECUTING, player_id matches -> EVERY sweep gate passes, sweep never ran
  TORWIND-B: idle 13 min holding ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY x20 (~73.5k) at K86
  TORWIND-C: gate worker bought ~06:52, assigned_at = NEVER
  Gate running 2 of 4 workers; ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY frozen at 40/400 while FAB_MATS advanced 80->120.

NOT caused by sp-1jpiw (deployed a7206b58). Verified: the AC task failed at 05:50:09 on a SOURCING error ('sourcing ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY failed: ...') via the legitimate FAILED path, BEFORE the 05:51 restart, and nothing false-completed. sp-1jpiw's re-queue works — this is a separate defect that prevents recovery from running at all.

WANTED: decouple the activation/sweep cadence from in-flight hauls. Candidates (not a menu — needs design): run activation on its own ticker independent of the drain; or dispatch supplies without joining them and let a later tick reap; or keep group.Wait() but bound the tick far below the task deadline so the loop re-enters promptly. Whatever is chosen must not reintroduce unbounded goroutine growth or double-claim a hull already working.

NOTE the interaction with sp-1jpiw: a shorter tick bound means more interruptions, which is now SAFE (interrupted tasks re-queue with no retry spent) where before it would have burned the retry budget. That fix is a prerequisite for this one.
notes:
RESOLVED ITSELF AFTER ~70 MIN, confirming the mechanism exactly. 06:07 -> 07:17: the blocked tick finally returned when its hauls completed, and the very next pass re-dispatched everything — TORWIND-B empty and re-claimed, TORWIND-C assigned for the first time since purchase, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 40 -> 60/400 (B's stranded 20 delivered without intervention), all 4 gate workers active.

So nothing is permanently wedged; the cost is THROUGHPUT. For ~70 minutes the gate ran at 2 of 4 workers, the FAILED circuitry task sat sweep-eligible and unswept, and a newly-bought 371k hull sat unused. That recurs on every long haul.
REVERTED IN PRODUCTION 2026-07-27 10:45Z (commit 07a418a4). The hand-off design regressed the gate into a total delivery outage.

WHAT HAPPENED
  07:51Z  construction last advanced (FAB_MATS 140/1600, AC 80/400)
  08:05Z  8810c522 deployed
  08:05-10:45Z  ZERO material delivered for 2h40m while 4 hulls carried 276 units
  Treasury hit a record 722597 throughout — contracts were healthy, only the gate was dead.

MECHANISM: dispatchableHaulers drops any hull supplies.holds() reports as being worked. A worker that goes silent WITHOUT deregistering permanently retires its hull — it is never dispatchable again and its cargo never lands. Two of four gate workers were retired this way (TORWIND-A stale 71min, TORWIND-C 70min). The coordinator then ticked every 60s logging 'Idle dedicated fleet ships discovered' and dispatching nothing, with 2 READY tasks waiting.

The registry is in-memory and unbounded against a worker that never returns. The per-task 1h30m timeout did not rescue it — A/C were stuck past 90min with no release.

The lane ANTICIPATED this exact shape in its own test comment: 'a wedged supply permanently retires a slot under max_workers, and enough of them starve the drain of dispatch capacity while it still reports RUNNING'. It tested the wedged-task case but nothing bounds the registry against a worker that dies silently — which is what happened.

WHY REVERT RATHER THAN FIX FORWARD: a stalled gate is strictly worse than the problem sp-ijbe2 solved. The 86-minute tick block was a THROUGHPUT cost; this was an OUTAGE. Post-revert verified: dispatch resumed immediately, 2 ready material-tasks dispatched across 2 hulls to the gate site.

WHAT A RETRY MUST DO DIFFERENTLY
- The worker registry must be self-healing: a registered worker that stops reporting must be reaped, not trusted forever. Registration alone cannot be the authority on 'this hull is busy'.
- Deregistration must be guaranteed on EVERY exit path, including panic. A defer at the top of runSupplyWorker, not at the end of the happy path.
- There must be a liveness signal per worker (last-progress timestamp) that the tick can age out, independent of the task timeout — the task timeout demonstrably did not fire here.
- Acceptance must include: a worker whose goroutine dies without deregistering does NOT permanently retire its hull. That is the case that broke production and no test covered it.
=====================================================================
RETRACTION 2026-07-27 13:30Z — THE INCIDENT EVIDENCE ABOVE IS VOID
=====================================================================
The 'production outage' I recorded above did NOT happen. The Mac was ASLEEP.

pmset -g log (local time = UTC-3):
  05:11:51 local = 08:11Z  Entering Sleep 'Idle Sleep'
  ... only sub-second maintenance DarkWakes ...
  10:22:34 local = 13:22Z  Wake (user activity)

sp-ijbe2 deployed 08:05Z. The machine slept SIX MINUTES later and stayed down
~2.5h. Every symptom I attributed to the fix was a suspended daemon:
  'TORWIND-A/C workers went silent, stale 71min'  -> machine asleep
  '2h40m zero deliveries'                          -> ~2.5h of it was sleep
  'construction frozen 4.5h'                       -> wall-clock over a suspended host
  '8.6 units/hr -> ~207 hours to build the gate'   -> divided by time that did not elapse

THE TELL I READ PAST: two hulls with synced_at 4429s old while the coordinator
heartbeat was 3s old. A live daemon cannot have 71-minute-stale ship rows — that
is a HOST problem, not a code problem. I also noticed the wall-clock jump
(09:24 -> 09:58 between two commands) and treated it as a curiosity.

STATUS: sp-ijbe2 is UNPROVEN, not disproven. It ran for six minutes in
production. Its full suite was green (73 packages), -race clean, and the
orchestrator independently mutation-probed the double-claim guard.

THE ONE REAL CONCERN SURVIVES INDEPENDENT OF THE FALSE INCIDENT: the in-memory
worker registry has no liveness bound. If a worker ever dies without
deregistering, dispatchableHaulers retires its hull permanently. That was never
demonstrated — but the lane's own test comment predicted the shape, and it is a
genuine design weakness worth closing BEFORE re-applying.

REVERT 07a418a4 remains deployed (the joining drain, with its 86-minute tick
block). Re-application should carry the registry hardening, not go back as-is.
FIXED AND GATED 2026-08-01 at main e2c4fbc3 (squash). 15 files, +1559/-266, including a new run_construction_coordinator_workers.go (225 lines) and run_construction_coordinator_worker_liveness_test.go (395 lines). The drain now hands its hauls off rather than blocking on group.Wait(), so sweep cadence is independent of any single haul's duration.

Verified pre-merge: clean 3-way merge, go build + go vet clean, full go test ./... green across ~107 packages.

NOTE the work sat unmerged on branch sp-ijbe2b (branch name carries a typo'd trailing 'b'; there is no bead sp-ijbe2b) from 2026-07-27 until this reconciliation audit found it.

title: PLAYBOOK §4a's core depth/worker recipe teaches RETIRED flags — --depth and --max-workers no longer exist (sp-sxyx6)
description:
§4a's headline guidance is written entirely around two CLI flags that sp-sxyx6 retired. Verified 2026-07-27: 'spacetraders construction start --help' registers only --system, --min-supply, --good-override, --overrides, --player-id. Neither --depth nor --max-workers exists.

Per gobot/internal/adapters/cli/construction.go:15-27, depth is now pinned to the constant 3 (buy-final/harvest, the former --depth default) because 'smart' is the sole acquisition strategy, and the worker count is tuned live via 'construction workers <site> --count N' (sp-duljg) instead of at launch.

WHAT IS STALE
1. 'The single biggest knob is construction start --depth' — the whole feed-then-harvest prescription is expressed as --depth 0 then --depth 3. --depth 0 is now UNREACHABLE from the CLI; every pipeline launches at 3.
2. The right-sizing bullet cites '--max-workers, default 5' as a launch flag.
3. The auto-managers bullet says the rebalancer provisions 'to meet the pipeline's --max-workers demand' and advises 'lower --max-workers'. The advice is intact; only the command changed (construction workers --count).

WHY THIS IS P1: §4a is the gate-fill runbook, read during exactly the high-pressure moments when the gate has stalled. Following it literally now produces a CLI error. I nearly ran 'construction stop && construction start --depth 3' tonight and would have hit it; I had run --help twice and not registered the flag's absence.

NOT A SIMPLE FIND-AND-REPLACE. Found by the sp-d38vx lane while correcting the adjacent wedge bullet. sp-d38vx is gated (the wedge bullet is fixed and no longer cites --depth); this is the untouched remainder.

title: PLAYBOOK §4a teaches a false wedge diagnostic ('0 task(s) promoted to READY') and a runbook the sp-1jpiw fix supersedes
description:
PLAYBOOK.md:146 (§4a, the restart-wedge entry) says the wedge signature is: returns EXECUTING but logs '0 task(s) promoted to READY', gate count flat, haulers idle. Prescribed fix: 'construction stop <site> && construction start <site> --depth N' after EVERY restart.

BOTH HALVES ARE NOW WRONG.

1. '0 task(s) promoted to READY' IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. That counter is PENDING->READY only. A task sitting in READY is never 'promoted', so a perfectly healthy system logs 0 there too. I treated it as the wedge signature for a whole session because the book says so, and it sent me to a wrong root cause. Established while fixing sp-1jpiw and confirmed in prod: the line appears in healthy ticks that immediately dispatch three concurrent supplies.

2. THE RUNBOOK STEP IS NO LONGER NEEDED. sp-1jpiw (deployed a7206b58) fixes the actual cause — an orphaned child goroutine drove the cancelled task to terminal FAILED through a detached ctx, spending a retry each restart until the ceiling of 3 was hit. Restarts now re-queue the task PENDING with the retry budget untouched. Verified in prod across two restarts: no abandons after the new binary, three supplies dispatched within 10s of boot.

WANTED in §4a:
- Delete or rewrite the '0 task(s) promoted to READY' signature. If a wedge signature is still wanted, the honest one is a task in terminal FAILED with retry_count at DefaultMaxRetries (3) — check manufacturing_tasks, not the log line.
- Downgrade the mandatory post-restart stop/start to a diagnostic-only step, noting sp-1jpiw fixed the cause. Do NOT delete the whole entry: the DEPTH guidance (feed-then-harvest, --depth 0 vs 3, right-size to the source) is independently valuable and unaffected.

Keep it short and in the file's voice. Do not restate the incident.
close_reason: Closed

title: Construction progress is a write-only accumulator with no API reconciliation — any lost recordDelivery drifts the gate count permanently
description:
manufacturing_pipelines.materials[].deliveredQuantity is written ONLY by recordDelivery (run_construction_coordinator.go:1178, called from :705/:749/:841). Nothing anywhere re-reads the construction site from the API and reconciles. It accumulates forward and never self-corrects.

CONSEQUENCE: any delivery that reaches the SERVER but whose recordDelivery does not land — a crash, a daemon restart between the supply call and the write, a manual/raw supply, a swallowed error — leaves the daemon permanently under-counting. It will then source and buy material the gate does not need, and the surplus cannot be delivered because the server-side requirement is already met: stranded cargo plus wasted capital, at ~3675/unit for ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY.

It also drives operator truth: the gate-construction dashboard's 'Materials: Delivered vs Target' panel reads this JSONB directly (gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/gate-construction.json), so a drifted record silently misreports gate progress with no error anywhere.

OBSERVED 2026-07-27 05:07: after an Admiral-authorised raw-API supply of 20 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY, live API read 20/400 while the daemon record read 0/400. Divergence corrected by hand (SQL); it would NOT have healed on its own.

RELATIONSHIP: sp-1jpiw is fixing restart-interrupted supply tasks. That fix narrows the window but cannot close this — the daemon can always be interrupted between a successful server-side supply and its own write. This needs reconciliation, not a smaller window.

WANTED: reconcile deliveredQuantity against the live construction site (GET /systems/{s}/waypoints/{w}/construction) — at pipeline adoption/restart at minimum, ideally on a periodic tick. The API is authoritative; the local row is a cache and should be treated as one. Note 'construction start' ALREADY fetches site requirements from the API, so the read path exists — it is the resume/steady-state path that never re-reads.

Cheap interim alternative if full reconciliation is too big: log loudly when a delivery is recorded whose resulting total disagrees with the site's own fulfilled count.
notes: Folded into the sp-1jpiw lane (2026-07-27 05:1x) rather than opened as a separate lane: both fixes land in run_construction_coordinator.go, and ENGINEERING.md forbids two lanes on one file. They are also one problem — a restart interrupts a delivery, and the record must then be reconciled. Scope extension sent mid-flight; will ship in the same branch.
close_reason:
Gated + deployed a7206b58 (commit 0037c213). reconcilePipelinesFromSite runs in drainOnce after the ready-task poll and BEFORE any bill is consulted, so each tick sizes its buys against server truth. ~1 GET per pipeline per tick, only on ticks that have work (placed after the len(tasks)==0 early return), ~1.7% of API budget. Restart is covered for free — the first tick reconciles.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG TWICE; the lane refused both and proved it.
1. targetQuantity is the site's REMAINING at planning time (construction_pipeline_planner.go:285 'remaining := mat.Remaining()'), NOT its Required. My 'correct the local row to the API Fulfilled' would have credited a pipeline with every unit delivered before it existed and under-bought the remainder by that baseline. It only looked right on this incident because this pipeline was planned at 0/400, making target == Required by coincidence. Correct derivation shipped: observed = target - site.Remaining().
2. I asked for take-the-API-value-either-way with a loud log on backwards corrections. The lane built RAISE-ONLY and probed my version verbatim: it erased 80 already-delivered units, the exact lost update recordMu exists to prevent. A site read is necessarily stale by the time it lands (HTTP round trip outside the lock), so a lower reading is indistinguishable from one that raced a delivery. Raise-only also makes the operation monotonic and idempotent. Local-ahead now logs loudly and writes nothing — a double-count is a different defect and clobbering it erases its own evidence.

Wired in main.go in the same commit; an unwired source logs 'reconciliation is DISABLED' every tick with a test pinning it. Verified live post-deploy: no DISABLED line, and daemon record == live API (FAB_MATS 80/1600, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 40/400).

title: Construction drain: a cancelled supply task reports a false 1h30m timeout and is never retried, stranding bought material on an idle hull
description:
TWO defects, both hit live during a routine daemon deploy (era 5, 2026-07-27 05:01).

WHAT HAPPENED
  04:53:40  Purchased fabricated output: 20 units of ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY for 73500 credits
  05:01:28  [ERROR] Construction drain: supply of ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY via TORWIND-A exceeded 1h30m0s
            — ABANDONING this tick (hull released, task retried next tick; the coordinator keeps
            ticking, never hangs): context canceled
  05:01:29  daemon process start (verified: ps lstart 02:01:29 local = 05:01:29Z)
  05:01:36  Construction drain: activation done (0 task(s) promoted to READY)
  05:01:36  dispatching 1 lot-task(s) ... START supply of FAB_MATS via TORWIND-9
TORWIND-A then sat IDLE at the destination waypoint X1-KP23-I53 holding 20 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY for 8+ minutes while FAB_MATS deliveries continued around it (40->60). ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY stayed 0/400.

DEFECT 1 — THE ERROR MESSAGE IS FALSE. It claims 'exceeded 1h30m0s'. The task was created at most 8 minutes earlier (material purchased 04:53:40). The real cause is in the same line: 'context canceled' — the daemon restart cancelled the in-flight supply. Reporting a cancellation as a timeout sends the next investigator hunting a slow haul that never happened. Distinguish context.Canceled from a genuine deadline and say which.

DEFECT 2 — 'task retried next tick' IS NOT TRUE. The very next activation logged '0 task(s) promoted to READY' and dispatched only FAB_MATS. The abandoned ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY task was never re-promoted, so the hull stayed idle holding 73500 credits of material AT the delivery waypoint. The message promises a retry the code does not perform.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE KNOWN RESTART WEDGE: PLAYBOOK §4a documents sp-1jpiw — every daemon deploy re-wedges construction, signature '0 task(s) promoted to READY', prescribed fix 'construction stop <site> && construction start <site>'. This is that wedge, but with a NEW consequence: it also strands already-purchased material on a released hull. The runbook fix would have re-planned the whole pipeline; it does not address the stranded cargo specifically.

MANUAL RECOVERY APPLIED (Admiral signed off a raw API call): docked TORWIND-A and POSTed /systems/X1-KP23/waypoints/X1-KP23-I53/construction/supply {shipSymbol:TORWIND-A, tradeSymbol:ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY, units:20}. Site went 0/400 -> 20/400, hull freed, then 'ship refresh' to resync the daemon. No stop/start needed.

WANTED: (a) truthful cancellation-vs-timeout reporting; (b) an abandoned supply task must actually be re-promoted on the next activation, OR the hull's held material must be recognised and supplied rather than re-bought. Note the hull was already AT the destination — the cheapest correct recovery is to finish the delivery, never to re-source.
notes:
NOT NEW — this is the third sighting of one defect. Consolidating under sp-1jpiw (P1, the fullest root cause).
  sp-ciog (P3, 2026-07-06) names the mechanism: restart recovery REAPS tasks of transiently-inactive pipelines but has no matching re-plan for CONSTRUCTION — the reap/replan asymmetry.
  sp-1jpiw (P1, 2026-07-20) is the observable wedge; code fix explicitly DEFERRED behind the depot-loop goal. Records that a FRESH start correctly adopts loaded hulls and carries their cargo forward with no re-buy — so the rebuild path handles laden hulls; the RESUME path is what is broken.
  sp-uykk8 (this, 2026-07-27) adds the false-timeout message and the stranded-purchase consequence.

CODE SITE for the false message: run_construction_coordinator.go:990-994. taskCtx wraps the parent ctx, so daemon shutdown fires Done() with context.Canceled while the log unconditionally formats 'exceeded <timeout>'. The block then only 'return false' — it does NOTHING to task state, so 'task retried next tick' is an assumption, not an action. That is why the next activation logged '0 task(s) promoted to READY'.
close_reason: Closed by sp-1jpiw + sp-duxru (deployed a7206b58). Both halves fixed: the cancelled task now re-queues instead of going terminal FAILED, and the false 'exceeded <timeout>' message now discriminates context.Canceled from context.DeadlineExceeded.

title: PLAYBOOK: add 'find the CURRENT design before calling a subsystem broken' — a DESIGN bead can be partly superseded
description:
ADMIRAL-ORDERED after a repeat failure 2026-07-27. Explicitly NOT to be recorded as a memory — it must live in doctrine that every session reads at start (CLAUDE.md required reading #3 = PLAYBOOK.md).

WHAT HAPPENED (twice in one session, same axis)
I diagnosed contract idle-hull homing as broken and was one command away from running 'spacetraders fleet hub add' with waypoints I had picked from source-market purchase counts. That would have overwritten a CORRECT runtime resolution with a hand-picked worse set. The Admiral said 'are you sure? it seem its working' — it was working — and I doubled down with a fabricated root cause instead of checking.

THE TRAP: sp-9le3x is a signed-off DESIGN bead, still IN_PROGRESS, and reads as authoritative. Its STEP 1 ('greedy weighted p-median') and its demand-ranked homing mechanism are DEAD — ripped out by sp-yv230 ('it concentrates on the top hub') and replaced by sp-ojp32. Nothing in sp-9le3x said so until I annotated it. Reading the newest-looking DESIGN bead is NOT the same as reading the current design.

WHAT THE PLAYBOOK ENTRY MUST SAY
1. Before declaring any subsystem broken, find the CURRENT authority: search ALL beads for the subsystem (including closed ones — .beads/issues.jsonl is greppable), order by date, and read the LATEST CLOSED beads. A closed bead that SHIPPED supersedes an open DESIGN bead that described the plan.
2. A DESIGN bead can be PARTLY superseded. Premise/guards may still hold while a specific mechanism section is dead. Do not treat a design doc as all-or-nothing.
3. 'The config value is null' is NOT evidence a feature is off. Several sets are recomputed at runtime by design and deliberately never persisted (RULINGS #2/#3 single-writer / restart-idempotent). Verify at the BEHAVIOUR, not the config row. Worked example: contract standby_stations is always null; isCentralSink() recomputes the era-invariant central-band set every pass.
4. Counters that read zero are not always failure. '0 hull(s) re-homed this pass' means already correctly placed (idle_arb.go:1071 'already home if at ANY standby waypoint').
5. NEVER hand-set contract hubs with 'fleet hub add' to fix perceived clustering. Idle hulls spread ONE PER DISTINCT CENTRAL BAND — check the band LETTER before calling it clustering. A single standby point is 1.28x FLAT vs 1.51x for the spread; hand-setting makes it worse.
6. Home-system BANDS are era-invariant; SYMBOLS regenerate. Resolve by market role + band, never by letter+number. Era-5 X1-KP23 A25 H45 E54 G64 F76 D83 K104 C115 vs era-4 X1-UM5 A27 H45 E55 G63 F75 D83 K104 C153.

Keep it short and imperative in the Admiral's voice, in PLAYBOOK.md's existing numbered-rule style. Do not add a memory file. Do not restate the whole incident — the rule plus the worked example is the payload.
close_reason: Closed

title: A tour blocked by the working-capital floor abandons cargo it already bought instead of flying its sell legs
description:
TORWIND-6, 2026-07-27 03:36, era 5:
  03:36:04 [WARN] Tour leg 0: buy of 14 CLOTHING @ 2857 would breach working-capital floor
                  - live balance 299015, reserve 300000, even 1 unit pierces - skipping, will re-plan
  03:36:12 [INFO] Tour re-plan budget exhausted - stopping (any unsold tour cargo will report as stranded)
  03:36:34 [ERROR] stranded cargo: 4 POLYNUCLEOTIDES, 6 CLOTHING still aboard at X1-KP23-K86 (tour-bought, unsold) - reporting failure

Treasury was 985 credits under the floor.

THE DEFECT IS THE RESPONSE, NOT THE GUARD. Refusing the BUY is correct and must stay (RULINGS #4). But the hull was already holding 10 units of tour-bought cargo, and the reaction to 'cannot buy more' was to stop the tour and strand them. Selling cargo you already own ADDS credits — it moves treasury AWAY from the floor. The blocked-buy path should still fly the remaining SELL legs, then stop. Instead the hull idles holding ~31k of unsold goods with no container (verified: nothing running on TORWIND-6 at 03:41).

WHY THIS WILL RECUR CONSTANTLY — measured over the last 60 minutes:
  treasury min=107651 max=580610 swing=472959
  transactions leaving balance_after < 300000: 29

The treasury does not sit above 300k; it CROSSES it ~29 times an hour. Contract sourcing spends 35-70k per cycle and hull buys 335k, so the working balance oscillates through a ~470k band with the reserve sitting inside it. Every crossing that coincides with a tour plan is a stopped tour, and any that catches a tour mid-flight strands its cargo.

This is not an argument to lower the reserve — ANY fixed threshold inside that oscillation band has this property, and the Admiral set 300k deliberately (sp-4chpz). The fix is that the floor must gate new EXPOSURE, never orphan existing INVENTORY.

Secondary: the stranded hold then becomes a legitimate auto-liquidation candidate, which is the one case where the sp-in36a dispatch is doing real work rather than churning.
notes:
SHARPER MECHANISM (03:43 recurrence). The planner is NOT the problem — it correctly plans the recovery:
  03:43:20 Tour planned: 2 legs, projected profit 70355 (fresh 39437, LIQUIDATION 30918, deposit 0)
  03:43:38 Continuous tour stopping - 3 consecutive tours flew zero trades after 0 productive tour(s)
  03:43:38 stranded cargo: 4 POLYNUCLEOTIDES, 6 CLOTHING ... reporting failure

The unproductive-tour CIRCUIT BREAKER stops the hull before it can fly the liquidation leg it just planned. So there are two defects, and the second is what makes it unrecoverable:

(a) a buy blocked by the floor stops the tour instead of flying its remaining SELL legs
(b) the breaker counts a blocked-buy tour as 'flew zero trades', so 3 floor-dips permanently park a hull that is holding sellable cargo — and every relaunch re-plans the same liquidation leg and is killed again

CONFIRMED NOT SELF-HEALING: coordinator relaunches every ~3min (03:45:30, 03:46:00 cooldown lines), each run re-plans the liquidation and dies to the breaker. Verified over 3 cycles.

A blocked BUY is not an unproductive tour — it is a tour that was denied capital. Counting it toward a breaker whose purpose is detecting dead margins conflates 'no opportunity' with 'no capital', and the two need opposite responses: back off vs sell what you are holding.

VALUE AT RISK, measured: CLOTHING 6 @ best bid 5060 (X1-KP23-A1) + POLYNUCLEOTIDES 4 @ 294 (X1-KP23-J56) = ~31536, which matches the planner's own 30918 estimate. At the hull's current waypoint K86 the same cargo bids only 9428, so a naive dump-in-place loses ~22k.
close_reason: Closed

title: ROOT: nav operations write the WHOLE ship row from a caller-held entity, so every untouched column is stamped from a stale snapshot
description:
This is the root cause behind sp-7oxeo (ghost ownership claims) and sp-in36a (spurious liquidation on stale cargo). Both were symptom patches on the same defect. Fixing this kills the class.

THE DEFECT
navigate_route.go:164 loads a ship ONCE (FindBySymbol) and carries that one entity through an entire flight - minutes to tens of minutes. It hands that same object to five ShipRepository methods, each of which calls the API, mutates the one or two fields it owns, then persists with r.Save(ctx, ship) - a WHOLE-ROW upsert built from the caller's snapshot:

  ship_repository.go:294  Navigate      -> owns nav_status, location, arrival_time, fuel
  ship_repository.go:346  Dock          -> owns nav_status          (Save at :368)
  ship_repository.go:379  Orbit         -> owns nav_status          (Save at :404)
  ship_repository.go:415  Refuel        -> owns fuel_current        (Save at :433)
  ship_repository.go:460  SetFlightMode -> owns flight_mode         (Save at :481)

Dock is the clearest illustration: it mutates exactly one field via ship.EnsureDocked(), then writes every column on the row. NONE of these five own cargo_units, cargo_inventory, assignment_status, container_id, assigned_at, or dedicated_fleet - yet all five write all of them, from a snapshot the code has no reason to believe is current.

CONFIRMED CONSEQUENCES (both observed in prod era 5, both already cost real money)
- sp-7oxeo: released ownership resurrected -> hull permanently orphaned. 5x on one hull in one day. Patched by preserving the ownership columns in Save's conflict branch.
- sp-in36a: cargo columns lag -> auto-liquidation dispatched against empty hulls, 6 spawns in 80min, zero cargo sold, each stealing the hull off contract work.

Anything else keyed off a cached ship column has the same exposure. These are the two we happened to notice.

THE FIX
Each operation persists ONLY the columns it owns. A targeted per-operation update, not a whole-row upsert from a caller-held entity. The alternative - routing through SaveWithRetry so the write reloads first - is the established sp-wa7c migration pattern and acceptable, but column-scoping is the more honest expression of what these methods actually do.

KEEP sp-7oxeo's preserve in place as defence in depth. It is cheap, it is proven, and Save remains reachable from other callers.

BLAST RADIUS IS THE WHOLE GAME. This is the nav write path for every ship on every flight. It needs the full suite green plus behavioural tests per operation, not a quick diff.
close_reason: Closed

title: DRIFT must be unreachable by policy: three paths still select it, and the model rates it faster than CRUISE
description:
ADMIRAL RULING (2026-07-26): "the navigate command never allows DRIFT. It only burns and refuels on the way." That is the intended design. The code does not enforce it - DRIFT is reachable from at least three independent places, and a production ship drifted an 885-second leg that CRUISE does in ~128s.

WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD, NOT THREE: the three defects below are the same policy hole seen from three angles, they sit in the same two files, and fixing any one alone still leaves DRIFT reachable. Fix them together.

1. ShouldPreventDriftMode CANNOT PREVENT DRIFT (ship_fuel_service.go:159). Its first guard is
     if segmentFlightMode != shared.FlightModeDrift { return false }
   so it only acts when the mode is ALREADY DRIFT. It is a "top off before you drift" nicety, not a "never drift" rule. A ship on a fuel station with a low tank and a planned BURN leg departs under-fuelled. (Previously filed as sp-3l9vs - fold it in and close that as a duplicate.)

2. THE AFFORDABILITY CLAMP LANDS ON DRIFT (route_executor.go, the downgrade path). It downgrades to whatever SelectOptimalFlightMode returns, and its own comment concedes DRIFT is the unguarded floor: DriftModeStrategy.CanUse is unconditional and DRIFT's FuelCost floors at 1, so ANY tank >= 1 "affords" DRIFT. Degrading is silent and unbounded.

3. NAVIGABILITY IS DEFINED AS DRIFT (ship_fuel_service.go CanShipNavigateTo, comment: "using the most fuel-efficient mode (DRIFT)"). The feasibility test itself assumes drifting is acceptable, so callers asking "can I get there" are answered "yes, by drifting".

AGGRAVATOR, fix in the same lane: FlightModeDrift.TimeMultiplier = 26 vs FlightModeCruise = 31 (shared/flight_mode.go:24-25). LOWER means faster, so the model claims DRIFT is FASTER than CRUISE. Production measured DRIFT ~7x SLOWER (885s vs ~128s on distance 123.81). Every travel-time estimate, ETA, tour/VRP cost and mode ranking is inverted for DRIFT - which is precisely why the fallback looks cheap. (Previously filed as sp-4anpp - fold it in and close that as a duplicate.)
   CAUTION: grep every TimeMultiplier consumer before changing the constant. Some call site may already compensate for the inversion; fixing the constant blind would then double the error.

TARGET BEHAVIOUR: refuel-or-fail, never silently degrade to DRIFT. If a leg cannot be flown at CRUISE or better, the correct move is to refuel (the planner already marks refuel stops - RouteSegment.RequiresRefuel, markLastSegmentForRefuel) or to fail loudly so the caller replans. A stranded-but-visible ship beats a ship that quietly takes 7x longer.

ESCAPE HATCH TO KEEP: there is one legitimate DRIFT use - refuel_retry.go:228 navigates to an alternate waypoint in DRIFT as a last-resort rescue for an already-stranded ship. Keep that path; it is the recovery of last resort, not a routine mode choice. Whatever policy you add must still permit it.

DO NOT weaken any money guard, and do not touch the sp-6n1bi fuel-reserve fix (route.go FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment) - it is correct and deployed; build on it.
close_reason: Closed

title: DRIFT TimeMultiplier is inverted: the model says DRIFT is faster than CRUISE, prod measured it ~7x slower
description:
FlightModeDrift.TimeMultiplier = 26 and FlightModeCruise = 31 (internal/domain/shared/flight_mode.go:24-25). A LOWER multiplier means faster, so our model claims DRIFT is FASTER than CRUISE. It is not.

MEASURED IN PROD (era 5, TORWIND-1, leg X1-KP23-B29 -> X1-KP23-I53, distance 123.81): the API gave a DRIFT arrival 885 seconds out. CRUISE does that leg in roughly 128 seconds. DRIFT is ~7x SLOWER, and our constants say it is faster.

CONSEQUENCE: everything that reasons about travel time is inverted for DRIFT - ETA estimates, route/tour cost comparisons, the VRP hop matrix, and any planner that weighs a DRIFT fallback. It makes the DRIFT fallback look CHEAP to the planner precisely when it is catastrophically expensive, so a planner may choose to strand a ship rather than avoid it.

Found while fixing sp-6n1bi (the greedy BURN upgrade). Not fixed there because it is a separate defect on a separate seam, and correcting a shared constant needs its own blast-radius check.

WHEN FIXING: grep every consumer of TimeMultiplier before changing the value - route planners, the tour/VRP cost model, ETA display, and anything that ranks modes. A constant this widely read cannot be flipped blind; some call site may already be compensating for the inversion, and fixing the constant would then double the error.

title: Refuel never fills the tank: 4 refuels in 6 minutes, frigate still at 121/400, every leg downgraded
description:
OBSERVED IN PROD, era 5 (TORWIND player 5, binary 9ae03194). The command frigate refuels constantly and the tank never fills, so every contract leg runs in a degraded flight mode and the whole contract cycle crawls.

EVIDENCE (daemon.log, frigate TORWIND-1, all within six minutes):
  12:10:30  Refuel transaction recorded in ledger
  12:13:24  Ship performing planned refuel
  12:14:26  Ship performing opportunistic refuel
  12:15:59  Ship performing planned refuel
  12:16:00  Ship flight mode upgraded after refuel
  12:17:35  Ship flight mode downgraded - insufficient fuel for planned mode   <-- 95s after the refuel
Live state after a forced ship refresh: fuel 121/400, cargo 35/40, IN_TRANSIT.
31 refuel events in this era so far.

So the ship refuels, is immediately judged affordable, and is back under the bar within ~95 seconds - and after four refuels in six minutes the tank sits at 121/400, i.e. under a third full. Refuelling is running; it is not restoring the tank.

CONSEQUENCE: route_executor.go:456 affordability clamp fires repeatedly and downgrades the leg to SelectOptimalFlightMode's choice. That clamp is correct and is doing its job (it prevents an un-fuelable BURN and an API 4203 crash) - the defect is upstream, in whatever decides how much fuel to buy.

NOTE ON A CLAIM I COULD NOT VERIFY: the downgrade log does not name the target mode and the local ship row carries no flightMode column, so I could NOT confirm the ship is in DRIFT. SelectOptimalFlightMode returns CRUISE whenever fuel covers it and DRIFT only as a last resort. Do not assume DRIFT - determine the actual mode as part of the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSE (do not assume): why does a refuel not fill the tank? Candidates - the refuel buys only enough for the next leg rather than topping up; a budget/affordability cap on the fuel purchase (treasury was down to ~81k after a large contract goods purchase, so a cost-gated partial fill is plausible); the market's FUEL supply is limited at that waypoint; or units-vs-fuel-units confusion in the purchase amount. Compare what the refuel path requests against what the API returns.

IMPACT: on the critical path. Contract income is what funds the first hauler and ultimately GATE entry, and every contract leg is currently slowed by a fuel-starved ship. This is the ONLY earner in a cold start.

MUST NOT: weaken the route_executor affordability clamp - it exists to prevent an un-fuelable BURN 4203 crash. Fix the fuelling, not the guard.
close_reason: Closed

title: An already-wedged purchasing frigate has no release path — the self-lock survives the sp-m0u51 fix
description:
sp-m0u51 makes the pivot's ask survive a restart, so the guard no longer frees the earner into a stall. It does NOT recover a fleet that is ALREADY wedged: once the frigate carries the purchasing dedication with zero haulers and an unaffordable ask, nothing in code releases it.

THE CLOSED CYCLE (verified in source):
- bootstrapFrigateRetirer.RetireFromContract is the primitive that would clear it (AssignFleet(..., "", pid) clears any tag), but its only caller is gated on obs.CommandFrigateOnContract (run_bootstrap_income.go:60). A purchasing-dedicated frigate carries "purchasing", not "contract", so it never fires.
- The frigate contract-loop start requires !obs.CommandFrigatePurchasing (run_bootstrap_income.go:78), so the earner can never restart.
Result: sole earner parked as the purchasing ship with nothing it can afford, treasury frozen, permanent.

REPRODUCED: staging TORWIND_DEV16 2026-07-26, treasury frozen at 423434 for 1.5h+, income/hr decayed to 0, 14 contracts fulfilled then nothing.

PROPOSED SHAPE (from the sp-m0u51 lane, not built):
- CONDITION: zero haulers AND frigate purchasing-dedicated AND ask-on-record > 0 AND treasury-ask < contractWorkingCapitalFloor AND no contract loop running. This is exactly 'the pivot would have HELD had it been evaluated now' — it reuses the guard's own predicate rather than inventing a second one.
- ACTION: clear the dedication via the existing retirer primitive. The loop-start gate then fires on the next tick unaided. No new mechanism, ZERO spend.
- SHAPE: condition-gated on an already-broken, self-limiting state, never spends, RULINGS #4 intact — same shape as the sp-2v69u rescue exception the Admiral authorized.

ORDERING (load-bearing): this MUST land AFTER sp-m0u51 (already merged, a6242990). Without the durable ask the release would oscillate — release, loop restarts, next tick the guard sees a false 0 and re-frees. With the durable ask in place the guard HOLDS after release, so the cycle is stable.

WATCH: the frigate may be mid-navigation to the yard when released; handle that interaction rather than assuming it is idle.
close_reason: Closed

title: Contract-hub set is recomputed every tick from the active contract — the hauler target is demand-driven, not fixed
description:
Bootstrap re-senses contract hubs EVERY TICK from the active contract's goods, producing the exact 'demand FLICKERS' pathology the signed-off contract-scaler design (sp-9le3x) exists to eliminate.

AUTHORITATIVE DOCTRINE (sp-9le3x DESIGN, economy-analyst 2026-07-21, Admiral-proposed, SIGNED OFF):
  'a SPECIFIC contract auto-scaler leaning on FIXED facts — home-system waypoint GEOMETRY is static +
   contract SUPPLY/DEMAND is fixed (analyst-analyzed, ~2 viable hubs, RULINGS #14 home-system sourcing).
   Because both are fixed, PRECOMPUTE an OPTIMAL FIXED algorithm instead of re-sensing every tick'
  'SIMPLIFICATIONS (what the stationarity makes unnecessary): Goods-to-stock: a constant list, not a
   ranking or a runtime read. Counts (hulls/stockers/depth): constants, not runtime physics formulas.'
  MOTIVATION section names the failure directly: 'demand FLICKERS (desired 0<->2 -> reassign-then-strand)'.

Hub geometry is STATIC and ERA-INDEPENDENT. It is not derived per tick, and it is not a function of
whichever contract is currently active.

OFFENDING CODE — run_bootstrap_income.go, actIncome:
  hubs := selectContractHubs(obs.Markets, obs.ContractGoods)
  desired := len(hubs); if desired > haulerTarget { desired = haulerTarget }
selectContractHubs gates viability on sourcing >= 1 of the CURRENT contract's goods (minHubSourceableGoods),
so the viable set — and therefore 'desired', which IS the hauler buy gate — moves with the active contract.

OBSERVED LIVE (staging TORWIND_DEV16, 2026-07-26): hubs flickered 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 1 within a single cold
start while market coverage was COMPLETE and STABLE at 29/29. The churn is 100% from ContractGoods, not
from scanning. This is the documented desired-0<->2 flicker, reproduced.

IMPACT: the contract fleet's size is set by whichever contract COSMIC last offered rather than by a fixed
plan. A contract whose goods source at one market collapses desired to 1 and stalls the ramp at 1 hauler
despite hauler_target=4.

FIX DIRECTION (per sp-9le3x, NOT a re-sensing variant): bootstrap must stop deriving hub counts at runtime.
Hubs/counts come from the precomputed fixed plan grounded in static home-system geometry (~2 viable hubs),
not from a per-tick read of contract goods. Align bootstrap's INCOME ramp with the fixed-plan model the
contract scaler already implements; do not invent a third hub-selection path (see sp-b2zb: converge the
existing paths, do not add).

DO NOT weaken any money guard or the staged one-buy-per-tick rule.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bootstrap phase gauge reads all-zero during COLDSTART — phase list not updated with the enum
description:
Shipped by the phase collapse (sp-3nmka). bootstrapKnownPhases in gobot/internal/adapters/metrics/bootstrap_metrics.go:11 still reads {DATA, INCOME, GATE, EXPANSION}. COLDSTART is absent, so RecordPhase(COLDSTART) zeroes all four known series and never sets a COLDSTART series at all.

Effect: for the entire cold start the gauge is all-zero, so the gate-construction dashboard panel (expr 'spacetraders_daemon_bootstrap_phase == 1') shows NOTHING — indistinguishable from a dead coordinator. It self-corrects only on reaching GATE.

Fix: bootstrapKnownPhases = {COLDSTART, GATE, EXPANSION}, plus a regression test driven from the exported Phase constants so the gauge list cannot silently drift from the enum again (that drift IS this bug). Also stale in the same file: the collector doc comment cites 'the DATA phase'/'the INCOME phase' for the two counters, and the Help strings on bootstrap_probes_total / bootstrap_haulers_total say the same. gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/gate-construction.json:15 description reads 'DATA / INCOME / GATE / COMPLETE' (COMPLETE was already stale before this).

Also required: RULINGS #5 amendment recording the Admiral's bounding of the parametrize rule — see the separate brief.

title: C: Reduce bootstrap knobs from 17 to 2 — fix the parameters as constants
description:
Parent epic sp-7ie7i. Admiral rationale: the game does not change, every INCOME to GATE run is the same, so these are not operational values.

KEEP TUNABLE, only these two:
- tick_secs — a real operational lever for API pacing (see the open API-budget P0s)

FIX AS CONSTANTS. For each, remove the config.yaml key, the prefixed launch key, the tune-registry entry, the command field, the run-config field, the live overlay and the default fallback; keep the value as a documented const:
probe_target 3, hauler_target 4, gate_worker_target 4, gate_min_haulers 2, gate_reentry_construction_pct 5, gate_reentry_streak_ticks 3, probe_ship_type SHIP_PROBE, hauler_ship_type SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER

- income_bar — cosmetic once the E-2 removal lands. It survives only inside two log strings, which can report the realized rate without a bar to compare against.
- defer_probe_to_freshsizer — removed by child A
- gate_surplus_floor — fix at 500000 as a constant. BETTER OPTION worth costing separately: derive the war chest from the construction site's ACTUAL required materials rather than a placeholder, which removes the guess as well as the knob.

OPEN DECISION for the Admiral, do NOT action without an answer: dry_run costs about 19 branches, one in nearly every action function, and is the largest remaining per-function complexity after the guards. Removing it is a large simplification but loses the observe-only safety valve.

DO NOT TOUCH: ContractWorkingCapitalFloor 150000 and common.ImmutableReserveFloor 50000. RULINGS 4 and 5 hard floors, already deliberately non-tunable.

BLOCKED BY: this cannot land before the in-flight dead-knob lane sp-71fvl (coverage_bar, gate_income_bar, min_contract_earners) and before child A removes defer_probe_to_freshsizer.
notes:
ADMIRAL DECISION: remove dry_run. The open decision is resolved — dry_run goes.

Scope: DryRun field on RunBootstrapCoordinatorCommand and bootstrapRunConfig; dry_run on config.BootstrapConfig; the bootstrap_dry_run prefixed launch key (key list, inject, OptionalBool read); the per-tick WARN in reconcileOnce; the dry-run branch of the heartbeat delta string; the now-dead reconcileResult.WouldBuy field; and roughly 19 'if cfg.DryRun' blocks across run_bootstrap_reconcile.go, run_bootstrap_income.go and run_bootstrap_gate.go.

Each dry-run block sits AFTER its readiness and nil-collaborator guards and BEFORE the side effect, so deletion is mechanical — but verify that per site rather than assuming. In acquireProbesToTarget the block also does 'spent += price; continue' to model cumulative spend; removing it means the loop simply buys, which is correct. Tests whose subject is dry-run behavior are deleted outright, since the behavior genuinely no longer exists.

EXPANSION freeze still applies: leave the dry-run branches inside actExpansion, launchHandoff and ensureStandingHandoff ALONE — that session owns them.

DECISION 2: gate_surplus_floor stays a CONSTANT at 500000. Do not attempt to derive it from the construction bill in this bead — the gate materials are MANUFACTURED by production chains, not purchased, so there is no bill price to read; deriving it properly means modelling chain input costs against required output volume. Separate bead if wanted.

title: B: Collapse DATA and INCOME into one cold-start phase
description:
Parent epic sp-7ie7i.

DATA and INCOME already run in parallel: the tick dispatch runs actIncome during the DATA phase, and the label only decides whether actData ALSO runs. actData self-guards to a no-op once probes are at target and scouting, so the distinction can only ever skip a no-op.

CHANGE:
- Phase enum: replace PhaseData and PhaseIncome with one cold-start phase. Keep PhaseGate and PhaseExpansion exactly as they are.
- derivePhase becomes: ConstructionComplete to EXPANSION (frozen branch, do not touch); ConstructionStarted to GATE; gateFunded to GATE; else COLD. This deletes the ProbeCount-at-target and ProbesScouting branch entirely.
- Dispatch: the cold-start phase runs actData then actIncome, both self-guarding. Deletes the parallel-window special case.
- Blocker precedence: preserve today's behavior, where the scanning blocker outranks the income blocker, but express it as plain ordering rather than a phase-conditional override.
- The early-launch window condition currently reading phase is DATA or phase is INCOME becomes phase is COLD.

MUST SURVIVE: obs.ProbesScouting stays on the Observation. It still feeds the heartbeat and the nextAction line; it just stops driving the phase.

DEPLOY NOTE: the spacetraders_bootstrap_phase gauge label set changes — DATA and INCOME disappear. Any Grafana panel or alert matching phase DATA or phase INCOME must be updated with the deploy. Check dashboards before merging.

title: A: Static buyer ownership by range — delete the runtime arbitration mesh
description:
Parent epic sp-7ie7i.

DELETE:
- deferProbeBuyToFreshsizer, the defer_probe_to_freshsizer knob, and obs.FreshsizerActive
- deferHaulerBuyToAutosizer and the contractHaulerTierSaturation constant. The in-source comment already marks this LEGACY single-buyer arbitration for the autosizer's DELETED contract-delivery scaling path, superseded by the dedicated contract scaler.
- the delay-launch coupling: the obs.TradeHullCount greater-or-equal-1 precondition on the contract-scaler early launch

NEW RULE: bootstrap owns seed acquisitions unconditionally and buys nothing beyond them — probes 0 to probe_target, contract hauler number 1, trade hull number 1, gate workers 0 to gate_worker_target. Standing coordinators own all growth above the seed and are launched unconditionally during cold start. No runtime is-the-other-buyer-alive check anywhere.

Money guards untouched (RULINGS 4). EXPANSION frozen.

title: EPIC: Simplify the bootstrap coordinator — static buyer ownership, one cold-start phase, fixed parameters
description:
The bootstrap coordinator re-implements the cold-start half of five standing coordinators' jobs (probe buying, contract scaling, trade seeding, gate-worker buying, keeping a hull earning) and then negotiates handing each back at runtime. That negotiation IS the complexity: two deferral mechanisms, a tier constant, a delay-launch coupling, and three observation fields whose only purpose is answering 'is the other buyer alive?'. One deferral is already documented in-source as LEGACY for a deleted code path.

Scale: ~3300 lines of reconciler + ~1400 of ports for a component whose job is 'reach a built gate, then exit'. 17 knobs, of which 3 were found fully dead in one session and 1 more cosmetic.

ENGINEERING.md 5: three or more bugs sharing one root cause means fighting the architecture — file the structural bead instead of patch N+1.

Children: static buyer ownership (A), collapse DATA/INCOME (B), knob reduction (C).

SCOPE FREEZE: the EXPANSION phase is being rewritten in a separate session. actExpansion, launchHandoff, ensureStandingHandoff, expansionHoldStreaks, expansionHandoffRetryTicks, PhaseExpansion and the ConstructionComplete branch of derivePhase are OFF LIMITS. Keep the HandoffLauncher interface signature stable.

FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED: child C hardcodes values that RULINGS 5 says must be config. That needs an explicit RULINGS 5 amendment (Admiral rationale: the game does not change, every INCOME->GATE run is the same), or the next session will read the ruling and re-parametrize.

title: Boot-standing launches starve when container recovery exhausts the shared 30s recoveryCtx
description:
Observed live 2026-07-25T22:29Z boot (build e645d6c0): the recovery goroutine in daemon_server.go:703 runs RecoverRunningContainers, recoverStorageOperations, ensureBootStandingCoordinators and reloadDepotRegistryAtBoot all under ONE context.WithTimeout(s.runCtx, 30*time.Second). Re-adopting ~250 containers against a saturated 2 req/s limiter ate the whole budget ('Warning: Ship startup sync failed ... rate limiter error: context deadline exceeded' in the boot log), so ensureBootStandingCoordinators ran with an expired context and launched NOTHING — silently: the only fmt.Printf warnings inside it fire on state-check/launch errors, and an already-dead ctx apparently short-circuits before those paths produce output. No bootstrap container existed for 1h48m after the deploy.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: on every previous boot the bootstrap container was RUNNING at restart (the sp-ycrml spin kept it alive), so recovery RE-ADOPTED it and boot-standing had nothing to do. The first boot where bootstrap was genuinely STOPPED (manually, after the spin) was the first boot where the launch mattered — and it starved.

IMPACT: mature fleet mid-era — negligible (standing coordinators re-adopted; bootstrap's only remaining job is the idempotent hand-off). ERA-5 mid-era restarts — real: any restart with a large container population + saturated limiter silently skips boot-standing launches of every stopped standing coordinator (sizer, scout-post, construction drain, bootstrap), and nothing retries until the NEXT restart.

FIX SHAPE (verify in code): give ensureBootStandingCoordinators (and reloadDepotRegistryAtBoot) their own context/budget independent of recovery's, or run boot-standing BEFORE the expensive re-adoption sweep (its EnsureRunning path is idempotent and skips RUNNING/PENDING rows, so ordering it first is safe by its own contract); make an expired-ctx skip LOUD either way.
acceptance_criteria: a boot whose recovery exhausts its budget still launches every boot-standing coordinator; an intentionally-expired ctx produces a visible warning naming each skipped launch; era-5-realistic test: many containers + slow limiter + a STOPPED bootstrap row => bootstrap launched
close_reason: Closed

title: isShipyardWaypoint returns false for an uncached waypoint — the gate between a cold map and first hull-price knowledge
description:
Surfaced by the era-4 cold-start audit as the ONE real cold-map concern it found (pre-existing; not introduced by any of the nine era-4 merges).

ShipyardScanner.isShipyardWaypoint reads the SHIPYARD trait from the local waypoint cache. That read is deliberately era-agnostic and TTL-agnostic (a physical trait never changes), which is correct — but it returns FALSE for a waypoint that is not cached at all. On a cold map almost nothing is cached, so the piggybacked shipyard scan never fires, and the fleet acquires no hull-price knowledge until waypoints happen to be cached by some other path.

WHY IT MATTERS AT COLD START: shipyard inventory is what the fleet autosizer and the probe buyer price their purchases against. NearestYardsSelling ranks candidates on the stored PurchasePrice, and the autosizer's scannedYardFallback returns cached prices as readable=true, which is what unblocks a heavy buy that would otherwise fail closed. No scan means no prices means those paths stay blocked or fall back to live reads on a budget that is already the binding constraint.

NOT URGENT AND NOT A STALL: the audit found no cold-start stall from it, and other paths do populate waypoints over time. This is about how QUICKLY era 5 learns where it can buy hulls, not whether it ever does.

INVESTIGATE BEFORE FIXING: establish what actually populates the waypoint cache early in an era and how long the gap really lasts, before changing the trait read. A false-negative on an uncached waypoint is the SAFE direction for a scan gate (it skips, it never invents a shipyard); making it fetch would put an API call on every non-shipyard waypoint visit, which is exactly the class of waste era 4 spent the day removing. The fix may well be to populate the cache earlier rather than to change this read.
acceptance_criteria: the true cold-start delay to first shipyard price is measured; any fix does not add an API call per non-shipyard waypoint visit; the trait read never invents a shipyard it has not seen
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-06: INVESTIGATED, ACCEPTANCE SATISFIED BY MEASUREMENT, NOTHING TO FIX -- closing. The code is unchanged: isShipyardWaypoint (shipyard_scanner.go:281) returns false on a nil repo, a read error, and an absent trait, exactly as described. But this bead's acceptance asks for a MEASUREMENT of the cold-start window, and the window is small: first container and first shipyard scan are minutes apart at most this era (the triaging lane measured ~12 min; the lead's independent query on a looser log pattern returned seconds -- both refute the open-ended gap the bead feared, though the exact figure differs by what was matched). The bead's own analysis says the false-negative is the SAFE direction and 'the fix may well be to populate the cache earlier rather than to change this read'. At this scale neither is warranted. METHOD NOTE worth keeping: the lane's FIRST measurement used min(last_scanned) from shipyard_inventory and returned ~40 hours -- wrong, because ReplaceScan OVERWRITES last_scanned, so it reports the oldest SURVIVING row, not the first scan. It caught this because the fleet bought haulers on 08-04 and could not have been pricing hulls 40 hours before it knew any prices. Measuring a field whose semantics do not match the question -- the same error class as the derived-vs-declared identity trap.
close_reason: Closed

title: Era-5 arming ledger: knobs that must be re-armed or re-checked after the era boundary
description:
Era 4 ends 2026-07-26T13:00Z. This is the checklist of arming state that does NOT survive the boundary correctly, or that is deliberately disarmed for cold start and needs re-arming later. Compiled during the era-4 cold-start audit.

WHAT PERSISTS AND WHAT DOES NOT (the load-bearing distinction, per CLI-PRIMER §3):
- config.yaml (source pattern B) is a FILE and is gitignored — it persists across the boundary verbatim. Every arm written there carries into era 5.
- Pattern-A persisted container config does NOT carry: era 5 gets a new player_id, hence new containers, rebuilt from code defaults. Every live 'tune' write made during era 4 is lost at the boundary.

ITEM 1 — gate_reconcile_enabled (config.yaml:231) is FALSE, deliberately disarmed 2026-07-19 for cold-start reasons, with an in-file note to 're-arm (true) + restart once the home post is adequately manned / past cold start'. Because config.yaml persists, era 5 correctly starts disarmed — which is right for cold start — but NOTHING re-arms it automatically and no alarm fires. Consequence while disarmed: the retroactive uncharted-frontier-gate sweep does not run. ACTION: re-arm mid-era-5 once past cold start, then restart the daemon.

ITEM 2 — era-4 live tunes that will reset to code defaults, listed so the reset is deliberate rather than a surprise. Most of these SHOULD reset (they were mature-fleet adaptations and the defaults are better for a cold map): freshsizer max_probe_fleet 100 (default 40), max_probes_per_system 2 (default 8), max_spend_per_cycle 2000000 (default 500000), purchase_cooldown_secs 300 (default 60), sla_seconds 10800 (default 3600), sla_seconds_restricted 10800, sla_seconds_weak 28800; frontier discover_scan_balance 1 (default 50 — cold start NEEDS discovery, so the reset is actively correct), reach_mode 1 (default 2), reserved_freshness_floor 55 (default 0), max_probe_fleet 100.
Also resetting: freshsizer hold_unscanned_market_posts 1 (default 0). This one was initially assessed as a cold-start hazard; the cold-start audit lane reports the premises hold but the conclusion does not — see its final report before acting on it.

ITEM 3 — ENGINEERING §6 violation, cosmetic, pre-existing: run_tour_coordinator.go:1933 carries a bare bead-id in a source comment. Also gofmt -l is dirty on gobot/internal/application/bootstrap/commands/run_bootstrap_muc5x_test.go and run_bootstrap_scaled_gate_test.go, both pre-existing on main and untouched by any era-4 lane.
acceptance_criteria: every item above is either actioned or consciously accepted before era 5 cold start; gate_reconcile_enabled has an owner and a trigger condition for re-arming mid-era

title: Arrival-state desync throws 2,480 Navigate-400s and 299 Dock-400s a day, some cascading to unrecoverable container crashes
description:
Found by the sp-v68tv attribution lane while measuring dock causes. This is a CORRECTNESS bug that also wastes API, and the crash cascade makes it the more serious of the two.

MEASURED over 24h (Prometheus increase() on spacetraders_daemon_api_requests_total, cross-validated against Postgres): 2,480 Navigate calls returning 400 and 299 Dock calls returning API code 4214 ('ship is in transit'). Together ~2,779 wasted calls/day ~= 1.8% of a saturated 2.00 req/s budget — but the lane reports SOME OF THESE CASCADE TO UNRECOVERABLE CONTAINER CRASHES, which costs far more than the requests.

The daemon believes a hull has arrived (or is dockable) when the server does not. 4214 is the server rejecting an action because the ship is still in transit, so the local arrival state is running ahead of the authoritative one.

Worth establishing: whether this is a clock/rounding issue on arrival_time, an event-ordering race between the arrival event and the next action, or optimistic local state written before the server confirms. The crash path matters most — a wasted request is cheap, an unrecoverable container is not.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: a separate intermittent nil-pointer panic on the container-SHUTDOWN path (releaseShipAssignments -> SaveWithRetry, container_runner.go:1217) is filed separately and is suspected to be the sp-wa7c SaveWithRetry migration. Do not conflate the two — that one only reproduces under full-suite parallel load.
acceptance_criteria: the desync root cause is identified with evidence; Navigate-400 and Dock-4214 rates fall materially; no container crash traceable to arrival-state desync; local arrival state never leads the server's
notes: MERGED to main as c67c8d98 (gate green, full suite). Root cause: NOT optimistic local state — a LOST navigate response (server applied, client timed out) meant StartTransit never ran locally; the blind network-error retry hit 4214 and every plan ran from a phantom position. 315 of 417 unrecoverable container crashes over 2 days were 4214-coded via the runner's lifetime restart budget. Fix: adopt the server transit on 4214 (navigate/dock/orbit), heal same-destination duplicates silently, typed ErrShipInTransit elsewhere, route executor waits adopted transits out via existing event machinery; SyncShipFromAPI arms the arrival scheduler mid-transit. Gate review added pins for three one-sided reconcile arms (parked-elsewhere race, non-4214 navigate/dock gates). NOT YET DEPLOYED — daemon runs e645d6c0; deploy rides with the probe-sensing final merge. LIVE ACCEPTANCE STILL OPEN: navigate-400s/day collapsing to seed rate, dock-4214s vanishing, zero 4214-coded container deaths. FOLLOW-UPS BEADED by the lane: jump-chain 4214 adoption; warp top-off dock; P2 doWithRetry blind re-POST of MONEY calls (lost BuyCargo response = silent double-buy, RULINGS #4-adjacent — prioritise next session).
close_reason: Closed

title: ListShips burns an extra empty page every sync and re-syncs the whole fleet per reconcile tick (12.8% of API budget)
description:
Found by the sp-v68tv attribution lane. List Ships is 19,473 calls/day = 12.8% of a saturated 2.00 req/s budget — the third-largest consumer after Navigate and Get Market.

TWO DEFECTS, one trivial and one structural.

1. EXTRA EMPTY PAGE (trivial, no safety tradeoff). SpaceTradersClient.ListShips (gobot/internal/adapters/api/client.go:228) is hardcoded limit=20 and its pagination loop parses meta.Total but NEVER USES IT, so it always fetches one page past the end to discover it is empty. At 253 hulls that is 14 HTTP calls per logical sync where 13 suffice — ~7% of all List Ships traffic, ~0.9% of total budget, for a one-line use of a field already being parsed. limit=20 is the API maximum (verified against api/openapi.json: maximum 20, default 10), so page size cannot be reduced.

2. FULL-FLEET SYNC PER RECONCILE TICK (structural, the larger share). Callers: bootstrapRefresher.RefreshFleet (gobot/internal/adapters/grpc/bootstrap_ports.go:136) runs per reconcile tick; negotiate_contract.go:123 before every negotiation (105/day); an ~hourly resync scheduler; and boot. Every one of those pages through ALL 253 hulls — including 206 satellites — to learn about whatever changed. Worth asking whether a targeted Get Ship (currently only 2.4/min) or a change-scoped sync can serve most callers, and whether every reconcile tick genuinely needs fleet-wide state.

Fleet size makes this worse superlinearly in wall-clock terms: each added hull is another 1/20th of a page on EVERY sync by EVERY caller.
acceptance_criteria: the trailing empty page is eliminated using the already-parsed meta.Total; callers that do not need fleet-wide state use a narrower read; List Ships share of API traffic falls materially from 12.8%; no caller observes staler ship state than it does today
notes:
=== BUILD LANE (branch worktree-agent-af14a36b42794c0c6) — DEFECT 1 SHIPPED, DEFECT 2 REFUSED ===

DEFECT 1 (trailing empty page): SHIPPED, commit ebbc21f1. ListShips now stops when the page
came back SHORT *and* meta.total accounts for every hull already read. Measured: 253-hull
sync 14 -> 13 HTTP calls (-7.1% of List Ships, ~1,390 calls/day, ~0.9% of the 152,275 budget).
Both signals are required because either alone truncates: a server that under-fills a page
(short but not done), or a total gone stale against a fleet growing mid-pagination (done but
not short). Truncation is not a cheap error here — SyncAllFromAPI treats a successful response
as the authoritative fleet and reconcileFleetToLive DELETES every row missing from it. Absent
or non-positive meta falls back to today's empty-page probe. A fleet ending exactly on a page
boundary therefore keeps its trailing probe BY DESIGN (measure-zero in production; 253 is not a
multiple of 20). limit=20 confirmed as the API maximum (openapi.json: maximum 20, default 10) —

     returns all 253 hulls for 13 calls; Get Ship is 1 call per hull. Crossover is 13 hulls.

  c) NO SERVER-SIDE NARROWING EXISTS. /my/ships accepts only page and limit (openapi.json).

     interleaved in symbol order.
