     sync refreshes only a nav location feeding a home-system fallback that never changes.
     Interesting, but per (c) it buys no calls.

  e) CHANGE-SCOPED SYNC IS CIRCULAR HERE. The refresh is the phantom-cache guard (captain L47);
     its premise is that the daemon's own belief about ship state is unreliable. Selecting
     "ships whose state could have changed" from that same belief cannot detect a desync the
     daemon does not know about.

  f) FREQUENCY AND TICK RATE ARE NOT SEPARABLE. reconcileOnce fails the tick CLOSED on a
     refresh error (no action), so a tick without a fresh pool is a tick that does nothing.
     Refreshing every Nth tick is behaviourally identical to an Nx longer tick. Any code that
     reduced refresh frequency would be a responsiveness/staleness tradeoff — forbidden by this
     brief's own constraint, and already exposed as the live-tunable tick_secs knob
     (bounds 10..86400, applied next tick, no restart) which is the captain's call, not code's.

  g) THE BRIEF'S NEGOTIATE PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG. negotiate_contract.go:123 is NOT called
     "before every negotiation". It sits inside `if result != nil && (ErrorCode == 4214 ||
     ErrorCode == 4244)` — a cache-desync RECOVERY path. The handler comment says the opposite:
     "OPTIMIZED: Skip GetShip call - try negotiate first, handle dock error reactively". Its
     fleet-wide scope is deliberate (cluster lesson L61: a desync strikes fleet-wide, so healing
     one ship leaves the rest poisoned and unable to self-heal). Narrowing it to a targeted Get
     Ship would revert a documented fix. Bounded above by 105 syncs/day even if EVERY negotiation
     errored; realistically a handful.

  Remaining callers are noise: hourly resync ~24/day x 13 = ~312 calls (0.2% of budget), boot

title: Dock/Orbit costs 3.9 API calls per transaction — attribute before fixing
description:
Measured live over 89.5 minutes: Dock 365 + Orbit 379 = 744 calls against 191 transactions = 3.9 calls per transaction, roughly 17% of a saturated 2.00 req/s budget.

Ideally a hull docks once, transacts every good it can at that market, and orbits once — so the ratio should fall as goods-per-visit rises. 3.9 suggests either one transaction per dock cycle, or docking for reasons that do not transact.

DO NOT FIX BEFORE ATTRIBUTING. Some of this is structurally required: a ship must be in orbit to navigate and docked to trade or refuel. The addressable share is unknown. Measure transactions-per-dock-cycle and the reasons for dock events that produce no transaction, then scope.

Three lanes this era correctly refused briefs that asserted a cause without measuring it. Measure first.
acceptance_criteria: dock events attributed to cause with counts; addressable share quantified; any fix preserves the dock-to-trade and orbit-to-navigate requirements
notes:
=== ATTRIBUTION (24h Prometheus increase() + Postgres; player_id=4) — VERDICT: STRUCTURAL, DO NOT FIX ===

BUDGET: Dock 5069 + Orbit 4807 = 9876 of 152,275 daily calls = 6.5% (not 17%; the 17%
figure came from an 89.5-min probe-light window).

RATIO, three ways:
  9876 / 2797 cargo txns (Buy 1506 + Sell 1291)      = 3.53  <- the brief's number
  9876 / 7022 market txns (cargo + 4225 Refuel)      = 1.41
  9876 / 4766 SUCCESSFUL DOCKS                       = 2.07  <- vs structural floor 2.00
The dock/orbit sequencing is 96.5% efficient. All 0.07 of slack is the 299 failed docks.

BRIEF PREMISE #1 REFUTED — goods ARE batched. 1427 trade visits / 2758 cargo txns =
1.93 txns per visit (741 visits x1, 347 x2, 339 x3+, max 45). Not ~1.

BRIEF PREMISE #2 CONFIRMED (with a twist) — 53% of docks carry no CARGO trade, but they
are not empty: they buy FUEL. Fuel is a market transaction with a credit cost.

DOCK ATTRIBUTION (24h):
  refuel-only stop (no cargo trade)   2703  53.3%   dock+orbit+refuel = 3 calls
  cargo-trade visit                   1427  28.2%   1424 of these ALSO refuel (same dock)
  contract accept/deliver/fulfill/negotiate, ship purchase, transfer, warehouse  ~636  12.6%
  failed dock (API 4214 in-transit)    299   5.9%
  total                               5069
Orbit 4807 ~= Dock 4766: one orbit per dock, no redundant orbit.

WHY: 46 fuel hulls fly 5503 legs/day and refuel on 0.75 of them.
  HEAVY_FREIGHTER 24 hulls, 2300 tank: 2094 refuels, avg fill 739 = 32% of tank, 0 planned
    (100% opportunistic), 1210 refuel-only.
  LIGHT_FREIGHTER 20 hulls,  600 tank: 2016 refuels, avg fill 397 = 66% of tank, 1476 refuel-only.
  206 probes: 25,829 legs, 0 refuels, 0 docks.
Cause: ConservativeRefuelStrategy (live, confirmed) tops off whenever fuel < 90% capacity.
ShouldRefuelAfterArrival is a flat percentage with NO next-leg lookahead — a heavy burns
32% of tank per leg so it trips the 90% bar every leg. CUT 1/2/3 (idempotent-dock skip,
stay-docked-after-refuel, skip-pre-departure-when-fuelled) already shipped; they are why the
per-stop cost is already 2.00.

ADDRESSABLE vs STRUCTURAL:
  structural  ~7300 calls/day  dock-to-trade + orbit-to-navigate + contract/purchase docks
  addressable ~2540 calls/day  1.7% of traffic — heavy-freighter excess refuels only
    (lights at 66% tank/fill are already at their integer floor; 600/397 = 1 leg per tank).
  Capturing it means running 2300-unit tanks to ~15% on a fleet already throwing 2480
  Navigate-400 and 299 Dock-400 per day from arrival-state desync (4214), some cascading to
  unrecoverable container crashes. Bad trade for 1.7%.

WHERE THE BUDGET ACTUALLY IS (24h): Navigate 30,635 (20.2%), Get Market 26,281 (17.3%),
List Ships 19,473 (12.8%), Get Jump Gate 16,779 (11.0%) = 61.3%. Dock+Orbit 6.5%.
LEAD (unbuilt, no safety tradeoff, 2x the dock/orbit prize): List Ships is
SpaceTradersClient.ListShips, hardcoded limit=20, and its loop ignores meta.Total so it always
burns one extra empty page — 14 HTTP calls per logical sync at 253 hulls. Callers:
bootstrapRefresher.RefreshFleet (per reconcile tick), negotiate_contract (before every
negotiation, 105/day), the ~hourly resync scheduler, boot.

title: tourInterSystemHops prices system pairs via the breadth-capped walk: silent 1-hop underpricing + fetch-through cost
description:
Surfaced by the sp-1ekrc lane while replacing the far-sink reach proof. Out of scope there and out of scope for sp-zj19z (that lane's decorator does not help it) — needs its own fix, by whoever picks up StoredHopDistances.

DEFECT. tourInterSystemHops still resolves system-pair distances through repositionNeighborsWithinJumps, which is breadth-capped at repositionBfsMaxSystems=64. In a dense cluster the walk truncates before reaching a pair, the distance goes unresolved, and the pair then silently defaults to the solver's flat 1-hop charge. A 3-hop crossing priced as 1 hop ranks roughly three times too well, so the planner picks tours whose travel cost it has understated.

Far-sink pairs are NOT affected: their proven distances override via mergeInterSystemHops. This is the base-set path only.

SECOND COST. The same walk reaches neighbours through gategraph.Connections, which is store-FIRST but falls through to a live GetJumpGate on a miss OR a stale set. So this path also burns live API on a budget that is already saturated (2.00 req/s server cap, running at or above it, 429s landing on Dock and Buy Cargo).

FIX SHAPE. gategraph.Service.StoredHopDistances (added in e3d90d53) is the primitive built for exactly this: one Adjacency pure store read plus an exact depth-bounded BFS with NO breadth cap, zero live API by construction. Uncached topology reads as unproven. Applying it here should both correct the pricing and remove the fetch-through burn.

CAUTION (cost this lane already paid once). RepositionPath is store-only but is the RELAXED probe/scout class that routes PAST unreadable gates, while the tour executor flies the STRICT resolver. Do not swap a strict caller onto it to save requests — that makes routing laxer than execution and strands a laden hull (RULINGS #4 weakening). Save requests by not fetching, never by relaxing which gates count as passable.
acceptance_criteria: base-set inter-system pairs resolve at their true gate distance or are refused, never silently defaulted to 1 hop; no live API on the pricing path; repositionBfsMaxSystems and the sp-jeou reposition path stay byte-identical; RED-first tests with mutations killed
notes:
MEASURED read-only against live era-4 (gate_edges, 921 systems, 49,240 base-set pairs). Two corrections to the original description:

1. THE UNDERPRICING MEASURES ZERO TODAY. Max gate degree in this universe is 9, so the breadth-capped walk never exhausts its 64-system budget before covering the tight allowedSystems cluster around home. It truncates only at the periphery, where no base-set allowed system lives. The defect is real in code (a RED test fails on a dense-enough graph) but LATENT, not firing. The 'a 3-hop crossing ranks three times too well' framing is not currently happening — do not treat this as a live revenue bug.

2. THE OBVIOUS FIX OVER-REFUSES CATASTROPHICALLY. StoredHopDistances refuses to expand THROUGH a stale system, and 32.9% of stored edge-sets are past the 24h TTL (median age 9.9h, p90 31h). Swapping it in wholesale would refuse 31.67% of base-set crossings today — charging 6 hops instead of 1 — rising to 47.65% and 60.60% as the graph ages between charting sweeps. Against PLAYBOOK §5 (wide multi-system tours out-earn single-system ~2.6x), that is a serious revenue regression traded for a defect measuring zero. Refusals from genuinely UNCACHED topology are only 0.77% (379 pairs) — staleness is the whole cause.

THE REAL PRIZE IS API, NOT PRICING. Per plan the current path touches a median 383 fetch-through Connections seams (p90 534, max 725), each a potential live GetJumpGate, and with 33% of sets stale a large fraction genuinely fetch. Get Jump Gate is ~30% of a saturated 2.00 req/s budget. Store-resolved cost is 0 live API and a median 11 adjacency reads.

SEPARATE CORRECTNESS BUG FOUND: an IMPASSABLE crossing (route exists only over an under-construction gate) also silently prices at 1 hop today. Independent of the breadth cap.

DIRECTION AUTHORIZED: stale-TOLERANT pricing walk. under_construction only ever goes true->false, so a stale false is still passable; a stale-but-incomplete set yields an over-estimate, the safe direction for a ranking input. Pricing is not a money guard — the guards are farSinkReachAt (admission) and the executor's strict resolver. HARD CONDITION: the far-sink admission path must stay byte-identical and must keep refusing expansion through stale systems, pinned by test. Commit 4b243707 (spec-conformant but regressive) was NOT gated.

title: Plan-time absorption reservations are invisible to CONCURRENT planners in the same tick — N hulls dispatched together all plan onto the same sink; externality pricing cannot prevent it by design
description:
ADMIRAL-ESCALATED 2026-07-25. The fleet will not disperse. At 45 haulers the working-system count FELL to 12 (from 28) and the top-5 sinks take 86.1% of all sell revenue. Only 18 of 45 hulls traded at all in the last 60 min; 20 traded nothing. This is the sink-surface ceiling, and the mechanism meant to prevent it is not firing.

=== WHAT IS ALREADY RULED OUT (verified live, do not re-investigate) ===
1. NOT the externality feature being unarmed or inert. sp-ircfy IS live and firing: config.yaml:191 externality_weight=0.35; the recovery table is present and WELL-FITTED for the current era (market_model.json era=torwind-2026-07-19, fit_version=2, RESTRICTED n_series=754, WEAK n_series=416, '' n=51, GROWING n=49 — no longer the thin era-07-05 priors); tour_solver.py:735 externality_priced = weight>0 and bool(recovery_tbl) therefore True; the charge is applied at tour_solver.py:914 eff_margin -= externality_cost_per_unit(...). Daemon build 0dbd793e started 03:16:52Z, config written 03:14:50Z — config predates the process, so it is loaded.
2. NOT the discovery horizon. candidate_hop_depth=3 is live and working: the solver's in-scope row count rose from ~240 to 425 (+77%), confirmed in routing.log.
3. NOT market freshness. Inside trade's working set freshness is 86.9% usable against the planner's own activity caps. 102 systems sit within 3 gate-hops at 68.6% fresh — the fleet uses 12 of them. The surface EXISTS and is fresh; the planner is not spreading onto it.
4. NOT solver capacity. Measured hop-depth 1-6 on the 3 most-connected homes: 15ms -> 88ms per solve, linear, ~341x under the 30s VRP_TIMEOUT.

=== ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (the one thing left) ===
The externality term prices the recovery burden a tranche imposes on a sink, computed from THAT SINK's own units/trade_volume/half-life. Its own code comment states the scope: 'term reorders PREFERENCE, it does not decide ELIGIBILITY'. It contains NO term for what other hulls are planning concurrently. So N planners running in the same tick each compute the IDENTICAL charge against the IDENTICAL market snapshot and each still rank the same sink best. They converge — each individually well-priced, all onto one waypoint. Externality cannot fix this by construction.
The mechanism that IS supposed to prevent convergence is the absorption ledger's PLAN-TIME reservation (hull A reserves depth -> hull B's planner sees less depth -> B picks elsewhere). That is what is not working.
SPECIFIC SUSPICION — a visibility/timing hole: a reservation appears to become visible to other planners only AFTER commit, so planners racing within one tick all read pre-reservation state.

=== EVIDENCE (live, today) ===
* THE TRIGGER IS BATCH DISPATCH. Five heavies were bought and dedicated in ONE atomic operation ('shipyard purchase --quantity 5 --fleet trade', 00:22Z). The fleet coordinator therefore discovered FIVE idle hulls on the SAME discovery tick and launched five near-simultaneous tours.
* FOUR OF THE FIVE PLANNED IDENTICALLY: TORWIND-F9/FA/FB/FC each bought 180 FOOD at X1-YY85-A11A + 45 CLOTHING at X1-YY85-C15C (~430-450k each), then hauled as a pack to X1-QM8. The only QM8 sink for those goods is X1-QM8-XF1B: FOOD trade_volume 180, CLOTHING 60, BOTH SCARCE — i.e. ~240 units of per-tick depth targeted by 720 FOOD + 180 CLOTHING. Three of them then docked at X1-QM8-A12D, a DIFFERENT waypoint from the sink.
* CONTROL CASE: TORWIND-F8, the fifth hull, did NOT herd (it went to PA17 alone) and returned 1,052,595 in sells for +368,680 net in the same window, while its four packmates returned ZERO. Same ship class, same hour, same config. The hulls are fine; the simultaneous planning is the defect.
* 74 'Tour absorption reserve breached the fleet-wide sink cap - re-planning' events in 30 minutes at 24 hulls, naming the new hulls. The ledger DOES detect the collision — but only AFTER the plans are made, as a breach-and-replan, not as a plan-time steer.
* CURRENT STATE AT 45 HULLS: working systems 12, top-5 sink share 86.1% of revenue across 9 systems, 24 of 45 hulls FULL, 20 of 45 traded nothing in 60 min.

=== WHAT TO INVESTIGATE FIRST ===
1. In planAndReserve / the absorption ledger: is a PLANNED reservation written and COMMITTED before the next planner's depth read, or only at tour commit? If the latter, concurrent planners in one tick are all blind to each other by construction.
2. Does the fleet coordinator serialise tour launches within a tick, or fire them concurrently? If concurrent, even a correct reservation may lose the race.
3. Does re-plan RELEASE the reservation (run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go releaseTourReservations) and thereby re-open the sink to the very hulls that just breached, producing the observed breach/replan churn?

=== FIX DIRECTIONS (not prescriptive) ===
a) Make the plan-time reservation visible to concurrent planners (write-then-read within the tick, or a short-lived claim taken before planning).
b) STAGGER dispatch: the coordinator should not launch N tours in one tick. The reposition path already has an anti-herd cap (>=5 hulls/system); the tour planner has no equivalent.
c) Diversify explicitly: when launching multiple hulls in one tick, forbid identical (good, source, sink) triples across the batch.
=== RELATED === sp-ekt5z (laden success exit, fixed), sp-ircfy (externality, live and working as designed — NOT at fault), sp-1cuy6 (horizon, live at depth 3).
notes:
MERGED 069f2a70, DEPLOYED 04:36Z. Verified: 95 production lines (run_tour_coordinator.go +9, _absorption.go +13, _plangate.go +73) and 435 test lines. No proto, no Python — daemon-only restart.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, exactly as hypothesised: a tour planner nets OTHERS' outstanding depth, solves, and only THEN reserves what it chose — between that read and that write it is INVISIBLE. The trade-fleet coordinator launches a container per idle hull, each planning on its own goroutine, so a batch dispatch (five heavies in one shipyard call) puts N planners in the netting read at the same instant: all net the SAME pre-reservation snapshot, all rank the same sink best, all haul as a pack. The 74-per-30min 'reserve breached the fleet-wide sink cap - re-planning' churn was the ledger noticing only AFTERWARDS.

FIX: a per-player planning gate makes release -> net -> solve -> reserve ONE critical section, so each planner reads the depth the previous one just committed and steers off it WHILE planning. It deliberately covers the RELEASE too — a re-plan drops its own PLANNED rows first, which briefly showed an incumbent's held sink as free (the third investigation question, answered: yes, that window existed). The handler is a single mediator-registered instance shared by every tour container, so an instance-level gate serialises the whole fleet.

THE THREE ANSWERS I REQUIRED: (1) the reservation is committed only AFTER the solve, so concurrent planners in one tick were blind by construction; (2) the coordinator fires tours CONCURRENTLY, one goroutine per idle hull — so even a correct reservation lost the race; (3) YES, re-plan released its own rows and re-opened the sink, which is the churn source.

RACE VERDICT, stated plainly as demanded: CLOSED tour-vs-tour BY CONSTRUCTION. Cross-engine (idle-arb, arb-run, trade-route, contract fleet) is UNCHANGED and still on breach-and-replan — a known, scoped residual, not a claim of total fix.

RULINGS COMPLIANCE: #4 FAIL CLOSED — a planner that cannot be serialised exits infeasible and reserves NOTHING rather than planning blind into a sink another hull is taking; Reserve's all-or-nothing in-transaction cap check is BYTE-IDENTICAL and remains the hard backstop, so tours now succeed by picking an UNOCCUPIED sink and passing the same cap, never by relaxing it. #2 RESTART-SAFE — a mutual-exclusion TOKEN, not state; a restart starts it free, degrading one plan per hull to pre-fix behaviour, still backstopped by the DB ledger. Explicitly NOT the sp-zszff in-memory-ledger shape, which is the concern I raised on that bead.

ANTI-THEATRE: 7 mutations, and TWO found genuine FALSE GREENS in the lane's own first draft — 'gate acquired after release' and 'gate released before reserve' both SURVIVED initially, i.e. the tests could not see either invisibility window. Both were strengthened until they killed the mutants 3/3. The concurrency test is the real thing: 6 planners through ONE handler against the REAL DB-backed ledger, with an arrival barrier and a ledger spy forcing BOTH windows open — not a sequential test dressed up as one.

DEPLOY-TIME STATE (04:40Z, 4 min post-restart): full hulls 23 -> 32 of 45, 2 sink systems / 3 sells in 5 min. This is NOT a regression signal: the gate prevents NEW convergence and cannot unwind cargo already bought, and the restart interrupted tours mid-flight. The 32 laden hulls acquired their loads before the gate existed and must drain through the same congested sinks. The discriminator is whether NEWLY PLANNED tours stop stacking on one sink — not the laden count, which will get worse before it gets better.

title: Tour reports success=true and releases the hull while it is still FULL of unsold cargo — 4 heavies parked laden at X1-QM8 (900 units, ~1.75M) after 'Tour run complete'
description:
LIVE 2026-07-25 01:50Z, player 4. A tour can buy a full hold, sell NOTHING, and still exit as SUCCESS — releasing the hull laden. This is the Admiral's banned condition ('we absolutely cannot buy cargo and not sell it') arriving through a path sp-pcxju does not cover: the BUY was correctly sink-gated, but the tour then terminates successfully without ever executing the sell.

=== EVIDENCE (verbatim, daemon.log) ===
[22:46:27] [tour-run-TORWIND-F9-61e422be] INFO: Tour run complete
[22:46:27] [tour-run-TORWIND-F9-61e422be] INFO: Container completed successfully
[22:46:27] [tour-run-TORWIND-F9-61e422be] INFO: Released 1 ship assignments (reason: completed)
[22:46:27] [tour-run-TORWIND-F9-61e422be] INFO: Published completion event for ship TORWIND-F9 (success=true)
Identical shape for TORWIND-FB and TORWIND-FC at the same timestamp.
STATE AT THAT MOMENT AND STILL NOW (verified twice, 40s apart, per-ship direct read — not a container-list race):
  TORWIND-F9 225/225 DOCKED @X1-QM8-A12D  container=NONE  lifetime sells=0  net -452,052
  TORWIND-FB 225/225 DOCKED @X1-QM8-A12D  container=NONE  lifetime sells=0  net -442,827
  TORWIND-FC 225/225 DOCKED @X1-QM8-A12D  container=NONE  lifetime sells=0  net -428,832
  TORWIND-C2 225/225 IN_ORBIT @X1-QM8-XF1B container=NONE  last sell 71 min ago
  (TORWIND-FA, same cohort, still has a RUNNING container — so this is not fleet-wide)
900 units and ~1.75M of cargo sitting idle. success=true is FALSE on its face: zero units sold.

=== HOW THEY GOT THERE — the herding that set it up ===
Admiral ordered 5 heavies (bought 00:22Z, X1-YY85-AD6C, atomic --fleet trade). FOUR of the five were dispatched to buy IDENTICAL cargo at IDENTICAL waypoints:
  F9/FA/FB/FC each: 180 FOOD @ X1-YY85-A11A + 45 CLOTHING @ X1-YY85-C15C
They then hauled as a pack to X1-QM8. The only QM8 sink for those goods is X1-QM8-XF1B: FOOD 2336/u vol 180, CLOTHING 5334/u vol 60, BOTH SCARCE. So one sink with ~240 units of per-tick volume was the target for 720 FOOD + 180 CLOTHING carried by four hulls. Three of them are docked at X1-QM8-A12D — a DIFFERENT waypoint from the sink at XF1B.
The planner sized each hull's tour as if it were the only new hull; the absorption ledger's plan-time reservation did not prevent four identical plans converging on one shallow sink.

=== WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM EXISTING BEADS ===
* NOT sp-pcxju: that bead is about buying without a firm sink. Here the buy was gated and the hulls DID reach a system with a real sink. The defect is the tour terminating SUCCESSFULLY with the hold still full instead of selling, failing, or retrying.
* NOT sp-vz8hj: that is laden-hull-without-container arising from COMPLETED-kill failure / retry exhaustion / released-failed. Here the exit is an explicit clean success path (reason: completed, success=true).
* The false SUCCESS signal is the core harm: it suppresses every downstream recovery. A failed tour gets relaunched with backoff; a 'successful' one just releases the hull, and the fleet coordinator sees an idle laden hull with no error to react to.

=== FIX DIRECTION ===
1. A tour MUST NOT report success while the hull holds cargo the tour itself bought. At minimum: if cargo_units > 0 at tour end AND the tour executed any PURCHASE_CARGO, terminate as INCOMPLETE/FAILED (not success) so the existing relaunch+backoff machinery engages. Cheap, and it converts a silent strand into a tracked retry.
2. Do not let N hulls plan identical (good, source, sink) triples against one shallow sink. The absorption ledger already models per-sink depth at plan time — the four plans should have breached against each other and diversified. Investigate why four concurrent plans for the same good/sink were all admitted (possible: plan-time reservation released on re-plan, or the new hulls planned before the others' reservations landed).
3. Anti-herd on DISPATCH: the fleet coordinator relaunches idle hulls in a loop; when multiple hulls are launched in the same tick, their plans should be diversified (the reposition path already has an anti-herd cap of >=5/system — the tour planner has no equivalent).
4. Sanity: a hull should not dock at A12D when its sink is XF1B in the same system with the hold still full.

=== IMPACT ===
Fleet is still net-positive (+1.67M/60m, treasury 60.6M) because the established 19 hulls carry it, but 4 of the 5 newly-bought heavies (10.22M spend) have produced ZERO revenue in 90 minutes. The one that did NOT herd, TORWIND-F8, completed a clean cycle: 1,052,595 sells, +368,680 net. That is the control case proving the hulls work and the HERD is the problem.

BUT THE HERD PERSISTS, AT A NEW LOCATION: TORWIND-F9, FA and FC are now ALL at X1-RD54-BF7B, ALL still 225/225 full. Same convergence pattern the bead describes at X1-QM8, reproduced one hop later. title: Tour-path recovery-externality pricing: fleet anti-herd (sp-78ai part (b), the unbuilt half)
description:
ECONOMY-ANALYST DESIGN, brainstormed with the Admiral 2026-07-25. Full spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-tour-path-externality-pricing-design.md (uncommitted; RULINGS #13 reserves main docs commits for the Admiral).

MEASURED PROBLEM (matched 3h windows either side of the sp-4ki1x deploy at 22:15Z):
  pre-fix  19:15-22:15: 29 sink systems, top3 32.7%, top5 45.3%, gross 28.8M
  post-fix 22:15-01:15: 34 sink systems, top3 36.7%, top5 51.0%, gross 33.2M
The fleet reaches MORE systems (+17%) and earns MORE (+15%) while concentrating HARDER (top5 45.3->51.0). Visibility was necessary and NOT sufficient. Caveats: 3h windows, single boundary, small n, GROSS not net (PLAYBOOK 8) - suggestive, justifies the build, does not validate it.

DO NOT REBUILD - verified armed in live code: absorption ledger sp-78ai L2/L3/L4 (market_absorption_ledger, SetAbsorptionLedger on tour+arb+trade-route, assembleAbsorption run_tour_coordinator.go:1850); net_absorption tour_solver.py:407; filterShadowedLanes; sp-tl68 circuit-path price de-ranking armed at cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:909; sp-tp5c3 multi-hop pricing; candidate_hop_depth 2 + max_tour_systems 4 armed.

THE GAP IS A PATH ASYMMETRY: the live fleet flies TOURS (tour-run-* containers), not circuits. The circuit path has fleet PRICE de-ranking (sp-tl68 self-compression + shared cooldown debt); the tour path has only CAPACITY netting. On tours, once capacity remains nothing de-prices a hammered sink. net_absorption deliberately keeps head prices at step 0 (correct for PAST crush, already in the quote) leaving FUTURE crush unpriced. The fitted recovery half-lives are loaded at tour_handler.py:44-46 and per sp-78ai's own audit are 'consumed by NOTHING at decision time'.

SCOPE (3 components):
1. CORE - recovery-externality pricing: each planned SELL tranche into (sink,good) charged proportional to crush inflicted x activity-fitted recovery half-life / reference window x one fitted externality_weight. Reuse the SINGLE existing half-life table - no redeclaration in Python (the sp-4ki1x two-cap-tables lesson). No double-count by construction: past crush = in the quote; planned depth = netted as capacity; future crush = the new term. Three disjoint accounts.
2. Cross-plan A-cap continuity: the 2-tranche per (market,good,side) A-cap RESETS at plan boundary, so consecutive plans rebuild the D39 ladder at one sink. Carry it in the existing ledger under recovery decay.
3. Proactive reposition targeting (Admiral chose 'reposition instead of idle'): today reposition is reactive only (margin-death / <40% median). Make continuous - when best post-externality lane < fleet median opportunity, deadhead toward highest UNRESERVED absorption (ledger already knows). Reuse reposition_reach deadhead-decay + per-system anti-herd cap; only the trigger changes.

GUARDS (RULINGS #4): externality term is an OBJECTIVE term -> fails OPEN to today's behaviour (the measured baseline). The A-cap bounds BUY COMMITMENT -> fails CLOSED; ledger read failure degrades to the current per-plan cap, never unbounded. NO FLAG (standing Admiral policy) - ships ARMED at a fitted default; revert = externality_weight 0 + restart, the candidate_hop_depth pattern.

VALIDATION: primary discriminator = top-5 sink revenue share FALLS while net cr/hr holds or rises (spread without rate loss). Honesty guard = tour_plan_rate{phase=projected|realized} divergence must not worsen. Counter-metric: if share AND rate both fall, weight too high. Net credit deltas only, matched-length windows only (unequal windows produced a spurious result during design), min 4 clean post-arm hours. Baseline to beat: 34 systems / top3 36.7% / top5 51.0%.

REFUTED: VRP territory partition (optimises coverage not cr/hr; rebalance churn at 30min/hop); hard sink mutex (1-bit quantisation, wastes deep EXCHANGE sinks vol 180-240, starvation risk); new trading coordinator (duplicates shipped machinery).

SEQUENCING RISK: sp-1cuy6's hop-depth numbers were measured THROUGH the sp-4ki1x defect and are known-pessimistic. Do NOT arm this and re-run the depth sweep simultaneously - they confound. ERA: reset 2026-07-26T13:00Z; PLAYBOOK 1 bars arming unvalidated inside the final 12h, so arming must complete by ~2026-07-26T01:00Z or it waits for next era.
notes:
=== IMPLEMENTATION PLAN WRITTEN 2026-07-25 (economy-analyst) ===
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-25-tour-path-externality-pricing.md (6 tasks, TDD, uncommitted per RULINGS #13).

NEW BLOCKING FINDING (discovered while writing the plan, not in the original design):
The fitted artifact services/routing-service/model_artifacts/market_model.json is stamped era=torwind-2026-07-05 — the LIVE era is torwind-2026-07-19. PLAYBOOK 12 rules last era's coefficients FALSE PRIORS. Sample counts are thin: STRONG n_series=1, GROWING n_series=3, untagged n_series=3; only RESTRICTED (22) and WEAK (20) are meaningfully fitted. This design MULTIPLIES BY those half-lives, so pricing against them is arbitrary for exactly the fast-moving tiers where the charge matters most. => Plan Task 1 re-runs model/calibrate.py and BLOCKS arming; any tier with n_series<5 falls back to the pooled untagged half-life. Verified: recovery is consumed by NOTHING at HEAD — it appears only in the tour_handler.py:44-46 log line counting tiers, and in comments. sp-78ai's claim holds.

EXACT INSERTION POINT (verified by reading the code, not inferred):
utils/tour_solver.py greedy pairing loop selects on key = (margin, -j, -(i...)) at ~line 825. The externality subtracts from margin there: eff_margin = margin - externality_cost_per_unit(...). DEPOSIT pairings stay exempt (kind != 'deposit', matching the existing sp-2v69u treatment). CRITICAL: the min_margin eligibility gate keeps testing the RAW margin — the term changes PREFERENCE ORDER, not ELIGIBILITY; moving eligibility would silently tighten a spend gate (RULINGS #4 forbids as a side effect).
Crush per tranche = 1 - the fitted sell-decay factor the tranche builder already applies (price *= factor); DEFAULT_SELL_DECAY=0.9 is only the unfitted-tier fallback. The caller MUST thread the same resolved per-tier factor from the artifact impact map (keys SUPPLY|ACTIVITY) — two decay values for one market would be the sp-4ki1x two-tables defect in a new place. NOTE: an earlier draft of this plan referenced a constant IMPACT_PER_TRANCHE — that constant DOES NOT EXIST; corrected.

TASK 6 (proactive reposition, spec 4.3) IS DELIBERATELY SEQUENCED AFTER TASK 5's MEASUREMENT, not bundled: Tasks 2-4 change PREFERENCE, Task 6 changes POSITION. Bundling them makes the spread measurement unattributable. Task 6 must reuse the existing dwell-45m / anti-herd cap / improvement-ratchet thrash guards — a third trigger that bypasses the dwell timer will thrash the fleet.

STATUS: design + plan complete, NOT dispatched. Awaiting shipwright pickup. Economy-analyst is read-only (no code, no config, no gate) — build ownership transfers on dispatch.
MERGED 0dbd793e (21 files) and DEPLOYED 03:05Z. Scope Tasks 1-4 + Task 5 step 1. Task 6 NOT started, as instructed. Verified UNARMED: externality_weight is absent from config.yaml => 0 => inert, pairing order byte-identical.

=== A FLEET-WIDE TOUR OUTAGE OPENED ON MERGE, AND MY FIRST REMEDY MADE IT WORSE ===
The lane flagged it correctly and urgently: the daemon reads market_model.json from the repo checkout and sends it as expected_model_version; the ROUTING SERVICE loads its artifact ONCE at process start; the solver FAILS CLOSED on mismatch. The merge moved the artifact 2@torwind-2026-07-05 -> 2@torwind-2026-07-19 while routing still held the old one.
I restarted routing first, as the lane recommended. THAT WAS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT AND IT INVERTED THE MISMATCH INTO AN ACTIVE OUTAGE: routing came up on 07-19 while the ALREADY-RUNNING tour containers had cached expected=07-05 AT LAUNCH, so every tour immediately returned 'feasible=False legs=0 cph=0 reason=model_version_mismatch: expected 2@torwind-2026-07-05, artifact 2@torwind-2026-07-19'. Closing it required restarting the DAEMON too, so every tour container relaunched and re-read the artifact. Post-restart: 'feasible=True' with cph 221k-703k on 07-19 both sides.

DURABLE OPERATIONAL RULE (this cost a live outage window, record it): a market_model.json artifact change requires BOTH restarts, and the daemon side is NOT optional, because a tour container resolves expected_model_version at LAUNCH and holds it for its lifetime. Restarting only routing does not fix a mismatch — it flips which side is stale and takes every in-flight tour down with it. Correct sequence: routing FIRST (loads the artifact, regenerates the gitignored Python stubs — confirmed 'Generating protobuf files (missing or stale vs routing.proto)'), THEN the daemon immediately, with no measurement pause between them.

=== TWO LIVE BEHAVIOUR CHANGES SHIPPED WITH THE DEPLOY, INDEPENDENT OF ARMING ===
These ride the recalibrated artifact and the ledger change, NOT the (unarmed) weight. They are ACTIVE NOW.
(1) EVERY HALF-LIFE ROSE 4-6x on the re-fit: pooled 1074->2849min, GROWING 181->1942, RESTRICTED 414->2367 (n 22->754), WEAK 279->1599 (n 20->416), STRONG 386->1578 (n=4, still under the floor of 5 -> prices on the pooled fallback, enforced in code and pinned by a test). The absorption ledger's 12h ExecutedHardCap was chosen as '~two half-lives of the slowest TAGGED tier (RESTRICTED ~6.9h)'. Under the new fit RESTRICTED is 39.4h and WEAK 26.6h, so 12h is now well under ONE half-life for EVERY tier: a shadow that used to self-clear in ~4.6h now blocks ~73% of its units right to the hard-cap sweep. DEPTH NOW FREES FAR MORE SLOWLY, fleet-wide, for every engine. Lever if too tight: absorption.executed_hard_cap in config.yaml (wired, no code change, currently unset/default).
(2) UNTAGGED SINKS NOW RESERVE DEPTH. 4,224 of 17,821 live market_data rows (23.7%) are untagged and there were ZERO untagged EXECUTED shadows — confirming they were all being dropped. They now reserve like any other sink, against a pooled half-life of 47.5h versus the 12h cap, so an untagged sink is substantially embargoed for the full 12h after a real sale. Intended anti-herd direction, but a live throughput change across a QUARTER of the sink universe. Ledger now holds 982 rows.
BOTH are Admiral economics calls, reported not resolved.

=== ANTI-THEATRE: 20 MUTATIONS, ALL KILLED, AND A REAL FALSE GREEN FOUND ===
The false green is the valuable part: the lane's first 'prefers the faster-recovering sink' test asserted membership of both sinks in the winning plan — and probing showed the plan used BOTH sinks in BOTH the priced and unpriced cases, so both assertions were tautologically true and would have survived the charge being DELETED. Root cause: the charge is deliberately invisible to projected profit, so it can only move a plan where competing allocations earn the SAME profit; otherwise sequence selection (which ranks on profit) decides and the term is inert. Every plan-level test was rebuilt profit-invariant by construction. The same probe caught that the fixture's 'fast' tier was THIN and fell back to the pooled half-life — i.e. it was actually the SLOWEST, inverting the test's premise.
Also honestly reported: M5/M8/M9 each killed the unit-level fail-open test but NOT the plan-level one (a surviving layer short-circuits first); only M12, removing BOTH fail-open layers, kills the plan-level test. The lane reported that rather than glossing it.

RULINGS #4 both directions, each pinned: the externality is an OBJECTIVE term and fails OPEN (unreadable/absent recovery table -> charge 0 -> today's exact ordering, two independent layers). The A-cap bounds BUY COMMITMENT and fails CLOSED (ledger read failure -> no view -> the solver still binds on its own per-plan cap AND the conditional Reserve re-checks in-transaction; no pooled fit -> untagged shadow stays UNDECAYED, never optimistically freed). The guard #4 actually protects here is min_margin: test_externality_never_gates_eligibility_only_preference proves a lane whose RAW margin exactly clears min_margin stays eligible even at weight 50; mutation M2 moves eligibility onto the adjusted margin and that test kills it.

NOTABLE DEVIATIONS (all defensible): (1) fixed a QUADRATIC query in extract_control_series that made Task 1 undeliverable — a per-(waypoint,good) LIKE test evaluated once per HISTORY ROW (195,245 rows x 43,279 transactions, two unindexable patterns); ran 50 minutes without finishing, hoisted to one evaluation per DISTINCT pair (8,609) + anti-join, 3 minutes, identical predicate. This is almost certainly WHY the artifact had sat at era-07-05. (2) Repinned EXTERNALITY_REFERENCE_MINUTES 279.0 -> 1599.2 so the weight keeps the meaning the design gave it — without this the plan's 0.35 would have behaved ~5.7x hotter against the new fit. (3) Replaced a shipped test (TestAbsorptionLedger_Convert_UntaggedSink_WritesNoShadow) that asserted the rule Task 4 exists to overturn — called out explicitly as normally-cardinal-sin, correct here.

ARMING STATE: unarmed. One line under trade_fleet: externality_weight: 0.35. Revert = same line at 0 + daemon restart. title: No operator path to ship-to-ship cargo transfer: TransferCargoCommand is built and used by gas/stocker/tour coordinators but has no proto RPC and no CLI verb
description:
The capability EXISTS and is exercised in production — it simply cannot be commanded.

BUILT AND IN USE: internal/adapters/api/client.go:1248 TransferCargo(ctx, fromShip, toShip, good, units, token) -> POST /my/ships/{s}/transfer (classified at endpoint_classifier.go:20). The mediator command internal/application/gas/commands/transfer_cargo.go TransferCargoCommand is registered twice (cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:1416 and internal/application/setup/handler_registry.go:139) and driven by THREE production callers: gas siphon workers (run_siphon_worker.go:316), the stocker coordinator (run_stocker_coordinator.go:1192), and the tour coordinator's haul-to-storage deposit (run_tour_coordinator.go:1738).

MISSING: no proto RPC and no CLI verb. A CLI-wide sweep of every command group finds no 'transfer' anywhere, so an operator cannot move cargo between two co-located hulls. Transfer happens only as a side effect of gas siphoning, warehouse stocking, or a tour deposit.

WHY IT IS NEEDED NOW: modules are transferable between hulls ONLY through cargo. Proven live this session on TORWIND-F6: 'ship outfit remove --module MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I' places the module in the ship's cargo as a normal good (cargo_inventory shows {symbol: MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I, units: 1, name: 'Warp Drive I'}), and 'ship outfit install' refits it (fee 100 each way). So the ONLY route to give a warp drive to a hull that did not ship with one is: remove from an explorer -> transfer ship-to-ship -> install on the target. There is no market alternative — MODULE_WARP_DRIVE appears in 0 of our 2,974 scanned markets, so it cannot be sold and re-bought.

Without this verb, warp capability is permanently locked to explorer hulls, and the whole retrofit question (can a freighter warp?) is unanswerable.

WORK: thin operator shell over the EXISTING mediator command — proto RPC + daemon handler + 'spacetraders ship transfer --from <SHIP> --to <SHIP> --good <SYMBOL> --units <N>'. Do NOT reimplement transfer logic and do NOT modify the gas TransferCargoCommand or its handler; the three existing callers must be byte-identical. Follow the shape just established by the warp verb (sp-nhr0g, merged 90fb7a78): proto message + handler + CLI verb mirroring the ship/route conventions, surfacing typed errors verbatim rather than flattening them.

CONSTRAINTS: the API requires BOTH ships at the SAME waypoint; the receiving hull needs cargo space. Both failure modes must surface as readable operator errors, not generic failures. RULINGS #3 — the daemon performs the mutation; the CLI issues an RPC and never calls the API itself.
acceptance_criteria: 'spacetraders ship transfer --from <A> --to <B> --good <SYMBOL> --units <N>' exists, appears in 'ship --help' alongside its siblings, and delegates to the EXISTING gas TransferCargoCommand with no duplicated transfer logic. The three existing production callers (gas siphon worker, stocker coordinator, tour coordinator deposit) are byte-identical. RED-first tests: a successful transfer between two co-located hulls against a fake API; ships at DIFFERENT waypoints is refused with a readable error; insufficient cargo space on the receiver is refused with a readable error. Anti-theatre confirmed (break the implementation, watch the tests fail). build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.
notes:
MERGED f6eaf75a (gate squashed branch 8fa6fb6f). Verified independently: numstat matches the report exactly, and 'git diff 90fb7a78 f6eaf75a -- internal/application/ internal/adapters/api/client.go' is EMPTY — the three existing production callers (gas siphon worker, stocker, tour deposit) and the API client are genuinely byte-identical, not merely claimed to be. route_executor_warp.go untouched (sp-iierd's territory), no cross-lane conflict.

OPERATOR SURFACE: 'spacetraders ship transfer --from <A> --to <B> --good <SYMBOL> --units <N>'. The retrofit chain is now closed end to end and documented in the verb's own help: outfit remove -> transfer -> outfit install.

DESIGN CALL — SYNCHRONOUS mediator RPC, not a tracked container. Accepted, and the reasoning is better than my brief's: (1) a transfer is instantaneous, so there is nothing for RULINGS #2 recovery to re-adopt — a container would need a ContainerType + spec + recovery func whose only job is to re-run an op that already completed; (2) synchronous is what makes the refusals READABLE — a container hides the outcome behind 'container logs <id>' (the warp verb has to tell operators to go read it), whereas this prints on the terminal; (3) both bookends of the retrofit chain (outfit remove/install) are already synchronous, and an operator needs each step's result before choosing the next. Pinned by TestTransferCargoStaysASynchronousMediatorOpNotAContainer.

BOTH REFUSALS SURFACE VERBATIM (the mandate): refusals ride back in the response error field rather than as a gRPC status error (which would bury them under 'rpc error: code = Unknown desc ='). Different-waypoint refusal names the condition AND both locations ('ships must be at the same location for transfer: X at ..., Y at ...'); full-receiver refusal passes the server's own capacity wording through whole. Tests assert on the fragments and assert the API is never touched on the co-location refusal.

ANTI-THEATRE — EXCEPTIONAL, and it caught a FALSE GREEN in its own suite. Five deliberate mutations: swap from/to (2 fail); flatten the error to 'transfer failed' (both failure-mode tests fail — the exact flattening the brief warned about, now caught); register as a container spec (TEST STILL PASSED — it was passing on 'missing or invalid ship_symbol, destination', a CONFIG error, and could not distinguish that from the absent registration; tightened to require 'unknown command type', re-broke, confirmed it now FAILS, restored); remove the units>0 guard (fails); unregister the CLI verb (fails). Finding and fixing a test that cannot tell two failure modes apart is exactly the discipline the anti-theatre gate exists for.

DELIBERATE OMISSION (correct): no pre-flight receiver-space check. The handler's comment claims it verifies space but does not; adding one would duplicate transfer logic (out of scope) and would race the cached ship row anyway. The API's own refusal, surfaced verbatim, names the condition better than a cache-derived guess.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION: the stocker caller lives at internal/application/trading/commands/run_stocker_coordinator.go, not under gas/ as I wrote.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED: pre-existing gofmt drift on main (run_bootstrap_muc5x_test.go, run_bootstrap_scaled_gate_test.go) — confirmed unformatted before this branch existed; left alone to avoid conflicting with a live bootstrap lane.

title: Warp strand guard is measuring the WRONG distance: ensureWarpFuelSafety uses system-relative waypoint coords for a CROSS-system leg, so required fuel is computed far too small and the guard fails OPEN
description:
CONFIRMED with live data. ensureWarpFuelSafety (internal/application/ship/route_executor_warp.go:216-256) computes the leg cost as warpFuelCost(origin.DistanceTo(destination)) where origin/destination are WAYPOINTS. Those X/Y are SpaceTraders waypoint coordinates, which are relative to their OWN system's centre — they are NOT galactic coordinates. For a warp (which is BY DEFINITION cross-system) the two waypoints live in different coordinate frames, so the computed distance is meaningless and typically tiny.

LIVE EVIDENCE (era 4):
  system_coords X1-YY85 = (18099, 10194); X1-TY66 = (17803, 10616) -> true inter-system distance 515.
  waypoints: TORWIND-F6 at X1-YY85-ZD2D = (3, -12); TORWIND-59 at X1-JT9-FC6Z = (9, 45).
Waypoint coords are single/double digit, system-relative. So DistanceTo across systems returns tens of units where the real separation is hundreds — the guard sees a leg ~10-50x cheaper than it is.

WHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: the guard's whole purpose is refusing a leg that would strand the hull, and RULINGS #4 requires guards to fail CLOSED. Under-computing  means: 'cost exceeds a full tank' never trips; 'already have enough fuel' passes spuriously; the top-off branch is skipped. The guard therefore WAVES THROUGH exactly the legs it exists to refuse, and a hull can warp off the gate network and strand with no fuel and no fuel station. This is a fail-OPEN safety guard.

COMPOUNDING: this stacks with sp-tvjzo (warpFuelCost itself assumes the CRUISE rate, 1 fuel/distance, never validated against the live API). Two unvalidated assumptions in series, both feeding the same guard. Fixing warpFuelCost's RATE without fixing the DISTANCE input leaves the guard just as broken.

THE FIX MUST USE INTER-SYSTEM DISTANCE. system_coords already carries per-system galactic X/Y (era-scoped) and is the source the reposition/gate planning already reasons over. The guard needs the origin SYSTEM and destination SYSTEM coordinates, not the waypoints'. Keep the four-branch structure and the fail-CLOSED posture; only the distance input changes. An unreadable system coordinate must fail CLOSED (refuse), never fall back to the waypoint distance.

DO NOT weaken any branch while fixing this (RULINGS #4). Expect the corrected guard to start REFUSING legs it previously allowed — that is the point, not a regression.

ORIGIN: found by the sp-nhr0g lane as a code trace while building the warp operator path; independently CONFIRMED here against live system_coords and ships rows. RELATED: sp-tvjzo (fuel RATE validation — these two should be fixed and validated together), sp-nhr0g (the verb that finally makes warp commandable), sp-xhzc6 (auto-acquire loop must not fire before this is fixed).
acceptance_criteria: ensureWarpFuelSafety computes the leg cost from INTER-SYSTEM distance (system_coords galactic X/Y for the origin and destination systems), not from waypoint-local coordinates. A RED test pins the defect: a cross-system leg whose true separation exceeds a full tank is REFUSED with ErrWarpWouldStrand, where today's waypoint-coordinate math lets it through. An unreadable/missing system coordinate fails CLOSED (refusal), never degrading to the waypoint distance. All four existing branches keep their fail-closed posture and their typed ErrWarpWouldStrand fields. Non-warp callers unaffected. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.
notes:
TYPO REPAIR: in the description, the sentence beginning "Under-computing  means:" lost a word to shell substitution when this bead was filed. It should read "Under-computing the REQUIRED fuel means:". No other content was affected.
ADMIRAL REDIRECT 2026-07-24 — DO NOT FIX THIS BY CORRECTING THE ARITHMETIC. The bead as filed says 'the fix must use inter-system distance'. That is now SUPERSEDED. Fixing the math preserves the actual defect, which is architectural: we are REIMPLEMENTING A RULE WE DO NOT OWN. Every divergence between our copy and the server's real rule is a bug by construction, and we have already found two (waypoint-local distance frame; hardcoded FlightModeCruise ignoring the hull's real flight_mode). A third will appear the next time the game retunes a multiplier.

THE LOCAL PREDICTION IS NOT LOAD-BEARING — PROVEN TWICE LIVE. The server refuses insufficient-fuel warps AUTHORITATIVELY and PRE-FLIGHT, with the hull never moving:
  attempt 1: X1-YY85->X1-FD3, 400 code 4203, fuelRequired=831 fuelAvailable=800, fuel unchanged at 800/800
  attempt 2: X1-CD11->X1-UM5, 400 code 4203, fuelRequired=1144 fuelAvailable=798, fuel unchanged at 798/800
The refusal carries STRUCTURED DATA (fuelRequired/fuelAvailable) — the real number from the entity that enforces it, strictly better than any local estimate.

NEW DESIGN — stop predicting, start reacting:
1. DELETE the local fuel-sufficiency prediction. Do not model the game's fuel formula. warpFuelCost's whole reason to exist ('so the executor can compute strand-risk locally without a round-trip to the API') is a false economy — it buys one saved API call and costs a fail-open safety guard.
2. KEEP the refuel orchestration. Topping off at the origin is ACTION, not prediction — the server will not do it for you. This is the genuinely valuable half of ensureWarpFuelSafety.
3. TREAT 4203 AS THE AUTHORITY: parse fuelRequired/fuelAvailable from the typed API error; if the origin sells fuel, refuel to the stated requirement and retry ONCE; if it cannot be satisfied, terminate immediately (this also resolves sp-tsqkg's retry-storm, since a 4203 becomes either actionable or terminal, never a blind restart-budget burn).
4. ADD THE CHECK THE SERVER CANNOT DO — ONWARD VIABILITY. This is the real safety property and NOTHING currently checks it. The server only guarantees you can AFFORD THE LEG; it will happily let a hull warp somewhere it can never leave. Near-miss this session: X1-TY66 was the only system inside a full 800 tank of X1-YY85 and reads as gate-connected, but it has ZERO scanned markets (no fuel) AND its gate X1-TY66-I58 has under_construction=true. Warping there (arrive with 285 fuel) would have STRANDED a 722,511-credit explorer. Refuse a warp whose destination has no reachable fuel AND no traversable exit — checking under_construction on the escape gate, not mere adjacency.

RULINGS #4 NOTE (flagged, not assumed): this DELETES a guard. The argument that it is not a weakening: the protection does not vanish, it moves to the authority that actually enforces it (demonstrated twice, fail-closed, zero side effects), AND we add the strand check that was genuinely missing. If the Admiral reads #4 as barring the deletion, keep a thin local check purely as an API-budget saver — but it must then be documented as advisory-only and must NOT be the thing standing between a hull and a strand.

SUPERSEDES the original acceptance criteria. sp-tvjzo (rate validation) is largely MOOT under this design — there is no local rate left to validate; its surviving value is the recorded measurements (CRUISE 1.0x and BURN 2.0x confirmed against the live server) as documentation of what the game actually does.
MERGED bd3c4aaa (parent f6eaf75a). Verified independently: numstat matches the report; 'git diff f6eaf75a bd3c4aaa -- internal/application/system/ internal/domain/system/' is EMPTY, so gategraph and the strict Path/PathWithinJumps/Routable resolvers at MaxJumpPath=5 are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely by claim. First gate run returned Stale:true (main advanced to sp-lzhsd mid-lane); rebased, re-ran build/vet/gofmt/-race, re-gated clean.

DESIGN: deleted warpFuelCost and the four-branch ensureWarpFuelSafety PREDICTION. The executor now issues the leg, parses the server's authoritative 4203 (fuelRequired/fuelAvailable) and either refuels-to-requirement-and-retries-once or terminates typed; keeps the origin top-off as pure ACTION; and adds a NEW fail-closed ensureOnwardViability guard (typed ErrWarpDeadEnd) over a WarpEscapeReader port + SystemEscapeReader.

RULINGS #4 — the deletion is NOT a weakening, three load-bearing parts: (a) the deleted code was a GUESS, not a guard, and was already failing OPEN in both directions (waypoint-local coords on a cross-system leg; hardcoded CRUISE ignoring a real BURN hull at 2x) — both errors UNDER-compute, so all four branches waved through exactly the legs they existed to refuse; weakening presupposes strength. (b) Protection MOVED to the enforcing authority rather than vanishing: every fail-closed verdict is still rendered in satisfyWarpFuelRefusal, now off the SERVER's number (required>capacity -> strand; !origin.HasFuel -> strand; still short after refuel -> strand), and the typed ErrWarpWouldStrand contract to callers is unchanged. (c) Net protection strictly INCREASED — onward viability was previously unguarded by anything.

NEW GUARD FAILS CLOSED (each pinned by a test AND a killed mutation): unreadable destination -> ErrWarpDeadEnd with zero warp calls; nil/unwired reader -> refused, and warpEscapeReader is a REQUIRED parameter of WithWarpSupport (not an option) so the COMPILER names every wiring site and a nil cannot silently bypass; waypoint-source error -> error, not 'no fuel'; adjacency error -> error, not 'no gate'. ADJACENCY != TRAVERSABILITY: an escape requires a neighbour edge with UnderConstruction==false AND Stale==false — a stale row's build state is unverified, and an unverified claim is not an escape. This is precisely the X1-TY66 near-miss encoded.

ANTI-THEATRE — 13 mutations, and ONE SURVIVED, which found a REAL GAP rather than confirming the work. Mutation 3 replaced the '!origin.HasFuel -> strand' branch with 'return nil' (re-creating the blind retry) and the suite stayed GREEN: the single 4203 test used required 831 > capacity 800, which short-circuits at the FIRST branch, so two of the three terminal branches were never exercised. Reworked into a three-case table (requirement exceeds a full tank / origin sells no fuel / refuel leaves the tank still short, the last via a finite-stock fuel mediator). Mutation 3 then died, and a NEW mutation 4 (drop the post-refuel re-check) died at the third case — a branch nothing had ever covered. All 13 killed after the fix. This is the anti-theatre gate doing exactly its job.

ACCEPTED DEVIATIONS: new typed ErrWarpDeadEnd rather than overloading ErrWarpWouldStrand (a dead-end has no fuel arithmetic; printing 'required 0 fuel, available 800' would mislead the operator) — no production errors.As on ErrWarpWouldStrand existed outside the warp file. A top-off FAILURE still fails the leg; the lane considered demoting it to best-effort now the server adjudicates fuel and DECLINED under #4 as an unrequested relaxation — correct instinct. The 4203 refuel-retry path is reachable mainly when the top-off does not fill the tank (finite market stock, or a stale/wrong HasFuel trait), which is how it is tested.

POLICY QUESTIONS RAISED FOR THE ADMIRAL (reported, not resolved — correct escalation): (1) onward viability makes uncharted off-gate exploration STRICTER: a destination with no known fuel seller and no BUILT gate is now refused outright. SystemEscapeReader reads fuel through the same fetch-through waypoint source the verb uses (public endpoint, no ship required), so a never-charted system answers truthfully rather than reading as empty — but a genuinely fuel-less, gate-less system is now unreachable by warp. The missing third escape is 'arrives with enough residual fuel to warp back out', which cannot be evaluated pre-flight without re-introducing the very local prediction this bead deletes. (2) Cost: up to 2 reads per leg (waypoints, usually already warm from resolveDestination; plus one Adjacency() DB read, no API). (3) Stale-row strictness: refusing a stale UnderConstruction:false as unverified could occasionally refuse a system whose gate is genuinely built, given the 24h gate TTL — deliberate fail-closed choice, relaxable to 'stale-but-built counts' on Admiral say-so.

title: No operator path to warp: ExecuteWarpLeg/ExecuteWarpRoute are built and wired but have NO proto RPC and NO CLI verb — only the frontier explorer dispatcher can ever fire a warp
description:
We now OWN a warp-capable hull (TORWIND-F6, FRAME_EXPLORER, MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I confirmed installed, 800/800 fuel, docked X1-YY85-ZD2D) and STILL cannot execute a warp, because warp has no entry point.

ESTABLISHED (live, this session): slice-A RouteExecutor.ExecuteWarpLeg / ExecuteWarpRoute exist and are wired at cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:789 (WithWarpSupport). grep confirms the ONLY caller is the frontier expansion coordinator's explorer dispatch (internal/adapters/expansion/explorer_dispatch_adapter.go, slice C). There is NO warp entry in the gRPC proto and NO 'ship warp' verb in the CLI ('spacetraders ship --help' lists jump/navigate/route only). So warp is reachable ONLY as a side effect of frontier expansion choosing to dispatch an explorer to an off-gate target — it cannot be commanded, and therefore cannot be MEASURED.

WHY THIS BLOCKS REAL WORK: warpFuelCost (route_executor_warp.go:53-55) assumes warp burns at the CRUISE rate (1 fuel/distance) and has never met the live API (sp-tvjzo). That constant is the sole input to the strand guard, and it fails OPEN in the dangerous direction. Validating it requires executing ONE warp with a known distance and diffing the fuel — impossible today.

RULINGS #3 forbids the shortcut: 'The daemon is the ONLY writer of ship state... New operations become daemon containers or daemon RPCs, not CLI-side orchestration.' title: Long-haul pathfind stalls on the 90s budget: storedThenVerify live-probes GetWaypoint PER HOP on the chosen path — cost scales with hop count, so bound-25 lanes self-veto
description:
SIGNATURE (live, TORWIND-59 container log, repeating every ~90s from 21:26Z): 'gate construction probe failed — treating edge as under construction (fail closed)' immediately followed by 'resume sell of 60 FABRICS failed: no jump-gate route from X1-CA43 to X1-JT9: pathfind exceeded the 1m30s budget (pathological planning stall)'. Start 21:26:05 -> error 21:27:35 = exactly the 90s budget.

ROOT CAUSE (pinned read-only): gategraph storedThenVerify (internal/application/system/gategraph/service.go:767-800) is two steps. STEP 1 PLAN — RepositionPath (:684-706) is a PURE store read + in-memory BFS over stored adjacency and ALREADY excludes UnderConstruction edges (:699). Milliseconds; NOT the stall. STEP 2 VERIFY — the loop at :791-798 calls gateUnderConstruction (:552-563) for EVERY hop on the chosen path, and each call is a LIVE, rate-limited apiClient.GetWaypoint. An 11-hop long-haul path = 11 live probes serialized inside the 90s longHaulPathfindBudget (:60). Under live API pressure that blows the budget; the in-flight probe dies on the deadline, fails CLOSED (:560), returns ErrUnroutable, and the wrapper (:757) reports the budget error.

WHY IT IS A LONG-HAUL-SPECIFIC SELF-VETO: probe count scales with HOP COUNT. Short bound-5 lanes verify <=5 gates and pass; the 7-12-hop exotic lanes long-haul exists to fly are exactly the ones that exceed the budget. The engine therefore self-vetoes its own reason for existing. sp-0o9ub already removed the far worse 'probe every edge of the whole BFS frontier' cost; this is the residual per-chosen-hop cost it left.

EVIDENCE THE VERIFY IS DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH, NOT THE PRIMARY GUARD (per the resolver's own docstring, :725-729): stored adjacency already filters under-construction edges at plan time, AND jump_ship.go's source/destination construction checks plus the live jump API remain the authoritative fail-closed backstop AT HOP TIME regardless of this plan. The plan-time verify exists only to catch an edge that went under construction SINCE the last stored sync (a staleness window).

FIX DIRECTION (crafter to root-cause and choose; do NOT weaken a guard as a side effect — RULINGS #4): make verify cost independent of hop count. Preferred: use the stored UnderConstruction state already present in Adjacency() (gate_edges carries the column; 315 of 3807 era-4 rows set) as the primary signal and live-probe ONLY where stored state is stale/unreadable, and/or bound the live probes to the imminent hop(s) rather than all N. Explicitly REJECTED: merely raising longHaulPathfindBudget — it does not remove the O(hops) live-probe cost, it just moves the wall, and more hops re-crosses it.

MUST NOT REGRESS: the sp-8qhu invariant (never route INTO an under-construction gate) and the hop-time fail-closed authority both stay intact. Non-long-haul callers (tour/manual/one-shot arb at MaxJumpPath=5 via the strict Path/PathWithinJumps) must remain byte-identical — this resolver is long-haul-only, do not touch the strict resolvers.

RELATED: sp-ry741 (Fix A LegJumpBound — live and working; this is the residual blocker on its behavioral ACCEPT), sp-0o9ub (introduced storedThenVerify), sp-if4lx (introduced the 90s budget), sp-ibirm (the strategic route-bound refactor; its notes flag that B must address bound-25 LATENCY — this bead IS that latency, scoped tight).

No 'pathfind exceeded the 1m30s budget' in the long-haul worker logs across a full delivery circuit. A genuinely under-construction gate on the chosen path STILL fails the plan closed (sp-8qhu invariant intact) — proven by a RED test that a bad gate is still rejected. title: Tour path double-filters staleness: the solver's FLAT 75-min cutoff silently nullifies sp-t5sh5's activity-fitted caps — 81.5% of our discovered market universe is invisible to the trade fleet
description:
ADMIRAL-FLAGGED 2026-07-24. The trade fleet's planner sees only 18.5% of the markets we have discovered, because two staleness filters are stacked and the SECOND one throws away exactly what the FIRST was built to preserve.

=== THE DEFECT (both sites read, live code) ===
The tour path filters market rows for staleness TWICE:
1. GO SIDE — services/tour_snapshot.go:75 (BuildTourSnapshot) drops each good against ITS OWN activity-conditioned cap (sp-t5sh5): 'if observedKnown && age > caps.For(activity)'. Fitted caps, domain/trading/ranker_age_cap.go:26-29 — WEAK=480min, RESTRICTED=180min, GROWING=60min, STRONG=30min. The code comment states the intent explicitly: 'not one flat market-wide threshold, so a market with mixed activities keeps its WEAK rows and drops its STRONG ones.'
2. PYTHON SOLVER — services/routing-service/utils/tour_solver.py:1643-1648 then RE-FILTERS the same rows against a FLAT cutoff: 'age_cap = constraints.get("max_snapshot_age_minutes") or MAX_SNAPSHOT_AGE_MINUTES_DEFAULT(75); cutoff = time.time() - age_cap*60; rows = [r for r in snapshot if r["observed_at_unix"] >= cutoff ...]'. And the Go caller passes exactly 75: run_tour_coordinator.go:1868 'MaxSnapshotAgeMinutes: int(maxListingAge.Minutes())' where run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:851 'const maxListingAge = 75 * time.Minute' (HARDCODED, not config).

=> A WEAK row that the Go side DELIBERATELY preserved at 2-8 hours old — precisely sp-t5sh5's purpose — arrives at the solver and is SILENTLY DROPPED at 75 minutes. sp-t5sh5's activity-fitted model is defeated for every row aged between 75min and its fitted cap. The Go side even emits tour_lanes_stale_excluded_total for ITS drops; the solver-side drop is unmetered (only the all-rows-gone case surfaces, as 'no_fresh_market_data').

=== DAMAGE (measured live, market_data, 2026-07-24 21:55Z) ===
Whole discovered universe = 17,223 market rows.
  visible under FLAT 75min (what the solver actually sees): 3,190 = 18.5%
  visible under the ACTIVITY-FITTED caps (what sp-t5sh5 intended): 4,586 = 26.6%
  => +1,396 rows, +44% more visible markets, recovered by removing ONE contradictory cap.
By activity (rows_total / visible_flat75 / visible_fitted):
  WEAK        7,157 / 1,358 / 2,269   (+67% — the WORST hit, and WEAK is where staleness matters LEAST: weak activity means prices barely move)
  RESTRICTED  5,668 /   997 / 1,288   (+29%)
  (none)      4,079 /   789 /   991   (+26%, falls to the RESTRICTED cap by design)
  GROWING       290 /    43 /    35   (flat-75 is slightly LOOSER than the fitted 60min here — correct to tighten)
  STRONG         29 /     3 /     3   (unchanged; fitted 30min is already tighter)
The fix is directionally SAFER, not looser, for fast-moving markets: STRONG/GROWING get TIGHTER caps than the flat 75 they enjoy today.

=== WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS — it explains three open symptoms ===
* 'The fleet will not spread' (Admiral, this session): the only markets reliably <75min old are the near hubs WE refresh by trading them. Everything else ages out and vanishes from the plan, so the planner keeps re-choosing the same cluster. The concentration is partly a FRESHNESS artifact, not only a horizon one.
* Horizon widening underdelivers: measured live freshness by gate-hop distance from our 6 busiest hubs — hop1 62.5%, hop2 56.9%, hop3 32.1%, hop4 33.1%, hop5 43.9%, hop6 51.4% fresh<75m. Widening candidate_hop_depth adds far systems whose rows are then discarded by this very cutoff, so the widening buys much less than replay predicts (see sp-1cuy6).
* Frontier ROI: we keep 2,244 import sinks / 255 systems discovered and refresh ~416/hr, but the trade planner can only ever act on the <75min slice. Most discovery value never reaches the fleet.

=== FIX DIRECTION ===
The Go side ALREADY did the correct per-activity filtering before the request is built, so the solver's cap should be a BACKSTOP, not a second opinion that overrides it. Two options, prefer (a):
(a) SIMPLE: have the Go caller pass the WIDEST fitted cap (max(caps) = 480min WEAK) as max_snapshot_age_minutes instead of the flat 75. The per-activity precision is already enforced upstream; the solver then only rejects genuinely ancient rows. Smallest diff, no solver change, no new plumbing.
(b) THOROUGH: teach the solver the same activity-conditioned table — the snapshot rows ALREADY carry an 'activity' field (see the row shape in tour_solver / replay reconstruction), so it can apply caps.For(activity) itself. Costs plumbing the cap table over the wire; benefit is one staleness model with no upstream/downstream skew.
EITHER WAY: keep ONE definition of the cap table (domain/trading/ranker_age_cap.go) — do not redeclare it in Python. And add a solver-side counter for rows dropped by the backstop so this can never go silent again.

=== VALIDATION BAR ===
* The 75 is HARDCODED (const maxListingAge, run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:851) and is ALSO used by the ranker/lookback/offload/distress/stocker paths — verify which of those genuinely want a flat 75 before changing the const itself; prefer changing what the TOUR path passes rather than the shared const, unless the same defect is proven there too.
* Replay first: replay_hopwiden_TEMP.py reconstructs snapshots with STALENESS_MINUTES=75 baked in (line 55) — that harness must be parameterized or it will not be able to measure the fix.
* Expect the honest gain to be SMALLER than +44% of rows: many recovered rows are low-value WEAK markets. Measure fleet-$/hr, not row count.
* Interaction: this likely changes the sp-1cuy6 hop-depth answer — re-run the depth sweep AFTER this lands, since far-system rows are exactly the ones this cap was discarding.

title: Bounded 3-hop multi-hop tours: gate-graph travel matrix + widen tour discovery horizon to hop-depth 3 (solve-time feasibility PROVEN ~31ms)
description:
ADMIRAL-REQUESTED (2026-07-24). Capture the out-of-1-hop lanes the tour solver silently drops, by giving the solver a REAL multi-hop travel cost and widening its discovery horizon to a BOUNDED 3 gate hops — inside the hardened trade fleet, instead of the separate unbounded long-haul executor.

=== WHY (live leak, measured) ===
The tour planner's discovery horizon is 1 gate hop (tourSystemsFrom = home + neighbors, MAX_TOUR_SYSTEMS=2, an explicit Admiral decision — sp-mtvg). Source and sink of exotic lanes sit 3+ hops apart, so they NEVER co-occur in one snapshot: the lane is ABSENT, not rejected. Live daemon.log emits ~200 'Tour horizon dropped N profitable lane(s) whose best sink is beyond the gate-neighbor graph (sp-mtvg)' events per 30 min. Dropped lanes are large:
 * AI_MAINFRAMES X1-RJ40-CB4E(29337) -> X1-UM5-A1(57830)  spread 28493/u  (~6.4M on one 225-unit tour, into HOME)
 * AI_MAINFRAMES X1-MH84-E16Z(28877) -> X1-UM5-A1(57830)  spread 28953/u
 * ANTIMATTER   X1-CQ98-EC7B(3645)  -> X1-VB94-D23E(11173) spread 7528/u
 * ANTIMATTER   X1-AA14-F17C(3116)  -> X1-VB94-D23E(11173) spread 8057/u
 * SHIP_PLATING / SHIP_PARTS lanes 5040/u+
Consequence: the trade fleet does NOT spread. Sink systems served per hour over 4h: 11,12,14,13,9 — oscillating, NOT growing. 19 trade hulls concentrate on the same near hubs (CD11 2.9M, PA17 2.8M, VM73 2.5M over 2h) while 61 of 81 fresh-import systems go unserved.

=== WHY NOT the existing alternatives ===
(a) reposition_reach / reposition_rate_floor ARE armed but are CONDITIONAL — they only relocate on margin-death or <40%-of-median under-earning. A healthy-but-concentrated fleet never triggers them; live logs show only scout/probe repositioning, zero trade-hull relocation.
(b) long-haul arb (sp-mepj) was the CHOSEN option-(b) capture path and is DEAD: all 4 hulls stranded in a resume-sell retry loop ('no jump-gate route from <src> to <sink> within 5 jumps'), 146 units undeliverable, 0 captures in 3.5h+ (see sp-ry741). Its unbounded reach keeps producing bound-mismatch bugs (reachability family sp-e059j / sp-ju9pn / sp-1bme8 / sp-ry741). A BOUNDED horizon sidesteps that entire failure class.

=== THE ONE REAL BLOCKER — and it is NOT performance ===
sp-mtvg / sp-mepj kept the 1-hop horizon as a LOAD-BEARING guard (RULINGS #4) for TWO stated reasons: (1) mis-pricing — the solver's _make_travel_fn prices EVERY inter-system crossing as exactly ONE gate hop (2*GATE_HOP + JUMP_COOLDOWN), so widening allowed_systems without a real travel model mis-prices a 3-hop lane ~3x and corrupts cph selection; (2) assumed ortools VRP blowup on the larger candidate set.

REASON (2) IS NOW DISPROVEN — captain ran the pre-existing feasibility probe (services/routing-service/probe_timing_TEMP.py, cap-4 RATE, live snapshot 2026-07-24 21:22Z, 3 MOST-CONNECTED homes = worst case):
  home        depth  |allowed|  scoped_mkts  solve_s
  X1-PA17       1        3          75        0.014
  X1-PA17       2        8         176        0.032
  X1-PA17       3       14         207        0.034
  X1-QM8        3       12         116        0.037
  X1-KQ55       3       12         117        0.023
  avg per-solve: depth1=0.010s  depth2=0.020s  depth3=0.031s
=> hop-depth 3 grows candidates ~3 -> 12-14 systems (markets 75 -> 207) and still solves in ~31ms, worst case 37ms — roughly 1000x under the service's existing 30s VRP_TIMEOUT. Solve-time is a NON-ISSUE. (Caveat: single live snapshot, 3 homes; margin so wide that 10x more systems would not threaten it.)

=> Therefore the ONLY remaining work is REASON (1): travel-model correctness.

=== SCOPE ===
1. TRAVEL MATRIX (the core change): replace the flat 1-hop cost in the tour solver's _make_travel_fn with a REAL gate-graph shortest-path cost, so an N-hop crossing is priced as N jumps + N cooldowns (+ fuel), not 1. Source of truth = gate_edges (BFS/APSP over the gate-adjacency map; the same map replay_hopwiden_TEMP.fetch_gate_neighbors/systems_within_hops already walks). Precompute a distance matrix the solver consumes — no per-solve pathfinding.
2. WIDEN THE HORIZON to a BOUNDED hop-depth 3 at the candidate-construction sites (tourSystemsFrom Go side + compute_allowed shape in the solver path). Bounded is the point: NOT unbounded like long-haul.
3. The arb scanner shares the identical horizon (scanLanes -> neighborSystems) — decide explicitly whether it widens with the tour solver or stays at 1 hop; do not let them drift silently.
4. sp-mtvg shipped a mechanism-lock test guarding against ACCIDENTAL horizon widening — this is the DELIBERATE widening, so that test must be updated in the same change (expect it RED first), not bypassed.
5. Keep MAX_TOUR_SYSTEMS (per-tour distinct-system cap) a separate knob from the DISCOVERY hop-depth — they are different dials; widening discovery must not implicitly change the per-tour cap.

=== VALIDATION BAR ===
* Offline first: replay_objective.py already supports --candidate-hop-depth and --widen (rate-only multi-cap sweep) — run depth 1 vs 2 vs 3 fleet-$/hr on reconstructed real snapshots BEFORE arming. --verify-bfs proves depth-1 is byte-identical to today's shape (regression fence).
* The travel matrix must make a 3-hop lane's projected hours ~3x a 1-hop lane's — pin that in a test; it is the exact mis-pricing the guard existed to prevent.
* projected-vs-realized honesty: tour_plan_rate{phase=projected|realized} must not diverge more at depth 3 than at depth 1 (i.e. the new travel model is honest, not just permissive).

=== NOTES ===
* Feasibility probe files are UNCOMMITTED throwaways in services/routing-service (probe_timing_TEMP.py, replay_hopwiden_TEMP.py) — someone was already benchmarking exactly this. Reuse or delete deliberately; do not ship them.
* Admiral framing: this is the durable answer to 'why aren't we spreading the fleet' — it spreads reach WITH correct pricing, versus a random-walk (which spreads coverage but still leaves every tour 1-hop, so it cannot capture the 28k/u cross-hop lanes).
* Complementary to, not a duplicate of, sp-ry741 (fix long-haul). If 3-hop tours land, reconsider whether the separate long-haul executor is still worth its bug surface.

title: Raise single-sink absorption depth cap: fleet sells 0.70 tranches/visit, leaving ~4x throughput on the table
description:
ECONOMY-ANALYST FINDING (torwind-2026-07-19, measured 2026-07-24T21:10Z, player 4).

The absorption-based single-sink depth cap armed 2026-07-23 00:42 is now the binding depth constraint (supersedes TOUR_SOLVER_MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES, per st-wisp-zmtu3). It is calibrated far too conservatively.

MEASURED (12h, tour_leg_telemetry JOIN market_data):
- avg sell leg 52.4 units into avg sink trade_volume 92.6 => 0.704 tranches per sink visit
- heavies are 225-cap => 23% hull utilization; median leg 40 units
- sell-leg realization 99.7% (25,360/25,438 units) => sinks are NOT refusing volume
- fresh IMPORT+EXCHANGE capacity 546,045 units/tranche vs TOTAL fleet cargo 3,550 units (154x headroom)

ECONOMICS OF GOING DEEPER (avg buy 2,794 / sell 4,224 => margin 1,430/unit = 33.9% of sell price):
- now:       52 units x 1,430 = ~74.9k profit per sink visit
- 2 tranches: 185 units x ~1,346 = ~249k per visit (3.3x)
- fill hull:  225 units x ~1,324 = ~298k per visit (4.0x)
Same nav/dock overhead in all three. Price-impact assumption 1.5%/tranche (PLAYBOOK 2 prior).
ROBUSTNESS: still ~2.9x even if decay is 4x worse (6%/tranche). Turns net-negative only at ~18.8%/tranche decay (12.5x the prior) - not physically plausible.

ASK: expose the cap's aggressiveness as a knob and raise target depth from ~0.7 to ~2.5 tranches (or min(2.5 tranches, remaining hull capacity)). Preserve the fail-closed behavior (RULINGS 4) - this raises a performance ceiling, not a money guard.

SECOND (smaller) LEVER: the planner routes to sinks with median trade_volume 80 while fresh available sinks median 120 - candidate shortlist may be too narrow (TOUR_SOLVER_FULL_SCORE_TOP_N=35, clamp 100).

ERA CLOCK: reset 2026-07-26T13:00Z. Hull-purchase freeze T-10h = 2026-07-26T03:00Z. This is a config/calibration change, so it can pay back inside the window; hull capex largely cannot.
notes:
MERGED to main as 15940747 (gate green: full suite, Merged=true, EmptyMerge=false). DEPLOYED
2026-07-29 11:37 local — PYTHON ONLY, so routing-service restart via `ENV=prod make deploy-routing`
(com.spacetraders.routing, pid 38876 -> 56931). NO daemon restart, no proto, no Go. Verified serving:
4 tours planned post-restart, zero routing errors.

BEAD NUMBERS RE-DERIVED FOR OUR ERA BEFORE BUILDING (the bead was player 4 / era torwind-2026-07-19; we
are player 5, era 5) and they replicate:
  - 42.4% of planned sell legs pinned at EXACTLY 1.0 x trade_volume (211/498) — the cap was genuinely binding
  - 496 of 499 planned sell legs realized EXACTLY the planned units, ZERO stranded, 3 under
  - avg realized depth 0.668 tranches/visit (bead said 0.704) against 225-cargo heavies

IMPORTANT EVIDENCE CORRECTION THE LANE MADE: the bead's "99.7% sell-leg realization" CANNOT license the
raise, because it is measured UNDER a cap of 1 and so cannot distinguish "tranche 2 would realize" from
"we never attempt tranche 2". What actually licenses it is the FITTED DECAY: the tiers carrying the volume
decay only 1-2% per tranche (SCARCE|WEAK 0.9888 n=3189, LIMITED|WEAK 0.9783 n=944, SCARCE|GROWING 0.9886
n=718) — better than the bead's 1.5% prior. At 33.9% margin, tranche 4 is still profitable on the worst
well-sampled tier.

BUILT: REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES_PER_VISIT 1 -> 2.5, ARMED, no enable seam. Env-overridable exactly like
TOUR_SOLVER_MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES: TOUR_SOLVER_REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES, float cast, clamp [1.0, 6.0],
resolved once per solve_tour and threaded to the single read site. Disarm =
TOUR_SOLVER_REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES=1 + restart routing, which reproduces sp-2v69u byte-for-byte (pinned by
a test). min(2.5 tranches, remaining hull capacity) needed no work — slack = hold_cap - max(occ[i:j])
already binds ahead of the cap, and that ordering is now pinned.

A GAP IN THE BEAD, NOW RECORDED: TWO independent bounds govern this quantity and the bead named only one.
The per-(market,good,side) pool ladder holds max_planned_tranches x tv for the whole tour, so effective
depth is min(realized_sink_tranches, max_planned_tranches) x tv. run.sh:40 arms

that run.sh knob re-clips this one. Verified armed at 3 in the live run.sh before deploying.

THE GAIN IS LARGER THAN THE BEAD ESTIMATED. Six shipped tests moved, all one root cause, and the root
cause IS the feature: a hull no longer needs a second visit to lift a second tranche. The golden tour
collapses A->D->E->D->E to A->D->E with an IDENTICAL per-price trade set and IDENTICAL profit — same
cargo, one round trip instead of two, 2 x 1800s of crossing time saved. So the 3.3-4.0x per-visit estimate
UNDERSTATES the effect: it counted profit per visit but not the travel removed. Re-pinning shipped
expectations is normally a cardinal sin; correct here only because raising this exact calibration IS the
bead, and each test's property was preserved rather than deleted. The closed-rate flip window was
