/ 1 skipped (test_replay_objective.py cannot collect — missing sqlalchemy, confirmed failing identically
on main, pre-existing and unrelated). PROPERTY SWEEP over 400 randomized boards: 483 per-leg sell
allocations, ZERO exceeding int(cap x tv), max observed depth exactly 2.500, 195 pinned at the cap —
nothing became unbounded. 10 mutations, ALL KILLED, each naming its target. M10 (cap applied to DEPOSIT
pairings) SURVIVED the lane's own file and was killed by 9 pre-existing deposit tests — reported straight
rather than banked, because the deposit exemption was not changed and so the new file has no coverage for it.

reduces planned units; hull capacity, spend cap, min_margin and the fleet-wide absorption netting are
byte-untouched and still bind ahead of it; the 1.0 floor means it cannot be tuned to plan no sells.

MEASUREMENT TO WATCH: per-visit depth 0.668 -> ~1.7-2.5 tranches; realized sell price per good for
concentration erosion; legs-per-tour should FALL (that is the travel saving).

sp-brr68 (executed_hard_cap 12h vs re-fitted 26-39h half-lives) and sp-4mpxh (planner sells into median
tv=60 sinks while fresh sinks are median 120 — compounds directly, since this cap is a MULTIPLE of tv).
POST-DEPLOY MEASUREMENT: THE CHANGE IS CORRECT, HARMLESS, AND INERT. It raised a ceiling that is not the
binding constraint. Do NOT raise the cap further; no value of it changes anything. Measurement script
b74cf07e on sp-28lw9-m: gobot/scripts/sp28lw9_effect_measurement.sql.

DEPLOY VERIFIED FIRST, before blaming anything else: merge 15940747 landed 14:39:41Z, routing PID 56931
started 14:40:07Z (26s later), no TOUR_SOLVER_REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES override in its environment, main's
source has REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES_PER_VISIT = 2.5, and main's actual solver run against a live-shaped
fixture (hull 225, tv 69) planned 2.00 tranches. The code is live and works.

THE MEASUREMENT (n~290 good-loads, 12h):
  mean units carried of the good sold ... 64
  mean sink trade_volume ............... 131
  mean carried, in tranches ............ 0.66
  loads carrying >1 tranche ............ ~7%
For a 2.5-tranche cap to bind, a hull must carry 2.5 x 131 ~= 328 units of a SINGLE good. It carries 64.
The binding term is buy_rem in units = min(buy_rem, sell_rem, slack, afford) — SOURCE POOL DEPTH, i.e.
export markets at 51-80 units. Post-deploy discriminator confirms: max planned sell depth still EXACTLY
1.000 x tv, zero legs above the old cap.

THE FLAW IN THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS — MINE AND THE LANE'S: sp-28lw9's headline was "42.4% of planned sell
legs pinned at exactly 1.0 x trade_volume", read as the SELL cap binding. That figure is EQUALLY
CONSISTENT WITH THE BUY SIDE BINDING at the same value, because source depth and sink trade_volume are
both ~one trade_volume — both hypotheses predict the identical pin. Raising the cap and re-measuring is
what separates them, and nothing moved. It was the buy side all along. This is the SAME "the evidence
cannot distinguish the two hypotheses" flaw the lane correctly flagged in the bead's own 99.7%-realization
figure, reproduced one paragraph later in its own analysis. The measurement that should have run BEFORE
building is the carrying measurement above — units of a good per load vs sink tv — one query.

THE CHANGE IS NOT HARMFUL AND SHOULD STAY: it only ever RAISES a ceiling, is byte-identical wherever the
ceiling is not reached, and its 20 mutations plus the full suite stand. It is a correct PREREQUISITE that
pays the moment a hull can fill on the buy side. It simply is not doing anything yet.

(a) NET EFFECT NOT MEASURABLE, and not close: 4 closed cycles POST vs 84 PRE in 49 minutes, against
hourly margin swinging -18.6% to +61.5%. And since the mechanism is not firing there would be no signal
with more hours either.
(b) The "more, smaller legs" shape is NOT the cap: average planned tranches went DOWN (0.659 -> 0.584)
and max stayed pinned at 1.000. A depth cap cannot produce more legs — only bigger ones. On 25 post legs
this is composition/noise, most likely the ~15:20 daemon restart relaunching tours.
(c) DO NOT RAISE. Effective depth is min(realized_sink_tranches, max_planned_tranches, buy_rem, slack,
afford) x tv. Measured binding term is buy_rem at ~0.66 tranches. Raising realized 2.5 -> 4 changes
nothing; raising max_planned_tranches 3 -> 4 changes nothing. Both are upstream-dominated. My framing
that the pool ladder was "the next constraint" was wrong — it is THIRD in line.
(d) Statistical honesty from the lane: at a ~7% rate of >1-tranche loads, observing zero in 25 post legs
has probability ~0.16, so the post window ALONE cannot prove the cap never fires. The carrying
measurement (n~290) is the robust evidence and is independent of the deploy window.

STRUCTURAL LIMIT WORTH RECORDING: 13 of 18 trade hulls are 80-hold lights and 80 is BELOW the 131 mean
sink tv, so the sell cap is unreachable for lights BY CONSTRUCTION, independent of the buy side. It can
only ever fire on the 5 heavies.

THE ORDERED CONSTRAINT CHAIN, measured end to end:
  source pool (~64 units) -> hull capacity (80 for 13 of 18) -> sink depth (131) -> the 2.5 cap
  BINDS                      BINDS                              slack               slack
The single number that decides the next lever is UNITS ACQUIRABLE PER GOOD PER VISIT: currently 64
against holds of 80 and 225.

ADMIRAL PRINCIPLE the fix MUST enforce: 'We absolutely cannot buy cargo and not sell it. If we buy cargo, we must sell it, not stall the fleet.' A buy must be gated on a GUARANTEED, RESERVED, REACHABLE, FRESH, sufficiently-DEEP sink for the sell BEFORE the cargo is purchased; if no sink can be firmly guaranteed the hull must NOT buy (wait/reposition). === ROOT CAUSE (code-level) ===
The tour engine treats the absorption 'reservation' as PLAN-TIME inter-container coordination bookkeeping, NOT a firm, execution-time, market-backed sell guarantee. The buy commits on that soft reservation with no re-validation at buy time. It is a COMBINATION of all three candidates (A + C + B):

--- A. BUY COMMITS ON A SOFT, RELEASABLE, NEVER-REVALIDATED RESERVATION ---
Order of operations: plan -> reserve(PLANNED) -> [fly] -> buy@source leg -> haul -> sell@sink leg. There IS a reserve-before-buy, but it does not guarantee the sell:
* planAndReserve() reserves BOTH buy & sell tranches all-or-nothing at PLAN time, retrying on breach (tourReserveMaxRetries=2) BEFORE flying — run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:69-107.
* The reservation is a per-(waypoint,good,side) COORDINATION cap = tourACapTranches(2) x trade_volume, and it only excludes OTHER tour containers; it reserves NO real market liquidity/price. absorption_ledger_repository.go:123-134 (Reserve: decayed outstanding + this plan <= CapUnits); buildTourReserveEntries run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:146-200.
* The BUY commits leg-by-leg in executeBuy (run_tour_coordinator.go:1421-1539). It sizes units by: cargo space, BUY-market trade_volume, maxSpend, working-capital floor, buy-price ceiling — and NEVER re-validates that the downstream SINK is still reserved/fresh/reachable/deep. CONTRAST: the long-haul engine's achievableUnits bounds the buy by the sink's LIVE absorption headroom (run_longhaul_arb_selection.go:16-34, line 27) — exactly the execution-time gate the tour buy lacks.
* By the time the hull reaches the sink leg the sell can be SKIPPED ENTIRELY if the live price moved past tourPriceTolerancePct (executeTrade run_tour_coordinator.go:1402-1413) or only PARTIALLY filled if live trade_volume shrank (executeSell run_tour_coordinator.go:1581-1586) -> already-bought cargo stays in the hold. NOTE sellsBeforeBuys (run_tour_coordinator.go:1345,2335) only orders sells-before-buys WITHIN a leg; buys and sells sit on DIFFERENT legs/waypoints, so the buy is committed a full leg (travel) before its sell is even attempted.

--- C. RE-PLAN AFTER A BUY RELEASES THE RESERVATION AND STRANDS THE CARGO ---
* On any leg degradation, runOneTour re-plans, bounded by replanLimit=2 (run_tour_coordinator.go:1223-1262). Re-plan calls planAndReserve -> releaseTourReservations FIRST, DROPPING the hull's own PLANNED sink rows (run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:311-323), then re-plans cargo-aware. On a saturated sink surface (14 heavies) the re-plan breaches (2 retries) -> exits infeasible -> tour STOPS holding the cargo (run_tour_coordinator.go:1231-1235 'any unsold tour cargo will report as stranded'). This is the live 'breached the fleet-wide sink cap - re-planning against the now-occupied sink' churn (reserveTourPlan run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:131-135).
* The after-the-fact rescue maybeOffloadHeldCargo (run_tour_coordinator_offload.go:130-205) is best-effort and bounded to ONE reposition per episode ('no hop-scotching', line 141) and exits STILL-LADEN if no reachable candidate can absorb the held cargo (line 165-170).

--- B. NO FLEET-LEVEL BUY / INVENTORY THROTTLE ---
* The ONLY throttle is the per-sink coordination cap (2 x trade_volume), which DECAYS via EXECUTED-shadow half-life (absorption_ledger_repository.go:493-505, blockingResidual/decayedUnits) — sinks 'reopen' in the ledger's view before the real market recovers.
* There is NO aggregate gate that fleet-wide outstanding unsold inventory <= total reachable sink absorption. 14 heavies independently plan+reserve+buy and collectively overshoot the sink surface. run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go only relaunches idle hulls + runs the liveness watchdog; it NEVER checks aggregate inventory vs absorption before dispatching more buy-tours. (grep confirmed: only the long-haul engine has an absorption-headroom buy bound.)
* The 12-min liveness watchdog (defaultWatchdogStallSeconds=720, run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:99) does NOT catch these hulls: it keys on PROGRESS (plan/navigate/arrive/buy/sell), so a hull that keeps re-planning/navigating/occasionally-buying 'progresses' indefinitely without ever clearing its hold; IN_TRANSIT hulls are skipped outright.

=== FIX DIRECTION (for shipwright; do NOT fork the ledger) ===
Enforce the Admiral principle by making a firm sink the PRECONDITION of the buy, and add a fleet aggregate throttle:
1) EXECUTION-TIME SINK GATE on the buy: before executeBuy commits, re-validate that this cargo has a firmly-reserved, reachable, FRESH, sufficiently-deep sink still held for it, and SIZE the buy to the sink's live absorption headroom — port the long-haul achievableUnits pattern (run_longhaul_arb_selection.go:16-34) into executeBuy (run_tour_coordinator.go:1421). If headroom<=0 or the sink reservation is no longer firm/fresh, buy 0 (skip -> re-plan/wait), never buy on spec. Fail-closed (RULINGS #4: adds a spend precondition).
2) HOLD THE SINK RESERVATION FIRM THROUGH THE SELL: do not release-then-rebreach the sink out from under already-bought cargo. Re-plan/offload of a laden hull must PRESERVE (not drop) the reservation backing cargo already in the hold (revisit releaseTourReservations run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go:311 + the re-plan path run_tour_coordinator.go:1244-1249). 3) FLEET-WIDE BUY THROTTLE: gate new buy-tours on remaining fleet-wide sink-absorption headroom so aggregate outstanding unsold inventory <= total reachable absorption (buy rate <= sink absorption rate). title: Break the construction buy-only deadlock — deferred gate material must recover via FABRICATE source, not just buy-market
description: ROOT CAUSE (verified live on DEV15 + in code): the thin-drain construction path BUYS a gate material from the factory's own EXPORT market without feeding the factory. The next DELIVER_TO_CONSTRUCTION task is then planned buy-only with no clearable source, so it becomes DEFERRED (IsDeferredConstruction: DeliverToConstruction && sourceMarket=='' && factorySymbol=='', task.go:374). resourceDeferredConstructionTask (task_activator.go:290) only ever calls FindConstructionSource (market_locator.go:482 — buy-market, MODERATE-gated, skips SCARCE) and only assigns a BUY source (UpdateSourceMarket) — never a factory. A manufactured EXPORT never regenerates its market supply without being FED, so the task is stuck PENDING forever. The feeder (unified_gate_fill produce path, run_construction_coordinator.go:799) that WOULD feed F45 only runs for READY tasks -> deadlock. FIX: when the deferred-recovery finds no buy source, resolve a FACTORY that exports the good (reuse the planner's fabricate/factory resolution) and set it on the task (add a domain UpdateFactorySymbol if needed) so IsDeferredConstruction()=false -> task goes READY -> the produce path fabricates+feeds the factory (buy inputs, feed, harvest, deliver). Under always-on unified gate-fill (sp-9i4mq) fabricate should be the PRIMARY recovery for a manufacturable good; buy-market is the fallback for goods with no factory. title: Probe-buyer relay self-jumps/fail-loops: shared buyer hull relayed CONCURRENTLY by frontier+freshsizer with no journey claim desyncs the no-reload multi-hop loop (NOT graph corruption) — probe fleet starved 156 vs cap 200
description:
SYMPTOM (live-verified 2026-07-24 ~14:07Z, player 4, era 4 torwind-2026-07-19)
The satellite/probe fleet is STUCK at exactly 156 and will not grow toward its cap (max_probe_fleet=200 on both the frontier and the freshsizer), though aggregate probe demand ~281-302 >> supply 156. Only 1 probe PURCHASE_SHIP in the last 90m (13:43:09 @ X1-DY16-X12D, -27907) — the fleet is essentially not growing. Loosening the pacing tunes (freshsizer purchase_cooldown 60->15, max_spend 500k->2M) had no effect: pacing is NOT the binding constraint. Probe BUYS are FAILING on navigation.

Both the frontier AND the freshsizer relay their probe buy through the SAME buyer hull (TORWIND-19), and both fail at a mid-route jump:
- Freshsizer 14:05:43: "buy failed (fail-closed): failed to relay probe buyer to X1-BT98-A11Z: ... jump TORWIND-19 to X1-MH84 (hop 2 of 4 toward X1-BT98) failed: no jump gate connection from origin gate X1-KG37-A11A to system X1-MH84 after 3 live reads".
- Frontier 13:45:44: "failed to relay probe buyer to X1-AA14-C16F: ... jump TORWIND-19 to X1-UJ44 (hop 3 of 4 toward X1-AA14) failed: no jump gate connection from origin gate X1-YP49-E25D to system X1-UJ44 after 3 live reads".
INTERMITTENT: the 13:43 DY16 buy succeeded, then subsequent buys fail — a buy succeeds only when the picked yard's full route is live-connected from the buyer's current position.

LIVE DB VERIFICATION (era 4, read-only @ ~14:07):
- TORWIND-19: location X1-KG37-A11A, origin_symbol X1-YP49-E25D, IN_ORBIT, undedicated (the shared relay buyer).
- gate_edges FROM X1-KG37 = {X1-KK42, X1-UJ44, X1-YP49} — NOT X1-MH84. gate_edges INTO X1-MH84 = {X1-CQ56, X1-NY55, X1-VY63, X1-YP49}. So X1-YP49 -> X1-MH84 IS a valid stored edge, but X1-KG37 -> X1-MH84 is genuinely ABSENT (not under construction). The committed plan therefore contained the consecutive pair X1-KG37 -> X1-MH84 (hop 1 YP49->KG37 is valid and explains origin_symbol=YP49; hop 2 KG37->MH84 is invalid), i.e. the plan disagreed with live connectivity, and the valid approach to MH84 is from YP49, not KG37.
- Target X1-BT98-A11Z = fresh (scanned 14:07) era-4 HIGH SHIP_PROBE yard; X1-AA14-C16F = era-4 MODERATE probe yard — both legit current-era picks. A REACHABLE current-era fallback existed: X1-MH84 has TWO era-4 SHIP_PROBE yards (X1-MH84-E26A, X1-MH84-F18C), and X1-MH84 is 1 hop from X1-YP49 over the valid YP49->MH84 edge — yet the buy fail-looped the unreachable X1-BT98 pick.

ROOT CAUSE (code-level) — THREE different graph views gate / commit / execute the buy, none live-validates the committed route before flying, and there is no fallback on failure:
1. SELECTION (reachability signal, STORED graph): ProbePurchaser.resolveProximalBuy (internal/adapters/expansion/adapters.go:211) -> reachableYardsByBuyerSystem (adapters.go:267) -> ReachableYardFinder.NearestYardsSelling (internal/application/shipyard/queries/reachable_yards.go:68) -> hopDistances, a BFS over the PERSISTED stored adjacency (reachable_yards.go:135-174, f.gates.Adjacency, under-construction excluded, bound MaxJumpPath=5). This marks the far yard "reachable" from the buyer's system purely from the stored gate graph. Its own doc admits the rank is only "a SIGNAL ... optimistic" (reachable_yards.go:46-49).
2. COMMIT (flight plan, FETCH-THROUGH cache): BuyProbe (adapters.go:150) -> relayAndRecheck (adapters.go:541) -> navigateBuyerToYard -> NavigateRouteCommand (adapters.go:559) -> NavigateRouteHandler.tryCrossSystemNavigate -> crossSystemRouter.RepositionToWaypoint (navigate_route.go:377) -> travel -> travelWithJumpBound(...,0,0,0) (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:267) -> the STRICT fetch-through Path / PathWithinJumps (internal/application/system/gategraph/service.go:605/619) over the Connections CACHE (gate_edges + on-miss live fetch). The ordered system sequence is computed ONCE at travel.go:325 (jumpPath).
3. EXECUTION (LIVE per-hop): the hop loop (travel.go:397-418) jumps to each path[i] with NO reload/re-plan, trusting each jump lands the hull on path[i]'s gate; jump_ship resolves the next gate from the ORIGIN gate's LIVE connections and, after 3 re-reads confirm the planned next system is genuinely absent, fails at internal/application/ship/commands/navigation/jump_ship.go:519. travel.go:406 wraps it ("hop N of M toward"), RepositionToWaypoint wraps it (travel.go:509), the relay surfaces it (adapters.go:564).

The committed route contained a hop the live gate rejects — a chart-vs-reality mismatch the plan (built over the cached/stored graph) did not catch and that sp-hguq3's 3-read retry cannot rescue (3 reads correctly confirm GENUINE absence). Two compounding gaps:
- No LIVE, route-level reachability validation before the buy commits: the reachability signal is stored-graph-only (view 1), the flight plan is cache-based (view 2), and only the per-hop live read (view 3) sees the truth — by then the hull is already flying and the buy fails.
- BuyProbe fails CLOSED on the relay error (adapters.go:158-161) with NO fallback to the next-nearest REACHABLE current-era probe yard. resolveProximalBuy re-runs next cycle and, from the same buyer position + same stored graph, re-picks the SAME live-unroutable yard -> a fail-loop. The own-system 0-hop fallback (mergeReachByMinHops, adapters.go:331) only engages when demandProximalReachable is EMPTY; here the far yard is (wrongly) judged reachable by the stored-graph finder, so that fallback never triggers.
RESULT: probe buys clear only when the picked yard's full route happens to be live-connected from the buyer's current position; otherwise fail-loop. Fleet starved at 156 vs cap 200 (1 buy/90m), starving market freshness — the gating lever for absorbing the trade fleet.

FIX (recommended shape; shipwright designs the implementation):
- Validate the target yard's reachability under LIVE gate connectivity BEFORE committing the buy — verify the CHOSEN path's hops live, mirroring the sp-0o9ub "plan cheap over stored adjacency, verify only the chosen path" resolver (PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify, service.go:708) but extended to LIVE connectivity, not just under-construction. REUSE the ONE shared reachable-route resolver (sp-mepj / Lever-1 REUSE INVARIANT) — do NOT fork path logic; ideally make the reachability signal and the flight planner agree on ONE graph view (or gate the pick through the SAME resolver the flight uses) so selection can never deem reachable a route the flight cannot fly.
- On a failed reposition, FALL BACK to the next-nearest REACHABLE current-era probe yard (iterate the ranked candidates, skipping the one that just failed live) instead of failing closed and re-picking the same unreachable yard. Bound the fallback (try a few reachable candidates per cycle, not an unbounded sweep).
- The intermittent successes and the DB prove reachable current-era probe yards exist (e.g. X1-MH84's two era-4 yards 1 hop from YP49), so this is a selection/validation/fallback fix, not a supply problem.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Probe buys succeed and the fleet grows toward max_probe_fleet whenever a reachable current-era probe yard exists.
- A probe buy NEVER fail-loops on a live-unroutable yard while a reachable current-era yard exists — it falls back to the reachable one in the same or next cycle.
- The reachability judged for the buy is consistent with the flight planner's live route (no stored-vs-cached-vs-live divergence that commits an unflyable route).
- Regression test: a buyer at a poorly-connected origin gate with a stored-graph-reachable-but-live-unroutable demand yard AND a reachable nearer yard -> the buy lands at the reachable yard (no fail-loop); byte-identical non-interference for the happy path. build / vet / gofmt / go test ./... (-race) green.

RELATED: sp-xvi15 (frontier probe-buyer targeted an unreachable far yard — its reachability fix is STORED-graph-based, so THIS is the residual live-vs-stored gap it left open), sp-hguq3 (charted-but-live-rejected hop; its 3-read retry addresses MISSING-connection transients at EXECUTION, not a route committed over a disagreeing graph with no re-plan/fallback), sp-ju9pn / sp-0o9ub (gate-graph planning cost + the PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify "plan cheap, verify chosen path" pattern to REUSE for the live verify), and the market-freshness beads sp-wuksw / sp-j4kjv this unblocks.

CONSTRAINTS: RULINGS #4 money-guards UNTOUCHED — fail-closed is SAFE (non-functional, zero bad spend; the 25% treasury ceiling and the live-dock re-price stay intact; the fix restores function without weakening any guard). #2 restart-idempotent (re-derive from the persisted store, no in-memory-only state). #13 land via captain-gate. Protected paths NOT modified: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**. ONE shared route resolver (sp-mepj REUSE INVARIANT) — do not fork path logic.

CLASSIFICATION: RECURRENCE of the sp-xvi15 / sp-hguq3 reachability family — specifically the residual case neither closed: the reachability signal sp-xvi15 added is stored-graph-based and diverges from the live route, and sp-hguq3's 3-read fix confirms-but-does-not-rescue a route committed over a disagreeing graph when there is no fallback.

title: Demand-weighted freshness: prioritize probe freshness by realized fleet trade-flow, not intrinsic market value
description:
PROBLEM (structural; Admiral-escalated 2026-07-24 "the fix must be automatic, not manual"): freshness allocation is DECOUPLED from where the fleet actually earns. The freshsizer weights its P90-age target by per-market INTRINSIC value Sigma(trade_volume x price) (run_market_freshness_sizer_coordinator.go:114-115,219) -- NOT by the fleet's realized demand through a sink. Under supply<demand (live era-4: freshsizer reports 238 probe demand vs 154 supply) the triage therefore starves the fleet's TOP REVENUE sinks. Live evidence: of the top-12 realized-revenue sinks (48h), 4 are currently UNRANKABLE -- X1-CC13-EX3B (8.5M sell, the #1 sink, 717m stale, past its ranker cap), X1-KQ55-EX1C (7.7M, #3, fully DARK), X1-YY85-FE9A (5.9M, 582m), X1-CD11-X11C (4.1M, 614m). ~26M of recent sell-value on sinks the ranker can't reach. value_weighted=2 (max) does NOT fix it: intrinsic market value != earned value. Today the only remedy is a human pinning scout posts by hand -- the crutch this bead removes.

CHANGE (feature, ship ARMED -- Admiral: no flags EVER): make freshness prioritization DEMAND-AWARE. Add a realized-sink-demand weight per market/system from tour_leg_telemetry sell legs (EWMA of realized sell-value or units per sink over a rolling window -- the SAME telemetry the auto-outfit coordinator already reads; SELECT-only; scope by player_id). Use it as the PRIMARY weight source for the value-weighted percentile / per-system demand triage, with the existing intrinsic Sigma(trade_volume x price) as the COLD-START PRIOR for markets not yet traded. Effect: when supply<demand the freshsizer automatically holds SLA on the sinks the fleet earns through and lets zero-demand markets breach -- no manual pinning. Auto-adaptive: a newly-discovered deep sink the trade/long-haul fleet starts hitting auto-climbs freshness priority (EWMA rises); a decayed lane drops off. Also relieves long-haul's single-sink clustering by keeping several deep sinks fresh to rotate across (fallow-recovery, per the freshness report -> higher margin).

KNOB SHAPE (RULINGS #5, defined-once): reuse the existing value_weighted mode. Make mode 2 (the armed default) use DEMAND-PRIMARY weighting (intrinsic fallback); keep mode 1 = off (plain count percentile) as the existing escape. EWMA half-life = a tune knob (default ~2-4h, matches the lane-decay priors). No NEW flag.

GRACEFUL FALLBACK (data-driven, not a flag): no telemetry / cold start / a market never traded -> intrinsic value prior -> BYTE-IDENTICAL to today when there is zero realized-demand data. Value-weighted P90 + release/hysteresis logic INTACT -- this changes only the WEIGHT SOURCE, not the sizing math or the SLA.

GUARDRAILS: orthogonal to and MUST NOT touch the ranker cap (sp-t5sh5) or per-activity SLA (sp-j4kjv) -- it changes WHICH markets win scarce freshness, not the caps or the freshness-vs-frontier split. Execution money guards (#4) untouched. Protected paths untouched. Multi-player: scope every telemetry read by player_id (the tables are multi-player).

MEASURE (armed): per-sink freshness of the top-N realized-revenue sinks (should stay under their ranker caps), routable-revenue-sink count, fleet $/hr. Refit the EWMA window per era.

RELATION: completes the freshness family -- sp-t5sh5 (ranker caps) + sp-j4kjv (per-activity SLA) + THIS (demand-weighted prioritization). Orthogonal to sp-tlekc Phase 4 (freshness-vs-frontier probe split; this is intra-freshness prioritization). Interim manual stopgap until it lands = captain pins scout posts on the starved sinks (CC13/KQ55/CD11) -- but the Admiral has ruled the durable fix must be automatic, which is this.

Refs: report https://claude.ai/code/artifact/018f0d6a-570c-4e2c-ab53-781aeb042050 ; bd memory economy-analyst-freshness-profit ; captain consult reply st-wisp-zqr7k ; era-4 live data 2026-07-24.

Knob: value_weighted mode 2 (armed default)=demand-primary, 1=off; demand_ewma_half_life_secs (default 3h). No new flag. Verified live: daemon healthy, freshsizer cycling. title: Trade fleet over-saturates at 8+ heavies: sp-m3122 liveness watchdog false-kills hulls mid jump-cooldown on sp-tp5c3's widened far tours — orphans reserved sells, thrashes, sells never keep pace with buys
description:
SYMPTOM (live-verified 2026-07-24 03:39-04:18Z, player 4, era torwind-2026-07-19)
The 14-hull trade fleet (9 heavy freighters cap-225 + 5 lights) over-saturates: it buys ~2-3x faster than it sells, hulls sit FULL and cannot offload, throughput collapses at 8+ heavies.
- Buys >> sells: last 60m 63 PURCHASE_CARGO (-9.7M) vs 34 SELL_CARGO (+8.58M); last 15m only 8 sells across 3 systems while buys keep going.
- All hulls loaded: 04:17Z snapshot 9 heavies at/near 225/225 (6 exactly full), lights 80/80; almost none empty/cycling.
- Watchdog kill CASCADE: the sp-m3122 trade-fleet liveness watchdog killed+relaunched nearly EVERY trade hull every ~12min for "no progress >=12m" — TORWIND-81/E/80/56/57/16 each killed 2-3x in 40m, kills clustered at 12m0s-12m29s. Each kill logs "reclaimed N absorption reservation(s) held by non-existent containers" (2 to 18).
- Treasury drains as cash ties up in unsold inventory.

ROOT CAUSE (code-level) — the sp-m3122 liveness watchdog FALSE-KILLS a trade hull that is legitimately waiting out a multi-hop JUMP COOLDOWN on an sp-tp5c3-widened far tour; the kill orphans the hull's reserved-but-unexecuted sells, relaunch re-plans the same far tour, and the fleet thrashes so sells never complete. This is NOT the leading hypothesis (#1 shared cold-cache reach storm); it is a NEW liveness-signal defect closest to candidate #4 but caused by the watchdog, not the absorption re-plan.

Chain (paths absolute under gobot/):
1. The liveness signal is LOG-DERIVED: internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:105-107 LastTourProgress = LatestLogTimestamps = the newest container-log line; its own doc (:99-101) says the trail "advances on every real step (plan/navigate/arrive/buy/sell) but NOT on the wall-clock heartbeat (writes no log on success)."
2. The jump-cooldown wait is SILENT: internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:83 logs "Waiting out jump cooldown before continuing the circuit" ONCE at the START of the wait (action jump_cooldown_wait), then emits nothing until the cooldown ends and the next jump logs. LIVE PROOF (TORWIND-B0, container tour-run-TORWIND-B0-02477cbe): jumps succeed in ~1s but consecutive jumps are 03:54:45 -> 04:04:25 apart = a 9m40s SILENT gap; a farther jump (or jump->cooldown->in-system navigate) crosses 12m of log-silence.
3. The watchdog kills on that silence: internal/application/trading/commands/watchdog.go:84-96 — for a PARKED (not IN_TRANSIT) container-claimed hull whose LastTourProgress is >= threshold, StopTour kills the container and relaunch (:106) starts a fresh one. The IN_TRANSIT skip (:60-67) does NOT protect a cooling-down hull: the jump already COMPLETED, so the hull is IN_ORBIT (parked) during the cooldown wait — exactly the watchdog's kill target. Threshold = defaultWatchdogStallSeconds=720 (run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:99), live 12m (no config override).
4. The TRIGGER is sp-tp5c3's ARMED widening: config.yaml:189 max_tour_systems=4 + :190 candidate_hop_depth=2 (re-armed 2026-07-23). The solver now plans tours spanning up to 4 systems / sinks 2 gate-hops out, so execution must reposition MULTIPLE hops; each far jump's game-mechanic cooldown (5-10+ min) is waited out silently and the silent stretch reaches >=12m.
5. The CASCADE: each false-kill (StopTour -> StopContainer) releases the hull and reclaims its PLANNED absorption reservations (the "reclaimed N ... non-existent containers" line, 2-18 per kill) — the sinks the hull had reserved for its 225-unit fan-out but was killed before selling. Relaunch re-plans the SAME widened far tour, re-reserves, and is killed at the next cooldown. Perpetual thrash: the hull never finishes its multi-sink sell fan-out, stays loaded, and the fast near-source buy leg outpaces the sell side that never completes -> over-saturation.

WHY NOT candidate #1/#2/#3: Trade execution routes cross-system legs via the STRICT fetch-through Path at MaxJumpPath=5 (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:220-223), NOT the bound-25 PathWithinJumps that stormed long-haul; B0's jumps resolve in ~1s (WARM cache). Reach is NOT collapsed: the absorption ledger shows 272 EXECUTED sells across 98 DISTINCT sink waypoints, sells spread over 13 systems/60m — dispersion IS happening. So the widened solver (sp-tp5c3) works AND the reach is warm; the binding defect is the watchdog converting legitimate cooldown latency into kills.

COMPOUNDING (secondary, quantified, not dominant):
- Shallow sinks (sp-2v69u depth problem): 276 of 281 EXECUTED sells are WEAK/RESTRICTED tier at avg ~53 units/sell, so a 225 heavy needs ~4-5 distinct sinks to offload — a long multi-hop fan-out that MULTIPLIES cooldown-wait exposure and thus false-kill probability.
- Freshness (economy-analyst candidate): 396 fresh vs 286 stale distinct IMPORT sinks (~58% fresh) — freshness shrinks the surface but 396 fresh sinks is AMPLE for 14 hulls, so it is a minor amplifier (a hull forced to a FARTHER fresh sink incurs a longer cooldown -> higher false-kill odds), NOT the binding constraint. The dominant defect is reach/depth-agnostic: even a near sell journey with ONE silent cooldown >=12m is killed.

RELATION TO sp-ju9pn (VERDICT: SAME symptom class + SHARED watchdog engine, but DISTINCT root — does NOT unify under the stored-adjacency reach fix):
- sp-ju9pn/sp-0o9ub: the hull is silent because a cold-cache fetch-through STORM (PathWithinJumps bound-25, live GetJumpGate per uncached system) blocks PLANNING ~20min; fixed by planning over stored adjacency. A PLANNING hang.
- THIS: the hull is silent because it waits out LEGITIMATE game-mechanic jump COOLDOWNS on the widened far tour; planning is warm/fast. A liveness-SIGNAL defect, not a reach defect — the sp-0o9ub stored-adjacency reposition fix does nothing here.
- BOTH share the sp-m3122 watchdog engine (watchdog.go) and the SAME failure mode: the watchdog false-kills a hull on a legitimately-long multi-hop leg. PRECEDENT: the long-haul watchdog was DISABLED entirely (commit bba4cba3: "false-killed workers mid strict multi-hop reposition to far sources ~12-36m 'no progress' kills exceed the 12-min stall threshold") — that commit said "trade-fleet watchdog unaffected," but candidate_hop_depth was re-armed to 2 the SAME day, so trade tours now reach the same far, long-cooldown systems and suffer the identical false-kill. The fix belongs in the SHARED watchdog/liveness so it serves trade + long-haul + arb coherently (the sp-mepj REUSE INVARIANT applied to the shared watchdog engine, not the route resolver).

FIX (shipwright designs; recommended shape — make the liveness signal cooldown-aware in ONE shared place; do NOT just disable the trade watchdog: trade genuinely needs hang detection for the sp-2v69u stuck-full case):
- PRIMARY (fix the SIGNAL at the shared watchdog): make relaunchHungContainers cooldown-aware — a parked hull whose jump/reactor cooldown has not yet expired is legitimately waiting, not hung; skip it (extend the watchdog.go:60-67 IN_TRANSIT skip to "IN_TRANSIT OR cooldown-active"). One change in the shared watchdog.go serves trade + long-haul + arb. Read the ship's cooldown expiry (already tracked in ship state) for the wait-state decision instead of trusting the log timestamp.
- COMPLEMENT (make the truth visible): have the jump-cooldown wait (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:83) emit a BOUNDED periodic heartbeat log during the wait (mirror the in-transit safety-resync at travel.go ~:312 that already re-logs), so LatestLogTimestamps advances and any log-derived liveness consumer sees progress. Reuse ONE shared cooldown-wait heartbeat across the trade/long-haul/arb travel machinery (REUSE INVARIANT).
- DEFENSE (optional, weakest): scale the stall threshold above the widened horizon's max realistic cooldown or make it horizon-aware — but prefer the signal fix; a fixed higher threshold is brittle as the horizon changes and slows genuine-hang detection.
- Do NOT weaken the sp-2v69u depth/offload guards or any money guard.

ACCEPTANCE:
- At high heavy count (9+) the fleet completes multi-hop sell fan-outs without the watchdog killing hulls that are merely waiting out jump cooldowns: watchdog-kill rate on trade hulls drops to near-zero except genuine hangs; the "reclaimed N absorption reservations" churn drops sharply.
- Sells keep pace with buys (SELL_CARGO count/rate approaches PURCHASE_CARGO over a steady window); no persistent all-hulls-full state; distinct sell-systems/unit-time holds or rises; no throughput collapse at 8+ heavies.
- Regression test: a parked hull inside an active jump cooldown is NOT killed by relaunchHungContainers even past the stall threshold; a genuinely-silent hull with NO active cooldown IS still killed (hang detection preserved). Byte-identical for hulls with no cooldown.

title: [BUG] Long-haul arb hangs empty at source jump gate: reposition's strict fetch-through PathWithinJumps (bound 25, sp-e059j) storms live GetJumpGate per uncached system with no deadline; sp-m3122 watchdog relaunches into the identical hang, zero value captured
description:
SYMPTOM (live-verified 2026-07-24 ~00:15-00:26Z, player 4, era torwind-2026-07-19)
Long-haul hulls TORWIND-59 and TORWIND-82 (dedicated_fleet=long-haul) capture ZERO value: they navigate to a jump gate, then hang there EMPTY.
- DB (both hulls): nav_status=IN_ORBIT, flight_mode=BURN, location=X1-MH71-Z22C (waypoints.type=JUMP_GATE), cargo 0/225 (EMPTY), fuel ~1352-1368/2300 (partially drawn), assignment_owner=container.
- Worker container (e.g. longhaul_arb-TORWIND-82-769da6a1, RUNNING): logs EXACTLY 4 lines then goes SILENT — "Container started" -> "Claimed ship TORWIND-82 for container (operation long-haul)" -> "Startup jitter: waiting Nms before first API call" -> "Executing iteration" -> (nothing). ZERO gate/jump/reposition/cooldown logs. NO "Starting jump operation", no out-leg, no buy/sell.
- Coordinator (longhaul_arb_coordinator-player-4-..., RUNNING): sp-m3122 watchdog has killed+relaunched BOTH hulls 5x each over ~2h; each cycle "made no progress for ~12m (>= 12m0s stall threshold) — HUNG: killed container ... relaunched fresh ... (sp-m3122)", plus periodic "reclaimed N absorption reservation(s) held by non-existent containers". Zero transactions, cargo never non-zero.
The old sp-e059j error ("no jump-gate route ... within 5 jumps") is GONE (0 occurrences) — the 5-jump cap fix deployed, but the hulls now HANG instead of error-looping.

ROOT CAUSE (code-level) — the long-haul reposition-to-source does an UNBOUNDED, DEADLINE-FREE, SILENT strict fetch-through pathfind at the sp-e059j bound of 25, which storms one live GetJumpGate API read per uncached system across a huge neighborhood and exceeds the 12-min watchdog window.

Chain (all paths absolute under gobot/):
1. Worker episode: internal/application/trading/commands/run_longhaul_arb_worker.go:217 calls h.reposition.RepositionToWaypoint(source) BEFORE the out-leg log at :226 (so a hang here prints nothing).
2. Wiring: internal/application/trading/commands/run_longhaul_arb_wiring.go:46,64-66 — longHaulReposition.RepositionToWaypoint -> RepositionToWaypointStrictWithinJumps(..., longHaulRepositionJumps=25).
3. Travel: internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:499-508 (RepositionToWaypointStrictWithinJumps) -> travelWithJumpBound(...,strictJumpBound=25). For the at-gate hull, waitForInTransitArrival returns immediately (IN_ORBIT, not IN_TRANSIT), then the FIRST real step for a cross-system leg is jumpPath at :277 -> :655 h.gateGraph.PathWithinJumps(from, dest, playerID, 25).
4. Gate graph: internal/application/system/gategraph/service.go:595-632 PathWithinJumps -> bfsPath with a neighbor closure that calls Connections per visited system. Connections (:183) on a store MISS/stale -> fetchAndStore (:328) -> readConnectionsBounded (-> s.apiClient.GetJumpGate, a LIVE API call per uncached system). On a cold/frontier route a bound-25 BFS fetch-through visits a very large neighborhood, one rate-limited GetJumpGate each -> multi-minute-to->12min silent block. This is the SAME cold-cache fetch-through cost sp-yginc measured at ~10-11.5min and removed from DISCOVERY (DiscoverLanes.hops now rides stored-adjacency RepositionPath) — but sp-yginc explicitly left "sp-e059j reposition path byte-untouched", so the EXECUTION-time twin still storms. sp-e059j raising the strict bound from MaxJumpPath=5 to 25 turned a small bounded fetch-through (seconds) into a whole-universe one.
5. No deadline: internal/adapters/grpc/container_runner.go:752-755 runs the handler with r.ctx and NO per-iteration timeout (only DB ops get context.WithTimeout). So the pathfind blocks INDEFINITELY; the only thing that ends it is the sp-m3122 watchdog's StopTour (ctx cancel) at 12 min — which relaunches into the identical cold fetch-through.
6. Watchdog acts (not skips): internal/application/trading/commands/watchdog.go:60-92 skips only IN_TRANSIT hulls; a hull blocked in the pathfind stays IN_ORBIT on the gate (not flying) with no log/state change, so LastTourProgress is stale and it is killed at 12 min.

Elimination proof it is the PATHFIND, not the jump/nav: every post-pathfind step emits a log (jump_cooldown_wait on jump success, jump_cooldown_ride on a 409, an episode_error on a non-cooldown jump error, arb_resume_transit_wait in waitForInTransitArrival, the out-leg log at worker.go:226). NONE appear. The ONLY silent, log-free, multi-minute operation between "Executing iteration" and the next expected log is PathWithinJumps' strict fetch-through BFS (successful GetJumpGate reads are silent; sp-ikx1 made the unreadable-gate BFS exclusion silent too). Discovery is ruled out — sp-yginc verified it at ~68s and the hull is physically on a jump gate (reposition territory).

MONEY-SAFETY (RULINGS #4 intact): the hulls never buy — cargo 0/225, and worker.go checks reachability (a completed reposition) BEFORE any buy. Zero spend, zero bad exposure. This is fail-closed-safe: BROKEN (captures zero value), not DANGEROUS.

DISTINCT FROM sp-m3122 (argued from code, not vibes): sp-m3122 is a TRADE-tour stateful "resume-mid-jump-but-never-replan" strand-after-RESTART bug; its remedy is the shared liveness watchdog + stateless recovery, which long-haul REUSES. This is a NEW, long-haul-specific EXECUTION hang: a cold-cache strict fetch-through storm at the bound-25 reposition. It reproduces deterministically on iteration 1 of EVERY fresh relaunch (not a one-time restart artifact), only on long-haul hulls (the ONLY caller of the bound-25 strict PathWithinJumps via RepositionToWaypointStrictWithinJumps; every other strict caller keeps MaxJumpPath=5, whose fetch-through neighborhood is tiny and completes in seconds), and it leaves the hull EMPTY. The sp-m3122 watchdog is only the shared MITIGATION that catches it (as designed: "one watchdog serves trade tours AND long-haul") — it masks the hang by kill+relaunch into the identical storm, so it is a stopgap, not the cure.

FIX (shipwright designs; recommended shape — prefer reuse + deadline over indefinite block; on a stuck route abort the lane cleanly rather than hang):
1. PRIMARY (bounds the hang): give the reposition pathfind a bounded context (context.WithTimeout, e.g. a couple minutes, well under the 12-min watchdog) and, on deadline OR resolve-failure, treat the lane as unreachable-this-scan and CONTINUE to the next lane — reuse the EXISTING gategraph.ErrUnroutable skip already at run_longhaul_arb_worker.go:218-222 (add a sentinel for the deadline case). The episode then makes progress or idles cleanly (backoff) instead of hanging silently.
2. ROOT (kills the storm): mirror sp-yginc — resolve the reposition's SYSTEM SEQUENCE over the FAST stored adjacency (the same gateGraph.RepositionPath discovery already rides), and let the existing per-hop present-ship chart-on-arrival (sp-bcsu chartArrivedGate -> ChartPresentGate) verify each gate AS the empty hull flies it, instead of a remote cold-cache fetch-through. Note: during the OUT reposition-to-source the hull is EMPTY (buy happens only after a completed reposition), so the sp-e059j "laden heavy could strand at an unverified gate" concern that motivated keeping this path STRICT does not apply to the empty outbound repositioning; the buy still fires only after a verified arrival at the source (RULINGS #4 preserved). Keep ONE shared travel/route resolver (sp-mepj REUSE INVARIANT) — do not fork path logic.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A long-haul hull completes a haul end-to-end (reposition -> buy -> multi-jump -> sell) on a cold route, OR cleanly ABORTS a stuck/uncharted lane and moves to the next reachable one — with NO silent >12m stall and no dependence on the sp-m3122 watchdog to unstick it.
- No worker sits IN_ORBIT-and-silent on a jump gate past a bounded pathfind budget.
- A regression test drives a cold-cache/uncharted deep route and asserts the reposition returns (unroutable/deadline) within the budget instead of blocking; a byte-identical non-interference test for warm routes.
- build / vet / gofmt / go test ./... (-race) green.

RELATED: sp-mepj (long-haul engine), sp-e059j (raised the reposition strict bound 5->25 — introduced the storm), sp-m3122 (shared watchdog = the mitigation, distinct root cause), sp-yginc (fixed the DISCOVERY-side twin the same way; proves the ~10-11.5min cold fetch-through cost and that the reposition path was left untouched).

CONSTRAINTS: RULINGS #4 money-guards untouched (no buy without a completed/verified reposition; hull empty = zero spend); #2 restart-idempotent / stateless recovery; #13 land via captain-gate. Protected paths NOT to modify: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**. sp-mepj REUSE INVARIANT: ONE shared travel-cost/route fn — no duplicated path logic. Keep the strict-vs-relaxed isolation (only long-haul carries the large bound; tour/manual/trade/arb keep MaxJumpPath=5).
close_reason: Root cause FIXED + shipped via sp-0o9ub (duplicate — same reposition fetch-through storm; sp-ju9pn's option-2 ROOT fix IS what sp-0o9ub deployed: PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify plans over stored adjacency + probes ONLY the chosen path, not the bound-25 frontier). VERIFIED live: reposition planning ~20min→11s; the exact symptom (hulls hanging silent+empty at a jump gate, watchdog relaunch loop) is GONE — T59/T82 moved off X1-MH71 to X1-US87 and are jumping regularly (00:29/00:37), zero watchdog kills. sp-e059j strict path retained, MaxJumpPath=5. sp-ju9pn's option-1 (bounded-context deadline as defense-in-depth) tracked separately as focused hardening — the storm being gone makes it belt-and-suspenders, not load-bearing (and the naive whole-reposition form is unsafe: it'd false-kill legitimate multi-hop flights; the correct form bounds only the pathfind).

title: Long-haul arb (sp-mepj) non-functional live: reposition-to-source capped at 5 jumps, so it error-loops on the far lanes it's designed to fly — zero value captured; needs true multi-hop reposition + reachability-gated lane fallback
description:
SYMPTOM (live-verified 2026-07-23, player 4): sp-mepj (long-haul arb engine) is deployed + armed but captures ZERO value — it error-loops. TORWIND-59 and TORWIND-82 are tagged dedicated_fleet='long-haul', owned by longhaul_arb workers under a RUNNING longhaul_arb_coordinator (all launched 19:52). Both hulls sit EMPTY (0/225) at RJ40 and log the SAME failure every ~2 min, completing ZERO hauls:
  "Long-haul episode error for TORWIND-59: reposition to source X1-ST3-B13B failed: reposition of TORWIND-59 to X1-ST3-B13B failed: no jump-gate route from X1-RJ40 to X1-ST3 within 5 jumps" (20:01:23, 20:03:19, 20:04:51); identical for TORWIND-82 (20:01:27, 20:03:22, 20:04:54).
Discovery/ranking WORKS (the coordinator picked the top lane, source X1-ST3-B13B). The failure is EXECUTION: the hull cannot reposition to the lane's SOURCE because it is >5 gate jumps from the hull's position (RJ40), and the engine RETRIES THE SAME unreachable lane indefinitely instead of falling back to a reachable one.

ROOT CAUSE — a DESIGN/IMPLEMENTATION CONTRADICTION inside sp-mepj:
- DISCOVERY layer ranks lanes from BestSinksAcrossSystems "spanning ANY number of gate hops" and prices them over "the actual gate-graph route" (sp-mepj Section 2). It correctly identifies FAR lanes — the engine's whole purpose.
- EXECUTION layer caps the reposition-to-source at 5 gate jumps ("no jump-gate route from RJ40 to ST3 within 5 jumps"). So the travel machinery CANNOT fly the far lanes the ranker selects. Discovery (any-hops) and travel (5-jump cap) DISAGREE -> the engine picks lanes it structurally cannot execute.
- NO reachability gate + NO fallback: the ranker does not filter candidate lanes by SOURCE reachability under the actual travel reach, and on a failed reposition it retries the SAME top-$/hr lane every cycle rather than falling back to the next reachable lane. Same "retry-the-unreachable-target" pattern as sp-xvi15 (probe-buyer targets a yard >5 jumps) and sp-hguq3 (router commits to an unreachable/live-rejected hop).

SEVERITY: the deployed engine captures ZERO value (100% error-loop) — sp-mepj's entire deliverable (capture the out-of-horizon exotic lanes, the measured ~200-400k/hr leak) is non-functional. The 5-jump reposition cap directly DEFEATS the engine's reason to exist (far, multi-hop lanes). It IS fail-closed safe: the hulls never reach the source, so they never buy -> no bad spend, no money at risk (RULINGS #4 intact). So: broken, not dangerous.

FIX (both halves):
1. TRUE MULTI-HOP REPOSITION for long-haul (the engine's premise): the reposition-to-source AND the out/backhaul jumps must plan over the FULL gate-graph, not a 5-jump-capped route finder. sp-mepj's design SPECIFIED reuse of "the shared travel()/route machinery ... spanning any number of gate hops"; the implementation is using a 5-jump-capped reposition instead. Either raise/remove the 5-jump cap on the long-haul reposition path, or route long-haul via a genuine multi-hop gate-graph pathfinder. This is the SAME 5-jump-reach-cap defect family as sp-xvi15 and sp-hguq3 — likely a SHARED reposition/route cap; fix once in the shared path and all three benefit.
2. REACHABILITY-GATE + FALLBACK the lane selection: rank/consider ONLY lanes whose SOURCE (and sink) are reachable under the actual travel reach; on a reposition failure, FALL BACK to the next-best reachable lane rather than retry the same unreachable top pick. NEVER error-loop on an unreachable lane (bounded, one skip/cycle, log the skip).

ACCEPTANCE:
- A long-haul-tagged hull given a top-$/hr lane whose source is many gate hops away REPOSITIONS to the source over the full gate-graph and executes the haul (buy -> multi-jump -> sell). No "within 5 jumps" failure on a genuinely gate-connected far source.
- If a lane's source is genuinely unreachable, the engine SKIPS it and takes the next reachable lane; it NEVER retry-loops on an unreachable lane.
- Money guards unchanged (fail-closed; no buy without a completed reposition) — RULINGS #4 intact.
- A long-haul haul completes end-to-end LIVE (buy at a >5-jump source, sell at sink) capturing realized $/hr.
- build/vet/gofmt/-race green.

EVIDENCE: longhaul_arb-TORWIND-59-adfb24dc + longhaul_arb-TORWIND-82-181047ca logs (episode error "reposition to source X1-ST3-B13B failed: no jump-gate route from X1-RJ40 to X1-ST3 within 5 jumps", repeated 20:01/20:03/20:04); longhaul_arb_coordinator-player-4-9be4bf0c RUNNING (workers launched 19:52); ships: 59+82 dedicated_fleet=long-haul, 0/225, parked at RJ40 (never reached the source).

RELATED: sp-mepj (this defect makes its deliverable non-functional as deployed — this is a sp-mepj follow-up/defect). Same 5-jump-reach-cap family as sp-xvi15 (frontier probe-buyer targets an unreachable far yard) and sp-hguq3 (gate router) — a SHARED multi-hop-reposition fix likely resolves all three. Also relates to sp-tp5c3 (Lever 1 multi-hop travel model for the tour solver) — the common need across tour + long-haul + probe-buy is one true multi-hop gate-graph travel/route machinery.

CONSTRAINTS: RULINGS #4 (money guards fail-closed, untouched), #2 (restart-idempotent), #13 (captain-gate). Reuse the shared travel/route machinery (sp-mepj REUSE INVARIANT) — fix the reach cap in the shared path, not a copy.
close_reason: Deployed (135117da gated/merged → restart-daemon) + verified live: long-haul now routes past the old MaxJumpPath=5 cap to far sources (T59/T82 reached far sources X1-DY16 / X1-QM8, >5 jumps, executing real multi-hop repositions — jump + cooldown — with zero 'within 5 jumps' errors). Strict large-bound reposition (PathWithinJumps + longHaulReposition adapter @ bound 25) isolated to long-haul; tour/manual keep MaxJumpPath=5; relaxed RepositionPath untouched; reachability fallback skips ErrUnroutable before any buy (RULINGS #4 intact). The cold-start slowness first observed was a separate discovery-latency issue (sp-yginc, now fixed: ~68s vs ~11.5min). 7 RED→GREEN tests; -race green 107 pkgs.

title: Captain reservations silently reaped: the sp-6asm stale-reservation reaper cannot distinguish a deliberate 'ship reserve' from a leaked one and reaps operator-held hulls — violates the reserve contract
description:
SYMPTOM (live 2026-07-23, player 4): a DELIBERATE captain reservation was silently cleared and a coordinator re-adopted the hull — directly violating the `ship reserve` contract. The captain ran `ship reserve --ship TORWIND-81 --force --reason "relieve trade over-saturation — empty heavy per Admiral"` to hold 81 OUT of the trade fleet, jettisoned its cargo, and left it parked/idle (never ran `ship release`). ~30-60 min later 81 was back in trade (assignment_owner='container', dedicated_fleet='trade', loaded 213/225, actively trading). Two hulls reserved at the same time (TORWIND-59, TORWIND-82) KEPT their reservations — they were IN_TRANSIT in live captain nav containers; 81 was parked with no live container.

CONTRACT VIOLATED (`spacetraders ship reserve --help`, cli/ship.go:512-534): "A captain reservation ... survives daemon restarts and is excluded from the stale-claim reconciliation pass — NO COORDINATOR CAN CLAIM A RESERVED HULL OUT FROM UNDER YOU ... Use 'ship release' when you're done with it." The contract text landed 2026-07-08 (663bee40); the offending reaper landed 2026-07-19 02:29 (4ce4ed24) and silently voided it.

ROOT CAUSE (CONFIRMED by proof-by-elimination + code read; subagent investigation):
The sp-6asm "stale-captain-reservation reaper" reaped 81. `reapStaleCaptainReservations` (gobot/internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:840-907) is called from reconcileOnce:507; predicate `isStaleCaptainReservation` (:917-931) + caller reap a hull that is: DedicatedFleet=="trade" (:875) / owner=captain+active (:918) / released_at NULL (:922) / !IsInTransit i.e. parked (:925) / reserved >= 1800s/30min ago (:930, defaultReapIdleThresholdSeconds :112) / NOT named by any live-or-recent container via ActiveContainerShipsPort which reads the CONTAINERS table not ships.container_id (:881). Release at :890 via the single-writer ReleaseCaptainReservation (RULINGS #3 OK).
- 81 matched EVERY condition (parked+idle after jettison, no nav container, aged). 59/82 were doubly excluded (in-transit AND live nav container).
PROOF IT'S THE ONLY CAUSE: a trade tour re-adopt requires ClaimShip, which HARD-REJECTS owner=captain (ship_repository.go:1273-1275; domain AssignToContainer :47-52). So the reservation had to be cleared to idle first. The ONLY writers that clear owner=captain->idle are (a) the `ship release` command (release_ship.go:65 — NOT run) and (b) the reaper (:890). ReleaseAllActive (restart cleanup, daemon_server.go:623) EXCLUDES owner=captain (ship_repository.go:1205). reconcileStaleClaim (refresh) is double-guarded against captain reservations. releaseShipAssignments/markContainerFailed/ForceRelease are all container_id-keyed (a reservation has container_id=NULL -> never in set). Sync* PRESERVE owner/reason. => the reaper is the mechanism.

THE DESIGN FLAW (the deeper finding — why this is not a one-off):
1. The reaper NEVER consults assignment_reason — the deliberate operator `--reason` string IS persisted (ReserveForCaptain -> ship_repository.go:1378, surfaced CaptainReservationReason ship_assignment_ops.go:100) but is ignored.
2. CRITICAL: NO automated code path creates an owner=captain reservation. The ONLY creators are the operator's own `ship reserve`/`--force` (ReserveForCaptain :1334 / PreemptForCaptain :1462). The bridge-authority pass-through the reaper claims to clean up (sp-sfoe CAPTAIN-CONTEXT PASS-THROUGH, container_runner.go:1105-1133) PRESERVES an existing reservation and never creates one; an unreserved hull under a manual op is claimed owner=CONTAINER (:1135) and released normally on completion. So the reaper's premise ("reclaim orphaned captain reservations left by bridge-authority ops") is FALSE — there is no distinct orphan class. EVERY owner=captain reservation the reaper can reap is a deliberate operator reservation. Its "parked + no live/recent container" heuristic (activeShips) necessarily misfires on the perfectly-legitimate reserve -> jettison/park -> hold-idle flow (exactly this incident).

ARMING: code-default OFF (config/trade_fleet.go:205 no default; injected only when true container_ops_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:251-253; read via OptionalBool command_factory_registry.go:593; resolveTradeFleetConfig CLEARS the key on every rebuild/restart :173). NEITHER committed config arms it (gobot/config.yaml, captain/config.yaml trade_fleet: have no reap_* key; git log -S: never committed anywhere). But the reap demonstrably happened, so it WAS armed at incident time via a no-committed-trace vector: (a) a deploy-local/uncommitted config.yaml at the daemon cwd / SPACETRADERS_CONFIG override (config.go:202-223); or (b) env var ST_TRADE_FLEET_REAP_STALE_CAPTAIN_RESERVATIONS_ENABLED=true (config.go:82-84 SetEnvPrefix ST + AutomaticEnv + SetEnvKeyReplacer(".","_")); or (c) the sp-nc0m arming ledger. DURABLE EVIDENCE = the daemon log line "sp-6asm reaper: stale captain reservation (reserved ... ago, parked, no live/recent container)" (ship_repository.go:1428) — note the subsequent ClaimShip re-adopt WIPES release_reason back to '' (:1309), so the LOG LINE, not the current ships row, is the smoking gun. (Captain note: the trade_fleet coordinator container log had already rotated past the ~40-min-old event, so it wasn't grep-able at investigation time, but proof-by-elimination stands.)

FIX (preferred — positive opt-in marker so only truly-reclaimable reservations are reapable):
1. Add an explicit reclaimability marker set at reservation creation (a new AssignmentOwner value e.g. captain_ephemeral, or an assignment_reclaimable bool), threaded through ReserveByCaptain/ReserveForCaptain/PreemptForCaptain.
2. Default `ship reserve`/`--force` to NON-reclaimable — a deliberate operator reservation is SACROSANCT. Only an explicit opt-in (e.g. `ship reserve --ephemeral`, or an automated caller) creates a reapable one.
3. Make isStaleCaptainReservation REQUIRE the marker: reap only if reclaimable-marked AND parked AND aged AND no live/recent container. A plain `ship reserve` never matches.
4. Keep release on the single-writer ReleaseCaptainReservation (RULINGS #3; already at :890).
ALTERNATIVE (simpler, justified by the design finding): since no automated path creates owner=captain reservations, there is arguably NO legitimate orphan class — REMOVE the reaper (or permanently disarm it) and instead surface long-idle captain reservations as an ADVISORY (ship list warning / captain event) prompting a human `ship release`, never an automated release.

SAFE INTERIM (do now, byte-identical to default-off): disarm in the LIVE config the running daemon loads — set trade_fleet.reap_stale_captain_reservations_enabled=false / remove the key / unset the ST_ env var — and restart (resolveTradeFleetConfig re-clears it). Update the sp-nc0m arming ledger. reapStaleCaptainReservations returns early at :849 when disarmed.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A deliberate `ship reserve` (or `--force`), with or without --reason, is NEVER reaped — even when parked + idle + reserved > 30 min + no live/recent container (the exact TORWIND-81 state). RED-first regression: reserve -> jettison/park -> advance clock past threshold -> run reaper ARMED -> reservation still owner=captain.
- If a reclaimable class is introduced: a marked ephemeral reservation orphaned past threshold STILL is reaped.
- Disarmed reaper is byte-identical (no release attempts, no port reads).
- Release stays on ReleaseCaptainReservation (RULINGS #3, no direct assignment writes).
- The reserve --help contract ("no coordinator can claim a reserved hull out from under you") holds for every deliberate reservation. build/vet/gofmt/-race green.

KEY FILES: reaper run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:840-931 (predicate :917-931, caller :507, release :890, threshold :112); config trade_fleet.go:196-206; arming inject/clear container_ops_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:159-262 + read command_factory_registry.go:593 + resolveTradeFleetConfig :173; reserve creation ship_repository.go:1334-1390 + ship/commands/assignment/reserve_ship.go; bridge-authority pass-through container_runner.go:1105-1133; contract text cli/ship.go:512-534; config loader config.go:82-84,202-223.
RELATED: sp-6asm (introduced the reaper), sp-nc0m (arming ledger), sp-sfoe/sp-lxwn/sp-zhii (the bridge-authority reservation tech debt the reaper was meant to paper over). RULINGS #3 (single-writer), #7 (never-poach — the reaper effectively poaches an operator-held hull).

No automated path creates an owner=captain reservation, so there was no legitimate orphan class — the reaper could only misfire on deliberate operator holds (TORWIND-81). Durable regression lock added (TestTradeReconcile_DeliberateCaptainReservation_SurvivesReconcile); -race green; sp-m3122 watchdog byte-untouched. ship reserve contract restored.

title: Widen the tour-solver horizon via a real multi-hop (gate-graph) travel model — let the trade fleet disperse across the wide sink surface instead of over-saturating the 1-hop cluster
description:
PROBLEM (live-proven 2026-07-23): the trade fleet over-saturates and STALLS at high hull count. With 8 heavies + 5 lights (13 hulls), the fleet-wide sink cap is breached fleet-wide -> hulls churn re-planning against the same near sinks -> 0 sells for 45+ min (authoritative ledger). Tour logs show hulls DROPPING huge far lanes — ANTIMATTER spread ~20,247/u and ~18,500/u; sp-mepj measured AI_MAINFRAMES ~28k/u into home — because "best sink is beyond the gate-neighbor graph (sp-mtvg)". The fleet CANNOT disperse: it is confined to a 1-gate-hop sink surface that N hulls saturate.

KEY INSIGHT — the dispersion MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS; it's the HORIZON that binds. The fleet-wide absorption ledger (sp-2v69u REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES + market_absorption_ledger) already pushes hulls off each other's sinks: "Tour absorption reserve breached the fleet-wide sink cap - re-planning against the now-occupied sink" IS dispersion trying to happen. But "elsewhere" is still the same small near cluster because of the 1-hop horizon. Expand the reachable sink surface and the EXISTING absorption cap disperses the fleet automatically — no new anti-herd logic required.

ROOT CAUSE (code): the tour solver's _make_travel_fn prices EVERY inter-system crossing as ONE gate hop (2*GATE_HOP + JUMP_COOLDOWN), and MAX_TOUR_SYSTEMS=2 (explicit prior Admiral decision). So the solver cannot safely look past 1 hop — a 3-hop lane is mis-priced ~3x, corrupting cph (credits-per-hour) selection. The 1-hop discovery horizon is shared by the tour coordinator (tourSystems) AND the arb scanner (scanLanes -> neighborSystems) per sp-mtvg.

THE FIX:
1. MULTI-HOP TRAVEL MODEL: replace _make_travel_fn's flat 1-hop pricing with the REAL gate-graph path cost — hops*(jump+cooldown) + intra-system legs over the actual gate route. The machinery ALREADY EXISTS: the shared travel()/route machinery that scout_reposition (sp-s232), the gas workers, and the arb circuits already reuse computes true multi-hop routes. REUSE it (do NOT copy); extract to a shared location if embedded, so the tour solver, arb scanner, and long-haul (sp-mepj) all price via ONE travel-cost function.
2. WIDEN THE SYSTEM CAP: raise MAX_TOUR_SYSTEMS beyond 2 as a LIVE tunable (e.g. tour_max_systems) so the horizon width is dialed without redeploy. Safe now because travel is priced correctly.
3. CANDIDATE DISCOVERY: surface out-of-1-hop sinks to the solver — reuse BestSinksAcrossSystems (the read-only global-best-sink port sp-mtvg added).

WHY DISPERSION FOLLOWS: with the horizon widened and travel priced honestly, each hull's candidate sink set spans many systems; the existing fleet-wide absorption cap then spreads hulls across that large surface (hull B avoids A's reserved sinks, now able to reach farther uncontended ones) instead of churning the near cluster. Wider surface + existing cap = dispersion.

REUSE INVARIANT (HARD, Admiral order — mirrors sp-mepj): ONE travel-cost function shared by the tour solver, arb scanner, and long-haul engine. A grep must show shared call sites and ZERO duplicated travel/path-cost logic. The SAME gate-graph travel cost sp-mepj wants for long-haul is what the tour solver needs here — extract once.

RISK / RULINGS #4 (why this was deferred): this changes the LOAD-BEARING tour solver's cost model — a naive widen mis-prices multi-hop ~3x and corrupts cph selection (sp-mepj declined it for exactly this reason and built a separate engine instead). MUST get the multi-hop pricing correct: validate cph rankings with the real travel cost do NOT degrade vs the 1-hop baseline on near lanes, and that far lanes price at TRUE $/hr (not inflated). DEFAULT-OFF behind tunables (tour_multihop_travel + tour_max_systems); A/B realized $/hr before arming (PLAYBOOK section 10). Money guards untouched — this is a cost-model + horizon change, not a spend-guard change (RULINGS #4/#5 intact).

RELATIONSHIP TO sp-mepj (ALTERNATIVE ARCHITECTURES — Admiral chooses; do NOT build both for the same purpose):
- sp-mepj = capture the far lanes with a SEPARATE long-haul engine on operator-tagged hulls, leaving the 1-hop tour solver UNTOUCHED (solver-risk-free; two fleets to manage; trade fleet still size-capped).
- THIS (Lever 1) = widen the tour solver ITSELF so the TRADE FLEET disperses and reaches far lanes natively (one coherent fleet; higher risk to the load-bearing solver).
- For the trade-fleet case they largely SUBSTITUTE: if Lever 1 lands, the trade solver reaches far lanes on its own, making sp-mepj's separate engine largely redundant FOR TRADE (sp-mepj may still add value as a dedicated aggressive-envelope long-haul path). Decide one.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Tour solver prices inter-system crossings by the REAL gate-graph route cost (shared travel fn), not a flat 1 hop; a >1-hop lane's trip_time reflects actual hops.
- tour_max_systems is a live tunable; raising it makes hulls plan tours to sinks 2-3+ hops out.
- At high hull count the fleet DISPERSES: distinct sell-systems per unit time rises, the fleet-wide sink-cap-breach re-plan churn drops, and throughput does NOT collapse at 8+ heavies (the live failure).
- cph selection on existing 1-hop near lanes is NOT degraded (A/B vs baseline).
- REUSE grep: one shared travel-cost fn (tour + arb + long-haul), zero duplicated path-cost logic.
- Default-off tunable; build/vet/gofmt/-race green.

EVIDENCE: live stall 2026-07-23 (8 heavies + 5 lights, 0 sells/45m, fleet-wide sink cap breached, heavies parked full with no cooldown); tour logs dropping ANTIMATTER @20,247/u and @18,500/u beyond the gate-neighbor graph; sp-mtvg proof (1-gate-hop horizon shared by tourSystems + scanLanes); sp-mepj description of _make_travel_fn 1-hop pricing + MAX_TOUR_SYSTEMS=2.

CONSTRAINTS: RULINGS #4 (money guards untouched — cost-model change only), #5 (50k floor untouched), #13 (lands via captain-gate). Protected paths untouched. Coordinate with sp-mepj on the shared travel-cost extraction (do it once).
close_reason: Gated + deployed (Go + routing). Real multi-hop gate-graph travel model in the tour solver: _make_travel_fn prices a crossing as gate_hops x per-crossing charge (was flat 1 hop), fed from TourConstraints.inter_system_hops the Go coordinator resolves over the same gate graph (reuses repositionNeighborsWithinJumps; the Python solver has ZERO gate-graph logic). Computed only when max_tour_systems>2 (byte-identical below); only >1-hop pairs emitted so NEAR lanes stay byte-equal even armed, killing the ~3x under-pricing that corrupted cph. NO FLAG — always on, armed via the existing numeric max_tour_systems + candidate_hop_depth knobs. Near-lane cph undegraded PROVEN (stop-ship gate: 1-hop lane identical cph/profit/trip_time; far 3-hop = 3x1800). Money guards untouched (#4/#5). Reuse consistent w/ sp-mepj (same hopsxper-hop+intra shape). 16 pytest + Go RED->GREEN; -race green 107 pkgs, pytest 213 passed. Candidate #3 served by existing widenedTourSystems (now unblocked); BestSinks->allowedSystems NOT wired (unroutable-leg risk + sp-mepj overlap) — optional follow-up.

title: INCOME→GATE gate is too weak: fires on gate_min_haulers(2)+income, not a genuinely scaled contract op — graduates INCOME with 2 hulls
