title: Contract scaler hangs on its first iteration (RUNNING-but-frozen, ~11h silent, no liveness watchdog) — never ramps the fleet
description: TORWIND_DEV13: contract_scaler-player-1-16dbbbce logged 'Container started'→jitter→'Executing iteration'→'Contract scaler starting (disabled=false,dry_run=false)' at 00:49:11 then went SILENT for ~11h. Only 4 log lines total. RUNNING per the container store but frozen mid-first-iteration (blocked call after 'starting' — likely role-resolution / market read / API with no timeout). No error, no panic, supervisor never restarts it (hung!=dead). Result: the contract fleet never scaled past the bootstrap's 2 seed haulers despite 757k treasury (>> the price+200k cushion). FIX: root-cause the first-iteration blocking call + add a liveness watchdog/iteration-timeout (mirror sp-m3122's trade-tour 'RUNNING-but-hung' watchdog: a RUNNING scaler with zero progress past a stall threshold is killed + relaunched fresh). Found during staging.
design: ROOT CAUSE (systematic-debugging, evidence-based): reconcileOnce passes the container's long-lived ctx (no deadline) straight into its per-tick DB reads — armedPlanFor→ResolveRoles→homeMarkets (HomeSystem + ListBySystem + GetMarketData/waypoint, all GORM/Postgres) and liveCeiling (liveconfig Snapshot). Go database/sql has NO connection-acquire timeout (QueryContext waits for a free pool conn until ctx cancels); pool is capped at MaxOpen (connection.go:105) and there is NO server-side statement_timeout anywhere. So a read issued when the pool is momentarily exhausted (coordinator contention) blocks FOREVER. Froze mid-ResolveRoles on tick 1 for ~11h, RUNNING, 4 log lines, no error (blocked != errored), no watchdog. Daemon restart drained the pool -> fresh scaler resolved instantly. THE DEFECT: every other daemon DB op is wrapped in context.WithTimeout(ctx, dbOperationTimeout=5s) (container_runner.go, 8 sites); the scaler reconcile loop is the ONE path that skips the idiom. FIX (root cause, matches idiom): bound the two top-of-tick DB reads (armedPlanFor + liveCeiling) with a 5s read-timeout. A stuck read errors at 5s -> reconcileOnce returns err -> logged -> retried next tick (armedPlanFor does not cache a failed resolve). Self-recovering; no false-kill (reads are quick DB bursts, not rate-limited API; the buys keep the original ctx). FOLLOW-UP (defense-in-depth, separate bead): liveness watchdog for the residual mid-tick-exhaustion class (mirrors sp-m3122).
close_reason: Closed

title: Trade tours hang on daemon restart — stateful mid-jump resume can complete the jump but never re-plan, stranding hulls full for hours; needs liveness watchdog + stateless recovery
description:
SYMPTOM (live-verified, era torwind-2026-07-19, player 4, 2026-07-23): a daemon restart at 04:33 UTC silently stranded two trade heavies (TORWIND-57, TORWIND-59) FULL (225/225) for 2+ hours with ZERO sells — while dozens of fresh, high-value sinks existed for exactly what they held (57 held equipment/machinery/iron/ship-plating; live market_data showed 66 fresh equipment sinks @≤7724, 88 machinery @≤6918, 59 iron, 36 ship-plating @≤16536). NOT a market-depth problem, NOT stale reservations (only 80 units stale). The hulls simply had no working tour driving them.

ROOT CAUSE (from tour container logs): the restart's recovery path re-adopted the in-flight hulls MID-JUMP and logged "Reposition resume: re-adopted mid-jump toward X1-RJ40 ... completing the jump before re-planning (RULINGS #2)" — then went DEAD SILENT. 57's tour container (tour-run-TORWIND-57-c0556c27) completed the jump to RJ40 and NEVER re-planned; its last log line was 04:34:02, 2+ hours before discovery, yet the container was still marked RUNNING. 55/56 recovered fine; 57/59 hung. So the stateful "resume mid-jump then re-plan" recovery is UNRELIABLE — it can complete the jump leg and then fail to resume planning, leaving the container RUNNING-but-hung and the coordinator none the wiser (it trusts RUNNING = healthy, so it never relaunches). Manual remedy today: `container stop <hung-tour>` to force the coordinator to relaunch a fresh tour (done for 57/59).

Also observed: on the container cancel, "Tour absorption release failed ... release planned absorption ... context canceled" — a killed container's PLANNED absorption reservations are not reliably released on restart (a secondary phantom-contention hazard; TTL sweep eventually cleans up, but not promptly).

WHY P1: a daemon restart is ROUTINE (every deploy). Trade freezing part of the fleet for hours per restart, only recoverable by manual kicking, is unacceptable. Distinct from sp-2v69u (optimizer capacity/held-cargo) and sp-hguq3 (gate routing) — this is a tour-worker RECOVERY/LIVENESS defect.

FIX DESIGN (resilience, priority order):

1. LIVENESS WATCHDOG (primary, the big one). The coordinator must not trust RUNNING = healthy. Track a per-tour last-progress timestamp (advanced on any real step: plan, navigate, arrive, buy, sell). A RUNNING tour that makes ZERO progress for N minutes (config, e.g. 10-15m) is declared HUNG → killed → relaunched fresh. This self-heals ANY hang (restart-induced or otherwise), and is exactly the manual judgment applied here (spotted 2h of silence, kicked it). Single most valuable mechanism — makes trade resilient far beyond restarts. Must be careful to advance the heartbeat during legitimately-long legs (jump cooldowns, multi-hop travel) so a slow-but-healthy tour is not falsely killed — key on PROGRESS events, not wall-clock alone.

2. STATELESS RESTART RECOVERY (secondary). On restart, do NOT resume a tour's fragile internal mid-jump state. Re-derive desired state from the DB (which hulls are trade-dedicated + their current cargo/position) and relaunch FRESH tours. A fresh tour re-plans from scratch against current sinks; held cargo is handled by the existing held-cargo-aware offload (sp-2v69u PRIMARY). Stateless recovery cannot hang on resume because there is no resume. (If mid-jump resume is kept for efficiency, it MUST be backstopped by the watchdog in #1.)

3. RESERVATION CLEANUP ON RESTART (tertiary). Immediately release absorption-ledger reservations belonging to containers that no longer exist, rather than waiting for the TTL sweep, so phantom reservations from killed containers never make open sinks look contended.

PRINCIPLE: align trade tour recovery with the "re-derive desired state and relaunch" pattern the rest of the daemon's recoverable coordinators already use, and add a liveness watchdog so a stuck worker can never masquerade as healthy.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A tour container that stops making progress for the watchdog threshold is automatically killed and relaunched (test: simulate a hung/silent RUNNING tour -> coordinator relaunches within threshold).
- A simulated daemon restart mid-tour leaves every trade-dedicated hull with a healthy, progressing tour within one reconcile interval (no RUNNING-but-hung containers, no hull idle-full beyond the watchdog threshold).
- Absorption reservations from non-existent containers are released promptly on restart.
- The watchdog does NOT kill a healthy tour that is legitimately mid-long-leg (jump cooldown / multi-hop) — heartbeat keys on progress events.
- build/vet/gofmt + -race green.

EVIDENCE REFS (read-only, live daemon DB :5432 + container logs 2026-07-23): tour-run-TORWIND-57-c0556c27 last log 04:34:02 (silent 2h, RUNNING); daemon restart 04:33 UTC (prod spacetraders-daemon --force, uptime confirmed); market_data fresh-import-sink counts for 57's goods (66/88/59/36); market_absorption_ledger PLANNED entries = 11 rows / 472 units, only ~80 units genuinely stale.

CODE POINTERS: the trade-fleet coordinator's tour (re)launch + recovery path (run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go; the "Reposition resume / re-adopted mid-jump" recovery logic), tour container lifecycle/heartbeat, and the market_absorption_ledger release-on-cancel path.

RELATED: surfaced during the sp-2v69u + sp-hguq3 post-fix re-wedge validation. Not a wedge — a recovery hang. The "market only supports 2 heavies" read was WRONG; the market carries 4, the hulls were brain-dead.
close_reason: Gated to main. Trade tour liveness watchdog + stateless restart recovery + dead-container absorption reclaim. Watchdog: per-tour last-progress heartbeat (plan/navigate/arrive/buy/sell); a RUNNING tour with zero progress past the stall threshold is killed+relaunched fresh, keyed on PROGRESS events so a legit long leg (jump cooldown/multi-hop) is NOT false-killed. Stateless recovery: re-derive from DB + relaunch fresh, no fragile mid-jump resume. Absorption reclaim: release market_absorption_ledger reservations of non-existent containers on restart+after-kill. No flag; #2 deterministic/restart-idempotent. 9 RED->GREEN tests. Agent died on a 502 pre-commit; shipwright verified (build/vet/tests green) + committed+gated. Watchdog/recovery mechanism is REUSED by sp-mepj.

title: [contract] Arm the era-invariant central-band standby set — idle delivery hulls cluster because standby_stations is null
description:
ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed live): the contract coordinator container config has standby_stations=null — the fixed era-invariant standby set was NEVER armed. Homing therefore falls to the ResolveStandbyForHoming auto-fill fallback (sp-bu6ma auto hub-placement / sp-54uif), which resolves only the TOP-DEMAND central parks (~4). DistributeIdleHullsAcrossStandby is occupancy-aware and spreads correctly, but across only that short set — so 8 idle hulls pile onto ~4 waypoints. OBSERVED LIVE: A1x3, K83x2, G49x1, H55x1; the E/F/D/C central bands sit EMPTY. This IS the design's warned-of failure (sp-9le3x line ~52: 'all idle hulls piling ... caps the op at ~1.28x' vs 1.51x for the full demand-ranked spread across the distinct central set).

DESIGN (sp-9le3x, SIGNED OFF): home-system geometry is era-INVARIANT (letter->distance bands; central set = H/E/C/F/K/D/A + G depot band). Resolve central parks ONCE AT ARM by MARKET ROLE (inner-band waypoints that import the manufactured contract goods) — NOT by letter, NOT by number (names+numbers regenerate each era; the BANDS recur). Delivery-hull count saturates at 7-8 = number of distinct central waypoints => hulls must spread ONE PER distinct central waypoint.

EVIDENCE — X1-UM5 era-4 inner-band markets by band (waypoints table, traits LIKE MARKETPLACE, era_id=4, ordered by dist): A(A1..A4 dist27) H(H52..H55 dist45) E(E42..E44 dist55) G(G47/G49 dist63) F(F45/F46 dist75) D(D40/D41 dist83) K(K83 dist104) C(C38 dist153). One inner-band contract-sink per band = the central standby set.

FIX: ensure the FULL era-invariant central-band standby set is ARMED (populated in the coordinator standby_stations) so the occupancy-aware DistributeIdleHullsAcrossStandby spreads hulls one-per-waypoint. PREFERRED per design: auto-resolve-by-market-role AND PERSIST the resolved set to the coordinator config at launch / first discovery pass when standby_stations is empty (durable, era-adaptive, restart-idempotent RULINGS #2, single-writer persist RULINGS #3, no manual 'fleet hub' needed). Investigate where the current auto-fill (ResolveStandbyForHoming/standby_demand.go) narrows to top-demand and broaden it to the full distinct-central-band set (and/or persist it). NO FLAG — armed on deploy. Do NOT weaken any money guard (#4). Frigate excluded (#7).

NOTE: the fallback 'already home if at ANY standby waypoint' check (idle_arb.go:1071) means clustered hulls are never rebalanced — with a full armed set this is moot (they land distinct), but confirm the balancer doesn't need a rebalance pass for pre-existing clusters.
acceptance_criteria: With N idle contract hulls and M distinct central waypoints (N<=M), each idle hull homes to a DISTINCT central waypoint (no clustering). standby_stations resolves to the FULL central-band set (one per band), not a top-demand subset. Verified against the live symptom: the current 8-hull pile on 4 parks becomes one-per-distinct-central-park. RED-first (clustering / short-set reproduced before fix), build/vet/gofmt/-race green. No flag.
close_reason: Gated to main. Armed the full era-invariant central-band standby set: isCentralSink() now classifies inner-band parks by the DURABLE MARKETPLACE trait (not transient scanned imports), so all distinct central bands join the standby set every pass (one-per-band, saturates 7-8 per sp-9le3x) — fixing the live A1x3/K83x2 pile (8 hulls were spreading across only the ~4 dock-scanned sinks). Recomputed from durable inputs, no config write (RULINGS #2/#3), money guards untouched (#4), frigate untouched (#7). Shared ResolveRoles fix also corrects the auto-scaler's delivery composition. title: Cold-start DEADLOCK: bootstrap frees the frigate earner to buy the 1st contract hauler while capital-gated (unaffordable) → income source stops → treasury never clears the gate
description:
Found on staging TORWIND_DEV12 (recurs; DEV8 showed the same prelude). The bootstrap first-hauler PIVOT freezes the whole cold-start.

EVIDENCE (daemon.log, DEV12):
- 23:30:25 'Bootstrap hauler buy decision: price=363473 treasury=127060 floor=150000 cushion=(treasury-price)=-236413 affordable=(cushion>=floor)=FALSE — BLOCKED by the working-capital floor'
- 23:31:12 'Bootstrap first-hauler PIVOT: FREED the command frigate TORWIND_DEV12-1 at the inter-contract window (loop stopped + dedicated the exclusive purchasing ship) — positioning it at the home shipyard ... (sp-5nd2 fault-2)'
- Result: frigate parked DOCKED at the shipyard, batch_contract_workflow canceled ('Released 1 ship assignments, reason: canceled'), contract_fleet_coordinator idle ('No ships available'). Treasury flat 127060 (only ever went 175k->127k from probe capex; ZERO contract rewards). blockers=capital_gate for 10+ min, no recovery.

ROOT CAUSE: the pivot that STOPS the frigate contract loop and dedicates it as the exclusive hauler-purchaser is NOT gated on hauler affordability. It fires at treasury 127k when the hauler needs treasury>=price(363473)+floor(150000)=513473. Stopping the earner kills the only income source, so treasury can never reach the gate -> permanent deadlock. The frigate had JUST gotten a viable sourcing plan (23:30:56 'Sourcing plan for ALUMINUM_ORE: 77u @ 62 at X1-XD86-B7') 16s before being pulled off it.

SECONDARY: contract_lifecycle_service.go:119 returns the error on a profitability-EVAL failure (return nil, err), aborting the cycle — contradicting the documented 'log only, always accept' design (run_contract_workflow.go:29). Only the !IsProfitable branch accepts-anyway; the can't-compute branch hard-fails. This made the early coverage-lag ticks (23:11-23:29, before B7 was scanned) hard cycle-failures.

PROPOSED FIX: gate the first-hauler pivot on affordable==true — keep the frigate running the contract loop (earning) until treasury-price>=floor, THEN free it to buy. The hauler price is already known before the pivot (363473 in the decision log), so affordability is computable pre-pivot. Do NOT stop the sole income source while the buy is capital-gated. (Consider also making lifecycle:119 accept-anyway per the design, but the pivot gate is the decisive fix.)

Protected-path note: bootstrap logic is in internal/application/bootstrap/** (NOT protected). Money floors (RULINGS #4/#5) must stay intact — the fix TIGHTENS behavior (don't pivot until affordable), never weakens the floor.
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate-crossing auto-router bounces forever on charted-but-live-rejected jump edges (chart-vs-reality); needs circuit-breaker + self-heal
description:
SYMPTOM (era torwind-2026-07-19 / era_id 4, player 4, live 2026-07-23): the shared gate-crossing auto-router commits to a multi-hop jump route that its own cached chart (gate_edges) says is valid, the LIVE game rejects a hop at execution, and the router then RETRIES FOREVER — bouncing the hull between two systems, never reaching the destination, never bailing. Driveless hulls (FRAME_HEAVY_FREIGHTER — jump-gate-only inter-system) are the most exposed.

AIRTIGHT REPRO (TORWIND-56, a 225-cargo heavy trying to reach a FOOD/CLOTHING sink at X1-XD86-J57):
- gate_edges (era 4, under_construction=f) shows a valid path RJ93 -> CA43 -> XD86:
    X1-RJ93 -> X1-CA43  (edge exists, f)
    X1-CA43 -> X1-XD86 | gate_waypoint X1-XD86-I54 | era 4 | under_construction=f | synced 2026-07-22 21:52:19
    reciprocal: X1-XD86 -> X1-CA43 | gate_waypoint X1-CA43-I56 | f   (so CA43's gate = X1-CA43-I56, exactly where the ship sat)
- The router planned RJ93->CA43->XD86, executed HOP 1 (RJ93->CA43) fine, then HOP 2 (CA43->XD86) FAILED at execution. Container navigate-TORWIND-56-549cf210, 2026-07-23 02:25:32:
    "failed to navigate TORWIND-56 to cross-system destination X1-XD86-J57: reposition of TORWIND-56 to X1-XD86-J57 failed: jump TORWIND-56 to X1-XD86 (hop 2 of 2 toward X1-XD86) failed: no jump gate connection from origin gate to system X1-XD86"
  ...for an edge that IS in the chart (era 4, not under construction). Log also shows "Ship is driveless but at a complete jump gate" / "Ship already at jump gate" — the ship WAS at the gate; the connection itself was live-rejected.
- It then "Retrying after error in 30s (attempt 2)" and bounces RJ93 <-> CA43 indefinitely. Second data point: TORWIND-57 reached the KQ55 system (KQ55-A16A) then bounced back to its origin RD54 on a re-navigate — same class of flakiness.

CORE DEFECT: chart-vs-reality mismatch. The cached gate topology (gate_edges, synced ~5h before the failure) says the CA43->XD86 jump is legal; the live jump gate rejects it. The router trusts the stale/incorrect chart, commits to the route, dead-ends on the bad hop, and retry-loops forever.

WHY P1 (blast radius): this is the SHARED gate-crossing / cross-system multi-jump travel path (sp-9l4p; reposition/NavigateRouteCommand) used by (1) manual `ship navigate`, (2) the trade-fleet coordinator's tours, AND (3) the sp-2v69u offload/distress repositioning. So it is a DEEPER CAUSE of the heavy-wedge (sp-2v69u): even a correct "disperse this laden hull to a reachable sink" decision cannot execute if the router bounces on a stale/wrong gate edge. The retry-forever also burns API calls + fuel and strands the hull. Same-system hops are reliable (TORWIND-59 UM5-D41->UM5-B7 and TORWIND-55 in-CC13 both worked); the defect is specifically MULTI-HOP CROSS-SYSTEM gate execution vs the cached chart.

ROOT-CAUSE CANDIDATES (investigate; delegate the code+live read):
1. STALE gate_edges — the cache says the edge is valid but the live jump gate's connection set changed (gate went under construction / connection dropped) since the ~5h-old sync. gate_edges already has an `unreadable_since` + `attempt_count` column — are they being used? Fix: live-verify the destination gate's connection before committing a multi-hop route, and/or refresh/invalidate the edge when a live jump is rejected.
2. ASYMMETRIC / mis-charted edges — gate_edges stores directed edges (system_symbol -> connected_system, gate_waypoint = DESTINATION-side gate). Verify the charter (ShipyardScanner / gate charter) faithfully reflects the live jumpgate connection list (GET /systems/{s}/waypoints/{w}/jump-gate). Check the under_construction flag is attributed to the correct gate (source vs destination) — note CA43->ST87 and XD86->ST87 are both `t`, implying under_construction tracks the DESTINATION gate; confirm that's consistent everywhere.
3. PATHFINDING bug — the router may depart from the wrong gate_waypoint or select a path whose hop is invalid when a valid alternative exists.

REQUIRED FIXES:
- CIRCUIT-BREAKER (highest priority, stops the bleeding): a hull must NEVER bounce forever on a failed hop. After N failed attempts on a hop, ABORT the route and bail to the nearest reachable-AND-verified sink (or park + emit a stranded/distress signal). No indefinite retry-loop. This alone stops the fuel/API burn + indefinite strand even before the chart bug is fixed.
- LIVE-VERIFY / SELF-HEAL: on a live jump rejection for a charted edge, mark that gate_edges edge unreadable/under-construction (use unreadable_since) and re-plan around it; trigger a re-chart of that gate.
- Freshness: reconcile gate_edges more aggressively for era-current systems on the active trade graph, or verify-before-commit for multi-hop routes.

CODE POINTERS: the gate-crossing / cross-system multi-jump travel path (sp-9l4p "cross-system multi-jump travel"; reposition_*, NavigateRouteCommand), the gate_edges repository + the gate charter that populates it, and the Python routing service if it participates in inter-system gate pathing.

DATA REFERENCE (read-only, live daemon DB postgresql://...@localhost:5432/spacetraders): table gate_edges(system_symbol, connected_system, gate_waypoint, era_id, synced_at, under_construction, unreadable_since, attempt_count). Current era_id = 4.

RELATED: sp-2v69u (heavy-wedge) — this routing unreliability is a contributing/deeper cause; a fix here is a prerequisite for reliable offload/dispersion. sp-0ms61 (atomic buy+dedicate) is unrelated.
close_reason: Gated to main (24be446b). ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED — the bead's stale/incorrect-chart premise was FALSE: gate_edges is a verbatim snapshot of the API's GetJumpGate.connections (single writer, can't fabricate), and live DB+API were confirmed to MATCH (CA43->XD86 in both). The real bug: the API intermittently returns a 200 OK with an empty/incomplete connections list; the retry layer only retries on status codes, so a bad-but-200 read slips through, and jump_ship turned that one transient read into a PERMANENT 'no jump gate connection' -> coordinator re-flew the hull forever (the bounce). The assigned self-heal (mark edge unreadable) would have POISONED a valid live connection — deliberately NOT built. SHIPPED: resolveDestinationGateWaypoint re-reads the origin gate up to 3x (rate-limited + 750ms) before concluding no-connection — happy path exactly 1 read (zero overhead), transient recovers, genuinely-absent fails cleanly after 3 reads (no infinite bounce). No cache poisoning, no edge-marking, no flag; covers all jump callers. RED->GREEN 3 tests incl. the exact incident error. Deployed in the same restart as sp-x80j3/sp-3tsjz/sp-0ms61 follow-on. Human redirected the approach mid-build.

title: [depot] Warehouse/stocker ClaimShip must REJECT the command frigate — orphaned container re-claims it on recovery (sp-gvvph only clears the tag)
description: LIVE: TORWIND-1 (command frigate) kept coming back as a warehouse. ROOT CAUSE: sp-gvvph's frigate exclusion works at the SCALER reclaim (isReclaimable) + LAUNCH viability (depotElementHullViable/launchDepotWarehouse), and it un-dedicates the frigate — but it does NOT stop the warehouse CONTAINER. On daemon restart the orphaned warehouse-TORWIND-1 container RECOVERS via the container registry (not launchDepotWarehouse), re-runs ClaimShip(operation=warehouse), and re-claims the frigate — with dedicated_fleet='' (no tag), so 'fleet remove' can't even touch it (had to 'container stop' it manually). The recovery path bypasses every sp-gvvph guard. FIX (single robust point): the operation-checked ClaimShip for warehouse AND stocker ops must REJECT IsCommandHull (mirror the sp-l7h2 operation guards) — so the frigate can never be claimed for a depot role on ANY path (launch, grow, OR recovery). Additionally/optionally: the frigate eviction should STOP+delete the warehouse container (not just remove the depot element) so no orphan remains to recover. RULINGS #7 (frigate special), #2 (restart-idempotent — the guard must hold across recovery), #3 (single ClaimShip write path). Armed, no flag.
acceptance_criteria: A warehouse/stocker container's ClaimShip refuses the command frigate (IsCommandHull) on every path incl. restart recovery; an orphaned depot container for the frigate does not re-claim it after a daemon restart; a regular hauler is claimed normally. RED-first, -race green. Armed, no flag.
close_reason: Gated to main — command frigate can never be claimed by a depot container. Guard in the single atomic write path ShipRepository.ClaimShip (RULINGS #3/#7), placed ahead of the transient already-assigned retry so it fail-fasts on every claim path incl. restart-recovery + idempotent re-claim. New shared.ShipIsCommandHullError; grpc depot-op constants derived from domain/contract (anti-drift). Orphan self-resolves via sp-cr86 terminal path (rejected recovery -> FAILED -> never re-recovered). Durable fix for the T-1 warehouse recurrence. Armed, no flag. Full -race suite green at gate.

title: [contract] Immediate homing on contract delivery — home the hull the moment its contract-work container completes (not next idle-arb pass)
description: Admiral request (2026-07-22): a contract hauler must drive home IMMEDIATELY after delivering, not loiter. TODAY homing is periodic/lagged: the between-legs hook (run_fleet_coordinator.go:855) fires only on the NEXT contract's ship-selection change, and the standing idle-pool pass (sp-54uif) fires each idle-arb tick (~90s). So a just-delivered hull sits at the delivery waypoint up to ~90s+ before homing. FIX: at the contract-completion point (where the coordinator detects a completed contract-work worker — the 'Contract completed by X' log), dispatch HomeShipCommand for that hull IMMEDIATELY, reusing the SAME homing path (ResolveStandbyForHoming + standbyDemandProvider + HomeShipCommand) the between-legs hook and idle-pool pass use. One HomeShip path (RULINGS #7), frigate excluded, no-thrash (skip if already at a sink), home-scoped (#14). Armed, no flag.
acceptance_criteria: A hull whose contract-work container just completed is dispatched to a demand-ranked standby sink in the same tick (not waiting for the next idle-arb pass / selection change); a hull already at a sink is not re-dispatched; frigate excluded. RED-first, -race green. Armed, no flag.
close_reason: Gated to main — immediate homing on contract delivery. Homes the delivering hull the moment its contract-work worker completes (success branch), via the existing standby-demand HomeShip path. Frigate excluded, no-thrash skip when already at sink, home-scoped. Armed, no flag. Full -race suite green at gate.

title: Atomic buy+dedicate for manual shipyard purchase (--fleet role, optional) — close the operator-intent drift gap
description:
PROBLEM (operator-intent drift, live-verified era torwind-2026-07-19 player 4):
`spacetraders shipyard purchase` lands a hull UNDEDICATED (dedicated_fleet=''). Every automated dedication path treats an empty tag as "provisioning pool — fair game" (isReclaimable requires DedicatedFleet()=='' at contract_scaler_ports.go:731; depot launcher crews only an undedicated hull at container_ops_depot_launch.go:431-432). So in the window between an operator's manual purchase and a later manual `fleet assign`, any coordinator's idle-reuse can legitimately claim the hull. There is NO manual pin — no Manual flag, nothing in reservation_overrides; operator INTENT on an undedicated hull is invisible to the code.

LIVE EVIDENCE: operator bought 5 heavy freighters intending ALL for `trade`. 55/56/57 got the `trade` tag written (protected thereafter by never-poach RULINGS #7 at container_ops_depot_launch.go:446-452 — an automated path leaves a non-empty foreign tag alone). But 58 was never tagged -> the contract scaler's depot reclaimer grabbed it and stamped dedicated_fleet='warehouse' (AssignFleet at container_ops_depot_launch.go:455); 59 was never tagged -> ran an undedicated op, completed, now sits idle/undedicated/full (225 cargo) with no path back to trade. ~3M of heavy capital mis-allocated purely because the tag write lagged the purchase.

ADMIRAL REQUEST (2026-07-22): make purchase + dedication ATOMIC. "We purchase for a role (optional)." Add an optional role/fleet to the manual purchase so the hull is bought AND dedicated in one operation, before it is ever observable as an undedicated pool hull.

DESIGN:
- CLI: `spacetraders shipyard purchase <sys> <wp> <shipType> [--fleet <name>] [--player-id N]`. `--fleet` is OPTIONAL (alias --role/--dedicate at shipwright discretion, but match the EXISTING `fleet assign --fleet` vocabulary for consistency). "role" == the named dedicated fleet tag (dedicated_fleet). Omitted -> byte-identical current behavior (hull lands undedicated). Extend internal/adapters/cli/shipyard.go.
- ATOMICITY (the crux): reuse the EXISTING atomic buy+dedicate mechanism the autosizer already uses — Purchaser.BuyAndDedicate (fleet_autosizer_ports.go:365-442) buys the hull then stamps AssignFleet on the freshly-bought symbol in the same breath. Route the manual purchase through that same single-writer daemon path so the `trade` (or named) tag is committed BEFORE the hull is exposed as reclaimable. Do NOT invent a second/parallel dedication path — AssignFleet stays the single sanctioned dedication write (RULINGS #2/#3).
- CLOSE THE WINDOW: a crash between buy-success and tag-write must not leave a reclaimable undedicated hull (or must be recovered on restart). Prefer committing the dedication atomically with the purchase record, or at minimum within the same daemon command before it returns, so no coordinator tick can observe the untagged hull.
- Fleet name: accept any non-empty tag consistent with `fleet assign` (operator may target trade/warehouse/contract/custom). No HullClass inference — the operator names the fleet explicitly.
- Affordability/era-scoping/ship-type validation: unchanged (existing purchase logic); the only new behavior is the optional atomic dedicate.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `shipyard purchase ... --fleet trade` -> hull ends with dedicated_fleet='trade' and there is NO observable window where it is undedicated (test: a reclaimer/idle-reuse pass concurrent with/just after purchase never sees it as fair game).
- `shipyard purchase ...` with no flag -> hull undedicated, byte-identical to today (back-compat test).
- Reuses BuyAndDedicate / the single AssignFleet write path; no new dedication path introduced.
- build/vet/gofmt + go test green.

SCOPE NOTE: does NOT retro-fix already-orphaned hulls (58 in warehouse, 59 undedicated) — that is operator cleanup (`fleet assign`) or a separate orphan-recovery bead. This bead is prevention only.
RELATED: the orphan-recovery gap (nothing returns a completed idle undedicated heavy to trade) is a separate follow-up.
close_reason: Fixed + gated to main 1ce6d333: shipyard purchase --fleet <name> now atomic buy+dedicate per hull via the sanctioned AssignShipFleetCommand path (same terminal AssignFleet write, no parallel path), before the container returns — a manual purchase is never observable as an undedicated reclaimable pool hull. Closes operator-intent-drift (the frigate/heavy poaching class). Omitted/whitespace byte-identical; dedication-failure hard-aborts. No flag. 105 pkgs -race green. NOT yet deployed — bundling with the frigate-claim-guard + immediate-homing restart.

title: Scout partition leaves a probe idle: PartitionFleet VRP minimizes total cost, not tour-TIME balance — a floored home post (sp-2ci9y) yields fewer than N non-empty tours
description: Found during staging cold-start (DEV11 @ X1-CH36, 27 markets, HEAD w/ 73dee8fe+6c6445f8, 2026-07-23). sp-2ci9y correctly floors the home scout post to HULLS=probe_target (3), but only 2 probes actually scout; the 3rd slot is empty. ROOT CAUSE: the routing-service VRP partition (PartitionFleet: handlers/routing_handler.py + utils/routing_engine.py) minimizes TOTAL tour cost, so splitting 27 markets across 3 identical anchored probes packs them into 2 tours (cheaper than 3) and leaves the 3rd ship with an EMPTY assignment. Evidence: log Re-partitioned X1-CH36 into 3 disjoint tours over 27 markets but only 2 scout_tour containers RUNNING, scouting=2; run_scout_post_coordinator.go:2094 slotMarkets returns slot.Partition() which is empty for slot 3 -> No markets to scan for post slot yet -> unmanned. Before sp-2ci9y the post was SLA-sized (~2 hulls, both used) so this never surfaced. IMPACT: coverage climbs at 2-probe not 3-probe speed -> slower discovery -> contracts cannot source (required good market stays unscanned longer). ADMIRAL FIX SPEC: the partition must BALANCE TOTAL TOUR TIME (min-makespan) across ALL N probes, NOT the market count per tour (uneven geography makes equal-count tours unequal-freshness); ALL N ships must get a NON-EMPTY tour. OR-Tools: time dimension + SetGlobalSpanCostCoefficient (min-makespan) + all-vehicles-used / min-nodes-per-vehicle. DEPLOY: routing-service special (regen both proto sides ONLY if the interface changes -- likely internal objective change, no proto change; kickstart routing FIRST then daemon). Relates sp-2ci9y (6c6445f8). Files: handlers/routing_handler.py, utils/routing_engine.py, tests/test_fleet_partition.py.
notes:
LIVE VALIDATED on TORWIND_DEV12 (fresh cold-start, 29-market home, routing restarted with min-makespan fix at be98164d). Re-partition on 1→3 hull-budget change (after 3-cycle debounce) cut 3 disjoint non-empty tours over 29 markets: slots got 1/6/22 markets — deliberately count-UNbalanced, the fingerprint of the SetGlobalSpanCostCoefficient time objective (a count objective would give ~10/10/9). All 3 satellites manned onto distinct scout_tour ids; scouting=3, tours=3, post=3h/3/3; phase advanced DATA→INCOME. Pre-fix was 2 tours capped ~41%.
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (mechanical, open-bead-vs-main sweep) — 1 commit(s) on main name this bead in the SUBJECT line:

  be98164d 2026-07-22 fix(routing): scout fleet partition balances tour time (min-makespan), all N probes used (sp-cc2na)

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: this is evidence that code was written and MERGED for this bead. It is
NOT a verdict that the bead is satisfied — the sweep matched commit subjects, it did not check
this bead's acceptance criteria. Several beads in this sweep are epics, are explicitly partial
(their own commit says 'residual' / 'deferred from' / 'part B+C'), or have acceptance criteria
that are a MEASUREMENT rather than a shipped artifact, and those correctly stay open.

Before closing on this evidence, read the acceptance criteria and confirm the commits above
actually satisfy them. A changed file is not a fixed bead.
AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-02: DONE — single defect (PartitionFleet minimized total cost, not tour-TIME balance, leaving a probe idle). Commit be98164d switches the partition to min-makespan with all N probes used — both halves of the stated defect.
close_reason: Closed

title: [contract] Homing never relocates SITTING idle-reserved hulls → J59 pile persists (both hooks miss the held-idle pool)
description: LIVE: 6 reserved-idle contract haulers sit DOCKED at X1-UM5-J59; contract_fleet_coordinator reports '0 hull(s) re-homed' every pass post the homing-spread deploy (ba361fc7). ROOT CAUSE: the two homing triggers don't cover a hull that is simply sitting idle. (1) Between-legs homing (run_fleet_coordinator.go:855) only homes previousShipSymbol when the contract SELECTION changes — with 1 active contract only 1 hull cycles, so the other 7 are never 'previous' and never homed. (2) Idle-arb re-home (mediatorShipHomer, ~:1119) only fires AFTER a hull completes an arb leg; the reserved hulls are skipped:reserved for arb, so they never do a leg -> never re-homed. Neither path homes the held-idle pool that actually piles. FIX: add a standing homing pass in the idle-hull discovery loop — for each IDLE, off-station, dedicated contract hull NOT launched on an arb leg this pass, dispatch HomeShipCommand to the demand-ranked standby set (reuse ResolveStandbyForHoming + the wired provider). Homing a reserved hull is correct — it POSITIONS it for the next contract (the sp-9le3x design intent: 'idle hulls home to standby instead of parking where they finished'), compatible with the reservation. No-thrash: a hull already AT a standby stays (mirror home_ship.go's at-station short-circuit); one home dispatch per hull per pass. Armed, no flag. RULINGS #2 (no thrash), #14 (home-scoped).
acceptance_criteria: An idle, off-station, dedicated contract hull (incl. reserved, not arb-launched this pass) is dispatched to a demand-ranked standby sink; a hull already at a standby is left; a hull on an arb leg / in transit / on a contract is untouched. Idle contract haulers spread off J59 to the central sinks. RED-first, -race green. Armed, NO feature flag.
close_reason: Fixed + gated (c584de53 → main): the standing idle-pool re-home (rehomeDriftedHulls) now auto-resolves the demand-ranked central-park sinks (ResolveStandbyForHoming) instead of bailing on the empty pinned fleet-hub set — the sitting reserve-floor pool homes off J59 to the sinks. Armed, no flag; one HomeShip path (#7), frigate excluded, #14/#2 intact. 10/10 rehome tests green.

title: [depot] Frigate/depot eviction (sp-gvvph) leaves SUPPORTED cargo aboard the freed hull → buffer walks off + hull stranded full
description: LIVE after the sp-gvvph deploy: the command frigate TORWIND-1, evicted from warehouse duty, now sits idle+undedicated+FULL (40/40 SILVER — a SUPPORTED depot good) at X1-UM5-G49. evictStrandedDepotElement (container_ops_depot_launch.go) un-dedicates + releases the hull but does NOT transfer cargo (it mirrors the stranded-stocker eviction). Consequences: (1) 40 SILVER walked OFF the depot buffer; (2) the frigate can't resume its command role until cleared, and can't re-deposit — stocker reports 'warehouse group at X1-UM5-G49 full (0 aggregate free space across 5 ops)', partly from the sp-g0mdl pollution (TORWIND-58 = 210 FOOD). Self-clear is uncertain: scaler won't reclaim it (sp-gvvph exclusion), idle-arb won't (RULINGS #7); only the frigate's own contract loop would sell the SILVER if it picks the hull up. FIX: on depot-element eviction, DEPOSIT the hull's SUPPORTED depot goods into a co-located warehouse with free space BEFORE releasing (keep the buffer, free the hull empty); jettison only NON-supported cargo. title: Daemon restart wipes ALL live-config tune overrides — no persistence layer; persist tunes to DB + reload on boot
description:
PROBLEM: live tune overrides (the 'tune' command / LIVE layer) are held IN THE DAEMON'S MEMORY ONLY. There is NO persistence — confirmed: zero tune/override tables in the daemon DB (:5432/spacetraders). So a full DAEMON restart or redeploy reverts EVERY tuned knob to its config.yaml default. This silently (a) disables load-bearing operational settings (e.g. max_probe_fleet, discover_scan_balance, scout_cross_system_relay_enabled — all observed wiped this session by the 20:27 rebuild and the 07-19 reset) and (b) DISARMS SAFETY GUARDS (sp-ve3q: max_probe_price overpay ceiling -> 0 on restart). Operators must manually re-arm after every restart, and usually don't know a restart happened.

DISTINCT FROM the existing beads: sp-ve3q (CLOSED), sp-rsgc (CLOSED), sp-vgg0 (OPEN) all address the COORDINATOR-restart case only — restarting ONE coordinator via its 'start' verb while the daemon is alive re-applies the in-memory value via the sp-rsgc re-adopt helper. NONE of them survive a DAEMON process restart / redeploy, because the source of truth is in-memory and is lost with the process. That is the gap.

FIX: add a durable tune-override store (DB table, e.g. tune_overrides keyed by (player_id, coordinator/operation, knob)) written on every successful 'tune' set, and RELOAD it on daemon boot — applied as coordinators start, taking precedence over config.yaml defaults (same precedence the live layer has now). Then a redeploy preserves the operator's armed state.

CONSTRAINTS: RULINGS #5 — immutable money-guard consts (ImmutableReserveFloor etc.) must NOT become persisted-tunable; only the existing tune-registry knobs persist. Fail-safe: a corrupt/absent store falls back to config.yaml defaults (never blocks boot). Consider era-scoping the store (wipe on era reset) OR persisting across eras — decide per knob.

ACCEPTANCE: set a tune value, restart the daemon (make restart-daemon), and the value survives (not reverted to default); a money-guard const is unaffected; boot succeeds with an empty/corrupt store. Ties to the arming-ledger (sp-nc0m) — persisted tunes make the 'closed is not armed' re-arm dance mostly unnecessary.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-06: FALSIFIED -- the premise searched for the wrong SHAPE. The bead says 'live tune overrides are held IN THE DAEMON'S MEMORY ONLY, zero tune/override tables'. There is indeed no tune_overrides TABLE -- but tunes persist to a COLUMN: tune CLI -> TuneContainerConfig -> MutateContainerConfigKey -> container_ops_tune.go:321 -> containerRepo.UpdateContainerConfig, writing containers.config, which coordinators re-read each tick. EMPIRICAL PROOF (lead-verified): probe_sensing_coordinator, scout_post_coordinator, opportunity_relocator and contract_fleet_coordinator are RUNNING with started_at 2026-08-04 19:52 and non-empty configs (95/82/58/186 bytes) -- and the daemon restarted today at 14:33 UTC. Config written two days ago survived the restart this bead says destroys it. PRIOR CONTRADICTION THE BEAD MISSED: sp-ve3q's own correction (quoted in sp-nc0m NOTES, predating this bead) says 'DAEMON restart PRESERVES live-tunes; it is frontier start (relaunch stopped coordinator) that WIPES to config defaults'. sp-w9zfx claims to be 'DISTINCT FROM sp-ve3q' while inverting the very finding it distinguishes itself from. The real gap -- COORDINATOR RELAUNCH wiping to defaults -- is narrower and already open as sp-vgg0.

title: bug
description:
SYMPTOM (era torwind-2026-07-19, player 4): 5 SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER (225 cargo) added to the 'trade' fleet get stuck FULL and idle. Live DB: TORWIND-59 holds 225 PLATINUM_ORE, TORWIND-58 180 FOOD+45 ADV_CIRCUITRY, TORWIND-55 180 FABRICS — all parked IN_ORBIT, cycling dozens of tour-run containers that complete in 8-40s (churn). Overall trade throughput dropped after adding them.

ROOT CAUSE (layered; dominant defect = offload-rescue is held-cargo-blind):

(1) Capacity-blind loading. tour_solver.py:139 MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES_PER_MARKET_GOOD_SIDE=2 and the beam hold-packing bound (sp-gm00) have NO awareness of hull capacity. Filling a 225 hull forces either 180-225 units concentrated into 1-2 high-tv goods or a 6-8 good fragment; both stress shallow markets (market_absorption_ledger shows ~20-60 units/sell at WEAK/RESTRICTED) far harder than an 80-cargo light.

(2) Buys gated on MODELED not REALIZED sell depth. score_sequence (tour_solver.py:728-770): a buy exists only as a (buy_leg,sell_leg) pairing, units=min(buy_rem,sell_rem,slack,afford) — so on paper every buy has a sell. But sell depth is the fitted 2-tranche impact model. When multiple heavies concentrate on the SAME good (evidence: TORWIND-57/58/59 each sold 180 FABRICS = 540u in 18min) or buy/sell are time-separated, the realized sink is crushed, the execution sell-floor rejects, and 100-225 units strand.

(3) DOMINANT: the offload/reposition machinery is structurally blind to held cargo. run_tour_coordinator_reposition.go:905 sets shipState.Cargo=nil (clears the hull's real cargo when ranking candidate destinations — fix for a prior clogged-hold bug 2B-0691151d). Combined with freshProfit = ProjectedProfit - HeldLiquidation - DepositValue gated vs the 25000 floor (reposition.go:281,900), a FULL hull has zero slack (solver occ=[total_initial]*n => no fresh buys => freshProfit~=0 < floor) so it can NEVER clear the reposition floor, AND destinations are chosen for fresh arb, never for a sink that can absorb the held good. A full heavy can neither be steered toward a sink for its load nor rescued.

(4) No distress liquidation + honest-exit relaunch loop. Stranded detector (reposition.go:463) is OBSERVATION-ONLY and scoped to a narrow gate-inaccessible shape (candidates==0 && neighbors==0) the heavies never hit. The stranded VETO (run_tour_coordinator.go:1083 strandedReason over netBought) only covers cargo BOUGHT THIS run; a hull relaunched already-full has empty netBought so it exits Completed=true despite 225 unsold units => coordinator relaunches new tour container on the still-full hull => same infeasible/zero-trade plan => starvation exit => relaunch forever.

Reachability evidence: TORWIND-58 sits at X1-QM8 holding 180 FOOD but X1-QM8 has NO fresh FOOD import sink; TORWIND-55/56 parked together at X1-GD21 holding FABRICS with no fresh FABRICS sink there — while dozens of fresh FABRICS/FOOD sinks exist in OTHER systems the cargo-blind reposition won't steer toward. TORWIND-59's 225 PLATINUM_ORE has only ~200/u sinks (near-worthless) anywhere.

Answers to the 4 investigation Qs: (1) buys ARE gated at plan-time but on OPTIMISTIC modeled depth, not realized/fleet-contended depth; (2) PLANNED sells don't 'stall in the ledger' — they are reservations released/expired on tour exit; the SALE never completes because the hull can't reach an absorbing sink and repositions/relaunches instead (stuck EXECUTION, not stuck ledger transition); (3) YES capacity-vs-depth mismatch is the core — no reachable-sink absorption budget for the loaded position, no held-cargo-aware offload; (4) YES heavies degrade lights via shared fleet-wide absorption A-cap + sink crush (540u FABRICS) + shared markets.

FIX (concrete, default-OFF per PLAYBOOK section 10):
 PRIMARY — held-cargo-aware offload/reposition. When a continuous tour hull is laden (e.g. cargo > 50% capacity) and margins-died with no feasible fresh plan, add a HELD-CARGO OFFLOAD mode: rank reposition candidates by reachable SINK ABSORPTION for the goods currently held (margin-exempt cash recovery), and jump toward the ground that best liquidates the held load. Do NOT clear cargo (or run a parallel held-aware pass) for this mode. Reuses existing net_absorption / market-depth reads.
 SECONDARY — capacity-aware buy budget. Cap per-tour BUY commitment per good to what the reachable sink graph can absorb for the hull's capacity net of fleet-wide absorption, so a 225 heavy never loads 180 of a good its reachable sinks can't take.
 TERTIARY — escalate the stranded detector from observe-only to a bounded DISTRESS liquidation for the laden + no-fresh-plan + reposition-cant-rescue case, so a hull never churns indefinitely full.

READ-ONLY diagnosis; no code changed, no game state mutated. Evidence from live daemon DB + container logs 2026-07-22 ~20:55.
notes: TERTIARY (bounded distress liquidation) LANDED on main 69388afb: new run_tour_coordinator_distress.go — chain fresh->offload->distress, one action/episode, shares RepositionDisabled kill-switch; sell-side floor-free, loss booked, no buy-guard change (#4). Armed. -race green. STATUS: PRIMARY + TERTIARY on main; SECONDARY (Python capacity-aware buys) still building. Bead closes when SECONDARY lands + all 3 deploy.
close_reason: COMPLETE + DEPLOYED (all armed, no flags): PRIMARY held-cargo offload rescue (6eac20ed) + TERTIARY bounded distress liquidation (69388afb) live on the daemon; SECONDARY capacity-aware per-good buy cap (7a6b4a63) live on the routing service (deploy-routing, healthy). Depth cap supersedes MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES; analyst watching prod fleet cr/hr on the affected class (arm-and-measure — deep-sink single-visit dumps now restructure into revisits, same load+profit). RULINGS #4/#5 intact.

title: Contract coordinator: over-fetched cargo on a fulfilled contract -> 4509 self-healing stall (resists jettison + container-stop; needs fleet-unassign to break)
description:
OBSERVED 2026-07-21 (era torwind, player 4, contract_fleet_coordinator-player-4-a1f4ec84 -> auto-recovered b37c3368).

STALL: the whole contract operation wedged on ONE ship's orphaned cargo. TORWIND-19 over-fetched FERTILIZERS for a contract whose delivery terms were then MET (contract fulfilled=true), leaving 64 leftover FERTILIZERS on the hull. The coordinator looped forever: select TORWIND-19 -> "Waiting for TORWIND-19 to complete contract" -> worker tries to deliver the excess -> API 400 code 4509 "Contract delivery terms for FERTILIZERS have been met" -> retry -> loop. TORWIND-D (2nd contract hauler) sat idle behind it; NO new contract negotiated. `contract list` showed ALL contracts fulfilled=true, so the stuck reference is a stale in-progress assignment against an already-fulfilled contract.

SELF-HEALING / RESISTS THE OBVIOUS UNSTICKS:
 - `ship jettison` of the excess FAILED repeatedly: "lost the claim-handoff race (attempt 7/7): ship TORWIND-19 is already assigned to container contract-work-TORWIND-19-...". The running worker holds the ship reservation, so the jettison never claims the ship.
 - `container stop` of the coordinator was futile: it is a RECOVERABLE container and auto-recovered (new suffix b37c3368) within seconds, re-spawning a worker that re-claimed TORWIND-19.
 - WHAT FINALLY WORKED (captain workaround): `fleet unassign --ship TORWIND-19` (return to general pool) -> the worker released the ship -> `ship jettison` executed (cargo 0/80) -> coordinator dropped the phantom contract -> "Negotiating new contract" -> normal flow resumed. Then re-dedicated TORWIND-19 to the contract fleet.

ROOT CAUSE: when a ship over-fetches contract cargo and the contract's terms are met by a partial delivery, the leftover cargo has no delivery target. The coordinator retries delivery (hits 4509) instead of (a) recognizing terms-met/fulfilled and releasing the ship, or (b) dumping/selling the orphaned over-fetch and moving on. The recoverable-container auto-recovery makes it un-stoppable via the normal container-stop path, so the operator has to fleet-unassign the ship to break the grip — non-obvious.

FIX (either/both):
 1. On a 4509 "delivery terms met" (or fulfilled-contract) delivery failure, mark the assignment complete and RELEASE the ship (dump or sell the orphaned over-fetch), do NOT retry delivery.
 2. Don't over-fetch beyond the contract's remaining needed units in the first place.

IMPACT: wedges the entire contract income stream (this era's contracts = ~4.1M revenue in the day's P&L) on a single ship's leftover cargo — 2nd hauler idle, no new contracts negotiated. Recurs whenever a contract fulfills with a partial delivery that leaves excess on the hull. Captain recovery is non-obvious (jettison + container-stop both fail; needs fleet-unassign).

VERIFY-FIXED: force an over-fetch (assign a hull more contract cargo than the remaining need), let the contract fulfill on a partial delivery; the coordinator should release the hull (excess dumped/sold) and negotiate the next contract WITHOUT a 4509 retry loop.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE VERIFIED FROM CODE + LIVE STATE (contract-debug, systematic debugging, 2026-07-21, player 4 era torwind, coordinator ...-b37c3368). READ-ONLY; no game/code mutated.

THE DIVERGENCE (proven, the crux of everything):
Local DB contract cmrupci6t4tmkuo6zlkaixxl9: accepted=true, fulfilled=false, delivery FERTILIZERS -> X1-UM5-K83 UnitsRequired=64 UnitsFulfilled=0. SERVER: 4509 'terms for FERTILIZERS have been met' (i.e. 64/64). Local UnitsFulfilled=0 never recorded the server-side fulfillment. It is the ONLY unfulfilled row in the DB (294 contracts, 293 fulfilled). TORWIND-19 sits DOCKED at the delivery dest X1-UM5-K83 holding exactly 64 FERTILIZERS; TORWIND-13 (running worker) holds 64 and just logged 'Resuming existing active contract -> Purchase needs calculated -> Contract cargo delivery initiated -> Ship navigation requested' (about to 4509 too).

RC#1 — THE STALL (the P1 fleet-wedge). There is NO 4509 / terms-met reconciliation anywhere in contract app or domain code (grep confirmed: the only 'already fulfilled' checks read LOCAL state). Loop:
 - contract_market_service.go:79-96 NegotiateContract short-circuits on contract_repository.go:40-43 FindActiveContracts (WHERE accepted AND NOT fulfilled) -> keeps returning the stale local row; the negotiate API (and any server refresh) is never called.
 - run_fleet_coordinator.go:457-463 allDeliveriesFulfilled reads stale local UnitsFulfilled=0 -> concludes 64 still needed -> sources + dispatches.
 - delivery_executor.go:548-554,582-585 DeliverContractCargo computes unitsToDeliver=min(cargo64,remaining64)=64>0, navigates, calls deliver API.
 - deliver_contract.go:95-107 callDeliverCargoAPI wraps the 4509 as a plain 'failed to deliver cargo' error (no code inspection); ProcessSingleDelivery (delivery_executor.go:288-291) returns it -> worker container CRASHES.
 - Coordinator recordWorkerCompletion logs failure, main loop restarts -> re-negotiate returns SAME stale row -> re-selects SAME cargo-laden hull (distance 0.00) -> deliver -> 4509. Infinite. LIVE PROOF: 22:21:12 & 22:29:02 'Worker TORWIND-19 failed: 4509 ... -> Negotiating new contract'. Excess never dumped, hull never released, no new contract.

RC#2 — THE DOUBLE-LOAD / OVER-FETCH (downstream of RC#1). Over-fetch is 'delivered-0-kept-all': a hull sources 64 for the contract, but by arrival the server terms are already met, so it delivers 0 and keeps all 64 orphaned. Two hulls each hold 64 for the SAME contract because after each 4509 crash the coordinator reclaims the crashed hull to idle (run_fleet_coordinator.go:337 unconditional ReclaimShipsFromInterruptedWorkers) and then dispatches a DIFFERENT hull. The cross-ship reservation guard calculateInFlightCargo (run_fleet_coordinator.go:1453-1516) counts cargo ONLY on RUNNING-worker ships + FAILED-with-cargo ships — NOT on IDLE hulls just reclaimed from a crashed worker. So the reclaimed hull's 64 FERTILIZERS are invisible, inFlightCargo reads 0<64 (line 562 gate), and a fresh hull is sent to source another 64. Per-ship buy math cargo_manager.go:125-145 CalculatePurchaseNeeds=unitsRemaining-currentUnits keys off the same stale local contract; it never reconciles server truth.

CONTRACT GET 'NOT FOUND' ODDITY — CLI wart, NOT the bug. cli/contract.go: 'contract list' prints a 9-char TRUNCATED short id (shortContractID line 150-156, printed line 281); 'contract get' does exact full-id match (gormContractStore.GetContract line 90-97, WHERE id=?). Full id = cmrupci6t4tmkuo6zlkaixxl9; the displayed short 'cmrupci6t' never matches. Both read the same local DB (no API). Red herring w.r.t. the stall.

MINIMAL FIX (root cause, dissolves stall AND makes the over-fetch self-heal):
 PRIMARY: handle 4509 at the deliver call site as authoritative server truth. In DeliverContractHandler/callDeliverCargoAPI (deliver_contract.go:95-107) detect code 4509 (mirror the existing idiom IsInsufficientCreditsError insufficient_credits.go:53-57: strings.Contains(err.Error(),"code":4509) — the *APIError body preserves it). On 4509: sync the contract from the API (or set the matched delivery UnitsFulfilled=UnitsRequired) and PERSIST, then return a terminal success (units=server count) instead of an error. Effect: worker sees UnitsFulfilled>=UnitsRequired -> returns -> CanFulfill()=true -> FulfillContract claims reward -> contract leaves FindActiveContracts; the orphaned excess is now unrelated to any active contract, so the existing FilterUnrelatedCargo + auto-liquidation path (run_fleet_coordinator.go:608-623) sells/dumps it and the hull re-enters candidacy. No crash, no re-dispatch, no fleet-unassign needed.
 DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH (secondary): (a) count contract-good cargo on IDLE reclaimed hulls in calculateInFlightCargo so the double-load can't recur even under other divergences; (b) re-sync the active contract from the API on the resume/negotiate path so FindActiveContracts cannot serve an indefinitely-stale row.

EVIDENCE: live logs (4509 loop 22:21/22:29), ship info (TORWIND-19 64 FERT @X1-UM5-K83 docked; TORWIND-13 64 FERT @X1-FD3 orbit), contract get cmrupci6t4tmkuo6zlkaixxl9 --json (0/64 local vs server-met), grep (no 4509 handler). Files: deliver_contract.go, services/delivery_executor.go, services/cargo_manager.go, services/contract_market_service.go, commands/run_fleet_coordinator.go, persistence/contract_repository.go, adapters/cli/contract.go, services/insufficient_credits.go.
REGRESSION HUNT (contract-debug, 2026-07-21, read-only git+live). The Admiral asked why this broke NOW after ~3 eras. Answer: the introducing change is the contractscaler epic sp-9le3x, landed AND deployed 2026-07-21 (daemon 735e72fb). It did NOT remove a contract-state re-sync (that specific hypothesis is REFUTED). It replaced a DEFAULT-OFF, topology-bounded contract-delivery model with an ARMED, persistent MULTI-HULL dedicated 'contract' fleet, which now continuously trips the pre-existing (always-latent) over-fetch/double-load race -> server-met/local-unmet divergence -> the always-absent 4509 handler -> infinite loop.

HYPOTHESIS REFUTED (deleted periodic contract API re-sync): no such sync ever existed.
 - ContractRepository (domain/contract/ports.go:6-9) is LOCAL-ONLY: FindByID, FindActiveContracts, Add. No Sync/Refresh method, ever.
 - apiClient.GetContract (the only server contract-state read, API GET /my/contracts/{id}) has exactly ONE caller: negotiate_contract.go:169, in the 4511 'agent already has contract' branch — present since early history, NOT touched by the deletion. And NegotiateContract short-circuits on FindActiveContracts (local) before ever calling the API, so even that never refreshes a stale active row.
 - The deleted capacity stack read contract state via the LOCAL repo (RecentContractDemand) and emitted capital DEMAND only. contract_delivery_bridge.go is a CapitalDemand bridge (reconciler->autosizer), not a state sync. Nothing deleted pulled server UnitsFulfilled/fulfilled into local.
 - The missing-4509-handler AND the double-load / negotiate-on-delivery (sp-qpmi e5defd4e, 2026-07-08) race are PRESERVED byte-for-byte across the deletion — always latent.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED (introducing commits, all 2026-07-21, epic sp-9le3x, deployed daemon 735e72fb):
 - 1a5a4bbd 15:29 contractscaler C2b actuation (container type + contract_fleet_max_hulls tune, def 2 / max 16), default-off.
 - f861cd7c 16:38 DELETE the boot-standing capacity-reconciler contract-delivery stack (NET -16573) — the prior standing contract-delivery driver — and the autosizer contract-delivery AUTO-SCALING path.
 - 735e72fb 16:46 scaler RECLAIM tier: before every buy, re-dedicate an idle UNDEDICATED cargo hull EXCLUSIVE to the 'contract' fleet (contractScalerReclaimer.FindReclaimable/Reclaim). Aggressively grows the dedicated fleet from owned idle hulls.
 - ARMING: contract_scaler_early_scaling (default 0 = OFF, 'Armed by the shipwright after validation') is ARMED in this deploy — contract_scaler-player-4-5b33758c is RUNNING live (since 19:52:20). It ramps TORWIND-19/-13/-D into the exclusive 'contract' fleet.

WHY IT WORKED ~3 ERAS, BREAKS NOW:
 - BEFORE: routine contract-hauler auto-scaling was DEFAULT-OFF / arm-gated (fleet_autosizer.go:183-186 sp-nkqn contract-delivery hull class; capacity reconciler idled when topology satisfied). Contracts ran LEAN — effectively the bootstrap frigate + minimal reserve-floor hulls. The coordinator's single-worker loop rarely had a SECOND cargo-laden dedicated hull to alternate onto, so the crash->reclaim->redispatch double-load (and the server-met/local-unmet divergence it creates) essentially never arose. The unhandled 4509 + negotiate-on-delivery race stayed latent.
 - NOW: the ARMED scaler makes a persistent MULTI-HULL exclusive 'contract' fleet the steady state (def 2, ramping toward 7-8+). With >=2 dedicated cargo hulls, the coordinator's crash->reclaim->redispatch (calculateInFlightCargo blind to idle reclaimed cargo, run_fleet_coordinator.go:1453-1516) routinely sources the SAME one-active-contract onto a second hull; one meets the server terms, the other's local view stays 0/N -> the divergence PERSISTS -> 4509 loop (RC#1). Live proof: TORWIND-19 (64 FERT @dest X1-UM5-K83) + TORWIND-13 (64 FERT, diff system) both loaded for cmrupci6t (local 0/64, server met).

NET: the fix (RC#1 4509 reconciliation) is still the correct P1 remedy and is architecture-independent. The REGRESSION that surfaced the latent bug is the sp-9le3x armed multi-hull contract scaler (daemon 735e72fb), NOT a deleted sync. Secondary hardening (count idle reclaimed-hull cargo in calculateInFlightCargo) directly kills the double-load the scaler now makes common. Evidence: git log/show f861cd7c e5defd4e 1a5a4bbd 735e72fb; ports.go; fleet_autosizer.go; live container list (contract_scaler running).
ADMIRAL FIX DIRECTIVE 2026-07-21 (coordinator hull-selection fix; complements RC#1).

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR: the contract coordinator must select exactly ONE hull DETERMINISTICALLY to fulfill a given contract, and that hull stays the SOLE hull working the contract UNTIL its delivery completes. Only AFTER the delivery does the coordinator choose the NEXT hull — selected ALWAYS by shortest distance to the source (the warehouse holding the good, or the market that sells it).

WHY THIS IS THE FIX:
 - Serializes contract fulfillment to ONE active hull per contract -> eliminates the concurrent multi-hull over-fetch / double-load (RC#2). That double-load is the amplifier the armed sp-9le3x contract scaler turned continuous (multi-hull became steady state); serializing removes it regardless of how many hulls the scaler provisions.
 - DETERMINISTIC selection means a crashed/reclaimed hull is re-chosen as the SAME hull on the next cycle, not a different cargo-laden one -> no second hull ever accumulates orphaned cargo (kills the 128-for-64 pattern directly).

STILL REQUIRED alongside this (do NOT drop RC#1): authoritative 4509 / "terms met" handling at the deliver site (deliver_contract.go:95-107) to reconcile the server-met/local-unmet divergence and UNWEDGE the current stale row (cmrupci6t: local 0/64, server met). Single-hull selection prevents the double-load, but a single hull can still deliver-to-a-server-already-met contract (local record lag) and hit 4509 — so the reconciliation is what makes the loop impossible and clears the live wedge.

COMPLETE FIX = (a) deterministic single-hull-per-contract selection, next hull by shortest-distance-to-source [this directive] + (b) 4509 reconciliation at the deliver site [RC#1] + (c) count idle reclaimed-hull cargo in calculateInFlightCargo (run_fleet_coordinator.go:1453-1516) as defense-in-depth.
CROSS-REF: sp-yxs7s (contract subsystem simplification, Admiral knob-audit). The deterministic single-hull-per-contract dispatch + 4509 reconciliation fix here IS a shared deliverable with sp-yxs7s — it fixes this stall AND removes the multi-hull over-fetch/double-load complexity that sp-yxs7s targets. Once single-hull dispatch lands, the secondary hardening (count idle reclaimed-hull cargo in calculateInFlightCargo) becomes unnecessary.
CROSS-REF WITHDRAWN (Admiral ruling 2026-07-22): the earlier trailing note linking this bug to the sp-yxs7s contract-simplification is withdrawn. sp-1pf0r is SOLELY the P1 contract-stall bug + its approved fix (deterministic single-hull-per-contract dispatch + 4509/terms-met reconciliation + no over-fetch). Contract SIMPLIFICATION is a separate AUDIT-ONLY track with NO removals authorized — not part of this bug.

title: Frontier coordinator should auto-locate a shipyard and position a buyer hull — currently fail-closes 'probe unpriceable' and stalls fleet growth
description:
OBSERVED 2026-07-21 (era torwind-2026-07-19, player 4, container frontier_expansion_coordinator-player-4-b6b49c56).

SYMPTOM: the frontier probe fleet is pinned at 9/40 (0 idle) and cannot grow. Every cycle logs:
  "no purchase: probe unpriceable (fail-closed): no idle undedicated ship is stationed at a probe-selling shipyard"
The coordinator has open post slots (2+), declared posts sitting unmanned, and WANTS to buy probes to man them — but the buy path fail-closes because pricing a probe requires an idle *undedicated* ship already parked at a probe-selling shipyard, and none happens to be there. The coordinator does NOT proactively find a shipyard or position/relocate a ship to one, so once the fleet drifts away from yards, probe-buying halts indefinitely.

EXPECTED (Admiral directive 2026-07-21): the frontier expansion coordinator should AUTOMATICALLY (a) locate the nearest reachable probe-selling shipyard, and (b) position/relocate an eligible hull there (claim/route an idle undedicated ship) so the buy path can price and purchase. Fleet growth must be self-sufficient, not contingent on a hull happening to sit at a yard.

IMPACT: blocks the active frontier-expansion objective. With the fleet maxed at 9 and no buy path, declared posts queue unmanned; combined with the core-cluster reach constraint (sp-u8jc) and the reaper-off jam (post_inflight_timeout_secs=0), expansion stalls. Observed over ~30 min: in-flight cap pinned then EXCEEDED (5/5 -> 6/5), unscanned marketplaces flat then regressing (34 -> 19 -> 36), ~1 virgin charted per 5 min, last probe buy 24m+ ago.

RELATED: sp-u8jc (probes clustered in core, no relay to dense hubs — the REACH side). probe_reuse_enabled knob (relay-existing-probe-before-buy; an alternative reach lever, default-off — sidesteps buying but does NOT fix the buy-side gap). sp-3u5d (per-unit probe price ceiling). sp-0pw6 (scout-reposition relay config). THIS issue is the complementary BUY-SIDE gap: even with reach solved, the fleet cannot grow if the coordinator can't position a buyer at a yard.

INTERIM WORKAROUND (captain-side): manually unassign an idle hull to undedicated and park it at a probe-selling shipyard (e.g. X1-UM5-A2) to restore pricing/buys.

VERIFY-FIXED: with the frontier fleet below max_probe_fleet and no hull sitting at a shipyard, the coordinator locates a reachable yard, positions a buyer hull there, and resumes probe purchases automatically — no recurring "probe unpriceable (fail-closed)" stall, fleet grows toward the cap, posts get manned.

title: C2d: warehouse/stocker deep runtime actuation for the contract scaler
description:
C2d of epic sp-9le3x — WAREHOUSE/STOCKER DEEP RUNTIME ACTUATION for the contract scaler. Banked by the C2b lane (sp-049a9, landed on main 1a5a4bbd).

## THE GAP
C2b's Purchaser buys+dedicates the plan's Warehouse + Stocker PlanUnits to the "contract" fleet (via HullClassContractDelivery) and homes them to the central hub. But their RUNTIME DUTIES are NOT wired:
- Warehouse hull: goods-to-stock (accumulate contract goods at the depot waypoint).
- Stocker hull: source-legs (haul from producing markets into the warehouse).
A "contract"-dedicated warehouse/stocker hull is currently INDISTINGUISHABLE from a plain delivery hull to the fleet coordinator — it will just behave as another delivery hauler. So the depot geometry is bought but not operated.

## THE FIX (two options — pick in design)
(a) A dedicated contract-depot actuator that reads the scaler's role assignment (warehouse vs stocker vs delivery) and drives the corresponding runtime loop, OR
(b) Adopt the "contract"-dedicated warehouse/stocker hulls into the EXISTING depot/stocker machinery (the depot-role coordinator the reconciler used) — reuse rather than rebuild.
Prefer (b) if the existing depot machinery can be pointed at a fixed, scaler-owned role set without the reconciler's churn; escalate if it can't.

## PRIORITY: LOW / DEFERRED
MOOT until the contract ceiling (contract_fleet_max_hulls, default 2) is raised past the delivery-hull count. Under the default the ramp only ever buys the first 2 DELIVERY hulls; warehouse/stocker units are never purchased. So this is a Phase-2 lever (depot mesh), not a Phase-1 gate blocker. Do NOT build until the op is proven at 2 delivery hulls and the Admiral decides to scale past it.

## RULINGS / ENGINEERING
RULINGS #2 (restart-safe role state), #3 (daemon single-writer), #4 (money guards fail closed — the 200k cushion + kept 9aoc floor), #14 (home-system only), #12/#13 (commit --no-verify + captain-gate; verify SHA), #19 (default-off; arming separate). ENGINEERING §6 (short WHY-only comments). Protected paths untouched. Dispatch via nw-software-crafter.

Depends C2b (sp-049a9, DONE). Does NOT block C3 (scrap-the-reconciler is independent). Blocks: full contract depot operation at scale.
notes: CORRECTED DESIGN (2026-07-21, verified against live durable store + daemon.log): there is NO general-economy warehouse system. The 2 warehouses (TORWIND-15/11) + stocker (TORWIND-18) at hub X1-UM5-I56 ARE the ONE contract depot — reconciler-built 07-21 13:22 ('Launched reuse-staffed depot ... 2 warehouse, 1 stocker, 1 delivery'), persisted in the durable depot store, boot-reloaded every restart. It is ORPHANED: log shows 'depot buffer re-solve deferred to armed reconciler ... left to the reconciler's supported_goods' — and C3 (f861cd7c) deleted the reconciler, so nothing manages what the depot stocks. FEATURE = make the scaler the depot's fixed-plan DRIVER (the role the deleted reconciler played): (1) role-aware ramp reusing the EXISTING launchDepotWarehouse/launchDepotStocker to grow the EXISTING depot; (2) depot registry as source-of-truth for actuated warehouse/stocker units so the ramp reconciles the existing depot instead of buying duplicates; (3) scaler OWNS supported_goods (far-source goods lookup) — fixes the orphan. Delivery ramp untouched. Default-off: ceiling=2 never reaches a warehouse unit = byte-identical. Admiral: 'make it as simple as possible, reuse the wheel, elegant' + 'do it'.
close_reason: C2d depot actuation DONE + gated (c7fb2b0e) + deployed + verified. Scaler drives the existing depot: role-aware ramp (one hull/tick, next role, placed), reconcile-not-duplicate via depot registry, reuse-before-buy per role, FIXED 8-symbol supported_goods pinned once at arm (no on-demand miner, per Admiral + analyst st-wisp-2h6r5). Default-off byte-identical at ceiling=2; ready to arm by raising contract_fleet_max_hulls. 12 tests -race green.

title: Make construction pipeline max_workers LIVE-TUNABLE (no restart) — scale gate throughput without stop+start churn
description:
Admiral-directed (2026-07-21). Today a construction pipeline's max_workers is a LAUNCH param (construction start --max-workers N), frozen for the pipeline's life; changing it needs stop + fresh construction start — which risks the sp-1jpiw restart-wedge every time and aborts in-flight hauls. Expose it as a LIVE override so gate throughput scales instantly, no restart.

## MECHANISM (the seam already exists)
resolveWorkerCap (internal/application/manufacturing/commands/run_construction_coordinator.go:306) reads the pipeline's max_workers PER-TICK (drives errgroup.SetLimit at ~:315-316). So if a live command updates the RUNNING pipeline's stored max_workers, the coordinator picks it up next tick (Pattern-C, no restart) — same live-provider pattern the 'construction override' verb already uses for per-good gating.

## FIX
Add a live override for the running pipeline's max_workers, following the 'construction override' verb pattern (adapters/grpc + adapters/cli/construction.go). Preferred: 'spacetraders construction override --site <site> --max-workers N' (site-level, not per-good) -> gRPC updates the pipeline's max_workers in its store -> resolveWorkerCap reads it next tick. (Or a dedicated 'construction workers <site> <n>' verb if cleaner.) Validate bounds (>=1). Must SURVIVE a daemon restart (RULINGS #2 — the pipeline's max_workers is already persisted; the override amends it).

## ALSO VERIFY (related)
Confirm 'construction start --max-workers N' is actually HONORED — live obs shows 'worker cap 1' in the dispatch log despite a --max-workers 10 start; either the fresh pipeline had not dispatched yet or the flag is not wired through. Confirm the launch flag path works; fix if it does not (same max_workers field).

## RULINGS / ENGINEERING
RULINGS #2 (override survives restart), #3 (daemon single-writer — via gRPC, not CLI-side), #12/#13 (commit --no-verify + captain-gate only; verify SHA), ENGINEERING sec6 (short WHY-only comments). Protected paths untouched.

## ACCEPTANCE (RED-first)
- On a RUNNING gate pipeline, a live max-workers override -> the NEXT drain tick's 'dispatching ... (worker cap N)' reflects N and hulls fan out to N concurrent, with NO daemon/pipeline restart. (RED: today no live path; cap frozen at launch value.)
- Bounds: 0/negative rejected.
- Restart-safe: the live-set cap survives a daemon restart (persisted).
- 'construction start --max-workers N' honored at launch (regression/confirm).

VERIFY-FIXED (live): set it on the I56 gate pipeline, watch the dispatch-log cap change + the fan-out, no restart.
notes:
MERGED b3bc38f5 + DEPLOYED (daemon b3bc38f5, healthy). New verb: construction workers <site> --count N (mirrors goods factory workers; live, no restart — resolveWorkerCap re-reads max_workers per tick). ALSO FIXED a real bug found via TDD: construction start --max-workers was HONORED on fresh-create but SILENTLY IGNORED on RESUME (StartOrResume re-persisted minSupply/goodOverrides but not maxWorkers) — THAT is why the live gate pipeline showed 'worker cap 1' despite --max-workers 10 (it was a resume). Fixed (resume persists explicit max_workers, guarded so unset never clobbers a live-tuned cap). EFFECT-POINT VALIDATED LIVE: post-deploy the gate pipeline resumed at 'worker cap 10' (was 1), fanning out 8 concurrent lots; gate FAB_MATS ripped 1020->1265+ (was creeping at 86/hr under the removed pace). 11 RED-first tests, -race green. title: Construction drain defers FAB_MATS as 'unsourceable' despite an ABUNDANT export source — gate stuck 864/1600, no CLI knob recovers it
description:
OBSERVED 2026-07-21 (era torwind-2026-07-19, player 4, gate X1-UM5-I56). Gate FAB_MATS FROZEN at 864/1600 (54%); circuitry+stabilizers complete.

SYMPTOM: every construction-drain tick logs 'Deferred unsourceable construction material FAB_MATS for resupply' and 'Factory already has ABUNDANT supply of FAB_MATS - skipping input production', and ALL supply runs END drained=false with NO 'Supplied N FAB_MATS' (zero delivery). Runs start+end in the same second (instant abort, no haul).

CONTRADICTION: FAB_MATS IS abundantly sourceable — market get X1-UM5-F46 shows FAB_MATS SUPPLY=ABUNDANT, GROWING, volume 43, ask (sell price) 1087. Its inputs are MODERATE+. So the export exists, is abundant, and is affordable.

EARLIER IN SESSION IT WORKED: right after a --depth 3 start the SAME pipeline logged 'Purchased fabricated output: 43 units of FAB_MATS' x2 and delivered +86 (778->864). Then it shifted into permanent 'unsourceable' and never recovered.

CLI LEVERS EXHAUSTED (none recover it): --depth 0 AND --depth 3; --max-workers 5..12; construction override strategy=prefer-buy; min-supply=SCARCE; price-ceiling-mult=3.0 (set live + verified re-read via discovery pass — still unsourceable, so it is NOT the buy-ceiling); 6+ stop+start runbook restarts; capacity_reconciler AND worker_rebalancer both container-stopped.

HYPOTHESES (for triage): (a) the PHASE-2 ProduceGood/source path mis-evaluates 'sourceable' for a buy-final (depth-3) good when the source is ABUNDANT (supply-state or reservation check inverted?); (b) contention accounting — with N idle haulers the drain fans out N lots, and after the source-availability is 'claimed' by the first lots the rest evaluate unsourceable and the whole task defers without any lot completing; (c) stale market-scan gating: the drain's sourceability check may require a fresh ship-scan of F46 that isn't happening, so it can't 'see' the abundant supply the market cache shows.

IMPACT: gate cannot complete — the final ~736 FAB_MATS won't source. This is the SECOND gate-blocking construction-drain bug this era (after sp-9f24o timeout + sp-1jpiw restart-wedge). Blocks era Phase-2.

VERIFY-FIXED: on gate X1-UM5-I56 with F46 FAB_MATS ABUNDANT, observe >=1 'Purchased ... FAB_MATS' + 'Supplied N FAB_MATS' + gate count climbing past 864. Repro: run a depth-3 fill against an abundant single-source export with an idle-hauler pool > the source's per-cycle volume. Related: sp-9f24o, sp-1jpiw, sp-3idiw, sp-vh1s.
notes:
SHIPWRIGHT VERIFIED (2026-07-21): hypothesis (b) CONFIRMED in code. planDispatchLots (run_construction_coordinator.go:454-531) sets lotCeiling=len(idleShips) (:490), capped only by remaining-bill/hull-load (totalLotDemand :491) — NEVER by the SOURCE's per-cycle volume. FAB_MATS remaining 736 → ~10 lots, all sourcing F46 (single export, vol 43). Availability is NOT shared across concurrently-planned lots → they over-subscribe F46 → unsourceable → the WHOLE material defers (deferTask :1316/1336) → zero delivered. Confirmed by the pool-size correlation (5 delivers / 13 deadlocks; worked then flipped exactly when the idle pool grew 5→13) — rules out (a) supply-state-invert and (c) stale-scan. HOT: dispatching opus fix. Interim (captain fleet-ops): shrink the construction-claimed idle pool to ~5 to match F46 volume — RECOMMEND re-dedicating ~8 hulls to another fleet (non-destructive) over selling.
REFINED DIAGNOSIS 2026-07-21 (CORRECTS the 'unsourceable / zero-delivery' framing above — it is neither).

ROOT CAUSE = the sp-vh1s PACE GUARD, not a sourceability failure. Direct observation during a live watch: the drain DID deliver +30 FAB_MATS via TORWIND-E (gate 864 -> 894). The raw coordinator log for every 'skipped' lot reads:

  "Pacing gate output-buy of FAB_MATS at X1-UM5-F46 - trailing-hour throughput budget (k×tv=86) reached; skipping this lot so the factory keeps producing (sp-vh1s)"

So FAB_MATS is being THROTTLED to ~k×tv=86 units/trailing-hour and delivered in tiny bursts, NOT deadlocked. The 'Deferred unsourceable construction material FAB_MATS' line is misleading dressing on the pace-skip; there is no true sourcing failure. This is exactly why NO CLI lever helped: depth / max-workers / price-ceiling-mult / min-supply / strategy do not touch a throughput budget, and there is no override flag for the pace.

WHY IT'S WRONG HERE: the pace exists to avoid out-buying the factory's production ("so the factory keeps producing").
