title: Construction drain runs deep-tier supply as ONE monolithic 30-min hull task — deep goods (FAB_MATS) NEVER complete a run (0 deliveries) while shallow goods succeed; gate cannot fill
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-07-20 (era torwind-2026-07-19, player 4, gate X1-UM5-I56, pipeline 6eeef4f6 @ depth 3, prefer-buy override active). Gate stuck: FAB_MATS 300/1600 for 25+ min, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 400/400 COMPLETE.

HARD EVIDENCE (construction_coordinator log, 600 lines):
  - 'END supply of FAB_MATS ... drained=true'  => count = 0  (FAB_MATS NEVER delivered a single run)
  - 'END supply of ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY ... drained=true' => count = 2 (shallow good delivers fine)

ROOT CAUSE — monolithic supply run + fixed per-run timeout that deep chains can't meet:
Each 'Construction drain: START supply of <good> via <hull> -> gate (timeout 30m0s)' assigns ONE hull a SINGLE task that must complete the ENTIRE supply op within 30 min. For a shallow good (ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY = buy finished from D41 export, haul to gate) that finishes fast. For a DEEP-TIER good it cannot:
  FAB_MATS chain = fabricate IRON (buy IRON_ORE @ J59 -> deliver to H52 iron factory -> buy IRON) + buy QUARTZ_SAND -> deliver both to F46 (FAB_MATS export factory) -> await F46 production -> buy FAB_MATS -> haul to gate. All input markets SCARCE + geographically spread (D/F/H/I/J clusters).
Timeline proving the miss: 20:27:27 'START supply of FAB_MATS ... timeout 30m0s' + 'Starting fabrication of FAB_MATS (requires 2 inputs)' + 'Starting fabrication of IRON (requires 1 inputs)'. At 20:51:52 (24 MIN LATER) it had only just 'Purchased fabricated output: 25 units of IRON'; 20:52:12 'Found factory for FAB_MATS at F46' — still had NOT bought FAB_MATS, let alone delivered. It will hit the 30m wall (~20:57) and ABANDON before the first delivery, then retry from scratch next tick. Perpetual churn, ZERO throughput.

SECONDARY DEFECTS observed in the same abandon path (on tick cancel/restart):
  - 'Could not persist failed construction task <id>: failed to update task: context canceled'  (partial progress NOT persisted -> retry restarts the whole chain instead of resuming)
  - 'Could not release hauler <hull> after construction tick: failed to query ship: context canceled' (hull-release also fails on cancel)

IMPACT: any gate whose bill-of-materials includes a deep-tier good sourced from a scarce/spread supply chain can NEVER complete — the deep good is starved to 0 delivery while shallow goods finish. This is map-agnostic (triggers whenever one run's full deep chain > 30 min).

FIX (any of, in preference order):
  1. DECOMPOSE deep-chain supply into independent, separately-timed sub-tasks: 'fabricate/replenish input IRON', 'deliver inputs to factory F46', 'buy+deliver finished FAB_MATS' — each completes and PERSISTS on its own, so no single task must span the whole chain. (This is the sp-vh1s per-node model — strong evidence to prioritize it.)
  2. SCALE the per-run timeout by chain depth / #sub-inputs / input scarcity (a depth-3 scarce chain needs far more than a buy-and-haul's 30m). Cheapest interim mitigation.
  3. PERSIST partial progress across abandons (fix the 'Could not persist failed construction task ... context canceled' path) so retries resume rather than restart, and inputs already delivered to the factory count.

VERIFY-FIXED: on a gate with a deep-tier good, observe >=1 'END supply of <deep good> ... drained=true' and the gate material count incrementing.

Related: sp-vh1s (unified gate-fill / per-node gates — the full fix; #1 above is its core), sp-b27a2 (feedstock mis-route — distinct, routing now correct), sp-1jpiw (pipeline restart-recovery).

title: Depth-0 construction fabrication strands feedstock at the WRONG factory: IRON_ORE parked at circuitry factory/gate, never routed to the IRON_ORE importer — FAB_MATS chain stalls, feedstock can't even be dumped
description:
OBSERVED 2026-07-20 (era torwind-2026-07-19, player 4, gate X1-UM5-I56, pipeline dd37c2e1 @ --depth 0). FAB_MATS froze at 300/1600 after an early burst (120->300 via buying F46 export) while ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY kept flowing.

ROOT CAUSE — feedstock mis-routing in the deep FAB_MATS chain:
System topology (market find): FAB_MATS chain = IRON_ORE -> H52 (the ONLY IRON_ORE importer = iron factory) -> IRON -> F46 (FAB_MATS export factory, imports QUARTZ_SAND) -> gate. Circuitry chain = COPPER/SILICON -> D41 (ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY export) -> gate.

The coordinator sourced IRON_ORE for FAB_MATS but PARKED the IRON_ORE-laden haulers at D41 (the CIRCUITRY factory) and at the gate I56 — NEITHER imports IRON_ORE. Not one hauler was routed to H52 (the correct importer). Result: haulers clog at 80/80 with un-deliverable IRON_ORE, FAB_MATS fabrication stalls.

SMOKING GUN (repeated 19:32/19:48/19:49/19:50): '[WARN] Could not unload IRON_ORE to free cargo space — market may not import it'. Note 'to free cargo space' — the coordinator has ABANDONED the IRON_ORE as feedstock and is trying to DUMP it as junk, but can't (D41 doesn't import it). So the deep-chain feedstock is both mis-routed AND un-sheddable.

Material-flow tally (200 log lines): 24x 'supply of ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY', 0x FAB_MATS; 8x drained=false vs 1x drained=true (deliveries mostly failing); 7x 'Deferred unsourceable ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY'. Circuitry is BOUGHT from D41 at ~4300/unit (86320cr/20u) — expensive, but flows; FAB_MATS deep-fab is dead.

IMPACT: gate cannot complete — FAB_MATS is ~1300 of the remaining units and its fabrication path is broken. Requires manual intervention (stop pipeline, clear stranded feedstock, restart at shallower depth) — no self-heal.

ASK: the fabrication coordinator must (a) route each intermediate/feedstock to a market that IMPORTS it (validate import-capability before dispatch; IRON_ORE -> H52, not D41), and (b) never strand feedstock it can't unload at the dispatched waypoint. This is the deep multi-tier management that sp-vh1s (unified gate-fill, per-node supply/price gates) was written to fix — strong evidence for prioritizing it. Related: sp-1jpiw (restart-recovery), sp-vh1s.

title: Construction coordinator: warehouse-first sourcing — withdraw gate materials from an in-system depot warehouse before buying at source (no double-buy; mirror contract InventorySourceFinder)
description:
ADMIRAL-DIRECTED (goal "make gate depots work — seamless, both operations", 2026-07-20). FOUNDATIONAL half of the gate-depot feature (paired with sp-3idiw). Land FIRST — it is the "one controller per resource" enforcement that makes a gate depot arm-safe (no double-buy).

## WHY (design settled by the sp-3idiw escalation, shipwright-verified)
A gate depot only adds value if its stockers pre-buy gate materials into an in-system warehouse near the gate AND the construction coordinator WITHDRAWS from that warehouse instead of buying at source. Today construction is BUY-ONLY: construction_pipeline_planner.go:524 planMaterial → marketLocator.FindConstructionSource (market buy); run_construction_coordinator.go supplyTask → ProduceGood + DeliverToConstructionSite. NO inventory/warehouse-first path (VERIFIED: grep of the pipeline planner + coordinator shows only FindConstructionSource; no Inventory/withdraw/warehouse). If a depot stocker pre-buys while construction still buys-at-source → TWO buyers on one market + TWO haulers to the gate = RULINGS #4 double-buy + one-controller-per-resource violation. So construction MUST learn warehouse-first sourcing BEFORE the reconciler emits gate-depot demand.

## PROVEN PATTERN TO MIRROR (the contract path already does exactly this)
internal/application/contract/inventory_source.go: SourcingSource "INVENTORY" (:27) "sources the good from an in-system warehouse at zero cost" (:22); InventorySourceFinder (:62) locates in-system warehouse inventory; used in run_fleet_coordinator_depot_routing.go (~:139-141). Mirror this for construction sourcing.

## FIX (construction-side ONLY; additive; arm-safe alone = byte-identical with no warehouse)
In construction sourcing (constructionSourcingNode ~run_construction_coordinator.go:872 / planMaterial construction_pipeline_planner.go:509-543): BEFORE buying at source (FindConstructionSource), check for the material in an in-system depot warehouse and WITHDRAW from it (zero-cost inventory source), mirroring the contract InventorySourceFinder/SourceInventory. Only fall through to the market buy for the residual not covered by warehouse inventory. NO warehouse present → falls through exactly as today (BYTE-IDENTICAL — this is what makes it safe to land + deploy before the reconciler half).

## HARD REQUIREMENTS
- NO DOUBLE-BUY (RULINGS #4): warehouse-first means the construction buy is only ever the residual after warehouse withdrawal; a stocker filling the warehouse + construction withdrawing it = ONE buyer (the stocker), ONE haul lane. Fail-closed: warehouse read fails → treat as no inventory → buy as today (never skip a needed material).
- ONE CONTROLLER PER RESOURCE: construction withdraws (consumes) from the warehouse; it does not also buy the same units. The stocker is the sole buyer→warehouse for buffered gate materials.
- RESTART-SAFE (RULINGS #2): warehouse inventory + withdrawal state survive restart (warehouses already persist).
- SINGLE-WRITER (RULINGS #3): all ship moves/withdrawals via the daemon.
- BYTE-IDENTICAL with no depot warehouse present (the arm-safety property — verify with a test).

## ACCEPTANCE (RED-first)
- Construction material available in an in-system depot warehouse → construction WITHDRAWS it (zero-cost inventory source), does NOT buy it at market. (RED: today always buys.)
- Partial coverage → withdraw what's in the warehouse, buy ONLY the residual. No double-buy of the covered units.
- NO warehouse for that material → construction buys at source exactly as today (BYTE-IDENTICAL — prove with a test).
- Warehouse read error → fail-closed to market buy (never starve the gate).
- Restart mid-fill → withdrawal/inventory state consistent.

## CONSTRAINTS
RULINGS #2/#3/#4, #12/#13 (commit --no-verify + captain-gate only; verify SHA), ENGINEERING §6 (short WHY-only comments; no bead-ids/changelog prose). Protected paths untouched. Mirror the contract inventory_source.go pattern; do NOT invent a parallel one if it can be shared/generalized.

## RELATIONSHIP
BLOCKS sp-3idiw (reconciler gate-depot demand + fleet-scaling) — that half is NOT arm-safe until this lands. Ship CODE + tests; deploy/arm is the shipwright's. Deploys byte-identical (safe to batch anytime). Economy-analyst consult (non-blocking): which gate materials the depot buffers (withdraw) vs. which stay direct-pipeline (fabricated/scarce).

title: Reconciler must serve GATE-CONSTRUCTION depots (blind to gate haul demand today) + auto-scale depot topology to fleet size — seamless, both operations
description:
ADMIRAL-DIRECTED (in-chat 2026-07-20, goal "make this work — gate construction is where we most need depots to make money; seamless; auto-scale to fleet size; support BOTH operations"). This is the in-chat Tier-3 approval (RULINGS #20 — Admiral present + directing).

## THE OUTCOME BUG (Admiral-identified, shipwright-confirmed in code)
The capacity reconciler builds contract-delivery depots but is BLIND to gate-construction haul demand — the single biggest haul of Phase 1. During the gate fill it ranks 0 gate hubs → desires 0 depots → the highest-value hauling runs UNCOMPRESSED. "Depots are Phase-2" was a WRONG framing (rubber-stamping a broken outcome). Depots serving the gate fill is exactly PLAYBOOK §4's fill model.

## CONFIRMED FACTS (recon)
1. Reconciler demand = contract-history ONLY: internal/adapters/capacity/sensor.go:155 `demand := s.senseDemand(contracts, now)`; sense_demand.go aggregates the `contracts` table. Gate demand never enters. Sense() (sensor.go:144) is where a 2nd demand source plugs in.
2. Gate shortfall IS a queryable signal: internal/domain/manufacturing/construction_site.go `UnfulfilledMaterials()` / `remaining` per material (construction_material_target.go: tradeSymbol/targetQuantity, e.g. FAB_MATS 1600, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 400). Gate site symbol available from the construction site repo (live gate = X1-UM5-I56).
3. Downstream machinery DONE + deployed (main 2a5f80ff): rank hubs → size depot → REUSE idle hulls (sp-pa5wq) → LAUNCH depot coordinators (sp-rt3b6) → warehouse ORBITS + fails-loud (sp-f0u0e) → real cap (sp-rt3b6). A gate hub flows through ALL of it.
4. Construction pipeline (internal/application/manufacturing/{commands/run_construction_coordinator.go, services/construction_pipeline_planner.go}) buys-at-source, hauls DIRECT to the gate. NO warehouse/buffer/depot awareness today.
5. Cap/topology NOT fleet-scaled — fixed ceiling (fleet_ceiling_contract_delivery, derived). Admiral wants fleet-proportional.

## DESIGN-FIRST (settle BEFORE implementing; ESCALATE if it spans beyond the depot side)
THE cooperation question: a gate depot must COMPRESS the gate supply chain (stockers source→warehouse-near-gate; delivery hulls warehouse→gate short hops), NOT double-haul against the construction pipeline's direct source→gate haul. Options to evaluate + pick with rationale:
 (a) Depot INTERPOSES: stockers fill the warehouse; the construction pipeline's delivery leg pulls from the warehouse instead of sourcing direct (pipeline change — bigger).
 (b) Depot AUGMENTS: depot delivery hulls deliver to the gate in parallel; construction pipeline sees materials arrive + backs off its own haul (needs a hand-off/no-double-buy guard).
 (c) Other. Whichever: NO double-buy, NO two coordinators hauling the same material to the same place (RULINGS: one controller per resource). If the chosen model needs construction-pipeline changes beyond the depot/reconciler, STOP + report the design (do not half-build) — this may then decompose into a paired construction-side bead.

## IMPLEMENT (if bounded to the depot/reconciler side)
1. GATE-CONSTRUCTION DEMAND SOURCE: read the gate's UnfulfilledMaterials → a demand hub at the gate waypoint, fed into Sense() alongside contract demand. Rank/value model: gate demand ∝ remaining-unfulfilled-units × source-haul-distance (the compression value), so it ranks HIGH during active fill and → 0 when remaining → 0 (gate complete → depot dissolves, hulls return). Contract-isolated value math stays; gate value is its own term. It must serve BOTH: contract hubs AND the gate, same reconciler.
2. FLEET-SCALED SIZING: desired topology + cap sized as f(fleet size) — small fleet → small/no depot; larger fleet → scale up. Replace/augment the fixed ceiling with a fleet-proportional bound (keep an absolute backstop). Reuse-before-buy (sp-pa5wq) + launch (sp-rt3b6) already staff/launch it from the fleet.
3. SEAMLESS: no manual step, no phase-gate. Armed, it auto-builds a fleet-sized gate depot during the fill and dissolves it after.

## SAFETY / RULINGS
#2 restart-safe (depot + demand state survive restart); #3 daemon single-writer (launch/haul via daemon); #4 money guards fail closed, none weakened, NO double-buy; #7 ownership (only idle; never frigate/pinned/active); #14 (contract legs single-system — the GATE depot is intra-system X1-UM5, fine; keep it so); #12/#13 (commit --no-verify + captain-gate only; verify SHA); ENGINEERING §6 (short WHY-only comments). Protected paths untouched.

## ACCEPTANCE (RED-first)
- Reconciler with an active gate site + unfulfilled materials DESIRES a gate depot hub (warehouse at/near gate + stockers + delivery), sized to fleet. (RED: today desires 0.)
- Gate depot staffed from idle/reuse + LAUNCHED (containers spawn, warehouse orbits) — NO double-buy vs the construction pipeline (the cooperation guard holds).
- Gate complete (remaining → 0) → gate demand → 0 → depot dissolves, hulls freed.
- Fleet-scaled: small fleet → ≤ its share; large fleet → scales up; absolute backstop holds.
- BOTH ops: contract hubs still served alongside the gate.
- OFF/unarmed path byte-identical; other domains unchanged.

## DEPLOY / ARM
Ship CODE + tests (arming/deploy is the shipwright's). Live daemon = 2a5f80ff (trade-blind + reuse + launch + cap ARMED; watchkeeper DOWN by Admiral order). Deploy batches on a daemon restart; validate on live output (gate depot builds, warehouse orbits + stocks, gate climb rate improves, NO double-buy).

## RELATIONSHIP
Builds on sp-pa5wq (reuse) + sp-rt3b6 (launch+cap) + sp-f0u0e (warehouse orbit). Supersedes the "depots are Phase-2, hold off" framing (economy-analyst st-wisp-m54zw was CONTRACT-depot-across-many-hubs; a SINGLE gate depot during the fill is a different, high-value case). Advances sp-bu6ma (reconciler = single hub authority). Economy-analyst consult candidate: the gate-demand VALUE model + fleet-scaling curve (non-blocking; watchkeeper down).
notes:
=== DESIGN + ESCALATION (build-agent recon 2026-07-20; worktree sp-3idiw was READ-ONLY, no code committed, worktree removed) ===

VERDICT: ESCALATE. Genuinely a 2-subsystem change. The only clean cooperation model (INTERPOSE) needs
construction-pipeline changes beyond the depot/reconciler side, AND the reconciler half cannot be safely
ARMED alone (it would double-buy). Do-not-half-build gate tripped (RULINGS #4; "closed is not armed").

CHOSEN COOPERATION MODEL: (a) INTERPOSE.
Rationale: the only model that satisfies "one controller per resource" with NO double-buy. The depot stockers
become the SOLE buyer->warehouse for the gate materials the depot buffers; the construction coordinator
WITHDRAWS those from the in-system warehouse instead of buying at source (mirrors the contract path's proven
inventory-first sourcing). Fabricated / non-buffered materials stay 100% on the construction pipeline's direct
source-or-factory->gate path (partition by what the depot buffers).
- Option (b) AUGMENT rejected: still needs the construction pipeline to "back off" (construction-side) AND a
  warehouse->gate delivery capability the depot side does NOT have.
- Option (c) bounded-to-reconciler: none exists (evidence below).

WHY NO MODEL IS BOUNDED TO THE RECONCILER (file:line evidence):
1. Construction owns the gate haul end-to-end (buy-at-source -> direct-to-gate), NO warehouse awareness:
   run_construction_coordinator.go supplyTask (~L615-755) -> producer.ProduceGood (buy/fabricate) +
   DeliverToConstructionSite; constructionSourcingNode (~L872-900) builds a BUY or FABRICATE node, never a
   warehouse withdrawal. construction_pipeline_planner.go planMaterial (L509-543) buys at FindConstructionSource
   -> DELIVER_TO_CONSTRUCTION(sourceMarket, site).
2. Construction sourcing has NO inventory-first path (unlike the contract path): no InventorySourceFinder /
   SourceInventory anywhere in production_executor.go / production_strategy.go / input_source_selector.go.
   (Contract path DOES: run_fleet_coordinator_depot_routing.go L28-33,139-141 — PlanSourcing/InventorySourceFinder
   prefers the in-system warehouse over market.) storage_source_finder.go is GAS-storage integration, not construction.
3. Depot has NO warehouse->gate delivery path. depot.DeliveryHullFleet ("depot-delivery", delivery.go:14) is
   dispatched ONLY via routeContractViaDepot (run_fleet_coordinator_depot_routing.go L68-106), keyed on a
   CONTRACT's delivery geometry (contract.Terms().Deliveries), withdrawing from a warehouse and delivering to a
   CONTRACT destination. No construction-site trigger exists. DeliverToConstructionSite lives in the construction
   subsystem. The reconciler architecture forbids reinventing buy/move (domain/capacity/ports.go Actuator doc L46-49).
4. Arming the reconciler half ALONE = double-buy: stockers pre-buy material X->warehouse while the construction
   coordinator still buys X at source -> two buyers on the same source market + two haulers to the gate ->
   RULINGS #4 (no double-buy) + "one controller per resource" violated; and the warehouse fills with nothing
   moving it to the gate.

WHAT IS BOUNDED TO THE RECONCILER (the reconciler half — feasible, but NOT arm-safe alone):
- Gate demand source: a NEW sensor collaborator (e.g. GateShortfallReader) — a live-API boundary like sensor.go
  TreasuryReader (L28-30), because the construction site's required/fulfilled is API-ONLY
  (adapters/api/construction_site_repository.go GetConstruction) and NOT in the daemon DB the DB-only sensor reads.
  Reads gate UnfulfilledMaterials (construction_site.go:69) -> a HubDemand{HubSymbol: gate wp, GoodMix from
  remaining materials} fed into Sense() (sensor.go:144-155) alongside senseDemand. Flows unchanged through
  HeuristicPlanner -> DesiredHub.
- Value model: shape the gate GoodDemand so value ~ remaining-units x source-haul-distance. Fits the existing
  value-density scorer (heuristic_planner.go scoreBufferGood L567: freq x (0.030*dist + 0.147*avg_units) / avg_units,
  which REWARDS distance) + hub coverage score (L211: freq x cycle_penalty x payment). remaining->0 => demand->0
  => depot dissolves via the existing shrink path.
- Stocker is good-generic (run_stocker_coordinator.go — "a dedicated hull that fills a home warehouse" with ranked
  goods) => reusable to pre-stage gate materials.
- Fleet-scaled sizing/cap: replace the fixed Calibration.ContractDeliveryHullCeiling (governor.go L67-80, currently
  tied to the autosizer's fleet_ceiling_contract_delivery) with an f(fleet size) bound + absolute backstop, applied
  in coverageWalk.exceedsCeiling (heuristic_planner.go L356).
- OPEN reconciler-design item: the ComputeDesired hauler-first early return (heuristic_planner.go:154 —
  ContractHaulerCount < 2 => desires NOTHING) currently suppresses the gate depot too; a gate depot probably should
  not be gated by the CONTRACT op's hauler count.

PROPOSED DECOMPOSITION (ordering: construction-side FIRST):
- NEW BEAD (construction-side, FOUNDATIONAL, land first): "Construction coordinator withdraws gate materials from
  an in-system depot warehouse before buying at source (warehouse-first construction sourcing + no-double-buy)."
  Add an inventory-first check to the construction supply path (constructionSourcingNode/ProduceGood) mirroring the
  contract InventorySourceFinder: if an in-system depot warehouse holds the material, WITHDRAW (short hop) instead of
  buying at source. Additive + arm-safe alone (no warehouse => buys as today, byte-identical). This is the
  "one controller per resource" enforcement: depot = sole buyer of buffered gate materials; construction = the
  warehouse->gate delivery leg for them. Guard: a withdrawal is not a buy, so the material is bought ONCE.
- THIS BEAD (sp-3idiw, reconciler-side): the bounded reconciler half above (gate-shortfall demand source +
  fleet-scaled ceiling). DEPENDS on the construction-side bead for arm-safety (no double-buy). Default-off; armed
  only after the construction-side bead lands.

OPEN QUESTIONS (economy-analyst-owned; non-blocking, watchkeeper down):
- The exact gate-demand VALUE curve (synthetic frequency + payment for a one-shot gate fill so it ranks correctly
  vs recurring contract hubs WITHOUT starving them) and the FLEET-SCALING curve (depot hull share as f(fleet size)
  + absolute backstop).
- Partition policy: which gate materials the depot buffers (buyable-direct only?) vs. left on the construction
  pipeline (fabricated / SCARCE-source).
- Whether the hauler-first early return should be bypassed for gate demand.
BLOCKED-BY sp-crjla (construction warehouse-first sourcing). The sp-3idiw lane ESCALATED: a reconciler-only gate-depot = RULINGS #4 double-buy (stocker pre-buys + construction still buys-at-source). title: Construction pipeline wedges after a container recycle: returns EXECUTING but 0 tasks promote; 'construction start' resume can't repair it — only stop+fresh-start works
description:

SYMPTOM: after the 13:32 container recycle (see sp-e6jg9), construction pipeline f1400144 came back Status=EXECUTING but was WEDGED:
  - construction_coordinator ran every 60s but logged ONLY 'Construction drain: activation done (0 task(s) promoted to READY)' for HOURS — promoted nothing.

  - Gate materials frozen byte-identical for hours (FAB_MATS 120/1600, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 140/400; pipeline internal 5.4% -> 5.4%).

KEY FINDING: 'spacetraders construction start X1-UM5-I56' on the existing pipeline REPORTS 'Resumed existing pipeline' but does NOT repair the wedged tasks or respawn workers — hulls stayed idle, 0 promoted, no delivery. Restart-recovery must either (a) fully re-hydrate the pipeline's tasks + respawn workers on adoption, or (b) detect the wedged state and auto-rebuild. Today a human must notice + manually stop/fresh-start. This is the same stall signature that motivated sp-vh1s (unified gate-fill) — likely fixed by that redesign, but the restart-recovery gap should be tracked/fixed regardless. MITIGATION at deploy: verify construction survives; if wedged, re-fresh (stop + start --depth 0) or hand the captain that runbook. Gated + deployed a7206b58 (two commits). Restart-interrupted supply tasks now re-queue PENDING with the retry budget untouched, instead of being driven terminal FAILED.

ROOT CAUSE was NOT where I briefed it. I pointed at the abandon branch's inert 'return false'; StartExecution() is never persisted so the row was still READY and re-promotable. The killer was the ORPHANED CHILD GOROUTINE: supplyTaskBounded returns on taskCtx.Done() but supplyTask keeps running, hits 'context canceled', falls into failTask — which persists FAILED through a DETACHED ctx engineered to survive that very cancellation. title: e2e depot launch: reconciler must LAUNCH depot coordinators on the reuse path (mirror the buy path's StartWarehouse dispatch) — complete-hub-first, idempotent, reuse counts toward the 12 cap
description:
ADMIRAL-DIRECTED (2026-07-20). Completes the auto-scale contract-depot loop. Today: reconciler senses→desires→reuses idle haulers into depot roles (sp-pa5wq) + emits capital demand→autosizer buys (capped 12). GAP: the reconciler's tier-1 reassign only RE-TAGS the dedication — nothing LAUNCHES the depot coordinator, so reused hulls sit dedicated-but-IDLE (never orbit/operate). The BUY path already auto-launches (autosizer's StartWarehouse dispatch bridge); the REUSE path does not. FIX: give the reuse path the same launch dispatch.

## ARCHITECTURE (confirmed by the shipwright)
- depot LAUNCH: `depot start <name> <spec>` (sp-38xc, internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_depot_lifecycle.go) is the live-activation that starts a depot's warehouse/stocker/delivery coordinators. Depots persist restart-safe (container_ops_depot.go:194 reload-on-restart registry).
- StartWarehouse RPC: internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_warehouse.go (persistAndRunWarehouse) builds the recovery-visible warehouse container.
- BUY→launch is WIRED: the fleet autosizer dispatches StartWarehouse on a warehouse-class buy (internal/adapters/grpc/fleet_autosizer_warehouse_ports.go, SetWarehouseProvider = "the StartWarehouse dispatch bridge").
- REUSE→launch is NOT wired: the reconciler actuator (internal/application/capacity/commands/run_capacity_reconciler_coordinator.go, VerbReassignHull→TierReuseIdle :468) reassigns the dedication only. Live proof post-deploy: TORWIND-7/A/B dedicated 'warehouse', F 'stocker' — all IDLE, no warehouse container spawned.

## FIX — wire the reuse/reassign path to LAUNCH the depot coordinators
When the reconciler reassigns (tier-1 reuse) an idle hull into a warehouse/stocker/delivery role for a desired hub, it must ALSO dispatch the depot-coordinator launch for that hub/hull — the same StartWarehouse/depot-start dispatch the autosizer's buy path uses. Reuse the EXISTING launch seam (the autosizer's StartWarehouse dispatch bridge and/or the sp-38xc depot lifecycle); do NOT build a parallel launcher.

## VERIFY-FIRST (escalate if wrong, like the sp-a9bhc lane did — bank findings + report BEFORE a large build)
(a) Does a reused-into-depot hull COUNT toward fleet_ceiling_contract_delivery (=12)? (the sp-pa5wq lane flagged this open.) (b) Does the ladder drain the idle pool COMPLETE-HUB-FIRST (top-ranked hub fully staffed before hub #2)? If either is false, the design changes — report before building.

## HARD REQUIREMENTS / SAFETY
1. COMPLETE-HUB-FIRST: launch a hub's depot only when FULLY staffed (warehouse+stocker+delivery). Never scatter limited hulls into partial, non-functional depots across many hubs. (Pacing the desire is NOT needed — the 12 cap + idle-bounded reuse + ranked draining bound it; this ordering is the property that matters.)
2. REUSE COUNTS TOWARD THE CAP: total depot capacity = reuse + buy <= fleet_ceiling_contract_delivery (12), NOT reuse + a fresh 12. Fix if reuse currently bypasses the class ceiling.
3. IDEMPOTENT: never relaunch an already-running depot; a re-converge tick or an already-serving hull is a no-op.
4. RESTART-SAFE (RULINGS #2): depots persist (sp-38xc registry); on daemon restart the reconciler re-converges WITHOUT double-launching; reload adopts running depots.
5. MONEY-SAFE (RULINGS #4): depot buys still go through the guarded autosizer path; the launch actuation spends nothing beyond guards; no guard weakened.
6. OWNERSHIP (RULINGS #7): only genuinely idle hulls; never the command frigate / pinned / actively-working.

## ACCEPTANCE (RED-first)
- Idle haulers reused into a hub's depot roles → the reconciler LAUNCHES the coordinators (warehouse/stocker/delivery containers spawn) and the hulls ORBIT/operate (not idle-dedicated). (Currently: reassigned, no container, idle.)
- Complete-hub-first: hulls enough for only 1 full hub → exactly 1 fully-staffed depot launches; NO partial depot at hub #2.
- Idempotent: a second tick over the same state launches NOTHING new.
- Restart-safe: after a daemon restart, existing depots reload + are NOT double-launched.
- Cap: reuse + buy total <= 12.
- Regression: non-contract domains unchanged; trade_blind-OFF path byte-identical.

## CONSTRAINTS
RULINGS #2/#4/#7, #12/#13 (commit --no-verify + captain-gate only; verify merged SHA), ENGINEERING §6 (short WHY-only comments). Protected paths untouched (internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**). Ship CODE + tests only — arming/deploy is the shipwright's.

## RELATIONSHIP
Completes the e2e auto-scale contract-depot loop (sense→desire→reuse[sp-pa5wq]→LAUNCH[this]→converge; warehouse orbit sp-f0u0e; reuse-before-buy sp-pa5wq; cap 12; guard a28846fa). Advances/overlaps sp-bu6ma (reconciler = single hub authority) — SAME reconciler files; serialize if sp-bu6ma later runs. Interim (ops, no code): captain `contract depot start` J59.
notes:
FORK RESOLVED (Admiral goal 'make this work', 2026-07-20): BUILD launch wiring + option (A) cap-the-planner. The prior lane verify-first-escalated: (b) complete-hub-first = TRUE; (a) FALSE — the ContractDeliveryDemandBridge hardcodes Current=0 (contract_delivery_bridge.go, VERIFIED) so the autosizer's fleet_ceiling_contract_delivery=12 NEVER binds (class always 0/12; real bound = fleet_ceiling_total 150). Also: reuse path persists NO depot, senseTopology reads persisted depot rows → hub stays uncovered → gap never closes → latent unbounded buy toward 150 (masked now by the rate-guard block). FIX = (1) LAUNCH wiring via the sp-38xc depot lifecycle StartDepot (persist depot + launch coordinators idempotently), optional-injection launcher port on the reconciler handler (nil=byte-identical, mirror SetContractGraduationReader), driven after converge, !dryRun; complete-hub-first from executed reassigns; idempotent (covered-hub→0 reassigns; startDepot idle-gate); restart-safe (reloadDepotRegistryAtBoot re-adopts). title: Reconciler must REUSE idle contract-dedicated haulers into depot roles (tier-1) before emitting capital-BUY demand — reuse-before-buy
description:
ADMIRAL-DIRECTED (2026-07-20). With the trade-blind arm LIVE, the reconciler desires ~62 hull-roles (16 hubs: warehouse/stocker/delivery) and emits the FULL gap as tier-4 CAPITAL-BUY demand — even though we have IDLE contract haulers that should fill those depot roles. Buying when idle capacity exists is wrong (Admiral). FIX: the reconciler reuse tier must REPOSITION idle contract-dedicated haulers into depot roles FIRST; only the residual (desired − current − reusable-idle) may emit as capital-buy demand.

## ROOT (why it buys instead of reusing)
Idle contract haulers are tagged dedicated_fleet='contract'. The reconciler reuse pool EXCLUDES them (per the sp-iwra3 lane: a reuse-eligibility filter in internal/adapters/capacity + the ladder's `reusable` guard both drop contract-dedicated idles). So the tier-1 idlePool reads empty → the whole desired-vs-current gap falls through to TierCapital → capex_emitter emits the full 62-hull gap to the autosizer bridge → wants to buy up to the ceiling. NOTE: tier-1 reuse is the reconciler's OWN reassignment (reassign_hull), NOT an autosizer buy — so reuse bypasses the autosizer money/rate guards entirely: staffing depots from idles needs no purchase and is unaffected by the era_payback/realized_rate block currently gating buys.

## RECON (entry points)
- internal/domain/capacity/ladder.go: LadderDiffer.Diff (:92) walks TierReuseIdle(1)→TierRebalance→TierBufferAdjust→TierCapital(4) (:373). idlePool (:408) = tier-1 supply; `reusable` guard (:437, never-poach/never-mispick); tier-1 reuse action minted ~:250; reusableWorkerSurplus (:480).
- internal/adapters/capacity/sense_utilization.go: senseUtilization builds IdleHulls (Idle = container_id empty); isFreeContractHauler (:25)/countContractHaulers (:36) are the hauler-TIER count (separate). Find the reuse-eligibility filter (the sp-iwra3 lane cited a reuseEligibleIdleHulls in sensor.go) that drops contract-dedicated idles.
- internal/domain/capacity/action.go: Tier enum (TierReuseIdle=1 … TierCapital=4).
- internal/domain/capacity/capex_emitter.go: emits the tier-4 sum → bridge. After the fix, tier-4 = RESIDUAL only.

## FIX
1. Make IDLE contract-dedicated haulers REUSE-ELIGIBLE for depot roles — include dedicated_fleet='contract' idles in the reuse pool (they are the contract op's own hulls; repositioning them within the contract op is not poaching).
2. The tier-1 reuse (reassign_hull) must be able to fill ALL depot roles (warehouse + stocker + delivery), not just delivery-worker — idle haulers staff warehouses/stockers via reposition.
3. REUSE-BEFORE-BUY accounting: the ladder consumes reusable idles into the gap FIRST so TierCapital (capex_emitter) emits only the RESIDUAL (desired − current − reused). Idle capacity covering the desire → capital-buy demand 0.
4. OWNERSHIP (RULINGS #7): never poach a PINNED hull, the COMMAND frigate, or a hull ACTIVELY running an op — only genuinely IDLE (container_id empty) contract haulers. Keep the never-poach/never-mispick `reusable` guards; only widen eligibility to contract-dedicated IDLES.

- Depot desire EXCEEDING idle capacity: reuse consumes all idles; capital-buy demand = residual only (not the full gap).
- Regression: never poaches pinned/command-frigate/actively-working hulls; a truly-empty idle pool still emits capital (unchanged); non-contract domains unchanged.

RULINGS #7 (ownership — never poach pinned/frigate/active), #4 (money guards fail closed), #2 (restart-resilient), #12/#13 (commit --no-verify + captain-gate only; verify SHA), ENGINEERING §6 (short WHY-only comments). Protected paths untouched.

Related to sp-bu6ma (reconciler idle-worker homing) — same "reconciler utilizes idle contract haulers" area (ladder/heuristic_planner); coordinate if both run (SAME files → serialize). Deploy batches with the next daemon restart; validate end-to-end (idle haulers repositioned into depot roles, warehouses orbit via the sp-f0u0e fix, NO buy).

The coordinator never ORBITS/undocks the hull. - Regression: a hull already correctly parked+orbiting issues no spurious nav.

This resolves the 3-way fragmentation.

## TANDEM (the captain's ask, explicit)
ONE brain (reconciler: demand-ranked hubs + workers/depots per hub), ONE executor (the contract-fleet coordinator's `fleet hub` homing). Pairs with sp-10nn (reconciler depot ADD-gate fix) so the SAME reconciler hub ranking drives BOTH depot/warehouse placement AND idle-worker homing. Together = the reconciler owns contract-hub topology end-to-end: hub selection -> workers/depots per hub -> idle-worker distribution.

Concretely: the live 4-at-J59 pile spreads to K83/A1/C38/E43/J59 following the reconciler's ranking, on the next discovery pass. The capacity reconciler never files a contract-depot proposal despite recurring hubs, because its contract-delivery ADD gate benchmarks a new hub against the TRADE-contaminated fleet-wide per-hull average. File: internal/domain/capacity/heuristic_planner.go

FleetPerHullCrHr = incomeVelocityPerHour / hullCount (sense_economics.go:29,58) sums ALL transactions incl. TRADING_REVENUE. Live: arb SELL_CARGO +1.38M/2h => FleetPerHullCrHr ~17-42k/hr/hull, so a contract depot must beat the trade-inflated average => walk stops => 0 proposals. 3. Fail-closed preserved (RULINGS #4): unreadable contract $/hr => no add (never a phantom-positive add).
4. Default-off arming (PLAYBOOK §10): ship byte-identical behind a knob; arming is a separate ledgered step.

## SCOPE
IN: the contract-delivery ADD gate + depot compression-value model. OUT: cross-op contract-vs-trade fleet ALLOCATION — if we ever want it, it belongs in a dedicated layer with real marginal/saturation curves, NEVER a per-hull average. Do not fold trade back in via any average.

- Dead code: the contract-hub coordinator (run_contract_hub_coordinator*.go) is unwired (handler at main.go:802, no ContainerType, nothing sends the command). Wire or delete — redundant with this planner.
- Fragmentation: 3 hub-selection paths disagree (bootstrap selectContractHubs=2, this planner, the dead coordinator). One authority (this planner).

Diagnosis + evidence: this bead's notes. Economics: sp-qqwm. Related engine work: sp-27at (aggressive scaling), sp-cr2v (staging order).

title: CONSULT (economy-analyst): at 1M treasury, scale contract hulls AGGRESSIVELY (2+ now for contract $/hr + idle-arb) vs the capital-constrained 1-hauler staging?
description:
CONSULT (refute-first; ADMIRAL-DIRECTED). Owner: economy-analyst. Asker: captain.

CONTEXT: your earlier sp-u5nh answer prescribed CONSERVATIVE staging (1 cheapest cargo hull first, measure, add only if the source-leg binds). But that was CAPITAL-CONSTRAINED — treasury was ~200-300k and the 25% guard on the cheapest hull was the binding constraint. WE ARE NOW FLUSH; that premise is dead.

LIVE SNAPSHOT (torwind-2026-07-19, player 4): treasury ~1.0M, income/hr ~+90-100k (recovered after the 1st hauler buy). Fleet: 1 LIGHT_HAULER (TORWIND-5, on contract), command frigate (TORWIND-1, purchasing/command role), 3 probes (scouting, sp-7pdo now partitioning them). Phase INCOME. Contract engine is SERIAL (one active contract at a time).

ADMIRAL THESIS (refute or confirm): at 1M capital we are TOO CONSERVATIVE. We could easily buy 2+ hulls NOW to (a) increase contract $/hr AND (b) run idle-arb trading on the idle capacity. The 1-at-a-time, rolling-income-gated pacing is capital-era caution that no longer applies at a flush treasury.

QUESTIONS:
1. Is the conservative 1-hauler staging still correct at ~1M treasury, or should we scale contract hulls AGGRESSIVELY (buy 2-4 now)? Re-derive the optimal contract-hull count for FLUSH capital, not capital-constrained.
2. Contract $/hr is CYCLE-TIME-won on a SERIAL engine (one active contract). What is the MARGINAL contract $/hr per added hull (from source+deliver leg parallelization, hub staging, closest-ship-wins sourcing)? Where does it plateau for CONTRACTS specifically (you cited a ~2-hull single-system arb ceiling for TRADE — does the same hold for contracts, or higher)?
3. IDLE-ARB: the contract-fleet coordinator runs an in-process idle-arb dispatcher on idle contract haulers. How much SECONDARY $/hr can idle contract hulls generate via arbitrage between contract legs? Does idle-arb justify buying hulls BEYOND pure contract need — i.e., a hull that pays for itself on idle-arb even when contracts don't need it? (This is the Admiral's double-duty thesis.)
4. Given ~1M treasury + RULINGS #6 (25%/hull) + the immutable 50k working-capital floor, how many hulls can/should we buy THIS wake, and of what type — more LIGHT_HAULERs (contract cargo), or a heavier frame, or a dedicated arb hull? Note: the fleet autosizer is currently throwing a ZERO-EFFECT alarm trying to buy ~10 HEAVIES (trade), blocked by unscanned heavy-yard price — is that premature Phase-2 sizing, or a signal there IS real trade demand worth serving now?
5. Does aggressive scaling now change the GATE-timing calculus (more haulers -> faster contract cycle-time -> earlier GATE-entry + more surplus haulers to repurpose as gate builders)?

Answer as a bd note (Recommendation / Evidence / Confidence / What would change my mind) + a nudge; I close + act on it (this is the refute-first gate before I aggressively buy — RULINGS #3). Answer-by: next wake (~few hours). Full snapshot above.
notes:
STALL EVIDENCE (for your sizing answer): the 2nd hauler is NOT firing on its own — haulers=1/4 held while treasury CLIMBED ~1.0M->1.07M, blockers=none. The bootstrap STAGED 'buy contract hauler 2/2' (target=2, one per viable hub, hubs=2) but the fleet autosizer's contract-delivery class shows NO shortfall (it sizes to the RECONCILER's contract-delivery demand, which reads 1). So bootstrap-target (2) and reconciler-demand (1) DISAGREE, and via the autosizer_early_scaling single-buyer deferral neither buys the 2nd. KEY QUESTION added to your consult: is the reconciler UNDER-sizing contract-delivery (should be 2+ at 2 hubs) or is 1 correct + the bootstrap over-targeting? This bears directly on the aggressive-scaling verdict + the sp-27at engine fix (the pacing AND the demand-model may both need work).
CONSULT ANSWER — sp-qqwm (refute-first, Admiral-directed): scale contract hulls aggressively at ~1M vs conservative 1-at-a-time?

## Recommendation

**CONFIRM the Admiral thesis — we ARE under-scaling — but the lever is DESTINATION-DEPOT topology (recurring-hub coverage), not "buy N generic haulers," and the ceiling is ABSORPTION, not the 25% rule.** The reconciler is measurably under-sizing contract-delivery; fix its demand model. Do NOT weaken RULINGS #6/#4 (and you don't need to).

Verdicts:
1. **Reconciler is UNDER-sizing (captain is right).** It desires 1 hauler / 0 depots because it sizes to CONCURRENT active contracts (=1, the serial-engine limit) and ignores RECURRING-DESTINATION coverage. Measured recurrence (40 contracts, 39 fulfilled, ~5h): destinations concentrate hard — K83 ×8 (20%), C38 ×5, A1 ×5, E43 ×4 = 55% of all contracts in the top 4 hubs, with per-hub recurring goods (K83: ALUMINUM×3/FERTILIZERS×2/PLASTICS×2). That is exactly the depot-cluster (sp-u9xa) case, and the reconciler is blind to it.
2. **Correct aggressive topology (data-sized):** pre-position ~3-4 delivery hulls at the recurring hubs (K83, A1, C38, E43) + a DESTINATION DEPOT at K83 FIRST (warehouse + 1-2 stockers + co-located delivery hull) stocked with ALUMINUM/FERTILIZERS/PLASTICS. K83's 8 contracts drop ~11-13min -> ~3min (proven sp-u9xa compression). Then A1/C38. Cap at recurring hubs — the 1-contract tail does not justify a depot.
3. **Contract plateau is ~4 (recurring-hub count), NOT the 1 the reconciler wants nor a naive 2.** Bootstrap's target=2 is closer but still under the measured 4 recurring destinations. Beyond the recurring-hub count, extra CONTRACT hulls add ~0 (serial engine, 1 active contract) — further scale belongs to TRADE.

## Q1 — conservative-1 still correct at 1M? NO — scale, but to the MEASURED topology
1M kills the capital constraint (my sp-u5nh answer was explicitly capital-gated; that premise is dead). Aggressive is right. But "aggressive" = build the recurring-hub depot topology (~3-4 delivery hulls + K83 depot), NOT buy generic haulers. Optimal contract-hull count for flush capital = ~4 (one per recurring destination hub) + stocker(s) for the K83 depot.

## Q2 — marginal contract $/hr per hull + plateau
- On a SERIAL engine, $/hr = payout / cycle_time; the ONLY lever is cycle-time. Cycle is TRAVEL-bound: acc->1st-buy ~1.7-3.6min (reposition-to-source) + last-buy->fulfill ~1.4-3.4min (haul-to-dest); source_span=0 (buying is instant — a SOURCE buffer saves little; the DESTINATION depot is the lever).
- Marginal hull at a recurring hub: a pre-positioned hull kills the reposition leg (~2-3min); a DEPOT (stored-near-demand) kills the whole haul leg (~11-13min -> ~3min). Both are real on the serial engine.
- Plateau = the recurring-destination-hub count (~4 here), NOT a flat 2. Beyond that, contract $/hr per hull -> ~0. (Higher than the ~2-hull TRADE arb ceiling because contracts have multiple recurring destinations, each a distinct cycle-time win.)
- Evidence: destination recurrence table (K83 8 / C38 5 / A1 5 / E43 4 / tail 1-3); leg-split (cycle 3-6min, source_span=0); sp-u9xa proof (~3min covered vs ~11-13min uncovered).

## Q3 — idle-arb double-duty: justify hulls beyond contract need?
NOT on current evidence. Checked ALL player-4 transactions: ZERO arb sells ever (only TRADING_COSTS = contract-sourcing buys). The contract-fleet idle-arb dispatcher is producing NOTHING. So "buy hulls for idle-arb double-duty" = buying on a capability that isn't firing — speculative. FIX FIRST: launch the trade-fleet coordinator (NOT running) and MEASURE realized arb $/hr. Then trade-scale to the arb absorption ceiling (~6 single-system; 11 clearing lanes but VOL CAP ~20 & realized ~0.5x quoted), then WIDEN. The depot hulls above are justified by CONTRACT recurrence (proven) — keep that separate from the unproven arb.

title: Bootstrap cold-start: scout-post coordinator caps a post at 1 hull — never mans N hulls / VRP-partitions probes into disjoint tours
description: Found on Era-4 prod cold-start (harbormaster, 2026-07-19). SYMPTOM: the scout-post coordinator manned home post X1-UM5 (27 markets) with only ONE hull (TORWIND-2), assigning all 27 markets to a single ~1h21m circuit — despite logging 'Scout post X1-UM5 undersized: 27 markets over 1 hull(s) ~1h21m circuit exceeds its 1h freshness target - needs 2 hulls'. It NEVER added the 2nd/3rd hull. The other 2 probes (bought to probe_target=3) had nothing to do: the gate-reconcile sweep (gate_reconcile_enabled) grabbed them to chart frontier gates; after that was disarmed they just sat IDLE at the gate. So coverage climbed on ONE probe (~1 market/few-min, and a single long transit leg froze ALL coverage progress — observed flat at 33% for ~9 min while TORWIND-2 flew one leg). This starves the INCOME-phase contract engine: batch-contract loops 'Contract profitability evaluation failed' because no market selling the contract good has been scanned yet, and won't be for a long time at 1/3 the scan rate. Manual workaround that fixed it instantly: 'spacetraders workflow scout-markets --ships TORWIND-3,TORWIND-4 --markets <27> --iterations -1' VRP-partitioned the 2 idle probes into disjoint tours (11 + 16 markets) — EXACTLY what the coordinator should do itself. ROOT CAUSE: the coordinator caps a post at 1 manned hull; it DETECTS 'needs N hulls' but never (a) mans N idle probes into the post nor (b) VRP-partitions the post markets across them. Aggravating: the gate-reconcile sweep out-competes an under-manned home post for spare probes. FIX (for a flawless next-era cold start, zero manual steps): (1) scout-post coordinator scales a post's manned hull count to its freshness target — needs-N-hulls => man up to N available idle probes AND VRP-partition the post markets across them into disjoint tours (reuse the same VRP the manual scout-markets uses; idempotent, re-partition on hull-count change); (2) the cold-start home post takes PRIORITY over the frontier gate-reconcile sweep for spare probes (sweep defers to an under-manned home post). Result: probes bought to target all tour the home system on disjoint partitions, coverage climbs ~Nx faster, contract engine finds goods far sooner. Epic sp-difa (auto-pilot cold start); relates to sp-9ujl (scout-post manning). Found: harbormaster.

title: Cold-start: bootstrap must buy probes but NOT assign them; scout-post coordinator mans them; reconciler must never dedicate a PROBE to contract-delivery
description:
ADMIRAL DESIGN INTENT (verbatim): 'Bootstrapper should only buy the first 2 probes but not assign them to anything. The scout-post coordinator should man those probes.' So: probe BUYING stays with the bootstrap (buy to target); probe MANNING/scouting belongs to the SCOUT_POST_COORDINATOR. The bootstrap must NOT run its one-shot SCOUT_FLEET_ASSIGNMENT sweep or otherwise assign/dedicate the probes — it leaves them idle for the scout-post coordinator to claim.

OBSERVED (armed cold-start validation, staging TORWIND_DEV6 @ X1-DS76, HEAD bf932d2b; arms: autosizer_early_scaling + scaled_gate_entry + contract_delivery_hulls_enabled=1):

RUN-BLOCKING BUG: the CAPACITY RECONCILER dedicated a PROBE to the contract-delivery fleet. Log 09:02:58: 'Fleet dedication written: TORWIND_DEV6-4 -> depot-delivery (frame FRAME_PROBE, cargo 0) [assigner=capacity-reconciler]'. A satellite (cargo 0) cannot haul a contract — this is tier-1 reuse-idle grabbing an idle probe. It STARVES scouting: the scout-tour cannot claim DEV6-4 ('ship TORWIND_DEV6-4 is dedicated to fleet depot-delivery and cannot be claimed by an undeclared operation'), churning 8 FAILED scout tours, and COVERAGE FREEZES at 4/26 (15%) indefinitely (8+ identical heartbeats).

ARCHITECTURE DIVERGENCE: the bootstrap still owns probe buying AND scouting via one-shot SCOUT_FLEET_ASSIGNMENT sweeps (10 COMPLETED) that HOLD the probes. SCOUT_POST_COORDINATOR is RUNNING (sp-9ujl) but perpetually UNMANNED: 'Scout post X1-DS76 unmanned: no in-system satellite — reposition one or wait' — every probe is held by the bootstrap sweep or the reconciler dedication.

FIX:
(a) Bootstrap: buy probes to target but do NOT assign/dedicate them; drop the one-shot SCOUT_FLEET_ASSIGNMENT sweep; leave probes idle.
(b) Capacity reconciler + contract-delivery hull selection: NEVER claim/dedicate a satellite/probe (FRAME_PROBE / cargo 0) as a contract-delivery hull — guard by frame+cargo.
(c) Scout-post coordinator: mans the now-idle probes (claim -> VRP-partition -> scout).

IMPACT: without this the armed cold-start STALLS in DATA (coverage frozen 15%), so INCOME/GATE never validate — blocks the sp-difa phase-1 staging validation. Repro: armed cold-start on a fresh agent. Evidence in deploy/staging/run/daemon.log (this staging run left up).

Only ~1 probe (DEV6-2) actually produces scans; the rest contend over the same hulls, and coverage crawls (to 31%) under the churn. The scout-post coordinator would never do this (one partitioned tour per hull). Strengthens fix-part-(a): RIP OUT the bootstrap sweep, do not merely quiet it.

title: Cold-start economic progression broken: INCOME/contract-scaling skipped, reconciler inert, GATE entered prematurely (no treasury floor, hauler never bought)
description:
ADMIRAL-SPECIFIED intended cold-start economic sequence (encode this):
1. Cold-start frigate runs contracts (bootstrap).
2. Buy a light hauler the INSTANT it is affordable — cash-flow critical; without it contract throughput cannot sustain and the operation runs out of working capital.
3. The CAPACITY RECONCILER scales the contract operation — buys contract workers (haulers) + warehouse + stockers — to grow $/hr. THIS is the reconciler's job.
4. ONLY once the contract operation is HEALTHY (scaled, sustained $/hr) does the surplus $/hr FUND gate construction.
5. Hold a MINIMUM TREASURY FLOOR throughout so the contract operation never runs out of working capital.

OBSERVED (fresh cold start, staging X1-FB55, TORWIND_DEV4) — nearly inverted:
- Phase went DATA (23:45) -> GATE (01:15) DIRECTLY; INCOME never appeared. GATE entered with haulers=0/4, treasury=280k, income/hr=105k — contract op still the lone frigate, UNSCALED. GATE-entry derivation keys on treasury/income thresholds, NOT on a healthy scaled contract operation.
- Capacity reconciler (domain contract_delivery) is INERT: 'Capacity reconciler starting' at boot, then '0 actions executed, 0 proposals filed' every tick (15+). It never computes a contract-scaling need; never buys workers/haulers/warehouse/stockers. Step 3 never happens.
- No hauler ever bought (step 2 skipped): bootstrap wanted 4 but was blocked (no_purchaser, sp-py5r); reconciler bought none. Fleet still FRAME_FRIGATE x1 + FRAME_PROBE x3.
- No minimum treasury floor enforced.
- Result: raced to GATE with an unscaled op, then deadlocked buying gate workers (sp-py5r) — a downstream symptom of entering GATE far too early.

FIX SCOPE (shipwright to design):
- Capacity reconciler MUST scale the contract operation toward a demand-sized desired topology (contract workers/haulers + warehouse + stockers); today it computes nothing — investigate why its desired-topology is empty/inert.
- Buy a light hauler as soon as affordable, ahead of any gate spending.
- GATE-entry derivation must require a HEALTHY SCALED contract operation (haulers + warehouse + stockers + sustained $/hr), not just treasury/income.
- Enforce a minimum treasury floor (contract-operation working capital) that gate spending cannot breach.

RELATED: sp-py5r (GATE purchaser starvation = downstream symptom), sp-9ujl (scouting not armed), sp-lor4 (goods_factory crash). Epic sp-difa.
EVIDENCE: staging/daemon.log phase timeline (DATA->GATE, no INCOME), first GATE heartbeat haulers=0/4 treasury=280k, capacity_reconcile 0-action ticks, fleet has no hauler.

title: Cold-start: scout/freshness reconciler not armed — freshness post declared but UNMANNED (no standing owner for market coverage)
description:
Admiral-confirmed intent: a scout/freshness-domain reconciler MUST boot and MAN the standing freshness post (assign a probe, partition the system, drive P90-freshness rescans and coverage). It does not boot.

Observed on a fresh zero-intervention cold start (staging X1-FB55, TORWIND_DEV4):
- MarketFreshnessSizer (armed, sp-orgp) DECLARES the post. scout_posts row: system=X1-FB55, freshness_target_seconds=3600, kind=standing, hulls=1. Log 00:20:25: 'Declared standing freshness post X1-FB55 sized to 1 probes (SLA 1h) - reconciler will man and partition'.
- Post is UNMANNED: scout_posts.assigned_hull, tour_container_id, primary_partition ALL EMPTY. No probe assigned, no partition.
- bootStandingCoordinatorTypes (internal/adapters/grpc/daemon_boot_standing.go:33-66) has only 4 members: ConstructionCoordinator, MarketFreshnessSizer, BootstrapCoordinator, CapacityReconciler. NONE mans scout_posts. The CapacityReconciler that boots is domain=contract_delivery (log: 'Capacity reconciler starting (domain contract_delivery)'; 0 actions per tick) - the contract-hauler reconciler, not scout/freshness.
- Net: the P90-freshness market-scan assigner has NO standing owner at boot. Only scanning is the bootstrap ONE-SHOT SCOUT_FLEET_ASSIGNMENT (status COMPLETED) + 3 scout_tour workers doing the initial sweep - slow (speed-9 probes, ~20min hops). With no standing owner, an idle probe (DEV4-3 parked 17min at A2) is never re-tasked and coverage risks capping below the 90pct bar.

Impact: defeats zero-intervention market freshness/coverage. No standing rescan to hold P90 (SLA 1h) after the one-shot sweep; idle probes not re-dispatched; coverage may plateau below the bar with nothing to finish it. 'closed != armed' pattern (cf sp-nc0m arming ledger): the scout-post manning coordinator exists in code (container_ops_scouting.go / container_ops_frontier_expansion.go / container_ops_scout_posts.go) but is NOT armed in bootStandingCoordinatorTypes.

Fix direction (shipwright to pin exact mechanism): arm the scout/freshness reconciler in bootStandingCoordinatorTypes (or run CapacityReconciler with the scout/freshness domain) so the declared post is manned at boot.

Related but distinct: sp-gucu (mislabels MANNED posts as dark) assumes posts are manned; this bug is that nothing mans them at cold-start.

Evidence: staging/daemon.log 00:20:25 (declared), scout_posts (unmanned), capacity_reconciler domain=contract_delivery. Repro: fresh cold start, observe scout_posts.assigned_hull stays empty.
notes:
SHARPER ROOT CAUSE (from run_market_freshness_sizer_coordinator.go:1-30, the sizer's own design comment):

1. The sizer EXPLICITLY delegates ALL movement/manning/partitioning to 'the existing scout-post reconciler (sp-cxpq/sp-enry)'. THAT is the unarmed reconciler this bug is about — it is not in bootStandingCoordinatorTypes, so the declared post is never manned.

2. COVERAGE vs FRESHNESS are separate coordinators: freshness = this sizer (sp-orgp, ARMED); coverage = the frontier-expansion coordinator (sp-8w89), which ALSO auto-sizes/buys probes and is ALSO absent from the boot list. So the standing scouting stack is 3 parts — frontier-expansion (coverage buy) + freshness sizer (freshness buy) + scout-post reconciler sp-cxpq/sp-enry (man/move/partition). Only the sizer boots. Manning + coverage do not, so the bootstrap falls back to its hardcoded probe-buy + one-shot SCOUT_FLEET_ASSIGNMENT sweep.

3. The demand formula IS market-count-aware: required_probes = ceil(markets * per_market_cycle / sla), with per_market_cycle MEASURED from scan telemetry and only SEEDED until telemetry exists. The observed 'demand 1 probe' for ~14 markets is a cold-start SEED artifact (seed cycle << real ~20min slow-probe hop); 1 probe breaks the 1h SLA (~4.7h/lap for 14 markets).

4. CLOSED-LOOP BREAK: the sizer self-corrects demand upward via measured per_market_cycle telemetry + empirical P90-age breach (sp-r57g) — but that feedback REQUIRES a manned post generating scan telemetry and a P90 signal. With the scout-post reconciler unarmed (this bug), no post is manned -> no telemetry, no P90 breach -> demand stays stuck at the seed (1) forever. So arming the reconciler also unblocks the sizer's auto-sizing.

Fix scope: arm the scout-post reconciler (sp-cxpq/sp-enry) at boot (and verify the frontier-expansion coordinator sp-8w89 for coverage); then the hardcoded bootstrap probe-buy + one-shot sweep become redundant and can be retired.
CONFIRMED the reconciler to arm = ContainerTypeScoutPostCoordinator (SCOUT_POST_COORDINATOR, run_scout_post_coordinator.go). What it does when running: CLAIMS a satellite to the post (scout fleet, occupancy not a permanent pin — releases on completion/restart), VRP-PARTITIONS the system's MARKETPLACE-trait waypoints across the manned probes (sp-enry synthetic-anchor partitioner), DISPATCHES tours + reposition relays, and ROTATES a probe to the next candidate post on reposition failure (failure cooldowns sp-o34q/sp-s232). All launch config carries RULINGS #5 defaults (tick 30s, reposition cooldowns), so it is boot-standing-able exactly like the freshness sizer — the fix is to add ContainerTypeScoutPostCoordinator to bootStandingCoordinatorTypes. Once manning starts, the sizer closed loop (measured per_market_cycle + empirical P90 breach) self-corrects hull demand off the cold-start seed-of-1 and buys/mans more probes. Scope note: FRONTIER_EXPANSION_COORDINATOR (coverage of NEW systems beyond home) is a SEPARATE arming concern; for home-system DATA coverage the scout-post coordinator + sizer suffice. Known edge bug in the manning path: sp-gucu (census mislabels manned posts as dark).
RESOLVED in main: commit 8c196177 (2026-07-19 01:14) cites sp-9ujl — adds ContainerTypeScoutPostCoordinator as the 5th bootStandingCoordinatorTypes member (exactly the identified fix) + the missing double-launch guard + warm-restart re-adopt (+3 tests). Confirmed in HEAD daemon_boot_standing.go:76. Observed unarmed on a STALE binary; my manual 'scout start' this session validated the manning/VRP-partition mechanism live. Fixed in code; redeploy to pick it up.

title: Trade haulers dark for hours (3 at 25-30h) inside continuous tours: deadhead/jump/arrival-wait dominates, profitable legs rare — the REAL under-dispatch (NOT cooldown)
description:
INVESTIGATION (economy-analyst 2026-07-19, systematic-debugging — the real finding behind the cooldown red herring). SYMPTOM: of 39 trade-dedicated haulers (player_id=3), 8 have landed NO profitable tour_leg for >2h and 3 for 25-30h (TORWIND-15=30h, 7D=28h, 12=26h — spanning multiple daemon restarts). Only 12/39 fresh (<=30min), 19 stale (30min-2h). This is the actual under-dispatch (fleet visibly quiet: ~18-19 active in any 30-min slice of 39 eligible), and it is NOT the cooldown machinery (ruled out, see sibling bead) and NOT wholly the sp-nxrt park-relaunch gap.

VERIFIED STATES (mixed — messier than a single mode; daemon.log): (1) alive-but-CIRCLING: TORWIND-15 last line 'Jump successful / Waiting out jump cooldown before continuing the circuit'; TORWIND-12 'Arrival resync still IN_TRANSIT with a future ETA, continuing to wait' — live continuous tours jumping/repositioning endlessly without landing a profitable leg AND without hitting the honest both-systems-dead exit. (2) STOPPED-container parked: TORWIND-7D 'tour-run-TORWIND-7D … status: STOPPED, not RUNNING' — genuinely idle, tour ended and was not relaunched (coordinator leaves it because... needs tracing). Aggregate state keywords over the 3 (recent): 129 Arrival-wait, 62 IN_TRANSIT, 48 Reposition, 34 'margins died', 28 'Waiting out jump cooldown', 10 'no profitable', 10 'Continuous tour stopping' — nearly all time in deadhead/transit/cooldown-wait/reposition, rare profit.

HYPOTHESIS: this is the extreme tail of the SAME tempo problem the 12h retro found (56% of hull-time between/deadhead + ~50min fixed overhead) — hulls whose reachable neighbourhood is margin-thin spend their whole life jumping+repositioning+waiting cooldowns hunting a lane, occasionally exiting (margins-died) and relaunching into the same thin ground; a subset end in STOPPED containers that never relaunch. sp-nxrt's escalate-to-movement targets the park-relaunch gap but (a) shows 0 fires (continuous tours self-reposition before a 2nd fast-fail) and (b) does nothing for in-tour deadhead or stopped-container parking.

NEXT (Phase-1, shipwright): trace run_tour_coordinator.go — (i) the continuous-tour honest-exit condition (why a 30h-unproductive tour never exits), (ii) the reposition/deadhead loop (RepositionToWaypointWithinJumps / reach) burning jump-cooldowns without converging, (iii) why STOPPED tour containers (7D) are not relaunched by the fleet coordinator. Likely overlaps the deferred pipelining (sp-g9td.1) but is a distinct liveness/productivity defect. Reproducible: last-profitable-leg query + per-hull daemon.log grep in the analyst scratchpad. Parent epic sp-g9td.
notes:
session died
ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (2026-07-19): the dark hulls are downstream of sp-ig6x — the all-ships resync is not completing (fleet-wide synced_at stale 12.5h+), so persisted nav never refreshes and arrival_wait.go (reads persisted state per-poll; live-API reconfirm only on the past-ETA park path) can never observe a wedged hull's arrival. The zero-trade wedge subset (TORWIND-15/7D/12/74) is this. The sporadic-circling subset (17/9/B — reposition-resets-streak at run_tour_coordinator.go:1086 + episode-reset-on-single-trade at :1010) is a SEPARATE, secondary mode. Fix sp-ig6x first; re-measure how many dark hulls remain.
SHIPWRIGHT PHASE-1 TRACE COMPLETE (fmxp-tour-trace, 2026-07-19, code+log+DB airtight). REFRAMES the earlier 'downstream of ig6x' note: the dark hulls have THREE distinct causes; ig6x (resync) rots OBSERVABILITY but is NOT the primary darkness — cause (ii) is. (i) CONTINUOUS-TOUR EXIT is NOT broken: tourExitStarvation fires after 3 no-progress tours (run_tour_coordinator.go:84/1055/1094), a hull DOES exit repeatedly & the fleet coordinator RELAUNCHES it 3min later (proven: TORWIND-12 honest-exit@00:03:45 + relaunch@00:07:05) onto the SAME contended ground -> ~30h of short relaunched containers, not one stuck tour. Latent gap: 'progress'=flew>=1 tranche (line 1010), NOT net-profit, so break-even churn never starves. Lever = RELAUNCH POLICY, not the exit. (ii) HIGHEST LEVERAGE = the true under-dispatch: reposition ranking is CONTENTION-BLIND. planAtCandidate (reposition.go:850/885-887) only PRICES a ground, reserves nothing, blind to the fleet-wide absorption ledger -> ranks a sink as if the hull owned it; on arrival reserveTourPlan->absorptionLedger.Reserve returns ok=false 'breached fleet-wide sink cap' (absorption.go:142-154) -> 'tour unavailable: could not reserve tour depth (sinks contended)'. 37 RUNNING hulls chase a few sinks, each deadheads 10+min toward already-claimed ground -> cap breached -> margins die -> reposition/relaunch -> never converges (thundering-herd/TOCTOU). Compounded by gate-unreachable rich lanes (sp-mtvg). (iii) TORWIND-7D NOT relaunched = ORPHANED CAPTAIN RESERVATION, not the STOPPED container: ships row assignment_status=active owner=captain released_at=NULL container_id=NULL since 03:06:41 (tour went STOPPED); IsReservedByCaptain()=true -> partitionTradeFleet (run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:496) drops it from BOTH idle-relaunch + running-count. Origin = manual captain bridge-authority ops (dock/orbit/navigate) that never dropped the reservation (log 00:06-00:10; tagged tech-debt sp-lxwn/zhii/sfoe). Nothing reaps a stale captain reservation. OVERLAPS: sp-nxrt 0-fires EXPLAINED (continuous tours self-reposition within-container so coordinator never sees a 2nd fast-fail; 7D never enters idle bucket) — nxrt cannot fix any of these. sp-g9td.1 pipelining cuts (ii) deadhead cost but not the convergence defect. Filed children: contention-aware reposition (ii, P1), stale-captain-reservation reaper (iii, P1), profit-aware streak + relaunch backstop (i, P2). Immediate op unblock for 7D: captain/ops release or fleet re-add.

title: Bootstrap over-serializes DATA->INCOME: contracts (funding floor) must start at HOUR-0 in parallel with scanning, not gated behind coverage_bar
description:
Era-4 staging rehearsal design review 2026-07-18. Current bootstrap derivePhase gates DATA->INCOME on market coverage >= coverage_bar (0.90), so contracts don't start until scanning is ~complete. This violates RULINGS #1 (contracts are the funding floor, from hour 0) and needlessly delays income at every era start.

CORRECT MODEL — DATA (scanning) and INCOME (contracts) are PARALLEL workstreams, not sequential phases:
1. HOUR-0, immediately + autonomously: (a) buy probes to MINIMUM 3 total scanning (frigate docks the nearest shipyard, buys to target in ONE pass — see sp-hh0h); (b) start the frigate contract loop. The frigate does the quick shipyard run + probe buy, then runs contracts; probes scan in parallel.
2. Accept contracts immediately (upfront payment regardless of coverage). Each contract SOURCES as soon as its OWN relevant source market is discovered — a contract needs its source market known, NOT global 90% coverage.
3. Coverage stops being an INCOME gate; it just determines how many contracts are sourceable yet, and climbs as the 3 probes scan.
4. GATE phase still triggers when funded/gate-ready.

VERIFY before building: does the contract engine hold an accepted-but-not-yet-sourceable contract gracefully (pick it up when the market appears) or thrash on missing market data?

title: Trade coordinator FULL-HOLD GRIDLOCK: ~half the heavy fleet buys full loads it can't sell — sink over-subscription + multi-good holds landing at non-buying waypoints
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-07-18 ~03:15Z (player 3 TORWIND). ~HALF the heavy fleet is gridlocked: full 225/225 holds, ZERO sells, chasing sinks they never reach.

EVIDENCE — per-heavy SELL_CARGO count last 45m (15 real HEAVY_FREIGHTERs):
  0 sells: 6D, 73, 75, 7C, 7D, 87, 88  (7 of 15 = 47%)
  1-3 sells: 84,86,74,7B,6C,76,85 ; 8 sells: 89
ALL SEVEN zero-sell heavies are FULL (cargo 225/225) — they bought a full load and cannot offload it:
  TORWIND-6D  IN_TRANSIT X1-XM20-D10F  225/225
  TORWIND-73  IN_ORBIT   X1-JR51-F14X  225/225
  TORWIND-75  DOCKED     X1-JR51-EZ9Z  225/225
  TORWIND-7C  IN_ORBIT   X1-XM20-A21A  225/225
  TORWIND-7D  IN_ORBIT   X1-XM20-A14B  225/225
  TORWIND-87  IN_ORBIT   X1-UJ49-D29X  225/225
  TORWIND-88  IN_ORBIT   X1-UJ49-D29X  225/225   <-- 87 AND 88 both full at the SAME waypoint (sink collision)

CLUSTERING (smoking gun): multiple full heavies converge on the same waypoints and orbit without selling — 87+88 both at X1-UJ49-D29X; 7C/7D/6D across XM20; 73/75 at JR51. They arrive at a target sink, find it occupied (fleet-wide sink cap), re-plan, move to another occupied/wrong sink, repeat — for HOURS (7D last sold 215min ago; 86 193min).

ROOT CAUSE (two compounding):
1. SINK OVER-SUBSCRIPTION: the coordinator lets N heavies BUY full loads targeting M profitable sinks where N>M (fleet-wide sink absorption cap). Buys outrun sink capacity, so surplus hulls sit full. Adding heavies (6 bought earlier) made N>M worse (heavy premium collapsed 3x->1.1x = spread cannibalization).
2. MULTI-GOOD HOLDS AT NON-BUYING WAYPOINTS: 7D validated live carrying 5 goods (SHIP_PARTS 6, LIQUID_NITROGEN 39, URANITE 60, HYDROCARBON 60, CLOTHING 60). Its waypoints buy NONE of them: X1-XM20-A21A market imports only FUEL+ANTIMATTER; X1-XM20-A14B live tradeGoods buys []=nothing. So even when it 'arrives', it can't sell. The tour planned buys whose sink got occupied, leaving a multi-good hold no reachable waypoint absorbs.

IMPACT: ~7 of 15 heavies (the fleet's biggest earners, 225 cargo) contribute ~0 for hours; ~1.5M+ cargo value locked; directly caps fleet $/hr (sustained ~4.4M vs earlier peaks). Manual force-sell is whack-a-mole (confirmed: freed 86 partially by selling FABRICS 180 where a waypoint happened to buy it; 7D unsellable at any local waypoint).

FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) gate BUY on a RESERVED/available sink with enough absorption headroom (don't buy a load whose sink is already claimed by another hull); (b) cap concurrent heavies per sink; (c) when a hold can't be sold at any reachable waypoint within K hops, fall back to nearest lower-tier market that buys the goods rather than orbit-and-rechase; (d) fleet-size heavies to sink capacity (stop over-subscribing). Relates to over-fishing: fleet is over-capitalized for available profitable depth.

REPRO: observe player-3 heavies; count SELL_CARGO/hull/45m and cargo fill — full+zero-sells clustered on shared waypoints = the gridlock.

title: Fresh-market depth blocked: cross-system relay BUILT+WIRED but UNARMED (reverted post-reset, sp-ve3q) — 49 idle probes vs 90-deep queue; re-arm scout_cross_system_relay_enabled + make default-on
description:
THE PROBLEM (live 2026-07-17, Admiral escalated 'we need more markets'): the fleet has saturated its ~93 scanned systems (economy-analyst: heavy premium 3x->1.1x, $/hr 14M->6M->1.7M declining, depth is the binding constraint). There IS abundant fresh depth available but we cannot reach it:

INVENTORY OF UNREACHED FRESH DEPTH (DB-verified):
- 5 CHARTED-but-unscanned DENSE HUBS, gate-connected (6-13 gate edges each), each with a jump gate: X1-BG81 (26 marketplaces), X1-QJ93 (26), X1-AF2 (25), X1-GU51 (25), X1-TR56 (14) = ~116 dense fresh markets. 18 of their gate-neighbors already have scanned markets, so they ARE in our gate cluster.
- Frontier 'dark backlog' reports 35 systems / 424 unscanned marketplaces.
- Plus the virgin queue (31 reachable virgin systems).

ROOT CAUSE — PROBE DISTRIBUTION + NO CROSS-SYSTEM RELAY TO DECLARED POSTS:
1. Our ~96-98 probes are ALL clustered in the CORE (VB74/UF64/CH49/HK75...) redundantly re-scanning the already-fresh 93 systems (freshsizer: supply 98 >= demand 93 — OVER-covered). ZERO probes are near the dense hubs (query: probes within 1 hop of any hub-neighbor = 0 rows).
2. The SCOUT coordinator will only man a declared post from an IN-SYSTEM satellite — it does NOT reposition a probe cross-system ('Scout post X1-AF2 unmanned: no in-system satellite — reposition one or wait'). I declared scout posts for all 5 hubs (persisted); they sit permanently unmanned because no probe is in-system and nothing moves one there.
3. The FRONTIER coordinator (sp-6vep) DOES reuse+relay probes, but only within edge_relay_max_hops, and it fixates on deep BK75-region posts the core buyer can't route to ('no jump-gate route from X1-VB74 to X1-BK75 within 5 jumps'), jamming its 5/5 in-flight cap. Its scan-half + discovery-half both wedge on the same deep-reach limit.

NET: we have 116+ dense fresh markets one gate-cluster away and 96 idle/over-provisioned probes, but NO mechanism redistributes probes from over-covered core to reachable unscanned hubs. More probes does NOT help (we're over-provisioned); REDISTRIBUTION does.

THE FIX (options):
(a) Teach the SCOUT coordinator to man a declared post by relaying the nearest reusable probe CROSS-SYSTEM (mirror sp-6vep's frontier reuse-relay), pulling from OVER-covered core systems (freshsizer surplus) — this alone mans the 5 hub posts I already declared -> ~116 fresh markets.
(b) Raise/parameterize the relay reach (multi-jump chaining) so dense reachable hubs beyond 5 jumps can be staffed; the 5-jump router cap is per-navigate, not physical (probes are fuel_cap=0 gate-users, cannot fuel-strand — chain hops).
(c) A rebalance pass: detect over-covered systems (probes > per-system need) and redeploy surplus probes to declared-but-unmanned posts.

ACCEPTANCE: with 5 hub scout posts declared and 0 in-system probes but surplus probes in over-covered core systems, the coordinator relays probes to man the hub posts and their ~116 markets get scanned into market_data (tradeable depth), without hand-piloting.

CONTEXT: substantial change, will NOT land before era reset 2026-07-19 13:00Z (~34h) — future-era infra. This era: discovery trickles ~1 system/30min via sp-6vep; dense-hub depth stays unreachable. Related: sp-6vep (frontier reuse — the pattern to mirror), sp-gucu (census 4h-bar mislabeling), sp-jhht (probe supply governance), sp-ve3q (restart wipes tunes).

WHAT THE CODE SHOWS (current main, read-only):
- The cross-system reuse relay this bead built is FULLY BUILT + WIRED. Mechanism: run_scout_post_coordinator.go (SystemProbeDemandReader L322-331, relay gated on ScoutCrossSystemRelayEnabled L236-245).     (reader already wired; the flag is live-tunable -> takes effect next tick). Expect the 49 idle probes to relay onto the unmanned hub / dark-market posts; openSlots and the futile buys fall.
(2) DURABLE — the real fix (else it reverts on every restart/era-reset, sp-ve3q): make cross-system relay DEFAULT-ON — flip defaultScoutCrossSystemRelayEnabled 0->1 (run_scout_post_coordinator.go:117) or arm it in config.yaml so it survives restarts. title: FINDING: fleet is NOT depth-saturated — 593 reachable/sourceable profitable sinks unworked (optimizer coverage gap, not market depth). Upgrades sp-fguo to #1 $/hr lever
description:
economy-analyst data analysis (2026-07-17, player_id=3). CORRECTS the earlier depth-saturation diagnosis. The trade fleet's $/hr ceiling is the tour solver's CANDIDATE-COVERAGE/REACH, not exhausted market depth. There is confirmed reachable, sourceable, profitable margin the optimizer is blind to.

== EVIDENCE (from current market_data + gate graph + tour_leg_telemetry) ==
Profitable export->import lanes in data we ALREADY hold, deflated hard (distinct sinks, FRESH <75min, >=15% margin, NOT traded in 4h), then reachability+source-stock checked via gate-hop BFS:
- 1,250 fresh untraded profitable sinks; after realism filters:
- ACTIONABLE SET = 593 sinks (40 goods, 84 systems) that are ALL: (a) 100% sourceable — source export supply ABUNDANT(990)/HIGH(260), 0 thin; (b) 0 unreachable — src->sink gate path exists; (c) near fleet — sink within 3 gate-hops of the fleet's current footprint; src->sink <=4 hops.
- SMOKING GUN: 344 of them are IN systems the fleet is ALREADY trading, untraded — pure solver blindness (hull physically present, good sourceable <=4 hops, sink pays, no lane constructed).
- Same high-value goods the fleet already trades: CLOTHING(21 sinks, 9305 margin), MACHINERY(34), MEDICINE(9062), ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY(11859), URANITE(7522), EQUIPMENT(19), FABRICS(11).
- Concrete: fleet sells URANITE at ~4005 realized while FRESH URANITE sinks at 8700-9190 (incl. GP32 @ 8778, 17min fresh — a system the fleet operates in) sit untraded.

== DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION ==
Earlier I diagnosed depth-saturation (heavy per-hull premium collapsed 3x->1x, $/hr softening 9.5M->6M). That was WRONG on cause. The map has abundant reachable margin; heavies' premium collapsed because they cycle a SATURATED LOCAL LOOP while 593 reachable profitable sinks sit unworked. Ceiling = optimizer coverage/reach, NOT market depth.

== MECHANISM (why the solver misses them) ==
The Go caller (run_tour_coordinator.go) passes only ~1 gate-hop of candidate systems to the solver, so it cannot PAIR these sources with these sinks even when both are reachable. The 344 in-footprint misses show the candidate PAIRING is incomplete even within systems hulls already occupy. Both are in sp-fguo's scope (wider candidate set + longer tours).

== RECOMMENDATION ==
Reprioritize: #1 = sp-fguo (candidate-window widening + pairing coverage) is THE $/hr lever, ABOVE sp-acb8 (tranche/concentration tuning, which extracts more per market but can't reach markets the solver never sees). This finding is the evidence to bump sp-fguo P2->P1 and front-load the 'widen candidate systems' child (sp-jsng).

== METHOD (reproducible) ==
market_data EXPORT(buy=purchase_price)->IMPORT(sell=sell_price) pairs, margin>15%, sink freshness via last_updated<75min, anti-join vs (good,sink_system) traded last 4h; gate_edges BFS for src->sink hops + multi-source BFS from fleet footprint; source stock via export supply level.

== CAVEATS (honest) ==
Margins are SNAPSHOT (pre-impact) — impact-crush haircuts them on fill, and opp=margin*tv are ceilings not captured credits (shared source/hull capacity). But goods are the same-magnitude high-value ones the fleet already realizes thousands on, so margins survive the haircut. Realistic $/hr uplift needs the fitted impact curve applied to the 593 (separate follow-up). Direction is certain: reachable money the optimizer isn't seeing.

Relates: sp-fguo (longer tours/wider candidate — the fix), sp-acb8 (tuning — second-order), sp-jeou (hull adoption at frontier).
