title: Frontier discovery: teach the coordinator to REUSE existing probes (relay from the edge) instead of buy-and-relay — fixes the deep-frontier deadlock
description:
MOTIVATION (live-confirmed 2026-07-17, era end ~36h): frontier discovery is fully wedged and cannot chart the remaining virgin systems, which are the fleet's only source of new MARKET DEPTH — and depth is now the binding constraint (economy-analyst: fleet $/hr 14M->8M->6M, heavy premium collapsed 3x->1.1x, fleet has outgrown available profitable depth). So a broken discovery engine directly caps earnings.

ROOT CAUSE — the coordinator is PURCHASE-ANCHORED. To staff a frontier post it BUYS a new probe at a yard near the target and relays a BUYER there (resolveProbeBuy/resolveProximalBuy in internal/adapters/expansion/adapters.go). Every existing knob (proximal_yard_hop_penalty, max_probe_price, probe_sibling_price_margin, max_spend_per_cycle) only tunes the PURCHASE. At the deep edge, no yard/buyer is reachable: log repeats 'failed to relay probe buyer to X1-BK75-ZD5B: no jump-gate route from X1-VB74 to X1-BK75 within 5 jumps'. The 5 posts jam the in-flight cap (5/5) with NO timeout -> permanent deadlock; discovery = 0. The coordinator has NO concept of reusing a probe that already exists — that is the missing capability, and no buy-path tuning fixes it.

THE MANUAL INSIGHT (what a human operator does): we ALREADY have probes parked at the charted frontier edge (live: 1 each at BK75/CH49/FS70/FZ18), and every queued virgin (JF7, JX74, MV9, N81, NH87, NJ31, PJ97, QK40, QQ26, RJ33) is hops=1 — ONE gate from that edge. A human just hops the edge probe over and scans. No purchase, no deep-yard relay, no deadlock.

ALGORITHM CHANGES:
1. REUSE-BEFORE-BUY: when staffing a post, first try to relay an EXISTING probe from the nearest covered system; buy only as last resort.
2. ANCHOR RELAY-REACH TO THE NEAREST USABLE PROBE, not a fixed buyer. Today reach is measured 'from VB74 (buyer home) within 5 jumps' -> always fails because VB74 is far. Measure 'hops from nearest edge probe to target' (~1 for these virgins). Turns 'unreachable' into 'one hop'.
3. SNOWBALL: after a relayed probe charts a virgin, auto-enqueue THAT system's neighbors as next targets, so one probe walks the frontier outward.

NEW KNOBS:
- probe_reuse_enabled (bool, default on): try existing probes before buying.
- edge_relay_max_hops (int, ~3): max hops to relay an existing probe to a post; replaces the fixed 5-jump-from-buyer wall.
- reuse_value_ceiling (credits): only BORROW a probe off a freshness post whose system trade-value is below this — cannibalize low-value deep-edge freshness to fund exploration, never strip a probe off a high-value core market (the depth-vs-freshness judgment).
- snowball_neighbors (bool): toggle walk-outward.

CLEANER ARCHITECTURAL OPTION: frontier stops buying entirely and just DECLARES reachable virgins as desired scout posts; the SCOUT coordinator (already relays existing probes to keep systems fresh) staffs them with the same edge-probe reuse. Unifies 'explore new' + 'keep fresh' under one probe-relay engine instead of two coordinators with divergent (one broken) sourcing.

ACCEPTANCE:
- With probes at charted edge systems and hops=1 virgins queued, the coordinator charts the virgins by relaying existing edge probes (0 purchases needed), not deadlocking on unbuyable deep yards.
- In-flight posts that cannot be staffed within edge_relay_max_hops are abandoned/retried (no permanent 5/5 deadlock — also fixes the no-timeout bug observed live).
- Reuse never strips probes off systems above reuse_value_ceiling.
- Snowball: charting system S enqueues S's uncharted neighbors.

RELATED: sp-ve3q (restart wipes tuned knobs incl. this coordinator's), sp-jhht (deep probe-supply decision), sp-gucu (census 4h-bar vs SLA mislabeling). NOTE: substantial algo change — will NOT land before the current era reset; this is future-era infra. The manual workaround this era = redirect existing edge probes by hand (out of scope here).

title: frontier coordinator: add a scan_only knob (decouple scanning discovered markets from expanding to virgin)
description:
PROBLEM
The frontier expansion coordinator entangles two behaviors with no way to separate them:
  (a) EXPAND — reach new virgin systems (depth pathfinders punching to deepest-reachable virgin, probe-buying, charting new systems). This GROWS the discovered-but-unscanned ("dark") market backlog.
  (b) SCAN — sweep the markets of already-discovered / charted-but-unscanned systems (breadth sweep-once posts).
There is no control to do (b) without (a). The ONLY off-switch for expansion is stopping the whole coordinator container — which also kills (b), i.e. all market scanning. Tuning breadth_fraction_percent / max_depth_pathfinders biases the breadth-vs-depth split but does NOT cleanly stop expansion, and does NOT restrict the sweep set to the full discovered-dark backlog (the queue is expansion-frontier-scoped, ~30 systems, while the real dark backlog was 65).

LIVE SYMPTOM (2026-07-16, player 3, ~3 days pre-reset)
Expansion charted new systems faster than probes could scan them (dark market-system count grew 58 -> 65 under load). Operator wanted to STOP the growth and let probes drain the discovered backlog (where the cheap exotic sources are). The only available lever was `container stop` on the coordinator — which stopped market scanning entirely (had to be restarted immediately). No knob exists for "monetize what we've discovered; stop reaching for more."

DESIRED KNOB
Add a live-tunable `scan_only` knob (int, 0/1, default 0) to the frontier expansion coordinator. Default 0 = today's behavior, byte-identical (default-safe). When `scan_only = 1`:
  1. Declare NO depth-pathfinder posts — no punching to virgin (skip the depth branch / frontier_depth_policy declarations).
  2. Buy NO probes — no fleet growth for expansion (skip decideAndMaybeBuy).
  3. Restrict the sweep-candidate set to ALL charted-but-unscanned MARKET systems — systems that have MARKETPLACE waypoints AND zero player market_data — ranked by market count. NOT just the expansion-frontier subset. This is the true "discovered backlog" (the 65, not the ~30 the expansion ranker surfaces).
  4. KEEP declaring breadth sweep-once posts for that set; the scout-post reconciler mans them and scans the markets. When the backlog is fully scanned, the coordinator idles (emits a NoWork reason) — it does NOT reach for virgin.

SEMANTICS: scan_only = "drain the discovered-market backlog to zero, then idle; add no new dark systems, spend nothing on probes." Freshness sizer and gate_reconcile sweep are unaffected (separate). Reversible live (scan_only 0 resumes full expansion).

GUARDS / IDEMPOTENCY
- Default 0 => byte-identical to today (RULINGS #5 optional-knob discipline).
- Live-tunable via the existing tune plumbing: `spacetraders tune --operation frontier scan_only 1`. Applies next tick, survives restart (config is the recovery source), audited as config.tuned.
- Overrides breadth_fraction / max_depth_pathfinders when set (those become moot in scan_only).
- No effect on freshness sizing or the scouting gate_reconcile sweep.

FILES (located this session; shipwright to confirm exact lines)
- internal/application/expansion/commands/run_frontier_expansion_coordinator.go — ReconcileOnce (~:673): gate the depth-post declaration and decideAndMaybeBuy (~:757) behind `!scan_only`; when scan_only, source candidates from the full charted-unscanned-market set.
- the ExpansionCandidates / buildExpansionQueue path (~:693 / ~:930) + scanner.ExpansionCandidates — add a scan-only candidate source = charted systems with MARKETPLACE waypoints and no market_data, ranked by market count (broaden beyond the expansion-frontier ranking).
- internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_tune.go (~:105) — add `scan_only` to the ContainerTypeFrontierExpansion knob registry (int, bounds [0,1], default 0, "scan discovered markets only; declare no expansion/depth posts and buy no probes").
- expansionCmd.FrontierTunableDefaults() — add `scan_only` default 0.
- Test: with scan_only=1, assert (i) no depth posts declared, (ii) no probe buy, (iii) sweep posts declared for every charted-unscanned market system, (iv) idles when backlog empty; with scan_only=0, behavior byte-identical.

WHY NOW / VALUE
Operability gap: turning off expansion should be a config knob, not a destructive container-kill that also stops scanning. Concretely needed late-era to drain the discovered-market backlog (cheap exotic sources) without growing it or spending on probes, while keeping the scan machinery and the trade fleet untouched. Lineage: complements sp-bcsu (gate-charting) and the sp-fguo tour work; pairs with the existing frontier tune knobs (breadth_fraction, max_depth_pathfinders, max_probe_fleet) added under sp-rjgr/sp-vwek.

title: Widen gate-chart sweep scope: market-only → active-route transit gates
description:
reconcileGateChartSweep targets gateUnchartedMarketSystems (MARKET-bearing systems only). Structural flaw: a system's market status is unknown until its gate is charted, so a market-scoped sweep can only re-chart already-explored systems and CANNOT expand the frontier. Evidence (2026-07-16): backlog plateaued at 16 era-3 markers = 4 market-system (drain normally) + 12 marketless transit-system gates the sweep ignores by design. Those 12 marketless transit gates are a residual GetJumpGate-400 source: traders jumping THROUGH uncharted transit systems 400 on the gate read regardless of market presence — this is a chunk of the API-400 rate we fought all day.

FIX (Admiral ruling: 'transit gates on active routes'): widen the sweep target set from market-only to any uncharted gate with a STALE backoff marker within probe jump-bound, market or not. Rationale: gate_edges backoff markers (connected_system='') are SET BY the 400ing fleet traffic itself, so a stale marker IS the 'active route traverses this gate' signal. Marketless dead-end gates no traffic touches never get markered → naturally excluded (bounded scope, no over-exploration). Keep all other constraints (jump-bound ≤12, idle-probe availability, era scoping, backoff staleness/anyStale, K-correction).

Do NOT chart ALL reachable uncharted gates (Admiral rejected that as over-exploration). Scope strictly to markered (traffic-touched) gates.

title: Gate-reconcile 0-hop dispatches never chart: same-system travel returns before chartArrivedGate + targets a market not the gate — backlog won't drain
description:
ROOT CAUSE (code-confirmed, VH23/TD90 stuck-marker investigation).

SYMPTOM: sp-bcsu Part 2 gate-reconcile sweep dispatches idle probes to backed-off/uncharted-gate systems 'to chart on arrival', but the stubborn backed-off systems (VH23 attempt_count 12, TD90 8, UT91 10, climbing) NEVER clear — 30 dispatches, only 2 charts succeeded (the multi-hop ones), 0 stubborn markers cleared. So the retroactive backlog does not drain.

WHY (two coupled facts):
1. travelWithJumpBound (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:259-264) short-circuits the same-system case:
     if currentSystem == destSystem { navigate(destinationWaypoint); return ship,nil }
   This RETURNS before chartArrivedGate (:380). So a 0-hop reposition (probe already IN the target system) never reaches the charting call. The MULTI-hop path works only because the jump lands the hull ON the destination system's gate and :380 charts it before the gate->market hop; a 0-hop has no jump, so no gate landing.
2. The reconcile sweep's reposition destination is a MARKET waypoint (reconcileGateChartSweep -> pickRepositionDestination(markets) in run_scout_post_coordinator.go), NOT the gate. So even reaching the destination, the 0-hop probe is at a market, not on the jump gate — and charting (CreateChart/GetJumpGate) requires the hull ON the gate.

WHY IT'S THE PRIMARY BLOCKER: the sweep picks the NEAREST idle probe (selectNearestSatelliteByHops). For a backed-off system, the nearest idle probe is very often the one already stranded IN it (0-hop). So the systems most needing charting are exactly the ones only reachable 0-hop, which never chart. Confirmed: TORWIND-3F->VH23 (0 jump), TORWIND-6A->TD90 (0 jump) — both 0-hop, both stuck.

FIX (INVARIANT): after a gate-reconcile dispatch to system X, if a probe reaches X (0-hop OR multi-hop), X's jump gate must get charted. The 0-hop path must route the probe TO the gate waypoint and chart it (navigate-to-gate + chartArrivedGate/ChartPresentGate, best-effort/non-fatal).

SCOPING CONSTRAINT (critical): the same-system branch at :259 is shared by ALL same-system travel (normal trade legs). Do NOT make every same-system navigate detour to the gate + chart — that would divert trade hulls and waste API. Scope the gate-visit+chart to the reconcile's charting INTENT only (e.g. reconcile targets the GATE waypoint for 0-hop targets and the same-system branch charts when the destination IS a jump gate; or a flag threaded from the reposition-for-charting path; or the reconcile directly navigates the present probe to the gate and calls ChartPresentGate). Crafter picks the cleanest scoping.

GUARDS: best-effort/non-fatal (mirror chartArrivedGate — never fail the leg); only chart genuinely-uncharted (store-first guard, reuse sp-lv2n path); ship must be ON the gate when CreateChart/GetJumpGate fire.

VERIFY: RED test — a 0-hop reconcile dispatch (probe already in the target system) ends with the target gate charted (currently it does NOT). GREEN: normal same-system TRADE travel is byte-unchanged (no gate detour). Related: sp-bcsu (Part 2 sweep), sp-lv2n (CreateChart — the charting primitive this must invoke on the 0-hop path).

title: Daemon never CreateChart's jump gates — uncharted frontier gates re-read live per jump, 49% of GetJumpGate calls 400, jump-outs fail
description:
ROOT CAUSE (evidence-based, DA78 400 investigation).

SYMPTOM: reposition/jump OUT of frontier systems fails with API 400 code 4001 'Waypoint X1-DA78-C24B is not accessible — uncharted or no ship present' (jump_ship.go:313), even though gate_edges HAS X1-DA78's system-level edges (DA78→GP32/GQ22/HJ65/K93/NH14, era 3). Also: 107 of 220 live GetJumpGate calls (49%) are 400s — a large slice of the session's API churn.

CHAIN:
1. jump_ship.go:311 does a LIVE GetJumpGate(originGate) on every jump to resolve the destination gate WAYPOINT (e.g. X1-GQ22-K82) — the jump API needs the waypoint, not the system.
2. gate_edges stores connected_system (system symbol) only, NOT the gate waypoint — so the jump cannot fall back to the DB; it is forced into the live read.
3. DA78-C24B (a JUMP_GATE) is uncharted-PUBLIC. On an uncharted gate GetJumpGate requires a ship physically AT the gate waypoint; it 400s otherwise.
4. THE GAP: the daemon has NO charting capability. 'Chart Waypoint' (/my/ships/*/chart) is classified in endpoint_classifier.go:31 but has ZERO calls ever (Prometheus). gategraph (ChartPresentGate/fetchAndStore, service.go) only GetJumpGate-READS gates and stores our own edge copy — it never CreateChart's them. sp-bcsu's chartArrivedGate/chart-on-arrival reads+stores but does not publicly chart.
5. So an uncharted gate that only OUR ships visit stays uncharted-public forever: every jump-out re-reads it live and 400s whenever the jumping hull is not precisely on the C24B gate waypoint at read time (nav timing / hull at a different DA78 waypoint like the CF1B market).

CONFIRMED: DA78 IS reachable + tradeable (TORWIND-16 trading ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY at DA78-CF1B live) — the failure is specifically jumping OUT via the uncharted gate. Ships table shows the hulls are NOT on C24B when the read fires.

FIX: add a CreateChart (POST /my/ships/{ship}/chart) client method + call it when a ship is present at an uncharted jump gate — in the existing chartArrivedGate (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:407) / ChartPresentGate seam where a hull is already on the gate. Charting once makes the gate publicly readable forever → jump-outs resolve the destination waypoint without a fragile live ship-present read, and the ~49% GetJumpGate 400 re-read storm collapses. Consider also persisting connected-gate WAYPOINTS (not just systems) in gate_edges so the jump path can resolve the destination waypoint from the DB with no live read at all (belt-and-suspenders). Guard: only CreateChart when GetJumpGate/traits indicate uncharted (don't re-chart charted gates). Non-fatal/best-effort like chartArrivedGate.

IMPACT: unblocks frontier jump-outs (the Admiral's expand-the-frontier goal) AND removes ~half of Get Jump Gate API load (49% 400 rate). Related: sp-bcsu (chart-on-arrival read, this completes it), sp-4bm3 (GetJumpGate 400 neg-cache), sp-ph7t.

title: Cut redundant movement API calls in the tour path (idempotent Orbit/Dock + stay-docked refuel→trade + skip fuel top-off)
description:
Movement verbs are 46% of API traffic and the account is rate-limited (server 429s + client queuing, ~0.9s wait/call). Prometheus window: Navigate 61, Dock 36, Orbit 35, Refuel 21. Three cuts, all in the tour hot path (route_executor.go + Dock/Orbit/Refuel command handlers):

1. IDEMPOTENT ORBIT/DOCK (biggest, safest): in DockShipHandler and OrbitShipHandler, if the in-memory ship nav status ALREADY equals the target (DOCKED for dock, IN_ORBIT for orbit), skip the API call and return success with state unchanged. The ship's NavStatus is kept current by every nav command's response, so it is reliable. This guards ALL callers (route executor, contract delivery, manufacturing, liquidation) at once. On a genuine state-mismatch the existing retry path recovers.

2. STAY DOCKED THROUGH REFUEL->TRADE: route_executor.refuelShip (:731) does dock->refuel->orbit; when a trade immediately follows at the SAME waypoint the ship then docks again — 2 dock + 2 orbit for one stop. Some paths already gate on fuel>=next-leg-cost (:422); make refuelBeforeDeparture (:151) consistent — only dock+refuel when Fuel().Current < next-leg FuelCost + DefaultFuelSafetyMargin. A ship with enough fuel for the next leg skips the whole dock/refuel/orbit trio.

HOT-PATH CAUTION: this touches ship state transitions and fuel safety. RED->GREEN per cut, mutation-prove each guard is load-bearing (removing it re-introduces the redundant call). Do NOT skip a transition on stale/uncertain state — only when the in-memory NavStatus is authoritative. Preserve all existing retry/reroute behavior (sp-vsfn). title: frontier-expansion coordinator must chart jump gates, not just markets (unstrands frontier, unblocks sp-mtvg)
description:
VERIFIED SPEC (captain ran a code-investigation subagent; the original framing below the PROBLEM was corrected against the actual code — see CORRECTION note).

PROBLEM
The frontier expands markets but never charts jump gates. A probe/hull jumping into system X always LANDS on X's jump gate, but the travel code immediately flies the gate->market hop without ever reading X's gate connections. Reading a gate's outbound edges requires a ship physically present at the gate (an uncharted gate returns HTTP 400 code 4001 "no ship present"), so that in-transit moment on the gate is the ONLY chance to read it — and it is thrown away. Result: gate_edges for X stays empty.

CONSEQUENCES (both confirmed live, player 3, era3)
- Empty gate_edges => the strict pathfinder fails closed on X (gategraph/service.go:337-371) => hulls routed through/out of X STRAND. Hand-rescued heavies + mediums this session at X1-QF75, X1-XJ34, X1-AD31, X1-SQ68.
- The tour planner's computeUnreachableLanes DROPS every lane whose sink is outside the gate-neighbor graph (run_tour_coordinator_unreachable_lanes_test.go) — the sp-mtvg blind spot — because the rich sinks live in exactly that uncharted frontier.
- A remote-fetch mitigation (growFrontierGraph, adapters.go:583-630) tries to read X's gate with NO ship present => 400 => enterBackoff latches X unreadable (5m->30m->2h, service.go:62-74). X's gate then stays uncharted PERMANENTLY. (This is sp-dc50's partial, insufficient fix.)

CORRECTION vs the first draft of this bead:
- The fix does NOT belong in container_ops_frontier_expansion.go — the coordinator NEVER moves probes (it only measures/declares/buys; RULINGS #7). 
- warp_system_charter.go is the WRONG charter — it is warp/SHIP_EXPLORER-only and is DORMANT in prod (main.go never calls SetOffGateTargetSelector). 
- The correct, minimal seam is the shared gate-crosser arrival, reusing the already-wired gategraph.Connections. The manual SQL backoff-clear is replaced by store.Replace's self-heal on a present-ship read.

FIX SPEC (add chart-on-gate-arrival to the gate-crosser; mirror of route_executor_warp.go:149 chartOnArrival)

1) internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go
   In travelWithJumpBound the hull is guaranteed on destSystem's jump gate at :362-365 (freshShip reloaded, BEFORE the gate->market hop at :375). Insert a best-effort gate chart there, and also after each intermediate jumpHop in the loop at :346-360 (the hull is on nextSystem's gate; intermediates are usually already charted => cheap store hits).

   // NEW (sp-bcsu): hull is physically on destSystem's jump gate — the one moment its
   // outbound connections are readable. Chart+persist now, before flying to market.
   h.chartArrivedGate(ctx, freshShip, playerID)

   Helper (new method on RunTradeRouteCoordinatorHandler):
   func (h *RunTradeRouteCoordinatorHandler) chartArrivedGate(ctx context.Context, ship *navigation.Ship, playerID int) {
       if h.gateGraph == nil { return }
       loc := ship.CurrentLocation()
       if loc == nil || !loc.IsJumpGate() { return }
       if _, err := h.gateGraph.ChartPresentGate(ctx, loc.SystemSymbol, playerID); err != nil {
           common.LoggerFromContext(ctx).Log("INFO", fmt.Sprintf(
               "chart-on-arrival: gate read for %s failed (non-fatal): %v", loc.SystemSymbol, err))
       }
   }

2) internal/application/system/gategraph/service.go
   Add a presence-forced read that BYPASSES the backoff short-circuit (a plain Connections short-circuits on the latch at :166-173 and would skip the four already-latched systems even with a ship present). On a now-succeeding present-ship read, fetchAndStore -> store.Replace deletes all rows INCLUDING the backoff marker (self-heal, gate_edge_repository.go:116-117):

   func (s *Service) ChartPresentGate(ctx context.Context, systemSymbol string, playerID int) ([]system.GateEdge, error) {
       if edges, ok, err := s.store.Edges(ctx, systemSymbol); err != nil {
           return nil, err
       } else if ok && len(edges) > 0 {
           return edges, nil   // already charted — idempotent skip, no API (guard 1)
       }
       return s.fetchAndStore(ctx, systemSymbol, playerID)
   }

3) internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator.go
   Add ChartPresentGate to the GateGraph interface (:368-387). *gategraph.Service already satisfies it; h.gateGraph is already wired in prod (already exposes Connections at :387). No composition-root change needed.

4) Tests: RED pin that a probe/hull jumping into an uncharted-gate system leaves gate_edges populated for that system; and that a backed-off system is HEALED on a present-ship arrival. Use the existing fakeGateGraph idiom (sp-fwxm/kl16).

GUARDS / IDEMPOTENCY (all satisfied)
- Don't re-chart charted gates: the Edges len>0 early return (one store read, zero API).
- Backoff latch: ChartPresentGate bypasses it ONLY when a ship is present; success self-heals via Replace; a genuinely still-failing gate re-enters backoff unchanged (fetchAndStore:212-214).
- Rate limit: charting piggybacks on arrivals the hull already makes — no new fan-out/burst.
- Never fails the leg: best-effort, logged and swallowed (same discipline as chartOnArrival).

SCOPE DECISION (one knob)
travelWithJumpBound is shared by probes (repositionJumpBound > 0) and heavies/trade (bound 0).
- RECOMMENDED: chart on ALL gate arrivals (fixes heavy strands too; safe because store-first makes charted systems free and backoff caps re-probes).
- CONSERVATIVE: gate the call on repositionJumpBound > 0 (probe/reposition only), keeping the hot trade path byte-identical.
Suggest a reversible flag [routing] chart_gate_on_arrival (default on). No new backoff config — [routing] gate backoff (main.go:804-812) already governs fetchAndStore.

SELF-HEAL OF THE 4 STRANDED SYSTEMS
Probes reach QF75/XJ34/AD31/SQ68 via RepositionPath, which already routes PAST unreadable gates over stored adjacency (service.go:396-418, sp-8k9m); the forced arrival read then clears each latch. Removes the captain's manual per-gate "UF64 procedure."

RELATED BEADS
- sp-dc50 (PARENT root cause): "Frontier caps at hop-1: sweep charts markets but not jump gates, so no hop-2 adjacency" — its growFrontierGraph remote-fetch is the partial/insufficient fix. sp-bcsu is the correct, complete implementation of what sp-dc50 identified.
- sp-mtvg: tour/arb good-level blind spot (20k+ exotic bids never traded) — the tour-planner consequence this unblocks.
- sp-4bm3: negative-cache the GetJumpGate 400 (the backoff this fix must bypass on presence).
- sp-8k9m: RepositionPath routes past unreadable gates (the relaxation whose comment falsely claims arrival re-reads the gate).
- sp-4imi / sp-0xd0: warp explorer + chart-on-arrival for OFF-gate systems (the pattern mirrored here for gate arrivals).
- sp-fwxm / sp-yuq9 / sp-7gr2 / sp-8qhu: prior strand/routing incidents + fakeGateGraph test template.

FALSE COMMENTS TO FIX (they assert the missing behavior)
- gategraph/service.go:386-387 and run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:411-413 both claim a reposition arrival "re-reads the gate it crossed (the relaxation retires itself)". That re-read is NOT implemented — it is precisely the missing step this bead adds.
notes:
session died
RETROACTIVE BACKFILL — REQUIRED (added 2026-07-16 per Admiral). The prospective chart-on-arrival alone does NOT clear the existing uncharted-gate debt.

WHY THE PROSPECTIVE FIX ISN'T ENOUGH
chart-on-arrival only fires when a hull is physically standing on a gate. A system that was already market-swept (sweep-once done) and has EMPTY gate_edges will never be revisited by the coordinator, because growFrontierGraph declares no deeper post beyond it (no stored adjacency to extend from) — so no probe is ever routed through it, and its gate stays uncharted forever. Bootstrapping chicken-and-egg. This is exactly why the captain's manual UF64 procedure exists.

PARTIAL SELF-HEAL (opportunistic, NOT guaranteed)
Probes use the relaxed RepositionPath (sp-8k9m) which routes PAST unreadable gates over stored adjacency. So any probe whose path to a DEEPER target transits an already-uncharted system will arrive on its gate and chart-on-arrival clears the latch. As expansion pushes outward, probes transiting the older ring backfill it for free — but only for systems that lie on a path to some reachable deeper target. Dead-end / frontier-edge uncharted systems are never transited, so they do NOT self-heal.

REQUIRED SECOND HALF — one-time reconcile sweep (automates the UF64 procedure)
Enumerate systems that are market-charted OR backoff-latched but gate-uncharted — i.e. gate_edges has no connected_system rows for the system, or has rows with unreadable_since set / empty connected_system. For each, dispatch a probe to that system's JUMP_GATE waypoint and call ChartPresentGate (presence-forced read -> store.Replace self-heals the latch). This clears the current backlog (QF75 partial / XJ34 / AD31 / SQ68 + the WAVE strand systems); chart-on-arrival then keeps it current forever after.

Implementation options for the reconcile: (a) a startup/periodic coordinator pass that builds the uncharted-but-market-known set and enqueues gate-chart posts for idle probes; or (b) a one-shot admin/CLI verb the captain runs once against the current backlog, with the coordinator handling steady-state going forward. Recommend (a) so it is self-maintaining, with (b) as the immediate manual unblock.

title: Impact-aware lane ranking: fitted price-impact + recovery model for the tour ranker — predicts next-leg price 40-49% better than snapshot; compressed lanes need HOURS-long cooldown (half-life ~520min, not minutes)
description:
Wire the fitted price-impact + recovery model into the trade lane ranker (rankLanesByCircuitRate / scanLanes). Community research confirmed top ST bots trade on raw snapshots ('predict the recovery curve' = unsolved); this model beats snapshot pricing 40-49% out-of-sample on our own era-3 telemetry — a real edge on the stream that is ~80% of income.

## THE FITTED MODEL (era-3, 886 consecutive-leg pairs from tour_leg_telemetry; refit-per-era script in economy-analyst scratchpad, seconds to rerun)
IMPACT (per trade, x = units/tradeVolume of the market):
  BUY leg:  dP/P = +0.0499 * x   (R2=0.33, n=505) — buying one full tradeVolume moves the ask ~+5%
  SELL leg: dP/P = -0.0152 * x   (R2=0.14, n=381) — selling one full tradeVolume moves the bid ~-1.5%
OUT-OF-SAMPLE (70/30 time split): model MAE 0.0121 vs snapshot 0.0235 on buys (+49% better); 0.0050 vs 0.0083 on sells (+40% better).

RECOVERY (6,300 organic decay pairs from market_price_history, own-trade intervals EXCLUDED):
  pooled deviation half-life ~520 MIN (~8.7h); by tradeVolume tier: tv<=40 ~339min, 41-80 ~663min, 81-240 ~1681min.
  => KEY CORRECTION: compressed lanes do NOT recover in ~25-30min (that earlier anecdote reflected other traffic refilling a busy lane, not organic reversion). Organic mean-reversion is WEAK — a lane you hammer stays compressed for HOURS.

## WIRE-IN (two changes to the ranker)
1. EFFECTIVE SPREAD for a candidate lane given plannedUnits: buy_eff = ask*(1 + 0.050*(plannedUnits/tv)/2); sell_eff = bid*(1 - 0.015*(plannedUnits/tv)/2)  (half-terminal-impact approximates the average fill price across the tranche). Rank on (sell_eff - buy_eff), not the snapshot spread.
2. LANE COOLDOWN LEDGER: after we trade U units on a lane, carry a compression debt = (0.050+0.015)*(U/tv) on that lane's expected spread, decaying as exp(-dt/750min) (per-tier tau if preferred). The ranker subtracts the live debt when re-ranking, so hulls naturally ROTATE to fresh lanes instead of stacking a compressed one and re-discovering the compression the expensive way (each wasted leg burns API budget + travel).

## EXPECTED EFFECT + ACCEPTANCE
Fixes the measured pathologies: 28% ADV_CIRCUITRY spread erosion from stacking; the 20x per-hull $/hr spread (laggards on compressed/filler lanes). ACCEPTANCE: (a) harness/replay — ranker with model predicts realized next-leg prices better than snapshot ranker on held-out telemetry (reproduce the 40-49% MAE gain); (b) live — median per-hull tour $/hr rises and the worst-hull/best-hull ratio narrows; no regression in total net/hr.
REFIT-PER-ERA: coefficients are era-3-derived; the FORM is stable. Refit needs ~1 day of telemetry (consecutive-leg pairs); keep coefficients as config, not constants.
Related: sp-lk9x (same delivered-formula pattern), sp-zbe6 (unserved-lane gate), tour ranker rankLanesByCircuitRate. Origin: Admiral-approved ML program, economy-analyst derivation 2026-07-16.

title: Autosizer heavy bought at a far shipyard is orphaned off-circuit — adopt idle trade hulls at ANY system (or reposition-on-buy)
description:
The fleet autosizer buys heavies AT the heavy-freighter shipyard (a far, off-circuit system), but the trade_fleet_coordinator's adoption/reposition scope only reaches idle trade hulls already ON the circuit — so every autosizer-bought heavy is ORPHANED at the yard, trade-dedicated but never adopted into a tour, earning zero until a human notices and hand-launches a tour. This orphans the exact asset the heavy-acquisition path exists to produce.

The autosizer bought 2 heavies (TORWIND-6C @2.44M, TORWIND-6D @2.43M) at X1-UF64-AX2B — the only known SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER yard, deep off-circuit. ## ROOT CAUSE
The trade_fleet_coordinator's maybeReposition (idle hull with no local lane flies <=12 jumps to a >=25k-margin system) lives INSIDE an active tour container — a hull must already be ADOPTED into a tour to reach it. The coordinator's pickup/sweep scope for adopting idle trade hulls is scoped to the circuit's neighborhood, so a trade-dedicated idle hull sitting at a far yard (UF64) is outside pickup range and never gets a tour launched for it. The autosizer buys where the yard IS (far), but nothing hands the resulting hull to the trade engine. Producer (autosizer) and consumer (coordinator) have a coverage gap between them.

## REQUIREMENT
An autosizer-purchased trade hull must reach the trade engine automatically from wherever it was bought — no captain in the loop. Pick ONE:
1. ADOPT-ANYWHERE (preferred): the trade_fleet_coordinator sweeps trade-dedicated idle hulls at ANY system (incl. far yards) and launches a continuous tour-run for each. The tour's own planner (which already considers the hull's system + fresh gate neighbors — it found IRON at UF64) trades it and, via continuous re-plan, migrates it toward the circuit. Simplest: drop the proximity filter on the idle-hull sweep.
2. REPOSITION-ON-BUY: the autosizer, immediately after a heavy purchase at an off-circuit yard, launches a tour-run (or a reposition) on the new hull so it's never left bare-idle. Couples acquisition to activation.
3. Both (defense in depth): reposition-on-buy for immediacy + adopt-anywhere as the safety net for any hull that slips through.

When a tour is launched on these hulls (manual CLI `workflow tour-run`, and per the config.yaml trade_fleet comment the coordinator's 0-default too), the working-capital reserve resolves to the tour's 50000 DEFAULT, not the fleet-standard 1M (6D logged: "working-capital reserve resolved to the 50000 default (launch config carried no reserve) - every buy is floored at 50000"). ## IMPACT
- Activates every autosizer-bought heavy automatically: the heavy-acquisition path the Admiral just funded (150 fleet ceiling, heavy-yard hunt) produces hulls that TRADE instead of sitting as dead capital. A 2.4M heavy earning 276k/tour vs 0.

Systemic to the heavy-acquisition path: EVERY heavy the autosizer buys is bought at a far yard (that's where heavy yards are) and will orphan the same way. title: Autosizer stop-buy guard mismeasures saturation: 'realized_rate DECLINING' blocks buys from hull CONCENTRATION, not true absorption — must condition on unserved-lane inventory (blocked a valid 2.43M heavy despite 28 unserved lanes)
description:
The fleet autosizer's marginal-return guard (realized_rate) treats a DECLINING aggregate realized tour-rate as an absorption-saturation stop-buy signal. It is measuring the wrong thing: the aggregate rate of CURRENTLY-FLOWN lanes declines when the fleet PILES onto a few fat lanes and compresses them — that is a hull-placement/concentration effect, NOT a true opportunity limit. When profitable UNSERVED lanes exist, the NEXT hull flies a FRESH lane at fresh economics, not the compressed aggregate — so the declining-rate stop-buy blocks profitable capacity.

## LIVE INCIDENT (2026-07-15, player-3)
Heavy-freighter yard found (X1-UF64-AX2B, 2.43M, reachable). Autosizer heavy buy ran; EVERY guard passed (price/treasury/payback/ceiling-now-150) EXCEPT realized_rate[BLOCK: marginal 70206 but rate DECLINING => 'absorption saturating — stop-buy']. Simultaneously demand[shortfall = 28-31 unserved profitable lanes]. So the guard blocked a valid buy while the SAME system reported 28-31 profitable-but-unflown lanes.

## ECONOMY-ANALYST ADJUDICATION (evidence, ledger + tour_leg_telemetry, last 90m)
1. CONCENTRATION not saturation: fleet sold into only 6 of 32 systems; 40 of ~57 legs on DF86+GP32 alone; ~26 systems COMPLETELY UNFLOWN. The 28-31 unserved lanes are real.
2. Compression is LOCAL: ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY still sells ~6,700/u (GP32 6,694 / DF86 6,746) — not saturated.
3. EMPIRICAL: adding 3 lights ~2h earlier RAISED net ~1.39M (1M/hr -> 2.1M/hr). Added capacity finds fresh profit — measured, not solver-optimism. A saturated market would have diluted.

## ROOT CAUSE
The stop-buy uses trailing AGGREGATE realized-rate of flown lanes as a proxy for 'will the next hull be profitable'. Those diverge when unserved profitable inventory exists: aggregate declines (concentration) while the marginal (next-unserved-lane) rate stays high.

## REQUIRED FIX
Condition the declining-rate stop-buy on UNSERVED-LANE INVENTORY (the signal ALREADY EXISTS — sp-4ewi's ProfitableLaneReader.UnservedLaneCount):
- If UnservedLaneCount > threshold (profitable lanes sit unflown): a declining aggregate realized-rate must NOT trigger stop-buy. The next hull will fly an unserved lane. Proceed to buy (other guards permitting).
- Fire the declining-rate stop-buy ONLY when unserved-lane inventory is low/near-zero (genuine saturation: hulls have spread to most lanes AND rate is still declining).
- Better marginal estimate (optional, stronger): gate on the EXPECTED rate of the next-ranked UNSERVED lane (from the solver's ranked list), not the trailing aggregate of flown lanes.

## ACCEPTANCE
- With N unserved profitable lanes (N > threshold), a declining aggregate realized-rate does NOT block the buy; the autosizer proceeds (other guards permitting). The 2.43M-heavy scenario (28 unserved) PASSES.
- Stop-buy on declining rate fires ONLY when unserved-lane inventory is low/zero.
- Regression: a genuinely saturated market (few unserved lanes + declining rate) STILL stops buying.
- Decision log shows the unserved-lane count alongside the rate so the gate is auditable.

Related: sp-1txd (autosizer), sp-4ewi (heavy seam + ProfitableLaneReader.UnservedLaneCount — the signal to condition on). Blocks correct heavy/light auto-scaling into the 26 unflown systems. Origin: captain consult st-wisp-ttrdr + economy-analyst adjudication st-wisp-zuqom, 2026-07-15.

title: Probe buyer is MOVEMENT-FREE (buys where an idle hull sits, not the cheapest yard) — spikes home yard 4x (A2 20k->86k) AND defeats sp-hej4 frontier buying; navigate to the cheapest reachable probe-yard
description:
The probe purchaser is MOVEMENT-FREE: it buys using an idle hull ALREADY SITTING at a probe-yard (cheapest among those), instead of NAVIGATING a hull to the genuinely-cheapest / nearest-target yard. Idle hulls cluster at the home hub, so this both spikes the home yard's price 4x AND fully defeats sp-hej4 target-aware buying. Make the buyer select + navigate to the cheapest reachable probe-yard.

## PROBLEM (measured 2026-07-15, from live transactions)
resolveBuyerAtProbeYard scans idle undedicated hulls for one sitting at a probe-selling yard and buys there. Consequences:
- CONCENTRATION + PRICE SPIRAL: 48 of 66 probe buys (73%) landed at X1-VB74-A2, driving its price 20,670 -> 86,497 (4.2x) as repeated buys depleted its supply to SCARCE — while sibling home yard X1-VB74-C39 sat at 37,329 (half price) and frontier yards far cheaper. Avg paid: A2 46,191 vs C39 30,856. ~700k overpaid across the A2 buys.
- sp-hej4 DEFEATED: on a buy targeting frontier post QA71, X1-QA71-F11F was a SCANNED probe-yard selling probes at 20,670 (AT the target, no relay needed) — yet the buyer bought at home A2 for 86,497 (4.2x) and relayed the probe out, because no idle hull happened to be sitting at QA71. The frontier log even labels the buy 'at X1-QA71-F11F' (the target) while the transaction shows the money left at X1-VB74-A2.

## ROOT CAUSE
The movement-free constraint ('buy where an idle hull already is') short-circuits BOTH price-shopping AND sp-hej4's target-awareness. proximal_yard_hop_penalty can't help — it only ranks among yards that ALREADY have a pre-positioned idle buyer, and those are all at the home hub. A cheaper/nearer yard with no idle hull parked at it is never considered.

## REQUIREMENT
Select the genuinely-cheapest REACHABLE probe-yard by (live price x supply-state x relay/distance cost) and NAVIGATE a hull to it — do not merely buy where a hull is parked. One change fixes the price-spiral and activates sp-hej4's frontier buying.

## DESIGN
1. CANDIDATES = all KNOWN probe-selling yards (shipyard_inventory) reachable within a hop budget — home + frontier + target-adjacent — NOT just yards that currently have an idle buyer.
2. SCORE each = live_price + relay_cost(hops to where the probe is needed) − supply_headroom. Reuse sp-hej4's proximal_yard_hop_penalty for the price/distance tradeoff, but evaluated over ALL candidate yards.
3. NAVIGATE a hull to the winning yard (a probe relay is cheap vs a 4x price premium). Fall back to home only when NO cheaper reachable yard is known. Re-check live price at the dock before buying.
4. SUPPLY-DEPLETION AWARENESS / LOAD-BALANCE: repeated buys at one yard raise its price (LIMITED->SCARCE). Spread buys, or stop buying at a yard once its price exceeds a sibling by a margin, so we never spiral one market to 4x.
5. Applies to BOTH probe buyers (freshness sizer sp-orgp + frontier expansion sp-8w89) — shared resolver.

## IMPACT
- Kills the home-yard price spiral (A2 20k->86k): buy at 20-37k, not 86k.
- Activates sp-hej4 frontier buying (buy AT the target frontier yard, e.g. QA71 @ 20k, zero relay) — the feature currently NEVER fires.
- Cuts probe capex 2-4x per probe + removes needless home->frontier relay latency.

## RELATED
sp-hej4 (target-aware buying — this movement-free resolver is exactly WHY it never fires), sp-42ow/sp-rhju (shipyard scan — supplies the yard prices; more frontier yards scanned = more cheap candidates; QA71/DA78 already scanned and cheap), sp-8w89 (frontier expansion — owns the buyer), sp-orgp (freshness sizer — shares it).

## PRIORITY P1
Live 4.2x overpayment on every probe (86k vs 20-37k), ~700k already overpaid, and it fully defeats a shipped feature (sp-hej4). High-frequency spend path — the fix pays for itself immediately.

sp-orgp sizes against a single hard max-age SLA (sla_seconds=3600): EVERY market must be <1h or the system "breaches." 18/22 systems breach — but the breaches are the STALE TAIL, not the bulk. Age percentiles (minutes):
  VB74 (151 mkts): P50=21, P90=106, max=106   (half very fresh; tail flat ~106)
  DA78 (105):      P50=22, P90=62,  P99=167, max=167   (90% under 62min = basically at target; top 1% drags max to 167)
  DF86 (75, arb core): P50=3, P90=41, max=54   (fully fresh)
  KN83 (70):       P50=57, P90=62,  max=137
  GP32 (70):       P50=3,  P90=63,  max=123
The max-age target forces chasing the stalest 1-10% — the hardest and least valuable markets to keep fresh (low-traffic stragglers, blocked by travel / probe reassignment). This inflated freshness demand to 68 probes (buying at 75k+ each), draining the shared satellite pool and starving the frontier DEPTH push (sp-iopd) — while arb THRIVES anyway (+2.1M this session) on the already-fresh bulk. We are "18/22 breaching" a target that arb does not need and big systems cannot physically hit.

## REQUIREMENT
Size to a PERCENTILE of the measured age distribution, not the max. Tolerate the tail. Align freshness spend with the fresh bulk that arb actually uses, and release the freed probes to the pool.

## DESIGN
1. TARGET = (percentile, age) instead of (max, age). Default P90 <= 3600s (tunable). Optional richer DISTRIBUTION target — a small curve, e.g. P50<=1200s, P90<=3600s, P99<=14400s ("most markets very fresh, tail allowed to lag"). Ship the single (P90, SLA) point first; the curve is the extension.
2. CLOSED-LOOP on the MEASURED percentile: each tick, compute the actual per-system age percentile from market_data.last_updated (directly computable via percentile_cont). Add probes if measured P_target > target age; release if comfortably under. Empirical feedback, not an open-loop model estimate.
3. TAIL EXPLICITLY TOLERATED: markets beyond the target percentile do NOT drive probe demand. This is the cost saving — stop paying for stragglers. Bounds big-system demand to the achievable P90 instead of the unachievable max (DA78 P90=62 vs max=167).
4. PER-SYSTEM independent targets; the percentile makes big (VB74 151, DA78 105) and small systems size sanely to the same profile.
5. VALUE-WEIGHTED PERCENTILE (key extension): compute the percentile over trade-VOLUME/VALUE-weighted markets so a high-value stale market pulls the percentile but a low-traffic straggler in the tail does not. Keeps the arb core (VB74/DF86/GP32) tight while the peripheral frontier lags cheaply — the correct allocation.
6. AUTO-RELEASE the freed probes to the shared pool (-> frontier depth) via the existing release hysteresis (sp-iupr). Percentile sizing frees a large slug at once.

## EXPECTED IMPACT (from the measured data)
Most systems' P90 is already near/under 1h (DA78 62, KN83 62, DF86 41, GP32 63) while their max is 120-170. A P90 target drops aggregate demand from ~68 toward ~30-40 probes => releases ~25-30 probes to the depth push, with negligible arb impact (arb already thrives on the fresh bulk; the arb-core systems stay tight under value-weighting).

## TUNABLES

Fold sp-tor9 into this), sp-iopd (freshness-vs-frontier probe allocation — percentile sizing cuts freshness demand, directly easing the contention that starves depth), sp-iupr (release hysteresis — sheds the probes percentile sizing frees), sp-dc50 (expansion — new market systems enter percentile sizing automatically).

## PRIORITY P1
Fixes the freshness mis-optimization (chasing a tail-dominated target while arb is fine) AND frees ~25-30 probes for the active depth campaign. Supersedes the hard-SLA premise of sp-tor9 (P1). High leverage on both the freshness and depth fronts.

title: Waypoint cache is per-system-scoped: cross-system waypoint lookups fail-closed ('not found in cache for system X') instead of resolving/auto-syncing — stalls contract sourcing AND frontier probe-buying
description:
The daemon's waypoint cache is scoped PER-SYSTEM. When an operation targets a waypoint in a DIFFERENT system than the ship's current system, the lookup (keyed by the ship's current system) misses and the operation FAILS-CLOSED instead of resolving the waypoint's real system (its symbol encodes it) or auto-syncing it from the API. Recurring across subsystems; currently the ceiling on the frontier depth campaign and the cause of a live contract stall.

## ERROR SIGNATURE (identical both times)
"failed to navigate ...: waypoint <WP> not found in cache for system <SYS>. Destination waypoint is missing from waypoint cache. Please sync waypoints from API"

## OCCURRENCES (2 subsystems, recurring — measured 2026-07-15)
1. CONTRACT SOURCING (live incident, related sp-ue1s): contract worker on TORWIND-E (physically in X1-DF86) tried to navigate to the home copper source X1-VB74-J58; cache scoped to DF86 => "waypoint X1-VB74-J58 not found in cache for system X1-DF86" => worker failed, was reclaimed, re-selected, failed again => 80-minute COPPER_ORE->H51 stall (net -90k).
2. FRONTIER PROBE-BUYING (sp-hej4 target-aware buy, ongoing): frontier tried to buy a probe at a frontier shipyard X1-KN83-AF7C while resolving from X1-VB74 => "waypoint X1-KN83-AF7C not found in cache for system X1-VB74" => buy fail-closed => frontier can't grow its probe pool at the edge (supply 0 idle, depth demand unmet). Repeats every cycle (18:26:59, 18:28:00, ...).

## ROOT
Waypoint symbols self-encode their system (X1-KN83-AF7C -> system X1-KN83). The cache lookup requires the waypoint to already be in the CURRENT ship's system cache, rather than resolving the waypoint to ITS OWN system's cache or fetching it. The error text ("Please sync waypoints from API") shows a sync path exists but is NOT invoked automatically on a cross-system miss — it just fails.

## FIX
On a waypoint-cache miss where the target is in a different system: (a) parse the waypoint's own system from its symbol and look up THAT system's cache; and/or (b) auto-sync the target system's waypoints from the API on-demand (bounded + cached, once per system), then retry — rather than fail-closing. Apply in the SHARED navigation/RouteExecutor + shipyard-buy paths so BOTH consumers (contract sourcing, frontier probe-buy) are fixed by one change. Keep fail-closed only as the last resort AFTER a sync attempt, not before.

## IMPACT
- CEILING on the active frontier DEPTH campaign: the depth push (breadth=1, 6 pathfinders, cap 60) can dispatch its current probes but cannot BUY more near the frontier edge because the target-aware buy fail-closes here. Depth throttles as soon as the near-pool is consumed.
- Caused a live 80-min contract stall + net -90k (occurrence 1).
- Systemic: ANY cross-system navigate/buy is fragile. One fix unblocks multiple subsystems and hardens all cross-gate operations.

## RELATED
sp-ue1s (contract home-scoping — home-scoping AVOIDS triggering this bug for contracts, but the cache defect itself remains for any legitimate cross-system op), sp-hej4 (target-aware probe buying — its cross-system buy is the current victim), sp-rjgr / sp-8w89 (frontier depth — throttled by the failed edge-buys), sp-iopd (freshness-vs-frontier probe allocation — the frontier's probe supply is capped by THIS bug on top of the pool contention; both must clear for depth to be fully fed).

## PRIORITY P1
Blocks active strategic work (frontier depth probe supply at the edge) AND caused a live financial incident (contract stall, -90k). Recurring across >=2 subsystems with an identical signature. One shared-path fix; high leverage.
notes: SHIPPED 9291b302 (deployed). Cross-system navigate resolves+auto-syncs the dest system graph (cache-first, force-refresh once, API-frugal) then delegates the physical move to CrossSystemRouter.RepositionToWaypoint (gate BFS) at the shared NavigateRouteHandler — fixes BOTH contract sourcing (the -90k stall) + frontier edge probe-buy (depth-campaign ceiling). Additive/inert (WithCrossSystemRouter, no-router=byte-identical fail-closed). title: Frontier breadth-vs-depth BALANCE: reserve a tunable slice of scout capacity for DEPTH pathfinders that punch to the deepest-reachable ring (today pure-BFS breadth — 84 hop-1 vs 1 hop-2 ever, never reaches heavy-yard depth)
description:
The frontier expansion coordinator (sp-8w89) does PURE BREADTH-FIRST search and has NO depth policy — so it never reaches the deep frontier where a heavy-freighter yard would be. Add an explicit, tunable BREADTH-vs-DEPTH balance so a reserved slice of scout capacity always punches OUTWARD to the deepest-reachable ring.

## PROBLEM (measured live 2026-07-15)
The coordinator scores all virgin systems and picks by score; all hop-1 virgins score equal, and a hop-2 system only becomes a candidate AFTER its hop-1 parent is charted. That is textbook BFS: it charts ring N entirely before ring N+1 is reachable. With scout throughput (~5 concurrent frontier posts) SMALLER than the ring width (12+ hop-1 virgins), the first ring never drains, so the next ring never opens. Evidence: 84 'hops=1' declarations vs exactly 1 'hops=2' EVER; the deepest resource we could ever find is one hop out. This is not churn (verified: FU43 chosen 5x but NEVER visited = throughput latency; SH23 actively charting) — it is a structural absence of any depth drive. Pure BFS cannot self-correct into depth; it must be told to.

## WHY IT MATTERS
The frontier's strategic PURPOSE right now is to find a heavy/bulk-freighter yard for the autosizer's live 14-heavy shortfall (sp-1txd). A heavy yard, if gate-reachable at all, is plausibly at hop-2/3/4+ — exactly the depth we NEVER reach. Breadth (markets) still matters for arb economies, so the answer is not "go depth-only" — it is to BALANCE the two deliberately.

## DESIGN
1. CAPACITY SPLIT (the balance knob): reserve a tunable fraction of scout capacity for DEPTH vs BREADTH (default ~65/35 breadth/depth; live-tunable via `spacetraders tune`).
2. BREADTH slice = current behavior: BFS ring-fill for market coverage (arb economies live in breadth; keep it).
3. DEPTH slice = "pathfinder" probes. Each cycle a pathfinder beelines to the DEEPEST-REACHABLE virgin system along a DISTINCT bearing/branch, charts its jump gate (persisting gate_edges -> reveals the next ring), and repeats outward — punching deep holes rather than waiting for the near ring to drain. It PENETRATES (does not stop to fully scan every near market — the breadth slice fills in behind it). Multiple pathfinders take DIFFERENT branches: a heavy yard could be in any direction, so never bet all depth on one corridor. Bound by a max-depth cap.
4. OBJECTIVE-AWARE BIAS: when a deep-resource objective is unmet — autosizer heavy shortfall > 0 AND no heavy yard known (today's exact state) — auto-shift the split TOWARD depth until a yard is found or max-depth is hit; relax back toward breadth when markets are the priority. Depth effort tracks actual strategic need instead of being static.
5. DIRECTION HEURISTIC: with no signal where a heavy yard is, fan pathfinders across the widest-angle DISTINCT branches from the current edge. As shipyard_inventory (sp-42ow) accumulates, optionally bias bearings toward regions more likely to hold heavy yards (larger systems / certain types); default is blind fan-out.

## COUPLINGS
- THROUGHPUT (sp-iupr): the depth slice needs spare probes to move. Today the freshness sizer HOLDS 33 probes vs demand ~19 = 14 surplus never released (sp-iupr auto-release not firing). A depth slice with no free hulls does nothing — so this composes with sp-iupr: freed probes feed both slices. Fixing depth-policy WITHOUT freeing probes just starves breadth to pay for depth.
- OFF-GATE ESCALATION (sp-4imi): this bead balances depth WITHIN the gate-reachable graph. Once the depth pathfinders EXHAUST the gate-reachable frontier and STILL find no heavy yard, that exhaustion is the clean trigger to escalate to the warp explorer (sp-4imi) for OFF-GATE reach. Sequence: saturate gate-depth here first, then go off-gate there.

## TUNABLES
breadth:depth ratio; #pathfinders; max-depth cap; objective-bias aggressiveness — all via the live tune mechanism (sp-vwek), no restart.

## RELATED
sp-8w89 (frontier expansion coordinator — this is a new policy on it), sp-dc50 (expansion charting — pathfinders drive the ring-by-ring gate charting harder), sp-iupr (probe over-hold — HARD coupling: frees the hulls the depth slice needs), sp-1txd (autosizer — its heavy shortfall is the objective-aware depth trigger), sp-42ow (shipyard scan — pathfinders scan deep yards; supplies the heavy-yard find that ends the depth push), sp-4imi (warp explorer — the OFF-GATE escalation once gate-depth is exhausted), sp-cxpq (scout reconciler — relays probes to the pathfinder targets).

## PRIORITY P1
The frontier's core strategic purpose (reach depth -> find a heavy yard for the live 14-heavy shortfall) is currently WHOLLY UNMET (1 hop-2 ever). Not a daily-ops blocker, but it blocks the entire heavy-hull unlock. Build alongside sp-iupr (its throughput dependency).

title: Depot topology over-commits the ENTIRE contract-worker pool to hub pins — leaves ZERO home general-sourcing workers for UNBUFFERED-good contracts (must reserve N home workers)
description:
STRUCTURAL ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-07-15 contract stall (distinct from sp-ue1s, which is the home-locality band-aid). The depot topology (sp-u9xa/sp-9j9c) converted the flexible general contract-worker pool into hulls PINNED to hubs as depot-delivery, on the assumption that co-located buffers deliver every contract locally. That assumption is FALSE for unbuffered goods: a contract whose good is not staged at a hub still needs a general SOURCING worker to fly buy it — and the depot model left NONE.

## EVIDENCE (live census, player-3, 2026-07-15 ~16:45Z)
24 haulers total:
- depot-delivery: 9 (10,15,18,1B,1C,6,8,9,F) — IDLE, no container, pinned at hubs, and EXCLUDED from the contract grab (sp-3l64 exclusion, working as designed).
- trade/arb: 6 (16,17,5,7,B,C). warehouse: 4. stocker: 4. contract-work: 1 (E, scavenged from FOREIGN DF86).
=> ZERO undedicated home general-sourcing workers.
Result: COPPER_ORE->H51 (unbuffered good) sat 0/60 for 80 min. Nine idle hulls sat at home, all depot-delivery-locked and thus untouchable by the contract coordinator, which then reached across the gate for E.

## THE HOLE
The depot design pinned the WHOLE pool to hubs. Buffered-good contracts deliver from co-located stock (great). Unbuffered/remote-good contracts have no worker at all — the pool that would source them was converted to hub pins + excluded from the grab. The exclusion that keeps delivery hulls on their hubs is the SAME exclusion that starves general sourcing.

## REQUIRED (either/both)
1. RESERVE a home general-sourcing worker pool (config: min_home_contract_workers, e.g. >=6 per Admiral) that is NEVER converted to depot-delivery pins — kept undedicated + home + available to the contract coordinator's grab for unbuffered/remote-good contracts.
2. TEMPORARY UN-PIN: allow an idle depot-delivery hull to un-pin, source an unbuffered contract, and RETURN to its hub — so idle hub hulls aren't dead weight when a general contract needs sourcing.
Depot topology sizing (sp-9j9c / autosizer / st-7zk) must SUBTRACT the reserved home-worker floor before pinning hulls to hubs — never pin the last general workers.

## ACCEPTANCE
- After applying a depot topology, >= min_home_contract_workers undedicated home haulers remain available to the contract coordinator.
- An unbuffered-good contract is sourced by a home general worker (or an un-pinned idle depot hull), NOT starved and NOT a foreign-system grab.
- Regression: buffered-good contracts still deliver from co-located depot hulls.

title: sp-orgp follow-up: freshness sizer over-provisions — (1) telemetry-starved systems stuck at seed default (ZY16 3mkts=8), (2) no auto-release of surplus probes on slack (demand 27->25, supply 27->32, retired=0)

ANY post whose probes don't cycle stays permanently over-sized.
FIX options: (a) make the seed default scale with market count instead of a flat 8; and/or (b) if a post hasn't accumulated telemetry within N cycles, fall back to a conservative market-count-based estimate rather than the seed; and/or (c) ensure a manned post's probe actually runs its scan loop so telemetry is produced.

title: Shipyard scouting + heavy-hull auto-detection: scan shipyards during scouting, persist ship-type availability, surface nearest heavy/bulk-freighter yard to the autosizer (sp-4ewi is fail-closed for lack of this signal)
description:
Build SHIPYARD SCOUTING + HEAVY-HULL AUTO-DETECTION: as the frontier/scout explores each system, scan its SHIPYARDS (not just markets), persist per-shipyard ship-type availability, and expose a "nearest reachable heavy-hull yard" signal that the heavy-hull autosizer consumes to locate and buy. Fully automatic — no operator ever hand-hunts shipyards.

## PROBLEM (today)
Scouting scans MARKETS only. There is NO shipyard table in the daemon DB at all, so there is zero automated knowledge of where heavy/bulk freighters are sold. The heavy-hull autosizer (sp-4ewi / sp-1txd) is fail-closed — not because its buy logic is broken, but because no reachable heavy-hull yard is KNOWN and nothing discovers one. Confirmed manually this session: every shipyard in the 1-2 hop reach (VB74/DF86/SB42 + AZ25/GP32/RP9/SH23/SP39/XJ34) is light-class only; a heavy yard, if it exists, is deeper, and finding it requires exploring + querying each system's shipyard — which nothing automates. Operator had to do it by hand and it goes stale immediately.

## REQUIREMENT
When the scout visits a system (it already goes there for markets), it must ALSO scan that system's shipyards, record which ship types each sells (with prices), persist it, and surface a heavy-hull availability signal. Auto-detect + auto-feed. As the frontier expands, new systems' shipyards are scanned automatically and any heavy yard enters the signal with no operator action.

## SPEC
1. SHIPYARD SCAN piggybacked on the scout tour: for each SHIPYARD waypoint in a visited system, fetch shipTypes (+ prices when a hull is present). Do it on the same visit that scans markets — no extra probe trips.
2. PERSIST a shipyard-inventory store (new — none exists): {system, waypoint, ship_type, price, supply, last_scanned, era_id}. Keyed like market_data; refreshable on the same freshness cadence.
3. HEAVY-HULL DETECTION: flag shipyards selling a configurable "heavy" class set (default SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER, SHIP_BULK_FREIGHTER; make the list config so it survives type additions).
4. EXPOSE a signal for the autosizer: nearest reachable heavy-hull yard(s) = {system, waypoint, hull types available, price, hop-distance from anchor}. Ranked by hop-distance then price.
5. FEED sp-4ewi / sp-1txd: the heavy-hull autosizer, when heavy demand exists (its unserved-trade-lane signal), routes the purchase to the nearest known heavy yard from this signal — closing the fail-closed gap. The buyer stays guarded (treasury %, spend cap, cooldown, fleet cap).
6. AUTO-DETECT WITH EXPANSION: every newly-explored system (sp-dc50) has its shipyards scanned as it's scouted; a heavy yard appearing anywhere in the reachable graph enters the signal automatically.
7. MILESTONE SURFACE (optional but useful): emit an event / mail when the FIRST heavy-hull yard is detected, since it flips a previously-impossible capability (heavy acquisition) to possible.

## WHY THIS ORDER
Frontier expansion (sp-dc50, live) reaches new systems; this feature turns each visit into shipyard knowledge; the autosizer (sp-4ewi) then acquires the heavy the moment a yard is in range. The three together make "buy a heavy hull" a self-driving outcome instead of a manual expedition.

title: Market-freshness auto-sizer: standing scout tours that AUTO-RESIZE + AUTO-BUY probe capacity to hold every market under a freshness SLA (<1h)
description:
Build a MARKET-FRESHNESS AUTO-SIZER: a standing coordinator that keeps every scanned market's data fresh within a configurable SLA by auto-sizing AND auto-buying probe capacity — the same way the frontier expansion coordinator (sp-8w89) auto-sizes/buys for post coverage, but the demand signal is market-freshness, not post-coverage.

## PROBLEM (today)
Scout posts are 1-probe-each and sweep_once. Freshness scales AGAINST market count: one probe cannot re-walk a market-rich system inside the freshness window, so the most valuable systems are the most stale. Measured (player-3): VB74 = 26 markets with last-scan timestamps spanning ~8h; DF86 = 12 markets spanning ~6.5h — against an intended ~1h freshness. Coverage is complete, freshness is not. Nothing sizes probes to the freshness demand, and nothing keeps market-rich systems on continuous (standing) tours.

## REQUIREMENT
An automation that holds EVERY market under a freshness SLA, and that RESIZES AND BUYS ITS OWN CAPACITY. Operators must not hand-compute probe counts (they go stale the moment expansion adds a system). Properties:
1. Configurable freshness SLA (default: every market re-scanned <= 1h; per-system override allowed).
2. Standing (continuous re-scan) tours for market-bearing systems — sweep_once stays for pure discovery, but a system found to hold markets is promoted to a standing freshness post.
3. AUTO-SIZE probe capacity to the SLA, per system.
4. AUTO-BUY probes (guarded) when capacity is short; AUTO-RELEASE when slack.
5. AUTO-RESIZE continuously as the market set changes (frontier adds systems/markets; markets retire).

## SIZING MODEL (coordinator computes this itself, every tick — do NOT hardcode a probe count)
- Per system: required_probes = ceil( markets_in_system * per_market_cycle_seconds / sla_seconds ).
- per_market_cycle_seconds MUST be MEASURED empirically from live scan telemetry (rolling median of the intra-system market-to-market scan interval per probe), not a constant — travel time varies by system layout. Fall back to a seeded default only until enough telemetry exists.
- Split a rich system's markets across its N probes for parallel tours (each probe owns markets/N, cycles them within the SLA).
- Aggregate demand = sum of required_probes across all market-bearing systems.

## AUTO-BUY / AUTO-RELEASE (reuse the frontier guard stack, sp-8w89)
- Buy a probe when freshness_capacity_demand > available_scout_probes, subject to the SAME guards: price <= 25% live treasury, max-spend-per-cycle, purchase cooldown, max-probe-fleet. Count in-pool idle + in-flight probes as supply so it does not over-buy (the sp-njwy lesson).
- Release/return a probe to the general pool when a system's demand drops (markets retired, or comfortably under SLA with slack).

## CLOSED FEEDBACK LOOP (the real correctness signal)
- Each tick, measure ACTUAL freshness = max(now - last_scan) per system (the oldest market's age).
- If a system is breaching SLA, raise its required_probes (add capacity) even beyond the static model — the empirical age is ground truth, the model is the estimate.
- If a system is comfortably under SLA, allow release. This makes it self-correcting rather than open-loop.

## AUTO-RESIZE WITH EXPANSION
- New systems/markets discovered by the frontier (sp-dc50) enter the freshness demand automatically; the sizer buys to cover them.
- Marketless/retired systems drop out and free their probes.
- No operator action at any point — pointing the frontier outward should transparently grow scouting capacity.

## RELATED
sp-8w89 (frontier expansion auto-sizer — reuse its buy/guard machinery + demand-vs-supply pattern), sp-cxpq (scout-post coordinator — standing tours + relay), sp-dc50 (expansion that feeds new markets into this demand). This is the freshness analogue of the coverage auto-sizer.
notes: SHIPPED 3eb0aa5e (gate green, -race green, 15 .go +1908/-2). Closed-loop: SystemsFreshness census -> RequiredHulls/FreshnessRequiredHulls sizing (SLA+hysteresis) -> guarded auto-buy via extracted probebuy.GuardedProbeBuyer (25% treasury/fleet-cap/shared ledger cooldown vs frontier) -> release/retire w/ empty-census fail-safe. Boot-standing coordinator, auto-arms on deploy. Deferred: (1) scanner-id attribution for true per-probe cycle under multi-probe manning, (2) rolling-window measurement over market_price_history (adapter-only), (3) per-system SLA override config passthrough (map needs structured config), (4) frontier adoption of shared GuardedProbeBuyer. Follow-up bead filed.

title: Depot contract routing: source UNBUFFERED goods with the hull nearest the SOURCE, not the destination-pinned depot hull (~2x travel + leaves hub uncovered)
description:
EFFICIENCY BUG observed live (2026-07-15 ~05:00, player-3 X1-VB74). The depot routes an owned-destination contract to the destination hub's delivery hull and selects by proximity to the DESTINATION (sp-9j9c nearest-hull). That is correct ONLY when the good is in the hub buffer (deliver from stock, ~0 travel). When the good is NOT buffered, the good must be SOURCED, and destination-nearest selection is backwards.

## LIVE EVIDENCE
Contract: AMMONIA_ICE x50 -> J58 (owned destination). AMMONIA_ICE is NOT in J58 buffer (holds EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE/FIREARMS/ELECTRONICS/CLOTHING/MACHINERY). Only sources: B7/H53, ~750 units from J58.
- System chose T15 (J58 depot-delivery hull, sitting AT J58 = ~750 from source). Route: J58->source(~750 empty)->J58(~750 loaded) = ~1500 units.
- Hull 18 was sitting IDLE at H52 = ~0 distance from the ammonia source (H53). 1C idle at D41 (~38), 10 idle at G50 (~57). Any of these sources the good far cheaper.
- Optimal: 18->H53(~0)->J58(~750 loaded) = ~750 units. HALF the travel, on an already-idle hull.

This is a SYSTEMIC loss on every unbuffered-good depot contract, and it is a large part of why J58 averages ~30 min cycle-time (its contract goods are frequently unbuffered + remotely sourced).

## REQUIRED
When a depot/owned-destination contract's good is NOT available in the hub buffer, decouple SOURCING from delivery: select the sourcing hull by minimizing SOURCE->hub path (prefer the hull nearest the good's SOURCE market), rather than the destination-pinned depot hull. Keep the depot delivery hull at its hub for buffered-good contracts (also avoids leaving the hub uncovered for ~30 min). For buffered goods, current destination-nearest behavior is correct and must be preserved.

## ACCEPTANCE
- For an unbuffered-good owned-destination contract, the hull dispatched to source is the one nearest the source market (not a destination-pinned hull far from the source), measurably cutting total travel vs today.
- Buffered-good contracts still deliver from the co-located depot hull (no regression).
- Depot delivery hull is not pulled off its hub to source a good when a closer idle hull exists.

Related: sp-9j9c (nearest-hull selection, currently destination-only), sp-3l64 (depot-hull exclusion/atomicity), and the J58 buffer-whitelist gap (economy-analyst).
notes: SHIPPED + DEPLOYED 2026-07-15. Coordinator branches on SourcingPlan.Source (resolveContractHullRoute): SourceInventory (buffered) -> co-located depot hull; SourceMarket (unbuffered) -> UseDepotHull=false, falls through to SelectClosestShip against the source market (plan.Market). sp-3l64 exclusion means only a genuinely-idle non-depot hull is picked. routeContractViaDepot stays pure. ~halves travel on unbuffered depot contracts + keeps hub covered. 3 .go, tests RED->GREEN (3348 pass), -race clean. Deferred: any-in-system-warehouse buffered semantics; J58 buffer-whitelist (economy-analyst).

title: Frontier caps at hop-1: sweep charts markets but not jump gates, so no hop-2 adjacency (expansion queue empties, blocks reaching heavy-freighter yards)
description:
The frontier expansion coordinator caps out at hop-1 and never ranks a hop-2+ candidate — the gate-graph it walks never extends past the 1-hop systems, so expansion halts and the queue goes empty.

## SYMPTOM (player-3, 2026-07-15, daemon d78038f3)
Gate X1-VB74-I55 built; frontier scouted all four 1-hop virgin systems (DF86/JQ93/ZY16/NM33; SB42 skipped — already charted). Since then EVERY frontier cycle logs:
  `Frontier expansion cycle: demand 0 open slots + 0 queue, supply N idle probes, 5 frontier posts in flight — no purchase: no unmanned slot to serve`
The expansion QUEUE is 0 — no hop-2 system is ever ranked, even though expansion-max-hops defaults to 3 and the 1-hop systems' gates connect onward (e.g. X1-DF86-X16D has connections). Expansion is frozen at the 5 posts.

## LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (shipwright to confirm)
The frontier ranks only systems reachable over CHARTED gate connections. The scout sweep-once tours scan a system's MARKETS but do not chart its JUMP GATE waypoint — so the onward (hop-2) connections never enter the gate-graph the expansion scanner walks. No hop-2 adjacency => empty queue. To confirm: (1) does the sweep chart the jump-gate waypoint of the scouted system, and (2) does buildExpansionQueue's candidate source require the intermediate gate to be charted?

## IMPACT
Expansion is capped at 1 hop regardless of expansion-max-hops. Concretely this blocks acquiring a HEAVY freighter: no shipyard in the entire 1-hop reach (VB74 / DF86 / SB42 shipyards) sells heavy/bulk freighters — all light-class — so the heavy-hull autosizer (sp-4ewi) has nothing to buy, AND the frontier cannot reach the hop-2+ systems where a heavy yard would plausibly be. Frontier delivered its first ring and then went inert.

## FIX DIRECTION
Chart the frontier system's JUMP GATE as part of (or a follow-on to) the sweep, so its onward connections enter the gate-graph and the frontier can rank hop-2+ candidates. Alternatively, have the expansion scanner chart-on-demand the gate of each covered frontier system to grow the reachability graph one layer at a time. Either way: after a ring is scouted, the next ring must become visible.

## RELATED
sp-8w89 (frontier), sp-cxpq (scout), sp-njwy (hop-0 exclusion — just shipped).
notes:
CORRECTION (after probing the live gate graph): the 'sweep doesn't chart gates' hypothesis is WRONG. The hop-1 gates ARE charted — X1-DF86-X16D returns 6 onward connections, JQ93 5, ZY16 6, NM33 3, SB42 5 — and the hop-2 ring they reach (AZ25/GP32/RP9/SH23/SP39/XJ34, +uncharted GC87/HJ65/RV71) is largely charted too (shipyards queryable). So the graph is visible to hop-2.

REVISED ROOT CAUSE: the expansion queue is empty because every gate-reachable system in the ALREADY-CHARTED graph is either covered (the 5 posts) or charted-and-known (the hop-2 ring) — no VIRGIN system remains to post. The frontier does not push into the uncharted hop-3+ deep frontier: it only scouts systems reachable over already-charted gates and never charts the hop-2 gates onward to surface hop-3 virgin candidates. Expansion halts at the pre-charted boundary.

OPERATIONAL NOTE (why this bead was opened): there is NO heavy/bulk freighter shipyard anywhere in the hop-1 OR hop-2 reach — every yard across VB74/DF86/SB42 and AZ25/GP32/RP9/SH23/SP39/XJ34 is light-class only. Reaching hop-2 does NOT solve the heavy-hull need; a heavy yard (if it exists in this cluster) is hop-3+.

REVISED FIX: to keep expanding, the frontier must chart the gates of covered/charted frontier systems to extend reachability into the uncharted deep frontier (hop-3+), instead of stopping when the pre-charted graph has no virgin left. Retitle toward 'frontier does not extend past the initially-charted region.'
DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE (verified in code + daemon gate_edges table; supersedes both earlier notes):

The scanner (internal/adapters/expansion/adapters.go ExpansionCandidates) BFSes the PERSISTED gate adjacency (table gate_edges) from the anchor up to maxHops. TWO compounding gaps cap it at the first ring:

1) PARTIAL / ACCIDENTAL ADJACENCY PERSISTENCE. gate_edges has edges FROM X1-VB74 (5) and X1-DF86 (6, synced 02:09 after DF86's sweep) but ZERO from X1-JQ93 / X1-ZY16 / X1-NM33 / X1-SB42. Scouting a system's MARKETS does not persist its gate's edges — that only happened for DF86 (a probe incidentally hit its gate). So the BFS dead-ends at every hop-1 system except DF86; adjacency growth is accidental, not systematic.

2) THE charted-but-0-known-markets SKIP. buildExpansionQueue line ~631: 'if c.KnownMarkets==0 && !virgin { continue }', where virgin:=!c.Charted and (adapters.go:226) charted:=hasEdges||marketCount>0. The hop-2 systems the BFS reaches via DF86 have gate edges => Charted=true, but their markets were never scanned => KnownMarkets=0 => dropped as 'charted but marketless — nothing to scan.' They may well have markets AND shipyards (incl. a heavy yard) we just haven't scanned.

NET: frontier scouts the visible first ring then goes inert (queue 0). It neither extends the adjacency (gate charting isn't part of the sweep) nor scouts charted-but-unscanned systems.
