Full suite green. Deploying with sp-w3yd.

title: captain ship reserve CANNOT preempt a coordinator container claim — operator locked out of own hull, no --force/override
description:
SYMPTOM: A hull actively claimed by a coordinator container cannot be reclaimed by the captain. 'ship reserve' fails hard ('ship X is already assigned to container Y'). 'fleet unassign' clears the fleet DEDICATION but not the coordinator's live work-CLAIM (the hull keeps being routed by the coordinator). There is NO --force/--preempt flag on reserve and no commandeer/release-any verb. The operator has zero authority to take back their own ship.

CONCRETE (2026-07-13): TORWIND-8 holding 80 validated-real FAB_MATS was claimed by goods_factory-FAB_MATS-a6984433. The factory drags it around (F48 -> I55 -> J57) but cannot use it (a hull full of the factory's OWN OUTPUT product) and will not deliver it to the gate (not its job). Captain could not reclaim it: 'fleet unassign' reported success but the factory kept routing the hull; 'ship reserve' rejected outright with 'already assigned to container goods_factory-FAB_MATS-a6984433'. 80 real units stranded, no operational recovery except stopping the factory (which kills FAB production).

IMPACT: P1 control gap. When any coordinator misclaims a hull (see the factory-grabs-its-own-output assignment bug, sp-e55b/ko6x family), the captain cannot intervene. Cargo/capital strand with no recovery short of tearing down the coordinator. The captain is supposed to be the operator/owner — a coordinator claim should never lock the operator out.

EXPECTED: captain 'ship reserve' must PREEMPT a coordinator claim — either reserve always wins (operator authority), or add an explicit '--force' flag that revokes the coordinator's claim and reassigns the hull to the captain. The preempted coordinator must gracefully release and re-plan (no crash, no stranded task). Ideally 'fleet unassign' should also break the live work-claim, not just the dedication.

RELATED: factory claims a hull full of its own output then blocks reclaim (assignment bug, sp-e55b / sp-ko6x); sp-9ptm (on-hand deliver works only for drain-owned hulls).
close_reason: Merged (verified on main): captain 'ship reserve --force' preempts a coordinator claim via atomic single-writer transfer (PreemptForCaptain, SELECT FOR UPDATE, RULING #7) + 'fleet unassign --break-work-claim'; coordinator re-plans emergently (FindByContainer next tick); non-force path byte-identical (regression-locked); full suite + race green. KNOWN RESIDUAL (tracked in follow-up): preempt not yet fully deterministic — the un-migrated plain-Save ops (Navigate/Dock/Orbit/Refuel/SetFlightMode) can resurrect a claim via last-write-wins in a narrow load→save window on an actively-driven hull; becomes deterministic once those 5 verbs move to SaveWithRetry (sp-wa7c). Net: large improvement over total operator lockout, no regression, forward-compatible. NOT yet deployed — folding into the sp-pdb3 bounce.

title: ROOT: daemon ship-state cache is not written back after server-mutating ops (cargo/nav) — decrements silently lost, drives phantom-cargo desync
description:
ROOT-CAUSE bead behind the phantom-cargo/hang cascade (sp-j09q, sp-6zkg) and the desync-interim (sp-wa7c). The question 'why does the cache desync?' — evidence points to the daemon NOT writing back ship-state to its local cache after its own server-mutating operations (or the write-back being lost to optimistic-lock version conflicts).

SYMPTOM CLASS: after an operation changes ship state SERVER-side, the daemon's cached ship row keeps the OLD value until an explicit 'ship refresh' reconciles it:
  - Construction supply removes cargo server-side, but cached cargo stays at pre-delivery value -> phantom cargo (sp-j09q). Confirmed: server API returns 4219 'ship has 0 units' while cache shows 80/80; 'ship refresh' -> 0/80.
  - Reproduced on TORWIND-C (80 ADV, 19:46), TORWIND-F (80 FAB, 20:22/20:23), TORWIND-8 validated real vs phantom via refresh.

CORROBORATING SIGNAL: 'ship list' CACHE AGE showed 15h+ on ships that were actively navigating/trading (TORWIND-C, TORWIND-8) — i.e., the cache row's last-write is ancient despite continuous activity, consistent with operational code paths not updating the cache (or writes dropped).

HYPOTHESES (for triage):
  (a) The success path of mutating commands (construction supply, cargo buy/sell, navigate) updates server state but omits the local cache write-back.
  (b) The write-back IS attempted but lost to optimistic-concurrency version conflicts (ship_version_conflicts_total, sp-wa7c) — a concurrent writer with a stale version clobbers or drops the decrement.
  (c) Read path prefers a stale cache tier over the just-written value (launch-frozen/store-tier issue, cf. sp-aoy2 pattern).

WHY IT MATTERS: this single coherence gap cascades into phantom cargo (sp-j09q) -> re-delivery loop -> 4219 -> drain hang (sp-6zkg) -> gate stalls after ~every delivery. Fixing the root (guaranteed cache write-back / resync on every server-mutating op, conflict-safe) collapses the whole class.

ASK: identify which of (a)/(b)/(c) it is and guarantee post-mutation cache coherence — either write-back-after-success with conflict retry, or invalidate+resync the ship row after any server-mutating command. Add a metric/assertion when cached cargo != server cargo on a delivery attempt.

RELATED: sp-j09q (phantom symptom + re-delivery loop), sp-6zkg (hang consumer of the resulting 4219), sp-wa7c (desync/version-conflict interim), sp-aoy2 (launch-frozen read-tier precedent).
close_reason: Merged (drain-hang cascade killed): post-supply cargo write-back via SaveWithRetry (no phantom, root sp-v5d1→kills sp-j09q loop) + per-task timeout so drainOnce always returns & 4219→resync+defer instead of hang (sp-6zkg) + per-step logging. TDD RED→GREEN, full suite+race green, sp-9ptm/2me2/yfzi preserved. Deploying.

title: construction drain re-routes ship to re-deliver PHANTOM cargo after successful supply — cached cargo not decremented, loops on API 4219 until manual refresh
description:
SYMPTOM: After a ship successfully supplies material to a construction site, the daemon does NOT decrement that ship's cached cargo. The drain then sees the (phantom) cargo still aboard, re-routes the ship to the gate, and re-attempts delivery — which the server rejects (API 400, code 4219, 'cargo does not contain N units, ship has 0'). The ship loops: route -> arrive -> supply-fail -> re-route, burning fuel/API/cycles, and appears 'laden' in ship list while truly empty.

OBSERVED (2026-07-13, gate X1-VB74-I55):
  - 19:23:47 drain logged 'Supplied 80 ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY to construction site X1-VB74-I55' (gate ADV 120->200). This was TORWIND-C's delivery.
  - Cache never decremented: ship list continued showing TORWIND-C cargo 80/80 (CACHE AGE 15h — stale).
  - Drain repeatedly re-routed TORWIND-C to I55; each arrival: 19:46:33 'Construction supply failed for ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY: API error 400 {code 4219: Ship TORWIND-C cargo does not contain 80 unit(s) of ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY. Ship has 0 unit(s).}'. Looped ~23 min (19:23->19:46+), including opportunistic refuels and market scans each cycle.
  - 'spacetraders ship refresh --ship TORWIND-C' reconciled from server -> real cargo 0/80. Phantom cleared, hull freed.
  - Same signature appeared harmlessly for TORWIND-F at 19:24:18 (20 FAB_MATS already delivered at 19:22:55, retry failed 'ship has 0'); TORWIND-F happened to move on, TORWIND-C got stuck.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis): the construction-supply success path updates the site totals but does not write-back the delivering ship's decremented cargo to the daemon cache (or the write is lost to a version conflict). Next drain discovery reads stale cargo and treats the emptied hull as still-laden -> re-delivery loop. Related to the desync/version-conflict family (sp-wa7c).

EXPECTED: On successful construction supply, immediately decrement (or server-resync) the delivering ship's cached cargo so the drain does not re-route it for phantom cargo. Also: a supply failure with 4219 'ship has 0 units' should trigger a cargo resync + drop the phantom task, not silently re-loop.

IMPACT: P2 — no gate-count corruption or material loss (recoverable via refresh), but strands a drain hull in a futile fuel/API-burning loop during a gate build, and makes operations mis-read 'laden' hulls as pending deliveries (this exact confusion cost real diagnosis time). Compounds under the fresh sp-9ptm on-hand-deliver path.

REPRO: Have the drain deliver material from a hull to a construction site; observe the hull's cached cargo remains at pre-delivery value; observe the drain re-route it and fail with 4219 on the next tick.

RELATED: sp-9ptm (on-hand deliver — the path that now routes laden hulls), sp-wa7c (desync/version-conflict interim), sp-a5j7 (buy guard).
notes: ESCALATED P0-class (mail to shipwright): this phantom is the TRIGGER for sp-6zkg hang, not just wasted cycles. After a successful supply the delivering hull's cargo isn't decremented -> drain re-attempts -> 4219 -> sp-6zkg HANGS the drain. Reproduced twice: TORWIND-C 19:46 (ADV), TORWIND-F 20:23 (FAB). Gate hangs after ~every delivery. Fix jointly with sp-6zkg.
close_reason: Merged (drain-hang cascade killed): post-supply cargo write-back via SaveWithRetry (no phantom, root sp-v5d1→kills sp-j09q loop) + per-task timeout so drainOnce always returns & 4219→resync+defer instead of hang (sp-6zkg) + per-step logging. TDD RED→GREEN, full suite+race green, sp-9ptm/2me2/yfzi preserved. Deploying.

title: Re-enable scarcity-gated recursive production FLEET-WIDE (reverse sp-jav2 X1 depth-1 cap) — produce scarce intermediates, buy abundant, every factory + construction
description:
ADMIRAL DIRECTIVE 2026-07-13 (consciously overrides sp-jav2/sp-naw6): re-enable recursive supply-chain production for EVERY factory (goods_factory + construction), not just the gate. sp-jav2 (ef2281b8) capped fabricate recursion at depth-1 (market-buy inputs) per sp-naw6's 'raws are 0.29% of spend, market-buy always wins' ruling — but that premise fails for a SCARCE mid-tree intermediate (ELECTRONICS SCARCE system-wide → buying it depletes/explodes price → gate + any dependent factory stalls). sp-naw6's own flip conditions (zero-source input blocking a >150k/hr chain; input >400/u) are now firing on ELECTRONICS (~2595/u, no MODERATE+ source). Admiral overrides the analyst ruling.

MECHANISM (all exists, just capped — NOT deleted): SupplyChainResolver.shouldBuyGood already has StrategySmart = 'fabricate if SCARCE/LIMITED (and a factory exists), buy if HIGH/ABUNDANT' (supply_chain_resolver.go:342). buildTreeRecursive already recurses with a cycle/visited guard (:143,151). ProduceGood(Fabricate) already recurses node.Children. TWO things block it: (1) resolver DEFAULTS to StrategyPreferBuy (:42) — buys everything; (2) fabricate depth cap defaults to 1 (fabricate_depth.go:21) — buildTreeRecursive:181 force-buys any node at path depth>=maxDepth regardless of scarcity.

FIX (config-gated + reversible):
1. RAISE the fabricate depth cap default from 1 to a safe bound (e.g. 3) via config fabricate_max_depth (config/manufacturing.go:54); keep fabricate_depth_cap_disabled. The cap is a SAFETY backstop — StrategySmart is the real terminator (buys abundant → stops recursing; produces scarce → recurses).
2. ACTIVATE StrategySmart for the production paths (currently default prefer-buy). Confirm/route the strategy for goods_factory (via manufacturing_demand_finder SetStrategy:320) AND construction. Scarcity now gates recursion fleet-wide.
3. CONSTRUCTION path: the drain's constructionSourcingNode (run_construction_coordinator.go ~:363-432) hard-codes a ONE-LEVEL fabricate node and BYPASSES the resolver tree — so lifting the resolver cap alone does NOT help construction. Swap its fabricate branch to SupplyChainResolver.BuildDependencyTree (depth-capped via WithFabricateDepthCap from the pipeline's SupplyChainDepth), preserving the buy-final branch. (This folds in sp-3bza's drain half — sp-3bza's construction-self-FABRICATE framing was the wrong anti-pattern; this is scarcity-gated PRODUCTION via the resolver.)

SAFETY / RULINGS: StrategySmart only recurses into SCARCE goods with a factory (abundant goods still BUY — byte-identical to today for them). Cycle guard already prevents MACHINERY<->IRON loops. Depth bound caps runaway. #4 money guards on every buy leg unchanged. #1 an unsourceable/factoryless leg DEFERS/buys, never dies. #5 depth + strategy are config. #2 deterministic. Config-gated so it's dial-back-able.

ACCEPTANCE: a factory/gate whose scarce intermediate (e.g. ELECTRONICS from SILICON+COPPER) has a factory now PRODUCES it recursively instead of buying it scarce; an ABUNDANT intermediate is still bought (regression); recursion terminates at abundant goods + on cycles + at the depth bound; BOTH goods_factory and construction decompose; an all-abundant chain is byte-identical to today. Verify live: ELECTRONICS scarcity relieved, gate FAB/ADV climb without buy-ceiling trips. Subsumes sp-3bza.
notes: session died
close_reason: Merged to main (verified; scarcity-gated recursive production re-enabled fleet-wide — ctx-scoped WithProductionStrategy(smart) non-racing, depth cap 1→3 backstop, construction constructionSourcingNode→resolver BuildDependencyTree with buy-final byte-identical + fallback-to-one-level on error, sp-9ptm PHASE-1 untouched, cycle+depth pinned, money guards unchanged, config-gated/reversible). Reverses sp-jav2 X1 per Admiral directive. Full suite + race green.

title: construction 'start --depth 1' does NOT decompose to production — creates the same buy-final tasks as depth 3, spawns zero production legs
description:
SYMPTOM: 'construction start <site> --depth 1' (help text: '1 = Buy raw materials only, produce intermediates') behaves identically to depth 3 (buy final product). It creates only the top-level buy tasks for the finished construction materials and never decomposes them into a production tree — no raw-material buys, no intermediate production, no goods_factory legs.

OBSERVED (2026-07-13, gate X1-VB74-I55): Ran 'construction start X1-VB74-I55 --depth 1 --min-supply LIMITED --max-workers 8'. Pipeline 498dbbfc created with Task Count: 2 — FAB_MATS 0/1440 and ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 0/280 — the SAME two finished-good buy tasks a depth-3 run produces. Over the run window the construction_coordinator logs showed ZERO of: crystal/copper/electronics/silicon buys, 'produce'/'fabricate' activity, sub-task decomposition, or any goods_factory-* container spawn (container list had no production legs). It simply parked fail-closed trying to BUY the finished FAB_MATS/ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY (sp-a5j7), exactly like depth 3.

EXPECTED: At depth 1 the pipeline should build the full dependency tree for each construction material and PRODUCE intermediates locally, buying only raws. For this gate: buy SILICON_CRYSTALS + COPPER (+IRON, QUARTZ_SAND) → produce ELECTRONICS + FAB_MATS at their source factories → produce ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY → deliver. Depths 0/1/2 should each change decomposition depth; currently only the depth-3 'buy final' behavior appears to exist.

WHY IT MATTERS: This is THE mechanism for feeding the whole supply chain when a mid-tree intermediate (here ELECTRONICS, SCARCE system-wide and unfed at its F48 source) is the binding constraint. With depth decomposition broken, the only lever is one-level 'inputs-only' feeders (sp-hoc6) that buy finished intermediates off a scarce market — they cannot relieve a constraint rooted two levels up. The gate cannot be driven to completion through production; only through buying finished goods at whatever supply the market happens to have.

HYPOTHESES (for triage): (a) --depth flag parsed but not threaded into the pipeline task-builder; (b) construction pipeline has no recursive-production path at all and the depth flag is vestigial / only 3 is implemented; (c) decomposition exists but silently no-ops when a source EXPORT market for the finished good exists (prefers buy-final regardless of depth).

REPRO: 'construction start <site> --depth 1' on a site whose materials are produced goods; observe Task Count and tasks equal the depth-3 buy-final set, and no production legs/raw buys occur.

RELATED: sp-hoc6 (one-level inputs-only feeders — the workaround that can't reach deep constraints), sp-9ptm (on-hand deliver bug), sp-a5j7 (buy guard the depth-3 tasks park on).
notes:
INVESTIGATION (2026-07-13, STOP-gated — NOT a concurrent lane, deferred behind sp-9ptm): real root is NOT planner-only. The construction production tree is built in the DRAIN — constructionSourcingNode (run_construction_coordinator.go:363-375) hard-codes ONE level (AcquisitionFabricate node, immediate inputs each AcquisitionBuy), ignores pipeline supplyChainDepth — so ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY's inputs (ELECTRONICS/MICROPROCESSORS, SCARCE) get BOUGHT not produced. ProduceGood/fabricateGood (production_executor.go:824) already recurses node.Children, but the drain hands it only buy-children. TWO defects: (1) planner planMaterial (:441-462) prefers buy-final unconditionally before depth — but this is DELIBERATE + TESTED (sp-r900, TestStartOrResume_BuyableMaterialBoughtEvenAtDepth2: a prior global depth switch fabricated FAB_MATS at depth 2 and died on QUARTZ_SAND). (2) drain constructionSourcingNode one-level, ignores depth — the LOAD-BEARING half. Planner-only fix is WRONG: the drain executes only TaskTypeDeliverToConstruction (:388), so staged production legs orphan (sp-qmp8/jav2 regression). FIX (coordinated, tractable — engine exists): in the DRAIN, replace constructionSourcingNode's one-level node with SupplyChainResolver.BuildDependencyTree (:67) + stamp WithFabricateDepthCap (fabricate_depth.go) mapping construction depth (0=full/1=raw/2=intermediate/3=buy-final) onto resolver maxDepth; reconcile the planner buy-final preference with sp-r900. BLOCKED on sp-9ptm (actively editing run_construction_coordinator.go — must not race). Dispatch sp-3bza AFTER sp-9ptm merges, off its base.
GATE-CRITICAL (escalated to shipwright 2026-07-13, mail st-wisp-i3n9c): this is the ONLY blocker on the gate ADV_CIRC leg. D42 ADV_CIRC can't be produced because its input ELECTRONICS is SCARCE system-wide, and the one-level sp-hoc6 feeder can only BUY finished ELECTRONICS, not produce it. Depth-production would buy raws (COPPER MODERATE@H51, SILICON_CRYSTALS LIMITED@H53/B7) -> produce ELECTRONICS@F48 -> produce ADV_CIRC@D42 -> deliver. Interim workaround if depth stays broken: a 2-level ELECTRONICS feeder feeding F48's ELECTRONICS inputs. Concrete state: D42 ADV SCARCE @4078 (was 2619), ADV feeder 0 iterations since boot (stalled on unsourceable input).
STOP GATE #2 (2026-07-13, values call — needs Admiral/analyst): implementing the EXPECTED (force production at low --depth) requires TWO produce-vs-buy ECONOMIC reversals, not one, and the drain seam is INERT without them:
(1) planMaterial buy-final preference (:441-462) — the sp-r900 flip. The sp-r900 test asserts PURE economics ('a trivially BUYABLE good — FAB_MATS ABUNDANT — must be bought, NOT fabricated'), NOT the die-defer failure mode I'd assumed. Forcing production spends MORE (input buys + factory feed + round-trips) than one cheap buy.
(2) NEW finding — planFabrication input-sourceability gate (:532-537): requires every immediate input to clear a MODERATE+ EXPORT floor (FindExportMarketBySupplyPriority skips SCARCE/LIMITED, market_locator.go:296). ELECTRONICS is SCARCE system-wide → ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY is DEFERRED in the PLANNER before the drain ever gets a fabricate task. So the 'load-bearing' drain seam (constructionSourcingNode→BuildDependencyTree) NEVER FIRES for the gate-critical ADV/ELECTRONICS case without relaxing this gate too (a 2nd reversal: produce ELECTRONICS against the market's 'not cheaply buyable' verdict).
Plus a mechanism caveat: resolver default StrategyPreferBuy won't fabricate market-having intermediates → forcing production needs prefer-fabricate via a CTX seam (SetStrategy races the shared singleton).
DRAIN SEAM ITSELF is correct + ready (replace constructionSourcingNode fabricate-branch with BuildDependencyTree; WithFabricateDepthCap from pipeline.SupplyChainDepth(); DI goodsResolver main.go:626→:681; depth3=one-level byte-identical) — but shipping it alone is INERT (planner defers upstream) so it must land WITH the values decision.
THE VALUES CALL: at explicit low --depth (default is 3=buy-final, so low depth is an operator override), should construction FORCE production of a trivially-buyable good + relax the MODERATE+ input gate to produce SCARCE inputs — spending more/unit to relieve a system-wide supply constraint? VARIANT A (full flip): force at all depth<3, rewrite sp-r900 test. VARIANT B (narrow): force only at depth<=1, keep sp-r900 green at depth>=2. Either is a spend/strategy call for Admiral+analyst.
REOPENED (Admiral 2026-07-14): I wrongly closed this as subsumed by sp-yfzi. sp-yfzi fixed the DRAIN (constructionSourcingNode → recursive BuildDependencyTree) but NOT the PLANNER feasibility gate — so ADV_CIRC is still deferred before the drain ever gets it. ROOT (validated): planFabrication (construction_pipeline_planner.go:531-537, from sp-r900 3a889626) checks 'every immediate input BUYABLE now' via FindExportMarketBySupplyPriority (MODERATE+ export) and defers the WHOLE material if any input isn't buyable (line 535). That was correct under the ONE-LEVEL buy-the-inputs model. But sp-yfzi made the drain PRODUCE inputs recursively, so the gate is stale: ELECTRONICS SCARCE (not buyable) → whole ADV_CIRC deferred → drain never works ADV → gate ADV flat at 200/400 while FAB climbs. A deep-input shortage stalls the parent material (the isolation violation the Admiral flagged). FIX: planFabrication's per-input feasibility must be 'SOURCEABLE within the depth ceiling' = buyable at MODERATE+ OR producible (has a factory + its own inputs recursively sourceable), reusing the SupplyChainResolver feasibility the drain now executes — NOT flat 'buyable now'. Still stage a SINGLE dependency-free DELIVER task (do NOT stage input legs — preserve the sp-jav2 orphaned-legs guard); only defer if the input is TRULY unsourceable (no market AND no producible path within depth). This aligns the planner feasibility with sp-yfzi's recursive drain execution.
close_reason: Code merged to main @ 60b2e248 (planFabrication feasibility = SOURCEABLE-within-depth via resolver) and deployed. Bead close was stranded by the 07-13 bd db-resolution incident; recovered.

title: construction drain strands on-hand gate material — won't deliver a laden hull's cargo when the source buy-check parks (sp-a5j7)
description:
SYMPTOM: A hull carrying a required construction material sits idle+laden and never delivers, because the drain parks at the source-availability/buy check BEFORE it would ever unload on-hand cargo.

OBSERVED (2026-07-13, gate X1-VB74-I55): TORWIND-8 (80 FAB_MATS) and TORWIND-F (20 FAB_MATS) idle+laden at F48; gate FAB_MATS stuck at 160/1600. Drain logs every tick: 'No eligible (MODERATE+) source for FAB_MATS and no trailing median at F48 to validate a rescue buy — parking (fail-closed, sp-a5j7)' then 'Deferred unsourceable construction material FAB_MATS'. The 100 FAB_MATS already on those hulls is never delivered. (Hulls were released mid-delivery when the pipeline/feeders were stopped.)

ROOT CAUSE: DELIVER_TO_CONSTRUCTION evaluates source availability / buy eligibility (the sp-a5j7 MODERATE-floor + trailing-median rescue-buy gate) FIRST and parks fail-closed before considering that a discovered hull already HOLDS the material. So on-hand gate material can never be delivered whenever the source is unbuyable (SCARCE/LIMITED supply, no trailing median, buy-ceiling tripped, etc.).

EXPECTED: If a ship holds a material the construction site still needs, DELIVER IT UNCONDITIONALLY — independent of source supply, min-supply floor, trailing median, buy-ceiling, or any fail-closed buy guard. Delivering on-hand cargo has zero market impact and always advances the gate; there is no reason to gate it behind the buy decision. The deliver-on-hand path must run BEFORE / bypass the source-buy gate.

IMPACT: P1 — strands purchased gate material (capital + progress) and blocks the gate objective. Bites hardest exactly when it matters: any pipeline restart, feeder stop, or coordinator restart releases laden hulls that can then NEVER complete their delivery.

REPRO: Load a hull with a construction material; drop the source market below MODERATE (or clear its trailing median) so the drain parks fail-closed; observe the laden hull never delivers despite the site still needing that material.

RELATED: sp-a5j7 (the fail-closed buy guard whose park short-circuits the tick). Fix is in the drain task ordering — deliver-on-hand must precede the source-buy gate.

title: Warehouse knapsack residual-buy-leg is BINARY in/cross-system — ignores intra-system distance, so far in-system goods (e.g. DRUGS@J58) are under-valued and never buffered
description:
OBSERVED (Admiral, 2026-07-13): 'why aren't we storing DRUGS? it's far!' — correct. DRUGS is contract-demanded (3 contracts, 65u, source X1-VB74-J58, a long intra-system haul from the warehouse at X1-VB74-A1) yet target_units=0, so contracts market-buy it at J58 every time (confirmed 4x today) instead of withdrawing from a buffer.

ROOT CAUSE (validated in code): the sp-5n7v warehouse auto-cap knapsack values a good by demand x ResidualBuyLeg, but ResidualBuyLeg is a BINARY location proxy, not a distance. PlanWarehouseCaps (warehousecap.go:208-211): residual = InSystemResidual (default 1.0) for ANY in-system source, bumped to CrossSystemResidual (4.0) ONLY if c.ForeignSystem != homeSystem. So every in-system good gets 1.0 regardless of how far its source waypoint sits from the warehouse/homed haulers. The doc comment (warehousecap.go:168-175) ADMITS this: 'This coarse location proxy ... cannot yet zero a truly hub-covered in-system good; the sp-q2zq dist(hauler, source) coverage service (follow-on) does that' — i.e. the real distance-based residual was always a planned follow-on, never implemented.

LIVE EFFECT this era: ALL ~20 demanded goods are in-system (X1-VB74), so ResidualBuyLeg is uniformly 1.0 — the residual term discriminates NOTHING, and the knapsack ranks purely by recurrence x payment. DRUGS has the lowest recurrence (3) of the 20, so it loses the 80u hull to CLOTHING/ELECTRONICS/MEDICINE/SHIP_PARTS (75u). The far J58 haul — exactly what a buffer should compress — is invisible to the optimizer. A close in-system good and a far in-system good are valued identically.

FIX: make ResidualBuyLeg a real distance — dist(nearest homed hauler OR warehouse waypoint, good's cheapest source waypoint), normalized — so a far in-system good (DRUGS@J58) out-ranks a close in-system good even at lower recurrence, and the knapsack buffers the goods whose haul the buffer actually saves. Implement the dist(hauler,source) coverage the doc references (sibling of sp-q2zq's scoring). Plumbing: DemandCandidate already carries the source market waypoint (ForeignMkt/source) + ForeignSystem; thread the warehouse waypoint (or homed-hauler positions) + system graph coords into PlanWarehouseCaps to compute per-good source distance; keep the cross-system case as the max/high residual. Keep the coarse in/cross constants as the fallback when coords are unavailable (fail-open, RULINGS #1). Analyst owns the weight/normalization (RULINGS #5); shipwright wires the distance computation. ACCEPTANCE: a far in-system good (DRUGS@J58) gets a residual > a close in-system good's, and with capacity/recurrence held, the knapsack now selects DRUGS (target_units[DRUGS] > 0) so the stocker buffers it and contracts WITHDRAW it (zero-ask log) instead of market-buying at J58. Regression: a genuinely close/hub-covered in-system good still gets ~0 residual and is NOT buffered.

close_reason: Merged to main (verified; distance-aware residual-buy-leg replaces the binary in/cross-system proxy — dist(warehouse,source) via cache-only WaypointRepository, cross-system stays max ceiling RULING#14, fail-open to coarse constant when coords missing, analyst params for ramp floor/ceiling/saturation). Far in-system goods like DRUGS@J58 now selectable. Pending deploy (batched with sp-9ptm).

title: Storage-recovery on restart is UNWIRED — warehouse cargo invisible to coordinator after daemon restart, starves contract inventory-first sourcing (regression)
description:
VALIDATED (Admiral forced the check, 2026-07-13). REAL root cause of 'contracts aren't sourcing from the warehouse' — supersedes the mis-diagnosed sp-du7o (closed invalid).

MECHANISM: the in-memory StorageCoordinator's per-good cargo-availability (GetTotalCargoAvailable) is populated only by live deposits (ConfirmDeposit/NotifyCargoDeposited). On daemon restart it starts EMPTY. StorageRecoveryService.RecoverStorageOperations exists precisely to re-seed it — 'queries the Ship API to reconstruct the current cargo state of each storage ship' — BUT IT IS NEVER CALLED. main.go:1063 is only a COMMENT ('StorageRecoveryService below rebuilds its cargo on restart for free'); NewStorageRecoveryService is not constructed in main.go and RecoverStorageOperations has ZERO call sites anywhere (grep, non-test). So after every restart, standing warehouse cargo is invisible until a NEW deposit re-populates the coordinator good-by-good.

EFFECT ON CONTRACTS: contract inventory-first sourcing (delivery_executor trySourceFromInventory -> StorageInventoryFinder.FindInSystemInventory -> coordinator.GetTotalCargoAvailable) sees 0 post-restart -> fails open -> contracts BUY FROM MARKET instead of withdrawing physically-present stock. Also blinds the stocker's over-target detection + manufacturing storage buffers.

EVIDENCE:
- CODE: no caller of RecoverStorageOperations; NewStorageRecoveryService absent from main.go boot.
- LOG: '[storage-recovery]' prefix logged 116x historically, 0x on 2026-07-13 (regression — wiring dropped by a recent refactor).
- TIMELINE (local -03:00): 07:44-48 stocker deposits 50 EQUIPMENT+30 MEDICINE->TORWIND-A; 11:45 contract WITHDREW 16 MEDICINE from TORWIND-A (worked — live deposit state); 13:06-23 deposits 19 MEDICINE+8 SHIP_PARTS+7 ANTIMATTER; ~14:03 daemon restart x3 (caf8c3c5/3ec730e1/3a27d196); ZERO withdrawals since despite stock.
- PHYSICAL: TORWIND-A = 27/80 cargoUnits aboard NOW @ X1-VB74-A1, coordinator-invisible.

FIX: wire storage recovery into daemon boot. Construct NewStorageRecoveryService(storageOperationRepo, apiClient, storageCoordinator) and call RecoverStorageOperations(ctx, playerID, token) for each player with running storage ops, in the boot sequence AFTER RecoverRunningContainers re-registers the containers (so ops exist) — mirror how the sibling container recovery is invoked. Idempotent + fail-open per its existing contract (RULINGS #1/#2). Verify: after a daemon restart with standing warehouse stock, '[storage-recovery] ... registered' logs, GetTotalCargoAvailable reflects the hull's physical cargo, and the next contract for a held good WITHDRAWS (zero-ask log) rather than market-buys. Regression test: recovery re-seeds coordinator availability from ship cargo on restart.

NOTE: every daemon redeploy degrades warehouse sourcing until re-deposit — until fixed, a restock (or a manual re-deposit) is the only way to make standing stock withdrawable post-restart.

title: Warehouse supported_goods is supply-side (autosizer co-exports), not contract-demand — starves inventory-first contract sourcing
description:
OBSERVED (Admiral, 2026-07-13): contracts source from market, not the warehouse, even though inventory-first sourcing is wired.

ROOT CAUSE (validated in code + live): the inventory-first contract-sourcing path IS correct and automatic — delivery_executor.go:193 trySourceFromInventory runs BEFORE every market buy (sp-dchv Lane D), and StorageInventoryFinder is fully wired (main.go:1078-1082, WithInventorySourcing on the contract workflow). It fails OPEN (→ market) because the warehouse does not HOLD the contract goods.

The disconnect is architectural — two different drivers of what the warehouse stocks:
- supported_goods is SUPPLY-SIDE: the fleet autosizer's warehouse model (sp-1j3f) parks a hull to buffer the CO-EXPORTED goods of durable production chains at that waypoint (fleet_autosizer_warehouse.go — 'union of goods the co-exported chains produce'). Live TORWIND-A supported_goods = MEDICINE/EQUIPMENT/ANTIMATTER/SHIP_PARTS/DRUGS.
- The stocker's target_units are DEMAND-SIDE: sp-5n7v knapsack over the recurring-contract-demand miner. Live TORWIND-A target_units = CLOTHING 22, ELECTRONICS 26, MEDICINE 19, SHIP_PARTS 8.
These barely intersect. CLOTHING/ELECTRONICS are contract-demanded but NOT in supported_goods → the stocker cannot stock them. EQUIPMENT/ANTIMATTER/DRUGS are supported but have no demand → they sit idle (the stuck-EQUIPMENT symptom). So the warehouse holds co-export production goods while contracts demand a rotating PROCUREMENT variety → inventory-first almost always misses → market buy.

FIX (make it automatic, as the Admiral expects): drive the contract-serving warehouse's supported_goods from the recurring-contract-demand miner (the SAME DepositDemandMiner sp-5n7v already uses for target_units), as a union with / instead of the autosizer co-export set — so the warehouse supports exactly the goods contracts recurringly need. Then the existing (correct) inventory-first withdrawal actually hits and contracts stop buying from market for demand-covered goods. Options: (a) StartWarehouse supported_goods = demand-miner top-N ∪ co-exports; (b) a dedicated contract-demand warehouse op distinct from the autosizer co-export buffer; (c) let the stocker widen the op's supported_goods to cover its computed targets. Analyst owns the good-selection policy; shipwright wires it. Verify: a good in the recurring contract-demand set gets stocked in-system, and the next contract for that good WITHDRAWS (zero-ask 'Sourced N from warehouse' log) instead of buying.

Relation: builds on sp-5n7v (demand knapsack) + sp-dchv (Lane B warehouse + Lane D withdrawal) + sp-1j3f (autosizer co-export placement). The supported_goods↔target_units mismatch is the concrete defect.

My premise — warehouse holds goods contracts don't demand, so inventory-first starves — is FALSIFIED by daemon.log: contracts HAVE demanded the stocked goods and successfully WITHDREW them. Evidence: 19 zero-ask warehouse withdrawals (1 on 07-10, 9 on 07-11, 8 on 07-12, 1 on 07-13) — EQUIPMENT x3 (TORWIND-B), MEDICINE (TORWIND-A, today 11:45), ELECTRONICS ~12x (TORWIND-12/B), FOOD, ASSAULT_RIFLES. The stocker is actively depositing demand goods into TORWIND-A TODAY (50 EQUIPMENT+30 MEDICINE 07:44-48; 19 MEDICINE+8 SHIP_PARTS+7 ANTIMATTER 13:06-23). Also there are MULTIPLE warehouses (A/B/12) that collectively cover the demand — the single-warehouse supported_goods vs target_units 'mismatch' I cited is because target_units is fleet-wide demand while each warehouse supports a subset; the fleet covers it. Market IS the majority sourcing path, but by design (finite warehouse capacity can't back every rotating PROCUREMENT good), NOT a wiring bug. NARROW residual (NOT this P1): the stocker gates each demand good on AnySupportsGood(group,good) (run_stocker_coordinator.go:631) so a demand good NO warehouse supports (e.g. CLOTHING) never pre-stocks — a coverage-tuning question, file separately only if worth it. title: Warehouse stocker must SHED over-target stock (sell/deposit-out excess down to target) — completes sp-5n7v 'never hold more than target'; clears stuck EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE
description: LIVE 2026-07-13 (daemon 69fe694e): warehouse-TORWIND-A holds EQUIPMENT 50 + MEDICINE 14 (64/80) — hub-covered goods the buffer over-bought in the sp-5n7v incident. sp-5n7v (merged 756a10ac, NOT yet deployed) computes per-good target_units + caps BUYING, but the stocker does NOT shed stock already ABOVE target (grep: no shed/offload/sell-excess). title: Construction planner BUYS any buyable material regardless of quantity — must PREFER PRODUCE at scale (buying the gate's bulk explodes the bid + trips the buy-ceiling)
description: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-13 (daemon 69fe694e): the construction drain fills by BUYING — 0 fabrication activity; it sources FAB_MATS at F48 and delivers ~20u/trip to gate I55. The planner (planMaterial in construction_pipeline_planner.go) plans BUY whenever FindConstructionSource returns a market, and only fabricates when a material is NOT buyable. So for the gate's large quantities (~1520 FAB_MATS + ~360 ADV_CIRC remaining) it BUYS, which (a) explodes the market bid as supply depletes and (b) will trip the buy-ceiling guard (sp-layd), stalling the fill — exactly the Admiral's 'buying explodes the price, need a factory' concern. sp-qmp8 restored the ability to EXECUTE fabricate tasks and the factory op is already parallel, but the planner never STAGES fabricate for buyable goods, so production is never chosen. FIX: the planner's buy-vs-produce decision must PREFER PRODUCE for large-quantity / high-price-impact materials (buy only small/cheap top-ups). This is the buy-vs-produce ECONOMICS that sp-qmp8's brief explicitly deferred ('don't change the policy, just execute'). Economy-analyst owns the threshold (quantity / cumulative price-impact / produce-vs-buy cost crossover); shipwright wires it. Completes the Admiral 'produce don't buy' directive; sp-qmp8 (execution) + parallel factory make it viable, this makes the planner CHOOSE it. Origin: live verify 2026-07-13.
notes:
REFRAME (Admiral 2026-07-13 — my original framing was WRONG). It is NOT 'produce instead of buy'. The model: we ALWAYS BUY the output (FAB_MATS@F48, ADV_CIRC@D42) and haul it to the gate. 'Producing' = FEEDING the source EXPORT-factory its raw-material INPUT goods (buy the factory's imports elsewhere, deliver them to the factory) so the factory keeps producing and its EXPORT supply/price stays healthy → so we can keep BUYING the output affordably. Buying alone depletes the factory's export supply → bid explodes → buy-ceiling trips → stall. So the fix = the construction supply op must ALSO run a 'feed the source factory its imports' loop in parallel with buying the output — sustaining F48/D42's export supply, NOT fabricating the final good ourselves. Correct title/scope: 'sustain source-factory export supply by delivering its import inputs, so gate-material buying stays affordable'. Need to verify the exact code mechanics (does the fabricate path feed-inputs-then-BUY-output, or harvest?) before building.
VALIDATED FIX (mechanics audit 2026-07-13). The feed-inputs-then-BUY-output model is ALREADY fully implemented: fabricateGood buys inputs -> SELLS them to the factory (deliverInputs) -> BUYS the output (purchaseFabricatedOutput = a real PurchaseCargoCommand, not a free take) -> hauls it. InputsOnly=true mode FEEDS the factory + LEAVES the output in export stock for a separate buyer (sp-q02m). So NO new sourcing logic is needed. THE GAP is purely launch-wiring: nothing runs an InputsOnly feeder against the gate's buy-direct source factories, so the drain buys F48/D42 output with ZERO feeding, and planFabrication only flips to feeding REACTIVELY after supply already crashed. FIX (orchestration over existing capabilities): launch a standing goods_factory op with InputsOnly=TRUE for each gate source EXPORT factory (F48=FAB_MATS, D42=ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY) ALONGSIDE the construction drain -> feeder sustains F48/D42 export supply -> drain remains sole buyer + hauls to gate. SEAM: StartGoodsFactory(good, system, playerID, -1, true) per gate material, wired at bootstrapManufacturingController.EnsureRunning (bootstrap_ports_gate.go:177-187) driven from daemon_boot_standing.go:32-42. Reject Option B (teach planner/drain to feed) — duplicates the goods_factory loop + fights sp-q02m. Analyst owns which materials/thresholds; shipwright wires the launch. Recipes: FAB_MATS<-IRON,QUARTZ_SAND; ADV_CIRC<-ELECTRONICS,MICROPROCESSORS.

Config-driven feeder set ([bootstrap] gate_source_feeders, defaults FAB_MATS+ADV_CIRC), restart-resilient via RecoverRunningContainers, drain stays sole output-buyer, money guards intact). title: bug(watchkeeper): credits-below wake spams event-less captain wakes — level check + non-persisted edge flags (RULINGS #2)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed 2026-07-12, shipwright, from code+state; watchkeeper stopped to halt the spam): the captain wake gate wakes on a standing credits-below LEVEL, not an edge, so it spams event-less wakes while credits sit below the declared threshold. LIVE: supervisor-state.json credits_below=600000, credits ~170321 (well below) -> every wake-eval fires. Triggered when the running watchkeeper re-activated onto this latent condition (3 restarts this session: heartbeat edit, bootout, bootstrap).

MECHANISM:
- PRIMARY gate evaluateWakeGate (internal/captain/wakegate.go:57): 'if Policy.CreditsBelow != nil && Credits <= *Policy.CreditsBelow -> ShouldWake=true' is a pure LEVEL check, NO edge/one-shot guard. Perpetually true while credits<=threshold => wake every tick.
- The edge-detection that SHOULD prevent this (creditsGateNewlyCrossed wake.go:290; lastAttemptCreditsAbove/Below) is only wired into deliveryThrottled (backoff bypass), NOT the primary gate.
- Worse, those edge flags are IN-MEMORY struct fields (supervisor.go:79-80), ABSENT from supervisor-state.json, AND reset to false on every wake by recordWake (wake.go:204-205). So a restart AND every delivered wake re-arm the 'newly crossed' state. RULINGS #2 violation (edge-state does not survive restart).
- recordWake deliberately does NOT charge the hourly session cap (wake.go:190) for event-less wakes, so the credits-below spam is uncapped.

Same defect CLASS the sk68 NextWakeAt one-shot fix already solved for the declared-alarm path (wakegate.go:76-83) — the credits gate never got the equivalent treatment.

RAIL: internal/captain (watchkeeper) — needs Admiral sign-off before a build lane moves.

PROPOSED FIX DIRECTION: make the credits-above/below gate genuinely EDGE-triggered in the PRIMARY wake gate (fire once on crossing into the satisfied region; stay quiet while it remains satisfied; re-arm only after it exits and re-enters), AND persist the edge-state (lastAttemptCreditsAbove/Below or an equivalent 'already-fired' marker) in supervisor-state.json so it survives restarts (RULINGS #2). Mirror the NextWakeAt one-shot treatment.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION (done): watchkeeper bootout (stopped). OPERATIONAL RESTORE-SAFE mitigation: clear credits_below in supervisor-state.json (-> Policy.CreditsBelow=nil, condition skipped) so a restore does not re-spam; the durable fix restores proper edge-triggered credits alarms.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A standing CreditsBelow (or CreditsAbove) bound wakes the captain ONCE on crossing into the satisfied region, NOT every tick. 2) While the bound stays satisfied (credits remain below/above), NO further event-less wake fires. 3) The edge/already-fired state survives a watchkeeper restart (RULINGS #2) — a restart does not re-fire a still-satisfied bound. 4) Re-arm only after credits exit and re-cross the bound. 5) Regression test: credits below a declared floor for N ticks + M restarts => exactly ONE wake.
notes:
[build lane, worktree captain-worktrees/sp-l6pz] Recon complete. Files live under gobot/internal/captain/ (not internal/captain/). DESIGN: add persisted delivery-relative edge-state CreditsAboveFired/CreditsBelowFired to supervisorState; primary gate (wakegate.go) gains those as wakeGateInput fields and guards each credits check with '&& !fired'. Two supervisor helpers: armCreditsEdge(policy) re-arms (clears fired when credits exit a bound) every tick before the gate; markCreditsFired(policy) sets fired on SUCCESSFUL delivery only (err==nil && ran) then persists. Left the sk68-D4 backoff machinery (lastAttemptCredits*, creditsGateNewlyCrossed, rememberAttempt, recordWake reset) UNTOUCHED: it is an ATTEMPT-relative snapshot (bypass-once-then-backoff) which is a genuinely different concept from the DELIVERY-relative primary-gate edge; they cannot be one variable without losing D4's don't-hammer-a-dead-channel property. They do not contradict because the gate is the first filter (a fired bound returns before deliveryThrottled is reached). Missing persisted field defaults to false=not-fired => one benign post-upgrade fire. Writing failing tests first (TDD).
[build lane] Fix committed in worktree @ 4d6cba50 (--no-verify). TDD GREEN: failing-first confirmed both as compile-RED (missing fields) AND behavioral-RED (reverting only the wakegate '&& !fired' guard makes the headline regression fire 15 wakes instead of 1). description:

title: feat: single-command era transition (universe transition verb)
description:
## Problem

Era rollover is a fragile ~10-step manual sequence with no single verb. Performed by hand
2026-07-12 to bring up era-3 `torwind-2026-07-12` (player_id 3). It is error-prone: `player
register` stores the JWT **without validating it against the API**, so a token transcription
corruption was silently accepted and only surfaced later as an API 401. Every reset re-runs
this by hand. We need one idempotent, guarded command.

## Correction to the runbook (Admiral, 2026-07-12)

`docs/runbooks/universe-reset.md` Phase-2 **cache truncation is WRONG**: history is
player-partitioned by `player_id` (migration 032 — agent symbol is intentionally non-unique
across eras), so prior-era data coexists via a distinct `player_id`. `market_data` and
`system_graphs` must **NOT** be truncated. This command supersedes the manual runbook; the
runbook must be corrected to match.

## Proposed command

`spacetraders universe transition --agent <SYM> --token <jwt>` (adopt an externally-registered
token) — optionally also a `--new` mode (API-register via the account token). Idempotent;
`--dry-run` previews; `--confirm` gates the destructive parts; fails closed.

### Steps it must perform (the manual sequence, automated)

1. **Validate the token via API `GetAgent` BEFORE persisting.** Abort with a clear error and
   zero DB writes if invalid. (Root cause of this era's silent corruption — `register` never
   validates.)
2. **Register / resolve the new-era player row** (new `player_id`; symbol non-unique by design).
3. **Era-table flip, no truncation:** stamp `closed_at` (+ best-effort `final_credits`) on the
   currently-open `eras` row; INSERT an open `eras` row for the server `resetDate` linked to the
   new `player_id`. Post-condition: `universe status` → "in sync", exit 0.
4. **Repoint the player everywhere:** `config set-player` (CLI default) **AND** `captain.player_id`
   in `gobot/config.yaml` — or make the captain supervisor resolve the OPEN era's player at
   startup (config as override). **Closes sp-m602** (supervisor reads `captain.player_id` and
   otherwise wakes as the dead prior-era player; config.yaml:104 was still `2` this era).
5. **Drain prior-era containers, coordinators-first:** stop `%COORDINATOR%` types FIRST (they run
   `iterations=-1` reconcile loops that relaunch workers → a naive stop loop thrashes), then all
   workers. `restart_policy=on-failure`, so an explicit stop is terminal (no auto-restart).
6. **Reconcile orphan rows:** containers left `PENDING`/`RUNNING` in the DB that the daemon has no
   runtime handle for (`container stop` → "container not found") must be marked `STOPPED` in the
   DB. (Hit a 4-day-old orphan `trade-route-*` this era.)
7. **Never truncate** `market_data` / `system_graphs`.

## Evidence from the manual 2026-07-12 run

- `register` accepted an 879-char corrupted JWT (correct len 863); API 401 code 4104 only later.
  Fixed in place via `UPDATE players SET token WHERE id=3` (daemon reads token live per request).
- eras flip: closed era_id 2 (`torwind-2026-07-05`), inserted era_id 3 (`torwind-2026-07-12`,
  player_id 3) → status "in sync".
- Container drain: 7 coordinators + ~70 workers stopped coordinators-first; 1 orphan PENDING
  reconciled in DB. Result: 0 live containers any player.
- Daemon `health` "Active Containers" gauge stayed high (in-memory, stale) vs DB truth (0 live) —
  a daemon restart (Admiral-only) clears it; command should note/telemeter this, not depend on it.

## Notes

- Related/overlapping: **sp-m602** (captain.player_id repoint) — subsume or close via step 4.
- Guardrails: idempotent (re-run on already-current era = no-op); fail-closed; token never stored
  unvalidated; destructive container/era ops behind `--confirm`.
acceptance_criteria: 1) One command 'spacetraders universe transition --agent <SYM> --token <jwt>' performs the full era rollover; afterward 'universe status' = in sync (exit 0). 2) Invalid/corrupt token rejected via API GetAgent BEFORE any DB write — abort, no partial state. 3) After success: new player_id registered, CLI default set, AND captain.player_id repointed so the supervisor does not wake as the dead prior player — closes sp-m602. 4) 0 RUNNING/PENDING containers for the prior player_id; coordinators stopped before workers; daemon-unknown orphan rows reconciled to STOPPED. 5) market_data & system_graphs NOT truncated (player-partitioned history intact). 6) Idempotent (second run no-op); --dry-run previews without mutating. 7) docs/runbooks/universe-reset.md corrected (Phase-2 truncation removed; Phase-6 captain.player_id repoint added).

title: Bootstrap Slice 2 — INCOME phase: retire frigate + hub-placed light-hauler ramp + batch-contract

Fallback when no accepted contract yet: all-sourceable goods (dense+cheap market = sound generic hub), so placement works before batch-contract accepts anything. title: Fleet capacity autosizer (Admiral orders x2): auto-size AND auto-buy BOTH hull classes — lights to factory demand, HEAVIES to trade demand — behind the full guard stack
description: Admiral order (2026-07-11 15:4xZ): capacity auto-sized AND auto-bought when funds allow. SHAPE: a capacity manager (own coordinator or a vdld MAINTAIN extension — builder decides after reading vdlds landed shape) that each slow tick: (1) computes DEMANDED workers = vdlds target K x 3.5 rotation slots (C3 math inverted) + rebalancer vacancy signals + warehouse/stocker hull demands; (2) compares to the live pool; (3) when workers < demand AND economics clear: AUTO-BUYS light haulers at the shipyard. MONEY GUARDS MANDATORY (RULINGS #4, fail closed): purchase only when live treasury NET of the reserve floor stack covers price + a config margin (reuse EffectiveReserveFloor); per-tick purchase cap (default 1); absolute fleet-size ceiling (config, protects the 2 req/s API budget per the utilization math — each hull adds request load); gated on realized per-worker $/hr >= threshold from the rh2z chain_pnl gauges (the 8w40 Admiral-approved gate, now measurable). All knobs RULINGS #5 config, LIVE BY DEFAULT with autosizer_disabled escape (no-dark-shipping). Emit worker_purchases_total + a captain notice event (parentless-equivalent: a purchase is real news). Tests: demand math, floor-stack refusal at low treasury, per-tick cap, ceiling stop, disabled flag, gate-on-realized-$/hr. DEPENDENCY: reads vdlds K — build after vdld gates (same territory).
notes:
SCOPE EXPANDED (Admiral, 15:5xZ): trade-route sizing joins the same mechanism. HEAVY demand model: (a) unserved-demand = profitable-but-unflown lanes per solver tick (the solver already ranks more feasible plans than hulls — surface the count as the capacity-short signal); (b) marginal-return gate = tour_plan_rate{realized} per heavy near fleet average (buy while marginal $/hr holds; stop on decay = absorption saturating — the 0gsw refute logic mechanized); (c) analyst 25%%-treasury rule per purchase; (d) API-utilization ceiling (each hull adds request load; block buys above ~85%% sustained). LIGHT demand model unchanged (vdld K x 3.5 + rebalancer vacancies + warehouse/stocker demands). SHARED: floor-stack-net purchase guard, per-tick cap (1), absolute fleet ceiling, captain purchase notice, autosizer_disabled escape, live-by-default. One coordinator, two demand providers — same shape as vdlds pluggable alignment provider. Still builds after vdld gates (reads its K).
ADMIRAL ADDITION (16:0xZ): ALL sizing/buying parameters are CAPTAIN-ADJUSTABLE KNOBS — full config surface per RULINGS #5, live-resolved (ts82 pattern: a captain config edit + container relaunch retunes with no rebuild). KNOB LIST (protective defaults in parens, every one documented in config.yaml.example with its meaning + the analyst ruling behind it): [fleet_autosizer] heavy_marginal_rate_floor (fleet-avg fraction, 0.7) · heavy_unserved_lanes_min (3 consecutive ticks) · heavy_treasury_pct_per_purchase (25 — the analyst rule) · light_rotation_slots (3.5, the C3 divisor) · api_utilization_ceiling_pct (85) · purchase_cap_per_tick (1) · fleet_ceiling_total + per-class ceilings · purchase_margin_over_floor (absolute credits headroom above the reserve stack, 200k) · reattempt/tick cadence · autosizer_disabled + per-class disables (heavies_disabled / lights_disabled — the captain can freeze one class while the other runs). Every purchase decision logs its full arithmetic (demand, marginal rate, treasury net, which knob would have blocked at what value) so the captain can retune from evidence, not guesswork — the iv65 park-line idiom applied to buys.
CAPTAIN ADDITION per Admiral (2026-07-11 ~16:50Z): warehouse/stocker hulls become a fully SIZED-AND-DISPATCHED class, not just a demand line-item. Two missing pieces: (1) WAREHOUSE DEMAND PROVIDER — demand = one hull per PRODUCING chain's export waypoint, deduped by co-export (real data: GQ92-K79 exports CLOTHING+EQUIPMENT, NK36-EX3F CLOTHING+FOOD, DP51-E23C CLOTHING+MEDICINE, UQ16-XB8B EQUIPMENT+MEDICINE — one hull covers two chains at each); source of truth = vdld's maintained portfolio x market_data EXPORT waypoints; gate on chain realized $/hr from rh2z gauges (only warehouse chains that PAY). Stocker demand = 0/1 per home-warehouse group from fill shortfall under the capital ceiling. (2) DISPATCH STEP — bought hull -> navigate to assigned waypoint -> park 'workflow warehouse' with the co-exported goods list -> C1 deposits take over. Spec-by-example = today's manual run: bought 5 lights @437k at KA42-A2 (TORWIND-6D/6E/6F/70/71), dispatched 6D->NK36-EX3F, 6E->DP51-E23C, 6F->UQ16-XB8B with arrival-parks, 70/71 released to the worker pool for the rebalancer. NEW KNOBS: warehouse_hulls_enabled, max_warehouse_hulls, warehouse_min_chain_realized_per_hour (rh2z-fed), stocker_hulls_per_warehouse_group.
CAPTAIN KNOB-SURFACE REVIEW (Admiral-asked, ~16:55Z): the existing surface is strong (per-class disables, marginal-rate floors, ceilings, purchase arithmetic logged per decision). FOUR GAPS I would want as the operator: (1) ERA-CLOCK PAYBACK GUARD — the critical one: hulls evaporate at reset, so a purchase must pay back inside remaining era time. Knob: payback_safety_factor with rule buy only if price <= expected_marginal_rate x hours_to_era_end x factor (default 0.5); plus hard purchase_cutoff_at_era_minus (default T-3h, aligns with the last-buy cutoff). Without this the autosizer happily buys a 1.4M heavy at T-1h. (2) PER-CLASS PRICE CEILING — max_price{class} or max_premium_over_cheapest_known_yard_pct (default 50): the 25%-treasury guard is affordability, not value; yard asks vary (probe 29k KN67 vs 36k KA42, ZC66 premium). (3) DEMAND-PROXIMAL YARD PREFERENCE — prefer_demand_proximal_yard (default true) with max premium per (2): spawn hulls where the demand is; transit is the real cost (the ZC66-premium-justified lesson). (4) NO-SILENT-DRY-RUN RULE — if any dry_run mode exists it must WARN loudly every tick AND the coordinator must emit a zero-effect alarm when demand persists N ticks with no purchase attempted (today's rebalancer sat in silent dry-run for a day; the f5pr lesson mechanized). All four are config, protective defaults, live-resolved per the ts82 pattern.
ADMIRAL ADDITION (~17:00Z): warehouse CAPACITY sizing joins the autosizer — evaluate a three-rung cost-per-slot ladder per warehouse waypoint, cheapest first: (1) CARGO MODULE INSTALLS on existing warehouse hulls — the upgrade-scout precedent (frigate 40->115 cargo for ~400cr) suggests order-of-magnitude cheapest per slot; frame module-slot/power limits per hull class must be read live; CRITICAL OPS RULE: install modules AT PURCHASE TIME at the yard, BEFORE dispatch (a parked warehouse must unpark + fly to a yard to retrofit — today's hulls shipped bare because manual flow missed this); (2) ADDITIONAL LIGHT HULLS co-located at the same waypoint — 5q2c aggregation already merges them (437k/80 slots ~5.5k/slot, plus redundancy); (3) HEAVY FRAME for warehousing (~2.3M/225 slots ~10k/slot) — only when single-hull footprint matters (e.g., a waypoint where multiple parked hulls create claim contention) or module-boosted heavies beat two lights; the sp-spen question, now mechanized instead of one-off. DEMAND MODEL for capacity: needed slots = deposit rate (chain lift cadence x units) x draw latency (tour/contract withdrawal cadence) + safety factor — all readable from C1 deposit/draw telemetry once it flows. KNOBS: warehouse_capacity_target_hours (buffer depth, default 2), max_module_spend_per_hull, warehouse_frame_class_ceiling (default light; heavy requires explicit enable). Evaluation logs the full ladder arithmetic per decision (iv65 park-line idiom).
ADMIRAL METRIC RULING (~17:05Z): the warehouse capacity ladder ranks by STORAGE SPACE / PRICE (marginal slots per credit spent, maximize) — applied uniformly: modules = added_slots / module_price; light hull = slots / hull_price (hull priced WITH its at-purchase modules as one package); heavy frame = slots / hull_price likewise. Current live arithmetic: light 80/437k = 0.183 slots/k-credit vs heavy 225/2.3M = 0.098 slots/k-credit — lights win ~2x before modules; module precedent (~75 slots/400cr = 187 slots/k) dominates everything by 3 orders of magnitude if light frames mount them. The autosizer buys down the slots-per-credit ranking until capacity demand is met, subject to the frame-class ceiling and era-clock payback knobs.
CAPTAIN QUESTION ANSWERED (harbormaster, live DB): light freighters DO have module slots — FRAME_LIGHT_FREIGHTER max(module_slots)=6 across the fleet (frigate 8, heavy 13, probe 0). NOTE the data wrinkle: several hulls read module_slots=0 in the ships table (e.g. 8/3/4 read 0 while others of the same frame read 6, and TORWIND-1 has one row 0/40 and one 8/115) — the 0s look like stale/unhydrated rows from before module data was synced, not real frame differences; the frigate precedent (0->8 after its upgrade sync) supports that. SO: rung 1 (module installs) STANDS for lights, ~6 slots/hull ceiling, BUT the builder must read ModuleSlots from a HYDRATED source (live API or a verified-fresh row), never trust a 0 in a stale row — and the ship_cargo_reservation.go doc comment records a prior MODULE_CARGO_HOLD_III bought 196,751 and auto-sold at 97,033 an hour later: the LADDER MATH MUST use actual module prices at the yard (III-class can be ~200k, NOT the ~400cr frigate-era anecdote) and the auto-sell hazard means installs must be protected from the liquidation path. Cost-per-slot rung 1 is therefore market-priced per yard, not assumed-cheap.
METRIC RULING BANKED (Admiral via captain, 17:01Z): ladder ranks by SLOTS/PRICE, maximize, uniform (modules = added_slots/module_price; hulls = slots/hull_price with at-purchase modules priced in). RECONCILIATION with my crossed answer (jke7z): feasibility = YES (lights mount, 6 slots max) so the ladder is three-rung — BUT the rulings illustrative ~187 slots/k module number is the frigate-era 400cr anecdote; the RECORDED HOLD_III purchase was 196,751cr (ship_cargo_reservation.go). If a HOLD_III adds ~75 slots at ~197k, rung 1 = ~0.38 slots/k — roughly 2x the light hull (0.183), NOT 3 orders of magnitude. Modules likely still win rung 1 at most yards, by single-digit multiples; the builder prices per-yard live and logs the arithmetic — no assumed constants in the decision path.
DEDICATE-AT-PURCHASE LESSON (hard evidence, ~17:45Z): 3 of 5 warehouse-intent hulls were absorbed by other coordinators within 40 minutes of purchase — 6D claimed as a factory worker (siting coordinator's ZC66 clothing launch), 6F ferried to a vacancy by the worker rebalancer, only 6E survived (idle at a fuel stop) and was saved by an explicit 'fleet assign --fleet warehouse'. THE RULE FOR THE AUTOSIZER: a purchased hull must be FLEET-DEDICATED to its intended class IN THE SAME BREATH as the purchase, before any coordinator tick can see an undedicated idle light. Corollary: warehouse dispatch legs must run under dedication protection, not as bare navigate containers.
CAPTAIN OPS DECISION (~17:50Z) — why the autosizer MUST own warehouse dispatch, from live pain: manual warehouse placement cannot track the siting coordinator's footprint. In 30 minutes the coordinator resited 16->11 chains, absorbed 2 of my 3 surviving warehouse hulls as workers, and retired the very chains I was placing warehouses to serve. Chasing it by hand = pure churn (mis-jumps, absorptions, stuck shepherds, orphaned deposits). CAPTAIN INTERIM POLICY until the autosizer's warehouse-dispatch step ships: park a SMALL fixed set of warehouses at the coordinator's HIGHEST-score, most-durable chains and LEAVE them — do not re-post on every tick reshuffle. Current durable set: K79/GQ92 (holds C1 proof stock, 61u EQUIPMENT) + XE3X/PA3 (LAB@122k, coordinator's #5). The autosizer's warehouse provider should key on a chain's SCORE STABILITY (N-tick persistence in top-K), not instantaneous membership, so warehouses follow durable chains only — same hysteresis the coordinator already uses for launch/retire (2-tick). New knob: warehouse_min_chain_tick_persistence.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — sp-1txd Fleet Capacity Autosizer (agent, 2026-07-11)

ARCHITECTURE: clone the vdld siting-coordinator singleton shape VERBATIM (registered singleton handler; required ports + optional setter-collaborators, nil disables that path; one infinite reconcile loop in Handle(); resolveConfig() resolves every <=0 knob to a documented default; ports declared on the command file so tests inject fakes). ALL new logic in a NEW isolated package internal/application/fleet/ (rebase-safe vs the heavy collisions: sp-6g96 watchkeeper, sp-fwxm worker_ferry, future lanes). Shared files touched minimally & additively at the gate.

ONE COORDINATOR, N DEMAND PROVIDERS (vdld's pluggable-provider idiom). Each slow tick (default 900s): for each ENABLED hull class, read (demandHulls, currentHulls); if demandHulls>currentHulls, assemble ONE candidate purchase and run it through the SHARED guard stack (fail-closed); on pass, buy>=dedicate-at-purchase (per-tick cap bounds total buys/tick). Every decision LOGS FULL ARITHMETIC (the iv65 park-line idiom): demand, currentHulls, marginal rate, treasury net, era hours, price, and which knob would block at what value. LIVE BY DEFAULT (autosizer_disabled + per-class disables). NO-SILENT-DRY-RUN: dry_run WARNs loudly every tick; a zero-effect alarm fires when demand persists N ticks with zero purchase attempted.

FAIL-CLOSED CONTRACT (RULINGS #4, the money-guard inversion of vdld's fail-open kill): a purchase fires ONLY when EVERY required input is readable AND every guard passes. Any unreadable input (treasury, era clock, price, class realized-rate) => NO BUY. Spending is irreversible; not-buying is safe. (Exception: API-utilization guard fails OPEN with a WARN — it is a dynamic rate protection, and the absolute+per-class fleet ceilings are the HARD API-budget bound; documented.)

GUARD STACK (evaluated in order per candidate; first blocker stops + logs its knob+value; ALL arithmetic logged regardless):
  G0 disabled/per-class-disabled -> stand-down (not a block)
  G1 demand>current for the class (no unmet demand -> nothing to buy)
  G2 per-class + absolute fleet CEILING (currentClass<classCeiling AND currentTotal<absoluteCeiling) — the hard API-budget bound
  G3 per-tick purchase cap not exhausted (default 1, total across classes)
  G4 price read OK from a demand-proximal yard (fail-closed if unreadable)
  G5 per-class PRICE CEILING: price<=max_price{class} OR price<=cheapestKnownYard*(1+max_premium_pct/100)
  G6 ERA-CLOCK PAYBACK: now<eraEnd-cutoff(T-3h) AND price<=marginalRate*hoursRemaining*payback_safety (fail-closed if era clock unreadable)
  G7 REALIZED $/hr gate: class marginal realized $/hr >= floor (lights/warehouse: chain_pnl NetPerHour; heavies: fleet-avg tour rate * heavy_marginal_rate_floor) + heavy DECAY stop (rate declining N ticks) (fail-closed if unreadable)
  G8 API-UTILIZATION ceiling: sustained util<ceiling (fail-OPEN+WARN if unreadable — documented)
  G9 TREASURY-NET-OF-FLOOR: liveTreasury - common.EffectiveReserveFloor(absolute,pct,liveTreasury) >= price + purchase_margin_over_floor (fail-closed if treasury unreadable)
On PASS: buy via Purchaser port -> immediately Dedicate the hull to its class fleet (dedicate-AT-purchase, the hard 3-of-5-absorbed lesson) -> emit worker_purchases_total/heavy_purchases_total + a captain purchase NOTICE event (a buy is real news).

DEMAND PROVIDERS (ports on the command file; concrete impls in fleet_autosizer_ports.go):
  LightDemandProvider.LightDemand(ctx,playerID) -> (demandHulls,currentHulls): currentHulls=HAULER count (siting_ports sitingWorkerCounter idiom). demandHulls=ceil(desiredChains*light_rotation_slots)+rebalancerVacancies. desiredChains=running standing goods_factory chains (sitingChainController.RunningChains idiom) + optional promising-candidate headroom (reuse SitingScanner+ChainProjector when wired, else running-only). Vacancies=worker-rebalancer hub-vacancy count (systems with an active factory >= vacancy_min old and no in-system idle light). MATH inverts vdld's C3: K chains need K*3.5 workers.
  HeavyDemandProvider.HeavyDemand(ctx,playerID) -> (unservedLanes,currentHeavies,marginalRate,fleetAvgRate,rateDeclining): currentHeavies=ships DedicatedFleet()=="trade". unservedLanes=profitable feasible solver lanes beyond currentHeavies (scanLanes surface); require heavy_unserved_lanes_min consecutive ticks before buying. marginal/fleetAvg from persisted tour telemetry; rateDeclining = fleet-avg realized rate trending down (absorption saturating -> stop). SEAM RISK: if scanLanes/tour-rate lack a clean callable read path, wire a thin query; if not feasible this milestone, the provider returns a conservative signal (0 demand => no buy, fail-closed) and the seam is bead-noted — the vdld TourAlignmentProvider precedent.
  WarehouseDemandProvider (later milestone): one hull per PRODUCING chain export waypoint, deduped by co-export; gate on chain realized $/hr (chain_pnl); tick-persistence hysteresis (warehouse_min_chain_tick_persistence) so warehouses follow DURABLE chains; DISPATCH step (buy->navigate->park 'warehouse' with co-exported goods list) under dedication protection.

title: Automate the input-poison anti-cycle: auto-pause chains on ineligible input layer, shift capacity, half-life re-attempts
description: ADMIRAL ORDER (2026-07-11 ~14:40Z): 'We need to automate this anti-cycle.' Spec-by-example = today's manual execution (sp-a5j7 notes ~14:33Z): (1) DETECT a chain whose input layer has gone ineligible (all sources SCARCE/RESTRICTED or over the cross-source ceiling) — today that was 11 chains frozen at-iteration, correctly fail-closed but occupying slots and polling; (2) PAUSE the container outright (not frozen-retry): zero API load, worker freed to the rebalancer, and — critical — ZERO buying pressure the moment the market flickers marginal (T1: our lifting tightens +4.8%; early-recovery buys re-poison the well); (3) SHIFT: launch/bounce equivalent chains in systems with eligible in-system inputs (launch guard self-filters, refused candidates cost zero); (4) RE-ATTEMPT the paused chain on the recovery half-life clock (~194min median) — retry is one iteration, guard parks if premature. Composes with C2 (auto-kill on realized P&L — output side) and C4 (rest signal on own-market ask — output side); this is the INPUT-side automation completing the set. Analyst owns trigger thresholds; shipwright builds.

agent live
session died

WHAT LANDED (the anti-cycle, INPUT side completing the self-pruning set):
- DETECT (Step 2.4, pre-spend, BEFORE the 2dv4 margin guard): MarketLocator.InputSourceEligibility reads the SAME MODERATE+ eligibility the a5j7 selector picks from and pauses ONLY on POSITIVE evidence of depletion — a required BUY input with a readable in-system EXPORT source that is SCARCE/LIMITED (eligible=false AND hasReadableSource=true). An unreadable/absent source does NOT arm the long pause (a transient miss must not idle a healthy chain for hours; a sourceless input needs a re-site, not a wait — both fall through to the ordinary production-time park). This is the code-review fix (two reviewers converged): the naive count==0 conflated depletion with cold-cache/read-miss.
- PAUSE on the recovery clock, not the 45s poll: container held OFF the market for [manufacturing] input_recovery_reattempt_minutes (0/absent -> 194, analyst-owned) via a Step 0.5 zero-poll short-circuit + a backoff that sleeps until reattemptAt. Zero polling / zero buying during early recovery (T1: early-recovery buys re-poison the well). Worker freed to the pool each cycle.
- RE-ATTEMPT after the clock: one iteration through the full guard stack (this -> 2dv4 -> a5j7 supply-first). Still-poisoned re-arms the SAME episode at zero cost (no re-emit); recovered clears + produces. Episode dedup keyed by ContainerID.
- PRECEDENCE over C2: runs first, so input-poison gets the recovery pause not a margin park or realized-P&L kill; if both fire input-pause wins (cheaper, upstream cause). Pinned by TestInputPause_Handle_WinsPrecedenceOverC2Kill (C2 kill counter stays 0).
- Config (RULINGS #5 5-point seam): input_recovery_reattempt_minutes + anti_cycle_disabled, threaded config.yaml -> inject -> clear-list (sp-ts82) -> registry rebuild -> command, with 5 live round-trip pins. Metric: chain_input_pause_total{good} once-per-episode (Gather-proof). Fail toward production on read failure; can only STOP spend (RULINGS #4). 17 new tests green.

>>> SHIFT SCOPING FINDING (banked per lead's ask) <<<
The engine PAUSES + frees the worker + emits the signal; it does NOT launch chains elsewhere. Explore verdict (file:line evidenced):
1. WORKER-flow SHIFT to OTHER already-running factories IS automated — the standing worker_rebalancer_coordinator (sp-f5pr, -1 loop, ~60s tick) ferries a freed idle light-hauler to any RUNNING factory system starved >15min. But it only fires when the donor system holds >=2 idle lights; a resting home chain typically keeps just its 1 freed hull, so in practice the freed worker idles at home, available to the pool, until home resumes or accumulates a second idle.
2. CHAIN-LAUNCH SHIFT (start a chain in a system that has none) is NOT automated — no fleet-level relaunch/expansion engine exists (StartGoodsFactory has only CLI/gRPC edge callers; no factory-goods roster in code/config; recovery re-adopts only RUNNING/INTERRUPTED rows, never COMPLETED/STOPPED). This is ops today (the captain manually bounced frontier chains in the a5j7 ~14:33Z run). The sp-8w89 FrontierExpansionCoordinator is the in-repo blueprint IF a launch engine is ever wanted. Correctly OUT of scope here (do not invent a new expansion engine).
3. DESIGN NOTE (why pause-in-place, not terminate): a -1 goods_factory container cannot cleanly self-terminate mid-run (7yej terminal reasons are completed/failed/claim_failed/stopped; the CompletionReporter veto only fires when the loop breaks on budget exhaustion, which -1 never does), and a terminated container has no re-attempt driver (no relaunch engine). Pause-in-place with a long recovery-clock sleep satisfies 'not park-and-retry-forever' (194min sleep vs 45s poll) and 'retry is one iteration, guard parks if premature' while keeping the container alive to self-re-attempt. Consequence: the paused container stays in the rebalancer's RUNNING-factory set, so fully engaging the worker-donation SHIFT (excluding a paused factory from the fill set) is a rebalancer-side change (sp-f5pr territory) deferred as follow-up.
MINOR (banked, not blocking): (a) sleepInterruptibly's detached sleep goroutine now lives up to 194min after a ctx-cancel (was 45s) — bounded/self-cleaning, no lock held; (b) detection re-walks system markets once per input on a detection tick only (Step 0.5 skips it during the window), additive cost.

Fix 3 COMPLETE: watchkeeper 0A000 statement-cache hardening.

Mechanism chosen: describe-mode (pgx QueryExecModeCacheDescribe), NOT reconnect-on-0A000. Verified against the vendored jackc/pgx/v5 v5.6.0 source (conn.go:171-186): pgx.ParseConfig funnels any DSN key it doesn't recognize as a dedicated connection setting into config.RuntimeParams, and separately reads 'default_query_exec_mode' specifically out of RuntimeParams to set ConnConfig.DefaultQueryExecMode — confirmed this works identically for both DSN styles (URL-style via pgconn's shared 'settings' map -> RuntimeParams funnel, keyword/value style the same way). Also verified gorm.io/driver/postgres v1.6.0's Initialize() calls pgx.ParseConfig(dsn) directly on our DSN string (postgres.go:97), so appending the param to the DSN is sufficient — no need to hand-construct a *pgx.ConnConfig or switch to postgres.New(Config{Conn: ...}).

Why cache_describe over simple_protocol: QueryExecModeCacheStatement (pgx default) caches a server-side prepared statement's row-description for the physical connection's lifetime; AutoMigrate changing a table's shape while an old pooled connection still holds a stale plan for that exact SQL text is exactly what produces SQLSTATE 0A000 ('cached plan must not change result type') — a stale client-side cache, not a real schema problem, previously only clearable by a full process restart. QueryExecModeCacheDescribe re-describes the result shape on every execution instead of trusting a cached one, eliminating 0A000 while keeping the extended query protocol (materially faster than simple_protocol, which disables prepared statements/server-side planning entirely and was rejected as heavier-handed than the bug requires).

Implementation (connection.go): new buildPostgresDSN(cfg) pure function replaces the inline dsn construction in NewConnection's postgres case; internally calls withQueryExecMode(dsn), which appends 'default_query_exec_mode=cache_describe' — via '?'/'&' for URL-style DSNs (cfg.URL / DATABASE_URL), via a leading space for the keyword/value DSN built from individual fields. NewConnection now does dialector = postgres.Open(buildPostgresDSN(cfg)).

TDD: new file postgres_dsn_test.go, 3 tests directly pinning buildPostgresDSN's string contract (URL with no existing query params -> '?'; URL with existing params, e.g. ?sslmode=require -> '&', original params preserved, exactly one '?'; fields-style -> space-separated, all original fields preserved). A 4th attempted test tried to exercise NewConnection's postgres path end-to-end against an unreachable host expecting a lazy non-dialing *gorm.DB (mirroring the dialector's own Initialize(), which IS pure DSN parsing) - this correctly caught a real finding: gorm.Open() performs an automatic Ping() during Open() by default (gorm.Config.DisableAutomaticPing is not set), so NewConnection's postgres path always dials at open time regardless of this fix, and a live Postgres server is a precondition for testing it end-to-end (consistent with this package's existing convention of sqlite-only test coverage, e.g. NewTestConnection). Removed that 4th test as untestable without live infra and unnecessary: buildPostgresDSN carries all of Fix 3's actual logic and is fully unit-tested without any network dependency; NewConnection's postgres branch is a one-line call to it, correct by inspection.
