title: Consult (Admiral-directed): FULL review of the factory operation — design + architecture. What can be made better? Too complex or too simple? Deliverable: a ranked redesign brief
description: ADMIRAL ORDER (13:00Z): review the ENTIRE factory operation design and architecture, not just sourcing. SCOPE FOR THE ANALYST: (1) ARCHITECTURE AS-BUILT vs AS-DESIGNED — original docs (gobot/docs/GOODS_FACTORY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md 2025-11-22, GOODS_FACTORY_DYNAMIC_SHIP_DISCOVERY.md, supply_chain_resolver.go, run_factory_coordinator.go, the parallel task coordinator) vs what actually runs: per-good coordinators + shared worker pool + one-work-unit rotation + demand-gated harvest + tour-realized margins. (2) THE ERA'S EVIDENCE FILE, all on beads: sourcing blowups all from SCARCE sources (wedx ruling — supply-first restoration already spec'd, a5j7); iv65 price-ceiling failed on poisoned baseline; worker P&L thin (~72k/hr best) while tour-side realization ~6.6M/hr gross flowed through factory goods (8w40); export-ask-subsidy signal (tours paying premium at OWN markets = rest signal); chain rotation works engine-side; era-1 lesson: capacity-without-workers. (3) THE QUESTIONS: is the design too complex (16 chains, recursive dependency trees, dual coordinator designs, fabricate ladders) or too simple (no chain-level P&L accounting, no supply awareness at buy time, no per-chain kill-switch on realized margin, value realization unmeasured because it flows through tours)? What single change most improves fleet $/hr? Should chains be FEWER and deeper (top-3 goods only) or broader? Should factory output feed TOURS explicitly (planner-visible stock) instead of passive export markets? (4) DELIVERABLE: ranked redesign brief — keep/kill/change per mechanism, sized by expected $/hr impact and build cost; becomes the era-3 factory doctrine and the shipwright's build list. Era context: T-24h, treasury cycling low, factories currently 14 chains running (2 furnaces dead pending a5j7).
notes:
ARCHAEOLOGY DATUM for your review (from shipwright, file:line): the original supply-first ranking is ALIVE at market_locator.go:254 (FindExportMarketBySupplyPriority — ABUNDANT>HIGH, skips SCARCE/LIMITED, doc comment cites 43cr vs 6,863cr cost data) — buyGood at production_executor.go:286 simply calls the price-first sibling FindExportMarket instead, while LOGGING the supply data it ignores. The class was fixed once (b469484, 2025-12-02) scoped to RAW materials only; fabricated inputs kept price-first — the ADV_CIRC path. So the architecture question sharpens: the design was right, implemented, and then bypassed in one call site for half the input space — a review finding about DRIFT CONTROL as much as design (how does a one-line selector swap in a money path escape notice for 7 months? the dangerous function keeps its innocent name). a5j7 now carries the restore + poison-proof baseline; furnaces dead until it deploys.
TRADE-ANALYST: FULL FACTORY OPERATION REVIEW — RANKED REDESIGN BRIEF (sp-hzz5, Admiral-directed) — 2026-07-11 ~13:10Z
Evidence spine: sp-wedx (sourcing incidents), sp-8w40 (erosion + attribution), sp-v8ha (tour-feed values), sp-naw6 (raw-input economics), sp-spen (warehouse/stock model), the trade audits, and the design docs (GOODS_FACTORY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md verified).

## THE VERDICT ON "TOO COMPLEX OR TOO SIMPLE": BOTH — in exactly opposite places.
**The ACQUISITION side is over-built; the REALIZATION side is under-built.** The design invests its complexity in recursive input trees and dual coordinators — where the era's ledger says almost no money lives (raw inputs = 0.29% of spend, market-buy permanently correct per naw6). Meanwhile the side where ALL the money lives — output realization, which flows through tours at ~6.6M/hr gross — has NO stock model, NO chain-level P&L, NO kill-switch, and is discovered by tours only via market-cache side-effects. Workers show ~72k/hr while their chains' goods gross 6.6M/hr through tours: the value is real but UNMEASURED AND UNMANAGED at the chain level. The redesign moves complexity from input trees to output realization.

## KEEP (proven, cheap, load-bearing):
K1. **In-system chain rule + make-led operation** — simple, correct, guard-verifiable (Guard-1 caught biocomposites).
K2. **Shared worker pool + rotation** — THE anti-erosion mechanism (chains sustain ~1 visit/1.5h recovery; a camper grinds its chain AND its own P&L to zero — 8w40, measured). Engine-side rotation works; keep it.
K3. **Demand-gated harvest** — only lift what has a sink; prevents inventory rot.
K4. **Supply-first sourcing** (a5j7 spec, already ruled at sp-wedx) — the leading-indicator fix for every blowup this era.
K5. **Launch-time chain-margin guard (2dv4)** — refused candidates cost zero; keep the boldness-with-verification pattern.

## KILL (complexity without money):
X1. **Recursive fabricate ladders beyond depth-1.** Raw inputs are 0.29% of buys; naw6 ruled market-buy permanently correct with named flip conditions that have never fired across 397 markets. Depth-1 (buy inputs at market, lift output) captures everything; fabricate-the-inputs-of-inputs is dead weight in code, API calls, and failure surface. The furnace class lived here.
X2. **One of the two coordinator designs.** One job, one design — whichever the shipwright designates legacy dies. Dual designs are a maintenance tax with zero $/hr.
X3. **Standing tail chains under ~50k/hr feed value** (micro/machinery/jewelry/plastics class). The tour book says 5 goods carry 80%+ of factory-good revenue. Tail goods stay as opportunistic arb legs, not staffed chains.
X4. **iv65 trailing-SELF-median ceiling as primary protection** — demote AND fix: it failed on a poisoned baseline (a ladder drags its own trailing median up behind it, so the ceiling chases the ladder). Backstop becomes 1.5x the median ask of ELIGIBLE (healthy-supply) sources cross-market — a baseline the ladder cannot poison.

## CHANGE (ranked by expected $/hr x build cost):
C1. **PLANNER-VISIBLE STOCK — the headline redesign (+300-600k/hr, build: medium).** Unify factory output with the warehouse/pre-positioning model: a factory IS a stocker whose acquisition method is 'lift cheap local production' instead of 'haul cheap cross-system goods.' Factory lifts DEPOSIT into warehouse stock with cost basis recorded; the tour solver sees stock as a reservable zero-ask source at basis (the dchv chain already proved deposit -> zero-ask withdrawal end-to-end); contracts already withdraw. This closes the leak where tours discover factory output only through the market cache and BUY IT AT THE LADDERED ASK — the export-ask-subsidy inversion (tours paying a premium at our own markets, the 8w40 signal) becomes structurally impossible: stock withdraws at basis. One model replaces two (factory-output handling + warehouse) — this is the change that REDUCES architecture while adding the most money.
C2. **CHAIN P&L LEDGER + KILL-SWITCH (+100-200k/hr, build: small).** Per-chain realized = stock withdrawals at market value − input costs − lift costs (my psql attribution is the working prototype). Auto-pause any chain under 30k/hr realized over a 6h window. The portfolio becomes self-pruning; today's hidden losers survive precisely because value flows through tours unmeasured.
C3. **CHAIN COUNT RE-SIZE: 14-16 -> 8-10, tour-book-aligned, rotation-sized (+50-150k/hr, build: config).** Correct sizing = workers x 3-4 rotation slots, concentrated on the tour book's top goods per system (clothing/adv_circ/equipment/medicine/lab). Fewer, deeper, aligned — not broader. Kill-list per X3.
C4. **Mechanize the REST signal (build: small).** The 8w40 export-ask-subsidy signal becomes an automated trigger: own-market lift ask > cross-source eligible median => chain rests one recovery window. Humans stop having to notice it.
C5. **iv65 baseline fix per X4 (build: small).**

## THE SINGLE CHANGE THAT MOST IMPROVES FLEET $/HR: C1.
It is simultaneously the biggest money (+300-600k/hr at current 6.6M/hr factory-good flow, from tours realizing at basis instead of laddered ask) and a net REDUCTION in architecture (two models become one). If era-3 builds exactly one thing from this brief, build C1.

## FEWER-OR-BROADER, answered: FEWER AND ALIGNED. 8-10 chains max at current worker count, all in the tour book's top goods, rotation-sized. Breadth is the tours' job (they arbitrage 39 systems); the factories' job is to make the 5 goods the tours sell most of cost less.

## ERA-3 DOCTRINE (one paragraph, portable):
"A factory is a stocker with a local acquisition method. Its output is planner-visible stock at cost basis, never passive market supply. Chains are few, tour-aligned, and rotation-sized to the worker pool. Sourcing is supply-first with cross-source price backstops. Every chain carries its own P&L and dies automatically when it stops paying. Input recursion beyond depth-1 is forbidden — raw inputs are bought, not made."

**Confidence:** HIGH on the economics of every keep/kill/change (each traces to a measured ruling on a bead); MEDIUM on the C1 build-cost estimate (shipwright owns that); the $/hr ranges use the same rested-lift honesty clause as v8ha — plan on the low ends. T-24h note: C2-C5 are small enough to land this era; C1 is era-3's first build.

VALIDATION ADDENDUM (Admiral challenge, ~13:25Z) — epistemic status of the C1 cycling claim, link by link: MEASURED: feeding lowers asks/grows supply (1.17M dump: D39 4,681->3,919 overnight; export vols 6->15-22 over era); double-draw ladders asks (D40 3,444->6,901 under factory+tour draw; +21%/11 tranches); tours pay premium at own markets (home medicine inversion); rest recovers (fitted per-tier half-lives). PROVEN n=1: stock->zero-ask withdrawal (dchv 19:44->19:55Z). DERIVED not observed: the +300-600k/hr (tour book paid-ask vs rested-lift deltas x measured volumes — real numbers, unbuilt mechanism). ASSUMED, not isolated: that lifting sustains the export market's production (correlates only: fed markets go GROWING, unfed RESTRICTED — no controlled separation of feed vs lift effects). TWO VALIDATION TESTS ATTACHED TO THE DOCTRINE: (T1, runnable THIS ERA, free) pick two comparable fed chains, lift one on rotation, leave one unlifted 6h — supply-state divergence isolates the assumed link; (T2, C1 acceptance metric) tours' avg acquisition cost for factory goods must track the RESTED ask series, not the ladder — single telemetry series, pass/fail at burn-in. Era-3 doctrine inherits C1 CONDITIONAL on T2; T1's result updates the lift-cadence parameter either way.
T1 ANSWERED FROM HISTORICAL DATA (pandas analysis over 32,669 history rows / 14,815 export observations, full era span — Admiral-directed): **THE ASSUMED LINK IS FALSE IN THE SAFE DIRECTION: export production does NOT require our purchase-demand.** Q1, treatment-group comparison of 317 export series (>=4 obs, >=12h span): UNTOUCHED exports (n=115, probe-observed only, zero fleet transactions) held supply perfectly (median drift 0.0 [0,+1]) with asks SOFTENING -2.5% — production continues and supply accumulates with no buyer at all. FED-ONLY (n=63): softest asks of any group (-4.1%) — feeding builds output supply even unlifted. FED+LIFTED (n=128): the ONLY group with tightening (supply -0.5, asks +4.8%) — OUR LIFTING is what tightens markets, not what sustains them. Q2 event study (n=97 series with pre/post coverage around our first lift): ask +6.5%, supply 2.3->1.9 — lifting consumes, full stop. IMPLICATION FOR C1: routing tours to stock-at-basis CANNOT starve market production — feeding alone keeps export markets healthy and soft; C1 is BETTER than projected. T2 (burn-in acquisition-cost telemetry) remains the deploy gate. Q3 BONUS — independent recovery re-fit: 31 spike-decay events, half-life median 194min IQR [149,270] — VALIDATES the model artifact's tagged tiers (180-414min) from our own era's data; the rotation doctrine's foundation is confirmed twice over. HONEST CAVEATS: observational, not randomized — untouched series skew toward penny goods (we touch what's valuable); and one correction to my own earlier claim: trade_volume is essentially STATIC per market (median growth 1.00 in ALL groups) — the D39/D40 vol 6->15-22 growth was a rare threshold event, not the normal feed benefit; the feed benefit is PRICE and SUPPLY-STATE, not volume. Era-3 doctrine updated accordingly.

GIT FINDING (captain): the original design doc specifies SupplyChainResolver 'Market Ranking: Prefers STRONG activity, HIGH supply' + 'Price Tracking: Returns cheapest market' — i.e., SUPPLY-FIRST selection, price as tiebreaker within healthy-supply candidates. The 07-11 furnace incident (ADV_CIRC chasing a SCARCE laddered market to -6.6M) could not have happened under the original ranking — it would have re-sourced. Current state: iv65 price ceiling live (lagging backstop), sp-a5j7 filed for supply-gate + buy-side absorption. ANALYST ASKS: (1) confirm/refute that supply-first ranking (the original design) is the correct primary sourcing policy vs the current cheapest/nearest+ceiling approach; (2) rank the three mechanisms (supply-state ranking, trade_volume tranche caps, price ceiling) as primary/secondary/backstop; (3) any case where price-first beats supply-first (e.g., era-end liquidation buys)? DELIVERABLE: a ruled sourcing policy the shipwright implements as sp-a5j7's final spec — restoration of the original design's intent, not an invention.
notes:
TRADE-ANALYST RULING (sp-wedx, Admiral-directed, ~12:40Z) — verified the doc first: GOODS_FACTORY_GAP_ANALYSIS.md lines 71-72 say exactly what the captain found ('Market Ranking: Prefers STRONG activity, HIGH supply' / 'Price Tracking: Returns cheapest market'). The original design made RANKING govern selection with price as information/tiebreak; the current implementation inverted it to price-first-with-ceiling. **(1) CONFIRMED: SUPPLY-FIRST IS THE CORRECT PRIMARY POLICY** — and not on the doc's authority alone: the era's own incident ledger proves it. EVERY input blowup began with a buy from a SCARCE/LIMITED source (D39 parts -220k, the 19-26k/u micro chase, the -891k electronics contract, the -6.6M furnace); ZERO blowups originated from ABUNDANT/HIGH sources. Mechanism: supply state is the LEADING indicator (my fitted tier model: SCARCE/RESTRICTED regenerates at 413min half-life — it ladders IMMEDIATELY under draw; ABUNDANT absorbs draw without repricing). Price is the LAGGING signal — by the time the ask ladders, the money is spent. **(2) MECHANISM RANKING: PRIMARY = supply-state eligibility+ranking; SECONDARY = trade_volume tranche caps; BACKSTOP = iv65 price ceiling.** The spec for sp-a5j7: (a) ELIGIBILITY: supply in {ABUNDANT, HIGH, MODERATE}; SCARCE/LIMITED ineligible EXCEPT (no eligible source exists) AND (chain blocked) AND (ask <= 1.2x trailing median) — the rescue clause. (b) RANKING among eligible: supply state desc > activity (STRONG > GROWING > WEAK > RESTRICTED) > price asc > distance. (c) TRANCHE SIZING: <=2 tranches/visit at MODERATE, <=3 at HIGH/ABUNDANT (measured ladder ~+2%/tranche keeps basis drift <6%). (d) RE-SOURCE TRIGGER (the furnace fix): if the selected source's supply state degrades below MODERATE mid-chain, re-run the locator instead of continuing — the original design would have re-sourced; the incident is the proof of what happens without it. (e) BACKSTOP: iv65 ceiling at 1.5x trailing-6h median stays, catching stale supply states and simultaneous multi-source depletion. **(3) WHERE PRICE-FIRST LEGITIMATELY WINS — three narrow cases:** (i) ERA-END MODE (< T-6h): mean-reversion has no time to work; a cheap-but-SCARCE ask that clears margin NOW beats waiting — flip to price-first-with-margin-check at the same T-6h boundary as the stocker rundown; (ii) SINGLE-TRANCHE MICRO-BUYS (<=1 tranche cannot move supply — acceptance tests, fillers); (iii) EXCHANGE-type markets (narrow fixed spreads, supply semantics weak — rank by price there). Everywhere else: supply-first, no exceptions. RULING SUMMARY FOR THE SHIPWRIGHT: restore the original design's intent — ranking governs, price tiebreaks, ceiling backstops; this is a RESTORATION, not an invention, and the era's P&L says the original designers were right.
RULED + CLOSING (12:45Z): supply-first CONFIRMED as the primary sourcing policy — the original design doc verified at lines 71-72, and the era's own ledger is the proof: every input blowup (parts -220k, micro chase, electronics -891k, furnace -6.6M) originated at a SCARCE/LIMITED source; zero from ABUNDANT/HIGH. Mechanism order ruled: (1) supply eligibility+ranking PRIMARY, (2) trade_volume tranche caps SECONDARY, (3) iv65 price ceiling BACKSTOP. Plus the furnace-specific fix: a RE-SOURCE trigger on mid-chain supply degradation (don't park forever — move to the next healthy source). Price-first survives only: era-end T-6h mode, single-tranche micro-buys, EXCHANGE markets. The Admiral's original design vindicated by the era's own data. a5j7 spec finalized on that bead; shipwright builds the restoration.

Frequency: first occurrence post-4hl5 multi-system tours — likely a live-scan-era plan shape the fixed graph now produces. comments.text:
MILESTONE 1 — Reconnaissance complete: strand-capable exit-path table + seam choice (build agent, sp-39oi)

## Deliverable #1 — Strand-capable exit paths (trading + contract commands)

Legend: STRAND = terminates with cargo aboard, no recovery; SELL = liquidates before exit; PARK = keeps cargo with a re-adoptable worker (contract-only); PRE-BUY = aborts before any cargo is bought (no strand possible).

### TRADING — run_arb_coordinator.go
| Path | line | class | cargo on exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| routability / location / margin / max-spend / spend-floor / buy-ceiling aborts | 487-659, 761-787 | PRE-BUY (floor/margin/max-spend) | none — abort before buy |
| reload/travel/dock/sell dispatch errors post-buy | 354-401 | error-exit | **STRAND** |
| sell-floor abort (sp-lbbm) | 423-437 | **floor-abort** | **STRAND** ("held aboard for later liquidation") |
| destination cannot absorb | 438-447 | starvation | **STRAND** (action arb_stranded_cargo) |
Arb has NO liquidation loop; comment defers held cargo to "the m5kv/next-leg liquidation path" (an external future actor that, for a parked idle hull, never comes).

### TRADING — run_trade_route_coordinator*.go (circuit)
| Path | line | class | cargo on exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| max_visits / no_lanes / margin_exhausted / unroutable | 502-590 | orderly / margin | none (epilogue liquidates or pre-buy) |
| cargo_blocked pre-flight (starts laden) | 599-607 | pre-existing strand | **STRAND** (parks, minFreeCargoForCircuit gate — the trading-side twin of FilterUnrelatedCargo) |
| runCircuit epilogue liquidateHeld SUCCESS | circuit.go 745-753 | SELL | none — the one real trading liquidation |
| runCircuit epilogue liquidateHeld gives up (3 fails) | circuit.go 759-765 | **floor/error** | **STRAND** (CargoStranded=true) |
liquidateHeld (circuit.go:37) = bounded 3-attempt deliver-to-lane-dest+sell. Lane-specific (sells only at the lane's known importer), not a generic best-in-system-bid liquidation.

### TRADING — run_tour_coordinator*.go
| Path | line | class | cargo on exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| buy caps / floor / ceiling in executeBuy | 1034-1152 | max-spend/floor | none — caps just buy less |
| CargoStranded veto (FINAL exit) | 764-769 | **floor/margin** | **STRAND** — no liquidation |
| re-plan budget exhausted / infeasible | 860-886 | starvation | **may STRAND** |
| reposition "honest-exit" (maybeReposition) | reposition.go | margin-death | defers (rides the jump, m5kv), never liquidates |
Tour has NO bounded liquidation engine.

### TRADING — run_stocker_coordinator.go
| CargoStranded veto (FINAL) 292-297; warehouse-full haulAndDeposit/depositGood 678-719 | starvation/capacity | **STRAND** (undeposited; no market-sell fallback) |

### CONTRACT — delivery_executor.go / run_contract_workflow.go
Contract "parks" (cargo stays with the SAME worker, later re-adopted to resume) — not lost, but a parked laden worker is filtered from NEW candidacy.
| insufficient-credits / ladder-cap / no-progress parks | delivery_executor 233-299; workflow 119-190 | margin/starvation | **PARK** (re-adoptable, but blocks candidacy) |
| JettisonWrongCargoIfNeeded | cargo_manager 81-170 | — | destructive jettison of WRONG cargo only (value-destroying, not a market sell) |

### THE JAM SEAM — ship_pool_manager.go FilterUnrelatedCargo (489-533)
Any hull whose hold HasItemsOtherThan(requiredCargo) → `parked`, excluded from `claimable`. In run_fleet_coordinator.go:566-582, when every candidate is parked/held, the coordinator logs "No spawnable ships - N hold unrelated cargo" and waits forever. This is where cargo stranded by ANY workflow above (arb/trade/tour/stocker/contract) converges into "cannot re-enter contract candidacy" = the fleet-scale jam.

### Existing liquidation subsystems
- ONLY real one: MANUFACTURING orphaned_cargo_handler.go + liquidate_executor.go (standing discovery-loop scan → sell at best in-system bid via marketRepo.FindBestMarketBuying; jettison below MinLiquidateCargoValue=10000). ZERO references from trading/contract — that is the gap.
- Trading: liquidateHeld (lane-specific, bounded) + sellWithFloor primitive. No standing pickup of an already-idle stranded hull.

## Seam choice — CHOSEN: contract candidacy-rejection seam (Seam A), NOT container-exit hook (Seam B)

Standing auto-liquidation dispatched from the contract fleet coordinator's parked-ship path (FilterUnrelatedCargo → parkedShips), mirroring the proven manufacturing OrphanedCargoHandler doctrine.

Why NOT Seam B (container_runner.go releaseShipAssignments, the 7yej hook):
1. DECISIVE: the acceptance targets hulls ALREADY parked (crisis-era strands) — their containers died long ago. An exit-time hook only fires at the moment of death, so it can NEVER pick up an already-idle laden hull. Only a standing scan on the discovery loop clears both already-parked hulls AND future strands.
2. Wrong layer: releaseShipAssignments runs in the gRPC adapter on teardown, context.Background() + short dbOperationTimeout, no market/nav/sell capability. Navigate+sell is a multi-minute workflow; it would have to spawn a worker anyway, coupling a generic adapter to one workflow. It also fires on normal "completed" exits (empty holds) — cost on the hot path.
3. Doctrine match: manufacturing already solved this identical jam class with a standing discovery-loop scan. Contract gets the same doctrine at its candidacy seam.
4. Whole-jam-class: the jam is "laden hull rejected from candidacy." Cargo from ANY workflow converges at FilterUnrelatedCargo, so clearing it there covers the class regardless of cargo origin.

## Planned mechanism
- New one-shot worker container `cargo_liquidation` (twin of worker_ferry): deps shipRepo + marketRepo + mediator; dispatches existing Navigate/Dock/Sell/Jettison mediator commands (reuse, no new I/O).
- Ladder: sell at current waypoint if it bids the good → else nearest in-system market with a bid (navigate+sell) → jettison ONLY as last resort below min-value threshold (default 0 = OFF). Money guards fail-closed: sale is revenue (floors don't block), movement/fuel respects guards; if unaffordable to move, sell-in-place-or-hold+log (never dump valuable cargo).
- Coordinator spawns it on each parked-with-cargo hull; on completion the hull releases empty and re-enters candidacy.
- Config (ae64f03 4-point seam): contract.auto_liquidation.disabled (default false = sell ON) + contract.auto_liquidation.min_jettison_value (default 0 = jettison OFF).

2. No heavy hull and no decile worse than -5% (no segment harmed beyond -5%).
3. N >= 20 snapshots, INCLUDING >= 3 thin-board snapshots.
4. LOAD-BEARING GUARD: median plan duration-estimate error < 15% in the SAME replay. Rationale: a rate objective (profit / wall-clock) fails UNGRACEFULLY when time estimates are bad — if durations are mis-estimated, $/hr ranks on garbage. This guard gates the whole change; without it, criteria 1-3 can pass on mis-estimated time and still ship a worse ranker.
Posture: replay-first, live-second (sp-78ai Q3). The live acceptance criteria already on this bead (rankers choose higher-$/hr in >=1 live case each, projected-vs-realized logged) apply AFTER this replay gate clears. Trade-analyst (st-wjz) should confirm/expand if the lost mail body carried further nuance.
STAGE-0 DESIGN MEMO (fable, sp-1wp8) — where $/hour lives, per surface. Citations at main 7edd710.

## 1. WHERE rate-normalization applies — the three surfaces traced

(a) SOLVER INTERNAL OBJECTIVE (tour_solver.py). What it literally maximizes today: solve_tour scores the top-20 beam candidates and sorts `(-profit, -cph, summary)` (tour_solver.py:697) — absolute profit primary, cph TIEBREAK only. That is the explicit Admiral decision of 2026-07-09 (docstring :27-35): rationale was that single-tour $/hr 'prefers concentrated dumping (ignores the sink-crush externality)'. ## 2. The correct time estimator per surface

- SOLVER: already computes real per-plan seconds — travel_fn (CRUISE formula on request-carried coords :221-260, inter-system = 2×450+900s, flat 300s degraded) + DWELL_SECONDS_PER_LEG=60 per stop (:479-487), cph = profit/hours (:487). Leg times live in the RESPONSE as TourLeg.TravelSecondsFromPrev; cph as ProjectedCreditsPerHour. NO new estimator needed.
- REPOSITION (Go): candidate rate = freshProfit / (jumpOverhead + replanAllowance + planSeconds). planSeconds recovered EXACTLY from the pre-flight plan by inverting cph (seconds = profit/cph×3600 — pure algebra on the solver's own numbers, no proto change, Stage 1 stays Go-only). jumpOverhead = crossSystemHopSeconds (352s, the production-observed jump+cooldown figure already named in the same package, travel.go:461); replanAllowance = 60s named const. cph<=0 (no time estimate) → fall back to freshProfit ordering (the regression pin).
- CIRCUITS (Go): rate = SpreadPerUnit×VolumeCap×HoldFit / estimatedCircuitHours; estimatedCircuitSeconds = inSystemCircuitBaselineSeconds + (cross ? crossSystemRoundTripHops×crossSystemHopSeconds : 0). There is NO fitted per-action constant in the repo; the baseline is DERIVED from the existing calibration anchor hullOpportunityCreditsPerSecond=75 (travel.go:481, itself derived from the fleet's sustained 250-300k/hr home-lane class): a ~300k-value circuit at 75 cr/s ⇒ ~4,000s ≈ 67min per in-system circuit (docks, tv-chunked transactions, refreshes, refuel — not just flight). CRITICAL CONSTRAINT DISCOVERED: the captain-ruled DP51 pin (run_trade_route_coordinator_xsyspenalty_test.go — 'the ruling's required test') requires the cross/in-system time ratio ≤ 409,920/335,033 = 1.223, i.e. baseline ≥ ~3,150s; a naive travel-only 720s baseline FLIPS the captain's ruled outcome (frontier would lose to the saturated home lane). The 75 cr/s-anchored ~4,000s baseline (ratio 1.176) preserves the DP51 pin AND the 'genuinely-better home lane still wins' property — the two constants stay mutually calibrated. Real per-lane cruise distance is a second-order refinement (needs a coords port into the circuit handler) — deferred, noted.
- Realized (metrics): actual wall-clock from plan-accept to tour end (clock-injected), profit = cash revenue − spend delta.

## 3. Interaction with D39 calibration and the m5kv held-liquidation split

D39: rate normalization divides the SAME projected profit already computed from the per-tranche calibrated price schedule (tranche_prices + net_absorption); no fitted coefficient, no impact-curve, no tranche-availability math changes on ANY stage — Stage 2's flip reorders choice among fully-priced candidates. The concentration risk D39 taught is now bounded upstream by the fleet-wide ledger cap (78ai), not by the selection rule.
m5kv HELD-LIQUIDATION: liquidation cash realizes over the SAME wall-clock as fresh trades, so inside the solver's cph it normalizes IDENTICALLY (profit total / plan hours) — correct, cash is cash. At the REPOSITION surface the numerator deliberately stays FRESH profit (total − held_liquidation − deposit_value, the existing :160 discipline): launch cargo liquidates anywhere, so it must not flatter a dead ground — but the DENOMINATOR is the plan's FULL wall-clock (liquidation legs consume real time; excluding their time while excluding their revenue would over-rank liquidation-heavy grounds' fresh rate... it slightly UNDER-states fresh rate instead — the conservative direction, and consistent: we rank grounds by fresh-cash-per-hour-of-total-plan). DepositValue books zero cash at execution; realized rate is cash-only (deposits' value realizes later via contracts) — projected uses the solver's total-profit cph; the projected-vs-realized histogram pair will show that structural gap on deposit-heavy plans; acceptable and documented.

SELECTION-LEVEL (Stage 1, low-risk, reorders choice among ALREADY-LEGAL plans): reposition candidate ordering (floor stays absolute at 25k, gates the CHOSEN candidate); circuit lane ordering (bid-floor MinBidMargin, selectLane discipline, absorption consult, directed-lane waiver ALL untouched — the waiver maps to 'directed lane ranks at the in-system baseline'); equal-rate ties break on absolute value then per-unit spread. title: Capture out-of-horizon exotic lanes (~200-400k/hr): multi-hop travel model OR long-haul arb path
description: Follow-up to sp-mtvg. sp-mtvg PROVED the exotic 'blind spot' is a 1-gate-hop DISCOVERY horizon shared by the tour coordinator (tourSystems) AND the autonomous arb scanner (scanLanes -> neighborSystems): source and sink of LASER_RIFLES/HOLOGRAPHICS/QUANTUM_DRIVES sit 3+ gate hops apart, so neither optimizer ever sees both in one snapshot. sp-mtvg added observability only (tour_candidates_dropped_total{reason=counterparty_system_unreachable}) — it does NOT capture the value. Capturing it is Admiral-level architecture and was intentionally deferred: the tour solver's _make_travel_fn prices EVERY inter-system crossing as ONE gate hop (2*GATE_HOP+JUMP_COOLDOWN), so simply widening allowed_systems beyond 1 hop mis-prices a 3-hop lane ~3x and corrupts cph selection; and MAX_TOUR_SYSTEMS=2 is an explicit Admiral decision. Options: (a) give the solver a real multi-hop travel matrix (gate-graph path cost) so the horizon can widen safely; (b) a dedicated long-haul single-good arb path not bound by neighborSystems (directed like the p4ua one-shot, but autonomous, lane-selected by spread). Watch the new counter to size the leak before choosing. Evidence: bd remember sp-mtvg-pinned-replay-proven.
design:
LONG-HAUL ARB ENGINE — authoritative design (brainstormed + Admiral-approved 2026-07-23). Follow-up to sp-mtvg.

== GOAL ==
Capture the out-of-horizon exotic lanes the 1-gate-hop discovery horizon hides from BOTH the tour solver and the arb scanner (proven by sp-mtvg). Live leak (measured): AI_MAINFRAMES X1-VM73-AX8E->X1-UM5-A1 spread ~28k/u (into home!), LASER_RIFLES ->X1-XD86 15-18k/u, NOVEL_LIFEFORMS ->X1-YN88 10-11k/u. Do it WITHOUT touching the load-bearing 1-hop horizon (RULINGS #4 — widening the solver mis-prices multi-hop lanes ~3x).

== DECISIONS (brainstormed) ==
1. APPROACH: a DEDICATED long-haul arb engine (new coordinator), NOT the multi-hop solver rewrite. Leaves the solver's 1-hop horizon untouched (RULINGS #4-safe).
2. HULL SOURCE: an operator-tagged `long-haul` fleet (dedicated_fleet='long-haul'), populated manually (`fleet add --operation long-haul --ship X`). Engine touches ONLY long-haul-tagged hulls — never contract (exclusive), warehouse/stocker, or untagged trade hulls. Operator owns capacity; engine never buys/borrows hulls.
3. LANE SELECTION: AUTONOMOUS, ranked by REALIZED $/hr (from BestSinksAcrossSystems), gated by a min-spread floor + a safety exclusion + the money envelope.
4. MONEY ENVELOPE: AGGRESSIVE (default ~1M/haul, ~2M total exposure), LIVE-tunable. Admiral-authorized sizing; the MECHANISM stays fail-closed.
5. TRIP LOADING: single-good OUT + opportunistic single-good BACKHAUL (each leg one directed lane; NOT a full multi-good VRP — that would be the rejected solver rewrite).
6. PRICING: PRICE-IMPACT-aware (realized per-tranche integral, BOTH buy + sell sides), optimal-volume-capped.

== REUSE INVARIANT (HARD REQUIREMENT — Admiral order) ==
Reuse, do NOT copy. The engine CALLS the existing shared components; where a needed function is embedded in the tour solver / trade coordinator, EXTRACT it to a shared location so BOTH callers use the one copy. One price-impact model, one travel path, one guard set, one watchdog.
ACCEPTANCE: a grep shows shared call sites and ZERO duplicated tranche/travel/guard/watchdog logic.
Reused components:
- price-impact/absorption model: the tour solver's realized-sink-tranche logic (sp-2v69u REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES) + market_absorption_ledger + market_data supply-level/trade_volume.
- multi-hop travel: the shared travel()/route machinery scout_reposition (sp-s232) / gas workers / arb circuits already reuse.
- BestSinksAcrossSystems: the read-only global-best-sink port sp-mtvg added.
- money guards: idle-arb's per-leg/exposure helpers + the common ImmutableReserveFloor/EffectiveReserveFloor (compile-time-locked, shared with the contract scaler + capacity reconciler).
- recovery/liveness: the sp-m3122 tour watchdog + stateless-recovery mechanism (ONE watchdog serves trade tours AND long-haul).
- held-cargo: the sp-2v69u held-cargo-aware offload.

== SECTION 1 — ARCHITECTURE & ISOLATION ==
New standing coordinator LongHaulArbCoordinator (recoverable container, modeled on idle-arb / the contract scaler): arms once, runs forever, most cycles a cheap no-op. Operates on the `long-haul` fleet tag ONLY. Each cycle, per idle tagged hull: discover -> rank -> assign top lane -> execute directed haul. Isolated: own hull set (the tag), own money envelope; spends shared treasury but FENCED from the 200k contract cushion. Separate coordinator — does NOT touch the tour solver or its 1-hop horizon.

== SECTION 2 — DISCOVERY, HONEST PRICE-IMPACT PRICING, OPTIMAL VOLUME, OUT/BACKHAUL ==
- DISCOVERY: read candidate lanes from BestSinksAcrossSystems (read-only) — per good, best sink across ALL systems + cheapest source -> (good, source, sink, ask, bid) spanning any number of gate hops.
- HONEST MULTI-HOP PRICING: compute REAL economics over the actual gate-graph route: net/unit = sink_bid - source_ask - fuel_over_the_real_route; trip_time = hops*(jump+cooldown) + intra-system legs. (This is exactly what the solver LACKS — it prices every crossing as 1 hop — hence a separate engine.)
- PRICE-IMPACT (both sides): realized proceeds = per-tranche integral Sigma(bid(q) - ask(q)); source ask RISES as supply depletes, sink bid FALLS as it saturates. REUSE the tour solver's realized-sink-tranche model + market_absorption_ledger + market_data supply/trade_volume; EXTEND to the buy side (source depletion) if that half is not already modeled.
- OPTIMAL VOLUME: buy/sell only while the MARGINAL unit still clears the floor: optimal_q = argmax Sigma(bid(q)-ask(q)) s.t. marginal >= floor. Achievable = min(cargo cap, spend_cap/avg-price, optimal_q, sink absorption headroom). Often optimal_q is WELL UNDER a heavy's hold on a thin exotic.
- RANKING: realized $/hr = (realized net at optimal_q) / trip_time. Filters: min-spread floor; SAFETY EXCLUSION (open-contract goods + active construction materials — inherit idle-arb's contract-good guard so long-haul never cannibalizes contracts or the gate); the money envelope (Section 3).
- TRIP (out + backhaul): assign top out-lane -> buy G1 @ optimal_q -> multi-jump -> sell per-tranche (reserve via market_absorption_ledger); then re-rank return lanes RESTRICTED to origin-near-sink / end-near-source -> if best clears floor+guards load G2 and sell, else deadhead back. Each leg is ONE directed single-good lane.

== SECTION 3 — MONEY GUARDS (aggressive, fail-closed) ==
Envelope: default ~1M/haul, ~2M total long-haul exposure, both LIVE-tunable. A buy proceeds ONLY while ALL hold (else NO buy, RULINGS #4):
  (1) treasury - buy_cost >= 200000 contract cushion (FENCED — long-haul never dips into contract working capital);
  (2) buy_cost <= per-haul cap;
  (3) running_long_haul_exposure + buy_cost <= total-exposure cap.
Exposure = capital tied in in-flight long-haul cargo (bought, not yet sold), released on sale; the BACKHAUL buy counts against the same envelope. REUSE the shared ImmutableReserveFloor/EffectiveReserveFloor helper + idle-arb's per-leg/exposure guard helpers (not copies). 50k immutable floor (RULINGS #5) untouched (200k > 50k). Aggressive SIZING is Admiral-authorized (documented so the crafter IMPLEMENTS the caps rather than refusing them as guard-weakening; RULINGS #4 binds build agents, the Admiral sets values) — the mechanism is intact.

== SECTION 4 — EXECUTION, RESTART-RECOVERY, TESTING ==
- EXECUTION: one episode per cycle (serial, like idle-arb -> bounded, restart-idempotent). buy G1 @ optimal_q -> multi-jump via the SHARED travel()/route machinery -> sell per-tranche against the absorption reservation -> backhaul (rank return lanes; buy G2 if clears floor+guards else deadhead) -> re-evaluate.
- RESTART-RECOVERY (REUSE sp-m3122 — the reason sp-mepj sequences AFTER tour-watchdog): a long-haul hull is mid-multi-hop for a long time = the exact sp-m3122 hang risk. STATELESS re-derive on restart (read long-haul-tagged hulls + cargo/position from the DB, re-plan fresh: holding G1 -> resume selling toward its best sink; empty -> pick a new lane; NO fragile mid-jump resume). LIVENESS WATCHDOG: a long-haul container with zero PROGRESS for N minutes -> killed + relaunched; keyed on progress events so a legit long leg (jump cooldown/multi-hop) is NOT false-killed. ONE watchdog serves both trade tours + long-haul (shared, not copied).
- FAILED SELL / HELD CARGO (REUSE sp-2v69u offload): market moved / sink collapsed -> offload held cargo to the best available sink, book the loss, re-plan empty. Never strand a hull full; no buy-guard change.
- TESTING (RED-first): realized-price-impact ranking (thin-huge-spot lane ranks BELOW a solid one); optimal-volume caps the buy short of a collapsing market; guards fail-closed (cushion/per-haul/exposure, backhaul counted); execution buy->travel->sell->backhaul + deadhead fallback; restart mid-trip re-derives + resumes / silent container watchdog-relaunched / long leg NOT false-killed; isolation (never touches contract/untagged hulls); REUSE grep (zero duplicated tranche/travel/guard/watchdog logic, shared call sites only).

== CONSTRAINTS ==
No feature flag — ARMED on deploy. RULINGS: #2 deterministic/restart-idempotent; #3 single-writer for any config/claim; #4 money guards fail-closed + cushion fenced + never weakened; #5 50k floor untouched; #7 the command frigate is NEVER a long-haul hull; #13 lands via captain-gate. Protected paths untouched.

== SEQUENCING ==
Build AFTER sp-m3122 (tour-watchdog) is merged to main (reuses its watchdog + stateless-recovery). tour-watchdog gated first.

== ACCEPTANCE ==
- A long-haul-tagged hull autonomously discovers, prices (realized price-impact, both sides), and runs the top out-of-horizon lane by realized $/hr; opportunistic backhaul loads the return when profitable.
- Volume capped at optimal_q — never oversells into a collapsing market.
- Money guards fail-closed (cushion-fenced, per-haul + exposure caps, backhaul counted); caps live-tunable.

title: Consult: put TORWIND-1 (frigate, upgraded) on contract work? 115 cargo + speed 36 vs 400 fuel capacity
description: Admiral-directed consult (2026-07-10 16:22Z). QUESTION: should the command frigate join the contract pool? ANALYST ASKS: (1) net cycle-time delta including refuel stops (contract legs are mostly in-KA42 where fuel stations are dense — does the 400 cap even bind?); (2) marginal $/hr of adding it vs the pool's current positioning gain; (3) any reason the command hull should stay reserved (era-close tasks, emergency bridge capacity).
notes:
TRADE-ANALYST VERDICT (sp-pof6: frigate onto contract work) — 2026-07-10 ~16:30Z

**YES — pool it, with one policy tag. This is the least marginal call of the week: T1 is the fleet's PROVEN best contract hull, it now fits every contract in one trip, and it currently earns zero.**

**(1) The 400-fuel cap does NOT bind on KA42 contract cycles — by geometry and by station density.**
- Geometry: home legs are short. My hub analysis measured weighted mean travel-to-source 38.8u on a 4-hub net (13.8u on 6); the contract-source clusters (A1-A4 co-located, D39/40, E41-43, H49/50/52) sit 50-130u apart. Even the far-tail legs (J56 cluster, 620-800u) fit inside one 400-fuel tank one-way.
- Density: EVERY home market I have read sells fuel at 68-72, vol 180+. Refueling happens at docks the cycle already visits (buy stop, delivery stop) — zero extra stops. The cap would only bind on cross-gate tours, which contracts don't fly. Fuel cost delta vs a light: nil (burn scales with distance, not speed).
- Precedent: T1 ran 69 cycles/day on 07-08 — the fleet record — on this same tank, WHILE double-tripping ~58% of contracts on its old 40-hold. The fuel question was already answered by a day of the hardest chaining any hull has done.

**(2) Marginal $/hr: ~+40-55k/hr, and it's the TAIL-KILLER.**
- Cycle structure (sp-5bmq): ~2/3 travel. Speed 36 cuts travel legs ÷2.4 → a ~20min mean cycle falls toward ~12min when T1 flies it. On the serial pipeline (cadence ~3/hr fleet, mean 46.6k ≈ 140k/hr), T1's marginal contribution is taking the legs it is uniquely best at: (a) the FAR-SOURCE tails my decomposition blamed for 5/8 of 30-min cycles — a 763u leg drops from ~21min at spd-15 to ~9min; (b) every fat-tier contract (108-181k, delivers J56/A1) that currently rides a light. Expected cadence lift 3→~3.8-4.2/hr ≈ **+37-56k/hr**, against its current contribution of ZERO (idle at JP61-D12X). At 45h remaining that's +1.7-2.5M of era income for no capex.
- Fit: 115 hold ≥ every observed contract (corpus max 78u, median 47) — single-trip on 100% of loads; its old record was set despite double-tripping.
- Housekeeping: sell/jettison the 2 dead processor units at the first dock (frees slots, ~zero value).

**(3) Reserve arguments — one is real, and a TAG solves it, not idleness.**
- Era-close tasks: administrative (register/archive), not hull-bound. No reservation needed.
- Emergency bridge/courier: REAL but thin — T1 is the fastest hull, and 'fastest courier' is worth preserving as an OPTION. Solution: pool it with a release-on-demand tag (dedicated_fleet=command retained, coordinator treats it as claimable; captain can yank it in one order). An idle option costing 40-55k/hr for 45h is a 2M premium for insurance we have never once used — the tag buys the same insurance for free.
- Watchdog noise (jetm exemption): ops detail — if pool membership changes its heartbeat profile, adjust the exemption rather than the assignment; do not let monitoring config decide fleet economics.

**Confidence.** HIGH — every input is measured (fuel geometry from waypoint coords, cycle structure from 450-contract decomposition, T1's own 69-cycle day, current idleness from the snapshot). **Flips:** if contracts start demanding >115u loads (none in 450+ observed) or a cross-gate contract class appears (fuel cap then matters), re-examine; if the serial pipeline's negotiation rate — not travel — becomes the binder after the hub+frigate lifts, further speed adds nothing and T1 should return to lab-shuttle duty between claims (dual-duty like the lights).

Release-on-demand = repin to command, one command, doctrine noted here. Processors DON'T sell anywhere (analyst's sell-at-dock failed: not listed at any market, scout survey confirmed) — 2 units ride as ballast in the 115 hold. T1 homeward: JP61 gate -> UQ16 -> PA3 -> KA42 (speed 36, ~15min); contract coordinator claims it at home. Expected lift: +40-55k/hr, kills the far-source tails (763u leg 21->9min), single-trips every load.

title: Tour P2 economics: absorption reservations + recovery-externality pricing — five engines coordinate the shared market depth (1ek0 P2 flagship)
description: Admiral-greenlit (in-chat 2026-07-10) as the 1ek0 P2 flagship. THE PROBLEM: continuous packed tours + arb-run + idle-arb legs + pre-positioning deposits all absorb the SAME market depth with zero cross-container coordination — the lbbm co-dump (-80k, bid 19,950→4) was this class; the lane mutex + flat 20min hold are the tactical patch. THE DESIGN GOAL: (a) ABSORPTION RESERVATIONS — a planner that schedules tranches against a market-good-side RESERVES that depth for its plan horizon, and other planners see remaining-unreserved depth (the A-cap generalized cross-plan); (b) RECOVERY-EXTERNALITY PRICING — dumping into a market prices the recovery time it imposes (the model's per-tier half-lives, 180-413min) against every engine's future legs, so the planner internalizes the crowding cost instead of the mutex externally blocking it. DESIGN PHASE FIRST (fable per RULINGS #9): where reservations live (daemon-side store vs solver input), staleness/expiry semantics, which engines consume (tour solver via snapshot; arb/idle-arb via dispatcher), interaction with the depth model + profit-primary + the D39 calibration, and what replaces/subsumes the lbbm mutex+hold. Design lands on THIS bead; Admiral rules on open questions; build lanes follow.
design:
# sp-78ai DESIGN — absorption reservations + recovery-externality pricing
Design-investigation pass (fable, RULINGS #9), 2026-07-10. NO code in this pass.
Every load-bearing claim verified in code; citations are file:line at HEAD (600ec5d).

## 0. The problem, verified

Five engines absorb the same market depth; the ONLY cross-engine signal is the market
cache, which is refreshed synchronously after every executed transaction
(cargo_transaction.go:305,443-463 — refreshMarketData → ScanAndSaveMarket overwrite).
So EXECUTED absorption is visible within seconds; what is invisible is:

- **Window 1 — in-flight absorption (plan→execution gap).** Engine A plans/dispatches
  against quoted depth; until A's trade lands and the cache refreshes, engine B quotes
  the same pre-absorption prices. This is exactly sp-lbbm (both hulls quoted the
  pre-crush 19,950 bid; −80k). Duration: minutes (arb leg) to hours (late legs of a
  6-hop tour).
- **Window 2 — post-execution recovery (the externality).** After A dumps, the cache
  truthfully shows the crushed price, so followers avoid the sink (self-correcting for
  AVOIDANCE). But (a) nothing tells the FIRST mover that its marginal tranche costs
  everyone a 3-7h recovery window (fitted half-lives: GROWING 180.7min / WEAK 279.1 /
  STRONG 386.1 / RESTRICTED 413.7 / untagged 1074.3 — model_artifacts/market_model.json
  `recovery`), and (b) the per-plan A-cap resets at every plan boundary: consecutive
  plans can each lawfully take 2 tranches at the same sink — the D39 ladder rebuilt
  ACROSS plans. The artifact's recovery half-lives are loaded (tour_handler.py:44-46)
  and consumed by NOTHING at decision time; the only recovery behavior in the fleet is
  the flat 20-min hold (idle_arb.go:144-151), whose own docstring concedes the model
  knows the real window and 20min deliberately understates it
  (idle_arb_lane_mutex.go:39-52).

Per-engine coordination status, verified:
- **Tours** (one-shot + continuous, Iterations=-1: run_tour_coordinator.go:99): the only
  depth-aware planner. Tranche prices decay per (supply|activity) tier per
  tradeVolume-sized tranche (tour_solver.py:96-125); pools are shared per
  (waypoint, good, side) across the whole tour ("depth is a property of the market, not
  of the leg index", tour_solver.py:299-302); A-cap = 2 planned tranches per
  (market, good, side) per tour (tour_solver.py:85,274-275), documented as "the interim
  stand-in for phase-2 recovery-externality pricing" (tour_solver.py:37-44). Sees
  nothing another container has planned.
- **Trade-route circuits**: scanLanes ranks cached spreads with no depth model and,
  confirmed under sp-q1ca, NO awareness of other circuits — two daemons "WILL rank
  identically and both select the same top lane"; resolution is emergent cache refresh
  or a bid-floor stop, "not the ranker itself" (run_trade_route_coordinator_lanes.go:29-46).
- **Arb-run one-shots**: quoted margin at dispatch, live re-verify fail-closed before
  buy, per-tranche sell floor at a fraction of the quoted bid — the H50 fix
  (run_arb_coordinator.go:15,43-60,347-358). Live truth only; no cross-container view.
- **Idle-arb legs**: uohe guard stack + the lbbm lane mutex — one hull per (good, sink)
  in flight + flat 20-min post-termination hold (idle_arb.go:537-583,
  idle_arb_lane_mutex.go:63-160). IN-MEMORY and per-dispatcher
  (idle_arb_lane_mutex.go:54-61): blocks only its own legs; a tour selling into a sink
  an idle-arb leg just crushed is invisible to it, and vice versa.
- **Pre-positioning deposits**: the deposit SIDE is a synthetic sink with no market
  impact, no decay, no A-cap (routing.proto:415-433, tour_solver.py:287-297) — nothing
  to reserve there. But the BUY side of a deposit leg absorbs real ask-side depth in a
  foreign market; it rides the tour plan's pools already, so it coordinates exactly as
  far as the tour does (i.e., not across containers).
- sp-2dv4's "absorption bound" (chain_margin_guard.go:30,146) is a single-container
  pre-spend projection — a within-plan bound like the A-cap, not coordination.

Decomposition the design follows: **reservations fix window 1; a decaying recovery
shadow fixes cross-plan laddering and re-entry timing; the honest externality "price"
is expressed in quantity space (occupied depth), not as an objective term** (§3).

## 1. Q1 — Reservation store + semantics

**Where: a daemon-side DB table (the w3he shape), not an in-memory coordinator, not
solver state.** The clinching argument is the EXECUTED shadow: a restart could
re-assert in-flight plans from recovered containers (they know their plans), but an
executed dump's recovery shadow is derivable from nothing after a restart — in-memory
loses it exactly when lbbm punished it. DB rows survive (RULINGS #2), and the
factory_spend_reservations machinery is the proven sibling: insert-then-check under a
per-player transaction-scoped advisory lock, release-on-every-exit, self-cleaning
stale sweep inside Reserve, no background job
(spend_reservation_repository.go:22,28,43,66-128,132-156; model at models.go:459-481;
wired at main.go:579; consumer discipline at production_executor.go:316-325).
The Python solver stays stateless per locked spec decision #5 — it NEVER reads the
store; Go assembles the netted view into the request (§2).

**One table, two row states** — `market_absorption_ledger` (name = build-lane detail):

| column | notes |
|---|---|
| id (uuid PK), player_id (idx), container_id, engine | engine ∈ tour/arb/idle-arb (telemetry + reclaim) |
| waypoint_symbol, good_symbol, side | composite idx with player_id — the outstanding query |
| state | PLANNED (in-flight intent) or EXECUTED (recovery shadow) |
| units | planned absorption / realized absorbed units |
| tier_at_write | supply\|activity stamped at write; readers resolve half-life from the artifact |
| quoted_price | telemetry only |
| created_at, executed_at, expires_at (idx) | lifecycle below |

**Lifecycle.**
- **PLANNED**: written at plan-accept (tours) or dispatch (arb/idle-arb). Released by
  the owner on every exit path (w3he defer discipline). Converted to EXECUTED per
  (waypoint,good,side) when the trades there complete, stamped with realized units +
  the live tier read the executor already performs (executeTrade's live re-verify).
  Expiry: per-plan TTL = 2× projected tour seconds + slack floor (flags, RULINGS #5) —
  a wedged container cannot hold depth past it. Dead-container reclaim: PLANNED rows
  whose container_id is no longer live in the container registry are swept inside
  every Reserve (the sp-vjwb orphan-reconcile precedent) — age alone cannot
  distinguish dead here (unlike w3he's 5-min window: healthy absorption reservations
  legitimately live the whole flight, w3he's live seconds).
- **EXECUTED**: never blocks by full units forever — readers decay it as
  units × 0.5^(elapsed/half_life(tier_at_write)) and treat the residual as occupied
  depth. expires_at = executed_at + hard cap (flag, default ~24h ≥ 2× the worst named
  tier); reads filter `expires_at > now`, physical deletion happens in Reserve's sweep
  (reads never write). No threshold for writing markers: units are recorded as-is and
  the tranche arithmetic (units/trade_volume) self-scales micro-trades to zero effect.
- **Reserve is CONDITIONAL (fail closed, RULINGS #4)**: inside the advisory-lock
  transaction — sweep, insert all rows for the plan, then check per (waypoint,good,side):
  decayed outstanding (all states, all containers) + this plan's units ≤
  fleet-wide cap = A-cap tranches × trade_volume. Any breach → roll back the WHOLE
  plan's rows (all-or-nothing) and report which sink failed. The tour coordinator
  treats a rejected reservation exactly like a degraded leg: stateless re-plan
  (machinery exists, run_tour_coordinator.go:503-531) against a fresh snapshot whose
  netting now shows the contested sink occupied. This closes the snapshot→accept
  TOCTOU the same way w3he closes check→buy. Lock key = (namespace "ABSB", player_id)
  — per-player serialization like w3he; per-row locks invite ordering deadlocks and
  Reserve calls are rare (per plan-accept/dispatch) and fast.
- **Era-scoping: NO era_id column.** These are ephemeral operational rows (the w3he
  "deliberately no FK" rationale, models.go:466-470). An era reset kills the
  containers → PLANNED rows are swept by the dead-container reclaim; EXECUTED rows
  age out on their hard cap and refer to (waypoint,good) keys whose quotes reset
  anyway. Era columns are for rows that persist weeks (waypoints/gate edges), not
  minutes-to-hours.
- **Restart (RULINGS #2)**: rows are DB state — they survive. Recovered containers
  still match their container_id and keep their holds; unrecovered containers' rows
  are swept. Strictly stronger than the lane mutex's documented in-memory concession
  (idle_arb_lane_mutex.go:54-61), which cannot protect the post-termination hold or
  anything cross-engine across a restart.

## 2. Q2 — Who writes, who reads, and the Go/Python boundary

**Writers (reserve + convert):**
- **Tour coordinator** (flagship): reserve at plan-accept — after the Feasible check
  at run_tour_coordinator.go:480, before executePlan at :503 — one PLANNED row per
  (waypoint,good,side) in the plan. On re-plan (:524): release all outstanding
  PLANNED rows for this container, reserve fresh from the new plan. Convert
  PLANNED→EXECUTED per sink as legs complete. Release-all on every exit path
  (deferred). Continuous circuits do this naturally per tour iteration.
- **Arb-run and idle-arb dispatchers**: reserve the sell side at launch — the exact
  seam where noteLaunch marks the mutex today (idle_arb.go:583) — units = full-hold
  worst case, TTL = 2× projected flight + slack. Release immediately if the launch
  fails post-reserve. The arb container converts to EXECUTED at sale completion with
  realized units + live tier (it already live-reads the market for the sell floor,
  run_arb_coordinator.go:347-358).
- **Deposits**: no writer — synthetic sink has no market depth (verified §0); the
  deposit's real BUY side is already inside the tour's plan rows.
- **Trade-route circuits: READ-ONLY in v1** (open question #1, §6). Circuits have no
  discrete bounded plan to reserve (reserving a circuit's future is unbounded), they
  move one hold per iteration, and the bid-floor stop bounds their loss class. Their
  executed trades already surface through the cache refresh.

**Readers (remaining-depth):**
- **Tour planner — via a new request field (the bc27/dchv additive-proto precedent),
  not Go-side snapshot mutation.** Mutating snapshot rows would have to lie (shrink
  trade_volume = wrong transaction size; pre-decay quotes = wrong prices). Instead:
  `repeated MarketAbsorption absorption = 6` on OptimizeTradeTourRequest
  (routing.proto:434-442): {waypoint_symbol, good_symbol, side, units_planned,
  units_recovering} — Go decays EXECUTED rows at assembly time so the solver stays
  clock-free and the recovery curve is consumed in exactly ONE place (the Go decay
  fn). Solver netting semantics (the price-honesty subtlety):
  - **units_planned** (in-flight, cache still pre-absorption): consume tranche
    capacity AND advance the price schedule — the plan's first tranche at that sink
    is priced at decay step ceil(units_planned/trade_volume), because those earlier
    tranches are being taken by someone at those prices.
  - **units_recovering** (executed, cache already shows the crushed quote): consume
    tranche CAPACITY ONLY — pricing still starts at the live quote's step 0, or the
    damage would be double-counted (quote already reflects it).
  Mechanically this is _TranchePool initialization + the cap arithmetic in pool()
  (tour_solver.py:128-148,264-278); the A-cap budget now counts pre-consumed tranches,
  which makes the cap FLEET-WIDE-outstanding instead of per-plan — the A-cap
  generalized cross-plan, exactly the bead's design goal (a).
- **Idle-arb dispatcher**: one batched outstanding query per pass →
  pickHubLocalLane consults the map — skip:reserved (new reason alongside
  skipReasonLaneHeld, idle_arb.go:387-394) when planned outstanding > 0 on the
  (good,sink) or the decayed recovering residual ≥ the shadow floor (knob, §6). v1 is
  binary skip, not quote-adjustment: the leg's own live-verify + relative floor +
  sell floor already own price truth, and this keeps the dispatcher loop pure — note
  the mutex docstring's objection (idle_arb_lane_mutex.go:44-46) was to coupling the
  dispatcher to the ROUTING SERVICE (an RPC in the decision loop); loading the
  repo-checked artifact JSON once at boot into a pure decay function is a different
  weight class entirely.
- **Trade-route scanLanes**: read-only — subtract decayed outstanding from each
  lane's effective depth in ranking and skip sinks under a heavy shadow, replacing
  "discover the collision by margin-death" (run_trade_route_coordinator_lanes.go:44-46)
  with avoid-by-knowledge.

**Go-side model access**: Go loads the SAME market_model.json at daemon boot (path
flag, RULINGS #5; version logged; fit pipeline and artifact untouched). Artifact
unreadable Go-side → decay cannot be computed → EXECUTED residuals are treated as
UNDECAYED until their hard-cap expiry (fail closed on reserved depth per RULINGS #4)
while trading on unreserved depth continues unhindered — reconciling #4 with the
spec's "trading is never blocked on the planner" posture.

## 3. Q3 — Recovery-externality pricing: the honest form

The marginal cost a dump imposes on OTHERS is the profit that depth would have earned
during the recovery it triggers. Computing that exactly requires future demand at the
sink — unknowable. The three candidate forms:

(a) **Objective term** (profit − externality): requires a utilization factor λ (how
much of the recovery window others would actually have used) — a made-up knob whose
error silently reshapes tour selection. It also re-introduces a shaped objective
through the side door after the Admiral explicitly ruled profit-primary against
rate-shaping (tour_solver.py:27-35, spec §Solve-4 revision), and it would need its own
reporting split to keep plan-vs-realized telemetry honest.

(b) **Reduced-available-depth with half-life decay** (the EXECUTED shadow of §1):
prices the externality in QUANTITY space — the absorber doesn't pay a synthetic tax;
instead nobody (including its own next plan) can step into the hole until the model
says it has regrown. Enforceable, fail-closed, and it is precisely "the cap can relax
to the economics" promised in tour_solver.py:41-44: fleet-wide outstanding absorption
at any sink is bounded at A-cap tranches, decaying on the fitted curve.

**Recommendation: (b) now; (a) as a REPORTED shadow-price only.** Every plan logs
`projected_recovery_burden` (per sink: units × half_life(tier), summed) next to
profit/cph — the Admiral gets the externality made visible in telemetry, selection
stays profit-primary, and if burn-in evidence ever shows (b) leaving value on the
table, (a) can graduate from reported to selecting the same way cph earned its
tiebreak seat. D39 calibration untouched: no fitted coefficient changes, no change to
how impact curves price the tranches a plan DOES take (§2's double-count rule keeps
price math exact); only tranche AVAILABILITY is consulted differently.

## 4. Q4 — What subsumes lbbm's mutex + flat hold; what stays

Retires (lane 5, after burn-in evidence):
- **The flat 20-min hold** → replaced by the EXECUTED shadow decaying on fitted
  half-lives (a RESTRICTED sink stays occupied ~hours, honestly, instead of 20min).
- **The in-flight (good,sink) mutex** → subsumed by PLANNED reservations: cross-ENGINE
  now, not just cross-pass within one dispatcher; within-pass dedupe property is
  preserved because the reservation is written synchronously at dispatch (same seam,
  idle_arb.go:583). Restart posture strictly improves (§1).
  Rollout: mutex runs in parallel with store consultation for one observation window
  (flag-gated, RULINGS #5), then idle_arb_lane_mutex.go is deleted.

Stays, untouched (RULINGS #4 — layered defense, live truth outranks any ledger):
- **Per-tranche sell floor** (run_arb_coordinator.go:347-358) — the last line when
  reservations are wrong/late; live truth beats the model.
- **Live re-verify + relative margin floor** (idle_arb.go:414-421; tour tolerance
  check) and every money guard beneath them.
- **The per-plan A-cap** stays in v1: the fleet-wide cap equals it only when the store
  is consulted and healthy; the per-plan form is the proven local guard and costs
  nothing. Its RELAXATION (to >2 tranches when the shadow says depth exists) is
  deliberately the LAST lane, gated on the Admiral's evidence standard (§6).

persistence/absorption_ledger repository + model (+ AutoMigrate at models.go:610

tour_handler.py conversion; grpc_routing_client.go + mocks; run_tour_coordinator.go
reserve/convert/release at :480/:524/executeTrade/exit paths; assembly-time decay in

## 6. Q6 — Open questions for the Admiral

1. **Trade-route circuits: read-only v1 (recommended) or full reserve-writers?**
   Writing means inventing a plan horizon for an engine that has none and touching the
   oldest money path; the residual circuit-vs-circuit race is the documented sp-q1ca
   class with a one-hold bound. Join later if telemetry shows circuit-vs-tour
   collisions.
2. **Shadow aggressiveness knobs** (economics, not engineering): the floor fraction at
   which a recovering shadow stops blocking (proposal: 50% of one tranche), and the
   EXECUTED hard-cap lifetime (proposal: 24h). Both flags (RULINGS #5).
3. **Externality objective term**: confirm REPORT-ONLY (projected_recovery_burden
   logged per plan, never selecting) — or name the telemetry bar at which a
   shadow-priced objective experiment is warranted.
4. **A-cap relaxation standard**: what evidence relaxes the per-plan 2-tranche cap
   (the tour_solver.py:41-44 promise)? Proposal: only after L5 telemetry shows the cap
   binding on a meaningful share of profitable plans AND zero cross-plan ladder
   incidents over the window.

## 7. RULINGS compliance

#2 store is DB-backed, restart-survivable, dead-container-swept (w3he/vjwb idioms).
#3 daemon-only writers; Python stays stateless/read-nothing. #4 conditional Reserve
fails closed; artifact-unreadable degrades to MORE conservative blocking, never less;
no existing guard weakened (sell floor/live-verify/A-cap all stay). #5 every knob a
flag (TTL slack, shadow floor, hard cap, consult gates, artifact path). #9 this pass
is the deliberate economics design; lane tiers assigned. D39: fit pipeline, artifact,
and per-tranche price math untouched — only tranche availability is consulted
differently, with the planned-vs-recovering split preventing price double-counting.
