design:
# Fleet-Allocation Ownership Architecture — Design (for Admiral/captain review)

Status: DESIGN ONLY, no code written. Author: harbormaster (shipwright rig).
Rev 2: converges sp-snmb's shipped mechanism into this design (not a parallel
one) and locks the three open questions from rev 1 as decisions.

## 1. Root cause, restated precisely from code (not just symptoms)

The fleet has **three independent "claim a ship" code paths today**, only one
of which is atomic, and **one dedication concept that only one of five
coordinators knows about**:

| Coordinator | How it claims a ship | Atomic (DB-locked)? | Dedication-aware? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Manufacturing | `ShipRepository.ClaimShip` (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` tx) | Yes | Discovery only (via `FindIdleLightHaulers`) |
| Factory | `claimShipForFactory`: in-memory `ship.IsIdle()` check → `AssignToContainer` → `shipRepo.Save` | **No** — classic read-modify-write race | Discovery only (same `FindIdleLightHaulers` call) |
| Contract | `ClaimShip` (fleet coordinator) + `FindIdleDedicatedShips` for its own pool | Yes | **Read+write** — the only coordinator that sets `DedicatedFleet` |
| Trade-route | Direct `shipRepo.FindBySymbol` → mutate → `shipRepo.Save` | **No** — same race as factory | **None** — doesn't call `FindIdleLightHaulers` at all |
| Gas | Same pattern as trade-route | **No** | **None** |

Two distinct bugs are being conflated by the "poaching" symptom, and the
design has to fix both:

- **Bug A — missing tags, not a race**: `task_assignment_manager.go` already
  calls `contract.FindIdleLightHaulers`, which already excludes any ship with
  `DedicatedFleet() != ""`. TORWIND-19 was poachable because *no fleet ever
  tagged it* — `bulk_circuit`/trade-route/gas dedication doesn't exist as a
  concept yet, only `contract` does, and only when the operator remembers to
  pass `--dedicated-ships`. This is a **coverage gap**, fixed by generalizing
  the tag + a real assign/unassign command (sections 4, 7).
- **Bug B — the real race**: `dedicated_fleet` is checked in exactly one
  function (`FindIdleLightHaulers`), which is a **discovery** read. The
  **claim/write** path (`ClaimShip`) never checks it. Any caller that skips
  discovery — or any of the two non-atomic claim paths above — can grab a
  dedicated hull with zero resistance. This is a **structural enforcement
  gap**, fixed by moving the check into the one atomic choke point (section 4).

Fixing only the tag-coverage gap (giving trade-route/gas/factory a fleet name)
without fixing the enforcement gap leaves the TOCTOU exactly as exploitable as
today — it would just take a different bug to trigger it. Both are in scope.

## 2. Design principle (binding constraint)

Per Admiral doctrine already on record: **prefer static dedicated assignment
over dynamic claim arbitration**. This design does not introduce priorities,
tethers, or a scoring/arbitration engine. It generalizes the one static
primitive that already shipped (`Ship.DedicatedFleet()`), and it accepts idle
time on a dedicated hull as a price, not a defect, when the owning line's
throughput matters more than fleet-wide utilization.

## 3. sp-snmb → general convergence (read this before section 4)

sp-snmb already shipped a **partial, contract-only** version of this exact
mechanism. Nothing below is a parallel system — every shipped piece folds
into the general one, and Phase 1 (section 9) is scoped specifically to make
that true in code, not just on paper.

| sp-snmb piece (shipped) | Today | After convergence |
|---|---|---|
| `dedicated_fleet` column | Contract-only values (`"contract"` or `""`) | **Same column, same type, zero migration.** Becomes multi-valued: `"contract"`, `"manufacturing"`, `"factory"`, `"trade_route"`, `"gas"`, or operator-chosen sub-fleet names (`"bulk_circuit"`). |
| `reconcileDedicatedFleet` (write path, driven by the `--dedicated-ships` CLI flag at coordinator startup) | Direct field mutation via `shipRepo.Save`, additive-only (no unassign), **the only setter that exists today** | **Demoted to a thin bootstrap wrapper.** At startup, for each configured symbol it calls the same `AssignShipFleetCommand{ShipSymbol, Fleet: "contract"}` that the new `fleet assign` CLI calls (section 7) — not a second write path. The direct-`Save` mutation is deleted, not kept alongside. |
| `FindIdleLightHaulers`'s `DedicatedFleet() != ""` skip (discovery-filter) | **The only enforcement that exists today** | **Unchanged, kept permanently — this is layer 1 of 2.** Cheap, read-side, shared by every caller "for free," no lock needed. It stays exactly as a fast pre-filter: don't even attempt a claim on a hull you can already see is spoken for. Layer 2 is the new atomic check inside `ClaimShip` (section 4) — the authoritative guarantee, closing the TOCTOU between a discovery read and a claim write. **Both layers coexist deliberately**: layer 1 is an optimization, layer 2 is the correctness guarantee; dropping either regresses something (drop layer 1 → every coordinator wastes cycles attempting doomed claims; drop layer 2 → the TOCTOU reopens). |
| `FindIdleDedicatedShips(ctx, playerID, shipRepo, dedicatedShips []string)` — contract's own symbol-list lookup; comment notes the caller-supplied list itself *is* the authorization, not a `DedicatedFleet()` check | Only contract has this; the list is whatever symbols the coordinator remembers from its own `--dedicated-ships` startup flag | **Replaced by `FindIdleShipsByFleet(ctx, playerID, shipRepo, fleet string)`** — filters `allShips` where `ship.DedicatedFleet() == fleet`, the mirror-image of `FindIdleLightHaulers`'s exclude filter. This is not additive — the symbol-list variant is deleted. Reason it can't just stay alongside: once `fleet assign`/`unassign` (section 7) can change dedication at any time, a coordinator's *remembered* symbol list goes stale the moment the captain reassigns a ship without restarting that coordinator. Reading `DedicatedFleet()` from the DB on every discovery pass is what makes reassignment actually live instead of "live after next restart." |
| `HomeShipHandler` (standby homing) | Contract-owned by package location only; its logic is already fleet-agnostic (`ShipSymbol` + `StandbyStations []string` in, stateless navigate-to-nearest, no contract-specific code in the body) | Moves to a neutral package; invoked by fleet name. Standby stations stop being a parameter the contract coordinator passes from its own CLI flags and become a property of the fleet itself (decision in section 10) — `HomeShipHandler` looks them up by fleet name instead of receiving them per-call. |

Net effect: after convergence there is exactly **one** column, **one**
writer (`AssignShipFleetCommand`), **one** read-side pre-filter
(`FindIdleLightHaulers`'s exclude check, unchanged), **one** "give me my
fleet's idle ships" query (`FindIdleShipsByFleet`, generalized), and **one**
homing handler. sp-snmb's contract behavior is preserved bit-for-bit from the
operator's point of view — same flag, same effect — it just stops being a
separate code path underneath.

## 4. Ownership model — the converged mechanism

**The write side**: a new CQRS command, `AssignShipFleetCommand` /
`AssignShipFleetHandler`, modeled 1:1 on the already-shipped sp-i1ku pattern
(`ReserveShipCommand` → `ReserveShipHandler` →
`ShipRepository.ReserveForCaptain`, same row-locking transaction shape).
`AssignShipFleetCommand{ShipSymbol, Fleet, PlayerID}` where `Fleet == ""`
clears dedication — this is what closes the additive-only gap in
`reconcileDedicatedFleet` (section 3) and is the real captain command from
requirement #4 (section 7). This is the **only** legitimate way to change
`dedicated_fleet` after convergence.

**The enforcement side**: `ClaimShip`'s signature grows one parameter —
`ClaimShip(ctx, shipSymbol, containerID, playerID, operation string) error`
— and its existing locked transaction grows one more branch, symmetric to
the `ShipReservedByCaptainError` check already there: if
`model.DedicatedFleet != "" && model.DedicatedFleet != operation`, return a
new `ShipDedicatedToOtherFleetError`. This is deliberately kept as a
*second* command from the assignment write, not fused into it — "who
permanently owns this hull" (assign) and "who holds it right now" (claim)
are different concerns, and fusing them would force every reallocation to
also force-claim the ship immediately, which isn't always wanted (e.g., let
the current job finish, new owner claims it next cycle).

**Why not just extend `ClaimShip` alone (no new command)?** That was
considered and rejected: it closes the enforcement gap but gives the captain
no way to *set* the tag, so requirement #4 still needs something — and
whatever that "something" is would end up being this same command. Building
both together, rather than deferring the command, is what makes this a
convergence instead of a second later patch.

**Why not keep `reconcileDedicatedFleet`'s direct-mutation approach and just
call it from more coordinators?** Rejected — perpetuates the additive-only
bug, keeps the write un-atomic (`Save`, not a locked transaction — two
operators reconfiguring dedication concurrently can race each other), and
gives the captain no CLI verb. Doesn't satisfy requirement #4 and is exactly
the "parallel mechanism" this revision is required to avoid.

No schema migration required — `dedicated_fleet` is already free-text
(section 3). Namespace stays a flat string, not a structured
`{operation, sub_fleet}` type (decision in section 10).

Implementation note to flag for whoever builds this: `ClaimShip` already
calls `r.shipListCache.Delete(playerID.Value())` after its write — there's
an in-memory cache in front of the repo. `AssignShipFleetHandler` must
invalidate the same cache after writing the tag, or a freshly-dedicated ship
can still show up in another coordinator's discovery for one stale-cache
window.

## 5. Cargo-fit / type-aware hull selection

Today, hull selection inside an operation is nearest-only
(`task_assignment_manager.go`'s `m.shipSelector.FindClosestShip`) — no
capacity check at all. This directly produces two of the cited symptoms:
frigates multi-tripping contracts, and the heavy freighter dumping 225 units
into a negative-margin vol-20 sink (the only hull *discovered* was grossly
oversized for the lot, and nothing in selection prefers a right-sized hull
over an oversized one).

**Recommended shared policy** (generalizes the Admiral's contract-specific
ruling into one reusable function, e.g.
`ship/selection.SelectHullForCargo(candidates []*Ship, unitsNeeded int, from Waypoint) (*Ship, Mode, error)`):

1. Filter candidates to role `HAULER`.
2. Among haulers, keep only those whose `CargoCapacity() >= unitsNeeded`
   (single-trip fit). If any exist, return the **nearest one among the
   fitting set** — never the nearest overall, so a right-sized hull always
   beats an oversized one that happens to be one hop closer.
3. If no hauler fits in one trip, return the nearest hauler regardless of
   capacity, tagged `Mode = MultiTrip` — an explicit, logged multi-trip
   decision, not a silent frigate substitution.
4. Only if **zero haulers are idle at all** (not merely zero that fit) does
   the command ship/frigate become eligible, and only if the caller opted in
   (mirrors today's `CommandShipPolicy`) — last resort, never a first choice.
5. If nothing qualifies, return `NoHullAvailable` and let the caller decide
   to wait or escalate.

This is a pure function over already-loaded candidates, so it drops into
contract's existing selection point today and into mfg's
`task_assignment_manager.go` / trade-route's circuit-fill logic / the heavy
freighter's dispatch with no repository changes. Package placement: **not**
inside `contract` (mfg/trade-route importing from `contract` would be a
layering smell) — lives in a neutral package, e.g.
`internal/application/ship/selection`, that `contract` also imports going
forward, deleting the contract-local copy.

## 6. Standby / pre-positioning

Converges per section 3's table, corrected from rev 2: `HomeShipHandler`'s
*destination-selection* logic is **not** staying untouched — see "Balanced
hub assignment" below, which replaces its one `shared.FindNearestWaypoint`
call. What's still a pure generalization, as originally stated: everything
else in the handler's body (stateless, no temporary container/assignment
ceremony, no contract-specific code) — only a package move and a call-site
change, becoming invokable by any coordinator with idle dedicated ships, by
fleet name.

**Decision (section 10): standby stations are a property of the fleet, not
a per-coordinator flag.** Defined once per fleet name and looked up by
`HomeShipHandler` at homing time, instead of every coordinator re-declaring
its own `--standby-stations` list. This is the one piece of this design that
isn't a pure generalization of existing code — it implies a small
fleet-config record (fleet name → standby stations, and a natural home for
future fleet-level settings) alongside the per-ship `dedicated_fleet` tag.
Sized deliberately small: a lookup keyed by fleet name, not a new subsystem.

**Invariant: continuous re-homing, every cycle, not just at startup.** This
is not new behavior to build — it's already live in
`run_fleet_coordinator.go`'s per-task ship-selection loop (~lines 356-375):
whenever the loop rotates from one selected ship to a different one, the
*previous* ship is homed if it's dedicated (fire-and-forget `HomeShipCommand`
dispatch) — on every rotation, for the lifetime of the coordinator process,
not a one-shot call at boot. The generalization in this section must
preserve that shape as a **guaranteed invariant**, stated explicitly so
Phase 3 can't regress it by accident: *any idle-and-waiting dedicated
hauler is re-homed every cycle it goes idle, for as long as the coordinator
runs, using whichever event that coordinator's own loop already uses to
detect "this ship just freed up."* The trigger event's exact shape differs
per coordinator (contract's is `previousShipSymbol != selectedShip` inside
one rotating loop; other coordinators may detect idleness differently) —
Phase 3's coordinator-by-coordinator rollout (section 9) is exactly where
each coordinator's own "ship just went idle" event gets wired to the shared
homing call. What must not vary is the guarantee itself: homing is
re-evaluated every time, never cached from the last decision or run once at
startup.

**Balanced hub assignment (replaces `FindNearestWaypoint`).** Today's
`HomeShipHandler` (sp-snmb) sends every idle dedicated hauler to the single
nearest standby station via `shared.FindNearestWaypoint`. Observed in
production: this clumps the fleet — e.g. 3 haulers parked at J56, none near
H49/B7 — because "nearest" is evaluated per-ship with no knowledge of where
the *other* idle haulers already are or are headed. A hauler homed to a
station nobody needs covered isn't pre-positioned, it's just parked.

Precedent already exists in this codebase for capacity-aware, non-greedy
distribution — this policy adapts rather than invents:
- `domain/contract.FleetAssigner.AssignShipsToTargets` already distributes a
  ship list across target waypoints with a per-target cap
  (`MaxShipsPerMarket`) and nearest-available-with-remaining-capacity
  selection, specifically to avoid over-concentration.
- `BalanceShipPositionHandler`'s `ShipBalancer.SelectOptimalBalancingPosition`
  already scores candidate markets by a "Distance + Coverage Score" for the
  *non*-dedicated hauler case, taking the rest of the idle-hauler pool into
  account rather than scoring each ship in isolation.

Neither existing mechanism weights by contract value — both are pure
distance/capacity balancers. The new policy for dedicated standby hubs:

1. Each standby station carries a **value weight** — the trade-analyst crew
   role's per-hub contract-value ranking. This design treats the ranking as
   an external input it consumes, not a Go ranking engine it builds; the
   fleet-config record from the decision above is the natural home to store
   it (e.g. station entries become `{waypoint, weight}` instead of a bare
   symbol list).
2. A station counts as **covered** if a dedicated hauler is already sitting
   there or already homing there — both count, which is what stops two
   haulers converging on the same already-covered hub in the same cycle.
3. When a dedicated hauler goes idle: assign it to the **highest-weight
   currently-uncovered** standby station in its fleet's list. Break ties by
   travel distance (cheapest reposition among equally-valuable uncovered
   options).
4. If every standby station is already covered, fall back to nearest
   station overall (today's behavior) — a second hauler stacking onto an
   already-covered high-value hub still beats parking at a low-value one
   for the sake of being "uncovered."
5. Rebalancing is implicit, not a separate scheduled pass: because step 3
   runs on every idle-transition (per the continuous re-homing invariant
   above), the assignment recomputes fresh every time a hauler frees up, or
   a previously-homed hauler gets dispatched away and un-covers its station
   for the next idle hauler to claim.

This explicitly **replaces** the `shared.FindNearestWaypoint` call in
`HomeShipHandler` (today at `home_ship.go:85`) with a coverage-weighted
selection over the fleet's standby list plus the current
position/in-flight-destination of sibling dedicated ships — the handler
needs read visibility into the rest of its fleet, which it doesn't today
(today's call is single-ship, stateless). That's a real, if small, increase
in what the handler reads — it still costs no container/assignment
ceremony (per section 3), just a wider read before the same single
navigate-if-needed write.

## 7. Captain re-allocation command

**Decision (section 10): one `fleet` command group**, not folded into
`ship`:

```
spacetraders fleet assign   --ship TORWIND-19 --fleet bulk_circuit
spacetraders fleet unassign --ship TORWIND-19          # clears dedication (Fleet: "")
spacetraders fleet list                                 # every fleet name, its members, its standby stations
```

Precedent for the plumbing: sp-i1ku's `ship reserve`/`ship release` pair —
CLI → gRPC daemon-client call → `AssignShipFleetCommand` →
`AssignShipFleetHandler` → repository, persisted, restart-safe. `fleet
assign`/`unassign` follow the identical shape, just a new command group and
a new handler instead of reusing `ReserveShip`'s.

This supersedes `reconcileDedicatedFleet`'s coordinator-flag-only mutation
as the *only* sanctioned way to change dedication (section 3) — the
`--dedicated-ships` startup flag becomes a convenience wrapper that calls
`fleet assign` once per symbol at boot, not a separate path.

## 8. Restart-survival

Already satisfied for the static tag today — `dedicated_fleet` is a
persisted `ship_models` column, not in-memory state, so it survives a
restart regardless of which coordinator set it. The new fleet-config record
(section 6, standby stations) needs the same treatment: a persisted table,
not coordinator-local memory, or standby homing would silently lose its
target list on every restart.

The gap is on the *dynamic claim* side for the two non-atomic paths
(factory, trade-route, gas): their `Save`-based claims persist fine, so a
restart doesn't lose the assignment record itself — the risk is concurrent
corruption *before* a restart, not data loss *at* restart (see section 9,
Phase 2). `ReleaseAllActive`'s existing restart-reconciliation pass already
correctly excludes captain reservations by `assignment_owner`; it needs no
change for dedication, since dedication and active-assignment are already
orthogonal fields.

## 9. Migration plan (phased, so contract's income-critical path is never blocked)

**Phase 1 — converge, don't parallel-build:**
- Add the `ShipDedicatedToOtherFleetError` branch inside `ClaimShip`'s
  existing transaction (section 4).
- Ship `AssignShipFleetCommand` + `AssignShipFleetHandler` + the `fleet`
  CLI/gRPC surface (sections 4, 7).
- **Delete `reconcileDedicatedFleet`'s direct-`Save` mutation** and replace
  it with calls to `AssignShipFleetCommand` — this is the specific change
  that prevents two live write paths to the same column existing at once.
- **Delete the symbol-list `FindIdleDedicatedShips`** and replace contract's
  call site with the generalized `FindIdleShipsByFleet(ctx, playerID,
  shipRepo, "contract")` — this is the specific change that prevents two
  live "find my dedicated ships" queries existing at once.
- `FindIdleLightHaulers`'s exclude filter is untouched (section 3) —
  nothing to converge there, it was already correct and shared.

Net: contract's operator-facing behavior (`--dedicated-ships` flag) is
bit-for-bit unchanged; underneath, there is exactly one setter and one
fleet-scoped query, not one-per-coordinator. Manufacturing (already on
`ClaimShip`) gets TOCTOU-closed for free the moment Phase 1 ships, with zero
changes to manufacturing's own code.

**Phase 2 — migrate the two non-atomic claim paths onto `ClaimShip`:**
Factory's `claimShipForFactory` and trade-route/gas's raw
`FindBySymbol`→mutate→`Save` calls switch to
`ClaimShip(ctx, symbol, containerID, playerID, operation)`. This closes
Bug A's remaining exposure and the read-modify-write race itself (today's
weakest link, weaker than the dedication gap) — not just adds
dedication-awareness to these three coordinators. Each coordinator gets a
constant `operation` identity (`"factory"`, `"trade_route"`, `"gas"`).

**Phase 3 — behavioral generalization:**
Wire in the shared `SelectHullForCargo` policy (section 5) and the
generalized `HomeShipHandler` + fleet-config standby stations (section 6)
coordinator-by-coordinator, lowest-risk first (trade-route's circuit-fill
and the heavy freighter's dispatch are the two symptoms explicitly cited,
so they lead). This is also where `HomeShipHandler`'s destination selection
flips from nearest-only to the balanced hub assignment policy (section 6):
the `shared.FindNearestWaypoint` call at `home_ship.go:85` is replaced
outright, not kept as a parallel path — the policy's own step 4 already
degrades to nearest-overall once every standby station is covered, so no
second code path is needed alongside it. Each coordinator picks up hull
selection and balanced homing together in the same migration step, since
both are changes to the same generalized call site it's adopting.

Phase 1 is small, additive to every caller except the two sp-snmb functions
it explicitly retires, and directly addresses the income-critical contract
line with the least churn — recommend starting there regardless of how the
rest of the phasing is sequenced.

## 10. Decisions locked for this revision (recommended, Admiral to confirm)

1. **Flat-string fleet namespace — keep flat.** sp-snmb already ships this
   (`"contract"` as a bare string); a structured `{operation, sub_fleet}`
   type would be new schema and code for a distinction the fleet doesn't
   need yet — one flat string already carries sub-fleet names like
   `"bulk_circuit"` fine. Recommended, Admiral to confirm.
2. **Standby stations are a property of the fleet**, not a per-coordinator
   flag (section 6). Defined once per fleet name, looked up by
   `HomeShipHandler` at homing time. Avoids every coordinator re-declaring
   the same station list and keeps homing config attached to the ownership
   tag it travels with. This is the one real scope increase in the design
   (a small fleet-config lookup) — still recommended over the duplication
   alternative. Recommended, Admiral to confirm.
3. **Command surface is one `fleet assign/unassign/list` group** (section
   7), not folded into `ship`. Keeps the ownership-tag verbs together and
   distinct from `ship reserve/release`'s captain-manual-use semantics,
   which is a different mechanism (dynamic personal claim, not static
   dedication) that shouldn't be confused with this one. Recommended,
   Admiral to confirm.

title: Captain wake model: captain-declared wake conditions + interrupt/defer event routing
description:
DESIGN + IMPLEMENT via the shipwright flow (design first, surface the design for Admiral sign-off, THEN TDD implement). gobot only: daemon event recorder (internal/adapters/grpc/container_runner.go) + captain supervisor (internal/captain/). Builds directly on the just-landed cadence persistence (internal/captain/state.go, <workspace>/state/supervisor-state.json, commit 6cdf671).

PROBLEM. The supervisor wakes the captain on ANY unprocessed event, including routine successes. A contract fulfillment fires workflow.finished -> a full max-effort captain turn. In a productive era this is near-constant and almost all of it is the captain being woken to be told an expected success succeeded. The Admiral flagged this as wasteful (2026-07-06).

DESIRED CAPABILITY (two parts):
1) Interrupt-vs-defer event routing. Classify events: INTERRUPT NOW (failures/anomalies: workflow.failed, container.crashed, contract.failed, income.stalled, stream.down, container.heartbeat_lost) vs DEFER (routine successes: workflow.finished, contract.completed, credits.threshold up). Deferred events queue and are delivered batched on the next wake, never interrupting on their own.
2) Captain-declared wake conditions. At session end the captain declares its own next-wake policy: a next-wake-at time (dynamic replacement for the fixed 45-min heartbeat), credit thresholds (wake at >= X or <= Y), and which event types count as interrupts for its current posture. The supervisor honors it: wake on interrupt-class events, on a threshold crossing, or at next-wake-at; otherwise let events accumulate. This lets the captain choose 'steady grind, leave me 3h unless something breaks' vs 'construction shakedown, wake me on any anomaly'.

FOUNDATION. The wake policy is a natural extension of the persisted supervisorState (state.go). Reuse that file; do not invent a second store.

RELATED. sp-82qs (contract.completed/failed are declared but never emitted; fulfillment surfaces as generic workflow.finished). The interrupt/defer split wants first-class contract events. Design should decide whether to fold that fix in or sequence it first.

CONSTRAINTS. gobot only. Must NOT regress delivery of genuine anomalies. Persist across restarts (reuse supervisor-state.json). Keep a max-interval fallback so the captain cannot set a pathological never-wake. Preserve the hourly wake cap + escalation.

DESIGN QUESTIONS for the shipwright to resolve in the design phase:
- Wake-policy schema and WHERE the captain writes it (a captain-facing CLI like 'spacetraders captain wake set ...'? a file the captain writes? piggyback on 'captain events ack'?).
- How the supervisor evaluates policy each tick (interrupt allowlist; threshold eval reusing the credits detector; next-wake-at as dynamic heartbeat).
- Safe DEFAULT policy when the captain has not declared one (interrupt on failures, defer successes, heartbeat fallback).
- Migration / backward-compat with current every-event behavior.

NOTE: supervisor is currently unloaded (kill switch cleared, service bootout) pending this work; do not assume it is running. This is the reason event delivery is paused.
notes:
# sp-sk68 — Captain wake model: design for Admiral sign-off

## Problem (recap)
`supervisor.go:134` gates the wake on `len(events)==0 && !heartbeatDue` — the captain wakes on ANY unprocessed event, with zero type discrimination. A routine contract fulfillment (`workflow.finished`) triggers a full max-effort captain turn. Wasteful in a productive era.

## Design in one line
Change ONLY the wake **gate** (when to wake), not the delivery (what's delivered). Events already stay unprocessed until the captain acks them and `bridgeWake` already batches all unprocessed events — so "defer" = "don't wake FOR this event; it rides the next wake's batch." Minimal, low-blast-radius.

## Part 1 — Interrupt-vs-defer routing
Classify by event **type** against a **policy-driven interrupt set** (not a new DB column):
- **INTERRUPT (wake now)** default set: `workflow.failed`, `container.crashed`, `container.heartbeat_lost`, `contract.failed`, `income.stalled`, `stream.down`.
- **DEFER (queue, batched onto next wake)** default: `workflow.finished`, `contract.completed`, `credits.threshold`, `ship.idle`.
- The captain may override the interrupt set for its current posture (see Part 2).

New wake gate in `Tick` (replaces supervisor.go:133-142):
```
interrupts, deferred := partition(unprocessed, policy.InterruptTypes)   # default set if unset
effectiveNextWake := policy.NextWakeAt (if set) capped at lastSession + MaxWakeIntervalMinutes
                     else lastSession + HeartbeatMinutes            # existing 45-min fallback preserved
creditWake := (policy.CreditsAbove set && credits >= above) || (policy.CreditsBelow set && credits <= below)
shouldWake := len(interrupts) > 0 || now >= effectiveNextWake || creditWake
if !shouldWake { return false }        # deferred events stay queued, no wake
# hourly cap + bridgeWake unchanged — bridgeWake delivers ALL unprocessed (interrupts + deferred), batched
```
`credits` reuses `CurrentCredits()` (detectors.go:224). Result: failures interrupt immediately; routine successes accumulate and ride the next interrupt/heartbeat/credit wake.

## Part 2 — Captain-declared wake policy
Schema (captain-owned fields):
```go
type WakePolicy struct {
    NextWakeAt     *time.Time `json:"next_wake_at,omitempty"`      // dynamic heartbeat; nil → HeartbeatMinutes
    CreditsAbove   *int       `json:"credits_wake_above,omitempty"`// wake when credits >= X
    CreditsBelow   *int       `json:"credits_wake_below,omitempty"`// wake when credits <= Y
    InterruptTypes []string   `json:"interrupt_types,omitempty"`   // override interrupt set; nil → default failure set
    DeclaredAt     time.Time  `json:"declared_at"`
}
```
Captain declares via a NEW CLI verb under the existing `spacetraders captain` tree (captain_ops.go):
`spacetraders captain wake set [--next-wake-at +3h|<ts>] [--credits-above N] [--credits-below N] [--interrupt-types a,b,c]` (+ `captain wake show`). The captain calls it at session end alongside `captain events ack`.

### KEY DECISION — where the policy is stored (needs your ruling)
The bead says "reuse supervisor-state.json; do not invent a second store." But the investigation found that file is **supervisor-private**: loaded once at startup, overwritten wholesale on every `saveState` (every wake/nudge), written non-atomically. A captain process writing it today would be clobbered and never re-read.

Two ways to honor the intent:
- **(A, recommended) Reuse the file, made dual-writer-safe.** Split ownership: supervisor owns cadence fields, captain owns WakePolicy fields. Make writes atomic (temp+rename) and read-merge-write (each writer touches only its own fields). Supervisor re-reads the file at the top of each Tick to pick up policy. Honors "one store"; cost = one atomic-write refactor + tick re-read. Small, contained.
- **(B, fallback) DB-mediated policy row** (`captain_wake_policy`, one row/player). This is actually how the captain and supervisor already communicate (they share state ONLY through Postgres — the CLI is DB-wired, events live in `captain_events`). Cleaner concurrency, but it "invents a second store" and needs a migration.

I recommend **(A)** to honor the directive, with the atomic read-merge-write safety work. Flagging (B) because the DB is the *actual* captain↔supervisor channel today, so if you prefer strict consistency over the one-file rule, (B) is the more architecturally honest choice. **Your call.**

## Safe default (no policy declared)
Failures interrupt, everything else defers, 45-min heartbeat. Preserves anomaly delivery (no regression); the only behavior change is that routine successes no longer wake. `lastCredits` moves INTO the persisted state so credit-wake survives restart (today it's in-memory, zeroed on restart).

## Never-wake guard
`MaxWakeIntervalMinutes` (new config, propose 180 = 3h) caps `NextWakeAt`: the captain can say "leave me 3h" but cannot set a pathological never-wake. Hourly cap (`MaxSessionsPerHour=6`) and escalation (renudge→Admiral) are UNCHANGED; a capped anomaly still escalates via the existing renudge path, so the cap doesn't swallow genuine anomalies.

## sp-82qs (contract.completed/failed) — SEQUENCE SEPARATELY, do not fold in
sp-sk68's P1 win lands fully at `workflow.*` granularity: contract SUCCESS already surfaces as `workflow.finished` (→ DEFER, correct) and contract FAILURE as `workflow.failed` (→ INTERRUPT, correct). First-class contract events add payout FIDELITY but aren't required to stop the wasteful wakes. I'll classify `contract.completed`/`contract.failed` now (forward-compatible), so when sp-82qs later adds the emitter (daemon-only, container_runner.go:409 branch), events route correctly with no further wake-model change. Keeps this P1 tight and off `container_runner.go`.

## TDD plan (tests first)
1. Classifier: default interrupt set vs defer set; captain override respected.
2. Wake gate: deferred-only before next-wake → NO wake; deferred + interrupt → wake, batch includes both; next-wake-at reached → wake; credits≥above / ≤below → wake; pathological next-wake capped at MaxWakeInterval → wake; hourly cap still suppresses; default policy = failures interrupt / successes defer / 45-min heartbeat.
3. Persistence: `captain wake set` writes policy; supervisor re-reads; atomic read-merge-write preserves cadence (LastSession/Renudges/Escalated) and policy across interleaved writes; policy + lastCredits survive restart (restoreState).
4. No-regression: container.crashed / workflow.failed still wake immediately.

## Files (implementation, AFTER sign-off — this is Tier-3 / internal/captain rail work)
- `internal/domain/captain/events.go` — default interrupt-set classifier helper.
- `internal/captain/state.go` — extend supervisorState with WakePolicy + lastCredits; atomic write + read-merge-write helper.
- `internal/captain/supervisor.go` — new Tick wake gate; re-read policy each tick; credit-wake via CurrentCredits.
- `internal/adapters/cli/captain_ops.go` — `captain wake set` / `wake show` verbs.
- `internal/captain/config/defaults.go` — MaxWakeIntervalMinutes.
- Tests alongside each. NOT touching container_runner.go (that's sp-82qs).

## Open questions for the Admiral
1. **Policy store: (A) reuse supervisor-state.json with atomic read-merge-write [recommended], or (B) a DB policy row [more consistent with the real channel]?**
2. Confirm **sp-82qs sequenced separately** (I file/keep it as a follow-up P2), not folded into this P1.
3. MaxWakeIntervalMinutes = 180 (3h) acceptable as the never-wake ceiling?

Harbormaster reviewed the design (2026-07-06): sound + minimal — changes only the wake GATE, not delivery, and reuses bridgeWake's existing batching. Routed to Admiral for the 3 rulings the shipwright escalated. Harbormaster recommendation: (1) policy store -> B (DB row): supervisor-state.json is supervisor-private/single-writer and the captain<->supervisor channel is ALREADY Postgres (captain_events); the 'reuse the file' directive was based on a wrong assumption about that file. (2) sp-82qs sequenced separately -> AGREE, keeps this P1 tight and off container_runner.go. (3) MaxWakeIntervalMinutes=180 -> acceptable. Implementation HELD pending Admiral sign-off.
SIGN-OFF (Admiral, via recommended defaults; Admiral is AFK / standing 'always use recommended' directive): (1) policy store = REUSE supervisor-state.json made dual-writer-safe (atomic temp+rename read-merge-write, split field ownership, supervisor re-reads each Tick); (2) sp-82qs SEQUENCED SEPARATELY (P1 lands at workflow.* granularity; contract.* classified forward-compatibly); (3) MaxWakeIntervalMinutes = 180. Proceeding to TDD implementation per the design note above.

title: Engine: captain-gate pathspec-less commit contaminates shared main checkout on merge
description:
captain-gate SquashMerge does a pathspec-less `git commit` into the SHARED main checkout, so it commits whatever other live agents have staged — not just the branch diff.

MECHANISM (internal/captain/worktree.go SquashMerge, ~L97-104): `git merge --squash <branch>` then `git commit -m <msg>` with NO pathspec, run in --repo (the rig-root main checkout). In the multi-agent fleet, that checkout's index routinely holds other agents' staged work.

DEMONSTRATED during sp-s7b7 (post-reset pipeline verification, 2026-07-06): with captain + harbormaster + 3 others live in the checkout, the gate's merge swept 5 peer-staged files (.beads/issues.jsonl, .claude/settings.json, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, city/.beads/issues.jsonl) PLUS a stray root issues.jsonl into the fix commit. A manual unstage/re-stage workaround also lost to a concurrent peer index write. Recovered by rebuilding a clean 7-file commit in the worktree (git commit --no-verify) and fast-forwarding main to it (git merge --ff-only) — an FF moves the ref without a commit, so it cannot sweep staged files.

SECONDARY DEFECT: core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks installs a pre-commit hook that runs `bd hooks run pre-commit`, exporting the beads DB to issues.jsonl and staging it. In a git worktree (no .beads/ layout) the export misfires to the worktree ROOT (./issues.jsonl instead of .beads/issues.jsonl), and root issues.jsonl is NOT gitignored — so it gets committed and rides the squash-merge onto main.

IMPACT: any gated merge performed while peers have a dirty index produces a contaminated commit on main. This is systemic for the shared-checkout topology, not specific to this bead.

FIX DIRECTIONS (captain-gate is a Tier-3 safety rail — needs Admiral/human approval; shipwright must NOT modify it):
1. Gate must commit ONLY the branch's own diff. Options: (a) perform the squash in a dedicated clean checkout / temp worktree and fast-forward main to the result; (b) reset/clean the --repo index to HEAD before `git merge --squash` and commit with an explicit pathspec limited to the branch diff; (c) refuse to merge when the --repo index is dirty, forcing a clean window.
2. Add root `issues.jsonl` to .gitignore and/or make the beads export hook worktree-path-aware so it never writes to a worktree root.

Verifier note: the gate's build+test+freshness stages themselves passed cleanly (GatePassed=true, Stale=false) — the defect is purely in the merge/commit stage's interaction with the shared, concurrently-written checkout.
notes:
new contamination vector (shipwright, 2026-07-07): the worktree-bd wiring (b63071b) runs a bd export hook ON COMMIT inside worktrees and auto-stages issues.jsonl into whatever is being committed — build-71bj's feature commit picked up 123 lines of bead-db churn; a plain recommit re-added it; only 'git commit --no-verify' after unstaging produced a clean 3-file commit. Mainline convention says code commits do NOT carry issues.jsonl (checked 44be3ea/b63071b/829d15f). Suggest: hook should export WITHOUT staging, or stage only for dedicated bd-sync commits.
Surveyor 2026-07-08: still open while ~20 beads landed around it overnight — evidence of queue-skip, not deprioritization by judgment: the shipwright's documented queue query is broken (sp-lcjd: --type bug,feature matches ZERO) and all overnight work arrived via mail-nudge; sp-ezar was never nudged. This bead remains the highest-blast-radius open engine item (autonomous squash-merge commits the shared main INDEX — prior silent data-loss 2026-07-03, see worktree.go:97-104). RECOMMEND P1 + immediate pickup once nudged. Cheap interim guard: assert clean 'git status --porcelain' on the main checkout before SquashMerge, abort gate if dirty.
SECOND realized instance (transcript survey 2026-07-08): the sp-s7b7 gated merge produced 'Frankenstein commit' 71221b2 (verified exists) — shipwright transcript: peer sessions' dirty files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, both .beads/issues.jsonl) 'swept into my commit'; recovery needed a manual ff-only merge, itself a role-rule exception. This now recurs on EVERY gated merge while any of the 6 agents has a dirty shared checkout — which is the NORMAL state of a 6-agent city. P1 case is now two realized incidents + structural certainty.
Admiral approved P1 bump 2026-07-08. Top of the repair queue: two realized incidents (2026-07-03 data-loss, 71221b2 Frankenstein). Interim guard acceptable as first commit: abort gate if 'git status --porcelain' on the main checkout is dirty; durable fix: explicit pathspec or merge from the isolated worktree.
GUARD SPEC CORRECTED (surveyor, 2026-07-08, per harbormaster's analysis — verified correct): my earlier 'git status --porcelain' interim guard was WRONG and would brick all merges — the main checkout is routinely dirty-UNSTAGED (verified now: many M/D lines, index empty), and a pathspec-less 'git commit' (no -a) commits only the INDEX. Contamination vector = pre-staged files: 71221b2's swept files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, .beads/issues.jsonl) were exactly the staged A/M entries in the checkout at the time. CORRECT interim guard: BEFORE 'git merge --squash', assert empty index ('git diff --cached --quiet'); on failure abort loudly naming the staged files. Unstaged/untracked dirt is harmless to the commit and must NOT abort. Durable fix unchanged (explicit pathspec is awkward with squash — prefer performing the squash-merge in a clean dedicated checkout/worktree of main, or a temp index). TRANSITION (Admiral authority, in-chat 2026-07-08 'approve the rest, delegate to shipwright' — this bead was decision item 1): implementation sign-off GRANTED to shipwright, same precedent as sp-1hak/sp-qv71 (Admiral approval unlocks rail work); the body's 'shipwright must NOT modify' line is superseded by this sign-off. awaiting-human removed, shipwright label added. P1 — take FIRST.

title: Plan A Task 6 Step 11 is wrong: 'tune expansion_enabled 0' does NOT lift the override on a container launched while it was set
description:
FOUND IN THE FIELD 2026-08-07 while executing the step. Plan A (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-06-heavy-trade-wave-plan-a.md) Task 6 Step 11 specifies lifting the operator override with 'tune --operation sensing expansion_enabled 0' — 0 being the revert-to-default verb, chosen deliberately so no override is left looking intentional to the next operator. IT DOES NOT WORK, and it fails SILENTLY: the command reports success and the coordinator keeps the old value.

THE MECHANISM. A coordinator captures its config AT LAUNCH. The sensing container was launched while expansion_enabled=2 was set, so it holds 2 in memory.
  - 'tune ... 0' DELETES the persisted key. The live reader then finds no key and KEEPS WHAT IT HAS -> still 2.
  - 'tune ... 1' is a NO-OP: with the key deleted the registry already reports 1 (source=default), so it writes nothing -> still 2.
  - 'tune ... 2' would write, but is the wrong direction.
So no tune value can dislodge it. Verified live: two full sensing cycles after the revert still logged buy_spending_paused=true and expansion_spending_paused=true, and the container's persisted config showed the key genuinely ABSENT (config::text LIKE '%expansion_enabled%' = f) while the running coordinator stayed paused.

THE ONLY FIX IN THE FIELD was a daemon restart, so the container re-launched from a config with no key and picked up the compiled default of 1. Immediately after: buy_attempts=5, buy_bought=5, buy_spending_paused=false.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PLAN: the same shape applies to EVERY tunable whose live reader treats absent-or-zero as 'keep current'. Reverting such a knob on a running container is a no-op that reports success. That is a false-green in an operator tool, the same class as sp-4bgic's comment-audit -only bug.

ASK: (a) correct Step 11 in the plan to say the revert requires a container relaunch, or give the exact working sequence; (b) decide whether the DAEMON should make revert-to-default actually reach a running coordinator — a revert that silently does nothing is worse than one that refuses; (c) audit which other tunables have a live reader that keeps its current value on an absent key, and whether 'tune <key> 0' is documented as working for them.

NOT A BLOCKER for the epic: the override is lifted, the wave owns probe buying, and both readers agree.

title: shipyard_inventory reads in the sensing screen are not era-scoped, and a comment claims the opposite
description:
FOUND during the sp-4bgic comment sweep of internal/adapters/parkedsensing, while verifying whether a rewritten comment was true. The comment work is merged; this is the CODE fact it uncovered.

THE INCONSISTENCY. WaypointCatalogPort.distinctColumnSet (adapters/parkedsensing/screen_ports.go, the Where at ~:457) filters shipyard_inventory and sensing_slots on player_id ONLY — no era predicate. But ShipyardInventoryModel CARRIES an indexed EraID and its own doc comment (adapters/persistence/models_market.go:150) says 'EraID mirrors GateEdgeModel/ScoutPostModel: reads are era-scoped'. Other shipyard_inventory reads ARE era-scoped. This one is not. Verified on main, both halves.

AND A COMMENT ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE: screen_ports.go:495 claims the LastListingScan memo is 'the one read in this file that is not' era-scoped. That is false while distinctColumnSet exists unscoped in the same file — so a reader auditing era-scoping is told the audit is already done. Pre-existing in main, untouched by the sweep.

WHY IT MATTERS, PRECISELY (do not overstate it): this is the EXCLUSION half of the outstanding-yards work list. Being unscoped makes it MORE excluding, not less — a waypoint catalogued while a previous era was open still holds a shipyard_inventory row and stays excluded forever. So the effect is a permanently narrower work list, not a wrong purchase. It is not a money-guard defect and there is no evidence it is currently harmful.

FIRST QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: is the missing era predicate DELIBERATE (cross-era exclusion is desirable because a yard catalogued once need never be re-screened) or an OVERSIGHT? Those have opposite fixes. If deliberate, the fix is to say so at the query and correct the :495 claim. If an oversight, adding the predicate WIDENS the work list and must be sized first — it re-admits every yard catalogued in a closed era. Do not add the predicate before establishing which, and do not assume the model's doc comment settles it: the comment describes an intent the code does not implement.

title: Once-only container guards are check-then-act: no transaction, no lock, no unique index on (player_id, container_type)
description:
FOUND during sp-sy3dl Task 4's idempotence review, as the RESIDUAL after a wider race was fixed. Not a regression from that work — it is the shape every sibling guard already has.

THE REMAINING WINDOW: the guard reads (SELECT the live container of this type) and then acts (containerRepo.Add) as two separate statements, with no transaction, no lock, and no unique index on ContainerModel (player_id, container_type) (models_agent.go:44). Two launches interleaving between the SELECT and the INSERT both observe an empty fleet and both persist a coordinator. Realistic triggers: an operator running the launch verb while an EXPANSION-tick hand-off fires, or a client retry.

SAME SHAPE ACROSS THE REPO — long-haul, scout posts, auto-outfit, shipyard backfill and the bootstrap hand-offs all guard this way, so a fix should be structural rather than per-call-site.

WHY IT MATTERS MOST FOR THE HEAVY BUYER: two fleet-growth coordinators means two spenders bidding against one treasury for seven-figure hulls. That is the exact hazard sp-sy3dl Task 4 is atomic in order to prevent, so the guard being probabilistic undercuts the design's central safety argument. For the other five it is duplicated work rather than duplicated spend.

REMEDY (either, and prefer the first): a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX on (player_id, container_type) WHERE status IN ('RUNNING','PENDING') — the database enforces it and no caller can forget; or a re-read inside the same transaction as the insert. A third option — retry-on-conflict — needs the index anyway to have a conflict to detect.

ALREADY FIXED, DO NOT RE-DO: the WIDER hole in the same helper. firstContainerIDOfType read RUNNING and PENDING as TWO queries (bootstrap_ports_gate.go:74-75 on main), so a row promoted PENDING->RUNNING between them was in NEITHER result — and a launch IS that transition, so the window opened exactly when two launches collided. Nine call sites across five files inherited it. Task 4's branch replaces it with a single-statement read (persistence.ListActiveByTypeSimple) plus a deterministic RUNNING-over-PENDING/lowest-id rank. That lands with Task 4; this bead is only the narrower check-then-act residual that remains after it.

ALSO NOTED, one-line, unrelated: container_ops_tune_growth_test.go asserts bound.Min == 1 for every growth knob, which is stronger than its own stated rationale (Min != 0). The same registry legitimately carries minimums of 10, 50, 60 and 300, so the first cadence-shaped growth knob will fail it with a message that misdiagnoses the cause. require.GreaterOrEqual(t, bound.Min, 1) states the intended claim.

title: P8: no end-to-end test pins which fuel figure the refuel call site uses — needs a ship-moving fake AND something further that gates the planned refuel
description:
TWO REMAINING RESIDUALS FROM sp-rnm3q, filed together because they share the route-executor file territory and MUST be one lane — concurrent lanes on one file is this repo's single worst corruption path.

(A) CRITERION 7 — RE-TEST THE ORIGINAL WAYPOINT BEFORE COMMITTING TO A DETOUR. When an ESSENTIAL refuel fails at waypoint A, the executor reroutes to alternate B without ever re-trying A. The observed trigger class is TRANSIENT (a local DNS outage; any upstream 5xx reproduces it), so A is usually working again by the time the detour is planned. The detour is the expensive branch — the original incident cost 27-29 minutes of DRIFT per hull. Re-test A before committing, and again on arrival at B before buying there. NOTE the ordering constraint: this only applies to the ESSENTIAL branch now. sp-medpu made the non-essential branch try once and continue, so a non-essential failure never reaches the detour at all — do not re-introduce retrying there.

(B) P8 — A SURVIVING MUTANT, and the honest reason it survives. Swapping the call site from fuelForSegmentsAfter back to Route.FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment is NOT caught end to end. fuelForSegmentsAfter is unit-tested directly, but no test drives ExecuteRoute over a MULTI-SEGMENT route where the two figures differ, because the package's mediator fake NEVER MOVES THE SHIP so post-departure state cannot be staged. THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE MUTANT: FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment stops accumulating at the first fuel-capable waypoint (navigation/route.go, 'if segments[i].ToWaypoint.HasFuel { break }'), so it reads ZERO at exactly the waypoints a refuel is attempted at. Reusing it would silently reclassify a genuinely-REQUIRED refuel as non-essential — the money-adjacent direction. The call site is currently correct; nothing pins it.

DO (B) FIRST IF TAKING BOTH. A ship-moving fake is what makes (A) testable across a detour as well, so it likely pays for itself twice. But VERIFY that rather than assuming — the sp-medpu lane found my equivalent guess wrong: its assertions lived at a seam where the existing fixture already staged the hull, so a ship-moving fake would not have helped there at all. Check where (A)'s decisive assertions actually sit before building infrastructure for them.

RULINGS #4: (A) must not weaken the essential path's guarantees — a refuel the remaining legs genuinely need must still ultimately escalate if the original waypoint stays dead. Re-testing A is an ADDITIONAL attempt before the detour, not a replacement for it. The predicate stays fail-closed.

VERIFY BY BEHAVIOUR: for (A), assert the original waypoint was re-attempted before any alternate was resolved — and assert a refuel was ACTUALLY ATTEMPTED at each point, since a refuel that never ran satisfies an ordering assertion for the opposite reason.
notes:
PART (A) — CRITERION 7 — DONE and merged. NO PRODUCTION CHANGE WAS NEEDED: the behaviour already existed and was simply unpinned. The retry loop already probes the ORIGINAL waypoint once more AFTER the budget fully elapses — sp-l7zha's 'always makes at least one more attempt' guarantee IS criterion 7's re-test-before-the-detour. PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED: a mutant that shortens the loop so it stops without that final probe left EVERY existing refuel test green, and is now killed. Both directions pinned: origin recovers -> no detour; origin stays dead -> still escalates (RULINGS #4 untouched).

THE CRITERION'S SECOND HALF IS NOT ACTIONABLE and is dropped deliberately: 're-test A again on arrival at B' cannot help, because by then the hull IS at B and refuels there — the cost the criterion exists to avoid is the FLIGHT, which is already spent. Re-testing at that point could only send it back.

PART (B) — P8 — STILL OPEN, and the blocker is now NARROWER but real. The ordering guess (mine) that (B) would pay for (A) was WRONG and was refuted by evidence: (A)'s assertions sit at refuelShipWithRetryCore and the fake they need (fakeWaypointRepo, route_executor_test.go:401) already existed.

WHAT HAPPENED ON (B), worth keeping: an end-to-end test was written and WENT GREEN — then the sweep showed the P8 mutant SURVIVED it. Diagnosis: because the package's mediator fake never moves the hull, every refuel happens at the ORIGIN, so the failure the test observed was the PRE-DEPARTURE refuel, not the post-arrival classification. It passed for a reason unrelated to its claim — exactly the flaw P8 exists to close. THE TEST WAS REMOVED RATHER THAN BANKED.

A ship-moving fake IS needed (the bead was right), but it is NOT SUFFICIENT. Opt-in movement was wired (the executor passes both Ship and DestinationWaypoint at route_executor.go:383-389; Ship exposes EnsureInOrbit/StartTransit/Arrive), the package stayed green, and the planned refuel STILL was not attempted — something further gates it, and finding that is the next step. The movement code was reverted rather than left dead without a consumer.

REQUIREMENT FOR WHOEVER TAKES (B): the fixture must ALSO keep the origin fuel-less, so the pre-departure refuel cannot masquerade as the post-arrival one. That is what made the first attempt vacuous.

WHY (B) MATTERS BEYOND THE MUTANT: FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment stops accumulating at the first fuel-capable waypoint (navigation/route.go, 'if segments[i].ToWaypoint.HasFuel { break }'), so it reads ZERO at exactly the waypoints a refuel is attempted at. Swapping the call site back to it would silently reclassify a genuinely-REQUIRED refuel as non-essential — the money-adjacent direction. The call site is correct today and nothing pins it.
close_reason:
Merged, both parts. (A) criterion 7 needed NO production change — the retry loop already probes the original waypoint after the budget elapses; a mutant shortening it left every existing refuel test green and is now killed. The criterion's second half (re-test on arrival at the alternate) is not actionable: the cost it avoids is the flight, already spent.

(B) P8 SOLVED. The blocker was not a second unknown mechanism — it was the stationary fake wearing two faces. refuelShip skips gracefully when !ship.CurrentLocation().HasFuel (route_executor_refuel.go:263), so with the hull left at the origin: a FUEL-LESS origin swallowed the planned refuel entirely (nothing attempted anywhere), while a FUEL-SELLING origin let the PRE-DEPARTURE refuel masquerade as the post-arrival one. The anti-masquerade requirement and the attempt-something requirement were mutually exclusive until the hull actually moves. BOTH halves were reproduced before fixing, not inferred.

FIX: recordingMediator now relocates the hull on navigate (EnsureInOrbit -> StartTransit -> Arrive), matching the real handler, and answers a same-location hop the way the real handler does (already_at_destination, no fuel spent) rather than erroring. Made unconditional after measuring that the whole tree stays green — a fixture that stopped lying, not a behaviour change. NO PRODUCTION CHANGE: the call site was already correct, merely unpinned.

The swap-the-call-site mutant now DIES, named by one test. Two fixture-integrity probes guard the fix itself: neutering relocate() (restoring the exact lie that made the prior attempt vacuous) is killed, and the origin-sells-fuel probe SURVIVES — reported honestly as structural rather than a coverage hole, because the fixture needs a tank above the 90% top-off threshold at B, which forces a full tank at A, so no pre-departure top-off can fire either way. The anti-masquerade guarantee is carried by an asserted refuel LOCATION instead.

TWO OVERSTATED CLAIMS WERE CAUGHT BY REVIEW AND CORRECTED rather than inherited: 'four independent discriminators' is really three (route status is FAILED in BOTH arms — FailRoute fires for any non-ErrArrivalWaitExhausted error), and an assertion called 'demonstrably live' was firing only in a DIFFERENT fixture configuration than the one committed; it is now stated plainly as a guard against fixture drift.

HANDBACK FOR SIBLING LANES: recordingMediator moves the hull on every navigate now. Any future test in internal/application/ship assuming a stationary hull after a navigate will behave differently.

title: A non-essential refuel still burns the FULL retry budget before being absorbed — a gate hull stands on the delivery site for minutes before delivering
description:
DEFERRED RESIDUAL from sp-rnm3q (merged). That fix stopped a non-essential refuel failure from ABANDONING a completed delivery — a large win, and the hull no longer flies away. But it did not change WHEN the failure is absorbed: the refuel still exhausts the full elapsed-time retry budget (sp-l7zha's 10-minute budget, observed live as 14m45s and 13m45s including capped backoff) before the classification declares it non-essential and continues.

CONSEQUENCE: a hull that has physically ARRIVED at the construction site, holding the exact cargo the gate needs, sits there for the length of the retry budget before delivering — for a fuel top-up the remaining route does not need. Delivery costs zero fuel. Far better than the observed 29-minute detour in DRIFT, but it is pure dead time on the critical path of gate construction, and it recurs on every transient upstream flake.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the classification already knows the refuel is non-essential (fuelForSegmentsAfter proves the remaining legs are covered). That knowledge is available BEFORE the retries, not only after them. A refuel the remaining route does not need should retry once at most, or not at all, and be absorbed immediately — the retry budget exists to rescue a refuel the route DEPENDS on, and spending it on one nothing depends on is the defect.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE ESSENTIAL PATH (RULINGS #4). A refuel the remaining legs genuinely need must keep the full budget and the escalation. The predicate must stay FAIL-CLOSED: an unreadable fuel figure means essential, means full budget. This bead narrows only the branch already proven non-essential.

VERIFY BY BEHAVIOUR, NOT BY THE ABSENCE OF AN ERROR: after the change, a post-arrival opportunistic refuel failure must show delivery proceeding within seconds rather than minutes. Assert on elapsed time to the supply call, and assert the supply call COUNT (sp-rnm3q's criterion 3 trap — a test checking only the returned error passes while the delivery never happens).

RELATED DEFERRALS FROM THE SAME LANE, both still open and both smaller: (a) criterion 7 — re-test the ORIGINAL waypoint before committing to a detour and again on arrival at the alternate, since the trigger is usually transient; (b) P8 — a surviving mutant: no end-to-end multi-segment test pins the call site, because the package's mediator fake never moves the ship, so the reserve-vs-fuelForSegmentsAfter distinction is untested end to end. (b) is test infrastructure that would make this bead's verification easier and is worth doing first if the two are taken together.
notes:
=== FIXED — commit 47efb6b7, 3 files, base 98155dc1. Not gated, not pushed. ===

THE CHANGE: the non-essential branch now tries the refuel ONCE and lets go, instead of running it
through the full elapsed-time budget before absorbing. New NonEssentialRefuelBudget = 0; the retry
loop always makes one attempt before consulting the budget, so zero means try-once. Helper renamed
refuelShipWithoutEscalation -> attemptNonEssentialRefuel, because it no longer merely declines to
escalate — it declines to retry, and the old name described half of that.

RULINGS #4 — ESSENTIAL PATH UNTOUCHED AND NOW PINNED. A refuel the remaining legs need keeps the
whole budget and the escalation, and the predicate stays fail-closed. Added a test asserting the
essential branch still spends the FULL budget and still retries, so narrowing one branch cannot
quietly narrow the other. Mutating the essential call site to the non-essential helper is killed
by two tests.

RED first: "the hull waited 10m2s on a refuel the remaining route does not need — it must not
sleep even once before carrying on."

VERIFICATION MEASURES WAITING ON THE MOCK CLOCK, which advances only when the retry loop sleeps.
That asserts the absence of retry waiting itself rather than wall-clock elapsed time, which would
pass on a fast machine for the wrong reason. Both tests also assert a refuel was ACTUALLY
ATTEMPTED — a refuel that never ran satisfies a timing assertion for the opposite reason.

MUTATION SWEEP (pre-checked: tree clean AND the new marker present in HEAD before sweeping, per
the rule patched after the sp-ppc2e miss):
  M1 non-essential given the full budget back   KILLED (the new timing test)
  M2 budget widened to one backoff interval     KILLED (the new timing test)
  M3 essential path narrowed to the same helper KILLED by 2 (the RULINGS #4 guard + the sp-rnm3q
                                                 fatal-when-required test)
  M4 predicate's nil-fuel default flipped open  EQUIVALENT — not a gap. Proven by enumeration:
     both construction paths (NewShip and ReconstructShip) call validate(), which rejects nil
     fuel, and Ship's fields are unexported so no other package can build one. The branch is
     unreachable, so no test can kill it without constructing an object the domain forbids. Kept
     anyway: it is a cheap fail-closed default on a money-adjacent predicate, and deleting a
     safe default to raise a mutation score is the wrong trade.

go vet caught the one stale call site the rename left in a test file — go build does not compile
_test.go, so the rename would otherwise have looked clean.

gofmt + go build + go vet ./... clean; 10 packages green under -race, including the delivery suite
whose supply-call-count guard covers the case this timing sits in front of (7/7 pass).

P8 ORDERING, AS ASKED: I did NOT take P8 first, and it would not have helped here. This lane's
decisive assertions are mock-clock waiting and refuel-attempt count at the handlePostArrivalRefueling
seam, where the sp-rnm3q fixture already stands the hull at its destination — no ship movement is
needed to stage it. P8 pins a different thing entirely (that ExecuteRoute wires fuelForSegmentsAfter
rather than the flight-mode reserve at the call site), and a ship-moving fake would not have made
these timing assertions stronger. P8 stays open and independent.

STILL OPEN from the same family: criterion 7 (re-test the ORIGINAL waypoint before committing to a
detour and again on arrival at the alternate) and P8 above.
close_reason:
Merged. NonEssentialRefuelBudget = 0 — the non-essential branch tries the refuel ONCE and lets go (the retry loop always makes one attempt before consulting the budget). refuelShipWithoutEscalation renamed attemptNonEssentialRefuel, because it no longer merely declines to ESCALATE, it declines to RETRY, and the old name described half of that.

VERIFIED ON A MOCK CLOCK, NOT WALL TIME — the clock advances only when the retry loop sleeps, so the test asserts the ABSENCE OF RETRY WAITING rather than elapsed real time, which would pass on a fast machine for the wrong reason. Both tests also assert a refuel was ACTUALLY ATTEMPTED, since a refuel that never ran satisfies a timing assertion for the opposite reason.

MUTATIONS: M1 (full budget restored) KILLED; M2 (budget widened to one backoff) KILLED; M3 (essential path narrowed to the new helper) KILLED by 2. M4 (nil-fuel default flipped open) EQUIVALENT — ENUMERATED, NOT ASSUMED: both construction paths (NewShip, ReconstructShip) call validate(), which rejects nil fuel, and Ship's fields are unexported so no other package can build one; the branch is unreachable, so no test can kill it without constructing an object the domain forbids. The default was KEPT — deleting a safe fail-closed default on a money-adjacent predicate to raise a mutation score is the wrong trade.

The mutation sweep ran AFTER the pre-check (tree clean AND the new marker present in HEAD) rather than relying on the failure-text tripwire. go vet caught the one stale call site the rename left in a _test.go file, which go build cannot see.

P8 ORDERING RESOLVED: taking P8 first would NOT have helped and was not done.
