P8 pins something orthogonal: that ExecuteRoute wires fuelForSegmentsAfter rather than the flight-mode reserve AT THE CALL SITE. P8 and criterion 7 stay open and independent.

title: Flaky spend-guard test: parked count asserted as exactly 1 when 2 is equally correct — the TEST's expectation, not the guard (P2 confirmed)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-06 (discovered incidentally during sp-mc05f, NOT caused by it). production_executor_aggregate_spend_test.go:221 fails roughly 1 run in 20 under -race with: 'exactly one of the 3 buyers must be parked ... got 2 parked'.

PROVEN NOT TO BE THE LANE'S CHANGE, with a controlled comparison. The first comparison was CONFOUNDED — one test on the clean tree vs the whole package on the changed tree, two variables moved at once. Redone properly: whole package, 3 runs on the changed tree and 3 on clean, all green; then 20 runs of the test ALONE reproduced one failure. So it is a pre-existing race in the test (or in what it exercises), independent of the operation-context work.

WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS FAILURE RATE: it is a GUARD test. A money guard that cries wolf teaches every future reader to dismiss its failures, which is precisely the sp-yeiq cried-wolf lesson. A 1-in-20 flake on a concurrency guard is the worst kind — frequent enough to be seen and dismissed, rare enough that nobody chases it, and indistinguishable from a real breach when it finally matters.

FIRST QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: is the flake in the TEST's synchronisation (the fixture races its own three buyers and the assertion samples mid-flight) or in the GUARD (two buyers genuinely both proceed under a real interleaving)? Those have opposite severities — the second is a live aggregate-spend-cap breach and a P0. Do not assume the first because it is more likely; the guard is the thing being asserted, so a real breach is exactly what a flaky result would look like. Establish which before proposing a fix, and if it is the guard, stop and escalate rather than stabilising the test.

REPRO: go test -race -run TestConcurrentConstructionSupplyBuys_CannotBreachReserveInAggregate ./internal/application/manufacturing/services/ -count=20
notes:
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-06. IT IS THE TEST'S EXPECTATION — not the guard, and not the fixture's synchronisation either. Severity stays P2. RULINGS #4 is NOT implicated.

THE DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE (three independent lines, any one sufficient):
1. ASSERTION ORDER SETTLES IT STRUCTURALLY. The money criterion (finalBalance >= reserve) is asserted FIRST at :215 with require, which fails fast — and the test's own comment says why: 'asserted first: behaviour before bookkeeping, so a later assertion can never render this one unreachable.' Therefore EVERY observed failure at :221 PROVES the money assertion had already passed. A real breach fails at :215 and can never present as a :221 failure. 0 occurrences of the breach message across 330 runs.
2. THE DIRECTION IS WRONG FOR A BREACH. Every failure is 'got 2 parked' — the guard was MORE restrictive. A breach is UNDER-parking.
3. TRACED INTERLEAVING (instrumented, not inferred): buyer1 RESERVES, COMMITS (treasury drops) while its reservation is still OPEN, then buyers 0 and 2 both evaluate inside that window and both park, then buyer1 releases. Inside the window buyer1's spend is counted TWICE — once in the reduced live treasury, once in the still-open reservation — so each remaining buyer computes headroom below the reserve and parks.

THE DOUBLE-COUNT IS DELIBERATE AND CANNOT BREACH. Production reserves (production_executor.go:478) and DEFERS the release (:482), so release always follows commit. The guard's comment (spend_guards.go:431-432) states the invariant: committed spend is in the transaction ledger, uncommitted in the reservation ledger, nothing falls between. THE PRICE OF NEVER HAVING A GAP IS AN OVERLAP, and the overlap only ever subtracts MORE from computed headroom — it can cause a refusal, never an approval.

-race reported ZERO data races across 330 runs; the fixture is correctly mutex-protected.

WHY THE ASSERTION IS THERE (do not simply delete it): parked==1 exists to stop a VACUOUS pass — its comment reads 'the cap must have ACTED, not merely been present. Without this a harness whose buyers never actually contended would satisfy the assertion above for the wrong reason.' That property must survive any fix.

FIX SHAPE: assert the invariants that hold under EVERY interleaving — treasury never below reserve, AT LEAST ONE buyer parked, spend internally consistent with the parked count — rather than pinning parked to exactly 1. NOTE the third assertion (totalSpent == 2*aggBuyCost) over-specifies for the same reason and must move with it. Do NOT serialise the buyers: the file's own warning at :227-233 says that would make the companion _PerBuyOnlyCheckingBreachesInAggregate vacuous, and that companion is the proof this test CAN fail.

TRAP FOR WHOEVER VERIFIES A FIX — THE WINDOW IS TIMING-SENSITIVE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Heavyweight instrumentation (a DB connection inside the buyer goroutine) drove the rate to 0/120; lightweight instrumentation drove it to 67/150 (~45%). Anyone 'verifying a fix' with a heavy probe will see green and conclude wrongly. Uninstrumented rate measured 1/60 and 3/40 (~2-7%). Instrumentation must NOT be committed — it would fail CI constantly.
=== FIXED — commit 9c738cd2, one file, one commit on base 7d91a15d. Not gated, not pushed. ===

THE CHANGE: replaced the exact `parked == 1` and `totalSpent == 2*aggBuyCost` with the guard's
actual contract, as BOUNDS:
  parked >= 1            the cap acted (something was stopped)
  parked <  aggBuyers    it stopped the breaching buy, not the whole fleet
  totalSpent == (aggBuyers - parked) * aggBuyCost   spend agrees with the observed count
The money criterion at :215 is untouched and still asserted FIRST. The fixture is untouched and
the buyers are NOT serialised — serialising would make the companion breach-reproducing test
vacuous, which is the file's own warning.

VERIFICATION, UNINSTRUMENTED, SAME RUN COUNT BOTH SIDES:
  pre-fix   200 runs -> 12 failures (6.0%), all "got 2 parked", 0 breaches, 0 races
  post-fix  200 runs ->  0 failures,                            0 breaches, 0 races
Whole package -race green. No instrumentation committed (a heavyweight probe in the buyer
goroutine drove the rate to 0/120 and would have made any verification meaningless).

MUTATION PROBES against the COMMITTED fix — the new bounds are load-bearing, not decorative:
  P1 cap unwired (a real aggregate breach)   CAUGHT by the money criterion :215
  P2 guard parks the WHOLE fleet             CAUGHT by parked < N  <- ONLY the new upper bound
                                             sees this; money passes trivially (nothing spent)
  P3 a parked buyer spends anyway            CAUGHT by the money criterion :215
  P4 lower bound widened to >= 0             SURVIVED — honest result, see below
  P5 a completed buyer never spends          CAUGHT by parked >= 1 <- ONLY the new lower bound
                                             sees this; money passes (treasury untouched)
P4 and P5 together are the precise picture: the lower bound is NOT exercised by ordinary runs
(parked is 1 or 2, so >=0 and >=1 are indistinguishable), but it IS the only assertion that
catches a run where the cap never acted AND completion did not imply spend. The committed
comment initially called it merely "a second lock on the same door"; P5 disproved that, and the
comment was corrected to match the evidence before the commit was amended.

PROCESS FAILURE, SECOND TIME THIS SESSION, WORTH RECORDING: the first probe sweep ran against
the ORIGINAL assertions because the fix was still UNCOMMITTED and the probe harness's
`git checkout -- gobot/` restore destroyed it. The probes "passed" and proved nothing about the
change. Caught by noticing P2 was attributed to a require.Equal at a line my edit had replaced —
i.e. the failure message named an assertion that should no longer exist. COMMIT FIRST is not
advice; an uncommitted change is indistinguishable from an absent one, and every probe result
against it is a false reading of the old code.
close_reason:
Merged. The flake was the TEST'S EXPECTATION, not the guard — parked was asserted as exactly 1 when 2 is an equally correct outcome of the cap working as designed. RULINGS #4 never implicated.

DIAGNOSIS SETTLED STRUCTURALLY, not statistically: the money criterion (finalBalance >= reserve) is asserted FIRST at :215 with require, which fails fast — the test's own comment says 'behaviour before bookkeeping, so a later assertion can never render this one unreachable'. So every failure at :221 PROVES the money assertion already passed; a real breach fails at :215 and can never present that way. Corroborated twice: 0 breach messages in 330 runs, and every failure was 'got 2 parked' — the guard being MORE restrictive, where a breach is UNDER-parking. -race clean across 330 runs; the fixture's synchronisation was never at fault.

MECHANISM: production reserves and DEFERS the release, so a committed spend sits briefly in BOTH ledgers. The guard's invariant is that nothing falls between committed and uncommitted — and the price of never having a gap is an overlap. The overlap only ever subtracts MORE from computed headroom, so it can cause a refusal, never an approval.

FIX: bounds instead of exact counts — parked>=1 (the cap acted), parked<aggBuyers (it stopped the breaching buy, not the fleet), totalSpent==(aggBuyers-parked)*aggBuyCost (spend agrees with the count observed). Money criterion untouched and still first. Fixture untouched; buyers deliberately NOT serialised, which would have made the companion _PerBuyOnlyCheckingBreachesInAggregate vacuous — and that companion is the only proof this test CAN fail.

MEASURED, same run count both sides, uninstrumented: 12/200 (6.0%) pre-fix, 0/200 post-fix.

THE BOUNDS ARE LOAD-BEARING, PROVEN BY PROBE: a mutant that parks the WHOLE fleet is caught by parked<N and ONLY that (money passes trivially — nothing is spent); a mutant where a completed buyer never spends is caught by parked>=1 and ONLY that (treasury untouched, money passes again). HONEST RESIDUAL: widening the lower bound to >=0 SURVIVED, because ordinary runs produce parked of 1 or 2, so >=0 and >=1 are indistinguishable there. The bound catches a real code defect; its exact value is not itself pinned.

VERIFICATION TRAP RECORDED FOR ANYONE REVISITING: the window is timing-sensitive in BOTH directions. Heavyweight instrumentation (a DB connection inside the buyer goroutine) drove the rate to 0/120; lightweight drove it to 67/150 (~45%). A green run after a change proves nothing unless the harness is uninstrumented and the run count is large enough to have seen the old failure. Instrumentation must never be committed.

title: Navigating coordinators never stamp an OperationContext, so hulls they ferry book refuel as 'manual' — the gap is upstream, NOT in the refuel path
description:
MEASURED LIVE (staging, 2026-08-06, on the deployed sp-wxgd2 build): in the 19 minutes after that fix deployed at 16:05:45Z, sensing/scouting spend stamped correctly — 50 rows of operation_type='sensing coverage'. But 7 rows in the SAME window still landed in 'manual', and ALL SEVEN are REFUEL / FUEL_COSTS.

THE GAP IS UPSTREAM OF THE REFUEL PATH. The refuel path is CLEAN end to end — refuel_ship.go:226 reads OperationContextFromContext, route_executor_refuel.go:241 passes ctx through unchanged, and production route_executor*.go has no go func / context.Background / context.TODO. A test against the UNMODIFIED recorder proves inheritance works (stamp a sensing-coverage context on ctx, drive the handler, the row comes back stamped).

THE REAL DEFECT: navigating coordinators never stamp an OperationContext at all, so the refuel correctly inherits an unstamped ctx and correctly books 'manual'. Zero WithOperationContext stamping files in internal/application/fleet, internal/adapters/grpc, internal/application/shipyard — CALIBRATED against a known-positive (run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:384 DOES stamp), so those zeros are evidence, not a broken grep.

UNSTAMPED NAVIGATE SITES: bootstrap_ports_acquire.go:316 and :398; contract_scaler_ports.go:207; shipyard/purchase_ship.go:271 (post-purchase delivery); contract/commands/home_ship.go:121. (fleet_autosizer_heavy_ports.go:269 is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — see sequencing below.)

FITS THE EVIDENCE: the 7 manual REFUEL rows landed in a window when sensing was actively BUYING probes. A newly-bought hull ferried to its destination refuels en route, and purchase/ferry are exactly the unstamped paths.

WHY IT MATTERS: fuel is a continuous cost on every operation. operation_type='manual' is the ELSE BRANCH — 'unpropagated' — not a real category, so each of these is a miss, and the spend silently understates the cost of whichever operation actually burned it.

*** THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL ONE-LINE-PER-CALLER SWEEP. *** OperationContext is NOT attribution-only: its ContainerID is used as a reservation label by two concurrent-spend guards (application/contract/services/delivery_executor_spend_cap.go and application/manufacturing/services/production_executor_spend_guards.go). Stamping a coordinator that previously went unstamped CAN CHANGE SPEND-GUARD BEHAVIOUR (RULINGS #4). Each new stamp must be checked against both guards before it ships.

SEQUENCING: do NOT stamp fleet_autosizer_heavy_ports.go — the autosizer is deleted by epic sp-sy3dl migration step 6. The fleet-growth coordinator that replaces it needs its own stamp; fold that one into sp-sy3dl.

ACCEPTANCE: a refuel performed during a ferry/purchase/homing route books under that operation's type, not 'manual'. A genuinely operator-initiated refuel (CLI verb, no enclosing operation) MUST still book as manual — that is the correct use of the else branch; do not collapse the two. Prove both with tests. Verify live post-deploy that the manual REFUEL rate drops while TOTAL REFUEL VOLUME IS UNCHANGED — a drop in both means refuels stopped happening, not that they got attributed.
notes:
MERGED for the non-contested scope. Three entry-point stamps (bootstrap tick; contract-coordinator tick; shipyard purchase ferry) plus operation propagation across all FOUR homing/repositioning goroutines. 6/6 final mutants killed, each naming its tests.

THE ENTRY-POINT STAMP ALONE WAS INERT AND THAT WAS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. All four homing dispatches rebuild ctx from context.Background() carrying only the logger (run_fleet_coordinator_homing.go:34/66/119, run_fleet_coordinator_wiring.go:140). With the tick stamped and the goroutines untouched the test still FAILED — 'the goroutine dropped it, so its fuel books as unpropagated'. Shipping the stamp alone would have closed this bead over a live defect. Fix carries the VALUE across each goroutine and keeps context.Background() as the base, deliberately: the flight must outlive the tick, so cancellation must keep not crossing.

MY OWN EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD WAS THE TRAP. It recorded that no go func / context.Background exists in route_executor*.go and generalised to 'the path is clean end to end'. That check was real but path-local; the homing path was never walked. Verifying a mechanism in ONE path and treating it as cleared globally is what hid this.

THE SWEEP EARNED ITS KEEP THREE TIMES — three separate mutants survived along the way, each a real hole: (1) the contract tick stamp survived because the propagation test handed homing an ALREADY-STAMPED ctx, pinning the second link and leaving the first unpinned — reads as covered, isn't; (2) the two repositioning goroutines survived because the homing test drives only the completed-hull one; (3) the idle-arb re-home survived even after the other three were fixed. SHARING A FIX DID NOT SHARE THE COVERAGE — each dispatch needed its own test.

LABEL DECISION, deliberate and recorded: the shipyard ferry uses the STABLE label 'shipyard-purchase', not a generated per-call id. Reason is semantic, not cardinality (cardinality was separately verified safe — container id is never a Prometheus label): a purchase is not a container, so a per-invocation id would file an INVOCATION into a column where every other writer files an OPERATING CONTEXT, fragmenting 'what do shipyard purchases cost to fly?' and meaning something different from the same column elsewhere. The liquidation precedent differs — that id names a container row that is actually created. Ferry-to-purchase correlation survives via ship symbol + timestamp already on the row.

RULINGS #4 re-verified end to end: ContainerID appears exactly once in spend_reservation_repository.go (line 151, the INSERT); the aggregation is Where(player_id) only; Release is reservation-id-scoped, ExpireStale time-only. Attribution moves, no reservation does.

STILL OPEN — homing remains unattributed from ONE direction: contract_scaler_ports.go:233 is the other, unstamped caller of HomeShipCommand and was held out (contested file, user reverted sp-tg9no). fleet_autosizer_heavy_ports.go:269 deliberately unstamped — the autosizer is deleted by sp-sy3dl migration step 6; its replacement needs its own stamp. Neither fix alone closes homing.

title: [BUG] Route-executor refuels record metadata.ship_symbol as an empty string — every REFUEL row is unattributable to a hull
description:
MEASURED (staging, 2026-08-06, sampled while diagnosing sp-wxgd2): 649 of 649 REFUEL rows in the
operation_type='manual' bucket carry metadata.ship_symbol = "" (the empty string, not NULL). That
is why those rows cannot be attributed to a hull even RETROACTIVELY, and it will keep producing
unattributable rows after sp-wxgd2's operation-context fix lands — sp-wxgd2 restores the
OPERATION, this bug is about the HULL.

ROOT CAUSE, LOCALISED. RefuelShipCommand carries two ways to name the hull:

    type RefuelShipCommand struct {
        Ship       *navigation.Ship // Primary: use when ship is already loaded (avoids API call)
        ShipSymbol string           // Fallback: used only if Ship is nil
        ...
    }

The ledger recorder reads ONLY the fallback. internal/application/ship/commands/tactics/refuel_ship.go:209
writes `"ship_symbol": cmd.ShipSymbol` into the transaction metadata, and :221 builds the description
as fmt.Sprintf("Refueled ship %s", cmd.ShipSymbol). Neither consults cmd.Ship.

The dominant caller sets Ship and leaves ShipSymbol empty:
internal/application/ship/route_executor_refuel.go:236

    refuelCmd := &types.RefuelShipCommand{
        Ship:     ship,
        PlayerID: playerID,
        Units:    nil, // Full refuel
    }

The route executor is on EVERY navigate leg the fleet flies, which is why the emptiness is total
(649/649) rather than partial. The corroborating tell in the same rows is the description: it reads
"Refueled ship " with a trailing space and no symbol.

The other two constructors (adapters/grpc/command_factory_builders.go:397 and
adapters/grpc/container_ops_ship.go:202 — the one-shot refuel container and the CLI/RPC verb) go
through the ShipSymbol path and DO record the hull, so this is a per-caller hole, not a
column-wide one.

WHY IT MATTERS
1. Fuel cost cannot be attributed per hull, per frame class or per fleet. "Which hulls burn the
   fuel" is unanswerable from the ledger for the ~99% of refuels that ride the route executor.
2. It defeats retroactive repair. sp-wxgd2's fix attributes future spend to an OPERATION; without
   a ship symbol the historical rows cannot be re-attributed by hull even by hand, and neither can
   future ones be cross-checked against the operation they claim.
3. It is a silent, total loss of a field that costs nothing to record — the handler already holds
   the loaded hull in cmd.Ship.

RELATED: the standing note that ledger `transactions.ship_symbol` is an empty string on REFUEL rows,
so an `IS NOT NULL` filter builds a phantom blank hull rather than excluding the row. Same defect,
now root-caused to the caller/recorder seam.

FIX SHAPE (not implemented here — sp-wxgd2 deliberately kept its diff to the operation-context
propagation). Resolve the symbol once at the top of the refuel recorder from whichever field the
caller supplied — cmd.Ship.ShipSymbol() when Ship is non-nil, else cmd.ShipSymbol — and use that one
resolved value for the metadata, the description and the log fields, which today all read the
fallback directly in four places (:188, :209, :221, :241, :247). Check whether any other handler in
ship/commands makes the same Ship-vs-ShipSymbol assumption before fixing only this one.
acceptance_criteria: Every REFUEL ledger row names the hull it refuelled in metadata.ship_symbol (and in its description), whichever field the caller populated. A test drives a route-executor-shaped RefuelShipCommand (Ship set, ShipSymbol empty) and asserts the recorded row names the hull.
close_reason: Merged (squashed onto main). The recorder now takes the hull from the LoadShip-resolved ship rather than re-implementing the Ship-vs-ShipSymbol duality inside itself, so a ledger row structurally cannot name a hull other than the one actually refuelled; one resolved value replaced five fallback reads. The symbol-only CLI/RPC shape is pinned by its own test so the two caller shapes can't be traded off. Scope check was structural, not an empty grep: CargoTransactionCommand and JumpShipCommand declare ShipSymbol as required with no Ship alternative, so they cannot exhibit the defect; the duality exists only in the types.*ShipCommand family and Refuel is the only member that writes a ledger row. NOTE: this does NOT move the manual REFUEL count — that is sp-mc05f, a separate upstream gap. Verify by metadata.ship_symbol being non-empty on new REFUEL rows while total REFUEL volume holds.

title: Heavy-pricing errand vacates a parked-sensing slot without releasing it (stale PARKED row, suppressed replacement)
description:
FOUND WHILE DELIVERING sp-gmfvw (heavy-yard pricing errand now flies a spare parked probe).
Not a regression of that fix — a pre-existing gap the fix makes REACHABLE for the first time.

THE GAP. The errand navigates a `sensing_parked` probe to a heavy yard and issues no return leg
(deliberate — a return itinerary written by the autosizer would be a second placement authority
over the sensing pool). The probe therefore leaves a waypoint whose parkedsensing ledger row is
still SlotStateParked and still names it. Nothing appears to reconcile that:

  - parkedsensing/scanner.go inRotation() keeps the slot scannable (State==PARKED && kind
    MARKET|YARD), so the scanner goes on issuing reads "from" a probe that is no longer there.
  - slotbook.staffed[waypoint] stays true, which SUPPRESSES buying a replacement for that market.
  - probe_orphan_dispatch only reaches hulls that hold NO slot row, and probe_sensing_adoption
    skips hulls already indexed by an IN_TRANSIT/PARKED row — so neither pass re-places it.

BOUNDS THAT MAKE THIS SMALL, NOT ZERO: heavyPricingErrandsInFlight = 1 (one probe fleet-wide at a
time), and the errand only fires while an unpriced heavy yard is in reach — it stops the moment
the ask lands. Worst case observed-by-reading is one market's freshness plus one idle probe until
something else moves it.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in increasing order of scope:
 1. Prefer a SlotKindSpare probe as carrier (the sensing engine's own reserve pool) — needs the
    errand's PricingErrandHull to carry a "spare-kind" fact, i.e. a ledger read in the adapter.
 2. Release/re-WANT the vacated slot when the errand takes its hull, the way the sensing engine's
    own seed-errand claim does (parkedsensing/slotbook.go newSlotBook's onErrand filter is the
    existing precedent for "this hull is away on a mission").
 3. A drift detector: a PARKED slot whose named hull is no longer at the slot waypoint and is not
    in transit is a vacated slot.

Option 2 reuses machinery that already exists for exactly this shape and is probably the cheapest
correct answer. Verify the claim above against the live ledger before building — it is read from
the code, not from a live drift observation.

title: Sensing/scouting never stamp an OperationContext, so all probe spend lands in the 'manual' bucket — 686k unattributed
description:
MEASURED (staging, 2026-08-06): operation_type='manual' holds 762 transactions netting -686,731. Essentially none of it is manual.

  REFUEL       649 rows   -182,865
  JUMP         113 rows   -579,597
  SELL_CARGO     2 rows    +70,332

'manual' IS NOT A CATEGORY — IT IS THE ELSE BRANCH. All four assignment sites share one shape:

    if opCtx := shared.OperationContextFromContext(ctx); opCtx != nil && opCtx.IsValid() {
        recordCmd.OperationType = opCtx.NormalizedOperationType()
    } else {
        recordCmd.OperationType = "manual"   // 'No operation context - mark as manual transaction'
    }

Sites: ship/commands/cargo/cargo_transaction_ledger.go:157, ship/commands/tactics/refuel_ship.go:232,
ship/commands/navigation/jump_ship_fee.go:98, ship/commands/outfitting/outfitting.go:354. All are LEAF
spend paths, deep in utility calls far from wherever the operation began. The label reads as 'an
operator did this' and means 'attribution was lost'.

ROOT CAUSE, NARROWED TO ONE SUBSYSTEM: parkedsensing, scouting and adapters/parkedsensing contain
ZERO WithOperationContext calls. Every other spender stamps one -
  contract (balance_ship_position, delivery_executor), gas (siphon, storage_ship), liquidation,
  manufacturing (construction, 4 production_executor sites), storage (warehouse),
  trading (trade_route, arb_run, tour_run, contract_workflow).
Sensing is the only spending subsystem that never did.

CONFIRMED BY HULL: all 113 unattributed JUMP rows (-579,597) name hulls that are FRAME_PROBE /
dedicated_fleet=sensing_parked / role SATELLITE. The 'manual' bucket is, in practice, SENSING SPEND.

WHY IT MATTERS:
1. Cost attribution has a 686k hole. Any per-operation P&L understates by whatever share belongs to
   it, and sensing looks cheaper than it is - which is exactly the subsystem whose cost was under
   debate (sp-9k3yw: 206 idle probes at 21% of the API budget; sp-gtc0c: Get Jump Gate at 11%).
2. It corrupts live diagnosis. When staging's income/hr swung negative during a probe-buying burst,
   spend landing in 'manual' is invisible to any operation-level breakdown of why.
3. The label actively misleads. A reader takes 'manual' to mean human action and skips it.

FIX SHAPE: stamp an OperationContext in the sensing/scouting coordinators the way every other
subsystem already does (shared.WithOperationContext at the top of the reconcile/worker, carrying the
container id and a stable operation name). Follow the existing idiom exactly - do NOT invent a second
attribution mechanism, and do NOT add the context at the four leaf sites, which would paper over the
propagation gap rather than close it.

INVESTIGATE FIRST: enumerate which sensing/scouting entry points can reach a spend (jump fee, refuel,
cargo, outfitting) and stamp at the boundary that owns the work. Some paths may run under a ctx
already stamped by a caller - check before adding a second stamp, since NormalizedOperationType would
then depend on which won.

NOTE: sp-7e5j6 (merged) removes ~30 doomed jump attempts per hull per cooldown, so the JUMP share of
this bucket should shrink once deployed. Re-measure after that lands before sizing the remainder.

RELATED: the accepted-risk note in this codebase that operation_type='manual' means unpropagated
rather than a category - now measured and localised for the first time.
acceptance_criteria: Sensing and scouting spend carries an operation_type naming its coordinator, not 'manual'. The 'manual' bucket falls to genuine operator actions only (expected: near zero in an unattended run). No second attribution mechanism introduced - the existing WithOperationContext idiom is used. A test asserts a sensing-initiated jump fee records the sensing operation type.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sensing placement retries jumps against hulls it knows are on cooldown — ~30 doomed API calls per hull per cooldown
description:
OBSERVED LIVE (staging, 2026-08-06 14:05-14:07Z, during the first EXPANSION phase after gate completion).

The sensing placement path attempts a gate jump, gets a 409, and logs 'the step from X into Y was refused — the placement is held and retried'. The refusal is NOT a routing problem: it is a jump COOLDOWN.

  API error (status 409) code 4000: 'Ship action is still on cooldown for 201 second(s)'
  data.cooldown: totalSeconds 262, remainingSeconds 201, expiration 2026-08-06T14:09:28Z

RATE: ~7-8 refusals per minute, one per distinct hull, sustained across three consecutive minutes (8 hulls, 6 hulls, 8 hulls). A 262-second cooldown retried on the sensing tick is roughly 30 doomed calls per hull per cooldown.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT JUST NOISE: the cooldown expiry is ALREADY KNOWN before the attempt. navigation.Ship carries CooldownExpiration (domain/navigation/ports.go:299) and IsOnCooldown() (domain/navigation/ship_state.go:146), and that function's own doc comment describes exactly this state: 'A PARKED hull mid-cooldown is legitimately waiting out a game timer.' The placement path does not consult it before jumping. Every one of these requests is spent re-learning a fact already in memory.

COST: sensing's pacer was measured at 0.460 req/s during the window; ~0.12 req/s of that is jumps that cannot succeed — about a quarter of the sensing budget — against the hard 2 req/s account ceiling that sp-9k3yw (206 idle probes, 21% of budget) and sp-gtc0c (Get Jump Gate, 11%) are already competing for.

IT ALSO CORRUPTS THE SIGNAL: these log as WARNING with routing language ('the step ... was refused'), which reads like a gate/topology problem. During the first EXPANSION run they were the most visible line in the sensing log and looked like expansion was blocked when it was in fact working correctly.

FIX SHAPE: consult IsOnCooldown() (or compare CooldownExpiration to now) before attempting the jump, and hold the placement without an API call until expiry. Do NOT weaken any guard — this removes a doomed call, it does not authorise a new one. Consider whether the log line should distinguish 'held: cooldown until T' from a genuine routing refusal, since the two currently share wording.

CHECK BEFORE FIXING: whether other movers (contract, trade, gate-feed) share this pattern. The same doomed-retry shape may exist wherever a jump is attempted without a cooldown pre-check.
acceptance_criteria: A hull on cooldown is held without an API call until its expiry. Sensing's doomed-jump rate goes to zero, measured in the container log. The held-for-cooldown log line is distinguishable from a genuine routing refusal. No guard weakened. Test asserts no jump is attempted while IsOnCooldown() is true.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED on branch sp-7e5j6 @ 3bacb497 (base 4708d40d). NOT gated, NOT deployed — lead gates.

DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED BEFORE FIXING. Jump site: adapters/parkedsensing/mover_ports.go stepThroughGate, step TWO (the branch where the hull is already ON its gate). The cooldown IS trustworthy there: JumpShipCommand CAS-writes it the instant a jump succeeds (persistPostJumpNav -> SetCooldown), and GetShipQuery -> ShipRepository.FindBySymbol is a direct db.First on the ships row with NO cache in front of it. IsOnCooldown is the right predicate (not something narrower) — its own contract treats a nil/past expiry as not-on-cooldown, so a stale timestamp cannot hold a free hull.

FIX. stepThroughGate consults IsOnCooldown(now) before the jump and holds without an API call. The guard sits on the JUMP, not on the step: a cooling hull is still flown ONTO its gate (step one is productive, and the cooldown gates the jump ACTION only), so the flight branch pays no query. Fails OPEN on an unreadable row — an unknown cooldown must never hold a hull, or one whose row cannot be read would never jump again. Nothing cached (RULINGS #2), no guard weakened (RULINGS #4), no spend path, no flag.

LOG SPLIT. The hold is now INFO, action parked_sensing_gate_step_cooldown_hold, naming ship_symbol / from_waypoint / next_system / cooldown_until. parked_sensing_gate_step_failed stays reserved for a genuine refusal, and RouteAcross discriminates on a typed *jumpCooldownHold rather than parsing a message. Doomed-jump rate is measurable in the container log as that action rising while the cooldown-flavoured gate_step_failed goes to zero.

WIDER THAN THE BEAD. The defect was in the helper BOTH parkedsensing walkers share, so seed_ports.go JumpTo (the charting seed, also a tick machine, also unguarded) is fixed by the same change.

BLAST RADIUS CLOSED. Only THREE non-test files construct JumpShipCommand{}: this one (fixed), adapters/grpc/daemon_service_ship.go (CLI one-shot, human-issued, no retry loop — not a defect), and trading jumpHop (filed as sp-a4tjg P3: blocking traveller, ONE doomed 409 per resumed tour, not 30). Contract / gate-feed / gas / storage / manufacturing / liquidation / scouting movers issue no jumps at all (NavigateDirect/NavigateRoute consume no cooldown); RouteShipCommand delegates to travel(), which waits out per-hop cooldowns inside the call. gas/run_siphon_worker.go:112 already reads CooldownExpiration off the row — the same idiom.

TESTS: 6 new. Package 145 PASS / 0 FAIL -race. Full suite 88 packages ok, 0 FAIL, 0 races, go vet ./... clean. Mutation probe (guard condition -> 'false && held', compiles, anchor 1->0 asserted) killed TestRouteAcross_HoldsTheGateStepWhileTheHullIsOnCooldown and TestSeedJumpTo_HoldsTheGateStepWhileTheHullIsOnCooldown.

title: Trade engine's own cooldown debt is still lost on restart — RULINGS #2 covers it and sp-hxqao's replay deliberately does not
description:
sp-hxqao restores the GATE FEED's compression debt on boot. The trade engine's own debt is
still lost, and that is a RULINGS #2 gap in its own right.

## The shape

  trade accrues   LaneKey{Source, Dest, Good}   run_trade_route_coordinator_circuit.go:191
                                                 via laneCooldownKey(), impact.go:69-71
  pacing reads    LaneKey{Source, Good}          SourceDrainKey(), Dest empty

Disjoint namespaces, so trade's entries never influence pacing and vice versa. sp-hxqao's
replay writes only the source-aggregate key and therefore restores only what pacing reads.
That scoping is CORRECT for that bead -- replaying trade's purchases would write full-lane
keys that pacing never consults, changing nothing for the guard while silently re-ranking a
well-earning engine as a side effect of a persistence fix.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL REASONING: the sp-hxqao lane justified the exclusion as
"replaying trade's purchases would rebuild a debt the running fleet never accrues". That is
not right -- the fleet DOES accrue it, at circuit.go:191. The real reason is the disjoint
key namespace. Same decision, different and checkable justification.

## Why this is still a defect

RULINGS #2 names cooldown clocks as operational state that must survive a restart. Trade's
ledger entries ARE cooldown clocks. They have never been held to that standard because a
RANKER that forgets recent compression self-heals -- it just mis-ranks briefly -- whereas a
money GUARD that forgets fails open. Same data structure, two standards, and nobody noticed
until sp-zq2yb started reading it as a guard.

Consequence today: after any restart the trade engine re-ranks lanes as though no recent
compression exists, so it can re-enter a market it just drained. Bounded and self-healing,
which is why this is P2 and not P1.

## Acceptance
1. Restore trade's full-lane debt on boot using the same cooldownreplay package -- it
   already has the window, the tv floor, and the double-count guard.
2. NAME THE RANKING CHANGE. This alters lane selection for an engine that is currently
   earning well. Measure trade throughput before and after, do not assert it is fine.
3. Reuse sp-hxqao's tv lower-bound (largest single PURCHASE_CARGO in window bounds
   historical tv), so reconstruction can only under-accrue, never over-arm.
4. The double-count guard must still hold: refuse any key already carrying debt.
5. Mutation probe naming its kills, provenance stated.

RELATED: sp-hxqao (the gate-side replay this extends), sp-zq2yb, sp-jekjf, RULINGS #2.
notes:
FEASIBILITY LARGELY ANSWERED IN ADVANCE by sp-hxqao's blocker analysis (lead-verified).
Read this before designing -- the obvious approach is blocked.

THE sp-hxqao REPLAY CANNOT SIMPLY BE POINTED AT TRADE'S KEYS.

  trade key    LaneKey{Source, Dest, Good}     needs a DESTINATION
  PURCHASE_CARGO metadata keys, verified:
      agent, good_symbol, selector_branch, ship_symbol, units, waypoint

`waypoint` is where the BUY happened -- the source. THERE IS NO DESTINATION FIELD ON THE
ROW. So a purchase row cannot produce a trade LaneKey, which is precisely why sp-hxqao's
replay writes only the source-aggregate key (Dest empty) and why its exclusion of trade was
correct on the KEY-SHAPE grounds, not on the "fleet never accrues it" grounds it originally
gave.

Recovering Dest would mean joining each buy to a later SELL_CARGO by ship_symbol + good.
sp-hxqao's lane assessed that as ambiguous across multi-leg trips and simply ABSENT when a
buy stranded and never sold. Treat that as a starting assessment, not a settled one -- but
do not assume it is easy.

THREE PATHS, PRICE THEM BEFORE BUILDING:
1. Join buy->sell to recover Dest. Cheapest if it works; verify the ambiguity assessment
   above against real rows, including stranded buys, before committing.
2. Persist the ledger directly to a table. sp-hxqao avoided this because the MANUFACTURING
   models are not in AutoMigrate -- CHECK WHETHER THE TRADING MODELS ARE; that constraint
   may not apply here, in which case this is the straightforward answer.
3. Record the destination on the transaction row going forward. Fixes it permanently but
   restores nothing historical, so the first restart after deploy is still blind.

REUSABLE FROM sp-hxqao (do not re-derive):
- the tv lower-bound trick: the largest single PURCHASE_CARGO in the window bounds
  historical trade_volume, so reconstruction can only UNDER-accrue, never over-arm
- Rebuild refuses any key already carrying debt -- structurally idempotent, so correctness
  does not rest on boot ordering
- window = 3 x tau, derived from the configured tau rather than pinned

STILL REQUIRED: name the trade-ranking change and MEASURE throughput before/after. This
alters lane selection for an engine that is currently earning well.

SHIPPED AND DEPLOYED 2026-08-06 11:33:15 (main 6f5ad5de). Boot line printed exactly as the
lane specified:

  Lane cooldown persistence: armed, restored 0 trade lane(s) of compression debt

That is the falsifier and it passed -- no line at all would have meant
armLaneCooldownPersistence never executed. "restored 0" is the CORRECT value: construction
is idle, so no full-lane debt has been written yet. Replay unregressed (434), 0 panics,
14 containers.

THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE WAS FALSE, AND IT WAS THE LEAD'S. I wrote "this alters lane
selection for an engine that is currently earning well" as a measurement criterion. The
trade-route coordinator has NEVER RUN ON STAGING -- lead-verified: 0 trade_route containers
and 0 trade_route transactions in the entire recorded history. The 270 TRADING containers
are all command_type=tour_run. TRADE_FLEET_COORDINATOR launches tours, not trade routes;
StartTradeRoute is reachable only via CLI->gRPC. So measured trade-ranking impact is
exactly zero, provable from reachability rather than measurable from throughput.

CORRECTION TO THE LANE'S OWN FRAMING -- "costs nothing while dormant" understates it.
The READ side is dormant (trade_route never runs). The WRITE side is LIVE: the gate feed
accrues a FULL-LANE key on every leg at gate_feed.go:155, alongside the source-aggregate
key. So the persister fires on live construction traffic -- one synchronous DB upsert per
feed leg. Mitigated and acceptable: the write-through runs OUTSIDE the ledger lock (pinned
by a 5s-timeout test), and store.Save errors are handled inside the sink so they cannot
fail a leg. But it is not a no-op path.

PATH 2's BLOCKER DID NOT EXIST. database.AutoMigrate calls db.AutoMigrate(AllModels()...)
and the manufacturing models ARE registered, enforced by an existing AST guard. The note
carried into this bead from sp-hxqao was wrong on that point.

PATH 1 REJECTED ON A SAFETY FLAW, not just ambiguity: the tv lower-bound trick DOES NOT
TRANSFER. Trade accrues against lane.VolumeCap = min(source.Volume, dest.Volume), but a
sell tranche is bounded by the DESTINATION alone. So the largest single sale bounds dest,
not the minimum, and max(today, largestSale) can land BELOW the historical VolumeCap --
which OVER-accrues, the exact direction the bead said to design against first.

HAZARD FOUND AND CLOSED: the ledger mutex is shared with the LIVE gate feed's Debt reads.
A sink under that lock would put a DB round-trip on the spend guard's hot path, and a sink
that read the ledger back would deadlock the daemon.

VALUE IS CONTINGENT: this only pays off if trade_route is ever armed. Correct, cheap, and
currently protecting an engine that does not run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cooldown decay should be activity-conditioned — one tau spans a 5x spread (RESTRICTED 9.0h vs STRONG 1.7h half-life)
description:
From sp-k9xuo's measurement. LaneCooldownLedger uses a single tau=750min (half-life ~8.7h).
Measured recovery half-lives differ ~5x by market activity:

  RESTRICTED  ~9.0 h   (tau is nearly exact here)
  STRONG      ~1.7 h   (tau is ~5x too slow)

Under STRONG the guard therefore stays armed roughly 5x longer than the market needs,
withholding buys from a source that has already recovered. Conservative direction
(RULINGS #4-safe) but it costs throughput.

title: [P2] Gate-feed source pacing loses its compression memory on daemon restart — in-memory ledger, one leg of blindness per source
description:
Follow-up to sp-zq2yb, filed by the implementing lane rather than left implicit (the lead's
explicit instruction: persist it, or name the accepted risk with RULINGS #2 cited).

sp-zq2yb paces the gate feed against sources it is draining by consulting
trading.LaneCooldownLedger. That ledger is IN-MEMORY by design — its own doc says a restart
"simply forgets recent compression, which self-heals". That is true for its original consumer
(the trade ranker, where forgetting costs a slightly mis-ranked lane) and NOT true for a money
guard, where forgetting means the guard fails OPEN. RULINGS #2: operational state survives
restarts.

## Why it was accepted rather than blocking

The blindness is bounded to roughly ONE LEG per (source, good), because a single hull-load
usually exceeds one trade_volume and the bound is one tranche's debt:

  H51 IRON       hull 80 / tv 60  = 1.33 tranches -> debt 0.087 > bound 0.065  -> re-armed after 1 leg
  H53 QUARTZ_SAND hull 80 / tv 180 = 0.44 tranches -> debt 0.029 < bound 0.065  -> re-armed after 3 legs

So a restart costs one to three unpaced legs on a source, not sustained blindness. Combined with
the never-refuse fallback (pacing can only ever reorder a leg, never stand one down), the failure
mode is "we take one extra tranche from a drained source after a restart" — real, bounded, and far
smaller than the defect sp-zq2yb fixes.

## Work

Persist the ledger, or reconstruct it on boot. Reconstruction is likely cheaper than a new table
and needs no new storage: every PURCHASE_CARGO row already carries units + timestamp +
operation_type, and market_data carries trade_volume, so the boot path can replay the last few tau
worth of buys into Accrue. That also fixes it for the TRADE engine, which has the same amnesia and
has simply never been held to a guard's standard.

Do NOT fix this by giving the gate feed a private persisted ledger — sp-zq2yb deliberately shares
the trade engine's one so both see a single compression picture.
notes:
REVERTED 2026-08-06 ~10:32 UTC-3. The merge (1b6aca44) PANICKED THE DAEMON AT BOOT and took
staging down for ~13 minutes. Reverted as 2dd68f3d; staging recovered and verified healthy.

  panic: player_id must be positive
    shared.MustNewPlayerID(...)   internal/domain/shared/player_id.go:22
    main.run(...)                 cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:834
    main.main()                   cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:98

CAUSE: the replay was wired immediately after the ledger is constructed, but the player ID
is not resolved at that point in boot. It panics before the daemon ever listens.

THE GATE PASSED AND COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS. go build clean, go vet rc=0, 88 packages
green, 4 mutations killed, every test written before its implementation. All true. The unit
tests call Rebuild directly with a VALID player ID, so nothing exercised the BOOT ORDER.
This is the same gap sp-4i59r closed for metrics with an AST test that inspects the CALL
SITE rather than the function -- thorough coverage of a function says nothing about where
it is plugged in.

THE LOGIC IS NOT IN QUESTION. The source-aggregate re-key (sp-jekjf) and the replay itself
were sound and well-verified -- 0 of 14 pairs needed the tv floor, IRON@H51 restores 2.68
against a 0.065 bound, double-count guard structurally idempotent. ONLY THE WIRING POINT IS
WRONG. Do not redesign; re-wire.

ON REDO, REQUIRED:
1. Wire the replay AFTER the player ID is resolved. State which line and why it is safe there.
2. A test that FAILS against the reverted commit -- boot-order, not another Rebuild unit
   test. If it passes against 1b6aca44 it is not the test this needs.
3. The replay must still run BEFORE any coordinator can accrue, or the double-count guard
   starts refusing live debt. Prove both orderings hold simultaneously.
4. Best-effort must mean best-effort: a replay that cannot run must LOG AND CONTINUE, never
   panic and never fail boot. Assert that a failing replay still boots.

REOPENED. The merged fix (dec14f8d) is SAFE BUT INERT ON STAGING. It does not panic and it
does not work.

  players on staging: 1 (id 1, TORWINDSTG)
  construction PURCHASE_CARGO rows for player 1: 434
  cfg.Captain.PlayerID on staging: 0 (captain: enabled: false, no player_id key)

Deployed build printed:
  "Lane cooldown replay: no player configured, starting with no compression memory"

That is the SKIP path. On the only environment we deploy to, the replay would never run --
booting clean, logging, and doing nothing, forever. The lead read that line as evidence the
fix worked and reported it as such; it is evidence the fix is inert.

LESSON (lane's, and it generalises): "it doesn't panic" and "it does the thing it exists to
do" are different claims, and only the first was ever verified. Every test written encoded

FIX: resolveReplayPlayer -- configured captain player when set, otherwise THE SINGLE STORED
PLAYER. It deliberately refuses to guess further: LaneKey{Source,Dest,Good} carries NO

title: Minimum construction tranche is pinned to trade_volume, so a DEEPER market is harder to afford — creates an affordability cliff
description:
OBSERVED (staging, era 6, gate at 1520/1600 with 80 FAB_MATS remaining):

  tv=24 -> "UNAFFORDABLE EVEN AT THE MINIMUM TRANCHE: 24 units would cost 60456"
  tv=59 -> "UNAFFORDABLE EVEN AT THE MINIMUM TRANCHE: 59 units would cost 148621"

The minimum tranche tracks the market's trade_volume. Consequence: as a market gets
DEEPER the minimum buy gets LARGER, so a healthier market is HARDER to afford. That is
backwards from the intuition and it produces an affordability cliff.

Concretely today: deployable capital is ~31% of treasury (measured across the log's full
range -- treasury 790480/reserve 534288/deployable 256192 at the top, 263217/217930/45287
now). At tv=24 the gate could buy at treasury ~194k. At tv=59 it needs treasury ~480k for
the SAME remaining 80 units. Nothing about the requirement changed; only the market depth did.

Result: buys are opportunistic, firing only when tv happens to dip into the deployable
band. The last three tranches were 33, 24 and 28 units, all on low-tv moments.

NOT A MONEY-GUARD PROBLEM. The reserve is behaving correctly and must not be weakened
(RULINGS #4). The question is only why the FLOOR of a buy scales with depth.

## Acceptance
1. Establish why a minimum tranche exists at all. Likely trip efficiency -- a hauler leg
   has fixed fuel/time cost, so a 3-unit purchase may genuinely not be worth flying.
   NAME the real reason before changing it; if it is deliberate, this bead is invalid
   and should be closed as such.
2. If the floor is about trip economics, it should be derived from trip cost and the
   remaining requirement, NOT from the sink's depth. A gate needing 80 more units should
   be able to buy 20 now rather than wait for 59 to become affordable.
3. RULINGS #4: any change makes buys SMALLER or identical. This bead LOWERS a floor; it
   must not raise any ceiling, and must not let a buy exceed what the reserve permits.
4. Do not reintroduce the sp-xcjuy failure: a leg that cannot afford the full tranche must
   still partial-fill rather than abort. That fix is working and is visible in the log as
   "Stopping purchase of IRON after 33 units".
5. Regression: a trivially small remaining requirement must not produce a spam of one-unit trips.

NOT URGENT. The gate completes on its own either when tv dips or when treasury reaches
~480k. Filed because the cliff is structural and will recur on every future construction.
notes:
LANE FINDING 2026-08-06: the stated mechanism is FALSE. There is no tv-pinned minimum and no
affordability cliff. A real but DIFFERENT defect exists; this bead should be re-filed on it.

CRITERION 1 -- why a minimum tranche exists. It is DELIBERATE and named:
  minViableTrancheUnits = defaultFeedSaturationMinUnits = 25   (feeding_policy.go:37-40)
  "<25u moves activity nothing, so a balanced tranche is never sized below this
   (a dribble is wasted hull-hours)" -- analyst-verified, FOR FACTORY FEEDING.

THE PREMISE IS FALSIFIED ON FOUR COUNTS:
1. Not pinned to trade_volume. All 52 decline rows carry min_units=25, a constant.
2. The "59"/"24" in the quoted lines are the ATTEMPTED tranche (tv-derived), not the minimum.
   Full line: "59 units would cost 148621 ... the reserve leaves room for only 17 units
   against a 25-unit minimum."
3. The threshold does NOT scale with depth. affordableTrancheUnits returns
   min(want, headroom/ask), so for any want>=25 the gate condition affordable>=25 reduces to
   headroom >= 25*ask -- ALGEBRAICALLY INDEPENDENT OF tv. The observed decline had
   headroom/ask = 45287/2519 = 17 < 25, which fails at ANY tv, including 24. The "~194k at
   tv=24 vs ~480k at tv=59" figures assume the buy must be the FULL tv; it must not.
4. "last three tranches 33, 24, 28, all on low-tv moments" -- tv was 59 from 10:40 onward.
   Those are SHRINK OUTPUTS, the sp-xcjuy resize working: 59->53, 59->33, 57->33, 59->28,
   48->28, 48->26 (action=tranche_resized). Deeper markets shrink MORE successfully, not less:
   headroom between the 25 floor and tv is what the resize has to work with.

What was actually observed is the money guard correctly declining when deployable capital
(45,287) could not cover the 25-unit minimum (62,975 at ask 2,519). RULINGS #4 behaving.

THE REAL DEFECT (narrower, and it is mine): the 25-unit floor is justified ENTIRELY by factory
activity saturation, but BuyAtTerminalFactory -- the GATE DELIVERY buy, which purchases the
terminal factory's OUTPUT for construction site X1-KP46-I55 -- routes through the same shared
fillFromSource and inherits it. A construction site has no activity to move; it has a BILL.
17 units toward a 1600-unit gate is 17 units of permanent progress. The saturation rationale
does not apply to that sink. This matches the bead's criterion-2 PRESCRIPTION (derive the floor
from trip economics and the remaining requirement) while contradicting its diagnosis.

MEASURED COST: 52 declines over 2h33m (09:51:39 -> 12:24:12), affordable=17 each time, with
only 80 units remaining. Self-resolved at 12:25 when treasury recovered (shrink 59->53).

PROVENANCE -- I introduced this coupling in sp-xcjuy (458d7970) by using the feed constant as
the shrink floor in the shared loop. Before that commit these same cases did
`logSpendFloorStop; break` -- 0 units, leg aborted. So the floor blocks NOTHING that previously
worked; it bounds how far my rescue reaches. Incomplete fix, not a regression.

FLAG, NOT A CLAIM: the floor's factory-side justification ("<25u moves activity nothing")
deserves re-examination given sp-k9xuo, but I have NOT falsified it. sp-k9xuo measured input
STOCK vs output RECOVERY RATE; it did not measure delivery SIZE vs activity TRANSITIONS.
Different claim, untested.

PREMISE FALSIFIED (sp-9eor3 lane, lead-verified). THERE IS NO tv-PINNED MINIMUM AND NO
AFFORDABILITY CLIFF. The bead was filed on a TRUNCATED LOG LINE -- the lead cut it at 140
chars, ending immediately before the clause that names the real minimum, then reasoned from
the truncation.

FULL LINE:
  "Parked input purchase of FAB_MATS at X1-KP46-F45 — UNAFFORDABLE EVEN AT THE MINIMUM
   TRANCHE: 59 units would cost 148621 against a reserve of 217750, and the reserve leaves
   room for only 17 units against a 25-unit minimum. 0 already aboard"

The 59 is the ATTEMPTED tranche. The MINIMUM is 25, constant across all 52 decline rows.

  minViableTrancheUnits = defaultFeedSaturationMinUnits = 25  (feeding_policy.go:37-40)
  "<25u moves activity nothing, so a balanced tranche is never sized below this
   (a dribble is wasted hull-hours)" -- analyst-verified, FOR FACTORY FEEDING.

Four counts against the filed premise:
1. Not tv-pinned: all 52 decline rows carry min_units=25.
2. affordableTrancheUnits = min(want, headroom/ask), so for want>=25 the condition
   affordable>=25 reduces to headroom >= 25 x ask -- ALGEBRAICALLY INDEPENDENT OF tv.
   The observed decline had 45287/2519 = 17 < 25, which fails at ANY tv including 24.
3. The ~194k-vs-~480k figures assumed the buy must be the full tv. It must not.
4. "33, 24, 28 all on low-tv moments" is wrong: tv was 59 from 10:40 onward. Those are
   shrink OUTPUTS (action=tranche_resized): 59->53, 59->33, 57->33, 59->28, 48->26.
   sp-xcjuy's resize is working. A DEEPER market shrinks more successfully, since the
   headroom between the 25 floor and tv is what the resize has to work with -- the
   OPPOSITE of the filed direction.

DO NOT BUILD THIS BEAD AS WRITTEN -- it chases a mechanism that does not exist.
Superseded by the real defect, filed separately.

title: [P2] Era sell-impact coefficient is fitted ~2.3x too low — measured 0.0349/tv against the 0.015 default, leaving every depth guard slack
description:
Measured while fixing sp-gpoxh. The sink-depth guard shipped there sizes a buy from
trading.DefaultSellImpactCoefficient (era-3 fit, 0.015 = 1.5% bid fall per full
trade_volume sold). Staging says that number is materially low.

MEASURED (staging, the sp-gpoxh incident run, SHIP_PARTS -> X1-KP46-H52, trade_volume 6):
  sold 29 units = 4.833 full trade volumes
  bid 7,265 -> 6,039 = -16.88% total
  => -3.49% per full trade_volume, i.e. 2.33x the 0.015 default

The BUY side is wrong in the other direction on the same run: ask 3,445 -> 3,555 over the
same 4.833 volumes = +0.66%/tv against a 0.050 default, i.e. 7.6x too HIGH. The two errors
roughly cancel in the combined slope the ranker uses (modelled k 46.9 credits/unit vs 46.1
observed), which is why lane RANKING has looked fine — but any guard that reads only the
SELL slope inherits the full 2.3x error.

CONSEQUENCE: the sp-gpoxh depth bound is q <= tv*(1-sellFloorFraction)/sellImpact. At 0.015
with the 0.80 floor that is 13.3 full tranches, which is slack on all 36 currently-profitable
lanes in staging AND on the incident run itself. At the measured 0.0349 it is 5.7 tranches.
The guard is correct in shape; the coefficient is what gives it teeth.

WORK: refit buy_impact and sell_impact on current-era telemetry (transactions carries the
tranche-by-tranche ladder for both sides; group SELL_CARGO/PURCHASE_CARGO by
operation_type+good+waypoint and regress dP/P on units/trade_volume). The knob already
exists as config.TradeImpactConfig — this is a refit, not new surface. Note the two sides
must be fitted SEPARATELY; the pooled slope hides both errors.

OPEN QUESTION worth answering in the same pass: impact looks tv-dependent (the thin tv=6
sink moved 3.49%/tv, a tv=60 COPPER sink moved 0.94%/tv over 2 runs). A per-tv-tier fit may
beat a single pooled coefficient — the cooldown tau already documents per-tier half-lives
(339/663/1681 min for tv <=40 / 41-80 / 81-240) for the same reason.

title: [P2] Long-haul reads other engines' in-flight absorption but publishes none of its own — the contention view is one-way
description:
Found by the sp-kw2em lane while wiring the absorption consult (merged a6fcf55a).

Long-haul now READS the absorption ledger to see other engines' in-flight PLANNED units, but it
never RECORDS its own. So trade-route, tour and idle-arb still cannot see long-haul's in-flight
dumps when they size their own buys.

The contention model only works if every engine both reads and writes. Symmetric coverage needs a
RecordPlanned at leg launch, following idle-arb's existing pattern.

WHY IT IS P2, NOT HIGHER: long-haul has not run in era 5 or era 6 — its last execution was prod era
4, 2026-07-23 to 07-25 (38 containers, 158 transactions). So nothing is currently blind to anything.
This becomes real the moment the long-haul worker is launched again, and it should be fixed BEFORE
that rather than after.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Long-haul records its planned units at leg launch and releases them on completion or failure,
   following idle-arb's pattern rather than inventing a second one.
2. A leg that fails or is cancelled must not leave a permanent phantom reservation — that would
   shrink every other engine's buys forever. Test the failure path explicitly, not just the happy one.
3. Another engine sizing against a sink long-haul is already dumping into must see the reduced
   headroom. That is the whole point; assert it end to end rather than asserting the write alone.
4. RULINGS #4: this can only ever TIGHTEN other engines' buys. State the direction and pin it.

RELATED: sp-kw2em (the read half, merged a6fcf55a).

title: [P2] Grafana coverage panels use unqualified sum() with no player_id filter — dead-era series already scraped will drag 'Fresh Market Coverage' down until they age out
description:
The other half of the fix sp-hrko6 landed, deliberately left out of that bead's scope by the lane.

sp-hrko6 (merged 50d4a33b) stopped the COLLECTOR emitting label series for dead players. It does
not and cannot fix two remaining things:

1. SERIES ALREADY IN PROMETHEUS PERSIST until they age out of retention. Every dashboard reading
   these metrics stays wrong in the meantime.
2. THE PANEL QUERY ITSELF HAS NO player_id FILTER. Verified in
   gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/market-dynamics.json:

     (sum(spacetraders_daemon_market_coverage_fresh{age_threshold="300s"})
      / sum(spacetraders_daemon_market_coverage_total)) * 100

   Exactly one expression references these metrics and ZERO of them filter by player_id, while the
   metrics ARE labelled by player_id. So a closed era contributes a permanent non-zero _total
   against a permanently-zero _fresh and drags the ratio down forever. At the last measured ratio
   (~27k dead rows against 3.3k live) that is most of the number — the panel has probably been
   reading low for as long as there have been multiple eras.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS: 'Fresh Market Coverage' is an operational health panel. A number
that is structurally wrong in a known direction either gets trusted (and misleads) or gets learned
as unreliable (and then a REAL coverage collapse is dismissed as 'that panel is always low'). The
second failure is the worse one and it is invisible.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Coverage expressions scope to the live player — a template variable or an explicit
   player_id filter, consistent with how other dashboards in this directory handle it. Check
   whether one already exists before inventing a convention.
2. Sweep the other dashboards in gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/ for the same unqualified-sum
   shape against any player-labelled metric; this is unlikely to be the only one.
3. State whether a Prometheus-side cleanup of already-scraped dead series is wanted, or whether
   waiting for retention is acceptable. That is an operational decision, not a code one.
4. Verification is visual — the panel must read plausibly against a hand-computed
   fresh/total from the live player's rows. A green test proves nothing here.

RELATED: sp-hrko6 (merged 50d4a33b — the collector half).

title: [P2] captain/detectors_scout.go doc comment carries TWO false claims about market_data — the second one ('empty between eras') is the dangerous half. PROTECTED PATH
description:
Found by the sp-hrko6 lane's tree-wide sweep. It could not fix this: gobot/internal/captain/** is a
PROTECTED PATH that build agents must not modify, and the captain/orchestrator does not hand-edit
code either. It needs an Admiral-authorised change.

LOCATION: gobot/internal/captain/detectors_scout.go, lines 265-268, in the doc comment on
postedSystems. Exact current text:

    // exactly as the scout-post repository's ListActive does: era close wipes market_data
    // but leaves closed-era scout_posts rows behind, so an un-scoped read would let a
    // dead-era post suppress a live-era proposal. Between eras (no open era) nothing is
    // posted — and market_data is empty then anyway, so no proposal fires regardless.

TWO FALSE CLAIMS, AND THE SECOND IS THE DANGEROUS ONE:
 1. 'era close wipes market_data' — true only of the --confirm-gated 'universe close', NOT of the
    documented rollover path. 'universe transition' calls TransitionEra, which never truncates.
 2. 'market_data is empty then anyway, so no proposal fires regardless' — between eras market_data
    is emphatically NOT empty. It retains every prior era's rows; the last measured figure was
    ~27k dead-era rows against 3.3k live. This sentence asserts a safety property that has never
    held, and reasoning built on it would be wrong.

THE CODE IS FINE — ONLY THE JUSTIFICATION IS WRONG. postedSystems' actual safety is the
closed_at IS NULL era scope in its own body, which returns an empty set when no era is open. That
is sound and unaffected. This is a documentation defect, not a behaviour defect, which is exactly
why it is P2 and not higher — and also why it is worth fixing, since the next person to touch this
will reason from the comment.

SUGGESTED REPLACEMENT (from the lane that found it):

    // exactly as the scout-post repository's ListActive does: closed-era scout_posts rows
    // survive a rollover, so an un-scoped read would let a dead-era post suppress a live-era
    // proposal. Between eras (no open era) nothing is posted, and that empty result is the
    // whole guard — NOT any emptiness of market_data, which retains every prior era's rows
    // ( does not truncate; only the gated  does).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Both false claims removed; the real guard (the era scope returning empty) named as the reason.
2. No behaviour change — this is comment-only.
3. Consistent with sp-hrko6's landed wording in parkedsensing/surge_ports.go, which now states the
   two-mechanism invariant (the KEY prevents cross-era collision on writes, the FILTER prevents
   cross-era reads, and neither is truncation).

RELATED: sp-hrko6 (merged 50d4a33b — the same defect in the non-protected file), sp-hdr4p (merged
99c50774 — the key half of the invariant).

title: [P2] Two comments assert that era transition TRUNCATES market_data — it does not, and believing them would license removing the player_id filter that is the actual safety
description:
A documentation defect of the dangerous kind: it asserts a safety property the running code does not
provide, and acting on it would CREATE the money bug that currently does not exist.

THE FALSE CLAIMS:
 - parkedsensing/surge_ports.go:62-68 — 'what keeps it honest is that the era transition TRUNCATES
   the player-partitioned market cache'
 - captain/detectors_scout.go:265-268 — 'era close wipes market_data'

THE TRUTH: the documented rollover path does NOT truncate. 'universe transition' calls TransitionEra,
which explicitly never truncates (era_transition.go:26-31). Only the SEPARATE, --confirm-gated
'universe close' calls CloseEra -> truncateCaches (era_repository.go:220-228). The normal era
rollover leaves every stale row in place.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD AND NOT JUST AN EDIT: the REAL safety on the read side is the
'player_id = ?' predicate carried by every market_data read. A future engineer who believes these
comments could reasonably drop that predicate as redundant — 'the table is truncated at rollover, so
why filter?' — and THAT WOULD BE THE MONEY BUG: a stale-era price winning a ranked query and feeding
a spend decision. The comment does not merely misinform; it argues for the exact change that would
break the system.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Both comments corrected to state the actual invariant: reads are safe because they are
   player-scoped, NOT because the table is emptied. Name TransitionEra vs CloseEra explicitly so the
   distinction survives.
2. Grep for any other comment or doc asserting truncation-on-transition and correct those too.
3. If sp-t2wqv (the era_id key fix) lands first, these comments must describe THAT invariant instead.

SECONDARY, same file family: metrics/market_metrics.go:268-273 enumerates DISTINCT player_id with no
filter and emits Prometheus label series for dead players, so every era permanently adds a label set.
Unbounded cardinality — cost and noise, not correctness — but it compounds with the same never-pruned
rows and is worth fixing in the same pass.

Found by the sp-20eyn lane.
notes:
CROSS-REFERENCE CORRECTION: acceptance criterion 3 names 'sp-t2wqv', a bead ID written before the
companion existed and which does not resolve. The era_id key fix is **sp-hdr4p**.
INVARIANT CHANGED BY sp-hdr4p — correct the comments to the NEW truth, not the old one.

Before: market_data was player-partitioned only by CONVENTION — every read happened to carry
player_id = ?, and nothing in the schema required it. The comments in
parkedsensing/surge_ports.go:62-68 and captain/detectors_scout.go:265-268 credited the safety to
'the era transition TRUNCATES market_data', which is false on the path that actually runs
(universe transition -> TransitionEra never truncates; only the gated universe close ->
CloseEra does).

After sp-hdr4p: market_data's PRIMARY KEY is (player_id, waypoint_symbol, good_symbol). The
partitioning is now STRUCTURAL — the server enforces that two eras' rows are distinct objects,
and one era can no longer occupy a key another era needs.

So the corrected comments should say neither 'truncation keeps it honest' (never true on the
live path) nor merely 'the player_id filter keeps it honest' (true, but now understated). The
accurate statement is: rows are keyed per player, and every read filters on player_id — the key
makes cross-era collision impossible, the filter makes cross-era READS impossible. Two
mechanisms, both real, neither of them truncation.

Filed from the sp-hdr4p lane.
INVARIANT CHANGED — sp-hdr4p landed as main 99c50774, so these comments must now describe TWO
mechanisms rather than one, and neither of them is truncation:
  THE KEY    market_data's PRIMARY KEY is now (player_id, waypoint_symbol, good_symbol), which makes
             a cross-era COLLISION impossible.
  THE FILTER every read carries player_id = ?, applied before any ORDER BY / MIN / MAX / DISTINCT ON,
             which makes a cross-era READ impossible.
So the corrected comments should say neither 'truncation keeps it honest' (never true on the live
path — TransitionEra does not truncate, only the separately-gated universe close does) nor merely
'the player_id filter keeps it honest' (true, but now understated).

The original hazard this bead names is UNCHANGED and still the reason it exists: someone who believes
the truncation claim could drop the player_id predicate as redundant, and that would be the money bug
— a stale-era price winning a ranked query and feeding a spend decision. The new key prevents
collisions on WRITE; it does NOT make the read filter redundant.
close_reason:
FIXED and MERGED as main 50d4a33b (lane a0bd1fc1). Gate: GatePassed:true Stale:false Merged:true
EmptyMerge:false. go vet rc=0, go test rc=0, 87 packages, 0 FAIL — verified independently by exit
code and wall time.

THE COMMENT is rewritten to name both mechanisms and which half each guards — the KEY for WRITES
(cross-era collision impossible), the FILTER for READS (cross-era read impossible) — and states

SWEEP RESULT: exactly one further truncation claim tree-wide, in internal/captain/ (protected path,

THE METRICS ITEM WAS RECLASSIFIED FROM COST TO CORRECTNESS, and this is the part worth remembering.
I told the lane to fix it if clean and leave it if a consumer wanted the dead series. It checked the
consumers instead of accepting my framing, and they argued the opposite way:
configs/grafana/dashboards/market-dynamics.json computes
  (sum(market_coverage_fresh{age_threshold='300s'}) / sum(market_coverage_total)) * 100
with an UNQUALIFIED sum(). I verified this directly: one expression references these metrics, ZERO

forever — at ~27k dead rows against 3.3k live, most of the number. The dead series were not inert

Also fixed in passing: getActivePlayersAndSystems returned two independent lists the caller
CROSS-PRODUCED, discarding the query's own knowledge of which (player, system) pairs actually hold
