title: Gate surplus cargo has no disposal route; TORWINDSTG-A holds 36 dead ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY units
description:
Deliberately scoped out of sp-v2a2h. That fix stops the fleet CREATING new gate surplus; it does not dispose of surplus already held.

LIVE INSTANCE: TORWINDSTG-A is a gate hauler holding ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY x36 for a material that is already at 400/400 COMPLETE. The construction site can never accept them. That hold is occupied indefinitely, reducing effective gate-hauling capacity while the FAB_MATS build is still running.

WHY IT WAS NOT AUTO-FIXED. Automatic disposal means SELLING at market: choosing an importing waypoint, navigating there, and accepting whatever bid stands. That is a routing decision plus real money risk. freeCargoSpace already carries an explicit protection born of a -258k dump, so the codebase has been burned here before. Improvising a sell path into a live gate build, as a side effect of a money-bleed fix, was the wrong trade - correctly declined by the lane.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: observability, so the state is unmissable rather than silent - gate_material_overshoot_units_total plus an operator WARNING naming the hauling-capacity cost. The 436-vs-400 overshoot was previously only visible by summing the transaction ledger by hand.

SCOPE TO DECIDE (this needs a judgement call, not just code):
- Manual disposal of TORWINDSTG-A's 36 units is available NOW and needs no code. Consider doing that first and separately.
- Whether automatic disposal is wanted AT ALL, given the -258k precedent. Options: sell only into a confirmed IMPORT waypoint above a floor price; transfer to another hull that needs the good; or hold and simply surface it for a human. The safest useful version may be transfer-or-alert, never blind sell.
- Any auto-sell MUST respect the existing freeCargoSpace protection rather than route around it.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether automatic disposal is wanted. If yes: surplus gate material is transferred or sold only under an explicit price/venue guard, the freeCargoSpace protection is respected, and a test proves no blind dump. TORWINDSTG-A's 36 units resolved either way.

title: Intermittent DATA RACE in internal/adapters/api budget-tracker fallback test reddens pre-merge sweeps
description:
TestRequestFallsBackToGlobalBudgetTrackerWhenNoneSetOnClient in gobot/internal/adapters/api intermittently trips the race detector under 'go test -race ./...'. Reproduces roughly 1 run in 4-9; does not reproduce every sweep.

FOUND BY: the sp-z7u71 lane, which changes ZERO files under gobot/internal/adapters/ — so it is pre-existing and not caused by that work. Confirmed by that lane's final clean -race sweep passing (85 packages ok, exit 0).

WHY IT MATTERS: it randomly reddens the pre-merge -race sweep that every lane must pass. An intermittent red gate trains agents and humans alike to re-run until green, which is exactly how a REAL race gets waved through. A flaky race detector finding is worse than none.

LIKELY SHAPE: a global/package-level budget tracker being read and written by concurrent tests (the test name itself says the client has none set and falls back to the GLOBAL tracker). Suspect shared mutable package state across parallel tests rather than a race in production code — but that must be confirmed, not assumed: if the shared global is also shared in production, the race is real.

FIRST STEP: run the single test in a loop with -race -count=N to get a reliable reproduction and capture the full race report (both stacks), before touching anything.
acceptance_criteria: Reliable reproduction captured with both goroutine stacks. Root cause identified as either test-only shared state or a genuine production race, stated explicitly. Fix applied. 'go test -race -count=20' on that package is green.

title: FindCheapestMarketSelling has no positive-price filter: a 0-priced row sorts FIRST, is selected, and the contract evaluation reports maximal profit
description:
ROOT CAUSE behind sp-gef01, deliberately left untouched there because the blast radius is wider than that bead.

FindCheapestMarketSelling orders by purchase_price ASC WITH NO POSITIVE-PRICE PREDICATE. A row holding 0 therefore SORTS FIRST and is selected as the cheapest source. Downstream, the domain calculatePurchaseCost computes purchaseCost += 0 x units, so the contract evaluation SUCCEEDS AND REPORTS THE CONTRACT AS MAXIMALLY PROFITABLE — free goods, pure margin.

sp-gef01 STOPPED THE SPEND (an unpriced lot now refuses to buy) BUT NOT THE BOGUS PROJECTION. The planner will still select that market and still rank the contract as maximally profitable; it just will not execute the buy. So sourcing decisions and profitability rankings are still computed off a price known to be wrong.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN sp-gef01: that query is SHARED with manufacturing and the trade engine, so adding a predicate there has a materially wider blast radius than the contract source-buy path the P1 was scoped to. It deserves its own change and its own review rather than riding along.

CURRENT EXPOSURE IS LATENT, MEASURED: staging holds 39,352 market rows with purchase_price NOT NULL, minimum 3, p01 24, and ZERO non-positive rows. So nothing is firing today. The defect is that nothing PREVENTS it — one bad upstream row, one bad write, or one schema default and the selection flips to a phantom free market.

FIX DIRECTION: a purchase_price > 0 predicate at the query, or an explicit rejection of non-positive prices where the row is adopted. Enumerate every consumer first — contract, manufacturing and trade all share it, and a filter that silently drops rows could starve a caller that currently tolerates them.
acceptance_criteria: A 0-priced or negative-priced market row is never returned as the cheapest source, and a contract evaluation cannot report profit computed from a non-positive unit price. Every consumer of the query is enumerated and checked for starvation before the predicate lands, with a deliberate positive control (insert a 0-priced row, confirm it is not selected).
notes: Split out of sp-gef01 by that lane, which fixed the spend and explicitly declined the root cause as wider-blast-radius. Related: sp-gef01 (the spend guard), sp-ps2oc (the aggregate cap whose projectedCost <= 0 fail-open this feeds).

title: The Postgres advisory-lock branch of the spend reservation is exercised by NO test — cross-process atomicity ships unverified
description:
PRE-EXISTING (sp-w3he shipped it this way), surfaced by the sp-ps2oc review as its one cannot-verify item.

The spend reservation takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(namespace, playerID) to close the READ COMMITTED phantom-read hole where two concurrent inserts each miss the other uncommitted row. That branch is guarded by a dialect check: if tx.Dialector.Name() == "postgres".

NO TEST REACHES IT. NewTestConnection is in-memory SQLite with MaxOpenConns(1), so the postgres branch is DEAD IN EVERY TEST — while PRODUCTION IS POSTGRES. The consequence is that no test in the repo can distinguish a working advisory lock from a DELETED one: the cross-process half of the atomicity argument ships unexercised.

WHY IT IS NOT CURRENTLY A CRISIS: the deployed topology is a SINGLE daemon, and the in-process per-player lock added by sp-ps2oc carries correctness for that case. The advisory lock matters for the multi-process case, which is not the shape running today. That is why the sp-ps2oc review rated it not-a-blocker and not-a-regression.

WHY IT STILL NEEDS CLOSING: MaxOpenConns(1) on SQLite means the test suite also cannot produce genuine connection-level concurrency, so the whole class of cross-connection races is invisible to the current harness. Anyone who later deletes or reorders the advisory lock will see a fully green suite.

FIX DIRECTION: a real Postgres test connection for this repository, or an integration test tier that runs the reservation suite against Postgres. Also worth asserting the dialect branch is TAKEN under Postgres, so the guard cannot be silently skipped by a dialect change.
acceptance_criteria: At least one test executes the pg_advisory_xact_lock path against a real Postgres, and a deliberate positive control (delete or no-op the advisory lock) makes it fail. The dialect branch being taken is itself asserted.
notes: Raised by the sp-ps2oc review as its sole cannot-verify item. It ran no test against staging Postgres and started nothing there.

title: feedGateLeg parks forever on a factory hull that ends a leg with a full hold: it buys BEFORE it feeds and short-circuits at capacity<=0
description:
RESIDUAL WEDGE for the factory role, found during phase 3 task 5 while checking task 7 §4's reasoning. The task-5 scoping decision is UNAFFECTED and correct; this is a separate defect in task 4's file.

MECHANISM: gobot/internal/application/manufacturing/commands/run_construction_coordinator_gate_feed.go:90 short-circuits the leg when the hull's free capacity is <= 0. But feedGateLeg BUYS BEFORE IT FEEDS. So a hull that BEGINS a leg with a full hold NEVER REACHES FeedFactory — it parks. And because the buy is sized to the WHOLE FREE HOLD, a SUCCESSFUL BUY FOLLOWED BY A FAILED FEED leaves the hull exactly in that state: full. Task 4's own comments name the state ('the cargo stays aboard for the next leg' on feed error / Refused).

RESULT: a factory hull whose feed fails once ends the leg full, then parks on every subsequent leg. Nothing empties it. The hull is out of the fleet until a human intervenes.

WHY task 7 §4's STATED reasoning is wrong (its CONCLUSION still stands): §4 justifies task 5's scoping with 'a factory hull full of inputs is recoverable (FeedFactory sells them)'. It is not recoverable by that route, because the capacity guard fires before FeedFactory is called. The scoping conclusion is still right for a different reason — declining the factory role at dispatch would be STRICTLY WORSE: the hull would be permanently invisible AND still never emptied, and it would kill every healthy laden factory hull too.

FIX: feedGateLeg should FEED WHAT IS ALREADY ABOARD when capacity == 0, rather than treating a full hold as nothing-to-do. That inverts the guard from 'no room to buy, so stop' into 'no room to buy, so deliver what you have'.
acceptance_criteria: A factory hull that begins a leg with a full hold of legitimate factory inputs delivers them rather than parking; pinned by a test that starts the hull at zero free capacity and asserts units actually transferred (not merely that no error was returned).
notes: FINAL SHA SET: 450a94b7 / 2fb509e0 / 2570fd7f. 2570fd7f additionally made the full-hold outcome HONEST IN THE LOG: the full_hold_fed INFO line previously claimed 'freeing the hull rather than parking it' UNCONDITIONALLY, including at units==0 — the same action tag for a real recovery and a hull still wedged, in a file whose own doctrine is that the log IS the counter. Zero units now emits a distinct WARNING (action full_hold_fed_nothing). Reviewed separately: BUG FIX SOUND, with the interlock traced end to end — deliverInputs (0,0) -> FeedResult{Units:0, Refused:false} -> completeOrDefer -> deferTask -> next leg re-enters the hold path — and both deliverInputs callers confirmed to run the sp-b27a2 departure guard, so failing closed cannot strand a hull.
close_reason: FIXED on branch gate-factory-phase3 by 450a94b7 (+ 2fb509e0 test). Premise VERIFIED in code first: the capacity guard at L102 precedes the buy (L108) and FeedFactory (L140), and the flush only unloads GATE materials so an input-filled hold frees nothing. FIX: guard INVERTED and MOVED ABOVE planGateFeed, plus new feedGateLegFromHold/planGateFeedFromHold that select the step off THE HULL'S HOLD. Three judgement calls: hold-driven selection rather than neediest-material (otherwise the hull flies somewhere importing nothing it carries and parks politely — the same defect in better clothing); no SOURCE resolution on this path, since an era that exports nothing is precisely when the hull is stuck (this is WHY the check had to move above planGateFeed, which parks on !planned before the hold is considered); ABUNDANT now ORDERS the choice but no longer VETOES it, being a spend guard on a path that spends nothing. NO NEW SPEND PATH — pinned twice plus probe M8. Probe M11 kills on the behaviour: 'a full FACTORY hull was driven through the whole drain and fed 0 factories'. New test TestConstructionDrain_RecoversAFactoryHullFullOfFabricationInputs demonstrates the recovery end-to-end.

title: PlanReallocation: an unroled hull inflates the BaselineMix denominator, and a guard-skipped candidate does not consume the need it was selected for -> role churn
description:
In gobot/internal/domain/manufacturing/gate/reallocation.go, an UNROLED hull (post-b9134020 that means the legacy 'manufacturing' tag and nothing else) sits in the BaselineMix(n) DENOMINATOR but in NEITHER HaveDelivery NOR HaveFactory. That is a standing 1-hull deficit.

PlanReallocation selects the unroled hull to fill it. If that hull is busy, the busy guard skips it — AND A SKIP DOES NOT CONSUME THE NEED IT WAS SELECTED FOR (reallocation.go ~:216-226 continues without touching haveDelivery/haveFactory). The deficit falls through to an already-correctly-roled hull, which chases it; that INVERTS the deficit to the other role, and the next tick the same hull chases it back.

MEASURED (T2Fix, run in the real code both ways, then reverted clean): unpaused and HELD unpaused, stable crew of 2, one unroled hull permanently busy (legacy, mid-haul), one movable roled hull, dwell 1h, per-process ledger stamped on every executed move exactly as the drain would.
  - Symmetric dwell (shipped): 1 move in 8 ticks; ticks 1-7 all {Ship:D-1 Reason:dwell}.
  - Borrow-only dwell: 8 MOVES IN 8 TICKS — D-1 ping-pongs gate-delivery<->gate-factory every tick forever, reason MoveReasonResumeToBaseline each time.
  - Census under BOTH runs: have=1D/0F want=1D/1F, then have=0D/1F want=1D/1F.

CONSEQUENCE: THE DWELL GUARD IS NOT DAMPING A LEGITIMATE OSCILLATION — IT IS MASKING A BROKEN CENSUS. Standing cost is one role-flip per dwell period while any unroled-and-busy hull exists. Bounded by adoption latency (an idle legacy hull gets adopted and leaves the unroled set), so TRANSIENT rather than permanent — which is why it was deferred out of the task-2 fix round rather than fixed there.

FIX (option (c), the principled one): compute BaselineMix over the ROLED CENSUS ONLY, driving adoption from NextRole directly so the phantom deficit stops existing. SEQUENCING IS LOAD-BEARING — re-express adoption FIRST (NextRole-driven, additive unroled->roled, never re-roling an already-correct hull), THEN narrow the denominator. Done in the other order, 4 legacy hulls give BaselineMix(0) -> no deficit -> NOTHING IS EVER ADOPTED.

Cold start must still work: 4 legacy + 0 roled walks NextRole(0,0)->delivery, NextRole(1,0)->factory, ... landing D/F/F/D.

OPEN QUESTION the fix must answer: when the fleet is PAUSED and an unroled hull is adopted, which role does it get? NextRole (D/F/F/D) means the all-factory paused target immediately wants to move it again — one wasted move per adoption, a fresh churn source. Adopting straight to factory agrees with the pause target but means D/F/F/D no longer determines a paused-era adoption. Pin whichever is chosen with a test; 'adopted while paused' currently has no coverage.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) floor the borrow at min(1,n) delivery — leaves the phantom deficit in place and still masked, treats the symptom. (b) a guard-skipped candidate RESERVES its slot — kills the churn at the root but causes head-of-line blocking and silently suppresses move_cap skips for hulls past the reserved deficit, i.e. trades churn for LOST SKIP VISIBILITY, which is the opposite of what this operation is being rebuilt for.
acceptance_criteria: An 8-tick run with a stable crew, one unroled hull permanently busy, and one movable roled hull produces ZERO role flips (not one per dwell period), with the dwell guard removed from the return direction entirely. Legacy adoption still lands D/F/F/D from a 4-legacy/0-roled cold start. 'Adopted while paused' is covered by a test.
notes:
RIDER FROM TASK 2 RE-REVIEW — fix these in the same slice, they live in the file this bead's fix must edit:
(1) reallocation_test.go:584 asserts `if moves > 1`, which A PLANNER EMITTING ZERO MOVES SATISFIES. The test is TestPlanReallocation_TheDwellDampsAnUnreachableBaselineInTheUnpausedDirection — it cannot distinguish 'damped correctly' from 'does nothing at all', which is precisely the bug class this phase kept producing. The 8 ticks were traced: moves == 1 EXACTLY, so `moves != 1` is the available tightening. It is also weaker than its own comment at :583 ('One move...'). NOTE the interaction with this bead: once the census defect is fixed the correct answer may become ZERO moves, so tighten to the value the fixed planner actually produces and re-trace rather than assuming 1.
(2) reallocation_test.go:498 Add(-1) is ONE NANOSECOND but reads like '-1 minute'.

ORIGINAL BEAD CONTEXT UNCHANGED: MUST LAND BEFORE the wiring task that gives PlanReallocation its first production caller — while it has none this is a one-file pure-domain change; afterwards it costs the wiring too. Discovered when T2Fix FALSIFIED an asymmetric-dwell ruling of mine by running it both ways in the real code. Same denominator-inflation shape as the foreign/empty-tag membership bug fixed in b9134020.
close_reason: FIXED ON-BRANCH by 438369b2 (option (c): target computed over the ROLED census, adoption re-expressed from NextRole first) plus 512397b2. Re-reviewed and ACCEPTED. The asymmetric dwell became safe as a consequence and was implemented: post-(c) the same 8-tick repro gives 0 moves in BOTH directions (pre-(c) it was 1 masked / 8 asymmetric). Safety rests on a verified invariant, not the repro — Want sum == have sum == roled holds at every moveTarget call, so needs are exact negatives and only surplus-role hulls are ever selected; adoption is need-NEUTRAL because NextRole keys only on (d+f) mod 4. Real cost was 133 insertions / 48 deletions in one production file plus its test, no exported signature changed. Both rider minors resolved: the 'moves > 1' assertion's test was rewritten (premise gone — (c) made the baseline REACHABLE) and Add(-1) fixed in 1f3b6e39.

title: Era-invariance source guard covers only internal/domain/manufacturing/gate/ — services/ production code is unguarded
description:
The era-invariance source guard in gobot/internal/domain/manufacturing/gate/fill_test.go sweeps filepath.Glob("*.go") RELATIVE TO ITS OWN PACKAGE DIRECTORY. It therefore guards ONLY internal/domain/manufacturing/gate/ against hard-coded waypoint and system symbol literals in production code.

internal/application/manufacturing/services/ has NO equivalent guard, and that is where the gate two-fleet operation's live executor code now lives — production_executor_gate_feed.go (phase 3 task 3, commit ad994771) and the forthcoming feedGateLeg. Those are exactly the files most likely to acquire a hard-coded waypoint, because they resolve real destinations.

Discovered when a phase-3 implementer CORRECTED a standing constraint I had been repeating to every lane ('fill_test.go is a shared conflict point'). It is a conflict point only for tasks touching the gate package.

FIX: extend era-invariance source-guard coverage to internal/application/manufacturing/services/, either by a sibling guard test in that package or by making the existing guard walk a configured set of directories. Phase 3 task 7 is the natural home.
acceptance_criteria: A source guard fails the build when a waypoint or system symbol literal is introduced into production code under internal/application/manufacturing/services/; verified by a deliberate positive control (add a literal, see it fail, remove it).
notes: Goods names are era-invariant and MUST remain allowed — FAB_MATS and ADV_CIRCUITRY exist in every era and are the design's anchor. Only waypoint/system symbols are forbidden. Test fixtures may use literals; the guard is about production code.
close_reason:
FIXED on branch gate-factory-phase3 by 48bc282e (+ 17ae0522). The era-invariance source guard now covers internal/application/manufacturing/services/ AND commands/, not just the gate domain package. POSITIVE CONTROL RUN AND PASSED: a waypoint literal was added, the build FAILED, and it was removed — killed in BOTH packages, with the services one reporting the ../services/ path, which proves the cross-package sweep really reads that directory rather than silently globbing its own. Two BY-DESIGN survivors prove the scope is right: a literal in a _test.go fixture, and era symbols in a COMMENT.
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE THAT MATTERS: the guard scans AST STRING LITERALS, not file text. The originally-specified strings.Contains(src, "X1-") recipe would have FAILED THE BUILD ON THREE PRE-EXISTING HARMLESS DOC COMMENTS in services/ (construction_pipeline_planner.go:115, market_levels.go:51, supply_chain_resolver.go:330, all 'e.g., "X1-FB5-I61"' style) — and a guard that fails on documentation gets deleted within a day. Comment exclusion is itself tested both ways. A follow-up commit made the guard report the WHOLE symbol rather than its first two chunks.

title: Pattern-B regression on the gate delivery floors would pass the spec's liveness test — need a guard the round-trip test cannot give
description:
Raised by the phase-2 plan drafter as a spec objection, upheld by the orchestrator 2026-08-03.

THE SPEC'S GUARD IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. The two-fleet design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-gate-construction-two-fleet-design.md) requires delivery_buy_floor / delivery_resume_floor to be PATTERN C (live provider, re-read per tick, no restart) and pins that with a test asserting a tune survives a daemon restart.

WHY THAT TEST WOULD NOT CATCH THE REAL REGRESSION. A pattern-B mistake would not reintroduce a config key in the same commit. It arrives LATER, as someone tidying the floors into config.yaml alongside the other manufacturing knobs — which is a natural thing to do, since manufacturing IS pattern B. At that point:
  - the domain object still round-trips, so the restart-survival test still PASSES;
  - resolve*Config clears the persisted keys and re-injects from config.yaml on every build, so the live value is CLOBBERED on the next boot.
The operator sets the knob, sees it work, and it silently reverts at the next restart. That is the exact defect class this session opened by deleting (unified_gate_fill, sp-k87tl): a knob that appears to work and does nothing.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY GUARD IT: a test asserting that no resolve*Config path touches these keys. The drafter looked for a clean seam for that and could not find one, and declined to ship a test that looks like coverage without being coverage — the right call, which is why this is a bead rather than a silently weak test.

BEST AVAILABLE MITIGATION (fold into phase 2, not a substitute for this bead): assert the floors are read off the pipeline row ON EVERY LEG rather than cached at handler construction. That per-tick read is what makes the knob live, and a test pinning it fails loudly if someone hoists the read out of the loop.

SEQUENCING: not a phase-2 blocker — phase 2 can ship the knob correctly. This is about keeping it correct. Land it before anyone next touches manufacturing config resolution.

title: WarpSystemCharter.scanWaypointTelemetry WIPES market listings for every marketplace it is not standing at
description:
Found by an independent reachability probe during gate-topology phase 1 verification. LATENT (no live gate impact measured) but it degrades market data fleet-wide, so it is not scoped to construction.

MECHANISM. UpsertMarketData (adapters/persistence/market_repository.go:30-74) is the SOLE writer of market_data and is all-or-nothing per waypoint: DELETE every row for (player, waypoint), then INSERT the full goods slice, in one transaction. If the incoming goods slice is EMPTY, the guard len(goods) > 0 is false, so the rows are deleted and none are inserted — the waypoint ends with ZERO rows.

THE CALLER THAT TRIPS IT. WarpSystemCharter.scanWaypointTelemetry (application/ship/warp_system_charter.go:164-178) calls ScanAndSaveMarket for EVERY marketplace waypoint in a charted system while the hull stands at ONE of them. Market detail (tradeGoods) is only returned for the waypoint the ship is actually at; the others come back empty and are therefore WIPED.

CONSEQUENCE: a charter pass can blank the listings of every marketplace in a system except the one the hull occupies. Downstream readers (FindExportMarket, FindImportMarket, FindAllMarketsInSystem, the new gate feed-destination guard) then see nothing there and treat it as 'no such market' rather than 'not observed lately' — the unknown-is-not-impossible failure mode.

NOTE it produces an EMPTY listing, not a PARTIAL one, so it does not create the export-without-imports state the gate guard would refuse on. That state was measured as non-existent: 4,827 waypoints have EXPORT rows, 0 have exports with neither imports nor exchange.

RELATED RACE (same probe, separate symptom): produceInputsForFactory runs BETWEEN the factory locate (production_executor_fabricate.go:77) and the new feed-destination guard (:125) and can take minutes. A charter wipe of the factory waypoint inside that window flips the guard's destination read to nil and refuses the trip. Narrow; frequency unquantified.

FIX SHAPE: do not upsert a waypoint whose scan returned no detail — skip it rather than writing an empty set. A no-data scan should leave the previous observation in place (stale data beats no data for these readers), or write a freshness marker instead of deleting rows.

title: MarketLocator conflates 'nothing exports this good' with 'market repo is down' — a recursive DAG walk would prune live branches during a transient outage
description:
Found during gate-topology phase 1 review (Task 2), by two independent reviewers.

MarketLocator.FindExportMarket and FindImportMarket both return (nil, error) for BOTH causes:
  - 'nothing in this system exports/imports this good' — a NORMAL planning outcome
  - 'the market repo is down / query failed' — an OUTAGE
They are indistinguishable at the call site: one opaque error, no sentinel.

WHY IT MATTERS. Today every caller refuses on either cause, which is correct and fail-closed, so there is no live defect. It becomes one the moment a caller walks the recipe DAG recursively over these methods: a transient repo failure at one node then reads as 'this good is unavailable this era' and the walk SILENTLY PRUNES A LIVE BRANCH. That is a fail-OPEN outcome built on top of a fail-closed primitive, and it is the classic 'unknown is not impossible' failure — a feasibility filter must reject on POSITIVE evidence (we looked, there is no way), never on absence (we could not look), or it degrades exactly when the system is coldest or most stressed.

EVIDENCE (verified by direct read, not grep):
- FindExportMarket not-found: market_locator.go:163-165 -> (nil, error)
- FindImportMarket not-found: market_locator.go:66-68 -> (nil, error)
- The isShipType detour into findShipyardSellingShip (market_locator_shipyard.go:57) returns (nil, error) on ALL FOUR of its failure paths (yards==nil, repo error, len(shipyards)==0, bestShipyard==nil at :134-136). So FindExportMarket can never return (nil,nil).
- CONTRAST: two SIBLING locators in the same file DO use (nil,nil) for 'absent, not an error' — FindExportMarketWithGoodSupply (:593) and the source-market lookup (:455). So the file already carries two conventions, and neither is pinned by a contract test.

FIX SHAPE: a sentinel (e.g. ErrNoSuchMarket) wrapped at the not-found returns, so callers can errors.Is() to distinguish 'definitively absent' from 'could not determine'. Pair it with a contract test pinning the convention for each exported locator method — the absence of such a test is why two conventions coexist today.

SEQUENCING: must land BEFORE any phase adds a recursive walk over these methods. The gate-construction two-fleet design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-03-gate-construction-two-fleet-design.md) phase 3 adds exactly such a walk (factory fleet feeding the chain recursively), so this is a prerequisite for that phase, not optional cleanup.

NOT FIXED IN PHASE 1: the ambiguity originates in MarketLocator, which phase 1 is constrained not to modify and which has many callers outside gate construction. Deferred deliberately, with a ruling recorded in .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-03-gate-topology-phase1/progress.md.
notes: No spend change and no money-guard impact either way (RULINGS #4 untouched) — this is about distinguishing two failure causes, not about weakening a refusal. Both causes must keep refusing; the point is that the CALLER should be able to tell them apart before it decides to prune.

title: Manufacturing worker starvation guard is fully implemented but wired to NOTHING - delete it or arm it (behaviour decision)
description:
Found during the RPP L1-L4/Mikado tail sweep (epic sp-n2uve). NOT a refactor question - it needs an operational ruling, so engineering did not decide it unilaterally.

EVIDENCE (verified on main dc630e8a):
- internal/domain/manufacturing/reservation_policy.go declares WorkerReservationPolicy +
  NewWorkerReservationPolicy + ShouldAssign, fully implemented, with a live test file
  (reservation_policy_construction_test.go).
- Its stated purpose, verbatim from its own doc: 'prevents task type starvation in
  manufacturing. Without reservation, one task type could monopolize all workers, causing
  deadlock (e.g., all workers doing ACQUIRE_DELIVER, nothing collecting).'
- A module-wide grep for WorkerReservationPolicy / ShouldAssign returns ONLY that file and
  its own test. ZERO production callers.
- The thresholds MinCollectSellWorkers=3 / MinAcquireDeliverWorkers=3 (domain/manufacturing/
  task.go:98-104) are likewise read ONLY by the dead policy. No live allocator consults them.

SO: the manufacturing worker allocator currently has NO task-type starvation protection.
Either (a) the deadlock it guards against is impossible now for another reason and the code
+ constants should be deleted, or (b) it was written and never wired, and manufacturing can
starve one task type today.

Deleting it silently removes the option; wiring it CHANGES BEHAVIOUR on a live money path.
Both are captain/Admiral calls, not a drive-by refactor - hence this bead rather than an edit.

Engineering can execute either outcome once the call is made.
acceptance_criteria: Ruling recorded: delete (with the constants) or wire into the worker allocator with a test proving the starvation case is blocked
close_reason: Operator ruled: delete. WorkerReservationPolicy + TaskTypeAllocations removed with its test in e2221c28. Manufacturing now has NO task-type starvation protection — by decision, not accident. Reversible from git if the deadlock it guarded against reappears.

title: [bug] Parked-sensing probe-yard trait fallback re-offers ALREADY-PRICED yards — buy drain exhausts its candidates with ZERO attempts
description:
The trait fallback in WaypointCatalogPort.ListProbeYards fires when a system holds no
SHIP_PROBE row, which is NOT the same as holding no rows at all. It therefore returned
yards we had ALREADY PRICED and found probe-less, dressed as unexplored candidates. The
buy queue resolved candidates onto them, the listing memo refused every one for free, and
the drain ended its tick with an exhausted candidate list and ZERO attempts.

A yard with ANY stored shipyard_inventory listing has been priced, and if it sold a probe
it would already have been returned by the evidenced branch above the fallback — so "has
rows" is exactly the right disqualifier, read from the same table.

STATUS: a complete 28-line fix EXISTS, uncommitted to main, on branch `probe-resolve`
(HEAD d96c28a4, 2026-07-28, worktree .claude/worktrees/probe-resolve). It was never
tracked by any bead, which is why it was never gated — found during a worktree/bead
reconciliation audit on 2026-08-01.

DOES NOT MERGE AS-IS: main has since reworked the same file (screen_ports.go) with
YardCatalogFrontier + ListWithTraitInOpenEra + a persistence import, so `git merge`
conflicts on exactly this hunk. The fix must be re-applied against current main rather
than merged, and re-verified — the fallback's surroundings have changed shape.

NOT YET VERIFIED against current main: the zero-attempt symptom was diagnosed on the
2026-07-28 tree. Confirm the defect still reproduces before spending a lane on it.
notes:
SUPERSEDED — DO NOT APPLY THE probe-resolve PATCH. Found on re-reading main before dispatching a lane.

main's ListProbeYards has been REWRITTEN since the probe-resolve branch was cut. It no
longer has the either/or structure the patch targets. It now builds a per-waypoint
candidate UNION: every waypoint carrying a probe row, PLUS every charted SHIPYARD-trait
waypoint, deduped, priced-first.

The rewrite's own measurement inverts this bead's premise. From the source: the old
either/or meant one priced yard switched the fallback off for the WHOLE system, and
'81 of 614 charted shipyards were lost that way — a yard nothing can see is a counter we
can never buy at, because buying needs a hull already standing there.'

The probe-resolve patch EXCLUDES already-priced yards from the trait fallback. main
deliberately INCLUDES them. Applying the patch would re-create precisely the invisibility
defect main measured and removed.

The zero-attempt drain symptom this bead describes was diagnosed on the 2026-07-28 tree
and is NOT confirmed against main's union structure. If it recurs it needs re-diagnosis
from scratch, not this patch.

Closing as superseded. The probe-resolve branch is retired.
close_reason: Closed

title: P0: 75% of charted marketplaces are NEVER priced - parked probes cover 1 waypoint per system, so 72% of systems can never form an in-system lane and the fleet cannot spread
description:
## Symptom

The fleet does not spread. 28 completed relocation intents in 24h, ALL 28 targeting
systems already being traded; zero reached new ground. Systems-traded-per-hour flat
over 12h (22,24,30,25,26,31,26,24,24,22,18,25) while the trade fleet grew 41 -> 51 hulls.

## Root cause: we CHART systems thoroughly, then PRICE one waypoint each

Charting a waypoint (it appears in `waypoints` with a MARKETPLACE trait) is not the
same as pricing it (a row in `market_data`). Pricing needs a ship physically at the
waypoint. Sensing does the first exhaustively and the second once per system.

    marketplaces CHARTED        23,788
    ever PRICED                  5,904   (24.8%)
    NEVER priced                17,884   (75.2%)

By system (2,044 systems that have marketplaces):

    0 priced markets   1,040 systems   <- cannot form an in-system lane
    1 priced market      432 systems   <- cannot form an in-system lane
    2+ priced markets    572 systems   <- tradeable

1,472 of 2,044 systems (72%) are structurally incapable of ranking as a trade
candidate. We trade 39 of the 572 that qualify.

## Why that blocks the relocator specifically

`scoreRepositionNeighbors` (run_tour_coordinator_reposition.go:624) pre-ranks every
candidate system by `bestInSystemLane` -> `trading.RankSpreads`, i.e. CappedSpread =
SpreadPerUnit x VolumeCap of the best IN-SYSTEM arbitrage lane. An in-system lane needs
a fresh BUY market and a fresh SELL market in the SAME system. One priced waypoint
cannot be both sides, so the system scores 0 / no-waypoint, never ranks, and no hull
is ever sent there. The loop is self-reinforcing: we price where hulls are, hulls go
where prices exist.

## The lever, proven in our own data

1,037 parked SATELLITEs occupy 649 systems (811 outside the traded footprint). The
hulls are already deployed and already there. Probe count per system vs usability:

    probes  systems  marketplaces EXIST  markets PRICED  % lane-capable
      1       490          13.80             1.11             4.5%
      2       105          16.31             2.55            88.7%
      3        15          12.33             3.20            73.3%
      4        10          15.90             4.80            90.0%

The 1 -> 2 step takes a system from 4.5% to 88.7% lane-capable. 489 of the 490
one-probe systems DO have 2+ real marketplaces, so they are unlockable, not barren.
6,216 unscanned marketplaces sit in one-probe systems alone; 7,916 across all
probe-occupied systems.

## What is NOT the cause (each measured and excluded)

- Hop radius. `defaultRelocatorRegionHopRadius = 2`. 107 untraded systems are already
  inside 2 hops; 74 of them pass candidate generation. Not binding.
- Staleness. The effective cap is NOT 75 min - `listingMaxAge` resolves through
  `marketscan.FreshnessCap` to MaxStaleness = (14,799 x 8) / 0.7 req/s = ~47h (live
  daemon banner: "0.700 req/s ... value clamp 8x"). Only 11 systems within 2 hops are
  stale-rejected. dab3549d is live and working (observed: "licensing TORWIND-349 ->
  X1-QN51 on a STALE snapshot (6h8m0s old, cap 3h0m0s) - accepted deliberately").
- Candidate budget. `relocationRegionCandidateBudget = repositionMaxCandidatesDefault
  = 3`, but only ~6 candidates pass per origin anyway, and new ground reaches the top 3
  for 22 of 38 origins. Not binding.
- Scan budget rate. Spending 0.269 req/s against a 0.700 allowance (38% utilisation).
  The limiter is not the constraint; read OPPORTUNITY is.
- Probes being idle. They are not. Systems WITH a parked probe: p50 freshest market
  2.8h, 596/605 inside the bound. Systems WITHOUT: p50 139.6h, zero inside. Probes
  work perfectly - each just covers one waypoint.

## Proposed fix

Parked probes rotate across their own system's charted MARKETPLACE waypoints instead
of holding one. Zero new hulls, zero new spend - the probes are already stationed. A
system needs only 2 priced markets to become lane-capable, so even a slow 2-position
rotation converts the 432 one-priced systems and opens the 1,040 zero-priced ones.

Note `parkedsensing/expansion.go` already has SEEDS/TOURS that chart a system through
"one waypoint per tick" and then stand the seed down into a single placement. The gap
is between charting and pricing, and it is at the STANDING-DOWN step: once parked, the
probe stops covering the rest of the system it just charted.

Verify with: marketplaces never priced (target: falls from 17,884), and systems with
2+ priced markets (target: rises from 572).
notes:
CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSED FIX (same measurement, different cause).

The design does NOT park one probe per system by choice. sensing_slots already holds
a slot per marketplace waypoint and WANTS them covered:

    WANTED     MARKET   9,255   <- wants a probe, unfunded
    PARKED     MARKET     976
    IN_TRANSIT MARKET      62
    QUEUED     MARKET      19
    PARKED     SPARE        4

So rotation is the wrong fix. The queue is unfunded, not unplanned.

WHY IT IS UNFUNDED. The running PROBE_SENSING_COORDINATOR carries
`expansion_enabled: 2`, and PROBE_BUYER_COORDINATOR is STOPPED. Per its own knob doc
(container_ops_tune.go:141): "probe SPENDING switch: 1=on, 2=off ... OFF BUYS NOTHING:
no probe for a coverage placement (operation_type='sensing coverage'), no charting
seed, no off-gate explorer." Confirmed 2=off is the tri-state convention, matching
sizing_enabled at :100.

The knob doc also promises the free path stays open: "re-tasking idle probes you
already own ... keeps running". There is nothing to re-task — 1,040 satellites, 0 with
assignment_status='AVAILABLE', 976 already PARKED on slots. So with expansion off,
coverage is frozen exactly where it is.

CAUSAL CHAIN, END TO END
  probe buying off -> 9,255 coverage slots stay WANTED -> 75.2% of charted
  marketplaces never priced -> 1,472/2,044 systems have <=1 priced market ->
  bestInSystemLane cannot form a lane -> system never ranks in
  scoreRepositionNeighbors -> relocator has only the 39 traded systems to choose
  between -> hulls shuffle inside the footprint -> no spreading.

This is the operator pause ("paused buying because profits of some hulls are too
thin") reaching further than intended: it was aimed at TRADE HULLS, but
expansion_enabled also gates the probes, and probes are what open the new ground that
would fix thin margins. The two are pulling against each other.

COSTED OPTIONS (treasury 59,589,635; probe avg 52,683 over 1,039 buys in 7d,
min 19,713)

  A. TARGETED, recommended. Fund a SECOND probe only in the 86 probe-occupied systems
     at 1-2 gate hops from the traded footprint -- exactly the ring the relocator can
     already see. ~86 x 52,683 = ~4.5M, 7.6% of treasury. Converts that ring from 4.5%
     to ~88.7% lane-capable and creates relocation candidates adjacent to hulls that
     are already there. Highest credits-per-probe of any option because it targets the
     only systems the relocator can reach today.

  B. Second probe in all 432 one-priced systems: ~22.8M, 38% of treasury. Opens ground
     the relocator's 2-hop radius mostly cannot reach yet, so it would need the radius
     widened too -- more spend, later payoff.

  C. Drain the whole 9,255-slot queue: ~488M. Not fundable.

Option A is the one to take, and it is a config change plus a bounded buy, not a code
change. Re-check after: marketplaces never priced (17,884), systems with 2+ priced
markets (572), and whether relocations start landing on untraded systems.

NOT A CODE DEFECT. Everything measured in the description is the system behaving as
designed with spending switched off. The relocator, the scan budget, the probes and
the freshness cap are all working correctly -- see the exclusions list. Re-triage as
an operator decision unless the Admiral wants the coverage queue to degrade more
visibly when it cannot be funded (today 9,255 WANTED rows sit silent and nothing
reports that coverage is frozen).
MEASURED AND AUTHORIZED 2026-07-31. Depth pays, the placement plan is fine, and the defect is a MECHANISM GAP — sharper than this description.

REVENUE PER PROBE STATIONED, 24h, legs executed in each system over probes parked there:
  1 probe    465 systems / 465 probes / 11 with any leg /   7.5M /  16,128 per probe
  2 probes    95 /190 / 26 with a leg /  71.5M / 376,260
  3-5         20 / 75 /  8 /  64.3M / 857,378
  6+          29 /256 / 29 / 254.9M / 995,885
A probe in a 6+ system earns 62x a lone probe. 47% of parked probes produce 1.9% of revenue.

THE LONE WAYPOINTS ARE NOT QUIETLY CARRYING CROSS-SYSTEM BUSINESS: 11 of 465 (2.4%) appear in ANY executed leg in 24h. Dead weight in both modes, so the 'redistribution is not free because a lone waypoint is still a cross-system leg' caveat does NOT bind. (Cross-system is 74.6% of profit vs intra 25.4%, which argued against depth until this cut settled it.)

REVERSE CAUSALITY RULED OUT — they are not better systems, they are better-covered ones. Lone-probe systems average 14.26 marketplaces and ALL 465 could support depth; the 6+ bucket averages 17.59. Richness differs 1.23x while coverage differs 9x. With sp-o2dzb's controlled replay (same systems, same hulls, 2->4 visible = +82%) the causal case is solid.

THE PLAN ALREADY WANTS DEPTH. WANTED slots: 0-probe systems 4,804; 1-probe systems 3,483 (7.5 each); 2-probe 824; 6+ only 46. planSlots wants ~8 per system nearly everywhere. It is doing its job.

THE MECHANISM GAP, verified in code: filling a MARKET want requires BUYING, and buying is off. The only hull-reuse path is foothold.go, and two guards make it structurally unable to help:
  foothold.go:119 - 'if target.Kind != SlotKindSpare || target.State != SlotStateWanted { return false, nil }' fills SPARE (buying-foothold) wants ONLY, never MARKET wants.
  newSurplusPool (:247+) - pools only parked MARKET slots that are REDUNDANT within their system ('the least valuable redundant market a system holds').
A LONE PROBE HAS NO REDUNDANCY BY CONSTRUCTION, so the 465 hulls in the worst configuration are exactly the set the only redistribution mechanism can never touch. I verified both guards directly.

scoreRepositionNeighbors IS CORRECT. An in-system lane genuinely needs two sides; scoring 0 on a one-market system is honest. The defect is that sensing never creates the second side — the systems hold 14 marketplaces and we price one.

POLICY CALL — I AUTHORIZED THE BUILD RATHER THAN ESCALATING, and this is the reasoning so the Admiral can overrule cleanly. A MARKET->MARKET drain is superficially the footprint-scoping rejected on sp-ntgfj. But that rejection had ONE stated ground: 'Footprint-scoping risks never looking again at a system we stopped trading in', and the SAME note endorsed the alternative: 'A priority queue with an anti-starvation guarantee keeps looking at everything, just at a frequency proportional to value.' The authorized variant IS that design applied to placement rather than scan ordering — source reverts to WANTED (foothold.go's own 'coverage is DEFERRED, not abandoned' precedent) plus a starvation floor. Also material: moving the probe takes those systems from 7% coverage (1 of 14 marketplaces) to 0%, not from sighted to blind, and they carry 2.4% leg participation. RULINGS #20 forbids blocking on an AFK Admiral with a measured 62x lever open.

BINDING CONDITION, in the Admiral's own acceptance language from sp-ntgfj: 'prove the anti-starvation guarantee with a TEST, not an argument.' A test must show a vacated system cannot be starved indefinitely even while richer systems keep outranking it. If it can only be argued, it is not built — that condition is the entire basis on which this was authorized rather than escalated. Also required: ferry cost priced (~8M one-time at 465 x ~3 hops x 5,900 — and note a probe relocation is POST->POST, which may not be the same quantity as ferrycost.go's YARD->POST, so it must be argued not assumed); value-ordered draining; a per-tick cap with a stated reason; and moves attempted/completed/SKIPPED-with-reason counters in the same change, because the existing relocator emits no metric and a coordinator losing every decision looks exactly like an idle one.
AUTHORIZATION RETRACTED 2026-07-31 ~21:15 UTC. My earlier note authorising a MARKET->MARKET redistribution build is WITHDRAWN — I authorised it having read only this bead's DESCRIPTION, not its NOTES, which is the exact failure this repo has burned people on before and which I had twice warned the lane about.

WHY IT IS WRONG. The NOTES establish that the queue is UNFUNDED, not unplanned: sensing_slots already WANTS 9,255 MARKET slots. And the decisive fact I never checked — 1,040 satellites, 0 with assignment_status='AVAILABLE', 976 already PARKED. THERE IS NOTHING TO RE-TASK. Redistribution cannot close a 9,255-slot gap; it relocates the shortage, blinding one system per system it converts. Buying one probe converts a system for ~52,683 with nothing blinded. The NOTES' reasoning dominates mine.

WHAT SURVIVES: the 62x revenue-per-probe gradient, the confound rejection (lone-probe systems average 14.26 marketplaces vs 17.59 in the 6+ bucket — richness differs 1.23x while coverage differs 9x), and the finding that only 11 of 465 lone waypoints appear in ANY executed leg in 24h. That last one kills the 'lone waypoints are quietly carrying the cross-system business' objection. This work does real service: it PRICES the NOTES' Option A, which was argued on coverage alone. Option A's 86 target systems sit at 16,128/probe today against 376,260/probe in the 2-probe regime, a 23x step; even discounted an order of magnitude for the observational confound, payback on ~4.5M is days, with sp-o2dzb's controlled replay (+82% for 2->4 visible, same systems same hulls) as the conservative bound.

THIS IS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT A CODE DEFECT, exactly as the NOTES re-triage it. The root cause is that expansion_enabled=2 gates PROBES as well as trade hulls, so an operator pause aimed at thin TRADE margins also froze coverage — and coverage is what opens the new ground that would fix thin margins. The two are pulling against each other.

STATUS: the Admiral has STOPPED THE DAEMON and instructed no restarts. Both lanes stood down, nothing built, nothing gated. probe-depth clean at 0346650b. No knob was touched — expansion_enabled remains 2. This bead now awaits an operator call on Option A (~4.5M, 7.6% of a 59.6M treasury) and must not be actioned as code.

ONE GENUINE CODE-SHAPED GAP for later, not now: 9,255 WANTED rows sit silent and nothing reports that coverage is frozen — the same shipped-and-unmeasurable pattern as sp-zml2u. Worth a small bead when work resumes.
UNMERGED WORK PRESERVED, DO NOT MERGE. A lane's build crossed with the retraction above and produced a domain core before standing down.

  branch probe-depth @ 037f74c1, worktree .claude/worktrees/probe-depth, clean, NOT gated
  2 new files only: domain/parkedsensing/redistribute.go + redistribute_test.go
  main is UNCHANGED at 0346650b

WHAT IT CONTAINS: SelectRedistribution, a value-ordered priority queue with a wall-clock anti-starvation bound (DefaultStarvationBound 6h). A destination waiting past the bound outranks EVERY value-ordered candidate, oldest first, on any gain including a negative one; the guarantee holds because eligibility grows monotonically with time and cannot be outranked indefinitely by any distribution of values. DefaultMaxMovesPerTick=2 sized for OBSERVABILITY rather than arithmetic; DefaultMinSourceDwell=2h as the anti-thrash partner of the bound.

THE STARVATION CONDITION WAS MET AND PROVEN BY TEST, not argument — the Admiral's own acceptance language from sp-ntgfj. The test is a SIMULATION rather than a comparison because the claim is 'eventually': it runs ticks against two rivals that outrank the poor destination at every tick forever, with the poor destination's gain NEGATIVE so no value ordering could ever pick it, asserts the fixture is genuinely unwinnable on value BEFORE starting, then asserts selection after the bound, within one tick of it, attributed Starved=true.

THREE MUTATIONS, each naming targets. A (override removed) and B (bound ignored, always starved) are a TWO-SIDED proof: A shows the branch is load-bearing, B shows the BOUND gates it rather than the branch firing always — a guarantee that fired immediately would pass A, and B is what catches that cheat. C (dwell guard removed) killed RefusesAHullThatJustArrived.

FERRY QUESTION ANSWERED CORRECTLY: FerryCost yes (post->post is the same physical quantity as yard->post), LandedProbeCost NO (it adds a purchase quote and nothing is bought here) — the lane applied the sp-1ngte lesson to itself rather than reaching for a function because it exists. RedistributionGain subtracts ferry via FerryHops' one-gate floor, so an unwalked cross-system move can never price as free.

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION I FLAGGED AS MOST LIKELY TO FAIL: the guarantee DOES hold under a fixed probe count. It degenerates into a bounded rotation among low-value systems — refilling a starved system drains another, which ages and is itself refilled — i.e. 'keeps looking at everything, just at a frequency proportional to value', with the period bounded by the dwell and the per-tick cap.

NOT BUILT (and the lane correctly refused to ship it inert): QueuedSlot.VacatedAt plumbing (clock should come from sensing_slots.updated_at — durable, re-derivable, survives restart per RULINGS #2); the actuation pass (recommended shape: extend foothold.go by relaxing the :119 Kind==SlotKindSpare early-return and newSurplusPool's redundancy requirement, gated by SelectRedistribution, which reuses its proven reach walker, ledger transitions and dispatch and inherits 'coverage is DEFERRED, not abandoned' — rather than a duplicate sibling broker); and metrics (attempted/completed/skipped-by-reason with Starved as a label, which is why RedistributionChoice.Starved exists).

STATUS: the mechanism is UNWANTED under the current diagnosis — with buying funded (Option A) redistribution is not needed, and with buying off there is nothing to re-task. Preserved only because the starvation primitive is sound and would be expensive to rebuild if a future design wants it.
TRIAGE 2026-08-06: P0 -> P2 LATENT. And the captain's hypothesis that this BINDS EXPANSION was
CHECKED AND DOES NOT HOLD.

Raw numbers look catastrophic — 11,955 marketplaces charted, 29 priced (0.2%), and 1,098 of 1,099
systems with zero priced markets, against the bead's 24.8% / 72%. That reading is an ARTIFACT.

The era-6 fleet is FIVE SHIPS — 3 probes, 1 frigate, 1 light freighter — two days old. This bead's
mechanism is one-probe-per-system PARKING starving lane formation; with 3 probes there is nothing to
distribute. Era 5 had 51 trade hulls and 1,037 parked probes across 649 systems. It is a
MATURE-FLEET phenomenon and cannot express itself at this size.

ON THE 'IS IT A CAUSE OR A CASUALTY' QUESTION (captain asked it be tested, not assumed): it is a
CASUALTY. The fleet has 5 hulls and has made ZERO jumps — there is no relocation being blocked,
because there is nothing to relocate. Fleet size is the binding constraint, not lane formation.

Mechanism intact and unfixed in main (scoreRepositionNeighbors / bestInSystemLane; one bead-sync
chore commit, no fix).

RE-ARM TRIGGER: SELECT count(*) FROM ships WHERE frame_symbol='FRAME_PROBE' past ~50, or ships
spanning 20+ systems — at which point the 1->2 probe step (4.5% -> 88.7% lane-capable) becomes
testable again.

title: probebuy.GuardedProbeBuyer has the same sticker-price affordability defect — latent while PROBE_BUYER_COORDINATOR is stopped
description:
SIBLING OF sp-e46yc (merged as 665af566). Same shape, different coordinator, currently NOT bleeding.

THE DEFECT: probebuy.GuardedProbeBuyer's affordability guard is 'credits - price < ReserveFloor' on the STICKER price. Its DefaultHopPenaltyCredits = 50_000 is documented as 'a SIGNAL only' used for YARD SELECTION — so the path makes its CHOICE hop-aware while its AFFORDABILITY CHECK stays sticker-priced. That is exactly the split sp-e46yc fixed in parkedsensing: knowing distance matters when picking, then forgetting it when deciding whether the purse can take it.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT — measured 2026-07-31:
- The 258-probe / 16.6M overrun that motivated sp-e46yc came through SensingCoverageOperationType (parkedsensing/buyqueue.go:59), the path already fixed, NOT this one.
- Over 48h the only ship-buy lines are 'sensing coverage' (330 buys / 12.5M) and 'fleet expansion' (108 / 83.9M, avg 776k = heavy freighters, not probes). There is no distinct probebuy spend.
- PROBE_BUYER_COORDINATOR is STOPPED.
So this is latent, not live.

MUST BE FIXED BEFORE THAT PATH IS RE-ARMED. A stopped coordinator is one tune away from running, and this guard would then under-price every ferried probe exactly as parkedsensing did.

WHAT TO REUSE: domain/parkedsensing/ferrycost.go already exists and is pure — FerryHops (floored at 1 for a ferried counter with an unresolved hop count), FerryCost (each factor clamped independently), LandedProbeCost (floored at the quote so no malformed input can weaken the guard), DefaultGateFeeCredits=5900. Do not reimplement it; the whole point is one meaning of landed cost.

CONSTRAINTS: this touches a different coordinator's RULINGS #6 guards. Do NOT weaken ReserveFloor or any money guard — adding ferry cost makes the check STRICTER, which is the only acceptable direction. Do NOT reduce probe count as the mechanism (standing warning on sp-ntgfj; an earlier max_probe_fleet cap was reverted for it). Ship armed, no flag.

SIZING GAP TO CLOSE FIRST: nobody has measured this path's actual ferry distances, because it has not run. Either measure them before choosing the hop term, or state plainly that the fleet-mean constant is being used as a conservative stand-in and why that fails safe.

ACCEPTANCE: the affordability guard binds on landed cost; a test proves a probe whose post is many gates from the yard is refused at a treasury that affords the local one; mutation-test it and name the killed tests; prove no guard became more permissive (a local buy must be term-for-term identical to today).
notes: CORRECTION: the follow-up bead is sp-obua8 (doc note on probebuy.Config.ReserveFloor), not sp-9ppqf — that ID was a placeholder written before the bead was created and never existed.
close_reason:
REFUTED — not-a-defect / won't-fix. Real as code SHAPE, but every premise that made it worth fixing fails. Three independent reasons, any one sufficient. I verified the first two directly rather than accepting the negative.

(1) THE GUARD IS UNREACHABLE — the bead's operative claim ('a stopped coordinator is one tune away from running') is FALSE for this path. probebuy.GuardedProbeBuyer has exactly one caller, run_market_freshness_sizer_coordinator.go:969, and that command type is in retiredCommandTypes (adapters/grpc/daemon_server.go:1235, entry at :1246) whose own comment says 'the registry refuses to build them either way'; the refusal is enforced at :1366. frontier_expansion_coordinator, the other probebuy consumer, is retired at :1247 too, and its purchaser adapter expansion.NewProbePurchaser is never constructed. No mediator registration, no command-factory entry. Live DB agrees: zero sizer containers for player 5; the only two that ever existed are player 4 FAILED with exit_reason 'retired_command_type: command type market_freshness_sizer_coordinator retired' and player 3 STOPPED. Re-arming needs CODE — a builder, a registry entry, deletion from retiredCommandTypes — and whoever writes that touches this guard stack anyway. (The two remaining live importers of probebuy, adapters/parkedsensing/ship_ports.go and application/autooutfit/coordinator.go, use only the probebuy.TreasuryReader interface. Nothing touches the buyer.)

(2) EVEN RE-ARMED THE NAMED GUARD IS INERT. floorGate is ReserveFloorGate{Active: cfg.ReserveFloor > 0}, and the sizer builds probebuy.Config{MaxProbeFleet, MaxSpendPerCycle, PurchaseCooldown, SpendWindow} — verified at run_market_freshness_sizer_coordinator.go:569-574, NO ReserveFloor. So Active==false and Holds() never fires; the package doc says so outright ('NO CALLER SETS THIS TODAY ... 0 (the default) DISABLES it'). Adding ferry to 'credits - price < ReserveFloor' would be DOUBLY inert: unreachable call site AND disabled comparison — a build that would have looked successful and shipped nothing. If this path is ever revived, the guards that would actually bind are the 25% treasury rule (price*100 > credits*25, RULINGS #6) and the per-window spend cap. NEITHER IS NAMED BY THIS BEAD; record that for whoever revives it.

(3) IT WOULD PRICE THE WRONG LEG. probeBuyPlan.relay moves an EXISTING IDLE HULL to the counter so the purchase can happen there (relayAndRecheck re-prices at the dock) — the relay is BUYER->YARD. The newly-bought probe reaches its post separately; the sizer's own log says 'landed undedicated, reconciler will relay'. sp-e46yc's LandedProbeCost models YARD->POST for the hull being bought. Applying it here adds a cost for a journey this path's price never covers while ignoring the relay leg it does incur — a DIFFERENT QUANTITY, not a conservative stand-in. Reusing ferrycost.go here (as this bead instructed) would put two meanings of 'landed' behind one name, the opposite of the consolidation that instruction was protecting. The distances also cannot be measured, for the same reason the path is safe: it has never run on this player, so there is no ledger to learn from.

PROVENANCE: the flag came from the sp-e46yc lane, which correctly identified the code shape but had not checked reachability before flagging. Filing this bead on that flag was mine. The lane refused to build and returned the refutation, which is the outcome I asked for — worktree left untouched and clean, nothing gated.

FOLLOW-UP: sp-9ppqf carries the proportionate action — a doc note on probebuy.Config.ReserveFloor, which already exists purely as a trap for the next implementer.

title: Travel is 24.4% of net trading margin in steady state, essentially all tour execution — largest single profit lever
description:
GOAL: more profitable trades. This is the biggest lever measured today and it is currently nobody work.

MEASURED LIVE (player 5, 6h window, verified independently of the lane that surfaced it):
  gross trading margin (TRADING_REVENUE + TRADING_COSTS)   +31,556,215
  jump gate fees (TRAVEL_COSTS)                            -13,918,193
  fuel (FUEL_COSTS)                                         -1,050,346
  travel+fuel as a share of gross                           47.4%
Rate: 394 jumps/hour at a mean 5,888 credits = 2.32M credits/hour spent moving hulls.

Nearly half of every credit the fleet earns trading is spent on transit. Nothing else measured today is close: fill is fine (hulls 80.5% loaded, 32 of 47 at exactly 100%), the solver caps are inert under controls (max_spend byte-identical at x100, REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES worth +0.3%), and the purse binds 0% of allocations across five replays.

THIS NUMBER WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL TODAY. Jump fees were charged by the API, parsed into JumpResult.TotalPrice, and discarded — no ledger type, no consumer (sp-shq63). So every prior analysis of trade profitability, every dashboard, and the solver own objective were blind to it. sp-wtc47 has since priced fees into the solver projected profit and deployed, which is the first-order fix; this bead is about what remains.

WHAT TO DETERMINE, and do not assume the answer is "jump less":
(a) DECOMPOSE the 13.9M. How much is tour execution vs relocation vs scouting vs bootstrap? The lane that surfaced this measured tour travel+fuel at 8.62M (25% of gross) and the remainder as manual travel — relocations and scouting — reaching 14.83M (43%). If a third of the spend is repositioning rather than trading, that is a different bead with a different owner.
(b) Is the fee per jump a CONSTANT or does it vary by route? 5,888 is a mean. If it varies materially by gate pair or distance, route choice can avoid expensive gates specifically rather than avoiding jumps generally.
(c) Now that sp-wtc47 prices fees into the objective, MEASURE WHETHER ROUTING ACTUALLY CHANGED. Jumps/hr read 501 before that deploy and 394 over the 6h since — suggestive but the window straddles the change and the fleet was also growing. Establish it properly before crediting or discrediting the fix.
(d) What is the counterfactual? A tour that jumps less may simply trade less. The relevant metric is margin NET of travel per hull-hour, not jumps avoided. A change that halves jumps and halves revenue is worthless.

CONSTRAINT WORTH KNOWING: max_tour_systems is 2 by Admiral ruling (sp-0hodc replay verdict: cap-4 projects -26.1% vs cap-2, cap-6 -37.9%), so "tour more systems per trip to amortise jumps" has already been measured and REJECTED. Do not re-propose it without new evidence that beats that replay.

ALSO RELEVANT: the ortools sequencer runs on a 3-second WALL-CLOCK budget and the box is currently 2.8-3.2x oversubscribed, so tour plans today are produced by a degraded search. Any before/after routing measurement has that confound in it — within-snapshot comparisons hold, absolute levels do not travel between runs.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not "fewer jumps". It is MARGIN NET OF TRAVEL PER HULL-HOUR, measured over a window long enough to survive the 20-minute buy/sell oscillation (buckets swing -3.9M to +5.6M; use 3h+). Report the decomposition from (a) first — that alone may redirect this bead to a different subsystem.
notes:
RE-ANCHORED 2026-07-31 on the travel-cost lane's decomposition. I verified the arithmetic independently and it reproduces to the credit (41,176,818 net / 8,664,643 fees for 06:00-14:00 UTC).

THE 47.4% HEADLINE WAS INFLATED BY A ONE-TIME EVENT AND IS WITHDRAWN.
Probe placement was 43.4% of travel spend / 18.8% of gross in that window — 258 probes bought today ferrying to post, a ~60x step in probe jumps from 15:00 UTC. That is a transport bill for a fleet expansion, not a routing leak. Split out to sp-e46yc (sensing subsystem).

STEADY STATE, 06:00-14:00 UTC (8h, clean, past the 3h bar):
  net trading margin  41,176,818
  jump fees            8,664,643  (21.0%)
  fuel                 1,372,733
  TRAVEL TOTAL        10,037,376  = 24.4% of net, probes only 2.3% of it
Independent decomposition by container over 12h: tour-run 2,317 jumps / 14,179,643 / avg 6,120; no-container (sensing) 1,239 jumps / 6,785,368 / avg 5,476.

SO: travel is 24.4%, essentially all tour execution. Still the largest single lever and still P0, but half the headline. Any future claim on this bead must use the tour-only steady-state number.

THE FEE MODEL IS SETTLED AND THE SHIPPED COMMENT IS WRONG.
tour_solver.py:270 says 'the real fee is distance-scaled ... a per-pair lookup would fix that'. Measured over 1,625 reconstructed pairs:
  corr(fee, euclidean distance) = 0.124
  variance SD: overall 1,141 / within-destination 344 / within-pair 98 / WITHIN-ORIGIN 67 -> origin explains 99.7%
  decisive: X1-KD64->X1-KY38 = 6,760 vs X1-KY38->X1-KD64 = 5,313. Same edge, 27% apart. Distance is symmetric; the fee is not.
  frame-independent (heavy vs light differ ~1%); across 286 gates range 3,816-11,074, median 5,160.
  origin reconstruction validated: 100% of 2,016 (orig,dest) pairs are real gate_edges rows.
=> The fix is a per-ORIGIN-SYSTEM scalar: 286 numbers, NOT an ~81k per-pair matrix, each learnable from a single observed jump, and 6h of them already sit in the ledger. _build_inter_system_hop_index already keys on (system, system); it needs only a scalar keyed on the DEPARTURE system. Far cheaper than the comment assumes. Correct the comment when this lands.

FLAT-6000 IS WELL-CALIBRATED ON AVERAGE AND BLIND PER CROSSING: tour actual mean 6,236 (bias +236/jump), MAE 948 = 15.2% per crossing, aggregate bias only +286k/6h. So the win is routing quality per decision, not a headline fee reduction — size expectations accordingly.

sp-wtc47 TIMING CORRECTION — MY PREMISE WAS WRONG. It lives in the Python solver, which loads code at process start. Solver PID 59460 started 17:50:24 UTC; the commit is 16:53:41 UTC. It was live ~1h55m at window close, not 6h. The 501->394 jumps/hr movement therefore CANNOT be attributed to it, and that movement is dominated by the probe surge (4/hr -> 270/hr) anyway.
Tour jumps per trading-hull-hour, hourly: 3.48 3.59 3.72 3.83 3.83 3.52 3.75 3.11 3.60 4.38 3.85 4.16 4.24 (last two post-deploy). NO step down; post-deploy sits at the top of the day's range. Not evidence of harm either — the window is confounded (FULL_SCORE_TOP_N armed 100->150 at 17:57 UTC, 7 min in; daemon restarted 19:32 UTC).

DO NOT BUILD THE PER-GATE TABLE YET. Landing a second routing change on top of an unmeasured one destroys both readings. Clean measurement window opens at the 19:32 UTC daemon restart; measure at 22:32 UTC or later.
THE MEASUREMENT, specified so it can just be run: tour-only jumps per trading-hull-hour, and net trading margin net of tour travel per hull-hour, over >=3h with no config change or restart inside the window. Compare against the pre-deploy day range 3.11-4.38 jumps/hull-hr. Confirm no arming/restart happened mid-window before trusting it.

CONSTANT CORRECTION: the live solver runs --tsp-timeout 5 --vrp-timeout 30, NOT the 3-second budget I stated. My 'every tour is planned by a degraded search' concern was based on the wrong constant and is withdrawn. Box load average was 34.7 on 14 cores throughout.

CAVEAT ON ALL OF THE ABOVE: the TRAVEL_COSTS ledger only begins ~04:00 UTC today (sp-shq63), so the 8h steady-state baseline is intra-day and no multi-day history exists to confirm it is typical. The fleet also grew by 5 heavy freighters at 13:00 UTC.
BUILT, NOT GATED, HELD 2026-07-31. The per-origin-gate fee table is complete and waiting on an operator decision — the Admiral cleared the session goal and intends the system halted, so nothing was merged or deployed.

  branch gatefee @ fac31fcc, worktree .claude/worktrees/gatefee, clean, 3 commits on main 0346650b
  16 files, +915/-89. Rebase onto local main is a NO-OP; main has not moved.

WIRED END TO END, not just the solver: ledger row now names origin_system (the jump handler already knew it) -> LedgerGateFeeReader learns {system: mean fee} and caches -> TourConstraints.gate_fees (proto field 13) -> handler bridge -> _make_gate_fee_fn prices the crossing's FIRST hop from the departure gate. Armed at boot in main.go, no flag.

AN INERT LINK WAS CAUGHT MID-BUILD: handlers/tour_handler.py builds the solver's constraints dict field by field and was DROPPING gate_fees on arrival — the table would have crossed the wire and priced nothing. Same dormancy class that made max_tour_systems inert before sp-syaz, and invisible to every solver-level test because those construct the dict themselves. Fixed in 31c5669c with a forwarding test.

THE TWO CONSTANTS RECONCILED, which is the thing that stops 6,000 and 5,900 drifting apart: traffic-weighted mean over JUMPS = 5,917 ('what does the average crossing cost?'); unweighted mean over GATES = 5,424 ('what does an unseen gate cost?'). They differ 9% because traffic concentrates on pricier gates. 6,000 and sp-e46yc's 5,900 are both traffic-weighted means of this same table on different windows — they agree BY CONSTRUCTION, not coincidence. 5,424 is the better estimate for a never-crossed gate and is deliberately NOT adopted: an empty table must stay byte-identical to the pre-table model, and over-charging an unknown gate errs toward not crossing.

MY 'concentrates error on rare gates' PREMISE WAS INVERTED, with numbers. A gate is in the table only if we have flown it, so anything rare is ABSENT and falls back to flat — identical to today. Coverage is traffic-weighted by construction. The residual sits on a few HEAVILY-crossed variable gates: 71.1% of traffic on gates varying <5% about their own mean, 24.2% at 5-15%, and 4.7% (THREE gates) above 15% — worst 43% CV. Traffic-weighted that is ~5% error against the flat charge's 15.2% MAE: a clear aggregate win that is NOT uniformly better.

MULTI-HOP IS DELIBERATELY NOT hops x origin_fee. Only the first hop leaves a gate we can name; the solver sees hop counts, not intermediate systems. So it charges origin_fee + (hops-1) x flat. Multiplying one gate's price across a path would charge the most extreme gate (11,074 vs a 5,424 typical) three times for a 3-hop crossing and be WORSE than flat. Under the standing max_tour_systems=2, tourInterSystemHops returns nil in production and every crossing is exactly 1 hop, so today this reduces to the exact per-origin price — and the multi-hop blend is therefore UNTESTED against live data.

TESTS: Go 84 ok / 0 FAIL, go vet clean, 8 new. pytest 269 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, 14 new. THE 2 FAILURES ARE PRE-EXISTING — I verified them myself on main 0346650b with the service venv, same assertion (11880 == 23880), no lane changes applied. They are sp-wtc47's stale goldens and are now sp-07igx. 6 mutation probes, each naming its target test.

MEASUREMENT NOTE FOR WHOEVER RESUMES: the table is EMPTY until origin_system rows accumulate post-deploy, and an empty table prices exactly as today — so merging cannot retroactively disturb a pre-merge window, but the onset is a RAMP, not a step (it fills as jumps land, taking effect at the first cache refresh), and a before/after boundary drawn at deploy smears over roughly the first hour. Do NOT measure this on fees-per-jump: the fleet pays what the gates charge and per-crossing fee is a property of the map, not of our routing. The signal is margin net of travel per hull-hour over 3h+.
GATED 2026-08-01 at main 907df605 (squash), on operator instruction that the 2026-07-31 halt is no longer in force. The 'BUILT, NOT GATED, HELD' state above is now resolved.

ARMED, not dormant — verified, not assumed: cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:1532 calls
tourCoordinatorHandler.SetGateFeeReader(NewLedgerGateFeeReader(transactionRepo, nil)). This
mattered because tourGateFees() returns nil for an unwired reader and nil prices every
crossing at the flat charge, i.e. byte-identical to pre-table behaviour. No config knob
gates it (no flag, per doctrine).

Pre-merge verification: full go build ./... + go test ./... green across ~107 packages;
go vet clean; protobuf codegen clean (field 13 vs main's field 12 from sp-ircfy, no
collision); routing-service pytest 269 passed vs 255 on pristine main (+14), zero new
failures. The two test_tour_handler failures seen post-merge fail IDENTICALLY on pristine
main and are pre-existing — filed separately as sp-m28ei.

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN. Its ACCEPTANCE is a measured outcome, not a shipped table: margin
NET OF TRAVEL per hull-hour over a 3h+ window. That measurement has NOT been taken and
requires the daemon running. Shipping the intervention is not passing the acceptance.

  907df605 2026-08-01 feat(tour): per-DEPARTURE-GATE jump fee table, threaded Go -> proto -> solver (sp-9idvn)

title: Route the last three Get Agent callers through the ledger treasury reader — they dilute the measured drop
description:
sp-muq66 landed the ledger-backed treasury reader (merged 55c27e8c, deployed) and routed the tour coordinator, trade-route guards, fleet autosizer and contract scaler. THREE trading-side callers were left, each a one-liner now the port exists, and they are the reason the measured Get Agent drop will look smaller than the change actually delivers:

  run_stocker_coordinator.go:1291  — has its own GetAgent mirroring depositCapitalCeiling verbatim
  run_arb_coordinator.go:860
  production_executor.go:692 and :744

Get Agent was measured at 0.165-0.191 req/s = 9-10% of the 2.00 ceiling. Whatever share these three hold survives the sp-muq66 deploy, so the post-deploy number understates the fix until they are routed.

USE THE EXISTING READER. Do not build a second treasury path — that is exactly the "second divergent treasury reader" sp-ovroh warned about and sp-muq66 avoided. The port and its DI wiring already exist in main; this is threading, not design.

CARRY THE CONTRACT UNCHANGED, all three properties:
  - common path reads the ledger, no API call;
  - a ledger older than the 30s bound falls back to the coalesced live read;
  - total failure propagates an ERROR, never a retained value and never 0. RULINGS #4: a failed treasury read must keep failing closed so the caller trades nothing that episode rather than sizing a buy on an unread treasury.

DO NOT route bootstrap_ports.go:253 (cold start has a legitimately empty ledger; reading 0 there deadlocks the fleet) or internal/captain/agentcredits.go (separate process, wake gate not a money guard, retain-last-live semantics are deliberately the opposite of fail-closed). Those exclusions were decided in sp-muq66 and are not up for revisiting.

CHECK EACH CALLER FIRST rather than assuming they are equivalent. The stocker one mirrors depositCapitalCeiling and may have its own failure semantics; production_executor has TWO call sites which may differ from each other. If any of them legitimately needs a live read, say so and leave it — with the reason.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not "the call sites compile". It is that each routed caller makes NO API call on the common path (assert GetAgent call count == 0 with the API client wired carrying a DIFFERENT balance, so a guard that quietly preferred the API still fails), and that total failure still propagates an error. Report measured Get Agent req/s before and after, and the treasury_reads_total{source} split.
