title: 25% of trade legs execute with no plan recorded — 290 of 1,158 legs realize ~63 units each with planned_units=0
description:
FOUND while investigating why hulls run half-full, and it invalidated my own analysis — recording that so nobody repeats it.

MEASURED (player 5, 3h window): 1,158 tour legs realized cargo. 290 of them (25%) have planned_units = 0 AND planned_unit_price NULL-or-zero, while realizing an average of 63 units each. They are real trades with real cargo and no plan behind them in telemetry.

WHY IT MATTERS TWICE OVER.

1. It corrupts any analysis that averages planned vs realized. Averaging those 290 zeros in produced "planned 44 units against 120 available depth, solver uses 36.7%" — a conclusion I acted on and had to withdraw. Restricted to legs that DO carry a plan, the solver is accurate: sells planned 51 / realized 50, buys planned 61 / realized 61, price error 0.0% and 0.8%, and sell outcomes split 252 better / 215 worse than model (unbiased). The planner is fine; the telemetry made it look broken.

2. A quarter of all trading activity is invisible to the planner own accounting. Whatever chooses those 63 units is not the tour solver, or is not reporting through the same path. Until that is known we cannot say what fraction of throughput the solver actually governs, and any future tuning of tranche sizing, decay factors or REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES_PER_VISIT is being fitted on 75% of the data with an unknown bias in the missing quarter.

WHAT TO DETERMINE FIRST, before any fix: are these (a) a distinct execution path that legitimately trades without planning — opportunistic top-ups, contract deliveries, liquidation, arb — or (b) the same tour path failing to persist its plan? Those need opposite responses. (a) is a telemetry gap: stamp the origin so the rows are attributable and exclude them from planner accuracy metrics. (b) is a real defect in plan persistence and means some tours run unplanned.

Do not assume (b) because it is the more alarming reading. Check what container/engine wrote those rows and whether they cluster by ship, by good, by time, or by tour_id.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not "planned_units is populated". It is that every leg with realized cargo is ATTRIBUTABLE to an engine, and that planner-accuracy queries can exclude non-planner legs without hand-filtering on planned_unit_price>0. If some legs legitimately have no plan, they must still say who made them.

Related: tour_leg_telemetry is the table; REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES_PER_VISIT=2.5 and MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES_PER_MARKET_GOOD_SIDE=2 (both Go and Python sides verified in lockstep) are the sizing constants any future fit would touch.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bootstrap has no admission guard: two coordinators can run at once and drain one treasury — the twin branch had one, main does not
description:
SURFACED BY THE twin-digital-twin MERGE (landed as b3c138a4, which tracked 92 twin/ files into main). The branch carried a money guard main has no equivalent of. It was deliberately NOT ported — see the risk below — but it is real and worth building properly.

WHAT IT DOES. activeBootstrapContainerID rejects a "workflow bootstrap" launch when a bootstrap coordinator is already RUNNING, PENDING or INTERRUPTED, and fails closed on a repository error. The branch comment names the hazard exactly: "a RECOVERED coordinator + a fresh one, two brains draining one treasury."

MAIN HAS NOTHING LIKE IT — verified by direct grep across all of gobot/, not merely by identifier: zero hits for activeBootstrapContainerID and no equivalent admission check on the launch path. So today, launching bootstrap while a recovered coordinator is still alive gives two coordinators spending the same credits with no mutual awareness.

PRESERVED, AND IT NEARLY WASNT. The implementation and its 98-line test live at commit 26828a19, which was ORPHANED when the merged branch was deleted — the object existed but was unreachable from main and would have been garbage-collected. It is now held by the tag preserve/bootstrap-admission-guard. Read it with:
    git show preserve/bootstrap-admission-guard:gobot/internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_bootstrap_admission_test.go
DO NOT DELETE THAT TAG until this bead is closed.

WHY IT WAS NOT PORTED WHOLESALE, and what this bead must do first. The guard changes the LAUNCH PATH in the riskiest subsystem in the codebase, and a guard keyed on "a coordinator is active" can make bootstrap UNLAUNCHABLE if a stale INTERRUPTED row lingers — a self-inflicted outage in exactly the machinery that starts the fleet. Before shipping it: ENUMERATE THE REJECTED CLASS AGAINST THE LIVE DB. Count how many bootstrap containers currently sit in RUNNING/PENDING/INTERRUPTED, and how many are genuinely alive versus stale rows nothing reaps. If stale INTERRUPTED rows exist, the guard needs a reaping or staleness rule paired with it, shipped in the same slice — not a follow-up.

That is the same failure shape as sp-rqhzh (a stranded PENDING ship-jump row wedging its hull permanently because nothing reaps a non-terminal container), so assume the stale-row case is real until the count says otherwise.

ACCEPTANCE. The falsifier is not "a second launch is rejected". It is (a) a second launch is rejected while a coordinator is genuinely alive, AND (b) a launch SUCCEEDS when the only thing present is a stale non-terminal row that nothing owns. Build both fixtures; (b) is the one that turns this guard into an outage. Also assert it fails closed on a repository error, which the original does.

Emit a counter for launches rejected, so a guard that starts rejecting everything is visible rather than silent.

title: Get Agent coalescing is unobservable: no counter for flights started vs joined, so a regression to N-calls-per-read looks identical to healthy
description:
FILED BY THE sp-ovroh LANE at the team lead's request, rather than reopening sp-ovroh.

WHAT SHIPPED. sp-ovroh replaced GetAgent's lock-across-the-fetch with true singleflight (adapters/api/client.go): a caller that misses the cache either STARTS the live /my/agent read or JOINS the one already in flight for the same token. N concurrent readers now cost ONE API call, and waiters take no rate-limiter token.

THE GAP. Nothing counts it. There is no metric for flights STARTED vs flights JOINED, so in production a coordinator that has silently regressed to one-API-call-per-reader is indistinguishable from a healthy one — the only external signal is total Get Agent volume, which is dominated by invalidation-driven cold reads and therefore moves for unrelated reasons. This is the 'ship the counter in the same slice as the mitigation' rule, missed.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE. The coalesced reader is the intended FALLBACK PATH for the sp-ovroh ledger-treasury work (blocked on sp-shq63). When the ledger goes stale, every worker falls back to the live read AT THE SAME MOMENT — precisely the burst singleflight exists to collapse. If de-duplication has regressed by then, the fallback amplifies exactly when the fleet is least able to absorb it, and nothing would show it.

SHAPE. Two counters on the existing daemon metrics registry: agent_flight_started_total and agent_flight_joined_total. joined/(started+joined) is the coalescing ratio; a ratio at or near zero under concurrent load is the regression. Cheap — both increments sit on paths that already take agentCacheMu.

FALSIFIER: not 'a metric exists'. It is that with N concurrent cold readers the joined counter reads N-1 and started reads 1; and that removing the join branch drives the ratio to zero rather than leaving the panel flat. Prove it against the existing coalescing tests, which already create that exact condition deterministically via the onAgentFlightJoin seam.

title: Expansion's MinBudgetRate and the sensing clamp floor are the same knob, so ANY braking makes expansion arithmetically unreachable
description:
STRUCTURAL, found while diagnosing why expansion never seeds a system. Not the throughput fix — see the note at the end — but a real correctness defect.

SensingRate = clamp(residual, minScanRate, ceiling) x brake, with the brake applied AFTER the clamp. Expansion then gates on SensingRate >= MinBudgetRate (expansion.go:457-458, returning Skipped: "budget"). And MinBudgetRate is derived from the SAME knob as the clamp floor: run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:1116 sets MinBudgetRate = float64(cfg.MinScanRateMilli)/1000.0, which is exactly minScanRate.

So whenever the residual sits at or below the floor — the normal state under load — the comparison becomes:
    0.1 x brake >= 0.1   <=>   brake >= 1.0
i.e. expansion requires a COMPLETELY UNBRAKED fleet. Any braking at all, however slight, puts it below its own threshold. It is not tuned too tight; it is arithmetically unreachable under any API pressure whatsoever.

Measured live: brake pinned at its hard floor 0.1, SensingRate 0.010 against MinBudgetRate 0.1, and seeds_requested/seeds_claimed/charted all 0 on every tick.

THE YIELD-ORDER INTENT IS CORRECT AND MUST SURVIVE. Expansion is the designated first yielder; SensingRate's sub-floor value exists precisely so deferrable consumers can read it and stand down (see the SensingRate doc comment). The defect is that 'yield first' has become 'never run', because the threshold and the floor are numerically identical by construction rather than by intent.

CANDIDATE SHAPES, to choose and justify: give expansion its own threshold decoupled from min_scan_rate; or express the gate as a fraction of the floor rather than the floor itself; or gate on a brake-independent term. Do NOT gate on PacerRate as a reflex — PacerRate is floored and therefore never pathological, which would make expansion immune to pressure and destroy the yield order this bead is trying to preserve. If you propose it, argue it.

BE HONEST ABOUT THE SIZE OF THE WIN. Fixing this alone lets expansion run at ~0.01 req/s, which seeds almost nothing. The throughput constraint is that the fleet consumes 1.79 of its 2.00 req/s ceiling and non-sensing alone exceeds even the 92% target, so there is no residual to hand back. This is a correctness fix that stops the gate being unreachable; it is not the fix for dark shipyards. Say so in the handback rather than implying otherwise.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is that expansion runs at a partially-braked fleet with the residual at the floor — construct exactly that state in the fixture. A test at brake=1.0 proves nothing, since that is the only case that passes today.

title: [P2, LATENT] bootstrapAcquirer.PriceCheck fans out one live shipyard read per yard in every system holding a ship — currently 3 reads, was 604 pre-reset; regrows with expansion
description:
Found by the sp-lr27k build lane, which correctly declined to fix it inside that lane because it
needs its own money-guard analysis. Independently verified 2026-07-31.

THE FAN-OUT. bootstrap_ports.go:514 bootstrapAcquirer.PriceCheck:
  - builds its system set from EVERY SHIP'S CURRENT LOCATION (:522-527), not from a target
  - for each system, ListBySystemWithTrait(shipyardTrait) (:533)
  - for each yard, priceAtShipyard (:539) -> GetShipyardListingsQuery -> ReadShipyard(Earning)

Earning-class reads SKIP the cached SHIPYARD trait filter, SKIP the rescanTTL floor, and CANNOT be
declined by the budget (shipyard_scanner.go:168-186). So every yard in the loop is an undeniable
live GET /shipyard.

MEASURED SCALE (live DB, player 5, 2026-07-31):
  systems holding a ship .................... 392
  SHIPYARD-trait waypoints in those systems .. 604

So one PriceCheck call fans out to up to 604 undeniable API reads, and the set grows with the
sensing footprint — which is currently expanding fast (364 systems with a parked probe, +102 new
systems in one 6h bucket). This scales with EXPANSION, not with buying.

TWO CALLERS DISCARD THE RESULT ENTIRELY:
  run_bootstrap_reconcile.go:574   _, _, _, _ = h.haulAcquirer.PriceCheck(ctx, cmd.PlayerID, haulerShipType)
Fully discarded, self-documented read-only. Hundreds of undeniable live reads whose output is
thrown away on the floor.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN sp-lr27k. The same method serves three capital-gate callers that spend
against the winning price with NO re-verification. Making it deniable would let a stale/cold price
reach a buy — a RULINGS #4 violation. The fix is not "class it Discretionary"; it is to change
WHERE the spending callers get their price, which is its own analysis.

CONFIRMED CONSEQUENCE: sp-lr27k's commit 2 will NOT bring shipyard reads to the 0.12 budget on its
own. The residual is this. sp-e4dkw's counters make it measurable via the class="earning" slice.

SCOPE (implementer to confirm — this is a hypothesis, not a spec):
  1. Split the read-only callers from the spending callers. The two discarding callers need no live
     read at all — delete the call or serve them from the store.
  2. For the spending callers, narrow the loop: price the yard(s) actually under consideration, not
     every yard in every system that happens to hold a probe. The system set should come from the
     BUY TARGET, not from FindAllByPlayer.
  3. Only then decide the class. Keep every read a money guard consumes undeniable.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - RULINGS #4 — money guards fail closed and may only get STRICTER. Every price a buy path spends
    against stays undeniable and live. This bead must not weaken a guard to reduce a number.
  - ARM IT. No feature flag, no default-off seam (standing Admiral order).
  - Verify with sp-e4dkw's counters before AND after; do not claim a reduction from the endpoint
    rate alone.
  - Mutation probe must NAME its target test.

METHOD NOTE: scope every search to gobot/ or use `git grep <pat> main`. `.claude/worktrees/` sits
under the repo root with 20 checkouts (4.1G); an unscoped `grep -r ... .` reads them as main. This
was confirmed on 2026-07-31 — an identifier absent from main returned 5 hits from a sibling lane.
notes:
CROSS-LINK: this bead ANSWERS the question sp-fbk1q (closed) left open.

sp-fbk1q measured the symptom — Get Shipyard at 21% of all requests, ~3.6x its 0.12 allowance, 97%
of spends classed Earning, 830 overdrafts — and concluded correctly that 'the only lever is HOW MANY
reads are classed Earning', explicitly inviting 'propose reducing the number of yards consulted per
decision instead'.

That is exactly this bead. The volume is bootstrapAcquirer.PriceCheck (bootstrap_ports.go:514)
fanning out to every SHIPYARD-trait waypoint in every system holding a ship — measured 604 yards
across 392 systems — with two callers discarding the result entirely.

It also explains sp-fbk1q's closing observation that '962 Get Shipyard calls produced 5 newly-priced
yards — the exchange rate is poor'. The calls are not discovering yards; they are re-pricing the
same 604 every tick to pick a cheapest.

sp-fbk1q's constraint carries over verbatim and is the reason this is not a one-line reclassify:
DO NOT reclassify a read that feeds a pre-buy or pre-sell guard. Three capital-gate callers spend
against PriceCheck's winning price with no re-verification, so the fix is to narrow WHICH yards are
consulted, not to make the read deniable.
MEASUREMENT NOW AVAILABLE THAT WAS NOT BEFORE — from the sp-fr19d lane (merged b257c956).

The API budget tracker records per ATTEMPT, so PriceCheck's 604 undeniable live shipyard reads land
in Rolling5m.TotalRequests at FULL WEIGHT. Before sp-fr19d they were diluted by a denominator that
counted minutes the observer had never been alive for — up to 13x understatement on a cold daemon,
which is exactly when a bootstrap fan-out like this one fires.

After deploy, Report().Rolling5m.PurposeCounts / PerHull should attribute this fan-out DIRECTLY,
at its true rate. That gives this bead a measurement it has never had: instead of arguing 604 reads
from the call graph, the cost can be read off the tracker and compared against the 2 req/s ceiling.

Worth taking that measurement BEFORE choosing a fix here — the two callers that discard the result
may or may not dominate, and the answer changes whether this is 'stop discarding' or 'stop fanning
out'.
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-06 P0 -> P2 (LATENT, not absent). Measured, not assumed. TWO OF THIS BEAD'S
LOAD-BEARING CLAIMS ARE WRONG and its proposed fix would DELETE EVIDENCE — read this before acting.

=== THE 604 IS DEAD: THE UNIVERSE RESET ON 2026-08-02 ===
This bead measured player 5 on 2026-07-31, PRE-RESET. That footprint no longer exists.
                              bead (era 5)      now
  systems holding a ship          392            1     (verified in BOTH prod and staging DBs)
  SHIPYARD-trait waypoints        604            3
The fan-out is 3 reads per PriceCheck, not 604 — a ~200x drop owing to the reset, not to any fix.

LIVE COST, off the tracker (staging on b257c956, post-sp-fr19d so the figure is no longer diluted):
  Rolling 5m: 0.50 req/s = 25.1% of the 2.0 ceiling. NOT saturated. 150 requests per 5 min total —
  a single 604-read fan-out would have been 4x that entire window.
  Endpoint totals (cumulative, 3047 requests): Get Market 1672 (54.9%) is the DOMINANT consumer;
  Get Shipyard is 235 (7.7%), down from the 21% sp-fbk1q measured in era 5.
BOOTSTRAP_COORDINATOR is RUNNING, so PriceCheck IS firing — it is simply bounded at 3 yards.

=== CORRECTION 1: 'TWO CALLERS DISCARD THE RESULT ENTIRELY' IS WRONG ON BOTH HALVES ===
Only ONE fully discards (reconcile.go:574). The second candidate, run_bootstrap_income.go:162,
reads 'ask, _, _, _ := h.haulAcquirer.PriceCheck(...)' and then USES it at :163 —
'if !pivotWouldHold(obs.Treasury, ask)'. It is a real consumer. VERIFIED in main by direct read.

=== CORRECTION 2: THE 'DISCARDING' CALL IS NOT WASTE — IT WRITES THE STORE ===
PriceCheck calls a.rememberAsk(playerID, shipType, cheapest) at bootstrap_ports_acquire.go:148,
so that call exists FOR ITS SIDE EFFECT: warming the ask that the first-hauler pivot later reads
via lastAsk when the yard is cold. Its own comment says so — 'Take the hauler ask too, so the
first-hauler pivot has evidence to weigh before it ever commits the sole earner.'
THEREFORE THIS BEAD'S FIX #1 ('delete the call or serve them from the store') IS BACKWARDS: it is
one caller, not two, and that call is what WRITES the store. Deleting it removes the pivot's only
cold-yard evidence. Anyone picking this up and following the description literally will break the
first-hauler pivot.

=== WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED NOW ===
This bead's OWN acceptance criterion is currently unsatisfiable: it requires verification with
sp-e4dkw's counters BEFORE and AFTER, and forbids claiming a reduction from the endpoint rate
alone. At 3 yards, going from 3 reads to 1 is invisible inside a 3047-request sample. Changing
three capital-gate spend paths — with RULINGS #4 exposure — to chase a cost that does not
currently exist, while verifying nothing, is the wrong trade.

=== IT IS LATENT, NOT ABSENT — THE MECHANISM IS INTACT ===
FindAllByPlayer -> system set (bootstrap_ports_acquire.go:115-124) is unchanged and scales with
expansion. It WILL regrow.

=== CORRECTED SPEC FOR WHEN IT IS RE-ARMED ===
The fix shape in the code comment is right: RANK ON THE STORE, THEN TAKE ONE LIVE READ AT THE
WINNER. Reads go N -> 1, strictly fewer, no guard weakened, and the price the capital gate spends
against stays live and UNDENIABLE — so nothing that depended on those reads completing changes.
Carry both corrections above: the 'discarding' caller must keep warming rememberAsk (or that
evidence must move somewhere explicit FIRST), and income.go:162 is a consumer.

=== RE-ARM TRIGGER (one query each, and either makes before/after verification meaningful) ===
  SELECT count(DISTINCT system_symbol) FROM ships;     -- climbing past ~20
  or Get Shipyard share climbing back toward 21%.

Credit: measured and re-scoped by the sp-9eor3 lane, which was asked to measure before fixing and
correctly declined to fix. Second time this lane has refused a fix and recommended re-scope
(sp-k76c0 was the first); both refusals were right.
SCOPE CORRECTION to this bead's own re-scope note, raised by the same lane on 2026-08-06.

'The footprint went 392 -> 1' is true of SYSTEMS HOLDING A SHIP — which IS the right quantity for
PriceCheck's fan-out, so the re-scope stands unchanged.

It is NOT true of the CHARTING footprint, which is 1,099 systems in era 6. That distinction was
about to mislead the sp-erdz7 and sp-trf2y triage, and it is recorded here so nobody reads this
bead's '1 system' as a general statement about the era. eras are separable via waypoints.era_id:
era 5 = 114,168 waypoints / 2,460 systems; era 6 = 54,614 waypoints / 1,099 systems.

title: MECHANICS.md still documents the capacity reconciler as a live boot-standing coordinator — the whole stack was deleted (78 files, -16.5k lines)
description:
f861cd7c (sp-y2ptq) deleted the entire capacity-reconciler stack — 78 files, -16,573 lines,
including internal/{domain,adapters,application}/capacity/**. The subsystem does not exist in
main.

MECHANICS.md still documents it as live:
  MECHANICS.md:72   lists "Capacity reconciler" in the BOOT-STANDING table
  MECHANICS.md:276  §6.6 documents it as a live coordinator, with full calibration constants

So the fleet's own reference manual describes a coordinator that was deleted, in the section a
reader consults to learn what runs at boot.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. This is the exact defect sp-mkr1 just fixed in the opposite direction
(stale DEPLOY-INERT comments corrected to BOOT-STANDING, commit 60555e99), and it will mislead the
next reader the same way. Worse, it interacts with a live audit hazard: three separate 2026-07-31
audit verdicts turned on "the subsystem was deleted, so the defect cannot fire" (sp-10nn, sp-cr2v,
sp-32ph). Anyone checking that claim against MECHANICS.md would conclude the opposite and reopen
work that is genuinely moot.

A doc that describes deleted machinery does not merely fail to inform — it actively contradicts the
code for anyone who trusts it, and this repo's own convention is that MECHANICS.md is authoritative.

SCOPE:
  1. Remove "Capacity reconciler" from the boot-standing table (MECHANICS.md:72).
  2. Remove or rewrite §6.6 (MECHANICS.md:276). If the replacement is
     internal/*/contractscaler, say so and point at it — a reader arriving from an old bead needs
     the forwarding address, not silence.
  3. Sweep for the same class rather than fixing these two lines: grep MECHANICS.md for every
     coordinator name and check each against main. f861cd7c and 712b6f66 between them retired
     several subsystems (contract hub, siting, goods factory, capacity reconciler) and this is
     unlikely to be the only stale entry.

METHOD NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: scope every search to gobot/ or use `git grep <pat> main`.
`.claude/worktrees/` sits under the repo root and currently holds 20 checkouts (4.1G); an unscoped
`grep -r ... .` reads them as main and will tell you a deleted symbol still exists. This was
confirmed on 2026-07-31 — an identifier absent from main returned 5 hits from a sibling lane.

Found during the 2026-07-31 bead audit (audit-p2d), out of that batch's scope.

title: [P0] Arming state cannot survive a restart: tune is in-memory only and config.yaml is gitignored — the root cause of the recurring 'closed is not armed' class
description:
Three independently-verified facts compound into one systemic defect: THE FLEET CANNOT
DURABLY REMEMBER THAT A FEATURE IS ARMED.

1. NO TUNE PERSISTENCE (sp-w9zfx, audited OPEN 2026-07-31, audit-p1d).
   Zero hits across all *.go and *.sql for: tune_overrides, TuneOverrideRepository,
   LoadTuneOverrides, SaveTuneOverride, PersistTune, tuneStore. gobot/migrations/ ends at
   048_add_sensing_slot_last_attempt_at with no tunes migration. So `spacetraders tune ...`
   is IN-MEMORY ONLY and every value set that way is LOST ON RESTART.

2. gobot/config.yaml IS GITIGNORED (verified: gobot/.gitignore:82).
   It is where every ARMED/DISARMED annotation lives. So the other arming channel is
   outside version control — unreviewable, un-diffable, and invisible to any audit that
   works from git.

3. A CONFIRMED CASUALTY (sp-u8jc, audited PARTIAL "present but not armed", audit-p1d).
   The cross-system relay is BUILT and production-wired (c2981195, reader at
   cmd/spacetraders-daemon/main.go:1110), but
   run_scout_post_coordinator.go:119 defaultScoutCrossSystemRelayEnabled = 0 and the key
   does NOT appear in config.yaml. It was armed live on 2026-07-22 — and that arm was
   wiped by the next restart, because of (1). Its sibling knob
   defaultHoldUnscannedMarketPosts (run_market_freshness_sizer_coordinator.go:170) is
   also 0.

WHY THIS IS THE ROOT OF A RECURRING CLASS. "Closed is not armed" has bitten this fleet at
least four separate times (sp-fguo 3x, sp-u8jc, and the dark_market_scanner instance found
2026-07-31). Each was treated as an individual oversight. It is not: the SYSTEM has no
durable place to record that a feature is on. A live `tune` survives until restart; a
config.yaml edit survives restart but not a fresh checkout and appears in no diff. There is
no channel that is both durable AND reviewable.

CONSEQUENCE FOR AUDITS: any bead whose resolution is "flip a flag in prod" is
STRUCTURALLY UNVERIFIABLE from git. The 2026-07-31 bead audit hit this directly and had to
downgrade verdicts (sp-0hodc corroborated only by an untracked config read; sp-rlgz ruled
UNCLEAR because deployment state is not determinable from code).

SCOPE:
  1. Durable tune persistence: a table + repository so `tune` survives restart. This is
     sp-w9zfx; this bead is its justification and should not duplicate its implementation.
  2. Decide the arming channel of record and make it ONE thing. Either config.yaml is
     tracked (with secrets extracted elsewhere), or arming moves entirely into persisted
     tunes. Two half-channels is what produces this.
  3. An arming LEDGER that is queryable at runtime: for every armable knob, its default,
     its live value, and where that live value came from. sp-nc0m was meant to be this and
     has decayed into a stale bd note (audited UNCLEAR: size_by_charted_markets,
     scaled_gate_entry, autosizer_early_scaling all now 0 hits in main).

CONSTRAINTS:
  - RULINGS #2: re-derive from durable state each tick, hold nothing cross-tick. A tune
    cache that goes stale against the table would recreate this defect one layer up.
  - RULINGS #5: const defaults stay const. This bead adds a durable OVERRIDE channel; it
    does not move defaults into config.
  - Standing Admiral order is NO NEW FEATURE FLAGS. This bead does not add flags — it makes
    the flags that ALREADY EXIST honest and durable, and it is a prerequisite to deleting
    them (sp-bgv09, the ~53-flag removal sweep).

ACCEPTANCE: set a tune, restart the daemon, and read the value back — it is still set. And
one command lists every armable knob with its live value and provenance.
notes:
PREMISE (1) IS FALSE — VALIDATED 2026-07-31 at the Admiral's instruction. I filed this bead
relaying a subagent's finding without checking it. Corrected:

TUNE DOES PERSIST TO SQL. container_ops_tune.go:322 MutateContainerConfigKey calls
containerRepo.UpdateContainerConfig, whose implementation
(persistence/container_repository.go:124) is a real SQL UPDATE on containers.config. Its own
error string is 'failed to persist tune to container %s config'.

EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION, not just a code read:
  - captain_events type='config.tuned' rows today at 14:30 / 14:39 / 14:42 / 16:03 / 17:21,
    each with new_source='live-config'
  - live RUNNING containers carry tuned knobs in SQL right now: contract_fleet_max_hulls=4,
    idle_arb_leash_radius=150, idle_arb_max_spend=200000, sizing_enabled=2
  - the daemon restarted several times between those tunes and this read; the values are still
    there

WHY THE AUDIT GOT IT WRONG, worth recording because it is a repeatable failure: it searched for
tune_overrides / TuneOverrideRepository / LoadTuneOverrides / SaveTuneOverride / PersistTune /
tuneStore — six spellings of a DEDICATED TUNE TABLE that does not exist — and concluded 'no
persistence'. Tunes live in containers.config, a JSON column on an existing table. Every one of
those greps was correctly empty and the conclusion drawn from them was wrong. An empty search is
unconfirmed, not absent; I relayed it into a P0 without reading the write path.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS NARROWER AND MORE PRECISE. The persistence is scoped to a CONTAINER
ROW, and coordinators are recreated as new rows: player-5 currently has 5 FLEET_AUTOSIZER rows,
3 CONSTRUCTION, 2 PROBE_SENSING, 74 BOOTSTRAP. A tune applied to one row does not carry to its
replacement, which starts from launch config. So the real defect is not 'tunes are not saved' —
it is 'tunes are saved against an EPHEMERAL INSTANCE'. That still produces the observed
'closed is not armed' symptom, and it still means an arm can silently vanish, but the fix is
different: carry tunes across relaunch keyed on (player, container_type, key), rather than
building a persistence layer that already exists.

PREMISE (2) STANDS — config.yaml IS gitignored (.gitignore:82), verified directly by me. The
'no channel that is both durable AND reviewable' argument holds for that half.

PREMISE (3) NEEDS RE-EXAMINATION under the corrected mechanism: sp-u8jc's relay arm may have
been lost to a container RELAUNCH rather than to a restart-with-no-persistence. Different cause,
different fix, same symptom.

DROPPED P0 -> P2: the acute claim was wrong. What remains is real but is a narrower
carry-across-relaunch problem, and sp-w9zfx should be re-read in the same light before anyone
builds a tune store that duplicates containers.config.

title: daemon.log has no rotation and config.yaml's entire logging block is inert, so the log grows unbounded (now ~2.4x faster)
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING sp-qkskz. Two separate findings, one bead.

1. THE logging BLOCK IN config.yaml IS ENTIRELY INERT. Verified by grep across all Go source: no code reads logging.format, logging.output, logging.file_path, or any key under logging.rotation. config.yaml lines ~101-115 declare format: json, output: stdout, rotation.enabled: true, max_size: 100 (MB), max_backups: 3, max_age: 28, compress: true — and not one of them reaches a code path. This matters beyond cosmetics: sp-qkskz's own root-cause hypothesis was 'logging.format: json is set but the sink ignores it', and the truth is that the key is never read at all, so anyone tuning logging from config.yaml is editing a file with no effect and will conclude the setting is broken rather than absent.

2. THERE IS NO ROTATION. daemon.log is produced by launchd redirecting the process's stdout and stderr straight to a file (deploy/launchd/com.spacetraders.daemon.plist.template lines 21-22, StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath). Nothing truncates, rolls or compresses it. The rotation settings in (1) describe an intent that was never implemented, and no lumberjack-style writer exists anywhere in the tree.

VOLUME, MEASURED. container_logs over the last hour: 14,954 rows, of which 12,805 carry a metadata payload; mean message 78 chars, mean metadata 112 chars. That is ~28 MB/day before sp-qkskz. sp-qkskz renders the structured payload onto the same line — deliberately, because every field in the daemon was otherwise unreadable from daemon.log — which adds roughly 12,805 x 113 bytes/hour, i.e. ~35 MB/day, for a new total near 63 MB/day and ~440 MB/week on an unrotated file.

That growth is the correct trade (an unreadable log is worth less than a large one, and the fields were invisible on every container, not just sensing), but it makes the missing rotation materially more urgent than it was.

SUGGESTED FIX. Either honour the rotation block that config.yaml already declares — a lumberjack.Logger wired as the daemon's stdout writer, reading max_size/max_backups/max_age/compress — or delete the whole inert logging block from config.yaml so it stops advertising behaviour that does not exist. Doing neither leaves a file that documents rotation while growing without bound.

DO NOT fix this by making the field rendering conditional or size-capped. Truncation recreates exactly the failure sp-qkskz closed: the one field an operator is hunting is the one dropped (the same reasoning refusalPayload already documents for its own untruncated payload). Rotation is the right layer.

Related: sp-qkskz.

title: Every structured field on the sensing heartbeat is dropped: the log sink renders only the format string and none are exported to Prometheus, so the yard counters are unobservable
description:
FOUND WHILE TRYING TO ANSWER 'is the yard presence pass doing anything?' — and I could not answer it. Not because the pass is broken, but because there is no channel on which its output is visible. This is a PRE-EXISTING blind spot that sp-fox5u and sp-7qhum inherited, not a defect either lane introduced.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED, END TO END.

The counters exist and the code path runs. DispatchYardPresence is called at run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:1027, its report flows into the heartbeat struct at line 1140 (presence: presenceRep), and probe_sensing_heartbeat.go maps them into the payload — 'yards_need_presence': hb.presence.Requested (line 147), 'yard_slots_queued': hb.buy.YardsQueued (line 169), and siblings. The running binary contains the symbols (confirmed with strings on the live daemon binary).

They are emitted ONLY as structured fields — the map[string]interface{} second argument to common.LoggerFromContext(ctx).Log("INFO", ...) in probe_sensing_heartbeat.go ~line 111. The human-readable format string that precedes it does NOT include any of them.

THE SINK DROPS THE ENTIRE PAYLOAD. Measured against the live daemon.log, occurrences of each key: parked_sensing_cycle 0, yards_read 0, probe_cap 0, rotation_slots 0, yard_slots_queued 0, yards_need_presence 0. NOT ONE structured field appears — not even the 'action' key. daemon.log contains only the rendered message: '[ts] [container] INFO: Parked sensing cycle: ... bought 6 reused 0 queued 6 ...'. So this is not specific to the new counters — every structured field on this heartbeat is invisible, including long-standing ones like yards_read and probe_cap.

THEY ARE NOT EXPORTED AS METRICS EITHER. Prometheus is healthy and serving 124,897 metric lines on :9090. The COMPLETE set of sensing/yard/probe metric names exported is four, and none is a yard counter:
  spacetraders_daemon_bootstrap_probes_total
  spacetraders_daemon_parked_sensing_rate_req_per_sec
  spacetraders_daemon_parked_sensing_slots
  spacetraders_daemon_parked_sensing_staleness_seconds

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE OF THE DROP: config.yaml line ~103 sets logging.format: json, but daemon.log is plainly text ('[ts] [container] INFO: msg'). Either that setting is not reaching this sink or this logger ignores it. Confirm before fixing — do not assume, and note config.yaml is gitignored live runtime state so a fix must not depend on editing it.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. Both lanes explicitly designed these counters so that a pass losing every decision would not look identical to an idle one — sp-fox5u split Requested/Dispatched/NoHull/Metered precisely to separate 'backlog with no hull' from 'backlog held by the meter' from 'backlog being worked'. That entire design is currently inert. Live consequence right now: yard pricing sits at 116 priced / 4 heavy of 86, probes ARE being bought again, and I cannot tell whether the relocation pass is dispatching and finding no work or not running at all. That is exactly the distinction the counters were built to make.

SCOPE. Fix the CHANNEL, not just the yard keys. Restoring only the yard counters would leave the identical trap set for every other structured field on this heartbeat and for any future one. Decide deliberately between (a) making the sink render structured fields, and (b) exporting the load-bearing ones as Prometheus metrics alongside the existing four — (b) is what the four existing metrics suggest is the house pattern, and it is what a Grafana panel can actually read. Say which was chosen and why.

ACCEPTANCE. The falsifier is not 'a field appears somewhere'. It is that a NON-ZERO value written by the coordinator is READABLE from outside the process, on a channel an operator would actually look at. Assert it end to end: drive a tick that produces non-zero yards_need_presence and yard_slots_queued, then read those values back from the sink. A test that only checks the map is populated re-creates the exact bug — the map was always populated.

title: Trade Flows: restore market freshness rendering — priced vs dark systems + a 0-12h freshness aura (and the 5th hardcoded 75-min assumption)
description:
ADMIRAL REQUEST 2026-07-30: /trade-flows must show market freshness again — which markets are PRICED
vs DARK, and a freshness AURA scaled 0 to 12h.

WHAT EXISTS. The data path is intact and good:
  GET /api/flows/freshness (visualizer/server/routes/flows.ts:388) returns per-system
  { system, totalListings, freshListings, freshnessPct, freshestAt, scoutPost{status,hull,kind} }
  shaped by server/utils/freshness.ts, era-scoped, with scout-post actuator state derived as
  manned/relay/unmanned. Types live at web/src/types/flows.ts:151. Mocks at web/src/mocks/mockFlows.ts:408.

WHAT IS MISSING. Nothing renders it. web/src/components/flows/FreshnessLayer.tsx was DELETED in the
nebula rewrite and web/src/nebula/ has no freshness module. The endpoint is served and unused.

TWO THINGS TO BUILD

(1) PRICED vs DARK. The endpoint OMITS zero-listing systems (freshness.ts: "Systems with zero
listings are omitted (dark = unsensed) UNLESS they carry a scout post"). So dark systems cannot be
drawn from this response alone — they must come from the difference against /api/flows/topology,
which returns every placeable system. Decide deliberately: either diff client-side, or extend the
endpoint to emit dark systems explicitly. If you extend it, keep the scout-post exception intact —
an actuator marker must render before its first scan lands.

(2) FRESHNESS AURA, 0 to 12h. Scale from `freshestAt` (age = now - freshestAt), NOT from
freshnessPct — pct is a binary share against a fixed cutoff and cannot express a continuous 0-12h
ramp. A system with no freshestAt is dark, not "12h stale"; render those as the dark state, never as
the far end of the ramp.

THE 12h NUMBER IS NOT ARBITRARY, and this matters for what the aura MEANS. sp-k4z5b just made the
solver's freshness cap DERIVED from the live scan rotation rather than a fixed 75 minutes: at the
current 4,389 markets the cap is ~13h56m, at 1,000 markets ~3h10m, at 8,000 ~25h24m. So 12h is
roughly "the current rotation bound", and the honest aura is one whose full-scale tracks that bound
rather than a constant. Prefer reading the bound from the server; a hardcoded 12h will be wrong the
moment the map size moves, which is the exact bug this bead also fixes below.

BUG TO FIX WHILE YOU ARE HERE — THE FIFTH INSTANCE. flows.ts:386 hardcodes
  const STALE_AFTER_MINUTES = 75;
with the comment "mirrors gobot maxListingAge (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:711) — the
solver's number; clients read it from the response, never hardcode it." That claim is now FALSE:
maxListingAge was removed by sp-k4z5b and the solver's effective cap is derived from rotation. This
is the fifth place the 75-minute assumption was baked in; the other four cost ~87% of trade
throughput for 40 minutes today (980 "stale (> 1h15m0s cap)" refusals in 15 minutes). The visualizer
version is not load-bearing for money, but it will paint most of the map red and mislead the reader
into diagnosing a sensing failure that is not happening.

ACCEPTANCE: /trade-flows visibly distinguishes priced from dark systems; a continuous freshness aura
renders from real per-system age with full scale tracking the solver's actual bound (not a hardcoded
75 minutes and not a hardcoded 12h if the bound is readable); a system with no price data renders as
dark rather than as maximally-stale; the scout-post markers still render; and the stale
STALE_AFTER_MINUTES comment is corrected or the constant removed.

caught (a stat panel silently falling through to "no data", a description string overflowing its
column, a numeric-epoch-vs-timestamp comparison that passed raw SQL). Vite dev server is on :5173,

title: release the 5 funded placements whose targets are mapped-and-disconnected — hulls that can never arrive hold a rotation slot forever
description:
## Five funded slots hold hulls that can never arrive, and nothing releases them

sp-1r08q stopped the fleet FUNDING placements in systems no hull can walk to. It deliberately did
not touch the ones already funded, because releasing them changes a money path
(CountOwnedProbes) and putting that beside a filter already altering what gets bought is how a cap
under-count ships unnoticed. This is that follow-up.

## Measured

5 slots (3 BOUGHT + 2 IN_TRANSIT) name a system that is MAPPED and DISCONNECTED — we have read its
gates and they connect nowhere the fleet can reach. Their hulls are bought, assigned, and cannot
arrive. Each consumes a rotation slot and a refusal-budget entry on every placement tick, forever,
and each represents ~59,584 cr of hull sitting idle.

The count is small and the filter stops it growing. This bead is about the standing leak, not a
crisis.

## Ask

Release a slot whose target is mapped-and-disconnected back to WANTED and return its hull to the
idle pool, so the hull can be re-used for a reachable placement.

## The constraint that makes this non-trivial

**CountOwnedProbes counts BOUGHT / IN_TRANSIT / PARKED rows carrying an assigned_ship, and that is
the probe cap's only view of how many hulls the fleet owns.** RULINGS #4: the OVER-count direction
is the safe one, because under-counting authorises re-buying a hull we already own. So a release
must not drop the hull out of that count while it still exists. Concretely: if the release clears
assigned_ship and sets the slot back to WANTED, the hull becomes invisible to the cap and the drain
may buy a replacement for a probe sitting idle in the fleet. Work out where the hull is accounted
for between release and re-adoption, and prove it with a test that asserts the count does not drop.

The orphan-dispatch and adoption passes already re-absorb an unassigned idle probe, so the hull
should not be lost — but "should not" is the thing to verify, not assume.

## Two further constraints

1. **Reachability is TIME-VARYING** (RULINGS #2). A system unreachable now becomes reachable when a
   wall refreshes or a gate finishes construction — and the wall set genuinely churns (179 systems
   stale earlier tonight, 59 now). So the release decision must be re-derived per tick and never
   persisted as a durable "unreachable" verdict, or a transient staleness permanently strands a
   placement it should have kept.
2. **Only mapped-and-disconnected qualifies**, exactly as sp-1r08q rules for funding. An UNMAPPED
   system is unread territory, not an impossible one; releasing on absence of evidence would strand
   placements into genuinely new frontier the moment the crawl lags.

## Not to do

Do not add a durable flag, a retry counter, or a "stranded" state. The condition is derivable from
the graph each tick and must stay that way.
notes:
HANDOVER from the sp-1r08q lane (not taken — declining at end of a long session rather than making a money-path change tired). Three things verified, so the next session need not re-derive them:

1. THE HAZARD IS PRECISE, and it is slot-shaped not hull-shaped. CountOwnedProbes (adapters/persistence/sensing_ledger_repository.go:572) counts SENSING SLOTS: 'WHERE player_id = ? AND state IN (BOUGHT, IN_TRANSIT, PARKED) AND assigned_ship IS NOT NULL'. So the cap's view of a hull IS the slot row that names it. Releasing a slot to WANTED and clearing assigned_ship therefore drops the count by exactly 1 per released slot, and the hull is invisible to the cap until something re-claims it into a counted slot. That is the RULINGS #4 under-count direction — it authorises buying a replacement for a probe we already own.

2. THE SAFETY ARGUMENT IS AN ORDERING ONE, and it looks achievable. There is an existing test named TestOrphanDispatch_RunsBeforeTheDrain_SoAFilledPlacementIsNeverAlsoBought, i.e. the orphan pass already runs BEFORE the drain reads the cap within a tick. So the property to prove is: a released hull is re-absorbed by orphan-dispatch/adoption into a counted slot before the drain's next CountOwnedProbes read. PROVE IT, do not assume it — assert the count never drops across the release+reabsorb sequence, not merely that it recovers eventually.

3. SCOPE MUST MATCH THE FILTER THAT SHIPPED. Only MAPPED-AND-DISCONNECTED qualifies (sp-1r08q): a system we have READ whose gates connect nowhere we stand. A system merely uncharted is UNKNOWN, not stranded, and releasing its hull would fight the cold-start protection. Reuse reachableSystems + GateGraph.Mapped from buyqueue.go rather than re-deriving; it already re-derives per tick and persists nothing, which constraint 3 requires.

Live count at handover: 5 slots (3 BOUGHT + 2 IN_TRANSIT) target mapped-and-disconnected systems. Low value, real hazard — worth doing carefully or not at all.

title: Record the real ship_symbol on PURCHASE_SHIP so hull capex can be joined per hull
description:
Discovered while building the hull payback panels (sp-ovvbv). A PURCHASE_SHIP transaction row
stores metadata->>'ship_symbol' as the ship TYPE ('SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER'), puts the same string in
metadata->>'transaction_id', and leaves related_entity_type / related_entity_id EMPTY. The `ships`
table carries no purchase price and no purchase timestamp either. Net effect: nothing in the
database can say what any individual hull cost or when it was bought.

CONSEQUENCE ALREADY SHIPPED AROUND: the payback panels charge every hull the MEAN PURCHASE_SHIP
price for its frame in the current era, and say so on every panel that uses it. On era 5 that
average sits within -10%/+14% of the true per-hull price, which moves published payback hours by
under 0.8h out of ~7h - tolerable, but it is an approximation the dashboard has to apologise for.
The 'Tenure' column has the same problem in time: it measures from a hull's first trade rather than
its purchase, understating age by the purchase-to-first-trade gap (2 to 75 min on era 5 heavies).

EVIDENCE THAT THE LINK IS RECOVERABLE TODAY BUT NOT SAFELY: hull symbols are AGENT-<hex> assigned
monotonically by the server, so rank-matching hulls (ordered by hex id) against PURCHASE_SHIP rows
(ordered by timestamp) reproduces exact prices and passes three independent checks on era 5 -
equinumerous within each frame class (20 heavies to 20 purchases, 17 light-frame hulls to 17
purchases), strictly monotone id-vs-time, and every hull's first trade postdating its matched
purchase (33/33). It is nonetheless NOT safe to ship: it depends on the counts staying
equinumerous, and a hull lost before it ever trades is unrecoverable from `transactions`, which
silently misaligns EVERY later hull in that frame class by a whole position. That is a worse
failure than a bounded average, so it was deliberately not used.

THE FIX: at purchase time the API response already names the ship it created. Persist it -
metadata->>'ship_symbol' should be the real hull symbol (keep the type under 'ship_type', which is
already populated), and ideally set related_entity_type='ship' / related_entity_id=<hull>. A
purchase timestamp on `ships` would fix Tenure too.

SCOPE NOTE: this only helps hulls bought AFTER the change; historical rows stay unattributable. So
the frame-average path must remain as the fallback for hulls with no recorded symbol, and the
payback panels should prefer an exact per-hull capex when one exists and fall back to the class
average otherwise, labelling which it used per row.

ACCEPTANCE: a PURCHASE_SHIP row for a newly bought hull carries that hull's real symbol; the
payback panels (129-138 in gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json) join it directly
for such hulls and keep the documented frame-average fallback for older ones.
close_reason: Closed

title: farsink staleness ager still assumes flat 1800s/hop after sp-smbgd — conservative, but may still suppress the far sinks affine pricing unlocked
description:
Found by the sp-smbgd lane and deliberately NOT fixed there — correctly, since changing a staleness
bound is money-adjacent calibration, not a comment tweak.

gobot/internal/application/trading/commands/run_tour_coordinator_farsink.go:33 defines
interSystemHopTravel at 30 min/hop and documents itself as mirroring
TOUR_SOLVER_INTER_SYSTEM_TRAVEL_SECONDS (2*GATE_HOP_ALLOWANCE 450 + JUMP_COOLDOWN 900 = 1800),
asserting the staleness ager must not diverge from the solver's price. sp-smbgd retired that
constant: the solver now charges 750 + 650*hops, so the two have diverged and the gap widens with
depth:
    hops   aged at 1800/hop   charged by solver   divergence
      1          1,800              1,400           +400
      3          5,400              2,700         +2,700
      5          9,000              4,000         +5,000

NO MONEY HAZARD — the direction is conservative at every depth: it AGES a far sink by more than the
solver charges to reach it, so it can only discard opportunities, never overcommit. That is why it
was safe to leave.

THE COST IS SUPPRESSED FAR SINKS, which is precisely what sp-smbgd set out to unlock (+21.4% on 3+
hop lanes in replay). A 5-hop sink is treated as 9,000s stale when the crossing now costs 4,000s, so
part of the win the affine model just bought may still be gated behind this ager.

Stale comments to fix in the same pass: farsink.go:33 and
run_tour_coordinator_candidates.go:56 (references "flat INTER_SYSTEM_TRAVEL_SECONDS pricing").

BEFORE CHANGING THE BOUND: it is a freshness/staleness guard, so loosening it admits older price
data into planning. Establish what staleness the tour actually tolerates before matching it to the
new charge — do not simply set it to 750 + 650*hops because that is what the solver charges. The
two quantities answer different questions (how long until this price is untrustworthy vs how long
until we arrive), and they were only ever coincidentally equal.
close_reason: Closed

title: Grafana: add per-hull payback panel + fleet aggregate payback to trading-hulls dashboard
description:
ADMIRAL REQUEST 2026-07-30: add a HULL PAYBACK panel plus AGGREGATE payback data to the
"SpaceTraders - Trading P&L by Hull" dashboard (uid spacetraders-trading-hulls), provisioned from
gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json (3,433 lines, 28 panels, ids 101-128).

Payback = how long a hull takes to earn back its purchase price from realised trading net.

THREE TRAPS. Each will silently produce a plausible-but-wrong number.

(1) PURCHASE PRICE CANNOT BE JOINED TO A HULL. Verified on the live row: a PURCHASE_SHIP
transaction stores metadata->>'ship_symbol' = 'SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER' -- the TYPE, not the hull --
and 'transaction_id' likewise, with related_entity_type/related_entity_id both EMPTY. So there is
no direct capex-to-hull link. Options, pick and DOCUMENT on the panel:
   (a) frame-type average: attribute each hull the mean PURCHASE_SHIP price for its frame_symbol.
       Robust, honest, loses per-hull precision. Prices move (heavies ranged 1.76M-2.11M tonight),
       so state it is an average.
   (b) temporal matching: pair each PURCHASE_SHIP with the hull whose first activity follows it.
       Gives true per-hull cost, but is fragile whenever purchases overlap.
   Do NOT present either as exact. If the panel implies per-hull capex precision it does not have,
   that is the defect. A third option -- record the real ship_symbol at purchase time -- is a
   separate code change and only helps FUTURE hulls; file it separately if you think it is worth it.

(2) PAYBACK MUST IGNORE THE DASHBOARD TIME FILTER. Every existing per-hull panel wraps
$__timeFilter(t.created_at); the dashboard opens at now-12h. Payback is a LIFETIME quantity: it
needs cumulative net since the hull's first trade, over FULL history. If you inherit
$__timeFilter, a hull older than the window silently reports only its last 12h of earnings and
looks unpaid forever, while the number still renders plausibly. This is the highest-risk item.
Consciously decide per panel whether it is windowed or lifetime, and label it in the panel
description so the next reader is not misled.

(3) THE EMPTY-STRING HULL. transactions rows carry metadata->>'ship_symbol' = '' (REFUEL in
particular), so a bare IS NOT NULL admits them and manufactures a phantom blank hull. Existing
panels already guard with COALESCE(t.metadata->>'ship_symbol','') <> '' -- keep that guard.

WHAT TO BUILD

  A. Per-hull payback table: hull, frame, tenure (hours since first trade), attributed capex,
     lifetime realised net, net/hour, payback %, and either hours-to-payback (if paid) or projected
     hours remaining at its own observed rate. Sort worst-remaining first -- the actionable end.
  B. Fleet aggregate: total hull capex, total lifetime realised net, count paid back vs not,
     median and p90 hours-to-payback among those that HAVE paid back (not a mean over censored
     data -- unpaid hulls are right-censored and a mean including them is meaningless).
  C. A payback distribution or cumulative-net-vs-capex-line timeseries, whichever reads better at
     20+ hulls.

Expected magnitude for sanity-checking: a heavy pays back in roughly 7 hours at recent rates
(158k/hull-hr observed against ~1.8M capex). If your panel says minutes or days, it is wrong.

title: Tour solver: replace flat inter-system per-hop charge with fixed+marginal (affine) — flat 1200s/hop over-prices 3-5 hop crossings ~25-30%, suppressing long lanes (e.g. MERITIUM 3-hop)
description: Economy-analyst measurement 2026-07-30, n=632 realized crossings/24h from tour_leg_telemetry (leg-to-leg dt across system changes, joined to gate_edges BFS hop counts, dt filtered 120s-3h): median s/hop by hop-count = 1:1,359 / 2:1,143 / 3:954 / 4:829 / 5:850. Mechanism: the to-gate + from-gate endpoint legs are FIXED cost amortized over the crossing while intermediate gate-to-gate jumps are cheap, so per-hop cost falls with depth — a flat per-hop model (current: TOUR_SOLVER_INTER_SYSTEM_TRAVEL_SECONDS=1200 x hops, sp-kab1c/sp-tp5c3) prices a 3-hop crossing at 3,600s vs ~2,860s realized (+26%) and 4-hop at 4,800 vs ~3,316 (+45%), suppressing long cross-system lanes the sensing expansion just made visible (MERITIUM XC31->AS39, 3 hops, ~450k/load). Affine fit from medians: total(h) ~= 750s + 650s*h (refit from the query in this bead before shipping). Proposal: travel fn charges base + per_hop*hops; keep both env-tunable with the current flat behavior as the default-compatible degenerate case (base=0). Validate via the existing replay harness (widen mode) before/after. Measurement caveat: dt includes arrival-leg dwell — uniform across hop counts, harmless for the shape.
notes:
ORCHESTRATOR RULING + INDEPENDENT REFIT (2026-07-30). Dispatching to a lane.

(1) SHIP IT ARMED. NO FLAG. The proposal's "keep both env-tunable with the current flat behavior as
the default-compatible degenerate case (base=0)" is REJECTED — not on the merits of the model, but
because it is a default-off arm-seam. Standing Admiral order: never add a flag, default-off path, or
arming seam; ship armed. Unproven economics means arm-and-measure-in-prod or do not ship — never
flag. So the affine constants land as the ACTIVE defaults. Keeping the two values env-tunable for
operational retuning is fine; shipping with base=0 so that nothing changes until someone arms it is
not. (I have been corrected on this 3+ times; it is not negotiable and it overrides the §10/replay-
bar instinct that produced this line in the bead.)

(2) MY REFIT AGREES ON SHAPE, DISAGREES ON LEVEL — reconcile before choosing constants. Same source
(tour_leg_telemetry, 24h, dt 120s-3h, leg-to-leg across system changes), BFS depth over era-5
gate_edges, n=627 (bead: n=632, so the same population):

  hops    n     median_total_s   median_s/hop     bead's s/hop
    1   268            987            987            1,359
    2   199          1,743            872            1,143
    3    98          2,237            746              954
    4    28          2,695            674              829
    5    34          3,431            686              850

My medians run ~25-30% BELOW the bead's at every depth. The monotonic decline — the whole mechanism
— reproduces cleanly, so the shape is not in doubt. The level is. Do NOT just take my numbers or the
bead's: refit from the query, and find the discrepancy (candidate causes: arrival-leg dwell handled
differently, a different dt ceiling, or hop depth by direct adjacency vs BFS). Whichever is right,
say which and why on this bead.

Affine fits to MY data:
  weighted by n    total(h) = 430 + 606*h      residuals  -49, +100, -12, -160, -30
  unweighted       total(h) = 467 + 584*h      residuals  -64, +108, +18, -108, +44
  bead's proposal  total(h) = 750 + 650*h

(3) THE CASE IS STRONGER THAN THE BEAD STATES. Current flat model is 1200*h. Against realized:
    1 hop  1,200 vs   987  = +22% over-priced
    2 hop  2,400 vs 1,743  = +38%
    3 hop  3,600 vs 2,237  = +61%   (bead said +26%)
    4 hop  4,800 vs 2,695  = +78%   (bead said +45%)
    5 hop  6,000 vs 3,431  = +75%
Long-lane suppression is worse than the bead's estimate, which raises the value of fixing it and
makes the constants worth getting right rather than approximating.

(4) VALIDATE VIA THE REPLAY HARNESS (widen mode) before/after, as the bead asks. Report the realized
delta on 3+ hop lanes specifically — MERITIUM XC31->AS39 (3 hops, ~450k/load) is the named case.

Code: gobot/services/routing-service/utils/tour_solver.py (INTER_SYSTEM_TRAVEL_SECONDS_ENV_VAR;
tests at services/routing-service/tests/test_tour_solver.py). Python service, not Go.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BUILD LANE RESULT (2026-07-30). Branch affine-hop-travel @ 92ad1080. SHIPS ARMED.

CONSTANTS CHOSEN: total(hops) = 750 + 650*hops, as the ACTIVE module defaults
(no flag, no default-off path). Both terms env-tunable under NEW names
(TOUR_SOLVER_INTER_SYSTEM_TRAVEL_{BASE,PER_HOP}_SECONDS), clamp [300,1800] each.

DISCREPANCY VERDICT: the BEAD's level is right; the orchestrator refit runs ~1 endpoint
leg low. Independent refit (tour_leg_telemetry, 24h, consecutive realized legs across a
system change, dt 120s-3h, BFS over the graph the Go caller actually feeds from — open-era
gate_edges, marker rows excluded, under_construction NOT traversable, per
gategraph.storedDistances):

  hops    1      2      3      4      5      6
  n     191    166    107     44     28     20
  med  1376   2105   2732   3571   3786   4161      => weighted fit 749 + 661*h

That is the bead's 750 + 650*h reproduced to 1s on the base and 11s on the slope. Fit is
stable across windows (12h/24h/48h/72h: base 642-833, per_hop 632-723).

All three candidate causes the notes listed are RULED OUT by direct measurement:
 - arrival-leg dwell: median intra-leg dwell is 0s at every depth; swapping first/last
   timestamps on either side of the pair moves medians <100s (<5%), not 25-30%.
 - dt ceiling: relaxing it RAISES medians (admits long crossings) — it cannot lower them.
 - BFS vs adjacency / era: all-era BFS is byte-identical to era-5 BFS on this population.
   Era-5 pairs are FULLY DISJOINT from era<5 pairs (5244 vs 5068, zero overlap), so the
   dead universe is a disconnected component and forgetting era_id is harmless for DEPTH
   here (it is not harmless for anything that ENUMERATES systems). Including
   under-construction edges moves only the 7-8 hop tail.

The actual signature: orchestrator fit 430 + 606*h vs mine 749 + 661*h — the slope agrees
within 9%, the whole gap is ~320s in the BASE. That is one fixed intra-system endpoint leg
(GATE_HOP_ALLOWANCE_SECONDS = 450), i.e. a measure of the gate-to-gate portion rather than
the market-to-market transition. The SOLVER's charge covers the whole market-to-market
transition — that is exactly why the constant was built as 2*GATE_HOP + JUMP_COOLDOWN — so
the regressand must be market-leg to market-leg dt, and the higher level is the correct one.

MECHANISM, precisely: the two named allowances always described an affine cost. The flat
model multiplied BOTH by hop count, re-charging the to-gate/from-gate legs on every hop.
base ~ 2*GATE_HOP_ALLOWANCE (endpoint legs, paid once), per_hop ~ JUMP_COOLDOWN (the jump).

vs the flat 1200/hop that was LIVE: 1 hop 1200->1400 (the flat charge was 13% UNDER-priced
there, so near-lane ping-ponging gets DEARER — this is not a blanket cheapening), 2 hop
2400->2050, 3 hop 3600->2700, 4 hop 4800->3350, 5 hop 6000->4000.

So it is mostly a REPRICING of the same plans, with genuine re-selection onto deeper lanes
in ~2% of cases.

title: [bug] Container liveness data lies twice: ctx-cancel exits leave rows non-terminal, and the heartbeat goroutine outlives an unrecoverable error (FAILED rows carry heartbeat_at 25min AFTER stopped_at)
description:
Found by the sp-h8mbb lane while root-causing orphaned containers. NOT touched there. This is a SECOND,
INDEPENDENT source of misleading liveness data, and it has already corrupted one analysis.

TWO DEFECTS, same area:

1. The runner's ctx-cancel exits (container_runner.go:471-477, 502-507, 576-581) release the hull WITHOUT
   persisting a terminal status. The container row is left non-terminal even though the runner is gone.

2. The heartbeat goroutine is NOT STOPPED on the unrecoverable-error path. Consequence: FAILED rows in
   the DB carry heartbeat_at LATER than stopped_at. Live example: tour-run-TORWIND-61-22653242 stopped
   04:26:29, heartbeat 04:51:54 — 25 minutes of heartbeats after the container was dead.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: any analysis that infers hull-hours or utilisation from container
RUNNING state or from heartbeat freshness is reading ghosts. This already misled one investigation on
this project into reporting hull idleness that did not exist (sp-srhs2, closed refuted — its 183
idle-hull-hours figure was partly built on exactly this). sp-h8mbb fixed the claim-break orphans; these
two paths still produce non-terminal rows and post-mortem heartbeats by a different route.

ASK: persist a terminal status on the ctx-cancel exit paths, and stop the heartbeat goroutine on the
unrecoverable-error path so heartbeat_at can never post-date stopped_at. Then check whether any
consumer (dashboards, the captain's detectors, utilisation queries) treats a non-terminal row or a fresh
heartbeat as proof of life — those consumers are the actual hazard, not the rows.

Ship ARMED, no flag. No money guard involved. Guard note: do not make a container's liveness depend on
the heartbeat alone — the fix is to stop lying, not to add a second inference.
notes:
MERGED to main as 0a237a4f (gate green, rebased onto 74fc56a1 first). DEPLOYED via restart-daemon;
24 containers recovered healthy.

HALF THE ASK WAS REFUSED, CORRECTLY, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE MOST VALUABLE PART. I asked for a terminal
status to be persisted on the ctx-cancel exit paths. That is CONTRARY TO A SHIPPED INVARIANT and would
have broken every restart. TestExecute_CtxCanceledMidIteration_ExitsResumableNotCompleted already
requires that branch to leave the row in {RUNNING, INTERRUPTED}. Mechanism: interruptAllContainers
cancels every runner's ctx, sleeps 1s, then writes INTERRUPTED ONLY IF containerEntity.Status() ==
RUNNING. Had the ctx-cancel exit terminalized, every container would flip terminal inside that 1s window,
interruptAllContainers would skip them all, and terminal rows sit OUTSIDE the INTERRUPTED + RUNNING
recovery set — so EVERY CONTAINER WOULD BE DROPPED AT EVERY DAEMON RESTART. sp-ovkn regression class,
RULINGS #2.

That path also produces NO lying rows: ctx is cancelled only by Stop() (writes STOPPED) and
interruptAllContainers (writes INTERRUPTED), so the canceller is always the last writer, and the DB shows
zero stale non-terminal rows attributable to it. ALL 17 LYING ROWS CAME FROM DEFECT 2 ALONE — 16 FAILED +
1 RUNNING, every one a "command execution failed:" row from execute's unrecoverable-error branch. Worst
overhang 2h39m40s (tour-run-TORWIND-41-e13a3217: stopped 23:49:50, still beating at 02:29:30).
COMPLETED and STOPPED rows were already clean because finishCleanExit and Stop both stop the heartbeat
before their status write. A test (TestResumableStopExit_DoesNotTerminalizeTheRow) now pins the resumable
exit staying non-terminal, so if anyone revisits this ask the answer is in the suite, not in a message.

THE FIX: stopHeartbeat() runs at the top of persistFailed rather than at one call site, so every
terminal-FAILED writer inherits it. Idempotent (sync.Once), so finishCleanExit's veto path is unchanged.
The ordering guarantee comes from stopHeartbeat WAITING for the goroutine to return — an in-flight
heartbeat write completes before the status write, so heartbeat_at <= stopped_at HOLDS rather than the
leak merely getting shorter. On the 2s-timeout path that is best-effort and the code says so rather than
claiming an absolute invariant. Nothing infers liveness from a beat; the runner simply stops emitting a
signal it knows to be false. Also fixed a latency bug found en route: stopHeartbeat waited the full 2s on
heartbeatDone even when the heartbeat was never armed (Start's claim-failure exit, and every test driving
execute directly) — now short-circuits.

MUTATIONS: 4 targets, TWO INITIALLY SURVIVED and were then pinned.
 M1 persistFailed drops stopHeartbeat (the shipped defect) -> FAIL first run
 M2 stopHeartbeat signals but never waits -> SURVIVED, then pinned by
    TestStopHeartbeat_WaitsForTheGoroutineToActuallyExit. The commit CLAIMED the wait established the
    ordering and nothing tested it.
 M3 drop the unarmed short-circuit -> FAIL
 M4 Start never arms heartbeatStarted -> SURVIVED, and worse: the arm flag is LOAD-BEARING IN PRODUCTION
    (unarmed, every real container's terminal path skips the wait) and deleting it killed NO TEST IN THE
    ENTIRE PACKAGE. Now pinned by TestStart_ArmsTheHeartbeat.
Chain now holds end to end: Start arms it -> armed means stopHeartbeat waits -> waiting means a beat
cannot post-date the status write.

CONSUMER AUDIT — NOTHING PROGRAMMATIC WAS MISLED, and the blast radius was narrower than I assumed. Every
consumer of heartbeat_at or container liveness filters on status: detectStaleHeartbeats
(captain/detectors.go:253, PROTECTED, not modified) filters status='RUNNING' so it never saw the FAILED
corpses — and it uses a STALE beat as a death signal, the safe direction, since a leaked beat can only
SUPPRESS a death alarm, never fabricate one. FindActiveCoordinatorByType orders by heartbeat_at DESC (the
one place a fresh corpse could have won a selection) but filters status IN (PENDING, RUNNING).
FindStaleManufacturingWorkers / StopStaleManufacturingWorkers both filter RUNNING. The visualizer
(contract-ops.ts, bot.ts, ContractCard.tsx's liveness dot) filters RUNNING or IN
('RUNNING','STOPPING','STARTED'). THE STATUS FILTER SAVED EVERY PROGRAMMATIC CONSUMER. What the lie
actually corrupted was DIRECT ROW INSPECTION — humans reading the table, and any analysis deriving
hull-hours or liveness from container state, which is exactly what produced the phantom 7.7x spread in
sp-5yrv4.

MY DISPATCH RATIONALE WAS ALSO WRONG: I dispatched this as "fix the substrate before the 8-heavy
re-measurement depends on it". The lane notes the fix does NOT change the method it would use — it will
still derive activity from transaction timestamps over a common wall-clock window, because container
state is the wrong denominator EVEN WHEN HONEST (it cannot see idle-but-assigned time, and the
accrual/open-position correction matters more than the liveness lie ever did). The fix is worth having as
a trap removed for the next reader of those rows; it does not make container-derived hull-hours
trustworthy and was not a prerequisite.

LEFT OUT: detectStaleHeartbeats' unbounded IN_TRANSIT exemption (sp-75fbq) — PROTECTED PATH, reported not
touched. Genuine hole: a hull stuck IN_TRANSIT forever is exempt from stale detection indefinitely and
nothing else would catch it.

title: [bug] Two freshness tables for one pipeline: the system shortlist scorer still uses the flat 75-min maxListingAge while BuildTourSnapshot uses activity-conditioned RankerAgeCaps — 76 sink-goods snapshot-usable but invisible to system selection (sp-4ki1x pattern repeating)
description:
Found by the sp-4mpxh diagnosis lane. Small but real, and it is the sp-4ki1x pattern repeating: TWO
freshness tables governing one pipeline.

THE DEFECT: the flat 75-minute maxListingAge is RETIRED for the tour snapshot — BuildTourSnapshot uses
activity-conditioned RankerAgeCaps (WEAK 480m / RESTRICTED 180m / GROWING 60m / STRONG 30m; unknown
falls back to RESTRICTED). But the SYSTEM shortlist scorer was never migrated and still applies the flat
75 minutes: shortlistByProfitableEdge -> freshListings(rows, now, maxListingAge) at
gobot/internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:851.

EFFECT (measured, era 5, player 5): 76 sink-goods (3.3% of the fresh universe) are SNAPSHOT-USABLE but
INVISIBLE TO SYSTEM SELECTION — the solver would accept them, but the system that contains them is never
shortlisted. They skew DEEP: median trade_volume 180 versus 120 for the rest.

SIZE IT HONESTLY BEFORE BUILDING: 3.3% is small, and the sp-4mpxh lane measured that deep sinks are
LOW-margin (corr(trade_volume, margin) = -0.39; the tv 120-164 band is worth 64,242/visit against
195,776 for the tv 60-112 optimum). So the 76 hidden sink-goods skewing deep may be worth LESS per visit
than what the planner already picks, not more. Do not assume recovering them is a gain — quantify
value/visit for those specific 76 before changing anything. The fix may be correct on consistency
grounds while being worth ~nothing on revenue, and that is a fine outcome to report.

THE REAL ARGUMENT FOR FIXING IT is consistency, not revenue: one pipeline should not carry two
freshness policies. The sp-4ki1x incident was exactly this shape — a flat cutoff silently nullifying an
activity-fitted table — and it cost us 81.5% of the discovered market universe before it was found.
A second divergence of the same kind is a latent repeat.

ASK: migrate the system shortlist scorer to the same activity-conditioned RankerAgeCaps the snapshot
uses, so there is ONE freshness policy. Reuse the existing table — do NOT redeclare it (that redeclaration
is precisely how sp-4ki1x happened). Report the measured revenue effect separately from the consistency
argument.

Ship ARMED, no flag. No money guard involved.

title: 7.7x net-margin spread across physically identical light haulers (141.8k vs 18.5k per hull-hour) — part is zombie-container measurement artifact, the rest is unexplained
description:
Found by the sp-bjrsm margin decomposition. Worth ~1.25x on net throughput if the tail can be lifted to
the median — no capital required.

MEASURED (24h, net margin per hull-hour, fuel excluded because REFUEL rows carry an empty ship_symbol —
~4% of margin, does not move the ranking): light haulers median ~99k/hull-hour, range 18.5k to 141.8k.
That is a 7.7x SPREAD ACROSS PHYSICALLY IDENTICAL HULLS — same frame, same 80-unit capacity, same fleet,
same era, all at 92-100% utilisation. Extremes: TORWIND-40 at 141.8k/hh vs TORWIND-D7 at 18.5k/hh.

PART OF THE TAIL IS MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, NOT REAL: TORWIND-D7 and TORWIND-61 are the two hulls with
zombie tour containers from sp-h8mbb (containers stuck RUNNING 2.9h and 4.0h after the hull was
reassigned). Hull-hours computed from container RUNNING state are inflated for exactly those two, which
depresses their credits-per-hull-hour. FIX sp-h8mbb FIRST or at minimum recompute this metric from
transaction timestamps rather than container state — otherwise the investigation chases a phantom.

But the artifact does not explain the whole distribution, and the middle of the range has no zombie
excuse. Candidate explanations to separate: lane assignment luck (which sinks a hull happened to win
under contention — see sp-ircfy), home-system placement and reposition reach, hold fill variation
(median 50% with p25 at 25%), or a genuine per-hull defect.

ASK: recompute per-hull net margin per hull-hour from a zombie-immune basis, then explain the residual
spread. If it is lane-assignment luck under sink contention, it is sp-ircfy's to fix and this bead closes
into it. If it is per-hull, find the hull-level cause.

Do not weaken any guard. Ship ARMED, no flag.
notes:
CLOSED — REFUTED. No real spread survives correct measurement. Diagnosis only, nothing committed.
Sixth premise refuted by measurement today.

THE SPREAD COLLAPSES AS EACH CORRUPTION IS REMOVED:
  original (container-RUNNING hull-hours, cash basis) .... 7.7x
  zombie-immune denominator, cash ........................ 2.29x
  + open-position corrected (accrual) .................... 1.95x

TWO corruptions were present, not one:
 1. DENOMINATOR (known): container-RUNNING hull-hours inflated for D7 and 61 — confirmed, sp-h8mbb.
 2. NUMERATOR (new, bites harder): per-window CASH margin is distorted by OPEN POSITIONS at the window
    boundary. TORWIND-5F bought 80 MERITIUM for -719,680 four minutes before the window closed; its
    apparent margin of 814 credits was almost entirely an unsold position, not bad trading. Correcting
    to inventory-at-cost moved 5F from 13th to 9th. This is a GENERAL flaw in per-window cash margin,
    independent of the zombie bug, and it will corrupt any future per-hull analysis done this way.

1.95x IS NOT A HULL PROPERTY:
 - Split-half Spearman rho = +0.176 (R^2 = 0.031 — first-half rank explains 3% of second-half rank). On
   the CASH basis it was -0.176: THE SIGN FLIPS WITH THE ACCOUNTING BASIS, which alone says there is no
   stable ordering. Non-adjacent thirds rho = -0.110. At n=13, significance needs |rho| ~ 0.56.
 - THE KILLER STATISTIC: a single hull varies against ITSELF by up to 2.27x between consecutive 8.5h
   windows (TORWIND-61: 721k -> 1,636k; D7: 464k -> 975k). WITHIN-HULL TEMPORAL VARIATION EXCEEDS THE
   1.95x SPREAD ACROSS ALL 13 HULLS. There is no hull effect to find.
 - TORWIND-61, one of the two hulls that motivated this bead, is 6th of 13 — ABOVE MEDIAN. Its "worst
   hull" status was entirely the zombie artifact. D7 is genuinely last but has a 2.10x self-ratio and
   moved 13th -> 10th between halves; it sits inside the noise.

METHOD NOTE — WHY TRANSACTION-TIMESTAMP CLUSTERING WAS REFUSED: the inter-transaction gap distribution is
smooth out to 135 minutes with NO natural break, because a legitimate multi-hop leg with jump cooldowns
produces hour-long silences indistinguishable from parking. Any session threshold would have manufactured
its own answer. A common wall-clock window was used instead (2026-07-28 22:00 -> 07-29 15:00, 17h, the
span where all 13 lights are present) — it touches no container state, no heartbeat_at and no status
column, so sp-b79f1's other liveness lies cannot reach it, and against a THROUGHPUT goal idle time is a
real cost rather than something to divide out. Also: tenure varies 3.5x (TORWIND-6 has 60.5h of trading,
D6/D7/D8 only ~17h), so raw lifetime margin is not comparable across these hulls at all.

RESIDUAL IS TIME-VARYING LANE LUCK, NOT HULL IDENTITY: units sold varies 1.63x (1232-2006), spread per
unit varies 1.67x (882-1476), and the two PARTIALLY OFFSET — TORWIND-40 moves the most units on a
middling spread, TORWIND-C the fewest on the best spread. No hull is systematically starved or favoured.
"Lift the bottom half to median" HAS NO TARGET: there is no stable bottom half, membership reshuffles
every 8.5 hours. The ~1.25x that modelling promised is not available from hull-level intervention.

HOLD FILL CORRECTED — AND THIS CORRECTS MY OWN REPEATED ERROR: lot sizes averaging 35-48 units against an
80 hold LOOK like a fleet-wide shortfall but are not — consecutive same-waypoint buys COMBINE INTO ONE
LOAD (observed: 5F buying 2x40 MICROPROCESSORS eight seconds apart). Measuring actual LOADING EVENTS:
64.9/80 units = 81.1% FILL, with 55.3% of loads completely full. That is healthy. Roughly 19% headroom,
real but ordinary — NOT the ~1.9x a naive read suggests. My earlier 50%-fill figure (from grouping buys by
container+waypoint, i.e. dock visits) was wrong and this is the third correction to it.

CROSS-CHECK: fleet tour net computes to 1,945,572/hr on this pipeline, consistent with the independent
~1.89M/hr 6-hour baseline. Two different methods agree.

WHERE THE 10M/HR GAP IS NOT: hull variance, hold fill, cycle time, idleness, sink selection, buy-side
chaining, or the sell depth cap. All seven measured and eliminated. The live constraint is source pool
depth (~64 units/good/visit) -> sp-kep8p.
