title: No credits-denominated realised-vs-planned tour metric: re-plan logging double-counts and liquidation inverts it — emit one per-tour completion line (blocks sp-ircfy's own honesty guard)
description:
Cheap, permanent fix for a measurement gap that has now blocked one investigation outright.

THE GAP: there is no way to compute realised-vs-planned tour profit in CREDITS from the logs. The
sp-bjrsm lane tried and had to abandon the metric, reporting honestly that both available aggregates are
artifacts:
  - naive aggregate says completed tours realise 32.9% of projected — but it DOUBLE-COUNTS, because every
    absorption breach forces a re-plan and every plan gets logged (223 breaches in 8h across 66 containers)
  - restricting to single-plan tours INVERTS to 255% (n=9), because `projected profit` blends fresh
    profit with held-cargo liquidation
Neither number is quotable. That matters because realised-vs-planned divergence is the HONESTY GUARD in
sp-ircfy's own validation plan (tour_plan_rate{phase=projected|realized} must not worsen when the
externality term arms) — so we are about to arm a change whose primary safety metric we cannot compute
cleanly.

ASK: emit ONE line at tour completion — "Tour completed: realised N vs planned N" — carrying, per tour
(not per plan): the final realised net credits, the ORIGINAL plan's projected net credits, the number of
re-plans, and a flag for whether held-cargo liquidation contributed. The per-tour identity and the
re-plan count are what make it immune to the double-count; separating liquidation is what stops the
255% inversion.

Emit it for every terminal outcome, not just success — a tour that exits honestly having traded nothing
is a realised value of 0 against its plan, and that is exactly the case the current logs hide.

Small, self-contained, no guard touched. Ship ARMED, no flag. Worth doing BEFORE or ALONGSIDE sp-ircfy so
the anti-herd arming has a trustworthy honesty guard.

title: TradeHasWork counts TRADE_FLEET_COORDINATOR — a launcher that spends nothing and is always RUNNING — so trade reads as constant-true and construction can never reach 100% of capital
description:
Found by the sp-bzvu2 lane while fixing the construction side of the capital sensor. Deliberately NOT
fixed there, for a stated reason — see the risk below.

THE FALSE POSITIVE: tradeCapitalContainerTypes includes TRADE_FLEET_COORDINATOR, which is a LAUNCHER that
spends nothing (no purchase call sites in its command file) and is always RUNNING while the daemon is up.
So TradeHasWork is effectively constant-true, and construction can never reach 100% of deployable capital
even with the entire trade fleet down.

WHY THE MIRROR IS NOT THE SAME BUG AS sp-bzvu2: construction has a COMPLETION CONDITION — its bill fills
and the engine goes quiet while still ticking, which is what made liveness a lie there. Trade has no
completion condition; a TRADING worker re-plans and buys every tick and is never "done", so liveness IS
demand and there is no bill to read. The fix here is therefore NOT "read a bill" — it is to stop counting
a non-spending launcher as a spender.

WHY THE LANE DID NOT JUST DO IT (respect this): it could not cheaply verify the boot/launch window. If
the coordinator is RUNNING before the first TRADING container row exists, dropping the coordinator from
the sensed set would report trade IDLE and hand construction 100% of deployable capital at exactly the
moment the trade fleet is starting up. Shipping armed with no flag, that is not a change to make on an
unverified assumption about launch ordering.

ASK: confirm that TRADING workers are persisted (at least PENDING) BEFORE the trade fleet coordinator
reports ready. If they are, drop TRADE_FLEET_COORDINATOR from tradeCapitalContainerTypes so the sensed set
contains only containers that actually spend. If they are not, fix the ordering first or leave it alone
and record why. Prove the boot window explicitly — that is the whole risk.

IMPACT TODAY IS ZERO (construction currently has no demand, so nothing is being denied), which is why
this is P2 and not urgent. It becomes real the moment a construction pipeline goes EXECUTING again.

Do not weaken any money guard (RULINGS #4). Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: [bug] Zombie tour containers stay RUNNING for hours after their hull is reassigned (4.0h and 2.9h observed) — only reaped by the restart recovery sweep; corrupts utilisation metrics and may hold phantom MaxConcurrentTours slots
description:
Found by the sp-srhs2 lane. Live, and it corrupts the utilisation metrics we reason about.

MEASURED: tour-run-TORWIND-61-f0c2c82f sat in status RUNNING for 4.0 HOURS and tour-run-TORWIND-D7-
f8033506 for 2.9 HOURS while the trade coordinator had already relaunched those same hulls into NEW
containers. Both were reaped at the SAME INSTANT (2026-07-29 04:52:37) by a single recovery sweep, each
failing with `recovery_failed: ship <hull> is already assigned to container <newer-container>`.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:
 1. Metrics corruption — these are why two hulls measured at OVER 100% utilisation. Any hull-hour analysis
    that trusts container RUNNING state is reading phantoms. This directly misled a prior investigation.
 2. Possible slot exhaustion — a phantom RUNNING tour may consume a MaxConcurrentTours slot, silently
    capping how many real tours can fly. VERIFY whether it does before assuming; if it does, this is a
    throughput bug and not merely a metrics one, and should be re-prioritised upward.

Note both zombies were only cleared by a recovery sweep that ran at daemon restart. Between restarts they
appear to persist indefinitely, so uptime makes this worse, not better.

ASK: establish why a tour container stays RUNNING after its hull has been reassigned, and have the
coordinator (or the assignment layer) reap or fail it at reassignment time rather than waiting for a
restart sweep. Confirm the MaxConcurrentTours question either way and state the answer explicitly.

A `zombie-workflow` agent has been active in this repo — CHECK FOR OVERLAP before building, and say so if
this is already covered rather than duplicating the work.

Ship ARMED, no flag. Do not weaken the assignment/claim guards (RULINGS #4/#7) — the reassignment that
orphans these containers is itself correct.
notes:
MERGED to main as 51ab4541 (gate green: full suite, Merged=true, EmptyMerge=false). DEPLOYED
2026-07-29 ~15:20 UTC via restart-daemon; 24 containers recovered healthy.

MaxConcurrentTours QUESTION ANSWERED — NO, a phantom container does NOT consume a slot. Verified by
direct read, not inference: run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:497 computes
runningTours := len(running) - watchdogKilled + watchdogRelaunched, the ONLY input to the cap check at
:543; `running` comes from partitionTradeFleet(ships) at :754 which iterates SHIPS, appending a hull once
if ship.IsAssigned(); ship assignment is single-valued (one container_id column, row-locked by ClaimShip)
so a reassigned hull points at its NEW container and is counted exactly once. Grepping the trading
package for any container-counting cap returned ZERO hits. So the zombie is counted zero times, not once.
This is METRICS CORRUPTION, NOT A THROUGHPUT BUG — do not re-prioritise on the slot-exhaustion theory.
Secondary: max_concurrent_tours is unset in every config file, so the cap is 0 = unlimited today anyway.

ROOT CAUSE — WORSE THAN THE BEAD ASSUMED, AND IT IS A DOUBLE-SPEND. The containers were NOT abandoned
rows: heartbeat_at was 20s before the reap and their own logs show them GENUINELY FLYING THE HULLS the
whole time — jumping, refuelling, buying and SELLING REAL CARGO. tour-run-TORWIND-61-f0c2c82f logged
"Tour leg 1: sold 33 EQUIPMENT (revenue 113817)" at 03:15, well after it had lost the hull. So we had TWO
LIVE CONTAINERS ON ONE HULL, BOTH SPENDING MONEY.

Trigger recorded verbatim in the coordinator log: "Relaunched continuous tour for trade hull TORWIND-61
(prior exit: fleet unassign (sp-w3yd)...)". ReleaseContainerClaim atomically severs the hull's live
work-claim — correctly — but NOTHING STOPS THE CONTAINER THAT WAS FLYING THAT HULL. It keeps iterating on
a hull it no longer owns; the coordinator reads ownership from the hull's single assignment row, cannot
see it, and launches a second container onto the same hull. Nothing reconciles them until the next
restart's recovery sweep fails the orphan — hence 4.0h and 2.9h, and hence UPTIME MAKES IT WORSE.
Timeline: fleet unassign ~03:26:09 -> 3m cooldown -> coordinator relaunches both hulls 03:29:24 -> old
containers keep running until the 04:52:37 restart. (Daemon restarts were 02:29:47 and 04:52:37, NOT
03:29 — that misreading is what suggested a "restart race".)

NOTE FOR THE OPERATOR (me): `fleet unassign` is one of the four defective call sites, and I ran it on
TORWIND-D7 and TORWIND-61 earlier in this session. I caused the two zombies that were then measured.

FOUR CALL SITES, ALL FIXED: fleet unassign, ship reserve --force (PreemptForCaptain), depot
re-dedication, depot eviction.

THE FIX: ReleaseContainerClaim now returns the container id it revoked (mirroring PreemptForCaptain),
read INSIDE THE SAME ROW LOCK as the write — no TOCTOU. Every claim-severing path hands that id to a new
daemon seam ReapOrphanedContainer: a live runner is stopped via the normal StopContainer path; a row
whose runner is already gone is terminalized STOPPED, outside the set boot recovery re-adopts. No guard
weakened (RULINGS #4/#7) — the reassignment stands, only the loser is cleaned up. Verified that stopping
the orphan CANNOT touch the hull's new owner: releaseShipAssignments looks up by the OLD container_id
(already cleared, returns nothing) AND its CAS closure re-checks sh.ContainerID() != thisContainer on the
fresh row. Two independent barriers.

8/8 MUTATIONS KILLED, each naming its target. M8 is worth keeping: GORM's Updates writes its map back
onto the model, so reading model.ContainerID AFTER the Updates is a NIL-POINTER PANIC inside a row-locked
transaction — the capture-before-write ordering is load-bearing and the test catches it.
..._ReapedOrphanIsNotReadoptedByRecovery is the symptom test: it runs the real RecoverRunningContainers
and asserts the reaped orphan is untouched while an UN-REAPED CONTROL in the same sweep gets the exact
recovery_failed outcome from the incident.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT — no runner self-check (a general backstop where the runner verifies between
iterations that it still owns its hull). Correctly declined: it changes behaviour for every container
type, ships ARMED with no flag, and "positive evidence the claim is gone" is subtler than it looks
(jump_ship transiently reassigns a hull to a ship-jump-<sym> container). Killing healthy containers is a
far worse failure than a metrics phantom. Filed separately.

OVERLAP CHECK INCONCLUSIVE: the lane messaged zombie-workflow for scope and got no reply before
finishing. It grepped main independently — no existing coverage of the claim-break -> orphan path, and
all four call sites were unguarded — so duplication is unlikely, but direct confirmation never arrived.
COVERAGE GAP CLOSED — second merge d88b845b. My gate on 51ab4541 ran while the lane's worktree was DIRTY (mid-mutation-probe, which necessarily leaves the tree briefly uncommitted) and swept two RULINGS #7 regression tests. Nothing shipped was wrong — 51ab4541 is complete and correct — but the coverage was lost. Verified lost by grepping both main's working tree and the committed tree for staleIndexShipRepo (0 hits each), then re-landed exactly in a fresh worktree and gated as d88b845b; verified present after merge (7 hits). OPERATOR LESSON, mine: ALWAYS 'git -C <worktree> status --short' and confirm empty BEFORE gating. The captain-gate-commit-first hazard is not only about the lane committing — the ORCHESTRATOR must check, because a lane running mutation probes is legitimately dirty for seconds at a time and cannot avoid it. WHAT THE RECOVERED TESTS PIN: reaping at reassignment time makes the release/re-claim race TIGHTER than the restart sweep it replaces, so the guard preventing a late reap from yanking a hull off its NEW owner needs explicit coverage. The subtlety: TWO barriers protect it and the production one HIDES the other — the claim break already cleared the hull's container_id, so releaseShipAssignments' FindByContainer returns empty and the CAS re-check is never consulted. A fixture built on the production shape would PASS WHILE PROVING NOTHING (the bound-tests-need-demand-past-the-bound trap). staleIndexShipRepo is adversarial on purpose: it hands the stale container's hull back from FindByContainer even though the hull has moved on, leaving the CAS closure's same-container re-check as the only thing standing. Uses the exact production shape (TORWIND-61 held by f0c2c82f, re-claimed by 2821d983). Mutation M9 (drop the sh.ContainerID() != r.containerEntity.ID() re-check): TestReapedOrphansReleaseNeverTakesTheHullFromItsNewOwner FAILS, TestReapedOrphanStillReleasesAHullItGenuinelyHolds PASSES. That split is the point — the guard is load-bearing AND does not over-fire; an orphan that genuinely still holds its hull must still release it, or the reap would leak the very claim it exists to clean up.
close_reason: Closed

title: No feedback from trading to sensing: a 'no-cached-market' reposition rejection dies in a Prometheus counter — the one moment we know exactly which system needs scanning, we discard it (cost ~35 hull-hours; 2 systems are one stale tick from recurrence)
description:
Found by the sp-srhs2 lane while diagnosing no-trade tour exits. Scoped to SENSING deliberately.

THE GAP: there is no feedback from trading to sensing. When a tour cannot reposition because a candidate
system has no cached market data, that rejection dead-ends in a Prometheus counter (reposition.go:249).
Verified two ways: `grep sensing` and `grep parkedsensing` across internal/application/trading both return
ZERO non-test files. The one moment we know PRECISELY which systems need scanning, we throw it away.

WHAT IT COST: a bootstrap deadlock on 2026-07-28 06:38->13:46 UTC. Five hulls (TORWIND-6/9/A/B/C) sat in
X1-KP23, a market-dead system whose five gated neighbours had never been scanned. scoreRepositionNeighbors
(run_tour_coordinator_reposition.go:646) requires cached market data for a system to become a reposition
candidate, so the hulls could not leave and nothing in the trading path went to get that data. ~50 tours
each, 251 identical `no-cached-market` rejections across all five neighbours, ~35 hull-hours. It resolved
BY LUCK — probe-sensing bought probes at 13:07 and the first market row for a neighbour (X1-AJ10) landed
13:42:32, freeing the last stuck tours at 13:38-13:46.

RECURRENCE IS LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Rejection has a second reason, `stale-data`, at a 75-minute cap
(maxListingAge). Counting only neighbours with data fresher than 75 minutes: X1-UN60 has 1 of 2 fresh,
X1-QC9 has 1 of 3. Both are one stale tick from re-entering the identical trap.

ASK: turn a `no-cached-market` (and `stale-data`) reposition rejection into a SCAN DEMAND on the
parkedsensing target queue — the trading side already knows the exact waypoint/system it needs and why.
Scope the change to the sensing subsystem's intake; do not reach back into the tour executor.

EXPLICITLY DO NOT: increase the relaunch backoff. The adaptive backoff (sp-1pli) is deliberately capped at
600s and run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go:54 records that a previous lane tried longer sleeps and it cost
~238 hull-hours/day of pure parking. That path is known-bad and already reverted.

COORDINATION: several lanes commit in the sensing subsystem (sensing-expansion-gate, parkedsensing work).
Check for in-flight overlap before starting. Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: [bug] parked_sensing_gate_walk_unroutable fires 207x/12h with a ZERO jump bound — 'no gate route within 0 JUMPS', structurally unsatisfiable, retried 50+ times per hull
description:
Surfaced by the sp-k7hez investigation lane, not acted on there.

MEASURED: parked_sensing_gate_walk_unroutable fired 207 times in 12 hours with the message
"no gate route could be named within 0 JUMPS of stored adjacency".

A ZERO bound. The walk is being asked to find a gate route within 0 jumps, which can only ever succeed
if origin and destination are the same system — so it is structurally guaranteed to fail and then be
retried. Hulls TORWIND-E6, TORWIND-EE and TORWIND-FD were held and retried 54, 52 and 50 times
respectively.

This is a bounded-retry loop burning API budget and holding probes idle. Establish where the bound is
computed and why it resolves to 0 (an unset/defaulted budget, a decremented counter reaching zero, or a
genuine "no hops available" that is being mis-rendered as a bound). Fix the bound, and make the failure
report the honest reason — a structurally impossible request should not be retried 54 times.

Not a money path. Ship ARMED, no flag.
notes:
RE-SCOPED 2026-07-31 (orchestrator, verified by direct read on main d3d15c89).

THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE. It was filed on a misread log line.

  ship_ports.go:578   const maxWalkRings = appSensing.SeedFlightUnbounded
  expansion.go:1149   'SeedFlightUnbounded means a charting seed's reach is bounded by THE GRAPH,
                       not by a number: the search walks until the traversable component is exhausted.'
  ship_ports.go:756   for ring := 0; (maxWalkRings <= 0 || ring < maxWalkRings) && len(frontier) > 0

0 is a SENTINEL meaning UNBOUNDED, not a zero budget. The walk was never bounded to nothing and the
placement request was never structurally unsatisfiable. Landed 2026-07-28 in 1477e962 — one day
BEFORE this bead was filed.

WHY IT MISLEADS: both the warning at ship_ports.go:636 and the error at :781 render the sentinel
through %d, so an unbounded search reports 'within 0 jumps'.

THIS EXACT LINE HAS NOW MISLED TWO INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATIONS. It produced three successive wrong
root causes during the 2026-07-30 frozen-probe investigation (the real cause was gate-edge sibling
condemnation, sp-ky85o), and it produced this bead. That promotes the rendering from cosmetic to
load-bearing: it is actively manufacturing false P-level work.

REAL REMAINING SCOPE — one honest-rendering fix, NOT a bound fix:
  Render the sentinel as 'unbounded' (or 'the whole traversable component') rather than '0 jumps',
  in BOTH ship_ports.go:636 and :781. If any other site formats a walk bound through %d, fix it in
  the same pass — grep for the sentinel, do not assume these two are the only ones.
  Do NOT change maxWalkRings. The bound is correct.

Note sp-cwnwb's 21f9d80a (worklist rotation) dilutes the '54 retries per hull' symptom this bead
cites, but does not touch the message. Cross-ref: sp-ex1wt covers MaxWalkRings=2, which is the
FOOTHOLD path's bound and a genuinely different constant — do not conflate them.

title: Per-hull State column reports IDLE for hulls actively on a tour — derived from window trades, not assignment
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-29: "why is heavy showing idle in the dashboard" - TORWIND-142 (the new heavy freighter) rendered as IDLE while it was demonstrably working.

DASHBOARD: gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json, uid spacetraders-trading-hulls. Panel "Per-Hull P&L - realised, deployed, and honest net".

== THE DEFECT ==
The State column is derived ONLY from trades inside the selected time window, never from the hull's actual assignment:

  CASE WHEN f.ship_symbol IS NULL          THEN 'RELEASED'
       WHEN COALESCE(tx.sells,0) > 0       THEN 'TRADING'
       WHEN COALESCE(f.cargo_units,0) > 0  THEN 'MID-RUN'
       WHEN COALESCE(tx.buys,0)  > 0       THEN 'MID-RUN'
       ELSE 'IDLE' END                     AS "State"

A hull that is claimed and executing a tour but has not yet reached its first buy leg has zero sells, zero buys and an empty hold, so it falls through every branch to IDLE.

MEASURED at the time of filing - the ships table said the opposite:
  ship_symbol  nav_status  system    cargo  assignment_status  container
  TORWIND-142  IN_ORBIT    X1-CJ56   0/225  active             tour-run-TORWIND-142-af241e80   (status RUNNING)
and its tour log showed a real plan: "Tour planned: 3 legs, projected profit 150726".

So IDLE in that column actually means "no trading activity in this window", which is NOT the same as "not working". An active, planning, repositioning hull is rendered identically to an unclaimed one doing nothing.

== WHY IT MATTERS ==
The worst case is the one an operator is most likely to be watching: a NEWLY PURCHASED hull whose first tour has not reached its buy leg. That is exactly when someone checks the dashboard, and exactly when it lies. It also misreports every hull in the gap between tours, and any hull whose tour is long (repositioning, replanning) relative to the selected window.

== FIX ==
The query ALREADY joins ships (alias f), so the truth is in hand - no new join needed. Use assignment_status and container_id:
  - assignment_status = 'active' AND container_id LIKE 'tour-run-%'  -> the hull is on a tour. Render TRADING, or introduce a distinct PLANNING state for the has-tour-but-no-trades-yet case (say which you chose and why).
  - Keep RELEASED for a hull absent from the trade fleet.
  - Keep the existing trade-derived states where they are more specific (sells in window -> TRADING, cargo aboard -> MID-RUN).
  - Only a hull with NO tour container AND no cargo AND no trades is genuinely IDLE.

Beware the FULL OUTER JOIN already in this query: f may be NULL for a hull that traded in the window but has since left the fleet, so guard every new f.* reference with the same care the existing RELEASED branch shows.

== VERIFY ==
A JSON-only check is NOT sufficient - a previous bug in this same dashboard (sp-y2jjn) had valid JSON, a valid query, and still rendered wrongly. Confirm in the LIVE Grafana that a hull which is active-on-a-tour-with-no-trades-yet renders as working rather than IDLE. TORWIND-142 is the live specimen; if it has since traded, any freshly relaunched hull between tours reproduces it.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Dashboard JSON only. No Go changes.
- Preserve uid spacetraders-trading-hulls and every panel id.
- Leave trading.json (uid spacetraders-trading) alone.
- Must still render with zero/degenerate data.
- Protected paths untouched: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**.

title: Best/Worst Hull stats always render noValue — reduceOptions.fields excludes string fields
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-28, on the freshly-merged dashboard (6547a161): Best Hull and Worst Hull show "no hull traded in window" for ALL windows.

DASHBOARD: gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json, uid spacetraders-trading-hulls. Panels id 109 (Best Hull) and id 110 (Worst Hull), both type=stat.

== THE QUERY IS FINE - THE PANEL CONFIG IS WRONG ==
Ran panel 109 rawSql directly against the live DB with the time macro expanded to a 3-hour window. Result:
    TORWIND-60   448,269 CR
One row, one column, correctly formatted. Not a data problem and not a scoping problem (MAX(id) FROM players resolves to 5 = TORWIND, verified).

ROOT CAUSE: both panels carry
    reduceOptions: { calcs: [lastNotNull], fields: EMPTY_STRING, values: false }
In Grafana, reduceOptions.fields set to the empty string means NUMERIC FIELDS ONLY. These two panels deliberately emit a STRING (hull name + to_char-formatted credits + CR suffix, pre-formatted server-side). With no numeric field present the stat reduces nothing, produces no value, and renders defaults.noValue - which is the literal text the Admiral is seeing.

FIX: set reduceOptions.fields to the all-fields regex (slash dot star slash) on panels 109 and 110 so the string field is selected. Do NOT change the SQL and do NOT convert the panels to numeric - the pre-formatted string is intentional and is what produces the "TORWIND-41   476,820 CR" presentation.

VERIFY: after the change, confirm in the LIVE Grafana that both stats render a hull name rather than the noValue text, at more than one time range. A JSON-only check is NOT sufficient - the whole defect is that valid JSON with a valid query still renders nothing.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE: audit every other stat panel in this dashboard for the same mismatch. Any stat whose target returns a non-numeric column has the identical latent bug. Report which you checked and which (if any) also needed fixing.

title: New trading dashboard: complete per-hull P&L, aggregations, correct number formatting
description:
ADMIRAL 2026-07-28: 'Build me a grafana dashboard for trading. There is already one but I want a new one. Format the numbers correctly. I want a complete breakdown of trading, per hull, aggregations, etc.'

== BUILD A NEW DASHBOARD, DO NOT MODIFY THE EXISTING ONE ==
Existing: gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading.json — 'SpaceTraders - Heavy Trading', uid spacetraders-trading, 36 panels (rows: Fleet Now / Economics / Tour Lifecycle / Grounds / Guards). It is HEAVY-hull oriented ('Per-Heavy Tour Profit' tables) and diagnostic-oriented (exit reasons, guard engagements, absorption grounds). LEAVE IT ALONE — new file, NEW uid, so both coexist.

The gap it does not fill: a straight per-hull trading P&L with aggregations. That is what to build.

== VERIFIED DATA MODEL (I ran all of these tonight; they work) ==
Table : id player_id timestamp transaction_type category amount balance_before balance_after description metadata related_entity_type related_entity_id operation_type created_at

  - Ship attribution lives in metadata JSON: metadata->>'ship_symbol'. Also metadata->>'good_symbol', metadata->>'units', metadata->>'waypoint'.
  - transaction_type values seen: PURCHASE_CARGO, SELL_CARGO, REFUEL, PURCHASE_SHIP, CONTRACT_ACCEPTED, CONTRACT_FULFILLED.
  - operation_type values seen: tour, contract, manual, arb_run, construction_supply, 'fleet expansion'.
  - amount is SIGNED (buys negative, sells positive). balance_after gives treasury trajectory.

WORKING per-hull P&L query — use this as the backbone:
  SELECT metadata->>'ship_symbol' AS hull,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE transaction_type='PURCHASE_CARGO') AS buys,
         COALESCE(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE transaction_type='PURCHASE_CARGO'),0) AS spent,
         COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE transaction_type='SELL_CARGO') AS sells,
         COALESCE(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE transaction_type='SELL_CARGO'),0) AS earned,
         COALESCE(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')),0) AS net
    FROM transactions
   WHERE player_id=5 AND created_at > now() - interval '2 hours'
     AND transaction_type IN ('PURCHASE_CARGO','SELL_CARGO')
     AND metadata->>'ship_symbol' IS NOT NULL
   GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY net DESC;

Sample output (real, 2h window): TORWIND-40 net +597,644 (5 buys/7 sells) ... TORWIND-B +70,700; then NEGATIVE rows for hulls with buys and no sells yet.

CRITICAL INTERPRETATION TRAP — the dashboard MUST NOT present these as losses:
  1. Newly-bought hulls (D6/D7/D8) show buys and zero sells simply because they are mid-first-run. Not a loss — cargo in transit.
  2. CONTRACT-fleet hulls (5/7/8/81) show only PURCHASE_CARGO because their revenue lands as CONTRACT_FULFILLED, which carries NO ship_symbol. A naive per-hull net makes every contract hull look catastrophically unprofitable. Either scope the per-hull P&L to operation_type='tour', or label the fleet per hull and show contract revenue separately at fleet level. Say which you chose.
  3. Unrealised inventory: a hull holding cargo has spent but not yet earned. Consider showing 'deployed (cargo in hold)' so net reads honestly mid-flight.

== FORMATTING — THE ADMIRAL CALLED THIS OUT EXPLICITLY ==
Every credit figure must be formatted, not raw. Grafana: set unit to 'currencyCR' if available, else 'locale', with sensible decimals (0 for credits). Tables need PER-COLUMN unit overrides — a table-level unit does not reach the columns. Counts use 'short'/'none', durations 's', percentages 'percent'. Right-align numerics. Colour net P/L by sign (red negative / green positive) via thresholds, and give the big aggregate stats a clear unit so 2380677 renders as 2.38M or 2,380,677 — never bare digits.

== CONTENT WANTED ==
- Per-hull table: buys, sells, spent, earned, NET, plus current state (system, hold used/capacity, active/idle, current tour container) by joining  and  (waypoints.waypoint_symbol = ships.location_symbol; waypoints has system_symbol).
- Aggregations: fleet totals, net per hour, revenue vs spend over time, gross margin %, best/worst hull, per-good and per-system profitability (metadata->>'good_symbol', metadata->>'waypoint').
- Operation split: tour vs contract vs manual vs fleet expansion — this is how you show that capex, not trade, moves treasury.
- Selectable time window via Grafana's $__timeFilter so 30m/2h/24h all work; do NOT hardcode intervals in every panel.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Dashboard JSON only. No Go changes, no new metrics.
- NEW uid (e.g. spacetraders-trading-hulls). Must not collide with spacetraders-trading.
- Datasources already wired in this repo's dashboards: grafana-postgresql-datasource uid 'postgresql', prometheus uid 'prometheus'. Give EVERY panel an explicit datasource.
- Must render with zero/degenerate data without erroring (COALESCE, and empty-state copy rather than a bare 'No data').
- Protected paths untouched: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**.
notes:
TEXT CORRECTION (filer): three table names were eaten by shell backtick expansion when this bead was created. Read them as:

  - Line "Table : id player_id timestamp ..." → the table is TRANSACTIONS.
  - Line "...by joining  and  (waypoints.waypoint_symbol = ships.location_symbol...)" → join the SHIPS table to the WAYPOINTS table.

So the three tables this dashboard reads are: transactions, ships, waypoints. Nothing else was lost.
BUILD LANE (sp-ypjck branch, SHA 60552c69, worktree .claude/worktrees/sp-ypjck):
Added gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/trading-hulls.json — 'SpaceTraders - Trading P&L by Hull',
uid spacetraders-trading-hulls, 28 panels. trading.json untouched.

FOUR CORRECTIONS TO THE FILED DATA MODEL (all verified against live DB):
1. REFUEL rows carry ship_symbol as an EMPTY STRING (277/277), not NULL. The bead's backbone
   query uses 'IS NOT NULL', which admits them and creates a phantom blank-named hull that
   absorbs all fuel spend. Every query here filters on <> '' instead. Fuel is fleet-level only.
2. ships.system_symbol exists directly — the waypoints join the bead specifies is NOT needed
   for the hull's system. waypoints IS still needed, but for a different purpose: mapping a
   transaction's metadata->>'waypoint' to a system in the per-system panel.
3. ships.dedicated_fleet ('trade'/'contract'/'purchasing'/'sensing_parked') is the clean fleet

4. PURCHASE_SHIP stores the ship TYPE in ship_symbol ('SHIP_PROBE'), not a hull.

CONTRACT TRAP: resolved by scoping per-hull P&L to operation_type='tour' (bead option A).
Verified CONTRACT_ACCEPTED/FULFILLED have zero ship_symbol coverage (0/28 rows), so contract
revenue is genuinely unattributable. Contract money reported whole at fleet level (panel 126).

MID-RUN TRAP: 'In Cargo' column reconstructs cost of cargo bought after a hull's last in-window
sale; 'Net @ Cost' = Realised Net + In Cargo. A freshly-bought hull reads ~0, not a red loss.

FORMATTING: credits use unit 'locale' (2,380,677). 'currencyCR' is not a real Grafana unit.
NB frontier.json uses 'unit: none' for credits, which renders bare digits — deliberately not
copied. Counts 'short', percent 'percent'. Per-column overrides on all 6 tables.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED PRE-HANDBACK: panel 119's original FULL OUTER JOIN produced NULL b.time for
buckets holding only non-tour transactions; Postgres sorts NULLs last in the window frame, so
those rows received the complete running total and spiked mid-series. Rebuilt on a single time
spine with a FILTER.

VERIFICATION: all 17 rawSql executed against live DB — 0 errors with data, 0 errors on an empty
400-day-old window with scalars returning 0 (not NULL). Structural validator confirms unique
ids, zero gridPos overlap (1800 cells), explicit datasource on every panel and every target,
no uid/title collision. NOT gated, NOT deployed — lead gates.

title: Seed stand-down at a yard writes a SPARE row that excludes the yard from staging
description:
FOUND BY ferryfix lane, 2026-07-28. Two readings recorded; NOT yet resolved.

MECHANISM (agreed): stagingYardFor requires staffedAt(yard) AND !book.occupied(yard, SlotKindSpare). standDownAsSpare writes Kind:SPARE State:PARKED. So a seed standing down ON a yard staffs it and disqualifies it for staging in the same write. Every usable staging origin today came from fillPlacement filling a MARKET slot that happens to sit on a yard, never from a seed standing down.

LIVE: X1-UV2-A10D holds both a PARKED SPARE and a PARKED MARKET row. X1-BT49-AA9E is about to: TORWIND-3F is IN_TRANSIT to it under a SPARE row.

READING A (ferryfix): a jam. Narrow occupied() to unfilled (WANTED/QUEUED) SPARE rows so a PARKED spare can staff a staging yard.

READING B (lead, after reading the code): (i) UNSAFE — slot key is (player_id, waypoint, slot_kind) and UpsertSlotMetadata writes only [system_symbol, whitelist_goods, depth_credits, era_id, updated_at], NOT state/assigned_ship (sp-wgjb7). A WANTED SPARE want at a yard already holding a PARKED SPARE hits THE SAME ROW, the state write is refused, no want is created — yet requestSeeds still increments SeedsRequested and calls book.addSpare(...WANTED). That in-memory phantom then satisfies takeSupplyFor and suppresses a real request: the suppression bug we just fixed, relocated to memory. (ii) LIKELY UNNECESSARY — buyerAt has NO kind check (waypoint + PARKED + assigned_ship), so a PARKED SPARE at a yard IS a valid buyer for local MARKET fills; and takeReachableSpare can dispatch that parked spare to any bordering target. The exclusion means 'one spare per yard at a time', which looks like intended serialization.

FALSIFIABLE TEST AGREED: when TORWIND-3F lands at X1-BT49-AA9E, do BT49's 12 QUEUED MARKET slots start filling? Reading B says YES (spare staffs the counter). Reading A implies NO. If they do NOT fill, this is a genuine P0 — dispatch with ferryfix's framing.

SEPARATE, UNMEASURED: if a seed's tour ends away from the system's shipyard the hull parks off-counter and staffs nothing. Tour-DESTINATION question, not placement ordering. Needs measurement before design (moving a hull to the yard costs navigation).

DEAD END, do not repeat: 'prefer the YARD slot in fillPlacement'. There are ZERO YARD rows live (356 MARKET, 30 SPARE, 0 YARD) and that is BY DESIGN — planSlots emits a YARD slot only if the yard is not already a placed market, and its CONTRACT comment states probe presence at a yard is WAYPOINT-wise never KIND-wise. Ordering a row set that does not exist achieves nothing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
RESOLVED BY ANALYSIS — both readings converged, no fix to build. Recording so nobody re-opens this.

READING A WITHDRAWN by its author after verifying against code+DB:

1. PHANTOM CONFIRMED — narrowing occupied() is UNSAFE. Conflict key IS (player_id, waypoint_symbol, slot_kind); sensingSlotMetadataUpdateColumns IS [system_symbol, whitelist_goods, depth_credits, era_id, updated_at], NO state/assigned_ship; requestSeeds runs rep.SeedsRequested++ and book.addSpare(...,WANTED) unconditionally after the upsert returns nil. WORSE than first stated: the phantom is HULL-LESS, so under the new takeSupplyFor it PASSES staffedAt (the yard is staffed by premise), counts as supply, and suppresses a real request — the suppression bug just fixed, relocated into memory where it is invisible. The occupied() exclusion is LOAD-BEARING. 'One spare per yard at a time' is the correct reading.

2. BT49 FRAMING WITHDRAWN — two mechanisms conflated. buyerAt has NO kind check, so a PARKED SPARE at a yard IS a valid buyer for that system's MARKET fills. The SPARE row blocks only stagingYardFor (writing a NEW seed want); it does not block funding local placements. Both parties now predict BT49's QUEUED MARKET slots become fundable once TORWIND-3F parks.

3. FIX (2) MOOT — confirmed 356 MARKET / 30 SPARE / 0 YARD live. Keying on KIND is exactly the mistake the planSlots CONTRACT warns against and that staffedAt avoids by keying on waypoint.

WHAT SURVIVES, unbuilt and unmeasured: a seed tour may END away from a shipyard, parking the hull off-counter so it staffs nothing. First sample: of 3 PARKED SPARE hulls, 2 stand off-yard, 1 on a priced yard. Suggestive only. Tour-DESTINATION question with a real navigation cost — needs more landings before anything is designed. DO NOT build on a sample of 3.

OPEN: the BT49 landing is the live confirmation that a parked spare funds local fills. Background watch set.

title: MaxWalkRings=2 bounds placement reach; 114 of 132 outstanding placements are farther
description:
MEASURED (ferryfix lane, live): 114 of 132 outstanding placements — 103 MARKET plus ALL 11 SPARE seeds — are more than 2 gate jumps from any system holding a probe yard with a docked buyer. MaxWalkRings=2 is the binding constraint on reach.

Deliberately NOT raised in the ferry lane, and that judgement was right: a hull bought past the walk's reach is stranded forever while holding probe-cap headroom — strictly worse than not buying. Raising the bound is a MOVER change and needs its own lane.

Does NOT block the seed-staging fix (sp-oish1): stagingYardFor already requires the origin to BORDER the target, so a correctly-staged seed is one jump and never walks. Revisit only after seed staging lands and the frontier starts widening, when reach becomes the next limit.

title: buyerAt requires the buyer DOCKED at the yard; being AT the waypoint is enough
description:
buyerAt (buyqueue.go) accepts a hull only if a PARKED slot at that waypoint has an assigned ship, or Ships.DockedProbeAt returns one — i.e. DOCKED specifically.

Verified one mediator hop down: ProbePurchasePort.Buy sends PurchaseShipCommand, whose handler DOCKS the ship itself if it is in orbit (purchase_ship.go:25 'Dock if in orbit', :254 NavStatusInOrbit -> DockShipCommand). So the purchase requires the buyer to be AT the yard waypoint, NOT already docked.

MEASURED (ferryfix lane): only 4 of 40 eligible docked probes are docked at a yard. Relaxing docked -> present-at-waypoint would likely take usable source systems from 3 to 5+.

Needs a blocking-wait check before shipping: confirm the dock step inside PurchaseShipCommand does not introduce a synchronous wait on the sensing tick (the engine had a prior P0 of exactly that shape, sp-uwxwo).

Ceiling to note: probes park at MARKET waypoints and planSlots gives a system only ONE yard slot, so 'system has a counter' still means 'its YARD slot is filled'. This widens who qualifies at a yard, it does not remove that structure.

title: [bug] probe_buy_relay claim owner is the same label-not-container-id latent FK bug (dormant)
description:
Follow-up from the sensing claim FK fix. internal/adapters/expansion/adapters.go:45 defines defaultProbeBuyClaimOwner = "probe_buy_relay" and uses it as the containerID argument to ClaimShip when a caller passes no owner.

That is the SAME defect that made every sensing probe purchase fail with FK 23503: ClaimShip's second argument is a container id, ships.container_id has an FK into containers(id), and 'probe_buy_relay' is a label with no container row (verified: SELECT count(*) FROM containers WHERE id='probe_buy_relay' -> 0).

DORMANT ONLY BY LUCK: every live caller currently passes a real container id, so the fallback branch is never taken. The moment one does not — a new caller, a refactor that drops the argument, a recovery path — it fails closed with an opaque FK error, exactly as the sensing path did for its entire existence.

NOTE: this file is part of the retired frontier-expansion adapters already on the legacy DELETE list. If that deletion lands first, this evaporates with it. Filed so the knowledge is not lost either way, and so nobody 'fixes' a future FK error by relaxing the constraint — the FK is the guard that caught both.

RECOMMENDED: delete the fallback rather than make it valid. A blank owner should fail closed, which is what the sensing fix chose: every candidate fallback is itself a label, so there is no correct default.

title: Instrument the per-operation capital budget (sp-ftqgp) with Prometheus gauges
description:
sp-g9sbz (frontier dashboard rebuild) could not surface the capital budget because sp-ftqgp emits LOGS ONLY — no Prometheus series and no Postgres table for the budget, its utilisation, or a denial.

The frontier dashboard therefore ships a 'Capital flow (realised, not budgeted)' row derived from the transactions ledger (SUM(amount) by operation_type, player-scoped). That is honest but it is the OUTCOME the budget governs, not the budget itself — it cannot show whether a spend was denied by the guard, nor the 60/40 split's actual utilisation.

WANTED (names indicative):
  spacetraders_daemon_capital_budget_credits{operation}       GAUGE  — allocated budget per operation
  spacetraders_daemon_capital_budget_used_credits{operation}  GAUGE  — consumed this window
  spacetraders_daemon_capital_budget_denials_total{operation} COUNTER — spends refused by the guard

The denials counter is the load-bearing one: a flat-zero counter is how you prove the guard is being consulted at all, rather than inferring from row outcomes (see memory 'root-cause-fix-behind-symptom-patches').

Once these exist, add a budget row to gobot/configs/grafana/dashboards/frontier.json between 'Probe economics' and 'Capital flow'. The dashboard already names this gap in its instrumentation-gaps text panel — update that text when the gauges land.

description:

  - grafana-postgresql-datasource, uid 'postgresql' (rawSql panels)
  - prometheus, uid 'prometheus'
Tables already used: containers, gate_edges, market_data, players, scout_posts, ships, slots, transactions. waypoints(waypoint_symbol, system_symbol, x, y, type, traits) is available for joins/geometry.
Prometheus: bootstrap_phase{phase} GAUGE (1=active) with phases exactly COLDSTART|GATE|EXPANSION; bootstrap_probes_total, bootstrap_haulers_total counters; a construction-pct gauge.

KNOWN GAP — do NOT fake it: sp-ftqgp (the new per-operation capital budget splitting deployable capital 60/40 between trade and construction) emits LOGS ONLY, no Prometheus metrics. If the lane wants a budget panel it must either derive something honest from existing tables or file a follow-up bead for the instrumentation. Inventing a series that does not exist is worse than omitting the panel.

== WHAT 'AMAZING AND USEFUL' MEANS HERE ==
This is an operator console, not a report: it is scanned to answer 'what is blocking expansion right now'. Design accordingly.
  1. PHASE IS THE SPINE. Current phase must read at a glance, plus a transition timeline showing when COLDSTART->GATE->EXPANSION happened. Phase context changes what every other panel means.
  2. LEAD WITH THE BOTTLENECK. 'Systems with cached market data' vs 'jump-reachable systems' is the expansion scoreboard. Make the gap unmissable and show it over time — flat = expansion stalled.
  3. MAKE THE FAILURE MODE VISIBLE. Neighbours known-but-unpriced is the actionable state. A table of jump-reachable systems with last_updated per system (NULL = never scanned) tells the operator exactly where to send a probe.
  4. THE HANDOFF. Gate completion + hulls redirected to trade is the phase's defining event — surface it, do not bury it.
  5. Encode state in FORM as well as number (severity colour/thresholds), so 'needs attention' reads without parsing digits. Semantic colour is separate from decoration.
  6. Keep the genuinely useful existing panels (probe economics, scout freshness, gate-edge backoff). This is a rebuild of the framing, not a teardown.

== CONSTRAINTS ==
- Dashboard JSON only. No Go changes, no new metrics (see gap above).
- Preserve uid 'spacetraders-frontier' so existing links/bookmarks keep working.
- Must render with ZERO rows / single-system data without erroring — that is the current live state and the most important case to get right.
- Protected paths untouched: gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**.

title: Trade infeasibility backoff swallows the brief solvency windows it should capture
description:
Observed live, era 5 TORWIND, 2026-07-27. When treasury sits near the trade_fleet.working_capital_reserve floor, two mechanisms fight each other and the trade op stalls indefinitely despite profitable plans existing.

MECHANISM
1. Tours plan fine (one projected +37,444 across 3 legs) but every buy is denied: 'buy of 19 CLOTHING @ 3440 would breach working-capital floor - live balance 270126, reserve 300000, even 1 unit pierces'.
2. Each capital-denied exit counts as 'unproductive' and escalates the fleet-wide infeasibility backoff (observed 3m -> 6m, growing).
3. Treasury near the floor is SPIKY, not flat: it clears the floor only for seconds right after a contract fulfills, before the next contract cargo buy spends it back down.

MEASURED INSTANCE
  22:54:44 CONTRACT_ACCEPTED  -> balance 306,347  (ABOVE the 300k floor)
  22:56:28 PURCHASE_CARGO     -> balance 283,782  (back below)
  => solvent window = ~104 seconds.
  TORWIND-6 backoff ran 22:52:07 -> 22:58:07. The ENTIRE solvent window sat inside the cooldown; the hull could not act on it.

WHY IT MATTERS
The backoff exists to stop wasteful replanning, but capital-denial is not the same failure as no-profitable-route. Backing off on capital-denial makes the hull sleep through exactly the windows that would unblock it — the longer the backoff grows, the more certain it is to miss the next spike. Self-reinforcing lockout.

PROPOSED FIX (design, not prescription)
Treat capital-denied exits as a DISTINCT class from route-infeasible exits:
  - do not escalate the fleet-wide infeasibility backoff on capital denial; and/or
  - reset/short-circuit the cooldown the moment live treasury crosses the reserve floor (event-driven wake rather than fixed timer).
Do NOT weaken the money guard itself — RULINGS #4. The guard behaved correctly; the scheduling around it is the defect.
notes:
INVALID — retracted by the filer, 2026-07-27. The premise fails on arithmetic I did not do before filing.

The 'missed solvency window' peaked at 306,347 against a 300,000 floor = 6,347 credits of usable headroom. The denied tour leg needed 19 CLOTHING @ 3440 = 65,360, and TORWIND-6's last productive run spent 102,972 on cargo. Launching inside that window would have bought ONE unit (tranche-shrunk to fit) and returned trivial profit.

So the backoff did not cost a productive tour — there was no fundable tour to lose. Declining to launch a hull that can fund nothing is correct behavior, not a scheduling defect. Both the money guard and the infeasibility backoff behaved as designed.

The real (and non-defective) situation: treasury near the floor simply has no working capital, and the fix is treasury recovery, which is underway.
close_reason: Closed

title: Trade fleet coordinator has no unconditional boot launch — absent from bootStandingCoordinatorTypes
description: ContainerTypeTradeFleetCoordinator is not in bootStandingCoordinatorTypes (which holds Construction, ProbeSensing, Bootstrap, ScoutPost, ProbeBuyer). It survives a daemon restart only via RecoverRunningContainers re-adopting a persisted RUNNING row, and is launched only from two bootstrap paths: the INCOME trade-seed (run_bootstrap_income.go:554) and — as of sp-hv4f6 — an ensure in actExpansion. Consequence: if the trade coordinator dies AFTER bootstrap has exited, nothing restarts it until the next bootstrap run, and every trade-tagged hull idles meanwhile. sp-hv4f6's ensure covers the bootstrap path but cannot cover this; a boot-standing entry is a daemon-boot change affecting every era and every player, so it was correctly kept out of that bead. Found by impl-hv4f6 during the sp-hv4f6 fix round; the underlying gap was surfaced by that bead's review. Fix: add the type to bootStandingCoordinatorTypes with an ensure* function following the existing pattern (see ensureProbeSensingStanding / ensureScoutPostStanding), plus a boot-standing set test.
notes: SEVERITY MATERIALLY REDUCED by sp-hv4f6's fix (verified in its fix-round re-review). ContainerTypeBootstrapCoordinator IS in bootStandingCoordinatorTypes, and EXPANSION is monotone — so every daemon boot now runs bootstrap, derives EXPANSION, and ensures the trade coordinator before exiting. This drops from 'a mature fleet may have no trade coordinator at all' (correctness) to 'a coordinator that dies mid-era, after bootstrap has exited, is not restarted until the next daemon boot' (recovery latency). Still worth the boot-standing entry, but no longer urgent.

title: adoptOrphanProbes silently skips in-transit hulls — invisible to the probe cap, authorises re-buying a hull we own
description:
At internal/application/scouting/commands/run_probe_sensing_coordinator.go:1210-1213, a scout-tagged hull with no current location (in transit at cutover time) is skipped with a bare 'continue' and NOTHING appended to failures. Consequence: no sensing_slots row is written for it, so CountOwnedProbes never counts it, so the probe cap under-reads and authorises buying a replacement for a hull we already own — the exact chain the cutover's own ordering comment at :980-986 exists to prevent. The hull also stays tagged 'scout', unmanaged, forever.

PRE-EXISTING (predates sp-x665h) but surfaced by its review: on the dominant success path adoption never re-runs, because markCutoverDone latches. sp-x665h removed the accidental second chance the all-screens-fail re-fire used to provide.

Do NOT fix by collecting the skip as a failure — that would hold the entire cutover hostage to any probe being in transit. The right shape is an adoption retry path independent of the cutover firing: make adoption idempotent and re-runnable, and run it periodically. Natural home is the reaper pass (sp-l3f3d) which already runs every tick doing exactly this class of bookkeeping. Note the kinship with sp-9tt15 (construction hull in transit at gate completion) — same in-transit-at-a-transition-edge failure mode in a different subsystem.
close_reason: Landed on sp-k6v8z (a2435106, 21676a42, dd7a248d, bcd2b23f, 04792b40): adoptStrandedProbes is a bounded sibling pass running every tick, gated on the cutover's durable trigger (NOT the in-memory done-latch, which a daemon restart clears — that would have disabled adoption permanently at the first bounce). Adopts any scout-tagged hull with no ledger row, not just the in-transit case. Two review rounds found and closed a same-waypoint eviction in both its shapes: two orphans at one waypoint, and an orphan evicting a live or hull-less placement — closed via two independent indexes (row-existence occupancy + hull-recorded) off one read, with three-way mutation probes proving each independently load-bearing. Residual filed as sp-dpfp8.

title: SupplyConstruction already returns the updated site but DeliverToConstructionSite discards it — free exact reconciliation left on the table
description:
sp-duxru (deployed a7206b58) reconciles delivered counters with one GET per pipeline per working tick, ~1.7% of API budget.

That read is avoidable. The SpaceTraders SupplyConstruction response ALREADY carries the updated construction site, so every successful supply returns exact server truth at ZERO API cost. The port discards it: ConstructionProducer.DeliverToConstructionSite returns (int, error).

Also: a boot-time recovery gap for tasks persisted EXECUTING/ASSIGNED — see sp-ciog notes. Related but separate.
