title: INVALID (filed on a false premise) — contract standby homing is working as designed
description:
MEASURED, era 5 at 03:53 (27 contracts in ~14h):
  total=27  accepted=27  fulfilled=26  currently open=1
Exactly ONE contract is ever open. All COSMIC — the faction issues the next only after the previous is fulfilled. Unit requirements observed: 18,18,18,19,21,22,46,49,74 — every one fits inside a single 80-capacity light hauler.

So contract work can occupy exactly one hull. With haulers=3/4 the fleet had TORWIND-7 on contract-work and TORWIND-5 (idle 17min) + TORWIND-8 (idle 12min) with nothing to do — roughly 690k of hull capital parked, heading to ~1.03M at the 4/4 target.

The designed fallback for idle dedicated hulls is idle-arb, and it IS running and evaluating them. Every candidate this pass was ELECTRONICS and every one was skipped:blacklist — correctly, DefaultIdleArbBlacklist excludes ELECTRONICS as too volatile to price against the live-verify floor (idle_arb.go:191). Margins offered were 1054-1291/u net against a 337 floor, so the capital is idle for want of an eligible GOOD, not for want of a profitable one.

NOT FILING THIS AS A BUG. There are two readings and I cannot choose between them from here:
 (a) haulerTarget=4 is sized for GATE construction (gate workers ramp to 4), so these hulls are pre-positioned capital that idles during COLDSTART and is consumed at GATE. Buying early costs idle time but removes a purchase from the critical path.
 (b) haulerTarget=4 assumes parallel contract throughput that the faction does not offer, and hulls 2-4 should be bought later or dedicated elsewhere (trade) until GATE needs them.

If (a), this is working as intended and the only question is whether the idle window is worth the schedule saving. If (b), the ramp is buying ~690k of capital roughly 2 hulls too early.

Admiral decision, not an engineering one. Recording the measurement so it is decided on data.
notes:
ADMIRAL CORRECTION 2026-07-27: the ramp is NOT sized for parallel contract work. Idle haulers are meant to be POSITIONED so they source the next contract earlier, raising contract $/hr. My 'sized for GATE vs oversized' framing was wrong — discard both readings.

VERIFIED THE MECHANISM IS OFF:
  containers.config->>'standby_stations' = null (JSON null, contract_fleet_coordinator-player-5-ac03d0d3)
  every idle-arb pass logs '0 hull(s) re-homed this pass'; 're-homed 1 total' is one historical event
  idle_arb.go:~100 — 'Empty (or a nil homer) disables re-homing entirely'
So rehomeDriftedHulls never stages anything; idle hulls dead-idle where their last leg ended (TORWIND-5 @ A1, TORWIND-8 @ F46 — neither is a significant source market).

BUT THE OUTCOME IS THE BEST OF THE ERA, so this is unrealized upside and NOT a defect. Contracts fulfilled per hour:
  07-26 13:00  1   11972      frigate only
  07-26 14:00  2   81290
  07-26 15:00  3   314687
  07-27 00:00  4   275987     hauler #1
  07-27 01:00  6   197418     (ghost-claim freezes in this window)
  07-27 02:00  4   114640
  07-27 03:00  5   518911     <- best hour of the era, at 2-3 haulers, staging disabled

WHY THE UPSIDE IS MODEST HERE — sourcing is dispersed, not concentrated:
  D41 8 buys | K86 6 | G47 5 | H49 4 | C38 4 | F45 4 | B7 3 | E42 2 | G48 2 | E43/D40/A1/J56 1 each
Busiest source is 8 of 42 buys = 19%, across 13 waypoints. Staging at any one hub shortens the sourcing leg under 1 time in 5. Delivery IS concentrated (J56 = 8 of 27 contracts, 30%) but a hull must source before it delivers, so staging at the delivery end does not shorten the long leg.

IF ENABLING: live, no restart —
  spacetraders fleet hub add --operation contract --waypoint X1-KP23-D41
  spacetraders fleet hub add --operation contract --waypoint X1-KP23-K86
D41+K86 = 33% of buys and 65% of contract spend. Recommend measuring across more than one era first: the good mix drives which markets matter and that is era-specific.
close_reason:
INVALID. Filed on a false premise; every observation was the system working.

standby_stations=null is CORRECT BY DESIGN. sp-ojp32 (closed, gated) resolves the era-invariant central-band standby set at RUNTIME every pass via isCentralSink() over the durable MARKETPLACE trait, and its close reason states 'Recomputed from durable inputs, no config write (RULINGS #2/#3)'. bootstrap_ports.go:736 passing nil standbyStations is therefore correct, not a root cause.

'0 hull(s) re-homed this pass' means ALREADY CORRECTLY PLACED, not disabled — see the 'already home if at ANY standby waypoint' check (idle_arb.go:1071, noted in sp-ojp32).

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-27 04:10, era 5: idle TORWIND-5 @ A1 (A band), idle TORWIND-8 @ F46 (F band), busy TORWIND-7 @ H49 (H band) — two idle hulls on two DISTINCT central bands, which is exactly the design target (one per distinct central waypoint).

Era-5 band structure A25 H45 E54 G64 F76 D83 K104 C115 matches the era-4 X1-UM5 record A27 H45 E55 G63 F75 D83 K104 C153 — era-invariant as designed.

I also cited sp-9le3x's STEP-1 'greedy weighted p-median'. That is SUPERSEDED: sp-yv230 ripped out demand-ranked distribution ('it concentrates on the top hub') in favour of FIXED per-hull standby homes. Read sp-ojp32 + sp-yv230 for the current design, not sp-9le3x STEP 1.

NEARLY CAUSED HARM: was about to run 'fleet hub add' with waypoints picked by source-market purchase counts, which would have overwritten a correct runtime resolution with a hand-picked worse set — by the design's own curve ('home to ONE standby point: 1.28x, flat') that likely reduces throughput.

title: Grafana dashboards scope by MAX(players.id); the visualizer proves that is not how you find the live era
description:
Every Grafana panel that filters by player scopes with player_id=(SELECT MAX(id) FROM players) — e.g. financial.json 'Fleet Inventory Value' does it twice, once for ships and once for market_data.

Five players already exist, ALL named TORWIND (eras 1-5). MAX(id)=5 is currently the live one, so the panels are right today — by coincidence, not by construction.

The visualizer solved this properly and documents why (visualizer/server/routes/contract-ops.ts:32-46, resolveLivePlayer): it picks the player whose CONTAINERS are actually RUNNING, ordered by freshest heartbeat, and falls back to last_active only if nothing runs. Its comment states outright that last_active alone 'can point at a dead era'. The same objection applies to MAX(id), which is weaker still — it tracks registration order, not liveness.

FAILURE MODE: register any new agent — a staging run against the same DB, a failed/retried registration, an era transition that mints a player before containers start — and MAX(id) points at a player with no containers. Every Grafana panel then silently reads a dead era: inventory, P&L, fleet counts all frozen at whatever that player last held, with no error and no empty panel to signal it. Indistinguishable from 'the numbers are stale'.

Note players.last_active is NULL for all 5 rows, so the visualizer's own fallback would also be unreliable here — RUNNING-container resolution is the only sound signal in this schema.

FIX: give the dashboards the same resolution the visualizer uses. Either a shared SQL snippet, or a view (e.g. live_player) both consumers select from so they cannot drift apart.

title: ships.synced_at is only advanced by full API resync, so the CACHE AGE column lies about current data
description:
ship list's CACHE AGE column is now - ships.synced_at. synced_at is written only on a full API resync, never by the writes that keep cargo/fuel/nav current, so the column reports hours of staleness over data that is correct to the second.

MEASURED 2026-07-27 03:33Z, DB vs a direct GET /my/ships for all 7 hulls - cargo, fuel and nav matched EXACTLY on every ship:
  TORWIND-5  LIVE 22/80 ASSAULT_RIFLESx22  ==  DB 22/80 ASSAULT_RIFLESx22   yet CACHE AGE 3h36m
  TORWIND-6  LIVE 10/80 POLYNUCLEOTIDESx4,CLOTHINGx6  ==  DB identical      yet CACHE AGE 2h31m
  TORWIND-7  LIVE 0/80 empty  ==  DB 0/80 empty                             yet CACHE AGE 24m

Arithmetic confirms the derivation: TORWIND-1 14h14m vs synced=13:18:59, TORWIND-5 3h36m vs 23:57:37, TORWIND-6 2h31m vs 01:02:07, TORWIND-7 24m vs 03:09:25.

WHY IT MATTERS
- An operator (or an agent) reading CACHE AGE cannot distinguish fresh data from stale. It cost me a wrong call in this session: I saw a 3h synced_at next to correct cargo, called it coincidence, and moved on.
- Any code that gates a re-sync on synced_at is wrong in BOTH directions - it will re-sync rows that are current, and it cannot detect the rows that genuinely ARE stale (sp-in36a, the contract-delivery boundary).
- Freshness is the exact property sp-w359k and sp-in36a turn on. A freshness indicator that does not track writes is worse than none.

NOTE: sp-w359k's scoped-write fix includes synced_at in the columns it updates, so it may close this incidentally. Verify after that lands before doing separate work here - and if it does close it, keep a test pinning that synced_at advances on a scoped write.

title: Auto-liquidation dispatches on a stale cargo snapshot: 6 spawns in 80min, every one found an empty hull
description:
Era 5, TORWIND-5. Six cargo-liquidation workers spawned since 01:39, every single one logging:
  'Liquidation: TORWIND-5 holds nothing - already clear, re-entering candidacy'

Zero cargo sold. Each spawn claims the hull off contract work, finds an empty hold, and releases.

MECHANISM
run_fleet_coordinator.go:1521 dispatchLiquidationForParked spawns a one-shot worker for every hull FilterUnrelatedCargo parked, each discovery pass, 5min per-hull cooldown (liquidationDispatchCooldown:1508).
ship_pool_manager.go:581 parks on ship.Cargo().HasItemsOtherThan(requiredCargo), where the ship comes from fleetBySymbol -> shipRepo, i.e. the DB ROW.

EVIDENCE THE ROW IS STALE, NOT THE PREDICATE WRONG
The 02:44:20 cycle: contract-work-c9db99b2 COMPLETED 02:44:20, cargo-liquidation-74d6750d started 02:44:20 and reported an empty hold at 02:44:23. Dispatch and execution are 3 SECONDS apart and disagree on whether the hull holds cargo. The worker is the one that actually looks before spending, so the filter's read was stale.

Same root class the sp-7oxeo RCA established: navigate_route.go:164 loads a ship once and carries that entity for a whole flight, writing it back whole, so cargo_units/cargo_inventory lag reality. sp-7oxeo defended the OWNERSHIP columns against that path; the CARGO columns are still exposed.

COST
- 6 wasted container spawns + API calls per 80min, per hull
- each briefly steals the hull from contract work
- it is the trigger surface that gave sp-7oxeo's ghost-claim race its opportunities (claim -> release -> stale write-back resurrects). The ghost is fixed; the pointless churn that fed it is not.

DO NOT disable auto-liquidation - a genuinely stranded hold must still self-clear (RULINGS #1). Fix the freshness of the read the dispatch decision is made on.
notes:
SUBSUMED BY sp-w359k (root cause). Lane stopped mid-flight 2026-07-27 03:10 — it was building a freshness special-case for the liquidation dispatch, which is a second symptom patch on the same defect. If sp-w359k lands, the cargo columns stop going stale and this dispatch becomes correct with no special-case read. Re-open only if sp-w359k is descoped.
PRECISE MECHANISM, with ledger evidence (2026-07-27, TORWIND-5):
  02:32:52  PURCHASE 18 EQUIPMENT   -34272   contract-work-c9db99b2
  02:44:19  CONTRACT_FULFILLED cms2lz183 +87638   <- the 18 leave the hold HERE
  02:44:20  CONTRACT_ACCEPTED  cms2mify0 +26896   <- new contract, different required good
  02:44:23  cargo-liquidation-74d6750d -> 'holds nothing'

This is not random cache drift. It is the CONTRACT-DELIVERY BOUNDARY, and it recurs on essentially every contract turnover:
  1. hull carries good A for contract 1
  2. delivery empties the hold (CONTRACT_FULFILLED, not SELL_CARGO)
  3. contract 2 is accepted in the same second, requiring good B
  4. FilterUnrelatedCargo reads the PRE-delivery row -> sees good A -> HasItemsOtherThan(B) is true -> parks
  5. worker spawns, reads live, finds nothing, releases

Delivery and next-contract-acceptance land within ~1s of each other, so the window is reliably hit. That is why the spawn count tracks contract turnover and will scale linearly with hauler count (8 spawns by 03:21 with 2 haulers).

Also explains why the ghost-claim race (sp-7oxeo) fired so often on this hull specifically: contract turnover was manufacturing a claim/release cycle every few minutes.
POST-sp-w359k EVIDENCE (2026-07-27 04:40): NOT fixed by the root fix, and my earlier assumption that it would be is WRONG — recorded so nobody repeats it.

sp-w359k landed at 04:36 (nav ops persist only owned columns; cargo columns are now fresh). At 04:40 cargo-liquidation-TORWIND-7-7757d007 still logged 'TORWIND-7 holds nothing - already clear, re-entering candidacy'.

So the dispatch is NOT (only) a stale-read problem. It is a TIMING problem at the contract-delivery boundary: the discovery pass evaluates HasItemsOtherThan while the hull legitimately still holds the outgoing contract good, the delivery empties the hold moments later (CONTRACT_FULFILLED, not SELL_CARGO), and the worker then finds nothing. A perfectly fresh read taken one second before delivery still parks the hull.

Freshening the read cannot close this. The dispatch decision has to survive the hull emptying between decision and execution.
close_reason:
Gated 6305555c, deployed 05:0x. Spawn-time re-verification against SERVER TRUTH (SyncShipFromAPI) before any container is persisted or hull claimed; cleared hold returns errHoldAlreadyClear and nothing is spawned. Fails CLOSED — an unverifiable hold is never claimed and the existing cooldown defers the retry (RULINGS #1). Replaces the old post-persist FindBySymbol DB read, so a skip now costs nothing instead of a claim/release cycle.

NOT a staleness fix — that was disproved: sp-w359k made the cargo columns fresh at 04:36 and a spurious dispatch still occurred at 04:40. The defect was TIMING at the contract-delivery boundary (delivery empties the hold and requiredCargo flips within ~1s), so the decision was right when made and wrong when acted on.

Mutation-probed BOTH directions by the orchestrator (lane went idle without reporting):
  remove cleared-hold skip -> FAIL HoldClearsBetweenParkingAndDispatch_NoWorkerSpawned
  make it never dispatch   -> FAIL ServerConfirmsStrandedHold_WorkerStillSpawned (+3 others)
Full suite green at gate.

title: ships.version regresses in production despite the sp-7oxeo clamp (v10 -> v1 -> v3)
description:
Sampled TORWIND-5 post-deploy of 1c3025bc, 45s apart:
  01:47:47  v10
  01:48:32  v1
  01:49:17  v3

sp-7oxeo added a locked-read version clamp, and its mutation probe 2 proves the clamp holds in test. In prod the column still goes backwards, so the clamp is not covering whatever writer does this.

HYPOTHESIS (not yet proven): the clamp is scoped to Save's CONFLICT branch. An entity constructed fresh from an API sync has PersistedVersion()==0, so shipToModel writes Version = 0+1 = 1. Its CAS (WHERE version = 0) cannot match a live row, so it lands in the conflict branch... which should clamp. Either that path bypasses Save, or another writer sets the column directly. Needs a writer census, not more sampling.

SEVERITY IS LOWER THAN IT LOOKS: ownership no longer depends on the version. The conflict branch preserves the assignment triplet from the locked row whatever the version does, and this was confirmed in prod - the 01:48:48 contract-work -> liquidation -> release -> re-claim race (the exact shape that orphaned this hull 5x today) completed clean with no sweeper running.

RESIDUAL RISK: with the row reset to a low version, an entity that loaded at that same low version can CAS-MATCH and write ownership from a stale snapshot without ever entering the conflict branch - the quiet path sp-7oxeo closed by making ownership writers bump the version. A regressing counter reopens a narrower version of it. Also makes ships.version useless as a staleness signal for any future work.

title: Bootstrap heartbeat income/hr reports large negative while treasury is rising
description:
Era-5 COLDSTART heartbeat reports income/hr=-138782 across consecutive ticks while treasury climbs 157684 -> 191949 (+34265 in ~10min, i.e. roughly +205k/hr). Sign and magnitude both disagree with the observed treasury delta.

Suspect the window still charges the two 315889 hull purchases as operating loss. Whatever the cause, the two readings cannot both be right.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics: income/hr is the wedge-detection signal in the validation loop ('treasury frozen across 2 checks with income/hr at 0 => suspect a wedge'). A permanently-negative reading makes that heuristic useless during exactly the phase it is meant to guard, and it makes GATE-readiness reporting untrustworthy.

Capex and operating income should be separated, or the metric renamed to say what it actually measures.
notes:
2026-07-27 02:06 — EVIDENCE FOR THE CAPEX HYPOTHESIS. income/hr flipped on its own: -85349 (01:54) -> +116194 (02:06), with no code change and no unusual earning event in between. The two 315889 hull purchases aging out of the trailing window is the parsimonious explanation, and it matches the sign flip timing.

+116194/hr is also roughly consistent with the real gain over the preceding hour (~192k -> ~274k = +82k, plus in-flight cargo), so the metric reads sensibly once capex is out of the window.

Confirms the defect is capex-in-window rather than a broken computation. Fix is to separate capital purchases from operating income (or rename the metric), not to change the arithmetic.

title: Trade-seed capital gate and trade working-capital reserve are independent numbers
description:
run_bootstrap_income.go:510 gates the cold-start trade-seed buy on cushion=(treasury-price) >= contractWorkingCapitalFloor (150k). The trade coordinator then refuses to trade below trade_fleet.working_capital_reserve. Two unrelated numbers, so the seed can always buy a hull that cannot yet trade.

Even after the reserve drops to 300k (sp-4chpz): seed at treasury 500k, price 315k -> cushion 185k passes the 150k floor, post-buy treasury 185k < 300k reserve -> hull idles until contracts lift treasury.

Fix: the seed gate should read the SAME reserve the trade coordinator enforces.

HARD CONSTRAINT: run_bootstrap_income.go:107-110 RETURNS after the seed attempt, and 5b gates contract hauler #3+ behind TradeHullCount >= 1. Making the seed gate stricter WITHOUT converting that return into a fall-through freezes the entire contract ramp. Defer-and-fall-through, never defer-and-return.

title: Routing service may still cost DRIFT legs with an inverted time model, silently mis-optimising routes
description:
sp-5iza5 made DRIFT unreachable on the GO side: the selector no longer produces it, the planner raises a DRIFT step to CRUISE, and mode ranking now compares travel time instead of iota order. The Python routing service was NOT touched and can still emit DRIFT steps.

WHY THAT STILL MATTERS: the Go side raises a planned DRIFT leg to CRUISE at execution, so a DRIFT step no longer strands a hull. But the solver COSTS its candidate routes with its own time model. If that model shares the inversion the Go side just had (DRIFT rated FASTER than CRUISE - it was 26 vs 31, corrected to 214 vs 31 against a production measurement of 885s vs ~128s over distance 123.81), then the solver is choosing routes that only look cheap because a DRIFT leg is priced as fast. Those routes get executed at CRUISE, so they are slower and more fuel-hungry than the solver believed - a silently mis-optimised plan rather than a stranded ship.

CHECK: the routing service's per-mode time model (gobot/services/routing-service/). Confirm whether it models DRIFT at all, and if so whether its DRIFT time is faster or slower than CRUISE for the same distance. Reconcile it with the Go constants in internal/domain/shared/flight_mode.go (BURN 15, CRUISE 31, DRIFT 214, all hand-tuned rather than the game's raw 12.5/25/250 - the Go model has no +15 term, so do not copy game constants blind).

IF IT DOES EMIT DRIFT: decide whether the solver should stop emitting DRIFT entirely (matching the Go policy - DRIFT is a rescue, never a route mode) or keep emitting it with a corrected cost. Stopping is simpler and matches the Admiral ruling; keeping it only makes sense if some route is genuinely only feasible by drifting, which the refuel-or-fail policy now says should refuel instead.

NOTE the routing service is a SEPARATE deploy step (ENGINEERING.md section 2): its Python proto stubs are gitignored, regenerate both proto sides in the service venv, and kickstart routing BEFORE the daemon.

title: ShouldPreventDriftMode only tops off when the planned mode is already DRIFT — a ship on a fuel station with a planned BURN leg departs under-fuelled
description:
ShouldPreventDriftMode (internal/domain/navigation/ship_fuel_service.go:159) only triggers a pre-departure refuel when the PLANNED mode is already DRIFT. A ship sitting ON a fuel station with a low tank and a planned BURN or CRUISE leg will not top off before departing.

The hole: the check asks "am I about to drift?" rather than "can I afford the plan I am about to fly, and am I standing somewhere I could fix that?". A ship that departs a fuel station under-fuelled on a planned BURN leg discovers the shortfall mid-plan, at a waypoint that may sell no fuel - which is exactly the strand shape sp-6n1bi fixed from the other side.

DID NOT BITE in the observed incident only because the intervening waypoint (X1-KP23-B29) is an ASTEROID that sells no fuel, so the ship could not have topped off there anyway. The departure point (X1-KP23-I54, FUEL_STATION) did refuel correctly. So this is a latent hole, not a live regression.

RELATED: sp-6n1bi fixed the other half - the executor no longer spends the tank the planner budgeted for later legs. With that in, a ship should rarely arrive short. This bead is the belt to that braces: top off while standing on fuel, when the remaining plan needs it.

WHEN FIXING: the natural condition is "the tank does not cover the planned remaining legs up to the next fuelling stop, and I am currently at a waypoint with fuel" - which is the same reserve quantity Route.FuelReserveAfterCurrentSegment() now computes for sp-6n1bi. Reuse it rather than deriving a second notion of "fuel I will need".

title: contract get <id> reports 'contract not found' for every contract that contract list shows
description:
OBSERVED IN PROD, era 5 (player 5, binary 9ae03194). Two CLI verbs over the same data disagree completely: "contract list" returns four contracts, and "contract get <id>" fails on ALL of them.

REPRO (every id taken verbatim from the list output):
  spacetraders contract list
    cms1wualv  fulfilled=true   pay=78840
    cms1toi6a  fulfilled=true   pay=13468
    cms1ww9it  fulfilled=false  pay=319425
    cms1v602e  fulfilled=true   pay=27880
  spacetraders contract get cms1ww9it
    Error: failed to get contract: contract not found: cms1ww9it
  Same for cms1wualv, cms1toi6a, cms1v602e.

Adding --agent TORWIND does not help, so it is not the usual player-scoping omission. It fails for fulfilled and unfulfilled alike, so it is not a status filter either.

LIKELY SHAPE (unverified - diagnose, do not assume): the two paths resolve the contract by different keys. "list" renders whatever the repository holds, while "get" looks up by a key that is not the id "list" prints - e.g. an internal row id vs the API contract id, or a player-scoped lookup that misses because the era-5 player_id is not threaded through. Start by comparing the query each path issues.

IMPACT: cosmetic but real - "contract get" is the only way to see a contract delivery terms and per-good progress, so an operator cannot inspect a running contract at all. It blocks diagnosis, not the engine; contracts themselves execute fine.

FIX: make "get" resolve every id "list" emits. If the two verbs legitimately key on different identifiers, make "get" accept the one "list" prints (that is the operator-facing contract), and add a test that feeds list output straight into get so the two can never diverge again.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tour hop matrix proving 0/N crossings since sensing deploy — stale-tolerant walk finding nothing
description: Observed post-sensing-deploy (55075c47 era): 'Tour hop matrix could not prove 28 of 28 system crossing(s) over stored gate topology' and 45/45 — vs 0.77% refusals measured at the stale-tolerant walk's merge (659c092a). Cost-not-veto (each unproven crossing charged bound+1 hops, tours rank worse but stay feasible) so not an outage, but cross-system ranking is now blind. Suspects: gate_edges era-scoping vs the adjacency read; the charted-set shrinking; or the ranking walk regressed by a later merge. Reproduce with StoredRankingDistances against live gate_edges before theorising.

title: Pin the DeclareHomeScoutPost equality guard — the home-floor restart contract is test-naked
description: Condition of the sp-tky2x Task 9 merge (reviewer I1). bootstrap_ports.go:806-810's equality guard ('minHulls > 0 && (home == nil || home.MinHulls != minHulls)') is what makes a restarted daemon's first EXPANSION tick a zero-write no-op when home's floor is already 1 — the handler-layer once-flag resets at restart, so this guard IS the cross-restart idempotency of the T9 home 3->1 retirement. It is pinned by NOTHING (grep for bootstrapScoutPostDeclarer in *_test.go is empty): a future 'simplify: always stamp' refactor dropping the inequality goes green today, costs per-cold-tick DB writes at 45s cadence plus one redundant write per boot, and silently voids the documented restart contract. Add adapter-level tests covering three shapes: existing floored post => zero UpdateScoutPostMinHulls calls; MinHulls=0 => single 0->1 write; absent post => create + stamp. Needs DaemonServer/DB scaffolding from the adapter suite — that is why it was deferred out of the task's own fix loop (scope fence), not because it is optional.

title: Explorer off-gate bridge dead after frontier retirement — arming explorer_hulls_enabled is now inert
description: Surfaced by the sp-tky2x Task 8 review collateral hunt. The frontier coordinator was the only writer of the explorer off-gate demand bridge; with frontier unwired, ExplorerDemand reads unreadable-forever (explorer_offgate_bridge.go:54-55 => false,0,false): zero demand, no errors, no spend — fail-safe, but the explorer hull class's arming knob (explorer_hulls_enabled) is now permanently inert. Decide: re-point explorer demand at the sensing coordinator's discovery signal, or retire the class + its knob and bridge explicitly. Also from the same hunt: the sp-255rz fail-closed-quote stall-breaker was frontier-side and was not carried to sensing (mitigated by probe-buyer fleet yard stationing) — fold the decision in here. And bootstrap's defer_probe_to_freshsizer (sp-tsn2) now never defers (no sizer exists) — re-point at sensing or retire the arbitration.

title: Sensing coordinator liveconfig reader: tune keys apply at rebuild, not next tick
description: Surfaced by the sp-tky2x Task 8 review. The probe-sensing coordinator (T6) resolves its config once at construction; unlike the sizer it has no liveconfig re-read at tick start, so every tune --operation sensing write lands in the container config column but only takes effect at the next daemon bounce/rebuild. The tune help's next-tick promise was corrected with a caveat (T8 fix round 1), but the right end state is the sizer-style per-tick liveconfig read so a money-cap tightening (max_spend_per_cycle) applies immediately. Add the reader + a test proving a mid-run tune changes the NEXT tick's behaviour.
close_reason: Closed

title: Collapse the cold-price dance into one acquirer primitive
description:
Epic sp-7ie7i follow-up (option 3). The reconciler currently knows that shipyard listings are PRESENCE-GATED — an adapter concern that has leaked into phase logic and been implemented three times.

Current surface:
- ShipyardScanner.EnsureHomeShipyardReadable — positions ANY idle undedicated hull
- ShipyardScanner.PositionPurchaserAtShipyard — positions a NAMED hull (the purchasing frigate)
- ensureShipyardReadable (reconcile wrapper, DATA probe path)
- ensureHaulerPriceReadable (income wrapper, hauler path, ~110 lines)
- the per-container price cache: cachedHaulerPrice + cacheHaulerPrice + seedHaulerPriceFromYard

The two port methods differ ONLY in which hull they send. That is one primitive with a preferred-hull argument, not two methods.

TARGET: one port method the reconciler calls when it wants a price, which either returns a live readable price or reports that it has dispatched a hull and the caller should wait. Positioning, hull selection and presence-gating live entirely in the adapter.

LOAD-BEARING POLICY THAT MUST SURVIVE (sp-muc5x): the first-hauler pivot tests affordability against the last-known price BEFORE freeing the command frigate from its earning loop. Freeing the sole earner while the hauler is permanently unaffordable is a permanent stall — treasury never grows. Whether the last-known price lives in the adapter (returned as a stale-flagged value) or stays reconciler-side is the main design decision; either is acceptable if the guard still fires.

RISK: this touches the first-hauler pivot, the most-patched path in the file (four separate faults closed around it: 7r7w, 5nd2 fault-2, muc5x, hh0h). Behavior must be preserved exactly — the blockers price_unreadable and positioning_purchaser_at_shipyard, the never-free-an-unaffordable-earner guard, idempotent no-re-navigation, and the rule that the purchasing-dedicated frigate is skipped by the undedicated-hull positioner.

Money guards untouched (RULINGS 4). EXPANSION phase frozen — another session owns it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove the dead coverage_bar knob from the bootstrap coordinator
description:
coverage_bar / coverage_bar_percent / bootstrap_coverage_bar is fully plumbed (config.yaml key, prefixed launch key, bare tune key with bounds, command field, run-config field, live overlay, default fallback, startup log) but NO decision reads it: derivePhase never consults CoverageFraction against a bar, and the tune registry entry already says 'no longer gates phase progression'. Remove the whole knob.

MUST SURVIVE: Observation.CoverageFraction() — it gates deferProbeBuyToFreshsizer (>0) and feeds the heartbeat + nextAction lines. Only the BAR goes, not the metric.

Two test traps: container_ops_tune_test.go bare-key-survives-rebuild test uses coverage_bar_percent as its vehicle and must be RETARGETED to another bare key, not deleted (it guards RULINGS #2). run_bootstrap_tune_test.go inert-for-phase test goes, but its intent (coverage never flips the phase) must be preserved by a test that does not reference the knob.
close_reason: Closed

title: doWithRetry blindly re-POSTs non-idempotent MONEY calls on network error (double-spend hazard)
description: Root enabler found during sp-y2u4j: retry_policy.go classifyNetworkError marks ANY network error (including a client-side timeout of a request the server ALREADY applied — proven live: server departureTime 22:04:45.312Z, client only ever saw the retry's 4214 at 22:04:50) as retryable, and doWithRetry re-sends up to maxRetries(10) times. For navigate this produced the 4214 storm (fixed by adoption). For Buy/Sell Cargo, PurchaseShip, Refuel and other MONEY POSTs the identical mechanism means: response lost after the server applied the buy => silent RE-BUY (double spend / double sell). Frequency: ~2 navigate network-error retries per ~hour of saturated ops (metrics spacetraders_daemon_api_retries_total reason=network_error), so money-path occurrences are plausible-rare but real; a lost BuyCargo response would ALSO desync the ledger vs treasury. Candidate shapes (verify, do not assume): (a) do not blind-retry non-idempotent POSTs on network error — reconcile state first (agent credits + cargo read) then decide; (b) per-verb idempotency classification on doWithRetry; (c) at minimum, metrics + a reconcile pass for trade verbs. RULINGS #4-adjacent: guards read balances AFTER the spend, so a double-buy slips under the pre-spend guard. Evidence: retry_policy.go:48-54,126-183; sp-y2u4j investigation notes.

title: Extend 4214 server-transit adoption to the jump chain (sp-y2u4j follow-up)
description: sp-y2u4j shipped server-transit adoption (types.ErrShipInTransit + SyncShipFromAPI + route-executor wait/resume) for navigate/dock/orbit. The JUMP chain (jump_ship.go, used by scout_reposition + tour-run hop travel) still surfaces raw 4214 'ship is in transit' errors: 526 'failed to jump ship' 4214 lines in daemon.log over the log's life. Most phantom-position jumps (the 53x 4255 'not connected to current location' crashes) should dry up once the navigate-side adoption lands, since the phantom position was their source — re-measure first, then wire the same adopt-and-wait contract into jumpWithOrbitRetry / the travel executors if a material residual remains. The typed error + classifier already exist in internal/application/ship/types/in_transit_error.go.

title: Max-age filter on shipyard price reads (unlocks a longer rescan TTL)
description:
The shipyard rescan TTL is pinned at 15m ONLY because shipyard_inventory rows double as the price basis for two spend decisions, and no consumer applies any staleness filter.

reachable_yards.go NearestYardsSelling ranks on stored PurchasePrice; ProbePurchaser feeds it into QuoteProbe then MaxProbePrice, 25pct treasury cap, reserve floor, per-window spend cap. Only the treasury cap is re-checked at the live price after the relay.

autosizerYardPriceReader.scannedYardFallback returns cached prices with readable=true, which unblocks a heavy buy that otherwise fails closed, then judges guardPriceCeiling on those numbers.

Add an explicit max-age to ListByTypes / NearestYardsSelling so price-sensitive consumers reject rows older than the window and fail CLOSED. Rows already carry LastScanned, already plumbed to YardCandidate.LastScanned, currently unused by any decision. Discovery consumers (depth_objective, backfill sweep, pickReachableRecruit, stall-breaker, milestone dedup) stay unfiltered.

With that in place the scanner TTL can safely go to hours: renewal math on the measured 10.8m mean per-yard interval gives ~97pct call reduction at a 6h TTL vs ~58pct at 15m.

CAUTION: enumerate the rejected class before shipping. If every reachable yard row is stale, probe buying starves.

title: Nil-pointer panic on container shutdown: releaseShipAssignments -> SaveWithRetry, only under full-suite parallel load
description:
Surfaced by the sp-9dhxz lane during a full 'go test ./... -race' run, and explicitly NOT caused by its diff (that lane touched no ship-repo or runner code; the package passes in isolation in 17.5s under -race, and a clean full re-run passed).

SYMPTOM: nil-pointer panic in internal/adapters/grpc on the container-shutdown path — releaseShipAssignments -> tradeRouteShipRepo.SaveWithRetry, container_runner.go:1217. Intermittent; only observed under full-suite parallel load, not in package isolation.

SUSPECTED ORIGIN: a shutdown race introduced by the sp-wa7c SaveWithRetry migration (3ec730e1).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FLAKE: an intermittent panic on this path will eventually fail some unrelated lane's gate run and be attributed to that lane's diff. Two lanes today already had to spend effort proving a failure was not theirs (this panic, and a separate test-DB pollution flake in adapters/persistence where concurrent packages share a Postgres and a residual row with a colliding gate_waypoint made an under-construction guard test fail). Both are test-isolation/shutdown-ordering defects, not production-logic defects, but they cost real time to disprove under a deadline.

ALSO WORTH A ONE-LINE CLEANUP (unrelated, pre-existing on main): gofmt -l fails on gobot/internal/application/bootstrap/commands/run_bootstrap_muc5x_test.go and run_bootstrap_scaled_gate_test.go. Verified present on e3d90d53 independent of any lane's commits.
acceptance_criteria: the shutdown path cannot dereference a nil repo; full-suite -race runs are stable across repeated invocations; the two gofmt-dirty bootstrap test files are formatted

title: Tour purchase-obligation ledger is IN-MEMORY — a daemon restart forgets it and re-opens the laden-success hole sp-ekt5z just closed
description:
sp-ekt5z (merged a3ec7cb5) closed the false-SUCCESS hole by tracking, per hull, how many units of each good the tour BOUGHT and has not yet discharged, then vetoing any success exit while that obligation stands. The ledger is deliberately keyed by SHIP symbol rather than container id, precisely so it outlives the container boundary — the lane's own diagnosis was that 'a purchase forgotten across that boundary is exactly how a full hold reached a success=true exit'.

THE RESIDUAL GAP, disclosed by the lane in its own source comment: the map is IN-MEMORY ONLY. 'a daemon restart resets it (acceptable — the hull re-accrues its obligation on its next buy, and the veto is a backstop for a strand the ordinary sell path is meant to prevent, not the only guard)'.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE COMMENT ALLOWS: RULINGS #2 is unambiguous — 'Daemon restarts are ALWAYS resilient... If you add state, you persist it and reload it on boot.' This adds state and does not persist it. The exact failure the fix exists to prevent — a hull holding bought cargo when its run boundary is crossed — reopens across a DAEMON restart, because the obligation is gone while the CARGO is not. The hull is then laden with untracked cargo and the next tour can exit success on it, which is the original defect.

FREQUENCY MAKES IT REAL, NOT THEORETICAL: this shipwright restarted the daemon THREE times on 2026-07-25 alone (deploys at ~22:17Z, ~00:41Z, ~01:20Z). Restarts are a routine part of the deploy loop, not a rare event, so the window is hit often. The four heavies in sp-ekt5z were laden across exactly such a boundary.

MITIGATING (why P2 and not P1): the failure degrades to PRE-FIX behaviour, never worse — a forgotten obligation means the veto simply does not fire, which is where we were before a3ec7cb5. It is a gap in a new backstop, not a regression. And the hull re-accrues an obligation on its next purchase, so the window is bounded to cargo bought BEFORE the restart and still held after it.

WORK: persist the per-hull outstanding obligation and reload it on boot, so the veto survives the restart it was explicitly designed to survive at the container level. The natural home is the same persistence the container config/ledger already uses — do NOT invent a second store (the sp-4ki1x two-tables lesson). Keep the drop-when-settled behaviour so a discharged obligation can never linger and wedge a healthy hull, and keep the in-memory path as the fast read.
ALTERNATIVE worth costing first: derive the obligation on boot from live cargo + the transaction ledger (a hull holding units of a good it has a PURCHASE_CARGO for under tour operation, with no matching sell) instead of persisting a new structure. That may be strictly better — it self-heals, needs no new schema, and cannot drift from reality. Evaluate both and report which is cheaper before building.

RELATED: sp-ekt5z (the fix this completes), sp-vz8hj (laden hull without container, the adjacent family), sp-pcxju (buy-without-firm-sink).
acceptance_criteria: A hull holding tour-purchased cargo across a DAEMON restart still has its obligation known after boot, and a tour on that hull cannot exit success while the hold stands. Proven by a test that seeds an outstanding obligation, simulates the boot path, and asserts the veto still fires. A settled obligation is still dropped and never wedges a healthy hull. If the derive-from-ledger alternative is chosen instead of persistence, the same test bar applies and the derivation is proven to ignore cargo the hull did not buy under tour operation. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.

title: Tour candidate hop-depth should be PER-ACTIVITY, not one global cap — a global limit is set for the worst row type and throws away the 74% that could travel further
description:
ADMIRAL-REQUESTED 2026-07-25, immediately after raising candidate_hop_depth 2->3.

THE INSIGHT: the staleness model is already PER-ACTIVITY, but the travel horizon is a single GLOBAL number. Those two must agree, and today they do not — so the global cap has to be set for the WORST row type and discards the majority that could safely travel further.

THE ARITHMETIC. Inter-system travel is a fixed 30 min PER HOP (INTER_SYSTEM_TRAVEL_SECONDS = 2*GATE_HOP_ALLOWANCE(450) + JUMP_COOLDOWN(900) = 1800s, tour_solver.py:163-175). One-way travel by depth: 2=60min, 3=90min, 4=120min, 5=150min, 6=180min. Against sp-4ki1x's fitted caps (domain/trading/ranker_age_cap.go — WEAK 480, RESTRICTED 180, GROWING 60, STRONG 30) the viable depth per activity is:
  WEAK       480min -> comfortably depth 6+ 
  RESTRICTED 180min -> depth 5 (150min) fits; depth 6 (180min) is marginal
  GROWING     60min -> depth 2 (60min) marginal; depth 3+ is already expired on arrival
  STRONG      30min -> depth 1 only; a STRONG sink cannot survive even a 60min haul
WEAK + RESTRICTED are 12,825 of 17,223 live market rows = 74% of the universe. A single global cap chosen to protect STRONG rows would sit at depth 1 and forfeit that 74%; a global cap chosen for WEAK admits STRONG sinks the hull provably cannot reach in time (the sp-pcxju 'buy cargo, sink gone on arrival' class).

WHY THIS IS NOT ACADEMIC: sp-pcxju was an Admiral-flagged UNACCEPTABLE defect — buying cargo with no firm sell guarantee. Admitting a STRONG-activity sink at depth 3 structurally reintroduces it: the row is fresh at plan time and provably stale at arrival. A per-activity horizon removes that by construction rather than by hoping the global number is conservative enough.

WORK: gate a candidate sink's admission on ITS OWN activity's fitted cap versus the ACTUAL travel time to reach it (hops * per-hop seconds), instead of a single global candidate_hop_depth. Derive from the SAME cap table sp-4ki1x already reads (RankerAgeCaps) — one definition, no second copy, so a retune moves both together (this is exactly the mistake sp-4ki1x was filed to fix: two staleness models disagreeing). Reuse the existing per-pair gate_hops matrix (tour_solver.py:587-588, fed from tourInterSystemHops) for the hop count — do NOT introduce a second travel model.
Then RAISE maxCandidateHopDepth (candidates.go:22, currently 3 with the comment 'spec 2-3 gate hops') — it is an arbitrary clamp predating the fitted caps, and it is what blocks depths 4-6 today. Keep a sane absolute ceiling as a typo guard, but the real limiter becomes the per-activity check.

COMPUTE IS NOT A CONSTRAINT AT ANY DEPTH (captain probe, live snapshot, 3 most-connected homes, cap-4 RATE): depth1 0.015s / depth3 0.037s / depth6 0.088s — growth is LINEAR, and even depth 6 sits 341x under the 30s VRP timeout. Do not re-litigate solve time.

WATCH: measured freshness by hop distance off the 6 busiest hubs is hop1 62.5% / hop2 56.9% / hop3 32.1% / hop4 33.1% / hop5 43.9% / hop6 51.4%. The dip at hop3-4 is a PROBE-COVERAGE artifact, not a physical law — far systems are stale because we scan them rarely, not because distance ages data. Do not encode that curve as a rule; it moves as coverage moves.

RELATED: sp-4ki1x (shipped the fitted caps this depends on), sp-tp5c3 (shipped the per-pair travel matrix), sp-pcxju (the sink-gone-on-arrival class this prevents), sp-1cuy6 (rescoped; carries the measurements), sp-cmwge (far-sink admission, same staleness-vs-reach tension).
acceptance_criteria: A candidate sink is admitted on ITS OWN activity's fitted cap versus the actual computed travel time to reach it, not on a single global hop depth. Cap values are read from the SAME RankerAgeCaps table sp-4ki1x uses — grep-verified single definition, no second copy in Go or Python. Hop counts reuse the existing per-pair gate_hops matrix; no second travel model. RED-first tests: a WEAK sink at depth 5 is ADMITTED; a STRONG sink at depth 3 is REJECTED (travel 90min exceeds its 30min cap) even though a WEAK sink at the same depth is kept; a GROWING sink at depth 3 is REJECTED. maxCandidateHopDepth is raised with a documented absolute ceiling retained as a typo guard. A measured before/after on tour cr/hr is recorded on the bead — grade on credits, not on candidate count. Anti-theatre confirmed. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.

title: Warp explorer coordinator: hull-agnostic standing op that reaches the 106 OFF-GATE systems the gate graph cannot, mode-selecting by range and reserving return fuel
description:
ADMIRAL-REQUESTED 2026-07-25. A standing coordinator that uses warp to explore and chart the systems the gate network CANNOT reach, hunting novel markets/goods. HULL-AGNOSTIC by explicit Admiral instruction: it operates ANY hull carrying MODULE_WARP_DRIVE, never a hardcoded frame or the SHIP_EXPLORER type.

=== THE TERRITORY (measured live, era 4) ===
  982  systems known (system_coords)
  876  gate-reachable from home over TRAVERSABLE edges (under_construction=false)
  106  OFF-GATE ONLY -> unreachable by any amount of jumping. This is the coordinator's exclusive target set.
  median hop distance from the nearest gate-reachable launch point: 919
Reachability of those 106 depends ENTIRELY on the hull's tank, because warp fuel = distance x flight-mode multiplier:
  at BURN   (2x, so range = tank/2): explorer(800 tank)=400 range -> 15 of 106;  heavy(2300)=1150 range -> most
  at CRUISE (1x, range = tank):      explorer=800 -> 43 of 106;                  heavy=2300 -> nearly all
  at DRIFT  (flat ~1 fuel):          ANY hull -> ALL 106, at the cost of time
This is exactly why the coordinator must be hull-agnostic: a warp-retrofitted heavy has ~2.9x the reach of an explorer, and cargo capacity is irrelevant in a scout role.

=== MEASURED WARP MECHANICS (do not re-derive; all three confirmed against the live server) ===
  CRUISE 1.0x distance (831-distance leg required exactly 831 fuel)
  BURN   2.0x distance (572-distance leg required exactly 1144)
  DRIFT  effectively FLAT 1 fuel (an 831-distance leg cost 1 fuel: hull departed 800/800, read 799/800)
  TIME is the real cost: that 831-distance DRIFT leg took 3h12m37s (departure 00:30:46Z -> arrival 03:43:23Z).
  Warp requires the hull IN ORBIT and charts the destination system on arrival (slice-A chartOnArrival already does this — reuse it, do not reimplement).
CAUTION: internal/domain/shared/flight_mode.go's fuel AND time tables are BOTH wrong against live data (sp-xeo9s). Do NOT compute ETAs or fuel from that table until sp-xeo9s lands; use the measured values above or the server's own numbers.

=== MODE STRATEGY (the Admiral asked for BURN; BURN alone does not work) ===
BURN costs 2x fuel and therefore HALVES range — it reaches only 15 of the 106 on an explorer. Use a per-target mode CHOICE, not a fixed mode: pick the FASTEST mode whose fuel cost fits the hull's usable budget for that leg (BURN if affordable, else CRUISE, else DRIFT). DRIFT is the universal fallback that makes every target reachable. Record the chosen mode in the heartbeat so the operator can see why a leg was slow.

=== THE HARD INTERACTION — sp-iierd's onward-viability guard WILL REFUSE MOST OF THESE TARGETS ===
sp-iierd (merged bd3c4aaa, LIVE) added a fail-closed guard that refuses a warp whose destination has NEITHER a reachable fuel seller NOR a BUILT gate — precisely to stop a hull stranding. Most of the 106 off-gate systems are uncharted and will have neither. So a naive coordinator is refused on nearly every target. DO NOT weaken or bypass that guard (RULINGS #4).
THE RESOLUTION IS ROUND-TRIP FUEL RESERVATION — the 'third escape' sp-iierd's lane explicitly flagged as missing: a hull is not stranded if it departs holding enough fuel to warp BACK OUT. In DRIFT this is trivially cheap (~1 fuel out, ~1 fuel back), so a full-tank hull can reach any of the 106 and still return. Design the coordinator to compute and RESERVE the return leg before dispatching, and extend the viability guard to accept 'provable return capability' as a third escape alongside fuel-at-destination and a built gate. That extension belongs in the guard (so it stays fail-closed and benefits every warp caller), NOT as a coordinator-local bypass.

=== SCOPE ===
1. Target selection over the OFF-GATE set: rank the 106 by expected discovery value (virgin > known-but-unscanned; nearer first at equal value), skipping targets already charted with markets. Reuse the frontier coordinator's ranking shape where it fits rather than inventing a second scoring model.
2. Hull selection: ANY idle hull with MODULE_WARP_DRIVE installed, never a frame/type check. Respect RULINGS #7 ownership — claim via the atomic ClaimShip occupancy path like every other coordinator; never poach a dedicated hull.
3. Per-leg mode + fuel plan: choose mode by affordability, reserve the return leg, dispatch, chart on arrival.
4. Standing reconciler shape (MECHANICS 2): observe -> derive -> act, idempotent per tick, fail-closed on unreadable inputs, one-line heartbeat (target, mode, fuel plan, blocker). Restart-resilient per RULINGS #2 — state persisted or re-derivable.
5. RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING CODE: sp-0xd0 slice C already has an explorer dispatch (internal/adapters/expansion/explorer_dispatch_adapter.go) that warps a bought explorer to an off-gate target via ExecuteWarpRoute. EXTEND/REUSE that seam rather than building a parallel one — and REPORT whether this coordinator should absorb it or sit alongside the frontier-expansion coordinator. Do not silently duplicate frontier's job.

=== ECONOMIC HONESTY (context, not a blocker) ===
This is a DISCOVERY play, not a $/hr play. We currently have 764 gate-reachable systems with NO markets scanned — 7x more unexploited territory reachable fast by jumping than warp could ever add. So this coordinator should run at LOW priority against the fleet's API budget and must never contend with revenue operations. Its payoff is optionality (novel goods/markets nothing else can see), not throughput.
acceptance_criteria: A standing coordinator claims ANY idle MODULE_WARP_DRIVE-equipped hull (proven by a test with a NON-explorer frame — hull-agnosticism is the Admiral's explicit requirement and must be pinned, not assumed), selects an off-gate target, chooses the fastest AFFORDABLE flight mode for that leg, reserves return fuel, dispatches the warp, and charts the arrival system. A target whose round trip cannot be afforded is REFUSED (fail closed), not attempted. The sp-iierd onward-viability guard is EXTENDED to accept provable return capability as a third escape — in the guard itself, not bypassed in the coordinator — with a test proving a destination lacking fuel AND a built gate is still refused when the return leg is NOT affordable. Idempotent per tick, restart-resilient, one-line heartbeat naming target/mode/blocker. No flag, ships ARMED. RED-first; anti-theatre confirmed. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.

title: flight_mode.go's fuel AND time tables are both wrong against live data — they feed fuel/ETA estimates across the whole codebase, not just warp
description:
internal/domain/shared/flight_mode.go:23-27 holds the fleet's model of every flight mode:
  CRUISE  {TimeMultiplier 31, FuelRate 1.0}
  DRIFT   {TimeMultiplier 26, FuelRate 0.003}
  BURN    {TimeMultiplier 15, FuelRate 2.0}
  STEALTH {TimeMultiplier 50, FuelRate 1.0}
Measured live 2026-07-25 against the SpaceTraders server, the FUEL column is right for CRUISE/BURN and wrong for DRIFT, and the TIME column is wrong by more than an order of magnitude.

FUEL — three live measurements:
  CRUISE 1.0x CONFIRMED: an 831-distance warp required exactly 831 (API 4203, fuelRequired=831).
  BURN   2.0x CONFIRMED: a 572-distance warp required exactly 1144 (API 4203, fuelRequired=1144).
  DRIFT  WRONG: the table predicts ceil(831 * 0.003) = 3 fuel. ACTUAL COST WAS 1 FUEL (TORWIND-F6 departed an 831 leg at 800/800 and reads 799/800). Either the rate is far below 0.003 or DRIFT is a FLAT 1 fuel, in which case the function's own 'if cost < 1 { return 1 }' floor is the entire rule. A second DRIFT measurement at a very different distance separates the two hypotheses — if a ~200 leg and a ~2000 leg both cost 1, it is flat.

TIME — badly wrong:
  TravelTime = distance * TimeMultiplier / engineSpeed. For the measured leg (831 distance, DRIFT, ENGINE_ION_DRIVE_II speed 36) it predicts 831*26/36 = 600 s.
  ACTUAL: departure 00:30:46.623Z -> arrival 03:43:23.623Z = 11,557 s. That is ~19x the prediction. Back-solving the multiplier gives ~500, not 26.
  The ordering is also suspect on its face: the table makes DRIFT (26) FASTER than CRUISE (31), inverting the game's semantics — DRIFT is the slow/cheap mode and should be the SLOWEST of the three, not the middle.

BLAST RADIUS — this is why it is not a warp bug: FuelCost and TravelTime are domain-level helpers. Any consumer estimating fuel or ETA from this table inherits the error. Enumerate every caller of FlightMode.FuelCost and FlightMode.TravelTime BEFORE changing the values, and report the list — a table correction silently changes behaviour everywhere it is read, which is exactly the 'awakened config' hazard where one edit is a fleet-wide behaviour change.

WORK: re-fit both columns against live measurements rather than guessing. Fuel needs one more DRIFT data point (and a STEALTH point if any consumer uses it). Time needs several legs across modes and engine speeds, since the 19x gap suggests the formula SHAPE may be wrong, not just its constant — warp/inter-system travel may not use the same time law as in-system navigation at all. Do NOT 'fix' by scaling the multiplier until the shape is confirmed on more than one leg.

DATA CAPTURED SO FAR (use it, do not re-spend API budget re-deriving): 831 distance / DRIFT / ION_DRIVE_II speed 36 => 1 fuel, 11,557 s. 831 / CRUISE => 831 fuel required. 572 / BURN => 1144 fuel required.
RELATED: sp-tvjzo (where these measurements were recorded), sp-iierd (the warp guard that should stop predicting fuel locally at all).
acceptance_criteria: FlightMode.FuelCost and FlightMode.TravelTime are re-fitted against live measurements, with each mode's values traceable to a recorded observation rather than a guess. The DRIFT flat-1-vs-tiny-rate question is settled by a second measurement at a materially different distance. Every caller of FuelCost and TravelTime is enumerated in the report with an assessment of how the corrected values change its behaviour. A test pins each mode's fuel cost to its measured value so a future silent drift fails loudly. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.

title: Warp container burns its full restart budget retrying PERMANENT API refusals (4203 insufficient fuel), holding the hull claim and blocking every other operation on that ship
description:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-07-24 23:28-23:32Z during the sp-nhr0g first-warp experiment.

A warp refused by the server for insufficient fuel (HTTP 400, code 4203, 'requires 31 more fuel for navigation', fuelRequired=831 fuelAvailable=800) is a PERMANENT condition for that (ship, destination, fuel-state) triple — no amount of retrying changes it. The warp container nonetheless retried it across its full restart budget (MaxRestartAttempts=3, ~5s backoff between attempts) before finally logging 'Container crashed (unrecoverable)' and 'Released 1 ship assignments (reason: failed)'. Elapsed from first refusal (23:28:52) to claim release (23:32:10) was ~3.5 minutes.

TWO COSTS: (1) each retry spends real API budget on a call that CANNOT succeed — and this fired while the account was already near its rate limit; (2) the hull stays CLAIMED for the whole retry window, so every other operation on it fails. Concretely: a 'ship route' issued at 23:30:37 lost the claim-handoff race 7 times and died with 'ship TORWIND-F6 is already assigned to container warp-TORWIND-F6-d5308de0', purely because the doomed warp was still retrying.

This is the pattern MECHANICS §1 already warns about: 'A coordinator that hits a transient dead-end must NOT return an error the runner burns its restart budget on.' Here the inverse applies — a PERMANENT dead-end is being treated as retryable. The restart budget exists for transient faults (5xx, network, rate-limit), not for a deterministic 4xx refusal.

FIX DIRECTION: classify the API error before deciding retryability. A terminal 4xx refusal (the ship cannot do this, as opposed to a transient failure) should terminalize the container IMMEDIATELY and release the claim, rather than consuming restart attempts. The codebase already has this exact distinction — isPermanentGateAbsence (gategraph/service.go:511) uses errors.As on *ports.APIError plus IsClientError() to separate a permanent 4xx verdict from a transient failure that never surfaces as a typed APIError. Reuse that classification rather than inventing a second one, and keep the failure path fail-CLOSED (a refused warp must still refuse — this is only about how FAST it gives up and releases).

SCOPE NOTE: likely not warp-specific. Any single-shot ship-op container that surfaces a deterministic 4xx will behave the same way. Check whether the shared container runner should own this classification rather than each op — but do NOT broaden the blast radius without evidence; start with the warp path where it is observed, and REPORT what else shares the code path.

RELATED: sp-nhr0g (added the warp verb; this was found using it), sp-iierd (the guard SHOULD have refused this leg locally and never reached the API at all — with sp-iierd fixed, this particular 4203 would not occur, but the retry-a-permanent-error class remains).
acceptance_criteria: A warp refused with a deterministic 4xx (e.g. 4203 insufficient fuel) terminalizes on the FIRST refusal: the container goes to FAILED and releases its ship assignment without consuming further restart attempts, and issues no further API calls. A TRANSIENT failure (5xx/network/rate-limit) still retries as it does today — proven by a test for each class. The refusal is still surfaced to the operator in the container log with its typed fields intact (no regression to sp-nhr0g's error surfacing). A subsequent operation on the same hull succeeds immediately after the refusal rather than losing a claim-handoff race. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.

title: replay_hopwiden_TEMP.py bakes STALENESS_MINUTES=75 — the replay harness cannot measure sp-4ki1x's own fix, and will silently under-report every hop-depth answer
description:
sp-4ki1x changed the tour path to pass the WIDEST activity-fitted cap (RankerAgeCaps.Widest()) instead of the flat 75min as the solver's snapshot-age backstop. The replay harness that measures tour/hop-depth outcomes reconstructs its snapshots with STALENESS_MINUTES=75 hardcoded (replay_hopwiden_TEMP.py:55), so it still models the PRE-FIX world: every replay silently discards exactly the WEAK/RESTRICTED rows the fix recovers.

CONSEQUENCE: (1) we cannot replay-measure sp-4ki1x's own gain — the harness reproduces the defect it is meant to score; (2) any hop-depth/candidate-widening answer produced by this harness is biased LOW for far systems, because far-system rows are precisely the ones aged past 75min (measured live: freshness by gate-hop from our 6 busiest hubs runs hop1 62.5% down to hop3 32.1%). That is the same bias sp-1cuy6's depth sweep was subject to.

WORK: parameterize the staleness value (accept the caps table or an explicit minutes argument rather than a module-level constant), so a replay can model both the pre-fix flat-75 world and the post-fix fitted-cap world and DIFF them. Keep ONE definition of the cap table (Go domain/trading/ranker_age_cap.go is authoritative) — do not hardcode a second copy of the fitted values in Python.

NOTE ON THE FILE: replay_hopwiden_TEMP.py is UNTRACKED in the working tree (a _TEMP analysis script, not committed source). Decide as part of this bead whether it graduates into the repo as a real harness or stays a scratch tool; an untracked measurement tool that gates real decisions is itself a risk — it can vanish with a checkout and takes its methodology with it.

ORIGIN: flagged in sp-4ki1x's own validation bar ('Replay first: ... that harness must be parameterized or it will not be able to measure the fix'); the sp-4ki1x lane did not do it. RELATED: sp-4ki1x (merged 4508307b), sp-1cuy6 (hop-depth sweep — re-run AFTER sp-4ki1x deploys AND this harness is fixed, or the sweep repeats the bias).
acceptance_criteria: The replay harness accepts the staleness model as a parameter and can reproduce BOTH the flat-75 baseline and the fitted-cap behaviour, with the fitted values sourced from the Go cap table rather than re-declared in Python. A diff run over the same input snapshot shows a non-zero difference in admitted rows between the two modes, proving the harness is actually sensitive to the knob. A decision is recorded on this bead about whether the harness graduates into tracked source.

title: Trade watchdog livelocks on a COMPLETED container: 'cannot stop container in COMPLETED state' retries forever and the hull stays stranded FULL (TORWIND-F, 80/80, cargo bought 59min ago, never sold)
description:
LIVE 2026-07-24 22:07Z, player 4. A trade hull is permanently stranded holding cargo it bought and never sold — the exact condition the Admiral ruled unacceptable ('we absolutely cannot buy cargo and not sell it') — because the fleet watchdog's recovery path cannot act on a COMPLETED container and retries the same failing kill forever instead of releasing the hull.

=== SYMPTOM (live-verified) ===
TORWIND-F (FRAME_LIGHT_FREIGHTER, dedicated_fleet=trade, assignment_owner=container):
 * DOCKED at X1-KQ55-AC7X, cargo 80/80 FULL — 40 LAB_INSTRUMENTS + 6 AI_MAINFRAMES + 22 BIOCOMPOSITES
 * last PURCHASE_CARGO 59 min ago; last SELL_CARGO 70 min ago (i.e. it bought, then never sold) ; REFUEL 25 min ago
 * NO container of any type is listed on the hull (container list shows zero tour-run-TORWIND-F-*)
 * It is the ONLY stranded hull right now — swept all trade hulls with cargo>0 and no running container: TORWIND-F is the only hit. Not (yet) spreading.

=== THE LIVELOCK (daemon.log, verbatim) ===
[2026-07-24T19:07:17-03:00] [trade_fleet_coordinator-player-4-2cf82186] WARNING: Trade fleet watchdog: failed to kill hung container tour-run-TORWIND-F-52ea6fe2 on TORWIND-F: cannot stop container in COMPLETED state
Repeating every ~31s. 22 occurrences, first at 18:57:19-03:00, still firing at 19:08:19-03:00 (~11 min and counting). Always the SAME container id (tour-run-TORWIND-F-52ea6fe2), always the same error.

=== READING (confirmed vs inferred) ===
CONFIRMED: the watchdog classifies TORWIND-F as hung (no progress past the stall threshold), attempts to stop tour-run-TORWIND-F-52ea6fe2, and the stop is REJECTED because the container is already in COMPLETED state. The watchdog does not give up, does not fall through to a release/relaunch, and does not stop retrying.
INFERRED (needs code confirmation): the hull stays in limbo because assignment_owner is still 'container' pointing at the dead/COMPLETED container, so (a) the watchdog's recovery is gated behind a successful kill that can never succeed, and (b) the fleet coordinator's normal idle-hull discovery does not re-claim it because it is not 'idle'. Net: neither path can ever recover the hull, and it holds bought cargo indefinitely.

=== WHY THIS MATTERS ===
* It is a PERMANENT strand, not a transient gap. Other hulls seen orphaned tonight (TORWIND-57, -83, -E) all self-healed within one coordinator tick; F has now persisted 20+ min across two checks and the log shows the mechanism that prevents recovery.
* It defeats sp-pcxju's guarantee at the fleet level: sp-pcxju correctly gates the BUY on a firm sink, but nothing re-drives a hull whose container COMPLETED while still laden, so the cargo is bought-and-never-sold anyway via a different route.
* It is silent to the throughput metrics — the fleet reads healthy (net-positive, cycling) while one hull is dead weight holding 80 units.

=== FIX DIRECTION ===
1. The watchdog's kill step must treat 'container already COMPLETED/terminal' as SUCCESS-equivalent (the container is, after all, no longer running) and proceed to the recovery it was going to do anyway — release the ship assignment and let the fleet coordinator relaunch. Today a terminal-state container is treated as a hard failure that aborts recovery.
2. Make the retry BOUNDED and escalate: an identical kill failure repeating on the same container id must not loop forever at 31s intervals. After N attempts, force-release the assignment (or mark the container reclaimable) and log/count it — a permanently-failing recovery must never be indefinitely silent-retrying.
3. Add a laden-hull-without-a-running-container sweep: any hull with cargo>0, dedicated_fleet set, and no RUNNING container is by definition stranded and must be re-driven (or its assignment released) regardless of WHY its container went away. That is the fail-safe that would have caught this independent of the COMPLETED-state bug.
4. Check the same path for the shared watchdog (sp-m3122 serves BOTH trade tours and long-haul) — if the kill/recovery seam is shared, long-haul has the same livelock.

=== RELATED ===
Same family as the container-contention/orphan issues seen tonight; distinct root (terminal-state kill rejection, not contention). Note also the captain memory: manual 'ship navigate' spawns persistent navigate-<ship> containers — any manual rescue of F must stop those afterwards.
notes:
=== CAPTAIN CORRECTION 2026-07-24 22:27Z — SEVERITY OVERSTATED ABOVE; RECOVERY IS DELAYED, NOT IMPOSSIBLE ===
I wrote 'PERMANENT strand' and inferred 'neither path can ever recover the hull'. FALSIFIED by observation 20 min later: TORWIND-F now HAS a running tour container again and is IN_TRANSIT. The fleet coordinator's normal relaunch path DID eventually re-drive the hull, independently of the watchdog's failing kill. So the hull is not unrecoverable — my inference about assignment_owner blocking re-claim was wrong, or at least not the whole story. Correcting the record rather than leaving shipwright to chase a phantom.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND STILL WORTH FIXING:
1. THE ZOMBIE RETRY LOOP IS REAL AND ONGOING. The watchdog has now logged 38 identical failures (was 22 at first report, +16 in 20 min, ~31s cadence) against the SAME dead container — verified all 38 lines are tour-run-TORWIND-F-52ea6fe2, so it is NOT rotating across hulls; it is one container retried forever. It kept firing even AFTER the hull was successfully relaunched onto a NEW container, i.e. the watchdog is retrying a container that is both COMPLETED and superseded. Nothing ever clears it. Fix items (1) treat terminal-state as success-equivalent and (2) bound the retry / escalate still stand, and (2) is the important one — an identical failure repeating forever is a defect regardless of blast radius.
2. THE HULL WAS STRANDED ~25+ MIN HOLDING BOUGHT CARGO (observed full+containerless across two consecutive 20-min checks, purchase 59 min before first observation, no sell in the 20 min after either). Recovery happened but was slow and was NOT driven by the watchdog that exists to catch exactly this. So the watchdog is not doing its job here even though the system self-healed by another route.
3. Fix item (3) — the laden-hull-without-a-running-container sweep — remains the right fail-safe, now justified by 'recovery took 25+ min' rather than 'recovery never happens'.
REVISED SEVERITY: keep P1 for the unbounded futile retry loop + the watchdog failing its purpose; the cargo-strand consequence is DELAYED RECOVERY (~25 min), not indefinite loss.
UNRELATED SIGHTING (not this bug): TORWIND-B briefly showed 38/80 with no container at 22:27 — partial cargo, IN_ORBIT at X1-AT85-D18A; consistent with the ordinary between-tours gap that self-heals in a tick, not the COMPLETED-state livelock (the log shows zero kill-failures for any B container).
=== SECOND INSTANCE, DIFFERENT MECHANISM — 2026-07-24 22:47Z — strengthens fail-safe item (3) ===
TORWIND-B (light freighter) is stranded laden with NO container of any type: 38/80 cargo (18 SHIP_PARTS + 18 SHIP_PLATING), IN_ORBIT at X1-AT85-D18A, last buy AND last sell both 37 min ago, observed containerless across TWO consecutive 20-min checks (22:27 and 22:47) — past the one-tick self-heal window.
MECHANISM IS NOT THE COMPLETED-STATE LIVELOCK: zero watchdog kill-failures logged for any TORWIND-B container (all 38 livelock lines remain TORWIND-F-52ea6fe2). B's own last log line is the cause: '[tour-run-TORWIND-B-c7621399] INFO: Released 1 ship assignments (reason: failed)'. Its tour FAILED, cleanly released the hull, and nothing re-claimed it for 20+ min while it holds bought cargo.
=> TWO different routes now produce the same end state (laden hull, no running container, cargo bought and unsold): (a) F — watchdog cannot kill a COMPLETED container, recovery delayed ~25 min; (b) B — tour exits 'failed', releases the hull, no re-claim for 20+ min. This is the strongest argument yet for fix item (3), the MECHANISM-AGNOSTIC sweep: any hull with cargo>0, dedicated_fleet set, and no RUNNING container must be re-driven (or explicitly released) regardless of how it got there. Fixing only the COMPLETED-state kill would NOT have caught B.
LIVELOCK STATUS: frozen at 38 lines — no new failures since 22:27, so the F retry loop DID eventually stop rather than run forever. Correcting my 'retries forever' framing again: it is unbounded-until-something-clears-it, not literally infinite. Item (2) (bound the retry + escalate) still stands but is lower severity than first written.
FALSE POSITIVE TO IGNORE: TORWIND-AF appeared in my stranded sweep this check at 225/225 but actually HAS a RUNNING container (tour-run-TORWIND-AF-4fb3088a, actively pre-positioning) — artifact of a race between two container-list calls in my sweep, not a real strand. Any implementation of item (3) must read container state ONCE atomically per sweep, or it will produce the same false positives.
=== THIRD INSTANCE + PATTERN CONFIRMED — 2026-07-24 23:07Z — this is recurring, not isolated ===
TORWIND-AF (HEAVY, cap 225) is now stranded FULL: 225/225, IN_ORBIT at X1-CD11-E12D, NO container of any type, last sell 55 min ago. Confirmed with a SINGLE atomic container read (I had wrongly dismissed AF last check as a container-list race — that call was WRONG; with the atomic read it still flags, and a direct per-ship query confirms zero containers).
MECHANISM 3 (again distinct): AF's last log line is '[tour-run-TORWIND-AF-4b32e4b9] INFO: Retrying after error in 2m0s (attempt 3)' — note the container id differs from the 4fb3088a that was RUNNING 20 min earlier, i.e. AF was relaunched, the new tour hit repeated errors, exhausted its retries, and vanished leaving the hull laden. Zero watchdog kill-failures for any AF container (all 38 livelock lines remain TORWIND-F).
RUNNING TALLY — 3 hulls, 3 DIFFERENT routes, ~1 hour, all ending in the identical state (laden hull, no RUNNING container, cargo bought and unsold):
  F  (light, 80/80)   — watchdog could not kill a COMPLETED container; recovery delayed ~25 min, eventually self-healed.
  B  (light, 38/80)   — tour exited 'Released 1 ship assignments (reason: failed)'; STILL stranded across THREE consecutive checks (22:27, 22:47, 23:07) = 40+ min, no re-claim.
  AF (HEAVY, 225/225) — tour exhausted retries after repeated errors; stranded ~20 min so far, holding a FULL heavy load.
TWO CONCURRENTLY STRANDED RIGHT NOW (B + AF). This is no longer a one-off: it is a recurring class with multiple independent entry points, and per-mechanism fixes will keep missing new ones. ELEVATES fix item (3) — the mechanism-agnostic laden-hull sweep — from 'belt-and-suspenders' to THE PRIMARY FIX. Recommend implementing (3) first and treating (1)/(2) as cleanup.
MEASUREMENT NOTE for whoever implements (3): read container state ONCE atomically per sweep (my non-atomic version produced a false positive on AF at 22:47), and treat 'no RUNNING container' as the trigger — F/B/AF each had containers in different terminal states (COMPLETED / released-failed / retry-exhausted), so keying on any single terminal state misses the others.
FLEET IMPACT: the load distribution reads 14/19 FULL, but 2 of those 'full' hulls (AF 225/225, B 38/80) are stranded, not cycling — so strands are inflating the full count and masking as clogging in the throughput view.
=== MAJOR CORRECTION 2026-07-24 23:30Z — MY DETECTION METHOD WAS PRODUCING FALSE POSITIVES; SEVERITY DROPS AGAIN ===
At 23:27 my sweep reported SIXTEEN stranded hulls. That was WRONG. tour-run containers had momentarily collapsed 16 -> 1 during a coordinator relaunch cycle; 45s later the count was back to 18, and BOTH hulls I had escalated (TORWIND-B and TORWIND-AF) now hold RUNNING containers (tour-run-TORWIND-B-decff366, tour-run-TORWIND-AF-4b32e4b9). Treasury simultaneously JUMPED +3.4M on 6.2M of sells — i.e. tours were COMPLETING SUCCESSFULLY and exiting, which is exactly when a point-in-time sweep sees hulls containerless.
ROOT OF MY ERROR: 'cargo>0 AND no RUNNING container' sampled at ONE INSTANT is not a strand signal. The coordinator continuously tears down and relaunches tours, so any single sample catches a variable number of hulls mid-cycle. Atomicity (which I added) does NOT fix this — the race is not between my two CLI calls, it is between my sample and the coordinator's relaunch cycle.
WHAT SURVIVES AS REAL:
 * The COMPLETED-state kill failure is REAL and verbatim-logged (38 identical lines, 'cannot stop container in COMPLETED state', one container, ~31s cadence, ~19 min). It stopped on its own and TORWIND-F recovered. Fix items (1) treat terminal state as success-equivalent and (2) bound the retry still stand as correctness/noise defects.
 * TORWIND-B genuinely sat laden across THREE consecutive 20-min checks (40+ min) with no sells — that persistence is the only observation that survives the false-positive critique, and even B has now recovered on its own.
WHAT I RETRACT: the 'three hulls, three mechanisms, recurring class' framing and the claim that item (3) should be THE PRIMARY FIX. F/B/AF each recovered without intervention. There is no evidence of permanent or systemic stranding.
REVISED RECOMMENDATION: DOWNGRADE to P2/P3. The defensible defect is the unbounded futile retry loop on a terminal-state container (noise + a watchdog not doing its job), not fleet-wide cargo stranding. If item (3) is implemented at all, its trigger MUST be persistence-based (laden + no running container ACROSS N consecutive ticks + no sell in that window), never a single sample — otherwise it will fire on every normal relaunch cycle, exactly as my sweep did.
CAPTAIN LESSON (for the record): I escalated three times on point-in-time samples and had to walk each back. Persistence across independent samples is the minimum bar for calling something stranded in this system.
=== NEW REPRODUCIBLE INSTANCE + THE EXACT MECHANISM (captain, 2026-07-25 04:35Z) ===
A manual 'spacetraders ship navigate' produces the SAME unrecoverable-hull state this bead describes, via a clean path, and I reproduced it 10x tonight while hand-dispersing the fleet.
SEQUENCE: manual navigate spawns navigate-<ship>-<hash>.
