title: warpFuelCost is an unvalidated guess (cruise rate, 1 fuel/distance) — every warp strand-refusal rests on it, and it has never met the live API
description:
route_executor_warp.go:49-55 computes warp fuel LOCALLY to avoid an API round-trip: 'warpFuelCost(distance) = shared.FlightModeCruise.FuelCost(distance)' — 1 fuel per distance unit, floored at 1. The comment states the assumption plainly: warp is costed 'at the CRUISE rate ... the same baseline navigate uses'. Nothing has ever checked that against the live server.

WHY IT MATTERS: this single constant is the sole input to ensureWarpFuelSafety (:216-256), the guard the slice describes as 'the key safety property'. Its four branches (cost>tank -> refuse; enough fuel -> proceed; short+fuel at origin -> top off; short+no fuel -> refuse) are all computed from it BEFORE any API call. If real warp fuel is CHEAPER than cruise, we over-refuse (merely wasteful — targets look unreachable that are not). If real warp fuel is DEARER than cruise, we UNDER-refuse and warp a hull into the exact strand the guard exists to prevent — off the gate network, out of fuel, possibly with no fuel station in the destination system. That is a hull-loss-class failure, and it fails OPEN, which is the wrong direction for a guard (RULINGS #4).

The spec (openapi.json, POST /my/ships/{shipSymbol}/warp) says only 'Warping will consume the necessary fuel from the ship's manifest' — it does NOT publish the rate, so the spec alone cannot settle this. The warp RESPONSE, however, carries post-warp fuel state (the executor already folds it back via UpdateFuelFromAPI at :168, and client_warp_test.go:62 asserts a 520/800 fuel parse), so ONE real warp yields the true cost as a measured delta.

WORK: before any production warp is ever dispatched, validate the constant on a SHORT leg with a full tank and compare predicted warpFuelCost(distance) against the observed fuel delta from the API response. If they diverge, correct the model and re-derive the guard's thresholds. Until validated, the safest posture is to treat the strand guard as calibrated-unknown and prefer over-refusal. Note this is currently UNREACHABLE in practice (no hull carries a warp drive, no market sells one) — so this bead gates the FIRST warp, not today's fleet.

BLOCKED BY: the warp-acquisition bead (no drive = no way to measure). File the measurement as the first action taken the moment a warp-capable hull exists.
acceptance_criteria: A short real warp leg is executed with a full tank and the predicted warpFuelCost is compared against the observed fuel delta parsed from the warp response; the measured rate is recorded on this bead. If the model is wrong it is corrected and ensureWarpFuelSafety's thresholds re-derived, with a test pinning the corrected rate. If the model is right it is documented as VERIFIED with the measurement cited, so no future reader re-opens the question. In either case the strand guard is proven to fail CLOSED at the corrected rate (RULINGS #4) via a test that a leg exceeding a full tank is still refused before any API call.
notes:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-07-24 23:29Z — warpFuelCost's RATE ASSUMPTION IS VALIDATED, but its DISTANCE INPUT is wrong (see sp-iierd).

THE MEASUREMENT: attempted warp TORWIND-F6 (FRAME_EXPLORER, MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I, 800/800 fuel) X1-YY85-ZD2D -> X1-FD3-A36F. The live API refused:
  400, code 4203: 'Ship TORWIND-F6 requires 31 more fuel for navigation.'
  data: fuelRequired=831, fuelAvailable=800

fuelRequired = 831 is EXACTLY the era-4 system_coords Euclidean distance X1-YY85(18099,10194) -> X1-FD3, which I had computed as 831 before firing. So:

1) THE CRUISE-RATE MODEL IS CORRECT. warpFuelCost = FlightModeCruise.FuelCost(distance) = 1 fuel per distance unit is CONFIRMED against the live server, at least at this magnitude. The assumption this bead was filed to question is SOUND — do not change the rate.
2) THE DISTANCE IS INTER-SYSTEM. The server prices the leg on system-to-system separation, confirming that ensureWarpFuelSafety's use of waypoint-local coords is measuring the wrong quantity entirely (sp-iierd).
3) THE GUARD FAILED OPEN, EMPIRICALLY. Our guard did NOT refuse this leg — the container logged 'Warping ... (off-gate)' and went to the API, which is what rejected it. A guard whose entire purpose is refusing an unaffordable leg let an unaffordable leg through to the server. That is no longer a code-trace hypothesis; it is observed behaviour.

COST OF THE EXPERIMENT: zero. The refusal is pre-flight server-side, the hull never moved, fuel unchanged at 800/800.

SO THIS BEAD NARROWS: the rate needs no correction. What remains is (a) fixing the distance input (sp-iierd owns that), and (b) re-validating end-to-end AFTER that fix, since a correct rate on a wrong distance is still a broken guard. Recommend sp-iierd and this bead land and be validated TOGETHER.

STILL UNMEASURED: warp transit TIME and whether warp incurs a COOLDOWN (jump does). An ACCEPTED warp returns an ETA in its response, so one successful short leg answers both without waiting for arrival.

SAFETY FINDING WORTH KEEPING: 'gate_connected' in gate_edges does NOT mean traversable. X1-TY66 is the only system within a full 800 tank of X1-YY85 and reads as gate-connected, but its gate X1-TY66-I58 has under_construction=true. Warping there (515 fuel, arriving with 285, no fuel market, no usable gate) would have STRANDED the hull. Any warp target selection MUST check under_construction on the escape gate, not just adjacency.
DRIFT WARP MEASURED LIVE 2026-07-25 00:30Z — the complete fuel model is now established, and flight_mode.go is WRONG on both axes.

THE SUCCESSFUL WARP (first ever executed by this fleet): TORWIND-F6, X1-YY85-C19X -> X1-FD3-A36F, inter-system distance 831 (era-4 system_coords), flightMode DRIFT.
  departure 2026-07-25T00:30:46.623Z ; arrival 2026-07-25T03:43:23.623Z
  fuel AFTER departure: 799/800  =>  the leg cost EXACTLY 1 FUEL.
  transit: 3h 12m 37s (11,557 s) for 831 distance.

COMPLETE MEASURED FUEL MODEL (all three against the live server):
  CRUISE : 1.0x distance  -> 831 required (refused at 800 available; code 4203)
  BURN   : 2.0x distance  -> 1144 required for a 572 leg (refused at 798)
  DRIFT  : ~FLAT 1 FUEL   -> 1 fuel for an 831 leg
So FUEL IS NOT A CONSTRAINT ON WARP RANGE. In DRIFT, warp reach is effectively unbounded and the only cost is TIME.

flight_mode.go IS WRONG ON BOTH AXES (internal/domain/shared/flight_mode.go:23-27):
  (a) FUEL: DRIFT is modelled at FuelRate 0.003, predicting ceil(831*0.003)=3 fuel. ACTUAL is 1. Either the rate is far lower or DRIFT is a flat 1 (the code's own 'if cost < 1 return 1' floor would then be the whole rule). Needs a second data point at a very different distance to separate 'flat 1' from 'tiny rate'.
  (b) TIME: TravelTime = distance * TimeMultiplier / engineSpeed. For this leg that predicts 831*26/36 = 600 s. ACTUAL was 11,557 s — ~19x the model. Back-solving gives an effective multiplier near 500, not 26. Note also the table's ordering is suspect on its face: it lists DRIFT 26 as FASTER than CRUISE 31, which inverts the game's own semantics (DRIFT is the slow/cheap mode).
This table feeds fuel and ETA estimates ACROSS the codebase, not just warp — file a separate bead to re-fit it against live data before anything else trusts it.

STRATEGIC VERDICT (the question that motivated all of this): WARP IS NOT A FREIGHT ACCELERATOR. The long-haul heavies covered comparable distance via ~10 gate hops at ~7.5 min cooldown each, ~75 minutes total. DRIFT warp took 3h12m for 831 distance. Where a gate path exists, JUMPING WINS DECISIVELY. Warp's real value is reaching systems the gate graph does NOT connect (X1-FD3 has no gate edge to X1-YY85 at all) — i.e. discovery/frontier expansion, which is exactly what sp-0xd0's slice-C explorer dispatcher was built for. Retrofitting a 1.7M heavy for warp trades cargo capacity for a slower route to places our trade lanes do not serve.

NOTE ON THE GUARD: the run also showed the guard's ORCHESTRATION half working correctly — it logged 'Warp fuel-safety: topping off before leg', refuelled to 800, then warped. That half is worth KEEPING (sp-iierd pin 2). It was the local PREDICTION half that was broken.

title: Warp capability is unreachable: MODULE_WARP_DRIVE is a tradeable good but stocked in 0 of our 2,974 scanned markets — sp-0xd0's three slices are dead code until one is acquired
description:
AUTHORITATIVE MECHANIC (gobot/api/openapi.json, POST /my/ships/{shipSymbol}/warp): 'The ship must be in orbit to use this function and must have the Warp Drive module installed. Warping will consume the necessary fuel from the ship's manifest.' So warp is MODULE-borne, not engine-borne, and gategraph's HasWarpDrive() check (domain/navigation/ship.go:299 -> ship_module.go:58, prefix MODULE_WARP_DRIVE) is CORRECT. An 'it checks the wrong field' hypothesis was raised and REFUTED against the spec — do not re-litigate.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER — ACQUISITION, not code. MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I/II/III ARE tradeable (they sit in the spec's 145-entry TradeSymbol enum alongside MODULE_JUMP_DRIVE_I/II/III), so they are purchasable in principle. But live market_data carries ZERO rows for MODULE_WARP_DRIVE* or MODULE_JUMP_DRIVE* across 17,225 rows / 2,974 markets. Our scanning DOES capture modules generally (MODULE_CARGO_HOLD_I-III, MODULE_SHIELD_GENERATOR_I/II, MODULE_SCIENCE_LAB_I etc. all appear in 9-25 markets each), so drives are simply a RARE good we have not yet found — not a category our scanner misses.

COVERAGE CONTEXT: we hold markets in 259 systems against 979 systems known from era-4 gate_edges = 26.5% of the known universe scanned. The drive almost certainly exists in the unscanned 73.5%.

CONSEQUENCE: sp-0xd0 shipped three slices (A execute: route_executor_warp.go / warp_navigator.go / warp_system_charter.go; B off-gate target selection; C explorer dispatch, wired main.go:789 + 1087) with 7 test files, and NONE of it has ever executed — ensureWarpCapable (route_executor_warp.go:104-112) fails closed on every hull we own (0 of 242 hulls carry any WARP module; 0 FRAME_EXPLORER). It passed unit tests because the fakes hand it a MODULE_WARP_DRIVE. This is the ENGINEERING.md §4 fake-blindness trap: boundary fakes validate logic but never the real catalog or its availability.

RETROFIT IS PHYSICALLY PLAUSIBLE once a drive is found: our 4 FRAME_HEAVY_FREIGHTER hulls have 13 module slots with only 7 used (6 free) and 40 reactor output. SHIP_EXPLORER is also purchasable (X1-GX25-DB3E, 661,010, ABUNDANT as of a Jul-23 scan) and per the sp-0xd0 code comment carries the drive stock — UNVERIFIED, since shipyard_inventory stores only type/price/supply and the live shipyard loadout read requires a hull AT the waypoint (our 3 probes in X1-GX25 sit at other waypoints).

WORK: (1) add a cheap standing DETECTOR so that the moment any scan observes MODULE_WARP_DRIVE* or MODULE_JUMP_DRIVE* in a market it surfaces as a captain event rather than sitting unnoticed in market_data — this is the whole acquisition trigger and costs nothing until it fires; (2) decide acquisition path (market-buy + outfit onto a heavy vs buy SHIP_EXPLORER) once a source exists; (3) verify the explorer stock-loadout claim with a live shipyard read when a hull is next at a shipyard waypoint. Do NOT mount a dedicated scanning campaign for this — coverage grows on its own via the freshsizer/scout-post machinery.

RELATED: blocked-by the fuel-model validation bead (warpFuelCost is unverified); main.go:786-788 carries a STALE comment claiming 'nothing dispatches a warp yet' though slice C is wired at 1087.
acceptance_criteria: A standing detector exists that raises a captain event the first time MODULE_WARP_DRIVE* (or MODULE_JUMP_DRIVE*) is observed in any market scan, with waypoint + price. Detector is proven by a RED test that fires it against a synthetic market row carrying the symbol, and proven silent against a market with no such row. Zero behavior change and zero added API calls while no drive exists (it reads rows the scanner already writes). The stale main.go:786-788 comment is corrected. build/vet/gofmt clean; go test ./... -race green.
notes:
ADMIRAL CORRECTION 2026-07-24: captain events are LEGACY — everything must be AUTOMATED. This bead's original acceptance criterion ('raises a captain event the first time MODULE_WARP_DRIVE* is observed') is VOID. Do not build an event/notification; build the closed loop.

REVISED INTENT: the moment a warp drive becomes obtainable, the engine ACQUIRES and INSTALLS it autonomously behind the standing money guards (RULINGS #4/#6) — detect source -> buy -> deliver to hull -> install -> mark the hull warp-capable — with no human or captain step anywhere in the path. Model it on the existing autonomous acquisition loops (auto-outfit's AcquireAndInstall and the fleet autosizer's BuyAndDedicate are the shape to copy: guarded, self-triggering, idempotent, restart-resilient per RULINGS #2).

ACQUISITION FACTS ESTABLISHED THIS SESSION (read-only, live):
- Modules are bought as MARKET GOODS at a shipyard waypoint, then installed from the hull's own cargo — 'spacetraders ship outfit install' help: 'Installing a module requires it to already be in the ship's cargo (buy it as a good at a shipyard first)'. The daemon atomically claims the hull, gates the shipyard fee on the working-capital reserve, docks, and installs.
- 'ship outfit remove' EXISTS and returns a module to cargo. So a drive is TRANSFERABLE between hulls — a retrofit path that needs no market at all, if any hull we can buy already carries one.
- Shipyard coverage is NOT the blind spot: 235 of 246 known shipyard waypoints already have market_data. Shipyard markets simply stock very few module types (only 6 distinct MODULE_*/ENGINE_* goods across all 235).
- Still ZERO MODULE_WARP_DRIVE* / MODULE_JUMP_DRIVE* rows across 17,225 market rows / 2,974 markets.
- ENGINE_HYPER_DRIVE_I by contrast is common and cheap (22 markets, ~42-46k, ABUNDANT) — engines are NOT the constraint; the warp MODULE is.

OPEN EXPERIMENT (in flight): bought one SHIP_EXPLORER at X1-VM73-AX3F for ~746,193 (buyer TORWIND-30, container batch_purchase_ships-TORWIND-30-66f5c50b) to settle whether an explorer ships with MODULE_WARP_DRIVE pre-installed — the sp-0xd0 code comment asserts it but nothing has ever verified it. If YES: warp becomes reachable immediately, and 'outfit remove' + 'outfit install' is the freighter retrofit path with no market dependency. If NO: warp is unreachable until a market selling the module is discovered, and this bead reduces to the detect-and-auto-acquire loop above.
EXPERIMENT RESULT 2026-07-24 22:25Z — CORE QUESTION SETTLED, live API read of X1-VM73-AX3F (loadouts returned because TORWIND-81 was DOCKED there; a shipyard read yields the full 'ships' array ONLY with a hull at the waypoint — a yard read with no hull present returns shipTypes+price only, confirmed twice).

SHIP_EXPLORER SHIPS WITH THE WARP DRIVE — the sp-0xd0 code comment is VERIFIED, not assumed:
  SHIP_EXPLORER price 746,193 | FRAME_EXPLORER, moduleSlots 8, fuelCapacity 800
    engine  ENGINE_ION_DRIVE_II speed 36 (power 6, crew 8); reactor REACTOR_FUSION_I power 40
    MODULES: MODULE_CARGO_HOLD_II, MODULE_CREW_QUARTERS_I x2, **MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I**, MODULE_GAS_PROCESSOR_I
So a warp drive IS obtainable today WITHOUT ever finding a market that stocks the module — buy the hull that carries it.

ENGINE LADDER (all measured live, complete for impulse+ion):
  ENGINE_IMPULSE_DRIVE_I  speed  9  power 1  crew 0   (probes, siphon drones)
  ENGINE_ION_DRIVE_I      speed 15  power 3  crew 3   (SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER / FRAME_LIGHT_FREIGHTER, moduleSlots 6, fuel 600, REACTOR_CHEMICAL_I power 15)
  ENGINE_ION_DRIVE_II     speed 36  power 6  crew 8   (our frigate + all 19 heavy freighters + SHIP_EXPLORER)
  ENGINE_HYPER_DRIVE_I    UNMEASURED — we own none and no readable yard sells a hull carrying it (sold as a market good at 22 markets, ~42-46k)
Engines govern SPEED only ('reduces the time of arrival when navigating'). NO engine grants warp; warp is strictly the module.

ENGINES ARE NOT SWAPPABLE — decisive for planning. The API exposes NO engine/reactor/frame install-or-remove endpoint; only /modules/install|remove and /mounts/install|remove exist. A hull's engine is fixed AT PURCHASE. Any 'upgrade the heavies to a faster engine' plan is therefore IMPOSSIBLE — the only way to obtain a hyper-drive hull is to buy a ship that comes with one. (This kills a hypothesis I had raised; recording it so nobody re-opens it.)

RETROFIT PATH IS REAL BUT COSTS CARGO: /my/ships/{s}/transfer exists, and /modules/remove places a module back into CARGO, so a drive can move explorer -> co-located heavy. BUT our heavies are 13/13 module slots FULL (3x MODULE_CARGO_HOLD_III + 4x MODULE_CREW_QUARTERS_I; power is free at 19/40, slots are not), and crew sits at 149/149 REQUIRED so quarters are likely not removable. Fitting a warp drive on a heavy therefore means removing a CARGO_HOLD_III — i.e. paying cargo capacity on a freight hull to gain warp. NOTE: an earlier note in this session claimed heavies had '6 free slots'; that was WRONG (it subtracted module COUNT from slot count, but modules consume multiple slots each). Corrected here.

STILL OPEN: MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I's own slot requirement (unknown until we hold one); whether warp incurs a cooldown; and the warpFuelCost validation (sp-tvjzo). Buyer TORWIND-8 is en route to the X1-YY85-ZD2D explorer yard to purchase and measure.

title: Route-bound refactor: one operation-scoped jump-bound instead of per-call threading across the twin-variant route primitives
description: WHY: 'long-haul reach = 25 jumps' is threaded piecemeal into ~4+ independent route entry points, and each recurrence of the same bug (sp-e059j reposition, sp-ry741 Guard-0 check, sp-ry741-residual arb-executor travel) was a separate call site that defaulted to MaxJumpPath=5. Every shared route primitive exists as a TWIN PAIR — a default-bound-5 variant and a *WithinJumps(bound) variant: Path/PathWithinJumps, Routable/RoutableWithinJumps, RepositionToWaypoint/RepositionToWaypointStoredThenVerifyWithinJumps, travel/travelWithJumpBound. The default-5 variants are landmines: any long-haul path that calls one silently gets 5, and the mismatch (check says reachable-in-25, flight tries 5) fail-loops. REFACTOR: carry the jump-bound as ONE operation-scoped value — on context.Context (a typed key, default MaxJumpPath=5) OR a RoutePolicy threaded once through the leg — that every shared route primitive reads. The long-haul engine stamps 25 ONCE at the top of its leg; everything downstream (discovery, reposition, Guard-0, travel) is coherent by construction; then RETIRE the redundant *WithinJumps parameter variants. Makes the class structurally impossible to reintroduce. SCOPE/RISK: touches the shared travel/gategraph/reposition machinery used by EVERY coordinator (tour, trade, arb, scout, long-haul) — large blast radius, needs careful RED-first + full -race sweep + byte-identical proof for all non-long-haul callers (they keep bound-5). RULINGS #2/#4/#13. RELATED: sp-ry741 (targeted fix A shipped first), sp-e059j, sp-0o9ub (PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify), sp-mepj (long-haul reuse invariant). Do this only when we want the class gone for good; the targeted fix A closes the current instance.

title: Per-activity freshsizer SLA (mirror sp-t5sh5 caps) — reallocate freshness by activity state
description:
COMPANION to sp-t5sh5 (activity-conditioned trade-ranker age cap). Report: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/018f0d6a-570c-4e2c-ab53-781aeb042050 | bd memory: economy-analyst-freshness-profit. Grounded in era-4 live state (analysis 2026-07-24).

PROBLEM: the freshsizer holds a SINGLE global SLA (sla_seconds, currently 10800/180m). With one SLA you must either under-serve (today: max_probe_fleet=40 -> observed RESTRICTED median age 228m, already PAST its 180m ranker cap -> those markets drop out of undirected ranking) OR hold 180m across all ~5,184 markets (~86 probes). Neither is efficient: WEAK (44%, 2,325 mkts) tolerates 480m and is being over-refreshed; RESTRICTED/GROWING/STRONG are under-refreshed for their tighter caps.

CHANGE (feature): make the freshsizer SLA a FUNCTION OF ACTIVITY STATE, mirroring sp-t5sh5's ranker caps at ~0.75x the cap (safety margin so a market rarely crosses the ranker cap between scans):
  WEAK        SLA ~360m   (cap 480)
  RESTRICTED  SLA ~135m   (cap 180)
  GROWING     SLA ~45m    (cap 60)
  STRONG      SLA ~22m    (cap 30)
  unknown/null activity -> RESTRICTED default (conservative middle)
The freshsizer already computes required_probes = ceil(markets x per_market_cycle / sla) and value-weights the P90; this makes `sla` per-activity in that sizing instead of global. Keep the release/hysteresis logic (release_slack_percent, release_stable_window_secs) and value_weighted P90 intact -- only the SLA input becomes per-activity.

EFFECT: reallocates freshness AWAY from over-served WEAK TOWARD under-served RESTRICTED/GROWING -- holds the correct freshness everywhere for ~25-40% fewer probe-equivalents than a global 180m SLA, while making MORE markets routable. Freed probe/API budget funds discovery (breadth).

DEPENDENCY: only pays off once sp-t5sh5 is live -- the ranker cap must be per-activity too, else keeping WEAK fresh only to 360m while the ranker still drops it at 75m makes it invisible. Deploy WITH or AFTER sp-t5sh5; do NOT arm standalone.

GUARDRAILS:
- RULINGS #5: per-activity SLAs are config/tune knobs with the above defaults, not hardcoded constants. Keep the "one place" property.
- Activity chicken-and-egg (shared with sp-t5sh5): activity state is read from a scan, so a WEAK market may have flipped to STRONG unseen. Size on last-known state; a STRONG/GROWING market at/over its tight SLA should be prioritized for re-scan.
- Out of scope / untouched: the execution money guards (RULINGS #4) and the trade-ranker cap itself (that is sp-t5sh5).

ARM + MEASURE: ship armed alongside sp-t5sh5. Watch: freshness-probe count, per-activity P90 age vs cap, routable-lane count, revenue-per-API-call. Refit the per-activity SLA values each era (caps/drift are priors, not constants).

All 5 on main (50a1ce1d..98341798), full go test ./... green each gate. Verified live post-deploy: daemon healthy (no panic); B2/B3 launched -> 4 long-haul workers RUNNING (sp-bwjyn uncap live, exposure-cap holds gone); sp-39hjn cooldown-aware watchdog + sp-if4lx pathfind deadline + sp-t5sh5 ranker age cap + sp-j4kjv per-activity freshsizer SLA all armed. Behavioral outcomes (trade sells catching up to buys, watchdog false-kill rate ->0, all 4 long-haul hulls completing hauls) observable over the next windows.

title: Activity-conditioned trade-ranker age cap (replace hardcoded 75m maxListingAge)
description:
CONTEXT (economy-analyst experiment, TORWIND era 3-4; n=3,236 matched trades + full market_price_history drift analysis). Report: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/018f0d6a-570c-4e2c-ab53-781aeb042050 | bd memory: economy-analyst-freshness-profit

FINDING: trade-selection freshness can be relaxed substantially to buy market BREADTH, because era3/4 prices barely drift (median <1% even at 8-24h stale). The staleness cost is sharply ACTIVITY-DEPENDENT, so the single uniform cap is the wrong shape.

CURRENT STATE:
- Gate = `const maxListingAge = 75 * time.Minute` (internal/application/trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go:776; also tour_snapshot.go and captain/detectors.go:166). Undirected ranking drops listings older than 75m (partitionListingsByAge); directed --dest retains stale + re-verifies live at execution (sp-xwa1). One value for all markets.

CHANGE (feature): make the ranker age cap a FUNCTION OF ACTIVITY STATE. Recommended defaults, fitted so p90 sell-side drift <= ~5%:
  WEAK       -> 480 min (8h)  [was 75m; loosen 6.4x; 44% of obs; p90 2.7%]
  RESTRICTED -> 180 min (3h)  [was 75m; loosen 2.4x; 53% of obs; p90 4.9%]
  GROWING    ->  60 min       [tighten;              3% of obs; p90 5.4%]
  STRONG     ->  30 min       [tighten;            0.5% of obs; p90 9.3%]
Activity comes from the listing row (market_data.activity / MarketPriceHistory.activity). Unknown/missing activity -> use the RESTRICTED default (conservative middle).

HARD GUARDRAILS:
- RULINGS #4: DO NOT touch the execution money guards (staleAskAborts, per-visit margin re-check, min-margin/price/reserve). This changes ONLY the ranker VISIBILITY cap. The execution guards are what make loose selection safe by aborting the tail; the whole recommendation depends on them staying intact.
- Preserve directed --dest behavior (retain stale + re-verify live). Only the UNDIRECTED auto-scan drop-threshold becomes activity-conditioned.
- RULINGS #5: caps are config/tune knobs (e.g. [trading] ranker_age_cap_minutes.{weak,restricted,growing,strong}), NOT a new hardcoded 4-way constant. Keep the "defined once" property (tour_snapshot.go references the same value).
- STRONG cannot be made safe by the cap alone (p90 ~9% even at 30m). Its protection is execution re-verification, not the cap. Optional hardening: a STRONG/GROWING listing over its (tight) cap should trigger a re-scan rather than silently vetoing -- resolves the activity chicken-and-egg (activity state is itself read from a scan; a WEAK market may have flipped to STRONG unseen).

ARM + MEASURE (Admiral policy: no flags; unproven economics -> arm+measure-in-prod). Ship ARMED with these defaults; rollout is a captain call. Watch: total realized profit, revenue-per-API-call (the real constraint = per-account rate limit), routable-lane count, abort/partial-fill rate. Rising revenue/API + flat aborts -> widen; aborts spike -> tighten.

CAVEATS: the drift curve is an era-3/4 PRIOR, not a constant -- refit the per-activity caps each era (analyst regenerates the table). The BREADTH benefit (do newly-visible markets have real absorbable spreads?) is unmeasured here; the prod metrics above close that gap.

title: Long-haul reposition cold-start latency: strict resolver probes every frontier edge (per-edge GetWaypoint) — ~20min planning per far reposition
description: FOLLOW-UP to sp-e059j/sp-yginc. After the watchdog disable let long-haul progress, the residual cost is the REPOSITION planning: ~20min between 'Executing iteration' and the first jump on a cold cache. ROOT CAUSE: the long-haul reposition uses the STRICT resolver (RepositionToWaypointStrictWithinJumps -> travelWithJumpBound strictJumpBound -> PathWithinJumps), whose neighbor closure calls gateUnderConstruction (one API GetWaypoint) PER EDGE EXPLORED across the whole bound-25 frontier (service.go:527,~505-545). On a cold cache that is hundreds of GetWaypoint calls. FIX (plan cheap, verify the chosen path): plan the route over the FAST persisted stored-adjacency (RepositionPath, no per-edge probe), then run gateUnderConstruction ONLY on the chosen path's gates (a handful). A path gate under construction -> treat as unroutable at PLANNING so sp-e059j's reachability fallback skips to the next lane (avoids the jump-time-failure LOOP that a pure stored-adjacency swap would cause). jump_ship.go remains the authoritative jump-time fail-closed backstop. ISOLATE to long-haul: do NOT change the shared strict Path/PathWithinJumps used by tours/manual/arb (bound-5). SAFETY: long-haul targets are charted (stored-adjacency discovery post-sp-yginc), so the sp-qxa4 unreadable-frontier concern does not apply; construction is caught by path-verify + jump API. RULINGS #4/#2 hold (routing/latency only, no money-guard change). No flag. ACCEPTANCE: cold-cache long-haul reposition to a far source plans in seconds (path-only probes, not frontier); an under-construction path gate -> unroutable -> fallback to next lane (no loop); a clean charted path flies; tours/manual strict routing byte-identical; MaxJumpPath still 5; -race green. RELATED: sp-e059j (reach), sp-yginc (discovery latency), sp-mepj (engine).
close_reason: Deployed (91bc862e+bd4ece72 → gated GatePassed/Merged → restart-daemon 00:19) + VERIFIED live: reposition planning ~20min → 11s. Post-deploy episode 00:20:00 'Executing iteration' → 00:20:11 'Starting jump operation' (11s), then jumped 00:20:32. PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify plans over stored adjacency + probes ONLY the chosen path's gates (probe count 31→6). No-loop safety: bad chosen-path gate → ErrUnroutable → fallback skips lane. Strict Path/PathWithinJumps/RepositionPath/bfsPath byte-untouched (75 ins/0 del), MaxJumpPath=5, sp-e059j strict path retained. jump_ship.go stays the hop-time backstop. -race green 107 pkgs.

title: Long-haul discovery cold-start latency: DiscoverLanes prices every lane via strict fetch-through gateGraph.Path → ~10-min first episode after each daemon restart
description: FOLLOW-UP to sp-e059j (whose reach fix is CORRECT and unrelated). SYMPTOM: the FIRST long-haul episode after every daemon restart spends ~10 min in discovery before any navigation (T59: 18:02:02 'Executing iteration' → 18:13:10 first 'Ship navigation requested'). PROVEN cold-cache, NOT a regression: the pre-fix 17:43 restart (old code, no longhaul-reach) had an identical ~9-min first-episode delay (17:43 → first error 17:52:41); steady-state (warm cache) is ~92s. ROOT CAUSE: run_longhaul_arb_discovery.go DiscoverLanes' hops() closure (:170) calls d.gateGraph.Path(ctx, fromSystem, toSystem, playerID) — the STRICT FETCH-THROUGH resolver — once per candidate (source,sink) pair in assembleLongHaulCandidates. On a cold gate-graph cache each Path fetches gate data per traversed system across many candidate lanes → slow first episode. FIX: discovery only needs an APPROXIMATE hop count for RANKING (trip_time ∝ GateHops) + a reachability signal — NOT the strict fail-closed guarantee (that is the reposition's job at execution, already correct post-sp-e059j). Replace the hops() estimate with the FAST persisted stored-adjacency resolver gateGraph.RepositionPath (reads persisted adjacency, no per-node fetch-through) at a generous bound; a lane with no stored-adjacency path within bound is dropped (acceptable — an uncharted-adjacency lane can't be reliably flown; re-appears once scouts chart it). Add RepositionPath to the gateGraphPathfinder interface (gategraph.Service already implements it). DO NOT touch the reposition path/adapter/PathWithinJumps/bound-25 (sp-e059j, correct). RULINGS #4 unchanged (ranking only). No flag. ACCEPTANCE: cold-cache discovery completes fast via RepositionPath (test: a fake whose fetch-through Path is slow/errors but RepositionPath fast → discovery uses RepositionPath, Path not called); far lanes still rank with stored-adjacency hop counts; reposition path byte-untouched; MaxJumpPath still 5; -race green. RELATED: sp-e059j (parent), sp-mepj (engine).
close_reason: Deployed (2feda26e → gated GatePassed/Merged → restart-daemon ~20:35) + VERIFIED live: cold-start discovery dropped from ~11.5 min to ~68s (~10x). Post-fix episode 20:36:01 'Executing iteration' → 20:37:09 'Starting jump operation' (68s); pre-fix was 20:21:32 → 20:33:12 (11.5 min). DiscoverLanes.hops() now rides gateGraph.RepositionPath (stored adjacency, no fetch-through) instead of the strict fetch-through Path. T59 executing a real multi-hop reposition toward far source X1-QM8 (past 5 jumps, no 'within 5 jumps' error). sp-e059j reposition path byte-untouched; MaxJumpPath=5. -race green.

title: [trading] sp-mepj long-haul v1 hardening: route-fuel in ranking, cross-worker absorption headroom, [long_haul] config live-tuning, impact debt lookup
description: Four nil-safe v1 deferrals from the sp-mepj daemon wiring (all backstopped by execution-time guards; none blocks discover→rank→guarded-execute→recovery, none is a money-guard gap): (1) routeCostEstimator left nil — the engine's routeCostEstimator port is func(gateHops int), which structurally can't consult a per-waypoint RoutePlanner for exact route fuel; ranking uses honest gate-hop TIME (dominant $/hr term) but omits route FUEL from net margin (negligible on 28k/u exotics; the arb executor's live-price re-check + realized-net>0 filter backstop marginal lanes). Fix needs an engine port-signature change (take the route, not a hop count) + wiring. (2) cross-worker absorptionHeadroom left nil — each lane's VolumeCap bounds a single buy to single-visit depth; collective oversell across multiple long-haul workers is still prevented by the absorption-ledger reservation at execution, but the RANKING doesn't consult others' in-flight reservations. (3) config.yaml [long_haul] live-tuning section NOT added — the money-envelope caps are ACTIVE at the Admiral-authorized aggressive defaults (~1M/haul, ~2M exposure) read from config keys, but there's no config.yaml section to dial them live; a resolveLongHaulConfig injects them additively, zero mechanism change (numeric tunables, NOT a flag). (4) impact-model debt lookup left nil — shared cooldown debt ≈ 0 for exotic cross-system lanes (not the same-system lanes the trade fleet hammers); the era-3 buy/sell impact coeffs still drive optimalVolume. NO FLAG on any fix — armed. RULINGS #4 intact (all execution guards unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: Route fuel folded into the ranking net (engine port takes the route); cross-worker absorption headroom consulted at ranking; [long_haul] config section makes the caps live-tunable; impact debt wired. Each RED-first, -race + pytest green as applicable. No flag.

title: [trading] Long-haul arb: exact in-flight-capital exposure tracking (replace the concurrent-haul proxy)
description: Follow-up to sp-mepj. The long-haul arb total-exposure guard shipped as a concurrent-haul PROXY (total÷per-haul, running hauls counted, fail-closed) — a conscious v1 decision. Safe, but it UNDER-utilizes the aggressive envelope when individual hauls are well under the per-haul cap: e.g. 2M total ÷ 1M per-haul = 2 concurrent hauls, so two small 200k hauls only ever deploy 400k of the 2M. The sp-mepj design specified EXACT in-flight capital (running_exposure + buy_cost <= total cap, released on sale) precisely to honour the Admiral's 'aggressive full loads' intent. Exact tracking needs a NEW daemon port summing live long-haul containers' persisted buy-costs (the cheap cargo-valuation estimate drifts as prices move). FIX: add that port + swap the concurrent-haul proxy for exact-capital exposure in longHaulEnvelope. Caps stay live-tunable; mechanism stays fail-closed; no flag.
acceptance_criteria: Long-haul total-exposure gates on the summed live in-flight buy-cost of all long-haul containers (not a haul count); many small hauls can deploy up to the full total cap; fail-closed on unreadable. RED-first, -race green. No flag.

title: Frontier probe-buyer targets an unreachable far shipyard and stalls the fleet at 100 probes, ignoring live probe yards in the buyer's own system
description:
SYMPTOM (live 2026-07-23, player 4, era 4): the probe fleet is STUCK at 100 and cannot grow toward the (raised) 160 cap, because the frontier's probe-buyer keeps targeting an UNREACHABLE far shipyard and fail-closes every cycle. Three consecutive frontier cycles (14:53:25, 14:54:29, 14:55:32) all logged:
  "no purchase: buy failed (fail-closed): failed to relay probe buyer to X1-AM3-Z13F: failed to navigate TORWIND-35 (then TORWIND-19) to cross-system destination X1-AM3-Z13F: reposition failed: no jump-gate route from X1-DY16 (then X1-VT63) to X1-AM3 within 5 jumps"

ROOT CAUSE: the probe-buyer selects shipyard X1-AM3-Z13F, which is beyond the 5-jump reach limit from the buyer probes (at X1-DY16, X1-VT63) — while there are MANY current-era SHIP_PROBE shipyards in the buyer's OWN or adjacent systems. From shipyard_inventory (ship_type=SHIP_PROBE, era_id=4), scanned within the last ~15 min:
  X1-DY16-X12D (MODERATE, 27907) <- SAME system as buyer TORWIND-35
  X1-VT63-D12B (HIGH, 23542)      <- SAME system as buyer TORWIND-19
  X1-CC13-D13Z (ABUNDANT, 21416), X1-RJ93-DF4E (HIGH, 23097), X1-RJ40-EC6C (HIGH, 19921), X1-UM5-A2 (MODERATE), X1-BT98-A11Z, X1-JT9-A12Z, X1-ZK26-A16D, X1-GD84-ZZ9C, X1-PA17-C42, X1-AA14-B12B ...
So the buyer at DY16 (or VT63) has a probe yard IN ITS OWN SYSTEM, yet the frontier relays it cross-system to the unreachable AM3 and retry-fails the SAME dead yard every cycle instead of falling back to a reachable one.

IMPACT: probe fleet can't grow past 100 -> caps discovery throughput. The frontier WANTS more probes (110-111 discovery queue, 0-5 idle probes, dark backlog low at 2-3 so scanning keeps up) but cannot buy them. Fail-closed (no bad spend), so no money lost — but real foregone discovery capacity, and the Admiral raised the cap to 160 expecting growth that can't happen. Same gate-reachability class as sp-hguq3.

FIX: the probe-buyer must select the NEAREST REACHABLE current-era probe shipyard (prefer the buyer's own system, then within the jump-reach limit), not a fixed/far yard. On an unreachable chosen yard, FALL BACK to the nearest reachable probe yard rather than retry-failing the same dead target every cycle. (The many live near yards make this a pure selection/fallback fix — the inventory is already there.)

ACCEPTANCE:
- With a reachable current-era probe yard in (or within reach of) the buyer's system, the probe-buy SUCCEEDS and the fleet grows toward the cap.
- A probe-buy never retry-loops on an unreachable yard when a reachable current-era probe yard exists in inventory.
- Yard selection is era-scoped (current era only) and prefers nearest-reachable.
- build/vet/gofmt + -race green.

EVIDENCE: frontier_expansion cycles 14:53-14:55 (X1-AM3-Z13F unreachable, buyers at DY16/VT63); shipyard_inventory SHIP_PROBE era 4 = 12+ yards incl. same-system ones; probe count 100 vs cap 160; discovery_share 30% (2 discovery/3 scan), dark backlog 2-3 (scanning healthy), systems charted 193->215 and markets 2289->2541 in the interval (discovery otherwise working).

RELATED: reach_mode frontier knob (bounds [1,3], currently 2=balanced; 3=deep composes "wider reuse relay") — MAY extend the buyer relay reach as a stopgap, but does not fix the core near-yard-selection defect. Same reachability family as sp-hguq3 (gate routing).
close_reason: Gated to main. Probe-buyer now selects the nearest REACHABLE current-era yard, not an unreachable far one. Root cause: resolveProximalBuy anchored reachability at the deep target system, but the relay routes from the BUYER's position (MaxJumpPath=5) -> a yard beyond the buyer's reach fail-closed + retry-looped every cycle, stalling the probe fleet at 100 vs the 160 cap. Fix (pure selection/fallback, REUSES the sp-255rz ProbeBuyerPositioner 'reachability where the buyer IS' pattern): anchor reachability per buyer system; keep the demand-proximal winner when reachable, else fall back to nearest reachable (own system first, 0-hop); selectRelayBuyer picks a hull that provably reaches the chosen yard. Era-scoped inherited. Money guards UNCHANGED (#4 verified via diff scrutiny — 25% treasury ceiling untouched, data gaps fail OPEN). No flag. RED->GREEN (own-system + one-hop, both pre-fix hit the exact live symptom); -race green 69 pkgs. Agent recovered from a transient ZlibError mid-build.

title: Autosizer realized-rate metric is stale (long trailing window) — blocks economically-correct heavy buys for hours after the fleet recovers from a disruption; make it recency-weighted
description:
SYMPTOM (live-verified 2026-07-23, player 4, era torwind-2026-07-19): the fleet autosizer BLOCKED every heavy buy for HOURS on a payback guard fed by a realized-rate metric that was still dominated by a past bad period — while the fleet was, in fact, highly profitable. It refused economically-correct capacity growth because its memory is too long.

EVIDENCE (the metric vs reality, same wall-clock):
- Autosizer (container fleet_autosizer-player-4-e694ebd4) heavy buy-decision, every tick 05:21 -> 13:14: BLOCKED. `era_payback[BLOCK: marginal rate unreadable/zero]` and `realized_rate[BLOCK: marginal -5698 >= floor 64067]` (earlier ticks: marginal -52450, -11075). Demand was strong the whole time (shortfall 104-122 unserved lanes), ceiling/price/treasury/api all OK — ONLY the realized-rate/payback guards blocked.
- ACTUAL current economics (financial `transactions` table, last 45m): SELL_CARGO +3,931,840, PURCHASE_CARGO -2,615,258, REFUEL -21,765 => NET +1,294,817 (~1.7M/hr). Heavies were the BULK: market_absorption_ledger shows heavies sold 1.66M of the 45m sell revenue (lights 267k). Proportional heavy net ~180k/hr/heavy — WILDLY above the autosizer's floor and nowhere near its -5,698 "marginal rate."
- So the marginal heavy's TRUE recent rate is strongly positive, but the metric reads negative. The metric IS updating (-52450 -> -5698 over ~2h) but FAR too slowly — it lagged the fleet's recovery by hours.

ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: the realized-rate the autosizer consumes (FleetTourRate / marginal MarginalRate, from persisted tour telemetry `ComputeFleetTourRate`) is computed over too long a window (cumulative / un-decayed trailing average). A bad period — here ~2h of wedged + stranded + loss-making tours triggered by a daemon restart at 04:33 (see sp-m3122) plus loss-making distress/manual liquidations — POISONS the metric for hours. After the fleet fully recovers, the metric takes far too long to reflect current reality, so the payback guards (correctly fail-closed on the number they're given) keep blocking.

IMPACT: the payback guards (era_payback + realized_rate, RULINGS #4) are only as good as the metric feeding them. A stale metric means after ANY disruption (wedge, daemon restart, a bad-cargo cycle) the autosizer stops buying for HOURS even once the fleet has recovered and is highly profitable — foregone, economically-correct capacity growth, and a confusing operator experience ("should we buy heavies?" — the machine says no, the ledger says yes). Fail-closed-safe direction (errs toward NOT buying), so no money lost — but real opportunity cost and decision confusion.

FIX: make the realized-rate metric RECENCY-WEIGHTED / bounded-window so it reflects CURRENT economics, not long-trailing history. This is about feeding the guards ACCURATE current data — NOT loosening the guard thresholds (RULINGS #4 untouched; unreadable/zero still blocks). Options:
- Rolling window of recent tours (last N tours or last M minutes) instead of cumulative/all-time.
- EWMA with a half-life on the order of the fleet's tour cycle time (tens of minutes), so a bad hour cannot poison the signal for many hours.
- Optionally exclude tours that occurred during a known-disrupted state (restart recovery, distress liquidation) from the payback metric — they are non-representative of steady-state.

ACCEPTANCE:
- After a simulated disruption (a run of negative/loss tours) followed by recovery to positive tours, the realized-rate reflects the recovered POSITIVE rate within ~one tour-cycle / the EWMA half-life, not hours later; the era_payback/realized_rate guards un-block within that window once true current economics clear the floor.
- Metric still smooths out a single outlier tour (not jumpy).
- Guards themselves unchanged (RULINGS #4): thresholds intact, unreadable/zero still blocks.
- build/vet/gofmt + -race green.

CODE POINTERS: ComputeFleetTourRate (persisted tour telemetry) — source of FleetTourRate/MarginalRate; wiring at fleet_autosizer_heavies.go (:37-40) + fleet_autosizer_ports.go (:38); the realized_rate + era_payback guards in fleet_autosizer_guards.go (:241-316) CONSUME the metric (the guards are correct — the number feeding them is stale).

RELATED: surfaced during the sp-m3122 restart-hang investigation; the 04:33 restart + ~2h of stranded/loss tours is what poisoned the metric. Complements sp-m3122 (fix the hang) — this fixes the autosizer's slow recovery-recognition. Also downstream of the disruptions sp-2v69u / sp-hguq3 caused.

title: [routing] Sync-time flaky gate read: fetchAndStore can cache a MISSING edge from an empty 200 (real connection invisible ~24h)
description: Follow-up to sp-hguq3 (which fixed the EXECUTION-time flaky read via bounded re-read in jump_ship.resolveDestinationGateWaypoint). The SAME flaky-read hole exists at SYNC time: gategraph.fetchAndStore copies GetJumpGate.connections verbatim and Replace()s the cache. If a charted gate's read comes back as a 200 OK with an empty/incomplete connections list (observed intermittently: 12 rapid CA43 reads returned 6 connections on 200s but sometimes 429s / empty bodies; the retry layer only retries on STATUS codes, so an empty-200 sails through), fetchAndStore will overwrite a real edge with a missing one — making a valid connection invisible until the next successful sync (~24h). FIX: have the API client (or fetchAndStore) treat an EMPTY connections list from a CHARTED jump gate as retryable CONTENT (not a valid snapshot) — retry a bounded few times before persisting, and/or refuse to Replace() a non-empty cached edge-set with an empty one from a charted gate. No flag, armed. RED-first (empty-200 sync overwrites a good edge before fix).
acceptance_criteria: An empty/incomplete connections list from a charted jump gate does NOT overwrite a previously-good cached edge set (either retried until non-empty, or the Replace is refused). A genuinely-empty gate still syncs correctly. RED-first, -race green. No flag.
close_reason: Gated to main. Sync-time flaky gate read fixed in the gategraph service (sibling of sp-hguq3 execution-time): (1) bounded re-read (max 3, 750ms) so a transient empty-200 recovers — happy path 1 read; (2) refuse-to-overwrite a known-good non-empty cached edge set when re-reads stay empty (first-sync/genuinely-empty still syncs empty). Single-writer intact (added a read; refuse skips the write, #3), deterministic (#2), money guards untouched (#4). No flag. RED->GREEN 4 tests. Note: gate needed a stray untracked copy of the new test file cleared from the main checkout (crafter leaked it there) before the ff-merge — verified identical to the branch version first.

title: Contract-hauler price cache is in-memory — restart mid-INCOME (or a stale-low cached price) can re-open the sp-muc5x pivot deadlock
description:
Follow-up to sp-muc5x. The fix caches the hauler price in an in-memory per-container map (the coordinator has no reconcile-reachable config WRITE path, holds no persisted state by design). Two narrow residuals remain because step-4 resume was NOT buildable (FrigateRetirer has DedicateAsPurchaser but NO inverse/un-dedicate primitive; StartLoop exists but a purchasing-dedicated frigate can't be cleanly released):
1. RESTART-HOLE: a daemon restart mid-INCOME (probes already at target ⇒ the DATA-phase seedHaulerPriceFromYard does NOT re-run; frigate on its loop; hauler still unaffordable) leaves the cache empty ⇒ the income.go:482 guard is inert ⇒ the frigate is freed ⇒ the original deadlock. Deploys restart the daemon, so this is reachable in active dev, though far narrower than the original always-on deadlock.
2. STALE-LOW cache: if the cached price is below the risen real price, the guard lets the frigate free, then the readable capital gate (income.go:~347) blocks unaffordable ⇒ frigate idle. Step-4 resume would catch both.
FIX OPTIONS: (a) add the un-dedicate primitive to FrigateRetirer + wire step-4 resume (free ⇒ if the readable price is unaffordable, release the dedication + StartLoop so the frigate resumes earning) — robust regardless of cache correctness; or (b) persist the hauler-price cache (needs a reconcile-reachable config writer collaborator + adapter + daemon wiring, cutting against the coordinator's no-persisted-state design). (a) is preferred. Money guards unchanged either way (RULINGS #4). Primary sp-muc5x deadlock (fresh cold-start) is FIXED + validated; this closes the edge.
close_reason: Closed

title: deploy/staging/down.sh can orphan the staging daemon when the pidfile is missing
description: Observed 2026-07-22: after up.sh restarts the daemon via nohup daemon --force, the staging pidfile /tmp/spacetraders-staging.pid was missing, so down.sh (staging_stop_if_ours) reported no daemon pidfile nothing to stop and left the staging daemon PID 34141 ALIVE and orphaned (socket removed, still consuming the shared API budget). Had to SIGKILL it manually by matching the -staging binary name. ROOT: up.sh backgrounds the daemon with nohup and relies on the daemon self-writing its config pid_file, but after a --force restart handoff that pidfile can be absent. FIX candidates: (a) up.sh writes the daemon child PID to a script-managed pidfile the way it already does for the routing service, so teardown never depends on the daemon self-writing it; (b) down.sh adds a fallback pkill -f spacetraders-daemon-staging which is safe because the -staging suffix can never match the prod spacetraders-daemon. IMPACT: an orphaned staging daemon keeps hitting the API on the shared account budget after a reported-successful teardown.
notes: FIXED + TESTED (shipwright, 2026-07-22): deploy/staging/down.sh now sweeps a surviving spacetraders-daemon-staging (TERM then KILL by the staging-unique binary name, mirroring the routing-orphan sweep + staging_stop_if_ours). Deterministic test: up.sh -> rm the pidfile (reproduces the --force orphan) -> down.sh -> the fallback kills the daemon, prod (2431) untouched. Committed b2cddd17 (down.sh only, 12 insertions). NOT PUSHED: local main is 68 commits ahead of origin (pre-existing backlog, not this fix); pushing sends all 68 - awaiting the human decision.
close_reason: Closed

title: CLI: scrap/retire a ship (ship scrap) — expose POST /my/ships/{symbol}/scrap; no verb removes a ship from the fleet
description: GAP: there is NO CLI verb to remove/scrap a ship. ship verbs = buy/dock/info/jettison/jump/navigate/orbit/outfit/refuel/release/reserve/reserve-cargo/route/sell(CARGO only)/unreserve-cargo; fleet verbs = add/assign/hub/list/remove/unassign (fleet membership only, ship keeps existing). So an Admiral 'retire N lights' order (fleet modernization — heavies replacing lights) CANNOT be executed: a light can only be unassigned (idle in the general pool), never scrapped or removed from the fleet. Live case 2026-07-22: bought 5 heavies for trade + ordered to retire 4 lights (TORWIND-5/6/7/10) — pulled them from trade but could not retire them. WHAT: add a CLI verb, e.g. 'spacetraders ship scrap --ship <symbol>', that calls the SpaceTraders scrap endpoint (POST /my/ships/{shipSymbol}/scrap) — scrap a ship at its CURRENT shipyard waypoint, credit the scrap value to the ledger, and drop it from the fleet/ship list. Requires the ship DOCKED at a waypoint with a shipyard (mirror 'shipyard purchase' presence rule). GUARD: refuse if the ship is mid-job/claimed by a container (or auto-release first, like the unassign+purchase path). ACCEPTANCE: 'ship scrap --ship X --player-id N' scraps a docked-at-shipyard ship, records the scrap credit in the ledger, and the ship no longer appears in 'ship list'; refuses cleanly for a non-shipyard location or a claimed ship. build/vet/gofmt + test green.
close_reason: Admiral: not needed. Parking the retired lights (unassigned + idle in the general pool) is an acceptable 'retire' — no ship-scrap CLI required.

title: CLI: query saved shipyard_inventory by ship type (current-era only) — e.g. 'shipyard yards --type SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER'
description:
Add a CLI verb to query the SAVED shipyard_inventory by ship type — CURRENT-ERA ONLY.

WHY: shipyard_inventory (the daemon's saved per-yard ship-type catalog, written by the ShipyardScanner) is queried INTERNALLY — NearestYardsSelling (internal/adapters/expansion/adapters.go + internal/adapters/grpc/fleet_autosizer_ports.go) and HasAnyOfTypes (internal/adapters/persistence/shipyard_inventory_repository.go, the "first heavy yard this era" predicate) — but there is NO CLI surface for it. `spacetraders shipyard list <sys> <wp>` only shows LIVE listings, which require a ship physically PRESENT + docked at the yard, so an operator CANNOT ask "which yards sell SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER?" from data we already have. Live cost: to execute an Admiral "buy 2 heavies" order the captain had to psql the daemon DB directly to locate the heavy-freighter yard (X1-KQ55-AE2A) — no sanctioned CLI path existed.

WHAT: add a query verb, e.g. `spacetraders shipyard yards --type SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER [--player-id N]` (name TBD), returning the saved yards that deal in the given ship type — system, waypoint, purchase_price, supply, last_scanned — ordered by price ascending. Support one or more --type; optionally no --type = all saved yards for the player. Back it with the existing NearestYardsSelling query or a direct era-scoped read of shipyard_inventory.

CRITICAL — CURRENT-ERA ONLY (Admiral requirement 2026-07-22): the result MUST be filtered to the CURRENT open era. shipyard_inventory is era-scoped (era_id column); an old-era yard may no longer exist or sell that type. Filter era_id = the current era resolved via the eras registry — the same era-scoping the `history` CLI already uses ("read-only queries over the live tables, scoped through the eras registry"). A closed-era-only row MUST NOT be returned. (Concrete: era 4 = torwind-2026-07-19 is current/open; rows from eras 1-3 must be excluded.)

DATA REFERENCE (verified 2026-07-22 against :5432/spacetraders — the LIVE daemon DB; :5434 refused, so :5432 is authoritative):
- Table public.shipyard_inventory columns: player_id (bigint), system_symbol (text), waypoint_symbol (varchar 64), ship_type (varchar 64), purchase_price (bigint), supply (text), last_scanned (timestamptz), era_id (bigint). PK (player_id, waypoint_symbol, ship_type); indexes on era_id and system_symbol.
- Existing queries to reuse: NearestYardsSelling(ctx, playerID, shipTypes, fromSystems) -> []shipyardQueries.YardCandidate; HasAnyOfTypes(ctx, playerID, shipTypes) -> bool. Both already era-scope — mirror their era filter.
- CLI to extend: internal/adapters/cli/shipyard.go (currently only `list` + `purchase`).

ACCEPTANCE:
- `spacetraders shipyard yards --type SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER --player-id 4` lists ONLY current-era heavy-freighter yards (system/waypoint/price/supply/last_scanned), price-ascending, with NO ship-presence required.
- A yard whose only shipyard_inventory rows are from a CLOSED era does NOT appear (add a test that seeds a closed-era row + asserts it is excluded).
- build/vet/gofmt + go test green.
close_reason: Shipped: 'shipyard yards --type' CLI queries saved shipyard_inventory by ship type, current-era only, no ship-presence needed. Gated to main.

title: Reserve-floor consolidation: collapse 6 duplicate 50k floors to one common source, re-home 150k/200k cushions as derived, close both money-guard gaps (idle-arb + source-buys), fix autosizer contract-delivery floor
description:
AUTHORIZED cross-cutting RESERVE-FLOOR CONSOLIDATION design (Admiral 2026-07-22). Doubly-motivated: (1) collapse the near-duplicate reserve floors into ONE immutable source, (2) close the two RULINGS #4 money-guard gaps. Read-only analysis; the shipwright implements. All claims cite gobot/ file:line on `main`. RULINGS #4 (never weaken a guard; add-only where unfloored) and #5 (single immutable source, no config/tune/launch seam) bind. Higher cushions kept as documented derived exceptions. sp-65xqo is ALREADY CLOSED (see §4).

## §1 FLOOR INVENTORY (value · location · tunable/immutable · spend paths gated)
THE SINGLE SOURCE (keep):
- common.ImmutableReserveFloor = 50000 (internal/application/common/reserve_floor.go:10) — IMMUTABLE const, RULINGS #5 lower bound.
- common.EffectiveReserveFloor(absolute, pct, treasury) = max(50k, min(absolute, round(pct%×treasury))) (reserve_floor.go:44) — the counter-cyclical resolver.
- common.DefaultReserveTreasuryPct = 40 (reserve_floor.go:18).

50k TIER — DUPLICATE consts of the same value (each a local `= 50000`), all mirroring ImmutableReserveFloor:
1. production_executor.go:82 `defaultWorkingCapitalReserve = 50000` — factory INPUT buys (spendFloorBreached :655, reserveConcurrentSpendOrPark :713) + (post sp-65xqo) the gate OUTPUT buy.
2. ship/commands/outfitting/outfitting.go:33 `defaultWorkingCapitalReserve = 50000` — outfitting installs.
3. trading/commands/run_trade_route_coordinator.go:75 `defaultWorkingCapitalReserve = 50000` — tour/trade-route buys.
4. autooutfit/coordinator.go:47 `defaultTreasuryReserve = 50000` — auto-outfit installs ("mirrors the outfitting handler").
5. capacity reconciler `DefaultReserveFloorCredits = 50000` (compile-time lockstep-guarded to ImmutableReserveFloor; referenced run_bootstrap_coordinator.go:68). NOTE: the capacity reconciler is being RETIRED (config.yaml capacity_reconciler DISARMED 2026-07-21; sp-y2ptq deletes the stack) — this const may vanish with it.
→ 6 definitions of the 50k floor (common + 5 duplicates).

HIGHER CUSHIONS — deliberately above 50k (keep, tie to base):
6. bootstrap `defaultContractWorkingCapitalFloor = 150_000` (run_bootstrap_coordinator.go:72) — CONTRACT operating capital; gates the bootstrap first-hauler + gate-worker buys (cushion≥floor at run_bootstrap_gate.go:384, run_bootstrap_income.go:323). Immutable (resolved only from the const, run_bootstrap_reconcile.go:289).
7. contractscaler `ContractCushion = 200_000` (contractscaler/commands/run_contract_scaler.go:40, RULINGS #6 amendment — "the SOLE money guard on a scaler buy") — scaler hull/depot CAPEX; gates :356, :466. Immutable.

CONFIG/TUNE SEAMS on the floor (the RULINGS #5 "no seam" targets):
8. `working_capital_reserve` — the EffectiveReserveFloor `absolute` term; per-run config, LIVE = 1_000_000 (config.yaml:208). Read by the factory/tour/trade coordinators.
9. `working_capital_reserve_treasury_pct` — per-run pct override of DefaultReserveTreasuryPct.
10. bootstrap `reserve_margin_percent` / ReserveMargin (run_bootstrap_reconcile.go:73, default defaultReserveMargin) — bootstrap's SEPARATE proportional capital gate ("max % of live treasury a single staged buy may spend"), tune-registry knob.
11. autooutfit `treasury_reserve` — tune-registry knob (container_ops_tune.go:100) + config (coordinator_config.go:18, default 50000).
ADJACENT (a MARGIN, not a floor — note, do not confuse): fleet autosizer `defaultPurchaseMarginOverFloor = 200000` (run_fleet_autosizer_coordinator.go:27) — headroom ABOVE the floor, distinct concept.

## §2 CLASSIFICATION / DISPOSITION
COLLAPSE → the one shared source (exact 50k dupes; RULINGS #5 immutable, byte-identical value): items 1-5 → replace each local `defaultWorkingCapitalReserve`/`defaultTreasuryReserve`/`DefaultReserveFloorCredits` with a reference to common.ImmutableReserveFloor. Delete the compile-time lockstep guard (redundant once there is one definition). (Item 5 rides the capacity-reconciler retirement if sp-y2ptq lands first.)
KEEP + TIE (documented derived exceptions): items 6 (150k) + 7 (200k). Re-home into common as two named, documented tiers derived from the base — e.g. `common.ContractReserveCushion = 150_000` (contract OPERATING capital = ImmutableReserveFloor + 100k, the sp-7r7w split) and `common.ContractScalerCushion = 200_000` (scaler CAPEX = ImmutableReserveFloor + 150k, RULINGS #6). Document WHY scaler capex reserves more than contract operating capital. This reconciles the 150k/200k contract split into two principled tiers with one base.
DELETE (config/tune/launch seams → single immutable source): items 8-11. RULINGS #4 PRESERVED — proof for item 8: floor = max(50k, min(absolute, prop)); removing the `absolute` cap gives max(50k, prop) ≥ current for all inputs (the min can only LOWER), so removal NEVER weakens; it strengthens at high treasury. ECONOMICS FLAG (confirm with the trade-analyst before landing, money-adjacent): removing the 1M `absolute` cap makes the floor purely counter-cyclical (40%×treasury, uncapped), which OVER-reserves at very high treasury (the cap prevented idle over-reserving). If a cap is wanted, define it as ONE immutable derived const, NOT a per-coordinator config knob. Item 10 (reserve_margin_percent) is a DELETE-CANDIDATE: it is bootstrap's parallel proportional gate; unify it onto EffectiveReserveFloor (a floor of (1−pct)×treasury is the dual of a pct spend-cap) — semantics-sensitive, evaluate before deleting.

## §3 UNIFORM-FLOORING DESIGN (the invariant)
INVARIANT: every credit-spend path resolves its floor from `common`, and no floor is defined outside `common`. Three tiers, one base:
- BASE (most paths): EffectiveReserveFloor(ImmutableReserveFloor, DefaultReserveTreasuryPct, treasury) — factory input+output buys, tour/trade, outfitting, autosizer non-contract, frontier (already on it: run_frontier_expansion_coordinator.go:1089), idle-arb legs + contract source-buys (newly, §4).
- CONTRACT OPERATING (contract haulers): common.ContractReserveCushion (150k) — bootstrap first-hauler/gate-worker (already) + autosizer contract-delivery (newly, §5).
- SCALER CAPEX: common.ContractScalerCushion (200k) — contractscaler (already, re-pointed to the common const).
Fail-closed everywhere (unreadable treasury → enforce the absolute/const floor, never proportional, never zero — the existing reserve_floor.go:40 contract).

## §4 CLOSE BOTH MONEY-GUARD GAPS (the RULINGS #4 holes)
sp-65xqo (construction gate-material OUTPUT buy, purchaseFabricatedOutput) — ALREADY CLOSED/FIXED 2026-07-22: floored identically to buyGood (spendFloorBreached + reserveConcurrentSpendOrPark serialization, reusing common.ImmutableReserveFloor, fail-closed park). Cite as the PRECEDENT/pattern; nothing to fold — verify it stays floored after the collapse (it references common, so the collapse must not change its behavior).
sp-sk0xm (contract op — OPEN; the bead itself names THIS consolidation as its fold-target) — SUBSUME. Two currently-unfloored paths to close (add-only proactive EffectiveReserveFloor, reuse common):
  (a) idle-arb legs — internal/application/contract/idle_arb.go: bounded ONLY by MaxSpendPerLeg (:86, DefaultIdleArbMaxSpend=100_000 :168) + margin floors, NO reserve floor. A leg can drop treasury below 50k within the 100k cap. STRONGEST gap → add EffectiveReserveFloor gate at the leg-spend decision.
  (b) contract worker source-buys (market PurchaseCargo) — reactive-only (ErrInsufficientCredits 4600 park), NO proactive floor → add a proactive EffectiveReserveFloor pre-check.
  The whole internal/application/contract package currently has ZERO ImmutableReserveFloor/EffectiveReserveFloor references (per sp-sk0xm) — this brings it onto the shared source.

## §5 RECONCILE sp-w5jr (autosizer contract-delivery floor mismatch — OPEN; SUBSUME)
The fleet autosizer's contract-delivery SCALING buys (haulers #2+) reserve the autosizer's uniform 50k `Reserve` (run_fleet_autosizer_coordinator.go:110-111, via EffectiveReserveFloor) — NOT the 150k contract operating cushion that bootstrap's hauler #1 + gate-worker already hold. FIX (fold in): add a PER-CLASS reserve so contract_delivery buys reserve common.ContractReserveCushion (150k) — the classGuardConfig/buildPurchaseRequest ReserveAbsolute is currently uniform across classes (sp-w5jr). DECIDE the low-treasury semantics: EffectiveReserveFloor's counter-cyclical min(absolute, proportional) means a 150k absolute won't strictly hold 150k below ~375k treasury; keep the counter-cyclical behavior (deadlock-safe) unless the analyst rules the contract op must hold a hard 150k. This is the right-floor-per-path fix the consolidation makes uniform.

## §6 TALLY
- Distinct floors collapsing to ONE: 6 → 1 (common.ImmutableReserveFloor); 5 duplicate 50k consts removed + 1 lockstep guard deleted.
- Higher cushions re-homed as documented derived exceptions: 2 (ContractReserveCushion 150k, ContractScalerCushion 200k) — reconciles the 150k/200k split.
- Config/tune knobs deleted: 4 (working_capital_reserve, working_capital_reserve_treasury_pct, reserve_margin_percent[candidate], treasury_reserve) — with the RULINGS #4 non-weakening proof + economics flag.
- Spend paths newly floored / corrected: 3 = 2 NEWLY floored (idle-arb legs, contract source-buys) + 1 CORRECTED (autosizer contract-delivery 50k→150k). Plus 1 already-closed (construction output-buy, sp-65xqo).

## §7 VERIFY
- Grep proof of single source: exactly ONE definition of the 50k floor (common.ImmutableReserveFloor); zero `= 50000` reserve consts and zero lockstep guard outside common; the 150k/200k cushions defined ONLY in common and referenced everywhere.
- Every credit-spend path resolves its floor via common (base/contract-operating/scaler-capex) — no spend without a floor; audit grep of PurchaseCargo/buy sites shows a reserve check upstream of each.
- Money-guard tests: idle-arb leg + contract source-buy PARK (fail-closed) when a buy would breach the floor; autosizer contract-delivery reserves 150k; construction output-buy stays floored (sp-65xqo regression). No existing floor lowered (no live floor drops: factory/tour/outfitting still ≥ their current effective floor; scaler still 200k; contract operating still 150k).
- make build + go test ./... + -race green.

## §8 BEAD DISPOSITION
- sp-65xqo: already CLOSED — leave; cite as precedent; add a regression assertion here.
- sp-sk0xm: SUBSUMED by this bead — close as folded-in when this lands (it explicitly nominated this consolidation).
- sp-w5jr: SUBSUMED by this bead (§5) — close as folded-in when this lands.

## REFERENCES
Admiral reserve-floor consolidation 2026-07-22 (epic sp-ktio). sp-65xqo (construction output-buy, CLOSED — precedent). sp-sk0xm (contract idle-arb/source-buy gap — subsumed). sp-w5jr (autosizer contract-delivery floor — subsumed). sp-7r7w (the 150k contract cushion split). Commit 11dff6da (the 50k lockstep origin). common.ImmutableReserveFloor / EffectiveReserveFloor (reserve_floor.go). RULINGS #4 (never weaken), #5 (single immutable source), #6 (scaler 200k cushion exemption).
notes:
Admiral ruling 2026-07-22: SCRAP the 40% proportional rule ENTIRELY (not just the 1M cap). Base reserve floor collapses to the FLAT 50k common.ImmutableReserveFloor everywhere — no proportional term, no cap. DELETE: working_capital_reserve + _treasury_pct + reserve_margin_percent + treasury_reserve + the 1M cap const + the whole 40%-of-treasury computation. Effect: spend down to 50k (solvency-safe, frees ~all capital; fleet nets +10M/day so aggressive deployment is fine). KEEP UNTOUCHED: the 150k/200k contract cushions — those are RULINGS #6 money guards, NOT the 40% rule. Final shape: ONE flat 50k base floor (manufacturing/trade/outfitting/autosizer/capacity) + the contract-scaler cushion as the single principled higher guard.

title: money-guard: floor contract idle-arb legs + source-buys with ImmutableReserveFloor — close RULINGS #4 gap (twin of sp-65xqo)
description:
RULINGS #4 money-guard gap (contract op) — TWIN of sp-65xqo (construction). Traced read-only by the contract-debug agent on current main (design for sp-g4h4b). FULL CONSUMPTION TRACE (all internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_depot_reserve.go):

  -> reserveHomeContractWorkers(intents, budget) (line 133-150): walks the depot launch's delivery-hull intents; while budget.remaining() (= Available - (Floor - ContractDedicated)) is positive it PINS; once the Floor budget is spent, every FURTHER in-pool delivery hull is RESERVED (line 147 `reserved[intent.shipSymbol]=true`) — held back from pinning.
  -> reclaimPinnedForFloor(budget, freshlyReserved) (line 109-118): when the fresh reserve can't reach the floor, RECLAIMS already-pinned delivery hulls (Pinned[:outstanding]) back to "contract".
  -> dedicateContractReserve() (line 248-256): AssignFleet(ship, "contract") on each reserved/reclaimed hull — removes it from the poachable pool while keeping it available to the coordinator's FindIdleShipsByFleet("contract").
IS IT FUNCTIONAL? YES. The Floor value directly determines remaining() -> which delivery-hull intents are reserved vs pinned, and reclaimPinnedForFloor's shortfall. A different Floor yields a different reserved/reclaimed set. It is NOT read-and-ignored.
INTERACTION WITH (a) dedicated fleet + (b) single-hull dispatch: ORTHOGONAL, not superseded. The floor governs DEPOT-DELIVERY PINNING of the UNDEDICATED home-general-hauler pool — a DIFFERENT population than the scaler's contract-tagged fleet. Single-hull dispatch (SelectClosestShip) PICKS one hull per contract FROM that pool, so it DEPENDS on the floor keeping the pool non-empty; it cannot replace it.
CONCRETE FAILURE WITHOUT IT (Floor=0): reserveHomeContractWorkers reserves NOTHING (remaining never binds) -> the depot launch (container_ops_depot_launch.go, positionDepotElementHull) pins EVERY declared delivery hull to depot.DeliveryHullFleet, EXCLUDED from the contract coordinator's grab (FindIdleLightHaulers + ClaimShip skip foreign-tagged hulls). An UNBUFFERED-good contract — ANY good outside the depot's fixed 8 far-source buffered goods (contractscaler.FarSourceGoods) — then has ZERO general home haulers to source it: the coordinator's home-scoped grab returns empty and the contract cannot be sourced. WHICH OP GRABS THE HULLS: the depot launch, pinning them to depot.DeliveryHullFleet. WHAT CAN'T SOURCE: every unbuffered-good procurement contract.
CAN IT DROP LIVE -> INTERNAL CONST? YES. Value = MinHomeContractWorkersDefault=6; currently resolved at the DEFAULT (live tune shows source=default, never retuned). Const-ify: delete the config field (contract.go MinHomeContractWorkers + mapstructure), the tune-registry entry (container_ops_tune.go), and the live>launch>default resolver (resolveMinHomeContractWorkers / liveMinHomeContractWorkers / activeContractCoordinatorConfig read of this key); inline the const 6 at homeContractWorkerReserve's Floor. Byte-identical (6==6). TRADEOFF (mild): loses live-retune — if the depot topology later needs a bigger sourcing floor it takes a code redeploy, not a `tune`. Acceptable: it is a starvation FLOOR (not a perf dial) and has never been retuned.
DISPOSITION: NOT deleted (load-bearing) but const-ified (6) -> removed from the operator surface. Operator-dial contribution: 0.

--- idle_arb 2 -> 1: fold `disabled` INTO `min_net_profit_per_unit` via a NEGATIVE sentinel ---
SINGLE KNOB: idle_arb.min_net_profit_per_unit (LIVE). Encoding:
  < 0  => idle-arb OFF (short-circuit).
  == 0 => default-ON (WithDefaults resolves to DefaultIdleArbMinNetProfit=100) — preserves today's "omitted key = default-on money guard" semantics.
  > 0  => the absolute per-unit net-profit floor (aggressiveness); gate stays net/unit >= max(floor, frozen 20% x buy) after 35/u fuel.
SENTINEL JUSTIFICATION (negative, NOT 0): a per-unit NET-PROFIT floor is semantically NON-NEGATIVE (you never chase a net-loss leg), so the entire negative range is unused and free to encode OFF UNAMBIGUOUSLY — zero collision with the legitimate value domain. 0 is NOT usable as OFF for two reasons: (1) 0 already means "default" (WithDefaults -> 100); flipping it to OFF would silently DISABLE idle-arb whenever a config omits the key, breaking the default-on money-guard convention (RULINGS #4, matching MarginVerifyFraction/Blacklist siblings); (2) the frozen net_profit_pct=20% relative floor still BINDS at 0, so 0 is neither "off" nor "take everything." The max_probe_price=0=disabled convention does not transfer here because 0 is already meaningful. Negative is the one unambiguous, collision-free sentinel.
SHORT-CIRCUIT (no efficiency loss): the dispatcher launch gate at run_fleet_coordinator.go:230 currently reads `if h.idleArbLauncher != nil && !cmd.IdleArbDisabled {`. Replace with `if h.idleArbLauncher != nil && idleArbEnabled(cmd.IdleArbMinNetProfit) {` where `idleArbEnabled(v) => v >= 0`. When OFF the dispatcher goroutine NEVER STARTS — no 90s eval loop, no candidate scan — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the old `disabled` bool (disabled skipped evaluation entirely, not evaluate-then-reject). DELETE: the IdleArbDisabled command field + the idle_arb.disabled config knob + its plumbing; the sentinel check replaces the branch.
BEHAVIOR WHEN ON: byte-identical — same 90s interval, same gate, same frozen consts (leash 150 / hub 250 / 8m / 100k spend / verify 80% / [ELECTRONICS] / recovery 20m / fuel 35 / net_profit_pct 20).

--- FINAL BEFORE -> AFTER: 31 -> 2 OPERATOR DIALS ---
OPERATOR-TUNABLE DIALS (2):
  1. contract_fleet_max_hulls (LIVE) — fleet size.
  2. idle_arb.min_net_profit_per_unit (LIVE) — idle-arb aggressiveness; negative = OFF (folds the old disabled).
LOAD-BEARING INTERNAL CONSTS retained (values preserved, NOT operator surface): ContractCushion=200000 (money guard; fold-target for the future reserve-floor consolidation), min_home_contract_workers=6 (depot-pin sourcing floor), tick=900, + 12 frozen idle_arb consts.

title: Simplify gate construction: DELETE the unified_gate_fill + fabrication_efficiency + strategy machinery (inline the sole paths), consolidate knobs 16->2 (worker count + price-ceiling)
description:
AUTHORIZED knob-consolidation + CODE-SIMPLIFICATION DESIGN for the GATE-CONSTRUCTION subsystem (Admiral rulings 2026-07-22). UPDATED: the Admiral wants the CODE simpler, not a value freeze — for anything that drives a BRANCH or a CONCEPT, DELETE the machinery (branch + concept + plumbing) and inline the sole surviving path; a plain VALUE (timeout, worker cap) may become an internal const. Behavior-preserving (same tasks + fabricate-vs-buy decisions at default) achieved via LESS CODE. Read-only analysis; the shipwright implements. All claims cite gobot/ file:line on `main`. Absorbs sp-4ylok. Sibling/《coordinates》 with sp-hoj8u (retires goods-factory + siting): several deletions here are ENABLED by sp-hoj8u (once construction is the only ProductionExecutor user) — the boundary is called out per item.

## SACRED CONSTRAINT
Gate construction is the sole surviving factory op. Behavior at default must be PRESERVED: a bare `construction start <gate>` stages the identical pipeline + task set and drives to COMPLETE with the same per-node fabricate-vs-buy decisions. This is achieved by DELETING dead alternative branches and inlining the path that is already taken today (unified_gate_fill=true, fabrication_efficiency=true, smart) — NOT by freezing a bool. No behavior change (e.g. supply-adaptive depth) is bundled in.

## §1 ENUMERATION — 16 behavior knobs (unchanged from prior rev; see layers A-E)
A. `construction start`: --depth, --max-workers, --min-supply, --good-override, --overrides (construction.go:378-387).
B. `construction override`: --min-supply, --strategy, --price-ceiling-mult, --clear (construction.go:731-736).
C. `construction workers`: --count (construction.go:820).
D. [manufacturing] config keys reaching construction (resolveConstructionUnifiedGateFill, container_ops_manufacturing.go:16-30): unified_gate_fill, fabrication_efficiency, feed_saturation_max_units, feed_saturation_min_units, feed_non_responsive_goods, construction_supply_task_timeout_seconds.
E. tune-registry construction knobs: NONE.
TOTAL BEFORE = 16.

## §2 CONSTRUCTION vs GOODS-FACTORY CONFIG (disjoint from sp-hoj8u) — unchanged
sp-hoj8u deletes the ~17 goods_factory-ONLY [manufacturing] keys (injectManufacturingConfig, container_ops_manufacturing.go:86-216). This bead owns the 6 construction-relevant keys (resolveConstructionUnifiedGateFill). No double-count. The construction drain uses the SHARED engine (ProductionExecutor / SupplyChainResolver / MarketLocator / input_source_selector) — KEPT — but sp-hoj8u makes construction the ONLY engine user, which is what makes the §3 branch deletions safe.

## §3 DISPOSITION — BRANCH/CONCEPT (delete machinery) vs VALUE (const OK)
### 3a. CONCEPTS — delete the machinery, inline the sole path
**unified_gate_fill (row 11) — DELETE the flag + OFF codepath + resolver + config key; inline recursive-feed as the sole path.** Every branch site (OFF arm dead once construction is the only engine user + always delivers to a gate site, post-sp-hoj8u):
  - run_construction_coordinator.go:792 `if cmd.UnifiedGateFill { WithUnifiedGateFill+WithDeliveryTarget }` → always stamp the construction-site DeliveryTarget (the toggle stamp itself becomes redundant).
  - :890 `if FactorySymbol=="" && !cmd.UnifiedGateFill { return 1 }` → `!UnifiedGateFill` is always false → DEAD; delete → buy-planned tasks also get chain-depth-scaled timeout (their real depth).
  - :1082 `if cmd.UnifiedGateFill { resolveFabricationTree first }` → UNCONDITIONAL: always resolve the full scarcity-gated tree, then the :1087 (no-factory→buy) / :1090 (fabricate) fallbacks. The planner's "frozen buy-vs-fabricate" OFF path is dead.
  - construction_pipeline_planner.go admissionFloor:110 + field:52 + SetUnifiedGateFill:91 → always default empty --min-supply to SCARCE; delete the field + setter (this is also how row-3 --min-supply becomes redundant).
  - input_price_ceiling.go:136,217 `if IsUnifiedGateNode(ctx)` → always margin-blind; inline the ON arm, delete the OFF arm.
  - unified_gate_fill.go: WithUnifiedGateFill / unifiedGateFillFromContext / the toggle half of IsUnifiedGateNode → collapse; IsUnifiedGateNode reduces to DeliveryTarget.IsConstructionSite() (and, with resale gone per below, effectively constant-true).
  Wiring deletes: container_ops_construction.go:101 SetUnifiedGateFill; resolveConstructionUnifiedGateFill (container_ops_manufacturing.go:16-30) + its call command_factory_registry.go:477 + the :981 cfg.OptionalBool read; types/construction_coordinator_types.go:33 field; ManufacturingConfig.UnifiedGateFill + config.yaml:217 key. RESULT: one code path, no `unified_gate_fill` conditional anywhere.
  EXPOSED-DEAD → COORDINATE WITH sp-hoj8u (the profit-factory *resale* concept, dead once construction is the only engine user): production_executor.go:1077 resale-margin/crushed-sink guard block (`if !ConstructionSupplyFromContext && !IsUnifiedGateNode` → always false); SellFabricatedOutputAtSink (:1263) + chain_margin_guard.go + the FindImportMarket-as-sink lookups. These are goods-factory resale machinery — delete with sp-hoj8u, not silently here, to keep the bead boundary clean.

**fabrication_efficiency (row 12) — TRACED: NON-TRIVIAL / LOAD-BEARING (STOP-AND-REPORT).** It is a feeding ALGORITHM, NOT a constant fudge factor — do NOT "fold it into a constant" (there is no constant). feeding_policy.go encodes real per-tick logic: balancedTranche (per-input cap = the LIMITING/min sourceable flow across the node's inputs via peekInputAvailability = live FindExportMarket + CalculateSupplyAwareLimit, clamped into [25,200]); orderTaprootFirst (feed scarcest/deepest input first); isFeedResponsive (BUY-OR-SKIP non-responders {EQUIPMENT,LAB_INSTRUMENTS,FOOD,MEDICINE}); saturation caps. The "~4x lever" is the EFFECT of balanced-vs-greedy feeding (+0.12 vs +0.03 activity), not a literal multiplier. Consumed at production_executor.go:851 feedingPolicyEngaged → :852 responsive-skip + :869 planBalancedFeed.

**--strategy / production strategy (row 7) — only "smart" survives; delete the other branches (coordinate with sp-hoj8u).** Construction's GLOBAL strategy is ALWAYS DefaultProductionStrategy="smart" (construction_pipeline_planner.go:678).
