title: Expose contract idle-arb params (leash_radius + siblings) as live tunables — Admiral-directed leash widen to ~400
description:
ADMIRAL-DIRECTED (via captain st-wisp-ldyg9): widen the contract idle-arb leash to put the 9 idle contract haulers to work. The idle-arb params are NOT live-tunable today (config.yaml Layer-B only, restart-applied); the contract coordinator's tune registry exposes only depot_buffer_min_source_distance + min_home_contract_workers.

## FIX (RULINGS #5 parametrize; the captain wants to tune it live)
EXPOSE the idle-arb params as LIVE tunables on the `contract` tune operation, following the EXISTING pattern (how depot_buffer_min_source_distance / min_home_contract_workers are registered in internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_tune.go).
- PRIORITY knob: idle_arb_leash_radius.
- IDEALLY also (same coordinator, marginal cost): idle_arb_hub_radius, idle_arb_max_leg_secs, idle_arb_max_spend, idle_arb_min_margin. The config-injected keys already exist in container_ops_contract.go (resolveIdleArbConfig / the idle_arb_* key list :276-289) and the struct is internal/infrastructure/config/contract.go.

## REQUIREMENTS
- Register the knobs in the contract tune bounds registry (container_ops_tune.go) with SANE bounds. leash_radius e.g. [0, 2000]. Bounds MUST keep idle-arb INTRA-SYSTEM (RULINGS #14) — the current hub_radius 250 / leash 150 are intra-system X1-UM5 waypoint distances; the bound must not let a tune enable cross-system legs.
- LIVE re-read: the idle-arb loop must read leash_radius from the live container config each tick (Layer C), not frozen at launch. VERIFY this; if it's launch-frozen, wire the live re-read so a `tune` lands next tick (like the other live-tuned coordinators). This is the crux — a registered knob that the loop never re-reads is a no-op.
- DEFAULT-OFF / byte-identical: registering a tunable does NOT change the current config.yaml value (leash stays 150 until armed). Arming to 400 is the shipwright's live-tune AFTER deploy (RULINGS #19) — do NOT bump the config default in code.
- Money guards (RULINGS #4) unchanged: widening the leash must NOT weaken max_spend / min_margin — those stay enforced; the leash only widens the geographic search radius.

## EVIDENCE (captain)
Profitable NON-reserved lanes blocked ONLY by the 150 leash: EQUIPMENT K83->C38 net 148/u (dist 199), K83->D40 net 171/u (dist 164). ~250 unlocks these; 400 is the Admiral's generous target. Caveat: many goods contract-reserved (skip:reserved ~40/pass) so the unlock is modest but real.

## ACCEPTANCE (test the mechanism)
`spacetraders tune --operation contract idle_arb_leash_radius 400` is ACCEPTED (in bounds), amends the container config, lands next tick, and SURVIVES a daemon restart; an out-of-bounds value is REJECTED before any write. The idle-arb loop uses the LIVE value (unit/integration test the re-read seam). Other idle-arb behavior unchanged; OFF/default path byte-identical.

## CONSTRAINTS
RULINGS #4 (money guards fail closed, never weakened), #5 (parametrize), #14 (contract ops single-system), #19 (closed is not armed — arming is separate), #12/#13 (commit --no-verify then captain-gate only; verify SHA). ENGINEERING §6 (short WHY-only comments, no bead-ids/changelog prose). Protected paths untouched.
notes:
ESCALATION (build-agent, per brief §3 STOP condition) — idle-arb loop CONFIRMED launch-frozen, not live-re-read. Stopping before implementation per explicit instruction; no code changed.

VERIFICATION ANSWER: the idle-arb harvest loop does NOT read leash_radius/hub_radius/max_leg_secs/max_spend/min_margin via a per-tick live re-read (the seam depot_buffer_min_source_distance/min_home_contract_workers use). It reads a value-typed config struct frozen once at container launch/restart-recovery. Evidence chain (gobot, worktree captain-worktrees/sp-a9bhc):

1. internal/application/contract/idle_arb.go: IdleArbDispatcher.cfg is a plain-VALUE IdleArbConfig field. NewIdleArbDispatcher sets `cfg: cfg.WithDefaults()` once at construction, never mutated after. Run/DispatchOnce/pickHubLocalLane/laneSkipReason/netProfitFloor/laneNetPerUnit/idleArbMinMargin all read d.cfg.X directly — no DB call, no reader interface, no per-tick snapshot.

2. internal/application/contract/commands/run_fleet_coordinator.go: NewIdleArbDispatcher(...) has exactly ONE production call site, inside RunFleetCoordinatorHandler.Handle() — the coordinator's one-time command-handler entrypoint (fires once per container lifetime, not per tick). The IdleArbConfig literal is built directly from cmd.IdleArb* fields.

3. internal/application/contract/types/contract_types.go: RunFleetCoordinatorCommand carries all IdleArb* fields, commented "All knobs flow from the persisted launch config (RULINGS #5); zero values take the contract package's documented defaults." A neighboring comment on the same struct (DedicatedShipsSeeded) explicitly names it "the immutable launch snapshot."

4. internal/adapters/grpc/command_factory_registry.go:953-1001 (buildContractFleetCoordinatorCommand): populates IdleArbLeashRadius(991)/HubRadius(982)/MaxSpend(983)/MinMargin(984)/MaxLegSecs(992) from cfg.OptionalInt("idle_arb_*", 0) — i.e. the container's persisted config column — but this function is only invoked by buildCommandForType, which fires ONLY at container creation + restart-recovery, never per-tick. Its own comment: "resolved LIVE from config.yaml by resolveIdleArbConfig on every build ... so a config edit + daemon restart retunes the harvest."

5. resolveIdleArbConfig (container_ops_contract.go, confirmed pre-summary): on every buildCommandForType call, DELETES all persisted idleArbConfigKeys and reinjects fresh from s.contractConfig.IdleArb (daemon's config.yaml loaded ONCE at boot). File comment: "the persisted idle_arb_* keys are dead."

CONTRAST #1 — the two existing live tunables (depot_buffer_min_source_distance, min_home_contract_workers) use a DIFFERENT seam: activeContractCoordinatorConfig, reading the coordinator's persisted config column FRESH FROM THE DB at the actual decision point (warehouse solve / depot launch) — not a loop-internal snapshot, not resolveIdleArbConfig's boot-reinjection. That seam does not exist for the 5 idle-arb knobs.

CONTRAST #2 — the ONE live-reread exception that DOES exist in this exact dispatcher: StandbyStations, via IdleArbDispatcher.SetStandbyResolver/resolveStandby, wired through RunFleetCoordinatorHandler.standbyProvider -> appContract.ResolveStandbyStations. Comment: "resolves from its own container config each pass instead of the frozen launch snapshot." Proves the authors know how to wire live-reread for this dispatcher and deliberately did NOT extend it to LeashRadius/HubRadius/MaxLegDuration/MaxSpendPerLeg/MinMarginPerUnit.

ADDITIONAL FINDING — a naive mechanical tune registration would be actively MISLEADING, not merely inert: because resolveIdleArbConfig deletes+reinjects from boot config.yaml on every buildCommandForType call, `tune --operation contract idle_arb_leash_radius 400` would (a) have ZERO effect on the running coordinator (cfg already baked in, never re-read), AND (b) be WIPED on the coordinator's next restart-recovery rebuild (resolveIdleArbConfig deletes the persisted key before the command factory re-reads it) — the tune would not even survive to be picked up later. A `tune --show` could report it as "live" while it's silently discarded twice over.

DECISION: per brief §3, stopping before implementation. No tune-bounds registration, no tests, no code edits, no commits made (pure read-only verification, as instructed).

OPTIONS for the shipwright:
A) Extend the bespoke SetStandbyResolver-style live-reader pattern (already proven in this dispatcher) to the 5 money-guard/geometry knobs, resolving from activeContractCoordinatorConfig each DispatchOnce/tick — same DB-read-at-point-of-use seam the 2 existing tunables use, for consistency.
B) Switch IdleArbConfig's target fields from a value baked in at construction to reads via activeContractCoordinatorConfig-at-point-of-use directly (bigger refactor: touches Run/DispatchOnce/every helper currently reading d.cfg.X).
C) Scope "live tunable" down to what's already supported: config.yaml edit + daemon restart (recovery-safe, RULINGS #2) — register nothing in the runtime tune-bounds registry; ship config.yaml as the sanctioned retune path; treat true no-restart live-tune as a separate follow-up bead.
D) Shipwright's judgment given the coordinator's broader roadmap.

Bounds guidance preserved for whichever option is chosen: live hub_radius 250 / leash 150 are intra-system X1-UM5 distances; any future tune bounds must keep the max within intra-system range (RULINGS #14) — e.g. leash_radius upper bound well under a cross-system jump distance.

No code changed, no tests written, no commit, no gate/merge attempted this session.
SHIPWRIGHT DECISION on v1 escalation (2026-07-20): v1 (sonnet) CORRECTLY escalated per the brief's STOP clause — the idle-arb params are LAUNCH-FROZEN (IdleArbDispatcher.cfg is a value struct set once in NewIdleArbDispatcher; resolveIdleArbConfig DELETES persisted idle_arb_* keys + re-injects from config.yaml every rebuild). A naive tune registration would be a MISLEADING no-op (frozen value + wiped on restart). Honest escalation — correct call.

DECISION — Option (A), SCOPED TO GEOMETRY ONLY:
- LIVE-TUNABLE: idle_arb_leash_radius, idle_arb_hub_radius, idle_arb_max_leg_secs (the search-radius knobs = the actual ask).
- KEEP CONFIG-ONLY (do NOT expose live): idle_arb_max_spend, idle_arb_min_margin — MONEY GUARDS (RULINGS #4). Making guards runtime-mutable is a separate careful decision, out of scope. leash/hub/max_leg fully cover the leash-widening need.
- IMPL: mirror the PROVEN live-reader already in this dispatcher — activeContractCoordinatorConfig (the seam depot_buffer_min_source_distance + min_home_contract_workers use) / the SetStandbyResolver-resolveStandby resolver pattern. Read the 3 geometry values fresh at the decision point each tick.
- RESTART SURVIVAL (RULINGS #2): resolveIdleArbConfig currently WIPES persisted idle_arb_* keys on rebuild — the 3 tunable geometry keys must SURVIVE a restart (a live tune must persist). Fix the clear-and-reinject precedence so a live tune of these 3 wins (mirror how depot_buffer_min_source_distance survives).
- BOUNDS: leash_radius [0,2000], hub/max_leg sane; all keeping idle-arb INTRA-SYSTEM (RULINGS #14).

RE-DISPATCH as OPUS (the resolveIdleArbConfig precedence + live-read seam is design judgment). DEFERRED until a lane slot frees — currently at the 3-lane cap with sp-iwra3 + sp-cu1ou, and urgency DROPPED (captain st-wisp-qezx5: idle haulers now on gate construction, leash is nice-to-have).
close_reason: Superseded by sp-g4h4b (full contract knob consolidation) per Admiral ruling 2026-07-22: idle-arb leash becomes a FROZEN internal const, NOT a live tunable — full consolidation chosen over expose+widen. If leash was already partially exposed, sp-g4h4b re-freezes it. Leash freeze value (400 per this bead's widen intent vs 150 current) pending Admiral in sp-g4h4b.

title: Captain wakes every ~11min despite heartbeat_minutes=60 — NOT the base-heartbeat value; suspect stale wake anchor [Tier-3 internal/captain]
description:
Captain waking ~7-11min apart (02:38/47/54, 03:05) despite config.yaml [captain] heartbeat_minutes=60. Low urgency (token waste, not blocking the op). Origin: captain mail st-wisp-h087p; follow-up to tb7kv/ndwc6/vpiyo.

## SHIPWRIGHT FINDINGS (verified code + live — the captain's "base heartbeat ~11min" is a misattribution)
- config.yaml:131 heartbeat_minutes: 60, mapped via mapstructure "heartbeat_minutes" (internal/infrastructure/config/captain.go:12). Fallback default when unset = 45 (defaults.go:212), NOT 11. So the ~11min cadence matches NEITHER the configured 60 NOR the default 45 → it is NOT the base-heartbeat VALUE.
- Watchkeeper (com.spacetraders.captain, PID 15525) runs cwd=gobot, reads gobot/config.yaml, started 23:38 (config was already 60 by then; heartbeat_minutes=60 since 2026-07-12). BD_REAL present in plist. So config IS loaded → a plain watchkeeper restart will NOT change anything (predecessor already restarted; config is correct — do NOT just re-restart).
- wakegate.go effectiveNextWake = base + HeartbeatMinutes, base = later(LastSession, Policy.DeclaredAt). A wake every ~11min with heartbeat=60 loaded implies EITHER:
  (a) LastSession/DeclaredAt anchor not advancing after a captain session → next-wake perpetually in the past → evaluateWakeGate returns "cadence due" every poll, rate-limited by max_sessions_per_hour=20 to ~3-11min (this MATCHES the symptom + the captain's "base heartbeat firing" read); OR
  (b) interrupt events (workflow.failed/container.crashed) firing ~every 11min — captain reports interrupt_types intact and "NOT routine events", which points AWAY from (b).
  → Leading suspect: (a) stale wake anchor.
- The watchkeeper does NOT log the wake-decision REASON (evaluateWakeGate.Reason is code-only, not emitted to captain-supervisor.log) → cadence is currently UNDIAGNOSABLE from logs. That opacity is the first thing to fix.

## FIX (Tier-3 — internal/captain is a protected rail, RULINGS #17 → needs Admiral bd human before code moves)
1. Add wake-decision-reason logging to the watchkeeper poll loop: log evaluateWakeGate.Reason + effectiveNextWake vs now + LastSession/DeclaredAt on each wake. Instantly disambiguates (a) vs (b) live, cheaply.
2. Verify LastSession is persisted AND advanced on every completed captain session (RULINGS #2 restart resilience). If the stale-anchor is root, fix the persistence/advance.

## ACCEPTANCE
Captain wakes ~60min apart (heartbeat cadence) absent interrupt events; the wake-decision reason is visible in captain-supervisor.log for every wake.

## CONSTRAINTS
RULINGS #17 (internal/captain protected — Admiral sign-off), #2 (restart resilience), #15 (one-shot wake triggers). LOW priority — do after the sp-iwra3 depot lane.
notes:
CAPTAIN CONFIRMATION (st-wisp-bnsrn 2026-07-20): last ~8 wakes carried NO interrupt events — all routine (contract.completed, ship.idle, scout.post_manning_stalled, workflow.finished, hull.containerless, prometheus.alert_firing), and interrupt_types is failures-only (verified via wake show), so those did NOT trigger the wakes => BARE CADENCE wakes. This CONFIRMS the stale-wake-anchor hypothesis (LastSession/DeclaredAt not advancing after a captain session -> effectiveNextWake perpetually in the past -> cadence-due fires every poll, rate-limited by max_sessions_per_hour to ~11min). Narrows the fix: (1) add wake-reason logging; (2) ensure a completed captain session PERSISTS + ADVANCES LastSession (RULINGS #2). Still Tier-3 (internal/captain) — awaits Admiral sign-off.
ADMIRAL SIGN-OFF (in-chat 2026-07-20): 'do sp-cu1ou' — Tier-3 (internal/captain) approval granted; cleared to dispatch a build lane.
session died

title: [design/WIP] Pre-stock delivery MESH for contract ops — distributed stocked warehouses + nearest-delivery (data-validated ~3-6x contract $/hr)
description:
STATUS: DESIGN IN PROGRESS (economy-analyst + captain, 2026-07-20). NOT ready to build. One open decision (warehouse hull-vs-station, below) gates the spec — continue the discussion before handing to the shipwright. All numbers are data-derived (era-3 full week + era-4 current); analysis method noted per section for reproducibility.

## CONCEPT (captain's proposal)
Replace dedicated contract delivery "workers" with a distributed MESH of pre-stocked mobile warehouses ("the warehouse doubles as worker") orbiting strategic contract-delivery SINKS, kept full by async stockers. On a contract, the NEAREST stocked warehouse to the sink delivers locally (~3-min withdrawal). Novel-good contracts fall back to live source+deliver by the same fleet. Goal: move source+haul OFF the serial contract clock onto a parallel stocker fleet -> compress cycle-time -> multiply contract $/hr.

## VALIDATION (data; method = per-sink good concentration + causal/prequential coverage)
- Sinks are CONCENTRATED, not random — a universe-invariant mechanic (IDENTICAL era 3 & era 4): mean 3.7 distinct goods/sink (universe ~38 goods), top-3 goods = 88% of a sink's demand. "Same waypoints demand the same products" = CONFIRMED (geometry transfers across eras; names/prices do not).
- CAUSAL coverage (could a mesh have pre-stocked it from that sink's history?) RAMPS as good-sets saturate: era-3 top-5-goods/sink = 80% overall, 91% by Q3 (mature); stock-all = 98-99% mature. The earlier "~55%" was an era-4 cold-start (Q1) artifact. Coverage is a RAMP: Q1 ~50% (learning) -> ~90% (mature).
- Value-coverage lags count slightly (covered skew lower-value): top-5 = 77% of value.

## REVENUE MODEL (era-3; method = renewal-reward, serial engine ran 100% back-to-back so cycle-compression converts directly)
- BASELINE (actual era 3): 454 contracts, 34.2M value / 148.5h = ~230k $/hr GROSS contract value (net ~0.4-0.6x). Cycle mean 19.6m, median 4.4m (slow long tail).
- OPTIMAL MESH (covered contract cycle -> W~3-min withdrawal): causal-online top-5 (80% cov) = 840k (3.65x); hindsight top-5 (95% cov) = 1.38M (6.0x); stock-all (100%) = 1.62M (7.0x). Robust to W: 4.5x even at W=5m.
- **KEY FINDING (answers mesh-vs-repositioning): FULL mesh (all 18 sinks) = 6.0x, but LEAN value-ranked sets are near-worthless — top-3 sinks 1.20x, top-5 1.23x, top-8 1.24x, ALL 6.0x.** The throughput gain lives in the SLOW LONG-TAIL sinks (the 19.6-min-mean contracts); top-value sinks are ALREADY fast (nothing to compress). => cover EVERY recurring sink, ranked by CYCLE-TIME-SAVED, not by value. Nearest-delivery across the full mesh beats any repositioning subset decisively.
- REALISTIC (after stocker/source-throughput limits, below): ~2-4x, still enormous vs 230k.

## SIZING under the 80-units/hull cargo cap (method = era-3 unit demand)
- Unit demand is LOW: 17,075 units total, ~115 units/hr, mean 37.5/contract, p90 71, 99.6% of contracts <=80 units (fit one load).
- STOCKERS ARE CHEAP (not the constraint): 80 cargo / ~10-min in-system round-trip = ~480 units/hr per stocker => ~1 stocker covers throughput even at 4x demand; ~4-6 for distribution logistics across sinks.
- WAREHOUSE SIDE is where 80 units bites: to deliver an UNKNOWN next good instantly, a warehouse must hold the sink's top-K goods SIMULTANEOUSLY, but 80 units holds only ~2 goods at contract-depth (mean 37.5 / p90 71). => warehouse-hulls/sink: top-2 goods (73% cov) = 1; top-3 (88%) = 2; top-5 (95%) = 3. x18 sinks = 18 / 36 / 54 warehouse-hulls.
- FULL 6x mesh ~= 54 warehouse-hulls + ~6 stockers ~= 60 hulls.

## BINDING CONSTRAINTS (ranked)
1. WAREHOUSE-HULL COUNT (the 80-cargo depth) — dominant: 18 (73% cov) -> 54 (95% cov).
2. API BUDGET (per-account rate limit, PLAYBOOK 6) — ~40-60 hulls stocking+delivering continuously is real pressure; may cap the practical mesh size below the economic optimum.
3. SOURCE-MARKET SUPPLY — comfortable at 3-4x (top good IRON ~50 units/hr vs trade_volume ~20), tightens at 6x (buy-side crush on the top goods).
4. STOCKER THROUGHPUT — cheap.

## OPEN DECISION — GATES THE SPEC (discuss next)
Are warehouses (a) 80-cargo MOBILE HULLS (captain's "double as workers"), or (b) fixed DEEP-STORAGE stations with small separate delivery hops? Swings the fleet from ~60 hulls (a) to ~20 (b): a deep station per sink holds all top-K goods, you pay only for stockers + delivery hops. HIGHEST-LEVERAGE question — resolve (incl. what the game actually allows) before speccing.

## OTHER OPEN QUESTIONS
- Coverage target vs hull/API budget: full 6x @ ~60 hulls vs pragmatic ~3x @ ~42 hulls (2 wh/sink, top-3) vs lean ~2.5x @ ~22 hulls (1 wh/sink, top-2). Recommend START lean, add warehouse depth at the highest cycle-time-saved sinks, bounded by API budget.
- Buffer-depth / stock-selection policy: rank stocked goods per sink by cycle-time-saved (the reconciler's value-density scorer already computes avoided-minutes).
- Cold-start ramp: fleet must do BOTH modes from day 1 (live-source early ~Q1 50%, pre-stock later ~90%).
- Stocker restock policy: standing buffer vs just-in-time; per-sink contract inter-arrival ~6h (3/hr / 18 sinks) gives ample restock window.

## RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK
- GENERALIZES sp-u9xa (few fixed depots) to a full nearest-delivery mesh over ALL recurring sinks.
- PREREQUISITE: sp-10nn (contract-delivery ADD-gate fix — remove the trade-contaminated FleetPerHullCrHr). The reconciler won't build ANY depot/warehouse until that lands; the mesh is the reconciler's depot topology scaled up.
- TIES sp-qqwm (depot economics / renewal-reward), sp-27at (aggressive-scaling engine), sp-cr2v (hauler-first staging).

## NEXT STEPS
1. Resolve the warehouse hull-vs-station fork (captain + game-mechanics check).
2. Lock the coverage target vs the API/hull budget.
3. economy-analyst writes the full build spec; shipwright builds DEFAULT-OFF (PLAYBOOK 10). Land sp-10nn first (prerequisite).

title: CONSULT (economy-analyst): is the capacity reconciler correctly SIZING the contract op at cold-start? desiring warehouse/stocker/depot-delivery with 0 haulers
description:
CONSULT (refute-first; file to BREAK the premise, not bless it). Owner: economy-analyst. Asker: captain.

QUESTION: is the capacity reconciler's DESIRED contract-op topology correct for the current cold-start state, or is it mis-sizing (over-desiring warehouse/stocker/depot-delivery before a hauler pool exists)?

== LIVE SNAPSHOT (torwind-2026-07-19, player 4, ~16:57) ==
treasury 195646, income 68818/hr, 5 contracts fulfilled (incl. 139896 + 123144). Coverage ~59% (16/27).
Fleet = 1 COMMAND frigate (TORWIND-1, on batch-contract) + 3 probes (scouting). ZERO light haulers, hubs, warehouse, stocker.
Bootstrap prematurely at GATE (separate shipwright bug filed). Era clock: next reset 2026-07-26.

== OBSERVATION ==
capacity_reconciler log: every tick it tries tier1_reuse_idle reassignments of the 3 cargo-0 probes into WAREHOUSE, STOCKER, and DEPOT-DELIVERY fleets (all blocked by the sp-r6f1 cargo-floor guard). So its desired topology WANTS warehouse+stocker+depot-delivery capacity RIGHT NOW, at cold-start, with a single frigate and no hauler pool.

== REFUTE/CONFIRM AGAINST DOCTRINE ==
PLAYBOOK 5 (warehousing staging): bootstrap (frigate+probe) = NO warehousing; hauler-pool-forming = still none; only when the contract-cap is BINDING do you stand up a LIGHT warehouse + stocker. By that doctrine the reconciler is desiring warehouse/stocker/depot-delivery PREMATURELY.

== QUESTIONS ==
1. Is the reconciler's desired topology (warehouse+stocker+depot-delivery at cold-start, 0 real haulers) correct, or over-desiring vs PLAYBOOK 5 staging?
2. What SHOULD the desired contract-op topology be at each stage (sole frigate -> hauler pool forming -> contract-cap binding), as a function of measured demand / $-per-hr?
3. Given 68k/hr income + 195k treasury but a SERIAL one-contract-at-a-time engine, what hauler count should we target FIRST (before any warehouse/stocker), and what is the binding constraint on contract $/hr right now?

Answer as a bd note on this bead (Recommendation / Evidence / Confidence / What would change my mind) + a nudge; I close the consult. Answer-by: next captain wake (~+3h).
notes:
CONSULT ANSWER — sp-u5nh (refute-first): is the capacity reconciler correctly SIZING the cold-start contract op?

## Recommendation

**The reconciler IS over-desiring (Q1: yes) — but that is the LESSER finding. The premise I break: a hauler should/could be provisioned NOW is ALSO false.** No cargo-capable hull is affordable under the money guards at this treasury, so the frigate-only op is the *correct* engine right now, and the money guards are correctly holding the line. Do not "fix" the reconciler and do not relax a guard.

Three verdicts:
1. **Q1 — over-desiring: YES**, warehouse/stocker/depot-delivery are premature per PLAYBOOK §5/§3/§4. BUT the mis-desire is currently **INERT** (tier-1 reuse-idle is blocked by the sp-r6f1/sp-pt7d cargo-floor guard; tier-4 capital is proposal-gated, ApprovalThreshold=0). It is signal-noise + wasted ticks, NOT a capital leak. Don't panic-fix it.
2. **The real binding constraint = treasury vs the 25%-per-hull guard (RULINGS #6) on the cheapest cargo hull.** At 224k treasury the 25% ceiling is 56k. Home yard (X1-UM5-A2): LIGHT_SHUTTLE 76.7k (needs ≥307k treasury to clear 25%), LIGHT_HAULER 324.8k (needs ≥1.30M). Nothing cargo-capable is buyable. The op is doing exactly the right thing: earn on the frigate until a cargo hull clears the guards.
3. **Q3 — target 1 cargo hull FIRST (the cheapest affordable, LIGHT_SHUTTLE ~77k), the moment treasury clears ~307k with cash-cushion intact (~2-3h at 36k/hr net). NO warehouse/stocker/depot until ≥2 haulers saturate the serial clock AND recurring-good demand history exists.**

## Q2 — correct desired contract-topology per stage (as a fn of the STAGE's binding constraint, not raw $/hr)

- **Stage A — sole frigate (treasury < ~307k; CURRENT STATE):** desired = the frigate batch-contract loop ONLY. Zero warehouse/stocker/depot/extra-hull. The reconciler's desired-topology should be ~empty of infra here. Current state is correct; the reconciler's warehouse/stocker/depot desire is the defect.
- **Stage B — first cargo hull (treasury clears ~307-330k, ~2-3h away):** +1 light cargo hull dedicated to contract-delivery. Frees the frigate (RULINGS #7 last-resort), parallelizes source+deliver. STILL no warehouse/stocker.
- **Stage C — second hull (ONLY if measured source-leg is multi-tranche-bound):** +1 more, cap ~2 for a single home system. Still no warehouse.
- **Stage D — contract-cap binding (serial clock saturated by the hauler pool + recurring-good demand visible):** NOW a LIGHT source-side warehouse + 1 stocker for the recurring receipt-demand whitelist goods. Depot-delivery clusters only for FAR-destination contracts + co-located delivery hulls (the sp-u9xa feature) — N/A at a single home system.
- **Stage-advance trigger:** the current stage's constraint SATURATES (per-hull $/hr plateaus), not a raw $/hr threshold. The reconciler's PLAN gate (FleetPerHullCrHr vs the 500 cr/hr floor) sees ~36-68k/hr/hull — vast headroom — so it greenlights capacity; the DEFECT is it doesn't encode STAGING ORDER. Fix = gate warehouse/stocker/depot desire behind "hauler tier saturated (idle-hauler headroom ≈ 0) AND measured buy-leg is the binding cycle-time component."

## Q3 — hauler count first + the binding constraint

- **Target FIRST = 1 cargo hull** (cheapest affordable = LIGHT_SHUTTLE ~77k), bought when treasury clears the 25% gate (~307k) with cash-cushion intact (PLAYBOOK §3 — leaves working capital + the 50k floor; the op churns ~286k/hr GROSS cargo, recycled on fulfillment, so a one-time 77k buy against 36k/hr net inflow is safe once the gate clears). Then MEASURE; add hull #2 (cap 2) ONLY if the slow contracts' source-leg is multi-tranche-bound. Do NOT pre-buy toward bootstrap hauler_target=4.
- **BINDING CONSTRAINT right now = treasury vs the 25%-per-hull money guard on the cheapest cargo hull.** Not warehousing, not the reconciler, not the slate. Correct response = TIME (let the 36k/hr net op grow treasury to ~307k), NOT weakening the guard (RULINGS #4/#6 — never weakened) and NOT standing up warehouses. Secondary: the frigate as sole last-resort hauler inflates cycle-time on the non-trivial contracts (that's what hull #1 fixes, once affordable).
- **Cheap lever worth a scan:** yard price varies up to ~8x (PLAYBOOK §5 prior); coverage is only 59%. A scouted neighbor yard MIGHT carry a cargo hull under the 56k ceiling → buyable NOW. Worth a cheap check before committing to the ~2-3h wait.
- **On sp-5nd2 (for the shipwright, not my lane):** the "no_purchaser deadlock" is PARTLY correct behavior — nothing is affordable under the guards, so refusing to buy is right. The genuine bug is the premature GATE (bootstrap should still be in INCOME staging a hauler-when-affordable, not at GATE) = the scaled_gate_entry (sp-fp3y) default-off symptom. But arming scaled_gate_entry alone does NOT unblock — the hauler still can't buy until treasury clears the guard. Treasury growth (time) is the unblock, not a knob. Caution: do not "fix" the deadlock by relaxing a guard.

## Evidence (all live, player 4, torwind-2026-07-19, pulled ~17:14)
- Fleet (ship list): TORWIND-1 COMMAND frigate (cargo 40, on batch_contract_workflow) + TORWIND-2/3/4 probes (cargo 0, scouting). Zero light haulers. No dedicated fleets (general pool). Confirms snapshot.
- NET credit delta: bal 175,000 → 224,461 over 1.36h = **+36.4k/hr NET** (the "68k/hr" is gross-ish; PLAYBOOK §8 — project from deltas). Op is healthy, never stalled.
- Contract cycle-time (accept→fulfill, 9 contracts): 0.9–39.4 min, slate-driven variance; payouts 2.1k–97.9k. 9 fulfilled in 38 min once warmed. Serial engine cycling fine on the frigate.
- Buy-leg: 18 PURCHASE_CARGO trips / 286k spend in 53 min — sourcing is active + capital-intensive (part of cycle-time for non-trivial contracts).
- Yard prices (shipyard_inventory, X1-UM5): LIGHT_HAULER 324,811; LIGHT_SHUTTLE 76,726; PROBE 25-27k. 25% ceiling at 224k treasury = 56k → no cargo hull buyable. Autosizer's own treasury_floor gate (price + 200k ≤ treasury − 50k) is even stricter (needs ~327k for the shuttle), so arming autosizer early-scaling wouldn't produce a hull yet either.
- Reconciler log (per bead): tier1_reuse_idle tries to pin the 3 cargo-0 probes into WAREHOUSE/STOCKER/DEPOT-DELIVERY — all blocked by the cargo-floor guard. Confirms over-desiring + inert.

## Confidence: HIGH
On the economic verdict (over-desiring; hauler-before-warehouse; binding constraint = treasury vs the 25% guard on the cheapest cargo hull). The decisive fact is hard live data: 324.8k hauler / 76.7k shuttle vs a 56k ceiling. MEDIUM only on the exact Stage-B trigger treasury (307k for a manual 25%-rule buy vs ~327k for the autosizer's cushion vs a cheaper scouted yard could lower it).

## What would change my mind
1. A scouted neighbor yard carries a cargo hull < ~56k → buy NOW, skip the wait (yard 8x variance is real; coverage only 59%).
2. Contract cycle-time is DELIVER-leg-dominated (not source) → hull #2's parallel-sourcing value drops; hull #1's value is mainly freeing the frigate. I have NOT isolated the source-vs-deliver leg split (needs per-leg nav telemetry) — that is the key unmeasured variable for the hull-#2 decision.
3. Slate shifts to consistently multi-unit contracts of ONE recurring good (demand history) → a source-side warehouse could jump ahead of hull #2 — but only after ≥1 hauler exists.
4. Working-capital churn drains treasury faster than the 36k/hr net implies → the affordability timeline slips.

title: Hauler-buy affordability is reserve_margin x treasury (proportional), not an absolute contract working-capital floor -> hauler arrives ~2x price, too late
description:
CURRENT MAIN behavior (verified in code, not the stale rehearsal binary). maybeBuyHauler in internal/application/bootstrap/commands/run_bootstrap_income.go (~line 254-273) gates the buy on:
  capBudget = treasury x reserve_margin   (reserve_margin default 0.50, defaultReserveMargin)
  affordable = price <= capBudget
So a light hauler is bought only when treasury >= price / reserve_margin ~= 2x the hauler price (a 314k hauler waits for ~628k treasury). The code comment states this is deliberate: 'A ~300k hauler simply waits until contracts have grown treasury past ~2x its price.'

DOCTRINE (Admiral, now PLAYBOOK section 3): buy the first light hauler as soon as it is affordable, where 'affordable' = the buy still leaves a SAFE CASH CUSHION to keep funding the contract operation. That cushion is an ABSOLUTE contract working-capital floor (contract goods + fuel, ~tens of k), NOT a proportion of a growing treasury, and NOT bare price.

GAP:
- The reserve_margin x treasury gate uses a PROPORTIONAL cushion (percent of a growing balance), not an absolute contract working-capital floor.
- At 0.50 it is over-conservative: the contract op needs ~tens of k of working capital, not ~314k, so the hauler could safely be bought at treasury ~= price + floor (e.g. ~365k) instead of ~628k. Buying late delays the cash-flow scaling the hauler exists to provide, which the doctrine calls cash-flow-critical.

FIX DIRECTION (shipwright): change the hauler-buy affordability gate from 'price <= reserve_margin x treasury' to 'treasury - price >= contract_working_capital_floor' (an absolute, configurable floor); buy as soon as that holds. Keep the money guard fail-closed (RULINGS #4). NOTE reserve_margin is a SHARED knob (it also paces the DATA-phase probe buy), so lowering it is a blunt workaround that loosens probe-buying too, not the real fix — the working-capital floor should be its own parameter.

RELATED: sp-ktio (economic-progression root: treasury floor + buy-hauler-ASAP), sp-py5r (the no_purchaser readiness gate is checked BEFORE affordability and can block the buy even when affordable). Epic sp-difa.
SOURCE: run_bootstrap_income.go maybeBuyHauler; reserve_margin default 0.50.

RULINGS #5 immutable const (crafter correctly overrode my tunable brief); #4 fail-closed (cushion<floor -> capital_gate, no buy); reserve_margin + sp-py5r untouched. ACTIVE ON DEPLOY (correctness fix). 102 tests green. Unblocks sp-bpdf (ktio-A floor unification).

title: No first-class staging environment: builds/services/config are single-env (prod) — staging isolation is hand-hacked and fragile
description: Era-4 staging rehearsal 2026-07-18. There is NO staging build/env separation — the daemon binary (bin/spacetraders-daemon), launchd services, config, DB, sockets, ports are all single-environment (prod). Running a staging game required hand-hacking isolation at EVERY step: build the daemon to a one-off 'spacetraders-daemon-stg' (else 'make build' overwrites the shared bin/ the LIVE launchd daemon runs -> a live restart picks up unvalidated code, e.g. sp-rype without sp-difa.1 re-running cold-start on the 234M fleet); swap the DB name into DATABASE_URL from the live config; override socket/pid/routing/metrics ports via a gitignored config.staging.yaml; wrap every CLI call in stc.sh with --player-id/--socket. This ad-hoc isolation is fragile — a hardcoded live pid nearly got the live daemon killed once this session. A REAL staging env needs: (1) env-aware BUILD ('make build ENV=staging' -> its own binary; staging never overwrites the prod binary); (2) a COMMITTED staging config (not gitignored ad-hoc); (3) first-class DB/socket/pid/port/metrics isolation parameterized by env; (4) boot/register/teardown scripts; (5) a separate staging service story (launchd/process mgmt) so staging can't collide with prod. GOAL: 'run a staging game' is one repeatable, provably-isolated command, not a hand-assembled hack. This is the substrate for all future safe live-API validation. P2, infra.

title: Bootstrap 5m tick is over-conservative — cold-start fleet is <0.1 req/s (20x+ API headroom); poll latency drags time-to-gate
description: Era-4 staging rehearsal 2026-07-18. defaultBootstrapTickSeconds=300 with comment 'slow, deliberate ramp' — the API-pacing rationale is VOID at cold start: the bootstrap fleet (1 frigate + 1-3 probes) makes a handful of calls/tick = <0.1 req/s vs the 2 req/s ACCOUNT limit (20x+ headroom). Bootstrap runs ONLY during cold start (exits at COMPLETE, gone before the fleet is ever large), so its tick can be SHORT for its whole lifetime with zero API concern. The 5m poll just injects up to 5min of dead time between a real event completing (frigate docks, scan finishes) and the coordinator reacting on the next tick — observed: probe-buy took ~3 ticks/~11min (dispatch->arrive->dock+buy), almost all poll latency not travel. FIX: drop the bootstrap tick to ~30-60s (or make acting event-driven via the wake/watch model — react to arrival/scan-complete instead of a fixed poll). Faster reaction -> faster time-to-gate -> more Phase-2 time -> higher rank. HARD DEPENDENCY: the freshly-bought-hull count-sync must be robust FIRST (obs.ProbeCount must observe fresh buys, or force a ship-sync post-buy) — at 5m the count self-heals before the next tick, but at 30-60s a stale count would OVER-BUY probes (the count-lag observed live this run, probes=1/3 after buying to 3/3). title: Frontier: per-unit probe price ceiling knob (defer overpriced deep-yard buys, keep cheap ones flowing)
description: Admiral 2026-07-17. The frontier probe buyer is cheapest-first w/ demand-proximal + sibling-spread (hop_penalty=5000, sibling_margin=40000) and buys cheap (~20-26k) wherever a cheaper yard is REACHABLE. The only current guard is max_spend_per_cycle (a trailing WINDOW budget) which is blunt: it conflates total-spend with per-unit-price, so blocking the 235k deep buys also blocks the 23k near buys (and the window gets polluted by past big buys, delaying cheap resumption). When the only quote for a target EXCEEDS the ceiling, DEFER the buy (leave that post unmanned/dark, retry next cycle when price recovers or a cheaper yard becomes reachable) — never crash/strand. Default-safe (0=disabled=today). Recommended armed ~50-60k (2-3x the ~20k market). Lets us then raise max_spend_per_cycle freely because per-unit price is independently capped. Reachability-bound deep systems simply stay dark rather than costing 10x.

title: Frontier: replace binary scan_only with a discovery_share budget-split knob + readable tune + 'frontier status' CLI
description:
MOTIVATION (found live 2026-07-17): the frontier coordinator's scan_only knob is binary and mutually-exclusive — scan_only=0 discovers new virgin systems but leaves their markets DARK (unscanned), scan_only=1 drains the charted-but-unscanned backlog but stops discovery. Live evidence: after restarting expansion we charted 5 virgin systems in ~1h (BK75/CH49/FS70/FZ18/CG76) holding 47 marketplaces total — and 0 were scanned, only 2 of 5 had any probe. Faster discovery just grows the dark-market pile with no trade value (the optimizer can't use unscanned markets). Operator had to manually flip scan_only back and forth. Also the tune CLI is write-only and opaque (no way to read current values, see live state, or discover knob names/bounds without grepping Go source).

DESIGN (approved by Admiral):

1) NEW KNOB: discovery_share (int, 0-100, unit=percent) on the frontier coordinator, REPLACING binary scan_only.
   - Each cycle the coordinator declares BOTH discovery posts (virgin systems) AND scan posts (dark-market backlog), splitting per-cycle probe capacity (post declarations + idle-relay + purchases) by the ratio.
   - 100 = pure discovery (== old scan_only=0); 0 = pure backlog-scan (== old scan_only=1); e.g. 60 = 60% served posts chart new / 40% drain dark markets, concurrently.
   - GRACEFUL DEGRADATION (target, not hard split): backlog empty -> scan share redirects to discovery; no reachable virgin frontier -> discovery share redirects to scanning. Capacity never idles because one side ran dry.
   - Supersede scan_only: keep scan_only as a DEPRECATED read-only alias reporting the equivalent share (scan_only=1<->share=0, =0<->share=100) so nothing breaks; discovery_share is the real control. Proposed default: 50.

2) CLI UX (both):
   a. Readable tune: 'tune --operation <coord>' (no knob/value) -> table of EVERY knob: name, current value, default, min/max, unit, description. 'tune --operation <coord> <knob>' (no value) -> that knob's current value + metadata. --json for scripts. (Applies to all coordinators, not just frontier.)
   b. New 'frontier status' command (+ daemon query) -> live state in one view: current effective split (e.g. '60% discover / 40% scan' or '100% discover — backlog empty'); discovery (systems charted total, +N last hour, virgin-queue depth); BACKLOG (dark-market systems + unscanned marketplace count); probes (fleet/cap, idle vs assigned, posts in flight); recent charts (system+time) + last probe buy (price+yard); blockers (spend-cap / cooldown / routing fail-closed reasons).

SCOPE/FILES: gobot — container_ops_tune.go (add discovery_share knob + scan_only alias + readable-tune table); frontier expansion coordinator logic (split served posts by ratio + graceful degradation); new frontier-status CLI command + daemon service query. Medium effort.

ACCEPTANCE:
- discovery_share tunable [0,100], live-applied; scan_only still readable as deprecated alias.
- With backlog>0 and virgin frontier>0 and share=50, a cycle declares both discovery and scan posts ~50/50.
- Backlog empties -> all capacity flows to discovery; no virgin frontier -> all to scan (no idling).
- 'tune --operation frontier' with no value prints all knobs w/ current values+bounds+descriptions.
- 'frontier status' shows split, discovery rate, dark-market backlog count, probe allocation, recent charts, blockers.

NOTE: future-era infra — will not land before the current era reset (2026-07-19 13:00 UTC).
notes:
COVERAGE GAP found live 2026-07-17 (must be handled by the discovery_share=0 / 'man' path): flipping scan_only=1 only scanned 1 of 5 freshly-discovered dark systems (BK75 -> 16 markets), then reported 'backlog fully scanned — idle' while CG76/CH49/FS70/FZ18 stayed at 0 market_data despite being charted with marketplaces (CH49 alone has 17). So the frontier's 'discovered backlog' does NOT equal 'all charted systems with unscanned marketplaces' — charting a system does not enqueue its marketplaces for price-scanning. ACCEPTANCE ADDITION: discovery_share=0 (and 'frontier status' backlog count) must reflect ALL charted-but-price-unscanned systems and actually drive scouts to record their market data, not just a narrow internal queue. Otherwise 'man the dark ones' silently leaves most discovered markets dark. Likely the charting (frontier) -> market-price-scan (scout/freshsizer) handoff is the missing link.

title: Gate-reconcile sweep fails-closed on uncharted TRANSIT gates — order charting BFS-outward from charted frontier
description:
Surfaced by the sp-4yse root-cause investigation. The charting mechanism is sound (0-hop probes chart their gate; markers drain). The RESIDUAL structural limitation is REACHABILITY, not charting: multi-hop reconcile relays fail-closed when a TRANSIT gate on the route is itself uncharted (596 SCOUT_REPOSITION FAILED today with 'jump ... hop N of N ... Waypoint ... uncharted' — this is also the residual Get Jump Gate 400-storm). A frontier system sitting BEHIND another uncharted gate is unreachable until the intervening gate is charted — an ordering/BFS-frontier problem.

Today the 0-hop charting path only fires when a probe happens to already be IN the target system (rare coincidence); once in-system probes are spent, the sweep falls back to multi-hop relays that strand on uncharted transit gates. So the backlog converges for in-reach systems but stalls on the ones behind uncharted gates.

FIX (targeting concern in reconcileGateChartSweep, run_scout_post_coordinator.go:2426 — NOT the charting mechanism): order the sweep to chart gates BFS-outward from the charted frontier (chart a transit gate before trying to reach systems behind it), and/or prefer genuinely 0-hop / nearest-reachable targets over deep multi-hop relays that will fail-closed. This turns the frontier from 'randomly poke at backed-off systems' into 'expand the charted boundary one reachable ring at a time'. Only pursue if the backlog STALLS after 29744162 converges the in-reach systems — measure first. Related: sp-4yse, sp-lv2n (CreateChart), sp-bcsu (chart-on-arrival), the paused frontier_expansion coordinator (active discovery, separate).

title: Reconcile scout-reposition relays keep a stale flag-less config across a deploy (the sp-4yse observation trap)
description:
Surfaced by the sp-4yse root-cause investigation (systematic-debugging). Scout-reposition container config is persisted ONCE at dispatch (PersistScoutRepositionWorker) and re-read on every recovery/rebuild. A relay first persisted by a PRE-fix binary therefore carries a flag-less config FOREVER — even after the daemon restarts onto the fixed binary. Concretely: relays dispatched before sp-4yse (e.g. TORWIND-5B/59/1F under 5324380c) have NO chart_gate_on_arrival key, so on rebuild OptionalBool('chart_gate_on_arrival') returns false (configReader:143 false-on-absent), they take the plain branch (scout_reposition.go:117 -> market waypoint), and never chart — while post-fix relays (TORWIND-6A under 29744162) get the flag and chart correctly. DB evidence: across 1196 SCOUT_REPOSITION configs, chart_gate_on_arrival ABSENT=1180, true=1, false=15.

IMPACT: not a charting-logic bug (charting is proven sound); it is a DEPLOY-SAFETY / observability trap — it made the working fix look prod-broken because in-flight relays straddled the deploy. Bounded: the 1180 NULLs are historical and age out as relays complete.

FIX (confirm the premise first — do NOT implement blind): verify that recovery actually REUSES stale container IDs across a deploy (vs re-dispatching fresh). If it does: either (a) have the coordinator re-persist/UPSERT the reconcile relay config on re-dispatch so chart_gate_on_arrival reflects the CURRENT binary, or (b) garbage-collect COMPLETED/FAILED reconcile scout_reposition containers so stale IDs can't be recovered. Files: internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_scouting.go (:192 persist, :214 rebuild); internal/adapters/grpc/command_factory_registry.go (:847 OptionalBool read, :143 false-on-absent); internal/application/scouting/commands/run_scout_post_coordinator.go (:2591 flag set / spawnReposition). Related: sp-4yse (the fix this stranded), sp-o34q (same persist->rebuild boundary for max_reposition_jumps). Not urgent — let 29744162 converge first.

title: impact_sample_rate: 0 can't disable impact sampling — resolver clamps <=0 to default 0.15
description: sp-v34b's ResolvedImpactSampleRate() does 'if c.ImpactSampleRate <= 0 { return defaultImpactSampleRate (0.15) }'. Because mapstructure leaves an absent float64 key as 0, the resolver cannot distinguish 'key absent (=> default ON 0.15)' from 'operator explicitly set 0 (=> OFF)'. So an operator setting impact_sample_rate: 0 to disable the deliberate post-trade impact instrumentation (behavior 2) silently gets 0.15 instead. The freshness-dedup gate (behavior 1, scan_max_age_seconds) must stay unaffected. FIX: make ImpactSampleRate a *float64 (mapstructure nil-when-absent): nil => default 0.15; non-nil *v<=0 => 0 (explicit off, clamp negatives to 0); *v>1 => 1; else *v. Preserve the 'absent section => era-3 default model-ON' invariant. RED test MUST decode actual YAML/config maps (not just construct the struct) to exercise the absent-vs-explicit-0 distinction, and assert ResolvedScanPolicy returns ok=true with ImpactSampleRate==0 when set to 0, 0.15 when absent. Grep all .ImpactSampleRate consumers for the pointer change.

title: Freshness-vs-frontier probe allocation: one satellite pool, two uncoordinated caps — freshness starves frontier depth (self-defeating: depth discovers markets -> freshness eats the probes -> depth starves)
description:
Two coordinators — the market-freshness sizer (sp-orgp) and the frontier expansion coordinator (sp-8w89/sp-rjgr) — draw from ONE shared satellite/probe pool with SEPARATE, uncoordinated caps and NO arbitration. Freshness starves frontier depth as it grows. Add a global probe allocator (or a reserved-slice floor) so exploration isn't cannibalized by scanning.

## PROBLEM — a self-defeating loop (measured live 2026-07-15)
- One physical probe pool; two independent caps: freshness max_probe_fleet=80, frontier max_probe_fleet=60. The caps DON'T compose — both draw the same hulls, so the higher-demand coordinator wins the pool.
- Live: freshness (after the sp-tor9 under-sizing fix) now sees 20 market systems, demand 46 probes, and holds 46 of the 46-probe pool — leaving ~0-2 idle. The frontier depth policy (sp-rjgr, correctly configured: breadth=1%, 6 pathfinders, objective-bias 75-100% depth) had 0 idle probes and sat at 'cap reached' — it could see hop-2 systems but couldn't dispatch to them (queued-not-reached).
- THE PATHOLOGY IS SELF-DEFEATING: frontier depth explores -> discovers new market-bearing systems -> each new market raises freshness demand -> freshness buys/holds more probes -> the frontier that DID the discovering is starved. Success at depth directly causes depth's own starvation via freshness. The tighter freshness's SLA and the more systems found, the worse it gets.

## STOPGAP IN PLACE (not a fix)
Raised frontier max_probe_fleet 40->60 and max_depth_pathfinders 3->6 (live tune). Gives ~14 probes headroom over freshness's 46 — workable NOW, but as depth succeeds freshness demand climbs toward 60 and re-starves the frontier. The stopgap buys time; it does not break the loop.

## REQUIREMENT
A single authority that budgets the shared probe pool between FRESHNESS (keep known markets fresh) and FRONTIER (explore/depth), by PRIORITY, so neither can cannibalize the other — and specifically so the active strategic objective (heavy-yard depth hunt) is never starved by scanning.

## DESIGN (MVP -> full)
1. MVP — RESERVED FRONTIER FLOOR: reserve N probes (tunable, default ~ max_depth_pathfinders) EXCLUSIVELY for the frontier that the freshness sizer treats as unavailable. Freshness sizes against (pool - N). Guarantees the frontier always has its depth probes regardless of freshness demand. Small, surgical, directly breaks the starvation. Symmetrically, a freshness FLOOR so frontier can't starve scanning below a relaxed SLA.
2. FULL — GLOBAL PROBE ALLOCATOR: one owner computes TOTAL demand = freshness_demand + frontier_demand, buys to a single GLOBAL cap (replacing the two independent caps that double-draw), and GRANTS probes to each coordinator by policy:
   - Freshness gets its floor = probes to hold every market under a RELAXED SLA (not the tight one).
   - The remaining budget goes to the higher-priority objective. While the heavy-yard hunt is unmet (frontier objective_bias active), FRONTIER DEPTH gets priority for the surplus; when the objective is met / no depth objective, freshness gets the surplus up to its full (tight) SLA.
   - Graceful degradation: under depth-priority, freshness relaxes its SLA (markets slightly staler) to fund exploration, rather than hard-starving one side.
3. Both coordinators draw from the allocator's grants, not independently. Global cap bounds total API/cost (fixes the current double-count where 80+60 caps overlap on one pool).

## PRIORITY SIGNAL
Tie priority to the strategic objective already modeled: frontier objective_bias_percent (heavy-yard shortfall unmet) => depth-priority; autosizer heavy shortfall (sp-1txd) as the same signal. When met, revert to freshness-priority.

## TUNABLES
reserved_frontier_floor / reserved_freshness_floor (MVP); global_probe_cap, relaxed_sla_seconds, depth_priority_toggle (full) — via the live tune mechanism (sp-vwek).

## RELATED
sp-orgp (freshness sizer — one consumer; sizes against a floor instead of the raw pool), sp-8w89 + sp-rjgr (frontier + depth policy — the starved consumer; the reserved floor feeds its pathfinders), sp-tor9 (freshness under-sizing fix — raised freshness demand to 46, the trigger that surfaced the contention), sp-iupr (probe over-hold/release — the allocator subsumes its release logic into a global budget), sp-1txd (fleet autosizer — the buy-side; the global allocator either lives here or coordinates buys with it).

## PRIORITY P2
Not blocking today (the 60-cap + 6-pathfinder stopgap holds). ESCALATE to P1 when freshness demand approaches the frontier's headroom (freshness demand > ~50 against the 60 cap) — at that point the frontier re-starves and the depth push stalls. The MVP reserved-floor alone would de-risk the current depth campaign cheaply.
notes:
DISPATCHED (MVP scope) 2026-07-15. URGENCY RAISED: sp-tor9 (just deployed 267eb5f3) lifted freshness demand to ~46 and it's CLIMBING (KN83 4->7 live, VB74/DF86/NM33 following toward the per-system cap) — approaching the bead's own P1-escalation trigger (freshness demand > ~50 vs frontier's 60 cap). Building the MVP reserved-frontier-floor now to de-risk the depth campaign before freshness re-starves it. FULL global allocator deferred to a follow-up. Freshsizer + frontier both merged (sp-tor9/sp-hej4/sp-rjgr) — no live-lane collision.
SHARPENED with live evidence (2026-07-15) — the exact mechanism: each coordinator counts the SHARED PHYSICAL pool against its OWN cap. Live: total probes=66; frontier logs 'cap reached (66/60 satellites)' — it counts all 66 (mostly freshness-held) against its 60 cap, so freshness holding 60+ single-handedly puts the frontier 'over cap'. CONSEQUENCE for the release->depth flow: when the percentile sizer (sp-r57g) releases surplus freshness probes to undedicated, the TOTAL pool stays ~66 (released != sold), so the frontier STILL sees 66/60 over-cap and will NOT claim the freed probes for depth — they sit idle. Verified: frontier had 14-16 open depth slots + 0-3 idle probes but stayed at 5 posts-in-flight, absorbing nothing. FIX must make each coordinator count only ITS OWN dedicated probes against its cap (or a global allocator grants freed probes to the frontier explicitly). Without this, sp-r57g frees probes that never reach depth. sp-r57g (release) + sp-iopd (absorb) are a PAIR — neither alone reallocates the pool to depth.
SHIPPED 8f5aa6ad (deployed). MVP reserved floors, DEFAULT 0=OFF (opt-in via tune). Enable: tune --operation freshsizer reserved_frontier_floor 6 + tune --operation frontier reserved_freshness_floor N. Full global allocator + count-own-probes deferred (noted in code).

title: Scan + auto-install ship MODULE/MOUNT upgrades (cargo capacity, fuel range): guarded upgrade automation that picks the highest-marginal-value (hull,module) pair off measured saturation telemetry
description:
As we explore, catalog available MODULES/MOUNTS (fuel tanks, cargo holds, etc.) and AUTO-INSTALL them to close capability gaps on EXISTING hulls — the module analogue of hull acquisition (sp-42ow/sp-1txd). Upgrading a hull's cargo/fuel is a capacity lever that does NOT require buying a new (or heavy) hull.

## PRIMITIVES THAT ALREADY EXIST (build ON these — do NOT rebuild)
- CAPTURE: market_data already records MODULE_/MOUNT_ goods (they are market goods). Found 2026-07-15: 6 types / 7 markets (crew-quarters, mineral-processor, science-lab modules; gas-siphon/mining/surveyor mounts). NOT yet in reach: MODULE_FUEL_TANK, MODULE_CARGO_HOLD — the two highest-value ones. Capture works; a watchlist must flag these when they first appear in reach.
- INSTALL: daemon has InstallModuleCommand + `spacetraders ship outfit install/remove/list`. Atomic claim, fee gated on the working-capital reserve, dock, install, persist new capacity. Single-hull manual verb today.
- TELEMETRY (the saturation signal — EXISTS, clean): tour_leg_telemetry(ship_symbol, realized_units, planned_units per leg) = per-hull cargo saturation; transactions REFUEL rows per hull = range-constraint proxy; market_absorption_ledger = demand-side lane-short signal.

WHAT'S MISSING = the closed-loop automation: a surface that CATALOGS available modules + a scorer that picks WHICH hull to upgrade with WHICH module + buys/delivers/installs behind guards, sized to demand.

## SELECTION MODEL — "which ship to enhance" (core design, validated on live data)
Do NOT pick ships abstractly or "busiest hauler first" (that heuristic is WRONG — evidence below). Pick the highest-marginal-value (hull, module) PAIR each tick:
1. HARD FILTERS: hull has a free frame module-slot the module fits (or a low-value module worth swapping via `outfit remove`); module matches hull ROLE (CARGO_HOLD -> cargo hulls only; FUEL_TANK -> range-constrained hulls only).
2. SCORE = benefit - cost, gated by payback:
   - benefit = capacity/range gained x MEASURED bottleneck (cargo: realized_units/capacity saturation from tour_leg_telemetry; fuel: refuel-stops-per-leg) x hull throughput ($/hr, legs/hr).
   - cost = module price + install fee + outfit logistics (buy-hop + divert-to-shipyard detour).
   - payback gate: cost-per-unit-capacity-gained must beat the new-hull alternative.
   - FAIL CLOSED on thin/missing telemetry (never upgrade a hull we cannot measure).
3. DRIVEN OFF THE AUTOSIZER SHORTFALL (sp-1txd): the autosizer's cargo-capacity shortfall names the SHORT LANES; the upgrader resolves each to "the saturated hull on that lane with slot headroom" and asks "is a cargo upgrade cheaper/sooner than the heavy we cannot reach?" -> a SECOND actuator on the same shortfall signal (upgrade-hull vs buy-hull, pick cheaper per unit capacity).

## LIVE VALIDATION (2026-07-15 — why the naive heuristic fails)
Per tour_leg_telemetry (6h, cap 80): TORWIND-16 & 17 = avg 76/80, 4/5 legs FULL -> SATURATED -> real CARGO_HOLD candidates. But TORWIND-7 = busiest hull (388 legs) + 2nd-most refuels (73) yet avg only 40/80, ~10% legs full -> a cargo module would sit mostly EMPTY. A "busiest-first" heuristic picks 7 and wastes the module; the marginal-value model correctly picks 16/17. CAVEAT: 16/17 have only 5 legs each (thin sample) — the fail-closed-on-thin-telemetry guard holds until more legs confirm.

## SPEC
1. MODULE/MOUNT CATALOG SURFACE: query market_data MODULE_/MOUNT_ goods ranked by (fleet-gap value) x (reachability hops) x price; plus a WATCHLIST (FUEL_TANK, CARGO_HOLD_II/III) that emits a captain event/mail when a wanted module first enters reach.
2. SATURATION/RANGE SIGNAL: aggregate tour_leg_telemetry (cargo) + refuel-per-leg (range) into a per-hull bottleneck read; fail-closed on thin samples.
3. GUARDED AUTO-OUTFIT: on a gap + available+affordable module + slot headroom, buy at nearest market, deliver to the hull, install via InstallModuleCommand. Guards: treasury%/reserve, price ceiling, per-tick cap, slot-availability, payback-vs-new-hull. Fail-closed on any unreadable input.
4. INTEGRATE with sp-1txd: outfitting is a capacity actuator alongside hull-buying; the autosizer weighs upgrade-existing vs buy-new by cost-per-unit-capacity and picks the cheaper.
5. AUTO-DETECT WITH EXPANSION (sp-dc50): new markets that sell fuel/cargo modules enter the catalog automatically; the watchlist fires on first appearance.

## STRATEGIC VALUE
- CARGO_HOLD upgrades = a GATE-INDEPENDENT partial answer to the autosizer's live 14-heavy shortfall: raise throughput on saturated light hulls without an off-gate heavy yard (bounded by light-frame slot/capacity ceilings — partial, not full relief).
- FUEL_TANK upgrades = range: compounds the warp-explorer strategy (sp-4imi — more fuel = farther off-gate reach) and cuts refuel-stop overhead on long arb lanes.

## RELATED
sp-1txd (fleet autosizer — sibling capacity actuator; shares guards + the shortfall signal; the upgrade-vs-buy arbitration lives here), sp-42ow (hull/shipyard scan — this is its module analogue; modules ride market_data so capture already happens), sp-4imi (warp explorer — fuel modules extend its off-gate range), sp-orgp (market freshness — module availability rides the same market scans), sp-dc50 (expansion — brings new modules into reach).

## PRIORITY P2
Not blocking today; the two highest-value modules (fuel/cargo) are not in reach yet. Build the CATALOG + WATCHLIST first (cheap, uses existing data) so we KNOW when fuel/cargo modules appear; build the auto-outfit scorer when they do. Escalates with the heavy shortfall (cargo upgrades are the gate-independent relief valve).

Guarded module/mount upgrade automation: marginal-value (hull,module) selection off tour_leg_telemetry saturation (saturated hull > busiest-but-empty); catalog+watchlist over market_data; fail-closed guard stack; autosizer second-actuator (upgrade-vs-buy by cost/unit); 6 knobs tune --operation autooutfit. Explicit 'workflow auto-outfit [--dry-run]', NOT boot-armed. Two banked enrichments (no-op-safe): live new-hull cost signal + per-hull throughput/refuel aggregation.
BLOCKED / cannot-fire (verified 2026-07-15): live shipyard API exposes only shipTypes + modificationsFee — NO standalone module/mount marketplace this era, so the catalog surface has zero supply and the auto-installer can never source a CARGO_HOLD/FUEL_TANK. More cargo/range = hull class (autosizer). Re-open ONLY if a module source (salvage / later era) appears. See bd memory 'module-exotic quest void 2026-07-15'.

Add a WARP-CAPABLE SHIP_EXPLORER as a hull class of the frontier expansion operation (sp-8w89), to reach OFF-GATE systems the gate-BFS can never touch — charting their jump gates to open entire new probe-scoutable clusters, and hunting the off-gate heavy-freighter yard the autosizer now needs.

Frontier expansion (sp-8w89) is bounded by the JUMP-GATE network. growFrontierGraph walks gate_edges; probes ride gates. Systems that exist in the universe but are NOT gate-connected to our graph are INVISIBLE and physically UNREACHABLE to every hull we own. When the gate-reachable virgin set exhausts (expansion queue -> 0, no new rings) OR a needed resource sits off-gate, expansion stalls PERMANENTLY — no probe can go one system further.

## CONCRETE PULL (verified live this session, 2026-07-15)
The fleet capacity autosizer (sp-1txd, launched live today) computes a HEAVY shortfall of 14 unserved profitable lanes wanting heavy hulls. But sp-42ow shipyard scanning found NO heavy/bulk-freighter yard anywhere in the current 2-3 hop gate reach — only light-class hulls + one SHIP_EXPLORER. If the heavy yard is off-gate, that 14-heavy shortfall can NEVER be filled by the gate-bounded frontier. Warp is the only tool that reaches it. This is the first hard, quantified signal that gate reach may not contain what the economy needs.

## THE TOOL (verified live spec — X1-GP32-ZC7X, 818,917 cr)
SHIP_EXPLORER: FRAME_EXPLORER, fuelCap 800, MODULE_WARP_DRIVE_I (inter-system travel WITHOUT a jump gate), MOUNT_SENSOR_ARRAY_II (charting), ENGINE_ION_DRIVE_II speed 36, cargo 40 (a scout/prospector, NOT a hauler). Warp is fuel-costed by distance; 800 fuel = meaningful off-gate range.

## HOW WARP EXPANDS THE FRONTIER
1. OFF-GATE REACH — warp to systems the gate-BFS can never discover or reach.
2. GATE-CLUSTER OPENER (the force multiplier + the key idea): on reaching a new off-gate system, chart its JUMP GATE and persist the edges to gate_edges. The CHEAP probe-based frontier (sp-dc50/sp-cxpq) then resumes ring-by-ring FROM that new gate, unlocking an entire new gate cluster for the price of ONE warp trip. One explorer seeds many probe-scoutable systems — warp opens the door, probes do the cheap sweeping.
3. HEAVY-YARD HUNT — reach off-gate shipyards, scan them (sp-42ow piggyback), surface an off-gate heavy/bulk yard -> unblocks sp-4ewi's fail-closed heavy buy -> fills the autosizer's 14-heavy shortfall.
4. MARKET/RESOURCE DISCOVERY — new systems' markets feed the freshness sizer (sp-orgp); new economies extend arb lanes (the DF86-only foreign-arb ceiling breaks when a second foreign economy opens).

## SPEC
1. EXPLORER HULL CLASS in the autosizer (sp-1txd): add "explorer"/"warp-scout" as a sized+auto-bought class behind the guard stack. Demand = off-gate exploration demand from the frontier coordinator (see 2). Guard is EXPLORATION-justified, NOT realized-$/hr payback (an explorer buys REACH, not $/hr) — hard-cap 1 (maybe 2), since one opens many clusters; price ceiling ~ observed 819k + premium; full treasury/reserve guards; fail-closed on any unreadable input.
2. OFF-GATE DEMAND SIGNAL from the frontier coordinator (sp-8w89), emitted when EITHER: (a) the gate-reachable virgin set is exhausted — expansion queue -> 0 with no new rings for N cycles (the "gate frontier fully explored, warp needed" signal); or (b) a needed resource is unfound in gate reach while demand exists (autosizer heavy shortfall > 0 AND no known heavy yard). Either raises demand for 1 explorer.
3. TARGET SELECTION: enumerate off-gate systems within warp range of the frontier EDGE (systems from the universe/system list with coordinates, NOT in our gate-connected graph), rank by warp-fuel distance + exploration value (unexplored; promising type/economy), pick nearest-highest-value. Needs a universe system-list source + a warp-range/fuel model.
4. WARP ROUTE EXECUTION: RouteExecutor gains warp support — warp between systems (fuel-costed), with refuel/fuel-safety management across hops given the 800 cap (never strand an explorer with no refuel path). On arrival it charts the system (waypoints, gate edges, markets, shipyards) via the same scan piggyback the scout tours use, and persists all.
5. HANDOFF TO THE CHEAP FRONTIER: once the explorer charts a new system's gate edges, growFrontierGraph picks up the new cluster and the probe machinery scouts it cheaply. The explorer moves to the NEXT off-gate target (continuous warp-scout loop) or parks until new off-gate demand arises.
6. GUARDS: hard explorer cap (1-2 — expensive, high leverage); full autosizer guard stack; warp fuel-safety guard (refuel path required before committing a warp leg); don't churn (a bought explorer stays dedicated to the frontier op, dedicate-at-purchase so no coordinator poaches it).

## WHY NOW / PRIORITY
Not blocking TODAY — the gate frontier is still actively expanding (12 market-bearing systems and growing). But the autosizer's live 14-heavy shortfall against ZERO known heavy yards is the concrete trigger to have this capability ready. ESCALATE when the gate frontier nears exhaustion (expansion queue stuck at 0) OR the heavy shortfall persists across many ticks with no in-gate yard found — at that point off-gate warp exploration becomes the ONLY path forward and this jumps to P1.

title: Frontier probe purchasing is location-blind: buys at HOME yard + relays across the network — buy at the probe-yard NEAREST the target frontier post (gated on sp-42ow shipyard data)
description:
Make frontier probe purchasing TARGET-AWARE: buy each probe at the probe-selling shipyard NEAREST the frontier post it will serve, instead of always at the home system and relaying it across the whole gate network.

## PROBLEM (today)
The ProbePurchaser port is location-blind: `BuyProbe(ctx, playerID, maxBudget) -> (price, shipSymbol)` takes NO target. It buys at the default (home-system cheapest yard — observed: X1-VB74-C39 at ~31k). The bought probe lands undedicated and the scout reconciler then RELAYS it across the gate network to the target post. As the frontier crawls to hop-2/3+, every probe travels the full home->edge distance under relay — wasted probe-hours and delayed coverage, worse with every ring. The buy step never considers where the probe is actually needed.

## COMPOUNDING DEPENDENCY
Even a location-aware purchaser has nothing to work with today: sp-42ow (shipyard scouting) is broken, so shipyard_inventory is EMPTY — there is no data on which frontier systems even sell probes. So this feature is gated on sp-42ow populating probe-selling-yard data across the frontier. Build order: sp-42ow first (shipyard data), then this.

## REQUIREMENT
When the frontier decides to buy a probe to serve a specific unmanned post, buy it at the nearest known probe-selling shipyard to that post's system (fewest gate hops), not always home. Minimize the buy->post relay distance.

## SPEC
1. BuyProbe takes the TARGET (the post's system / the unmanned slot being served).
2. From shipyard_inventory (sp-42ow), find probe-selling yards; pick the one nearest the target by gate-hop distance with an acceptable price.
3. Balance price vs distance: a slightly pricier NEAR yard beats a cheap FAR one when relay cost dominates (a probe is fuel-0 but each jump + reposition is real wall-clock + coordinator work). Make the price/distance tradeoff a tunable.
4. Fall back to the home/anchor yard when no nearer probe-yard is known yet (sp-42ow hasn't scanned that region) — never fail-closed on missing data.
5. Keep all existing guards (price <= 25% treasury, spend cap, cooldown, fleet cap).

## IMPACT
Cuts probe delivery latency + coordinator relay load as the frontier expands; the further out the edge, the bigger the win. Also lets a freshly-bought probe start scanning its target system almost immediately instead of after a multi-jump relay.

## RELATED
sp-8w89 (frontier expansion coordinator — owns BuyProbe + the decision), sp-42ow (shipyard scouting — HARD PREREQ: supplies the probe-yard locations), sp-cxpq (scout relay — shorter/eliminated relay when bought near the target).

title: Depot buffer auto-selection must gate on hub-contract-membership + local-production + source-distance (locally-produced non-contract goods like DRUGS@J58 get warehoused)
description:
The reward-ranked buffer selector (sp-wxf2) picks goods to warehouse at a hub WITHOUT checking (a) whether the hub actually contracts for the good, (b) whether the hub produces it LOCALLY, or (c) whether its source is far enough to be worth buffering. Result: locally-produced and/or non-contract goods get warehoused = pure waste of warehouse capacity + the stocker trip that hauls them.

## LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-07-15, player-3 X1-VB74)
J58 warehouse hull TORWIND-19 holds 45 units of DRUGS = 56pct of an 80-cap hull. DRUGS is NOT a J58 contract good (J58 contracts polynucleotides/medicine/assault-rifles/ammonia/firearms/equipment/explosives/clothing/food) AND J58 EXPORTS DRUGS locally (trade_type=EXPORT, supply MODERATE, ~1659/unit). So the delivery hull could buy on-site instantly; warehousing 45 wastes the slot + the stocker haul. T19 also holds ELECTRONICS 8, also not a J58 contract good.

## REQUIRED — add three CANDIDATE GATES before the reward/stall-prevention ranking
1. CONTRACT-MEMBERSHIP: buffer good g at hub H only if g is delivered TO H by contracts (H-scoped contract frequency > 0). A good never contracted to H is never a candidate for H.
2. LOCAL-PRODUCTION EXCLUSION: never buffer g at H if H's own market EXPORTS/EXCHANGES g (buy on-site instead of warehousing).
3. SOURCE-DISTANCE GATE: only buffer if g's nearest EXTERNAL source distance > threshold (near-/local-sourced goods barely benefit from a warehouse slot).
Then reward/stall-prevention-rank the survivors under the stocker-capacity budget, with per-good caps (~avg contract units + margin).

## ACCEPTANCE
- A good the hub produces locally is NEVER selected for that hub's buffer.
- A good never contracted to the hub is NEVER selected.
- Re-running selection on J58 drops DRUGS + ELECTRONICS; regression: remote-sourced J58 contract goods (e.g. ASSAULT_RIFLES) still buffer.

This is the buffer-selection subset of the Capacity Reconciler planner (epic st-7zk, slice st-hlw) — implement the gated selector in the existing buffer selector NOW; the reconciler planner reuses the same selector. Related: sp-wxf2 (reward-ranking), sp-obtr (source-aware routing). Also enables retiring the manual whitelist in favor of a fully computed desired-buffer. Origin: economy-analyst + Admiral 2026-07-15.
notes: GATED (merge 5e50277a) + DEPLOYED (daemon.log@5e50277a, 2026-07-15). Shared domain/buffer.Gate (3 gates) on BOTH the live depot selector + reconciler planner. J58 anchor + per-gate load-bearing mutations green. Gate-1 fails-open on thin-history membership (deploy-hazard fix). Knob depot_buffer_min_source_distance (default 25, tune --operation contract). Live on deploy: whitelists re-solved per reload, extant DRUGS drains. Known limit: cold-start seed ungated (J58 never cold-start).

title: depot start silently skips (and falsely reports 'launched') a declared element under an active captain claim
description:
ROOT CAUSE (found while unsticking J58 warehouse TORWIND-19 + stocker TORWIND-1A, parked at I55): sp-3l64 positionDepotElementHull/depotHullNeedsFreeing only frees a hull that is idle OR foreign-dedicated-fleet-tagged. A hull under an ACTIVE CAPTAIN claim (ships.assignment_status='active', assignment_owner='captain', dedicated_fleet='') is NEITHER — so depotHullNeedsFreeing returns false, the hull is not freed, and launchDepotStocker/Warehouse then hit 'if !ship.IsIdle() { return nil }' and SILENTLY skip the launch (benign already-flying path). No coordinator starts; the hull stays captain-squatted at the wrong waypoint.

TWO defects:
1) The launch does not preempt a stale captain claim on its OWN declared depot element. A captain manual-DOCK reservation (sp-sfoe/sp-lxwn) that outlives its container leaves the hull assignment_owner=captain/active forever; depot start can never adopt it. WORKAROUND (used live 2026-07-15): 'spacetraders ship release --ship <sym>' clears the captain reservation -> hull goes idle -> re-run 'contract depot start <name> <spec>' adopts it.
2) MISLEADING SUCCESS COUNT: startDepot returns len(planDepotLaunches(reg)) regardless of per-intent outcome, so the CLI always prints 'N coordinator(s) launched' even when launches were silently skipped (nil) or errored (fmt.Printf warning to daemon stdout only). A benign-skip produces ZERO operator signal.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) depotHullNeedsFreeing also frees a hull claimed by a NON-depot owner (owner=captain/manual) when it is a declared element of THIS depot — reclaim own infra from a stale squat; guard against yanking a hull the captain is ACTIVELY driving (running container) vs an orphaned claim (no container). (b) At minimum, make the skip LOUD: log 'depot element <sym> is <owner>-claimed at <wp>; not launched — run ship release first' and have StartDepot return an ACTUAL launched/skipped/errored breakdown the CLI surfaces, not the intent count. Prefer both.

- spacetraders_daemon_ledger_cost_total    CounterVec{operation_type,category,player_id} += (-amount) when amount<0

PROMQL (namespace spacetraders_daemon_, use $__rate_interval, *3600 for cr/hr):
