title: Destination-side warehousing to compress contract cycle-time (J58 first: 691u haul, 28 ctr, 1.85M) — 1-2 co-located warehouses + hub + 2-3 stockers, demand-gated
description:
# Destination-side warehousing to compress contract cycle-time (J58 first)

## Economic rationale (corrected — cycle-time is the UNCAPPED lever)
Contracts are SERIALIZED (1 active) but NOT supply-capped (Admiral: the faction always has contracts to accept). So contract $/hr = payment / cycle_time with NO ceiling — halving cycle-time doubles $/hr. Contracts are the DOMINANT engine (~432k/hr vs arb ~67k/hr today), so compressing their cycle is a first-class lever, not a sideshow.

cycle_time = buy-leg + HAUL-LEG + deliver + negotiate. Source-warehousing (done) killed the buy-leg. The HAUL-LEG (source→destination) is the dominant remaining term for FAR destinations and is totally unaddressed. Live haul-legs (source→dest distance):
  J58 = 691u, 28 contracts, 1.85M  ← biggest cluster by count AND payment
  H51 = 764u,  9 contracts, 668k
  H54 = 436u, 12 contracts, 229k
  (central dests A1/C39/D41/D42/K83 = 94–212u — short haul, source-warehousing already covers, NOT candidates)

## The mechanism
A destination-side warehouse pre-stages the contract goods NEAR the far destination. When a contract to that destination fires, the local hauler withdraws from the co-located warehouse and delivers locally (~0 haul) — the 691u haul is moved OFF the serialized contract critical path onto PARALLEL stockers. Contract cycle-time for far-dest contracts drops sharply → $/hr on the dominant engine rises. The haul is RELOCATED (stocker still moves 691u), not erased — the win is parallelization off the serialized bottleneck.

## Design capability CONFIRMED (in code)
Same-waypoint multi-warehouse is already supported (sp-5q2c): warehouse_selection.go:33 ("the Admiral runs MORE THAN ONE warehouse"), RunningWarehousesAtWaypoint() returns the co-located group, FindAllRunningByWaypoint() (storage_operation_repository.go:204), deposit targets the co-located group by free space (tour_deposit_candidates.go:195), ops keyed by container id not waypoint. So 2 warehouses at J58 is a solved capability. LATENT RISK to verify: FindRunningByWaypoint returns only the FIRST match (repo:189, NOTE says use FindAll) — audit that no live path (cap-optimizer aggregate capacity, stocker restock-all) uses the singular where it must aggregate the group.

## Build (J58 first, then H54/H51 if it proves out)
- 1–2 co-located WAREHOUSES at/near J58 (aggregate capacity for the broad buffer — J58 receives 9 distinct goods: AMMONIA_ICE, ASSAULT_RIFLES, CLOTHING, EQUIPMENT, EXPLOSIVES, FIREARMS, FOOD, MEDICINE, POLYNUCLEOTIDES).
- A HUB at J58 = contract hauler(s) pre-positioned to do local J58 deliveries (positional insurance; serialized so ~1 works at a time).
- 2–3 STOCKERS sized to the DRAIN: a J58 round-trip is ~1,380u (691u each way) — long — so keeping the buffer stocked against the contract drain needs real stocker throughput. Stocker count is set by (J58 contract arrival rate × units/contract) vs (stocker round-trip time). This is the REAL constraint (not a cap): if stockers can't refill faster than contracts drain, the buffer empties and contracts source fresh/far anyway.
- DEMAND-GATE the J58 buffer: reuse the warehousecap.go knapsack, but keyed on J58 RECEIPT demand (which goods J58 contracts require × recurrence × the 691u residual haul-leg saved), NOT source demand. Only pre-stage goods that recur enough to amortize the 691u speculative stocker haul (same coverage>depth logic; thin per-good J58 demand means broad-but-shallow).

## Economic parameters (economy-analyst owned)
- Which destinations: J58 (build now), H54/H51 (follow-on, gated on J58 result).
- J58 buffer whitelist + per-good caps: knapsack on J58 receipt-demand (analyst supplies).
- Stocker count: sized to J58 drain vs 1,380u round-trip (analyst sizes from observed arrival rate).

## BLOCKER / parallel track — MEASUREMENT
Warehouse→hauler withdrawals are non-monetary cargo transfers with NO ledger record (verified: no transfer/withdraw transaction type exists). So today we CANNOT measure whether a destination warehouse actually compresses contract cycle-time. Build the withdrawal-instrumentation fix (log warehouse→hauler transfers as a trackable event) IN PARALLEL — without it this build is unmeasurable and untunable (can't size stockers, can't prove the $/hr gain). Filed separately; link as a soft dependency.

## ACCEPTANCE
- 1–2 co-located warehouses run at J58; cap-optimizer sees Σ AGGREGATE capacity across the group; stocker restocks ALL co-located hulls (verify no singular FindRunningByWaypoint misuse).
- A contract delivering to J58 withdraws from the J58 warehouse and delivers locally (haul-leg on the contract's critical path ≈ 0, not 691u); the 691u haul appears on a STOCKER instead.
- J58 buffer holds only demand-gated goods (knapsack on receipt-demand), not all 9 blindly.
- Stockers keep the buffer non-empty against the observed J58 contract drain (measured via the instrumentation track).
- REGRESSION: with destination warehousing OFF, behavior is unchanged (source-side only).

## Admiral sign-off (hull allocation)
This commits ~5–6 hulls (1–2 warehouses + 1 hub + 2–3 stockers) to compressing the contract engine vs putting them on arb (parallel/uncapped). Corrected view: contracts are the BIGGER engine and now known cycle-bound-not-capped, so compressing them likely beats adding to the smaller arb stream — but it's a hull-mass call above analyst remit. Flag for Admiral alongside sp-vh1s.

CONFIDENCE: HIGH that cycle-time is the uncapped lever and the haul-leg is the dominant unaddressed term (J58 691u verified). HIGH that same-waypoint multi-warehouse is supported (code-verified). MEDIUM on stocker sizing + net $/hr — genuinely unmeasurable until the withdrawal instrumentation lands; that is why measurement is a parallel blocker, not optional.
notes:
DESIGN PRINCIPLES + SCOPE BOUNDARY (economy-analyst, 2026-07-14) — supersedes any sizing/positioning specifics below as DESIGN constraints; those are illustrative only.

1. ATOMIC UNIT (corrects a prior roving idea — retracted): warehouse + stocker(s) + a PINNED delivery hull are ONE inseparable unit per cluster. Rationale: SpaceTraders travel time is LOAD-INDEPENDENT (empty and loaded ships cover the same distance in the same time — LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION, verify against the twin before building). Therefore a destination warehouse served by a ROVING/central hull saves NOTHING — the hull pays the same haul-leg empty as it would loaded. The cycle-time win exists ONLY when the delivery hull is ALREADY at the destination cluster (the stocker paid the long haul in the background). So: no roving; a warehouse without a co-located pinned hull is pointless. The unavoidable cost is a pinned hull idle in every COLD cluster (only one cluster is hot — owns the single serial contract — at a time; game rule: one active contract per player).

2. DELIVERY-HULL POSITIONING POLICY: a cluster's delivery hull(s) FAVOR idling AT or beside their cluster's warehouse (SAME-WAYPOINT co-location permitted and preferred). Between contracts the hull returns to its warehouse waypoint, so a hot-cluster contract cycles as withdraw-local + deliver-local (~0 hull travel). Co-location preference is a POLICY the design must be able to express, not a hardcoded rule.

3. SCOPE BOUNDARY — DESIGN vs ANALYSIS are ORTHOGONAL. The DESIGN must be a FLEXIBLE MECHANISM supporting ARBITRARY positioning and sizing as PARAMETERS: arbitrary hull count, arbitrary warehouse count (incl. multiple co-located, sp-5q2c), arbitrary stocker count, arbitrary waypoints for hubs/warehouses/hulls — NONE hardcoded. The OPTIMAL positions and sizes (how many stockers, where clusters sit, how many hulls per cluster) are a SEPARATE economy-analyst deliverable produced against data, feeding the design's parameters. ⇒ The "J58 / 1-2 warehouses / 2-3 stockers / H54 / H51" figures in this bead are ILLUSTRATIVE PLACEHOLDERS (current-best estimate), NOT design constraints — the mechanism must not bake them in. Acceptance: instantiating a cluster with a different waypoint, hull count, warehouse count, or stocker count requires ZERO code change (config/params only).
CORRECTION to design principle #2 (I over-hedged it): CO-LOCATION OF DELIVERY HULLS WITH THEIR WAREHOUSE IS POLICY — a firm standing rule, NOT a tunable preference. A cluster's delivery hull(s) co-locate with (idle at / return to) their warehouse waypoint as policy. This is NOT part of the arbitrary/analyst-determined parameter space; it follows directly from the atomic-unit insight (warehouse+pinned-hull inseparable; a warehouse without a co-located hull is pointless; roving saves nothing because travel is load-independent). Clean split: (a) cluster PLACEMENT + SIZING (which waypoint, how many hulls/warehouses/stockers) = arbitrary parameters, analyst-determined; (b) hull<->warehouse CO-LOCATION = POLICY, firm, always. The design need not make co-location optional/expressible-as-one-option — it should ENFORCE it as the operating policy. Only WHERE the co-located pair sits and HOW MANY are parameters.
RETRACT the prior 'co-location is a firm hardcoded rule the design enforces' note — that was WRONG. CORRECT: ALL hull placement is PARAMETRIZED, per-hull, arbitrary — the design hardcodes NO placement. The economy-analyst ANALYSIS produces the placement (where each hull parks) = the POLICY (an analysis-determined config fed to the parametrized design). Co-location of a delivery hull with its warehouse is EXPECTED to be what the analysis recommends (minimizes cycle-time), but it is a POLICY OUTPUT, not a design constraint — the design must park each hull wherever the policy/config says, co-located or not. Same for warehouse/stocker placement and all counts: parametrized, analysis-determined. The design provides the mechanism (arbitrary per-element placement + sizing); the analyst provides the policy (the actual placements/counts). Nothing about positioning is hardcoded — not even co-location.
MIGRATION SIMPLIFIED (operator decision 2026-07-14): NOT a state-absorbing migration. Migration = STOP legacy coordinators + DECLARATIVE APPLY. Runbook: (1) let the in-flight contract finish (serialized, <=1 affected); (2) stop the legacy contract-fleet + warehouse + stocker coordinators/containers — releases their ships via the existing fleet-unassign/claim-release machinery (sp-w3yd), warehouse hull keeps its cargo; (3) declaratively apply the new cluster topology (bulk-apply CLI) which re-places the freed ships + warehouse(s) into clusters. STOCK CONTINUITY: map the legacy A1 warehouse hull → the CENTRAL cluster's warehouse (SAME hull/waypoint) so stocked goods carry over; far clusters (J58 etc) get fresh warehouses. So the 'legacy migration' build item collapses into the declarative bulk-apply CLI (already core) + clean coordinator-stop/ship-release + a documented runbook — NOT a data migration. Brief downtime (stop→apply gap) is accepted.
CONTRACT-ENGINE INTEGRATION = OPTION (a) (operator decision 2026-07-14): hook RouteContract directly into the existing contract coordinator. On an active contract, RouteContract(destination) -> if an owning cluster exists, deliver via that cluster's SelectDeliveryHull + prefer its destination warehouse as the withdrawal source (reuse the existing contract-worker inventory-withdrawal path); ELSE the existing default path, BYTE-IDENTICAL. Empty registry / no owning cluster = unchanged behavior (the natural off-switch — no flag). This is the load-bearing seam that makes the cluster mechanism actually function; it modifies the live contract engine, so the no-cluster fallback must be regression-guarded byte-identical.
CLUSTER-CONFIGURATION POLICY (economy-analyst) — the topology the sp-u9xa mechanism consumes
Data: player-3 fresh, 2026-07-14. Grounded in contract destination geometry + receipt-demand. This is CONFIG (fed to ApplyTopology), not code — every value here is a parameter.

## TWO CLUSTER TYPES (the mechanism supports both; parametrized)
- CENTRAL cluster = SOURCE-HUB based (buy-leg positioning; destinations are close, no dest warehouse needed). This is the migrated legacy setup.
- FAR cluster = DEST-WAREHOUSE based (haul-leg elimination): destination warehouse(s) + stockers (source→warehouse) + co-located delivery hull (withdraw-local → deliver-local). No source hubs.

## DESTINATION GEOMETRY (which destinations warrant a far cluster)
FAR (haul-leg dominates → dest warehouse pays): J58 696u/42ctr/3.06M · H54 419u/16ctr/348k · H51 764u/11ctr/681k.
CENTRAL (haul <235u → source-warehousing already covers): A1(233/32/3.06M), C39(159/25), D41(142/17), F49(92/11), D42(110/16), A2(106/11), K83(109/20), A4(106/3), H52(38/7), E44(98/15), F48(157/17). → ONE central cluster.

## TOPOLOGY (priority-ordered; hull budget gated)
Fleet: 12 light freighters (allocatable) + 1 frigate + 3 probes.

### CLUSTER 1 — CENTRAL (build via legacy migration, no new hulls)
- Type: source-hub. Owns all central destinations above.
- Source hubs: the current legacy hubs [E45, K83, D41, E44, I56] (already optimal top-5).
- Delivery haulers: the current contract haulers (TORWIND-5/6/7/9).
- Warehouse: reuse the legacy A1 warehouse hull (TORWIND-A) for A1-delivered central goods (A1 is central dest #1, 32 ctr) — preserves stock on migration.
- Migration: stop legacy contract-fleet + warehouse + stocker coordinators → apply this cluster (reuses the same hulls/waypoints). Stock preserved.

### CLUSTER 2 — J58 (BUILD NOW — biggest far cluster: 42 ctr, 3.06M, 696u haul)
- Type: dest-warehouse. Owns J58 destinations.
- Warehouse: 2 co-located @J58 (sp-5q2c multi-warehouse; aggregate ~160 cargo — J58 receives 6+ high-value goods).
- Demand-gated WHITELIST + caps (knapsack on RECEIPT-demand × recurrence × 696u haul-saved; coverage>depth, cap = max contract size). Fits ~160 cargo:
    MEDICINE 19 (7×, 809k)  ASSAULT_RIFLES 24 (5×, 511k)  FIREARMS 21 (5×, 503k)
    CLOTHING 24 (3×, 447k)  EQUIPMENT 22 (5×, 374k)  POLYNUCLEOTIDES 25 (7×, 55k)  [Σ135]
  EXCLUDE: FOOD (69u, only 2×), AMMONIA_ICE (76u, 224/u), EXPLOSIVES (low value) — big cargo hogs / thin recurrence; contract worker sources those fresh.
- Stockers: START 2 (J58 round-trip ~1,380u is long; sized to drain). MEASUREMENT-GATED — tune on sp-kqxe withdrawal data.
- Delivery hull: 1, co-located @J58 (config-placed; the mechanism does not prefer co-location, config puts it there).
- Hull cost: 2 warehouse + 2 stocker + 1 delivery = ~5 hulls.

### CLUSTER 3 — H54 (PHASE 2 — secondary far: 419u, 16 ctr, 348k) — weaker, DEPTH-constrained
- Receipt goods are BIG-UNIT precious metals (GOLD 70, SILVER 71, DIAMONDS 76, PRECIOUS_STONES 78) — each ~1 full hull, so the warehouse is depth-constrained (can pre-stage ~1-2 goods only).
- Warehouse: 1 @H54, whitelist {GOLD cap 70 (5×,165k), SILVER cap 71 (4×,113k)} — the 2 highest value×recurrence; DIAMONDS/PRECIOUS_STONES sourced fresh (big units, lower value).
- Stockers: 1 to start. Delivery hull: 1. Hull cost: ~3.
- Build AFTER J58 proves out + hulls free (gate completion / C1 reversal freed factory hulls).

### CLUSTER 4 — H51 (PHASE 3 — farthest 764u but only 11 ctr; DRUGS-driven) — marginal
- Only worth it for DRUGS (4×, 90u, 632k — high value). Ores are low-value cargo hogs (source fresh).
- Warehouse: 1 @H51, whitelist {DRUGS cap 25}. Stocker: 1. Delivery hull: 1. Hull cost: ~3.
- LOWEST priority — build only if hulls spare after J58+H54.

## HULL BUDGET
- Central: 0 new (migration reuses ~6 legacy hulls).
- J58: ~5 new. H54: ~3. H51: ~3.
- Available: 12 freighters. Central migration consumes ~6; J58 needs 5 → tight but feasible now (the C1 reversal freed factory hulls; gate completion frees more). H54/H51 phased as hulls free. Compete with arb for hulls — arb is near-fill (19/23 goods), so far-cluster hulls are a good use of surplus (orthogonal lever, per prior analysis).

## WHAT'S SET NOW vs MEASUREMENT-GATED
- SET NOW (structure): cluster count, types, waypoints, whitelists+caps, delivery-hull placement. These follow from geometry + receipt-demand, don't need instrumentation.

title: Distance-scaled warehouse buffer DEPTH — target_units = s_G × f(distance), deeper buffer for far-sourced goods (analyst owns policy)
description:
ENHANCEMENT (Admiral 2026-07-13), follow-on to sp-9274 (distance-aware residual selection). 

CURRENT: the warehouse knapsack (warehousecap.go valueGoods) buffers each SELECTED good at a flat quantity = s_G (single-contract fill size, MaxContractUnits), strictly 0/1. Distance (ResidualBuyLeg) affects only the SELECTION value, never the quantity. So a far-sourced good and a close-sourced good, both selected, get the SAME depth (one contract's worth).

PROPOSAL: scale buffer DEPTH by distance — target_units[G] = s_G × f(dist(warehouse, source)) — so a far-sourced good (expensive/slow to market-buy each top-up) holds a DEEPER buffer (e.g. 2-3 contracts' worth) that amortizes fewer far hauls, while a close good keeps a shallow s_G buffer it cheaply refills on demand. Bounded by hull capacity (deeper far-buffers = fewer DISTINCT goods buffered — the knapsack tradeoff).

ANALYST OWNS THE POLICY (this bead is pending economy-analyst's answer — see mail): the f(distance) shape (linear? capped step? threshold?), the max depth multiplier, and the capacity tradeoff (deeper buffers vs breadth). SHIPWRIGHT WIRES whatever the analyst specifies. DEPENDS ON sp-9274 (needs the per-good source-distance signal that fix introduces). RULINGS #5 (params analyst-owned), #2 (deterministic), capacity bound hard.

ACCEPTANCE (once policy set): a far good's target_units > s_G per the analyst's f(distance); a close good stays ~s_G; Σ target_units still ≤ Σ hull capacity (knapsack packs the deeper items); regression: f≡1 (flat) reproduces today's s_G behavior byte-identical.
notes:
CONSULT ANSWER — economy-analyst — sp-evdn (distance-scaled warehouse buffer DEPTH)

## RECOMMENDATION
Depth should scale with **restock-lead-time ÷ same-good inter-arrival-time** (expected stockouts during one refill), NOT with distance alone. Distance enters only THROUGH lead-time. Cap = 2. Breadth-gated (depth is spent only AFTER all high-value distinct goods are covered at depth-1). And ship it as a rarely-triggered tail enhancement, because CURRENT data shows ~no good actually needs depth>1.

## WHY DISTANCE-ALONE IS THE WRONG DRIVER (the load-bearing correction)
Buffer depth >1 pays back in exactly one situation: a SECOND contract for good G becomes active before the stocker finishes refilling G after the first draw. Contracts are SERIALIZED (1 active at a time), so same-good draws are spaced out — the second DRUGS contract can't start until the first finishes. So depth-2 is justified iff:
    restock_lead_time(G)  >  mean_inter_arrival(G)
Distance sets lead_time (far source = longer refill = more exposure). But INTER-ARRIVAL matters equally: a far good that rarely recurs will have its refill done long before the next draw → depth-1 suffices no matter how far. Distance-only f(dist) over-buffers far-but-RARE goods (wasting cargo on stock that won't be drawn twice) and under-buffers close-but-FREQUENT goods.

## THE DATA SAYS THE COMBO BARELY EXISTS TODAY (era torwind-2026-07-12, 129 contracts / 21.8h)
The far goods are RARE and the frequent goods are CENTRAL — the exact anti-correlation that makes depth>1 almost never pay:
  FREQUENT goods are all CENTRAL (short lead): POLYNUCLEOTIDES 12× (E45, ~87u), SHIP_PARTS 9× (D41), EQUIPMENT 7× (K83), MEDICINE 6× (F49). Inter-arrival 1.8–3.6h; central refill ~15min << that → depth-1 fine.
  FAR goods are RARE: DRUGS 1× (J58, 764u), ANTIMATTER 7× is the only moderately-far/frequent one (I56, ~220u) → inter-arrival 3.1h vs refill ~20min → still depth-1 fine.
No current good clears restock_lead > inter_arrival. So depth>1 fires ~never on today's mix. It is a robustness feature for a FUTURE era where a good is far AND frequent, not a live win.

## THE f() TO IMPLEMENT
PRINCIPLED (preferred — reuses sp-9274 distance + contract history):
    depth_G = clamp( round( restock_lead_time(G) / mean_inter_arrival(G) ), 1, DEPTH_CAP )
  - restock_lead_time(G): derive from dist(warehouse, source_G) (the sp-9274 signal) ÷ stocker speed, + a fixed dock/buy overhead. Analyst-tunable coefficient.
  - mean_inter_arrival(G): era_span ÷ contract_count(G) from contract history (same EWMA source warehousecap already reads). Thin-data guard: if count(G) < 3, treat inter-arrival as ∞ → depth 1 (never deep-buffer an unproven good).
  - DEPTH_CAP = 2 (see cap rationale).

PRAGMATIC FALLBACK (if arrival-rate is judged too noisy on thin data): a CAPPED STEP on distance, never linear:
    depth_G = 1 if residual_buy_leg(G) < D_THRESHOLD else 2
  - D_THRESHOLD ≈ central-cluster radius, ~150–220u (beyond it = the eastern outliers I56/J58). Analyst-owned.
  - Explicitly NOT linear (s_G × dist/k): linear scales depth with distance even when the good never recurs — the over-buffer failure above. A capped step at least bounds the damage.
  Prefer the principled form; the step is the "if you must keep it distance-only" version, and it still needs the cap + the breadth gate below.

## CAP = 2 (hard; maybe 3 only with evidence)
Coverage > depth for serialized contracts (established: a buffer's job is to have SOMETHING for whatever the next contract draws; one contract's worth per good already removes the far-haul from the critical path). Every extra depth-unit on G costs a DISTINCT good G' its slot in the hull. Depth-2 hedges the single realistic case (one unlucky same-good repeat during a far refill); depth-3 hedges a triple-cluster that serialization makes vanishingly rare. Cap at 2 now; only raise if a good is observed stocking-out-during-refill repeatedly.

## CAPACITY / BREADTH TRADEOFF — depth is BREADTH-GATED
This is the critical wiring constraint: the knapsack must pack in TWO passes, not fold depth into the value.
  Pass 1 (coverage): buffer every selected good at depth-1 (s_G), maximizing DISTINCT high-value goods covered — today's behavior.
  Pass 2 (depth): spend ONLY leftover capacity raising depth toward depth_G, in descending (restock_lead/inter_arrival) order.
So depth is never bought at the expense of covering another good — it consumes only slack. If the hull is full at depth-1 coverage, no good gets depth-2. This preserves coverage>depth and makes the enhancement strictly additive when spare cargo exists (e.g. after a 2nd warehouse hull is added, Σ capacity rises → Pass 2 has room).

## CONFIDENCE
HIGH that distance-alone is wrong and the driver is lead/inter-arrival (mechanics + the anti-correlation in the data). HIGH on cap=2 and breadth-gating (follows from serialization + coverage>depth, already established). MEDIUM on the exact restock_lead coefficient and D_THRESHOLD — tune against observed stocker round-trip times once sp-9274's distance signal is live.

## WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND / triggers to revisit
- A good appears that is BOTH far (>threshold) AND frequent (inter-arrival < its refill) → depth>1 starts paying; the principled f captures it automatically, the step form needs the threshold retuned.
- Stocker speed/overhead makes far refills much longer than assumed (raises lead_time, widens the depth>1 window) → recompute the coefficient from real round-trips.
- Contracts stop being strictly serialized (concurrent draws) → same-good overlap becomes possible independent of arrival spacing → depth math changes, revisit.
- f≡1 (flat) MUST reproduce today byte-identical (already in acceptance) — keep that as the regression floor.

## ONE-LINE FOR THE SHIPWRIGHT
Implement depth_G = clamp(round(restock_lead_time_G / mean_inter_arrival_G), 1, 2) with count(G)<3 ⇒ depth 1; apply it in a SECOND knapsack pass over leftover capacity after depth-1 coverage; fall back to a capped distance-step (D_THRESHOLD≈150–220u, cap 2) only if arrival-rate is too noisy to read.

description:
# Streamline the manufacturing/factory system — GROUNDED redesign (code-verified)

CORRECTION: the first draft of this epic was partly inference. A 4-way full code read corrected it. What actually holds:

## What the code actually shows (verified, cited)

1. **There is NO single "SpendGate."** Nine guards run at FOUR temporal points (guards read):
   - Coordinator launch-time, pre-hauler, pre-tree: G1 ChainMarginGuard (chain_margin_guard.go:102), G4 chain-pnl-kill (run_factory_coordinator_chain_pnl_kill.go:78, reads a 6h realized ledger, FAILS OPEN), G5 input-pause (run_factory_coordinator_input_pause.go:107, 194min recovery timer), G6 export-rest (run_factory_coordinator_rest_signal.go:102, 90min timer).
   - Per-fabricate-round: G3 inputRoundMargin (input_price_ceiling.go:199).
   - Per-tranche buy: G2 price-ceiling (input_price_ceiling.go:127), G8 spend-floor/9aoc (production_executor.go:631), G9 concurrent-spend-cap/w3he (production_executor.go:689).
   - Per-deposit (output side): G7 capital ceiling (planner_stock_depositor.go:165).
   Only G2+G8+G9 (+G3 as per-round pre-check) are mergeable — they're back-to-back at the executor tranche loop (production_executor.go:521/533/553), re-read live, park-the-buy. G1/G4/G5/G6 CANNOT move to point-of-spend: they run before the hull is acquired and (G5/G6) before the tree is built, hold hour-scale per-container timers, and G4 reads a rolling realized ledger + fails open — moving them defeats the "avoid the hull trip / no-poll recovery" design. G7 is output-disposal side.
   (My "6-7 guards -> 1" was wrong; also I mislabeled planner_stock_depositor as the 9aoc floor — it's sp-64je's capital ceiling; 9aoc is spendFloorBreached, a different guard.)

2. **Coordinators do NOT share an extractable score/maintain engine.** contract-hub's "reuses siting verbatim" header is overstated — the two share ZERO code/types (run_contract_hub_coordinator.go:34-35). Siting scores independently then sorts then maintains (two pure phases); contract-hub is a fused greedy facility-location loop where score depends on partial placement (run_contract_hub_coordinator_score.go:134) — no []Scored to hand a separate Select. Their act diverges (siting launch+retire+stateful; hub add-only+stateless). Factory/construction/arb aren't portfolio reconcilers at all. What IS shared: only the outer LOOP SKELETON (Handle for{} + tick race + Disabled gate + {Ticks,Errors}), duplicated verbatim across ~12 coordinators.

3. **The acquisition core is ALREADY unified; the real find is DEAD CODE.** Factory + construction both drive the single ProductionExecutor.ProduceGood (construction was refactored to a thin drain, run_construction_coordinator.go:46-53). A whole PARALLEL task-worker subsystem is DEAD (zero non-test callers): PipelinePlanner/CreatePipeline (pipeline_planner.go:78), FactorySupplyPoller, DualTaskQueue, SellMarketDistributor, CollectionOpportunityFinder (collection_opportunity_finder.go), ManufacturingDemandFinder. (Note: sell_market_distributor is deletable because it's UNUSED — not because it was "stir scaffolding"; my earlier "keep it, it's legit" was wrong on the keep, right that it isn't stir.)

4. **Observability data already EXISTS — it's just not surfaced.** Park reasons live in container-log metadata that the CLI renderer DROPS (container.go:280-284) and in an unpersisted NoWorkReason response field. buy_nodes/fabricate_nodes are computed but only logged (run_factory_coordinator.go:502-503). goods status silently DROPS 4 already-plumbed fields (ShipsUsed/MarketQueries/ParallelLevels/EstimatedSpeedup, container_ops_goods.go:140-143). And a full Prometheus layer (chain_pnl_realized_per_hour, chain_input_pause_total, manufacturing_factory_supply_level, task_starvation_minutes, profit_rate...) exists but only on /metrics, never in the CLI. So observability is SURFACE-existing-signals, not build-from-scratch.

## Grounded slices (dependency-ordered; every one cites the code it touches)

### A — DELETE dead code (biggest, safest win; do first; pure removal, zero behavior risk)
- **A1 — delete the dead task-worker subsystem** (each verified zero non-test callers; re-confirm per-file before removing): PipelinePlanner/CreatePipeline, FactorySupplyPoller, DualTaskQueue, SellMarketDistributor, CollectionOpportunityFinder, ManufacturingDemandFinder + their dead BuildDependencyTree caller in manufacturing_demand_finder.go. Large line removal, no runtime surface.
- **A2 — delete the siting stock-draw dead path** (StockDrawReader always-false; siting_alignment_service.go) — alignment uses tour-throughput directly. (= existing sp-7zhv.)

### B — Observability by SURFACING existing signals (cheap, additive, high value)

- **B2 — make park reasons queryable**: persist NoWorkReason and/or render the container-log metadata the CLI currently drops -> "why parked: <gate> <reason> <numbers>" in status.
- **B3 — pipe the existing Prometheus chain/factory series into goods/construction status**: per-material rate, realized P&L/hr, input-pause/export-rest counts, supply level, task starvation, bottleneck. Data exists on /metrics; surface it.

### C — Unify the per-tranche BUY gates only (narrow, verified-mergeable)
- **C1 — characterization tests** pinning G2+G8+G9+G3 current park behavior. Safety net.
- **C2 — one buy-side SpendGate** at the executor tranche loop (production_executor.go:521/533/553) wrapping G2+G8+G9 with G3 as per-round pre-check; PRESERVE per-guard reasons + G9's reservation handle; fold in the de-triplication of the 9aoc spend-floor shared with arb + trade-route (production_executor.go:631 / run_arb_coordinator.go:745 / run_trade_route_coordinator.go). Leave G1/G4/G5/G6/G7 exactly where they are (verified structural reasons above). [dep C1]
- **C3 (optional, code-shape) — collapse G4/G5/G6 into one generic "recovery-clock gate"** (three parallel state maps with identical arm/short-circuit/clear shape, run_factory_coordinator.go:102/111/120). Behavior-preserving.

### D — Collapse the duplicated buy-vs-fabricate DECISION
- **D1** — SupplyChainResolver.shouldBuyGood (supply_chain_resolver.go:283) and ConstructionPipelinePlanner.planMaterial/planFabrication (construction_pipeline_planner.go:429/505) are two impls of the same choice. Execution is already shared (ProduceGood); unify the DECISION (construction planner calls the resolver's decision, or extract a shared function). Behavior-preserving + test-guarded.

### E — Extract the coordinator LOOP SKELETON (broad, verified-clean)

NOT a generic score/maintain engine (verified not feasible). Behavior-preserving. [enables verifying via B]

- sp-5n7v stays a STANDALONE cap-optimizer coordinator (knapsack). It is NOT a "3rd instance of a shared engine" (that engine doesn't exist). It reuses E1's loop skeleton. Its shared-demand-model dep on sp-q2zq (contract-hub, done) is a data/model reuse, not an engine.

## Sequence
A (delete dead) first — shrinks surface for everything. B in parallel (cheap, enables verification). C1->C2->C3. D independent. E independent+broad. sp-5n7v after E1. Every slice a small PR; daemon green throughout.

- "6-7 guards -> 1 SpendGate": wrong — 9 guards/4 points, only 3-4 merge.

(2) C SpendGate SCOPE is unresolved — the 9aoc spend-floor spendFloorBreached is triplicated: production_executor.go:631 + run_arb_coordinator.go:~745 + run_trade_route_coordinator.go; and trading has its OWN buy/sell guard family (purchaseWithCeiling/sellWithFloor/laneClearsProfitFloor). title: Per-good buy-gating overrides (supply-strategy + price-ceiling + minSupply) — surgical bottleneck unstick without global over-spend
description:
PROBLEM: the supply-chain buy-gating knobs are all GLOBAL — to unstick a single bottleneck item (e.g. SILICON_CRYSTALS going LIMITED in the gate's ADV_CIRCUITRY chain) you must change gating chain-wide, which over-buys and over-spends on every good, not just the stuck one. Need SURGICAL per-good control: loosen the gate on the one bottleneck item while every other good keeps the safe global default.

THREE EXISTING GLOBAL GATES (all need a per-good override):
1. SUPPLY-STRATEGY gate — internal/application/manufacturing/services/supply_chain_resolver.go. AcquisitionStrategy is a single field on the resolver (StrategyPreferBuy | StrategyPreferFabricate | StrategySmart; Smart = fabricate when SCARCE/LIMITED, buy when MODERATE+). Set once via SetStrategy; applied uniformly to every node. StrategySmart already decides per-good FROM each good's supply tier, but the boundary/strategy itself is global — you can't say "for SILICON, buy even when SCARCE."
2. INPUT-PRICE-CEILING gate — services/input_price_ceiling.go + types/factory_types.go. InputPriceCeilingMultiplier (default 1.5) refuses an input buy whose live ask exceeds 1.5× the trailing-median ask (the sp-iv65 ladder-chase guard). One multiplier per run (WithInputPriceCeiling ctx); no per-good map.
3. minSupply SOURCING FLOOR — internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_construction.go, StartConstructionPipeline(..., minSupply string) (sp-ezz9). One EXPORT sourcing floor (e.g. "SCARCE") for the WHOLE pipeline.

WHY BOTH SUPPLY + PRICE (not redundant — keep both, override both): they gate orthogonal signals at different timescales. Supply-strategy = structural, coarse, decided once (buy-vs-fabricate + which market). Price ceiling = live, per-tranche, catches YOUR OWN buying walking the ask up DURING a round — the sp-iv65 bleed (ADV_CIRCUITRY bought inputs at ~19k/u = 4× market chasing its own ladder, −6.6M in 3h) happened WITH supply-gating + a launch-time margin projection in force, because the ladder climbed past the once-at-launch check. So a per-item knob must cover BOTH gates to actually move a bottleneck.

FIX: a per-good OVERRIDE map layered on all three gates, plumbed through the construction-pipeline / factory launch config:
    overrides: map[good] -> { strategy?: prefer-buy|prefer-fabricate|smart,  priceCeilingMult?: float,  minSupply?: SCARCE|LIMITED|MODERATE|HIGH|ABUNDANT }
At each gate's decision point, look up overrides[good]; if present use it, else fall back to the existing GLOBAL default (no behavior change for non-overridden goods). Analyst owns the override VALUES (which goods, what tuning); shipwright owns the plumbing.

MONEY-INTEGRITY GUARDRAIL (critical — a per-item price override is exactly the sp-iv65 bleed surface): a per-good priceCeilingMult override tunes the per-tranche ladder ceiling ONLY. It must NOT bypass (a) inputRoundMarginParked — the per-fabricate-round structural-underwater refusal (summed input ask > output/​sink bid) — nor (b) the 9aoc solvency floor / capital ceiling. So even a good with priceCeilingMult=3.0 still parks if the ROUND goes structurally underwater or treasury hits the floor. Optionally cap the override (e.g. hard max multiplier) so a fat-finger can't disable the guard. For CONSTRUCTION-supply goods (WithConstructionSupply, sp-qmp8), the resale-margin guards are already exempt (no resale), so the binding safety there is the solvency floor + a sane absolute ceiling — the override raises the ladder ceiling but the solvency floor stays hard.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A per-good override map can be supplied at construction-pipeline (and factory) launch.
- For an overridden good, the supply-strategy / price-ceiling / minSupply use the override; non-overridden goods use the unchanged global default (regression: a chain with one override + one normal good — normal good's behavior byte-identical to today).
- REGRESSION (surgical unstick): seed a chain where the bottleneck good is SCARCE with override {strategy: prefer-buy, priceCeilingMult: 3.0, minSupply: SCARCE} and a second normal good MODERATE with no override → assert the bottleneck good is bought aggressively (past the 1.5× global ceiling, down to SCARCE) while the normal good still follows Smart/1.5×/global-floor.
- REGRESSION (guardrail holds): with the same aggressive override, assert inputRoundMarginParked STILL fires if the override would make the fabricate ROUND structurally underwater, and the solvency floor still parks at the treasury floor. The sp-iv65 −6.6M bleed must stay prevented for both overridden and non-overridden goods.

ANALYST OWNS: which goods get overrides and their values (tuned per bottleneck/era). SHIPWRIGHT OWNS: the override-map plumbing + lookup + guardrail wiring.

Lineage: gate-construction supply-chain diagnostic (2026-07-13) — the gate self-manages via continuous fabrication + supply/price-gated buys; per-item override is the surgical spend knob for unsticking a single bottleneck item (e.g. SILICON_CRYSTALS) without global over-spend.

title: Auto-optimize warehouse buffer caps (knapsack over demand × residual-buy-leg, Σ real hull capacity) — sibling of hub optimizer sp-q2zq
description:
PROBLEM: the warehouse (contract-goods buffer) has no per-good caps AND no way to compute them — the config takes only a whitelist, so the stocker fills the hull greedily on the first/highest-priority goods and starves coverage of the rest. Static hand-set caps are the wrong altitude: the fleet can run MULTIPLE warehouse hulls, and cargo capacity varies (heavy frames, installed cargo modules) — so the ideal caps must be AUTO-COMPUTED from live demand and live capacity, exactly like hub placement (sp-q2zq).

LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-07-13, player-3): warehouse-TORWIND-A (80-cargo @A1), whitelist [MEDICINE,EQUIPMENT,ANTIMATTER,SHIP_PARTS,DRUGS], filled 80/80 with just EQUIPMENT 50 + MEDICINE 30 → 0 room for the other 3. Contracts for SHIP_PARTS (×2) and ANTIMATTER (×1) then bought FRESH (bypassing the buffer) while the 2 stocked goods sat undemanded. Root: internal/adapters/grpc/container_ops_warehouse.go builds config from only `supportedGoods []string` — no per-good target, no capacity model, no optimizer.

FIX — AUTO-CAP OPTIMIZER (sibling of the hub-placement optimizer sp-q2zq; SHARES its demand+coverage model). Compute per-good target_units as a 0/1 KNAPSACK, re-solved as demand/fleet change:
- CAPACITY C = Σ over all RUNNING warehouse hulls of ships.cargo_capacity. NEVER assume 80 — read the real per-hull capacity; a heavy frame, an installed cargo module, or a 2nd/3rd warehouse hull simply raises C and the knapsack buffers more. Bin-pack selected goods across the available hulls.
- Per contract good G:
    size  s_G = max (or p90) contract size for G — buffer FULLY or not at all (partial < 1 contract is useless ⇒ 0/1, not fractional).
    value v_G = smoothed(recurrence × payment) × RESIDUAL BUY-LEG_G, where residual buy-leg = dist(nearest homed hauler, G's cheapest source) — REUSE sp-q2zq's coverage_G. This makes the buffer COMPLEMENTARY to the hubs: hubs cover CENTRAL goods (0 buy-leg by positioning), the buffer covers FAR/orphan goods (0 buy-leg by pre-staging). A central, hub-covered good has ~0 residual buy-leg → ~0 buffer value → correctly NOT buffered.
- SOLVE: select the good-set maximizing Σ v_G s.t. Σ s_G ≤ C; target_units[G] = s_G for selected, 0 otherwise.
- STICKY: EWMA-smoothed demand + hysteresis (same as sp-q2zq) — only add/drop a good from the buffer on a DURABLE demand/coverage shift; never dump already-held stock on a one-tick flip.

WHY THIS FIXES THE INCIDENT: EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE are central + hub-covered → low residual buy-leg → the optimizer would NOT buffer them. It would spend the 80 cargo on DRUGS (J58, ~764u) and ANTIMATTER (I56, ~220u) — the goods a contract worker genuinely can't source fast. The current stocker did the exact inverse.

SHARED COMPONENT (build once, both consume): the smoothed-demand + residual-buy-leg (coverage_G) model is shared by sp-q2zq (allocates hauler POSITIONS) and this bead (allocates buffer CAPACITY). Coordinate so one demand/coverage service backs both. Analyst owns its weights.

ENGINE CHANGES: (1) container_ops_warehouse.go — add per-good target_units to the config, POPULATED BY THE OPTIMIZER (not hand-set); (2) stocker enforces target_units (hold each ≤ target, top up after consumption, never over-buy past target); (3) capacity read as Σ real hull cargo_capacity; (4) the knapsack optimizer + shared demand/coverage model.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Caps are COMPUTED from live demand + Σ real hull capacity, not static config.
- A hub-covered good (low residual buy-leg) is NOT buffered even at high recurrence/payment; a far-sourced good (high residual buy-leg) IS, capacity permitting. REGRESSION: seed the incident (hubs central-covering EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE; DRUGS/ANTIMATTER far) → assert the optimizer buffers DRUGS/ANTIMATTER over EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE.
- Adding a 2nd warehouse or a heavy/cargo-module hull raises C → knapsack buffers more goods, NO code change and NO assume-80.
- Σ selected s_G ≤ C; goods buffered fully (each at s_G), never partially.
- Stickiness: a one-tick demand/price flip does not churn bought buffer stock.

ANALYST OWNS: EWMA half-life, value-formula weights (recurrence/payment/residual-buy-leg blend), size percentile (max vs p90), hysteresis margin. Shipwright owns wiring + knapsack impl.

COLD-START FALLBACK (until enough demand history): static set DRUGS 24 / MEDICINE 20 / EQUIPMENT 20 / ANTIMATTER 8 / SHIP_PARTS 6 (Σ 78 ≤ 80).

Lineage: st-abx (design) → sp-5n7v evidence → sibling of sp-q2zq (hub optimizer; shared demand/coverage model).

title: Automate contract-hauler HUB placement (siting-coordinator sibling) — Phase 1: placement-only MVP
description:
Automate contract-hauler HUB placement (economy-analyst spec). Today hub geography is MANUAL (set at operation launch; recomputed by an economy-analyst consult on every hauler buy — done 3× in one session), and it DRIFTS as prices/demand move (e.g. MEDICINE's cheapest source flipped F49→D41 on a price tick, re-ranking the top hub). Automate placement off LIVE data. Build as a SIBLING of the factory siting coordinator (internal/application/manufacturing/commands/run_siting_coordinator.go + run_siting_coordinator_score.go) — reuse its candidate→score→maintain(top-K)+concentration-caps+staleness/reachability scaffolding; only the candidate set and the score differ.

SCOPE — PHASE 1 (this bead): PLACEMENT ONLY. When a light hauler is ADDED (or is idle+unhomed), auto-assign its home to the current best-open contract hub, computed live. Do NOT re-home already-homed haulers (that's Phase 2). This captures ~all the value (every new hauler lands optimally, no stale config) with ZERO thrash risk.

ECONOMIC ALGORITHM (economy-analyst OWNS the formula + all weights; shipwright owns wiring):
- OBJECTIVE: minimize payment-weighted contract BUY-LEG (maximize expected contract $/hr via closest-ship-wins).
- CANDIDATES: in-system waypoints that are the cheapest EXPORT/EXCHANGE source for ≥1 contract good (from market_data, player-scoped, current era). Single-system only pre-gate (RULINGS #14).
- DEMAND SIGNAL w_G per contract good G: EWMA-smoothed (payment_on_fulfilled × recurrence) over recent contracts (contracts.deliveries_json::jsonb). Smoothing is MANDATORY — the raw signal is thin/noisy (46 contracts, most goods 1×) and single-contract noise must not move placement. EWMA half-life = analyst-owned weight (start ~ half the era's contract count).
- SCORE a candidate hub C = MARGINAL payment-weighted buy-leg it eliminates, NOT raw payment:
    coverage_G   = min over already-homed hub positions H of dist(H, S_G)   (S_G = G's cheapest source; buy-leg a contract for G would incur under closest-ship-wins). Baseline (no hubs yet) = large constant so the first hub captures the highest-demand cluster.
    marginal(C)  = Σ_G  w_G × max(0, coverage_G − dist(C, S_G))
  This is a greedy max-coverage / facility-location score. It BAKES IN THE GEOMETRY with no special-casing: a central source cluster self-limits (2nd central hub adds ~0 marginal because coverage_G is already small), and outliers (e.g. I56 ANTIMATTER, J58 DRUGS) score high because no existing hub is near them. A naive raw-payment ranker would over-provision the central cluster — this avoids that.
- PLACEMENT: assign the new/idle-unhomed hauler to argmax_C marginal(C | current homes), subject to concentration caps (max haulers per hub / per source cluster — reuse siting maintain() caps). Portfolio K grows implicitly with fleet size.
- GUARDRAILS: idle-only (never strand a hauler mid-contract); fail-safe = leave homes untouched on transient market/read failure (the siting fail-open idiom); coverage uses home POSITIONS (serialized contracts → the next drop is served by whichever idle hauler is closest, so steady-state home geometry is what matters).

PHASE 2 (FOLLOW-ON bead, gate after Phase 1 lands — documented here so Phase-1 design accommodates it): cost-gated RE-HOMING of existing IDLE haulers on durable structural shifts. Re-home hub H_cur→H_alt ONLY IF  (marginal buy-leg savings of H_alt over H_cur) × (expected remaining contracts this era) > repositioning trip cost dist(H_cur→H_alt), plus a hysteresis margin. This rejects most re-homes (central savings ~70-90u vs ~100u move cost) and, with the EWMA, guarantees a one-tick price flip never triggers a move. Never re-home mid-contract.

ACCEPTANCE (Phase 1):
- A newly-added light hauler is auto-homed to the computed best-open hub off LIVE market+contract data (not a config constant).
- Demand smoothing verified: injecting a single new contract for a new good does NOT change an existing hauler's placement decision (only shifts the ranking marginally).
- Concentration caps respected (no all-haulers-on-one-hub).
- Fail-safe: a market-read failure leaves existing homes untouched (no churn on transient error).
- Regression seam for Phase 2: the re-home cost-gate is a pure function testable in isolation (a one-tick flip → no re-home).

ANALYST-OWNED KNOBS (I set/tune these, not hardcoded by shipwright): EWMA half-life, concentration caps, Phase-2 hysteresis margin + expected-remaining-contracts estimate, baseline coverage constant.

title: arb executor lacks per-trip live-profitability gate — runs net-negative lanes (generic fix)
description:
PROBLEM (money leak, small now, scales with hull count): the arb/trade executor runs buy->sell lanes without a per-trip live-profitability check, so it executes lanes that are net-negative after fuel. Observed 2026-07-13 (player-3, X1-VB74): a contract hauler (TORWIND-7) repeatedly bought POLYNUCLEOTIDES at its EXPORT (E45); its OWN buying walked the export price UP 223 -> 246 -> 272 /u across 3 trips in ~20min while the sell held ~280/u, collapsing gross margin +1240 -> +680 -> +80, and the last trip was net-negative after fuel. Low-value / thin-spread goods are the main victims and the fleet's own activity erodes the margin. Aggregate arb is still net-positive (~+314k/6h after fuel); this is a leak on the thin tail, not a systemic loss.

ROOT CAUSE: no per-trip profitability gate. If any gate exists it evaluates a cached / top-of-book quote once, which misses (a) buy-side self-inflation (repeated buys raise the EXPORT price) and (b) sell-side decay (dumping lowers the IMPORT price).

FIX — GENERIC, NO HARDCODED GOOD NAMES (must hold across eras/goods):
Before each arb buy, compute at CURRENT lot-adjusted prices for the candidate lane (buy good G at export E, sell at import S, lot size N):
  realized_buy_per_u  = avg price to BUY N units at E   (walks UP with N + prior buys — re-read live)
  realized_sell_per_u = avg price to SELL N units at S   (walks DOWN with N + prior dumps — re-read live)
  net_per_u = realized_sell_per_u - realized_buy_per_u - fuel_per_u
Execute the lane ONLY IF net_per_u >= floor. Otherwise skip it this cycle and re-evaluate next cycle.
CRITICAL: re-price EVERY trip against live next-lot prices — do NOT cache the up-front spread. The failure mode is the price moving under repeated trades; a one-shot spread check sails past it.

FLOOR (tunable config, not hardcoded per good):
  net_per_u >= ~100 after fuel, OR net_per_u >= ~20% of realized_buy_per_u, whichever BINDS (the % floor stops a high-priced good with a thin absolute spread from sneaking through).
  Grounding: fuel ~= 35/u on central lanes; POLYNUCLEOTIDES +33/u -> correctly rejected; fat lanes (FABRICS/CLOTHING/JEWELRY/MACHINERY/MEDICINE, ~800-1800/u) clear it 10x+.

SELF-REGULATING BEHAVIOUR (acceptance):
- A lane whose live lot-adjusted net_per_u drops below floor (from low base spread, sink decay, OR buy-side self-inflation) is skipped that cycle and AUTO-RE-ENTERS when the source/sink recovers.
- No hardcoded good list anywhere.
- Regression test: simulate a thin lane whose EXPORT price inflates with repeated buys (and/or IMPORT price decays with repeated sells); assert the executor STOPS trading it before net_per_u goes negative, and resumes after recovery.

MEASUREMENT NOTE (for whoever verifies P&L): arb P&L must be matched by COMPLETED buy->sell round-trips. A snapshot taken between the buy leg and the sell leg shows a phantom loss (observed: MEDICINE -121,040 bought 03:48, +181,760 sold 03:50 = +60,720 real profit). Do NOT gate or alarm on mid-round-trip treasury.

Consulted: economy-analyst (st-abx/st-tlg lineage). Rule is economic; implementation is the shipwright's.

title: feat(contract): live add/remove HUBS + balance the contract fleet across hubs (Admiral-directed; hub analogue of sp-4s9m live ship add/remove)
description:
DIRECTIVE (Admiral, direct order 2026-07-12): (1) ADD/REMOVE hubs to a RUNNING contract operation live (no restart) — the hub analogue of sp-4s9m's live ship add/remove; and (2) the contract-operation algorithm must BALANCE the contract fleet across the configured hubs.

CONTEXT: today 'fleet add --operation contract' only writes a ship's dedicated_fleet tag; hub placement is a separate mechanism (INCOME-phase hub-placement / parkedHub). This feature makes the HUB SET a first-class, live-mutable, persisted part of the contract operation, and makes the coordinator distribute its haulers across those hubs.

PART 1 — live add/remove hubs: CLI + daemon RPC to add/remove a hub waypoint on a running contract coordinator, no restart, persisted. Mirror the sp-4s9m pattern (thin CLI over a daemon RPC; the daemon is the single writer — RULINGS #3). CRITICAL: do NOT recreate the sp-86vb stale-seed trap for hubs — a live hub change must survive restart and NOT be overridden by a stale launch seed (co-design with / reuse the sp-86vb fix; treat launch hubs as first-boot-only / honor live state).

PART 2 — balance the fleet across hubs: the coordinator distributes its contract haulers across the configured hubs. Balancing objective (DESIGN PIN, captain refines at acceptance): EVEN distribution by hull count as the baseline; demand-aware weighting (per-hub contract availability/proximity) as a stretch if the signal is cheaply available. Rebalance triggers: on hub add/remove and on hauler idle — NEVER yank a hauler mid-contract to rebalance (RULINGS #7 clean hand-off; drain a removed hub's haulers to others only as their current leg completes).

DESIGN PINS: RULINGS #2 (hub set + assignments persist + reload; restart-resilient), #3 (daemon single writer; live change via RPC, not CLI orchestration), #5 (hubs are config/flags, not constants), #7 (no mid-contract poaching for rebalancing).

SEQUENCE/DEPS: grounds on the in-flight contract-hub mechanism trace; lands AFTER sp-86vb (same contract-coordinator files — collision) and reuses its restart-resilience fix. May decompose into children (live hub add/remove; balancing algorithm) at design time.

3. No mid-contract poaching: a rebalance never interrupts a hauler's active contract leg (clean hand-off, RULINGS #7).

title: CAS-retry: resolve ships.version conflicts by re-find + re-apply instead of last-write-wins clobber
description: The cheaper alternative to the sp-eum3 mailbox (chosen by the Admiral). sp-60ff's tripwire (d51c8a32) detects concurrent-writer conflicts (ships.version CAS: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE WHERE ships.version=loaded) and on RowsAffected==0 counts+logs then falls back to LAST-WRITE-WINS (clobbers a concurrent writer's mutation). The probe recorded 1058 such clobbers. FIX (optimistic concurrency, NO mailbox/actor model): on CAS conflict, RE-FIND the fresh row, RE-APPLY the intended mutation on top of fresh state, and RETRY the CAS Save, bounded (e.g. 3-5 attempts, counter incremented per attempt). If retries exhaust, fall back to the EXISTING last-write-wins so behavior never regresses — strictly improves. SCOPE: introduce a minimal SaveWithRetry / Mutate(fn) helper (Find -> fn(ship) -> CAS-Save -> on-conflict re-Find -> fn -> retry) and route ONLY the high-conflict write sites through it (scheduler arrival/cooldown/sweeper + claim/release — the sites generating the 1058). Do NOT do a fleet-wide Find-mutate-Save migration (that is eum3) and do NOT build per-ship goroutines/serialization. Reuse sp-60ff's PersistedVersion + CAS Save + counter. Config knob for max retries (RULINGS #5). This closes the lost-mutation class cheaply; the full mailbox (sp-eum3) remains the option if ordering/serialization is later wanted.
notes:
MERGED d5ce7a3e (squash into main). numstat: 7 files, +455/-72 — ports.go(+24), ship_repository.go(+168/-2), ship_repository_cas_retry_test.go(+194 new), ship_state_scheduler.go(+115/-72), daemon.go(+14), main.go(+7), config.yaml.example(+5).

WHAT: navigation.ShipRepository gains SaveWithRetry(ctx,symbol,playerID,ShipMutation)->(*Ship,saved bool,err). On a ships.version CAS conflict it RE-FINDS the fresh row, RE-APPLIES the mutation fn on top of fresh state, and RETRIES the CAS Save, bounded by resolvedCASRetries(); on exhaustion (or when disabled) it falls back to the EXISTING last-write-wins (saveLastWriteWins) so behavior never regresses below sp-60ff. Save() refactored into shared trySaveCAS + saveLastWriteWins helpers (Save behavior byte-identical to before). Conflict counter (shipVersionConflicts + metrics.RecordShipVersionConflict) increments per CAS attempt, so telemetry is kept across retries. NO mailbox/actor, NO per-ship goroutines (that remains sp-eum3).

WRITE SITES ROUTED (the 1058-clobber generators — all 4 Find->mutate->Save sites in ShipStateScheduler): handleArrival (Arrive+ClearArrivalTime), handleCooldownClear (ClearCooldown), sweepStuckShips arrival loop, sweepStuckShips cooldown loop. Each site's applicability guard (IsInTransit / CooldownExpiration!=nil) moved INTO the mutation fn so it is re-checked on every re-find (changed=false => skip write, no spurious version bump) — strictly MORE correct than before.

LEFT ON FALLBACK (by design, noted): the claim/release paths (ClaimShip/ReserveForCaptain/ReleaseCaptainReservation/ReleaseAllActive) do NOT use Save — they use SELECT FOR UPDATE row-locking + partial-column Updates in a tx (sp-i1ku/sp-l7h2) and are already race-safe by pessimistic locking; they generate no CAS conflicts, so routing them was unnecessary and out of scope.

KNOB (RULINGS #5, live-by-default + disable escape): DaemonConfig.max_cas_retries (0/unset -> built-in default 3) + cas_retry_disabled (false=ACTIVE; true=legacy last-write-wins). Documented in config.yaml.example.

Even-distribution of probes refreshes those lanes and raises the effective trade ceiling.   1/0   internal/adapters/grpc/command_factory_registry.go

  72/0  internal/application/scouting/commands/run_scout_post_coordinator_test.go

ROOT CAUSE: unmannedSlotTargets() emitted manning targets DEPTH-FIRST — every one of a post's slots before moving to the next post. sortPostsByPriority() puts the top-priority post first, and standing posts are often MULTI-HULL (sp-enry: N probes over N disjoint market partitions, N ExtraSlots). When such a post was fully unmanned, Pass 2b consumed the scarce idle-probe pool filling ALL N of that ONE post's slots before any probe reached a DISTINCT system. That is the herd: the whole idle group relayed to one target per cycle (live: 7->BT82, then 8->GS93) while HZ30/PD44/YP16/FQ55 stayed dark with zero probes — over-scout where 1 suffices AND uncovered high-value systems whose lanes then went stale/tour_lanes_stale_excluded. o34q relay routing was fine; the DISTRIBUTION order was the bug. Distinct from sp-8k9m (dead claim/move path, N-probes/M-slots min claims) — that was under-claiming; this was mis-ordering.

SPREAD HEURISTIC: breadth-first round-robin by slot TIER across the priority-ordered posts. Group each post's unmanned slots in slot order (posts kept in priority order); then emit tier 0 = every post's FIRST unmanned slot, tier 1 = every post's SECOND, etc. The full target SET is unchanged (same slots, reordered) — so once every uncovered system has its first probe, a multi-hull post still fills all its extra slots (depth preserved), and single-hull-only fleets are one tier (byte-equivalent). Emergent cap ~1/system until coverage achieved. In-system manning (Pass 2a) is unaffected (in-system sats are system-specific); the reorder only changes the SCARCE cross-system reposition pool (Pass 2b) that was being herded.

CONFIG (RULINGS #5, live-by-default): [scouting] coverage_spread_disabled=false => LIVE coverage-first; =true reverts to legacy depth-first without redeploy. title: Scout cross-system defects (8k9m follow-up): scout_tour crashes on cross-system markets (f) + orphan-sweep (verify vjwb overlap) + multi-ship VRP no-op (a) + waypoint cache auto-sync (e)
description: Split from sp-8k9m per the clean-cut ruling (evidence on that bead). (f) ROOT: scout_markets assigns CROSS-SYSTEM markets to a single posts tour while the hull sits at the origin; scout_tour calls NavigateRoute directly, which is IN-SYSTEM ONLY (validates destination against the ORIGIN systems waypoint cache, navigate_route.go:274) -> uniform crash "waypoint X1-<dest> not found in cache for system X1-<origin>"; 7 of the 11 KN67 probes are held by these crash-looping dash-prefix tours. DESIGN PRIOR (harbormaster): fix the ASSIGNMENT, not the tour — scout posts are per-system by design; cross-system coverage is the reconcilers job (ferry the probe, then in-system tour). scout_markets should partition markets per-system and refuse/loud-fail cross-system assignments to an unferried hull; making scout_tour cross-system-capable (routing through travel()) is the bigger-blast alternative — take it only if the analyst/captain want single-tour multi-system scans. Also in scope: (orphan-sweep) reconcile discovers orphaned in-cluster probes before ferrying — VERIFY overlap with sp-vjwb stale-claim reconciliation first, may be free; (a) multi-ship scout-markets VRP returns 0 containers silently; (e) deploy path auto-syncs waypoints on cache miss instead of failing the deploy. notes:
VJWB-OVERLAP VERIFIED (agent, from sp-8k9m): the orphan RECLAIM is ALREADY implemented by sp-vjwb (44ba6b9d, refresh_ship.go reconcileStaleClaim/isClaimOrphaned): a hull whose owning container is GONE (not found), PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED, or STOPPED is ForceRelease'd to idle — and this is INDEPENDENT of nav_status, so an IN_TRANSIT orphan (driver container dead) IS reclaimed. => orphan-sweep should NOT re-implement reclaim. Same-system re-seat then beats a 6-hop relay (captain's ask). Reclaim logic to REUSE, not rebuild: refresh_ship.go isClaimOrphaned.

title: iv65 completion (Admiral design point): input buys must gate on SUPPLY STATE + size tranches to trade_volume — price ceiling is the lagging backstop, supply is the leading indicator

title: arrival_wait safety resync false-positive: "not in transit" read as "arrived" before arrival is due — stale pre-departure snapshot class (trnp deeper root)
description: sp-trnp root cause one level up: arrival_wait.go:229 safety resync treats a not-in-transit position snapshot as arrival confirmation even when the scheduled arrival is not yet due (TORWIND-37: 30s into a 2m33s flight, stale snapshot -> "confirmed ship left transit" -> route completed with the hull still at origin -> downstream jump hard-crash). trnp (3fa8cc2) hardened the departure-hop->jump seam defensively; OTHER navigate-then-act flows can still receive a premature "arrived" from the same false positive (most tolerate via their own resync/dock — enumerate which do NOT). Fix shape: the safety resync must not confirm arrival before min(scheduled_arrival) unless the authoritative API position differs from origin; sp-ynuf/n7yp precedent. Kill the class at the source, then consider retiring trnps defensive layer to avoid double syncs.

FIX LANDED (branch commit c04e19a; final merge SHA on gating). arrival_wait.go class root fixed at source (one level up from trnp 3fa8cc2, which only hardened the leg-1 jump seam).

ROOT: waitForShipArrivalCore's safety resync treated ANY not-in-transit read as arrival. FindBySymbol is the DB (source of truth post-startup, NOT live API — SyncShipFromAPI is the live path) and can lag THIS leg's departure, returning the pre-departure snapshot: hull not-in-transit, still at ORIGIN. The wait reported arrival-at-destination while the hull was at the start of the leg. Note: applyArrival(ship) only flips the in-memory ship IN_TRANSIT->IN_ORBIT; currentLocation stays the destination StartTransit set, so the caller's ship LOOKS arrived-at-destination while the API reality is still in-transit.

FIX: before scheduled arrival (dueIn>0) a not-in-transit resync confirms ONLY when fresh.CurrentLocation()==ship.CurrentLocation() (the destination the in-transit hull heads to; origin!=destination is guaranteed by StartTransit rejecting a same-waypoint hop). Genuine early arrival at destination still passes; a stale origin snapshot falls through to keep polling (cache catches up -> confirm at destination; or the IN_TRANSIT branches take over; or the budget deadline parks it, sp-7yej honest exit). At/after ETA (dueIn<=0) UNCHANGED — confirm on status alone (surgical: zero new false-negative risk on the common on-time path). Reading position off the DB is sufficient BECAUSE the stale snapshot's position IS the origin (differs from destination) — no extra live sync needed inside the wait.

TOLERANCE TABLE — navigate-then-act consumers of WaitForShipArrival and blast radius of a premature "arrived" (all 5 inherit the fix; table = unmitigated behavior):

| Consumer (call site) | Post-wait act | Premature-arrived outcome | Tolerates? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tour/arb cross-system leg-1 departure hop -> JUMP (travel(); h.navigate -> NavigateRouteCommand -> RouteExecutor -> WaitForShipArrival) | jumpHop | jump_ship.go hard-rejects "not at a jump gate", NO auto-nav for driveless hull -> UNRECOVERABLE crash | NO — the proven trnp crash (TORWIND-37) |
| Trade-route dock, source/dest (run_trade_route_coordinator) | dock to buy/sell | dock hits "cannot dock while in transit"; sp-ynuf resync+retry (SyncShipFromAPI, bounded) reloads truth and retries, else aborts circuit cleanly | YES — self-heals via own resync |
| RouteExecutor same-system hops (route_executor.go waitForArrival / waitForCurrentTransit) | refuel(dock)/scan then next navigate | false IN_ORBIT bypasses the next waitForCurrentTransit idempotency wait; next dock/navigate fires vs a still-in-transit hull -> API 4214/cannot-dock -> route aborts -> container retry; transient DB mis-persist (IN_ORBIT@dest) reconciled by bg updater | MOSTLY — recoverable abort, no crash; costs a wasted retry + transient bad persist |
| Gas siphon (siphon_resources.go) | EnsureInOrbit + SiphonResources API | siphon API rejects (hull not in orbit at the gas giant) -> recoverable error -> worker retry | YES — API rejects the mis-siphon |
| Reposition/ferry (RepositionToWaypoint -> travel()) | same as travel(): jump or gate->wpt navigate | if the leg includes a departure-hop jump: same UNRECOVERABLE crash as row 1; else recoverable | NO if it jumps; else recoverable |

Only the JUMP seam is unrecoverable. Dock/siphon/same-system self-heal via their own API-rejection/resync. The source fix removes the trigger for all of them.

KEEP-VS-RETIRE — trnp 3fa8cc2 defensive departure-hop re-confirm (SyncShipFromAPI + waitForInTransitArrival + IsJumpGate() before the jump): RULING = KEEP (agrees with harbormaster prior).
- It asserts a DIFFERENT invariant than the source fix. My fix guarantees "the hull arrived where the navigate sent it" (pos==navigate-destination, read off the DB). The trnp layer independently verifies, on a FORCED LIVE API read, "the hull is physically ON a jump gate" right before the one operation that hard-crashes unrecoverably. Even a genuinely-arrived hull at a wrong/mis-routed waypoint — a class the arrival fix does NOT cover — is caught.

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
FLEET-ARCHITECT — AF2 GATE-COMPLETION GO/NO-GO FRAMEWORK (sp-oeop). This is the DECISION STRUCTURE + constraint math + hidden costs + the two inputs that close it — NOT a verdict. The bill is unread and the uplift is the analyst's door; I will not fabricate either (a go/no-go built on an invented bill or uplift is the narrative-outran-evidence failure).

WHAT'S KNOWN vs PENDING:
- KNOWN: treasury 3.2M growing 1.6-2M/hr; 5 heavies, 21 posts; AF2 edges FIVE core systems (GQ92/HU21/KA42/PA3/UQ16); era ends 07-12 13:00Z. Precedent datapoint: the FAB_MATS gate just completed cost ~2.98M in materials (one-time capex).
- PENDING (blockers to a real package): (1) the AF2 construction bill — materials x qty — needs the on-site construction-CLI read named in the bead; (2) the realized route-uplift $/hr — the trade-analyst's economics door.

THE CLOCK IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: ~46h to reset (07-12 13:00Z from now). The gate does NOT persist across reset, so 100% of payback must land in ~46h, and the window shrinks every hour of delay. This BLUNTS the usual structural-lever logic: route-collapsing infrastructure normally beats buying hulls, but a ~46h horizon can make THIS instance fail to pay back. Right lever, possibly wrong time — that is the whole tension.

THE GO/NO-GO MATH (falls out the moment both inputs land):
- B = delivered cost = material credits + fleet-time OPPORTUNITY COST of the hauls (see hidden cost).
- U = realized $/hr uplift from shortened routes, quantified by the analyst as hop-count reduction x fleet-time value — NOT a hand-wave.
- GO iff U > B / 46h, WITH margin: target payback < ~30h, because U is soft and the clock only shrinks. Thresholds for reference: a ~3M bill needs U > ~65k/hr (~3-4% of the current 1.6-2M/hr engine); a ~2M bill needs U > ~43k/hr.

HIDDEN COST the naive "bill vs uplift" misses: the material hauls DIVERT fleet-time from a 1.6-2M/hr engine. True cost = material credits + (haul-hours x current per-hull yield). At 1.6-2M/hr across 5 heavies, diverted heavy-hours are expensive — cost the hauls in opportunity terms, not just fuel+materials. This can flip a marginal case to NO.

DO NOT PRICE the speculative "opens whatever sits beyond AF2" upside into the go/no-go: unknown frontier, ~46h to expiry, unknown contents = an unpriceable call option. Justify the spend on the KNOWN inner-cluster route-shortening ALONE, and treat beyond-AF2 as unpriced upside that must NOT tip a marginal case to GO.

PROVISIONAL LEAN (conditional, pending the bill):
- Small bill (~1-1.5M): likely GO — modest route-shortening clears the bar in 46h even after the haul opportunity cost.
- FAB_MATS-scale bill (~3M): MARGINAL-to-NO — needs U > ~65k/hr AND a shrinking clock; real risk it does not pay back before reset. Lean cautious; demand a firm U before committing.

RECOMMENDATION (actionable now): the decision has DECAYING option value. Dispatch the on-site bill-read on the NEXT probe/hull pass IMMEDIATELY; run the analyst's route-uplift quantification in PARALLEL; reconvene with B and U, then the Admiral decides against this framework. I am NOT bd-human-flagging yet — the bead says flag "when costed," and it is not costed; flagging an un-costed package wastes the Admiral's decision. I flag the moment B and U land. Not closing sp-oeop.

title: Refute: staged tour max-spend raise 1M->1.5M->2M keyed to aggregate-exposure<=60% of treasury
description: CONSULT (refute-this-plan) for trade-analyst. Snapshot at ask (14:45Z): 46 hulls, 5 heavies touring (19/2B/2C/2D/2E, 1M caps), treasury 3.24M recovering from a 743k trough (capex #4+#5 + two first manifests concurrent), income ~1.6-2M/hr, era ends 07-12 13:00Z. EVIDENCE the cap binds: 2D's first manifest hit 972,669 of the 1M cap; high-unit-value goods (ANTIMATTER 151k/u, MEDICINE ~5k/u) fill 1M with hold slots idle; planner price error 0.8% (tour report). PLAN: raise per-tour --max-spend at natural re-plan boundaries, staged by AGGREGATE exposure (N_heavies x cap <= ~60% of liquid treasury): 12M+ treasury -> 1.5M caps; 16M+ -> 2M. Captain launch-flag only, no code. REFUTE ANGLES WANTED: does absorption (not the cap) actually bind most manifests (2B/2E bursts were ~520-540k)? does a bigger tranche crush sell-side bids past lbbm's 80% floor more often (held tranches = dead capital)? is the 60% exposure rule too loose given today's 90% drawdown?
notes:
TRADE-ANALYST REFUTATION (sp-i8vx: staged tour-cap raise 1M→1.5M→2M @ exposure≤60%) — 2026-07-10 ~14:55Z

**Verdict: WEAK REFUTE — approve the staged raise, but the plan protects against the wrong risk and rests on one wrong premise. Two amendments are the actual substance.**

**PREMISE CORRECTION (ledger fact):** no heavy bought ANY good above 10k/unit since 08:00Z — the "ANTIMATTER 151k/u + high-unit-value goods fill 1M with hold slots idle" framing is unsupported (151k was likely a leg TOTAL, not per-unit; antimatter trades 3-6k/u). The cap binds through plain hold-math: a ~360-hold at the current 2.8-4.5k/u manifest mix = 1.0-1.6M full load. That is the honest justification FOR the raise — 2D hitting 972,669/1M (97%) is a hold-limited full board, and every full-value board on a 360-hold will hit a 1M cap whenever avg unit cost >2.8k. Raise: justified.

**Refute angle (a) — absorption vs cap: MIXED, leaning cap.** 2B/2E's ~520-540k bursts were BOARD-bound (not enough profitable legs at those stops), not absorption-bound per se; 2D was cap-bound at 97%. Expect the cap to bind on any tour whose board is rich (ZC66/GQ92 multi-good stops) and to be slack on thin boards. The raise only pays on rich boards — which are exactly the tours producing the 1.6-2M/hr. No objection.

**Refute angle (b) — bigger tranche crushes sell bids past lbbm's 80% floor: STRUCTURALLY DISSOLVED.** Spend caps do not control UNITS; the hold (fixed) and per-market trade-volumes control units-per-sink-visit. A higher max-spend shifts the mix toward pricier goods at the SAME unit counts — sell-side crush risk is unchanged by the cap. Where held-tranche risk actually lives: pricier goods tend to have thinner sinks (adv_circ v40-100, parts/plating v6-30). AMENDMENT 1: per-good unit-tranche cap = min(hold share, ~1x sink trade_volume per market visit) for goods >5k/u — that protects the 80% floor at its real binding point, and it costs nothing on deep sinks.

**Refute angle (c) — is 60% too loose after today's 90% drawdown: THE GATES ARE FINE; THE HOLE IS STAGE-0.** The plan gates RAISES at 12M/16M treasury but is silent about TODAY: at 3.24M liquid, five 1M-cap heavies can load 5M concurrently = 154% exposure, and the ledger shows ~6.5M of purchases across the five heavies inside the 14:00 hour alone — survivable only because sells land continuously. The 743k trough IS the proof that instantaneous in-flight exposure ran ~90%. AMENDMENT 2 (the real protection): enforce the exposure rule CONTINUOUSLY from now — before any manifest load: (in-flight manifest value at cost + planned load) ≤ 60% of liquid treasury; stagger departures to satisfy it. At today's 3.24M that means ~2 concurrent full loads — matching the observed healthy cadence anyway. The staged raises then inherit a rule that already runs, instead of switching on at 12M.

**Era-clock check:** ~46h left; a raised cap pays back within one loop (~2-2.5h). No objection from the clock. Planner price error 0.8% is excellent — planning accuracy is not the risk; concurrency is.

**Confidence.** HIGH on the structural (b) dissolution and the premise correction (direct ledger queries); MEDIUM on manifest-level spend isolation (hourly buckets blur multi-load hours — 2C shows 4.6M/26-buys in hour 13, i.e., multiple fast loads; per-manifest telemetry would sharpen this, the tour report presumably has it).
**Flips:** if the tour planner CAN already stagger by in-flight exposure and today's trough was purely the capex collision → amendment 2 is already satisfied, approve as written. If any manifest actually contains a >10k/u good → my premise correction is wrong, re-examine hold-idle claim. If lbbm held-tranche events spike after the first 1.5M manifests → amendment 1 was insufficient, halve tranche caps for >5k/u goods.

Cross-ref (harbormaster 2026-07-10): sp-78ai (absorption reservations + recovery-externality pricing) closes this same in-flight-exposure hole from the MARKET-DEPTH side — the trade-analyst ruling explicitly pairs the two. Build lanes L2 sp-l2cq / L3 sp-ypbo carry the reference.

title: Trade engine: 3 execution bugs costing ~495k/3h (same-waypoint round-trips, stale-ask buys, wrong lab sink) - from Admiral-requested audit
description:
Source: trade-analyst FIFO-matched audit of 11:30-14:30Z window (full table on sp-zgbk note, 2026-07-10 14:30Z). Trading realized +4.10M/3h overall - these three bugs are the -495k drag; fixing them recovers ~+120k/hr.

BUG 1 - SAME-WAYPOINT ROUND-TRIPS (-142k): the engine bought and sold the same good at the SAME market: FERTILIZERS UQ16-FF5F->FF5F -75,200 (320u), ALUMINUM UQ16-AF2D->AF2D -55,680 (240u), FERTILIZERS JP61-Z10A->Z10A -11,520 (160u). Buying at ask and selling at the same market's bid is a guaranteed spread loss. Suspect: route-abort/hold-clearing logic dumping cargo where it stands, or the arb ranker allowing src==dst. Fix: hard-forbid sell-at-buy-waypoint except explicit emergency dump; make aborts carry cargo to the nearest positive bid.

BUG 2 - STALE-ASK BUYS (-247k): SHIP_PARTS D39->H50 realized -3,430/u x 64 (-219,532!) and D39->A2 -27,178. The buyer executed against a cached quote after D39's ask laddered past the sink bid (factory lift + arb draw share D39; ask moved 3,985->4,942->~7k within the hour). Fix: re-verify LIVE ask at dock immediately before purchase; abort leg if live ask breaks the min-margin that justified dispatch (bp6f re-verify exists for margins at dispatch - extend to buy-time).

BUG 3 - WRONG-SIDE SINK (-66k): LAB_INSTRUMENTS NK36-ED7A->GQ92-C37 -819/u x 80. GQ92-C37 is a lab EXPORTER (its bid is the sellback price ~2.4k), not an import sink. The router treated an exporter's bid as a destination. Fix: destination filter trade_type=IMPORT (or EXCHANGE) only - never sell into an EXPORT market's bid unless bid>cost explicitly.

Verification data: all three reproducible from transactions table, window 2026-07-10 11:30-14:30Z, player_id=2, FIFO-matched per (ship,good).

title: Container iteration-error restart: no backoff between the 3 attempts + dead-stays-dead after transient dependency outage
description: Found during sp-g5ct's caller audit (pre-existing, NOT introduced by the lazy-conn change — any handler error triggers this path). Two gaps at container_runner.go:393-404 + container.go:66/299: (1) MaxRestartAttempts=3 retries run back-to-back with ZERO backoff — against a fast-failing dependency (routing down = instant connection-refused on localhost) a container burns all 3 in milliseconds and dies; (2) once dead it STAYS dead (supervisor doctrine: found-dead stays dead until human relaunch) even after the dependency self-heals — the routing CLIENT now auto-reconnects (e471723) but a container that died during the outage needs manual relaunch.
