title: Contract-goods inventory pre-positioning: trade engine stocks cheap cross-system goods at home; contract workers source inventory-first (Admiral-endorsed)
description: Admiral design ruling 2026-07-10 (companion to RULINGS #14): contracts stay single-system; the PARALLEL trade engine does the cross-system logistics instead. SHAPE: (1) DEMAND SIGNAL — mine contract history (380+ this era) for recurring goods + quantities => a demand distribution per good (never speculative; RULINGS #6 spirit: stock to measured recurrence). (2) HAUL — tour/trade legs (sp-1ek0 P2 gains a 'deliver-to-home-storage' leg type; idle-arb may prefer contract-recurrent goods on hub-local legs) buy at cheap cross-system asks and deposit into HOME storage (storage ops domain exists — StorageOperationModel; check sp-8yf1's storage-pickup gap first). (3) SOURCE INVENTORY-FIRST — the sourcing optimizer treats home inventory as a zero-ask source ahead of market buys (PlanDeliverySourcing gains an inventory check; never-skip unaffected). (4) ECONOMICS GUARD — pre-position only when (home_ask − foreign_ask) × recurrence-weighted units > haul opportunity cost + capital carry; Guard-1-style logged decisions. DEPENDENCIES: sp-1ek0 P1b (the hauler), contract-demand stats from ledger, a storage-withdrawal path for contract workers (interacts with sp-8yf1). Sequencing: post-P1b; candidate for the sp-1ek0 P2 wave alongside absorption reservations + recovery-externality pricing (all three are 'market-state economics' siblings).
design:
# DESIGN — Contract-goods inventory pre-positioning (sp-dchv)

Investigation: read-only recon, 2026-07-10. Every load-bearing claim cited file:line.
Framing: RULINGS #14 keeps contract legs single-system; THIS feature feeds that constraint
by pre-positioning cross-system goods into HOME storage so the contract worker sources
in-system. The dormant cross-system machinery on the bead is REUSED, not re-invented.

## 0. The load-bearing facts (what actually exists on main)

- **Sourcing seam is ready.** `PlanDeliverySourcing` builds `best` from the in-system market
  candidate at `internal/application/contract/sourcing_optimizer.go:183`; both live callers pass
  `nil` reachability = in-system only (`run_fleet_coordinator.go:390`,
  `queries/evaluate_profitability.go:116`). The `SourcingPlan` struct (sourcing_optimizer.go:115)
  and its consumer `purchaseMarket := plan.Market` (`run_fleet_coordinator.go:401`) are exactly
  where an inventory-first branch slots.
- **Cross-system finder is real and wired.** `FindCheapestMarketsSellingAllSystems`
  (`internal/adapters/persistence/market_repository.go:230-267`, SQL `sell_price ASC`, player-scoped)
  behind interface `CrossSystemMarketFinder` (sourcing_optimizer.go:83). This is the "cheapest
  foreign ask per good" half of the demand→market join.
- **Storage warehouse primitives are real and general.** `StorageShip`
  (`internal/domain/storage/storage_ship.go:22`) holds ARBITRARY goods (`cargoInventory map[string]int`)
  with BOTH halves: deposit (`ReserveSpace`:194 / `ConfirmDeposit`:229 / `ReleaseReservedSpace`:212)
  and withdrawal (`TryReserveCargo`:264 / `ConfirmTransfer`:288 / `CancelReservation`:316). The
  `StorageCoordinator` (`internal/application/storage/coordinator.go`, in-memory) exposes the deposit
  path (`ReserveSpaceForDeposit`:460, `ConfirmDeposit`:491), the withdrawal path (`WaitForCargo`:153),
  and availability query (`GetTotalCargoAvailable`:430).
- **Deposit path proven** in gas siphon: `run_siphon_worker.go:255` does reserve→`TransferCargoCommand`
  →confirm (`TransferCargo` primitive `internal/adapters/api/client.go:987`, command
  `internal/application/gas/commands/transfer_cargo.go:13`).
- **Withdrawal path proven** in manufacturing: `storage_acquire_deliver_executor.go:153` does
  `WaitForCargo`→transfer→`ConfirmTransfer`:189; discovery via
  `StorageSourceFinder.FindRunningOperationForGood` (`storage_source_finder.go:47`).
- **RULINGS #2 restart model:** the coordinator is IN-MEMORY but survives restart because
  `StorageRecoveryService` reloads running `storage_operations` rows and re-reads each storage
  ship's LIVE cargo from the API (`recovery.go:116-135`). Source of truth = physical ship cargo +
  a persisted operation row. No new cargo table needed.
- **Demand signal half-exists.** `HistoryRepository.ContractsStats(...).ByGood`
  (`internal/adapters/persistence/history_repository.go:261-357`, field :52) already yields
  per-good CONTRACT FREQUENCY (count of contracts needing each good), era-scoped by player_id;
  contracts are never scrubbed (`era_repository.go:122-132` omits contracts). **Gap:** `ByGood` is
  a frequency count, NOT a units distribution — units live in `DeliveriesJSON`
  (`models.go:208`), unmarshaled in Go, no SQL good-filter.
- **No global home anchor.** HQ is stored but unused for routing
  (`register_player.go:134` → `player.Metadata["headquarters"]`, only read for CLI display
  `cli/player.go:263`). "Home" today is emergent = a ship's current system
  (`run_tour_coordinator.go:737`).

**THE decisive constraint (single-system withdrawal):** withdrawal is a physical ship→ship
`TransferCargo` at the storage ship's waypoint; the contract worker must fly there in-system
(RULINGS #14). So pre-positioned stock ONLY helps a contract whose **delivery system == the
storage system**. Pre-positioning targets ONE home system in v1; only home-system contracts
benefit. This is by design, not a limitation to fix.

## 1. Minimal v1 (delivers the Admiral's intent)

One dedicated storage hull parked at a chosen HOME waypoint, holding a whitelist of goods that
contract history proves we repeatedly need and that are cheap in a reachable foreign system. The
EXISTING trade/tour engine buys those goods cheap cross-system and DEPOSITS them into the
warehouse (a new sink leg). Contract workers, for home-system contracts, source INVENTORY-FIRST
at zero ask before any market buy. A fail-closed economics guard decides WHETHER to stock.

**In scope v1:** demand miner (frequency + units, home-system-scoped, current-era prices);
warehouse storage-op seam; haul-to-storage deposit leg (pseudo-sink); inventory-first sourcing
with reservation; deposit-side economics guard.

**Deferred (explicit):** multi-system warehouses; the "home never sells the good at all"
unsourceable-contract trigger (highest value but SPECULATIVE on price → violates #6/#4 spirit
without a known home ask — needs its own ruling); dynamic capital-carry pricing (v1 uses a
static min-savings-margin floor + a spend cap); auto-provisioning/buying a storage hull (v1
dedicates an existing parked hull, RULINGS #6/#7); idle-arb PREFERENCE for contract-recurrent
goods on hub-local legs (nice-to-have layer on top of the deposit leg).

## 2. Storage seam decision (with evidence)

**Reuse main's `StorageShip`/`StorageCoordinator` machinery; do NOT revive the parked sp-8yf1
branch; add ONE small warehouse constructor.**

- Rejected — revive parked sp-8yf1 (`d4a7866`, branch `shipwright/sp-8yf1`): it builds
  `STORAGE_COLLECT_SELL` (gas DISPOSITION — collect from storage and SELL at market), which is
  the OPPOSITE data flow (out of storage → market) and is NOT on main. Its `GasDispositionProducer`
  (threshold + dedup + idle-hauler decision engine) is a useful STRUCTURAL PRECEDENT for our
  pre-positioning producer, but we do not depend on the branch.
- The blocker: `NewStorageOperation` requires ≥1 extractor ship (`operation.go:77-79`). A warehouse
  has ZERO extractors — cargo arrives from a HAULER (tour leg), not an extractor. So reuse needs a
  `NewWarehouseOperation` constructor (OperationTypeCustom `operation.go:21`, 0 extractors, ≥1
  storage ship, supportedGoods = the whitelist) OR relaxing the extractor invariant for CUSTOM.
  Everything downstream (`StorageShip`, coordinator, recovery, `StorageSourceFinder`,
  `storage_operations` persistence, RULINGS #2 reconstruction) then works UNCHANGED.
- This is the cleanest seam: no facility model, no new persistence table, no new transfer
  primitive — the warehouse is a parked hull whose cargo IS the inventory, deposited and withdrawn
  by the two already-proven protocols.

## 3. Economics guard sketch (#4-compliant, fail CLOSED)

Guard lives on the DEPOSIT (stock) decision, not the withdrawal. Withdrawal from inventory is
always correct (paid-for = zero marginal ask), subject only to reservation + never-skip fallthrough.

Stock good G only when ALL are known and true (any unknown → do NOT stock; #4):
- `recurrence_weight(G)` from `ContractsStats().ByGood` ≥ `minRecurrence` (measured, never
  speculative — RULINGS #6). Requires per-good UNITS too (miner gap, Lane A).
- `home_ask(G)` KNOWN (cheapest in-home-system ask) AND `foreign_ask(G)` KNOWN (cheapest reachable
  foreign ask via `FindCheapestMarketsSellingAllSystems`). Unknown either → fail closed, skip.
- `savings = (home_ask − foreign_ask)` > 0 AND `savings × expected_units > minMarginFloor`
  (static floor stands in for capital-carry pricing in v1).
- `warehouse_capital_outstanding + foreign_ask × units ≤ spendCap` (a new pre-positioning spend
  cap sibling to sp-w3he's cross-container cap; must not touch the non-tunable 50k reserve #4/#5).

**Haul opportunity cost is EMERGENT, not a separate guard.** The deposit leg is offered to the
tour solver with a synthetic bid = `home_ask` (so the solver's `margin = home_ask − foreign_ask`
= the real savings, `tour_solver.py:282`). If a normal arb SELL leg is more profitable, the
solver picks that instead — the solver's own profit maximization prices the opportunity cost.
We only owe an HONEST pseudo-price (discounted for carry/uncertainty to stay fail-closed).

## 4. Build lanes (ordered, independently gateable)

**Lane B — Warehouse storage seam  [RISKIEST — load-bearing, RULINGS #2]**
Files: `internal/domain/storage/operation.go` (add `NewWarehouseOperation` / relax extractor
invariant for CUSTOM), `internal/application/storage/recovery.go` (ensure the owning coordinator
invokes recovery so cargo reconstructs on boot), a coordinator that owns the warehouse op +
registers the storage ship. Acceptance: a warehouse op persists a `storage_operations` row;
after a simulated restart its cargo is reconstructed from the ship API and re-registered
(RULINGS #2); a deposit→withdraw round-trip via the coordinator succeeds in an integration test.
Riskiest because it touches aggregate invariants, restart resilience, and a physically dedicated
hull (RULINGS #7 ownership).

**Lane A — Demand miner (candidate list)**  [parallel with B]
Files: extend `HistoryRepository.ContractsStats` (or a new `demand_miner.go` in
`internal/application/trading`) to emit per-good FREQUENCY + expected UNITS (unmarshal
`DeliveriesJSON`), filtered to the HOME system's delivery destinations, joined against
`FindCheapestMarketsSellingAllSystems` for foreign ask + `FindCheapestMarketSelling` for home
ask. Output: ranked `[good, recurrence, expected_units, home_ask, foreign_ask+waypoint,
projected_savings]`, fail-closed rows dropped. Acceptance: given seeded contract history +
market_data, returns the correct ranked home-system candidates with savings; drops goods with
unknown home OR foreign ask; respects `minRecurrence`.

**Lane C — Haul-to-storage deposit leg (pseudo-sink)**  [needs A + B]
Files (cross-language): `services/routing-service/utils/tour_solver.py` (three spots — the
`bid>0` pairing gate `:249`, the sell-pool quote `:233`, the margin `:282` — accept a synthetic
storage sink with bid = `home_ask`), `handlers/tour_handler.py`, `pkg/proto/routing/routing.proto`
(new trade/leg kind, mirrors bc27's `held_liquidation` field addition), `grpc_routing_client.go`,
`internal/domain/routing/tour.go` (leg kind — today only `TourTrade.IsBuy` bool `:72`),
`internal/application/trading/commands/run_tour_coordinator.go` (`executeSell` branches to a
deposit primitive reusing siphon `reserve→TransferCargo→ConfirmDeposit`; inject `StorageCoordinator`;
BYPASS the live-price re-verify `:572` for storage legs — no live bid exists). Interacts with
bc27 held_liquidation split (a deposit is the structural mirror: buy-with-no-sell vs
sell-with-no-buy). Acceptance: solver emits a deposit leg when savings justify it and NOT when a
better arb sell exists; executor deposits into the warehouse; no live-price crash on the sink leg.

**Lane D — Inventory-first sourcing + withdrawal**  [needs B]
Files: `sourcing_optimizer.go` `PlanDeliverySourcing` (before the in-system market candidate at
`:183`, check `StorageSourceFinder` for a running warehouse op IN the delivery system supporting
the good with `GetTotalCargoAvailable > 0` → emit a zero-ask `SourcingPlan` with a new
`Source=inventory` marker + `Market = storage waypoint`, `UnitAsk = 0`); add a delivery-system
filter to `StorageSourceFinder` (`storage_source_finder.go:47`); `run_fleet_coordinator.go` around
`:401` branches: inventory plan → fly to storage waypoint + withdraw (`WaitForCargo`→transfer→
`ConfirmTransfer`, mirror manufacturing) instead of market buy. Acceptance: a home-system contract
for a stocked good sources from inventory at zero ask; when inventory is exhausted MID-RUN it
falls through to the market candidate unchanged (never-skip, RULINGS #1); a reservation prevents
two contracts double-claiming the same units.

Ordering: **B (∥ A) → C, D in parallel.** C and D both consume B's warehouse; C also needs A's
candidate list to know WHAT to haul; D needs A only indirectly (it consumes whatever B holds).

## 5. Open questions (need Admiral/captain ruling before C/D dispatch)

1. **Home/storage anchor:** default to stored HQ metadata (`register_player.go:134`) as the home
   system, overridable by a `--storage-waypoint`/`--home-system` flag (RULINGS #5)? Confirm the
   anchor — there is no global home today.
2. **Storage hull:** v1 dedicates ONE existing parked hull as the warehouse (pinned, no purchase,
   RULINGS #6/#7) — confirm, and confirm which hull class / capacity target.
3. **Goods whitelist:** fully auto from the miner (top-N recurrent + cheap-cross-system, gated by
   `minRecurrence`), or an Admiral-approved allowlist on top? Recommend auto + a max-goods cap.
4. **Pre-positioning capital budget:** what ceiling on credits tied up in warehouse inventory
   (the `spendCap` in §3), and its relation to the 50k reserve and sp-w3he cross-container cap?
5. **"Home never sells the good" case:** the highest-value scenario (home-system contracts for a
   good no home market sells are currently un-sourceable in-system and stall) but SPECULATIVE on
   price. In scope for v1 as a separate trigger, or deferred to a v2 with its own ruling?

Confidence: HIGH on the seam decision, the sourcing hook, and the single-system constraint (all
verified on main). MEDIUM on the miner units-aggregation cost (JSON unmarshal, no SQL filter) and
on Lane C's cross-language solver change + live-price bypass (the second-riskiest work).

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
FLEET-ARCHITECT REFUTE — sp-5cyp (buy 1-2 arb light haulers ~250k ea). Treasury 1.17M, era ends ~62h.

VERDICT: QUALIFIED REFUTE. This is NOT a structural NO — do not lump it with the dead 5x buys. The era clock FAVORS a fast-payback hull (2-3h payback over ~62h remaining = ~20x if the payback is real), and demand is partly certified (plating +28.5k/pass, bio +35.3k/pass are PROVEN passes, not projections). Refuting on the era-reset template here would be wrong. But the 1-2-as-framed overstates in three measurable ways. Net: route idle capacity FIRST (zero capital), then at most ONE fast light — not two.

THE THREE SEAMS:

(1) "MORE legs than hulls" undercounts IDLE capacity — the binder may be ASSIGNMENT, not hull-count. The case counts only "free arb-dedicated hulls" (heavy on loop, 12/B contested) and ignores idle hull-HOURS: T3 is unassigned and ~half the fleet sits docked-idle. Any idle hull with hold can fly these legs. So before 250k moves, route idle hulls + measure what 1z2h idle-arb ALREADY harvests on these four named legs. This is the captain's own strongest angle and it is correct: if idle-arb already skims them, the dedicated hull captures the DELTA, not the full +75-140k/hr — and the 2-3h payback (computed on 100% greenfield capture) stretches 2-3x. DEMAND: current idle-arb realized capture on lab/adv_circ/plating/bio before buying.

(2) +75-140k/hr is a GREENFIELD CEILING; tranche/sink-crush at 3-4 visits/hr is unmodeled. Per-pass margin IS evidenced (+28.5k/+35.3k proven); the 3-4 passes/hr FREQUENCY and its SUSTAIN are the assumptions. "lab +3,710x20" is a 20-unit tranche — 3-4 passes/hr on the same sink depress its bid and exhaust the tranche (absorption ~42u/tick baseline). ONE flyer rotating four legs ~= 1 visit/leg/hr = gentle, tranches replenish. TWO flyers, or one flyer concentrating the best leg, crush the very legs that justify them. DEMAND: per-leg sink depth + margin-decay-vs-cadence. Until measured, +75-140k/hr is a ceiling, not a run-rate.

(3) Cap at ONE, and a FAST LIGHT — not two, not a heavy. Rule-3 line: 1 @ 250k = 21% (inside); 2 @ 500k = 43% (breaches 25%). Two also multiplies crush on a fixed four-leg board. One-shot arb legs are tranche-limited (~20u), so CYCLE TIME (speed + dock overhead) binds, NOT hold — a fast light dominates a heavy for this duty. Do NOT conflate with sp-n9vb's bulk-loop heavy (360 cargo is dead weight on a 20u tranche; different job).

DECISION RULE for the captain (actionable within the hour):
- Route idle hulls (T3 + docked-idle) onto the four legs and read what 1z2h idle-arb captures. If idle capacity covers the board -> buy 0.
- If a gap survives routing -> buy EXACTLY ONE fast light, rotate all four legs (tranche-safe).
- Do NOT buy two (breaches 25% + crush risk on a four-leg board).
- Treat +75-140k/hr as a ceiling; the proven per-pass margins are real, the frequency/sustain is not yet.

THREAD LINKAGE (flag, not a block): these are TRADING legs. If the Admiral's still-pending 5x objection is that trading is near a ceiling, that REINFORCES "route idle before buying." But the fast payback means this tactical buy does not require resolving the trading-vs-contracts steer first — it stands on its own leg-specific evidence. Not closing sp-5cyp.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <10k | 135 | 754k | +393k | +2,911 | 11,939/hr | **46.0%** | **2.4%** |

**Confidence.** HIGH on decomposition, class table, idle math (full-population ledger, exact linkage). MEDIUM on lever $/hr estimates (serial-pipeline arithmetic, not simulation). Honest gap: refuel costs sit between cycles and are excluded from per-contract nets (~2-3% of gross fleet-wide).

title: Payload-vs-OpenAPI validation for outbound SpaceTraders API requests (sp-423c check c)
description:
sp-423c ('Gate hardening: catch real-API-contract mismatches pre-deploy') specified three checks in priority order: (a) handler-registration completeness, (b) real API error-shape tests, (c) payload-vs-OpenAPI validation of outbound request payloads.

(a) and (b) shipped in sp-423c itself. (c) was explicitly deferred per team-lead's stated fallback: "If too big, file a follow-up bead and ship (a)+(b)."

Investigation confirmed: no OpenAPI/Swagger spec file exists anywhere in this repo (searched for *openapi*, *swagger*, and any YAML containing an `openapi:` key — zero hits). SpaceTraders does publish a public OpenAPI spec (https://spacetraders.stoplight.io / https://github.com/SpaceTradersAPI/api-docs) that could be vendored in.

Scope for this follow-up:
1. Vendor or fetch the official SpaceTraders OpenAPI spec into the repo (e.g. api/openapi.yaml), with a documented refresh process (it may drift from the live API over time).
2. Build a validation layer (likely in internal/adapters/api, at the client.go request-construction boundary) that validates outbound request payloads against the spec's schema before sending — at minimum in tests/CI, ideally as an optional runtime guard behind a debug flag.
3. Acceptance: a deliberately mis-keyed payload (wrong field name, wrong type, missing required field) fails a test/gate check BEFORE hitting the real API.

This closes the last of the three real-API-contract mismatch classes the gate-hardening epic targeted; (a) and (b) already catch unregistered handlers and known error shapes, but nothing today catches "we're sending the API a payload it will reject" until LIVE acceptance.

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
FLEET-ARCHITECT — initial refute framing for the 20x scaling path (sp-pwwe). Filed at rollover (~52h): this is the ARCHITECTURAL FRAMING + MEASUREMENT PLAN + DEPENDENCY MAP. The quantified numbers (per-hull req/s, hulls-to-ceiling, yard price deltas) are the NEXT session's first task — see HANDOFF. Not closing; captain's to close.

BOTTOM LINE (framing): For a 20x target inside a 3.5-day era, the binding constraint is almost certainly the SHARED API request budget, not capital and not hull count. Size hull buys to the MEASURED req/s ceiling, not to a lane count alone — this is the absorption law transposed to the request layer. Two of the three walls (API, era clock) cap 20x THIS era hard; absorption is the only wall that scales on the right timescale, and it scales by FEEDING sinks, not by buying hulls.

(a) HULL-BUY SEQUENCING vs API CEILING — the refute has teeth:
- The ceiling binds on SHARED daemon req/s. The dominant consumer is per-ship STATUS POLLING, not transactions — so per-hull req/s is set by poll cadence x hull count and saturates independently of how profitable each lane is.
- hulls_to_ceiling ~= sustained_rate_limit / per_hull_req_s. SpaceTraders' sustained limit is ~2 req/s (burst higher). If the daemon polls each ship even every ~1-2s, the ceiling binds in the single-to-low-double digits — potentially BELOW the current fleet, and far below any 20x fleet. That makes "how many more haulers" the wrong question: past the ceiling every hull gets SLOWER (429 -> crash-retry, a failure mode the captain already lists as a risk — and that mode BURNS budget, turning marginal hulls net-negative).
- MEASUREMENT (the honest ceiling number the Admiral wants): per_hull_req_s = (daemon API calls in a window) / (active-hull-seconds in that window); compare to the ~2 req/s ceiling. If we already emit req/s-vs-limit telemetry, this is a ~10-minute pull. If we do NOT (the captain's own open question), the observability IS the first deliverable — you cannot sequence buys against an unmeasured ceiling. RECOMMEND: file the observability ask (daemon request-budget utilization: req/s issued vs limit, ideally per-container) as a prerequisite to ANY hull-scaling past today's fleet. That bead gates step B.
- ARCHITECTURAL LEVER that beats buying hulls: if the ceiling is poll-dominated, poll-batching / event-driven state / 429-backoff raises the effective ceiling for ZERO capital — and survives the era reset as code. THAT is the 20x-relevant move, not more hulls.

(b) CONTRACT-LINE SCALING (does qpmi change 'contracts are the engine'?) — HELD, and here is why: this target rests on 'contracts are the biggest proven earner (+9.47M/day)', which is the corrected-attribution figure the Admiral is actively challenging (open steer on sp-w5dc / sp-f14n). I will not endorse scaling contract hulls until the Admiral resolves that. CONDITIONAL answer both ways:
  - IF Admiral confirms contracts-as-lever: qpmi's MEASURED per-hull contract-fulfillment throughput is the number that decides more-contract-hulls — and the SAME absorption law applies: scale to the measured contract-fulfillment ceiling (coordinator / API throughput), not to a hull target. The 74 ship-hr/day gap is a capacity claim to VERIFY (real and fillable?), not to buy against blind.
  - IF Admiral's objection is substantive (contracts finite / API-capped / saturating): (b) collapses — do not add contract hulls; the contract line is near its own ceiling and 20x must come from absorption-growth + trade circuits instead.

(c) YARD ARBITRAGE — the price question is second-order; TYPE is the real question:
- If a hauler pays back in a few circuits, a 10-15% yard-price delta is noise against lane throughput and the 3.5-day era clock. Do NOT sequence buys by cheapest yard.
- What WOULD matter: a novel hull TYPE at the ZC66/GQ92 yards with materially better cargo or fuel economy — that changes throughput-per-hull AND throughput-per-req/s (fewer, bigger hulls = more cargo per poll = higher effective API ceiling). That is worth wanting. Per standing rule, any novel type routes to the Admiral FIRST.
- Caveat: ZC66's six-yard inventory is 'F inbound' (not stocked yet) — a price/type sweep is premature until it lands. NEXT session: once ZC66 stocks, pull shipyard type+price across ZC66(6)/GQ92(3)/PA3(2)/home; report cheapest source of the SAME type and flag any novel type to the Admiral. Until then home @328k stands and price is not the binding variable.

CONFIDENCE: HIGH that the API request budget is the true 20x ceiling and must be measured before hull-scaling. HIGH that (b) is Admiral-gated. MEDIUM-HIGH that yard price is second-order to type. The req/s NUMBER and the yard sweep are UNMEASURED this session (rollover) — that is the handoff, not a conclusion.

HANDOFF (next session, first tasks, in order): 1) Check whether the daemon emits req/s-vs-limit telemetry; if not, file the observability bead (gates everything in (a)). 2) Compute per_hull_req_s from request logs / hull-seconds -> hulls_to_ceiling today. 3) Resolve the Admiral steer on contracts BEFORE answering (b). 4) Defer the yard sweep until ZC66 stocks. Do NOT buy ahead of the req/s measurement — the whole point of the refute is that the ceiling likely binds below where capital or sinks do.

comments.author: Andres Camacho
comments.text:
FLEET-ARCHITECT — CORRECTION to my (a) framing above. The captain's competitive intel (mail st-wisp-1s37) observationally REFUTES my "API request budget is the binding 20x ceiling" claim. Agents run 1,880-8,285 ships (MAWHRIN-SKEL 8,285, ALIEN-1 4,895, CHAMLIS 2,968, NGC38 1,880) — so the per-agent API limit does NOT bind anywhere near our scale. My error: I assumed ~2 req/s AND naive per-ship polling; thousands-ship fleets prove per-hull req/s can be driven far below that, so the API is not the wall. RETRACT "API ceiling binds below today's fleet" and the hulls_to_ceiling ~= 2/per-hull-req-s number.

WHAT RECASTS (not retracts): the real distinction is SOFTWARE ceiling, not API ceiling — at what hull count does OUR daemon's poll cadence degrade (queue latency, cache staleness)? That is a fixable code property, and it is exactly what sp-51ti (already filed by the captain) should measure: our daemon's per-hull req/s and the hull count at which cadence degrades. Poll-batching / backoff stays a valid EFFICIENCY lever, but NOT as "breaking an imminent API wall."

WHAT SURVIVES — on the captain's evidence, NOT my refuted API mechanism: the anti-bloat conclusion. Count without productivity is bloat — CHAMLIS 433k/ship vs MAWHRIN 56k/ship; WHYANDO 658M on just 62 ships (~120k/hr/ship SUSTAINED = our BURST rate). The 20x lever is per-hull SUSTAINED productivity, not hull count and not API headroom. That ties straight to our own idle hulls (TORWIND-3 unassigned, 6/11 docked idle): close the sustain-vs-burst gap on hulls we already own before buying any. Successor's revised (a) question, per captain: what fleet size does OUR daemon sustain before poll-cadence degrades (software ceiling), and what is the probe-swarm marginal cost per charted system? Measure via sp-51ti. Still not closing sp-pwwe.

- CROSS-GATE LANES AREN'T AUTONOMOUS YET: the deep sinks (PA3 vol12, GQ92 vol24) are across a gate, and ship jump has NO daemon handler — sp-n0x7 (P1) is MERGED but DEPLOY-HELD; today only the captain's manual direct-API jump crosses. A hauler bought now for a GQ92 lane is an IDLE hull until the daemon restart. In-system-only autonomous lane today = home vol6 WEAK, which one owned hauler already covers.
- LANE INFRA OVERSTATED: your snapshot claims 2 trade-route daemons (8@D40, 12@D39); at the moment I pulled operations status, ONLY trade-route-TORWIND-12 was running — TORWIND-8 showed an mfg-task, not a lane. Either it cycled or the second "proven lane" isn't actually up. Verify the second daemon is live before scaling it — you may be scaling a lane that's one container, not two.
- THE DEEP GQ92 SINK IS THE WRONG GOOD: your snapshot's deepest GQ92 absorption is MEDICINE vol80 @5.0k — 3x the component depth. But your factories make SHIP_PARTS/SHIP_PLATING, not medicine. Selling medicine at GQ92 means BUYING it cheaper somewhere first = arbitrage on the -2.96M/day TRADING line, with NO measured source spread in the books. vol80 depth is a mirage for our production: it rewards a medicine-sourcing lane we don't have, not another component hauler. If you have a cheap medicine source, THAT spread is the thing to measure — not hull count.
What flips me to BUY (exactly one): sp-n0x7 deployed AND one autonomous GQ92 circuit shows positive REALIZED margin (sink price − delivered cost − fuel) AND that circuit is absorption-starved (hull-limited, queue backing up), not price-crushed. Then buy 1 hauler for THAT lane. Not 2, not speculatively.

=== (b) REFINING_FREIGHTER 2.39M @GQ92 — REFUTED (hard defer) ===
Verdict: NO this era.
Evidence:
- Rule 3 BINDS at 25.5%; ~3.3d runway to era reset (07-12T13:00Z).
- Payback math: to break even it must net ~2.39M in ~3.3d ≈ ~725k/day from a standing start. Refining needs an INPUT feed (ore/gas → refined). Extraction is DEAD (ops: "No active gas operations"; 4 excavators parked, 0/15 cargo; plan concedes "tripwires silent"). You'd have to stand up an entire refine supply chain in <3.3d before the freighter earns its first credit.
- The plan already lists this under "NOT pursued now." I'm confirming it with the numbers: 25.5% of treasury for an unmeasured payback on a dead input chain against a 3.3d clock is the single worst risk-adjusted buy on the board.
What flips me: a LIVE refined-good sink with margin > input+fuel AND a proven ore/gas feed already moving — neither exists today.

=== (c) 4 PARKED EXCAVATORS → PA3-CORE SHUTTLES — REFUTED ===
Verdict: NO. Leave parked (or use as passive PA3 scouts only).
Evidence (live):
- They are NOT co-located with PA3. All four (TORWIND-9@KA42-A2, A@G48, C@C37, D@C37) sit in the HOME system. "PA3-core hops" first requires crossing the gate to PA3 — same manual-jump wall as (a), times four, and sp-n0x7 isn't deployed.
- Destination sink is PA3 vol12 WEAK — shallow and not growing. Four speed-9 / 15-cargo hulls (60 cargo total, glacial) feeding a weak vol12 sink is marginal throughput for real coordination cost.
- Claim/noise cost is real, not hypothetical: 8 of 20 hulls already carry 45–52h stale caches — every added coordinator claim is another stale-cache/crash surface (the sp-c2bc family). Four new slow claims into a weak sink you can't autonomously reach is negative expected value.
What flips me: excavators already at PA3 (post-jump-deploy) AND a co-located PA3 export→import pair with a live positive spread that a 15-cargo hop can clear inside one absorption tick. Absent that, they're parked capital best left parked.

=== (d) SHIP_EXPLORER 850k WARP — REFUTED (era-boundary write-off) ===
Verdict: NO — neither this-era nor next-era.
Evidence:
- Warp is a nav mode even less exercised than jump. sp-n0x7 just proved the JUMP executor was never registered ("never-exercised subsystem missing executor" doctrine). High risk the WARP handler hits the identical wall — you'd buy an 850k hull the daemon can't drive. (Flagged as risk, not verified — but the jump precedent is exactly this class.)
- Runway kills the this-era case: an explorer's payoff is scout→find richer sink→exploit. That cycle cannot complete in ~3.3d with warp cooldowns.
- "Next-era bootstrap" is a category error: the weekly reset (07-12T13:00Z) rebuilds the universe — hulls do NOT persist (your own plan gates every buy on payback-BEFORE-era-end for exactly this reason). An explorer bought now is gone at reset.
- YOU'RE ALREADY SCOUTING THE UNKNOWNS FOR 26k, NOT 850k: your snapshot shows satellites TORWIND-13+14 crawling to the PA3 gate (B10D) toward the 3 new unknowns (BG81/UQ16/ZC66). Those are GATE-reachable — a ~26k satellite reads them; you do NOT need an 850k warp hull for gate-linked systems. Warp only buys reach to NON-gate-linked systems, which is a next-era concern, and next-era doesn't inherit this hull. So the explorer pays 33x a satellite's price for a capability that's either redundant (gate unknowns already being scouted) or unusable (warp handler unproven + reset wipe).
What flips me: nothing this era. If warp-scouting is wanted, it belongs at the START of an era with full runway AND after the warp executor is verified live — file it as an era-2 opening move, not a day-3.3 buy.

=== THE REFRAME (the actual 5x lever) ===
Every target above feeds the -2.96M/day TRADING line. The +14.53M/day line is CONTRACTS. You cannot 5x a negative line; the target (2.5-3M/hr) lives on the contract line. The high-value composition question is NOT "how many trade haulers" — it is: what is the contract engine's throughput ceiling, and does it lift once sp-n0x7 lets contract goods reach cross-gate delivery points? Saturate owned idle hulls onto contract/mfg-for-contract first (free), deploy sp-n0x7, measure ONE autonomous cross-gate circuit, THEN buy to that single proven lane. That sequence reaches for 5x without adding idle hulls to a sink-capped, negative-margin trade line.

=== CONFIDENCE ===
HIGH: (b) defer, (c) no, trading-line-is-negative, absorption ceiling ~42/tick, owned pool unsaturated, cross-gate is manual-only today. HIGH: (d) is an era-boundary write-off. MEDIUM-HIGH: (a) — one GQ92 hauler MAY pay post-deploy; I'm refuting the timing and the count (2→at most 1, gated), not the existence of a lane. MEDIUM: the exact split of TRADING_COSTS between contract-COGS and loss-making arbitrage — resolve with a per-lane/per-activity P&L (recommend to trade-analyst); either way it does not justify buying ahead of measurement.

=== WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE WHOLE ANSWER ===
- sp-n0x7 deploys AND an autonomous GQ92 circuit posts positive realized margin + absorption-starvation → buy 1 GQ92 hauler (only).
- Per-lane P&L isolates a specific trade lane that is genuinely profitable and hull-limited (not sink-limited) → targeted single buy on THAT lane.
- Contract engine proven to scale with added fulfillment hulls (multi-ship B+1 already hints at this) → that, not trade haulers, is where capital should go.
- A live refined-good sink + a moving ore/gas feed → re-open the freighter case (still watch the 25% line).

=== DATA PROVENANCE ===
LIVE this session from gobot/: fleet roster+positions+cache-ages (ship list p2), ops containers (operations status), treasury 9,357,965 (player info), ledger cash-flow 07-08→09 (--player-id 2), markets home KA42-A2 / PA3-DF9E / GQ92-H48, shipyard KA42-A2 prices, universe/era clock, sp-n0x7 status. PLAN-GIVEN (yards read empty — no co-located ship to rescan, so NOT live-reverified): REFINING_FREIGHTER 2.39M, EXPLORER 850k. INFERENCE: warp-handler-missing risk (from jump precedent + doctrine), hull-non-persistence across reset (from era-reset history + plan's own payback-before-era-end gate).

title: DECISION: buy 2× SHIP_PROBE at PA3-XE3X (22,645 ea) to parallelize phase-2 sweep
description: refutation: sought from trade-analyst (fire-and-forget per hard rule 3 — ANY hull purchase). SNAPSHOT at ask (2026-07-09 00:28Z): treasury 8.69M; fleet 18 (8 haulers+1 cmd on contract/mfg engines, 5 satellites [2,4,5 home tours; E in X1-GQ92, F in X1-PA3 post-jump], 4 excavators parked); era ends 07-12T13:00Z, no new capital after ~day 5 (~07-10). CASE: 45.3k total (0.5% treasury) buys 2 probes AT PA3-XE3X (F present now); PA3 core is co-located (yard+4 moon markets same coords) → new probes sweep PA3 instantly while F advances to DF9E yard; accelerates route-commitment decision that gates hauler deployment into new systems. GQ92+PA3 both open+alive (GQ92: 12 mkts/3 yards; PA3: dense core, SHIP_PARTS import pays 15.6k SCARCE). REFUTE ANGLES for analyst: (a) is sweep speed actually the binder vs day-5 clock? (b) probe count vs jump-cadence (onward jumps need gate return — new probes are system-LOCAL only)? (c) anything in PA3 worth hauler commitment at all, or is GQ92 the real prize and PA3 probes waste? NOVEL HULLS (separate, NOT buying without Admiral): GQ92-A2 sells SHIP_EXPLORER 850k (warp frame — graph-independent) + SHIP_REFINING_FREIGHTER 2.39M (>25% treasury → mandatory consult if pursued).
notes:
TRADE-ANALYST REFUTATION + LANE RANKING (consult sp-j9nb) — 2026-07-09 ~00:45Z

**FIRST, A DATA CORRECTION THAT GOVERNS EVERYTHING BELOW.** The consult's headline numbers are ASK-side (SELL col), not bids: PA3-XE3X pays 7,738 for SHIP_PARTS (not 15.6k) and 7,238 for SHIP_PLATING (not 14.6k); GQ92-A1 pays 5,026 for MEDICINE (not 10.2k) and 4,093 for CLOTHING (not 8.6k). Same 2x column trap you corrected in me on 07-07. The cross-gate case SURVIVES the correction — but on DEPTH (vol 12-80 vs home's vol 6) and two-sided loading, not on price. Any $/hr projection built on the ask-side reads is 2x hot; cross-gate bids for components are actually slightly BELOW home's (A2 home pays 7,976 for parts vs XE3X 7,738).

**Recommendation (refutation verdict): REFUTED as specified, approved as redirected.** The 45k is noise (0.5%); the placement is wrong. PA3's sweep is effectively DONE — `market list` shows PA3 has 3 markets, all read, all being refreshed minutes-fresh by probe F, and the bead's own premise says the core is co-located (F reads it with zero travel). The real gap is GQ92: 2 of ~12 markets read, one probe (E), 3 unexplored yards — and GQ92 is where this ranking could still CHANGE (its circuit currently returns EMPTY; 10 unread markets could hide the return cargo). Redirect, actionable post-purchase since you proceeded: hop both new probes toward GQ92 (gate return costs satellite time, which is free — they have nothing to do in a 3-market system), or hop one and park one at XE3X as lane-freshness for the committed circuit. Better still if E confirms any GQ92 yard sells probes ~23k: buy the sweep capacity THERE next time.

**Refute angles answered.** (a) Sweep speed is NOT the binder — this entire ranking was computed from EXISTING cache; the hauler decision is ripe now and gated by the day-5 clock and transit time, not reads. (b) Correct and it bites: PA3-bought probes are system-local; if GQ92 is the prize they're stranded 45k sensors in a 3-market system with 3.5 days left. (c) PA3 IS worth hauler commitment — but for reasons the snapshot missed (FF4B, below), not the ask-side bids it cited.

**LANE RANKING (realized margin/u × per-visit depth × leg utilization; all reads ≤25m, fuel confirmed 68-72 vol 360-720 at ALL 5 new-system markets — fuel risk is dead):**

1. **Two-sided PA3 circuit: home D40/D39 components OUT, FF4B clothing BACK. ~410k gross per 80-cargo round trip.** Outbound: buy PLATING D40 ask 4,462 / PARTS D39 ask 4,576 (vol 15 each, MODERATE — recovered), sell XE3X (7,238/7,738, vol 12) + DF9E (6,632/6,737, vol 12) ≈ +2.8k/u avg × 80 ≈ 225k. Return: buy CLOTHING at PA3-FF4B ask 2,929 (HIGH, vol 40), sell home A1 5,235 / J56 5,188 (vol 20) ≈ +2.3k/u × 80 ≈ 184k. The return leg alone nearly matches the outbound — an empty-return gate run wastes half the circuit.
2. **Intra-PA3 shuttle: FF4B plating ask 3,925 (HIGH, vol 12) → XE3X bid 7,238 / DF9E 6,632.** +2.7-3.3k/u with ZERO gate transit, and it does NOT touch home export supply. ~75-100k per short local circuit. This is what a PA3-committed hauler does between gate runs while bids recover — and it's why PA3 commitment compounds. (New find: FF4B undercuts home D40 as a plating source.)
3. **GQ92 one-way (until its sweep fills in): home D39 MEDICINE ask 3,217 + PARTS/PLATING → A1 MEDICINE bid 5,026 at VOL 80 (full hold, single tranche, zero crush) + A2 components 7,263/6,955 at vol 24/33.** ≈ 200k outbound, return empty ≈ 200k/round-trip. D39 exports BOTH medicine and parts — one dock loads both. Rises to #1 if E's sweep finds a return cargo.
4. **Home-only new lanes from the A1 read — deployable TODAY, zero gate risk: D39 MEDICINE → KA42-A1 bid 5,201 (+1,984/u, vol 20/20) and K80 CLOTHING 3,421 → A1 5,235 / J56 5,188 (+~1.8k/u, vol 43→20).** ~150k per short home circuit on idle gaps. Nobody is serving these.
5. **SKIP: K80 clothing → GQ92-A1 (+672/u)** — dominated on both ends (FF4B sources at 2,929; home A1 pays 5,235 vs GQ92's 4,093).

**Cannibalization guard:** cross-gate component draw hits the SAME D39/D40 exports the 4 mfg workers buy, and home import bids (7.5-8k) exceed cross-gate bids — home mfg is still the better sell PER UNIT; cross-gate wins on depth per visit. So do NOT add net new draw on D39/D40: either re-route one mfg worker's volume through the gate (same draw, deeper sinks, no home bid-crush), or source plating at FF4B and leave home exports alone. The D39 MEDICINE line is new, uncontested draw — pure addition.

**Sizing honesty:** transit times are yours (I have no distance verb). Per-visit depth caps concurrent haulers: vol-12 XE3X/DF9E sinks tolerate ~1 hauler on PA3 components; vol 24-33 GQ92 sinks ~1-2. If a home⇄PA3 round trip exceeds ~4h, lane #1's $/hr drops under lane #4 home alternatives — check against your distance data before committing more than one hull.

**Confidence.** HIGH on the refutation (cache coverage is a fact; co-location is the bead's own premise) and on ranking ORDER. MEDIUM on absolute $/round-trip (transit + realized slippage on vol-12 sinks unmeasured). The column-semantics correction is not a confidence item; it's arithmetic.

**What would change my mind.**
- E's GQ92 sweep (10 unread markets) surfaces a return cargo ≥2k/u margin → GQ92 circuit takes #1; probe placement redirect becomes even more right.
- Gate topology permits direct PA3→GQ92 transit → merge #1+#3 into one grand loop (home → GQ92 sell → PA3 FF4B reload → home); re-consult for re-rank.
- Round-trip transit > ~4h home⇄PA3 → demote #1 under #4; commit zero dedicated cross-gate hulls, serve with occasional runs.
- First real circuit realizes <60% of projected margin (vol-12 crush worse than modeled) → cap PA3 at the intra-system shuttle (#2) only.

Footnote, unasked: GQ92-A2's SHIP_EXPLORER at 850k is 9.8% of treasury — rule-3-clean if the Admiral ever wants warp (graph-independent exploration changes next-era bootstrap economics). Flagging existence only; not my call and era clock argues against.

OUTCOME: refutation ACCEPTED in full. Ask/bid inversion acknowledged (my reads quoted purchasePrice as payout; real bids = sellPrice, ~half). Actions: (1) 13+14 redirected to PA3 gate B10D — 13 jump-tests the 3 NEW connections (B10D fans to 6: home, AF2/QJ93 [under constr], BG81/UQ16/ZC66 [unknown]); 14 continues via home gate → GQ92 second sensor. (2) trade-route daemon launched TORWIND-8 @ home (analyst lane-#4 class) — doubles as the long-awaited engine acceptance run. (3) Cross-gate hauler commitment DEFERRED to measured transit + sp-n0x7 (jump handler) — hand-fly only if the fix slips past ~07-10 morning. (4) Premise correction sent back: AD1F = 4th PA3 market (ADV_CIRCUITRY imp 7,185; AI_MAINFRAMES exp). Close when trade-route circuit result is in.

title: wake watch: one-shot per-ship/per-container wake predicates (ship arrival, container terminal) with built-in deadline
description: Admiral-proposed in-chat 2026-07-09 ~00:15Z. GAP: wake vocabulary is time (--next-wake-at), treasury (--credits-above/below), and event-TYPE interrupts — no way to say 'wake me when TORWIND-E arrives'. Type-level workflow.finished is unusable (fires tens/hr fleet-wide); captain must ETA-pin timestamps manually (brittle: ETA drift, multi-segment routes, and LOST arrival events silently strand the wake — genus species 2). PROPOSAL: one-shot watches checked in the supervisor event path before type filtering: 'captain wake watch add ship:<SYM>:arrival [--by +20m]' / 'wake watch add container:<ID>:terminal [--by ...]' / 'wake watch list|clear'. Semantics: fires a wake-mail on first match OR at --by deadline (whichever first, tagged which), then auto-disarms. Watches are operational ephemera — keep them OUT of wake-set replace semantics (separate subcommand family; recommendation over folding into wake set). Motivating case: 2 probes on ~15min crawls to new-system shipyards; had to curl /nav for ETAs and pin heartbeat +18m. DESIGN NOTE: --by deadline is mandatory-default (e.g. ETA+25%) so every evented wait is deadline'd at the sensing layer too. Acceptance: (1) watch add ship:X:arrival + wake show/watch list shows it armed; (2) arrival event triggers wake-mail within one supervisor tick, watch auto-clears; (3) event lost → deadline fires the wake, tagged deadline-fired; (4) standing policy (heartbeat/credits/interrupt-types) untouched by watch add/fire; multiple watches coexist. TIER-3: supervisor/watchkeeper surface — Admiral sign-off required before code (bd human flagged; Admiral proposed the capability in-chat, this bead is the formal spec gate).
notes: DEPLOYED (watchkeeper pid 43421, CLI installed; daemon untouched): merged 5dd7f28 verified 10 files +977/-7. title: Extend stale-claim reconciliation to TERMINAL-state owners (COMPLETED/FAILED/STOPPED) - 3rd orphan-claim variant pins ships
description: Captain st-wisp-9i32 (2026-07-08). title: captain-gate -provision reverts regenerated proto (daemon.pb.go) in the worktree — breaks build for any proto-changing bead
description: Discovered landing sp-q02m (2026-07-08). captain-gate -provision ('copy gitignored build artifacts into the worktree before gating') REVERTS the worktree's tracked, freshly-regenerated pkg/proto/daemon/daemon.pb.go + daemon.proto back to main's stale version (empirically: HEAD had InputsOnly; after 'captain-gate -provision' the worktree proto was dirty-reverted to remove it -> build failed 'GetInputsOnly undefined'; restoring from HEAD + building WITHOUT provision = green). So provision copies stale main artifacts OVER the worktree's newer tracked proto. IMPACT: ANY bead that regenerates proto (adds a daemon RPC field) will FAIL the gate under the captain's autonomous pipeline (which always uses -provision -merge) until its own change is on main — a chicken/egg that strands proto features. Note: ezar's squashMergeClean merges branch^{tree} (committed, correct) so a MANUAL FF-merge lands proto beads fine (how q02m was landed); the bug is purely in the -provision build-prep step clobbering tracked source. FIX: provision must copy only genuinely-gitignored artifacts (config.yaml etc.), never tracked files like daemon.pb.go — scope the copy set, or exclude tracked paths. Investigate the provision impl (cmd/captain-gate + internal/captain provision logic).
notes:
CORROBORATION (2026-07-08): bit a SECOND real bead. Landing sp-ezz9 (construction --min-supply — regenerates daemon.pb.go), captain-gate --provision clobbered the worktree's regenerated proto with main's stale copy -> spurious 'unknown field MinSupply' build error, first gate attempt FAILED. Workaround that landed it (merged 6a2c5ec): git checkout HEAD -- the two proto files, then re-gate WITHOUT --provision (wireWorktreeBeads already applied from attempt 1, so nothing lost). Now 2 hits (q02m originally, sp-ezz9 now); every proto-changing bead pays this tax. Fix scope confirmed: ProvisionWorktree (fixer.go:78-98) must skip copying a proto sub-path when the worktree already differs from repoRoot there.
Admiral APPROVED 2026-07-08 (live session): Tier-3 gate fix greenlit for build. Fix ProvisionWorktree to not clobber a worktree's regenerated proto (scope the copy to genuinely-missing/identical artifacts).

title: Consult: fleet expansion plan for 7.4M treasury - what hulls, what streams, what sequencing? (era clock 4.2d)
description: For fleet-architect, Admiral-prompted. Treasury 7.4M, capex rules trivial at these prices (hauler ~280k laddering, probe ~26k, drone ~40k). Current fleet 11: 1 command (contract pool) + 5 haulers (mfg 4-worker cap + fill + contracts overflow) + 2 siphons (parked, gas dead) + 3 probes. Question: what expansion actually RAISES $/hr given known constraints? Constraints to design against: (1) contracts API-capped at 1 active - extra contract hulls add only positioning; (2) mfg lanes measured strained at 2 concurrent sellers per lane, smart-strategy diversification helps but vol-20 lanes cap depth; (3) fill is supply-paced not hull-paced; (4) trade-route engine exists but zero-visits bug open - when fixed, idle-gap arb scales with hull count; (5) GATE opens cross-system trade in ~1-2 days - post-gate hull needs unknown (jump range, new-system market depth) - should we PRE-BUY capacity for expansion day? (6) mining consult running in parallel (trade-analyst) - if GO, drones+surveyor need hull-time. Deliverable: ranked expansion list with expected marginal $/hr each, sequencing vs the gate timeline, and what NOT to buy. Include the falsify condition per purchase per doctrine.
notes:
RANKED EXPANSION PLAN (fleet-architect) — consult sp-72es, Admiral-prompted. All data LIVE this session from gobot/ (cwd trap fixed). Bottom line up front: at 7.4M treasury money is NOT the constraint, so the answer is mostly what NOT to buy. The board's single highest-value outcome is FINISHING THE GATE, and the gate is not hull-limited — it is iron-limited.

=== KEY LIVE FINDINGS (that reframe the question) ===
- GATE (X1-KA42-I53) is 64.9% done and bottlenecked on ONE material: FAB_MATS 898/1600 (needs 702 more). ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY 400/400 and QUANTUM_STABILIZERS 1/1 are COMPLETE. So the gate = a FAB_MATS delivery problem, nothing else.
- FAB_MATS at F45 is SCARCE / RESTRICTED (buy 2036, vol 43). Its INPUT, IRON, is also SCARCE at F45 (buy 157, vol 60). The FAB_MATS->gate pipeline is SUPPLY-capped (fabricator starved of iron), NOT hull-capped.
- Fleet is 13 hulls (consult said 11): 1 command + 5 haulers + 3 probes + 4 EXCAVATORS. Mining already got stood up since the consult was written. The 4 excavators (T9/A/C/D) sit at C36/C37 carrying ore with NO assignment — T-A is full 15/15 and idle. That is the gas dead-end signature again (sp-8yf1: extraction runs, storage->pickup->haul integration missing).
- Of the 5 haulers, 4 are on FAB_MATS (2 per factory, the measured strain point) and 1 on contracts. Snapshot: 3 of the 4 mfg haulers are EMPTY (0/80, docked or repositioning), only 1 loaded. That is haulers WAITING ON PRODUCTION — supply-paced, textbook. Adding haulers here adds idle hulls.
- Command ship TORWIND-1 is DOCKED idle at the gate, no assignment (the HAULER-role-only candidate-set bug benches it — captain confirmed, fix filed). Free capacity sitting unused.
- LEDGER 07-06..07-08 (~48h, measured): NET +4.23M (~88k/hr net). Breakdown: CONTRACT_REVENUE +20.8M (the profit engine); TRADING lines +20.6M rev vs -35.1M cost = NET -14.5M; FUEL -513k across 2028 txns (the sp-c2bc refuel churn). Read carefully: contracts earn, mfg/trade nets NEGATIVE as direct P&L (it is a gate-input subsidy, not profit). More mfg/trade hulls do not raise $/hr — on these numbers they lower it.
- Capex confirmed trivial: probe 25,737; shuttle 88,246; light hauler laddered 257k->291,598 (each buy raises the next price); drone ~40k / surveyor ~29k per consult. 7.4M swamps all of it.

=== RECOMMENDATION: RANKED ===

RANK 0 — FREE, DO FIRST: unbench the command ship (0 credits). TORWIND-1 idle at I53; the candidate-set bug excludes COMMAND from selection. Fixing it (already filed) returns +1 positioning hull to contracts at zero capex. No purchase should precede this. Marginal $/hr: small-positive (positioning only, contracts are 1-active-capped) but FREE, so infinite ROI. FALSIFY: if T1 unbenched and contract $/hr does not rise within a day, contracts are truly serialized 1-at-a-time and no amount of contract-side hull helps — stop optimizing that lane.

RANK 1 — HIGHEST NEW-VALUE, but it is a MINING+ENGINE call, not a hull-buy today: the iron -> FAB_MATS -> gate critical path. The gate needs 702 FAB_MATS; FAB_MATS is starved of SCARCE iron. If mined ore can be delivered/refined to F45, it directly shortens the gate ETA — the most valuable outcome on the board (gate unlocks cross-system trade). BUT: (a) this is trade-analyst's GO/NO-GO on sp-an9j, not mine to declare; (b) it is GATED ON ENGINE — the 4 existing excavators already show the dead-end (full cargo, no assignment, sp-8yf1). Recommendation: DO NOT buy any more excavators/surveyors until the ore->F45 delivery path is proven to move FAB_MATS supply off SCARCE. If trade-analyst returns GO AND shipwright confirms the storage/pickup path works, THEN the minimal iron-delivery config (fix the 4 we own first; add 1 dedicated ore-hauler only if excavator output outpaces haul) is the #1 expansion because it accelerates the gate. Marginal $/hr: potentially the highest on the board via gate-unlock, but UNMEASURED and engine-blocked. FALSIFY: if ore delivered to F45 does not lift FAB_MATS off SCARCE within a day, iron is not the true bottleneck (or the refine path is broken) — kill mining hulls, gas precedent.

RANK 2 — the ONLY defensible pre-gate purchase: 1-2 PROBES (~26k each) for post-gate market scouting. The gate opens in ~1-2 days into a new system whose market depth and jump range are UNKNOWN. You cannot spec a post-gate hauler against unknown depth — but you CAN know you will need market visibility on day one, and probe specs do not depend on the unknowns. Pre-buying probes to scout the new system the moment the gate opens is the one pre-position that is not speculation. Marginal $/hr: indirect (buys the DATA that makes every post-gate hull decision correct). FALSIFY: if the gate slips past ~3 days, even probes were early — hold them in-system scouting, no loss.

=== WHAT NOT TO BUY (the bulk of the answer) ===
- NO more mfg/FAB_MATS haulers. Lane is SCARCE/RESTRICTED, 3 of 4 haulers already idle-waiting, trade P&L net-negative. Marginal $/hr ~= 0 to negative. This is the biggest single "do not."
- NO more contract haulers. API-capped at 1 active; extra hulls = positioning only, and the command-ship unbench (Rank 0) already supplies that for free.
- NO more excavators/surveyors until the mining engine path is proven (Rank 1). Buying extraction ahead of the haul/storage integration repeats the gas mistake exactly.
- NO speculative post-gate haulers. Unknown jump range + unknown new-system depth = you would be buying hulls you cannot spec. Wait for probe data (Rank 2), then buy to measured demand.
- NO "because capex is trivial" buys. Trivial capex is the TRAP here: the constraint is hull-TIME against supply/API/lane caps, and idle hulls still consume coordinator slots, fuel churn (sp-c2bc, 2028 fuel txns/48h), and attention. Cheap does not mean free.

=== SEQUENCING vs the gate (~1-2 days) ===
1. NOW: unbench command ship (free). Freeze all hull purchases. Push engine fixes: mining storage dead-end (sp-8yf1) and fuel churn (sp-c2bc) — both tax throughput-per-hull and both scale WITH hull count, so fix before growing.
2. PRE-GATE, conditional: if trade-analyst GO on mining + engine path proven, stand up the minimal iron->F45 config to shorten the gate. Buy 1-2 scouting probes.
3. GATE OPENS: probes read the new system's markets and jump range. ONLY THEN spec post-gate haulers against real depth data.
4. POST-GATE: expansion becomes data-driven; the trade-route zero-visits fix (open bug) is what makes idle-gap arb scale with hull count — sequence hull growth AFTER that fix lands, or new hulls just idle between visits.

=== CONFIDENCE ===
HIGH on "buy almost nothing now / the constraint is supply+engine, not hulls or money" — every lane read (gate FAB_MATS-bottleneck, F45 SCARCE iron, 3/4 haulers idle, trade P&L negative) points the same way. HIGH on the free command-ship unbench. MEDIUM on the iron-subsidy being the top lever — the linkage (iron SCARCE -> FAB_MATS SCARCE -> gate) is solid, but whether mining can actually feed F45 is trade-analyst's + shipwright's to confirm; I am flagging the linkage, not declaring mining GO. MEDIUM on probe pre-buy (depends on gate actually landing in 1-2 days). CAVEAT: the trade-line -14.5M P&L is a category-level read over 48h; it could partly be gate-subsidy accounting rather than loss-making loops — recommend captain/trade-analyst run a per-lane P&L to confirm before treating mfg as a cost center, but even the charitable reading does not justify MORE mfg hulls.

=== WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND ===
- FAB_MATS or iron at F45 flips to ABUNDANT/HIGH activity -> supply cap lifts, a mfg hauler could then pay; re-rank.
- trade-analyst returns mining GO AND shipwright proves ore->F45 delivery live -> Rank 1 becomes an immediate BUY (minimal iron config), highest $/hr on the board.
- Contract API cap raised above 1 active (server change) -> contract haulers immediately worth buying; that lane is the proven profit engine.
- Per-lane P&L shows a specific mfg lane is genuinely profitable (not gate-subsidy) and depth-limited only by hulls -> targeted hauler buy on THAT lane.
- Gate finishes early / new-system depth reads deep -> post-gate haulers spec'd to that depth become the main expansion.

=== COORDINATION with trade-analyst (sp-an9j mining) ===

title: Consult: can the mfg lanes support a 3rd concurrent seller (T6), or does bid recovery cap us at 2?
description: For trade-analyst. Situation: T6 (80-cargo hauler) idle ~95min - mfg caps (max-workers 2) keep it benched while T7+T8 fly full holds. Question: raise to 3 concurrent mfg workers, or is 2 the lane-depth optimum? Evidence AGAINST 3: the 00:09 three-hull dump collapsed same-market tranches 6,357->2,963/u (marginal tranche ~break-even vs ~2,500 cost). Evidence FOR: aggregate flow stayed strong (~350k/10min); multi-market routing (A2/C37/H50/A4 imports) spreads dumps; bid recovery between visits is unmeasured - that is the real capacity number. You now have hours of market history + the market history verb. Deliverable: 2-vs-3 worker recommendation + the bid-recovery half-life for SHIP_PLATING/SHIP_PARTS at the import markets. Note: T6 also serves as instant standby for the construction dispatch fix (defect #5) - if your answer is marginal, standby wins. Answer on this bead.
notes:
TRADE-ANALYST ANSWER (consult sp-xqdk: 2 vs 3 concurrent mfg workers) — 2026-07-07 ~03:55

**Recommendation.** Keep max-workers at 2. Do NOT add T6 as a 3rd concurrent seller — the lanes are not merely capped at 2, they are showing strain AT 2. Send T6 to construction standby (the defect-#5 optionality wins even before the market evidence, and the market evidence is decisive on its own). Separately: the 2-worker engine needs routing discipline or it will grind its own margin down — tranche caps and a buy-side floor, detailed below.

**Deliverable 1 — bid-recovery half-life (import side).** Two clean dump-then-recover observations, both at H50:
- SHIP_PARTS 23:17→23:40: bid 6,104→6,482, i.e. +378 = 22.8% of the gap to its 7,764 ceiling closed in 23 min → half-life ≈ 60 min.
- SHIP_PLATING 23:40→00:00: 6,195→6,357, +162 = 12.4% of gap in 20 min → half-life ≈ 105 min.
Call it **~1–1.5h to close half the gap** toward the SCARCE-state ceiling (n=2, thin but consistent). Practical read: a crushed lane (H50 plating at 3,942 vs ~7,500 ceiling) needs ~2–3h fallow before it pays again.

**Deliverable 2 — but the binding constraint has moved to the EXPORT side.** Fresh reads (≤7m): D40 SHIP_PLATING ask 2,504→**4,169** (ABUNDANT→MODERATE, +66%); D39 SHIP_PARTS ask 2,340→**4,208** (+80%). The 23:16 D40 history shows one buying session laddering the ask 2,543→3,067 (+21%) across ~11 vol-6 tranches — and 1.25h later the ask sat HIGHER (4,169), i.e. export regeneration at WEAK activity is SLOWER than the ~1–1.5h import recovery. Two workers drawing ~71u/hr (2×80 cargo / ~2.25h circuit) have consumed the exporters' surplus faster than production refills it.

**Current lane margins (before fuel), cost basis at fresh asks:**
- Plating: C37 7,639−4,169 = +3,470 (SCARCE, bids rose ALL night — premium lane, but shallow); A2 6,723−4,169 = +2,554 (LIMITED, healthy-ish); H50 3,942−4,169 = **−227 (UNDERWATER)**.
- Parts: C37 7,711−4,208 = +3,503; A2 6,816−4,208 = +2,608; H50 5,168−4,208 = +960 (marginal).
Standup margins were ~4.4–5.4k/u; compression is 35–50% at TWO workers. The 00:09 three-hull dump realized marginal tranches at 2,963 — BELOW today's ~4.2k replacement cost. That is the 3rd-worker world in miniature: it inflates everyone's cost basis (shared vol-6 exports), crushes shared bids faster than the 1–1.5h recovery refills them, and its marginal tranches sell below replacement.

**Why the ~350k/10min aggregate is not a counter-argument:** that was liquidation of accumulated holds (a stock), not sustainable flow. Sustainable flow = absorption budget × margin ≈ 50–70u/hr (combined goods, at ≥3k margins, judging by supply-state decay under the current draw) × ~3–3.5k ≈ **160–240k/hr fleet-wide** — and that budget is already fully claimed by T7+T8. A 3rd worker adds ~+36u/hr of draw (+50%) against a budget that is arguably already exceeded; it redistributes the same absorption over more hulls while making every unit cost more.

**Advisory for the 2-worker engine (captain's call, ops-side):**
- Tranche cap: stop selling into a market once its bid < cost basis + ~1,000; cap ~12–18u per market-visit; split holds across A2+C37 rather than full-dumping one lane.
- H50 plating fallow ~2–3h (needs ~2 half-lives from 3,942 back to ~6k+); H50 parts marginal, low priority.
- Buy-side floor: pause/stagger purchases when D40/D39 ask > ~3.2k; the tranche ladder shows same-session stacking is what doubles the basis. Let exports regenerate toward ABUNDANT between visits.
- C37 is the premium lane precisely because little has landed there — treat its SCARCE depth as fragile.

**Confidence.** HIGH on "no 3rd worker" — three independent signals agree (dead H50 plating lane, export asks +66–80% with no mean-reversion inside 1.25h, marginal dump tranches below replacement cost). MEDIUM on the half-life number (n=2 observations, 60–105 min band). The T6-standby tiebreak isn't needed but is strictly dominant: at ~37% reserve with capex frozen, T6 is the only free hull, and defect-#5's fix landing "any hour" makes standby the era-mission play (construction shakedown is the era's stated de-risking goal).

**What would change my mind.**
- Probes surface ≥2 NEW import markets for plating/parts → absorption budget grows materially → re-run this consult.
- D40/D39 return to ABUNDANT with asks <3k WHILE A2+C37 bids hold >6.5k → export regen is faster than modeled → 3rd worker plausibly fits with tranche caps.
- More recovery samples put the half-life <45 min → lanes deeper than modeled.
- Fabrication goes live (plating from IRON_ORE @ ~19/u J56): cost basis decouples from D40's ask entirely, sell-side absorption alone governs, and 3 disciplined sellers could fit. That is the real unlock and it is a pipeline/shipwright question, not a headcount one.
- Defect-#5 fix lands: T6 takes its standby job and this question closes itself.

Premise-correction ack (st-wisp-c3n): absorbed — T1 was never pool-eligible (coordinator is HAULER-role-only), so my earlier "+15% from hull #2" read was hold-size, not positioning; era-1's d-37/d-78 two-LIGHT-HAULER prior stands, new falsify baseline ~490k/hr gross at day mark. None of that changes today's answer: mfg worker count is bounded by lane depth, not by hulls available.

Data hygiene: all import reads ≤23m old, export reads ≤7m, history windows 18:44→00:26. T7/T8 observed at I53 with full holds — I53 sells only FUEL/ANTIMATTER; that is a refuel stop (both at 156/600), not a mis-route.
close_reason: Answered decisively: keep 2 workers (three independent strain signals at 2 - H50 plating underwater, export asks +66-80%, marginal tranches below replacement); T6 confirmed construction-standby; bid-recovery half-life ~1-1.5h import side, exports regenerate SLOWER. Captain follow-through: (a) mfg strategy switched prefer-buy -> smart to unlock fabrication (analyst's flagged unlock; era-1-proven; decouples cost basis from strained asks and feeding factory imports regenerates exports per L58); (b) routing-discipline knobs filed as shipwright feature; (c) re-consult triggers adopted.

title: acd prime/rig-list honor ambient GC_DIR over explicit --city (precedence inverted)
description:
acd prime (and rig list) resolve the target city from the ambient GC_DIR env var and let it OVERRIDE an explicit --city flag. --city should always win.

Repro (from any shell whose GC_DIR points at a DIFFERENT city, e.g. a Claude/gc window spawned as wise mayor):
  export GC_DIR=/Users/.../cities/wise/city
  cd /Users/.../cities/spacetraders/city
  acd --city "$PWD" prime harbormaster
    => renders WISE agents, or the generic "Gas City Agent" stub for names wise lacks (harbormaster), NOT spacetraders/agents/harbormaster/prompt.template.md
  acd --city "$PWD" rig list   => lists WISE rigs
Contrast: acd --city "$PWD" bd <...> DOES honor --city (bd resolves via cwd/.beads config + prefix router), so precedence is INCONSISTENT across subcommands.

Root cause: GC_DIR (baked at gc-session spawn from ambient GC_*) outranks --city in the prime/rig-list city-resolution path. Sharp edge of the sp-ugbk identity trap: a window spawned bound to one city silently runs acd against that city after you cd elsewhere, with NO error — prime returns a stub, acd bd hits the wrong Dolt server ("database st not found on 4077"). Looks like data loss; is pure misrouting.

Expected: explicit --city overrides GC_DIR everywhere (prime, rig list, bd, mail, sling). Absent --city, cwd discovery should outrank GC_DIR, or acd should warn on GC_DIR-vs-cwd mismatch.

Workaround: env GC_DIR=<city> acd <cmd>  (or export GC_DIR before invoking).

Refs: sp-ugbk (identity trap RCA), sp-v3eh (acd binary is a non-canonical stopgap). Found 2026-07-07 while priming harbormaster from a wise-bound window (GC_SESSION_ID=wi-j8t6, GC_TEMPLATE=mayor, GC_AGENT=daenerys).
notes:
City-side companion already on file: st-hvv (P3, harbormaster launch friction — foreign session env + unrendered template + gc mail misroute). Same trap, different db. Identity root: sp-ugbk.
shipwright: agent fixing in acd source repo (branch fix/sp-hyoa-city-precedence); install held for review per sp-v3eh stopgap.
close_reason: FIXED + INSTALLED. Source repo was neither guess: derrick/city/acd-go (proven via 'go version -m' on installed binary). Commit a1fc59aa on branch fix/sp-hyoa-city-precedence (derrick repo — NOT pushed; derrick owner merges). Root cause: acd under-forwarded --city to the gc engine (gcTakeover forwarded only the raw flag; prime capture/takeover forwarded nothing) so gc's GC_DIR step won. Now: acd resolves city once (--city > ACD_CITY > cwd) and forwards it on EVERY gc invocation + loud stderr warning on GC_DIR/cwd mismatch. 6 TDD tests green. Orchestrator-verified repro: GC_DIR=wise + --city spacetraders prime harbormaster renders the real harbormaster template (was 'Gas City Agent' stub); rig list lists spacetraders + warns.
