CORRECTS A CLAIM THE LEAD MADE AND PROPAGATED: the bead and the plan both assert that the manual 'spacetraders ship warp' verb keeps ExecuteWarpRoute alive, so retirement removes 'one of two callers, not the stack'. That is FALSE for ExecuteWarpRoute specifically.

VERIFIED: the manual verb rides a DIFFERENT method. internal/application/ship/commands/navigation/warp_ship.go:16-17 declares WarpLegExecutor with the single method ExecuteWarpLeg, and calls ExecuteWarpLeg. ExecuteWarpRoute's only non-test CALL SITE in the whole tree is internal/adapters/expansion/explorer_dispatch_adapter.go:98 - which the retirement deletes. Every other hit is a comment or the declaration itself.

So after sp-mn3it lands, RouteExecutor.ExecuteWarpRoute is an exported method with zero non-test callers, and its own tests.

DECISION TAKEN FOR THE RETIREMENT LANE: keep it, and comment it HONESTLY (it currently has no caller). Deleting it would expand a retirement slice into exported-API pruning and would touch the warp stack that slice deliberately fences off. The warp LEG path, the charter, the navigator and the escape reader are all genuinely still live via the manual verb - only the multi-leg ROUTE wrapper is orphaned.

WHAT THIS BEAD DECIDES: whether the orphaned wrapper is removed, kept as a deliberate exported API, or folded into ExecuteWarpLeg. Do NOT decide it inside the retirement lane.

CAUTION: it fails closed when warpNavigator or warpEscapeReader is absent (route_executor.go:55) - that fail-closed behaviour may be depended on by the leg path. Check before removing anything.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision on ExecuteWarpRoute: removed, kept-with-rationale, or merged into the leg path. If kept, its doc comment states plainly that it has no current caller rather than naming one that does not call it.

title: Counter-staffing borrow is in-system only; a system with no lendable hull still waits on foothold
description:
sp-ifl25's staffCounters lends a docked hull to an unstaffed probe counter so a cold fleet can buy its first probe. The borrow is deliberately IN-SYSTEM ONLY: a foothold justifies walking a hull we own across a gate over multiple ticks, but a borrowed contract hauler or command frigate does not - it has its own mission and must stay takeable.

CONSEQUENCE, made explicitly rather than by omission: a system whose probe counter needs staffing but holds NO lendable hull is not helped by this pass. It still waits on the foothold broker, which needs a releasable parked probe with goods redundancy - the original cold-start problem, just pushed one system outward.

This is the bounded-borrow trade. It is probably the right default: an unbounded cross-gate borrow would take working hulls off their lanes for multi-tick flights to buy information.

WORTH REVISITING ONLY IF observed live: watch the heartbeat. Nonzero seeds_unstaged with a FLAT counters_staffed means no hull was lendable and this limitation is biting. Nonzero seeds_unstaged with nonzero counters_staffed means the escape is working and this bead can stay closed.

DO NOT pre-emptively widen the borrow to cross-gate without that evidence - the cost lands on contract and gate hauling, which are load-bearing elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: Deferred pending live evidence. Reopen only if heartbeat shows sustained nonzero seeds_unstaged against a flat counters_staffed.

title: comment-audit's own package regressed past its baseline; the sp-21gkx re-baseline forgave it
description:
cmd/comment-audit is above its own recorded baseline: 71/605 (11.74%) at the time the baseline was written, 78/615 (12.68%) as shipped. That is a 0.9pp regression in the package that IMPLEMENTS the ratchet.

INHERITED, NOT CAUSED BY sp-21gkx. The sp-21gkx lane verified this rigorously before re-baselining: it cut a detached worktree at aa737933 (the merge commit of sp-pqmsh, before sp-21gkx touched anything) and reproduced the byte-identical violation there. So the regression arrived with sp-pqmsh, which recorded a baseline that did not match the code it shipped in its own tool package.

WHY IT MATTERS. sp-21gkx step (c) re-recorded the baseline from current truth, which was the correct instruction - but re-recording forgives any outstanding regression, and that is doctrinally the one move that defeats a ratchet. It was the right call there (the alternative was prose rewriting, explicitly out of that lane's scope) but it leaves the 0.9pp banked as the new normal.

FIX: sweep roughly 7 comment lines out of cmd/comment-audit under the ENGINEERING.md section 6 rule, then re-record the baseline so the package sits at or below its original 11.74%. Small and self-contained.

MORE IMPORTANT THAN THE 7 LINES: this is evidence the ratchet can be silently defeated by the ordinary act of re-baselining. Consider whether comment-audit should refuse to write a baseline that is WORSE than the one it is replacing without an explicit override flag, so banking a regression has to be a deliberate act rather than a side effect of running the documented command.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/comment-audit package at or below 11.74%. Baseline re-recorded. comment-audit-check exits 0. Separately: a decision recorded on whether -write-baseline should refuse to bank a regression without an explicit override.

title: Yard placement bonus orders purchases only, never relocates an already-parked probe
description:
yardqueue gives placements standing on an unpriced shipyard absolute precedence over ordinary markets - but ONLY in the buy queue ordering, i.e. only when deciding which yard to BUY a probe for. Nothing ever moves a probe that is already parked somewhere else.

CONSEQUENCE. The sweep-then-settle behaviour the design implies never happens. Yard value is a step function that collapses the instant the price is read; market value is a flow that persists. If the bonus also governed relocation, a probe would price a yard, watch its bonus drop to zero, and be pulled to the next dark yard automatically - touring the yards and settling onto markets once the backlog drains, with no tour scheduler ever written. Instead a probe that prices a yard sits there forever with its bonus spent, and any further pricing happens only by luck of where the drain next buys.

Also missing: a decay term. Prices go stale, so the bonus should climb back with age-since-last-read rather than latching at zero, which would give re-pricing rotation from the same mechanism.

DELIBERATELY LOW PRIORITY. This optimises ALLOCATION of probes. It is worth little until probes actually exist and flow - see the probe-supply deadlock bead, which is the binding constraint. Note also that its value FALLS as probe supply improves: when probes are plentiful the drain can simply buy one for each dark yard and relocation matters less. It matters most in the scarce-probe regime, which is precisely the regime the deadlock fix is meant to end.

DO NOT dispatch this before the probe-supply deadlock is fixed and the expansion phase redesign direction is settled - it may be work thrown away by that redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Deferred pending probe-supply fix and expansion redesign direction. If implemented: an already-parked probe relocates to a higher-ranked dark yard, the bonus collapses on successful pricing, and a decay term restores it with staleness.

title: Homing relocations are invisible: nothing counts when a hull is moved off a settled standby slot
description:
Follow-up from the sp-lkuh9 review. The standby placement fix makes slot ORDER load-bearing in every regime, and there is no signal at all when that order changes underneath a settled fleet.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: before the fix, AssignedSlot re-sorted the retained slot set on every call, which MASKED any churn in the underlying order — a demand re-rank could reshuffle the slot list and the re-sort would flatten it back. With the re-sort gone (correctly — it was the bug), the caller order is honoured, so a re-rank in the demand-ranked central fill past the four fixed anchors now PROPAGATES into real hull movement.

CHARACTERISED, not speculative: the reviewer traced both order sources. The operator-pinned fleet hub set is returned FIRST and is deterministic (JSON array, order-preserving append). The auto path TopDeliverySlots is deterministic too (fixed anchor tuple, SliceStable with a symbol tiebreak, no map iteration anywhere in the chain). So the churn vector is NOT nondeterminism — it is a genuine demand re-rank swapping, say, slots 5 and 6, which now swaps two hulls. Bounded to 2 hulls at a fleet of 5 or more, and a fleet of 4 or fewer never reaches the fill at all.

THE ACTUAL GAP IS OBSERVABILITY: nothing counts homing relocations. A recurring low-grade shuffle would burn fuel and cycle time indefinitely and look exactly like normal homing traffic in the log. That is the same shape as several defects found today — a real effect with no counter, so its absence and its presence are indistinguishable.

REQUIRED: a counter incremented when a hull is homed to a slot DIFFERENT from the one it previously occupied, distinguishing a genuine relocation from a first placement and from a re-issue of the same target. Name it so it is obvious on a graph, e.g. standby_homing_relocations_total.

DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: freezing the demand-ranked fill. The reviewer and the implementer both judged the exposure small and preferred visibility over a pre-emptive freeze. Measure first.
acceptance_criteria: A counter increments only when a hull moves from one settled slot to a different one, and does not increment on first placement or on a repeat dispatch to the same slot. A deliberate positive control (force a slot-order swap) shows it moving.
notes: From the sp-lkuh9 review, finding 5. Related: sp-lkuh9 (the fix that made order load-bearing), sp-ia0ny (repeat dispatch to the SAME slot — a different signal that this counter must not conflate with a relocation).

title: Refuel anomalies are log-only: add counters for over-capacity fuel and clamped refuel units
description:
Follow-up from sp-l7zha (P0, merged). That fix detects two refuel anomalies and reports BOTH as structured log lines only:
  - fuel_over_capacity — the live API returned current > capacity, which is impossible; the value is clamped.
  - refuel_units_clamped — a refuel request asked for more units than the tank could take; the request is clamped at the single funnel.

There is NO metric for either. The manufacturing/refuel path has no counter, so an operator cannot see rate or trend, only individual lines in a log. That matters here specifically because ONE of the two conditions is expected to be rare-but-real (over-capacity comes from upstream API weirdness, observed three times) and the other should be effectively never (units clamped means a caller computed a bad amount) — and a silent rise in either is exactly the kind of thing a log-only signal hides.

REQUIRED: refuel_fuel_over_capacity_total and refuel_units_clamped_total, or equivalent names matching the existing collector conventions.

SCOPE NOTE, and it is why sp-l7zha did not do this: a counter here needs a NEW COLLECTOR plus daemon registration, not just a metrics call — there is no existing collector on this path to hang it off. That is real wiring, which is why it was deliberately left out of a P0 whose job was to stop a 41-minute pipeline block.

RELATED CONTEXT worth knowing: over-capacity fuel is UNREPRESENTABLE in local state. ReconstructFuel has applied min(current, capacity) since 964111cd on 2026-07-09 and NewFuel rejects it outright, so the value can only ever exist in a live API response, in flight. The counter is therefore measuring an UPSTREAM anomaly rate, not a local corruption rate — name and document it accordingly, or the next reader will hunt for a bug in our own persistence that cannot exist.
acceptance_criteria: Both anomalies increment a registered counter visible on the metrics endpoint; a deliberate positive control (force each condition in a test or against staging) shows the counter moving. The metric names or their help text make clear that over-capacity measures an UPSTREAM anomaly, not local corruption.
notes: Recommended by the sp-l7zha review, which shipped the fix as SHIP with this as the sole follow-up. Existing prod metrics live behind collectors in internal/adapters/metrics — follow whatever registration pattern the neighbouring collectors use rather than inventing one.

title: Gate roles: a WEDGED LEGACY hull adopted into DELIVERY leaves the recovery built for it — same trap as F22, reachable only through adoption
description:
RESIDUAL of final-review finding F22, deliberately left open before the phase-3 gate. Bounded and self-healing on the same terms that made F22 non-blocking; filed rather than fixed because closing it requires re-opening a twice-reviewed pure planner minutes before a squash-merge.

THE TRAP (identical blast radius to F22): a LEGACY hull that is wedged at a full hold gets adopted into DELIVERY, because adoptionTarget resolves to RoleDelivery when unpaused. Once it is a delivery hull, wedgedAtFullHold is true — factory inputs are never bill materials — so it is declined every tick, never reaches flushOnHandGateMaterials, and feedGateLegFromHold is FACTORY-ONLY. The hull is out of the fleet until the next pause borrows it back into a factory role, which empties it.

WHY THE F22 FIX DOES NOT ALSO CLOSE THIS. F22 was closed at the CALLER (gateWorkforce) by scoping the not-Idle predicate to the FACTORY role. That is provably lossless for that role: moveTarget(RoleFactory, needD, needF) returns wanted=false whenever needFactory>0, so the ONLY move a factory-role hull can ever be selected for is ->delivery, and "not Idle" is exactly "do not return to delivery".

THE SAME SEAM PROVABLY CANNOT REACH THE LEGACY CASE. Worker.Idle is DIRECTION-BLIND — PlanReallocation reads it once, with no knowledge of the move target. For a legacy hull, marking it not-Idle would block ALL moves INCLUDING THE ADOPTION-INTO-FACTORY THAT HEALS IT. So a caller-side predicate makes it strictly worse, exactly as an unscoped version of the F22 fix would have.

FIX REQUIRES THE PLANNER: gobot/internal/domain/manufacturing/gate/reallocation.go must make its Idle check DIRECTION-AWARE — consult the move target so "loaded" blocks a move TO delivery while still permitting a move TO factory. That is a signature-and-logic change to a pure planner currently carrying 67 tests and 36 mutation kills across two reviews, and it deserves its own task and review rather than a pre-gate patch.

SYMPTOM IN THE LOG: the skip renders as the reason "busy", which is a misdiagnosis — the hull is LOADED and stuck, not busy. The F22 fix added a gateWorkforce line naming the hull and its hold for the factory-role case; the legacy case will still read "busy" until this is closed.
acceptance_criteria: A wedged LEGACY hull is not adopted into DELIVERY while it still carries undelivered factory inputs, AND is still adoptable into FACTORY (which is what empties it). Pinned by a test asserting units actually transferred, not the absence of an error. The skip reason distinguishes loaded-and-stuck from busy.
notes: Found by the FinalFix lane while pressure-testing my proposed F22 fix — it falsified the unscoped version (which would have blocked the borrow, converting a self-healing degradation into a permanent one) and then established the role-scoped version as provably lossless. Related: the F22 fix itself, and sp-2scwt (feedGateLegFromHold, the hold-path recovery this trap denies the hull).

title: Order-dependent flake: TestRequestFallsBackToGlobalBudgetTrackerWhenNoneSetOnClient fails in a full-suite run, passes isolated
description:
Observed during the phase-3 gate-factory full-suite sweep. TestRequestFallsBackToGlobalBudgetTrackerWhenNoneSetOnClient FAILED in a full 'go test ./...' run but PASSES isolated x5 and at package scope x3.

The test exercises a fallback to a GLOBAL budget tracker, so the likely cause is cross-test contamination of that global by whichever package ran before it — an ordering dependency, not a defect in the code under test.

RULED OUT as the cause: any phase-3 change. 'go list -deps' shows the failing test's package has ZERO dependency on any package touched by the gate-factory work.

Recorded rather than chased because it did not reproduce in isolation. If it recurs, the fix is to give the test its own tracker instance or to reset the global in setup rather than relying on run order.
acceptance_criteria: Either the test no longer depends on global tracker state (own instance or explicit reset in setup), or the contaminating package is identified and fixed.
notes: Seen alongside a SEPARATE, definitely-environmental issue in the same run: five packages reported [build failed] from parallel build-cache corruption; they passed alone and 'go vet ./...' was already clean. That class is resolved with 'go clean -cache', not by changing code.

title: CONTRACT_WORKFLOW worker goes silent-but-heartbeating after refuel-retry exhaustion — strands hull + contract cargo, invisible to every recovery path
description:
A CONTRACT_WORKFLOW worker goes PERMANENTLY SILENT after a refuel-retry exhaustion + alternate-fuel reroute, while still holding the contract cargo AND still heartbeating. Because it heartbeats, NO recovery path sees it: it is not FAILED (so the coordinator never relaunches), not crashed (so the supervisor never restarts), and not idle (so the hull is never re-selected). The contract cargo is stranded indefinitely.

OBSERVED (staging stack, agent TORWINDSTG, X1-KP46, 2026-08-05):
  container  contract-work-TORWINDSTG-7-472f01d4   status RUNNING   age 14 min
  hull       TORWINDSTG-7  DOCKED @ X1-KP46-D38  fuel 613/600  cargo 5/80 SHIP_PLATING
  contract   cmsfiheci  PROCUREMENT  5 SHIP_PLATING -> X1-KP46-A2  payment 65,735
  The hull was ONE LEG from delivery, fully fuelled, loaded with exactly the right good.

LOG-LINE CADENCE (the proof it is wedged, not merely slow):
  00:12  28 lines   <- container starts: plans route, sources cargo
  00:13  23 lines
  00:16   1 line    <- "Transient refuel failure, retrying with backoff" attempt 1
  00:19   1 line    <- attempt 2
  00:23   4 lines   <- attempt 3, "Refuel retries exhausted at waypoint, attempting alternate
                       fuel stop", "Rerouting to alternate fuel stop after exhausting retries"
  00:24   3 lines   <- "Sweeper: Unstuck TORWINDSTG-7 -> IN_ORBIT at X1-KP46-D38",
                       "Ship arrival event received" @ D38
  00:25   0
  00:26   0         <- SILENT. container heartbeat_at is CURRENT (seconds old).
  Every OTHER container logged normally throughout (bootstrap 00:26:32, scout_tour 00:26:37,
  trade_fleet 00:26:39), so the daemon and log are healthy — this worker alone is wedged.

SEQUENCE THAT TRIGGERS IT (hypothesis, one clean instance):
  refuel fails 3x at the planned waypoint -> retries exhausted -> reroute to an ALTERNATE fuel
  stop -> arrival event received at the alternate -> the worker never resumes its delivery route.
  The reroute appears to leave the route state such that arrival at the alternate satisfies no
  pending segment, so the worker waits on something that will never happen.

WHY THIS CLASS MATTERS MORE THAN A CRASH: a crashed worker is relaunched within seconds (observed
repeatedly on the prod stack, upstream 500s, self-healed every time). A heartbeating-idle worker
is INVISIBLE to every recovery path and holds its hull + cargo forever. It caps contract
throughput regardless of fleet size — the staging fleet had 4 contract haulers and still only
one hull was ever executing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A CONTRACT_WORKFLOW worker that takes no route/contract action for N minutes while its ship is
   DOCKED/IN_ORBIT (not IN_TRANSIT) either resumes its route or EXITS non-zero so the coordinator
   re-selects. Silent-and-heartbeating must not be a reachable terminal state.
2. Specifically cover the refuel-exhaustion path: after "Rerouting to alternate fuel stop", the
   worker must re-plan from its ACTUAL position to the delivery destination, and a test must
   assert it does (drive it with a refuel that fails 3x then succeeds at an alternate).
3. The stall must be OBSERVABLE: emit a counter/log when a worker is idle-but-heartbeating past
   the threshold, so this is detectable without reading log-line cadence by hand.
4. Regression: a worker legitimately waiting on a long IN_TRANSIT leg must NOT be killed (the
   liveness test must distinguish waiting-for-arrival from wedged-while-docked).

NOTE ON fuel=613/600: the live API reported fuel ABOVE capacity on this hull after the alternate
refuel. Probably harmless/cosmetic, but it is in the same code path and worth a glance while here.

Filed from the staging validation of epic st-drm (city bead st-9p1). The staging stack is
deploy/staging (isolated: own DB spacetraders_staging, socket /tmp/spacetraders-staging.sock,
metrics :9095) — reproduce there, NOT on prod.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-05, BEFORE ANYONE WORKS THIS — the stall is TRANSIENT, not permanent. The description above says 'PERMANENTLY SILENT' and 'stranded indefinitely'. THAT IS FALSIFIED.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: I measured the worker silent for ~2 min at 00:26 (docked at D38, cargo
aboard, container heartbeating). While I was writing this bead it RESUMED ON ITS OWN and departed
for the delivery waypoint X1-KP46-A2. Total silence was roughly 4 minutes, not indefinite.

So the real defect is a MULTI-MINUTE DEAD WINDOW after refuel-retry exhaustion + alternate-fuel
reroute, not a permanent hang. Revise severity accordingly: this is a throughput leak (minutes of
a loaded hull doing nothing, repeated), NOT a hull-loss bug.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA #1 IS THEREFORE WRONG AS WRITTEN — do not implement a watchdog that KILLS a
silent worker, because a worker that looks wedged may be about to resume, and killing it costs a
re-selection cycle (I did exactly that; see below). Better shape: instrument the dead window
(#3 stands) and fix the reroute path so the worker re-plans immediately (#2 stands) rather than
adding a killer.

MY INTERVENTION AND ITS COST (recorded so the next reader is not misled by the fleet state):
Captain stopped contract-work-TORWINDSTG-7-472f01d4 to 'free the hull' — ~90 seconds AFTER it had
already recovered and gone IN_TRANSIT to A2. Stopping the container does not recall the ship, so
T7 continued to A2 with its 5 SHIP_PLATING intact and contract cmsfiheci (65,735) stayed open with
6d23h remaining. Expected recovery path: on arrival T7 goes idle holding the contract good, and
idleContractCargoHolder short-circuits to select it for delivery. Cost is roughly one coordinator
pass, not a lost hull or lost cargo.

PROCESS LESSON (mine, not the engine's): I diagnosed a stall from a 2-minute silence, then spent
several minutes writing the bead, then acted on the ORIGINAL reading without re-checking. A
liveness verdict has a shelf life measured in the same units as the thing it measures. RE-READ
STATE IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ANY INTERVENTION, never from the analysis that motivated it.

MECHANISM FALSIFIED, PRIORITY DROPPED P1->P3 (sp-k0ye9 lane, lead-verified 2026-08-06).

TRIGGER IS EFFECTIVELY EXTINCT AND THERE WERE NEVER ANY STRANDINGS.
  "Refuel retries exhausted"          2   <- this bead's actual trigger
  "Rerouting to alternate fuel stop"  2
  "non-transient error, failing fast" 36  <- A DIFFERENT PATH (isRetryableRefuelError
                                             returning false; a 4xx that never reaches
                                             the reroute). The lead cited these 36 as
                                             evidence this bug was live. They are not.
Both real occurrences are 2026-08-05 (00:23:44 TORWINDSTG-7, 02:28:44 TORWINDSTG-8) and
both carry "attempts":3 -- the pre-sp-l7zha constant that fix DELETED. ZERO occurrences
since that deploy. Both self-recovered; ACTUAL STRANDINGS: ZERO.

THE HYPOTHESISED MECHANISM IS WRONG. The bead assumed the reroute leaves route state such
that arrival satisfies no pending segment, so the worker waits forever. The log refutes it:
  00:24:18  Ship arrival event received @ X1-KP46-D38   <- THE WAIT SUCCEEDED
  ...3m15s of total silence...
  00:27:33  Alternate fuel stop reroute also failed
The silence is INSIDE the single e.refuelShip(...) call at refuel_retry.go:299. It is not
a wedge; it is a blocking API call with no container-level output.

THE REAL DEFECT IS AN OBSERVABILITY ASYMMETRY:
  first refuel      -> refuelShipWithRetryCore, logs EVERY attempt          (visible)
  alternate-stop    -> refuelShip, bare mediator sends, no outer retry loop (invisible)
Same failure, one observable and one not. Underneath, the API client retries internally
(api.retry_policy max_attempts 3, 30s/request) and emits nothing at container level.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, RESOLVED:
  #1 watchdog/exit non-zero -- VOID. Nothing to kill; the worker is blocked in an API call,
     not idle, and it recovers itself.
  #2 re-plan from actual position -- ALREADY SATISFIED IN SHIPPED CODE. At 00:27:38-39 it
     does exactly that: "Resuming existing active contract", route D38 -> A2. A finding,
     not work.
  #3 make the stall observable -- STANDS. The one real gap. APPROVED to build.
  fuel=613/600 -- already settled by sp-l7zha (ReconstructFuel has clamped since
     2026-07-09); the local/remote disagreement WAS the clamp working.

SCOPE APPROVED: #3 only. No watchdog, no re-plan changes -- neither defect exists.
Cheap, and the next 500-storm reroute would otherwise be equally invisible.

#3 SHIPPED AND MERGED (main b35435c2). #1 and #2 NOT BUILT -- both falsified, see above.

Two changes, both log-only:
  - reportSlowRefuel, DEFERRED, warns when the dock/refuel/orbit trio blocks past
    SlowRefuelThreshold (30s), action=refuel_slow, with elapsed seconds. DEFERRED
    DELIBERATELY so it covers the ERROR paths: the incident spent 3m15s here and then
    FAILED, so a success-only report would have been silent through the exact case it
    exists for. Covers every refuelShip caller, not just the reroute.
  - refuel_alternate_started on the reroute path, so the silence is attributable WHILE
    IT IS OPEN. In the incident the last line for 3m15s was "Ship arrival event received"
    -- which reads as a healthy arrival, and is what made this look like a wedge.

30s threshold brackets the 3m15s observed incident. No Prometheus counter: sp-az5a5
already owns that gap; a second mechanism here would duplicate it.

NOT DEPLOY-VERIFIABLE, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The trigger has fired ZERO
times since sp-l7zha deployed, so there is nothing on staging to observe this against.
Unlike sp-k0ye9 there is not even a boot-time falsifier -- this code only speaks when a
refuel blocks past 30s. ITS EVIDENCE IS THE TEST SUITE ALONE.

A SURVIVING PROBE WAS THE MOST USEFUL RESULT. Probe 4 (hoist the timer above the
precondition skips) SURVIVED. The reason: the full-tank path sends no refuel command, so
the mock clock never advances and elapsed is 0 either way. The property is not merely
untested, it is UNOBSERVABLE -- a skip is a pure local read and cannot consume time, so no
fixture can make a hoisted timer misreport. The lane DELETED the test rather than leave a
test that cannot fail overstating coverage, and rewrote the comment to state the placement
as SCOPE rather than as a tested guarantee. That is the right disposition for a vacuous
test and worth copying.

FOLLOW-UP FLAGGED BY THE LANE, NOT INVESTIGATED: 36 "non-transient error, failing fast"
refuel lines are a DIFFERENT path (isRetryableRefuelError false -- a 4xx that never reaches
the reroute). Nobody has looked at WHY those 4xx are happening. Filed separately.
close_reason: Closed

title: deliverInputs re-reads the market at arrival and fails OPEN: listings=nil makes marketBuys accept every good, offering the whole hold unfiltered
description:
PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the gate factory fleet work — surfaced while reviewing phase 3 task 4, where an implementer's report claimed the case was 'unreachable'. It is not; it is narrowed.

There are TWO DIFFERENT MARKET READS AT TWO DIFFERENT TIMES:
1. The sp-b27a2 guard refuses to fly on an unreadable listing (checked before departure).
2. gobot/internal/application/manufacturing/services/production_executor_dock.go:336-338 — deliverInputs RE-READS the listing ON ARRIVAL and sets listings=nil on error.

When that second read fails, marketBuys (production_executor_dock.go:402-411) returns TRUE for everything, so the per-item filter in deliverInputs (dock.go:340-346) stops filtering and THE WHOLE HOLD IS OFFERED UNFILTERED to the destination.

gate_topology.go:203-208 records that the two nil-handlings are DELIBERATELY NOT SHARED, so this is a known divergence rather than an oversight — but the fail-open half is not documented where deliverInputs is read.

BLAST RADIUS IS SMALL: the path SPENDS NOTHING (it sells/transfers already-owned cargo), and the destination itself rejects goods it does not import. The exposure is offering cargo that was meant to stay aboard during a transient market-read failure between guard and arrival.

CORRECT CHARACTERISATION for anyone who reads the task 4 report: 'narrowed to a transient read failure between guard and arrival', NOT 'unreachable'.
acceptance_criteria: Either the arrival-time read failure fails CLOSED (offer nothing rather than everything), or the fail-open is documented at deliverInputs with the reason the two nil-handlings differ, so the next reader does not conclude it is unreachable.
notes:
FINAL SHA SET: 450a94b7 / 29446276 / 2fb509e0 / 2570fd7f. The last commit closed three LOW findings from the lane review, two of which were worse than the review characterised them:
LOW 1 — the M9a 'misleading line is absent' assertion scanned entriesWithLevel(WARNING) while 'does not buy it' logs at INFO (dock.go:364). Not merely dead: IT WOULD HAVE PASSED AGAINST AN IMPLEMENTATION THAT EMITTED THE LINE FOR EVERY GOOD ABOARD. Now scans every level and reports the level matched; probe M13's assert string carries the INFO marker the old scan could never reach.
LOW 3 — THE ZERO-UNIT OUTCOME WAS UNREACHABLE FROM ANY TEST: recordingFeeder mapped units:0 to a 40-unit default, so the fixture could not express 'the trip happened and the market took nothing' — precisely the state this bead's own fail-closed fix produces. A tookNothing flag had to be added first; without it the new test COULD NOT HAVE FAILED AT ALL. Zero units now takes its own WARNING with action full_hold_fed_nothing, naming the still-full state and the likeliest cause (probe M12 kills it), and the new test carries a non-vacuity guard that the feed was actually ATTEMPTED — otherwise the park path satisfies the same assertion.
LOW 2 — PrefersANonAbundantFactoryWhenEmptyingAFullHold gained the plan-order guard its sibling carries (probe M14 inverts the order and the guard fires; real indices 0 and 2).
close_reason: FIXED on branch gate-factory-phase3 by 450a94b7 (+ 29446276, 2fb509e0). Chose (a) FAIL CLOSED. DECIDING FACT — and it CORRECTS THIS BEAD'S OWN blast-radius reasoning: I wrote that the destination rejects goods it does not import, which is true only for UNLISTED goods. THE ONE THING A FACTORY DOES NOT REJECT IS ITS OWN EXPORT — it has a bid, the sell SUCCEEDS, and it LADDERS THAT BID DOWN (the resale-sink class). So the fail-open's worst case was never 'cargo meant to stay aboard'; it was DUMPING PRODUCT INTO OUR OWN BID exactly when we cannot tell EXPORT from IMPORT. Probe M9c shows it live. Fail-closed is safe because BOTH callers run the sp-b27a2 departure guard, so an arrival-read failure is transient and a retry always exists — and sp-2scwt's fix CLOSES THAT LOOP, since a full hull re-entering the gate leg now delivers instead of parking. The two fixes interlock. Probe M9b SURVIVES BY DESIGN (the nil default is unreachable today because the early return answers first); branch KEPT as a defensive fallback and documented in-code as such, including a warning not to 'fix' the survivor by weakening the caller to reach it.

title: supply_chain_resolver.go still carries the false 'raw materials exist in the map with empty inputs' claim
description:
Found by the sp-4irrr review — the SAME defect class that bead existed to kill, surviving in a second location.

supply_chain_resolver.go:323-324 comments: 'Raw materials like SILICON_CRYSTALS exist in the map with empty inputs {}'.

FALSE. SILICON_CRYSTALS is {"EXPLOSIVES"} (supply_chain.go:25), so hasRecipe is TRUE for it, not false. This is the identical mistaken premise sp-4irrr struck from GateTopology.IsRaw and from the two-fleet spec: 'has no recipe' is not 'is raw', because every actual raw material HAS a recipe entry.

THE CODE IS CORRECT ANYWAY — the factory-existence check at :328-335 is what makes it work, and that check is precisely the corroboration sp-4irrr cited for the curated-predicate approach. So this is a comment defect, not a behaviour defect.

WHY FILE IT: sp-4irrr's whole lesson is that a false premise in a comment propagates into later design. That premise was restated in FOUR places (IsRaw's comment, GateTopology's type comment, a test header, and the spec); three were corrected in 7a14b400 and this is the fourth. Leaving it invites the next author to re-derive the wrong rule from it.

FIX: correct the comment to name the real mechanism — the factory-existence check, not empty inputs.

title: IsMineableRawMaterial's comment claims 'no alternative fabrication path' but two entries have real recipes
description:
Found by the sp-4irrr review.

goods.mineableRawMaterials (internal/domain/goods/supply_chain.go:212) carries a comment at :209 saying its members have 'no alternative fabrication path'. That is inaccurate for at least two entries:
  - EXOTIC_MATTER (:238) has the recipe {LAB_INSTRUMENTS, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY} at :162
  - BOTANICAL_SPECIMENS (:239) has the recipe {LAB_INSTRUMENTS, EQUIPMENT} at :165

So the list is really 'prefer to source directly' rather than 'cannot be fabricated', and GateTopology.IsRaw (sp-4irrr, landed 7a14b400) now inherits that inaccuracy.

ZERO IMPACT TODAY: neither good is reachable from FAB_MATS or ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY — both chains traced by the reviewer — and IsRaw remains strictly better than the !hasRecipe rule it replaced.

MATTERS IF: phase 3 (or anything else) ever walks a NON-GATE chain using IsRaw. A good that IS fabricable would be treated as terminal and bought instead.

FIX: either correct the comment to say what the list actually means, or split it into two lists (truly-unfabricable vs prefer-to-buy) if any caller needs the stronger guarantee. Check callers before narrowing — IsMineableRawMaterial has other consumers.

title: freeCargoSpace logs 'Unloaded N units to free cargo space' while SELLING the cargo — an operator cannot tell a sale happened
description:
Found during gate-delivery phase 2, task 8.

gobot/internal/application/manufacturing/services/production_executor_dock.go:418-477 (freeCargoSpace) issues a SellCargoCommand for every item aboard except protectGood, and reads response.TotalRevenue — it SELLS. Its log line says 'Unloaded %d units of %s to free cargo space'.

WHY IT MATTERS: 'unloaded' and 'sold' are different events with different money consequences. An operator reading the daemon log during a stuck-hull investigation sees cargo apparently moved, not liquidated, and has no signal that revenue was booked or that inventory left the fleet permanently. The same understatement existed in a code comment in the construction dispatcher and was corrected there in d312156a; this is the same inaccuracy in the place operators actually look.

FIX: name the operation honestly in the log and include the revenue, e.g. 'Sold %d units of %s for %d credits to free cargo space'. No behaviour change.

CONTEXT: this path is load-bearing for the legacy fabricate role's recovery — makeRoomForOutputHarvest -> freeCargoSpace is how a hull with a full hold of stranded material gets unwedged, which is why the phase-2 role-scoping decision depends on it. Anyone auditing that recovery from logs alone would currently mis-read it.

title: The gate-leg routing predicate is pinned only at the decline site; the routing half has no behavioural test
description:
Found during gate-delivery phase 2, task 8, by a probe that SURVIVED.

runsGateLeg (run_construction_coordinator_gate_delivery.go:68) is consumed at two sites: the routing branch in supplyTask (run_construction_coordinator_supply.go:45) and the dispatch decline (run_construction_coordinator_dispatch.go:290).

Diverging the DECLINE site kills TestConstructionDrain_StillDispatchesAFullDeliveryHullWhenTheGateLegIsUnwired. Diverging the ROUTING site kills NOTHING.

CAUSE: supplyTask calls claimTaskForSupply UPSTREAM of the runsGateLeg branch, and the pinning test asserts claimCount == 1 — an assertion structurally incapable of observing which leg then runs. So the enabled() conjunct is behaviourally pinned on one side only.

NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT URGENT: the extraction in d312156a makes the two sites share one function, so a divergence now requires deliberately inlining a copy — which the decline-site probe does catch. This is about defence in depth, not a live defect.

WHY IT IS WORTH CLOSING: phase 3 gives RoleFactory its behaviour and WILL touch supplyTask's routing. That is exactly the edit where a behavioural pin on the routing half would matter, and exactly the divergence (decline broader than routing) that produced the D2 blocking defect in this task.

FIX: a test that observes WHICH LEG RAN rather than that a claim occurred — e.g. assert the gate buyer was consulted (or was not) for a delivery-tagged hull with the collaborator wired vs unwired.

title: universe transition preview claims a rollover on an already-synced universe
description:
`universe transition --agent X` with no --token and no --confirm routes to previewPendingMint (gobot/internal/adapters/cli/universe_transition.go), which loads the open era and prints 'New era <name> -> will be OPENED' WITHOUT consulting eraInSyncWith(). On an already-synced universe it therefore previews a rollover that --confirm would decline as a no-op.

Reproduced live on 2026-08-03 (worktree .claude/worktrees/sp-dqbzm, era 6 torwind-2026-08-02 open, server resetDate 2026-08-02):

  Prior era  torwind-2026-08-02 (player 6) -> will be CLOSED (no cache truncation)
  New era    torwind-2026-08-02 (new player) -> will be OPENED for resetDate 2026-08-02

The same era name on both lines — it would collide on the unique eras.name constraint if the run actually proceeded.

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by sp-dqbzm — deliberately left out of that lane to keep the diff reviewable. sp-dqbzm DID fix the confirmed-run half of the same gap (the in-sync check now precedes the irreversible mint, so a re-run no longer burns an account slot); this is the remaining preview-side inconsistency, now merely misleading rather than costly.

FIX SHAPE: previewPendingMint already has both openEra and status.ResetDate in hand — reuse eraInSyncWith() and print the same 'Universe already in sync ... No changes made.' line the confirmed path prints. ~4 lines plus one test alongside TestTransition_PreviewDoesNotMint.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A preview (no --token, no --confirm, or --dry-run) on an already-synced universe reports 'already in sync' instead of a pending rollover.
2. A preview on an out-of-sync universe is unchanged.
3. Neither case registers an agent or writes anything.

title: Runbook: gobot Mac<->GCP-VM game migration + scripts/migrate-game.sh
description:
Bidirectional migration of the gobot game between Mac (launchd) and GCP VM
(systemd). DB always co-locates with the daemon (a remote DB over WAN is too
slow); metrics (Prometheus/Grafana volumes) transfer optionally.

SCRIPT: scripts/migrate-game.sh <to-vm|to-local> [--no-metrics] [--keep-vm] [--yes]

INFRA: VM=spacetraders-gobot (pj-fisitalview-hml, us-east4-c). External IP is
EPHEMERAL (rotates on every stop/start). Firewall rules fmd36-allow-ssh +
fmd36-allow-metrics-ui take your (rotating CGNAT) IP as source; the script
re-points them before every network phase. SSH key ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine.

PROCEDURE to-vm: rebuild linux bins -> start VM + repoint firewall -> ship
source+bins, fix metrics bind to 0.0.0.0, refresh venv -> stop local + park
plists -> pg_dump -> transfer -> restore (DROP DATABASE WITH (FORCE) +
pg_restore --exit-on-error) -> enable+start systemd units -> verify the
active player is trading -> prune metrics to current era + stream volumes +
start VM prom/grafana.
to-local mirrors it: rebuild darwin bins (make) -> stop VM game -> dump ->
transfer -> restore local (FORCE) -> un-park + start launchd (WARP/50051
bounce) -> verify -> stream metrics VM->Mac -> defuse VM (disable units,
restart=no) -> stop instance.

GOTCHAS (accumulated over ~8 flips):
1. VM external IP rotates on every stop/start -> re-fetch natIP after start.
2. CGNAT rotates YOUR IP constantly, even mid-flip -> repoint firewall before
   each net op; a rotation mid-transfer truncates it.
3. gcloud USER auth expires every ~1-2 days, blocking every flip. Fix: a
   service-account key. Create SA, grant roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 +
   roles/compute.securityAdmin (+ roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor for IAP),
   download key JSON, export ST_MIGRATE_SA_KEY=/path/key.json. Then the script
   runs unattended. KEEP THE KEY OUT OF GIT.
4. Metrics volume grows unbounded within an era (0 -> 6.5G in a week) so big
   transfers truncate. Script prunes to the current era (universe resetDate
   cutoff) before transfer. A Prometheus retention cap would also bound it.
5. tar|ssh volume stream can hit 'connection reset' -> keepalives + a
   truncation guard (dst within 5% of src) + one retry (all in the script).
6. DROP DATABASE fails ('being accessed') because dashboard/visualizer hold PG
   conns -> WITH (FORCE) + pg_restore --exit-on-error.
7. Docker Desktop bind-mounts of /private/tmp/claude-* mount EMPTY -> stream
   volumes via ssh stdin/stdout, never bind-mount a scratch path.
8. zsh footgun: SSH="ssh -i k host"; $SSH "cmd" does NOT word-split -> inline
   ssh or a bash script (this is bash).
9. routing port 50051 is in the macOS ephemeral range; Cloudflare WARP grabs
   it -> bounce WARP (disconnect / kickstart routing / connect).
10. Weekly universe reset (~13:00 UTC on resetDate) WIPES the era and spawns a
    new player (3->4->5...); the old token 401s. Migration carries all players;
    the daemon recovers whichever has RUNNING containers -> verify the ACTIVE
    player, never a hardcoded id.
11. Rebuild local binaries from current HEAD each direction (Admiral commits
    ~20/day) or the game regresses code on the flip.
12. IAP (gcloud compute ssh --tunnel-through-iap) is IP-rotation-immune (source
    is Google 35.235.240.0/20) but ~1MB/s: fine for control SSH, too slow for
    the volume transfers.

title: market_data PK omits player_id while UpsertMarketData deletes scoped to it — latent cross-player insert collision
description:
Found by an independent reachability probe during gate-topology phase 1 verification. LATENT, not live.

The market_data primary key is (waypoint_symbol, good_symbol) — it does NOT include player_id. But UpsertMarketData (adapters/persistence/market_repository.go:30-74) deletes scoped to (player_id, waypoint_symbol) before inserting.

So if two players ever observed the same waypoint, player B's insert would collide with player A's surviving rows on the PK, because A's rows were not deleted by B's player-scoped DELETE.

NOT LIVE TODAY: measured 39,183 rows across 6,354 waypoints and 4 players, and no waypoint holds rows for more than one player. The live player is 5.

Becomes live the moment two agents share a universe/system, which multi-player or a shared-era setup would do. Fix is to include player_id in the PK, or to make the DELETE match the PK's scope.
notes: LATENT, not live: measured 39,183 rows across 6,354 waypoints and 4 players, and no waypoint holds rows for more than one player (live player is 5). Becomes live the moment two agents share a universe or era.

title: Era-invariance guard misses 2-segment system symbols and non-X1 sector prefixes
description:
Ledger item Task5-M2 from gate-topology phase 1, unfiled until now.

TestGateTopology_SourceContainsNoWaypointLiterals uses regex "[A-Z]\d+-[A-Z0-9]+-[A-Z0-9]+" plus a strings.Contains(src,"X1-") backstop.

TWO GAPS:
1. 2-segment SYSTEM symbols (X1-GZ7, X1-AU21, X1-FB5) do not match the 3-segment regex — only the X1- backstop catches them. Systems are era-regenerated too.
2. A non-X1 sector prefix (X2-GZ7) passes BOTH checks: the regex needs 3 segments, and the backstop is X1-specific.

Narrow today (the universe uses X1), but the guard's whole purpose is surviving regeneration, and the sector prefix is not guaranteed constant across universes.

ALSO (Minor 1 from the same review): the guard reads gate_topology.go ONLY, but phase 1 put live seam logic in production_executor_fabricate.go. Both files are clean today (grep count 0), so this is a gap in protection rather than a violation — widen the guard's scope when convenient.
notes:
STRENGTHENED by an independent mutation verifier, 2026-08-03. The scope gap is worse than 'the guard reads one file': it reads ONE HARDCODED RELATIVE FILENAME with no directory walk — gate_topology_test.go:459 os.ReadFile("gate_topology.go"), the only ReadFile in the file. So production_executor_fabricate.go, which holds the live seam logic phase 1 wired, is entirely outside the guard.

Worse: grep -rn 'production_executor_fabricate.go' across the whole services/ package returns rc=1 — NO test anywhere references that file. It has no era-invariance protection of any kind. Its clean state today (both waypoint greps rc=1, X1- count 0) is UNENFORCED and stays clean only by luck.

CHEAP FIX: make the guard read a LIST of files, or glob the package, rather than one literal name. Do this before phase 2 adds seam logic outside gate_topology.go — every phase that widens the seam widens the unguarded surface.

Independently re-verified in the same pass (control run confirmed GREEN on pristine HEAD first, so both failures attribute to the mutations): the regex IS load-bearing — an X2- literal, invisible to the strings.Contains X1- backstop (X1- count 0 on the mutated file), still fails at the regex branch line 466. And the 4-shape calibration is STRONGER than the implementer claimed: a tightened pattern blinds 3 of the 4 shapes, not 1; t.Fatalf merely short-circuits at the first.

title: fakeMarkets discards systemSymbol and playerID — era-invariance pass-through survives mutation untested
description:
Ledger item Task3-M1 from gate-topology phase 1, unfiled until now.

gate_topology_test.go's fakeMarkets signature is (_ context.Context, good, _ string, _ int) — it discards systemSymbol and playerID. A mutation writing FindImportMarket(ctx, good, "", 0) survives all tests.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: era-invariance is the entire point of the GateTopology seam. A hardcoded or dropped system argument is precisely the era-rollover bug class this phase exists to prevent, and it would go undetected. playerID is also a real tenant key in this codebase.

Blast radius is bounded by the fail-closed direction (wrong system -> no importer -> refusal, not a mis-dispatch), which is why it was deferred rather than fixed.

FIX: record args in the fake and assert the pass-through, for TerminalFactory and FeedTarget together (fixing one alone breaks the fixture's symmetry). 2-line change.

title: Gate feeding coverage pin is fixture-dependent — flipping outputSupply to HIGH silently restores the blindness it was added to prevent
description:
Ledger item Task4-O1 from gate-topology phase 1, unfiled until now.

TestFeeding_FedRunReachesTheHarvest_NotOnlyTheInputBuys pins that a fed run reaches guard -> navigate -> deliverInputs. Its 'reachable only past the guard' property is FIXTURE-dependent, not structural: it rests on balancedFeedingRepo's outputSupply == 'MODERATE' keeping collectExistingFactorySupply (production_executor_fabricate.go:282-328) shut. That path navigates and harvests while skipping BOTH the guard and deliverInputs.

Flipping that one fixture string to HIGH or ABUNDANT would let the pin pass through a route that proves nothing — silently restoring the exact class of blindness the pin exists to prevent, with no assertion noticing. This is the same defect class phase 1 just fixed (a test that passes green while having stopped exercising its path).

Mitigated today only by a fixture comment at line 41-42. Make it structural: assert the shortcut was NOT taken, or assert on outputSupply directly so an edit to it fails loudly.

title: Gate feed-destination guard runs AFTER the input spend — a persistently wrong-chain node re-buys inputs every pass
description:
Found during gate-topology phase 1, Task 4 (sp-b27a2 root-cause fix), by the implementer.

production_executor_fabricate.go now validates that the destination factory imports the cargo being hauled before NavigateAndDock — which is the correct place to stop the mis-route. But that guard sits AFTER produceInputsForFactory, so the inputs have already been BOUGHT by the time the destination is rejected.

CONSEQUENCE: a node whose destination is persistently wrong-chain re-buys its inputs on every coordination pass, then refuses to deliver them. Spend without progress, repeated.

WHY IT IS SAFE TO MOVE: destination validity depends on nothing produceInputsForFactory produces — it is a function of the factory's market listing and the node's children, both known before the spend. Hoisting the guard above the input purchase is strictly stronger and costs nothing.

NOT URGENT: the guard is new, and before it the hauler would have navigated and stranded instead — so this is a smaller loss than the bug it replaced, not a regression. Money guards untouched (RULINGS #4); the 50k floor still bounds every input buy.

title: Contract delivery plan can grow by +2 in a partially-charted system — sp-9suun's own comment asserts the opposite
description:
Found by adversarial review of sp-9suun.

standby_slots_test.go:124-126 asserts in PROSE: 'the anchor ordering repositions the delivery pool, it does not enlarge it.' Three lines later (:135-139) the same test expects 1 central park + 1 far anchor -> 2 slots. Measured: 3 central parks + 4 anchors -> 5 delivery hulls vs 3 before; plan length 12 -> 15.

CAUSE: plan.go:157-162 — anchorOrCentral claims a non-central anchor WITHOUT consuming a central park, and the two far anchors sit outside centralBandRadius=300 so they are never in the central pool to begin with.

BOUNDED, and NOT a spend change at shipped defaults: saturates at MaxDeliveryHulls=6, and total buys are min(planSize, ceiling) with a default ceiling of 3 — so at defaults this is a COMPOSITION shift (delivery vs warehouse, same SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER frame), not more hulls. RULINGS #4 intact.

UNREACHABLE IN THE MEASURED ERAS — era3/4/5 all resolve 12 deduped central parks. Reachable only in a partially-charted home system, i.e. early in an era before survey completes, which is exactly when the fleet is smallest.

FIX: either make anchorOrCentral consume a pool slot, or correct the comment and pin the real invariant with a test. The comment being wrong is the actual defect — an untrue invariant in a test is worse than no invariant.

title: fleet hub pins now truncate in PIN ORDER, not alphabetically — undocumented operator-facing change
description:
Side effect of sp-9suun's AssignedSlot truncation change, flagged by adversarial review.

Operator pins win untouched over computed placement (standby_placement.go:30-31) and are fed straight into AssignedSlot (run_fleet_coordinator_homing.go:96-104). ApplyStandbyStationChange (standby_stations.go:28-56) is an order-preserving append, so pins are stored in ADD order.

CONSEQUENCE: with more pins than hulls, the operator now loses the MOST RECENTLY ADDED hubs instead of the alphabetically-last. And 'fleet hub remove X' followed by 'fleet hub add X' silently demotes X to first-to-be-dropped — a no-op round trip that changes behaviour.

Nothing in adapters/cli/fleet_hub.go:34-52 conveys that pin order is now priority. No test covers it.

Pin-order is arguably MORE explicable than alphabetical, so this may be a documentation + test fix rather than a behaviour revert. Decide, then pin it with a test either way.

title: unified_gate_fill doc comments describe a config toggle that does not exist (hardcoded true; no key, no struct field)
description:
KNOB REVIEW finding, verified read-only against main 2026-08-02.

unified_gate_fill is documented throughout as a config toggle with an OFF contract, but it is an UNCONDITIONAL code path. There is no way to turn it off short of editing source.

EVIDENCE (exhaustive, main):
- NO yaml key. 'unified_gate_fill' appears in NO config file — not gobot/config.yaml (live), not gobot/config.staging.yaml, not any tracked or untracked yaml on disk. Repo hits are only: .beads/issues.jsonl, issues.jsonl, MECHANICS.md:350 (prose), gobot/docs/refactoring/lanes/app-manufacturing.md:46 (filename), and the compiled daemon binary.
- NO struct field. 'type ManufacturingConfig struct' does not exist in main. git grep UnifiedGateFill across ALL *.go returns exactly TWO non-test files: the stamper and the ctx-key definition.
- SINGLE stamper, literal true: run_construction_coordinator_supply.go:259, inside gateSupplyContext(), which also stamps the construction-site DeliveryTarget. So both conjuncts of IsUnifiedGateNode (toggle && IsConstructionSite) are always satisfied together at the ONLY site that sets either.
- Behaviour readers (4): input_price_ceiling.go:136,:217; input_source_selector.go:281; production_executor_fabricate.go:358 (note: an OR with ConstructionSupplyFromContext, so it fires on construction supply regardless).

THE DEFECT IS THE DOCUMENTATION, not the behaviour. The unconditional path appears to be the intended end-state (sp-vh1s shipped 2026-07-14). But:
- unified_gate_fill.go:82-83 claims the value is 'Fed from ManufacturingConfig.UnifiedGateFill via the coordinator's command' — a type and field that do NOT exist.
- unified_gate_fill.go:89 'defaulting to false (off) when unstamped' and :22 'reads the zero value: UnifiedGateFill off' describe an unreachable production state.
- input_source_selector.go:269 references 'the meaning of the unified_gate_fill toggle OFF = today contract'.

OBSERVED COST: these comments caused a session to assert 'unified_gate_fill is armed at config.yaml:235' as a premise for a construction redesign discussion. A false premise about arming state directly shapes design decisions. This is the 'closed is not armed' failure mode running in reverse — a knob that reads as armable but is welded on.

FIX: correct the comments in unified_gate_fill.go (stamper doc, zero-value doc, IsUnifiedGateNode doc) and input_source_selector.go:74-75,:269 to state that gate mode is unconditional for construction-supply runs and that no config toggle exists. If a real toggle IS wanted, that is a SEPARATE bead — do not add one here (Admiral standing order: no feature flags).

RELATED: re-scope sp-sn9x. Its premise 'any deploy that flips unified_gate_fill must be followed by a container reset' and '§8a removes the OFF-revert path' are both already false — there is no flip and no revert path. This makes §8a feeder deletion LESS risky than that bead assumes.
notes: Found during a knob review, NOT during sp-pt7d work. No code touched; read-only verification only. Do not fix in the sp-pt7d worktree (one worktree per lane).
close_reason: Landed on main as 177ee92f via captain-gate. Deleted the unified_gate_fill toggle entirely rather than only fixing its stale comments: no yaml key in any config, no ManufacturingConfig field, sole stamper passed a literal true beside the construction-site DeliveryTarget, so the toggle conjunct in IsUnifiedGateNode was always redundant with the target check. Non-widening verified by closing every bypass route (WithDeliveryTarget, ConstructionSiteTarget, ctx key, struct literals, numeric Kind, gateSupplyContext's single caller); price-ceiling and chain-margin exemptions unchanged, RULINGS #4 intact. 311 manufacturing tests -race + full suite green; mutation killed in both directions naming specific tests. Scope widened beyond the bead's comments-only FIX with rationale: an exported WithUnifiedGateFill was a live footgun (any caller could stamp false and silently kill gate mode with no config trace) — deleting it makes 'gate mode iff construction-site delivery' structural rather than conventional. FOLLOW-UP FILED SEPARATELY: MECHANICS.md Goods Factory section describes a wholly deleted coordinator (run_factory_coordinator.go, container_ops_goods.go, gate feeders all absent from main) — not surgically patched here because fixing one clause would lend false credibility to a dead section; overlaps sp-zm4vb.

title: Doc note: probebuy.Config.ReserveFloor must bind on LANDED cost, not sticker (residue of refuted sp-1ngte)
description:
DOC-ONLY. No behaviour change, no inert code. This preserves the one durable lesson from sp-1ngte, which was closed as not-a-defect.

probebuy.Config.ReserveFloor already exists purely as a trap for the next implementer — its own doc says the guard is kept because 'the tier mistake it now refuses is the one this package exists to make impossible for whoever wires the next probe buyer'. That is exactly where the landed-cost lesson belongs, because whoever revives this path is the person who needs it.

ADD to the ReserveFloor doc comment, in that comment's own voice:
- the floor must bind on LANDED cost (purchase + ferry), not the sticker price — see sp-e46yc, which fixed precisely this in parkedsensing and shipped domain/parkedsensing/ferrycost.go (FerryHops / FerryCost / LandedProbeCost, DefaultGateFeeCredits=5900);
- BUT do NOT reuse ferrycost.go here unexamined: this path's relay is BUYER->YARD (probeBuyPlan.relay moves an existing idle hull to the counter so the purchase happens there, and relayAndRecheck re-prices at the dock), whereas LandedProbeCost models YARD->POST for the hull being bought. They are different quantities and collapsing them puts two meanings of 'landed' behind one name;
- and note that ReserveFloor is not the guard that would bind first anyway: the 25% treasury rule (price*100 > credits*25, RULINGS #6) and the per-window spend cap are.

WHY IT IS ONLY P3: the call site is unreachable — its command type is in retiredCommandTypes (daemon_server.go:1246) and the registry refuses to build it — and ReserveFloor is unset by the only config builder, so the gate is inactive. Nothing is bleeding. This is knowledge preservation, sized to match.

SCOPE: comment text only. Do not add a ferry term, do not set ReserveFloor, do not touch retiredCommandTypes, do not revive the coordinator. If the change is anything other than comment lines, it has exceeded this bead.

VERIFY IT IS COMMENTS-ONLY the reliable way, not by eyeballing the diff: gofmt -r 'a -> a' on the before and after, strip comments, and compare hashes — a pairing heuristic is not proof.
close_reason:
Merged to main as 0346650b (1 file, +23/-0, comment lines only). Gate clean.

COMMENTS-ONLY PROVEN, not eyeballed. The lane built an AST stripper the reliable way — go/parser with ParseComments OFF so comments never attach, through go/printer, SHA-256 — because gofmt's rewrite is a formatting normalizer, not a comment stripper. Critically it CALIBRATED THE RIG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS first, since a stripper that always reports 'same' is indistinguishable from a correct one: inserting a throwaway comment left the hash unchanged, and changing one code token (maxTreasuryFractionPercent 25 -> 26) changed it. Then applied against 'git show HEAD:<path>' rather than a working-tree variable, so the thing hashed is the thing committed. HEAD and working tree both b972b85c008d709744510ebbee4a9a1aa3744eaf8a404b12f5152c7cfc96158d, and post-commit the committed blob's AST hash equals main's.

I verified independently before gating: 23 added lines, 0 non-comment/non-blank added lines, 0 removed lines, 1 file. (First attempt at this check had a failing grep stage whose empty output would have read as a pass — redone with a correct pattern.)

CONTENT — three points appended to the ReserveFloor doc block, in its own voice:
1. Bind on LANDED cost, not sticker, when next wired, with sp-e46yc's measurement (258 probes for 10,152,775 on budget, then 6,444,427 to fly them to post; landed 16.6M, 63% over) and a pointer to domain/parkedsensing/ferrycost.go.
2. Do NOT reach for that file unexamined: LandedProbeCost models YARD->POST for the hull being bought, while this path's probeBuyPlan.relay is BUYER->YARD (moving an existing idle hull to the counter, relayAndRecheck re-pricing at the dock, the new probe reaching post later under a different reconciler). Different quantities; collapsing them puts two meanings of 'landed' behind one name. Records that sp-1ngte was CLOSED rather than 'fixed' for exactly this reason.
3. ReserveFloor is not the guard that binds first — at 0 the gate is inactive entirely, so a ferry term added only here would be inert; the 25% treasury rule (price*100 > credits*25, RULINGS #6) and the per-window spend cap are what would actually refuse a buy, and both compare against price.

Gates: gofmt clean, go build OK, go vet clean, full sweep 84 ok / 0 FAIL. The AST proof is the stronger statement — identical ASTs cannot produce different behaviour.

title: Generalise the sp-97ine union to a nested cap ladder — cap-4 loses 21 of 60 cases to the cap-2 subset it contains, so the cap is masking dilution rather than pricing geometry
description:
sp-97ine proved a union restores the strict-superset property for ONE subset: after it, the wide
solve wins-or-ties the home-only solve on 64/64 real cases. The economy-analyst's own closing note
on the cap re-replay states the gap that leaves:

  "the residual above-cap-2 dilution is real (the union covers only the home subset)"

MEASURED, on the FIXED solver (f4686056, analyst, 60 joint cases, working rate objective):
  cap-2 754,316 cr/hr   vs   cap-4 582,579   =  -22.77%
  cap-4 wins 3 / loses 21 / ties 36
Aggregate and win-rate concordant, so unlike the earlier +19.5% this one is quotable.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A SETTING. cap-4's search space is a strict SUPERSET of cap-2's. A
superset that loses 21 of 60 cases is losing to plans it contains — the same proof shape sp-97ine
was built on, one level up. The cap is currently doing the job the union should do: it is holding
the search narrow because widening it makes the solver choose worse, not because wide tours are
worth less.

THE COST OF THE WORKAROUND. Every multi-system opportunity beyond 2 systems is permanently
unreachable, not because it is unprofitable but because the solver cannot be trusted to rank it.
cap-4 already wins 3 of 60 cases even while diluted, so the wide space demonstrably contains
winners we are declining to look for.

SCOPE (hypothesis — confirm before building):
  Generalise sp-97ine's union from "the home subset" to a NESTED LADDER: solve at cap-2, union those
  candidates into the cap-4 pool, and let stage-2 arbitrate over the union. By construction cap-4
  then wins-or-ties cap-2 on every case, which removes the reason the cap exists. If it generalises
  cleanly, the same argument extends to cap-6 over cap-4.
  Mirror the existing idiom (tour_solver.py ~1910, the sp-97ine home union; and the sp-y05b ortools
  union) rather than inventing a third pattern.

THE PREREQUISITE THAT MADE THIS POSSIBLE, and the reason not to attempt it before f4686056:
selection used to be NON-MONOTONIC in pool size — _sort_scored's whole-pool zero-time veto meant
adding a candidate could change the ordering RULE for every other candidate. Under that, no union
could deliver a guarantee; sp-97ine's union was correct code that could not work. f4686056 fixed it.
Any union work now rests on monotonic selection; if that regresses, this bead's premise dies with it.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - ARM IT. No feature flag, no default-off seam (standing Admiral order).
  - Additive-only: byte-identical output when the union contributes nothing.
  - Do NOT change the cap, FULL_SCORE_TOP_N, or the ortools node budgets. The cap is the analyst's
    call and stays 2 until a replay says otherwise. This bead earns the right to revisit it; it does
    not take it.
  - Watch cost. sp-97ine's home union costs +33-70 ms per multi-system plan on the beam path; a
    nested ladder multiplies that per rung, and under SEQUENCER=ortools the home union already costs
    +3.0 s/plan because the extra solve burns its own anytime budget. Measure per rung before
    proposing more rungs.

ACCEPTANCE — the analyst's harness, not fixtures:
  cap-4 must win-or-tie cap-2 on ~every joint case. HAND-BUILT FIXTURES ARE NOT ACCEPTABLE EVIDENCE
  HERE. sp-97ine's 80 fixtures all passed while the real harness failed, because fixtures carry
  ballast cargo so every candidate has a leg and none is degenerate — they engaged cph ordering that
  real pools never reached. Reproduce on real reconstructed snapshots or report that you cannot.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE ANALYST (asked, not assumed): the magnitude of cap-4's 3 wins is unknown. If
they are small, this bead buys optionality rather than credits and should be priced accordingly.
notes:
PRICING ANSWER (economy-analyst, fresh 60-case run on f4686056, asked-not-assumed): cap-4 won 1/60 (prior run 3/60) — X1-KP23, cap-2 55,561 -> cap-4 193,647 cph (+138k, +248% relative but small absolute). The wide space's rare wins are POOR-NEIGHBORHOOD RESCUES (cap-2's local best was ~55k vs fleet-typical 750-850k), not monster multi-system lanes. Expected fleet value of the ladder at current geometry: (1-3/60) x ~140k ~= 2-7k cph — NOISE. Verdict: OPTIONALITY, park it honestly per your own framing. RE-PRICE TRIGGERS (when either fires, re-run this pricing): (1) the opportunity relocator (sp-zvywu) starts placing hulls in sparse frontier neighborhoods where local cap-2 options are thin — exactly the X1-KP23 shape at scale, EXCEPT the relocator itself is the cheaper fix for that case (move the hull, not the tour); (2) 3+ system chained lanes appear in scanned data with per-load value >> crossing costs (MERITIUM-ladder class). Aggregate this run: cap-2 845,865 vs cap-4 686,410 (-18.85%), 1W/22L/37T — cap-2 verdict unchanged, now at n=120 across two concordant runs.
PARKED 2026-07-31 ON PRICING — do not build. Priced by economy-analyst at my request BEFORE any lane
was dispatched (st-wisp-fsbg8).

THE MEASUREMENT: fresh 60-case run on the fixed solver. cap-4 won 1 of 60 — X1-KP23, where cap-2's
local best was a poor 55k and cap-4 rescued it to 194k (+138k absolute). Across runs the win count
is 1-3 of 60.

WHAT THE WINS ACTUALLY ARE: poor-neighbourhood RESCUES, not monster multi-system lanes. That is the
opposite of the shape this bead assumed. Fleet EV ~2-7k cph — noise against ~4-5M/hr.

AND THERE IS A CHEAPER FIX FOR THAT EXACT SHAPE: the RELOCATOR. When a hull's local neighbourhood is
poor, the answer is to move the hull, not to widen the tour search every hull performs on every
plan. sp-e8d92 (relocation offer at the tour boundary) and sp-fjvlm (cadence 900s -> 120s) both
landed 2026-07-30 and address precisely this. Widening the cap would pay a per-plan solver cost
fleet-wide to rescue a case the relocator already handles by moving one hull once.

SO THE BEAD'S PREMISE SURVIVES BUT ITS VALUE DOES NOT. cap-4 IS still a strict superset losing to
its own subset — that remains a real defect in the solver's selection, and the reasoning in the
description stands. It is simply not worth the build: the dilution is real and the recovery is
noise.

RE-PRICE TRIGGERS (analyst's, recorded so this is revisited on evidence rather than on someone
re-deriving the superset argument from scratch):
  1. The relocator starts placing hulls in SPARSE FRONTIERS — then poor-neighbourhood cases stop
     being rare and rescues stop being noise.
  2. 3+ SYSTEM CHAINED LANES appear in scan data — then the wide space contains something the narrow
     one structurally cannot, which is a different argument from dilution.

CAP-2 IS NOW SETTLED: n=120 across two concordant runs, -18.9% and -22.8%. Do not re-open the cap
question without new evidence of one of the two triggers above.

PROCESS NOTE FOR WHOEVER FINDS THIS: I filed this bead from a correct superset proof and asked for
the magnitude before dispatching. The proof was right and the bead was still not worth building.
'Superset' implies 'contains a better answer somewhere'; it does not imply that answer is worth
reaching for.

title: [P1] Market scan budget divides by 14,570 charted marketplaces but only ~951 are readable — intervals ~15x too long and 60% of the allowance goes unspent
description:
The market scan budget divides its fixed allowance by the number of markets it BELIEVES it must
cover. That number counts every charted marketplace in the era — including the ~93% we physically
cannot read — so every interval is computed ~15x too long and most of the allowance goes unspent.

THE DENOMINATOR (verified by direct read, 2026-07-31):
  adapters/persistence/market_repository.go:556 ChartedMarketSystemCounts
    Table("waypoints")
      .Where("type != ?", "FUEL_STATION")
      .Where("traits LIKE ?", "%MARKETPLACE%")
      .Where(eraScopePredicate)          <- era-scoped, but NOT player-scoped and NOT presence-scoped
  It counts every charted MARKETPLACE waypoint in the era, globally.

MEASURED, LIVE:
  scan_budget_coverage{budget="market"} ......... 14,570   <- the divisor
  market waypoints we actually hold prices for ...... 951   <- what we can really read
  ratio ............................................ ~15x

WHY THE GAP IS STRUCTURAL, NOT TRANSIENT. A market returns tradeGoods WITH PRICES only while we
have a hull standing at the waypoint. We hold ~776 probes plus ~47 trade hulls, so the readable set
is bounded by hulls, not by what is charted. Charting more of the map RAISES the divisor without
raising the readable set at all — so the invariant "the more markets we know, the less often each is
looked at" is currently applying the decay against markets that were never scannable.

THE COST, MEASURED:
  market budget utilisation ......... 0.39x of its 0.70 req/s allowance  (~60% unspent)
  markets TRADED AT in last 24h ..... median 180 min stale, p90 474 min
  markets not traded ................ median 286 min, p90 1310 min
We are trading on three-hour-old prices at the median while holding most of the scan allowance in
reserve, because the pacer is rationing against 14,570 waypoints instead of ~951.

SCOPE (implementer to confirm — hypothesis, not spec):
  Make the denominator the set the fleet can actually READ, not the set it has charted. The
  readable set is where we have (or imminently will have) a hull: parked sensing slots plus hulls in
  transit to them. sensing_slots already carries exactly this and is player-scoped.
  Candidate source: the same presence signal buyqueue/placement already uses. Do NOT simply swap in
  "waypoints with a market_data row" — that is an OUTPUT of scanning and would feed back on itself
  (scan less -> fewer rows -> smaller divisor -> scan more). Pick a presence-derived input.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE:
  - The allowance itself (0.70 req/s market, config.yaml:286). This bead re-sizes the DIVISOR, not
    the budget. Total API cost must not rise: it should stay <= the allowance, which it already is
    with 60% to spare.
  - The coverage-decay invariant. It stays — it simply starts decaying against a true denominator.
    A growing READABLE set must still lengthen intervals.
  - RULINGS #4. No money guard is touched here.
  - ARM IT. No feature flag, no default-off seam (standing Admiral order).

RISK TO SIZE BEFORE BUILDING: shrinking the divisor ~15x shortens every interval ~15x, so more
markets come due at once. The allowance still caps the rate, so total cost cannot exceed 0.70 req/s
— but the QUEUE will saturate and ordering starts to matter much more than it does today. Confirm
the priority weighting behaves under saturation before arming. Scan attention currently tracks
realized value well (waypoints grossing >5M average 40.7 scans vs 4.9 for never-traded), so the
ordering is sound; the question is only whether it holds when demand exceeds supply.

VERIFY WITH: the sp-zi2hc dashboard. scan_budget_coverage should drop toward the readable set,
per-waypoint interval should fall, utilisation should rise toward 1.0 WITHOUT exceeding it, and the
median staleness of TRADED markets should fall from 180 min. The instrument-agreement panel must
stay ~99% throughout — if it moves, the change broke the accounting.

METHOD NOTE: scope every search to gobot/ or use `git grep <pat> main`. `.claude/worktrees/` holds
20+ checkouts under the repo root; an unscoped `grep -r ... .` reads other lanes as main.
notes:
PRIORITY DROPPED P1 -> P3 ON MEASUREMENT, 2026-07-31. I filed this bead BEFORE measuring what
fresher prices are worth. The Admiral asked for that number. It does not support the bead.

WHAT FRESHER PRICES ARE WORTH: ~0.2% OF GROSS, AND THE CORRELATION RUNS BACKWARDS.

7-day study, 6,990 legs with both a planned (cached) and realized (live) unit price. planned_at is
stamped ~1.1s before realized_at, so planned_unit_price IS the cached value the solver used and
realized_unit_price is what the API charged — the gap is exactly the cost of acting on stale data.

  total loss vs plan, 7d ...... 2.1M cr
  gross, 7d ................... 1,076M cr
  loss as share of gross ...... 0.195%

By data age at execution (positive = we did WORSE than the cached price predicted):
  <15 min   3983 legs   +0.39%   +2.16M
  15-60 min 1445 legs   +0.22%   +0.76M
  1-3 h      730 legs   -0.44%   -0.47M
  3-8 h      442 legs   -0.57%   -0.35M
  >8 h       390 legs   -0.18%   -0.02M

FRESH DATA SHOWS THE WORST OUTCOMES. Stale data shows a small GAIN. The effect is not staleness at
all — it is our own market impact, confirmed two ways:

  by our trading intensity at that (waypoint, good):
    hammer it (50+ legs)   231 legs   mean data age  18 min   loss +0.44%
    moderate (10-49)      4121 legs   mean data age  39 min   loss +0.29%
    light (<10)           2639 legs   mean data age 182 min   loss -0.02%

  by order size against the market's own depth:
    order >= 1x trade_volume   2453 legs   loss +0.33%
    order <  1x trade_volume   5238 legs   loss +0.05%

We scan most where we trade most, and we move the price against ourselves when the order approaches
the market's depth. Freshness is a PROXY for 'markets we hammer', not a cause of loss. This is the
same sink-contention already known from the absorption work.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD. The divisor is still WRONG — 14,570 charted vs ~951 readable is a real
correctness defect and the reasoning in the description stands. But the PAYOFF I claimed does not.
Arming this would cut intervals ~15x, pushing market scanning from 0.39x toward 1.0x of its
allowance and consuming materially more of a 2.00 req/s account that is already saturated — to
chase at most 0.2% of gross, most of which is not staleness. That is a bad trade while shipyard
reads sit at 2-3.7x their own budget (sp-oeo0q) and trade gets 3.5% of the account.

DO NOT BUILD THIS YET. Revisit only if (a) sp-oeo0q frees real headroom AND (b) a fresh measurement
shows a staleness cost that survives controlling for order-size-vs-depth. Keep the bead for the
correctness record.

THE REAL LEVER THE STUDY FOUND, for whoever needs it: sizing orders under market depth. If every
at-or-over-depth leg had carried the under-depth loss rate (0.081%), the 7-day saving is 1.04M cr —
about 150k/day, 0.017% of daily gross. Also small. Neither of these is where the money is.

title: RelocatorMetricsCollector.Register dereferences a nil receiver field — the nil-safety test only passes because another test file happens to nil the Registry first
description:
FOUND BY THE sp-rqhzh LANE and reported rather than fixed, because touching unrelated production code in a navigation lane was the wrong call. Verified at gate; filing so it is not lost.

(*RelocatorMetricsCollector).Register() dereferences c.ticksTotal on a nil receiver. TestRelocatorMetricsShould_BeNilSafeEverywhereMetricsAreDisabled therefore PANICS under any test ordering where Registry != nil. It passes today only by accident: daemon_component_metrics_test.go nils Registry on its way out, and file ordering happens to put it first.

The sp-rqhzh lane's new navigation_stranded_jump_metrics_test.go sorts between them and exposed it. That lane scoped around the problem with a withFreshRegistry save/restore rather than change production code — correct for its scope, but it means the latent bug is untouched and the suite is ONE FILENAME away from breaking again. Any new *_metrics_test.go that sorts before daemon_component_metrics_test.go re-breaks it.

Compounding it: Register's own doc comment already CLAIMS a nil-safety it does not have, so a reader checking the contract is told the opposite of the truth.

FIX: make Register genuinely nil-safe (guard the receiver and the field), then delete the ordering dependency so the test proves the property on its own rather than inheriting it from a neighbour's cleanup.

ACCEPTANCE: the falsifier is not 'the nil-safety test passes' — it passes today. It is that the test passes with Registry NON-nil and with the neighbouring file's cleanup removed. Force that ordering explicitly in the test rather than relying on filenames.

title: Trade Flows: the REGION band's freshness marks are pinned to one zoom — 0.73x to 4x across the bands they ride
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING sp-voyz7 — deliberately scoped OUT of that fix, which addressed the
salience inversion (dark out-shouting priced) and the hue collision on traded systems.

orbs.ts computes `worldPerPx = span / PX_SPAN / REGION_PX_ZOOM` with REGION_PX_ZOOM = 3,
so every mark it draws is WORLD geometry sized for exactly one camera zoom. The marks
never rescale, so their SCREEN size is proportional to the live zoom:

    z = 1.8  (REGION_EXIT)        0.60x design size
    z = 2.2  (REGION_ENTER)       0.73x
    z = 3    (design point)       1.00x
    z = 9    (SYSTEM_ENTER)       3.00x
    z = 12   (focusSystem zoom)   4.00x   <- MEASURED: aura radius 53.9 screen px
    z = 40   (MAX_FIT_RATIO)     13.3x

MEASURED at ?band=system against live data: DARK_RING_MIN_PX (8) becomes a ~32px-radius
hoop, so the map draws ~64px dashed circles over a drilldown whose own per-waypoint
freshness rings are ~10px. Before sp-voyz7's contour fix those hoops were the loudest
thing on the SYSTEM band; they are now subordinate to the priced contours but they are
still 4x the size they were designed at.

This is band-consistent — the orbs, the labels and the threads are all calibrated at z=3
too, so nothing is inconsistent WITH ITS OWN BAND. It is called out because the REGION
band spans z in [1.8, 9.0], a 5x range, and one design point cannot serve all of it.

WORTH KNOWING, not a defect: the SYSTEM band's OWN per-waypoint 'system-freshness' rings
exist only while a system is FOCUSED (systemBand builds on focus). Reaching SYSTEM by
wheel without focusing leaves layers.fx empty — confirmed by scene-graph probe, fx
{visible:false, n:0} at REGION and n:30 only under ?band=system, which auto-focuses. So
