wheel-to-SYSTEM shows the REGION marks and nothing else.

A fix would counter-scale the freshness box per tick against cam.scale/fitScale so the
marks hold a constant screen size. Non-trivial: the dark rings and the priced contours
are BATCHED Graphics spanning the whole map, so they cannot be counter-scaled per child
without moving their centres — it needs either per-system objects (265 + 376 of them) or
a rebuild on a zoom bucket change.

title: placement declares and funds slots without consulting reachability — 774 WANTED slots (11%) target systems no hull can walk to, and coverage-ascending ordering promotes them to the head
description:
## Placement slots are declared without consulting reachability, so the fleet buys hulls for systems the walker cannot route to

Measured live, era 5, 2026-07-30 ~13:15Z, after sp-ky85o and sp-cwnwb both deployed:

- **774 of 6,959 WANTED slots (11%)** name a system that is NOT reachable through the
  walker's own effective graph (stored gate adjacency, minus under-construction edges, minus
  systems whose edge set is condemned as stale).
- **22 of 313 currently in-flight slots (7%)** already have an unreachable target. Those hulls
  are bought, assigned, and cannot arrive — they will consume a refusal every rotation forever.
- Reachability itself is HEALTHY post-sp-ky85o: from X1-CJ87, 1,077 of 1,168 systems (92%) are
  reachable, and 179 systems remain walls (down from 436 pre-fix). So this is not a
  reachability collapse — it is that the ~8% which is unreachable is never consulted when a
  slot is declared or funded.

## Why it matters

The buy queue spends real money on these. `drainCandidates` filters fills by verdict
(`inScope[slot.System]`) and orders them coverage-ascending, but neither the screen that
declares a slot nor the queue that funds it asks whether a hull could ever walk there. A slot in
an unreachable system therefore looks maximally attractive to the ordering — it has coverage 0,
because no probe has ever reached it and none ever will. **The unreachable systems are
systematically promoted to the head of the queue.** That is the same shape as sp-2rfl's finding
that 92% of the probe queue was structurally unfillable: an ordering fix that does not first
partition by feasibility promotes the impossible entries.

Each such purchase is ~59,584 cr (the era's mean probe price) spent on a hull that will sit in
BOUGHT or IN_TRANSIT indefinitely, consuming a rotation slot and a refusal budget entry every
tick, forever.

## What this is NOT

Not sp-cwnwb: that bead is fixed and working — the worklist rotates and refusals no longer eat
the accepted-action budget. Not sp-ky85o: that is fixed too, and correctly leaves genuinely-stale
edge sets condemned. This is the third, independent question: *should we have declared this slot
at all?*

Not the dominant cause of the current IN_TRANSIT backlog either — only 22 of 313. The backlog is
the action budget draining BOUGHT first, which is expected behaviour.

## Ask

1. Consult reachability when declaring or funding a placement. Cheapest version: filter
   `drainCandidates` fills to systems reachable from the fleet's own footprint, so money is
   never spent on an unroutable target. The reachability walk is already implemented
   (`nextHopToward` over `GateNeighbours`) and is a pure store read.
2. Decide what to do with a slot that becomes unreachable AFTER it is funded — the 22 in flight
   now. A hull that cannot arrive should probably release its slot back to WANTED and return to
   the idle pool rather than hold a claim forever. That interacts with `CountOwnedProbes`
   (RULINGS #4: the over-count direction is the safe one), so releasing must not let the cap
   under-count.
3. Note that reachability is TIME-VARYING: a system unreachable now becomes reachable when a
   wall refreshes or a gate finishes construction. So this must be a re-derived check per tick
   (RULINGS #2), never a durable "unreachable" flag — otherwise a transient staleness would
   permanently blacklist a system.

## Related

Gate-edge refresh runs at ~121 systems/hour with no age priority, so ~24% of systems sit past
the 24h TTL at any moment and the wall set churns. Refresh throughput is adequate in aggregate
(a full 1,168-system sweep takes ~9.6h against a 24h TTL, and nothing is past 48h), so this is
an ordering inefficiency rather than a shortfall — but it is why the wall set, and therefore the
unreachable set, is large and moving. Prioritising refresh by age would shrink both. Same
least-recently-touched pattern as sp-cwnwb and the screening sweep.
notes:
PARTIALLY SHIPPED — verified in main d3d15c89 on 2026-07-31, downgraded P1->P3.

THE MONEY HALF IS FIXED. reachableFills (buyqueue.go:1330) runs at line 1199, BEFORE coverage ranking and before sp-7qhum's yard term, and it is well built: it rejects only on POSITIVE evidence (graph.Mapped[sys] && !reachable[sys]), fails open when the graph is unknowable, and distinguishes an UNREAD system from a genuinely disconnected one — of 126 unreachable systems, 59 are merely unread (funded) and 65 are walled (refused). So the bead's central harm — 'the buy queue spends real money on these' and 'unreachable systems are systematically promoted to the head' — no longer happens. sp-7qhum's comment at buyqueue.go:1208 pins the ordering constraint explicitly: 'Feasibility first, priority second.'

THE DECLARATION HALF REMAINS. screen.go still consults no reachability when declaring a slot (grep for 'reachab' in screen.go returns nothing), so WANTED rows are still created for systems no hull can walk to. Live: 6,689 of 9,204 WANTED slots sit in systems holding no probe — though note 'no probe in system' is NOT the same as 'unreachable' and must not be reported as such. Harm is now queue bloat and a misleading backlog count, not wasted credits, which is why this is P3 and not P1.

Do not dispatch this as a money-leak fix; it isn't one any more.

title: sceneData.ts drops the whole scene on one null lane row (unguarded l.from)
description:
visualizer/web/src/nebula/sceneData.ts:43 dereferences l.from with no null guard, in a file
whose own header promises it "never throws". A null row from /api/flows/lanes therefore
throws BEFORE relevance is computed, which empties the entire scene rather than dropping
one bad lane.

Reported by the sp-fw6a2 lane, which hit it while writing a robustness test and narrowed
the test rather than widen that bead's scope. Correct call; filing it separately.

Dormant today: /lanes does not currently emit null rows, so this is latent. It becomes a
blank /trade-flows the first time it does.

FIX: guard the dereference and skip the row, keeping the file's no-throw contract. The
regression test should feed a null-bearing lanes payload and assert the scene still
renders the surviving lanes -- not merely that it does not throw.
close_reason: Closed

title: /api/flows/topology returns no homeSystem — payload has it undefined, so the gold home ring never renders
description: Found by the sp-fw6a2 lane. The live /api/flows/topology payload carries homeSystem as undefined, so the visualizer's gold home ring does not render at all. The lane deliberately did NOT add homeSystem to its relevance seed for the lattice cull because of this: if homeSystem starts resolving and lands on a system we have never traded in, its ring would float unconnected at REGION band. So fixing this has a knock-on — once homeSystem resolves, check whether it needs adding to the relevance seed in orbs.ts, or the fix will look like a new bug. Player HQ is X1-KP23-A1 per player info. Not a money path. Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: [bug] buildSceneData throws on a null systemLanes row — sceneData.ts:43 dereferences l.from before any guard, contradicting the file's own 'never throws' contract
description: Found by the sp-fw6a2 lane while writing tests; pre-existing, not introduced. visualizer/web/src/nebula/sceneData.ts:43 dereferences l.from on each systemLanes row with no null guard, so a single null row throws. The file's own header documents a never-throws contract (it is the pure snapshot adapter for the /trade-flows poll, and a throw there takes out the whole scene rather than degrading). The lane's test originally asserted the stronger never-throws property and it FAILED, so the lane narrowed its test rather than widen scope — meaning the weaker assertion is what is now pinned and this hole is uncovered. Fix: guard the row and skip it, honouring the documented contract. Not a money path. Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: [bug] /trade-flows ?band=system crashes an error boundary — TypeError 'reading push' in pixi TexturePoolClass.returnTexture; reproduces on main, makes the SYSTEM-band QA seam unusable
description: Found by the sp-fw6a2 lane, reproduces identically on main so it is pre-existing and unrelated to the lattice work. Navigating to /trade-flows?band=system throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'push') inside pixi's TexturePoolClass.returnTexture / CanvasTextPipe.destroy, tripping the React error boundary. Consequence: the documented ?band= QA seam cannot be used to reach SYSTEM band; the lane had to reach it by wheel-zooming instead, which makes automated screenshot QA of that band impossible. Likely a texture/text teardown ordering problem when the scene mounts directly at SYSTEM rather than transitioning into it. Not a money path. Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: Manual 'ship dock' container silently invisible after acceptance — daemon-side reasoning says the row should exist (even FAILED), so suspect a container-list filter or CLI response handling; needs live repro
description:
Found by the zombie-workflow lane (sp-l8p3z). NOT reproducible from code — needs live evidence, which is
why it is filed rather than fixed.

SYMPTOM: a manual `spacetraders ship dock` was accepted by the CLI but the container was never visible
afterwards — silently discarded from the operator's point of view.

WHAT THE LANE RULED OUT BY READING THE CODE: the container id is unique (no collision), there is no
dedupe in Add that would swallow it, and a claim rejection terminalizes the container FAILED after ~9s of
retries. So on the daemon side the row SHOULD have existed and SHOULD have been visible in whatever state
it reached — including a FAILED row, which is itself informative and was not seen either.

THAT POINTS DOWNSTREAM, not at the daemon: most likely a `container list` filter hiding the row (e.g.
filtering to RUNNING, or to a container-type set that excludes ad-hoc dock containers), or CLI response
handling dropping the result. Both are cheap to check once someone has the actual row.

ASK: reproduce with a manual `ship dock` on an idle hull, then query the containers table DIRECTLY for
that ship symbol and time window rather than trusting `container list`. If the row exists in the DB but
not in the listing, the defect is the listing filter and the fix is small. If the row genuinely does not
exist, the daemon-side reasoning above is wrong somewhere and that is the more serious finding.

Low priority: operator-visibility issue, no known money or throughput impact. Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: Runner self-check as defence-in-depth: a container should notice its hull claim was revoked — deliberately declined in sp-h8mbb because jump_ship transiently reassigns hulls and a false kill is worse than a phantom
description:
Surfaced by the sp-h8mbb lane and DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED there. Read that refusal before building —
the lane's reasoning is the important part of this bead.

THE IDEA: have a container runner verify, between iterations, that it still owns the hull it is flying,
and stop itself if the claim is gone. A general backstop for ANY future claim-break path, where sp-h8mbb
fixed the four call sites that exist TODAY (fleet unassign, ship reserve --force, depot re-dedication,
depot eviction).

WHY sp-h8mbb DID NOT SHIP IT, and why this is not a trivial add:
 1. It changes behaviour for EVERY container type, not just tours.
 2. It ships ARMED with no flag (standing Admiral policy), so a mistake is live everywhere at once.
 3. "Positive evidence the claim is gone" is subtler than it looks: jump_ship TRANSIENTLY reassigns a
    hull to a ship-jump-<symbol> container. A naive "my id is not on the row, therefore stop" check would
    kill a healthy container mid-jump.
 4. KILLING HEALTHY CONTAINERS IS A FAR WORSE FAILURE THAN A METRICS PHANTOM. The asymmetry is the whole
    argument: sp-h8mbb's targeted reap already removes the known harm (two live containers on one hull,
    both spending), so this backstop is defence-in-depth against unknown future paths, not a fix for a
    live defect.

ASK, if built: the check must distinguish "my claim was revoked" from "my hull is transiently held by a
sub-operation on my behalf" (the jump_ship case, and any similar). Enumerate every container type that
may transiently reassign a hull BEFORE writing the predicate — an incomplete enumeration kills healthy
work. Fail SAFE: on any ambiguity or read error, keep running (the phantom is cheap, the false kill is not).

Do not weaken the assignment/claim guards (RULINGS #4/#7). Ship ARMED, no flag. Low priority: there is no
known live path this catches that sp-h8mbb does not already cover.

title: Orphaned construction tasks survive their CANCELLED pipeline (1 READY + 1 PENDING on two dead era-5 pipelines) — inert for capital after sp-bzvu2, still a leak for any reader that does not join pipeline status
description:
Found by the sp-bzvu2 lane. Inert for capital after ed01e652, but still a leak.

Both era-5 construction pipelines are CANCELLED (FAB_MATS 1474/1600 and 0/126) and each still has a task
orphaned on it — one READY, one PENDING. Nothing cleans them up.

After sp-bzvu2 these no longer affect the capital split (the demand read is scoped to EXECUTING
pipelines, so CANCELLED wreckage is excluded by construction). But orphaned READY/PENDING tasks against a
cancelled parent are a leak: they persist indefinitely, they are visible to anything that queries tasks
without also joining pipeline status, and a future reader that forgets that join inherits the same class
of bug sp-bzvu2 just fixed.

ASK: reap tasks whose parent pipeline is CANCELLED (or otherwise terminal), at cancellation time rather
than by a sweep. Check whether any other consumer reads tasks without joining pipeline status — that
consumer, not the rows, is the real hazard.

Low priority: no live impact today. Ship ARMED, no flag.

title: ShipSelector cargo-priority is unconditional too — same defect class as sp-5jce2, second layer (currently shadowed)
description:
Sibling of sp-5jce2, filed from that lane. NOT urgent — currently shadowed in
practice (see below). Filed so the class is on record rather than rediscovered.

== THE DEFECT ==
gobot/internal/domain/contract/ship_selector.go:63-79 (ShipSelector.SelectOptimalShip)
documents and implements:

  "1. Ships with required cargo have absolute priority (even if in transit)"

  for _, ship := range ships {
      if s.hasRequiredCargo(ship, requiredCargoSymbol) { shipWithCargo = ship }
      ...
  }
  if shipWithCargo != nil { return s.buildCargoSelectionResult(...) }  // distance never consulted

This is the SAME defect sp-5jce2 fixed one layer up: any quantity of the contract
good wins the assignment regardless of the hull's distance to the SOURCE market.
It also returns Distance: 0 for that pick, so the selection log understates it.

Two additional sharp edges beyond sp-5jce2's:
  - It has no tie-break: the LAST matching ship in iteration order wins, so the
    pick is not restart-deterministic (sp-zve2q went to some trouble to make the
    coordinator-level holder pick deterministic; this layer undoes that property
    if it is ever the deciding path).
  - "even if in transit" means a moving hull, whose position is stale, can win.

== WHY IT IS SHADOWED (i.e. why this is P3, not P1) ==
SelectClosestShip has exactly ONE production caller
(run_fleet_coordinator.go, the contract fleet coordinator), and it is reached
only in the ELSE branch of the holder short-circuit. Any hull this layer would
wrongly prefer is, in practice, already handled before it gets here:
  - a PURE idle holder is named by idleContractCargoHolder first, so sp-5jce2's
    weighed rule applies to it;
  - an IMPURE holder is removed from candidates by FilterUnrelatedCargo
    (NO-CARGO-DUMP) and handed to auto-liquidation;
  - an ASSIGNED holder is excluded from candidate discovery entirely.
So the reachable window is narrow. It is not provably empty, and it will widen
the moment a second caller appears or the holder short-circuit changes shape.

== FIX DIRECTION (when picked up) ==
Mirror sp-5jce2 rather than invent a second rule: reuse
domain/contract/holder_preference.go's WeighHolderAgainstSource (or factor the
scalar dist(hull,source) comparison out of it) so both layers weigh cargo
possession against source proximity with the SAME constants and the SAME
fail-closed posture. Keep cargo priority as a preference, not an absolute.
Add a deterministic tie-break (most units, then lexicographic symbol) and stop
ranking IN_TRANSIT hulls. Whatever a passed-over holder is carrying must still
reach the delivery — sp-5jce2's deliver-held mode is the mechanism that already
exists for that; do NOT hand the sourcing run away and leave a load to be
re-bought (that is the sp-1pf0r double-load).

== CONTEXT ==
- sp-5jce2 (the coordinator-layer fix) landed on main as d53e9d97.
- Deliberately left out of that change to avoid widening its blast radius
  mid-fix; team-lead concurred and asked for it as its own bead.

title: [CHORE] gobot/docs/cli/ is behind the binary: 39 missing pages, 23 drifted — run make cli-docs
description:
Found while fixing sp-bp21s (deliberately left out of that fix to keep a P1 docs bug reviewable).

gobot/docs/cli/ is committed generated output (Makefile:286-291, 'spacetraders docs markdown'), last regenerated at f2623873. Running 'make cli-docs' against the current binary produces:
  - 39 NEW pages for commands added since (sensing, tune, contract depot tree, fleet hub, captain gag, construction override/workers, ship route/transfer/warp, universe transition, workflow bootstrap/auto-outfit/fleet-autosizer/long-haul-coordinator/shipyard-backfill, frontier status, shipyard yards, ...)
  - 23 MODIFIED pages (drifted Short/Long/flags; e.g. 'operations' still says 'resource extraction and manufacturing operations' post-712b6f66)

The diff is entirely real content — no timestamps or environment churn, so it is safe and purely mechanical.

Caveat that makes this non-trivial: cobra's GenMarkdownTree NEVER deletes pages for removed commands, so a regen alone leaves orphans behind. sp-bp21s git rm'd the four goods orphans; a regen sweep should also diff the generated set against the tracked set and git rm any other orphans, then fix inbound links (the spacetraders.md index is the usual dangler).

No CI check enforces doc-gen freshness (verified: nothing in .github/ references cli-docs or gen-cli-reference), which is why it drifted. Consider adding one.

Note captain/CLI_REFERENCE.md is NOT affected — it self-heals, regenerated at every watchkeeper startup (cmd/watchkeeper/main.go:84); sp-bp21s committed a fresh regen of it.

title: Cutover adoption's record-before-tag ordering is unpinned — its test passes with the order inverted
description:
adoptOrphanProbes must record the ledger slot BEFORE tagging the hull: tagged-but-unrecorded is unrecoverable (the adoption filter never re-finds it and CountOwnedProbes never counts it, so the cap under-reads and authorises re-buying a hull we own), while recorded-but-untagged is safe in both directions (the cap counts it, the filter re-finds it, and placement re-asserts the tag on first use).

The invariant is NOT pinned. TestCutover_AdoptionRecordsTheHullBeforeTaggingIt makes the TAGGER fail, which pins the different property 'a failed tag does not fail adoption' — and it passes just as happily with the writes inverted. Pinning the ORDER requires making the LEDGER write fail and then asserting no tag was issued.

Found by impl-b2 during sp-0gp21: the equivalent mutation probe SURVIVED on its own new pass until it added exactly that test. It fixed its own pass and deliberately left the cutover's copy alone (reviewed, pinned, irreversible code — not to be touched mid-task). Fix: add the ledger-write-fails test to the cutover's adoption. Cheap, and it converts a comment-enforced invariant into a test-enforced one.

title: Per-tour spend cap is hull-blind (25% of treasury) — confounds heavy-vs-light measurement and under-fills big holds
description: tourDefaultMaxSpendTreasuryPct=25 sizes a cumulative per-tour spend cap re-resolved from LIVE treasury at each tour's plan (run_tour_coordinator.go:70-74, :1002-1006; TourConstraints.MaxSpend, routing/tour.go:75). It takes no account of hold size, so a heavy and a light hull get the SAME credits at equal treasury. It binds when unit_price × hold_capacity > 0.25 × treasury — roughly 2.8x easier to hit for a 225-slot heavy than an 80-slot light. Worked example at 2M treasury: a 500k budget is 6,250/unit across 80 light slots but only 2,222/unit across 225 heavy slots; above that the heavy sails partly empty for BUDGET reasons rather than demand. Two consequences: (1) large hulls are systematically under-filled on a thin treasury; (2) the sp-fwk8z headline metric (credits per tour-hour, heavy vs light) is confounded exactly in the thin-treasury window when the first heavy lands — early readings must be treated as a FLOOR on the true advantage, not an estimate. Fix direction: scale the cap by hold capacity, or express it per-unit rather than per-tour. Found by impl-h1 during sp-fwk8z Task 1 recon.

title: Whitelist widening: never-scanned slots keep a stale goods projection (sp-j2efq residual)
description:
The operator rescreen (sp-j2efq) resets verdicts, which fixes whitelist edits for every market a probe has SCANNED: market_data answers GoodsAt with the FULL goods list, so the slot's whitelist projection is never consulted and the re-screen re-matches against the new whitelist correctly. That covers every PARKED market — where hulls are at stake.

RESIDUAL: a remotely-discovered, never-scanned slot keeps the projection it was written with. If the whitelist WIDENS, that slot understates its goods until a probe parks there and scans (after which market_data takes over and it self-corrects). Permanent only for slots that never receive a probe.

DO NOT fix by clearing projections — verified destructive (impl-b2, sp-j2efq): recordSlots skips existing slots so the clear never heals; screenMarkets' cache branch keys on slot EXISTENCE not on a non-empty projection, so a cleared projection reads as an authoritative 'nothing wanted here' and suppresses the very refetch meant to repopulate it; and scanner observe() skips spread observation entirely when the projection is empty, so blanking would degrade the whole rotation to the unmeasured prior.

The real fix is a screen-semantics change: treat an empty projection as a GAP rather than an answer, and let recordSlots refresh an existing slot's metadata (goods/depth) through the metadata-scoped writer. NOTE this contradicts a DELIBERATELY PINNED decision — TestScreenSystemTreatsEmptyProjectionAsAuthoritative was added in sp-k6v8z T4 fix round 2 after review — so it needs its own design deliberation, not a drive-by change. It also raises steady-state screen API cost (more refetches) and touches the sp-wgjb7 column-ownership contract.

title: Construction hull in transit at gate completion waits for next daemon boot to redirect (sp-hv4f6 follow-up)
description: sp-hv4f6 redirects construction hulls to trade at EXPANSION entry, but a hull that is IN TRANSIT at the moment the gate completes is not redirected on that pass — it waits until the next daemon boot. Bounded and recoverable (the hull is not lost, just idle-on-arrival until reboot), and the implementer judged it not closable without holding the coordinator's terminal exit against its tick-budget rationale. Needs either an arrival-triggered sweep or a cheap re-check on the terminal path. Found and flagged during sp-hv4f6 implementation.

title: Narrow TransitionSlot/UpsertSlot column sets — lost-update window vs MarkScanned (sp-k6v8z follow-up)
description: TransitionSlot performs read-modify-write whose Updates map includes spread_ewma and last_scan_at (sensing_ledger_repository.go:299-312), the same columns MarkScanned writes; sensingSlotUpdateColumns includes them too. A MarkScanned committing between a transition read and its write is silently lost (slot reads staler than truth, re-scanned early — low harm). Predates sp-k6v8z T8 but the fix rounds documented it honestly. Fix: narrow each operation Updates map to the columns it owns. Found by T8 fix-round re-review; see the SDD ledger on branch sp-k6v8z.
notes: ALSO fix the production twin: internal/adapters/parkedsensing/ship_ports.go:855-862 states the pacer and TransitionSlot write sets are disjoint — same false claim T8 fix2 corrected in the psLedger fake. Correct alongside the column-narrowing.
close_reason: Landed on sp-k6v8z branch (912840f1): Option A split, blanket UpsertSlot deleted, TransitionSlot narrowed to state/assigned_ship/purchase_yard with dirty-tracking, per-writer conflict sets are strict subsets of the old blanket list (provably no-worse). Review approved clean. Production comment ship_ports.go rewritten truthfully (both this bead's halves done).

title: Reaper for QUEUED sensing slots stranded by verdict loss (sp-k6v8z follow-up)
description: DrainBuyQueue's candidate read drops MARKET/YARD slots in non-IN_SCOPE systems, so a slot already claimed to QUEUED when its system's verdict changes is never retried and never released — stranded forever (correctly never bought, but leaked). Needs a cheap reaper: periodic sweep transitioning QUEUED slots in non-IN_SCOPE systems back to WANTED (or removing them). Found in sp-k6v8z T5 review (minor #9). Natural home: the reconcile loop's screen sweep or a small dedicated pass in T8's coordinator; deferred out of T5 to keep the money-task scope tight.
close_reason: Landed on sp-k6v8z (a2061697 + 2f598fcf): bounded reaper reverts QUEUED->WANTED for MARKET|YARD slots in non-IN_SCOPE systems, clearing the stale yard preference; runs between screen sweep and drain so a verdict written this tick is honored this tick. Review approved clean (0 Critical/Important). Beyond-brief: the cap bounds WRITES not candidates — verified that a candidate-counting budget would let alphabetically-early in-scope stalled claims permanently starve stranded ones, reopening the leak.

title: Operator rescreen verb: whitelist edits mid-era require verdict+slot-cache invalidation (sp-k6v8z follow-up)
description: The parked-sensing screen stamps durable verdicts (NO_WHITELIST never re-screened) and slot rows cache a whitelist-PROJECTION of market goods. Both are correct under the spec axiom that the 12-good whitelist is era-invariant — but a mid-era config.yaml [sensing] whitelist edit silently understates goods lists (widening) or can strand PARKED hulls in systems that would re-verdict NO_WHITELIST (rotation). Needed: an operator rescreen action (CLI verb or tune-triggered) that resets verdicts to PENDING and clears/refreshes slot goods projections for the live player. Until it exists, whitelist edits mid-era are documented as requiring this manual invalidation. Context: sp-k6v8z T4 fix round 1 re-review, new-Important adjudication in the SDD ledger.
close_reason: Landed on sp-k6v8z (4998a801 + 3e8ffdc6): 'spacetraders sensing rescreen' resets sensing_systems.verdict to PENDING for the live player via one column-scoped, era-scoped UPDATE, so the sweep re-judges every system against the current whitelist. Review approved clean; the money guard is STRUCTURAL (different table — sensing_systems has no assigned_ship column), verified three ways. Scope deliberately narrowed to verdicts: clearing slot goods projections was demonstrated destructive (permanent blanking + suppressed refetch + dead spread observation) and the residual is filed as sp-ysg8h. Six doc/comment sites now name the verb and state the residual honestly.

title: Dead-era sensing_slots ghost rows accumulate against probe_cap — needs era-boundary sweep (sp-k6v8z follow-up)
description: CountOwnedProbes is deliberately era-agnostic within a player (fail-closed, RULINGS #4 — blessed in sp-k6v8z T3 review). Consequence: if a player_id ever survives an era boundary with stale PARKED sensing_slots rows, planning reads (era-scoped) go blind to them while the cap read keeps counting them — ghost hulls throttle probe buying forever. Today player_id rotates per era so the cliff is theoretical; it becomes real if player identity ever persists across resets. Owner needed: either an era-boundary sweep clearing prior-era slot rows for the live player, or cutover-time reconciliation. See T3 review minor #5 in .superpowers/sdd ledger (branch sp-k6v8z).
notes: RELATED CONSEQUENCE of the same premise (found during sp-k6v8z extension fix wave, and independently by the whole-extension review): the adoption passes' waypoint-occupancy guard is era-SCOPED while the write it guards is not. SlotsByState applies 'era_id = ? OR era_id IS NULL', so a prior-era slot row is invisible to the occupancy index — but UpsertSpareSlot's conflict target is (player_id, waypoint_symbol) with no era column, so it would still clobber that row. Same tagged-but-unrecorded bug class as the same-era collision closed in sp-0gp21, reached across an era boundary. Requires the premise this bead already describes: prior-era slot rows surviving for a live player. Fix alongside whatever this bead decides — an era-boundary sweep would remove the rows and moot it; if instead rows are retained, the occupancy index needs to read era-agnostically.

title: config.yaml.example documents the trade working_capital_reserve default as the 50k immutable floor; it is 150k
description:
gobot/config.yaml.example:281 reads:
  # working_capital_reserve: 0   # 0/absent => the flat immutable floor (sp-05glh; no proportional pct knob)

The absent/0 default for the trade engine is NOT ImmutableReserveFloor (50k). run_tour_coordinator.go:911-913 resolves absent to defaultWorkingCapitalReserve, which aliases common.NonContractWorkingCapitalFloor = ImmutableReserveFloor + 100_000 = 150000 (sp-q8bon made the 50k-150k band contract-exclusive).

config.yaml.example is the only TRACKED surface documenting this knob (config.yaml itself is gitignored, gobot/.gitignore:82), so this stale line is the sole reviewable documentation and it is wrong by 3x.

Same stale-50k claim was just corrected in the live config.yaml comment under sp-4chpz.

title: rate_limit_wait histogram undercounts since the epic deploy — telemetry only
description: Post-deploy the summed spacetraders_daemon_api_rate_limit_wait_seconds_count reads absurdly low (441 in 94min while scouts alone wrote 225 market rows in 15min => >=0.25 req/s of GetMarket). Scanning/trading unaffected; the LimiterPressure EWMA (pressure rotation input) may share the seam — verify Observe still fires per request at doWithRetry and whether a T4/T8 change moved RecordRateLimitWait behind a condition. Telemetry-grade, but ActiveShare depends on the EWMA, so a dead Observe would freeze share at 1.00 (fail-open, still worth fixing).

title: Warp top-off docks against a locally-KNOWN transit and crashes the container
description: 4 unrecoverable crashes over 2 days (of 417 total): 'command execution failed: [warp of X: warp top-off at Y failed:] failed to dock for refuel: cannot dock while in transit'. This is the LOCAL domain guard (ship.go:410 EnsureDocked) refusing a dock while local state correctly shows IN_TRANSIT — i.e. the warp/route flow attempted a top-off dock without first waiting out a transit it KNOWS about. Distinct from sp-y2u4j (server-side 4214 on a phantom position, fixed by adoption): here the caller has the truth and ignores it. Fix shape: the warp top-off path (ExecuteWarpRoute refuel) waits out a locally-known transit (waitForCurrentTransit) before docking, mirroring executeSegment step 1. Small blast radius, evidence in daemon.log 'cannot dock while in transit' crash lines.

title: Test/hygiene sweep from the era-4 cold-start audit
description:
Three small items found during the era-4 cold-start audit. None are defects; all are cheap.

1. LISTSHIPS REGRESSION PINS. sp-pc8cl's meta.total termination was measured correct for 1-ship, 2-ship and the 20/21 page boundary, but only the 0-ship case is pinned by a test. Behaviour is right; the coverage is missing. ~10 lines in the existing harness. Worth having because the failure mode if it ever regresses is a SHORT ship list, and reconcileFleetToLive treats a successful response as authoritative and DELETES every ships row missing from it — a truncation reads downstream as 'sold', not 'stale'.

2. FRESHSIZER MANNING-FLOOR ASYMMETRY. MinHulls > 0 is checked in releaseOutOfScopePosts but not in retireMarketlessPosts. Not currently reachable as a bug (retireMarketlessPosts has an unconditional empty-census guard), but the two paths should agree.

3. ENGINEERING §6 VIOLATIONS, cosmetic and pre-existing: run_tour_coordinator.go:1933 carries a bare bead-id in a source comment; gofmt -l is dirty on gobot/internal/application/bootstrap/commands/run_bootstrap_muc5x_test.go and run_bootstrap_scaled_gate_test.go. All three predate the era-4 lanes and were deliberately left untouched so no lane swept unrelated files into its diff.
acceptance_criteria: ListShips boundary cases pinned; the two freshsizer paths agree on the manning floor; the three §6 items cleaned

title: 206 idle probes burn 21% of the hard 2 req/sec API budget via /my/ships pagination — no CLI verb exists to retire a hull, and no resync-scope control
description:
ADMIRAL-ESCALATED 2026-07-25 (API at 100%, twice). The account API limit is a HARD ~2 requests/second. Measured live: 90 calls in 45s = 2.0 req/s. We are pinned at 100% by definition, not leaking — so the only fix is reducing DEMAND, and the single largest avoidable consumer cannot be touched from the CLI.

=== THE WASTE (measured, per-endpoint deltas over 45s) ===
  List Ships      19 calls/45s  (21%)
  Get Waypoint    19 calls/45s  (21%)
  Get Jump Gate   14 calls/45s  (16%)
  Get Market       8 calls/45s   (9%)
  Get Agent 5, Refuel 4, Orbit 4, Navigate 4, Get Construction 4, Dock 4, Jump 2, Get Shipyard 1
/my/ships PAGINATES 20 PER PAGE. Fleet census: 206 FRAME_PROBE + 24 heavy + 21 light + 1 frigate + 1 explorer = 253 hulls = ~13 pages per full resync instead of ~2. So List Ships costs ~6.5x what the revenue fleet alone would cost.
CRITICALLY: all 206 probes currently report assignment_status='idle'. I stopped scout_post_coordinator (it was running 156 scout_tour + 43 scout_reposition containers, 650 log lines/5min) to relieve the limiter — live wait/call fell 3.72s -> 0.15s and containers dropped 245 -> 44. The probes now do NOTHING, yet they still cost ~11 of every 13 List Ships pages. That is ~21% of the ENTIRE API budget spent enumerating hulls that are not working.

=== WHY THE CAPTAIN CANNOT FIX IT ===
1. NO RETIREMENT VERB. 'spacetraders ship --help' exposes only 'sell' (sells CARGO, not the hull). 'fleet remove' only unsets dedicated_fleet — the hull still exists and still paginates. There is no scrap / decommission / sell-ship path. The SpaceTraders API does expose ship scrapping at a shipyard; we have not wired it.
2. NO RESYNC SCOPE CONTROL. The periodic 'ship resync' pulls the whole fleet. There is no knob to resync only revenue hulls, or to widen the resync interval.
3. NOT TUNABLE. TRADE_FLEET_COORDINATOR reports 'has no live-tunable knobs yet'. Only freshsizer and frontier are tunable, and I verified their knobs do not touch this: I set max_probes_per_system 8->2, reach_mode 3->1, discover_scan_balance 40->1, and BOTH max_probe_fleet 140->100, and demand stayed 290 with probes stuck at 206 — because the sizer is UNDER-supplied (demand 290 > supply 200) so nothing ever sheds. The caps prevent growth; they cannot shrink.

=== ASKS, IN VALUE ORDER ===
1. SHIP RETIREMENT PATH ('spacetraders ship scrap' or 'shipyard sell'). Retiring ~180 idle probes takes the fleet 253 -> ~73 hulls = ~13 pages -> ~4, freeing roughly 15-17% of the total API budget permanently, and recovering scrap credits. This is the single highest-value API action available and it is currently impossible.
2. RESYNC SCOPE / CADENCE CONTROL: resync revenue hulls (trade/long-haul/contract/warehouse) frequently and probes rarely, or make the interval tunable. Cheaper than (1) and does not destroy assets.
3. Make the probe fleet size responsive to whether scouting is RUNNING. Right now stopping scout_post_coordinator leaves 206 probes alive and idle forever — the sizer's demand model does not know its consumer is stopped.

=== CONTEXT / TRADE-OFFS ALREADY TAKEN ===
* Scouting is currently STOPPED (scout_post_coordinator STOPPED, reversible via container start). Market freshness is decaying: of 17,837 market_data rows, 4,013 are <75min and 5,124 <180min. The planner's own caps are 180m RESTRICTED / 480m WEAK, so lanes will start dropping out of the snapshot within hours. This is a deliberate, temporary trade for API headroom and must not be left indefinitely.
* Trade was NOT harmed by stopping scouts: net +3.15M/60m on 9.8M gross, 18 tour-runs, zero strands. This corroborates the standing finding that we were scanning 113 systems while the planner can only reach ~8 (~240 in-scope rows of 17,837).
* I briefly moved 5 heavies trade->long-haul to relieve sink saturation, then REVERTED it: long-haul's 8-12-hop pathfinding is API-expensive (Get Waypoint + Get Jump Gate = 37% of calls) and it returned only +79,256 over 40 min on 9 hulls. Long-haul is back to 4, trade to 24.
=== RELATED === sp-1cuy6 (horizon widening — makes the scanning we pay for reachable), sp-kefkw (unblocks its measurement), sp-ekt5z, sp-vz8hj.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-06: SPLIT -- premise dead, capability gap real. Downgraded P1->P3 and re-scoped. THE PREMISE IS GONE: the 253-hull / 206-probe fleet exists nowhere. Staging has 33 probes with 0 GENUINELY idle (all 32 employed via sensing_slots.assigned_ship -- note the derived ships.container_id check reads them as idle and is wrong). The prod-name DB holds 5 hulls total: 3 probes, 1 frigate, 1 light freighter. At 33 hulls ListShips costs ~2 pages, not ~13, and the pagination overhead itself was separately reduced by sp-pc8cl defect 1. The 21%-of-budget waste was a property of THAT FLEET. ASK #1 IS STILL REAL: there is NO ship-retirement path. Lead-verified under several names rather than one: no 'Use: scrap|retire|decommission|sell' command for a ship anywhere in the CLI; 'ship sell' is explicitly 'Sell cargo from a ship' (ship_cargo.go:277); the 8 CLI files matching 'retire' are about retiring a PLAYER off contracts and a comment about a retired coordinator -- a substring superset, not a verb. HONEST LIMIT stated by the triaging lane: it measured the FLEET SIZE that drives the burn, not the live API burn itself; there is no current per-endpoint measurement to compare against the bead's 45-second sample. title: Make the arb-horizon lock assert its own precondition, so the bound cannot outlive its reason
description:
POLISH on sp-1cuy6's delivered lock (merged 2dc9adbf). Small, optional, test-only.

TODAY'S SHAPE: two paired tests in run_trade_route_coordinator_multisystem_test.go — one locking the arb scanner's 1-hop discovery horizon, one locking the hop-blindness of the cross-system surcharge that JUSTIFIES that horizon. They are coupled by a COMMENT: the second test's failure message tells the reader that teaching the surcharge real distance is the signal the horizon may be revisited.

THE IMPROVEMENT: make the coupling MECHANICAL rather than documentary. Have the horizon test open by asserting its own precondition — that the surcharge is still hop-blind (near-lane rate == far-lane rate) — and fail FIRST with an explanatory message if it is not. Then the bound cannot outlive its reason: the moment someone teaches the surcharge gate distance, the horizon test fails pointing AT the horizon as the thing to reconsider, instead of silently continuing to enforce a number whose justification has evaporated. A future reader also cannot mistake the bound for an unexplained constant.

ORIGIN: the sp-1cuy6 lane started exactly this after gating — extracting a shared crossSystemCircuitRates() helper returning (near, far, sameSystem) so both locks share ONE definition of the probe — but left it INCOMPLETE and NON-COMPILING in its worktree (the second test still referenced the old local 'lane'/'capacity' after the helper was extracted; build failed at :263 'no new variables on left side of :=', 'undefined: lane', 'undefined: capacity'). The broken WIP was discarded; main carries the complete, green, committed version. This bead exists so the idea is not lost with it.

SCOPE: extract the shared three-lane rate probe (near / far / same-system control) into one helper used by both locks, and add the precondition assertion at the top of the horizon test. Test-only; no production change; no deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Both arb locks share ONE definition of the cross-system rate probe. The horizon test asserts the hop-blindness precondition FIRST and fails with a message naming the horizon as the thing to revisit if the surcharge becomes distance-aware. Proven falsifiable by mutating the surcharge to be distance-aware and observing the precondition fire BEFORE the horizon assertion. gofmt/vet clean; go test ./... -race green. Test-only, no deploy.

title: Travel hop loop: outer-loop per-hop live-position reload vs a NON-coordinator mid-relay preempt (sp-1bme8 Part-3 deferred half)
description: sp-1bme8 fixed the probe-buyer desync at its root: Part 1's atomic ClaimShip exclusive journey claim prevents a SECOND COORDINATOR from moving a claimed hull mid-reposition, and Part 3's in-loop jumpHop re-anchor fixes the single-actor cooldown-ride self-jump (a jump success mis-reported as 409 re-firing from the just-arrived position). REMAINING GAP (belt-and-suspenders, low priority): the shared travel.go plan-once/no-reload hop loop (run_trade_route_coordinator_travel.go) still trusts the once-computed path across hops, so a NON-coordinator preempt that moves a claimed hull mid-journey (e.g. captain 'ship reserve --force' or a manual re-task during a multi-hop relay) could still desync a hop. FIX: reload the hull's live position before each outer-loop hop and, if not on the expected path[i-1] gate, re-plan the remaining path from the true position via the SAME jumpPath resolver (reuse, no forked logic) or abort cleanly. DEFERRED from sp-1bme8 because the shared travelShipRepo test harness returns the DESTINATION ship on every FindBySymbol, so a per-hop mid-flight reload collides with it and needs ~10+ production-critical arb/trade/scout travel tests reworked to supply per-hop positions — high churn in a load-bearing shared loop for a case Part 1 already prevents for the reported bug. Only materializes under a manual force-preempt mid-relay. CONSTRAINTS: RULINGS #2 restart-idempotent, #4 guards untouched, #13 captain-gate, ONE shared route resolver (reuse jumpPath). RELATED: sp-1bme8 (root fix, DEPLOYED), sp-ry741 (long-haul Guard-0 bound, DEPLOYED).

title: Long-haul reposition pathfind deadline (defense-in-depth): bound PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify's construction-verify, map timeout->ErrUnroutable->skip lane
description: FOLLOW-UP to sp-ju9pn/sp-0o9ub (option 1, defense-in-depth). sp-0o9ub killed the reposition fetch-through storm (pathfind ~20min->11s), so this is belt-and-suspenders, not load-bearing. GOAL: a hard bound on the long-haul reposition PATHFIND so no future slowness (e.g. API rate-limit on the chosen-path construction probes) can silently stall a hull. PLACEMENT (critical): bound ONLY the pathfind — gategraph PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify's RepositionPath + the ~6 gateUnderConstruction (GetWaypoint) probes, which returns the path BEFORE the flight. Do NOT bound RepositionToWaypoint as a whole — it also runs the multi-hop FLIGHT (jumps + cooldowns, legitimately many minutes); a whole-reposition deadline would false-kill legitimate flights (new bug). MECHANISM: context.WithTimeout(ctx, ~90s) around the verify loop inside PathWithinJumpsStoredThenVerify (or the RepositionToWaypointStoredThenVerifyWithinJumps caller, scoped to the pathfind step only); on deadline -> return gategraph.ErrUnroutable so the worker's EXISTING fallback (run_longhaul_arb_worker.go:218-224) skips the lane to the next reachable one. RULINGS #4 intact (skip is before any buy; hull empty=zero spend). ISOLATE to the long-haul resolver — do NOT touch the shared strict Path/PathWithinJumps (MaxJumpPath=5) or the flight machinery. ACCEPTANCE: a fake whose construction probe blocks -> the resolver returns ErrUnroutable within the budget (not indefinitely) and the worker skips the lane; a warm/fast path is byte-identical (returns the path, no deadline fired); the multi-hop FLIGHT is NOT bounded by this (a legit long flight completes). build/vet/gofmt/-race green. RELATED: sp-ju9pn (closed, this is its option 1), sp-0o9ub (root fix), sp-yginc.

title: [depot] Recovery-claim sets container_id but NOT dedicated_fleet → depot hull returns untagged after a bounce (poach-gap)
description: ROOT CAUSE (observed live, deploy of 473b8460): on daemon restart, a depot container recovers and re-claims its ship via attemptClaimShip's operation branch -> ShipRepository.ClaimShip, which sets ships.container_id but does NOT set ships.dedicated_fleet. The launch/grow path sets the tag separately via AssignFleet; the recovery path does not. RESULT: TORWIND-58 came back with container_id=warehouse-TORWIND-58-... (container owns + tasks it, 'Warehouse hull registered and ready') but dedicated_fleet='' — a claimed-but-untagged hull. Consequences: (1) the by-tag operational tally under-counts (read 13 vs the true 14); (2) LATENT POACH RISK — an untagged idle hull with capacity matches the contract scaler's isReclaimable (DedicatedFleet()=='' && IsIdle && !IsInTransit && CargoCapacity>0), so if the depot ever RELEASES it, the contract scaler grabs it. This is the same operator-intent-drift poach class sp-0ms61 closed for MANUAL buys and that launch/grow closes via AssignFleet — the RECOVERY-claim path is the remaining hole. Reconciled operationally this session via 'fleet add --operation warehouse --ship TORWIND-58' (tag now set), but it recurs on every bounce until fixed durably. FIX options: (a) in ClaimShip, when the claim is an operation-keyed DEPOT claim, also ensure dedicated_fleet==operation (single funnel — all claim paths inherit it; note RULINGS #3 single-writer AssignFleet/ClaimShip boundary); OR (b) the recovery rebuild path re-runs AssignFleet after a successful recovery-claim (mirror launch). (a) preferred (one funnel, matches where frigate-claim-guard sp-3tsjz already lives). Deterministic/restart-idempotent (#2); no money-guard change (#4); armed, no flag.
acceptance_criteria: A depot container that recovers on restart and re-claims its ship leaves ships.dedicated_fleet == the container's operation (warehouse/stocker), not empty. A non-depot recovery is unaffected. RED-first (recovery-claim leaves tag empty before fix), -race green.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-06: CODE CLAIM VERIFIED TRUE, BUT UNREACHABLE -- downgraded P1->P3. ClaimShip's update map (gobot/internal/adapters/api/ship_repository_claims.go, ~line 130-148) sets exactly: container_id, assignment_status, assigned_at, released_at, release_reason, assignment_owner, assignment_reason, version -- and NO dedicated_fleet. Lead-verified. The recovery-claim leaves the tag empty, precisely as filed. THE DERIVED-VS-DECLARED IDENTITY TRAP: one identity field is set and the other is not, so any check keyed on the wrong one is blind. UNREACHABLE TODAY: the depot subsystem has NEVER RUN on staging -- 0 warehouse/stocker/depot containers ever. Unlike sp-ph7t this is DORMANT, NOT DELETED: warehouse and stocker remain registered command types (command_factory_registry.go:193,208) and domain/contract/depot is intact, so the defect is latent and will bite whenever depot is next used. Checked for a live instance: exactly one hull is claimed with an empty tag (TORWINDSTG-2 on scout_tour), which is NOT an instance -- scout tours are not expected to carry a fleet tag. FIX IS CHEAP: a one-line addition at a single funnel, whenever depot work resumes.

title: [depot] Warehouse grow seats LADEN trade hulls holding non-depot cargo → dead warehouse capacity (TORWIND-58 = 225/225 FOOD)

acceptance_criteria: A warehouse hull holding non-supported inherited cargo clears it (or is not seated laden) so it can accept depot deposits; a warehouse hull holding only supported depot goods is untouched. RED-first, -race green.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-06: UNREACHABLE -- downgraded P1->P3. The depot subsystem has NEVER RUN on staging: 0 warehouse/stocker/depot containers ever (lead-verified). Dormant, not deleted -- both remain registered command types. CODE CLAIM NOT VERIFIED: the triaging lane looked for warehouse-grow cargo hygiene and found jettison logic only in the contract worker/pool paths, not the grow picker -- suggestive but NOT conclusive, and it said so rather than asserting. title: AUDIT (reference, no action): contract subsystem knob map — 7 components / 32 knobs [Admiral knob-simplification]
description:
⚠️ AUDIT / REFERENCE ONLY — NO ACTION, NO CUTS AUTHORIZED. Do NOT implement anything from this bead. This is a factual map of the contract subsystem, captured for the Admiral's knob-simplification review (the ~385-knob audit). Every component and knob STAYS unless the Admiral explicitly rules otherwise — in particular, idle-arb is kept (Admiral: "idle-arb trading is important"). No keep/remove/simplify verdicts are made here.

Source: read-only code + git + ~4000-line live-log window, player 4 era torwind, 2026-07-22 (contract-debug subagent).

## CONTRACT SUBSYSTEM MAP — 7 components, 32 knobs

### 1. Core loop — negotiate -> source -> deliver -> fulfill (run_fleet_coordinator.go + run_contract_workflow.go)
- Does: negotiates one contract at a time (game rule: one active/player), sources the good (in-system warehouse if stocked via inventory-first Lane D, else cheapest home-system market), delivers, fulfills for reward.
- Active: YES, continuously. (Live example: worked cmrupci6t FERTILIZERS via TORWIND-13, market-sourced.)
- Knobs (1): min_home_contract_workers = 6 (LIVE) — reserve floor of undedicated home haulers for unbuffered-good sourcing.

### 2. Contract Scaler (sp-9le3x)
- Does: standing coordinator sizing the dedicated 'contract' fleet — ramps one hull at a time (reuse-before-buy: reclaim an idle undedicated cargo hull, else buy) up to a ceiling, guarded by the 200k cushion.
- Active: YES — running since 19:52:20; ramped TORWIND-19/-13/-D in.
- Knobs (1 LIVE + 3 HARD): contract_fleet_max_hulls = 2 (LIVE); DefaultContractFleetMaxHulls = 2; ContractCushion = 200000; tick = 900s.

### 3. idle_arb
- Does: between-contract arbitrage harvest — an idle dedicated hull runs guarded one-shot buy-low/sell-high legs within a leash of its hub, gated by margin/profit/fuel floors + a lane mutex.
- Active: YES, evaluating ~every 90s. In the observed window it assessed many candidates and launched 0 legs (verdicts: 338 unprofitable, 149 leash, 144 reserved, 3 contract-good). Opportunistic — fires when a hub-local lane clears the profit floors; none did in that window. NOT dead weight.
- Knobs (14): disabled=false, reserve_hulls, hub_radius=250, leash_radius=150, max_leg_seconds=480, max_spend, min_margin, margin_verify_pct, interval_seconds=90, blacklist=[ELECTRONICS], recovery_hold_seconds=1200, min_net_profit_per_unit=100, net_profit_pct=20, fuel_cost_per_unit=35.

### 4. pre_positioning (sp-dchv Lane C)
- Does: haul-to-storage — deposits recurring contract goods into an in-system warehouse ahead of demand (from a demand miner + a running warehouse op) so future contracts source from the buffer.
- Active: NO in window — Enabled default OFF; needs a warehouse op + demand-miner + non-zero capital ceiling; 0 firings. (Config resolved on the tour coordinator.)
- Knobs (8): enabled=false, top_n, min_recurrence, capital_ceiling_pct=0 (parked), min_savings_per_unit, buy_leg_savings_per_unit, allowlist, blocklist.

### 5. source_preposition (sp-1ef0)
- Does: latency shaping — during a delivery leg, nudges an idle hull toward the market that sources the contract's next same-good delivery (via a pre-position hint in fleet rebalancing).
- Active: NO in window — default ON, but only fires via RebalanceContractFleet, which the running coordinator loop doesn't invoke and no rebalancer container is running; 0 firings.
- Knobs (2): disabled=false, confidence_threshold=0.8.

### 6. auto_liquidation (sp-39oi)
- Does: parked-hull self-clear — a hull parked holding cargo unrelated to the active contract gets a one-shot liquidation worker that sells the strand (jettison only below a value floor) so it re-enters candidacy.
- Active: YES — fired live, cleared TORWIND-D's stranded cargo at 00:13:58. (Also the path that recovers orphaned over-fetch cargo, cf. the sp-1pf0r stall.)
- Knobs (2): disabled=false, min_jettison_value=0 (sell-only, never dump).

### 7. depot reserve / buffering
- Does: contract depot — a warehouse-buffered hub with dedicated warehouse/stocker/delivery hulls; a contract whose destination the depot owns routes to the co-located delivery hull and withdraws from the local warehouse buffer instead of long-haul sourcing (depot routing + distributed delivery-hull selection + durable registry + inventory-first withdrawal).
- Active: PARTIAL — a depot IS configured (X1-UM5-I56: 2 warehouse, 1 stocker, 1 delivery-hull; warehouse-TORWIND-11 + stocker-TORWIND-18 running), but in the window: 0 depot-route matches, 0 "BUFFERED at hub", 0 warehouse withdrawals — the live contract was market-sourced. Infra deployed; contract-buffering path not exercised in the window.
- Knobs (1 LIVE): depot_buffer_min_source_distance = 25 — a good whose nearest external source is within 25 units is never buffered.

title: Bootstrap heartbeat pauses ~8min during the fault-2 frigate-positioning nav (blocks the reconcile loop)

title: player register --new orphans the agent on local-persist failure (API-created agent + token lost)
description:
Observed during staging mint testing: 'player register --agent X --new' created the agent on the SpaceTraders API successfully, then FAILED to persist locally (the staging DB schema was missing migration 042's eras.contracts_graduated column). Result: the agent exists on the API but has NO local record, and its token was only echoed to stdout ('SAVE IT NOW'). In an automated or token-masked flow the token scrolls past unsaved, so the agent is ORPHANED — unrecoverable, callsign burned (TORWIND_DEV5 was lost this way; clears at the era reset).

THIS instance's trigger was a stale ad-hoc staging DB schema; the official 'make build ENV=staging' + deploy/staging/up.sh runs AutoMigrate and avoids it. But the robustness gap is general: ANY local-persist failure after a successful API Register orphans the agent and loses its token.

FIX DIRECTION: on persist failure after a successful API Register, write the returned token to a recovery file (e.g. deploy/staging/run/<agent>.token) BEFORE returning the error, or retry the persist, so an automated mint never silently leaks an agent. Low priority — only triggers on a persist/schema fault, which the official env avoids. Repro: register --new against a DB missing a recent migration. Epic sp-difa.

title: Jump-set ship cooldowns arm no clear-timer -> 60s sweeper clears every one, logging false 'stuck cooldown' spam (fleet-wide, cosmetic + minor DB churn)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (systematic-debugging, economy-analyst 2026-07-19, CONFIRMED by grep): jump_ship.go:375,379 call ship.SetCooldown(cooldownUntil) after a successful jump and persist it, but arm NO clear-timer. ScheduleCooldownClear is called ONLY from ScheduleAllPending (ship_state_scheduler.go:198,216 — the startup one-shot). The repo Save path wires SetArrivalScheduler (arrivals auto-arm) but there is NO cooldown-scheduler equivalent. So every post-startup jump cooldown is cleared solely by the 60s RunSweeper (SweeperInterval=60s), whose query (ship_repository.go:2245-2249: cooldown_expiration IS NOT NULL AND <= now()) clears it and logs 'Sweeper: Cleared stuck cooldown for <SHIP>'. Trade haulers run multi-system circuits (routine jumps -> routine cooldowns), so this fires fleet-wide, forever: measured ~220 clears/1.2h post-restart, 213 of them sweeper (only 7 timer-based).

IMPACT: COSMETIC. The 'stuck' label is a misnomer (they are un-timer-armed, cleared 0-60s after expiry by the designed safety net) + minor DB churn (SaveWithRetry per clear per 60s). NOT a dispatch bug: VERIFIED no trade-dispatch path gates on ship CooldownExpiration — run_trade_fleet_coordinator.go partitionTradeFleet (:491-509) gates on DedicatedFleet=='trade' && !ReservedByCaptain && !IsAssigned && !IsInTransit; cooldownRemaining (:519-532) reads the coordinator's OWN relaunch backoff (assignment.ReleasedAt()), never the ship game-cooldown; the tour executor self-rides leftover jump cooldown (run_tour_coordinator.go:902, sp-wc5h). DB snapshot: of 11 cooldown-holders 9 were actively trading — cooldowns cluster on ACTIVE/jumping hulls, the opposite of a stuck-dispatch signature.

FIX DIRECTION (not implemented): arm a clear-timer on the write path — call ScheduleCooldownClear from the SetCooldown persist (or add SetCooldownScheduler on the repo Save, mirroring SetArrivalScheduler) so cooldowns clear on-time; and/or downgrade the sweeper 'Cleared stuck cooldown' line to DEBUG (it is not stuck). Files: jump_ship.go:374-380, ship_state_scheduler.go:126-217, ship_repository.go:2245-2249, daemon_server.go:670-675. Surfaced during the sp-nxrt tempo validation; cross-ref epic sp-g9td (not a $/hr lever — standalone hygiene).

title: Scout coordinators must ONLY claim scout-class ships (allowlist), never freighters
description: Root cause found live 2026-07-17: the scout_post/frontier coordinator grabbed 8 undedicated HEAVY_FREIGHTER hulls (TORWIND-2B/2C/2D/2E/37/39/4B/54) and ran scout_tour on them, and 1 more (19) on warehouse duty — while 71 PROBE hulls sat idle. Heavy freighters are the fleet's highest-value earners; using them as scouts/warehouse is a large opportunity cost. FIX: coordinators that claim ships for scouting/warehouse must exclude FRAME_HEAVY_FREIGHTER (and prefer FRAME_PROBE, then FRAME_LIGHT_FREIGHTER) unless no cheaper hull is available. Manual mitigation applied (fleet assign --fleet trade on all 9), but undedicated future/freed heavies remain grabbable until the eligibility filter is fixed in code/config.
notes:
AUTHORITATIVE RULE (Admiral, 2026-07-17): scout coordinators should ONLY grab scout-class ships. This is an ALLOWLIST, not a denylist — eligibility = scout-class only (FRAME_PROBE / satellite / explorer role). Exclude ALL freighters (heavy AND light), command, hauler, etc. Not 'exclude heavies'; rather 'include only scouts'. Acceptance: a scout/frontier coordinator seeking a ship to claim filters candidates to scout-class frames/roles and never selects a non-scout hull even when idle scouts are scarce (it should wait or request more probes, not borrow a freighter).
CORRECTION 2026-07-17: the 'heavies scanning' trigger was a MISDIAGNOSIS from the corrupt ships.frame_symbol column (new DB-corruption bug filed). The 8 hulls on scout_tour were actually FRAME_PROBE (verified live API: fuel/cargo cap 0) — the scout coordinator was CORRECTLY claiming scout-class ships. NO actual violation occurred. Keeping this only as a low-pri defensive invariant per Admiral's stated rule; it is NOT an active bug. Real root cause = DB frame corruption.
SEQUENCING + FLEET-KILLER (orchestrator, 2026-07-17): the 8 hulls this bead calls 'heavy freighters scouting' (2B/2C/2D/2E/37/39/4B/54) are the SAME 8 PROBES that sp-wn8u proves the DB mislabels as FRAME_HEAVY_FREIGHTER. The coordinator actually grabbed PROBES (correct). BLOCKED BY sp-wn8u: if this scout-class allowlist keys on the corrupt ships.frame_symbol, it will REJECT the coordinator's own mislabeled probes → scouting starves (guard-enumerate fleet-killer). Fix sp-wn8u first; then implement this allowlist keyed on the reconciled/LIVE frame, never the raw DB column. Enumerate the rejected class against live before shipping.

title: Scout-post manning watchdog: re-man a fully-manned standing post producing zero scan telemetry for N cycles (sp-iupr Bug 1c)
description: Deferred from sp-iupr. The freshsizer fix makes the SIZER robust to telemetry-starved posts (frees stranded probes instead of hoarding), but does NOT re-man the post — the ROOT cause of a manned probe producing no telemetry is a manning-loop concern the sizer can't see (it reads only the freshness census/CycleSamples, not ship nav-state or tour health). A starved post's probe may be repositioning (sp-s232 relay), blocked ('no markets to scan yet — leaving unmanned'), or park-backed-off (sp-py4n RespawnParkedUntil). FIX (in the scout-post reconciler run_scout_post_coordinator.go): detect a standing post that IsFullyManned() yet has produced zero new scan telemetry for N consecutive cycles, and take corrective manning action (re-relay / un-park / swap the hull), emitting a captain event. The manning analogue of the sp-iupr sizing fix. Repro seed: X1-ZY16 (3 mkts) was pinned at 8 probes producing no telemetry for 10+ cycles.
notes: SHIPPED 7faf6dab (deployed). Scout-post manning watchdog: fully-manned standing post + census MarketCount>0 + OldestAgeSeconds breaches FreshnessTarget + age-not-improving for N cycles => teardown (sp-tzqv seam) + same-tick re-man; N-cycle debounce (mutation-verified) + K-correction backoff (event persists after teardown stops). Deferred captain event scout.post_manning_stalled. Knobs manning_stall_cycles=4 / manning_stall_correction_cap=3 live-tunable (tune --operation scoutpost). Completes the sp-iupr Bug-1c manning-loop root cause: sizer (sp-iupr) frees stranded probes, watchdog re-mans the silent post. nil freshness-reader = safe no-op (partial rollout safe).

title: Frontier gap-2: distinguish never-scanned from genuinely-marketless (Scanned flag) to stop barren re-scout
description: Follow-up to sp-dc50 (shipped 804b8e32). Its gap-2 fix REMOVED the buildExpansionQueue 'charted-but-0-market -> skip' entirely, which unblocked the frozen frontier but does NOT distinguish a system whose markets were SCANNED-and-empty from one NEVER-scanned. Consequence: a genuinely-barren system (charted jump-gate but no marketplace anywhere) gets re-declared + re-scouted each cycle (declare -> sweep-once -> no market found -> post retires -> re-declare). Rare in practice (systems usually have markets somewhere) but wasteful. FIX: add a 'markets/waypoints scanned' signal to ExpansionCandidate (distinct from KnownMarkets>0) so buildExpansionQueue keeps a never-scanned reachable system as a scout target but DROPS a scanned-and-genuinely-marketless one. Re-establish the guard the old TestFrontier_ChartedMarketlessSystemNotDeclared encoded (renamed to ...ButUnscannedSystemIsScouted in sp-dc50) for the scanned-empty case. a24592 (sp-dc50 crafter) + hop2-lane3 both flagged this as the proper refinement. Source: sp-dc50 gap-2 shortcut 2026-07-15.

title: Wire depot delivery-hull rebalancing: recency-weighted per-hub arrival signal + scheduler (sp-9j9c #3 fast-follow)
description:
The pure PlanRebalance decision mechanism already exists (domain/contract/depot/rebalance.go, shipped in sp-9j9c). This is the runtime WIRING that makes it fire. economy-analyst-approved fast-follow (st-wisp-phc5r); Admiral requires rebalancing.

TWO PARTS:
(a) Per-hub arrival signal. Incremented where routeContractViaDepot routes a contract to a hub; persisted across restart. HARD POLICY REQUIREMENT (economy-analyst): the signal MUST be RECENCY-WEIGHTED — a sliding window over the last ~N contract-cycles OR an EWMA with a half-life of a few cycles — NOT a cumulative all-time counter. Rationale: a cumulative count freezes the hull distribution to the historical average and never adapts (a hub hot early stays 'hot' forever), which defeats demand-driven rebalancing. A cold hub must release coverage; a newly-hot hub must attract hulls.
(b) Periodic scheduler: reads idle delivery hulls + current hub arrivals -> PlanRebalance(RebalancePolicy) -> issues one NavigateShip per returned Migration.

POLICY VALUES (economy-analyst): MaxMigrations=3, MinArrivalGap=2 (>=2-contract demand gap before a hull migrates, so single-contract noise never churns). The recency window length / EWMA half-life is economy-analyst's to set.

COORDINATION w/ sp-dw0h (design together): both touch the contract coordinator's idle-hull acquisition path. sp-9j9c #2 positions idle delivery hulls AT their hubs but the durable ANTI-POACH RESERVATION that keeps them there between serialized contracts lives in dw0h's idle-hull guard — that guard must recognize depot delivery hulls as reserved, else the rebalancer places a hull and the contract coordinator immediately drafts it away. 

OWNER SPLIT: economy-analyst owns policy (recency half-life, cap, gap); shipwright owns code. Blocked-by nothing; do AFTER economy-analyst live-verifies sp-9j9c #1+#2 compression per cluster.

title: goods_factory + scout containers log 'No ship_symbol in metadata, cannot signal completion' on every clean exit
description: MINOR DEFECT (mentioned as 'cosmetic, no action' in a shipwright mail 2026-07-11 instead of filed — the pattern the Admiral called out). Factory-coordinator and scout-assignment containers emit '[WARNING] No ship_symbol in metadata, cannot signal completion' on every normal completion. It is benign (the work completed) but: (a) it is a WARNING level for a non-warning condition, (b) it fires constantly (every chain tick / scout reset), adding log noise, (c) 'cannot signal completion' hints a completion-signal path is silently no-op'ing for these container types — worth confirming nothing downstream depends on that signal. FIX: pass the owning ship_symbol (or mark these container types as ship-less by design and downgrade to DEBUG/skip).
notes: MERGED to main: d84ce38f8ae6d0b667900d28bf39a10704693bd2 (squash). numstat: container_runner.go +21/-1, container_runner_shipless_completion_test.go +128/-0 (new). ROOT CAUSE: signalCompletionWithStatus (container_runner.go:698) logged WARNING 'No ship_symbol in metadata, cannot signal completion' whenever a container reached the completion-signal path with no ship_symbol. That path publishes a WorkerCompletedEvent — a single-ship worker's signal to its parent coordinator, keyed on ship_symbol and routed by coordinator_id (coordinator subscribes via SubscribeWorkerCompleted(containerID)). Coordinator/dispatcher container types (goods_factory/manufacturing coordinator, scout-fleet-assignment, siting, ...) are ship-less BY DESIGN and reach clean exits with no ship to name AND no coordinator awaiting — so the WARNING cry-wolfed on every clean exit/chain-tick/scout-reset. The codebase already encodes this truth at createShipAssignments ('No ship_symbol in config = no ships to assign, e.g. scout-fleet-assignment') and treats it as a silent no-op; the completion path was the inconsistent one. FIX CHOSEN (option 2 — ship-less by design, not populate-the-symbol): discriminate on coordinator_id presence. coordinator_id set + no ship_symbol => a coordinator IS awaiting but the ship can't be named => genuine should-have-signalled-but-couldn't => stays WARNING. no coordinator_id + no ship_symbol => ship-less coordinator clean exit => downgraded to DEBUG. Robust across all current/future coordinator types (no brittle type allowlist). Pure log-level change; no behavioral or config surface (no RULINGS#5 knob needed — nothing to escape from). TDD: 4 pins in new test file (2 RED->GREEN: scout-fleet-assignment + manufacturing-coordinator emit no warning; 2 guardrails: coordinator-awaiting-but-no-ship still warns, ship-worker publishes+no-warn). Full go build + go test ./... green (2607 tests, 93 pkgs).

title: Auto-sync waypoints on in-system NavigateRoute cache miss instead of loud-failing
description: Split from sp-6zgs (e). Current behavior already meets the acceptable bar: validateWaypointCache (navigate_route.go:253-281) fails LOUDLY-RECOVERABLE — names the system + waypoint + the exact recovery ('sync waypoints from API'). This bead is the UX enhancement: auto-sync so no manual step is needed. TURNKEY DESIGN: in NavigateRouteHandler.loadAndEnrichWaypoints (navigate_route.go:188), after the cache-first GetGraph(ctx, systemSymbol, false, playerID), check the enriched waypoints; if the ship's current location is missing OR (the destination is missing AND shared.ExtractSystemSymbol(destination)==systemSymbol), retry ONCE with GetGraph(ctx, systemSymbol, true, playerID) force-refresh and re-enrich. EXCLUDE cross-system destinations — a foreign-system waypoint will never appear in the origin system's graph, and that case is the sp-6zgs (f) design error already refused at the scout-markets assignment seam. The trigger is narrow (fires only on a genuine in-system cache miss), so normal navigation is byte-identical and the shared-nav blast radius is bounded. TDD note: NavigateRouteHandler has no existing unit-test harness — either extract a pure shouldForceRefreshWaypoints(waypoints, origin, destination, system) helper and pin it, or stand up the first handler harness (shipRepo/graphProvider/waypointEnricher/routePlanner/routeExecutor mocks).
notes:
Merged to main: 5cc92b9cf375fed8d3d6a269ee1dc094849a0172 (squash). numstat: navigate_route.go +44/-0, navigate_route_test.go +83/-0.

APPROACH: Pure-helper (bead's PREFERRED path — NavigateRouteHandler's collaborators waypointEnricher/routePlanner/routeExecutor are concrete *structs, not interfaces, so a handler harness is heavy; skipped per bead). Extracted shouldForceRefreshWaypoints(waypoints, origin, destination, systemSymbol) bool and wired it into loadAndEnrichWaypoints AFTER the cache-first GetGraph(...,false,...)+enrich: on true it retries ONCE with GetGraph(...,true,...) force-refresh and re-enriches. All-present -> false, so normal navigation is byte-identical (no extra API call). At-most-once (no loop). validateWaypointCache still fires its loud-recoverable error if the force-refresh does not recover the waypoint.

CROSS-SYSTEM EXCLUDED (proof): helper returns shared.ExtractSystemSymbol(destination)==systemSymbol only when destination is absent; a foreign-system dest yields prefix != system => false. Pinned by test case 'cross-system destination missing -> DO NOT refresh (excluded)' (origin present, dest=X1-ZZ99-C3, system=X1-AB12 => want false) PLUS 'origin present, cross-system dest present -> no refresh'. Origin-missing dominates (returns true before the dest check) is pinned separately incl. with a cross-system dest.

CONFIG KNOB: none added (bead granted judgment: 'trigger is narrow enough it may not need one'). Rationale: the branch only fires on a genuine in-system cache miss — exactly the path that today hard-fails at validateWaypointCache — so there is no path where it degrades working navigation; blast radius is bounded to the already-failing case and one API call at most. Navigation package had zero config coupling; a knob would have needed constructor/boot threading, expanding blast radius against the bead's lean.

title: Tour reposition: chain-topology ranking nudge — prefer destinations that import the departure system's exports (look-back second-order)
description:
Second-order follow-up to sp-ed4i (look-back loading, merged 177c491). Look-back now LOADS the departure system's exports for the chosen destination's imports before the reposition jump, but the destination is still CHOSEN purely by its own fresh empty-hull arb (planAtCandidate ranks candidates on freshProfit). A chain-topology nudge would additionally weight a candidate by the look-back MANIFEST VALUE it can absorb (departure-export -> candidate-import), so the hull prefers rotating to systems that IMPORT what the current system EXPORTS (source->sink->source chains) over radial out-and-back grounds. title: No template defines who closes a consult bead after it is answered — fully-answered consults accumulate open forever
description: Surveyor finding from consult-bead sampling (8 open consults sampled, 4 read in full: sp-pof6, sp-spen, sp-5bmq, sp-zgbk). Root cause traced through templates: shipwright/prompt.template.md:47-51 (Consults section) explicitly instructs 'you do NOT close it' when answering a consult, deferring instead to mailing+nudging the captain. captain/prompt.template.md's own closing instruction ('close with outcome when observable') is scoped ONLY to decision-type beads ('Every non-trivial choice: bd create <decision> -t decision, link consults (bd dep add <decision> <consult> -t related), close with outcome when observable') — it links a consult to a decision but never instructs closing the linked consult itself. title: Watchkeeper/gate hardening batch: backoff, double-log, liveness, silent crash-drop, latent edges
description: From a full read-only code review of the captain engine (surveyor-triaged; shipwright verifies each before fixing). Six distinct TIER-3 (watchkeeper/gate) items: (1) Delivery backoff can't back off a dead channel while any interrupt is queued — wake.go:187-192 caps retry at 2xpoll when hasUnmailedInterrupt, so a total gc/bd outage with a standing interrupt retries every ~60s forever; the exponential/15-min ceiling never engages. Fix: full backoff even for interrupts when preflight/SessionAlive shows the channel fully down. (2) Every failed wake logs twice — supervisor.go:224-226 calls noteDeliveryFailure ('WAKE DELIVERY FAILING') AND returns the same err ('tick error'), diluting the grep signal. Fix: return nil once noted. (3) SessionAlive over-eager — gc.go:84 treats any non active/running state as dead -> double-spawn risk on transient startup. (4) nil captainRecorder silently drops crashes — captain_recorder.go:28 returns early when rec==nil with no startup warning; a mis-wired recorder makes container.crashed (and all synthetic events) vanish invisibly (same class as sp-vvnw). (5) Spurious credits.threshold wake on credit-source switch — supervisor.go:159-160 prevCredits baseline; refreshCredits (agentcredits.go:64) can flip ledger<->live between polls, firing a false interrupt wake on the first live read after fallback/restart. (6) Gate hardcodes literal 'main' — worktree.go:110-113 (merge-base --is-ancestor main); any repo whose default branch isn't 'main' has every merge refused as stale (latent). Citations from code review, surveyor spot-checked. TIER-3 — human sign-off.
notes: LIVENESS FALSE-POSITIVE flapping observed 2026-07-09: (1) watchkeeper logged 'STANDING SESSION DOWN captain' while the captain process (claude-fable-5, pid 93157) was ALIVE with tmux up (derrick socket) — nearly triggered an unnecessary manual relaunch. (2) bd flipped sp-s8qq AND sp-snmb to OPEN with false 'session died' notes (x2 each) while those agents were alive + completing. The liveness/orphan-reconciliation detector emits false-DOWN/false-died. RELIABLE liveness = process(ps)/file-mtime/git checks, NOT the watchkeeper 'session down' or bd 'session died' signals. Fix the detector's false-positive (it caused agent-death misdiagnosis + a near-miss captain relaunch this session).

title: friction: (s85) `construction start` is a SILENT FOOTGUN: it creates the pipeline row (pipeline_type=CONSTRUCTION) + tas
description: friction: (s85) `construction start` is a SILENT FOOTGUN: it creates the pipeline row (pipeline_type=CONSTRUCTION) + tasks and returns "Status: PLANNING", but spawns NO coordinator container and returns NO container id — the pipeline sits INERT at 0.0% forever with nothing executing it. The executor is the MANUFACTURING coordinator, which adopts pipelines ONLY at startup recovery (`FindByStatus(PLANNING,EXECUTING)`, `run_parallel_manufacturing_coordinator.go` recoverState at ~line 200) and NEVER re-polls the table in its main loop. So a construction pipeline created AFTER the coordinator booted is never seen. The undocumented required sequence is: `construction start` FIRST, THEN bounce `operations --manufacturing` so recovery adopts it. Candidate fix: either (a) `construction start` should signal the running coordinator to re-scan (or spawn its own coordinator), or (b) the coordinator loop should periodically re-poll for new PLANNING pipelines, or at minimum (c) `construction start` should WARN "no coordinator running — start operations --manufacturing to execute this pipeline". Nothing about the success output hints the pipeline is inert.
