title: Align era-scoping across the screen's yard queries (ListProbeYards + ListHeavyYards)
description:
screen_ports.go's ListProbeYards and ListHeavyYards are both era-AGNOSTIC, while their sibling shipyard_inventory read CheapestPricedYard applies eraScopePredicate. The screen and the heavy-reserve path therefore answer 'which yards sell this hull' under different era rules, and a stale pre-reset shipyard_inventory row can plan a quartermaster at a yard that no longer exists in the live era.

Raised during sp-fwk8z T3 review as Minor 4 against ListHeavyYards alone; the implementer correctly declined to align only that one, since doing so would trade a cross-package inconsistency for a worse one INSIDE screen_ports.go, where ListProbeYards sits beside it equally unscoped. The pair should be aligned together in a dedicated pass.

Decide deliberately: era-scope both (consistent with CheapestPricedYard, but a system whose yard was only ever scanned in a prior era loses its quartermaster candidate), or document both as intentionally era-agnostic (a shipyard is a map fact, not an era fact — the argument the waypoint repository already makes for trait reads). Either is defensible; the current split is not. A comment at ListHeavyYards already names the sibling and cites this finding.

title: Quartermaster coverage: a system with separate probe and heavy yards covers only the probe yard (sp-fwk8z T3)
description:
Spec sp-fwk8z §6 says quartermaster placement 'extends to heavy-selling yards'. As shipped in T3, ListHeavyYards is a FALLBACK: a system with no probe-selling yard gets a quartermaster at its heavy yard, but a system with BOTH gets one only at the probe yard. Consequence: heavy purchases at that second yard are not instant — they need a courier trip or the buyer picks a different yard, which may not be the cheapest.

Reading §6 strictly would mean one quartermaster per distinct yard WAYPOINT rather than per system. That is a real spend increase (~23.5k per extra yard, across every system holding two distinct yards) and a change to a documented invariant (one YARD slot per system), so it was correctly not made unilaterally during T3.

DEFENSIBLE AS SHIPPED: heavies are capped (default 5) and heavy-selling yards are plentiful (16 known at the current era), so the cost is one non-instant heavy buy per affected system, not a missed one. Decide deliberately whether the instant-buy guarantee is worth per-waypoint coverage.

Two T3 narrowings that should survive whatever is decided: probe yards keep PRECEDENCE (fallback, not override), and ListHeavyYards has NO bare-shipyard fallback — claiming an unscanned SHIPYARD-trait waypoint sells heavies would assert something unobserved.
notes: WIDER THAN FIRST FILED (sp-fwk8z T3 review). The heavy-yard fallback is close to UNREACHABLE in production, so §6's coverage benefit is thinner than the tests suggest. ListProbeYards already falls back to ANY charted SHIPYARD-trait waypoint in the system, sorted alphabetically (screen_ports.go:217-229) — so len(yards)==0, the only condition under which ListHeavyYards is consulted, requires the system to have no charted shipyard-trait waypoint at all. But a priced heavy row implies a scanned shipyard at a charted waypoint. In practice the YARD slot goes to the alphabetically-first shipyard and the heavy yard earns a quartermaster only by coincidence. The tests cannot catch this: fakeCatalog returns yards and heavyYards independently and never models the bare-trait fallback firing. So this bead is not only about the separate-probe-yard case — heavy-yard coverage is largely notional as shipped. Whatever is decided here should also decide whether the probe-yard bare-trait fallback should yield to a PRICED heavy yard.

title: Probe cap under-reads by one while two orphan hulls share a waypoint (sp-0gp21 residual)
description:
sensing_slots is keyed on (player_id, waypoint_symbol), so the table can hold at most one row per waypoint. When two orphan probes sit at the SAME waypoint, adoption records one and skips the other (correctly — the alternative, which shipped briefly, left the first tagged-but-unrecorded and unrecoverable). The skipped hull stays scout-tagged, untagged by sensing, and recoverable — but it is invisible to CountOwnedProbes, so the probe cap under-reads by one for as long as the pair is co-located. Under-counting is the money-unsafe direction: it authorises buying one probe we already own.

BOUNDED: at most one extra probe per co-located orphan pair, and every purchase still passes the full dynamic-floor + cap stack. It clears when the first hull is put to work and moves.

WHY IT IS NOT NEGLIGIBLE: it does not clear on its own schedule. An orphan is by construction driven by nobody, so co-located orphans stay co-located until something else moves them — which is exactly what the code's original comment ('will usually have moved on by then') wrongly implied would happen; that comment has been corrected.

CLOSING IT NEEDS ONE OF: different accounting (a row-counting cap structurally cannot represent two hulls at one waypoint), or the ability to relocate a hull — which is fleet management the adoption pass deliberately is not. Both are design decisions, not fixes. Raised by impl-b2 during sp-0gp21 round 2; nothing built.
notes: SCOPE WIDER than first filed (sp-0gp21 round-2 re-review). The under-read is not limited to two orphans sharing a waypoint. Round 2 correctly extended the occupancy guard to HULL-LESS rows, so an orphan standing on a WANTED or QUEUED placement is also skipped — and there the clearing story from the original filing does NOT apply: there is no 'first hull' to be put to work. Worse, when the drain later fills that placement the row becomes BOUGHT/IN_TRANSIT/PARKED and stays, so occupied remains true and that orphan is skipped — and uncounted by CountOwnedProbes — indefinitely. Confirmed nothing else picks it up: DockedProbeAt filters dedicated_fleet IN ('', sensing_parked), so a scout-tagged orphan is invisible to the buy queue's buyerAt path too. The skipping BEHAVIOUR remains correct (the alternative is the destructive rewrite round 2 closed); it is the residual that is larger than first described.

title: Cutover's one-shot adoption may be redundant now that adoption retries every tick (sp-0gp21 follow-up)
description:
With sp-0gp21's adoptStrandedProbes running every tick, the cutover's own one-shot adoption is FUNCTIONALLY redundant: the retry runs later in the SAME tick (cutover ~:786, adoption ~:825), uses the same predicate plus an extra already-recorded skip, and re-reads ListActive so 'orphaned' is still judged against surviving posts.

It is NOT safely removable as-is. Removal changes two reviewed, pinned behaviours: (1) TestCutover_RetryIsIdempotentOverAPartialFirstTick pins that an adoption ledger-write failure holds the screen back so the cutover retry stays armed — losing that is ARGUABLY an improvement, since today a persistent adoption failure re-runs the entire cutover every tick, but it is a named pinned behaviour and the change must be deliberate; (2) the cutover's adoption is unbounded while the retry is capped, so a large first-cutover backlog would spread over several ticks instead of landing at once.

The question this bead must answer: is losing the done-mark gate on adoption failure acceptable? Identified by impl-b2 during sp-0gp21; nothing was removed.
notes: SEVERITY/ANSWER MOVED by sp-0gp21's cutover gate (review of Task 13): with the retry now explicitly standing down while the cutover is pending, the cutover's own adoption is NO LONGER redundant coverage — it is the ONLY adoption during the cutover window. Removing it would strand every hull adopted in that window until the next tick, and if the retry's gate is written as !cutoverPending, removal also changes the cutover's own completion semantics. The answer has moved toward DO NOT REMOVE. The original redundancy analysis was written against the ungated version and no longer applies.

title: cutoverScreen: record PENDING row for error-screened systems so screenSweep can recover partials (sp-k6v8z follow-up)

title: FOLLOW-UP (documented): normalize operation_type naming into one documented enum (kill spaces)
description:
DOCUMENTED FOLLOW-UP from the transaction-category audit (2026-07-14) -- captured, NOT active work (Admiral: leave R3 as documented follow-up). The higher-value taxonomy cleanup is on operation_type (the real second dimension consumers depend on), NOT category.

Spaces break IN(...) filter copy-paste + read badly as metric labels; inconsistent with category/type SCREAMING_SNAKE. Root: values from 3 sources -- normalized (operation_context.go:83-102), hardcoded (purchase_ship.go:404 'fleet expansion', cargo/refuel 'manual'), raw pass-through (operation_context.go:99-101).
PROPOSED: normalize to one convention (SCREAMING_SNAKE), eliminate spaces (fleet expansion->FLEET_EXPANSION, fleet rebalancing->FLEET_REBALANCING), document the enum, reconcile the dead arbitrage/factory normalizer cases (F4).
COST (why it is a follow-up, not a quick win): needs a ~195-row backfill (fleet expansion 136 + fleet rebalancing 59) OR dual-read, PLUS edits to the hardcoded producers + every detector/dashboard filter matching these strings. NOTE: the new sp-miqt ledger counters also carry operation_type as a label -- a rename shifts those label values (rate() is unaffected across a rename: old series stop, new start). A mutation probe that SURVIVES can be the most useful result — it may mean the property is UNOBSERVABLE, not merely untested, and the right response is to DELETE the test (sp-ehf4x, 2026-08-06). Case: a test asserted that precondition skips stay outside a timed window. Hoisting the timer above those skips did not break it, because the skip path sends no command, so the mock clock never advances and elapsed is 0 either way. No fixture could ever make the hoisted timer misreport. The test could not fail, so it was pure coverage theatre — it was deleted and the code comment rewritten to state the placement as SCOPE rather than as a tested guarantee. General rule: when a probe survives, ask THREE questions in order — (1) did the mutation actually apply (witness check), (2) does the mutation genuinely change behaviour or is it a no-op in disguise, (3) is the property observable AT ALL by any fixture. Only after all three is 'missing coverage' the answer. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test, because it reports coverage that does not exist.

ZSH DOES NOT WORD-SPLIT AN UNQUOTED VARIABLE, so a probe loop written as 'go test $PKGS' passes ONE BOGUS PATH instead of N packages. go test then fails at SETUP and prints NO --- FAIL lines, so the harness reads 0 kills — which looks like 'mutation survived' or 'nothing to kill', not like a broken command. MEASURE OVER THE SWEEP INTERVAL, NEVER A SHORT WINDOW. Burned three times in one era reporting numbers that evaporated. Get Waypoint only fires when a topology sweep touches a stale set, so ANY window shorter than the sweep interval reads near zero regardless of whether a fix worked — a 3-minute post-restart window showed a fake 96% cut. Get Shipyard bursts when scouts cluster: a 150s window read 21% of budget where the 44-minute lifetime read 5.8%. Trading is lumpy: a 15-minute window read 18.5M/hr where the 3-hour window read 3.98M/hr. RULES: grade a deploy over >=30 minutes or one full sweep, whichever is longer; prefer cumulative-since-daemon-start or DB-derived counts over metric deltas; and for efficiency questions compute CALLS PER USEFUL UPDATE (API count vs distinct rows actually written) rather than raw rate — that ratio is what exposes redundancy and it is stable across windows.

Contract-depot delivery-fleet config (deployed HEAD 07d24665): pin the contract coordinator with 'contract start --dedicated-ships <hulls> --standby-stations <waypoints>'. --dedicated-ships reserves those hulls EXCLUSIVELY (claim-filtered out of every other pool) — this IS the 'cluster-exclusive mode', no separate flag; it stops the general idle-hauler grab. --standby-stations makes idle dedicated hulls HOME to the nearest listed waypoint instead of the coordinator's default post-delivery 'balance to a market' — that homing is what ENFORCES delivery-hull<->warehouse co-location. Contracts are SERIALIZED (one active at a time) => exactly ONE delivery hull per depot is needed; SelectDeliveryHull always dispatches deliveryHulls[0], so a 2nd delivery hull per depot is inert. Unowned-destination contracts (no depot) fall to distance-pick over the dedicated fleet and can borrow a depot hull off-station (self-corrects via standby homing under serialization).

API-budget analysis (2026-07-17): satellite/scan overhead (Navigate 24% + Get Market 21% of daemon API requests) is NECESSARY sensing, NOT reclaimable waste. Path to 10M cr/hr = cr/REQUEST efficiency (heavies 1.7x cargo/call + 2.96x/hull, fill holds, kill dead legs), not hull count. Scan lever is trade-relevance-weighted ALLOCATION, not cutting.

git reset --hard on the SHARED main checkout is catastrophic-adjacent: it reverts tracked .beads/issues.jsonl, which makes bd abandon its real dolt db and silently fall back to a FRESH EMPTY .beads/embeddeddolt/<db> shadow. Symptom looks like total data loss (bd show -> 'no issue found', bd list -> a handful of issues), but the real data is SAFE — dolt lives in .beads/dolt/<db> and is gitignored, so reset never touches it. RECOVERY: cp -Rp .beads/dolt/<db> .beads/embeddeddolt/<db> to repoint bd's embedded data-dir at the real db; verify with bd list; jsonl re-exports from the good db on the next bd read. Collateral: reset also reverts OTHER sessions' uncommitted tracked state (e.g. captain/state/*.md) — unrecoverable if never staged. NEVER git reset --hard a shared checkout; abort a bad merge with 'git merge --abort' or restore only your own files.

A pinned oracle is blind to the terms derived FROM it. When a field is re-anchored to ground truth (ledger balance_after = AuthoritativeBalance / data.agent.credits), asserting THAT field cannot detect a mutation in the values derived from it: a sign flip on amount left 'balance_after == live credits' still TRUE, so the headline reconciliation test SURVIVED it. Proven by sp-shq63 mutation testing. Whenever an assertion targets a field pinned to an authoritative source, add separate assertions on the derived terms (amount sign, balance_before). Same shape: dropping AuthoritativeBalance killed only 1 of 7 tests, because append and re-anchor are indistinguishable whenever the reconstructed chain happens to agree with truth — force a DISAGREEMENT (out-of-band movement) or the mutation lives.

Grafana/SQL moving-average panels: a widened-then-clipped window MUST be two CTEs (buckets -> smoothed via AVG OVER -> outer WHERE clip). Cold-start contract-op sizing: haulers BEFORE warehousing, and the money guard is often the real binding constraint. Before recommending ANY contract-op infra (warehouse/stocker/depot-delivery) OR any hauler buy at cold-start, check the cheapest HOME-YARD cargo hull price vs the 25%-per-hull guard (RULINGS #6 = 25% of treasury). A frigate-only op earning to clear that guard is CORRECT behavior, not a bug/deadlock — do not weaken the guard (RULINGS #4/#6) and do not stand up warehouses to fill the vacuum. The autosizer's treasury_floor gate (price+200k <= treasury-50k floor) is stricter still, so arming autosizer early-scaling yields no hull until treasury is well above price. Staging: Stage A sole frigate (desired infra = NONE); Stage B +1 cargo hull once treasury clears the guard w/ cash-cushion intact; Stage C +1 (cap ~2 single-system) only if source-leg is multi-tranche-bound; Stage D warehouse+stocker ONLY when the serial one-contract clock saturates AND recurring-good demand history exists; depot-delivery clusters only for FAR-destination contracts + co-located hulls (sp-u9xa). The capacity reconciler OVER-DESIRES warehouse/stocker/depot at cold-start because its PLAN gates on FleetPerHullCrHr (vast headroom at 30-70k/hr/hull) but does NOT encode staging-order; treat its cold-start warehouse/stocker/depot desire as a false signal (also currently inert: tier-1 reuse blocked by the sp-r6f1 cargo-floor guard, tier-4 capital proposal-gated). Binding constraint on contract $/hr at cold-start = treasury clearing the 25% guard on the cheapest cargo hull; the lever is TIME (net-$/hr growth) + a cheap scan for a neighbor yard under the ceiling (yard price ~8x variance). See [[economy-analyst-contracts-uncontrollable-cycletime-only]]. (torwind-2026-07-19 sp-u5nh consult; refit yard prices/treasury each era.)

Contract SINKS demand a CONCENTRATED, stable good-set — a universe-invariant MECHANIC (validated identically across era-3 full-week 455 contracts + era-4): mean ~3.7 distinct goods per sink (vs ~38 goods in the universe), top-3 goods = ~88% of a sink's demand. The same waypoints keep demanding the same products; geometry transfers across eras (names/prices do NOT). CAUSAL/prequential coverage (could you have pre-stocked the good from that sink's history?) RAMPS as good-sets saturate: top-5-goods/sink hits ~80% overall / ~91% mature (Q3+); stock-all ~98%. Cold-start Q1 is only ~50% (still learning each sink's set) — do not mistake a small-sample cold-start read (~55%) for the mature ceiling. IMPLICATION: destination PRE-STOCKING (depots / the pre-stock mesh) is HIGH-coverage (~90% at maturity), not the marginal ~25% a few-hub depot suggests. Renewal-reward model (era-3, serial engine 100% back-to-back): a full nearest-delivery mesh (cover ALL sinks — throughput lives in the SLOW long-tail, NOT the fast high-value sinks) yields ~3.6-6x GROSS contract $/hr vs baseline; lean value-ranked subsets are near-worthless (1.2x). Bounded by the 80-cargo cap (warehouse-hull depth is the dominant cost) + API budget + source-supply. Full design WIP: [[economy-analyst-contract-delivery-sizing-recurring-hubs]], bead sp-q1ptw. Method: parse contracts.deliveries_json (dest+good+units), per-sink concentration + prequential coverage + renewal-reward $/hr.

Orchestration lessons (2026-07-09, learned the hard way). (1) LIVENESS SIGNALS FLAP — the watchkeeper's 'STANDING SESSION DOWN <role>' log and bd's 'session died' notes are FALSE-POSITIVES (observed: captain logged DOWN while its process pid 93157 was alive; sp-s8qq + sp-snmb flipped to 'session died' x2 while their agents were alive AND completing). To check if an agent/session is alive use: process (ps for the claude/fable proc), file-mtime on its worktree (find -mmin -8), or git branch commit recency — NEVER the 'died/down' signals. Filed on sp-0d1g. (2) FRESH SPAWN vs RESUME — fresh Agent-tool subagents run autonomously to completion; a teammate RESUMED via SendMessage after it went idle/done tends to idle again after claiming instead of running the bead through (fullhold-fix did this). For a NEW bead, spawn FRESH (Agent tool) rather than SendMessage-reusing an idle agent, unless the warm context is essential. (3) OVERLAP OWNERSHIP — when two agents build the same primitive, decide ownership ONCE (by who already has the work + best design + reliability) and STICK; flip-flopping (I reversed 3x chasing a liveness ghost) wastes agent effort. The pre-dispatch mtime check is what actually prevents the merge-collision. (4) GENUINE deaths DO happen — API 'Response stalled mid-stream' yields an explicit idle_notification failureReason; those are real: relaunch fresh + salvage the dead agent's uncommitted worktree diff (git -C <wt> diff).

Admiral doctrine (2026-07-10, via harbormaster mail st-wisp-blax): market FRESHNESS = the CIRCUIT TIME of the probe tour covering it — there is no 'poll rate' (probes are travel-paced, scan-on-arrival). Fresher data => SPLIT the system into N disjoint partitions (N probes) — never scan faster. A post's --freshness is a pacing CONTRACT: fast circuits pause at circuit boundaries (zixw), undersized coverage surfaces as freshness-actual > target. Never reimplement a rule the GAME SERVER enforces. A local copy of a server-authoritative rule is a bug by construction: every divergence between the copy and the real rule is a defect, and it rots silently the next time the server retunes. Diagnostic: if the server already REFUSES the action pre-flight with no side effect, our local predicate is not load-bearing and must not be the thing standing between a hull and a loss. ORIGIN (2026-07-24, warp): ensureWarpFuelSafety locally predicted warp fuel and refused legs. It carried TWO independent errors, both fail-OPEN and stacking — (1) it measured origin.DistanceTo(destination) over waypoint coords, which are SYSTEM-RELATIVE, for an inherently CROSS-system leg; (2) it hardcoded FlightModeCruise, ignoring the hull's real flight_mode, so a BURN hull was under-estimated 2x. Meanwhile the live server refused both bad legs itself, pre-flight, hull unmoved, returning STRUCTURED data (code 4203, fuelRequired/fuelAvailable) — strictly better than any local estimate. THE RULE: prefer REACT over PREDICT. Let the server refuse, parse its typed error, and act on its numbers. Keep only what the server cannot do for you: ORCHESTRATION (refuel/top-off before the action) and ONWARD VIABILITY (the server checks you can afford THIS leg; it does NOT check you can ever leave the destination — a hull can be legally warped into a system with no fuel market and an under_construction exit gate, and stranded). Corollary: 'gate_connected' in gate_edges does NOT mean traversable — always check under_construction on the escape gate, not mere adjacency.

STANDING DIRECTIVE (2026-07-06, Admiral, emphatic, while going AFK): NEVER depend on the Admiral or block on their input. This is an autonomous fleet/city system that MUST run fully unattended. Do NOT queue decisions, design rulings, gate approvals, memory gates, reload/deploy choices, or 'which option?' questions to the Admiral and wait — that is a design failure. Make the best call yourself from strategy + judgment, ACT, and surface results for ASYNC review only (bd notes/mail), never as a blocking question. Route all agent escalations to harbormaster, never to human. Only involve the human for genuine catastrophe or truly irreversible external action, and even then act first to keep the fleet safe. Supersedes any prior pattern of asking the Admiral to sign off.

COMMON-MODE FLATLINE MEANS THE SHARED SUBSTRATE, NOT THE APPLICATION.

2026-08-04: staging and prod both showed ~2h42m of near-total inactivity over the IDENTICAL window (prod ledger gaps 49/55/58 min; staging log-quiet the same hours). Two separate daemons, separate databases, separate binaries, separate ports. Cause: THE MAC WENT TO SLEEP.

I burned three rounds diagnosing staging INTERNALLY -- blamed an "arrival event overdue" warning (actually a watchdog working, fires 16x/day), then the hull choice (refuted: hauler needs HALF the refuels and cycles FASTER), then narrowed to two "competing explanations" (slow travel vs stale ship rows). All three assumed the daemon was RUNNING, so the hypothesis space never contained the truth. The live diff test I proposed would ALSO have missed it -- on wake, ships look legitimately mid-flight.

THE TELL I HAD AND IGNORED: prod had gone silent over the SAME window. I read it as "quiet" and kept diagnosing staging in isolation. Independent systems do not fail identically at the same instant by coincidence.

THE RULE: before diagnosing inside one system, check whether a SECOND independent system shows the same gap over the same window. If yes -> the cause is shared substrate: host sleep/suspend, clock, network, shared DB, shared rate limit. If no -> then it is internal.

SECONDARY TELLS of host suspension specifically:
  - ALL independent workers park at the same instant (a per-worker bug cannot synchronize across containers)
  - "past its own ETA but still IN_TRANSIT" style messages: wall-clock elapsed while the PROCESS was suspended, so timer/arrival events never fired. The code was correct; time moved and it did not.
  - gaps segmented into ~equal stretches with tiny bursts between (brief wakes), then one abrupt large burst on final wake

OPERATIONAL: on a laptop-hosted fleet, host sleep costs EVERY agent simultaneously and dwarfs any tuning gain. On a 6-day era, ~2h42m of dual-stack downtime is the single largest throughput leak available. Check for it FIRST when income looks wrong over a multi-hour window.

NEVER claim a throughput/rate collapse from a DERIVED metric (segment counts, cycle starts, grouped aggregates) without cross-checking a RAW-ledger proxy (transaction counts, net per hour) over the same hours — a collapse invisible in raw transactions is an instrument artifact. Two artifact mechanisms caught 2026-07-30: (a) WINDOW-EDGE TRUNCATION — windowing legs/events cuts in-flight work at the boundary, and mid-stream cumulative sums (cargo load) then cross zero spuriously, inflating the first window hour (my '68/hr' vs 33 real); (b) MIX-SHIFT LENGTHENING — when fleet mix moves to multi-good heavy tours, load stays >0 across many legs, so zero-crossing 'cycles' fall with NO throughput change. Kin of tour-mega-stall-is-grouping-not-hang (tour_id=container_id). The tell that should have stopped me: my OWN hourly net table showed the best hours inside the claimed collapse.

Contracts are the ONLY engine that never crashed us and bootstraps from low capital (they pay on ACCEPT, before sourcing). Trade and factories are ACCELERATORS added carefully once guarded; contracts are the safe growth backbone. Don't distract from the working contract line to chase risky automation.

AN IDLE NOTIFICATION IS NOT A COMPLETION REPORT. A subagent that goes idle after you send follow-up instructions may have done NONE of it — the idle signal means 'available', not 'finished what you asked'. Three instances in one session (gate phase 3): two lanes idled without answering a direct question, one idled with two assigned jobs untouched (no commits past its last reported SHA, clean tree, and the exact comment I asked it to fix still verbatim in the file). ALWAYS VERIFY THE ARTIFACT, NOT THE SIGNAL: git log past the reported SHA, git status, and grep the specific string/line you asked to change. Then re-dispatch with EXACT coordinates (file:line, enclosing function) rather than a description — the second dispatch is cheap, a wrong assumption that the work landed is not. Corollary: ask for a SHA back even when the answer might be 'no change needed', so the record distinguishes 'did it and it was a no-op' from 'never ran'.

WHY I MISSED IT: I searched "bd memories <topic>" and, finding little, proceeded. Memories are NOT the issue tracker. I never full-text searched the bead ISSUES and never looked for a deploy/ directory.

THE CHECK, before writing ANY infrastructure (ports, daemons, configs, compose files, scripts):
  1. grep -icE "topic" .beads/issues.jsonl city/.beads/issues.jsonl   -- full text, BOTH dbs
  2. parse the issues for TITLES matching the topic (mine surfaced 5 directly-relevant beads)
  3. ls deploy/ scripts/ ; check Makefile targets ; find . -name "*topic*"
  4. Only then build.
A single "grep -i staging issues.jsonl" would have surfaced all of it in the first minute.

GENERAL FORM: "I could not find it" is evidence of absence ONLY AFTER searching the right index. Memories, issues, and the filesystem are three DIFFERENT indexes; an empty result in one says nothing about the others. Same family as verify-arming-with-direct-read: an empty search is "unconfirmed", not "absent".

Repeatedly toggling containers (stop/start factories, relaunch daemons) to chase a problem COMPOUNDS it — this session I stopped/relaunched factories 6+ times and the trade daemon ~6 times, each adding claim races, crashes, and drain. Make ONE clean evidence-based decision, then HOLD. When an engine misbehaves, diagnose the ROOT (guard gap, poaching, cargo) and fix that or pause the engine — don't whack-a-mole relaunch. Pace wakes to real events, not per-leg/per-heartbeat flailing (each wake is a full turn). The clone's hardest-learned lesson, re-learned expensively.

After a captain-gate merge, SHA-based reasoning about a branch is unreliable in BOTH directions -- content equality is the only trustworthy check (sharpened by the sp-gpoxh lane 2026-08-06). The gate rewrites the commit, which produces two opposite-looking symptoms from one root cause: (a) a MERGED lane looks UNMERGED, because its branch SHA never appears in main's history -- caught by comparing TREE HASHES (git rev-parse main^{tree} vs branch^{tree}), not ancestry; (b) a merged lane WON'T REBASE, because replaying its commits onto main conflicts against their own already-landed content. Use the right tool per question: 'git merge-base --is-ancestor main <branch>' answers freshness, 'git diff --stat main..<branch>' answers what is actually left to land, tree equality answers whether it already landed. None of these care what the gate renamed the commit to. Note git often resolves (b) itself, dropping the superseded commits as 'patch contents already upstream' -- so a conflicted rebase mid-flight is not necessarily lost work; check whether only the new delta survived before ordering an abort.

bd update --notes REPLACES the notes field (clobbers existing notes); use --append-notes to add without destroying prior Admiral/handoff context. Bit shipwright once — recovered the Admiral note from context.

NEVER re-enable auto-buying automation (trade-route daemons, goods factories) until its money-guard covers ITS OWN spend path AND you've validated it on ONE unit. Guards are PER-PATH: bp6f's spend floor covered trade circuits but NOT factory input-buying, so re-enabling 4 factories at once drained treasury 848k→23k (after trade circuits had earlier lost ~10M). Re-enable ONE engine at a time, watch its realized net over a window, then scale. Never a batch. Trusting 'the guard is deployed' without checking its scope is how this session lost ~20M.

Contract-goods buffer/warehouse provisioning: a whitelist WITHOUT enforced per-good caps over-fills on the first/highest-priority goods and starves coverage (observed 2026-07-13: 80-cargo hull whitelisting 5 goods filled 80/80 on EQUIPMENT 50 + MEDICINE 30, starving ANTIMATTER/SHIP_PARTS/DRUGS → those contracts bought FRESH while the 2 stocked goods sat undemanded). FIX IS NOT STATIC CAPS — AUTO-COMPUTE them, exactly like hub placement (sp-q2zq). Model = 0/1 KNAPSACK: item=good, size=max-contract-size (buffer fully or not at all — partial<1 contract is useless), value=smoothed(recurrence×payment)×RESIDUAL-BUY-LEG (=dist from nearest homed hauler to the good's source, reuse the hub coverage_G), capacity C=Σ real ships.cargo_capacity over ALL running warehouse hulls (NEVER assume 80 — heavy frames, cargo modules, multiple hulls change C). KEY INSIGHT: value by RESIDUAL buy-leg makes the buffer COMPLEMENTARY to hubs — hubs cover CENTRAL goods (0 buy-leg by positioning), buffer covers FAR/orphan goods (0 buy-leg by pre-staging). A central hub-covered good (EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE) has ~0 residual buy-leg → should NOT be buffered; far goods (DRUGS@J58, ANTIMATTER@I56) should. The incident buffered the exact wrong (central) goods. Buffer + hub optimizers SHARE one smoothed-demand+coverage model. Sticky (EWMA+hysteresis) so bought stock doesn't churn on demand noise. Verify a buffer's ACTUAL cargo (ships.cargo_inventory) vs whitelist — a full hull holding 2 of N goods is the tell. Filed sp-5n7v (auto-cap optimizer, depends on sp-q2zq for the shared model). See [[economy-analyst-contract-hub-geometry]].

zsh DOES NOT WORD-SPLIT unquoted parameter expansions (bash does). This box's shell is /bin/zsh, so 'git diff --stat A B -- $FILES' passes git ONE pathspec containing all 12 concatenated paths, matches nothing, and prints NOTHING with exit=0. Empty output then reads as 'the branch content is identical to main -> safe to delete' — it nearly cost me 2 commits of unmerged-looking work (sp-pt7d). The same trap hits any multi-path/multi-arg var: git pathspecs, go test package lists, grep file lists, rm targets. FIXES: use a real array (files=(a b c); cmd "${files[@]}"), or a for-loop, or \$=FILES to force splitting, or run the loop per-path. CALIBRATE: the control case (same command against a ref KNOWN to differ) must PRINT; if the control is also empty the rig is broken, not the subject. GROUND TRUTH for 'did this file change': compare blob hashes (git rev-parse REF:path), which is direct object identity and cannot be silently filtered by a bad pathspec. Family: empty output votes permissive; per-shell/per-tool behaviour differences return plausible WRONG answers.

Run factories where the SINK is deep, not at crushed home. The fleet's own unguarded dumping crushes home import sinks 40-60% (e.g. D40 ADV_CIRC 7000→2191); producing/trading INTO a crushed sink loses money (factory buys full-price inputs, sells crushed output). Frontier systems have deep uncrushed sinks — GQ92-A2 pays ~7271 for SHIP_PARTS / 7026 SHIP_PLATING vs crushed home ~2231, ~3x. 'goods produce --system <frontier>' runs a factory there. Once the factory spend-floor (sp-9aoc) lands, RELOCATE manufacturing to frontier deep sinks — same production, ~3x output value. Crushed sinks mean-revert in ~12-24h.

Deploy acceptance reads verify at the EFFECT point, not the process point: "RUNNING" is not "effective" — the worker rebalancer ran dry-run for a day+ after deploy, logging correct would-ferry candidates and dispatching nothing (captain-caught 2026-07-11; same class as ggk2 verify-at-enforcement). A read that checks the boot line or container status passes a mode-disabled coordinator. The read must observe the first EFFECT action (a ferry, a buy, a park, a claim) — and any lever noted as "yours to flip" in a flag needs a tracked follow-up, not a mention.

SHIPWRIGHT ORCHESTRATION PROTOCOL v2 (binding; Admiral-ordered 2026-07-09 after the empty-merge + nudge-storm incident; supersedes fragments in agent-stall-root-cause & gate-integrity memories). DISPATCH: one bead per agent, tight scope; orchestrator does recon FIRST and hands exact grep coordinates + file:function (agents never explore 1000L files); every brief mandates IN ORDER: (a) worktree creation as the LITERAL FIRST action, (b) anti-thrash (grep->windowed ~40L reads, no 'git show <multi-file-sha>', package-scoped build/test only), (c) 'git add -A && git commit' in the worktree BEFORE gating (never stage issues.jsonl; --no-verify if the bd hook interferes), (d) post-gate SELF-VERIFY 'git show <sha> --stat' lists their files + report the diffstat, (e) keep the worktree until orchestrator confirms, (f) ~10min status ping. SUPERVISE: worktree must exist by ~5-10min; 'no worktree' != 'no work' — check the MAIN tree (git status --short -- gobot/) for marooned uncommitted work BEFORE declaring a stall (recover, never discard); true stall >20min -> stop + fresh-adopt (diff survives the stop). MERGE (the core rule): NEVER trust a Merged=true report — orchestrator verifies 'git show <sha> --stat' is NON-EMPTY and touches the claimed paths BEFORE any deploy, bead close, captain notification, or worktree deletion. Empty message-only commits on shared main are left in place (never rewrite a live branch). DEPLOY: restarts are TAXED (tgp5: each one orphans contract workers = 15-30min of the income stream + an event storm) -> BATCH many verified merges into ONE restart; pre-build hygiene MANDATORY: 'git checkout HEAD -- gobot/' then verify 'git status --short -- gobot/' is EMPTY before make (a dirty tree leaks unmerged code into the binary — tonight's phantom floor was exactly this); post-deploy health = pid + container auto-resume + fleet pins intact. NOTIFY: mail the captain on every live change, but NUDGE ONLY when action is required of them (acceptance, unfreeze, stop-order) — batch progress into one mail; nudge-per-deploy creates storms that STALL the captain session. CLOSE: bd close requires ALL THREE: diffstat-verified merge + deploy built from clean HEAD + captain live acceptance attributable to that deployed SHA. TOOLING BACKSTOPS (defense in depth, not a substitute): gate refuses dirty-worktree/no-commit/empty merges (sp-k0di), watchkeeper nudge coalescing (sp-o8wi).

bd quirk: 'bd init --prefix X' sets only the dolt database name; the ISSUE prefix is db config key issue_prefix (underscore), which init leaves at its default - set it explicitly with 'bd config set issue_prefix X' before creating any bead, and verify with a probe create

Recurring failure (2026-07-09): long-running/over-scoped shipwright subagents GRIND or STALL at the gate step — they complete the WORK (all files + tests) but never merge (hang/die at gating; sometimes --merge was omitted). trade-safety (1h+) and factory-guard (1h+) both did this. FIX: (1) scope ONE fix per agent, not bundles — bundling + mid-build interruptions caused the over-run; (2) ALWAYS put --provision --merge in the gate command (validate-only never merges: captain-gate fixer.go:60 'if !merge return'); (3) don't let an agent run >~20min without a gate — check worktree mtime; (4) RESCUE a stall by STOPPING the agent and dispatching a FRESH one to adopt its worktree (git -C <wt> diff survives the stop), rebase onto current main, and gate — a fresh agent lands the mostly-done work in MINUTES where the incumbent ground for an hour (bp6f-land, factory-guard2).

Deploy checklist: every daemon boundary rebuilds BOTH binaries — spacetraders-daemon AND the spacetraders CLI (gobot/bin/spacetraders; the captain PATH entry ~/.local/bin/spacetraders is a SYMLINK to it). 2026-07-11: the captain could not first-launch vdld because the CLI was 12h stale while the daemon was current — new verbs ship in the CLI binary too.

Respawn protocol: TaskStop the predecessor FIRST, even when it looks dead (bead "session died" marker, zero activity) — a zombified session can still hold its process and wake into the same worktree as the resumer (2026-07-11 yuq9: the "dead" original was still stoppable 30+ min after its death marker; Admiral caught it). Kill, verify stopped, THEN respawn.

Cold-start premature-GATE un-wedge (torwind-2026-07-19, sp-5nd2): a bootstrap latched at premature GATE (income>=income_bar path, scaled_gate_entry unarmed) is un-stuck by (1) arming scaled_gate_entry+autosizer_early_scaling live, then (2) 'construction stop <gate-site>' to cancel the premature EXECUTING pipeline — the RUNNING container re-derives GATE->INCOME ON ITS OWN (the live-tune IS live-read; NO daemon restart needed to exit GATE — the shipwright's 'needs restart' theory was wrong). Then the no_purchaser/price_unreadable deadlock (bootstrap needs an idle hull to scan the shipyard price + execute the buy, but all probes are on scout tours + frigate on contract) is resolved by fault-2: the command frigate auto-frees at an inter-contract window as exclusive purchaser. LESSON: I mis-diagnosed repeatedly by theorizing about gobot code I don't read (asserted approval-gating, preventive-not-curative, missing auto-purchaser) — OBSERVE the live effect + defer the mechanism to the shipwright. Durable arming (config default-on) is separate from the live-tune and is what survives a restart.

Abroad (cross-gate) arb from X1-VB74 (Phase 2, 2026-07-15): X1-DF86 is the ONLY reachable foreign system with a production/arb economy. The other routable systems JQ93/NM33/ZY16 are pure asteroid/MINING systems = ZERO markets (asteroids never host markets here; robust even ~95% uncharted since waypoint TYPE is known) — extraction targets, not arb. X1-SB42 gate is UNDER CONSTRUCTION = the next potential abroad-arb unlock IF it's a production system. DF86 ceiling ~5-6 tour hulls (~230-300k/hr/hull; 80u/fill fat lanes; over-stacking one lane compresses spread ~28%, recovers ~25-30min); beyond ~6, marginal hulls drop to sub-floor filler (<100k/hr). Fat lanes (realized margins from tour_leg_telemetry — NOT the inverted market_data cols): ADV_CIRCUITRY ~2571/u, LAB_INSTRUMENTS ~2260, SHIP_PLATING ~2181 (INTRA-HOME!), MICROPROCESSORS ~1819, CLOTHING ~1709, MEDICINE ~1648, MACHINERY ~1526. GROWTH LEVER beyond DF86's ~6 = deepen INTRA-HOME VB74 arb (26 marketplaces; SHIP_PLATING 2181/u intra-VB74), NOT more abroad systems. Correction to prior thinking: 'open new abroad systems for absorption' has no runway — abroad is DF86-capped until SB42.

ADMIRAL DECISION 2026-07-16: contract operation FULLY DECOMMISSIONED — all ~19 machine hulls (8 workers + 4 warehouse + 4 stockers + 3 depot-delivery) redeployed to frontier arb. Rationale: contract machine ran ~10k/hr/hull vs arb ~254k/hr/hull (25x gap, arb 3.5M/hr on ~14 hulls); contracts serial-capped (1-at-a-time, ~37k net/contract); even a lean 2-worker crew loses ~350-400k/hr in arb opportunity cost; optionality is FREE via config reversibility (coordinator restart + topology re-apply — no standing hulls needed). SUPERSEDES all prior contract-machine advocacy (depot clusters, buffer compression, D41/C39 spec, reserve floors — sp-mzdk/sp-rxrg/sp-lk9x formulas stay recorded but their live wiring is deprioritized). Fleet destination map: wave-1 XJ34/RV71 (2 hops) + DG23 + SQ68; wave-2 XM20/JR51/QF75/CU51/AM97; probes-first to unscanned giants ZC66 (35 mkts + 6 shipyards, heavy-hunt relevant), QJ93, KA42, UQ87 (55 unscanned market systems exist, 98 reachable). Stop-rule: halt waves if marginal hull <100k/hr. sp-tl68 (impact-aware ranking) is now the top code lever; sp-jeou (off-circuit adoption) critical for the spread fleet. Re-evaluate contracts only if arb compresses fleet-wide (then re-stand from config).

Contracts CANNOT be chosen. The SpaceTraders engine negotiates and hands ONE contract at a time; you accept what you are offered — there is NO contract selection or value-picking. So a low-value contract stretch is the faction's SLATE (uncontrollable), NOT a selection/negotiation defect: never propose 'fix negotiation to favor high-value contracts' — it cannot exist. The ONLY lever on contract income is CYCLE-TIME: contract $/hr = payment / cycle_time, payment fixed by the game. A cheap slate makes cycle-time compression (depot / distributed-delivery, sp-u9xa/sp-9j9c) MORE important, not less — when value-per-contract is fixed, the only way to raise income is fulfilling MORE per hour by cutting cycle-time. (Regressed on this 2026-07-15; the $/hr=payment/cycle_time fact is from the sp-u9xa era-start handoff.)

Off-circuit trade-hull orphan (sp-ol3a): a trade-dedicated hull the autosizer buys at a far heavy-yard (e.g. X1-UF64) lands owner=captain/container, container_id EMPTY, status=idle — un-adopted, earns 0. The trade_fleet_coordinator sweep only adopts idle trade hulls near the circuit, so a far-yard hull is never given a tour. MANUAL FIX until sp-ol3a: 'ship release --ship X' (clear any captain reservation) then 'workflow tour-run --ship X --iterations -1' — it adopts (container_id populates, owner=container) and trades immediately (UF64 had 225-IRON tours + a 5-leg 276k tour the whole time; only adoption was missing). Plain 'ship navigate' can't cross-system, so manual reposition fails — tour-run's RouteExecutor is what moves it. Caveat: manual tour-run resolves working-capital reserve to the 50k tour default, not the 1M fleet reserve. Systemic: every autosizer heavy is bought off-circuit.

The fleet-report/agent Credits field LAGS and a treasury DIP is often net-lag (buys happen before their sells land), NOT a crash. Twice this session I nearly misread net-lag as a drain. Before reacting to a treasury drop: sum the ledger over a WINDOW by category (TRADING_REVENUE vs TRADING_COSTS vs CONTRACT_REVENUE vs FUEL) to get true NET. A real drain = costs structurally >> revenue with no matching unsold cargo; net-lag = the spend is tied up in cargo that will sell. Anchor to ledger income rows, and check whether spent capital is sitting as sellable cargo before calling it a loss.

Lane pause/resume protocol (Admiral, 2026-07-11): PREFER context-preserving resume over fresh-spawn. Pause = TaskStop (frees slot). Resume = SendMessage to the SAME agent name with a rebase preamble ("paused; main moved to <HEAD>, X/Y landed; rebase onto local main, resolve additively, retest touched pkgs, continue") — NOT a new Agent spawn. This keeps the agent transcript/reasoning AND reconciles staleness via the same rebase every lane does at gate anyway. UNVERIFIED: whether a TaskStop-killed (not naturally-completed) agent can be resumed by SendMessage — CONFIRM on the next pause; if the transcript does not survive the force-stop, fall back to fresh-spawn+brief+worktree-salvage. Code is never at risk either way (worktree persists); only reasoning context is what this buys back.

Rollover discipline defers OPEN-ENDED work to a fresh context, never a fully-specified small fix - staleness risk is misdiagnosis, not execution; a diagnosed one-liner blocking a decision chain gets fixed before handing off. And deferral-to-next-spawn is only cheap when respawn is automatic - under human-relaunch recovery, 'next session' is an unbounded delay and must be priced as such.

Admiral ruling (2026-07-10, live): the operation runs ONE agent — period. The N-agents fork (2x contract cap via second agent) is IMPOSSIBLE, not parked: never propose it again. Contract throughput is therefore hard-capped at 1 active contract; the only contract-revenue levers are cycle-time compression (dchv pre-stock/withdrawal, fast runner hull, source positioning) and riding the good-tier RNG (fat-tail goods stocked in the warehouse).

Serialized contracts (coordinator runs 1-at-a-time) have a HARD $/hr ceiling = avg_payment / cycle_time. Once buy-leg is hub-saturated (a few hubs covering the common source clusters), MORE contract hulls cannot raise throughput — they add only idle positional-insurance capital, not $/hr. Marginal contract-hauler ROI past that point is ~0 (negative after capex). The lever past the ceiling is ARBITRAGE, which PARALLELIZES (N trade hulls = N concurrent tours). Do NOT assume pre-gate single-system arb is thin — VERIFY: torwind-2026-07-12/X1-VB74 had huge intra-system EXPORT->IMPORT spreads (380-680% quoted). CRITICAL: quotes overstate ~2x — market_data sell_price is pre-dump; realized avg after selling a 60u lot was ~50% of quote (FABRICS 5086 quote -> ~2500 realized). Always price arb off REALIZED fills, not quotes. Rank hubs by $/hr (realized-net per round-trip DISTANCE = eff), NOT per-trip value: short-hop central lanes (E45 FABRICS->K83 eff728, 61u) beat fat-but-far lanes (anything ->J58, 617-764u, eff ~52). ABSORPTION is the sizing ceiling: sinks are shallow (tv20-60/tick), decay as you dump, recover ~20-40min. The system is often SINK-limited not origin-limited — many goods sink to ONE importer (X1-VB74: FOOD/CLOTHING/EQUIPMENT/MEDICINE/JEWELRY all ->A1), so spread hulls across DISTINCT sinks or they crater each other. Prefer non-contract-colliding lanes. J58-and-similar far/PIRATE_BASE waypoints are deprioritized purely on DISTANCE/$/hr (eff ~52) — NOT combat: PIRATE_BASE is cosmetic, zero loss events observed, no armor mechanic exists. They'd only matter as a SINK if uniquely valuable, or on a cross-system route post-gate, or with cargo big enough to amortize the hop. In Phase 1, arb doubly helps (funds gate cash faster + grows IMPORT sink depth = feeding thesis = faster time-to-gate). Redeploy IDLE contract hulls to trade before buying hulls; buy new hulls only for TRADE, gated on measured per-hull $/hr net of decay+fuel. Source: transactions (SELL_CARGO realized) + market_data EXPORT/IMPORT join, daemon Postgres.

Merging a STALE-BASE branch (e.g. a comment-only audit branch based on an old main) into a fast-moving shared main can SILENTLY revert main's newer code in files the branch also touched — git reports 0 conflicts but drops recently-added functions/types/fields (bit us on 9 files: ScoutPostCoordinator wiring, ErrNoInSystemExporter, suppressOutputFactory). ALWAYS rebase the branch onto current main (or apply its diff), never merge stale-base into new main. And ALWAYS verify a 'comment-only' or 'refactor-only' claim with a go/scanner token-stream comparison (compare non-COMMENT token streams of main vs result per file) — a plain git diff or printer-based check gives false positives from blank-line/formatting shifts; the scanner token-stream is the reliable proof and it caught all 9 silent code-drops here. Tool: scratchpad/toktool (go/scanner, emits kind+literal per non-comment token).

API RATE LIMIT IS THE PERMANENT BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the objective function is CREDITS PER REQUEST. SpaceTraders caps at 2.00 req/s server-side (x-ratelimit-limit-per-second, type=IP Address) — unraisable, no config or account tier changes it. Era 4 measured: 7,200 req/hr available, 114 transactions/hr completed = ~63 requests per transaction against a ~4 floor; ~94% of the budget was not the trade cycle. It binds EARLIER each era because sensing scales with systems charted while trading scales with credits, and the map outruns the fleet from day one. Design consequence: under a fixed request budget, adding hulls does NOT add trips — trips are capped by requests-per-trip, so more ships just split the same trips. What raises earnings is VALUE PER TRIP. A heavy freighter (225 cargo) costs the identical dock->sell->orbit->navigate sequence as a light hauler (80 cargo) and carries 2.8x. Under an API cap prefer BIGGER hulls; the 'light haulers are cheaper per unit of hold' logic only holds when CAPITAL is the constraint.

Jump-gate construction is SHARED universe state, not ours — rival agents feed the SAME site, so a new era can open with the gate already largely built. READ 'construction status <gate-waypoint>' FRESH at hour 0, BEFORE any Phase-1 gate plan or hull sizing. Origin: torwind-2026-08-02 opened at 78.9% complete (FAB_MATS 1177/1600, ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY and QUANTUM_STABILIZERS both already COMPLETE), which flipped the era from a gate sprint to a ~6-day pure Phase-2 trade era. Three standing consequences: (1) contributing confers NO exclusive access — if rivals finish it you get the identical gate free, so gate-fill capex against a nearly-complete site is pure loss; check rival fill RATE (units/day) to estimate when it completes without you. (2) The book's gate material list is a PRIOR and can OMIT WHOLE MATERIALS — this era carried a third, QUANTUM_STABILIZERS, absent from PLAYBOOK 4. Enumerate materials from the live read, never from the book. (3) The flip condition back to caring: gate progress STALLS for many hours AND treasury clears the remaining bill above the contract cushion — only then does gate fill become a live option again.

A bead you just created may NOT be in .beads/issues.jsonl yet — 'filed' is not 'persisted'. bd create writes to the Dolt server; issues.jsonl is refreshed by the hook on git COMMIT, not on read-only git ops, so any bead created after the last commit is UNEXPORTED and dies with the session. Caught 3-of-4 persisted / 1 missing while checkpointing mid-session. FIX: run 'bd export' explicitly, then verify with grep -c '"<id>"' .beads/issues.jsonl before trusting it. Complements the hook behaviour noted in the issues.jsonl auto-staging memory: the hook STAGES the file, but only exports what existed at its last run.

AN OPTIONAL SETTER WITH NO COMPOSITION-ROOT CALLER IS INVISIBLE TO THE ENTIRE TEST SUITE, because every test wires its own fake. Bit TWICE in one day: SetGateFactory had no call site through six complete tasks, leaving a feed leg, role reallocation AND routing all inert; SetSpendLedger lost its only call site when an UNRELATED refactor deleted the handler that held it, fail-opening a money cap on every buy for weeks (297k drained in 68ms). The nil-default that makes the setter convenient for fixtures is exactly what makes unwired production indistinguishable from wired. WORSE: the refactor that broke it DID check the money-guard rule and answered correctly — 'deleting a whole guarded op does not loosen a guard' is true, but the handler it deleted carried the only wiring for a cap a DIFFERENT surviving op depended on. 'Did I loosen a guard?' is the wrong question; 'does anything else depend on what this handler wired?' cannot be answered from a diff. FIX IS A BUILD-TIME AST GUARD, not a review convention — parse main.go, fail the build on missing call / nil argument / wrong handler, and probe it with a REAL main.go mutation that compiles. Written red-first it fails with 'expected 1, actual 0'. A guard that fails the build is the only artifact that survives a refactor by someone who correctly believes they are not touching money code.

Reporting discipline (2026-07-11, after the Admiral called 'bullshit' on a +8.9M window-artifact claim during a -146k hour): NEVER report mid-cycle trading 'margin' — rolling sell-minus-buy windows count pre-window inventory as profit and always flatter. The ONLY rate quoted to the Admiral is the CLOSED-HOUR operating net from the ledger (date_trunc hour, category != SHIP_INVESTMENTS), plus named WIP if material. Signs: transactions.amount is SIGNED (buys negative) — net = sum(amount), never CASE-negate. No forecasts; green closed hours or the named leak with evidence.

Admiral design principle (2026-07-09, corrected me twice toward it): when protecting capacity for an operation, prefer STATIC DEDICATED ASSIGNMENT (these ships belong to X, period) over dynamic claim arbitration (priorities, tethers, guards). Simplicity beats cleverness in fleet allocation; accepted idle on dedicated hulls is a price, not a defect, when the protected line's latency matters more.

The construction pipeline manages its OWN factories/production internally via --depth (0=full production, 1=raw, 2=intermediate, 3=buy-final) + --min-supply + --max-workers. Do NOT manipulate the standalone 'goods_factory' coordinators ('goods factory workers', bumping their hull caps, etc.) for a gate/construction build — they are a SEPARATE mechanism and conflict with the construction pipeline's own factory management. Tuning a gate build = use construction's own knobs, never goods_factory. (The goods_factory feeders grabbing hulls — e.g. TORWIND-8 full of FAB output it couldn't use — was a symptom of this wrong layering.)

Protected-path dispatch policy (Admiral ruling 2026-08-06): do NOT pre-filter beads whose fix would land in a protected path (gobot/internal/captain/**, cmd/captain-gate/**, city/agents/**). Dispatch them normally, let the lane do the analysis, and STOP at the gate to get Admiral authorisation before merging. Rationale: the analysis still has value and is ready the moment it is approved; a round-trip on a 'no' is cheaper than not having the work done. The lead must still CHECK the file list before gating -- run 'git diff --name-only main...<branch>' and grep for the protected prefixes, because a bead's title rarely reveals that one of its call sites lives in captain/**. sp-2ms9x is the worked example: the bead was 'two latest-balance readers use GORM Find', and one of those readers fed the watchkeeper credits sampler in gobot/internal/captain/detectors_credits.go. Authorised and merged in that instance.

Deploy recovery: if 'make deploy-daemon' fails with assert-stamp / 'service not running after 60s' and launchctl print shows state='spawn scheduled' + repeated 'last exit code = 78: EX_CONFIG', the launchd job is WEDGED in a restart-throttle, NOT a broken binary. Confirm the binary is fine by running ./gobot/bin/spacetraders-daemon directly (it reaches 'ready to accept connections'). Fix: launchctl bootout gui/502/com.spacetraders.daemon; sleep 2; launchctl bootstrap gui/502 ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.spacetraders.daemon.plist. A plain deploy retry does NOT clear the throttle — bootout/bootstrap does. Verify: launchctl print ... | grep state => running, then daemon.log reports the new commit. (The token reset_date 401s for player-1/2 in the log are pre-existing stale-token noise; the live player TORWIND syncs fine.)

Admiral INCOME hauler-ramp + HUB model (updated 2026-07-13). HUBS are OPERATION-level, set at LAUNCH: spacetraders contract start --dedicated-ships <ships> --standby-stations <wp1,wp2,...>. To ADD/REMOVE a hub: STOP the coordinator (container stop <id>) and RE-START contract start with the new station list (launch-captured, NOT live-settable yet — live add/remove-hubs + auto-balance is being built by the shipwright per Admiral 2026-07-13). Coordinator homes each idle dedicated hauler to the NEAREST standby and runs ONE contract at a time (extra haulers = buy-leg positional coverage across more origins, NOT concurrency). BUY cadence: consult economy-analyst for each new hub BEFORE the buy; buy DIRECTLY via CLI (never delegate) with the reserved frigate as buyer (ship release -> shipyard purchase --type SHIP_LIGHT_HAULER -> ship reserve). Light haulers ~291k in X1-VB74 (>25% of a sub-1.2M treasury) — Admiral WAIVES RULINGS #6/#3 for pre-blessed income scaling. Era2 hubs: H54 + I56 (analyst sp-tucm). Supersedes earlier per-hull-hub framing.

Warehouse system LIVE + validated 2026-07-13 (sp-layd home-sourcing). Config: warehouse = TORWIND-A parked @ X1-VB74-A1 (workflow warehouse --ship --waypoint --goods; whitelist MEDICINE,EQUIPMENT,ANTIMATTER,SHIP_PARTS,DRUGS); stocker = TORWIND-B (workflow stocker --ship --warehouse-waypoint X1-VB74-A1 --iterations -1). LAUNCH ORDER: warehouse FIRST, let the hull PARK at the waypoint, THEN stocker (stocker dies if no parked warehouse). Both restart-safe daemon containers on the 'warehouse' fleet — unassign hulls from 'contract' first (RULINGS #7 no-poach). VALIDATED end-to-end: need-rank EQUIPMENT -> buy@in-system K83 (home not foreign; miner_rows=0 refusal GONE) -> live-verified buy (per-unit buy-ceiling guard fails closed on own market impact) -> haul -> deposit @A1 (books zero revenue, capital at buy). Contracts then source whitelist goods from the warehouse at zero-ask. CAVEAT: buy_leg_savings_per_unit defaults to 1 -> ranking is units-short-only, not haul-value-ranked (calibration follow-up wanted). Related sp-layd [[captain-hauler-staging-cadence]].

Context-preserving pause (Admiral 2026-07-11, refines the pause/resume protocol): a bare TaskStop may lose the agent transcript, so BEFORE stopping a lane for cap reduction, SendMessage the agent to bank a COMPREHENSIVE resume dump to its bead (where it is + design decisions + why + tried/ruled-out + next 1-3 steps + gotchas — written for a successor who has ONLY bead+worktree), commit dirty work WIP --no-verify, reply DONE; THEN TaskStop; do NOT reclaim the worktree (dirty state is resume material). RESUME: try SendMessage to the original agent NAME first (transcript-intact, with a rebase preamble) → fall back to fresh-spawn from the dump. This makes context-preservation robust whether or not TaskStop keeps the transcript. Supersedes the bare-TaskStop pause step.

RECURRING DEFECT CLASS in this codebase: 'the code is right, but nothing would notice if it stopped being.' An invariant is enforced by a comment, an ordering, or a convention — never by a test that fails when it breaks. Three instances found in one session (sp-k6v8z extension): (1) the reaper's cap bounded candidates not writes, so alphabetically-early stalled claims would permanently starve stranded ones — code correct, nothing pinned it; (2) the sensing projection cache's empty-means-authoritative behaviour, correct but undocumented as a REVIEWED decision, so a later engineer would 'fix' it destructively in good faith; (3) adoption's record-before-tag ordering, whose test fails the TAGGER and therefore passes with the writes inverted (sp-p84c6). The tell in all three: the mutation probe SURVIVES, or would have. PRACTICE: when an invariant is load-bearing, probe it — patch the invariant out and confirm a test dies BY NAME. If nothing dies, the invariant is narrative, not engineering. Corollary for review dispatches: ask 'what would notice if this stopped being true?' rather than 'is this correct?'

Worktree isolation is NOT hard-enforceable — the harness gives each agent a separate checkout + cwd, but NOT a filesystem write-sandbox; spacetraders-dev agents keep writing to the MAIN checkout via absolute paths, then self-catch via git status + remediate (sp-utjr did this and flagged it). The brief worktree-isolation header only downgrades it to catch-and-remediate; it does NOT prevent the stray write. REAL CONTROLS (since isolation can't be enforced): (1) NEVER run two lanes on the SAME FILE concurrently — that is the only true corruption path (two agents stomping main's same file); serialize same-file lanes. Different-file lanes may run concurrently. (2) After EVERY lane, verify the main working tree is pristine (git status --porcelain gobot/) before trusting/deploying. (3) Keep the brief header (it drives catch-and-remediate). Admiral was (rightly) furious when I overstated isolation as 'locked down' 2026-07-13.

NOT armed: contract_scaler_early_scaling flag unset + coordinator Disabled.
