GENERIC arb-lane profitability gate (never hardcode good names — must hold across eras). Before each arb buy, evaluate the lane at CURRENT lot-adjusted prices: net_per_u = realized_sell_per_u - realized_buy_per_u - fuel_per_u, where realized_buy walks UP with lot size + prior buys and realized_sell walks DOWN with lot size + prior dumps. Execute ONLY if net_per_u >= floor (recommend: >=~100/u after fuel OR >=~20% of buy cost, whichever binds — the % floor blocks high-priced goods with thin absolute spreads). Re-price EVERY trip against live next-lot prices; do NOT cache the up-front spread. Self-regulating: any lane that goes thin (low base spread, sink decay, or buy-side self-inflation) auto-skips and auto-re-enters on recovery. GOTCHA 1 (mechanism): the dominant failure is BUY-SIDE SELF-INFLATION — a hull's own repeated buys at a shallow EXPORT walk the buy price up (observed POLYNUCLEOTIDES @E45 223->246->272/u in 20min, margin collapsed +1240->+80, net-negative after fuel). A one-shot spread check misses this; only live per-trip re-pricing catches it. Same mechanism, sell side, is sink decay (see [[economy-analyst-arb-vs-serialized-contracts]]). GOTCHA 2 (measurement): arb P&L MUST match completed buy->sell round-trips. A snapshot between the buy and sell shows a PHANTOM loss (observed MEDICINE -121,040 bought, +181,760 sold 2min later = +60,720 real profit). Never alarm/gate on mid-round-trip treasury; a live 'arb is losing money' reading is usually this. Filed generic fix sp-u4tv (shipwright). Thin low-value goods are the leak; fat manufactured-good lanes (~800-1800/u) clear any sane floor.

Fleet trade throughput is bounded by SINK COUNT x 2 tranches, not by hull count. gobot enforces tourACapTranches=2 per (waypoint, good, side) FLEET-WIDE (run_tour_coordinator_absorption.go), in lockstep with the solver's MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES_PER_MARKET_GOOD_SIDE. It is a margin guard against per-tranche price impact — never raise it (RULINGS #4). Staging 2026-08-06: 194 of 209 margins-deaths (93%) exited 'could not reserve tour depth (sinks contended by other containers)' against a working footprint of just 3 systems / 17 waypoints / 49 distinct sinks (65% in one system) shared by 9 trade hulls; 2,454 genuine breaches that day. CAUTION reading that verdict: the string is emitted on TWO conditions — a real breach OR a ledger-gate error (absorption.go:117) — so separate them before concluding economics: count 'reserve errored' (op fault) vs 'breached the fleet-wide sink cap' (real) vs 'release failed' (leaks depth until the TTL sweep). Here it was 0 / 2454 / 6, so the contention was real. Also do NOT infer 'no contention' from an empty market_absorption_ledger: reservations are released at the top of every re-plan, so the table is near-empty between planning instants even under heavy contention. CONSEQUENCE: adding haulers to a saturated footprint buys nothing — the marginal hull cannot reserve depth. Depth grows ONLY by adding markets/systems. See sp-9cwf4: the reposition ranker is the release valve for this pressure and it degenerates exactly on fresh unworked ground (prerank derives from CACHED spread, which virgin systems lack). Pairs with [[trade-throughput-is-sink-contended]].

A hull is stranded by WHERE it was bought, not by what it cost — but check whether it is TOPOLOGY or the RANKING before blaming the position. Staging 2026-08-06: a 1.88M SHIP_HEAVY_FREIGHTER (cargo 225) was bought at the yard X1-RX81-FX5D and executed ZERO tour legs, ever. 'market spreads --system X1-RX81' returns 'No profitable arbitrage lanes', so the PLACEMENT was genuinely bad — a yard system is selected for having a shipyard, not for having arbitrage. BUT the hull was NOT trapped: 'Reposition reach from X1-RX81: 18 candidate(s) within 12 jumps, 0 herd-excluded'. It could not leave because the reposition pre-rank only sends the top-3 to the solver and that score is ANTI-predictive of planned profit (Pearson -0.29, Spearman -0.11, n=139; the >=50k-prerank group returns the LOWEST mean fresh profit, 49,771, vs 74,180 for prerank=0). See sp-9cwf4. LESSON: 'the hull has no options' and 'the algorithm never evaluated its options' produce the SAME log line ('margins died') and the same zero revenue — separate them by reading the REACH count before the ranking outcome. Before approving any hull buy, price the yard system's own lanes AND the reposition path out. Corollary for refutes: 'we can afford it' and 'it pays back in N hours' are both satisfiable while realized income stays exactly 0. Also sp-dlfy6: that buy was 71% of treasury via the unguarded CLI shipyard-purchase path.

Probe assignment_status='idle' SNAPSHOTS are misleading — do NOT conclude 'probes are doing nothing' from an idle count. Probes cycle idle<->active in SECONDS while scanning (scan a market in 1-2s, then travel/wait = 'idle'), so a point-in-time snapshot catches most mid-hop as 'idle' even when scanning is HEALTHY. Observed 2026-07-15: '64 idle / 2 active' snapshot looked like a total stall, but market_data showed 112 markets scanned in the last 10min (newest 18s ago) — scanning was fine. VERIFY actual work via OUTPUT recency (market_data.last_updated: markets scanned in last N min) or gate_edges growth, NOT the idle/active ship snapshot. Also: don't churn coordinator tunables chasing a misread — I raised pathfinders 6->12 and frontier cap 60->80 chasing a phantom stall, which did nothing and degraded arb-core freshness (DF86 43->159min) via the reserved_frontier_floor shedding probes the frontier couldn't absorb (sp-iopd dispatch gap).

DB query hygiene (learned 2026-07-15, made this mistake TWICE in one session): the daemon Postgres MULTI-PLAYER tables — ships, market_data, shipyard_inventory — hold ALL players' rows, NOT just ours. ALWAYS add 'WHERE player_id=3' when counting/aggregating them. Skipping it counts competitors' data and manufactures phantom bugs: reported market_data '52 systems' (really 6 for p3) and ships '105 satellites / DB bloat' (really 32 for p3; player-2 has 70). It even spawned a bogus bead (sp-505y) off a bad number. EXCEPTION: gate_edges is universe-wide (no player_id) — correctly unscoped. Also: /my/ships paginates 20/page — read meta.total and ALL pages before counting probes (a 2-page scan undercounted 30->15).

Admiral ruling (2026-07-09): game-state ACTIONS go through the spacetraders CLI ONLY — never raw game-API curl (desyncs the daemon cache; the one sanctioned bypass pattern is unpin-then-CLI, not API). READ-ONLY psql against the local daemon DB is explicitly FINE and sanctioned for ledger analytics/forensics (aggregations the CLI lacks — sp-odd9 tracks the gap). Reads can't move credits or touch game state; don't over-correct them away.

HARD RULE from the 23%-utilization incident (2026-07-10): (1) EVERY wake's auto-assess runs a LITERAL fleet census — count idle hulls by class from 'ship list', never from memory; any unexplained idle gets tasked or explained in the wake note that same wake. (2) BUY-THEN-ASSIGN ATOMICALLY: no purchase completes its turn without its deployment orders issued — a hull bought into a coordinator claim-pool (like 22/23 → contract fleet, engaged in minutes) is the model; a hull bought with a mental TODO (the 4 probes, idle 40min) is the anti-pattern. (3) Captain-driven multi-leg journeys (jump chains) are LEAK-PRONE across busy wakes — prefer engine-owned assignments; where manual is unavoidable, the census (rule 1) is the safety net that catches the dropped leg.

container get serializes a coordinators LAUNCH-FROZEN in-memory metadata: live coordinator mutations (fleet hub add/remove, likely other live config) do NOT appear in container get until a daemon restart re-syncs from DB. The persisted DB config (Store A) + daemon boot + live homing read the new value immediately. NEVER treat a stale container-get field as a persist failure — this caused a wrong sp-jcke REJECT 2026-07-13. Verify live-mutated coordinator config via the behavioral EFFECT (where idle hulls home) or the DB row, not container get. Observability bug sp-aoy2.

A LOG ASSERTION BUILT FROM SUBSTRINGS CANNOT DISTINGUISH SUCCESS FROM FAILURE, because the failure message usually contains all the success message's NOUNS — only the VERB differs, and the verb is the one thing nobody asserts. Concrete (gate phase 3, task 4): RecordsTheGoodTheTargetAndTheOutcome asserted 'FAB_MATS', '-EXPORTER', 'GF-1'. A leg whose BUY FAILED logs 'buying IRON at IRON-EXPORTER for the FAB_MATS factory failed' — all three present, test passes. The success marker 'fed %d %s into' was asserted by NO test in the suite: declines were covered, the successful dispatch was not. CHECK: for every log assertion, write out the FAILURE message and ask whether it satisfies the assertion. Assert the outcome VERB or a success-only marker, not the entities. Same family as the buyer.goods() map-keyed catch (a repeat buy of the same good still reads len 1) and the plan.Unroled++/roled++ probe collision — three instances in one phase of 'the discriminating token is not the one being matched'.

SpaceTraders manufacturing/feeding VERDICT (4-agent web research 2026-07-16, sourced to official docs + top-player devlogs). The feeding mechanic is REAL but works AGAINST the 'factories create profitable routes' thesis: feeding a market's IMPORTS grows its paired EXPORT production (activity->STRONG, supply grows) BUT that DROPS the export's price (deeper supply = cheaper to BUY, not a profitable sink). So a factory creates a cheap SOURCE, not a new route — you STILL need ordinary arbitrage to profit; it just relocates arb's cheap-buy leg. Evidence: Stafford Williams devlog observed 'EXPORT IRON price DROP as I supplied its IMPORT IRON_ORE'; his oversupply/production strategy went income-NEGATIVE and was abandoned for arb. The #1 credits player (whyando) uses production-chain data as RECON only (no profit calc). Community meta = contracts->arbitrage(core)->mining; manufacturing is NOT a discussed standalone strategy. Import/export ROLES are fixed at universe gen; 'new goods from trade' is NOT IMPLEMENTED (cannot create new routes). Market development takes ~DAYS; economy resets ~2wk (high fixed setup cost per cycle). TRUE scaling ceiling = the GLOBAL API rate limit (2 req/s, burst 10/10s, fleet-wide) — added ships past saturation add queue depth not throughput; factory hulls consume the same scarce request budget as arb. LEGIT narrow use: production-chain awareness as arb source-recon, never dedicated factory hulls. Caveat: Reddit/Discord unreachable by agents (empirical meta lives there); no public $/hr numbers; our universe may differ, calibrate from own telemetry.

Before starting/restarting ANY income engine (factory, trade circuit, new lane): (0) RESTARTING A PAUSED ENGINE = 'opening an income stream' under Hard rule 3 — it REQUIRES a refute-first consult (fire-and-forget) + a decision bead with the refutation line. 'Un-pausing' is not a separate category; classifying it as continuation to skip the consult is the exact hole that cost −675k on 2026-07-09. A deploy green-light ('safe to re-enable') is NEVER the authorization — it means mechanically safe only. (1) RE-READ standing analyst intel (arb board / market-state beads) for an explicit contraindication — a 'do NOT X' line in consumed intel OVERRIDES any deploy green-light (the analyst had already written 'do NOT feed home factories' when I started one). (2) FIRST RUN IS MICRO-CAPITALIZED: cap spend ~20-30k / one churn, verify that churn's MARGIN from the ledger (not just 'sells landing'), THEN scale. 'One engine, watched' is not a guard — an unprofitable engine burns >2M/hr, faster than any wake cadence; caps bound losses, watching doesn't.

BACKTICKS INSIDE A DOUBLE-QUOTED SHELL ARG ARE COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — they silently delete text from bd descriptions, commit messages, and any other long prose you pass to a CLI. Hit it writing a bead: every `identifier` in the description was executed and replaced with nothing, leaving 'the skip renders as , which is a misdiagnosis'. zsh printed 'command not found: busy' but bd STILL SUCCEEDED, so the ticket was created looking complete. The success line is not evidence the text survived. FIX: single-quote the whole argument, or just don't use backticks in CLI prose — write the identifier bare or in double quotes. VERIFY AFTER: bd show <id> and grep the exact phrases you wrote. Same family as the zsh unquoted --include=*.go glob failure: a command that partly fails still returns something that reads like success.

Player-3 X1-VB74 contract sizes are ~uniform: cluster 54-78 units, normal MAX = 78 (verified distribution over ~150 contracts). Observed exactly ONE 168-unit outlier (COPPER_ORE->H51, real-vs-data-artifact unresolved). DIAGNOSTIC RULE: do NOT attribute slow contract cycle-times to contract SIZE — sizes are near-uniform. Long cycles = UNCOVERED-hub distance (source-and-haul, no co-located delivery hull, good not buffered) + sp-3l64 hull drift. The lever is hub COVERAGE, not buffer depth: reward-ranked buffers need only ~80-unit-per-good depth. Regressed once by blaming a 168 outlier for a 35-min stall; corrected by the Admiral.

FAKE-BLINDNESS (sp-1hp9, 2026-07-10): 1z2h's idle-arb passed a 20-cycle acceptance SIM but was DOA in prod — every claim hit FK fk_ships_container (23503) because the sim's port-boundary fakes had NO FK to violate; the insert-ordering bug (ship assign before container row) was invisible to them. RULE for briefs: when a feature WRITES rows with relational constraints, the test plan must include at least one end-to-end path through the REAL persistence layer (sqlite/test-DB with the FKs live) exercising the write ORDER — port fakes validate logic, never schema/ordering. Same family as the empty-merge lesson: the boundary you don't exercise is where it breaks.

NOTIFY AMENDMENT (Admiral order 2026-07-09, overrides Protocol v2 NOTIFY clause): EVERY captain mail is sent WITH a nudge — always, no rationing. Rationale: the watchkeeper is/may be down and the orchestrator's nudge is the captain's only wake signal; un-nudged mail sits unread. The anti-storm rule applies to the WATCHKEEPER's automated per-tick nudging (sp-o8wi coalescing), NOT to orchestrator notifications. Pattern: gc mail send captain ... && gc session nudge captain <one-line summary + mail id>.

spacetraders-dev build lanes edit the MAIN repo working tree via the absolute paths in their dispatch brief, then relocate the diff into their isolated worktree + restore main before gating (a5dq/aoy2 did this cleanly; s8vw caught mid-flight with main gobot/ dirty). RISK: concurrent lanes can stomp each other's main-tree edits. MITIGATION: dispatch briefs must tell agents to edit files INSIDE their worktree (paths relative to the worktree root), reserving the main-repo absolute path ONLY for the captain-gate --repo arg; keep concurrency modest; verify main working tree pristine after each lane gates.

Checking whether a prometheus metric exists on /metrics: grep the EXACT metric name anchored (^metric_name), never a broad keyword pattern piped through head — 'grep -iE credit|agent | head -6' matched hundreds of Get-Agent rate-limit buckets and truncated the real spacetraders_daemon_player_credits_balance line out of view, producing a false 'metric never implemented' diagnosis (sp-8cz9 treasury incident 2026-07-10). Also sample gauges MULTIPLE times — this one oscillated 0<->balance and a single sample lands either way.

Two standing auto-buyers racing ONE treasury: the buyer with the LOWER buy-floor wins every accumulation race and permanently starves the higher-threshold buyer — treasury gets pinned at the low floor and never reaches the expensive buyer's gate (e.g. cheap probe buys at a ~3.3M floor vs heavy freighters needing ~4x price ~8.4M under the 25% rule). Diagnose from the heartbeat ('held at the buy floor') + treasury trajectory pinned just under the low floor while capex flows to the cheap class. Fix: set the cheap buyer's floor ABOVE the expensive buyer's threshold (live tune), so cheap buys only happen from genuine surplus. Generalizes to any pair of guarded spenders sharing a treasury.

When specifying a constant that gets SUMMED or MULTIPLIED (fee x hops, cost x units, per-leg x legs), the right point estimate is the MEAN (E[X] is linear), never the median — on a right-skewed distribution the median under-charges expected totals (jump fees: median 5,622 vs mean 5,992 = -6.47% realized error vs -0.129%). Median answers 'what does one typical X cost'; mean answers 'what will N of them cost'. Match the estimator to how the term enters the model. (Shipwright correction on my sp-wtc47 spec, 2026-07-31.)

A small aggregate delta (~5-10%) from a replay over heuristic-solver cases is NOISE until the per-case WIN RATE confirms it: per-case deltas are heavy-tailed (one +338% outlier in 48 cases manufactured a +6.1% fleet aggregate that a 96-case powered A/B reversed to -1.2%, win rate 12W/33L). Before recommending any arm from a replay: double the samples, report wins/losses/ties + delta percentiles, and require the median and win-rate to agree with the aggregate. Decisive verdicts (like -26% with monotone cap ordering) don't need this; marginal ones always do.

LANE CAP IS NOT THE CAPTAIN'S CONCERN (Admiral ruling 2026-07-11, supersedes the 3-lane-cap tracking note): shipwright lane concurrency is Admiral<->shipwright business exclusively. Captain never counts, flags, or sequences engineering lanes — only states operational priorities (what unblocks $/hr first) and lets the shipwright schedule.

A market_model.json (or any daemon-read artifact) VERSION change requires restarting BOTH the routing service AND the daemon, in that order, with no pause between. Restarting only routing does not fix a mismatch — it INVERTS it and takes every in-flight tour down. WHY: the daemon resolves expected_model_version from the repo checkout AT TOUR-CONTAINER LAUNCH and holds it for that container's lifetime; the routing service loads its artifact ONCE at process start; the solver FAILS CLOSED on mismatch ('feasible=False legs=0 cph=0 reason=model_version_mismatch'). So after a merge that bumps the artifact, the two sides are stale in OPPOSITE directions depending on which you restart. Live cost (2026-07-25, sp-ircfy): merge moved 2@torwind-2026-07-05 -> 2@torwind-2026-07-19; running tours stayed green only because they had resolved the old string pre-merge; restarting routing alone flipped every tour to infeasible instantly; the daemon restart closed it (feasible=True, cph 221k-703k). COROLLARY: routing FIRST is still right — it regenerates the gitignored Python proto stubs (the sp-qzej staleness guard) — but treat routing+daemon as ONE atomic deploy step for artifact/proto changes, never as two decisions. Also: a merge can open a fleet outage window with no code defect at all, purely from a data artifact riding it; check whether a merge changes any artifact the two processes read at different lifetimes.

When a standing coordinator takes over a manual operator workflow, its config DEFAULTS must reproduce the operator's STANDING PRACTICE, not the code's per-run defaults — sp-1278's working_capital_reserve default (0 -> tour's 50k floor) silently replaced the captain's always-manual 1M, and the fleet legally drew down to 419k before anyone noticed (2026-07-11). At dispatch time, ask: what values did the human actually fly with? Encode THOSE as the coordinator defaults or force them in config at deploy.

WHEN SOMEONE PRICES AN OPTION FOR YOU, CONFIRM THEY ARE PRICING *YOUR* VERSION OF IT. A cost estimate silently inherits whatever implementation the estimator had in mind, and the gap is invisible because both parties use the same option name. Concrete (gate phase 3, option (c) census restructure): the implementer priced it 'breaks legacy adoption outright, task-sized', I deferred the option on that number, and it was ACCURATE — for a NAIVE (c) that narrows the denominator without touching adoption (4 legacy hulls -> BaselineMix(0) -> nothing ever adopted). The option I had actually specified was the SEQUENCED one (re-express adoption from NextRole FIRST, THEN narrow), which came in at 133 insertions / 48 deletions in one file plus its test with no exported signature change. My own escape-hatch criterion never fired; I retired a correct fix on a price tag belonging to a different implementation. CHECK: before accepting a cost that kills an option, ask 'which version did you cost?' and restate the sequencing you meant.

Before recommending ANY cap/limit raise (tranche caps, worker caps, spend windows, hop ceilings): measure the CARRYING DISTRIBUTION against the cap first — bucket actual values as a ratio of the limit. Zero mass at/near the cap = the cap is not binding = raising it is inert. An output-watch guardrail (plan-error, rate delta) CANNOT validate a cap move: 'released' and 'never binding' produce identical output. The one-query discriminator is the histogram of value/cap. Learned 2026-07-29: recommended MAX_PLANNED_TRANCHES 3->4 while zero heavy buy legs exceeded 1.0 tranche (shipwright refuted with the bucket table; REALIZED_SINK_TRANCHES 1->2.5 had shipped inert the same day for the same reason).

CORRECTED 2026-08-06 — the earlier version of this memory was WRONG and is retracted. It refuted 'buy more probes' on a route-idle-first argument ('you already own 54 idle probes'). That misread 'fleet list': a sensing_parked probe shows status 'idle' because it holds no CONTAINER assignment, but it is STANDING A ROTATION SLOT — it is committed, not spare. Census proved it: 54 sensing_parked hulls vs rotation_slots=54, exactly matched, zero spare, and 'dispatched: 0' every cycle because there is nothing to re-task. THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS HULLS, and the authoritative counter is the sensing_slots table, not any log line: state WANTED=9282, PARKED=54, QUEUED=4 across 1482 known sensing_systems — i.e. the engine wants 9,282 placements and has filled 0.58% of them. Scanning is NOT API-bound: pacer issued 0.623 req/s against sensing_rate 1.527 available with brake fully released (1.00). A market is UNSCANNABLE without a hull standing on it, and the rotation silently DROPS unscannable entries (see the 'rotation' field comment in probe_sensing_heartbeat.go), so 477 of 531 known markets simply never refresh and go permanently invisible to the tour planner's age cap. GENERAL RULES: (1) 'idle' in a fleet listing means no container, NOT available — check whether the hull is serving a standing post before counting it as spare capacity; (2) query the backing table (sensing_slots) for a backlog, never infer it from a heartbeat; (3) size a probe fleet from the API residual, not the probe_cap backstop (3000): at the observed 2.45x headroom, ~130-140 parked slots is where API starts to bind at the current ~hourly per-slot cadence, and that residual SHRINKS as the trade fleet gets busier. Pairs with [[economy-analyst-sink-cap-is-the-fleet-throughput-ceiling]].

Spawned fix-agents share this session's $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp — leftover scratch files (e.g. a prior task's commitmsg.txt) can be read by a later agent and cause wrong commit messages/inputs. fix-r3cl hit this (read a stale hs2j commitmsg), caught+amended it. When briefing agents that write to job tmp: have them use a unique per-bead filename or pass content inline, and verify the final commit subject before merge. Not an engine bug; a harness-hygiene note.

CACHE WHAT CANNOT CHANGE; RE-OBSERVE WHAT MUST BE. The single most productive question for API optimization: does this request buy information we do not already have? Three redundancy patterns found in era 4, all fixed: (1) re-asking a MONOTONE fact — jump gates go under-construction -> complete and NEVER back, so 84% of gate-construction probes returned already-built; a built verdict cannot go stale within an era, so age it never, only require that it was actually OBSERVED (a row whose synced_at is blank was never probed and its under_construction=false is a column default, not a reading). (2) PER-SET staleness on PER-ROW facts — 270 systems carrying one under-construction edge dragged 932 already-built edges onto a 2h refetch cycle forever. (3) NO RECENCY GATE on a repeated visit — shipyard scans ran unconditionally on every scout visit, 4.1 calls per useful update. CONTRAST, and this is the load-bearing half: MARKET PRICES ARE VOLATILE AND NON-MONOTONE. A market crushed by our own dumping recovers on its own and the ONLY way we learn it recovered is to send a probe. Scanning is not overhead competing with trading — it is the sensor that finds the sinks trading depends on.

Sizing the contract-delivery topology (serial engine): the CORRECT economics is recurring-destination-hub coverage — measured from contracts.deliveries_json (parse: DestinationSymbol + TradeSymbol + UnitsRequired; group by dest, then dest+good). Destinations concentrate hard (top ~4 hubs commonly ~55% of contracts) with per-hub recurring goods. Cycle-time levers on a serial engine, by impact: (1) DESTINATION DEPOT (warehouse+stocker+co-located delivery hull at a recurring hub) kills the whole HAUL leg -> that hub's contracts drop ~11-13min to ~3min (proven sp-u9xa); (2) PRE-POSITIONED delivery hull at a recurring hub kills the reposition-to-source leg (~2-3min). SOURCE-side buffer saves little (buy is instant, source_span~=0). Build the #1 hub's depot FIRST, MEASURE, then replicate; cap at recurring hubs (1-contract tail doesn't justify a depot). ENGINE STATE (verified by code read, torwind-2026-07-19; CORRECTS an earlier wrong claim that the reconciler 'keys on concurrent-contract-count'): the capacity reconciler ALREADY encodes this correctly — sense_demand.go populates per-hub HubDemand.ContractFrequency, heuristic_planner.go ranks hubs by ContractFrequency*cyclePenalty*AvgPaymentCredits + buffer goods by value-density + VerbAddCluster for uncovered hubs. So automatic recurrence-based hub selection + manning IS built. The LIVE gap is it emits 0 proposals despite real demand (K83 x8 etc.) — a runtime SENSE->proposal pipeline failure (filed sp-10nn P1 shipwright), NOT a demand-model rewrite. Also: a dedicated contract-hub coordinator (facility-location) is DEAD/unwired, and 3 hub-selection paths disagree (bootstrap selectContractHubs=2, reconciler planner, dead coordinator). IDLE-ARB double-duty: don't buy hulls for it until PROVEN (check for realized SELL/TRADING_REVENUE txns; if zero the dispatcher isn't firing — launch the trade-fleet coordinator + measure first). At flush capital the binding constraint is ABSORPTION, not the 25% guard. LESSON: verify engine BEHAVIOR against CODE before asserting a mechanism — behavior (0 proposals) != the mechanism you infer. Extends [[economy-analyst-coldstart-contract-op-staging]]; see [[shared-verify-deployed-head-before-filing]]. (refit hub geometry each era.)

CUT SENSING BY SCOPE, NEVER BY COUNT. Era-4 mistake worth not repeating: scouts were ~77% of daemon activity and ~84% of navigation, and I read that as waste and proposed capping max_probe_fleet. Wrong, and reverted. Cutting probe COUNT blinds the fleet everywhere — including on the markets we most want to watch recover, which are disproportionately the ones we crushed, i.e. our best sinks the moment before they come back. The freshness sizer is the recovery-detection mechanism: it sizes probes against per-activity SLAs (STRONG 22m, GROWING 45m, RESTRICTED 3h, WEAK 8h), flags a system when its P90 market age breaches its own SLA, and mans it for a rescan. It was already reporting demand 339 probes vs supply 200 — under-provisioned BEFORE any cut. The correct cut is by SCOPE: era 4 scanned 355 market-bearing systems while trading in 72 over 12h and 37 over 3h — ~5x more sensing than footprint. Scope the sizer's INPUT SET to the trading footprint plus a bounded discovery allowance; keep sensing inside that scope as fresh or fresher.

Admiral RULING (2026-07-12): the contract funding floor stays ALWAYS FLOWING; do NOT let contracts park/defer waiting for profitability. A stopped/parked/flailing contract frigate loses MORE (idle income foregone + fuel burned while parked) than the occasional rare contract loss - verbatim: "a stopped flow loses more money than some rare contract losses". So accepted contracts always source+deliver+fulfill immediately even at a rare loss (this is why sp-x8ck removes the coordinator negative-profit SOURCING guard). OPERATIONAL COROLLARY for the captain: a deferring/parked contract coordinator is the PROBLEM TO FIX (file the engine bead), NOT a state to preserve or hand-stop. Do not stop/interfere with a running coordinator to investigate - observe via logs, file the fix, let it run (captain twice misjudged the deferral here: once as a permanent deadlock, once as futile flailing, and wrongly stopped the coordinator mid-delivery).

Cache-desync doctrine (recurrence-watch; consolidates L32/L37/L47/L50 + L61 refresh-pool clause). `ship info` cargo/position/role can be a PHANTOM (stale cache) diverging from the SERVER, which is ground truth (delivery/sell API). It RECURS after each contract and after any purchase. The daemon now AUTO-HEALS it — sp-os5s (deployed) auto-refreshes on 4204 / cargo-mismatch / foreign-cargo / post-purchase signatures — so treat this as a recurrence-watch, not a manual routine. Symptoms: (a) a deterministic server cargo=0 failure — don't retry; (b) corrupted POSITION → API 4204 "already at destination"; (c) a phantom FOREIGN-CARGO hold silently BENCHES a hauler from the coordinator's eligible pool (looks half-full → not claimable); (d) a freshly-purchased ship caches EMPTY Role → invisible to role-based coordinators; (e) a hauler idle across sessions with stale partial cargo is a refresh candidate, not a lost ship (s81). Manual fallback if auto-heal regresses: `ship refresh --ship <sym>` (force GET /my/ships, allowlisted s32) is the in-band fix — do NOT restart a healthy daemon to clear a phantom. Desyncs strike FLEET-WIDE, so on any negotiate/workflow error naming ship state, refresh the WHOLE POOL (the daemon's dock-retry trusts the stale cache and can never self-heal on its own). If `ship refresh` is unavailable, recover POSITION by navigating to a THIRD waypoint (not the stale one, not the phantom "already-at" one). Role-visibility caveat: a phantom-cleared EXISTING-role idle hauler rejoins the eligible pool IN-LOOP with NO container restart (the contract coordinator re-discovers idle light haulers every contract-accept; s82/d-87 ran 3 contracts post-refresh), but a NEW/empty-role ship is picked up only on the coordinator's next CONTAINER RESTART. Diagnostic: a healthy daemon + RUNNING coordinator + FROZEN ledger emitting zero events was a silent error-loop — now also surfaced as a crash-LOOP detector signal (sp-no9i); check container logs. A merge self-deploy is itself a daemon event: the restart self-heals via ReleaseAllActive (open-era-scoped, sp-s7b7) and accepted contracts resume on next claim, but it reshuffles which hauler serves which stream (~5-10min) — after a deploy, verify every mid-workflow ship still has an executor.

HULL NAMING: ships after TORWIND-9 are TORWIND-A, TORWIND-B, ... (1-9 then A-Z), NOT TORWIND-10/11. Detection greps MUST use TORWIND-([0-9]|[A-Z]); a grep for TORWIND-1[0-9] MISSED TORWIND-A and mis-reconciled a buy (looked like 367k spent for 0 hulls when it was 1 hull TORWIND-A). SHIPYARD PRICE INFLATES with repeated buys at the same yard: X1-VB74-A2 light hauler climbed ~291k -> 305k -> 367k over ~5 buys. A 'shipyard purchase --quantity N --budget B' buys only as many as fit B (bought 1 of 2 requested when 2x367k > 700k budget). For more hulls: budget for the RISEN price, or buy from a fresh yard (H52 / C39) to dodge the inflated A2 price.

Fitted price-impact + recovery model (era-3, 2026-07-16, delivered sp-tl68). IMPACT per trade (x=units/tradeVolume): BUY dP/P=+0.0499*x (R2=.33,n=505), SELL dP/P=-0.0152*x (R2=.14,n=381) — buying a full tv moves the ask ~+5%, selling moves the bid ~-1.5%. Beats snapshot pricing 40-49% out-of-sample (the thing community bots don't model — a real edge). RECOVERY SURPRISE: organic deviation half-life ~520min pooled (tv<=40 ~339m, 41-80 ~663m, 81-240 ~1681m) — compressed lanes stay compressed for HOURS; the old '~25-30min recovery' anecdote was other traffic refilling a busy lane, NOT organic reversion. RULE: never assume a hammered lane is fresh again within the same shift; rotate hulls, carry a decaying compression debt (exp(-dt/750min)) per lane. Wiring = effective-spread + lane-cooldown ledger in the tour ranker (sp-tl68). Coefficients are per-era (refit from ~1 day of tour_leg_telemetry consecutive-leg pairs; script pattern: pair consecutive same-(waypoint,good,side) legs <=60min apart, regress dpct on units/tv through origin); the FORM is universe-stable.

Widening a budgeted heuristic search's candidate space usually makes chosen plans WORSE, not better: the fixed shortlist/scoring budget (FULL_SCORE_TOP_N, ortools node caps, beam width) gets diluted across more variants and the tight winners fall out. Measured twice in one day on the tour solver: max_tour_systems 4 vs 2 = -26% projected cph; FULL_SCORE_TOP_N 100 vs 35 = -29%. Corollary: never recommend loosening a cap/widening a search without a joint-feasible replay at LIVE geometry (candidate-hop-depth matters: the same cap comparison flipped sign between hop-1 and hop-3). Optimality claims about superset search spaces assume exhaustive search — heuristic solvers violate them.

ADVERSARIAL WORKFLOW MECHANISM DESIGN: a ONE-SIDED adversary produces a one-sided outcome. Layer 2 of sp-n2uve (archaeological comment collapse) ran 16 agents / 2.84M tokens and reduced the target population by 3.3% (975->943 markers, 25 of 470 files). Cause was MY brief, not the agents: I wrote 'when in doubt KEEP, bias hard toward conservatism' AND gave every cluster an adversary whose sole job was hunting OVER-deletion. Executors were punished for cutting too much and never for cutting too little, so keeping everything was the rational play — one reported 'candidates examined 31, blocks rewritten 1', another 'deliberately KEPT 110'. FIX: make verification TWO-SIDED — pair the over-deletion adversary with a DOCTRINE-COMPLIANCE adversary that hunts blocks which should have been cut and were not, and give executors an expected rate derived from the recon taxonomy so under-delivery is visible and must be justified per block. GENERAL RULE: whenever you brief a safety bias, ask what checks the OPPOSITE failure; if nothing does, the workflow will silently optimise to the unchecked side and report success. Note the run still looked healthy — 16/16 agents done, 0 errors, every guard green — because the guards only measured SAFETY, never YIELD. Always measure the outcome against the population, not the agents' self-reports.

The real arb lever is HULL COUNT — cover more of the ~13 floor-clearing lanes in parallel (near-fill ~5 hulls) — not supply. Reinforces the fixed-trade_volume fact. Caveat: ledger buy-side coverage is thin, but full sells imply full upstream buys.

Manual 'ship navigate' orphans a hull PERMANENTLY, and the symptom is the opposite of what you'd grep for. Depot buffer-selection score (CORRECTED, data-derived era-3 2026-07-16, unblocks reconciler arming sp-lk9x). A warehouse buffer's VALUE grows with source DISTANCE (far source = big avoided source-and-haul per contract), the OPPOSITE of the old broken heuristic_planner score which DIVIDED by distance (stripped far-sourced hubs like J58 to empty). CORRECT: bufferValue(g,H) = frequency * (0.030*sourceDistance + 0.147*avgUnits) [avoided-haul minutes; weights from regression cycle_min=0.030*dist+0.147*units-2.1, corr(dist,cycle)=+0.52]. SELECT by knapsack: rank hub's contracted+remote-sourced goods by valueDensity=value/avgUnits, fill the ~240u warehouse budget, NO absolute floor. GATES: only goods contracted TO the hub, exclude locally-produced (dist==0=buy on-site). Frequency window = demand-COUNT (recent-N), never wall-clock (a growing denominator ages established hubs to zero). Warehouse count=ceil(vol/80); stockers size to DRAIN throughput not hold volume. Mechanism (distance drives haul time) is universe-agnostic; re-derive weights per era.

A mutation probe's assertion must DISTINGUISH 'mutation applied' from 'sed silently missed'. If the assert string is present BOTH before and after the edit, a no-op patch and a real patch look identical, and you only learn the mutation landed FROM THE KILLS — which is backwards, because the kills are the thing you are trying to validate. Silence votes permissive. FIX: assert a POST-MUTATION-ONLY string, or a discriminating NEGATIVE assert (e.g. 'Reason: MoveSkipBusy must now reach 0 sites'). Caught by T2Fix auditing its own harness after the fact on probes 6a/6b (gate phase 3); the other 9 probes asserted post-mutation-only strings and were sound. Companion rule: a probe naming ZERO tests is an INFRASTRUCTURE failure, not a kill — go test prints [build failed] in the same shape as a real failure.

GORM Find: the empty-result hazard is Find into a SINGLE STRUCT, not Find generally. Find never returns ErrRecordNotFound; with a struct destination an empty result leaves it zero-valued and returns nil error, so the caller reads (0, nil) — unreadable silently becomes a value. With a SLICE destination it is safe: len==0 is observable. Two struct-form sites in this repo, both harmless where they live but both on the path the ledger-backed treasury reader will take (sp-2ms9x): captain/detectors_credits.go creditsFromLatestBalance, persistence/era_repository.go ~213. transaction_repository.go FindByPlayer uses the slice form and is NOT affected. Fix = First/Take + explicit errors.Is(err, gorm.ErrRecordNotFound) returning 'unreadable', never 0. Do not apply a blanket 'never use Find' rule — it condemns correct slice reads.

captain-gate rewrite hazard — a PARTIALLY-MERGED branch can NEVER be cleanly rebased onto main again (hit 2026-08-06). The gate REWRITES the commit when it merges (branch commit a7fd9512 landed on main as dec14f8d). If the lane then adds more work to the SAME branch and you tell it to 'rebase onto main', git replays the original commits onto a tree that already contains their content under different SHAs, and EVERY hunk conflicts with itself. The worktree ends up with UU on every touched file and HEAD reset to main, which looks like the lane lost its work -- it hasn't, the commits are still reachable by SHA. CORRECT MOVE after a partial merge: abort the rebase, cut a FRESH branch from current main, and apply only the new delta (cherry-pick the tip, or checkout the specific files from the old SHA). Never rebase the already-merged branch. Two follow-on traps: 'git checkout <ref> -- <path>' STAGES the file, so verify with 'git show HEAD:<path>' after committing; and never take a shared file like main.go wholesale from the old SHA, since main has moved -- apply only the specific line. Also: the gate refuses a stale branch (Stale:true, Merged:false) even when the merge would be CLEAN -- freshness is enforced independently of mergeability, so a clean 'git merge-tree' dry-run does not mean the gate will accept it.

captain-gate merges are now CONTAMINATION-CLEAN as of sp-ezar (2026-07-08, main ce5f46b+): SquashMerge uses commit-tree(branch^{tree}, -p HEAD) + merge --ff-only, bypassing the shared index AND the beads pre-commit hook, with a guard that ABORTS on any foreign staged file (exempting .beads/issues.jsonl root+nested). LIVE-VERIFIED: a real gated merge produced a 0-contamination commit. So shipwright can use 'captain-gate -provision -merge' normally again — the manual-FF workaround is retired. ONE EXCEPTION: sp-a3r9 (open P2) — captain-gate -provision REVERTS a worktree's regenerated proto (daemon.pb.go) to main's stale version, breaking the build for any PROTO-CHANGING bead. Warehouse/contract sourcing value is TIME/logistics, NOT credits saved. We pay for warehouse inventory when the stocker buys it at market; a contract sourcing from the warehouse at 'zero ask' is NOT savings — the cost was already spent upstream. Net credits are ~the same (stocker buys instead of hauler). The real win: warehouse sits at a central hub (A1) so contract haulers grab stock nearby instead of long round-trips to scattered source markets -> shorter fulfillment legs -> higher contract throughput (contracts/hr). Second-order only: stocker may buy ahead in bulk at better-timed prices. NOTE: the daemon log misframes this as 'realized savings NNNNN, contract sourcing cost 0' (double-counts — books avoided market cost as savings while ignoring the stocker already paid it); do NOT trust that metric for profitability/burn analysis.

A SHA quoted in a bead's NOTES is NOT a reliable ancestry key — captain-gate REWRITES lane commits, so the lane's own recorded SHA often does not exist in main at all (found 2026-08-06: sp-pc8cl's notes cite ebbc21f1; 'git rev-parse --verify ebbc21f1' fails with 'Needed a single revision', yet the change IS in main — verified by reading the code). Stopping at the failed ancestry check would have reported shipped work as unshipped. Rule: 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main' is only meaningful for SHAs that ARE main commits (e.g. 8743ef92, ac8471a1, 68aa9697 all resolved fine). For a SHA quoted from a lane handback or bead notes, verify by READING THE ARTIFACT in main — grep the symbol, read the code — not by ancestry. Same root cause as the two other gate-rewrite symptoms already recorded: a merged lane looks unmerged, and a merged lane will not rebase.

Empirical experiment (TORWIND era3-4, n=3236 matched tour arbitrage trades, FUEL excluded; treatment = market data-age at tour-SOLVE time reconstructed from market_price_history; outcome = realized unit margin). FINDING: SINK-market (sell) freshness has a robust POSITIVE partial association with trade margin (+0.016 to +0.026 margin-pct per ln(1+min); survives good + sink-market + units + era-time fixed effects; replicates in BOTH eras, Spearman ~+0.14). SOURCE-market (buy) freshness is ~NULL. It is NOT a loss driver: loss rate <1% at every freshness level (money guards bind, RULINGS #4). Direction is OPPOSITE the naive 'stale->losses' prior. Mechanism is mostly SELECTION (fat-margin under-worked sinks go stale while the fleet keeps high-traffic thin-margin sinks fresh) plus a smaller within-market component; the refuted candidate was bid-recovery (within-market realized sell price is ~flat vs staleness). IMPLICATION: freshness is not a direct profit lever and staleness is not causally 'good'; the payoff is coverage BREADTH -- keep frontier/low-traffic sinks fresh ENOUGH to clear the planner age cap so the fat-margin trades become routable, rather than over-freshening already-worked competitive sinks. Refines the freshness=planner-visibility contract (see captain-freshness-derives-from-planner-cap, shared-scout-freshness-model).

Worktree dispatch hazard (2026-07-15, st-780): a subagent given RELATIVE file anchors (gobot/internal/...) resolved them against the MAIN checkout, not its isolated worktree — its Edit/Write edits landed on main's working tree instead of the worktree. It self-detected (git status showed no worktree changes), migrated its files in via git apply, and restored main via git checkout HEAD -- <files>. Orchestrator MUST independently verify after any such report: (1) git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> HEAD == false; (2) git show HEAD:<file> | grep -c <newsymbol> == 0; (3) main working tree clean of the lane's files; (4) worktree branch has the commit. FIX for future dispatches: give WORKTREE-ABSOLUTE paths (or tell the agent 'your cwd IS the worktree; verify with pwd before every Edit'), not bare gobot/... relatives. Related to the cd-into-main stray-commit pattern (same root: edits/commits escaping the worktree).

Socket & backends doctrine (consolidates L19/L30). TWO backends: the socket (health/ship/container/workflow) is the DAEMON; market/ledger/player are POSTGRES. SQLSTATE errors on the Postgres side while the socket still answers = a DB outage, NOT daemon death — keep operating on socket data. A socket hang (context deadline exceeded) can be spontaneous and may not self-recover in-session. Scope it with ONE socket probe + ONE ledger probe (if the ledger answers, the daemon isn't dead); don't hand-probe repeatedly (token burn) — record, defer, it recovers between sessions. A multi-session blackout can be an out-of-band ops event, not a code bug.

Long-flying CLI workflows (anything that navigates ships in-process) must run in BACKGROUND, never under a foreground shell timeout - killing the CLI mid-flight orphans any daemon-side state it persisted (claims, assignments) with no cleanup path. Before running any workflow verb, know whether it executes in-process or dispatches to a daemon container; in-process executors die with your shell.

Coordinator DB-read hang class (sp-ljvxa): a long-running daemon coordinator loop that passes its container's long-lived ctx straight into DB reads can freeze FOREVER — Go database/sql has NO connection-acquire timeout and the daemon sets NO server statement_timeout, so QueryContext waits for a free pool conn until ctx cancels; on pool exhaustion (coordinator contention) that is forever: RUNNING-but-silent, no error, no panic. Daemon-wide idiom is context.WithTimeout(ctx, dbOperationTimeout=5s) per DB op (container_runner.go, 8 sites); any coordinator loop that skips it is a latent 11h-hang. Fix pattern: bound the reads → a stuck read errors → retried next tick. The RUNNING-but-hung container CLASS is also what sp-m3122 solved for trade tours via a progress-based liveness watchdog.

So going deeper = change one number + restart daemon; do NOT file it as an engineering build (I filed sp-1cuy6 wrongly on that premise and had to correct it). Verification doctrine (spine = L62; consolidates L20/L39/L42/L52/L60/L62). Merged is a CLAIM, not a result: declare a capability unblocked ONLY on its first observable OUTPUT — material/credits/rows — never on a merged fix. Exercise IMMEDIATELY after every merge, and re-verify capability state EVERY session (it flips) by testing permitted commands LIVE — don't trust stale "degraded" notes or a report's stale numbers (L20). Confirm by EXERCISING observed behavior, not status alone (L39). Never-exercised subsystems fail in CHAINS (s83-s91 construction: missing migration → no activation/executor → poisoned 0-task pipeline → over-strict market filter): plan for N>1 blockers and keep each probe cheap. Three ways "merged" lies: (1) a merged DAEMON fix takes effect only after the daemon RESTARTS (L39); (2) a client-side CLI panic can persist from a STALE BINARY after its fix merges — re-verify by exercising, reopen merged→new on recurrence (L42; `ship sell` confirmed crash-safe s28); (3) a merged feature with GREEN tests can still break production on SCHEMA — test DBs auto-migrate from GORM tags, production relies on hand-written migrations, so on a schema-touching `feat` re-check the earner next session and confirm the fix reached the LIVE DB (a 42703 self-heals once the column exists — leave the coordinator running, idempotent failed Saves) (L52). And a merged code fix does NOT repair the STATE the buggy binary already left behind: expect poisoned persisted rows as a SECOND, independent blocker (s87: an EXECUTING CONSTRUCTION pipeline whose tasks restart-recovery had reaped), and idempotent "resume" verbs turn that state into a permanent trap (StartOrResume returns any PLANNING/EXECUTING pipeline as-is — --depth ignored, no re-plan, nothing terminalizes a 0-task pipeline). So verify the DATA precondition (do the tasks/rows exist?) in the same breath as the code path, and put "tasks exist" BEFORE "output > 0" in the expectation chain (L60). Corollary: when a start verb fails on a market/data precondition, read the exact filter threshold in CODE before waiting for the world to change — the tolerant variant may already exist one function away (FindExportMarketBySupplyPriority vs FindExportMarketWithGoodSupply) (L62).

sp-gm00 root cause: tour planner's single-good manifests on heavy hulls are a BEAM defect, not allocation. score_sequence already packs multi-good (probe: 225u/4 goods on a direct SRC->SNK). The gap is beam_sequences: pair_gain credited only the single best good x FULL hold, over-valuing thin single goods (vol-6 sink can't fill a hold) and never surfacing diverse clusters into FULL_SCORE_TOP_N=20. Plus empty-ship seeds tie at 0 so alphabetically-late cluster SOURCES get pruned. Fix: pack_gain (multi-good, per-good capped at A-cap tranche depth) + seed lookahead by best outgoing pack.

t.Fatalf makes every later assertion in the SAME test unreachable — and a mutation probe that 'kills' such a test is killing on what the code REPORTED, not on what it DID. Confirmed 3x in one phase (gate factory fleet, phase 3), including in a probe I designed myself: probe 6a asserted !result.Refused via t.Fatalf FIRST, so the navigate assertion below it never executed and the leg's liveness was never proven. Two more found by sweep at gate_feed_test.go:70 and :193. FIX: put the BEHAVIOUR assertion first (the fixture file that did this is exactly why probe 6b landed correctly); or use t.Errorf when you want later assertions to run. CHECK: for every probe, ask 'which assertion actually fired?' — not 'did the test go red?'. Sibling class, same root: a fixture that ECHOES its input back as its output cannot separate the two values a test claims to separate (task 3's sell returned UnitsSold: cmd.Units, so offered==taken and an offered-vs-taken bug was undetectable; closed with a partial-fill mediator taking 4 of every 10 offered).

IDLE IS NOT COMPLETE, AND THE STATE CAN MOVE UNDER YOU. A subagent's idle notification means 'available', not 'finished what you asked' — verify the ARTIFACT (git log past its reported SHA, grep the exact string you asked changed), never the signal. BUT re-verify before reporting a lane FAILED: it can commit minutes after idling. Gate phase 3: BeadFix idled 04:01:53Z with both jobs undone (HEAD=29446276, comment verbatim), then committed at 04:05:25Z. My 'not done' and its 'already done' were both true, 3 min apart. CLOCK TRAP: git log --date prints LOCAL (box is UTC-3), teammate timestamps are UTC — same commit reads 01:05 local / 04:05Z, so a 3-minute race looks like a 3-hour contradiction. Verify from COMMITTED BLOBS (git show HEAD:path), not working files: a clean tree can hide a staging mistake.

Manual ship purchase (shipyard purchase --ship BUYER --type T --quantity N): (1) ASYNC — spawns a batch_purchase_ships-BUYER-* container, returns immediately; verify via ship count + transactions, not the CLI output. (2) Buys AT THE YARD WHERE THE BUYER IS DOCKED (TORWIND-1 docked at X1-VB74-A2 -> bought at A2 @543k home, NOT the cheaper remote SH23/SP39). So to control the yard, dock the buyer there first. (3) Firing multiple CONCURRENT single-buys on ONE buyer RACES ('lost the claim-handoff race ... already assigned') — only some land. Use --quantity N in ONE call for multiple, or sequence them. (4) Credits-delta is a bad cost proxy when trading/liquidation runs concurrently — read the 'Purchased SHIP_* at <wp>' rows in transactions for true per-unit price. Home LIMITED-supply price climbs ~15k/unit as you buy (543k->587k over 4).

Never judge a ranking function with a POOLED correlation over a top-K-selected sample — you measure the selection, not the ranker. Staging 2026-08-06: pooled corr(prerank, freshProfit) over the evaluated reposition candidates came out Pearson -0.29 / Spearman -0.11, and I wrote it up as 'the pre-rank is anti-predictive'. WRONG. Low-scoring candidates only ENTER the evaluated set in episodes where few high-scoring ones exist, so the pooled sample compares DIFFERENT EPISODES, not candidates competing for the same slots (range restriction + a collider on selection). The honest test is WITHIN-episode pairwise concordance: Kendall tau-a +0.475, 74% concordant — the ranker was fine. The real defect only became visible after partitioning by regime: when EVERY candidate ties at 0 the sort is degenerate and the stable tie-break (system symbol) becomes the only ordering, so top-K is the ALPHABETICALLY-FIRST K and, being deterministic, retries the identical failing slice forever (failure 78% all-tied vs 18% when the score has signal). GENERAL RULE: (1) test a ranker within its own selection episode; (2) partition by whether the score HAS signal before concluding it lacks signal — a score that is good-when-informative and absent-otherwise looks identical to a bad score in aggregate; (3) check whether a deterministic tie-break turns a retry loop into the same loop. See sp-9cwf4. Pairs with [[skew-is-evidence-of-a-policy]] and [[a-snapshot-class-is-not-a-cohort]].

register --new token print is deliberate last-resort recovery, NOT a routine echo — do NOT mask it. player_register_new.go:97 prints the agent token ONLY in the persist-FAILURE branch; the success path never prints it (token goes to DB). SpaceTraders mints an agent token once with no re-fetch, so on persist failure that terminal line is the sole surviving copy — masking it (as sp-c04g/byza-mirror tried) causes permanent identity loss. Closed sp-c04g won't-fix 2026-07-07. Token-masking (byza sp-byza) applies to ROUTINE echoes like 'player info' that run every wake, not to emergency recovery prints.

To read a hub's buffer/warehouse contents or roster, enumerate ALL hulls by location_symbol (+ role + container + cargo_inventory), NEVER an assumed/remembered hull set. Hulls get REPURPOSED into warehouse/stocker roles mid-era (e.g. TORWIND-19 manufacturing@I55 -> warehouse@J58 holding 45 DRUGS). Query: SELECT ship_symbol,role,container_id,dedicated_fleet,cargo_inventory FROM ships WHERE player_id=N AND location_symbol='X1-..-HUB'. Regressed twice 2026-07-15: declared J58 warehouse=11/12 only, then 'no drugs at J58' — both missed T19. Also: never buffer a good the hub EXPORTS locally (J58 exports DRUGS -> buffering 45 there is pure waste); and a buffered good that is NOT a hub contract good is suspect.

acd/gc mail: actionable crew mail MUST use --notify to nudge the recipient — WITHOUT it the message just sits in their inbox unseen (they aren't pinged). Applies to captain/economy-analyst/harbormaster/etc. Sent a whole session of un-notified mail before the Admiral caught it (2026-07-15). Default to --notify whenever you want the recipient to actually read/act; omit only for pure FYI/log-style mail.

Per-good net (revenue minus buy-spend) from the transactions table is MEANINGLESS without operation_type attribution: contract-sourcing buys book as TRADING_COSTS with a good_symbol but their payoff lands in CONTRACT_REVENUE with NO good attribution, so every contract-demanded good looks like a trading loss (07-28: FOOD showed -845k 'loss' that was really contract sourcing feeding +8.9M/day contract net). Same for construction_supply (FAB_MATS buys, no sells). ALWAYS split by operation_type (tour/contract/construction_supply/manual/arb_run) before judging any good or lane as net-negative. Also: the ledger CLI --json caps at 50 rows regardless of --limit 0 — full-window aggregates need SELECT-only SQL on transactions (scope player_id).

An unrecorded quantity can be MEASURED before the recorder ships, if the chain periodically re-anchors to truth. The ledger sets balance_before = AuthoritativeBalance - amount on re-anchored rows, so gap = balance_before[n] - balance_after[n-1] IS the credit movement nothing recorded. Pair those gaps with event timestamps from the daemon log and a ZERO-EVENT CONTROL validates the method: sp-shq63 got median gap 0 across 1781 zero-jump intervals, then -5343 / -10924 / -17424 for 1/2/3 jumps (linear). Two independent estimators agreed (~5.3k median, 6.3k mean per jump). Use the ORDERING-IMMUNE endpoint form (last.balance_after - first.balance_before - sum(amount)) for totals: same-instant rows tie-break on random UUID so per-row gaps carry large paired +/- noise that cancels only in aggregate. This beats 'ship it then wait for data'.

Module/exotic 'quest' is VOID this era (torwind-2026-07-12) — verified 2026-07-15, dropped, do NOT re-chase. More cargo/range = bigger HULL CLASS (heavy freighter 225 vs light 80), already automated via the autosizer. sp-buyd (module catalog/auto-install) is built but has zero supply to act on — can't fire. (2) EXOTICS export-only: across 287 scanned markets, ZERO import sinks for EXOTIC_MATTER/ENGINE_HYPER_DRIVE_I/REACTOR_ANTIMATTER_I (vs 17 for ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY). Terminal goods, not tradeable — their value is as FACTORY INPUTS to ADVANCED_CIRCUITRY. When a fix replaces a fixed mitigation with an ADAPTIVE mechanism and then deletes the mitigation as 'inert', the deletion is only safe if the adaptive value is verified IN THE FIELD. Staging 2026-08-06: sp-k4z5b (P0, Admiral: 'WE CAN'T GUARANTEE 75 MIN STALENESS ANYMORE') mitigated a 75-minute market-freshness cap by raising the floor to 720. sp-ry4r8 then REMOVED the 720 floor on the premise 'the cap is now max(floor, the live scan rotation's own anti-starvation bound), and at 4,389 markets that bound is ~13h56m -- so a 720-minute floor is inert.' In the field the bound computes 23m14s against a MEASURED ~7h real interval — wrong by ~18x — so effective cap = max(75m, 23m) = 75m and the original P0 re-armed itself: 3 of 54 parked markets inside the window, 91% of tours dying. GENERAL RULES: (1) a superseding bead's premise about a computed value is a CLAIM, not a fact — grep the live logs for the value the code actually prints (here the refusal line prints 'rotation bound Xm' right next to the cap, so it was one grep away); (2) when a symptom returns, search CLOSED beads for the same signature string before diagnosing fresh — the refusal text 'stale (> 1h15m0s cap)' matched the incident verbatim and handed over the proven mitigation value; (3) an adaptive bound that UNDER-estimates fails silently, because max(floor, bound) just quietly returns the floor and nothing reports that the bound lost. See sp-a2dc5. Pairs with [[closed-is-not-armed]] and [[log-numbers-can-be-sentinels]].

Tour-ranker calibration verdict (era-3, 439 circuits, 2026-07-16): the planner is UNBIASED — realized/planned net slippage median 1.000 in every bucket (impact exposure, cross-system); planned net rank-correlates 0.893 OOS with realized $/hr, duration model adds only +0.02. Do NOT invest in price/rate calibration layers. Duration facts: circuit hours ~= 0.25 + 0.50*cross_system (leg count irrelevant); cross-gate circuits ~38min vs 5min intra but net ~10x => $/hr comparable-slightly-better cross. The 20x per-hull $/hr spread is ALLOCATION (compressed-lane grinding, filler fallbacks, idle gaps) not mis-estimation — the lever is impact-aware ranking + lane cooldown (sp-tl68), not better point estimates.

HARD REQUIREMENT (Admiral 2026-07-09): daemon restarts MUST be resilient, because we patch the engine in REAL-TIME — every deploy = a daemon restart while the live fleet runs, so any state lost on restart means each patch damages the fleet. All operational state must survive/auto-recover across a restart. Current posture: SURVIVES — coordinators reconcile clean; dedicated-fleet/ownership is DB-persisted (l7h2 makes restart-survival a hard design requirement, reading fleet from DB not a stale startup flag); daemon is single-writer with claim-release-on-death. GAPS — (1) sp-perx factory auto-resume: DEPLOYED but NOT yet live-verified (captain flagged pending next restart); (2) sp-tgp5 OPEN: restart orphans in-flight contract-worker containers; (3) sp-w870 OPEN: ship reservations lost on restart. RULES: every daemon-changing deploy VERIFIES state-survival as part of captain acceptance; the restart-reconciliation family (sp-perx/sp-tgp5/sp-w870) is prioritized because it gates safe real-time patching; any NEW coordinator/state must persist + auto-recover on restart BY DESIGN (not a follow-up).

Before git worktree remove --force / git branch -D on a captain-worktree, CHECK (a) no active agent still works in it and (b) no uncommitted work (git -C <wt> status --short). A user/teammate calling a lane 'idle' can be stale/confused: flat-floor-2 (sp-05glh) was MID-TASK when I force-reaped it on that basis — it survived only because the crafter recovered the dangling commit via git fsck before GC. --force/-D bypass git's dirty-worktree safety. Prefer plain 'git worktree remove' (refuses if dirty) or gate/commit first.

A SURVIVING mutation can mean the property is UNOBSERVABLE, not that the test is weak — and then the right fix is to DELETE the test. sp-ehf4x: a probe hoisting a timer above two precondition skips survived, because those skips send no command, so the mock clock never advances and elapsed is 0 either way. No fixture can make a hoisted timer misreport, because a pure local read cannot consume time. Strengthening the fixture was impossible; the test asserted something that could not fail and inflated apparent coverage. Removed it and rewrote the code comment to state the placement as scope rather than a tested guarantee. Distinct from a weak fixture (bound tests need demand past the bound) and from an infra failure (mutation must name its target test): ask FIRST whether any input could make this assertion fail.

Worktree commits in the spacetraders repo must ALWAYS use --no-verify: the .beads pre-commit hook runs bd export AT COMMIT TIME (after staging), so a prior 'git reset -- issues.jsonl' guard does NOT protect — the hook re-sweeps issues.jsonl into the commit. Mechanism proven by the sp-mraj lane 2026-07-10 (caught pre-gate, soft-reset, recommitted --no-verify). captain-gate's squash path pins issues.jsonl to main regardless, but branch hygiene should not rely on that.

SENSING DOCTRINE — REVERSED by the Admiral 2026-08-04: 'forget the wake policy. You may build scripts to monitor stuff in the background.' Background monitoring is now ALLOWED; the wake policy is no longer the sensing backbone.

WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT with the earlier ban (2026-07, 'monitors/polling waste tokens'): the objection was to CONTEXT cost, not to observation. Inline polling burns a full model turn on unchanged state. A background script runs OUTSIDE the session context and only its state CHANGES reach the captain — same information, near-zero tokens.

ALLOWED: background scripts / Monitor tasks that emit ONE line per meaningful state CHANGE.
STILL BANNED: inline polling, sleep-and-recheck loops, re-reading unchanged state in context, monitors that stream raw output instead of changes.

BUILD RULES (each earned from a separate prior failure):
1. Make silence meaningful — cover every terminal AND failure signal. A monitor that greps only the happy path is silent through a crashloop, and silence then looks identical to healthy.
2. Calibrate every query BEFORE arming. A failed or empty query returns the PERMISSIVE answer, and the monitor then reports 'no change' forever. Prove each query against known-positive data, never against a subject that currently has nothing to find.
3. Guard one-shot/terminal events INSIDE the change check. A COMPLETE condition emitted outside it re-fires every tick and the monitor is auto-stopped for noise.
4. Poll local DB/CLI at 30-60s; remote APIs slower.

First instance: era-watch.sh for torwind-2026-08-02 (gate %, COPPER_ORE discovery, coverage/29, treasury deltas, contract fulfilment, container failures).

Margin and per-line P&L claims must come ONLY from a COGS-attributed source — ledger report profit-loss, or an analyst per-lane split — NEVER by subtracting a total-cost pool from a partial-revenue line. SpaceTraders books keep ONE TRADING_COSTS pool feeding BOTH market-sales COGS AND contract-delivery COGS, so computing trading margin as trade-revenue minus all-goods-cost is invalid: it double-counts contract COGS and can bury one-time mission capex (e.g. the FAB_MATS gate-construction bill) as a fake trading loss. That exact error produced a bogus trading-is-a-negative-line reframe on consult sp-f14n; the real split was TRADING +4.29M and CONTRACTS +9.47M, both positive. If attribution is not in hand, say unmeasurable — do not invent a split. Same failure class as the earlier false Postgres-down leg: narrative outran evidence.

Slow bead delivery is CPU CONTENTION + workflow overhead, NOT slow tests ('go test ./...' ~30s cold, 79 pkgs, no hangs/sleeps). ROOT CAUSE: many concurrent subagents each running the FULL suite starve the CPU -> 50-min tasks. FIXES: (1) cap concurrency at 2-3 subagents so they don't contend; (2) brief agents to test the CHANGED PACKAGE during TDD ('go test ./<pkg>/...' ~2s), full suite ONCE before gate; (3) skip test-quality-auditor for tiny/urgent fixes; (4) the gate's full-suite run is cached, fast on an unchanged tree. Do NOT 'gate it yourself' to go faster — the Admiral's directive (2026-07-09) is DELEGATE and keep the orchestrator context LEAN; self-reading diffs/build output bloats it. Orchestrator only dispatches, deploys (daemon restart), closes beads, notifies. Fable test-suite audit pending for deeper speedups + mutation-testing verdict.

Arb throughput = legs/hr x units/leg, and units/leg is the neglected term. Measure leg size as a FRACTION OF THE SINK'S trade_volume before adding hulls: if legs are <1 tranche, the fleet is paying full nav/dock overhead for a partial load and hull count multiplies the inefficiency. Torwind-2026-07-19 measured 0.70 tranches/sell-visit (52 units into tv~93) on 225-cap heavies = 23% hull utilization, while fresh IMPORT+EXCHANGE sink capacity exceeded TOTAL fleet cargo capacity ~154x. Sell-leg realization was 99.7%, so 'hulls cant offload' was FALSE - they were under-filling, not sink-blocked. Economics of going deeper: price impact ~1.5%/tranche (PLAYBOOK prior) against gross margin ~34% of sell price, so filling the hull (0.7 -> ~2.5 tranches) is ~4x profit per sink visit for ~7% margin loss, and stays net-positive even if the decay prior is 4x worse. Refines [[economy-analyst-arb-sink-limited-not-source]]: sink absorption is the ceiling at LARGE scale, but per-visit tranche depth binds first. Diagnostic: join tour_leg_telemetry to market_data on (waypoint,good) and compute realized_units/trade_volume.

Mail hygiene: 'gc/acd mail read <id>' does NOT reliably persist read-state through the rtk proxy — messages keep re-notifying ('[mail] You have mail...'). Use 'acd mail mark-read <id>' (or archive) to actually clear. Also: do NOT leave mail unread expecting a 'successor' session to read it — rollover/handoff was removed (sp-s8qq), captain is sole long-lived controller, so self-addressed handoff mail must be mark-read'd by you or it loops forever. Verify with 'acd mail count' (should reach 0 unread).

Single-system contract-hub placement (homing haulers at contract-good SOURCE origins for 0 buy-leg): rank hubs by PAYMENT-weighted value, not volume — manufactured goods (DRUGS/JEWELRY/MEDICINE/ANTIMATTER/EQUIPMENT) carry the money; bulk raws (COPPER_ORE/PRECIOUS_STONES/QUARTZ_SAND) are high-units/low-pay noise. KEY GEOMETRY RULE: home-at-source only pays off for geometric OUTLIER sources. A tight central source cluster is swept near-optimally by ONE central hub (all central buy-legs within ~10% of each other), so DON'T spend one hauler per central source — a 2nd central hub saves only the marginal inter-source hop. Dedicate haulers to outliers only when the demand recurs enough to amortize the long hop; pick the central anchor = the central source that is itself highest-value (zeroing its own buy-leg). DISTANCE/$/hr is the disqualifier for far sources, NOT combat risk: a distant PIRATE_BASE waypoint (e.g. X1-VB74-J58, 617-764u out) is deprioritized because the hop kills $/hr (eff ~52 vs 400-728 for central hubs), NOT because pirates threaten the hull. PIRATE_BASE is cosmetic in SpaceTraders — observed ZERO combat/loss events and clean buys already made there; there is no armor/durability mechanic that changes this. Method: cheapest in-system EXPORT per contract good from market_data (player-scoped, current era only — era resets change geometry); compute payment-weighted buy-leg per candidate home in Python; gate haulers past #3 on observed contract arrival rate (absorption), not on source count. Source: contracts.deliveries_json::jsonb in daemon Postgres (docker exec spacetraders-postgres).

A bead note added AFTER an agent claims the bead is invisible — agents read the bead once, at start, and do not re-read it. So a correction, a retraction, or a changed premise must go out as a NUDGE (gc session nudge <role>), not as bd note/--append-notes. The note is the durable record; the nudge is the delivery. Retitling helps a little (the title is re-read in queue listings) but do not rely on it. WORSE FAILURE MODE, and the one to watch: if you TUNE OR OTHERWISE CHANGE THE ENVIRONMENT the bead was measured in, you have invalidated its reproduction conditions for anyone already working it — their live reads will not match the bead's numbers and the symptom may look partly relieved, which reads as 'cannot reproduce' or 'already fixed'. Staging 2026-08-06: filed sp-a2dc5 from measurements taken at market_data_max_age_minutes=75, then tuned it to 720 as a stopgap while the shipwright was mid-build. ALWAYS nudge the holder with (a) what changed, (b) when, (c) the exact revert command to restore original conditions. GENERAL RULE: treat 'filed the bead' and 'the holder knows what I know' as separate facts, and treat your own operational changes as events the holder must be told about — you are mutating their test fixture. Pairs with [[bead-notes-can-invert-description]] and [[plain-text-never-reaches-a-teammate]].

The guarded trade-route daemon is NOT reliable to run unsupervised: it BUYS but doesn't reliably complete the SELL leg — exits mid-circuit leaving cargo aboard, draining working capital into unsold inventory (observed net -510k trade with ~343k stuck as unsold lab_instruments on the heavy). bp6f's spend floor prevents CATASTROPHIC drain but not this slow bleed. Until the loop/completion is fixed, prefer MANUAL hand-flown lanes (buy→sell verified per leg) or the ad-hoc arb-run command (sp-p4ua, one-shot targeted+capped). Also: manual cross-gate is high-friction — lights (600 fuel) can't reach a gate in one hop, 'ship navigate' is in-system-only (cross-gate needs manual gate→jump→navigate), and dock/orbit→navigate races on claim handoff (sp-ku8e). Heavy (2300 fuel) is the cross-gate hull.

RULE: when filing any friction/engine bead, label it into a real queue with an honest priority in the same breath. Ledger honesty: a backlog nobody can see is not a backlog.
